**Goal.** `sayLogsTail` (`src/cli/log-commands.ts`, complexity 18) is the `-n` tail view and its `-f` follow, shared by `logs --count` and the plain dump. One body interleaves three jobs: the `readEventsTailWithEnd` read plus the `shown` filter (only the four filters force the filter pass); the `--count` tally branch and the plain print loop, each with the same `!feed.json && (filtersGrepOrType || roles || notable)` empty-match guard that calls `sayLogsTailNoMatch`; and the follow, which computes the event-log path and runs `followUntilParentGone` seeded from `tail.coveredEnd`, re-applying `feed.filter` to every followed line. A reader asking "what does `-n` scan versus print?", "when does an empty tail print the empty-match line?" or "how does the follow seed and filter?" has only the one body to scan, and the empty-match condition is written twice.

**Approach.** Extract one module-private helper per concern in the same file, leaving `sayLogsTail` as the short orchestrator, and keep the existing `sayLogsTailNoMatch` (the wording) as the leaf:

- `function readTailShown(root: string, feed: LogsFeed, limit: number): { shown: HarnessEvent[]; coveredEnd: number }` — the current first block verbatim: `const tail = readEventsTailWithEnd(root, limit);`, the `shown` filter (`feed.grepLower !== null || feed.type !== null || feed.roles !== null || feed.notable ? tail.events.filter(feed.filter) : tail.events`), returning `{ shown, coveredEnd: tail.coveredEnd }`. It owns the scan-bound/print-bound distinction and the byte-end the follow must seed from.
- `function sayTailEmptyNote(shown: HarnessEvent[], feed: LogsFeed): void` — the shared empty-match guard, written once: `if (shown.length === 0 && !feed.json && (feed.filtersGrepOrType || feed.roles !== null || feed.notable)) sayLogsTailNoMatch(feed);`. It replaces both copies (the count branch's else and the plain view's `!feed.follow` branch) without changing either outcome.
- `async function followLogsTail(root: string, feed: LogsFeed, coveredEnd: number, seams: FollowSeams): Promise<void>` — the current follow tail from `const file = eventsLogPath(root);` onward: `await followUntilParentGone(file, coveredEnd, (lines) => { for (const line of lines.filter(Boolean)) { const e = parseEventLine(line); if (e && feed.filter(e)) sayEventLine(e, feed.json); } }, seams);`, with the seed-offset and filter-across-rotation comments moved with it. It owns the path resolution and the follow-loop locals.

`sayLogsTail` becomes: `const { shown, coveredEnd } = readTailShown(root, feed, limit);`; then `if (feed.count) { if (shown.length !== 0) sayTally(shown, feed.json); else sayTailEmptyNote(shown, feed); return; }`; then `for (const e of shown) sayEventLine(e, feed.json);`; then `if (!feed.follow) { sayTailEmptyNote(shown, feed); return; }`; then `await followLogsTail(root, feed, coveredEnd, seams);`. The doc comment stays, trimmed only to drop detail now carried by the helpers' own comments.

### `editAndAnnounce`'s complexity-18 flag/source/commit shell is split into one named helper per concern — the `--edit`/`--file` flag resolution, the editor round-trip, the unchanged report and the commit-plus-hold announcement — so "which flags does an edit accept?", "what does the editor round-trip write when the buffer is unchanged?" and "which message says the entry is still held?" are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the sibling `parsePromptArgs` split and the `parseInitArgs`, `movedSourceFindings` and `createTeamConfigKeyEditor` plans each extract one named helper per job the same way; independent in file of every Planned entry — before this entry `grep -c 'backlog-cli' PLANS.md` and `grep -c 'editAndAnnounce' PLANS.md` both print 0, so no `## Planned` entry names the symbol or src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts; PLANS-DONE.md records only behavior additions to the shell (the still-held prose and the `unchanged` no-op), never a split of `editAndAnnounce` (`grep -cE '^### .*editAndAnnounce' PLANS-DONE.md` counts three behavior entries, none a move of this body); docs/invariants.md names no `editAndAnnounce` symbol (`grep -c 'editAndAnnounce' docs/invariants.md` prints 0) — its INV-B5 binds the file only through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` and `announceFiled`, both preserved; touches src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `editAndAnnounce` (`src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, complexity 18) is the shared shell of `tumwater bug --edit` and `tumwater plan --edit`. One body interleaves four jobs: the `--file`/`--edit`/`--json` flag resolution with its repeat and stray-positional refusals; the ready-repo gate; the source resolution that either opens the entry in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` (an unchanged buffer reports and stops) or reads `--file`/positionals; and the tail that commits through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` and prints the prose or `--json` payload, with `stillHeldNote` when the entry stays held. A reader asking "which flags does an edit accept?", "when does the editor round-trip commit nothing?" or "which message says the entry is still held?" has only the one body to scan.

**Approach.** Extract one module-private helper per concern in the same file, leaving `editAndAnnounce` as the short orchestrator:

- `function parseEditArgs(args: string[], command: "bug" | "plan"): { path: string | null; json: boolean; positionals: string[]; position: number }` — the top block verbatim: the `args.indexOf("--file")`/`promptFileValue` extraction, the `rest` filter, the `rejectRepeatFlag(rest.includes("--file"), "--file")`, the `scanProseFlags(rest, command, { name: "--edit", example: "--edit 2" })`, the `rejectStrayWithFile(positionals[0])`, and the `position === null` `fail`. It owns the flag vocabulary and the position requirement; `fail` returns `never`, so `position` is a `number` on return.
- `function sayUnchangedEdit(command: "bug" | "plan", position: number, json: boolean, file: string, title: string): void` — the current `sayUnchanged` closure lifted to file scope: the `--json` `{ file, title, changed: false }` payload, else `unchanged ${command} ${position}: ${title}`. It owns the no-op wording.
- `function openEditInEditor(root: string, command: "bug" | "plan", position: number): { changed: false; file: string; title: string } | { changed: true; text: string }` — the `path === null && positionals.length === 0` branch: `showEntry`, `renderShownEntry`, `editInEditor(before, `${command}-${position}.md`)`, and the `after.trim() === before.trim()` comparison; an unchanged buffer returns `{ changed: false, file: command === "bug" ? "BUGS.md" : "PLANS.md", title: shown.title }`, otherwise `{ changed: true, text: after }`. It owns the editor round-trip and its file-name/title report.
- `async function announceEdited(root: string, command: "bug" | "plan", position: number, json: boolean, edited: { file: string; title: string }): Promise<void>` — the commit-plus-report tail: `warnIfUncommitted(await commitOperatorBacklogEdit(root, edited.file, stampedSubject("operator", `Edit ${command}: ${edited.title}`)), edited.file)`, the `backlogHolds` read and `position - 1` hold pick, then the `--json` payload or the `edited …` line plus `stillHeldNote(hold)`. It owns the commit subject and the still-held report.

`editAndAnnounce` becomes: `const { path, json, positionals, position } = parseEditArgs(args, command);`, `await requireReadyRepo(root);`, `let text: string | null = null;`, then `if (path === null && positionals.length === 0) { const opened = openEditInEditor(root, command, position); if (!opened.changed) { sayUnchangedEdit(command, position, json, opened.file, opened.title); return; } text = opened.text; } else if (path !== null) text = readPromptFileArg(path);`, then `const edited = text === null ? edit(position, positionals) : editText(position, text);`, `if (edited.unchanged) { sayUnchangedEdit(command, position, json, edited.file, edited.title); return; }`, `await announceEdited(root, command, position, json, edited);`. The exported signature stays; the doc comment stays, trimmed only to drop detail now carried by the helpers' own comments.

### `movedSourceFindings`'s complexity-17 body is split into one named helper per concern — the `-U0` moved-line delta, the receiver list, the moved-line count and the finding wording — so "which files received this source's moved lines?" and "how is the moved-source message worded?" are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-27 `missingPathFindings` split in this same file and its `garbledWordingFindings`/`staleNameFindings`/`movedNameFindings`/`parseRef` siblings each extract one named helper per job the same way; independent in file of every Planned entry — before this entry `grep -c 'movedSourceFindings' PLANS.md` and `grep -c 'src/run/stage-path-checks.ts' PLANS.md` both print 0, so no `## Planned` heading or touches list names the symbol or the file (the in-flight `reclaimPass`/`teamHold`/`planDependencyProblems`/`buildRunPrompt` splits take src/team/team-reclaim.ts, src/team/team-hold.ts, src/backlog/backlog-parts.ts and src/prompt/prompt.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` and `Subtract` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/roles, src/ui, src/gui, src/events, src/backlog, src/run/run-finalize.ts and src/run/run-apply.ts, none of them src/run/stage-path-checks.ts); PLANS-DONE.md records no split of `movedSourceFindings` (`grep -cE '^### .*movedSourceFindings' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; its prose mentions belong to the `missingPathFindings` split and the file's earlier behavior additions, never a move of this body); docs/invariants.md binds this file only as `gitLevelFindings` and `MAX_MISSING_PATHS` under INV-BK1/INV-BK2, both preserved, so it stays unchanged; touches src/run/stage-path-checks.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `movedSourceFindings` (src/run/stage-path-checks.ts, module-private) is complexity 17 and runs as one flat body: it reads each file's `-U0` delta via the shared `diffRemovedAdded` helper into a map of each file's removed lines and added-line set (thresholded at `MOVED_LINE_MIN_CHARS`), then for each `M` entry that is not record prose, finds the other files that received its removed lines, counts the moved lines, stops below `MOVED_LINES_MIN`, greps the staged tree for the old path, and words one finding. A reader asking "which files count as a receiver?" or "where does the moved-source message come from?" has only the one body.

**Approach.** All edits in src/run/stage-path-checks.ts; move code, do not rewrite it — every condition, threshold and message character stays exactly as today, and each existing `//`/doc comment stays with the code it annotates. Add a module-private interface and four module-private functions beside `movedSourceFindings`:
- `interface MovedLineDelta { removed: string[]; added: Set<string> }` — the map value the walk builds and the receivers/count helpers read.
- `function movedLineDeltas(diff: string): Map<string, MovedLineDelta>` — the delta map verbatim: it wraps the shared `diffRemovedAdded` helper (stage-checks-shared.js) instead of re-implementing a header walk — for each file it maps `f.removed`/`f.added` through `.trim()` and the `MOVED_LINE_MIN_CHARS` filter (added as a `Set`) and `files.set(f.path, { removed, added })`.
- `function movedLineReceivers(src: MovedLineDelta, others: ReadonlyArray<[string, MovedLineDelta]>): string[]` — the receivers expression verbatim: `others.filter(([, v]) => src.removed.some((l) => v.added.has(l))).map(([f]) => f)`.
- `function movedLineCount(src: MovedLineDelta, others: ReadonlyArray<[string, MovedLineDelta]>): number` — the count expression verbatim: `src.removed.filter((l) => others.some(([, v]) => v.added.has(l))).length`.
- `function movedSourceFinding(path: string, moved: number, receivers: string[], hits: string[]): string` — the template literal verbatim, `e.path` becoming `path`.
`movedSourceFindings` keeps its name, its non-export, its signature, its parameter names and its doc comment, and becomes the orchestration over them:
```ts
async function movedSourceFindings(
  wt: string,
  diff: string,
  entries: NameStatusEntry[],
): Promise<string[]> {
  const files = movedLineDeltas(diff);
  const findings: string[] = [];
  for (const e of entries) {
    if (e.status !== "M" || isRecordProse(e.path)) continue;
    if (findings.length >= MAX_STALE_PATHS) break;
    const src = files.get(e.path);
    if (!src) continue;
    const others = [...files].filter(([f]) => f !== e.path);
    const moved = movedLineCount(src, others);
    if (moved < MOVED_LINES_MIN) continue;
    const hits = await pathGrepHits(wt, e.path, e.path);
    if (hits.length === 0) continue;
    findings.push(movedSourceFinding(e.path, moved, movedLineReceivers(src, others), hits));
  }
  return findings;
}
```
`NameStatusEntry`, `isRecordProse`, `pathGrepHits`, `cappedList`, `MAX_STALE_PATHS`, `MOVED_LINE_MIN_CHARS` and `MOVED_LINES_MIN` keep their imports and definitions.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-path-checks.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `movedSourceFindings`'s body holds only the `movedLineDeltas` call, the entry loop with its `M`/record-prose skip, cap break, `files.get` guard, `moved < MOVED_LINES_MIN` guard and `hits.length === 0` guard, the `others`/`moved` resolution, the `pathGrepHits` call and the `findings.push(movedSourceFinding(...))`; it no longer inlines the diff walk, the receiver filter, the moved-line count or the message.
- `MovedLineDelta` and the four helpers are module-private (no `export`) and each is called only from src/run/stage-path-checks.ts.
- The complexity falls: the eslint one-shot (`npx eslint --no-config-lookup -c docs/code-metrics/eslint-complexity.config.mjs --format json 'src/run/stage-path-checks.ts'`) reports `movedSourceFindings` at 8 or below (it is 17 today) and `movedLineDeltas` at 8 or below, while `movedLineReceivers`, `movedLineCount` and `movedSourceFinding` report 1 and the file's other top-level functions keep the counts they report today (`parseNameStatus` 11, `gitLevelFindings` 7, `pathGrepHits` 7, `staleReferenceFindings` 8, `readStagedIndex` 5, `renameOriginPaths` 4, `missingPathTokens` 6, `missingPathsInDiff` 8, `missingPathFindings` 2).
- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/run/stage-path-checks.ts` still matches exactly `gitLevelFindings`; no import line in src/ or test/ changes.
- Behavior is preserved, including the moved-line threshold, the receiver list, the record-prose/cap skips and the exact finding wording, verified by the existing cases passing unedited — test/stage-check.test.ts "moving code out of a file that a doc still names yields the moved-source finding", "a reference inside the receiving file is reported too", "a move below the line threshold, a pure deletion, or a reference in record prose yields no moved-source finding", "archiving a backlog entry or moving a design-doc section is not a move source; a code move beside it still is" and "a basename-only reference is not reported".

Its local `handleKey` (the arrow at `tui-editor-config.ts:76`, complexity 21) interleaves three jobs in one body: the `Ctrl+<spec.openCtrl>` open/toggle arm with its Activity-view pin, `requireEmptyPrompt` fall-through and held-registry guard; the `Esc` cancel; and the `Enter` commit with the plain-integer exponent refusal, the `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` write, and a four-way nested-ternary flash that distinguishes a no-op clear from a real clear and an unchanged set from a real set. A reader asking "which view may open a team config editor?", "what refuses an exponent spelling?" or "which message says the key was already set?" has only the one `handleKey` body to scan, and the nested flash ternary is the branch pile that keeps the arrow at complexity 21.

**Approach.** Extract one named local helper per arm inside `createTeamConfigKeyEditor`, leaving `handleKey` as the three ordered guard checks and the `return false` fall-through, and keeping the returned `TuiEditorModule` shape, the `exit` helper and the `mode`/`restoreDraft` closure state unchanged:

- `const openOrToggle = (): boolean` — the `if (key.ctrl && key.name === spec.openCtrl)` arm verbatim: toggle `exit()` when open; `ctx.view !== 0` → false; the `spec.requireEmptyPrompt && session.input !== ""` fall-through returning false; the `session.editorEntryDenied(spec.mode)` returning true; then the pre-fill/take-draft/set `session.input`/cursor/`spec.openFlash` block. It is the only helper that reads `ctx` and touches `mode`/`restoreDraft` on open, so it owns the open/toggle rules.
- `const cancel = (): boolean` — the `if (key.name === "escape" && mode)` arm: `exit(); return true;`. It owns the cancel rule (the `mode` test stays in `handleKey`).
- `const commit = (): boolean` — the `if (key.name === "return" && mode)` arm verbatim: the `session.input.trim()`, the `spec.plainIntegerKey && text !== "" && isExponentSpelling(text)` refusal, the `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` call, the `result.ok` branch calling `exit()` and flashing, and the `result.error` branch staying in edit mode. It is the only helper that calls `setConfigKey`, `unsetConfigKey`, `isExponentSpelling` or the write-failure flash.
- `const commitFlash = (result, text): string` — the four-way message the successful commit flashes: the empty-line no-op wording (`${spec.configKey} is not set in tumwater.json, so nothing was cleared`), the non-empty no-op wording (`${spec.configKey} is already ${text}, so tumwater.json was not written`), `spec.clearedFlash`, and `spec.setFlash(text)`; `commit` calls it once. It moves the nested ternary out of the branch body.

`handleKey` becomes, in order: `if (key.ctrl && key.name === spec.openCtrl) return openOrToggle();`, `if (key.name === "escape" && mode) return cancel();`, `if (key.name === "return" && mode) return commit();`, `return false;`. The `_str` parameter and the exported factory signature are unchanged.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts` only. No new module, no export change, no interface change, no test file edited.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `handleKey`'s body contains only the three guard checks that delegate to `openOrToggle`/`cancel`/`commit` and the `return false`; it contains no `setConfigKey`, `unsetConfigKey`, `isExponentSpelling`, `session.flashMessage`, `spec.prefill`, `session.takeDraft`, `session.editorEntryDenied` or `session.held` occurrence.
- `openOrToggle`, `cancel`, `commit` and `commitFlash` each exist exactly once, are module-private local to the factory, and each owns the rules named above; `isExponentSpelling` and both config-write calls occur only inside `commit`.
- The move is behavior-preserving: the same write path, the same exponent refusal wording, the same no-op/clear/set flash wording, the same view/held/draft rules and the same return values for the same `(key, ctx, session, spec)`.
- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts` still matches exactly `createTeamConfigKeyEditor`, and no import line in src/ or test/ changes.
- The ESLint complexity report (`docs/code-metrics/eslint-complexity.config.mjs`) no longer lists the arrow at `tui-editor-config.ts:76` at complexity 21: `commit` carries the write branches and `commitFlash` the message branches.
- docs/invariants.md is not edited: the move changes no bound symbol or guarantee.

**Approach.** All edits in src/cli/cli-command-args.ts; move code, do not rewrite it — every condition, message string and threshold stays exactly as today, and each `//`/doc comment stays with the code it annotates. Add a module-private `interface InitArgs` (the six fields `parseInitArgs` returns today) and four module-private helpers beside it:
- `function assertInitFlags(args: string[]): void` — the vocabulary gate verbatim: `rejectUnknownDoubleDash("init", args, INIT_FLAG_SPECS)` and `rejectDuplicateFlags(args, INIT_FLAG_SPECS.flatMap((s) => s.names))`.
- `function resolveInitTemplate(args: string[], listTemplates: boolean): string | null` — the `--template` block verbatim: the `args.indexOf("--template")` early `null` return, the empty-value `fail("--template needs an id")`, the `templateIds().includes` check with `unknownTemplateError`, and the `listTemplates` conflict `fail("--list-templates takes no --template — it lists the catalog, it does not use one")`.
- `function resolveInitFileArg(args: string[], base: Omit<InitArgs, "prompt">): InitArgs | null` — the `--file` branch verbatim: the `args.indexOf("--file")` early `null` return, `promptFileValue`, the `claimed` positions (`--file` pair, `--branch` pair, `--template` pair, each `INIT_BOOLEAN_FLAGS` index), `failStrayArg(args, "with --file the prompt comes from the file", ...claimed)`, `readPromptFileChecked`, the `listTemplates` conflict `fail(LIST_TEMPLATES_PROMPT_ERROR)`, and the return `{ ...base, prompt: contents }`.
- `function joinInitPrompt(args: string[]): string` — the positional reconstruction verbatim: the `for` loop that skips the `--branch`/`--template` value token, drops `INIT_BOOLEAN_FLAGS`, and joins the rest with a single space.
`parseInitArgs` keeps its name, export, parameter name and its doc comment, and becomes the composition:
```ts
export function parseInitArgs(args: string[]): InitArgs {
  assertInitFlags(args);
  const branch = parseBranchFlag(args);
  const adopt = args.includes("--adopt");
  const dryRun = args.includes("--dry-run");
  const listTemplates = args.includes("--list-templates");
  const template = resolveInitTemplate(args, listTemplates);
  const base = { branch, template, listTemplates, adopt, dryRun };
  const fromFile = resolveInitFileArg(args, base);
  if (fromFile !== null) return fromFile;
  const prompt = joinInitPrompt(args);
  if (listTemplates && prompt.trim() !== "") fail(LIST_TEMPLATES_PROMPT_ERROR);
  return { ...base, prompt };
}
```
`INIT_FLAG_SPECS`, `INIT_BOOLEAN_FLAGS`, `LIST_TEMPLATES_PROMPT_ERROR`, `rejectDuplicateFlags`, `rejectUnknownDoubleDash`, `parseBranchFlag`, `templateIds`, `unknownTemplateError`, `promptFileValue`, `readPromptFileChecked`, `failStrayArg` and `fail` keep their imports and definitions.

### `reclaimPass`'s complexity-17 pass body is split into one named helper per concern — the pressure floor check, the per-candidate guard-and-clean, the collection loop, the freed/free result figures and the pass result, and the `disk_reclaim` log — so "when does pressure reclaim stop?", "which candidate gets cleaned?" and "what does the pass report?" are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — one named helper per concern, exactly as the 2026-10-27 `teamHold`/`buildRunPrompt`/`planDependencyProblems`/`runRows`/`resolveQueuedResult` plans split a body the same way; independent in file of every Planned entry — before this entry `grep -cE 'reclaimPass|team-reclaim' PLANS.md` prints 0, so no `## Planned` heading or touches list names the symbol or src/team/team-reclaim.ts, and the only `src/team/` matches in PLANS.md are src/team/team-hold.ts (the `teamHold` split) and src/team/team-orchestrator-info.ts (Subtract part 5l/6) and src/team/team-polls.ts (Subtract part 5d/6), none of them this file; `grep -nE '^### .*(reclaimPass|team-reclaim)' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0, so no finished plan splits it either — the `reclaimPass` entries in PLANS-DONE.md are behavior additions and guard tests, never a split; docs/invariants.md binds this file's `reclaimPass` and `isIdleExpired` and the move keeps every name, signature and guarantee, so it stays unchanged; touches src/team/team-reclaim.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `reclaimPass` (src/team/team-reclaim.ts, exported) steps one reclaim pass at complexity 17: it resolves the free-space sampler and the candidate list, samples free space once before the pass, walks the candidates — idle mode keeps only those `isIdleExpired`, pressure and manual modes re-sample and stop once free space reaches `reclaimGB`, each kept candidate is cleaned through `reclaimWorktree` with a guard failure skipped — then samples after, builds a `ReclaimPassResult` whose `freedGB` is the clamped before/after difference, logs exactly one `disk_reclaim`, and returns null when nothing was cleaned. The stop rule and each figure are the module's contract (docs/invariants.md's `reclaimPass`/`isIdleExpired` block and its pins), but the body is one flat sequence, so a reader asking "does idle mode ever sample?" or "where is freed space clamped?" scans all of it.

**Approach.** All edits in src/team/team-reclaim.ts; move code, do not rewrite it — every condition, arithmetic expression, object field and log field stays exactly as today. Add these six module-private functions beside `reclaimPass`:
- `pressureFloorReached(free: number | null, reclaimGB: number): boolean` — the `free !== null && reclaimGB > 0 && free >= reclaimGB * BYTES_PER_GB` stop test.
- `reclaimOneCandidate(root: string, candidate: ReclaimCandidate): Promise<boolean>` — `try { return await reclaimWorktree(root, candidate.dir); } catch { return false; }`, carrying the existing comment that a guard failure is not a reason to abort the pass.
- `collectReclaimed(root: string, candidates: readonly ReclaimCandidate[], mode: "pressure" | "idle" | "manual", idleHours: number, reclaimGB: number, sample: (root: string) => number | null, startedAt: number): Promise<string[]>` — the `for` loop: `if (mode === "idle") { if (!isIdleExpired(candidate, idleHours, startedAt)) continue; } else if (pressureFloorReached(sample(root), reclaimGB)) { break; }`, then `if (await reclaimOneCandidate(root, candidate)) cleaned.push(candidate.name);`.
- `reclaimFreedGB(before: number | null, after: number | null): number` — the `before !== null && after !== null ? Math.max(0, (after - before) / BYTES_PER_GB) : 0`.
- `buildReclaimResult(cleaned: readonly string[], before: number | null, after: number | null, startedAt: number): ReclaimPassResult` — the `const freeBytes = after ?? before ?? 0;` and the object literal `{ worktrees: cleaned, freedGB: reclaimFreedGB(before, after), freeGB: freeBytes / BYTES_PER_GB, durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt }`.
- `logReclaim(root: string, mode: "pressure" | "idle" | "manual", result: ReclaimPassResult): void` — the single `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "disk_reclaim", mode, worktrees: result.worktrees, freedGB: result.freedGB, freeGB: result.freeGB, durationMs: result.durationMs })`.
`reclaimPass` keeps its name, signature, parameter names and doc comment, and becomes the orchestration over them:
```ts
export async function reclaimPass(
  root: string,
  mode: "pressure" | "idle" | "manual",
  opts: { reclaimGB: number; idleHours?: number; sample?: (root: string) => number | null; candidates?: readonly ReclaimCandidate[] },
): Promise<ReclaimPassResult | null> {
  const sample = opts.sample ?? sampleFreeBytes;
  const candidates = opts.candidates ?? reclaimCandidates(root);
  const startedAt = Date.now();
  const before = sample(root);
  const cleaned = await collectReclaimed(root, candidates, mode, opts.idleHours ?? 0, opts.reclaimGB, sample, startedAt);
  if (cleaned.length === 0) return null;
  const after = sample(root);
  const result = buildReclaimResult(cleaned, before, after, startedAt);
  logReclaim(root, mode, result);
  return result;
}
```
As landed, `reclaimPass` adds a no-candidate fast path (`candidates.length === 0 ? [] : await collectReclaimed(...)`): with nothing to walk the pass resolves synchronously, preserving the both the pre-split return timing a no-live-team Ctrl+E flashes within the caller's same turn (test/tui-keys.test.ts "Ctrl+E on the Health view runs an in-process reclaim with no live team") and `collectReclaimed`'s empty-loop result.
The inline `opts` type may stay on `reclaimPass` exactly as today; `isIdleExpired`, `reclaimWorktree`, `ReclaimPassResult`, `sampleFreeBytes`, `BYTES_PER_GB`, `TUMWATER_SOURCE` and `logEventBestEffort` keep their imports and definitions.

### `teamHold`'s complexity-17 hold step is split into one named helper per concern — the deadline re-open, the account-level subscription window, which failures still count, the first qualifying provider+kind storm, the relapse escalation, and the hold duration — so "when does a hold re-open?", "which storm wins one poll?" and "how long does it last?" are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — one named helper per concern, exactly as the 2026-10-27 `buildRunPrompt`/`planDependencyProblems`/`runRows`/`resolveQueuedResult`/`scanTurnRecords` plans split a body the same way; independent in file of every Planned entry — before this entry `grep -c 'teamHold' PLANS.md` prints 0, so no `## Planned` heading or touches list names the symbol or src/team/team-hold.ts, and the only `src/team/` matches in PLANS.md are src/team/team-orchestrator-info.ts (Subtract part 5l/6) and src/team/team-polls.ts (Subtract part 5d/6 and its prose), neither this file; `grep -cE '^### .*teamHold' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 1 and that done heading is the 2026-10-17 dashboards plan that added `standingHolds`, a behavior addition, never a split of `teamHold`; the in-flight splits take src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/history/history-data.ts, src/history/history-queued.ts, src/backlog/backlog-parts.ts and Subtract part 5o/6's src/runner, src/config and src/gates files, none of them this file; docs/invariants.md binds this file's `teamHold`, `HOLD_STORM_WINDOW_MS`, `HOLD_BASE_MS`, `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS`, `HOLD_CAP_MS` and `heldProviders`, and the move keeps every name, signature and guarantee, so it stays unchanged; touches src/team/team-hold.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `teamHold` (src/team/team-hold.ts, exported; the orchestrator's `pollTeamHold` in src/team/team-polls.ts is its only caller) steps one provider's `TeamHold` at complexity 17: it re-opens a past-deadline hold and falls through, returns a rejected subscription window's hold at `resetsAt`, filters observations to those after the last re-open and inside the storm window, groups them by provider+kind in first-seen order, picks the first group with `HOLD_STORM_ROLES` distinct roles, computes the relapse escalation and the duration from the base, the Retry-After hints and the cap, and returns the new `TeamHold`. The order and each sub-rule are the module's contract (docs/invariants.md INV-BG1–BG4 and the module block), but the body is one flat sequence, so a reader asking "does the window hold outrank the storm?" or "where does the Retry-After enter the hold length?" scans all of it.

**Approach.** All edits in src/team/team-hold.ts; move code, do not rewrite it — every string, arithmetic expression, comparison and object field stays exactly as today, including the `prev`-itself return when nothing changed. Add these six module-private functions beside `teamHold`:
- `reopenTeamHold(prev: TeamHold, now: number): TeamHold` — the `prev.until !== null` block: return `prev` itself while open or still held (and not a re-evaluated reserve), else the re-opened skeleton `{ provider: prev.provider, until: null, kind: prev.kind, roles: [], escalation: prev.escalation, reopenedAt: prev.reserve === true ? prev.reopenedAt : now }`.
- `subscriptionWindowHold(observations: readonly HoldObservation[], now: number, reopenedAt: number | null): TeamHold | undefined` — the `observations.find(o => o.kind === "subscription-window" && (o.resetsAt ?? 0) > now)` and the window `TeamHold` it builds (`until: window.resetsAt!`, `kind: "subscription-window"`, `escalation: 0`, `reopenedAt`, and the `reserve` spread), or `undefined` when no window is rejected.
- `recentStormObservations(prev: TeamHold, observations: readonly HoldObservation[], now: number): HoldObservation[]` — the `observations.filter((o) => (prev.reopenedAt === null || o.at > prev.reopenedAt) && now - o.at <= HOLD_STORM_WINDOW_MS)`.
- `firstStormGroup(recent: readonly HoldObservation[]): { provider: string | undefined; kind: HoldKind; storm: HoldObservation[] } | undefined` — the `byProviderKind` map built with `getOrCreate` and the first group whose distinct-role set reaches `HOLD_STORM_ROLES`, returned as `{ provider, kind, storm }`, else `undefined`.
- `holdEscalation(prev: TeamHold, provider: string | undefined, kind: HoldKind, now: number): number` — the per-provider-and-kind relapse predicate over `prev.kind`, `prev.provider`, `prev.reopenedAt` and `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS`, returning `prev.escalation + 1` or 0.
- `holdDurationMs(escalation: number, storm: readonly HoldObservation[], now: number): number` — the `retryAfterMs` from each observation's own `at` and the `Math.min(HOLD_CAP_MS, Math.max(HOLD_BASE_MS * 2 ** escalation, retryAfterMs))`.
`teamHold` keeps its name, signature, parameter names, doc comment and return type, and becomes the orchestration over them:
```ts
export function teamHold(prev: TeamHold, observations: readonly HoldObservation[], now: number): TeamHold {
  const reopened = reopenTeamHold(prev, now);
  if (reopened.until !== null) return reopened;
  const window = subscriptionWindowHold(observations, now, reopened.reopenedAt);
  if (window !== undefined) return window;
  const group = firstStormGroup(recentStormObservations(reopened, observations, now));
  if (group === undefined) return reopened;
  const escalation = holdEscalation(reopened, group.provider, group.kind, now);
  const roles = sortedRoles(new Set(group.storm.map((o) => o.role)));
  return {
    provider: group.provider,
    until: now + holdDurationMs(escalation, group.storm, now),
    kind: group.kind,
    roles,
    escalation,
    reopenedAt: reopened.reopenedAt,
  };
}
```
`getOrCreate` and `sortedRoles` imports stay; `HOLD_*` constants and every type stay where they are.

```
const wanted = roleWantSet(role);
const scoped = scopedEvents(events, wanted);
const evidence = runRowEvidence(scoped, join, wanted);
const rows: RunRow[] = [];
for (let i = scoped.length - 1; i >= 0 && rows.length < limit; i--) {

return rows;
```

**Goal.** `scanTurnRecords` (src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts, module-private; called once from `rolloutLines`) scans one turn's records out of a rollout's text at complexity 18: it resolves each line's effective type (an `event_msg` wrapper's `payload.type`, else the outer `type`), handles `task_started` by moving `currentTurn` and restarting the five collectors when the line begins the read turn, then a `switch` over `turn_context` (first `payload.model`), `token_usage_record` (`payload.turn_token_usage` when it carries input or output tokens) and `token_count` (`payload.rate_limits` and its `plan_type`). The carrier resolution, the turn-restart and the two record-presence tests have no names, so a reader asking "which event sets `lastUsage`?", "which sets `lastRateLimits`/`planType`?" or "when do the collectors reset?" scans the whole loop. Extract each concern into a named module-private helper.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts; move code verbatim and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. No import changes: every symbol the moved code reads (`objectOrEmpty`, `optionalString`, `parseJsonObject`, `isJsonObject` and the `Json` type) is already imported, and the `TurnRecords` interface stays. Add these module-private declarations beside `scanTurnRecords`:

- `function lineCarrierType(parsed: Json, payload: Json): string | undefined` — `optionalString(parsed.type) === "event_msg" ? optionalString(payload.type) : optionalString(parsed.type)`, with the wrapper-discriminator comment.
- `function turnStartReading(payload: Json, sinceTurnStart: string | undefined): { turnId: string | undefined; readsTurn: boolean }` — `const turnId = optionalString(payload.turn_id); return { turnId, readsTurn: sinceTurnStart === undefined || turnId === sinceTurnStart };`, with the "each new task_started begins a fresh turn" comment.
- `function usageFromRecord(payload: Json): Json | undefined` — `const turnUsage = objectOrEmpty(payload.turn_token_usage); return isJsonObject(turnUsage) && (turnUsage.input_tokens !== undefined || turnUsage.output_tokens !== undefined) ? turnUsage : undefined;`.
- `function rateLimitsFromCount(payload: Json): { rateLimits: Json; planType: string | undefined }` — `const rateLimits = objectOrEmpty(payload.rate_limits); return { rateLimits, planType: optionalString(rateLimits.plan_type) };`.

`scanTurnRecords` keeps its signature, doc comment and module-private status; its loop body becomes:

```
const ptype = lineCarrierType(parsed, payload);
if (ptype === "task_started") {
  const start = turnStartReading(payload, sinceTurnStart);
  currentTurn = start.turnId;
  if (start.readsTurn) { sawTurn = true; lastUsage = undefined; lastRateLimits = undefined; model = undefined; planType = undefined; }
  continue;
}
if (sinceTurnStart !== undefined && currentTurn !== sinceTurnStart) continue;
switch (ptype) {
  case "turn_context": if (model === undefined) model = optionalString(payload.model); break;
  case "token_usage_record": lastUsage = usageFromRecord(payload) ?? lastUsage; break;
  case "token_count": {
    const reading = rateLimitsFromCount(payload);
    lastRateLimits = reading.rateLimits;
    if (reading.planType !== undefined) planType = reading.planType;
    break;
  }
  default: break;
}
```

`usageFromRecord(payload) ?? lastUsage` preserves the post-presence rule: a later malformed usage line leaves the earlier figure; `lastRateLimits = reading.rateLimits` stays unconditional (the original assigned even the empty object) while `planType` is assigned only when defined.

**Goal.** `claudeTranslator`'s nested `handleRateLimitEvent` (src/agent/claude/claude-stream.ts, complexity 19) folds a claude `rate_limit_event`: it builds one canonical `rate_limit` reading per entry of `rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows` other than the binding window, looks up the binding window's own record, resolves `resetsAt` and `utilization` from the top-level field falling back to that record, assembles the top-level reading's optional fields (`rateLimitType`, `status`, `overageStatus`, `isUsingOverage`) and derives `retryAfterSeconds` for a rejected window. It is one body whose concerns interleave; a reader asking which windows get their own reading, or how the binding window's reset time is resolved, has only the whole fold to scan. Extract one named module-private function per concern so `handleRateLimitEvent` becomes the three reads and the two calls, with no behavior change.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/claude/claude-stream.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the block it annotates. The handler is a closure but reads no `claudeTranslator` state (only `event` and module-level helpers), so the helpers are module-level functions beside `billingOf`:

- `function claudeRateLimitWindowReadings(info: Json, rateLimitType: string | undefined): string[]` — the `unifiedWindows` loop with its `// claude 2.1.295 reports every window's ...` comment, the `type === rateLimitType || !isJsonObject(raw)` skip, and the per-window `rate_limit` reading with its optional `resetsAt`/`utilization`.
- `function claudeRateLimitOwnWindow(info: Json, rateLimitType: string | undefined): Json | undefined` — the `own` lookup (`rateLimitType === undefined ? undefined : objectOrEmpty(objectOrEmpty(info.unifiedWindows)[rateLimitType])`).
- `function claudeRateLimitResetsAt(info: Json, own: Json | undefined): number | undefined` — `nonNegativeNumber(info.resetsAt, undefined) ?? nonNegativeNumber(own?.resetsAt, undefined)`.
- `function claudeRateLimitUtilization(info: Json, own: Json | undefined): number | undefined` — the same read for `utilization`.
- `function claudeRateLimitReading(info: Json, rateLimitType: string | undefined, status: string | undefined): Json` — calls `claudeRateLimitOwnWindow`, `claudeRateLimitResetsAt` and `claudeRateLimitUtilization`, then assembles the `out` object's optional fields and, for a rejected window, `out.retryAfterSeconds = secondsUntilUnixStamp(resetsAt, Date.now())` with its `// resetsAt is a unix-seconds stamp ...` comment.

`handleRateLimitEvent` keeps its signature and becomes:

```
const info = objectOrEmpty(event.rate_limit_info);
const rateLimitType = optionalString(info.rateLimitType);
const status = optionalString(info.status);
return [
  JSON.stringify(claudeRateLimitReading(info, rateLimitType, status)),
  ...claudeRateLimitWindowReadings(info, rateLimitType),
];
```

The `translate` dispatch site (`case "rate_limit_event": return handleRateLimitEvent(event);`) is untouched, and the reading-then-siblings output order is unchanged.

**Goal.** `PiStreamParser.applyAssistantMessage` (src/pi/pi-stream.ts) folds the final `message_end`/assistant event: it computes the contentless and produced-content flags from the message's content blocks, keeps the last non-empty text as `finalText`, records the nothing-to-do sentinel, folds the anchored refusal line (with the negating-reason clear and last-line-wins rule), records the verdict text, then sums turns, output/prompt/cache-read/peak-context/cost and freezes the pre-edit prompt prefix at the first edit/write turn, and finally records `stopReason`/`errorMessage`. It is one body whose concerns interleave the reply surface, the refusal, token accounting and stop state; a reader asking why the final message is contentless, or how the pre-edit prefix is frozen, has only the whole fold to scan. Extract one named private method per concern so `applyAssistantMessage` becomes the `messageText` call and the four folds in order, with no behavior change.

**Approach.** All edits in src/pi/pi-stream.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the block it annotates. Add these private methods beside `applyAssistantMessage`, each reading and writing `this` (no state threading):

- `private applyAssistantReply(msg: PiMessage, text: string): void` — the contentless `!messageContent(msg).some(...)` fold, the `if (!this.finalMessageContentless) this.producedAssistantContent = true;` line, `if (text.trim()) this.finalText = text;` and `if (isNothingToDo(text)) this.declaredNothingToDo = true;`.
- `private applyAssistantRefusal(text: string): void` — the refusal comment and `const refusal = extractRefusal(text);` fold with its `isNegatedRefusal` if/else, then `if (hasVerdictLine(text)) this.verdictText = text;`, so the verdict line still follows the refusal in the same order as today.
- `private applyAssistantUsage(msg: PiMessage): void` — `this.turns += 1;` through `this.costUsd += usageNumber(msg.usage?.cost?.total);`, keeping the `const promptTokens` local and the pre-edit-prefix comment and fold (`if (this.firstEditTurn === undefined) { this.preEditPromptTokens += promptTokens; if (messageContent(msg).some((c) => c.type === "toolCall" && (c.name === "edit" || c.name === "write"))) this.firstEditTurn = this.turns; }`).
- `private applyAssistantStop(msg: PiMessage): void` — `this.stopReason = msg.stopReason;` and the `errorMessage` if/else-if.

`applyAssistantMessage` keeps its signature and becomes: `const text = messageText(msg);` then `this.applyAssistantReply(msg, text);`, `this.applyAssistantRefusal(text);`, `this.applyAssistantUsage(msg);`, `this.applyAssistantStop(msg);`. The `feedLine` dispatch site (`this.applyAssistantMessage(event.message)`) is untouched.

### `resolveCommitDescription`'s complexity-21 body is split into one named helper per SUMMARY-recovery concern — the bounded follow-up turn both recovery paths share, the missing-SUMMARY recovery with its derived-subject fallback, the over-cap SUMMARY shortening, and the missing-SUMMARY warning's four-way wording — so "where does an aborted summary turn end the run?" and "why did the subject fall back to the changed files?" are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-25 `stageRunMerge` split created `resolveCommitDescription` as a named stage and left it one body, and the 2026-10-27 `runStageSelfCheck` split (done) split its sibling in the same file the same one-helper-per-concern way; independent in files of every `## Planned` entry — `grep -c 'resolveCommitDescription' PLANS.md` and `grep -c 'run-stage' PLANS.md` both print 0, and the in-flight plans take src/run/acceptance-greps.ts (`grepArgv`), src/failure/failure-render.ts (`pushTimeAndSpend`), src/agent/run-settle.ts (`settleClose`) and the Subtract part 5c/6 and 5n/6 files (src/report, src/runner, src/config, src/gates, src/status, src/events and src/roles), none src/run/run-stage.ts; PLANS-DONE.md records no split of its body — `grep -cE '^### .*resolveCommitDescription' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 1, the 2026-10-27 `runStageSelfCheck` heading, whose prose names `resolveCommitDescription` only as the stage the earlier `stageRunMerge` split created; docs/invariants.md names no symbol of it (`grep -c 'resolveCommitDescription' docs/invariants.md` prints 0) and its `src/run/run-stage.ts` bindings are `foldAgentCommitsSince` (INV-H1), `stageRunMerge`'s recordFlow write and the git-failure throw, which this private move leaves unchanged; touches src/run/run-stage.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `resolveCommitDescription` (src/run/run-stage.ts) derives the commit's subject and body from the reply's `SUMMARY` block, taking one bounded follow-up turn when the reply left none (`summary === null`) or left one the character cap would cut mid-word (`summaryOverCap(ctx.finalText) !== null`). It is one ~56-line body whose two recovery paths share a scope: each takes a base `headOf`, awaits `ctx.requestSummary`, folds the follow-up's commits, and returns `ctx.finishAbortedRun()` on abort, but they re-extract differently, warn with different four-way wording, and the missing path has a derived-subject fallback the over-cap path does not. A reader asking whether a missing summary's fallback ran, or which path ends the run on an aborted turn, has only the whole function to scan. Split each concern into one module-private helper so `resolveCommitDescription` becomes the ordered calls, with no behavior change: the same subject, body and `summaryDerived` come back for the same reply.

**Approach.** All edits in src/run/run-stage.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the block it annotates. Add these module-private declarations beside `resolveCommitDescription`, and add a `private` staging shape for the two recovery paths to mutate (mirroring how `applyStageFixUp` mutates `desc` and returns `RunOutcome | undefined`):

```ts
/** The commit description while `resolveCommitDescription` still has to recover its summary:
 * `summary` stays null until a recovery path fills it. */
interface PendingCommitDescription {
  summary: string | null;
  body: StagedBody;
  summaryDerived: boolean;
}

/** The result of the shared summary follow-up: the aborted-run outcome to return, or the
 * follow-up run (null when the run had no session to continue). */
type SummaryFollowUp = { aborted: RunOutcome } | { followUp: PiRunResult | null };
```

- `async function requestSummaryFollowUp(ctx: RunStageContext, over?: number): Promise<SummaryFollowUp>` — the block both paths share today: `const base = await headOf(ctx.wt, "HEAD"); const followUp = await ctx.requestSummary(ctx.wt, over); await foldAgentCommitsSince(ctx, ctx.wt, base);` then `if (followUp?.aborted) return { aborted: ctx.finishAbortedRun() }; return { followUp };`.
- `async function recoverMissingSummary(ctx: RunStageContext, pending: PendingCommitDescription): Promise<RunOutcome | undefined>` — the whole `summary === null` arm: `const result = await requestSummaryFollowUp(ctx); if ("aborted" in result) return result.aborted; const followUp = result.followUp;` then, when `followUp` is truthy, `pending.summary = extractSummary(followUp.finalText); pending.body = pending.body ?? extractCommitBody(followUp.finalText);` then, when `pending.summary === null` still, `pending.summary = fallbackSummary(await changedFiles(ctx.wt), ctx.role, ctx.state.runs); pending.summaryDerived = true;` then `ctx.warn(missingSummaryWarning(followUp, pending.summary));` and `return undefined`.
- `function missingSummaryWarning(followUp: PiRunResult | null, summary: string): string` — the exact nested ternary today renders: `"recovered it with a follow-up turn"` when `followUp && extractSummary(followUp.finalText) !== null`, else `"the follow-up run failed (<errorMessage || "no error message">); subject derived from the changed files: \"<summary>\""` when `followUp && !followUp.ok`, else `"follow-up gave none; subject derived from the changed files: \"<summary>\""` when `followUp`, else `"no follow-up session was available; subject derived from the changed files: \"<summary>\""`, all prefixed with `"reply had no SUMMARY line — "`.
- `async function shortenOverCapSummary(ctx: RunStageContext, pending: PendingCommitDescription): Promise<RunOutcome | undefined>` — the whole `summary !== null` arm: reads `const over = summaryOverCap(ctx.finalText); if (over === null) return undefined;`, takes `requestSummaryFollowUp(ctx, over)` and returns the aborted outcome on abort, else computes today's `const short = followUp && summaryOverCap(followUp.finalText) === null ? extractSummary(followUp.finalText) : null;`, applies `pending.summary = short; pending.body = pending.body ?? extractCommitBody(followUp!.finalText);` when `short !== null`, calls `ctx.warn` with today's two-way message (`"SUMMARY was <over> characters — shortened with a follow-up turn"` / `"SUMMARY was <over> characters — follow-up gave no shorter one; subject truncated"`), and returns `undefined`.
- `resolveCommitDescription` keeps its signature and doc comment and becomes: build `const pending: PendingCommitDescription = { summary: extractSummary(ctx.finalText), body: extractCommitBody(ctx.finalText), summaryDerived: false };`, then `const outcome = pending.summary === null ? await recoverMissingSummary(ctx, pending) : await shortenOverCapSummary(ctx, pending);`, then `if (outcome) return outcome;`, then `return { summary: pending.summary!, body: pending.body, summaryDerived: pending.summaryDerived };`. Drop the now-unused `const s = ctx.state;` (the fallback reads `ctx.state.runs` inside the helper).

**Files touched.** src/run/run-stage.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `resolveCommitDescription`'s body holds only the `pending` construction, the one ternary between `recoverMissingSummary` and `shortenOverCapSummary`, the outcome early return and the final `StagedCommitDescription` return: no `headOf`, `ctx.requestSummary`, `foldAgentCommitsSince`, `changedFiles`, `fallbackSummary`, `summaryOverCap` or `ctx.warn` call remains in it, and `const s = ctx.state` is gone.
- `requestSummaryFollowUp`, `recoverMissingSummary`, `missingSummaryWarning` and `shortenOverCapSummary` are module-private (no `export`), and each holds its one current block moved verbatim with its comments.

- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/run/run-stage.ts` still matches `foldAgentCommitsSince` and `stageRunMerge` only, and `PendingCommitDescription`/`SummaryFollowUp` appear in no export list.

**Approach.** All edits in src/run/acceptance-greps.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every existing `//` comment with the arm it annotates. Add these declarations beside `grepArgv`:
- A module-private `interface WordScan { words: string[]; cur: string; inWord: boolean; quote: "'" | '"' | null }` — the mutable scan state the helpers share, so the four signatures name one type (the private-interface move the `sayHistory`/`parseQuestionsInvocation` plans make with `HistoryFiltering`/`QuestionsScan`). The existing `words`, `cur`, `inWord` and `quote` locals become the fields of one `WordScan`.
- `takeSingleQuoted(cmd: string, i: number, s: WordScan): number` — pre: `s.quote === "'"`. The character at `i`: a `'` closes the quote (`s.quote = null`), anything else appends to `s.cur`. Returns `i + 1`. One home for "inside single quotes everything is literal".
- `takeDoubleQuoted(cmd: string, i: number, s: WordScan): number` — pre: `s.quote === '"'`. The character at `i`: a `\"` or `\\` appends the escaped character and consumes two characters, a `"` closes the quote, anything else appends. Returns the advanced index. One home for "double quotes honour only `\"` and `\\`".
- `takeUnquoted(cmd: string, i: number, s: WordScan): number | undefined` — pre: `s.quote === null`. The character at `i`: an unquoted `'`/`"` opens the quote and marks `s.inWord`, an unquoted `\\` appends the next character (if any) and marks `s.inWord`, an unquoted `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `$`, `(`, `)` or backtick returns `undefined`, whitespace pushes `s.cur` when `s.inWord` and resets `s.cur`/`s.inWord`, anything else appends and marks `s.inWord`. Returns the advanced index, or `undefined` for the shell refusal. One home for "where is shell syntax refused, and where does a word end?".
- `splitShellWords(cmd: string): string[] | undefined` — the loop: while the index is in range, dispatch to `takeSingleQuoted`/`takeDoubleQuoted` when `s.quote !== null`, else call `takeUnquoted` and return `undefined` when it refuses; advance by the returned index. After the loop, an open quote returns `undefined`; a pending `s.inWord` pushes `s.cur`. Returns the word list. One home for "walk the command and reject an unterminated quote".
- `grepInvocation(words: string[]): { file: "grep" | "git"; args: string[] } | undefined` — the shape pick: `words[0] === "git" && words[1] === "grep"` gives `{ file: "git", args: words.slice(1) }`, `words[0] === "grep"` gives `{ file: "grep", args: words.slice(1) }`, else `undefined`. One home for "what invocation does this word list name?".
- `grepArgv` becomes: `const words = splitShellWords(cmd); return words === undefined ? undefined : grepInvocation(words);` — no scanner branches remain in it.

**Goal.** `refShaFromFiles` (src/git/git.ts) is complexity 20: one ~27-line exported body that resolves a ref from the repository's files so the read-only probes avoid a `git rev-parse` spawn. It reads HEAD (a detached SHA, or a `ref: refs/heads/…` symref) in one branch, a full `refs/…` name with its plain-name and per-worktree guards in a second, and a short branch name in a third with its DWIM-order guards (`<gitdir>/<name>`, `refs/<name>` and `refs/tags/<name>` all outranking the branch) — all interleaved, so a reader asking "where is the short-name DWIM order encoded?" or "where is a detached HEAD read?" has only the one body. Extract one named helper per ref shape; `refShaFromFiles` keeps its name, its `export`, its signature and its doc comment, and becomes the repository lookup plus a three-way dispatch.

**Approach.** All edits in src/git/git.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every existing `//` comment with the helper whose code it annotates. Add these three module-private declarations beside `refShaFromFiles`, each taking the already-resolved `RepoFiles` so the helper cannot re-read environment or ownership state:
- `function refShaFromHead(repo: RepoFiles): string | undefined` — the current `if (ref === "HEAD")` body verbatim: read `<repo.gitdir>/HEAD`, return it when `isSha(head)`, else decode the `ref: ` target requiring `refs/heads/` and `isPlainRefName(target)`, and `return storedRef(repo.commondir, target) ?? undefined;`.
- `function refShaFromFullRefName(repo: RepoFiles, ref: string): string | undefined` — the current `if (ref.startsWith("refs/"))` body verbatim with its `!isPlainRefName(ref) || PER_WORKTREE_REF.test(ref)` guard and its `storedRef(repo.commondir, ref)` read.
- `function refShaFromShortName(repo: RepoFiles, ref: string): string | undefined` — the current short-name tail verbatim, carrying the `// A full object name means the object to git, ahead of any same-named ref.` comment and the `// \`<gitdir>/<name>\` outranks every ref.` comment: the `isSha(ref) || !isPlainRefName(\`refs/heads/${ref}\`)` guard, the `new Set([repo.gitdir, repo.commondir])` existence scan, the `refs/${ref}`/`refs/tags/${ref}` outranking loop, and the final `storedRef(repo.commondir, \`refs/heads/${ref}\`)` read.
- `refShaFromFiles` becomes: the unchanged `const repo = repoFiles(dir); if (repo === undefined) return undefined;`, then `if (ref === "HEAD") return refShaFromHead(repo);`, `if (ref.startsWith("refs/")) return refShaFromFullRefName(repo, ref);`, `return refShaFromShortName(repo, ref);`. Nothing new is exported.

**Goal.** `garbledWordingFindings` (src/run/stage-prose-checks.ts) is complexity 20: one ~55-line body that walks the diff line by line tracking the current file, added-line number and preceding added line, then for each added line outside record prose tries three detections in order — a `GARBLED_WORDING` regex hit on the raw line, a `DOUBLED_WORD` hit in its prose (via `proseOf`), and a phrase spanning the join with the preceding added line (via `spanningGarbled`) — and finally caps and words the finding. A reader asking "where is a phrase split across two lines joined?" or "where does a doubled word get checked?" has only the one body. Split the diff walk from the detections into named module-private helpers; `garbledWordingFindings` keeps its name, its `export`, its signature and its doc comment.

**Approach.** All edits in src/run/stage-prose-checks.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every existing `//` comment with the helper whose code it annotates. Add these module-private declarations beside `garbledWordingFindings`:
- `interface AddedDiffLine { file: string; lineNo: number; text: string; prev: string | null; }` — one added line's file, its 1-based line number, its text after the `+`, and the immediately preceding added line (for the across-lines join; null after a `diff --git` header, a `@@` hunk header or any non-added line).
- `function addedDiffLines(diff: string): AddedDiffLine[]` — the current `let file`, `let lineNo`, `let prevAdded` declarations and the whole `for (const line of diff.split("\n")) { … }` walk, but collecting instead of detecting: the `diff --git` header and `@@` hunk blocks, the `!line.startsWith("+") || line.startsWith("+++ ")` skip (the header, hunk and skip branches each setting the running `prev` to null), and on an added line `const text = line.slice(1)`, pushing `{ file, lineNo, text, prev }` when `file !== null`, then `prev = text; lineNo++`. Returns the array.
- `function singleLineGarbledHit(file: string, lineNo: number, cur: string): string | null` — the current `for (const re of GARBLED_WORDING) { … }` loop returning `${file}:${lineNo} "${m[0]}"` on its first hit, then the current `const prose = proseOf(file, cur); const m = DOUBLED_WORD.exec(prose); …` pair, returning null when neither matches.
- `function spanningGarbledHit(file: string, lineNo: number, cur: string, prevAdded: string | null): string | null` — the current `if (!hit && prevAdded !== null) { … }` block: `const head = prevAdded.trimEnd()`, the `joined` expression, the `spanningGarbled(joined, head.length, GARBLED_WORDING)` try and the `prose !== null && proseOf(file, prevAdded) !== null` fallback to `[DOUBLED_WORD]`; returns the `${file}:${lineNo - 1}-${lineNo} "${split}"` string or null.
- `garbledWordingFindings` becomes: `const hits: string[] = []; for (const { file, lineNo, text, prev } of addedDiffLines(diff)) { if (isRecordProse(file)) continue; const hit = singleLineGarbledHit(file, lineNo, text) ?? spanningGarbledHit(file, lineNo, text, prev); if (hit !== null) hits.push(hit); }` then the unchanged `if (hits.length === 0) return [];`, the `lead` constant and the `cappedList(hits, MAX_STALE_HITS)` return. Keep its doc comment; nothing new is exported.

The helper calls `withConfigLock` itself so the one-critical-section comment stays with the code that takes the lock.
- `function discardConfigRequest(requestFile: string, error: string | undefined): string | undefined` — today's trailing `try { fs.unlinkSync(requestFile) } catch` verbatim with its comment, returning the (possibly `??=`) error.
- `applyConfigRequest` becomes: read the file path and `readTextOrNull` with its `null` early return; declare `ignored`/`applied`/`error`/`unchanged`; in the `try`, call `parseConfigRequest`, then `checkCommandFrom`, then the `customRoles` array-shape check, then (when a command was declared) `verifyDeclaredCheck`, then `writeConfigRequest`; keep the `catch` that clears `applied` and sets `error`; call `discardConfigRequest`; keep the existing `unchanged ? … : …` return. **Goal.** `checkMainBaseline` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts, the exported entry that verifies main's own build/test suite at `wt`'s HEAD) is complexity 23: its ~95-line body interleaves the per-SHA cache read with the `observedOnly` inherited-green filter and the `shouldRerunRed` short-circuit, the exempt-path inherited-green walk with its post-await cache re-read, the in-flight dedup keyed by SHA-or-worktree, and — inside the `(async () => { … })()` closure it stores in `baselineInFlight` (itself complexity 17) — the declared-check detection, the check-permit run with its clean retry and two `onRun` calls, the `skipped` and slept-through-failure no-verdict returns, the green/red verdict construction with the prior-red fold, and the promote-unless-observed-green cache write. No phase has a name, so a reader asking "what makes a cached red re-run?", "where does the inherited green get re-read?" or "when does this run's verdict overwrite the cache?" scans the whole body plus its closure. Extract one module-private helper per phase and leave `checkMainBaseline` as the cache check, the inheritance call, the in-flight get-or-start and the cleanup.

**Approach.** All edits in src/baseline/main-baseline.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep each existing `//` comment with the code it annotates. Add these module-private declarations beside the function:
- `function cachedBaselineFor(sha: string, wt: string, opts: { reverifyRed: boolean; observedOnly: boolean; forceFresh: boolean }): { cached: MainBaseline | null; key: string }` — today's `const stored = baselineCache.get(sha)`, the `cached` expression (`observedOnly && stored?.inheritedFrom !== undefined ? undefined : stored`), the `if (cached && !forceFresh && !shouldRerunRed(cached, wt, reverifyRed))` short-circuit, and the `cached?.status === "red" ? \`${sha}\u0000${wt}\` : sha` in-flight key; it returns the usable cached verdict (or `null`) together with the in-flight key, so `checkMainBaseline` never re-derives either.
- `async function inheritedBaselineFor(wt: string, sha: string, config: CheckConfigSlice): Promise<MainBaseline | null>` — the `exemptPathsOf(config)` + `inheritedGreen(wt, sha, exempt)` walk, the post-await `baselineCache.get(sha)` re-read with its comment, and the `rememberBaseline(sha, inherited)` write, returning the carried-over verdict or `null`.
- `async function detectedBaselineOutcome(wt: string, config: CheckConfigSlice, onRun: ((run: BaselineCheckRun) => void) | undefined, sampleSleep: SleepSampler, tier: number): Promise<{ outcome: BuildCheckOutcome; durationMs: number } | null>` — the `detectBuildCheck(wt, config)` guard (returning `null` when there is no declared check) and the `withCheckPermit(config, tier, () => runWithCleanRetry(…), undefined, "main baseline")` call verbatim with its clean-retry and permit comments; the type named is whatever `withCheckPermit` already yields there.
- `function baselineFromOutcome(sha: string, wt: string, outcome: BuildCheckOutcome): MainBaselineCheck` — the settled `onRun?.({ outcome, durationMs })` is the caller's, so this holds the `outcome.status === "skipped"` return, the `outcome.status === "failed" && (outcome.run?.sleptMs ?? 0) > SLEEP_SPAN_TOLERANCE_MS` return, and the `outcome.status === "passed" ? green : red` verdict with the `priorRedFrom` fold; returns the `MainBaselineCheck` without writing the cache.
- `function rememberPromotableBaseline(sha: string, baseline: MainBaseline): void` — the `const current = baselineCache.get(sha)` guard (`current?.status !== "green" || current.inheritedFrom !== undefined`) and the `rememberBaseline(sha, baseline)` write with its comment.
- `async function runBaselineOnce(sha: string, wt: string, config: CheckConfigSlice, onRun: ((run: BaselineCheckRun) => void) | undefined, sampleSleep: SleepSampler, tier: number): Promise<MainBaselineCheck>` — replaces the `(async () => { … })()` closure: `detectedBaselineOutcome`, the no-check `{ baseline: null }` return, the final `onRun?.({ outcome, durationMs })`, then `baselineFromOutcome` → `rememberPromotableBaseline` (skipped and slept-failure verdicts return before the write, exactly as today) → `{ baseline }`.
- `checkMainBaseline` keeps its exported name, its `(wt, config, onRun?, reverifyRed?, forceFresh?, sampleSleep?, observedOnly?, tier?)` signature and its doc comment. Its body becomes: the `refSha(wt, "HEAD")` read and its unborn-branch return; `cachedBaselineFor`; when there is no usable cached verdict and neither `forceFresh` nor `observedOnly`, `await inheritedBaselineFor(wt, sha, config)` and return its settled verdict when it is not `null`; the in-flight key; `baselineInFlight.get(key)`, and when absent `runBaselineOnce(…)` stored and set; then the unchanged `try { return await pending; } finally { …delete… }`.

### Subtract, part 5i/6: The provider key leaves the semaphore and the lease — a run is admitted by `maxConcurrent` alone (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; the second of three finer parts replacing part 5b/6, requires Subtract part 5b/6 landed, since part 5b/6 removed every caller that set a cap; touches src/concurrency/semaphore.ts src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts src/concurrency/run-permit.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/merge/merge-verify.ts src/merge/merge-post-review-drain.ts src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts src/runner/runner-pi.ts src/review/review.ts src/git/worktree-pool.ts docs/invariants.md test/provider-lease.test.ts test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts test/review.test.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `Semaphore` owns one team total and nothing else: no per-key cap, no re-key, no forced lease, no key on a `SemaphoreLease`. A role run, a merge verify and a resolver all wait only on `maxConcurrent`. `seamConcurrencyKey` and the role/parked displays that read the key stay until part 5j/6, so this part leaves `snapshot().byKey` as an empty map and never populates `runner.state.parkedOn`.

**Approach.**
- `src/concurrency/semaphore.ts`: delete `enforcedKeyCaps`, `keyCaps`, `keyInUse`, `rekeyWaiters`, `keyAtCap`, `bumpKeyInUse`, `setKeyCaps`, `forceLease`, the `key`/`rekey` members of `SemaphoreLease` and the re-key loop in `drive()`; `acquireLease(tier)` takes no key and only owns the team permit, `canLeaseAtOnce(tier)` drops its key argument, and `pause`/`resume` stay. `snapshot()` keeps `byKey: {}` for part 5j/6.
- Replace `src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts` with `src/concurrency/run-permit.ts`: the same AsyncLocalStorage store carrying only the lease, with `withRunPermit(lease, run)` and `idleWithoutPermit(wait, signal)` (the pause/resume the reviewer retry needs); drop `ensureProviderLease`, `dropProviderLeaseKey`, `keyAtCap` and the piDefault/wait hooks.
- Call sites: `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts` stops computing the admission key, stops setting `runner.state.parkedOn`, drops the director's `forceLease`, wraps the run in `withRunPermit`, and emits `provider_wait` with `cap: "team"` and no `key`; `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts`, `src/merge/merge-drain.ts`, `merge-verify.ts`, `merge-post-review-drain.ts`, `merge-pipeline.ts` drop their key arguments and `withProviderLease`; `src/runner/runner-pi.ts` drops `ensureProviderLease`; `src/review/review.ts` calls `idleWithoutPermit`; `src/git/worktree-pool.ts` drops the `dropProviderLeaseKey()` call.
- `docs/invariants.md`: rewrite the Provider concurrency section and INV-P1–P3 to the one-team-permit rule; the review-retry pause keeps its guarantee under `idleWithoutPermit`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts` is gone and `src/concurrency/run-permit.ts` exists; `grep -rnE 'provider-lease|ensureProviderLease|withProviderLease|dropProviderLeaseKey|idleWithoutProviderLease|setKeyCaps|forceLease|keyAtCap' src/` finds nothing.
- No acquisition carries a provider key and no cap is ever set; a role run, a verify and a resolver wait on `maxConcurrent` alone.
- A failed review's in-place retry still hands its team permit back before the wait and takes it back before the next attempt.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.** Delete `test/provider-lease.test.ts`; keep its `idleWithoutProviderLease` cases as `test/run-permit.test.ts` cases for `idleWithoutPermit`. Update `test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts`, `test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts` and `test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts` to the one-bound admission (drop the per-key cases); update `test/review.test.ts` for the renamed pause. Run them, then the project's gate, and confirm green.

**Goal.** `isEligible` (src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, the exported run-scheduling predicate; complexity 23) is one long body of seven ordered early-return gates. Extract one module-private helper per gate so a reader asking "where does a queued prompt make a run due?" or "which clause reports the yield-scaled hold?" reads that helper, leaving `isEligible` as the ordered dispatch and a final `{ run: false }`. No behavior change: every gate's condition and returned `{ run, reason, skip }` value is the same, so no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/scheduling/scheduling.ts; move each gate's code verbatim, keeping each inline `//` comment with the helper it annotates. Add one module-private result type and one bare top-level `function` per gate, each with a one-line doc comment naming the single job it owns.
- `interface Eligibility { run: boolean; reason?: string; skip?: SkipReason }` (module-private) replaces the inline object-literal return type; `isEligible` keeps its exported signature and doc comment.
- `function blockedFromRunning(runner: RoleRunner, s: RunnerState): boolean` — the enabled/running guard: `!runnerEnabled(runner.config, runner.role) || s.running === true`. One helper (rather than two early returns) because the `||` decision would otherwise keep `isEligible` two shy of its 8 ceiling.
- `function directorGate(s: RunnerState, now: number, inboxCount: number, opts: EligibilityOptions): Eligibility` — the director arm verbatim (`inbox`; `leftover` admitted only at/after `nextRunAt`; else `{ run: false }`).
- `function resumeGate(s: RunnerState, now: number): Eligibility | undefined` — the `resumePending` gate: `{ run: true, reason: "resume" }` at/after `nextRunAt`, else `{ run: false }`; `undefined` when no resume is pending.
- `function inboxGate(inboxCount: number): Eligibility | undefined` — `{ run: true, reason: "inbox" }` when a queued per-role prompt exists, else `undefined`.
- `function gapGate(runner: RoleRunner, s: RunnerState, now: number, opts: EligibilityOptions): Eligibility | undefined` — computes `mult` (`yieldMultiplierFor`), `minGapSeconds` (`scheduleConfigForRole(config, role, planBacklogOpen === true)`), `minGap` (`opts.once ? 0 : minGapSeconds * 1000 * mult`), `sinceLast` and `woken` (`freshlyWoken`), and returns the `yield-gap` hold (or `{ run: false }`) inside the gap; `undefined` once the gap is passed.
- `function scheduledGate(s: RunnerState, now: number, mainHead: string, opts: EligibilityOptions): Eligibility | undefined` — the clock test (`now >= s.nextRunAt || (opts.once && s.backoffSeconds === 0)`) with the `startup`/`scheduled` reason, then the `main moved` wake, then `undefined`.
`isEligible` then reads `const s = runner.state;` and `if (blockedFromRunning(runner, s)) return { run: false }; if (runner.role === DIRECTOR_ROLE) return directorGate(s, now, inboxCount, opts); return resumeGate(s, now) ?? inboxGate(inboxCount) ?? gapGate(runner, s, now, opts) ?? scheduledGate(s, now, mainHead, opts) ?? { run: false };`.

- `function claimGroupAdmission(scope: SchedulingScope, runner: RoleRunner, reason: string | undefined): "admitted" | "skipped"` — look up `scope.claimGroups.get(baseRoleOf(runner.role))`; when absent, clear `runner.state.heldElsewhere` and return `"admitted"` (today's outer `else`); when `runner.state.claim` or `hasOutstandingWork(runner.state)` or `reason === "inbox" || reason === "resume"`, return `"admitted"`; when `group.hold`, `noteSkip(scope.root, runner, "claim-hold")` and return `"skipped"`; else `return assignClaim(scope, runner, group.eligible, group.held)`.
- `function assignClaim(scope: SchedulingScope, runner: RoleRunner, eligible: EligibleEntry[], held: Set<string>): "admitted" | "skipped"` — today's assignment block verbatim: `free` via `eligible.filter((e) => !held.has(e.key))`, `pick = assignNext(free)`, `heldTitles` via `eligible.filter((e) => held.has(e.key)).map((e) => e.title)`, the `runner.state.heldElsewhere = !pick && heldTitles.length > 0 ? heldTitles : undefined` line, then `if (pick) { recordAssignedClaim(scope, runner, pick, held); return "admitted"; }`, else the idle-sibling branch (`if (instanceIndex(runner.role) >= 2 || (heldTitles.length > 0 && !freshlyWoken(runner.state)))` → `noteSkip(…, "no-free-entry")`, the `once.active` settle, `return "skipped"`), else `return "admitted"`.
- `function recordAssignedClaim(scope: SchedulingScope, runner: RoleRunner, pick: EligibleEntry, held: Set<string>): void` — build `runner.state.claim` (the `baseRoleOf(runner.role) === BUGFIX_ROLE ? "BUGS.md" : "PLANS.md"` ternary and `scope.now`/`"assigned"` verbatim), `held.add(pick.key)`, and the `logEventBestEffort(scope.root, …)` block verbatim.

- `function runModelOf(start: HarnessEvent | null): string | null` — today's `typeof start?.model === "string" && start.model.length > 0 ? start.model : null`.
- `function runUsageTextOf(end: HarnessEvent | null): string` — `end === null ? "" : usageText(end)`.

### `renderRunDetail`'s complexity-25 body is split into one named helper per header cell and one per trail step, so the result, cut-off, duration, usage, prompt, pre-edit, peak-context and model cells and the commit/merged-as/merge-latency/reverted suffixes are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role;
