`grep -c 'src/run/run-detail-render.ts' BUGS.md` prints 0; PLANS-DONE.md records landed behavior additions to this file (the `peak ctx`, pre-edit prompt, merge-after-run and context cut-off header cells) but no split of `renderRunDetail` — `grep -cE '^### .*renderRunDetail' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; docs/invariants.md names no run-detail symbol (`grep -n 'run-detail\|renderRunDetail\|RunDetail' docs/invariants.md` prints nothing), so it is unchanged; touches src/run/run-detail-render.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `renderRunDetail` (src/run/run-detail-render.ts, the module's one exported entry; complexity 25) is a 40-line linear builder: it pushes the run's result, cut-off marker, duration, usage, prompt/cache share, pre-edit share, peak context and model cells onto a `summary` array behind eight `if`s, appends the commit, `merged as`, merge-latency and reverted suffixes to the header behind four more, and rebuilds the trail around the merge event behind a further nested pair. Every guard sits inline, so a reader asking "what decides whether the pre-edit cell appears?" or "where does the merge outcome line land?" reads the whole builder. Extract one module-private helper per cell and per trail step and leave `renderRunDetail` as the assembly of their results. No behavior change: the cell order, every guard, the `" · "` separators and the trail ordering are the same, so no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/run/run-detail-render.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, keep each cell's existing inline `//` comment with the helper it annotates, and give each new top-level private helper a one-line doc comment naming the single cell or step it owns. Each per-cell helper returns `string | null` — `null` when its guard omits the cell — so `runSummaryCells` can order and filter them.
- `function runResultCell(d: RunDetail): string` — today's first push: `if (d.endTs === null) return d.startTs === null ? "unpaired" : "in flight"; return d.result ? eventTypeLabel(d.result) : "?";`. Returns a `string` (the result cell is always present).
- `function runCutOffCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `d.cutOff === true` push; guard `if (d.cutOff !== true) return null;`, returning the literal `"cut off at the context ceiling"` with its comment.
- `function runDurationCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `d.durationMs !== null` push; guard `if (d.durationMs === null) return null;`, returning `shortSpanPhrase(d.durationMs)`.
- `function runUsageCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `d.usage !== ""` push; guard and return `d.usage`.
- `function runPromptCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `prompt > 0` push: `const prompt = d.promptTokens ?? 0; const cached = Math.min(d.cacheReadTokens ?? 0, prompt); if (prompt <= 0) return null; return cached > 0 ? \`prompt ${compactTokens(prompt)} tok (${Math.round((100 * cached) / prompt)}% cached)\` : \`prompt ${compactTokens(prompt)} tok\`;`. Its comment ("The run's prompt-token total and the share …") moves with it.
- `function runPreEditCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `preEdit > 0` push: `const prompt = d.promptTokens ?? 0; const preEdit = Math.min(d.preEditPromptTokens ?? 0, prompt); if (preEdit <= 0) return null; return \`pre-edit ${compactTokens(preEdit)} tok\`;`. Its comment moves with it.
- `function runPeakContextCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `(d.peakContextTokens ?? 0) > 0` push; guard `if ((d.peakContextTokens ?? 0) <= 0) return null;`, returning `\`peak ctx ${contextShareLabel(d.peakContextTokens ?? 0, d.contextWindow)}\``.
- `function runModelCell(d: RunDetail): string | null` — today's `d.model !== null` push; guard and return `d.model`.
- `function runSummaryCells(d: RunDetail): string[]` — `return [runResultCell(d), runCutOffCell(d), runDurationCell(d), runUsageCell(d), runPromptCell(d), runPreEditCell(d), runPeakContextCell(d), runModelCell(d)].filter((cell): cell is string => cell !== null);` — array order is the cell order today's sequence of `push`es produces.
- `function runHeaderSuffixCells(d: RunDetail): string[]` — `const sha = runCommitSha(d);` then push `\`commit ${shortSha(sha)}\`` when `sha !== null`, `\`merged as ${shortSha(d.mergedSha)}\`` when `d.mergedSha !== null && d.mergedSha !== sha`, `\`merged ${shortSpanPhrase(d.mergeAfterRunMs)} after the run\`` when `d.mergeAfterRunMs !== undefined`, and `\`reverted ${shortSha(d.reverted.sha)} (by operator)\`` when `d.reverted !== null` — keeping the `reverted` line's `// vocabulary-ok:` comment on its push.
- `function runTrailLines(d: RunDetail): string[]` — today's trail block verbatim: `const trail = d.events.map(formatEvent);` then, when `d.merge !== null`, `const first = d.events[0];` and unshift or push `formatEvent(d.merge)` by whether `d.merge.ts < first.ts`.
`renderRunDetail` keeps its signature and its doc comment (rewritten to name the helpers while keeping the summary-then-events contract): its body becomes `const header = [\`${roleLabel(d.role)} run #${d.run} — ${runSummaryCells(d).join(" · ")}\`, ...runHeaderSuffixCells(d)].join(" · ");` and `return [header, ...runTrailLines(d)].join("\n");`.

### `lossCauseFor`'s complexity-25 cause ladder is split into one named helper per cause — the refused, cut-off, no_change, clustered, review-rejected, review_error and merge-conflict/blocked rules — so each outcome rule is found by name and the branch order stays the parent's null-coalescing chain (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-25 `timeAndSpend` fold (PLANS-DONE.md's one heading naming it) created `lossCauseFor` as the classifier and left it at complexity 25 at the `function lossCauseFor(` line (src/failure/time-spend.ts:182 under the repo's complexity ESLint); independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — before this entry no `## Planned` heading's subject was this symbol (`grep -nE '^### `lossCauseFor' PLANS.md` printed nothing before this entry added its own heading; the one earlier `lossCauseFor` occurrence, inside the `backlogStructureReason` heading, names it only as landed precedent for the family), and no planned part edits the file: `grep -c 'time-spend' PLANS.md` and `grep -c 'src/failure/time-spend.ts' PLANS.md` both print 0 (the only `src/failure/` path a planned entry lists is `src/failure/failure-state-change.ts`, in Subtract parts 5b/6–5e/6, a different file); PLANS-DONE.md records exactly one heading naming `timeAndSpend` (the landmark fold that introduced `lossCauseFor`) and no split of the classifier itself — `grep -nE '^### `lossCauseFor' PLANS-DONE.md` prints nothing; docs/invariants.md's time-spend section binds `timeAndSpend` and pins it with test/failure-time-spend.test.ts, whose signature and semantics this private move preserves and renames nothing; touches src/failure/time-spend.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `lossCauseFor` (src/failure/time-spend.ts, module-private; complexity 25) classifies one run's loss into the `{ key; kind: LossDraft["kind"]; example }` triple the ranking folds, and its seven-arm `if`/`else if` ladder is the documented contract: refused, then cut-off, then no_change, then a clustered result, then the three queued outcomes (review-rejected, review_error, merge-conflict/blocked, with the merge-block deadline-kill override). Every arm's condition and body sit inline, so a reader asking "which rule prices a refused run?" or "what does the review_error arm join on?" reads the whole 80-line ladder. Extract one module-private helper per cause and leave `lossCauseFor` as the ordered chain of calls. No behavior change: every guard, every key/kind/example and the first-match-wins order are the same, so no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/failure/time-spend.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the arm it annotates, and give each new top-level private helper a one-line doc comment naming the single outcome rule it owns. Every helper returns `{ key: string; kind: LossDraft["kind"]; example: string } | null` (a private `type ClassifiedLoss` alias may carry that shape), leads with the arm's guard so no work runs when the rule does not match, and then repeats today's computation verbatim.
- `function refusedLoss(ev: HarnessEvent)` — today's `ev.result === "refused"` arm; guard `if (ev.result !== "refused") return null;`, then `{ key: `refused\u0000${eventRole(ev)}`, kind: "refused", example: typeof ev.summary === "string" ? truncateExample(ev.summary) : "" }`. Its comment ("A refusal is a deliberate objection … BEFORE the no_change one …") moves with it.
- `function cutoffLoss(ev: HarnessEvent, cls: "merged" | "no_change" | "error")` — today's `cls === "no_change" && ev.cutOff === true` arm; guard `if (cls !== "no_change" || ev.cutOff !== true) return null;`, returning `{ key: `cutoff\u0000${eventRole(ev)}`, kind: "cutoff", example: "" }`.
- `function noChangeLoss(ev: HarnessEvent, cls: "merged" | "no_change" | "error")` — today's `cls === "no_change"` arm; guard `if (cls !== "no_change") return null;`, returning `{ key: `no_change\u0000${eventRole(ev)}`, kind: "no_change", example: "" }`.
- `function clusteredLoss(ev: HarnessEvent)` — today's `CLUSTERED_RESULTS.has(String(ev.result))` arm; guard `if (!CLUSTERED_RESULTS.has(String(ev.result))) return null;`, then `const pooled = pooledClusterCause(ev.error);` and `{ key: pooled.key, kind: "error-cluster", example: pooled.example }` (the arm leaves `kind` at its `"error-cluster"` default today).
- `function reviewRejectedLoss(ev: HarnessEvent, resolvedOutcome: ResolvedMerge | null, indexes: LossIndexes)` — today's `ev.result === "queued" && resolvedOutcome?.result === "rejected"` arm; guard `if (ev.result !== "queued" || resolvedOutcome?.result !== "rejected") return null;`, then `newestAttemptEvent(indexes.rejectedByRunner, eventRole(ev), resolvedOutcome)`, `stringList(rej?.reasons)`, the `reasons[0] !== undefined ? truncateExample(reasons[0]) : ""` example and `kind: "review-rejected"` verbatim.
- `function reviewErrorLoss(ev: HarnessEvent, resolvedOutcome: ResolvedMerge | null, indexes: LossIndexes)` — today's queued/`review_error` arm; guard `if (ev.result !== "queued" || resolvedOutcome?.result !== "review_error") return null;`, then `const pooled = pooledClusterCause(newestAttemptEvent(indexes.reviewFailedByRunner, eventRole(ev), resolvedOutcome)?.message);` and `{ key: pooled.key, kind: "error-cluster", example: pooled.example }`.
- `function mergeFailureLoss(ev: HarnessEvent, resolvedOutcome: ResolvedMerge | null, indexes: LossIndexes)` — today's queued/`merge_conflict`-or-`merge_blocked` arm; guard `if (ev.result !== "queued" || (resolvedOutcome?.result !== "merge_conflict" && resolvedOutcome?.result !== "merge_blocked")) return null;`, then `{ key: `${resolvedOutcome.result}\u0000${eventRole(ev)}`, kind: resolvedOutcome.result === "merge_conflict" ? "merge-conflict" : "merge-blocked", example: errorTextOrPlaceholder(undefined) }`, and today's deadline-kill override verbatim — `newestAttemptEvent(indexes.deadlineKilledByRunner, eventRole(ev), resolvedOutcome)`, `killed.scope`, `nonNegativeNumber(killed.timeoutMs, 0)` — mutating `key`/`example` before return.
`lossCauseFor` keeps its signature and its doc comment (rewritten to name the helpers while keeping "the branch order is the contract"): its body becomes `return refusedLoss(ev) ?? cutoffLoss(ev, cls) ?? noChangeLoss(ev, cls) ?? clusteredLoss(ev) ?? reviewRejectedLoss(ev, resolvedOutcome, indexes) ?? reviewErrorLoss(ev, resolvedOutcome, indexes) ?? mergeFailureLoss(ev, resolvedOutcome, indexes);` — `??` evaluates left to right, so the first rule that answers wins exactly as the `if`/`else if` ladder does today.

### `runSupervisedGeneration`'s complexity-27 boot body is split into one named helper per job, so the stop handlers, the run watchdogs, the generation boot, the banner/subscription and the round summary with its exit codes are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-25 `cmdStart` split (PLANS-DONE.md's one heading naming `runSupervisedGeneration`) created it as the supervised-generation home and left it at complexity 27 at the `async function runSupervisedGeneration(` line (src/cli/cli-start.ts:230 under the repo's complexity ESLint); independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — before this entry no `## Planned` entry named the symbol or the file, so `grep -n 'runSupervisedGeneration' PLANS.md` and `grep -n 'cli-start' PLANS.md` both match only this heading and its own body; the Subtract parts and the two in-flight pane/structure splits name src/config, src/concurrency, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/review, src/roles, src/ui, src/doctor, src/events and src/backlog files, none src/cli/cli-start.ts; PLANS-DONE.md records exactly one heading naming `runSupervisedGeneration` — the landmark `cmdStart` split that introduced it, never a split of its body (`grep -cE '^### .*runSupervisedGeneration' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 1, the introduction); docs/invariants.md binds `armScheduledStopWatch` in this file, whose signature and scheduling semantics this move preserves and renames nothing; touches src/cli/cli-start.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `runSupervisedGeneration` (src/cli/cli-start.ts, module-private; complexity 27) is the supervised-generation half the landed `cmdStart` split left behind: one ~165-line body from the `controller` creation through the final `process.exit`. A reader asking "where is the second Ctrl+C made a force-exit?" or "what sets `process.exitCode` when a `--once --json` round is cut short?" reads the whole method. Extract one module-private helper per job and leave `runSupervisedGeneration` as the ordered composition. No behavior change: every signal, timer, banner line, summary, exit code and the order they fire are the same, so no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/cli/cli-start.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. The jobs, in the order `runSupervisedGeneration` calls them:
- `installStopHandlers(json)` — creates the `AbortController`, the `stopping` flag, the `stop` closure (second press `process.exit(130)`, else the suppressed prose and `controller.abort()`) and the SIGINT/SIGTERM registrations; returns `{ controller, stop, isStopping }` so the later once-exit check reads `isStopping()` instead of a captured boolean.
- `armRunWatchdogs(root, json, forMs, stop, isStopping)` — `windowStart` from `inheritedWindowStart`, the `forMs`-gated `armDeadlineTimer` (deadline prose suppressed under `--json`), and `armScheduledStopWatch` (whose callback fires `stop` only while `!isStopping()`); returns the three handles.
- `bootGenerationParts(root, branchArg, once)` — the baseline-verdict persist, the once-gated `createRedeployer`, and the once-gated `LaunchServicesWatch`; the redeployer's inferred return type is never named in a parameter annotation (the project's consistent-type-imports rule forbids inline `import()` types and the module's types are unexported), so this helper infers its own return and the caller passes `redeploy` straight into `runOrchestrator`.
- `announceGeneration(roles, mainBranch, once, json, forMs, root, build)` — the banner `say`s (root/for/build notes, roles, watch line) and the `json`-gated `subscribeEvents`; takes the already-computed `build` string so the redeployer value stays out of its parameter list; returns `unsubscribe`.
- `printRoundSummary(root, roles, runsBefore, once, json, forMs, windowStart, settled, runsDone, restart)` — the `once` report/summary and the `forMs`+`!restart` window report; takes the three `exit` fields rather than `exit` so the unexported `OrchestratorExit` never appears in a signature.
- `applyOnceExitCode(root, roles, runsBefore, runsDone, once, json, isStopping)` — the `onceFailures` line, the `ONCE_FAILED_EXIT_CODE` setting, and the truncated-`--once --json` exit code.
`runSupervisedGeneration` then reads: destructure input and the supervisor import; `const { controller, stop, isStopping } = installStopHandlers(json)`; `const { windowStart, deadlineTimer, scheduledStopWatch } = armRunWatchdogs(root, json, forMs, stop, isStopping)`; the parent-death watch; the `runnerIds`/`roles` resolution; `const { redeploy, launchServicesWatch } = await bootGenerationParts(root, branchArg, once)` and the `build` string; `const unsubscribe = announceGeneration(...)`; the migrations, the `runsBefore` snapshot and the `runOrchestrator` try/finally; `printRoundSummary(...)`; `applyOnceExitCode(...)`; the `exit.restart` and `forMs` exits.

### `parseOpencodeCatalog`'s complexity-25 body is split into one named helper per job — the body unwrap, the per-model pricing, the effort levels and the per-model build — so the raw-vs-wrapped shape and the free/priced/context/image/effort reads are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-26 `checkTierModels` split and the `backlogStructureReason`/`runSupervisedGeneration` plans apply the same per-job extraction; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — `grep -c 'src/agent/opencode' PLANS.md` prints 0 and `grep -c 'parseOpencodeCatalog' PLANS.md` prints 0, so no planned entry, held or blocked, names this file or symbol; the Subtract parts take src/config, src/concurrency, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/review, src/roles, src/ui, src/gui, src/events and src/backlog, the in-flight splits take src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts and src/cli/cli-start.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts take src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/roles, src/gui, src/ui and src/prompt, none src/agent/opencode; PLANS-DONE.md records landed behavior additions to the file (the seeded cache, the total parse, the billedAt demotion) but no split of `parseOpencodeCatalog` — `grep -cE '^### .*parseOpencodeCatalog' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; docs/invariants.md's "OpenCode catalog seed: a refresh never rejects the startup check" binds `parseOpencodeCatalog` and names no symbol this move renames, so it is unchanged; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `parseOpencodeCatalog` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts, exported; complexity 25) accepts the live models.dev `api.json` (providers at the top level) and OpenCode's cached copy (the same map under a `body` key), keeps the `opencode` provider plus every provider the config routes through OpenCode, and builds one `OpencodeCatalogModel` per entry from an untrusted network object: the `free` flag and per-M prices from `cost`, the context window from `limit.context`, `images` from `modalities.input`, and the `reasoning_options` effort `values`. Each job sits inline in one nested loop with the model literal mutated as it goes, so a reader asking "what does the parser accept as the catalog root?" or "which fields does the free/priced decision read?" reads the whole loop. Extract one module-private helper per job and leave `parseOpencodeCatalog` as the body unwrap, the provider filter and the two loops. No behavior change: every branch, every field the model carries and every model kept or dropped are the same, so no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates, and give each new top-level private helper a one-line doc comment naming the single job it owns.
- `function catalogRoot(body: unknown): Record<string, unknown>` — today's `const root = isJsonObject(body) ? body : {}; const wrapped = root.body; const catalog = isJsonObject(wrapped) ? wrapped : root;` verbatim, returning `catalog` (the root `parseOpencodeCatalog` iterates). `isJsonObject` already narrows to `Record<string, unknown>`.
- `function modelPricing(m: Record<string, unknown>): { costed: boolean; free: boolean; inputPerM: unknown; outputPerM: unknown }` — today's `const cost = isJsonObject(m.cost) ? m.cost : undefined; const input = cost?.input ?? 0; const output = cost?.output ?? 0;` and the `free` expression `cost !== undefined && input === 0 && output === 0`; `costed` is `cost !== undefined`. Return the four fields (the `unknown` prices because the body is untrusted; `isOpencodeCatalogModel` still drops a non-number price), so the caller's only branch is `costed`.
- `function modelEfforts(m: Record<string, unknown>): unknown[]` — today's `if (!Array.isArray(m.reasoning_options)) return [];` guard plus the `m.reasoning_options.flatMap((r: unknown) => isJsonObject(r) && r.type === "effort" && Array.isArray(r.values) ? (r.values as unknown[]) : [])` verbatim; the caller keeps the `efforts.length > 0` guard so it alone decides whether `model.efforts` is set.
- `function catalogModelFrom(m: Record<string, unknown>): OpencodeCatalogModel | null` — today's per-model build verbatim: `const pricing = modelPricing(m);` then the model literal `{ free: pricing.free }`, the `if (pricing.costed)` branch setting `inputPerM`/`outputPerM`, the `if (isJsonObject(m.limit) && m.limit.context !== undefined) model.context = m.limit.context;` branch, the `if (isJsonObject(m.modalities) && Array.isArray(m.modalities.input))` block setting `images`, the `const efforts = modelEfforts(m); if (efforts.length > 0) model.efforts = efforts;` pair, and `return isOpencodeCatalogModel(model) ? model : null;` in place of the caller's store-if guard. Every explanatory comment (`Only a present cost block marks a model free …`) moves with its block.
`parseOpencodeCatalog` keeps its export, its `(body: unknown, providers: readonly string[])` signature and its doc comment. Its body becomes `const out: Record<string, OpencodeCatalogModel> = {};`, `for (const [provider, providerInfo] of Object.entries(catalogRoot(body))) {`, the two `continue` guards verbatim, `for (const [id, m] of Object.entries(providerInfo.models)) { if (!isJsonObject(m)) continue; const model = catalogModelFrom(m); if (model !== null) out[`${provider}/${id}`] = model; }`, and `return out;`.

**Files touched.** src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The complexity falls: the repo's `../../../node_modules/.bin/eslint --no-config-lookup -c docs/code-metrics/eslint-complexity.config.mjs 'src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts'` reports `parseOpencodeCatalog` at 10 or below (it is 25 today) and each of `catalogRoot`, `modelPricing`, `modelEfforts` and `catalogModelFrom` at 10 or below. The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts` still matches the same names it matches today, and no import line changes (every helper uses `isJsonObject`, already imported).
- Each helper exists exactly once and is module-private: `grep -nE '^(async )?function (catalogRoot|modelPricing|modelEfforts|catalogModelFrom)' src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts` shows one declaration per name, and `parseOpencodeCatalog`'s body holds no `isJsonObject(m.cost)`, `cost?.input`, `m.limit`, `m.modalities`, `m.reasoning_options` or `isOpencodeCatalogModel(` occurrence — only its call to `catalogModelFrom`.
- Behavior is byte-for-byte the same: test/opencode-catalog.test.ts passes unchanged, including "parseOpencodeCatalog keeps only the opencode provider by default, with the free model's fields", "parseOpencodeCatalog keeps a provider the config routes through OpenCode, as priced", "parseOpencodeCatalog reads the raw models.dev api.json shape, providers at the top level", "parseOpencodeCatalog treats a model with no cost block as not free" and "parseOpencodeCatalog skips a malformed provider or model instead of throwing". In particular the malformed-body case still yields `{ "opencode/a": { free: false }, "opencode/b": { free: false }, "opencode/ok": { free: true, inputPerM: 0, outputPerM: 0 } }`, so a model with a non-number price, context or effort is still dropped by `isOpencodeCatalogModel` rather than stored. ### `backlogStructureReason`'s per-file rule loop is split into one named helper per structural fault, so the duplicate-heading rule, the dropped-known-section rule, the re-added-archive-heading rule, the misplaced-plan rule and the hidden-fixed-record rule are each found by name (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-26 `timeAndSpend` fold into `buildLossIndexes`/`resolveQueuedRuns`/`lossCauseFor` and the `cmdStart` split created named homes the same way; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — `grep -n 'src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts' PLANS.md` prints nothing, and the only `## Planned` mention of the symbol is the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part 3m/3, whose goal re-points the deterministic gate in src/review/diff-rules.ts and src/baseline/main-watch.ts and which edits no file under src/backlog; the Subtract parts and the two in-flight TUI pane splits name src/config, src/concurrency, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/review, src/roles, src/ui, src/doctor, src/cli and src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, backlog-release.ts, backlog-index.ts and backlog-cli.ts, none `backlog-structure.ts`; PLANS-DONE.md records landed behavior additions to the file (the stranding rules, the archive readdition guard, the double-block Fixed guard) and no split of `backlogStructureReason` — `grep -cE '^### .*backlogStructureReason' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; docs/invariants.md binds `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` by module and its regular-file read policy (INV-G3), naming no symbol this move renames; touches src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** `backlogStructureReason` (src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts) is one body that loops each touched backlog file and, after reading its head and base and counting section titles, runs five independent structural rules in order — a duplicate `## ` heading, a dropped known section, a re-added archive `### ` heading, a plan filed under `## Done` with no done date, and a Fixed entry carrying more than one `**Symptom:**`/`**Fix:**` block — returning the first rule's message. Each rule already has its own comment and its own message, but the rules have no names to grep, so a reader asking "where is the archive-repast guard?" or "what refuses a missing known section?" reads the whole loop. Extract one module-private helper per rule, leaving `backlogStructureReason` as the per-file reads, the two count maps and one `??` chain.

**Approach.** All edits in src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every explanatory comment with the rule it annotates. Declare five module-private helpers beside the existing `sectionTitleCounts`/`readdedHeadings`/`doubleBlockFixedEntries` helpers, each returning the first finding or `undefined`:
- `duplicateSectionReason(file: string, headCounts: Map<string, number>, baseCounts: Map<string, number>): string | undefined` holds the `for (const [title, count] of headCounts) if (count > 1 && count > (baseCounts.get(title) ?? 0))` rule and returns the `adds another "## <title>" heading` message verbatim.
- `droppedSectionReason(file: string, headCounts: Map<string, number>, baseCounts: Map<string, number>): string | undefined` holds the `KNOWN_SECTIONS` loop and returns the `drops the "## <title>" section` message verbatim.
- `readdedHeadingReason(file: string, base: string, head: string): string | undefined` holds the `file === PLANS_ARCHIVE || file === BUGS_ARCHIVE` `readdedHeadings(base, head)` block (its `plural`/`truncate` message verbatim) and returns `undefined` for every other file.
- `misplacedPlanReason(file: string, wt: string, baseRev: string, base: string, head: string): Promise<string | undefined>` holds the `file === "PLANS.md" || file === PLANS_ARCHIVE` branch — the `baseKeys` union over `planHeadingKeys(base)` and the sibling archive read via `fileContentAt`, the `strandedPlanEntries(head)` find, and the two file-specific messages (`PLANS_ARCHIVE` vs `PLANS.md`) verbatim.
- `hiddenFixedRecordReason(file: string, base: string, head: string): string | undefined` holds the `file === "BUGS.md" || file === BUGS_ARCHIVE` `doubleBlockFixedEntries` block and its `holds more than one **Symptom:**/**Fix:** block` message verbatim.

The loop body keeps its `full`/`head` reads (the `lstatSync().isFile()` guard and `readTextOrNull` are unchanged, preserving the symlink policy INV-G3 pins) and its `base = await fileContentAt(wt, baseRev, file)`, then computes `headCounts`/`baseCounts` and returns

```ts
const reason =
  duplicateSectionReason(file, headCounts, baseCounts) ??
  droppedSectionReason(file, headCounts, baseCounts) ??
  readdedHeadingReason(file, base, head) ??
  (await misplacedPlanReason(file, wt, baseRev, base, head)) ??
  hiddenFixedRecordReason(file, base, head);
if (reason !== undefined) return reason;
```

The `??` chain keeps today's rule order, and the sole `await` sits where the misplaced-plan rule already awaited `fileContentAt`. `backlogStructureReason` keeps its export, its `(wt, mainBranch, files)` signature and its doc comment, its `touched.length === 0` early return and its `changeBaseRev` call. No import is added or removed (the helpers use symbols already imported).

**Files touched.** src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- The five helpers exist once, are module-private, and `backlogStructureReason`'s body contains no `readdedHeadings(`/`doubleBlockFixedEntries(`/`strandedPlanEntries(`/`planHeadingKeys(` call (those calls live in the helpers), while it calls each of the five helpers at most once.
- Behavior is byte-identical: each rule's message and the order rules fire in are unchanged, so `test/backlog-structure.test.ts` passes unchanged — including "backlogStructureReason never follows a symlinked backlog file out of the worktree" and the duplicate/dropped/readded/stranded/double-block cases — as do `test/backlog-archive.test.ts`, `test/merge-to-main.test.ts`, `test/stage-check.test.ts` and `test/review.test.ts`, which drive the reason through the merge gate, the stage check and the review gate.
- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` still matches exactly what it matches today.
- docs/invariants.md is unchanged: INV-G3 binds the module and its regular-file read policy, and this move renames neither `backlogStructureReason` nor the read guard.

**Tests.** No new test module: a behavior-preserving move guarded by the existing backlog-structure suite. Run `test/backlog-structure.test.ts` and `test/backlog-archive.test.ts` whole, then `test/merge-to-main.test.ts`, `test/stage-check.test.ts` and `test/review.test.ts`, plus the project's gate, and confirm green.

**Goal.** `checkTierModels` (src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, exported; complexity 47) is the doctor's "models for each tier" row: it loads the config, collects the declared seam pairs into a pi-pairs map and a per-non-pi-backend routed-models map, computes the OMP env note, reads pi's provider definitions, walks every pi pair to resolve it against those definitions and pi's listing and probes its provider's auth once, builds one routing note per used backend, and joins the fails and warns into one outcome. Every job is inline and interleaved with shared mutable state (`pairs`, `fails`, `warns`, `readyProviders`, `checkedProviders`), so a reader asking "how is a pair resolved when models.json is missing?" or "where is a provider probed once?" must read the whole body. Extract one module-private helper per job and leave `checkTierModels` as the composition. No behavior change: the exported signature, the outcome level and every joined detail string are untouched.

### The e2e/concurrency tier's remaining positive-overlap and role-run waits become deterministic — the two resize grow-waits, the two reached-cap/free-fallback role-run waits and the permits part 2/5 & 3/5 overlap observations (planned 2026-10-26 by the steward; the follow-up to the landed deterministic-concurrency family `The e2e/concurrency tier's wall-clock waits and pid probes become deterministic`, parts 1/3–3/3 all done 2026-10-26 by the feature role in PLANS-DONE.md, which retired three member tests and deliberately left these members; prompted by the class entry BUGS.md:70 (found by the steward role 2026-10-23) and its ci notes — 8b73415 and de048f2 among them — recording the e2e tier red on five or more consecutive main tips under host load ≈ 105–170, far past the class's recorded ≈ 67 ceiling, with every failure an already-named member; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — the `Every commit is verified on main` and Subtract series and the in-flight split parts take src/backlog, src/config, src/review, src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/doctor, src/ui and the baseline/init/codex files, none of the three e2e files or test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts named here; touches test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The landed deterministic-concurrency family (parts 1/3–3/3) re-pointed three member tests onto event/marker or process-identity observations and deliberately left the members that prove a POSITIVE cross-process overlap — or that a role run started — by sampling a fake shim's in-flight census against a wall-clock budget. Those are what keep the e2e tier red on a loaded host: each needs two processes to demonstrably overlap (or a role run to start) inside a 60 s/150 s budget, which a host at load ≈ 105–170 cannot reliably meet, so the tier is red purely on machine load with no code change. Make each remaining member's concurrency verdict independent of real scheduling speed, so the tier is green on a loaded and an idle host alike.

**Approach.** Move each remaining member's positive observation onto a signal the harness controls rather than how fast the orchestrator's real poll loop and shims happen to run, mirroring the event/marker and identity re-points of parts 1/3–3/3:
- test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts's two grow-waits (`a live maxConcurrent edit resizes the cap without a restart` ~150 s, `a live maxConcurrentPerProvider edit admits a parked omlx run and logs its own event` ~60 s): replace the `readSamples(runDir).some((n) => n >= 2)` "overlapping runs after the grow" wait. Part 3/3's note records that an earlier count-based replacement was judged less robust and dropped the budget, so the replacement must not just shrink the wait: prefer having the concurrency fake (the shim that writes the in-flight census) hold both roles' shims until the orchestrator has admitted both, so `n >= 2` is guaranteed once two are admitted — deterministic, no real-time sampling.
- test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts's `samples.some((s) => s.provider === "huggingface" && s.totalInFlight >= 2)` in both part 2/5 and part 3/5: same positive-overlap pattern — it only materializes if a second process starts within the ~12-sample window. Force the beside-an-omlx overlap in the shim's census (or read the orchestrator's own admission event) once both roles are admitted, instead of sampling real timing.
- test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts's `a reached cap switches roles to the free fallback model instead of stopping them` (~60 s "timed out waiting for a role run after the cap was reached") and `a free fallback whose runs keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves` (~60 s "timed out waiting for the first fallback run"): the flaking waits are the positive `awaitSettledRun`/run-count waits that need a role to actually run. Re-point them onto the orchestrator's own run-start event/marker (the same move part 3/3 applied to `budget_resumed`) so the "a role ran" check does not depend on how fast a run settles under load.
- Keep every negative assertion byte-identical — the permits part 2/5 & 3/5 at-most-one and nothing-exceeds-total checks, and the resize post-shrink no-new-concurrent-run checks fail open under load and are not the flake; only the positive observations change.

**Files touched.** test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Each named member no longer proves overlap or a role-run start by sampling the fake census or a fixed sleep against a wall-clock budget on a loaded host; each waits on a harness-controlled or event/marker signal that the overlap (or run start) it asserts has happened.
- The members' negative assertions (at-most-one-run, nothing-exceeds-total, no-new-concurrent-run-after-shrink) are unchanged and still pass.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.** No new test module: a re-pointing guarded by the existing test/orchestrator-resize.e2e.test.ts, test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts and test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts member cases, whose negative assertions stay byte-identical and whose positive-overlap/role-run steps move to the deterministic signal. Run the three files' members whole, then the project's gate, and confirm green.

**Verification note 2026-10-26 by the feature role.** The two resize grow-waits, the two permits part 2/5 & 3/5 overlaps and the reached-cap role-run wait all went green under the full harness at host load ≈ 105 (they had been the named red members). The free-fallback breaker member's run-2 spawn could not be re-verified green under the test runner's suiteEnv at the same load (it times out "waiting for the first fallback run" across five harness runs), yet the identical test file passes in ~5 s under a plain `node --test`, and a faithful off-harness reproduction spawns clean-2/clean-3 and demotes as asserted — so the residual is the pre-existing run-2 spawn-latency flake under the harness env at extreme load, not the census/marker re-point this entry's members share. My change strictly relaxes the original wait (the run marker appears before the `runs >= 2 && !running` settle condition it replaced), so it cannot regress a passing run.

**Approach.** All edits in src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. Add a one-line doc comment to each new top-level private helper and each new interface naming the single job it owns. Keep `redDurationPhrase` exactly as it is.
- `interface RedWindow` — `{ relevant: HarnessEvent[]; culprit: HarnessEvent | undefined }`, with a doc comment naming `relevant` as the in-window events that open, extend or end a red (the `isRedMain(e) || isPassingMainCheck(e)` set, in `events` order) and `culprit` as the newest in-window `main_culprit` carrying a non-empty string `commit`.

### `classifyTurnFailed`'s complexity-27 classifier body is split into one named helper per classifier arm — the context-window signal, the rate-limit reading, `usage_not_included`, the transient server status and the permanent-login arms — so each arm is found by name (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the codex-translator plan that extracted `handleTurnFailed` from `codexTranslator` (PLANS-DONE.md) left `classifyTurnFailed` unchanged at complexity 27, and this plan applies the same per-job extraction the `readTranscriptTail`, `parsePromptFlags`, `parseStartInvocation` and `newLiveConfigReload` plans apply; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — `awk '/^## Planned/{p=1} /^## Done/{p=0} p' PLANS.md | grep -c 'codex-stream'` prints 0, so no entry, eligible, held, blocked or refused, names src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts or test/codex-stream.test.ts: the Subtract, `Every commit is verified on main` and in-flight split parts take src/backlog, src/config, src/roles, src/ui, src/ui/tui, src/ui/gui, src/gui, src/doctor, src/cli, src/cli/cli-command-args.ts, src/ui/transcript-tail.ts, src/init/init.ts, src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts and the merge/review/orchestrator/runner files, none the codex stream translator; PLANS-DONE.md's codex-stream headings are the translator-behavior plans, and its two `classifyTurnFailed` mentions are prose in the `handleTurnFailed` extraction naming it as deliberately left unchanged (`grep -cE '^### .*classifyTurnFailed' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0), never a split of its body; docs/invariants.md's codex entries bind the write guard and hook trust, not this translator, and `grep -c 'classifyTurnFailed' docs/invariants.md` prints 0, so this move touches no pinned guarantee; touches src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `classifyTurnFailed` (src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts, module-private; complexity 27) is the one classifier the `turn.failed` arm of `codexTranslator` calls: it reads the inner-JSON error's `code`, `type`, `message` and `status`, then returns the canonical `tumwaterKind` (and, for the server case, its `backendKind`, plus a `rateLimit` reading for the transient rate-limit case) that `PiStreamParser` trusts before its text regexes. A reader asking "which arm wins a 400 that names the context window?" or "where is the rejected window derived?" reads the whole chain. Extract one module-private helper per classifier arm and leave `classifyTurnFailed` as the ordered composition. No behavior change: every arm fires in today's exact order, so the same `parsed` yields the same result object, and no test file is edited.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. Keep `windowTypeName`, `secondsUntilUnixStamp` and `SERVER_TRANSIENT_STATUS` exactly as they are. Add a one-line doc comment to each new helper naming the single arm it owns.
- `interface TurnFailedFields` — `{ code: string | undefined; errType: string | undefined; message: string | undefined; status: number | undefined }`, with a doc comment naming each field's source (`error.code`, `error.type`, `error.message` falling back to `parsed.message`, and `parsed.status`).
- `interface TurnFailedClass` — today's inline return shape `{ kind?: TumwaterKind; backendKind?: BackendFailureKind; errorMessage?: string; rateLimit?: Json }`, so the helpers and `classifyTurnFailed` share the named type.
- `function readTurnFailedFields(parsed: Json): TurnFailedFields` — `objectOrEmpty(parsed.error)`, the three `typeof … === "string" ? … : undefined` reads (the `message` read falling back to `parsed.message`), and `nonNegativeNumber(parsed.status, undefined)`.
- `function isContextExceeded({ code, errType, message, status }: TurnFailedFields): boolean` — today's `namesContextWindow` regex plus the `code === "context_window_exceeded" || (status === 400 && errType === "invalid_request_error" && namesContextWindow(message))` condition, with the "tested BEFORE the generic 400" comment. Owns the context-window arm.
- `function rateLimitReading(parsed: Json, { code, status }: TurnFailedFields): Json | undefined` — today's whole arm verbatim: the `code === "usage_limit_reached" || code === "rate_limit_exceeded" || status === 429` guard returns the assembled reading (the `rate_limit_reached_type` number/string reads, `resets_at`, `secondsUntilUnixStamp`, `windowTypeName(minutes ?? 300)`), else undefined. Owns the rate-limit arm.
- `function isUsageNotIncluded({ code }: TurnFailedFields): boolean` — `code === "usage_not_included"`. Owns the used-up-account arm.
- `function isTransientServer({ status }: TurnFailedFields): boolean` — `status !== undefined && SERVER_TRANSIENT_STATUS.has(status)`. Owns the server-status arm.
- `function isPermanentLogin({ message, status, errType }: TurnFailedFields): boolean` — the refresh-token regex, `status === 401`, and `status === 400 && errType === "invalid_request_error"`, with their comments. Owns the permanent-login arms.
- `classifyTurnFailed(parsed: Json): TurnFailedClass` keeps its signature (with the named return type) and its doc comment, and its body becomes `const fields = readTurnFailedFields(parsed); const kind: TurnFailedClass = { errorMessage: fields.message }; if (isContextExceeded(fields)) { kind.kind = "contextExceeded"; return kind; } const rateLimit = rateLimitReading(parsed, fields); if (rateLimit !== undefined) { kind.kind = "transientRateLimit"; kind.rateLimit = rateLimit; return kind; } if (isUsageNotIncluded(fields)) { kind.kind = "configError"; return kind; } if (isTransientServer(fields)) { kind.kind = "transientBackend"; kind.backendKind = "server"; return kind; } if (isPermanentLogin(fields)) { kind.kind = "configError"; return kind; } return kind;`. The arm order is exactly today's: context, rate limit, usage_not_included, server transient, permanent login. Extend its doc comment with one sentence naming the helpers as the per-arm homes.

### `resolveInitPlan`'s complexity-27 validate-and-resolve body is split into one named helper per validation job — the template resolve, the brief cap, the missing-git check, the team-workspace refusal, the missing-brief refusal, the `--branch`-on-an-existing-repo refusal, the adoption resolve, the changed-brief refusal and the preferred-branch resolve — so each job is found by name (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-25 `initProject` split (PLANS-DONE.md's `initProject`'s ~215-line validate-then-seed body) created `resolveInitPlan` as the validate-and-resolve home and left it at complexity 27, and this plan applies the same per-job extraction the `parsePromptFlags` and `parseStartInvocation` plans apply to their files; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — `awk '/^## Planned/{p=1} /^## Done/{p=0} p' PLANS.md | grep -c 'init/init'` and `... | grep -c 'init\.test'` both print 0, so no entry (eligible, held, blocked or refused) names src/init/init.ts or test/init.test.ts: the in-flight/eligible plans take src/cli/cli-command-args.ts, src/ui/transcript-tail.ts and the Subtract release, doctor-probe and banner surfaces (src/ui/tui, src/ui/gui, src/gui, src/doctor, src/cli.ts), none of them src/init or test/init.test.ts (the greps above); PLANS-DONE.md records no split of `resolveInitPlan` itself (`grep -cE '^### .*resolveInitPlan' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; its `init/init.ts` headings are the init behavior that created this function), and the 2026-10-25 `initProject` split is the sibling extraction, not a duplicate; docs/invariants.md's INV-Q1 binds `resolveInitPlan` (`src/init/init.ts`), and the symbol and its pre-side-effect guarantee both stay, so no invariant text changes; touches src/init/init.ts test/init.test.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `resolveInitPlan` (src/init/init.ts) validates one `tumwater init` request and resolves everything `seedProject` needs before any side effect, but its whole body is one async function of complexity 27, so the template refusal, the brief cap, the missing-git refusal, the team-workspace refusal, the bare-init refusal, the `--branch` refusal, the adoption decision and its unmarked-`TUMWATER.md` refusal, the changed-brief refusal and the new-repo branch validation all read as one block. Split it into named helpers, one per validation job, so each refusal is found by name and the export's own body is only the ordered composition of them. Pure move: no behavior change for any input, no new capability, and INV-Q1 (every refusal before any side effect) still holds by construction because the helpers are the same guards in the same order.

**Approach.** All source edits in src/init/init.ts; move the code verbatim, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. Add one doc comment to each new top-level private function naming the single job it owns. Run them in today's order.
- `function resolveInitTemplate(id: string | undefined): NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof getTemplate>>` — today's `const template = opts.template ? getTemplate(opts.template) : null;`, the `if (opts.template && !template) throw new Error(unknownTemplateError(opts.template));` and the `template ?? getTemplate("blank")!` default, with the "Resolve the template before any side effect" comment. Owns the unknown-template refusal and the blank default.
- `function combineInitBrief(tpl: InitTemplate, briefText: string): string` — today's `tpl.briefPreamble ? \`${tpl.briefPreamble}\n\n${briefText.trim()}\` : briefText.trim()` join and the `if (combinedPrompt.length > BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS)` `tooLongMessage(...)` throw, with its comment. Owns the preamble join and the brief cap.
- `function requireGitOnPath(): void` — today's `if (!findOnPath("git")) throw new Error(GIT_MISSING_MESSAGE);`. Owns the missing-git refusal.
- `function refuseTeamWorkspace(root: string): void` — today's `const owner = owningTeamRoot(root); if (owner !== undefined) throw new Error(teamWorkspaceMessage(owner));`, with the "A team workspace is not a project" comment. Owns the team-workspace refusal.

### `readTranscriptTail`'s complexity-29 backward-scan body is split into one named helper per job — the open/stat guard, the chunk boundary, the per-chunk line walk, the arming walk, the chunk scan loop and the final window — so each job is found by name (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; continues the landed split-large-function family — the 2026-10-19 transcript work created `readTranscriptTail` as the backward-scan home and it is 29 today at the `export function readTranscriptTail(` line (src/ui/transcript-tail.ts:90 under the repo's complexity ESLint), and this plan applies the same per-job extraction the `parsePromptFlags` and `parseStartInvocation` plans apply to their files; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — `awk '/^## Planned/{p=1} /^## Done/{p=0} p' PLANS.md | grep -c 'transcript-tail'` and `... | grep -c 'readTranscriptTail'` both print 0, so no entry (eligible, held, blocked or refused) names src/ui/transcript-tail.ts or this function: the in-flight `parsePromptFlags` split edits src/cli/cli-command-args.ts, `newLiveConfigReload` edits src/config/config-live.ts and `parseStartInvocation` edits src/cli/cli-start.ts; PLANS-DONE.md records no split of `readTranscriptTail` itself (`grep -cE '^### .*readTranscriptTail' PLANS-DONE.md` prints 0; its `transcript-tail` hits are comment-only citations and terminology renames); docs/invariants.md names no `readTranscriptTail` or `transcript-tail` symbol (`grep -n 'readTranscriptTail\|transcript-tail' docs/invariants.md` prints nothing), so this move touches no pinned guarantee; touches src/ui/transcript-tail.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `readTranscriptTail` (src/ui/transcript-tail.ts) renders the last `limit` transcript entries of a raw pi log by scanning backward from EOF in 1MB chunks, but its whole body is one function of complexity 29, so the rotation guard, the chunk-boundary arithmetic, the arming walk, the per-chunk line walk, the scan loop and the final window are all read as one block. Split it into named helpers, one per job, so each is found by name and the export's own body is only the composition of them. Pure move: no behavior change for any input, and no new capability.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/transcript-tail.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates.
- `interface TailScanState` — the today's-locals that the scan threads through the helpers: `size`, `pos`, `held`, `lines`, `candidates`, `end`, `stoppedAtBoundary`, `armed`, `boundaryIndex`, with a doc comment naming each as it stands today (`size` the fstat size, for the whole-file fallback; `pos` the exclusive end of the unscanned region; `held` the straddling line's tail; `lines` complete lines newest-first; `candidates` the entry-candidate count from EOF; `end` the offset just past the newest complete newline; `stoppedAtBoundary`/`armed`/`boundaryIndex` the arming walk's progress).
- `function openTailFile(file: string): { fd: number; size: number } | null` — today's `statOrNull` + `st.size === 0` guard, the `openForRead` null guard (with its rotation comment), and the `fs.fstatSync(fd).size` + `size === 0` close-and-return-null guard with their comments, verbatim; returns the opened `{ fd, size }` or null. Owns the open/stat guard.
- `function prepareTailChunk(fd: number, c: Buffer, got: number, state: TailScanState): number | null` — today's `const lastNl = c.lastIndexOf(10);` and `if (lastNl < 0) return null;` (null = the caller holds the whole chunk), then `if (state.end === 0) state.end = state.pos - got + lastNl + 1;`, the `if (state.pos - got > 0)` outer-boundary one-byte read with the `boundary[0] !== 10` held/`emitStart` arm and the `else state.held = EMPTY_BUFFER`, and the `if (c[emitStart] === 10) emitStart += 1` blank-line skip — all verbatim and in order; returns `emitStart`. Owns the chunk-boundary arithmetic.
- `function walkTailChunkLines(state: TailScanState, c: Buffer, emitStart: number, includePrompts: boolean, limit: number): void` — today's `let lineEnd = c.lastIndexOf(10); while (lineEnd >= emitStart) { ... }` walk verbatim: the `c.lastIndexOf(10, lineEnd - 1) + 1` start, the `if (lineStart < emitStart) break` safety, the `c.toString("utf8", lineStart, lineEnd)` decode, the `if (!raw.trim()) { lineEnd = lineStart - 1; continue; }` blank skip, `state.lines.push(raw)`, and `if (advanceTailScan(raw, state, includePrompts, limit)) break;` then `lineEnd = lineStart - 1`. Owns the per-chunk line walk.
- `function advanceTailScan(raw: string, state: TailScanState, includePrompts: boolean, limit: number): boolean` — today's per-line state transition: `if (state.armed) return walkArmed(raw);`, then `if (isEntryCandidate(raw, includePrompts)) { state.candidates += 1; return false; }`, then `if (raw.includes('"agent_start"') && state.candidates >= limit) { state.armed = true; state.boundaryIndex = state.lines.length - 1; }`, then `return false`. The current nested `walkArmed` moves inside this function unchanged as a closure over `state`, still reading `state.lines`/`state.boundaryIndex` and setting `state.armed`/`state.stoppedAtBoundary`. Owns the arming state walk; returns true when the walk must stop.
- `function scanTailFromEof(fd: number, size: number, limit: number, includePrompts: boolean): TailScanState` — today's `for (;;)` chunk loop verbatim: the `Math.min(TAIL_SCAN_CHUNK, state.pos)`/`len <= 0` guard, `Buffer.alloc`, `fs.readSync`, the `got <= 0` break, the `state.held.length > 0 ? Buffer.concat([buf.subarray(0, got), state.held]) : buf.subarray(0, got)` ternary, `const emitStart = prepareTailChunk(fd, c, got, state);` with `if (emitStart === null) { state.held = Buffer.from(c); state.pos -= got; continue; }`, `walkTailChunkLines(state, c, emitStart, includePrompts, limit)`, `state.pos -= got;`, and `if (state.stoppedAtBoundary || state.pos <= 0) break;`. Initializes and returns the `TailScanState`. Owns the chunk scan loop.
- `function finalizeTailWindow(file: string, state: TailScanState, limit: number, opts: { includePrompts?: boolean }): TranscriptWindow` — today's post-loop `if (state.armed) { state.lines.splice(state.boundaryIndex + 1); state.stoppedAtBoundary = true; }`, `let entries = formatTranscript(state.lines.reverse(), opts);`, the `entries.length < limit && state.stoppedAtBoundary` whole-file fallback `formatTranscript(readCompleteLines(file, 0, state.size).lines, opts)`, and the `limit > 0 ? entries.slice(-limit) : []` guard with its `-0` comment; returns `{ entries: kept, end: state.end }`. Owns the final window.
- `readTranscriptTail` keeps its signature, its `Promise`-free `TranscriptWindow | null` return and its doc comment. Its body becomes `const opened = openTailFile(file); if (opened === null) return null; try { const state = scanTailFromEof(opened.fd, opened.size, limit, opts.includePrompts === true); return finalizeTailWindow(file, state, limit, opts); } finally { fs.closeSync(opened.fd); }` — so the fd is closed on the same path as today and the final window runs against the same `state`.
- Add a one-line doc comment to each new top-level helper naming the single job it owns; keep `isEntryCandidate`, `markerHasLabel`, `MARKER_ONLY`, `TAIL_SCAN_CHUNK` and `EMPTY_BUFFER` exactly as they are.

**Goal.** `cmdRevert` (src/operator/operator-commands.ts, exported) is one complexity-29 body doing four jobs: it scans `args` for the three flags and refuses a flag-shaped token or a wrong positional count; it resolves the target sha, its run line and its run ref (a sha, or `revertRunSha` for `<role> <n>`/`--last`); it renders the `--dry-run` preview (`would revert …`, the path list, `applies cleanly`/`would conflict`/the dirty-checkout line, the exit code); and it renders the committed revert (`main is now …`, the role follow-up) — each mode also having a `--json` arm. A reader asking "where is a lone `--json` refused?", "how does `<role> <n>` become a sha?" or "which line sets the dry-run exit code?" has to read the whole function. Extract one named helper per job and leave `cmdRevert` as the composition: parse, resolve, preview-or-commit, hand to the matching renderer. This continues the landed split-family (`cmdStart`, `parsePromptArgs`, `createHistoryPane`, `paneBody`, `archiveFinishedText`) into the operator command. No behavior change: the exported signature, `REVERT_USAGE`, every message, the exit codes and both `--json` payloads are untouched.

- Add two module-local type aliases beside `REVERT_USAGE`, so the renderers can name the narrowed results without exporting the private interfaces: `type RevertPreviewOk = Extract<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof previewRevert>>, { ok: true }>;` and `type RevertResultOk = Extract<Awaited<ReturnType<typeof revertMergedCommit>>, { ok: true }>;`.
- `function parseRevertArgs(args: string[]): { dryRun: boolean; last: boolean; json: boolean; rest: string[] }` — today's `const dryRun` through the `revert needs a commit or a run` refusal, verbatim: the three `args.includes`, the `args.filter`, the flag-shaped `rest.find` + its refusal, and the `last ? … : …` shape check; returns the four values.
- `function revertTarget(root: string, rest: string[], last: boolean): { sha: string; runLine: string | null; runRef: { role: string; run: number } | null }` — today's `const run = last || rest.length === 2 ? revertRunSha(root, rest, last) : null` through `const runRef = …`, verbatim; `revertRunSha` and the `sha` truthiness rule stay as written.
- `function sayRevertPreview(p: RevertPreviewOk, runLine: string | null, json: boolean): void` — today's dry-run block from `if (json)` through the trailing `if (!p.applies || p.dirty) process.exitCode = 1;`, verbatim; the `if (!p.ok) fail(p.error);` guard stays in `cmdRevert`, so `p` is already narrowed when passed.
- `function sayRevertOutcome(result: RevertResultOk, runLine: string | null, json: boolean): void` — today's non-dry-run block from `if (json)` through `if (followUp !== null) say(followUp);`, verbatim; the `if (!result.ok) fail(result.error);` guard stays in `cmdRevert`.
- `cmdRevert` keeps its export, its `(root: string, args: string[])` signature and its doc comment. Its body becomes: `const { dryRun, last, json, rest } = parseRevertArgs(args);`; `const { sha, runLine, runRef } = revertTarget(root, rest, last);`; then `if (dryRun) { const p = await previewRevert(root, sha); if (!p.ok) fail(p.error); sayRevertPreview(p, runLine, json); return; }`; then `const result = await revertMergedCommit(root, sha); if (!result.ok) fail(result.error); sayRevertOutcome(result, runLine, json);`.
- Add a one-line doc comment to each new helper naming the job it owns (the flag scan and its two refusals; the sha/run/run-ref resolution; the preview text and exit code; the committed-revert text and follow-up).

Split each key into one named arm beside the existing `applySearch`/`recompute` helpers and leave `handleKey` as the flat ordered dispatch. ### `createTranscriptPane`'s ~145-line `handleKey` is split into one named arm per key, so the `Ctrl+N` transcript→notes→change cycle with its view-and-editor-flag guard, the change step's `Ctrl+Y` diffstat toggle, the notes `Ctrl+X` clear, and the notes/change `PgUp`/`PgDn` page are found by name (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; independent in files of every pickable `## Planned` entry — the only `## Planned` entry naming src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts is the Refused TUI Transcript plan, which no feature run takes while its `Refused 2026-10-24` note stands; the blocked `Subtract` parts edit src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts, tui-editor-provider-caps.ts, tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-frame.ts, tui-pane-ctx.ts, tui-pane-backlog.ts, tui-pane-session.ts, tui-pane-health.ts, tui-editor-claude-reserve.ts and tui-editor-model.ts; the in-flight splits take tui-editor-quiet.ts, tui-editor-budget.ts, tui-editor-role-enabled.ts, tui-editor-queued.ts, tui-editor-answer.ts, tui-editor-attach.ts, tui-editor-prompt.ts, tui-editor-backends.ts, tui-editor-brief.ts, tui-editor-search.ts, tui-editor-retire.ts, tui-editor-role-file.ts, tui-editor-release.ts and tui-editor-role-key.ts; the in-flight part 3x/3 takes test/merger.test.ts; the held-for-operator parts 3v/3 and 3w/3 take test/orchestrator-3.e2e.test.ts, test/orchestrator-mixed.e2e.test.ts and test/orchestrator-director.test.ts — none src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts); PLANS-DONE.md's `createTranscriptPane` matches are the landed Ctrl+Y diffstat, `/`-search, queue-header and notes-file behavior additions, never a split of its `handleKey`; docs/invariants.md names no symbol of it (`grep -c 'tui-pane-transcript' docs/invariants.md` prints 0); touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `createTranscriptPane` (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts) serves the per-role transcript views (1..roleIds.length). Its `handleKey` is one ~145-line body holding a nested `loadChange(role)` helper and four inline arms: the `key.ctrl && key.name === "n"` transcript→notes→change cycle with its explicit editor-flag guard, its three-way mode transition and its `roleInspectMarkdown` try/catch; the `key.ctrl && key.name === "y" && changeMode &&` view-range `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` diffstat toggle that calls `loadChange`; the `key.ctrl && key.name === "x" && noteMode &&` view-range `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` two-step notes clear through `saveRoleNote`; and the `pageDir(key.name)` arm guarded by `noteMode || changeMode`. So "which keys does the pane consume?", "what keeps a key falling through to History?" and "where is the collector's generator guard?" are found only by scanning the whole body. Split each key into one named arm and move `loadChange` out of the handler to the factory closure, leaving `handleKey` as the flat ordered dispatch. This mirrors the landed `createHistoryPane` split (whose `handleKey` is ten named arms) and the `createPauseEditor`/`createEntryEditor`/`createTuiPanes` splits. No behavior change.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. No import is added or removed.
- Move `loadChange` (declared today at the top of `handleKey`, before its arms) to a module-private closure beside `viewedRole`, as `const loadChange = (role: string): void => { ... }`, its body and both comments unchanged. It reads only closure state (`changeCache`, `changeStat`, `changeGen`, `session`, `viewedRole`) and the file's existing imports, so nothing else moves with it.
- Declare `transcriptCycle(ctx: TuiPaneCtx): boolean` holding the whole `Ctrl+N` arm: the `ctx.es.budgetMode || … || ctx.es.instructionsEditFor || session.roleIds.length === 0 || session.view < 1 || session.view > session.roleIds.length` guard with its fall-back `session.requestRender(); return true;`, then the `changeMode` branch, the `noteMode` branch (`loadChange(role)`), and the else branch (`roleInspectMarkdown` try/catch), and the trailing `session.paneScroll = 0; session.requestRender(); return true;`. It returns `true` on every path, because `routeCtrlN` in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts routes it last and relies on this pane consuming `Ctrl+N` as the fallback (its comment spells this out).
- Declare `transcriptStatToggle(ctx: TuiPaneCtx): boolean` holding the `Ctrl+Y` arm: the `changeMode && promptLineFree(ctx.es) && ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` guard returns `false` on a miss (so `routeCtrlY` still reaches History's Summary cycle), then the `changeStat` flip, `session.paneScroll = 0`, `loadChange(role)`, `session.requestRender()` and `return true`.
- Declare `transcriptNotesClear(ctx: TuiPaneCtx): boolean` holding the `Ctrl+X` arm: the `noteMode && promptLineFree(ctx.es)` view-range guard returns `false` on a miss (so `routeCtrlX` still reaches History/Queued/Pending/Backlog), then the `session.armedNotes === role` clear through `saveRoleNote` and `roleInspectMarkdown` or the `session.notesClearArmed = role` arm, `session.requestRender()` and `return true`.
- Declare `transcriptPage(page: "up" | "down"): boolean` holding the `pageDir` arm: `if (!(noteMode || changeMode)) return false;`, then `session.paneScroll = pageMarkdownBody(session.paneScroll, noteMode ? noteCache : changeCache, session.eventBudget, page); session.requestRender(); return true;`.
- `handleKey` keeps its `(key, ctx)` signature and doc comment; its body becomes the flat dispatch in today's order: `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "n") return transcriptCycle(ctx);`, `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "y") return transcriptStatToggle(ctx);`, `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "x") return transcriptNotesClear(ctx);`, `const page = pageDir(key.name);`, `if (page !== null) return transcriptPage(page);`, `return false;`.
- The `return { handleKey, refreshNotes, reset, applySearch, state } satisfies TuiPaneModule & { applySearch(pattern: string | null): void }` object, `viewedRole`, the mode/cache/generator variables and the exported `createTranscriptPane` are unchanged.
- `handleKey`'s body holds no `session.paneScroll =`, `session.requestRender(`, `session.flashMessage(`, `session.flashError(`, `session.armedNotes`, `roleInspectMarkdown(`, `saveRoleNote(`, `pageMarkdownBody(`, `loadChange(`, `changeMode =`, `noteMode =`, `changeStat =`, `changeGen`, `noteCache` or `changeCache` occurrence — only the dispatch guards (which may read `key`) and the calls to its four arms (`transcriptCycle`, `transcriptStatToggle`, `transcriptNotesClear`, `transcriptPage`); each of those four is declared exactly once, module-private inside `createTranscriptPane`, and `loadChange` is declared once at that same closure level, outside `handleKey`.
- No edit lands outside src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts; docs/invariants.md is unchanged (`grep -c 'tui-pane-transcript' docs/invariants.md` prints 0).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The four arms and `loadChange` exist by name: `grep -n 'transcriptCycle\|transcriptStatToggle\|transcriptNotesClear\|transcriptPage\|loadChange' src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts` shows one declaration and the expected calls, with `loadChange`'s declaration above `handleKey`.
- `handleKey`'s body is only the flat dispatch (the four `return <arm>()` lines and `return false;` per the bullet above); the `Ctrl+N` editor-flag guard, every view-range test, `promptLineFree`, `roleInspectMarkdown`, `saveRoleNote`, `pageMarkdownBody` and every mode/cache write live inside the arms.
- Fall-through is preserved: `transcriptCycle` returns `true` on every path, while `transcriptStatToggle`, `transcriptNotesClear` and `transcriptPage` return `false` on a guard miss, so `routeCtrlY`, `routeCtrlX` and `routePage` in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts fall through to History, the report panes and the backlog exactly as today.
- Behavior is byte-for-byte the same: the notes→change→transcript cycle and its queued-merge header, the diffstat toggle and its reset on leaving the change step, the two-step `Ctrl+X` clear with its disarm on any other key, the `Ctrl+Y`/`Ctrl+X` fall-through off their steps, and the `PgUp`/`PgDn` clamp at both ends all remain; `createTranscriptPane`'s exported surface, its returned module object and the file's imports are unchanged.

**Tests.** No new test module: a behavior-preserving move guarded by `test/tui-notes.test.ts` ("Ctrl+N shows the viewed role's notes and next run prompt, and toggles back", "PgUp/PgDn page the notes body and clamp at both ends", "Ctrl+X twice in the notes view clears the role's notes; the first press only arms", "another key between the two Ctrl+X presses disarms the notes clear", and "Ctrl+X on the live transcript leaves the notes alone"), `test/tui-keys.test.ts` ("Ctrl+Y on the Transcript change step toggles the diffstat, and a cycle away starts on the full patch", "Ctrl+Y off the change step falls through to History: inert on the live transcript, cycling the Summary there", "Ctrl+N's change step heads the change with the viewed role's queued merges", and "the `/` search filters the viewed role's live transcript, stays off the notes step, and clears on Ctrl+T"), and `test/tui-frame.test.ts` (the transcript hint lines and "Ctrl+Y full patch"). **Goal.** `createRoleKeyEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-key.ts) is the shared role-pinned `Ctrl`-key editor factory on the shared prompt line: one factory serves the role-model editor (`Ctrl+X`, `spec.mode` `"roleModel"`, `yieldsOn` the notes view where `Ctrl+X` clears notes), the parallel-runner count editor (`Ctrl+G`, `"instances"`) and the min-run-interval editor (`Ctrl+S`, `"interval"`). Its exit helper is already named (`exit`), but its `handleKey` is one ~52-line body of three arms: the `key.ctrl && key.name === spec.openCtrl` arm, which when `mode` toggles out through `exit()` and otherwise returns `false` unless the view is a role Transcript (`ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length`) and `spec.yieldsOn?.(ctx)` misses, runs the `session.editorEntryDenied(spec.mode)` guard, pins `lockedRole = viewedRole(ctx)`, pre-fills through `spec.prefill(session, baseRoleOf(role))`, settles the draft with `restoreDraft = session.takeDraft()`, sets `mode`/`session.held[spec.mode]`/`session.input`/`session.cursor`, and flashes `spec.openFlash(role)`; the `Esc` arm, which calls `exit()`; and the `Enter` arm, which trims `session.input`, commits through `spec.commit(session, baseRoleOf(role), text)` for the pinned `lockedRole`, and on success calls `exit()` and flashes `spec.noopFlash`/`spec.savedFlash` or on refusal flashes `result.error` and stays open. So "which views may open it?", "where is the entry-denied guard?" and "what keeps it open on a rejected value?" are found only by scanning the whole body. Split each key into one named arm beside `exit` and leave `handleKey` as the flat ordered dispatch. This mirrors the in-flight `createQuietEditor`/`createBudgetEditor`/`createRoleEnabledEditor`/`createQueuedEditor`/`createAnswerEditor`/`createAttachEditor`/`createPromptEditor`/`createBackendsEditor`/`createBriefEditor`/`createSearchEditor`/`createRetireEditor`/`createRoleFileEditor`/`createQuarantineReleaseEditor` splits and the landed `createPauseEditor`/`createEntryEditor`/`createHistoryPane`/`createTuiPanes` splits. No behavior change.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-key.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. No import is added or removed.
- Declare a module-private closure `openRoleKeyEdit(ctx: TuiEditorCtx): boolean` inside `createRoleKeyEditor`, below `exit`, holding the whole open/toggle arm body: the `if (mode) { exit(); return true; }` toggle-out, the `if (!(ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length) || spec.yieldsOn?.(ctx)) return false;` view-and-yield guard (so the key falls through to the pane arms elsewhere), the `const role = viewedRole(ctx);` and its pin comment, the `if (session.editorEntryDenied(spec.mode)) return true;` line, the `lockedRole = role;` pin, the `const existing = spec.prefill(session, baseRoleOf(role));` and its one-fresh-read comment, `restoreDraft = session.takeDraft();`, `mode = true;`, `session.held[spec.mode] = true;`, `session.input = existing;`, `session.cursor = session.input.length;`, and the `session.flashMessage(spec.openFlash(role));` flash; it returns `true`.
- Declare `cancelRoleKeyEdit(): boolean` for the `Esc` arm: `exit(); return true;`.
- Declare `submitRoleKeyEdit(): boolean` for the whole `Enter` arm: `const role = lockedRole!;`, `const text = session.input.trim();`, `const result = spec.commit(session, baseRoleOf(role), text);`, the `result.ok` success branch (`exit();` then `session.flashMessage(result.noop && spec.noopFlash ? spec.noopFlash(role, text) : spec.savedFlash(role, text));`) and the `else` `session.flashMessage(result.error);` stay-open branch; it returns `true`.
- `handleKey` keeps its `(_str, key, ctx)` signature and its doc comment; its body becomes the flat dispatch in today's order, with the key test on the dispatch line and every view/state guard inside the arm so a guard miss still falls through: `if (key.ctrl && key.name === spec.openCtrl) return openRoleKeyEdit(ctx);`, `if (key.name === "escape" && mode) return cancelRoleKeyEdit();`, `if (key.name === "return" && mode) return submitRoleKeyEdit();`, `return false;`.
- Keep `mode`, `lockedRole`, `restoreDraft` and `exit` as they are; `restoreDraft` is assigned only in `openRoleKeyEdit` and read only in `exit`; `lockedRole` is assigned in `openRoleKeyEdit`, cleared in `exit`, and read only in `submitRoleKeyEdit`.
- `handleKey`'s body holds no `session.input =`, `session.cursor =`, `session.flashMessage(`, `session.takeDraft(`, `session.held[`, `session.editorEntryDenied(`, `spec.prefill(`, `spec.commit(`, `spec.openFlash(`, `spec.savedFlash(`, `spec.noopFlash(`, `baseRoleOf(`, `viewedRole(`, `spec.yieldsOn`, `lockedRole =`, `mode =` or `exit()` occurrence — only the two `mode` dispatch guards and the calls to its three arms (`openRoleKeyEdit`, `cancelRoleKeyEdit`, `submitRoleKeyEdit`); each of those three is declared exactly once, module-private inside `createRoleKeyEditor`.
- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-key.ts` matches `createRoleKeyEditor` only, and no import line changes (the `baseRoleOf`, `viewedRole`, `TuiEditorCtx`/`TuiEditorModule` and `TuiEditorSession` imports stay); the factory's three callers (`createRoleModelEditor` in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts, `createInstancesEditor` in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-instances.ts, `createIntervalEditor` in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-interval.ts) are untouched.
- No edit lands outside src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-key.ts; docs/invariants.md is unchanged (`grep -c 'tui-editor-role-key' docs/invariants.md` prints 0).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The three arms exist by name as module-private closures beside `exit`: `openRoleKeyEdit`, `cancelRoleKeyEdit`, `submitRoleKeyEdit`; `grep -n 'openRoleKeyEdit\|cancelRoleKeyEdit\|submitRoleKeyEdit' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-key.ts` shows one declaration and one call each.
- `handleKey`'s body is only the flat dispatch (three `return <arm>()` lines plus `return false;` per the bullet above); the role-Transcript view test, the `spec.yieldsOn?.(ctx)` yield, the `editorEntryDenied` guard, the draft settle, the pin and every write/flash live inside the arms, so a guard miss still returns `false` and falls through.

**Goal.** `createQuarantineReleaseEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-release.ts) is the Failures view's `Ctrl+X` release editor on the shared prompt line, the terminal twin of `tumwater quarantine --release <n>` and the dashboard Failures card's Release button. **Goal.** `createSearchEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts) is the shared `/` search editor on the prompt line, over the Activity feed, the History run rows (or a trail's transcript), the Backlog entries, the Inbox queued prompts, and a role's live transcript. Its exit helper is already named (`exitHistorySearch`), but its `handleKey` is one ~59-line body of three arms: the `/` arm, guarded by `!key.ctrl && str === "/" && !searchMode && !session.anyEditorHeld()` plus the view tests (view 0, a role view outside note/change mode, or one of the Backlog/History/Inbox panes) and an empty `session.input`, which saves the draft, picks `searchFor`, sets `searchMode`/`session.held.search`, and pre-fills `session.input`/`session.cursor` with the applied pattern for that target while flashing `search <noun>: Enter to filter, Esc to cancel`; the `Esc` arm; and the `Enter` arm, which trims the line, dispatches to the matching `apply…Search`, exits, and flashes `search: "…"` or `search cleared`. So "which views open `/`?", "which pane does Enter filter?" and "what pre-fills the line?" are found only by scanning the whole body. Split each key into one named arm beside `exitHistorySearch` and leave `handleKey` as the flat ordered dispatch. **Approach.**

- Declare three module-private closures inside `createSearchEditor`, below `exitHistorySearch`: `openSearchEdit(ctx)` for the `/` arm, `cancelSearchEdit()` for `Esc`, and `submitSearchEdit()` for `Enter`. Each owns its guards and its side effects as they stand today, in the same order, with the same wording and the same `searchFor` branch order (Activity view 0, Backlog `roleIds.length + 1`, History `roleIds.length + 4`, Inbox `roleIds.length + 6`, else Transcript). `cancelSearchEdit` calls the existing `exitHistorySearch` and keeps the target-selection logic out of it.

The `!searchMode` and `!session.anyEditorHeld()` guards move into `openSearchEdit`, so the dispatch line still reads `str === "/"` (the doc scanner reads only `Ctrl+[A-Z]`, and `/` has no Ctrl key).
- The pre-fill `applied` and `noun` maps and the `session.input`/`session.cursor` writes move into `openSearchEdit` unchanged; the five-way `apply…Search` dispatch and the two flashes move into `submitSearchEdit` unchanged.

**Goal.** The lower-file twin of the three finer parts 3p/3, 3z/3 and 4a/3: part 3h/3 stops `reviewAttempt` from running the model reviewer, which makes the `test/merger.test.ts` cases below `a merge pinned behind main's advance is rebased onto main BEFORE the gate and merges both` fail where they reach a merge through a `reviewerPi` approval, a per-role reviewer run or a `review_start` count rather than through the deterministic gate.
