**Approach.** In `test/merger.test.ts`, retire or re-point the pre-merge reviewer cases at or below `a merge pinned behind main's advance is rebased onto main BEFORE the gate and merges both`: `a merge pinned behind main's advance is rebased onto main BEFORE the gate and merges both`, `a synced rebase moves the merge ref so a failed gate keeps the tree that can merge`, `the merge checkout is shared, kept detached, and persists at a terminal outcome`, `a failing pre-check on a green main rejects the merge and spends no pi run`, `a fix-claim-blocked merge retries once, then rejects with the block reason`, `a failing pre-check on a red main keeps the pin, records no rejection, and spends no pi run`, `an all-rejected batch returns a defined result for every request without throwing`, `an abort after the last gate approved stops the batch before its shared check`, `a merge reports each change as it reaches it: the stack merges together, and a rejected change never reaches it`, and `the gate re-pins the merge ref to the head its verdict judged`. Prefer re-pointing over deletion: these cases' real subject is the rebase, check or batch/stack bookkeeping, so drive the same outcome through a deterministic gate rejection (a conflict-marker diff, a leaked credential or a failing declared check), or, where a case only asserts that no reviewer ran, keep that assertion without a `reviewerPi` approval behind it. Leave the blocks above `a merge pinned behind main's advance…` untouched — parts 3p/3, 3z/3 and 4a/3 own those — and edit neither fixture file (part 3e/3 deletes the reviewer-run helpers).

### `tumwater history <role> <n>` names how long the change took to land after the run ended — the per-change landing latency the day report shows only as a team median (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/run/run-detail' PLANS.md` matches only this entry and `grep -n 'mergeAfterRunMs' PLANS-DONE.md` prints nothing: the three eligible in-flight plans edit test/merger.test.ts, src/backlog and src/doctor+src/agent+src/inbox+src/roles+src/status+src/ui, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` and `Subtract` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/roles, src/gui, src/ui, src/prompt, src/request-timeouts.ts, src/concurrency, src/agent, src/budget and src/git — none src/run or src/history; the landed `run-detail` entries in PLANS-DONE.md are the `cmdRunDetail` split and the `--last`/`--grep` features, not this header line; touches src/run/run-detail-data.ts src/run/run-detail-render.ts docs/cli.md test/run-detail.test.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The `tumwater history <role> <n>` trail header (and `history <role> --last`, the same body) already names the run's own span (`shortSpanPhrase(durationMs)`), its pinned `commit <sha>` and, when the merge rebased, `merged as <sha2>`; it never says how long the pipeline between the run's end and that landing took. A run that ended hours before its commit reached main (a red main, a slow gate) looks exactly like one that landed in a minute. Add `merged <span> after the run` to the header when the run has both a `run_end` and a `merged` landing, so the operator reads one change's end-of-run → on-main latency without diffing timestamps in the trail. The day report's `Merge wait median` stays the team view; this is the per-change twin the report cannot show.

**Approach.**
- `src/run/run-detail-data.ts`: `RunDetail` gains `mergeAfterRunMs?: number`. The `merged` event is already what `mergedShaOf` finds (`newestMergedCommit(block, -Infinity, Infinity)` for a direct merge, `newestMergedCommit(scoped, merge.ts - merge.durationMs, merge.ts)` for a queued run resolved through `resolveQueuedResult`), so extract one module-private `newestMergedEvent(pool, from, to): HarnessEvent | null` returning that event and make `mergedShaOf` read its `commit` (keeping its existing signature, return type and null cases) rather than walking twice. In `detailFrom`, set `mergeAfterRunMs = merged.ts - end.ts` on the panel only when `end !== null`, the finder returns an event, and the difference is `>= 0`; spread it so the field stays absent otherwise.
- `src/run/run-detail-render.ts`: after the `merged as <sha>` cell, append ` · merged ${shortSpanPhrase(d.mergeAfterRunMs)} after the run` when the field is present. `shortSpanPhrase` is already imported for the duration cell; a run without the field keeps today's header byte-identical. Do not add the cell to the History listing table (its columns and their tests are unchanged).
- `docs/cli.md` (the `history <role> <n>` description in the Audit-adjacent table row that already documents `merged as <sha>`, `reverted <sha> (by operator)`, `cut off at the context ceiling` and the prompt/peak cells): add the `merged <span> after the run` cell beside `merged as`.
- `test/run-detail.test.ts`: add cases below.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A run whose change merged shows `merged <span> after the run`, where the span is the landing `merged` event's ts minus the run's `run_end` ts, for both a direct merge and a queued run resolved through `resolveQueuedResult`; the rendered span uses `shortSpanPhrase` like the duration cell.
- A rejected or failed merge, an in-flight run, a run whose `merged`/`merge_done` event rotated out of the scan, and a no-op fast-forward that logs no `merged` event render no `merged` cell — the header is byte-identical to today for each.
- `--json` carries `mergeAfterRunMs` only when present; `mergedSha`, `merge` and every existing `RunDetail` field are unchanged.
- `grep -n 'mergeAfterRunMs' src/` names `src/run/run-detail-data.ts` and `src/run/run-detail-render.ts` only; no History listing column or its test changes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `createPauseEditor`'s ~220-line `handleKey` is split into one named arm per key and one named writer per `Enter` intent, so a `Ctrl+Q` stop, a `Ctrl+R` restart or a per-role pause/wake write is found by name (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible and blocked part — `grep -n 'tui-editor-pause' PLANS.md` matches no `## Planned` entry: the blocked `Subtract` parts edit src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-pane-session.ts, tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui-frame.ts, tui-pane-ctx.ts, tui-editor-claude-reserve.ts and tui-editor-model.ts, and the in-flight plans edit test/merger.test.ts, src/backlog and src/run — none src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts; the refused TUI Transcript provider/thinking plan edits tui-editor-role-key.ts, tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-frame.ts, tui.tsx, tui-pane-ctx.ts, tui-pane-transcript.ts and two new tui-editor-role-*.ts — not this file; PLANS-DONE.md records only landed behavior additions to it (the `durationLabel` import for the Usage/Failures window line, the `anyEditorHeld` guard replacement and the `Ctrl+R` restart arm's view guard) and no split of `createPauseEditor`; docs/invariants.md names no symbol of it (`grep -c 'tui-editor-pause' docs/invariants.md` prints 0); touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `createPauseEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts) is the prompt-line editor for the team pause/stop/wake controls and the per-role controls, reached from the Activity and Transcript views. Its two mode helpers are already named (`exitPauseEditMode`, `openPauseEditor`), but its `handleKey` is one ~220-line body of seven quite different arms: the `Ctrl+F` team-pause toggle, the `Ctrl+Q` scheduled-stop toggle, the `Ctrl+R` Activity restart, the second-press close of a per-role pause/wake editor, the `Ctrl+P`/`A`/`W`/`V` per-role block, `Esc`, and the `Enter` writer — which itself has four parse-and-commit paths (scheduled stop, wake, role pause, team pause) hanging off one parse head. So "what writes a scheduled stop?", "where does an invalid wake entry keep the editor open?" and "which arm runs while the budget editor holds the line?" are found only by scanning the whole body. Split each arm into one named closure beside `openPauseEditor`, and split the `Enter` body's four commit paths into one named writer each, leaving `handleKey` as the ordered dispatch. This mirrors the landed `createHistoryPane` split (one named arm per key) and `createTuiPanes`'s key router. No behavior change.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. No import is added or removed.
- `teamPauseToggle(ctx: TuiEditorCtx): boolean` — the `Ctrl+F` arm body: the inner `pauseEditMode` → `exitPauseEditMode()` branch, then the `isTeamPaused` toggle (`resumeTeam`/`teamResumePhrase` vs `openPauseEditor(null, false, false, …)`) in its try/catch.
- `stopLaterToggle(ctx: TuiEditorCtx): boolean` — the `Ctrl+Q` arm body: the inner close-if-open branch, then `scheduledStopAt` → `cancelScheduledStopMessage` vs `openPauseEditor(null, false, true, …)`.
- `restartNow(ctx: TuiEditorCtx): boolean` — the `Ctrl+R` Activity arm body: `requestRestart(session.root)` and its ok/error flash in its try/catch.
- `closeRolePauseEdit(): boolean` — a second `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W` while `pauseEditRole !== null`: `exitPauseEditMode(); return true;`.
- `roleControlArm(name: "p" | "a" | "w" | "v", ctx: TuiEditorCtx): boolean` — the per-role block: `viewedRole(ctx)` and its four branches (paused → `resumeRole` flash, unpaused → `openPauseEditor(role, false, false, …)`, the `held.rolePromptFor`/`held.search` busy flashes, `requestAbort`, `requestResetCounters`, `openPauseEditor(role, true, false, …)`), in its try/catch.
- `cancelPauseEdit(): boolean` — the `Esc` arm: `exitPauseEditMode(); return true;`.
- `commitPauseEntry(): boolean` — the `Enter` arm head: the `target = pauseEditRole` read, `const stopParsed = pauseEditStop ? parseStopInInput(session.input) : null;`, `const wakeParsed = pauseEditWake && target !== null ? parseRoleWakeInput(session.input) : null;`, `const parsed = target !== null ? parseRolePauseInput(session.input) : parsePauseInput(session.input);`; then `if (stopParsed) { applyStopEntry(stopParsed); return true; }`, `if (wakeParsed) { applyWakeEntry(wakeParsed, target!); return true; }`, `if (!parsed.ok) { session.flashMessage(parsed.error); return true; }`, `if (target !== null) { applyRolePauseEntry(parsed, target); return true; }`, `applyTeamPauseEntry(parsed); return true;`.
- `applyStopEntry(stopParsed: ReturnType<typeof parseStopInInput>): void` — the `!stopParsed.ok` flash and the `requestScheduledStop` try/catch.
- `applyWakeEntry(wakeParsed: ReturnType<typeof parseRoleWakeInput>, target: string): void` — the `!wakeParsed.ok` flash and the `cancelWakes`/`requestWake` try/catch.
- `applyRolePauseEntry(parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseRolePauseInput>, { ok: true }>, target: string): void` — the `at`/`until`/`pauseRole` write and the `rolePauseMessage` flash, in its try/catch.
- `applyTeamPauseEntry(parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parsePauseInput>, { ok: true }>): void` — the `until`/`pauseTeam` write, the `forSuffix` and the `teamPausePhrase` flash, in its try/catch.
- `handleKey` keeps its `(_str, key, ctx)` signature and its doc comment; its body becomes the flat dispatch in today's order, with every guard staying on its dispatch line so a guard miss still falls through: `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "f" && !session.anyEditorHeld("pause")) return teamPauseToggle(ctx);`, the same for `"q"`, `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "r" && ctx.view === 0 && !pauseEditMode && !session.anyEditorHeld("pause")) return restartNow(ctx);`, `if (key.ctrl && (key.name === "p" || key.name === "w") && pauseEditRole !== null) return closeRolePauseEdit();`, the per-role line `if (!session.anyEditorHeld("rolePromptFor", "search") && ctx.roleIds.length > 0 && ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length && key.ctrl && (key.name === "p" || key.name === "a" || key.name === "w" || key.name === "v")) return roleControlArm(key.name, ctx);`, `if (key.name === "escape" && pauseEditMode) return cancelPauseEdit();`, `if (key.name === "return" && pauseEditMode) return commitPauseEntry();`, `return false;`.

**Files touched.** src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Output and marker outcomes are byte-identical for the same keys, drafts and inputs: `test/tui-operator-keys.test.ts` passes unchanged, including "Ctrl+P toggles the viewed role's pause marker and flashes the CLI's wording", "Ctrl+P, a duration, Enter pauses the viewed role for that long", "Esc cancels the role pause editor and restores the draft; an invalid entry stays in it", "Ctrl+W opens the wake editor; Enter on an empty line wakes the viewed role now", "Ctrl+W then a duration schedules the viewed role's wake", "Ctrl+W then 'cancel' drops the viewed role's scheduled wakes", "Ctrl+W with an invalid entry flashes and stays in the editor; Esc restores the draft", "Ctrl+F toggles the team pause marker through pauseTeam/resumeTeam and flashes the shared wording", "Ctrl+F then '1h maintenance' pauses with a deadline and reason shown in the team alert", "Ctrl+Q opens the stop editor, schedules a stop on Enter, and cancels a pending one at once", "Ctrl+R on the Activity view requests the pending self-redeploy when the build is stale" and "Ctrl+R on a fresh build refuses and writes no restart marker"; the TUI cases in test/tui-keys.test.ts that route these keys ("Ctrl+P opens the provider-caps editor on Activity and the pause editor on a role's Transcript" and its neighbours) pass unchanged.
- `handleKey`'s body holds no `try {`, `session.flashMessage(`, `session.flashError(`, `openPauseEditor(`, `parseStopInInput(`, `parseRoleWakeInput(`, `parseRolePauseInput(`, `parsePauseInput(`, `requestRestart(`, `pauseTeam(`, `pauseRole(`, `requestAbort(`, `requestResetCounters(` or `requestWake(` call — only the dispatch guards and the calls to the eleven named closures; each of `teamPauseToggle`, `stopLaterToggle`, `restartNow`, `closeRolePauseEdit`, `roleControlArm`, `cancelPauseEdit`, `commitPauseEntry`, `applyStopEntry`, `applyWakeEntry`, `applyRolePauseEntry` and `applyTeamPauseEntry` is declared exactly once, module-private inside `createPauseEditor`.
- The exported surface is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts` matches `createPauseEditor` only, and no import line changes.
- docs/invariants.md is unchanged (`grep -c 'tui-editor-pause' docs/invariants.md` prints 0), and no edit lands outside src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.** No new test module: a behavior-preserving move guarded by the existing `test/tui-operator-keys.test.ts` suite plus the TUI key cases that route `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+R` here. Run test/tui-operator-keys.test.ts and test/tui-keys.test.ts whole, then the project's gate, and confirm green.

**Goal.** `buildRoleRunPrompt` (src/run/run-prompt.ts, module-private, ~175 lines) does one long sequence of jobs in one body: it resolves the run's role through the catalog and `config.customRoles` and throws the shared unknown-role message; dequeues or peeks the per-role inbox request and strips its not-before marker; then renders five per-role observer evidence blocks that each degrade to no block on a read error — the selfcheck/feedback `selfcheckDigest`, the qa flow-coverage ledger, the ci parity block, the feedback filings ledger and the clean role's backlog-structure block; then reads the role's own notes plus their saved day and live backlog state; then builds the plan charter's stop-target note, the bugfix flake tally and the plan/feature no-check note; and finally calls `buildRunPrompt`. A reader asking "where is the qa coverage block read?", "which branch supplies `filings`?" or "where does the no-check declaration branch?" has only the one body to scan, and no stage has a name to grep. Extract each stage into a named module-private helper, so `buildRoleRunPrompt` becomes the ordered calls and the `buildRunPrompt` call. No behavior change: the assembled prompt, `userPrompt` and `userPromptFile` are identical for the same `(root, config, role, state, preview, backend)`.

(custom ? customRole(custom.name, custom.task) : undefined)` resolution and the `unknownRoleMessage` throw, returning `{ base, resolved }`.

**Goal.** `rolloutLines` (src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts, exported, ~117 lines) does two jobs in one body: it scans the rollout text's JSONL lines, tracking `task_started` blocks and collecting the read turn's `turn_context.model`, `token_usage_record` usage, `token_count` rate limits and `plan_type`; then it assembles the result's canonical `run_usage`, `billing` and up-to-two `rate_limit` lines, the `switchedTo` model comparison, and the empty reading. A reader asking "which event sets `lastRateLimits`?", "where is the cache-read subtraction?" or "where is `switchedTo` decided?" has only the one loop-and-assembly body to scan. Extract the scan and the assembly into two named module-private helpers, so each is found by name, and leave `rolloutLines` as the ordered calls. No behavior change: the emitted canonical lines, the `switchedTo` value and the empty reading are identical for the same `text`/`opts`.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates.
- Add a module-private `interface TurnRecords` (not exported) holding the scanner's state: `sawTurn: boolean`, `lastUsage: Json | undefined`, `lastRateLimits: Json | undefined`, `model: string | undefined`, `planType: string | undefined`.
- `scanTurnRecords(text: string, sinceTurnStart: string | undefined): TurnRecords` — the whole `for (const line of text.split("\n"))` loop and its local `currentTurn`, including the `task_started` restart, the `sinceTurnStart !== undefined && currentTurn !== sinceTurnStart` skip and the `turn_context`/`token_usage_record`/`token_count` switch; it returns the five fields as one object.
- `buildRolloutLines(records: TurnRecords, requestedModel: string): RolloutLines` — the `const lines: string[]`, the `run_usage` push with its `Math.max(0, input - cacheRead)` math, the `planType !== undefined` `billing` push, the two-window `primary`/`secondary` `rate_limit` loop, the `switchedTo` computation and `return { lines, ...(switchedTo !== undefined ? { switchedTo } : {}) }`.
- `rolloutLines` keeps its export, its `(text: string, opts: { sinceTurnStart?: string; requestedModel: string }): RolloutLines` signature and its doc comment; its body becomes the destructure, `const records = scanTurnRecords(text, sinceTurnStart);`, the presence check `if (!records.sawTurn || !isJsonObject(records.lastUsage)) return { lines: [] };` and `return buildRolloutLines(records, requestedModel);`. The presence check stays in `rolloutLines`, so `scanTurnRecords` never decides emptiness and `buildRolloutLines` never reads `sawTurn`.
- `findRollout`, its imports and every module-level helper (`str`, `finite`, `windowStatus`) stay unchanged; no import is added or removed.

**Goal.** `handleRefusal` (src/verdict/refusal.ts, exported; called from src/run/run-verdict.ts after the refusal-contradiction check) runs four jobs in one body: strip a newly added Refused note from any PLANS.md `## Planned` entry main still holds as blocked (`withoutBlockedPlanRefusals` + the atomic `writeTextAtomic`, with its drop warnings), pick the markdown notes to commit (`changedFiles` filtered to `.md`, PLANS.md dropped when the strip write failed), name the entries whose Refused note is new (`newlyRefusedTitles` per file/section), and land the notes (single-path commit, direct `ctx.merge`, the reset/no-commit branch, the thrown-merge guard, `state.lastError`, `clearSupersededRejection` and the `entry_refused` event). The rules have no names, so a reader asking "when is a refusal note dropped?", "which notes may merge?" or "what clears a superseded rejection?" scans the whole body. Extract each phase into a named module-private helper, leaving `handleRefusal` as strip → collect → name → land.

**Approach.** All edits in src/verdict/refusal.ts; move code verbatim and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. No import changes: every symbol the moved code reads (`withoutBlockedPlanRefusals`, `newlyRefusedTitles`, `fileContentAt`, `writeTextAtomic`, `changedFiles`, `commitPathsAndDiscardRest`, `resetWorktreeToMain`, `buildCommitMessage`, `commitTrailer`, `stampedSubject`, `baseRoleOf`, `errorMessage`, `clearSupersededRejection`, `logEventBestEffort`, `fs`, `path`) is already imported. Add these module-private declarations beside `handleRefusal` (below it, mirroring the file's order of public then private):

- `async function stripBlockedPlanRefusalNotes(ctx: RefusalContext, wt: string): Promise<boolean>` — the `plansFile` / `fs.existsSync` block: read main's PLANS.md through `fileContentAt(wt, ctx.mainBranch, "PLANS.md")` and the worktree's through `fs.readFileSync`, pass both to `withoutBlockedPlanRefusals`, and when `dropped.length > 0` `writeTextAtomic(plansFile, md)` and log one `warning` per dropped title; on a throw set the flag, log the "could not drop refusal note(s) …" warning and leave PLANS.md out of the commit. Returns whether the strip write failed (`plansUnstripped`).
- `async function collectRefusalNotes(wt: string, plansUnstripped: boolean): Promise<string[]>` — `(await changedFiles(wt)).filter((f) => f.toLowerCase().endsWith(".md") && !(plansUnstripped && f === "PLANS.md"))`.
- `async function collectRefusedEntryTitles(ctx: RefusalContext, wt: string, notes: string[]): Promise<string[]>` — the loop over `[{ file: "PLANS.md", section: "Planned" }, { file: "BUGS.md", section: "Open" }]`, skipping a file not in `notes` and calling `newlyRefusedTitles(await fileContentAt(wt, ctx.mainBranch, file), fs.readFileSync(path.join(wt, file), "utf8"), section)` inside the existing `try/catch` that swallows a read failure.
- `async function mergeRefusalNotes(ctx: RefusalContext, state: RunnerState, wt: string, reason: string, notes: string[], entries: string[]): Promise<RunOutcome>` — the tail from `let commit` through the final `return`: the note commit (`buildCommitMessage`/`stampedSubject`/`commitTrailer` + `commitPathsAndDiscardRest`), the no-commit reset branch, the `ctx.merge` call with its throw guard setting `state.lastError`, the non-`"changed"` branch, and the `clearSupersededRejection` + `entry_refused` event branch (named `mergeRefusalNotes` rather than the heading's `landRefusalNotes` because `land` is a retired identifier word under test/retired-names.test.ts).

### `cmdStart`'s ~235-line parse-and-boot body is split into a `parseStartInvocation` validation helper and a `runSupervisedGeneration` boot helper, so a pre-boot flag rule and a generation-boot step are each found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan and blocked part — the three in-flight plans edit src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/config/config-validation-roles.ts and src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts, the refused TUI Transcript plan edits src/ui/tui, no blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part (3h/3, 3i/3, 3j/3, 3d/3, 3e/3, 3f/3, 3m/3) names src/cli/cli-start.ts (`grep -n 'cli-start' PLANS.md` prints nothing), and PLANS-DONE.md names `cmdStart` only for landed behavior additions (`--once --json`, `--for --json`, the three dashboard-only flag guards, `onceSummary`'s split) and the tick→run rename, never a split of `cmdStart`; touches src/cli/cli-start.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `cmdStart` (`src/cli/cli-start.ts`) is one ~235-line body that first parses and validates the invocation before any team boots — the `--tui`/`--gui`/`--json`/`--port`/`--all-interfaces`/`--token`/`--role`/`--for`/`--branch` guards, the `--token` argv scrub, `runStartupCheck`, and the already-running-orchestrator refusal — and then boots the supervised generation: the stop closure and SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, the `--for` deadline timer and scheduled-stop watch, the parent-death watch, the baseline/redeploy/launch-services imports, the banner, the event subscription, `runOrchestrator`, and the once/window summaries and exit codes. A reader asking "which guard refuses `--port` without `--gui`?" or "where is the parent-death watch armed?" has only the one body to scan, and neither half has a name to grep. Split the two halves into module-private helpers, so a pre-boot rule and a generation-boot step are found by name and `cmdStart` becomes the parse call, the supervisor hand-off and the boot call.

**Approach.** All edits in src/cli/cli-start.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` and `/** */` comment with the block it annotates. Add `import type { TumwaterConfig } from "../config/config-schema.js";` with the other imports. Define two module-private interfaces and two module-private helpers; nothing new is exported.
- `interface StartInvocation { once: boolean; json: boolean; forMs: number | null; branchArg: string | null; roleFilter: string[] | null; config: TumwaterConfig; mainBranch: string }`.
- `interface SupervisedGenerationInput { root: string; config: TumwaterConfig; mainBranch: string; branchArg: string | null; once: boolean; json: boolean; forMs: number | null; roleFilter: string[] | null }`.
- `parseStartInvocation(root: string, args: string[]): Promise<StartInvocation>` holds the whole pre-boot half in its current order: `once`/`json`; the `--tui`/`--gui`-rival `failRivalShapes` pair on `--once`; the `--port`/`--all-interfaces`/`--token`-require-`--gui` refusals and `tokenValueProblem`; the `process.argv` `--token` scrub and its `say`; `forMs = parseRunWindow(args, once)`; `branchArg = parseBranchFlag(args)`; `await runStartupCheck(root, branchArg)` and its `"problem" in startup` `fail`; the `--role`-without-`--once` and `--json`-without-`--once`/`--for` guards; the `--json`+`--gui`/`--tui` pair; `roleFilter = parseRoleListFlag(args, knownRoleIds(config))` and its disabled/unknown guards; and `readOrchestratorInfo(root)` with the `orchestratorAlive` refusal. Returns `{ once, json, forMs, branchArg, roleFilter, config, mainBranch }`.
- `runSupervisedGeneration(input: SupervisedGenerationInput): Promise<void>` holds the supervised-generation body from `const controller = new AbortController()` to the end of today's `cmdStart`, destructuring `RUN_WINDOW_START_ENV`, `ONCE_FAILED_EXIT_CODE`, `startParentDeathWatch` and `expectedSupervisorPid` off its own `await import("../process/supervisor.js")`: the `stop` closure and SIG handlers; `windowStart`/`armDeadlineTimer`; `armScheduledStopWatch`; `startParentDeathWatch`; the `runnerIds`/`roles` resolution; the dynamic `main-baseline`, `redeploy`, `launch-services` and `orchestrator` imports; the banner and `subscribeEvents`; `runStartupMigrations` and the run-counter snapshot; the `runOrchestrator` try/finally; the once/window summary branches; `onceFailures` and `ONCE_FAILED_EXIT_CODE`; and the `RESTART_EXIT_CODE` exit. It takes no supervisor parameter: the plan's `typeof import("../process/supervisor.js")` annotation is rejected by the project's consistent-type-imports rule (inline `import()` type annotations are forbidden), and the `import type * as` namespace spelling lint-resolves to `any`, so the helper loads the (Node-cached) module itself rather than being handed it. A second dynamic import beside cmdStart's own is a cache hit and adds no page cost.
- `cmdStart` keeps its export, its `(root: string, args: string[])` signature and its doc comment. Its body becomes `const { once, json, forMs, branchArg, roleFilter, config, mainBranch } = await parseStartInvocation(root, args);`, then the kept lazy-import comment and `const supervisor = await import("../process/supervisor.js");`, then `if (!process.env[supervisor.SUPERVISED_ENV]) { cancelScheduledStop(root); await superviseStartCommand(root, args, branchArg, forMs); return; }`, then `await runSupervisedGeneration({ root, config, mainBranch, branchArg, once, json, forMs, roleFilter });`.
- Keep `superviseStartCommand`, `superviseDashboard` and every existing export unchanged; every moved line uses symbols already imported (plus the one type import), so no other import is added or removed.

Every view re-derives the same empty-match prose and threads the same locals, so a reader asking "where does `--count` scope its tally?", "which branch prints `no notable events`?" or "what seeds the follow's offset?" has only the one ~205-line body to scan, and no phase has a name to grep.

It returns the locals as `LogsFeed`, so no filter or rival check is left in `cmdLogs`.
- `sayLogsWindow(root, feed, ms, untilMs): void` — the `--since`/`--until` branch: its three rival checks (`-f`, `-n`, `--transcript`), the `readEventsSince` read and the `untilMs` filter, then the empty-window prose, the `--count` tally, the per-event print and the `SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE`. The current `windowPhrase` computation stays here.

It holds no flag scan, no `feedFilter`, no `say`/`sayTally`, no `readEventsSince`/`readEventsTailWithEnd` and no `followUntilParentGone` call.
- Order is preserved exactly: parse; `--since` window; `-n`/`--transcript`/`--prompt`; tail-and-follow. The `--since` rival checks still run before the transcript parse, as today.

### `initProject`'s ~215-line validate-then-seed body is split into one named validation helper and one named seeding helper, so an `--branch` refusal or the adopted-TUMWATER.md seeding rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan and blocked part — none edits src/init/init.ts: the three in-flight plans edit src/agent/claude, src/agent/opencode, src/config/config-write.ts and src/cli/log-commands.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/roles, src/gui, src/ui, src/prompt and src/request-timeouts.ts; the refused TUI Transcript plan edits src/ui/tui; the only shared file, docs/invariants.md, is edited by this plan at its Init section while the blocked parts 3f/3 and 3m/3 edit its merge and gate sections, so whichever lands second rebases there; `grep -n 'src/init\|initProject' PLANS.md` prints nothing; PLANS-DONE.md names `init.ts` only as the file other landed init behavior was added to, never as a split of `initProject`; touches src/init/init.ts docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `initProject` (`src/init/init.ts`, from its `const dryRun` line through the final `return`, ~215 lines) does three jobs in one scope: it validates the request (resolve the template; refuse an over-long brief, missing git, a team workspace, an empty prompt, `--branch` on an existing repo, an unmarked TUMWATER.md, and a differing prompt; resolve and validate the new-repo branch name), then seeds (git init, README/TUMWATER, PLANS/BUGS/QUESTIONS/PRINCIPLES, config, .gitignore, starter dirs, commit), then composes the result. Each refusal throws mid-body and each seed path pushes into the same `created`/`leftAlone` arrays, so a reader asking "where is an over-long brief refused?" or "where does the adopted repo's TUMWATER.md get written?" has only the one body to scan, and no phase has a name to grep.

**Approach.** All code edits in src/init/init.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the phase it annotates. Two module-private async helpers declared below `initProject`; no helper is exported.
- `interface InitPlan` (module-private) holds what validation resolved: `dryRun: boolean`; `tpl: NonNullable<ReturnType<typeof getTemplate>>` (the resolved template — `getTemplate`'s return type is not exported, so name it structurally, as today's `tpl` local already infers); `combinedPrompt: string`; `brief: string | null`; `readmeExists: boolean`; `adopted: boolean`; `wasRepo: boolean`; `preferredBranch: string | undefined` (the branch `git init -b` will use, set only when `!wasRepo`).
- `resolveInitPlan(root, briefText, branch, opts): Promise<InitPlan>` — today's validation in its existing order: `dryRun`; the `getTemplate`/`unknownTemplateError` resolution and `tpl`; the `combinedPrompt` build and its `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` refusal; `findOnPath("git")`; `owningTeamRoot`; `prompt` and the bare-init/empty-prompt refusal (with its README hint); `isGitRepo` and the `--branch`-on-existing-repo refusal; `briefFile`/`readmeExists`/`adopted`; the unmarked-TUMWATER.md refusal; the differing-prompt refusal. Last, only when `!wasRepo`, it resolves `preferredBranch` (`branch ?? git config --get init.defaultBranch ?? "main"`) and runs the `check-ref-format` refusal, so the invalid-branch refusal still precedes any side effect. It performs no write and no `git init`, and it allocates neither `created`/`leftAlone` nor a commit.
- `seedProject(root, plan): Promise<Pick<InitResult, "created" | "leftAlone" | "committed" | "repoInitialized" | "branch" | "bootstrap">>` — today's side-effecting half: when `!plan.wasRepo`, `git init -b plan.preferredBranch` (skipped on `plan.dryRun`), setting `repoInitialized`/`createdBranch`; `withCommits = plan.wasRepo && await hasCommits(root)` and `fresh = await isFreshProject(root, withCommits)`; the `created`/`leftAlone` arrays and the `claim`/`write` closures; the README/TUMWATER decision; the PLANS/BUGS/QUESTIONS/PRINCIPLES writes; the config seed with its `fresh` bootstrap; `ensureGitignore(root, plan.dryRun)`; the starter-directory `claim` loop; and the commit pathspec and commit. It returns `{ created, leftAlone, committed, repoInitialized, branch: createdBranch, bootstrap }`. It reads `plan.tpl`, `plan.combinedPrompt`, `plan.brief`, `plan.readmeExists`, `plan.adopted`, `plan.wasRepo`, `plan.preferredBranch` and `plan.dryRun`; it touches neither `opts` nor `briefText`.
- `initProject` keeps its export, signature and doc comment; its body becomes `const plan = await resolveInitPlan(root, briefText, branch, opts);`, `const seeded = await seedProject(root, plan);`, and `return { ...seeded, adopted: plan.adopted, dryRun: plan.dryRun, template: plan.tpl.id };`. It holds no refusal, no `claim`/`write`, no `created`/`leftAlone` array and no `git init`.
- Leave `InitResult`, `isFreshProject`, `isScaffoldingPath`, `ensureGitignore`, `BOOTSTRAP_PLANS`, `SCAFFOLDING_FILES`, the re-export line and every import unchanged; the moved code uses only symbols already imported, so no import is added or removed.

**Files touched.** src/init/init.ts docs/invariants.md

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `resolveInitPlan` and `seedProject` each exist once with the signatures above, are module-private, and `initProject`'s body is only the two helper calls and the composed `return` — it contains no `throw new Error`, no `fs.existsSync`/`writeTextAtomic`, no `git(`/`gitTry(` and no `saveConfig`.
- `git init` is called from exactly one site (`seedProject`) and only after `resolveInitPlan` returned; the refusals INV-Q1 names (over-long brief, `--branch` on an existing repo, invalid branch name, team workspace) still throw before any write, `git init` or commit, in a dry run too.
- stdout, stderr and exit status are identical for every invocation: `test/init.test.ts` and `test/init-templates.test.ts` pass unchanged, including "initProject validates before seeding: a bad prompt leaves no repo behind", "initProject rejects an over-long brief text before seeding", "initProject refuses --branch on an existing repo instead of silently ignoring it", "initProject refuses inside a team workspace and writes nothing", "an unknown template id and an overflowing preamble fail before any side effect", "initProject never clobbers existing files and is idempotent", "initProject --dry-run writes nothing: no files, no gitignore edit, no commit", "initProject seeds a git repo when the cwd is not one yet (BUGS.md 2026-09-08)", "initProject honors the caller's branch and git's init.defaultBranch preference (portability 2/7)", "initProject leaves no half-written file when a seeded write dies mid-way", "initProject appends both ignore entries to an existing .gitignore on their own lines", "initProject seeds bootstrap on a fresh project", "initProject leaves user's unrelated dirty files uncommitted" and "a repo that only gains a config reports it and stays uncommitted".
- `docs/invariants.md`'s init section keeps every `Guarantee` and `Pinned by` line byte-identical and changes only the `initProject` token in the `Binds.` lines of INV-Q1–Q5, each to the helper that now holds that body: INV-Q1 (`resolveInitPlan`), INV-Q2 (`seedProject`'s local `claim`, `ensureGitignore`), INV-Q3 (`resolveInitPlan`), INV-Q4 (`seedProject`), INV-Q5 (`resolveInitPlan`, `seedProject`, `ensureGitignore`); `owningTeamRoot`, `briefFile`, `writeTextAtomic`, `cmdInit` and INV-Q6's `isFreshProject`/`isScaffoldingPath` are unchanged.
- The exported surface of src/init/init.ts is unchanged: `grep -nE '^export ' src/init/init.ts` still matches only the `PLANS_TEMPLATE, BUGS_TEMPLATE` re-export and `initProject`.
- No edit outside src/init/init.ts and docs/invariants.md.

### `setConfigKey`'s ~250-line parse-and-write body is split into one named helper per parsed-key kind, so a `model.<tier>`/`backends.<id>`/legacy-`provider` rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'config-write' PLANS.md` matches only the refused TUI entry's Goal prose and no `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names src/config/config-write.ts; `grep -n 'setConfigKey' PLANS-DONE.md` names it only as the writer other landed features call, with no split of it; docs/invariants.md binds it only through INV-A4's legacy-key refusal and INV-B3's file-roles preservation, both behavior this private move leaves alone; touches src/config/config-write.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `setConfigKey` (`src/config/config-write.ts`) is one ~250-line function that canonicalises the key, parses it with `parseConfigKey`, screens an exponent-spelled plain-integer value, JSON-parses the raw text, and then branches: a dotted key (`parsed.kind !== "top"`) runs the `unknownRoleFieldError` check, the per-map validator, the `model.<tier>` string check and a `writeConfigMutation` whose callback is a chain of `if (parsed.kind === …)` arms for `map`, `tier`, `section`, `agent` and `role`; a top-level key runs `unknownConfigKeyError`, the legacy `provider`/`fallbackModel` absence refusal, `PER_KEY_VALIDATORS` and a second `writeConfigMutation` whose callback collapses a legacy/whole-section spelling (`backends`, `agentBin`/`piArgs`, `claudeWindowReserve`). A reader asking "where is `model.<tier>` merged?", "which arm drops the legacy pi alias?" or "where is the legacy `provider` refusal?" must scan the whole body, and no arm has a name to grep. Split each parsed-key arm into one named handler so `setConfigKey` becomes the canonicalise/parse/screen/parse and the two dispatches. No behavior change: every rejected key returns the same `fail` wording and every accepted write produces a byte-identical file (including the deep-equal `unchanged` no-op and the `model.<tier>` object-entry `note`).

**Approach.** All edits in src/config/config-write.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the arm it annotates. Add one unexported module-level result alias above `setConfigKey` and keep the existing nested state closure pattern — no state object, no new import, and no exported name changes:
- `type SetConfigKeyResult = { ok: true; value: unknown; oldValue: unknown; note?: string; unchanged?: true } | { ok: false; error: string };` — the union `setConfigKey` spells inline today; `setConfigKey`, `writeDottedKey` and `writeTopLevelKey` are annotated with it.
- The helpers are declared **inside** `setConfigKey`, above its body, so they close over `root`; the two merge groups close over the `let value`/`let unchanged`/`let oldValue` locals of the helper that owns the `writeConfigMutation` call.
- `exponentRefusal(parsed: ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, key: string, trimmed: string): string | null` — the existing plain-integer test (`PLAIN_INTEGER_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` for a `top` key, the `maxConcurrentPerProvider` map, `roles.<id>.instances`, `bootstrap.untilPlansDone`) plus the `!/^\d*\.?\d+$/` and exponent-spelling tests, returning the `must be a plain integer — no exponent notation` message or `null`.
- `writeDottedKey(parsed: Exclude<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "top" } | { kind: "error" }>, value: unknown): SetConfigKeyResult` — the whole `parsed.kind !== "top"` branch: the `unknownRoleFieldError` role check, the `map` validator selection (`checkDailyBudgetUsd` / `checkProviderConcurrencyCap` / `checkQuietHours`, label `` `${parsed.map}.${parsed.role}` ``), the `tier` string refusal, then one `writeConfigMutation` whose callback declares `let oldValue: unknown; let unchanged: true | undefined;` and is only `switch (parsed.kind) { case "map": return mergeMapEntry(record, parsed); case "tier": return mergeTier(record, parsed); case "section": return mergeSection(record, parsed); case "agent": return mergeAgent(record, parsed); case "role": return mergeRoleEntry(record, parsed); }`, then the post-write shaping (the `unchanged` return and the `model.<tier>` object-entry `note`).
  - `mergeMapEntry(record: ConfigRecord, parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "map" }>): TumwaterConfig` — the existing map arm: read `existing[parsed.role]`, set `oldValue`, the `isDeepStrictEqual` no-op, the spread merge and `preservingFileRoles(root, next)`.
  - `mergeTier(record, parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "tier" }>): TumwaterConfig` — the existing tier arm: `modelTierMap(record.model)`, `parsed.tier`, the promotion merge and `preservingFileRoles`.
  - `mergeSection(record, parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "section" }>): TumwaterConfig` — the existing fixed-shape-section arm.
  - `mergeAgent(record, parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "agent" }>): TumwaterConfig` — the existing backend arm, including the `parsed.id === "pi"` `agentBin`/`piArgs` deletion and the `claude` `windowReserve` deletion.
  - `mergeRoleEntry(record, parsed: Extract<ReturnType<typeof parseConfigKey>, { kind: "role" }>): TumwaterConfig` — the fall-through `roles.<id>.<field>` arm, read against `rawConfigObject(root).roles` / `objectOrEmpty`.
- `writeTopLevelKey(key: string, value: unknown): SetConfigKeyResult` — the top-level branch: `unknownConfigKeyError`, the legacy `provider`/`fallbackModel` absence refusal (`loadConfig(root)` probe), `PER_KEY_VALIDATORS[key]`, then one `writeConfigMutation` whose callback declares `let oldValue`/`let unchanged` and applies the spelling collapses.
  - `dropLegacyPiAlias(next: TumwaterConfig, key: string): TumwaterConfig` — the existing `agentBin`/`piArgs` branch (delete the matching `backends.pi` field, drop an emptied `pi` entry).
  - `dropNestedReserve(next: TumwaterConfig): TumwaterConfig` — the existing `claudeWindowReserve` branch (delete `backends.claude.windowReserve`, drop an emptied `claude` entry).
  - the `backends` whole-section case stays a call to the existing `collapseBackendAliases(next)`; the `key !== "roles"` `preserveFileRoles(root, next)` call stays in the callback.
- `setConfigKey`'s body is only: `key = canonicalConfigKey(key); const parsed = parseConfigKey(key); if (parsed.kind === "error") return fail(parsed.error); const trimmed = rawValue.trim(); const refusal = exponentRefusal(parsed, key, trimmed); if (refusal) return fail(refusal); let value: unknown; try { value = JSON.parse(rawValue); } catch { value = rawValue; } if (parsed.kind !== "top") return writeDottedKey(parsed, value); return writeTopLevelKey(key, value);`. It holds no `writeConfigMutation`, no `preservingFileRoles`, no `isDeepStrictEqual`, no `rawConfigObject`, no `unknownRoleFieldError`, no `unknownConfigKeyError` and no `PER_KEY_VALIDATORS`.
- Leave `setDailyBudgetUsd`, `setRoleModelFields`, `unsetConfigKey`, every import and every module-level helper (including `PLAIN_INTEGER_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`) unchanged.

**Goal.** `claudeTranslator` (`src/agent/claude/claude-stream.ts`) and `opencodeTranslator` (`src/agent/opencode/opencode-stream.ts`) each hold a `translate` closure that is one long `switch` over the backend's stream event arms. Claude's arms are `system` (with the `init`/`api_retry`/`compact_boundary` subtypes), `assistant` (the split-block fold), `user` (the `tool_result` ends), `rate_limit_event` (the per-window readings), `result` (usage, cost, error classification) and the dropped `tool_progress`; OpenCode's are the one-time session announcement plus `step_start`, `text`, `reasoning`, `tool_use`, `step_finish` and `error`. A reader asking "where is `system/api_retry` translated?", "which arm emits the per-`unifiedWindows` `rate_limit` readings?" or "where does `step_finish` fold usage?" has only the one body to scan and no arm to grep. Split each arm into one named handler, so each `translate` becomes the JSON parse and the dispatch. No behavior change: the emitted canonical lines, the run warnings and both returned translator objects are identical for the same stream.

**Approach.** Move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the arm it annotates. All handlers are declared **inside** their translator function, above `translate`, so they close over the existing run state and nested helpers; no state object, exported type or import is added, and no module-level function moves.
- Claude: add nested `handleSystem(event: Json): string[]` (the whole `system` case, `billingOf` call included), `handleAssistant(event: Json): string[]` (the pending-message fold and `startToolCall` pushes), `handleUser(event: Json): string[]` (the `flush` plus `tool_execution_end` pushes), `handleRateLimitEvent(event: Json): string[]` (the `unifiedWindows` loop and the top-level `rate_limit`), and `handleResult(event: Json): string[]` (the `run_usage`/`run_cost`/error `message_end`). `translate`'s body becomes `parseJsonObject`, the `str(event.type)` read and `switch (type) { case "system": return handleSystem(event); case "assistant": return handleAssistant(event); case "user": return handleUser(event); case "rate_limit_event": return handleRateLimitEvent(event); case "result": return handleResult(event); case "tool_progress": return []; default: record(type ?? "unknown"); return []; }`; the existing nested `flush`, `startToolCall` and `record` keep their bodies. The returned object (`translate`, `finalize`, `warnings`) and the module-level `billingOf` stay put.
- OpenCode: add nested `announceSession(event: Json): string[]` (the `sessionStarted`/`sessionID` check and the `session`+`agent_start` pushes), and `handleStepStart()`, `handleText(event)`, `handleReasoning(event)`, `handleToolUse(event)` (the `TOOL_NAMES` mapping and `calls` queue), `handleStepFinish(event)` (the usage fold and `flush(true)`) and `handleError(event)` (the `classifyError` fold, `flush(false)` and error `message_end`). `translate` becomes the parse (with its `record("malformed")` early return), then `const out = announceSession(event);` and `switch (type) { case "step_start": return [...out, ...handleStepStart()]; case "text": return [...out, ...handleText(event)]; case "reasoning": ...; case "tool_use": ...; case "step_finish": ...; case "error": return [...out, ...handleError(event)]; default: record(typeof type === "string" ? type : "unknown"); return out; }`; the existing nested `record` and `flush` keep their bodies. `opencodeExportLines` and the returned object (`translate`, `finalize`, `noteOpencodeUsagePartial`, `warnings`) are untouched.

**Goal.** `codexTranslator` (`src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts`) is one function whose `translate` closure is one ~200-line `switch (type)` over the codex stream's event arms: `thread.started` announces the session and agent start; `turn.completed` folds the usage block and abandons the open calls; `turn.failed` parses the inner-JSON error, classifies it and closes the turn; the top-level `error` arm either emits an `auto_retry_start` from the reconnect text or holds the message as the next failure's fallback; and `item.started`/`item.completed` is a second, nested dispatch over `command_execution`, `file_change`, `item.type === "error"`, `agent_message`, the dropped types and the unknown tail. Split each event arm into one named handler, so `translate` becomes the JSON parse, the type read and the dispatches. No behavior change: the emitted canonical lines, the run warnings and the returned `CodexStreamTranslator` are identical for the same stream.

**Approach.** All edits in src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the arm it annotates. The handlers are declared **inside** `codexTranslator`, above `translate`, so they close over the run's existing state (`sessionIdValue`, `sawTurnCompleted`, `sawTurnFailed`, `openCalls`, `warnedAbandoned`, `pendingFailureText`, `turnUsage`, `warnings`) and the existing nested helpers (`recordEvent`, `recordItem`, `recordErrorItem`, `abandonOpenCalls`) — no state object or exported type is introduced, every existing nested helper keeps its body, and no import is added or removed:

- `handleTurnCompleted(event: Json): string[]` — the `turn.completed` case: `sawTurnCompleted`, the `turnUsage` fold and `return abandonOpenCalls()`.
- `handleTurnFailed(event: Json): string[]` — the `turn.failed` case: `sawTurnFailed`, the inner-JSON parse, `classifyTurnFailed`, the `errorMessage` fallback to `pendingFailureText`, `abandonOpenCalls()`, and the `message_end` / `retryAfterSeconds` / `rate_limit` pushes.
- `handleErrorLine(event: Json): string[]` — the top-level `error` case: `RECONNECT`, the `auto_retry_start`, and the `pendingFailureText` hold.
- `handleItem(event: Json, started: boolean): string[]` — the whole `item.started`/`item.completed` case: the `item`/`itemType` reads, the `DROPPED_ITEM_TYPES` and unknown-tail (`recordItem`) returns, and the delegation by `itemType` to the four item handlers below. `started` is passed in (the dispatcher computes `type === "item.started"`, exactly as the case does today).
  - `handleCommandItem(item: Json, started: boolean): string[]` — the `command_execution` branch (the `innerCommand`, `openCalls` set/delete, `boundText`-capped result and exit-code error flag).
  - `handleFileChangeItem(item: Json, started: boolean): string[]` — the `file_change` branch (the `changes` filter, the `<id>-<i>` call ids, the `edit` tool calls and the mirror starts/ends).
  - `handleErrorItem(item: Json): string[]` — the `item.type === "error"` branch (`recordErrorItem`).
  - `handleAgentMessageItem(item: Json): string[]` — the `agent_message` branch (the one text `message_end`).
- `translate` keeps its exact `(line: string) => string[]` shape and its `parseJsonObject` early return, and its body is only: `const parsed = parseJsonObject(line); if (!parsed) return [];`, `const event = parsed as Json;`, `const type = typeof event.type === "string" ? event.type : "unknown";`, then `switch (type) { case "thread.started": return handleThreadStarted(event); case "turn.started": return []; case "turn.completed": return handleTurnCompleted(event); case "turn.failed": return handleTurnFailed(event); case "error": return handleErrorLine(event); case "item.started": case "item.completed": return handleItem(event, type === "item.started"); default: recordEvent(type); return []; }`. It holds no `JSON.stringify`, no `openCalls.` mutation, no `warnings.add(`, no `sessionIdValue =`, no `turnUsage =` and no nested `switch`.
- Leave the returned object (`translate`, `sessionId`, `turnCompletedUsage`, `flagUsagePartial`, `flagModelSwitched`, `finalize`), the exported `codexTranslator` signature and doc comment, and every module-level helper and import (`parseJsonObject`, `objectOrEmpty`, `nonNegativeNumber`, `boundText`, `innerCommand`, `classifyTurnFailed`, `DROPPED_ITEM_TYPES`, `RECONNECT`) unchanged.

### `cmdPrompt`'s ~195-line five-mode dispatch is split into one named helper per mode, so a `--cancel`/`--edit`/`--top` rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts\|cmdPrompt' PLANS.md` matches nothing and no `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names src/inbox: the four waiting plans touch src/backlog/backlog-cli-view.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/budget/budget-wiring.ts and src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status/status-polls.ts, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/roles, src/gui, src/run/run-apply.ts, src/prompt, src/request-timeouts.ts and src/ui (status-model.ts and gui), none src/inbox; PLANS-DONE.md holds no split of `cmdPrompt` — its `prompt-commands.ts` entries are landed behavior changes (the `--list --grep` match, `--list --role a,b`, `--edit` from a file, `--attach`) — and docs/invariants.md neither names the file nor the function (`grep -c 'src/inbox/prompt-commands\|cmdPrompt' docs/invariants.md` prints 0); touches src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `cmdPrompt` (`src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts`) is one ~195-line function that first parses the args, canonicalizes a non-list `--role`, chooses the id set for the mode, and refuses an unknown role; then dispatches five modes in one body — `--list` (filter the list-wide rows by `--role a,b` and `--grep`, then print the prose or `--json` listing or one of three empty/no-match lines), `--cancel <n>` (list-wide or role-scoped), `--edit <n>` (attachment gate, then open the editor for a bare position or write the typed/file text, list-wide or role-scoped), `--top <n>` (list-wide or role-scoped), and the default submit form (the `--at` due time, the `--attach` gate, then `submitRolePromptAndWake` and the confirmation). A reader asking "where does `--edit` open the editor?", "which branch resolves a list-wide `--top` position?" or "where is the `--attach` image gate?" has only the one body to scan, and no mode has a name to grep. Split it into one module-private helper per mode, so a mode's rules are found by name and `cmdPrompt` becomes the parse, the id set, the unknown-role refusal, `const role = parsed.role;` and the five dispatches. No behavior change: stdout, stderr and exit status are identical for every invocation.

**Approach.** All edits in src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the mode it annotates. The five helpers are module-private and synchronous (no branch contains an `await`), and each takes only the fields its mode reads — so no helper needs the private `PromptArgs` union type (`type PromptArgs` in src/cli/cli-command-args.ts is not exported) and no import is added:

- `runPromptCancel(root, position, role)` — the cancel body (`cancelListedPrompt`/`sayListedOutcome` and the role-scoped `runRolePromptCommand(root, target, position, cancelRolePrompt)`). Signature `(root: string, position: number, role: string | null): void`.
- `runPromptEdit(root, position, text, attachPaths, role)` — the edit body: the `readPromptImages` read, the image-input gate, the bare-position editor path (`queuedFileAtPosition`, `readQueuedPromptBody`, `editInEditor`, `editQueuedFile`) and the typed list-wide (`editListedPrompt`) and role-scoped (`editRolePrompt`) paths. - `runPromptTop(root, position, role)` — the top body (`resolveListedQueue`/`failQueueMiss` list-wide, `movePromptToTop` and `sayTopOutcome` both ways). Signature `(root: string, position: number, role: string | null): void`.

Signature `(root: string, text: string, atDelayMs: number | null, attachPaths: string[], role: string | null): void`.
- `cmdPrompt` keeps its exact signature and doc comment, and its body is only: `const parsed = parsePromptArgs(args);`, the `--role` canonicalization line, the `validIds` ternary, the unknown-role `if (…) fail(unknownRoleMessage(parsed.role, validIds));` refusal, `const role = parsed.role;`, then the five dispatches in today's order — `if (parsed.mode === "list") { runPromptList(root, args, parsed.json, parsed.grep, validIds); return; }`, the same shape for `cancel`, `edit` and `top`, then `runPromptSubmit(root, parsed.text, parsed.atDelayMs, parsed.attachPaths, role);`. TypeScript narrows `parsed` at each call, so the helper arguments type-check without a cast.

### `budgetFallbackView`'s ~200-line view derivation is split into one named helper per phase, so a fallback-view phase is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts' PLANS.md` matches no entry, the three waiting plans touch src/backlog/backlog-cli-view.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts and src/budget/budget-wiring.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status/status-polls.ts, src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts, src/config, src/cli, src/ui/status-model.ts and src/ui/gui+their tests, none src/budget; PLANS-DONE.md holds the landed plan that created this module (part 5b/8, 5c/8, 6a/7) but no split of `budgetFallbackView`; docs/invariants.md binds src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts only through `chainInfo` (INV-BN1, INV-BN2) and the `fallbackServingPair`/`pairDailyCost` imports, none of which this private move touches; touches src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `budgetFallbackView` (`src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts`) is one ~200-line function that derives the budget gate's fallback view from the verdict half's resolved inputs in six phases: it resolves the window move (`onFallback`, `seamBackends`, `windowOut`, `movedBackends`, `windowMove`) and the re-derive key (`resolvedKey`, `movedKey`, `fromKey`); installs `state.fallbackConfig` when the move or fallback changed, including the pinned-role and pinned-reviewer escapes; derives `windowTiers`; installs the director's `state.directorFrom`/`directorKey`/`directorView` and `directorMoved`; folds `state.prevWindowMoved` into `windowResumed`/`windowResumedBackends`; and derives `movedTiers` before calling `chainInfo` and returning the view. A reader asking "where is `windowResumed` computed?", "what makes the reviewer fall to its tier's pair?" or "which loop records `state.prevWindowMoved`?" has only the one body to scan, and a phase has no name to grep. Split it into one module-private helper per phase, so `budgetFallbackView` becomes the destructure, the six ordered calls, the `chainInfo` call and the return. No behavior change: the returned `BudgetFallbackView` and the cross-poll `state` mutations are identical for the same input.

**Approach.** All edits in src/budget/budget-fallback-view.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the phase it annotates. First extract the function's inline parameter type into a module-private `interface BudgetFallbackViewInput` with exactly the fields it names today (`state`, `config`, `now`, `states`, `providers`, `catalog`, `accounts`, `windowOutFor`, `directorWindowOutFor`, `priceResolved`, `servingResolved`, `chainPairs`, `pairNames`, `reached`), and give both `budgetFallbackView(a: BudgetFallbackViewInput)` and every helper that parameter. The six helpers are module-private and return `void` except where noted:
- `resolveWindowMove(a)` — the `onFallback` const and its comment, the `seamBackends` loop and its comment, the `windowOut`/`movedBackends` loop and its comment, `windowMove`, and the `resolvedKey`/`movedKey`/`fromKey` consts. Returns `{ onFallback, windowOut, movedBackends, windowMove, resolvedKey, fromKey }` (`movedKey` stays local to it).
- `installFallbackConfig(a, { onFallback, windowMove, windowOut, movedBackends, fromKey })` — the whole `if ((onFallback || windowMove) && (state.from !== liveConfig || state.fromKey !== fromKey)) { … }` block, including the `seamBlocked`/`available` closures, the `applyFallbackModel` call, the pinned-role loop, the pinned-reviewer adjustment and the three `state` assignments. Returns void and reads `a.state`, `a.config`, `a.providers`, `a.accounts`, `a.catalog`, `a.priceResolved`, `a.reached`.
- `deriveWindowTiers(a, windowOut, windowMove)` — the `windowTiers` const and its comment/loop. Returns the `Partial<Record<ModelTier, string>>`.
- `installDirectorFallback(a, resolvedKey, windowOut)` — the director's `state.directorFrom`/`directorKey`/`directorView` block and its comment. Returns `directorMoved` (boolean).

**Goal.** `applyBudgetGateWiring` (`src/budget/budget-wiring.ts`) is one ~140-line function that performs the budget gate's wiring for one poll in three phases: it publishes the demotion map, the engaged demotion, the spend/cap pair and the chain, logs the one `fallback_switched` event per changed tier and stores the new chain; then assigns every runner's config and `budgetFallbackActive` flag; then, on a cap reopen or subscription-window reset, hands in-flight fallback runs back with a `budget_handback` event and `handBackRun()`. A reader asking "where is `fallback_switched` logged?", "where is a runner's `config` assigned?" or "which loop calls `handBackRun`?" has only the one 140-line body to scan. **Approach.** All edits in src/budget/budget-wiring.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every `//` comment with the phase it annotates. The three helpers are module-private and take the input fields each phase reads:
- `publishBudgetWiring(root, info, budget, view)` — builds `demotions` from `budget.breakers` via `fallbackDemotion`, the `engagedDemotion` from `budget.engaged`, the `spend` pair from `view.spentUsd`/`view.capUsd`, and calls `publishInfoFields` with `fallbackDemotions`/`fallbackDemoted`/`budget`/`chain`; then builds `switched` by comparing `budget.prevChain` to `view.chain` per `MODEL_TIERS`, logs the single `fallback_switched` when `switched` is non-empty, and assigns `budget.prevChain = view.chain`. Returns void.

- `handBackFallbackRuns(root, runners, liveConfig, accounts, view)` — the reopen/window hand-back: the `handBack` predicate, the `resumedBackendSet`, the `resumedBackendForPair` closure, the `stillMoved` computation, and the loop that logs one `budget_handback` per pair and calls `r.handBackRun()`. Returns void.

Its body contains no `for`, no `publishInfoFields`, no `logEventBestEffort`, no `r.config =` or `r.budgetFallbackActive =` assignment and no `handBackRun(` call.

**Goal.** `buildTailAlerts` (`src/ui/team-alert-tail.ts`) is one ~190-line function (from its `const out` to its `return out`) that walks twelve independent alert arms in emission order, each testing a snapshot field, a feed argument or a `roles` predicate and pushing one `TeamAlert` into a local `out`: quiet hours, the maintenance allowance, a standing provider hold, a misconfigured per-provider cap map, the operator pause, capacity contention, a stale workspace pin, an undersized instance pool, a regressed fix, a stopped team, the image-input alert (its blue and amber branches share the `images` key), and the cached image-probe failure. A reader asking "where does the instance-pool alert come from?", "which arm reads `snap.imageProbeFailures`?" or "what is the emission order?" has only the one body to scan, and an arm has no name to grep. Split it into one module-private builder per alert arm, so a tail alert is found by name and `buildTailAlerts` becomes the destructure, the `out` array, the ordered calls and the return. **Approach.** All edits in src/ui/team-alert-tail.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every comment with the arm it annotates. Follow the file's existing push convention: each builder takes `out: TeamAlert[]` and the inputs its arm reads, tests the arm's condition, and pushes exactly the alert the arm pushes today, so the output order is the call order. The builders are module-private, return `void`, and own every arm-specific local (the `end`, `mq`, `phrased`, `left`, `textOnly`, `noTarget` and `targets` consts).
- `pushQuietAlert(out, snap)` — the `snap.inQuietHours && snap.quietHours` block, owning `end = quietWindowEnd(snap.quietHours)`.
- `pushMaintenanceAlert(out, snap)` — the `snap.maintenanceQuota.held.length > 0` block, owning `mq`.
- `pushProviderHoldAlert(out, snap, now)` — the `snap.providerHolds && snap.providerHolds.length > 0` block, owning `phrased`.
- `pushProviderCapsAlert(out, providerCaps)` — the `providerCaps.length > 0` block.
- `pushPausedAlert(out, snap, now)` — the `snap.paused` block, owning `left = pauseCountdown(snap.pausedUntil, now)`.
- `pushContentionAlert(out, contention)` — the `contention.length > 0` block.
- `pushWorkspacePinsAlert(out, workspacePins)` — the `workspacePins.length > 0` block.
- `pushInstancePoolAlert(out, instancePool)` — the `instancePool.length > 0` block.
- `pushRegressedFixesAlert(out, regressedFixes)` — the `regressedFixes` block.
- `pushStoppedAlert(out, snap)` — the `!snap.running` block.
- `pushImagesAlert(out, roles)` — the `textOnly` / `noTarget` blocks, both branches (owning `textOnly`, `noTarget` and the `targets` set).
- `pushImageProbeAlert(out, snap)` — the `snap.imageProbeFailures.length > 0` block.
- `buildTailAlerts` keeps its signature and exact body shape: `const { snap, now, contention, regressedFixes, roles, workspacePins, instancePool, providerCaps } = input;`, `const out: TeamAlert[] = [];`, the twelve calls in the arm order listed above, `return out;`.   - `statusHeaderLine(root: string, snap: StatusSnapshot, now: number): StatusLine` — the `running` array and the whole first line array (the `name`/badges composition).
  - `statusRowMetrics(root: string, snap: StatusSnapshot): StatusRowMetric[]` — today's `withMetrics` `snap.roles.map` over `roleRowCells`; the anonymous element type becomes a module-private `interface StatusRowMetric { s: RunnerState; m: { generated: number; peakCtx: number }; live: LiveProgress | null; phase: string; role: string; lastRunEndedAt: number | undefined }`.
  - `sharedRoleModel(snap: StatusSnapshot): string | undefined` — today's `inners`/`sharedModel` derivation.
  - `statusRoleRows(root: string, snap: StatusSnapshot, now: number, withMetrics: readonly StatusRowMetric[], sharedModel: string | undefined): StatusSpan[][]` — today's `rows` (`sortRolesByState` map and its name/state/result/next cells).
  - `statusTotalsRow(snap: StatusSnapshot, scoped: boolean, withMetrics: readonly StatusRowMetric[]): StatusSpan[][]` — today's `totalsRow`.
  - `statusColumnWidths(cols: readonly string[], allRows: readonly StatusSpan[][], maxWidth: number | undefined, snap: StatusSnapshot): number[]` — today's `widths` measurement, the `FLEXIBLE_COLUMNS` overflow loop and the name-column floor.
  - `statusLineFormatter(widths: readonly number[]): (r: StatusSpan[][], tone?: StatusSpan["tone"]) => StatusLine` — today's `fmt` closure including the span-wise `trimEnd`.
  - `statusRoleSummaries(withMetrics: readonly StatusRowMetric[]): StatusRoleRow[]`-shaped array — today's `roles` mapping over `withMetrics` (keep the returned element type structural exactly as today).

### `buildBacklogAlerts`'s ~240-line alert assembly is split into one named builder per alert arm, so a backlog alert is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/ui/team-alert-backlog.ts\|buildBacklogAlerts' PLANS.md` matches no `## Planned` entry (its only hits are PLANS-DONE.md history): the in-flight plans edit src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/failure/failure-render.ts and src/ui/team-alert-status.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status/status-polls.ts, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli, src/ui/status-model.ts and src/ui/gui/*, so none names src/ui/team-alert-backlog.ts; the landed 2026-10-25 split that extracted this file from teamAlerts (part 2/5) left its body one flat run, and no waiting work edits it; touches src/ui/team-alert-backlog.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `buildBacklogAlerts` (`src/ui/team-alert-backlog.ts`) is one ~240-line function that walks eleven independent alert arms in emission order, each testing one `BacklogAlertsInput` field and pushing one `TeamAlert` into a local `out`: open questions, stale questions, refused entries, operator-held entries, stalled entries, a broken plan-dependency clause, stranded plans, duplicated headings, finished history in the live files, validation-gap records and false-fix records. A reader asking "where does the operator-held alert come from?", "which arm reads `planDependency`?" or "what is the emission order?" has only the one body to scan, and an arm has no name to grep. Split it into one module-private builder per alert arm, so a backlog alert is found by name and `buildBacklogAlerts` becomes the destructure, the `out` array, the ordered calls and the return. No behavior change: the returned `TeamAlert[]` is deep-equal for the same input.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/team-alert-backlog.ts; move code, do not rewrite it, and keep every comment with the arm it annotates. Follow the push convention the sibling `buildStatusAlerts` split uses: each builder takes `out: TeamAlert[]` and the input field its arm reads, and pushes exactly the alert the arm pushes today, so the output order is the call order. The builders are module-private and return `void`.
- `pushQuestionsAlert(out, questions)` — the `questions.length` / `"questions"` block.
- `pushStaleQuestionsAlert(out, staleQuestions)` — the `staleQuestions.length` block, owning `first`, `rest` and the `moreDetail(rest.map(...))` fold.
- `pushRefusedAlert(out, refused)` — the `refused.length` block, owning `first`.
- `pushOperatorHeldAlert(out, operatorHeld)` — the `operatorHeld.length` block, owning `first` and its file-mix ternary detail.
- `pushStalledEntriesAlert(out, stalledEntries)` — the `stalledEntries.length` block, owning `first` and its hold-kind ternary.
- `pushPlanDependencyAlert(out, planDependency)` — the `planDependency !== null` block, owning the `titles` record.
- `pushStrandedPlansAlert(out, strandedPlans)` — the `strandedPlans.length` block, owning `first`, `rest` and `more`.
- `pushBacklogHeadingsAlert(out, duplicatedHeadings)` — the `duplicatedHeadings.length` block, owning `first`, `rest` and `more`.
- `pushBacklogArchiveAlert(out, liveFinished)` — the `liveFinished.length` block.
- `pushValidationGapsAlert(out, validationGaps)` — the `validationGaps.length` block, owning `first`, `rest`, `reason` and `more`.
- `pushFalseFixesAlert(out, fixClaims)` — the `fixClaims.length` block, owning `first`, `rest` and `more`.
- `buildBacklogAlerts` keeps its signature and exact body shape: `const out: TeamAlert[] = [];`, the destructure of `input`, the eleven calls in the arm order listed above, `return out;`. It pushes nothing itself and holds no `if`, `filter` or arm-specific `const`.
- Leave `BacklogAlertsInput`, the imports and the module doc comment as they are; every helper each arm calls (`entryKindLabel`, `entryListDetail`, `moreDetail`, `joinWithMore`, `liveFinishedRowList`, `missingSymbolNames`, `stripEntryStamp`, `plural`, `openBacklogAction`) is already imported, so no import is added or removed.

### `collectReportSince`'s ~190-line flat assembly is split into one named builder per output group, so an output group is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no other `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names src/report/report-data.ts (the one PLANS.md mention of it, in the `stageRunMerge` entry, is a stale independence note naming other plans' files, not a Files-touched list): the in-flight plans edit src/agent, src/run/run-stage.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config, src/cli and src/ui — none src/report; PLANS-DONE.md holds no split of `collectReportSince` (its many landed `report-data.ts` entries are behavior additions — the per-role token/notional maps, the main-red test and culprit maps, the deferral reasons, the slot/provider wait medians — and the only named-arm splits the archive records are `resolveRunVerdict` and `PiStreamParser`); touches src/report/report-data.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `collectReportSince` (`src/report/report-data.ts`, the collector behind `tumwater report --since` and `renderSinceReportMarkdown`) is one ~190-line body: it reads and folds the window into an `acc: UsageFold`, computes the coverage proof and the base-role scope, then assembles the `SinceReport` in a flat return literal whose role-scoping rule is a `scopedByRole(acc.X, bases)` call per field, with a ~30-line `scopedTotals` ternary and two anonymous IIFEs (main-red failing tests and culprits) buried inside. A reader asking "how does the window total commits?", "which fields are team-only?" or "where is the red-by-test flatten?" has only one large body to scan. Give each output group its own named builder, so the group's rule is found by name.

**Approach.**
- Keep `collectReportSince`'s signature, its timing/scope setup (`assertReportSinceMs`, `sinceWindowTiming`, `dayKey`, `scopeBases`) and `coversFullWindow` where they are.
- Extract the read-and-fold into a module-private `foldSinceWindow(root, cutoff, now, end, untilMs): { raw, acc }` (the extra `untilMs` keeps the `ts` filter's bounded-vs-open drop of events at/after `end` unchanged when `--until` is absent): the `readWindowEvents(root, dayKey(cutoff))` call, the full `acc: UsageFold` literal and the `ts` filter loop (`foldUsageEvent`). Its doc comment names that `raw` remains the one read the coverage proof and the main-red maps consume.
- Extract the `scopedTotals` ternary into `sinceScopedTotals(acc, bases): ReportTotals`, keeping both branches: team totals include the merge-slot fields (`mergeTokens`, `mergeCostUsd`, `mergeRuns`, `mergeFailed`), the role branch sums the base roles through `roleSum` and zeroes the merge counts.
- Extract each anonymous IIFE into `sinceMainRedByTest(raw, cutoff, end, bases): Record<string, number>` and `sinceMainRedByCulprit(raw, cutoff, end, bases): Record<string, number>`: each returns `{}` for a role scope (main's red is team-only) and flattens `mainRedFailingTestsByDay` / `mainRedCulpritsByDay` through `addTo`.
- Extract the return literal's role-scoped block into `sinceRoleMaps(acc, bases)`, returning the `scopedByRole` / `nonemptyObj` group (the runs/cost/tokens/rejections/revisions/refusals/failed/fallbacks/image-reroutes/commits/merge maps, the provider, backend and model maps, `notionalByRole` and `deferredByReason`), and lift each main-red IIFE into a named builder, so the return becomes a composition: `{ ...slice, ...(bases ? { role } : {}), totals, ...sinceRoleMaps(acc, bases), mainRedMs, ...nonemptyObj("mainRedByTest", sinceMainRedByTest(raw, cutoff, end, bases)), ...nonemptyObj("mainRedByCulprit", sinceMainRedByCulprit(raw, cutoff, end, bases)), coversFullWindow }`.
- Each new function is module-private, doc-commented with the output group it builds and its scope rule (team-only vs role-scoped), and carries no behavior change: same fields, same values, same absent-when-empty rules.
