### Split src/agent/run-agent.ts's runAgent, part 2/2: the streaming pipeline moves to src/agent/run-stream.ts (planned 2026-10-25 by the organize role; split 2026-10-25 by the plan role after feature held the whole too large (held 1); requires part 1/2 landed — the stream's `createAgentStream` consumes the `SpawnedRun` bundle part 1/2 introduces, and before it lands the streaming pipeline still lives in run-agent.ts; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no `## Planned` entry edits src/agent/*, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` series touches src/runner/runner-run.ts, not src/agent/run-agent.ts; touches src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/run-stream.ts (new) src/agent/run-spawn.ts test/pi.test.ts test/pi-watchdogs.test.ts test/agent-backend.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** With the build-and-spawn stage in run-spawn.ts (part 1/2), run-agent's remaining live lifecycle is the streaming pipeline — `emitNativeLine`, `feedCanonical`, the stdout/stderr `data` handler bodies, `onLine` and `finish`, plus the mutable state they share (`stderr`, `fallbackClone`, `stderrTail`, `nativeTail`, `nativeOverflow`, `streamMintedSession`, `settled`). Extract that into `src/agent/run-stream.ts` behind an `AgentStream` interface so run-agent is the coordinator only.

**Approach.**
- `src/agent/run-stream.ts` (new). Move `MAX_NATIVE_LINE_CHARS` and its doc comment here. Define:
  - `interface AgentStream { feedStdout(chunk: Buffer): void; feedStderr(chunk: Buffer): void; onLine: (line: string) => void; feedCanonical: (text: string, final?: boolean) => void; finish: (result: PiRunResult) => void; settled: () => boolean; stderr: () => string; fallbackClone: () => string | undefined }`.
  - `function createAgentStream(input: { opts: PiRunOptions; backend: AgentBackend; spawned: SpawnedRun; wd: ReturnType<typeof startPiWatchdogs>; onAbort: () => void; rawLog: AppendLog; nativeLog: AppendLog; runTmp: string; resolve: (result: PiRunResult) => void }): AgentStream` — `finish`'s settle/flush needs the two logs, the TMPDIR and the promise `resolve` on the input, so the caller passes them alongside the bundle, watchdogs and abort wiring.
- Move `emitNativeLine`, `feedCanonical`, `finish`, `onLine` and the stdout/stderr `data` handler bodies; `createAgentStream` owns the six stream locals. `feedStdout` does `wd.noteByte()` then `feedCanonical(decoder.write(chunk))`; `feedStderr` does `wd.noteStderr()`, decodes, runs `backend.matchStderrWarning?.(text, stderrTail)`, carries the 512-char tail and keeps the 64 KiB `stderr` window. `finish` keeps its settle logic unchanged: the `settled` guard, `parser.imageBlind` + `opts.onBlindRead`, `removeTree(runTmp)`, `wd.stop()`, `opts.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort)`, `translator.warnings?.()`, and the raw/native-log `end`-flush before `resolve`.
- `src/agent/run-agent.ts`: after the watchdogs and abort wiring, `const stream = createAgentStream({ opts, backend, spawned, wd, onAbort, rawLog, nativeLog, runTmp, resolve });`, attach `spawned.child.stdout?.on("data", (chunk) => stream.feedStdout(chunk))` and `.stderr?.on("data", (chunk) => stream.feedStderr(chunk))`, and assemble `RunSettleState` from the bundle plus `stream.onLine`/`stream.feedCanonical`/`stream.finish`/`stream.stderr`/`stream.fallbackClone`/`stream.settled`. Remove the moved locals and their `state` getters. Keep `export { MAX_NATIVE_LINE_CHARS } from "./run-stream.js";` so `test/agent-backend.test.ts`'s import from `../src/agent/run-agent.js` is unchanged.
- `src/agent/run-spawn.ts` needs no new fields: the bundle already carries `preSpawnSessionId`/`parser`/`translator`/`decoder`/`stderrDecoder`, and the two logs and the run's TMPDIR are the caller's setup locals passed straight to `createAgentStream` on its input; run-stream imports `AppendLog`/`SpawnedRun` from it as types only.

**Goal.** `createTuiPanes` (src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts) is the pane-navigation half of the TUI key dispatch. Its helpers are already named (`beginKey`, `editorCtx`, `cycleView`, `syncRoster`, `setLineBudgets`, `state`), but its `handleKey` is one ~155-line body of nineteen inline key arms plus the trailing `arrowDir`/`pageDir`/`escape` blocks. Every arm is a chain of `pane.handleKey?.(key, ctx) ?? false` calls whose order *is* the rule — Ctrl+N's Health → History → Pending → Transcript priority, Ctrl+G's per-view split, the Health-guarded Ctrl+S/P/L fallthroughs, the Ctrl+X/R/V chains, the arrow/page/escape fallbacks — with the ordering rationale in block comments between them. So "what does Ctrl+P do, and in what order do the panes see it" is found only by scanning the whole body. Split each key's arm into one named closure beside the other helpers and leave `handleKey` as the ordered dispatch, so a key's routing is found by name. This mirrors the landed `resolveRunVerdict` split (one named arm per decision), `PiStreamParser.feedLine` (one named applier per event family) and the in-flight `createHistoryPane` `handleKey` split.

**Approach.** All edits in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts; no exported symbol changes (`createTuiPanes`, `TuiPanesDeps` and the returned `TuiPaneModule` object are untouched).

  - `routeCtrlN` — the whole Ctrl+N chain (the four-pane priority and its ordering comment).
  - `routeCtrlG` — the per-view Ctrl+G split (Activity 0, History N+4, Pending N+5, report fallback).
  - `routeCtrlE` — the Health reclaim over the report trailing-window cycle.
  - `routeCtrlK` — the Health orphan-kill arm.
  - `routeCtrlW` — the History patch toggle.
  - `routeCtrlS` — the Health-view guarded arm followed by the History fallthrough, both `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "s")` blocks, as one closure.
  - `routeCtrlP` — all three `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "p")` blocks (report views N+2/N+3, Health N+7, History fallback), as one closure.
  - `routeCtrlA` — both `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "a")` blocks (Health N+7, Pending N+5), as one closure.
  - `routeCtrlU` — the Health re-sync-install arm.
  - `routeCtrlB` — the Health archive-backlog arm.
  - `routeCtrlL` — both `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "l")` blocks (Health N+7, History fallback), as one closure.
  - `routeCtrlY` — the Transcript change-step over the History Summary cycle.
  - `routeCtrlO` — the five-way Ctrl+O split (Activity 0, Health N+7, Pending N+5, Backlog N+1, History fallback).
  - `routeCtrlX` — the Ctrl+X chain (transcript → history → queued → pending → backlog).
  - `routeCtrlR` — the Ctrl+R chain (pending → health → history → backlog).
  - `routeCtrlV` — the Ctrl+V chain (history → queued → pending → backlog).
  - `routeArrow` — the `arrowDir` block (backlog → pending → queued, then false).
  - `routePage` — the `pageDir` block (activity → transcript → history → report → backlog, then false).
  - `routeEscape` — the `escape` block (pending then queued).
- `handleKey` becomes the dispatch only: `const ctx: TuiPaneCtx = { es };` then `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "n") return routeCtrlN(ctx);` … one line per Ctrl key in today's order, then `const arrow = arrowDir(key.name); if (arrow !== null) return routeArrow(ctx);`, `const page = pageDir(key.name); if (page !== null) return routePage(ctx);`, `if (key.name === "escape") return routeEscape(ctx);` and the final `return false`. The shared prelude comment ("The editor flags below are all false here …") stays on `handleKey`; each moved block comment travels with its arm. Move only the guard-and-call statements — the `arrowDir`/`pageDir` scans stay in `handleKey`, so no direction value is recomputed.
- No change to any state declaration, doc comment, or the returned module object; `docs/invariants.md` is not edited (it pins no pane-router key contract).

**Goal.** `stageRunMerge` (src/run/run-stage.ts) is the commit-staging layer: it derives the commit description from the reply (one bounded follow-up turn when the SUMMARY is missing or over cap), runs the pre-queue self-check with its fix-up turn, computes friction, builds and commits the message, holds the commit on the branch when the role already queues one, or pins and enqueues it, then records the qa flow and feedback filing. It is one ~306-line async function holding all of those rules inline in one scope, so a staging rule is found only by reading the whole body. Extract each decision into a module-private stage function beside `findingDigest` and `logSelfCheckOutcome`, and leave `stageRunMerge` as the ordered stage calls plus the final outcome.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-stage.ts: add a module-private `interface StagedCommitDescription { summary: string; body: StagedBody; summaryDerived: boolean } (a module-private `type StagedBody` structurally mirrors commit-message.ts's module-private `CommitBody`)` and these stages, each holding its current inline block moved verbatim (statements, order and comments):
  - `function revisionFields(ctx: RunStageContext): { revisionRound: number | undefined; priorReview: PriorReview | undefined }` — the `revisionRound` read and the `priorReview` derivation (both comment blocks included). Add `PriorReview` to the existing type import from `../merge/merge-queue.js`.
  - `async function resolveCommitDescription(ctx: RunStageContext): Promise<StagedCommitDescription | RunOutcome>` — the `extractSummary`/`extractCommitBody` reads, the missing-SUMMARY follow-up turn (`summaryDerived` derivation, path fallback and its warning) and the over-cap follow-up turn (shortening and its warning). Returns `ctx.finishAbortedRun()` when a follow-up aborts, otherwise the description.
  - `async function runStageSelfCheck(ctx: RunStageContext, desc: StagedCommitDescription): Promise<RunOutcome | undefined>` — the staged-moved-entry claims (`stagedMovedEntries`, `heldMovedFinding`, `assignedMovedFinding`, the `s.claim` assignment and its `claim` event), the `ctx.stageCheck` findings and the fix-up turn (`requestStageFix`, `foldAgentCommitsSince`), the reverted-change `no_change` return and the `logSelfCheckOutcome` reporting. Mutates `desc.summary`/`desc.body` exactly as the inline block mutates `summary`/`body`.
  - `function frictionSnapshot(ctx: RunStageContext): { minutes: number; authoringTurns: number; highFriction: boolean }` — the `minutes`/`authoringTurns`/`highFriction` computation and the high-friction warning.
  - `function stagedCommitMessage(ctx: RunStageContext, desc: StagedCommitDescription, revisionRound: number | undefined, friction: ReturnType<typeof frictionSnapshot>): string` — the `buildCommitMessage(stampedSubject(baseRoleOf(ctx.role), desc.summary), desc.body, commitTrailer(...))` call.
  - `async function pinAndEnqueueChange(ctx: RunStageContext, change: { commit: string; summary: string; body: StagedBody; highFriction: boolean; revisionRound: number | undefined; priorReview: PriorReview | undefined }): Promise<{ heldOnBranch: boolean } | RunOutcome>` — the `heldOnBranch` computation (`queuedMerges`/`hasUnmergedPin`), the `pinAndReset` failure error outcome, the `enqueueMerge` call with `entryRevisionFields`, the `s.revision = undefined` clear and the `merge_queued` event; returns `{ heldOnBranch }` when the run may finish queued.

**Goal.** `runAgent` (src/agent/run-agent.ts) is one 461-line function whose pre-spawn setup, `prepare` await, build-and-spawn, stream pipeline, watchdogs and settlement wiring share one scope of ~25 mutually-capturing locals; the settlement half already lives in src/agent/run-settle.ts behind the `RunSettleState` getter interface. This part extracts the build-and-spawn stage into `src/agent/run-spawn.ts` behind a `SpawnedRun` bundle; run-agent keeps setup, the watchdogs, the stream pipeline and the `error`/`exit`/`close` wiring. Part 2/2 extracts the stream pipeline next.

**Approach.**
- `src/agent/run-spawn.ts` (new). Move `AppendLog` and `openAppendLog` here (run-agent imports `openAppendLog` for its setup). Export:
  - `interface SpawnedRun { child: ChildProcess; resolved: ResolvedBackendBin; runSpec: AgentRunSpec; invocation: AgentInvocation; parser: PiStreamParser; translator: StreamTranslator; decoder: StringDecoder; stderrDecoder: StringDecoder; runMarker: string; preSpawnSessionId: string; blindRead: () => string | undefined }`.
  - `function spawnPiRun(backend: AgentBackend, logs: { raw: AppendLog }, runTmp: string, opts: PiRunOptions): SpawnedRun | Promise<SpawnedRun>`.
- Move today's build-and-spawn verbatim (after the coordinator's own setup): the `tumwater_run` marker write built from `opts.label`/`opts.kind`/`backend.id`; `new PiStreamParser(opts.onToolCallStart, { imageInput: seamImageInput(opts.config, readPiProviders(piModelsPath())), onBlindRead })`; `makeRunMarker()`; `backend.resolveBin(opts.config)`; the `nearestTumwaterRoot`/`ensureNotesShim` guard and its `onAgentWarning`; the `runSpec` object; the `warnEventBestEffort`-guarded `backend.prepare?.(runSpec)` call/await/catch; `backend.invocation(runSpec)`; `invocation.sessionId ?? opts.sessionName` as `preSpawnSessionId`; `recordSession`; `backend.translator()`; both `new StringDecoder("utf8")`; `spawn(resolved.bin, invocation.args, { cwd, stdio, detached, env: { ...invocation.env, TMPDIR: runTmp } })`; the `child.stdin?.on("error", () => {})` + `child.stdin?.end(invocation.stdin)` block.
- Blind-read termination: keep a per-invocation `blind: { read?: string; terminate?: () => void }` (a module-level one would be shared by concurrent runs); the parser's `onBlindRead` sets `blind.read = path` for an authoring run and calls `blind.terminate?.()`; `buildAndSpawn` / `spawnPiRun` assigns `blind.terminate = () => terminateChild(child)` right after `spawn`. The bundle's `blindRead` closes over `blind` (the `terminate` closure stays internal to run-spawn, since the coordinator kills via `terminateChild(child)` itself and never consumes a bundle `terminate`). Because a backend without `prepare` (pi, claude, opencode) returns the bundle directly rather than a promise, the coordinator does not `await` it and its watchdog start stays synchronous — the ordering the logical-clock tests pin (an `await` on even a settled promise defers the continuation to a microtask, moving `startPiWatchdogs`'s setInterval registration past the tests' immediate `clock.advance` and breaking the zero-byte quiet-kill test).
- run-agent.ts keeps: backend resolution (`backendById(opts.config.agent ?? DEFAULT_BACKEND) ?? piBackend`); the setup try/catch (`ensureDir`, `openAppendLog` for both logs, `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "tumwater-run-"))`, and its `setupFailureResult` resolution on failure); the `registerAgentBackend(...)` registrations (src/gates/startup-gate.ts imports this module for that side effect); `MAX_NATIVE_LINE_CHARS`; `startPiWatchdogs`; the abort wiring; the whole stream pipeline; the `RunSettleState` assembly; and `child.on("error"/"exit"/"close")`. Replace only the pre-spawn/build-and-spawn block with `const spawned: SpawnedRun = spawnPiRun(backend, { raw: rawLog }, runTmp, opts) instanceof Promise ? await ... : ...;` inside the existing inner try/catch that rejects on a synchronous throw, then bind the stream pipeline's `child`/`resolved`/`runSpec`/`invocation`/`parser`/`translator`/`decoder`/`stderrDecoder`/`runMarker`/`preSpawnSessionId`/`blindRead` from the bundle.

**Files touched.** src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/run-spawn.ts (new)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With the same `PiRunOptions`, every path returns the same `PiRunResult`: a setup failure (broken log, ENOSPC tmpdir) still resolves a failed run via `setupFailureResult`; a synchronous throw in the pre-spawn/build-and-spawn stage still rejects the run's promise; a normal run resolves only after both logs flush; the blind-read kill, abort and watchdog kill settle exactly as today.
- `src/agent/run-agent.ts` no longer constructs `PiStreamParser` or calls `makeRunMarker`/`backend.resolveBin`/`backend.prepare`/`backend.invocation`/`spawn`, and its only `recordSession` call is the stream-minted second ledger record in `emitNativeLine` (which moves with the stream pipeline to part 2/2); `src/agent/run-spawn.ts` holds the pre-spawn `recordSession` and every moved call.
- No runtime import cycle: `grep -n 'from "./run-agent.js"' src/agent/run-spawn.ts` shows a type-only import line (`import type { PiRunOptions }`), and run-spawn imports nothing else of run-agent's.
- Every `run-agent.js` export is unchanged; `test/agent-backend.test.ts` still imports `runAgent` and `MAX_NATIVE_LINE_CHARS` from `../src/agent/run-agent.js`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- No new behavior, so no new test module. The existing fake-pi suites are the guard: run `test/pi.test.ts`, `test/pi-watchdogs.test.ts`, `test/agent-backend.test.ts`, `test/claude-run.test.ts`, `test/codex-run.test.ts`, `test/opencode-run.test.ts` and `test/run-resume.test.ts` whole and confirm green.

### `main`'s command switch is split into one named handler per substantial command, so a command's parse-and-dispatch rules are found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/cli.ts' PLANS.md` matches nothing, and no `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names it: the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/cli/cli-role-command.ts and src/cli/help.ts (different files), plus src/config, src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/merge, src/baseline, src/doctor, src/status and src/ui; the in-flight plans edit src/agent, src/pi/pi-stream.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/run/run-verdict.ts and src/run/run-stage.ts, and parts 3n/3 and 3o/3 are test-only; PLANS-DONE.md holds no split of `main` (its `cli.ts` entries are landed behavior changes — the doctor retire/drop-pin flags and the logs notable cull); touches src/cli.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `main` (src/cli.ts) is one ~500-line function: after the Node-floor gate, the `--help` topic gate and the `repoToplevel` read, its switch inlines each substantial command's rules — flag-spec arrays, `rejectUnknownArgs` calls, ready-repo gates, lazy `import(…)` expressions, payload assembly and the exit-code write — so a command's parse-and-dispatch is found only by reading the whole switch. Extract each substantial case body into a module-private async handler beside `runTrailCommand` and leave `main` as the prefix gates plus the dispatch.

**Approach.**
- src/cli.ts: add these module-private handlers (not exported), each the current case body moved verbatim with its comments, and reduce each switch case to `await <handler>(root, args); break;`:
  - `cmdStartCase(root, args)` — the `start`/`run` case: `rejectUnknownArgs("start", args, START_FLAG_SPECS)`, `requireReadyRepo(root)`, the `cmdStart` import and call.
  - `cmdTuiCase(root, args)`, `cmdGuiCase(root, args)`, `cmdNotifyCase(root, args)`, `cmdArchiveCase(root, args)` — the same guard-then-lazy-import shape for their commands: `tui` keeps its two comments and `runTui(root)`; `gui` uses `GUI_FLAG_SPECS`; `notify` its `[{ names: ["--test"] }]`; `archive` its `[JSON_FLAG]`.
  - `cmdConfigCase(root, args)` — the `config` block: the `CONFIG_USAGE` import, the subcommand arity checks, `requireReadyRepo(root)` and `cmdConfig`.
  - `cmdReportCase(root, args)` — the `report` block: its flag specs with the `--days` validator, `refuseTeamWorkspace(root)`, the `cmdReport` import and call.
  - `cmdDoctorCase(root, args)` — the `doctor` block: `peelPositionals`/`rejectUnknownArgs`, `parseDoctorChecks`, the five optional reap flags with their text-vs-`--json` printing, the `withKill`/`withBacklogCommit`/`withResyncInstall`/`withBrokenPinDrop`/`withLeftoverRetire` payload chain, the `--problems` render choice and the `process.exitCode` write.
  - `cmdLogsCase(root, args)` — the `logs` block: its flag specs, `requireReadyRepo(root)` and `cmdLogs`.
  - `cmdHistoryCase(root, args)` — the `history` block: the `cmdHistory`-module import, the `if (historyTrailForm(args)) { await runTrailCommand(root, args); return; }` early exit, its flag specs, `requireReadyRepo(root)` and `cmdHistory`.
  - `cmdBugCase(root, args)` and `cmdPlanCase(root, args)` — the `bug`/`plan` blocks: each keeps its three lazy imports, its `usage` string, its `--show`/`--list`/`--edit`/`--cancel`/`--top`/`--release` arms and its final `fileAndAnnounce` call.
  - `cmdPromptCase(root, args)` — the `prompt` block: its rationale comment, `parsePromptArgs(args)`, `requireReadyRepo(root)` and `cmdPrompt`.
  - `cmdRetireCase(root, args)`, `cmdRevertCase(root, args)`, `cmdStopCase(root, args)` — the operator cases: each keeps its comment, its `rejectUnknownArgs` spec where it has one (`retire` `[ROLE_FLAG, FORCE_FLAG, DRY_RUN_FLAG, JSON_FLAG]`, `stop` `[STOP_IN_FLAG, STOP_CANCEL_FLAG]`, `revert` none), `requireReadyRepo(root)` and its `cmd…` call.
  - `cmdCompletionCase(root, args)` — the `completion` block: the `--roles`/`--config-keys`/`--config-value`/`--models` arms and the shell validation with its two `fail` messages and `completionScript`.
  - `cmdVersionCase(args)` — the `version`/`--version`/`-v` block: `rejectUnknownArgs("version", args, [])`, `packageVersion(PACKAGE_JSON)`, the broken-install `fail` and `say(version)`; takes no `root` because it reads none.
  - `cmdHelpCase(args)` — the `help`/`--help`/`-h`/`undefined` block: the arity check, the topic lookup and `say(topic)`/`write(HELP)`; takes no `root`.
- `main` keeps exactly: the `const [, , command, ...args] = process.argv;` destructure; the `packageEnginesNode`/`nodeFloorProblem` gate; the `helpTopicForArgs` gate; `const root = (await repoToplevel(process.cwd())) ?? process.cwd();`; and the switch, whose substantial cases are now the handler calls above while the short delegated cases stay inline (`init`, `status`, `diff`, `queue`, `reviews`, `backlog`, `quarantine`, `questions`, `brief`, `role`, `tick`, the seven-command `reset-counters`…`restart` fall-through group and `default`), with the same case labels, grouping, `{ … }` blocks and `// vocabulary-ok: command name stays` comment.
- No behavior change: the same flag specs, argument order, gate order, lazy imports, messages and exit codes; every handler is module-private, so no export changes; no module-scope import is added or removed, and each command module stays lazily imported inside its handler, preserving the cold-start rationale in the file header comment.

**Files touched.** src/cli.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `main`'s body is only the argv destructure, the Node-floor gate, the `--help` topic gate, the `root` read and the switch; each substantial case calls exactly one handler and the short delegated cases are unchanged.
- `grep -n 'rejectUnknownArgs\|requireReadyRepo\|parseDoctorChecks\|parsePromptArgs\|refuseTeamWorkspace\|historyTrailForm' src/cli.ts` matches only inside the new `cmd…Case` handlers, never inside `main`.
- Every moved statement, expression, comment, flag-spec array and message is preserved verbatim, in the same order; the only added lines are the handler signatures, their `Promise<void>` return types and the `await <handler>(…);` call lines.
- No handler is exported and no module-scope import is added; the lazy `await import(...)` expressions stay inside the handlers, so a command's module is still loaded only when that command runs.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- No new test module: the CLI suites are the guard. Run `test/cli.test.ts` and the `test/cli-*.test.ts` files whole (arg strictness, flag-value errors, help, preflight, operators, backlog follow, logs, history, queue, questions, status, team-workspace, doctor, start guards) and confirm green.

### `Redeployer.poll`'s 240-line state machine is split into one named private stage method per decision, so a stage's rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no entry under `## Planned` and no blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part names `src/redeploy/redeployer.ts` (the blocked series edits src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config and src/ui with their tests), and the in-flight plans edit src/agent, src/events/event-format.ts, src/config, src/pi/pi-stream.ts and src/ui/status — none src/redeploy; the other `## Planned` files-touched lists name `src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts` only via the landed 2026-10-25 self-redeploy plan, not this file; touches src/redeploy/redeployer.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `Redeployer.poll` (src/redeploy/redeployer.ts) is one ~240-line method that runs the whole self-redeploy state machine inline: observe a moved head, escalate a sustained pin, honour the restart cooldown and its forced-restart waiver, open an episode behind the boot gate, wait on the green check, compile the staged tree, then drain, swap and record the restart. The class already exposes its leaves as named private methods (`endDrain`, `refuse`, `block`, `noteFailure`, `escalateIfSustained`, `bootProblem`, `clearPending`, `consumeForcedRestart`, `effectiveCooldownUntil`, `logRestartPending`, `ensureBuildRedCheck`), so `poll` reads as one long block of their call sites interleaved with the stage rules themselves; a rule is found only by reading the whole method. Extract each stage into a named private method on the same class (all state stays on `this` — no state threading, no behavior change) and leave `poll` as the guard plus the ordered stage calls.

**Approach.**
- src/redeploy/redeployer.ts: add these private methods, each the current inline block moved verbatim with its comments, and reduce `poll` to call them in the same order. Every stage method returns `RedeployAction | null`, where `null` means "proceed to the next stage" and a returned action (`"none"`/`"hold"`/`"restart"`) is `poll`'s result unchanged:
  - `private async observeHead(mainHead: string, now: number): Promise<void>` — the `if (mainHead !== this.lastHead)` block: capture `wasStale`, set `this.lastHead`, `await this.deps.staleness(mainHead)`, log `build_stale`, update `staleSince`/`lastEscalationAt`/`forcedRestart`, and `clearPending()` when a pending head was superseded.
  - `private cooldownStage(mainHead: string, now: number): RedeployAction | null` — `ensureBuildRedCheck` inside the cooldown, `consumeForcedRestart`, `effectiveCooldownUntil`, the deferred-branch warning plus `probes.prewarm` and `endDrain` when still cooled, then the `cooldownWarnedUntil = null` reset and the urgent-early-lapse warning.
  - `private async startEpisode(mainHead: string, inFlight: InFlightCounts, now: number): Promise<RedeployAction | null>` — the `if (this.pendingHead === null)` block: `bootProblem`/`refuse`, set `pendingHead`, start `drainSince`/`drainWindowMs`, adopt the probe's green/compile, `logRestartPending`, return `"hold"` (or `null` when a pending head already exists).
  - `private greenStage(mainHead: string, now: number): RedeployAction | null` — the `!this.green?.done` hold, the `this.green.error` rejected-check branch (note, warn once per head, `clearPending`, `endDrain`) and the `this.green.result !== true` red-verdict branch (`block`, `endDrain`).
  - `private compileStage(mainHead: string, now: number): RedeployAction | null` — the missing/undone compile holds, then the `!c?.ok` branch: `noteFailure`, the rejected/undefined-compile warn-and-`clearPending` path, and the real compiler-exit `block` path.
  - `private async drainAndSwap(mainHead: string, inFlight: InFlightCounts, now: number): Promise<RedeployAction>` — the director/role drain holds, the second `bootProblem`, the `deps.swap` try/catch, `restartRecord.record`, `lastAutoRestartAt`, clearing `staleSince`/`lastEscalationAt`, the `restart` log and `pendingLoggedHead = null`, returning `"restart"`.
- `poll` keeps exactly: `this.autoRestartOn = autoRestart;`; the `!this.selfHosted || !mainHead` guard; `await this.observeHead(...)`; `if (this.staleness?.stale && autoRestart) this.escalateIfSustained(now);`; the `!stale || !autoRestart || blockedHead === mainHead` guard; then `await/const stage = this.cooldownStage(...)` — return when non-null, else `startEpisode`, `greenStage`, `compileStage`, and finally `return this.drainAndSwap(...)`.
- No change to the class's fields, constructor, `status`, `forceRestart`, any existing private method, any exported symbol, or any other file.

**Files touched.** src/redeploy/redeployer.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `poll`'s body is only the two top guards, the escalation call, and the ordered stage calls; it no longer contains the head-observation, cooldown, boot-gate, green-check, compile or drain/swap rules, each of which lives in exactly one named method above.
- Every moved line is preserved verbatim (statements, order and comments); the only added lines are the method headers, the call lines and the `RedeployAction | null` return plumbing.
- No public API change: `Redeployer`, its fields, its constructor, `status`, `forceRestart`, the existing private methods and every exported symbol are unchanged, and no other file is edited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- No new test module: a behavior-preserving move guarded by test/redeployer.test.ts (the cooldown, forced restart, boot-gate refusal, green-check reject/red, compile reject/fail, drain and swap cases), test/redeploy-escalation.test.ts, test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts, test/redeploy-rejected.test.ts, test/redeploy-startup-gate.test.ts, test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts and test/orchestrator-redeploy.test.ts. Run them whole and confirm green.

### `resolveRunVerdict`'s 299-line verdict tree is split into one named arm per decision, so a verdict rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names src/run/run-verdict.ts (the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part 3j/3 edits src/run/run-apply.ts, a different file, and the in-flight plans edit src/agent, src/pi/pi-stream.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts and src/report/report-data.ts), `grep -n 'src/run/run-verdict.ts' PLANS.md` matches nothing, and PLANS-DONE.md holds no split of `resolveRunVerdict` (its `run-verdict.ts` entries are landed behavior changes: the cut-off verdict reach, the config-request check declaration and the tick→run rename); touches src/run/run-verdict.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `resolveRunVerdict` (src/run/run-verdict.ts) classifies one finished pi run into `RunOutcome | null` and is one ~299-line async function: after the resume-missing record, abort guard, `pending.clear()` and the config-request consumption, it walks a verdict tree inline — quiet kill, progressing timeout, hard timeout, subscription-window rejection, budget cap, image-blind reroute, refusal, failed-dirty, revision drop and clean no-change — each arm's guard, `state.lastError` write, requeue and returned outcome written in sequence in the same scope. A rule is found only by reading the whole body. Extract each decision into a module-private arm function beside `abortWithResume`, and leave `resolveRunVerdict` as the setup plus the ordered arm calls.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-verdict.ts: add these module-private arms, each holding the current inline block moved verbatim (statements, order and comments). Every arm returns `RunOutcome` when its guard applies and `undefined` when it does not, so `resolveRunVerdict` returns the first non-`undefined` result and `null` when all fall through:
  - `function quietKillArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `pi.quietKilled` block.
  - `function progressingTimeoutArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `pi.timedOut && pi.timedOutProgressing` block.
  - `function timeoutArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the plain `pi.timedOut` block.
  - `function subscriptionRejectedArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `!pi.ok && ctx.role !== DIRECTOR_ROLE && subscriptionWindowRejected(pi)` block and its `abortWithResume` call.
  - `function budgetCappedArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `pi.budgetCapped` block and its `abortWithResume` call.
  - `function imageBlindArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): RunOutcome | undefined` — the whole `pi.imageBlind` block: the one-hop guard, the `imageReroute` lookup, the `s.imageReroute` assignment, the `image_reroute` event and every return.
  - `async function refusalArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): Promise<RunOutcome | undefined>` — the `pi.refused` block: `refusalContradiction`, the contradicted warning (which returns `undefined` to fall through) and the `handleRefusal` call.
  - `function failedRunArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext, changed: boolean): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `!pi.ok && (!changed || !pi.producedAssistantContent)` block.
  - `async function revisionDropArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext): Promise<RunOutcome | undefined>` — the `pi.nothingToDo && ctx.revisionRound !== undefined && s.revision !== undefined` block: the rejected-ref reset, `resetWorktreeToMain`, `deleteRef`, the `revision` `dropped` event and its `no_change` return.
  - `function noChangeArm(ctx: RunVerdictContext, changed: boolean): RunOutcome | undefined` — the `!changed` block: `diagnoseNoChange`, the without-changes warning, the cut-off requeue, and the flow/filed/ci recording plus the summary, returning the `no_change` outcome.
- `resolveRunVerdict` keeps exactly: `const { pi, state: s } = ctx;`; the `resumeMissing` record with its comment; `if (pi.aborted) return ctx.finishAbortedRun();`; `ctx.pending.clear();`; the config-request consumption with its comment; then `let arm = quietKillArm(ctx); if (arm) return arm;` through `imageBlindArm`, `arm = await refusalArm(ctx)`, `const changed = await isDirty(ctx.wt);`, `arm = failedRunArm(ctx, changed)`, `arm = await revisionDropArm(ctx)`, `arm = noChangeArm(ctx, changed)`, and `return null;` — the same order and short-circuiting as today.
- Keep `abortWithResume` as it is (the two arms call it). No change to `RunVerdictContext`'s fields (it stays module-private), to any exported symbol, or to any other file.
- docs/invariants.md is not edited: the sections that bind `resolveRunVerdict` (the flow/feedback/qa-coverage/ci-parity write guarantees and the image-reroute arm) name the function and its tests, which a pure move leaves unchanged.

**Files touched.** src/run/run-verdict.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `resolveRunVerdict`'s body is only the destructure, the resume-missing record, the abort guard, `pending.clear()`, the config-request consumption and the ordered arm calls; it no longer contains the quiet-kill, timeout, subscription, budget, image-blind, refusal, failed-dirty, revision-drop or no-change rules, each of which lives in exactly one named arm above.
- Every moved statement, expression and comment is preserved verbatim; the returned outcome objects, the `state.lastError` strings, the warning texts and the logged event payloads are identical to the current ones.
- Every arm's guard is unchanged, and the arms run in the same order with the same fall-through as today, so `resolveRunVerdict` returns the identical `RunOutcome | null` for every input.
- No public API change: `resolveRunVerdict` keeps its signature, `RunVerdictContext` and `abortWithResume` stay as they are, and no other file is edited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- No new test module: a behavior-preserving move guarded by test/run-verdict.test.ts (the abort/resume, quiet-kill, progressing-timeout, timeout, subscription-window, budget-cap, image-blind/reroute, refusal, failed-dirty, revision-drop and no-change arms, including the qa flow and ci parity recording and their failed-write warnings), plus test/run-resume.test.ts and test/revision.test.ts. Run them whole and confirm green.

### `PiStreamParser.feedLine`'s 176-line per-event application is split into one named private applier per event family, so a family's fold is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — `grep -n 'src/pi/' PLANS.md` matches nothing and no `## Planned` entry's Files-touched list names src/pi/pi-stream.ts (the in-flight run-agent split names `PiStreamParser` only inside its `SpawnedRun` interface prose and edits src/agent/run-agent.ts and src/agent/run-spawn.ts, not src/pi/pi-stream.ts), and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` series edits src/review, src/orchestrator, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/merge, src/baseline, src/status, src/doctor, src/config and src/ui with their tests, so none lists src/pi/pi-stream.ts; touches src/pi/pi-stream.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `PiStreamParser.feedLine` (src/pi/pi-stream.ts) is one 176-line method that parses one log line, classifies its error texts, folds cost, usage, rate-limit and billing, counts progress, tracks tool calls and folds the assistant `message_end` — each concern written inline in sequence, sharing the parser's fields directly. Its sibling dispatches have already been split by name (`foldUsageEvent`, `eventMessage`), leaving this as the one remaining inline event application. Extract each event family into a named private method on the same class (so every extract still reads and writes `this` — no state threading, no behavior change) and leave `feedLine` as the parse → classify → apply sequence.

**Approach.**

### `RunnerPi.runWithTransientRetry`'s ~100-line transient-retry machine is split into one named private method per decision, so a retry rule is found by name (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no entry under `## Planned` and no blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part names `src/runner/runner-pi.ts` or `test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts` (the blocked series edits `src/runner/runner-run.ts`, `src/runner/leftover.ts` and `src/runner/runner-state.ts`, and the in-flight plans edit src/agent, src/ui, src/config, src/pi and src/redeploy), and PLANS-DONE.md holds no split of this method (its `runner-pi.ts` entries name the never-throws fix and the seam-naming warning, both landed behavior changes); touches src/runner/runner-pi.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `RunnerPi.runWithTransientRetry` (src/runner/runner-pi.ts) is the one bounded transient retry every pi agent run goes through, and its decision rules sit inline in one ~100-line method: the multi-term admission predicate (the `!aborted && !timedOut && !quietKilled && (transient*) && !ok && !subscriptionWindowRejected` guard), the warning-text ladder (pi crash / 429-with-hint / stream-severed / timeout / idle-predict), the wait ladder (the Retry-After hint, its cap, and the hint-less refill pause), and the continuation attempt (the `continueSession` re-run and its folds/warnings). A rule is found only by reading the whole method. Extract each rule into a named private method on the same class (all state stays on `this`, the local `fold` closure is passed as a parameter — no behavior change) and leave `runWithTransientRetry` as the seam/fold setup, the first attempt, and the ordered calls.

**Approach.**
- src/runner/runner-pi.ts: add these private methods, each the current inline block moved verbatim with its comments:
  - `private transientRetryAdmits(run: PiRunResult): boolean` — the whole `if` condition, comments included (including the `subscriptionWindowRejected` clause and its comment); `runWithTransientRetry` calls `if (this.transientRetryAdmits(pi))`.
  - `private transientRetryWarning(run: PiRunResult, on: string): string` — the `this.host.warn(...)` argument ternary ladder, returned as a string; `runWithTransientRetry` calls `this.host.warn(this.transientRetryWarning(pi, on))`.
  - `private transientRetryWaitSeconds(run: PiRunResult): number` — the `hintS`/`waitS` computation (a non-positive hint falls back to `RATE_LIMIT_NO_HINT_RETRY_S`, the cap applies only to the 429 kind, timeout takes `RATE_LIMIT_NO_HINT_RETRY_S`), returned; `runWithTransientRetry` keeps the `if (waitS > 0) await (this.host.sleep?.(waitS * 1000) ?? sleepFor(waitS * 1000))` line.
  - `private async retryContinuingSession(opts: PiRunOptions, on: string, foldFinal: boolean, fold: (run: PiRunResult) => void): Promise<PiRunResult>` — the `const retry = await runPi({ ...opts, continueSession: true })`, its `warnFallbackClone`/`observeFreeModelCost`, the `if (foldFinal) fold(retry)`, the `warnBackendKindFloor(retry, on)` and the `return retry`, in that order; `runWithTransientRetry` returns its result.
- `runWithTransientRetry` keeps exactly: the `provider`/`pair`/`on`/`fold` setup, `await ensureProviderLease(opts.config)`, the first `runPi` plus its `warnFallbackClone`/`observeFreeModelCost`, `if (this.transientRetryAdmits(pi)) { this.host.warn(this.transientRetryWarning(pi, on)); fold(pi); const waitS = this.transientRetryWaitSeconds(pi); if (waitS > 0) await ...; return this.retryContinuingSession(opts, on, foldFinal, fold); }`, then `this.warnBackendKindFloor(pi, on); if (foldFinal) fold(pi); return pi;`.
- No change to the class's fields, constructor, `runRolePi`, `runMergePi`, `runGatePi`, `warnBackendKindFloor`, `retryCoversBackendKind`, any exported symbol, the two `RATE_LIMIT_*` constants, or any other file.

### A `maxConcurrentPerProvider` map that cannot do its job raises a standing amber alert — the doctor `provider concurrency` row's twin (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in behavior and files of the three in-flight over-cap alerts, which add a `snap` field and an alert at `team-alert-status.ts`'s `noBrief` clause while this adds a doctor-derived feed argument and its arm in `team-alert-tail.ts` beside `provider-hold`; no `## Planned` entry and no blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part edits `src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts`, `src/ui/alert-feeds.ts` or `src/ui/team-alert-tail.ts`; it shares `src/ui/team-alerts.ts` with the three plans at the positional argument list (this appends a trailing `providerCaps` argument; they add literals to the `snap` Pick above it), `src/ui/status-payload.ts` at the `teamAlerts(...)` call (this) against the payload field (they), and `docs/cli.md`'s `Check state` row with all three, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts src/ui/alert-feeds.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/team-alert-tail.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/cli.md docs/config.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor`'s `provider concurrency` row (`checkProviderConcurrency`, src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts) warns when a `maxConcurrentPerProvider` map cannot do its job: a cap key no seam resolves to (a typo, or a provider the team never runs on), a cap at or above `maxConcurrent` (it never binds), or a keyless seam in a capped team. The landed `contention` alert is the twin of the wait rows and fires only once a too-small cap has already parked runs; the `provider-hold` alert fires only after a provider storm. The static misconfiguration itself is visible only by running `tumwater doctor` (or opening the dashboard Health card), so an operator watching `tumwater status` sees role rows with an intended cap that silently does nothing. Add the always-on twin: a standing amber `provider-caps` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI, from the same predicate the doctor row uses.

**Approach.**

### The agent-run setup failure closes the logs it opened — INV-CQ1's fd-leak closing gets its test (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — no `## Planned` entry edits test/pi.test.ts, and the only `## Planned` edits to docs/invariants.md are the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part 3m/3's merge-gate section, far from the end-of-file INV-CQ1 — touching the same two files only at distant regions, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches test/pi.test.ts docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `runAgent` (src/agent/run-agent.ts) opens the raw and native append logs inside its setup `try` and, when a later setup step throws — `fs.mkdtempSync` for the run scratch dir, or the second `openAppendLog` — its `catch` calls `rawLog?.stream.end()` and `nativeLog?.stream.end()` before resolving the failed run, so no fd is leaked. docs/invariants.md's INV-CQ1 states this, and its **Guarantee** ends "A log opened before the failure is ended so no fd stays open; no test pins that closing." The two pinned setup-failure tests assert only `ok === false` and the error message, so a regression that dropped the two `end()` calls would leave the suite green while leaking one or two fds per failed run in the long-lived supervisor. Pin the closing at both failure timings and drop the caveat.

**Approach.**
- test/pi.test.ts, the existing `an agent run whose scratch dir cannot be created resolves as a failed run`: capture the streams `runAgent` opens by wrapping `fs.createWriteStream` through `patchFsMethod` (already imported) around the `runPi` call — record each returned `fs.WriteStream` and fall through — and restore it in the same `finally` that restores the `mkdtempSync` patch. After the run resolves, assert two streams were captured (the raw and native logs) and each `writableEnded === true`. This is the "both logs opened, a later setup step failed" timing.
- test/pi.test.ts, add `an agent run that cannot open its second log ends the first`: under `withPi` with the same one-line-assistant script, patch `createWriteStream` to throw `errnoError("EACCES")` on its second call and capture the first stream; call `runPi(runPiFixture(dir))`; assert `ok === false` and `errorMessage` matches `/^could not prepare the agent run: EACCES/`; after restoring, assert exactly one stream was captured and its `writableEnded === true`. This is the "first log opened, opening the second failed" timing. `runPiFixture` already supplies both `rawLogFile` and `nativeLogFile`, and `openAppendLog` calls `fs.createWriteStream` synchronously before the spawn, so the two calls are the only ones under the patch.
- docs/invariants.md, INV-CQ1: delete the "no test pins that closing" clause so the **Guarantee** ends "A log opened before the failure is ended so no fd stays open."; in **Pinned by**, name the new test beside the two existing names and say the scratch-dir case also asserts both opened logs are ended.

### The role-prompt backlog block names the named items it drops instead of truncating silently (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan and blocked part — no entry in `## Planned` and no `Every commit is verified on main` part edits `src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts` or `test/notes-backlog.test.ts`, and no other module writes that block; touches src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts test/notes-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `notesBacklogBlock` (src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts) renders "what the backlog says now about entries your notes name" so a note cannot keep a hold the backlog has lifted. It builds one line per named series, named part and named entry, then caps the block — `const shown = lines.slice(0, MAX_BLOCK_LINES - 1);` — and drops every line past the cap with no marker (the block is documented "at most 12 lines"). A role whose notes name more than eleven live items therefore reads a block that looks complete while the tail — often the very item whose hold changed — is gone, the same silent truncation the failure digest's capped sections no longer allow. The cap stays; the block names its remainder so a dropped item cannot read as a complete answer.

**Approach.**
- src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts, `notesBacklogBlock`'s tail: keep the `if (lines.length === 0) return undefined;` guard, then branch on the cap instead of slicing it blindly — `const cap = MAX_BLOCK_LINES - 1;` (the item lines; the header is the twelfth line). When `lines.length <= cap`, return `[HEADER, ...lines].join("\n")` exactly as today, so a block of eleven or fewer items is byte-identical. Otherwise `const shown = lines.slice(0, cap - 1);` and return `[HEADER, ...shown, `… and ${plural(lines.length - shown.length, "more named item")}`].join("\n")` — the remainder line replaces the would-be last shown item, so the block is still exactly `MAX_BLOCK_LINES` lines. `plural` is already imported.
- Update `notesBacklogBlock`'s doc comment (and `MAX_BLOCK_LINES`'s doc if it names the cap): the block is at most 12 lines and, when the notes name more items than fit, its last line says how many were dropped (`… and N more named items`).

**Files touched.** src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts test/notes-backlog.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Eleven or fewer named items render exactly as today — same lines, same order, no remainder line — so a normal block is byte-identical.
- More than eleven named items render at most 12 lines, and the last line is `… and N more named items`, where N is the number of built lines past the shown ones (for the existing forty-part fixture, `… and 31 more named items`). The header stays the first line, and the named-series line stays ahead of the part lines the block still shows.

### `tumwater history <role> <n>`'s header names the run's prompt tokens and their cache-read share — the last unsurfaced `run_end` usage fields (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; the sibling of the landed `peak ctx` run-detail plan, which added the previous `run_end` field to the same header; independent in files of every eligible plan and blocked part — no `## Planned` entry and no `Every commit is verified on main` part edits src/run/run-detail-data.ts, src/run/run-detail-render.ts, test/run-detail-data.test.ts or test/run-detail.test.ts, and it shares docs/cli.md only at the `Watch run history` row (this plan) while the in-flight brief and quarantine-release plans extend the `Check state` and `Control the roles` rows, so whichever lands second rebases at a distant row; touches src/run/run-detail-data.ts src/run/run-detail-render.ts docs/cli.md test/run-detail-data.test.ts test/run-detail.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

An expensive run whose cost is almost all uncached input therefore reads as a small `tok` count beside a large `$`, with no way to see the input side or how much the backend cached. `renderRunDetail` (src/run/run-detail-render.ts) is the one header the CLI, the TUI trail and the dashboard drill-down all render, so adding the run's prompt tokens and the share served from cache there surfaces it on every trail at once.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-detail-data.ts, `RunDetail`: add optional `promptTokens?: number` and `cacheReadTokens?: number`, doc-commented as the `run_end`'s prompt-token total and its cache-read subset (clamped to the total), both absent on a run that reported none and on an in-flight run — the `peakContextTokens` omit-when-zero shape, so a prompt-free or old-log run keeps today's exact payload. In `detailFrom`, beside the `peakContextTokens` read, `const promptTokens = end === null ? 0 : nonNegativeNumber(end.promptTokens, 0); const cacheReadTokens = end === null ? 0 : Math.min(nonNegativeNumber(end.cacheReadTokens, 0), promptTokens);` and spread `...(promptTokens > 0 ? { promptTokens } : {})` and `...(cacheReadTokens > 0 ? { cacheReadTokens } : {})` into the returned literal (`nonNegativeNumber` is already imported).
- src/run/run-detail-render.ts, `renderRunDetail`: after the `usage` summary push and before the peak-context push, when `(d.promptTokens ?? 0) > 0` push `` `prompt ${compactTokens(prompt)} tok` `` plus `` ` (${Math.round((100 * cached) / prompt)}% cached)` `` when `cached > 0`, with `const prompt = d.promptTokens ?? 0; const cached = Math.min(d.cacheReadTokens ?? 0, prompt);`. The `${n}% cached` wording and rounding are the report's `Prompt tokens by role` share; a run with prompt tokens and no cache reads shows no parenthetical, and a run with neither keeps today's header byte-identical. Import `compactTokens` from `../text/format.js`.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater history <role> <n>` clause of the `Watch run history` row: after "usage", name the run's prompt tokens and cache-read share — `` its prompt tokens and the share served from cache (`prompt 100.0k tok (80% cached)`, dropped when the run reported none) ``.

### `tumwater doctor`'s `brief` row warns when the brief's prompt block exceeds the 4096-character read cap — the hand-edited brief every role sees truncated (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible and blocked entry — `grep -rn 'BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS\|promptBlockOf\|brief truncated' PLANS.md BUGS.md PLANS-DONE.md` finds no entry naming the read-side brief cap in doctor, and no `## Planned` entry edits `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`; it shares only `test/doctor-checks.test.ts` with the in-flight `role notes` plan, which appends its own `checkRoleNotes` test there, and no source file with it (that plan's sources are `doctor-role-notes.ts`/`doctor.ts`/`doctor-check-names.ts`); the in-flight quarantine-release, Activity-hint and failure-digest plans edit `src/review`, `src/gui`, `src/ui/tui` and `src/failure`, and the blocked `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit `src/config`, `src/orchestrator`, `src/runner`, `src/merge`, `src/status` and `src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts`, not `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`; touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every run's prompt carries the project brief read through `readBrief` (`src/brief/brief.ts`), whose `extractPrompt` calls `truncateWithNote(prompt, BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS, "brief")` — so a brief block longer than `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` (4096) is cut and each role's prompt carries only the head plus `…[brief truncated at 4096 chars]`. Every writer already refuses an over-cap brief: `initProject` (`src/init/init.ts`) rejects an over-long seed, and `editBriefText` (`src/brief/brief-edit.ts`) rejects `tumwater brief --file`, `--edit` and the dashboard's Brief Save. The only way to exceed it is a hand edit (or a pre-existing repo), and the backstop is silent: `checkBrief` (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) reports `brief in README.md` `ok` as soon as it finds a marked file, never looking at the block's length. So either the operator sees a green `brief` row while every role runs on a truncated project brief, or — because the truncation note rides in the prompt — nothing tells them which length is the cap or how to fix it. Make the `brief` row warn when the resolved block is over the cap.

**Approach.**
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`, `checkBrief`: keep the `briefFile`/throw handling and the two existing `warn`/`no brief file` branches, and replace the `if (owner) return okOutcome("brief in ${owner}")` early return. When `owner` is non-null, read the file's raw text with `readTextOrNull(path.join(root, owner))` and extract its block with `promptBlockOf`; when the block is non-null and `block.length > BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`, return `warnOutcome` naming `owner`, the block's character count, the cap, the visible marker the role sees, and the fix (a hand edit of the block in the owner file, or the dashboard's Brief card). Otherwise return the current `okOutcome`. Add `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` and `promptBlockOf` to the existing `../brief/brief.js` import beside `briefFile`; `readTextOrNull` and `path` are already imported.
- Compare **characters**, not bytes: `truncateWithNote` cuts on `text.length` (UTF-16 code units), and `promptBlockOf` returns the same trimmed slice `extractPrompt` truncates (both trim the block between the first start and first end marker). `owner` from `briefFile` is the resolved basename (`README.md` or `TUMWATER.md`, `TUMWATER.md` winning when both are marked), so `path.join(root, owner)` reads the same file `readBrief` read. A `readTextOrNull` that returns `null` after `briefFile` succeeded falls back to `okOutcome`, matching today's behavior rather than crashing.
- No change to `extractPrompt`, `truncateWithNote`, `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`, the write paths, or `briefBlockMissing` (the always-on `no-brief` alert is the missing-marker state, a different finding). The row keeps its name and position, so `src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts` and `src/doctor/doctor.ts` are untouched.
- docs: none — `docs/cli.md` and `docs/how-it-works.md` do not itemize the `brief` row's ok/warn detail, and no invariant pins it; the warning is self-describing.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A repo whose brief block is longer than `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` characters makes the `brief` row `warn`, naming the resolved file, the block's character count, the 4096 cap, and an executable fix (a hand edit of the block or the dashboard's Brief card); the `brief` row for a block of exactly `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` characters, one under it, and the existing short marked-README/marked-TUMWATER.md cases still reads `{ level: "ok", detail: "brief in <file>" }`.
- The over-cap warn names the resolved owner (`README.md`, or `TUMWATER.md` when both are marked) and counts the characters of the block the prompt truncates, not the whole file and not its bytes.
- The unreadable-brief cases still `fail` with the same messages; the no-brief and README-without-markers cases still `warn` unchanged; the `brief` row's name and report position are unchanged.
- No file outside the Files-touched list is edited; `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts: add `checkBrief warns when the brief block is over the read cap` — `import { BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS } from "../src/brief/brief.js"` beside the existing imports; in a `makeRepo()`, write a README.md with `<!-- tumwater:prompt:start -->` / `<!-- tumwater:prompt:end -->` around `"x".repeat(BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS + 50)` and assert `checkBrief(repo).level === "warn"` with `detail` matching `/README\.md/`, `/4096/`, the count, and `/hand-edit/`; in a second `makeRepo()`, write the same shape with exactly `BRIEF_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` characters and assert the exact `{ level: "ok", detail: "brief in README.md" }`; add a TUMWATER.md over the cap beside a short marked README.md and assert the warn names `TUMWATER.md`.

### A role's notes file that the run prompt truncates is named by `tumwater doctor` — the read-side cap no operator surface reports (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible and blocked entry — `grep -n 'doctor-role-notes\|doctor-check-names\|doctor/doctor.ts' PLANS.md BUGS.md` finds no entry under `## Planned` naming these, and the in-flight dashboard/TUI quarantine-release, Activity-hint and failure-digest classification plans touch `src/review`, `src/gui`, `src/ui/tui` and `src/failure`, none of this plan's files, and it edits no `docs/cli.md`, so it shares no file with the in-flight `tumwater archive` or Activity-hint plans; no blocked `Every commit is verified on main` part edits `src/doctor` or `src/run/run-prompt.ts`; touches src/doctor/doctor-role-notes.ts (new) src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES` (src/agent/role-notes-write.ts) bounds a role's notes on write, but `readRoleNote` (src/run/run-prompt.ts) also bounds on read: a notes file over the cap that a hand edit or an old build left behind is cut, and `truncateWithNote` marks it `…[role notes truncated at 4096 chars]` in that role's prompt — so the role reads only the head of its own cross-run memory. Every operator surface reads the same file whole instead: `role-view.ts` reads it through `readTextOrNull` for `tumwater role <id>` and the TUI notes view, and the dashboard drawer edits the full text, so an operator sees notes the role never does. Nothing reports the gap: `grep -n 'ROLE_NOTES_MAX\|role notes' src/doctor` finds no check. Add a `role notes` doctor row that warns when the prompt would truncate a role's notes, naming the role, the size, and the fix.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-role-notes.ts (new): `export function checkRoleNotes(root: string): CheckOutcome` — `import { readdirSync } from "node:fs"`, `import path from "node:path"`, `import { readTextOrNull } from "../files/files.js"`, `import { roleNotesPath } from "../paths.js"`, `import { ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES } from "../agent/role-notes-write.js"`, and `okOutcome`/`warnOutcome` from `./outcome.js`. Compute the notes dir as `path.dirname(roleNotesPath(root, "role"))`; a missing or unreadable dir returns `okOutcome("no role notes recorded yet")`. For each entry whose name ends in `.md`, read it with `readTextOrNull`; skip null/unreadable files, and collect `{ role: name.slice(0, -3), chars: text.length }` when `text.length > ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES`. The bound is the read's own unit — `truncateWithNote` cuts on `text.length` (UTF-16 characters), not the write path's `Buffer.byteLength`, so the check must compare characters too or a multibyte note the prompt reads in full (e.g. 8000 bytes of emoji, 4000 characters) would false-positive; do NOT use `statSync().size`. If none collected, `okOutcome("every role note is within the 4096-character read bound")`. Otherwise `warnOutcome` naming the roles by byte-size descending with the count of characters, the largest first (cap the named roles at 3 and append `and N more` like the other doctor rows), and the fix: the role's prompt shows only the truncated head, so rewrite the note under the cap (`tumwater role <id> --notes-file <path>` or the `tumwater-notes` shim the run is told to use). Read-only against `.tumwater/`, like every check.
- src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts: add `"role notes"` to `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` directly after `"qa coverage"` (beside the other per-role observer rows), keeping the array's report order.
- src/doctor/doctor.ts: import `checkRoleNotes` beside `checkQaCoverage` and insert `{ name: "role notes", run: () => checkRoleNotes(root) },` directly after the `qa coverage` step. No other step or option changes; the row appears unconditionally, so a named run is `tumwater doctor "role notes"`.
- No change to `ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES`, `readRoleNote`, `validateRoleNote`, `role-view.ts`'s full-file read, or any alert/snapshot payload: this plan adds a doctor diagnostic only, and the dashboard Health card and TUI Health already render every doctor row through the shared report.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A `.tumwater/state/notes/<role>.md` file whose text is longer than `ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES` characters makes the `role notes` row `warn`, naming the role and the truncated character count; a file of exactly `ROLE_NOTES_MAX_BYTES` characters, a file under it, an empty notes directory, and a missing notes directory each read `ok` and name no role.
- `tumwater doctor` prints the row in report order after `qa coverage`, `tumwater doctor --json` carries it, and `tumwater doctor "role notes"` runs only it (per `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES`).
- Every other check's level and detail is unchanged, and no file outside the Files-touched list is edited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**

The ready repo has no notes, so the row reads `ok` like the rest.

**Goal.** `tumwater abort --role <id>[,<id>...]` aborts the listed roles' runs, and the dashboard's per-row Stop button aborts one role — but there is no way to abort every running role at once. `pause` and `stop` stop only NEW work (in-flight runs finish, each burning tokens until its `runTimeoutSeconds`), so an operator watching a runaway spend or a wedged fleet must list every running role by name. Add `tumwater abort --all`, one marker per enabled runner id through the existing `requestAbort` core, so the next poll cancels every in-flight run and every merge those roles own; give it the dashboard twin, an Abort all button on the Roles card, and leave the CLI's bare `abort` and per-role `abort --role` unchanged.

**Approach.**
- src/operator/operator-intent.ts: add `export function requestAbortAll(root: string): RequestResult` beside `requestAbort`. Return `{ ok: false, error: NO_HARNESS_ERROR }` when `orchestratorAlive(root)` is false (the same error and one-check shape `requestAbort` returns), `{ ok: false, error: "no roles are enabled to abort" }` when `runnerIds(loadConfigCached(root).config)` is empty, else `writeJsonAtomic(abortRequestPath(root, role), { at: Date.now() })` for every id and return `{ ok: true, message: `abort requested for ${ids.length} ${plural(ids.length, "role", "roles")} — the running team applies each within ~2s` }`. Import `runnerIds` from `../roles/runner-ids.js` (the module already imports `baseRoleOf` there) and reuse the already-imported `plural`/`loadConfigCached`/`orchestratorAlive`/`writeJsonAtomic`/`abortRequestPath`. Idle roles' markers are removed by `consumeAbortRequests`' per-marker sweep without aborting anything (`removeQuiet` runs even when no runner matches), so passing every enabled id is the same safe no-op it is for `abort --role` of an idle role.
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: add `export const ABORT_ALL_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--all"] };` beside `ROLE_FLAG`, documenting that `abort` alone takes it.

### A role stuck in a context-ceiling cut-off loop warns once and its row reads `cut off ×N` — the `cutOffStreak` no surface reads (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan — the in-flight history plan edits src/history/* and src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, the failure-digest plan edits src/failure/*, the usage-report plan edits src/report/*, and no-check 2/2 edits src/backlog/*, src/roles/*, a distant src/ui/team-alerts.ts block and test/status-payload.test.ts's other cases, none of which this plan's sources touch; the blocked part 3j/3 deletes a distant `changeGone` clear in src/run/run-apply.ts and part 3f/3 removes the `main red` label in src/ui/status-model.ts, so whichever lands second rebases at those seams; touches src/run/run-apply.ts src/run/run-finalize.ts src/ui/status-model.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-model.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-roles.ts docs/backends.md test/run-finalize.test.ts test/status-model.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts test/gui-client-roles.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** A run truncated at its model's context ceiling ends `no_change` with `RunOutcome.cutOff` (src/verdict/no-change.ts), `applyRunOutcome` counts it in `RunnerState.cutOffStreak`, and the harness resumes the compacted session until `CUT_OFF_RESUME_LIMIT` (3) consecutive cut-offs, then abandons the task for a fresh run (src/run/run-apply.ts). Every per-run surface now names a *single* cut-off — the run trail header, the `history` run table, and the failure digest's loss ranking — but the *episode* is invisible: only the next prompt's `buildCutOffNote` reads `cutOffStreak`, so a role cycling cut-off→resume burns an hour-plus per cycle (the file's own comment) with no operator signal, and its resting state cell meanwhile reads the benign ` · no change ×N` (a cut-off run is a `no_change`, so `noChangeStreak` counts it too). The error and quiet-kill streaks each raise exactly one warning when they cross; give the cut-off streak the same crossing warning and a ` · cut off ×N` cell so the operator can intervene — split the task, or raise the model's context window — before the give-up.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-apply.ts: export `CUT_OFF_RESUME_LIMIT` (currently a module-private `const = 3`) beside `QUIET_KILL_RESUME_LIMIT`, and extend its doc comment to name the crossing warning (`run-finalize.ts`) and the cell suffix (`status-model.ts` `rolePhase`), as `QUIET_KILL_RESUME_LIMIT`'s already names run-finalize. No behavior change in this file.
- src/run/run-finalize.ts: import `CUT_OFF_RESUME_LIMIT` and, right after the quiet-kill crossing block (which follows `applyRunOutcome`, so `s.cutOffStreak` already holds the new count), add its cut-off twin: `if (outcome.cutOff === true && (s.cutOffStreak ?? 0) === CUT_OFF_RESUME_LIMIT) warnEventBestEffort(root, role, ...)`. The `outcome.cutOff` guard makes it fire only on the run that increments the streak to the limit — every non-cut-off run resets the streak to 0 and a later cut-off sits above the limit — so exactly one warning per episode, the same once-per-episode rule the error and quiet-kill crossings use. Message: `` `${s.cutOffStreak} consecutive runs cut off at the context ceiling; give the role a smaller task or a longer context window` ``. No role guard, matching quiet-kill (a cut-off director prompt is re-queued but its streak still counts).
- src/ui/status-model.ts, `rolePhase`'s resting-cell suffix (the block that reads `s.noChangeStreak`): read `const cutOff = s.cutOffStreak ?? 0;` and prefer it — when `cutOff >= 2`, append `` ` · cut off ×${cutOff}` ``; otherwise keep today's `noChangeStreak >= 2` → ` · no change ×N` branch — doc-commented that a cut-off run is a `no_change`, so `noChangeStreak` counts it too and the plain suffix mislabels a window-burning episode as a benign idle one; cut-off wins because it names the costly cause. Observational only (no early return, no warning from here) and N=1 stays bare, exactly like the no-change suffix. This is the one home of the rendered phase, so the CLI `status` table and the TUI (status-render.ts's `renderStatusSpans` → `roleRowCells` → `rolePhase`) gain the label together.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: add `cutOffStreak: s.cutOffStreak ?? 0` beside `noChangeStreak` (same doc-comment shape) so the browser row's JS twin can apply the same precedence without re-parsing the phase text.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-model.ts, `phaseInfo`: extend the strip regex `/ · no change ×\d+$/` to `/ · (?:no change|cut off) ×\d+$/` so the new suffix cannot pollute the parsed key or detail.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-roles.ts, `phaseDetailBase`: build one suffix from the payload — `const cutOff = (l.cutOffStreak || 0) >= 2 ? " · cut off ×" + l.cutOffStreak : "";` then `const streak = cutOff || noChange;` — and append `streak` at the three sites that currently append `noChange` (`sleeping`, `queued`, and the default return), updating the comment to name both. The GUI shows `cut off ×N` for a cut-off episode and `no change ×N` otherwise, exactly as the phase text does.
- docs/backends.md, the "Truncated-at-the-ceiling turns look like normal stops" bullet that already documents the 3-cut-off give-up: add one sentence that the crossing logs one warning and the role's row reads `cut off ×N`, so the operator sees the episode before the harness abandons the task.

### `tumwater quarantine --release <n>` retires a quarantined flaky test the gate is excusing (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every in-flight and blocked entry — `grep -n 'quarantine\|known-flakes' PLANS.md` finds no entry under `## Planned`, and the five in-flight plans edit src/backlog+src/roles+src/run/run-prompt+src/prompt+src/doctor/doctor-project-checks (no-check 2/2), src/report (usage report), src/failure (failure digest), src/history+src/ui/gui/gui-client-history (history run table) and src/run/run-apply+src/run/run-finalize+src/ui/status-model+src/ui/status-payload+src/ui/gui/gui-client-model+src/ui/gui/gui-client-roles+docs/backends.md (cut-off episode); the blocked part 3d/3 edits src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md at the `--review-after-merge` clauses while this plan edits the quarantine stanza and clause, and the in-flight no-check 2/2 and history plans each append a clause to the same docs/cli.md table row, so whichever lands second rebases at those distant cells; touches src/review/known-flakes.ts src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/known-flakes.test.ts test/cli-quarantine.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** The flake quarantine (`.tumwater/state/quarantine.json`) is the review gate's memory of tests that failed then passed on the same tree: a red check naming only quarantined tests is treated as a known failure rather than a verdict (`onlyQuarantined`, src/review/known-flakes.ts, and `onlyKnownMainFailures`/`knownMainFailures`, src/baseline/main-watch.ts), so the suite's red is excused while the entry stands. Today the operator surfaces are read-only — `tumwater quarantine` lists the entries (src/review/quarantine-render.ts), and the amber `quarantine` alert and the doctor's `flaky checks` row share `quarantineWarning` (src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts) — and the one exit, `releaseQuarantine` (src/review/known-flakes.ts), fires only when the BUGS.md entry filed for a test leaves `## Open`. An operator who fixes a flake by hand, judges a quarantine entry wrong, or wants to stop excusing a test before its bug closes has no action: the command's own help says "read-only — a test leaves the list only when its filed bug leaves BUGS.md `## Open`", while the alert advises "fix the test or file the missing bug". Add `tumwater quarantine --release <n>`, the deliberate-removal verb `tumwater reviews --accept <n>` and `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` already have, so the operator can act without hand-editing `.tumwater/state/quarantine.json`.

**Approach.**
- src/review/known-flakes.ts: add `releaseQuarantinedTest(root: string, test: string): boolean` beside `releaseQuarantine`. It loads the list, removes the one entry whose `test` matches exactly, and saves through `tryOrWarn(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, ...)` (the `quarantineTests` failure contract: a failed write warns and changes nothing). It logs one `warning` under `TUMWATER_SOURCE` via `warnEventBestEffort(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, ...)` — `` `${test} released from the flake quarantine at the operator's request — the gate no longer excuses its failures` `` — and returns whether the entry was present and the write succeeded, so the caller can answer a concurrent removal. The doc comment names it the manual twin of `releaseQuarantine`'s automatic release and the CLI as its one caller. `releaseQuarantine` (plural) is unchanged.
- src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts: `cmdQuarantine` routes `if (args.includes("--release")) { await cmdQuarantineRelease(root, args); return; }` before its `rejectUnknownArgs`, exactly as `cmdReviews` routes `--accept` (src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts). `cmdQuarantineRelease` parses with `scanPositionArgs(args, "--release", "--release 2")` (the `cmdReviewsAccept` idiom: `--release <n>` the one valued flag, `--json` the one boolean, `--help`/`-h` tolerated, `rejectUnknownArgs("quarantine", rest, [])` for the rest), fails `--release needs a position (usage: tumwater quarantine --release <n>)` when absent, gates with `requireReadyRepo(root)` (the read path keeps its no-gate `refuseTeamWorkspace` stance), then resolves the position against `quarantineRows(loadQuarantine(root))` — the same oldest-first 1..N list `tumwater quarantine` prints — failing `no quarantined test at position <n> (flake quarantine holds <depth> tests)` out of range. It calls `releaseQuarantinedTest(root, rows[position - 1]!.test)`: `--json` prints `{ released: { position, test } }`; otherwise `released quarantined test <n>: <test> — the gate no longer excuses it`. A `false` return (a concurrent release) fails `quarantined test at position <n> is already gone`. Update the `cmdQuarantine` module comment to say the command is read-only except the one destructive `--release <n>` mode.
- src/cli/help.ts: the `tumwater quarantine` stanza becomes `tumwater quarantine [--release <n>] [--json]`, replacing the trailing "it is read-only — a test leaves the list only when its filed bug leaves BUGS.md ## Open" with a sentence that `--release <n>` removes the Nth entry the list prints, logs a warning, and is for a flake fixed or judged gone before its bug closes.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater quarantine [--json]` clause in the "Check state" row: add `--release <n>` and replace "read-only — a test leaves the list only when its filed bug leaves BUGS.md `## Open`" with "read-only except `--release <n>`, which removes the Nth entry the list prints at the operator's request, logging a warning; otherwise a test leaves the list when its filed bug leaves BUGS.md `## Open`".

### The doctor's opencode row stops reading a catalog-free model that billed as `free` — the `billedAt` demotion `opencodeModelFree` applies but the row ignores (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every in-flight and blocked entry — `grep -n 'doctor-opencode-checks\|doctor-model-checks' PLANS.md` finds no entry under `## Planned`, and the five in-flight plans edit src/backlog+src/roles+src/run/run-prompt+src/prompt+src/doctor/doctor-project-checks (no-check 2/2), src/report (usage report), src/failure (failure digest), src/history+src/ui/gui/gui-client-history (history run table) and src/run/run-apply+src/run/run-finalize+src/ui/status-model+src/ui/status-payload+src/ui/gui/gui-client-model+src/ui/gui/gui-client-roles+docs/backends.md (cut-off episode); the cut-off plan edits docs/backends.md's "Truncated-at-the-ceiling turns look like normal stops" bullet while this plan appends one sentence to the OpenCode section, so whichever lands second rebases at that distant paragraph; touches src/doctor/doctor-opencode-checks.ts docs/backends.md test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** OpenCode's catalog calls a model free until a run reports a nonzero cost on it; `observeOpencodeRun` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) then stamps `billedAt` on that cache entry, and the one freeness predicate, `opencodeModelFree(cache, key)` (`entry.free && entry.billedAt === undefined`), flips to false — so the budget gate (`piPairFree` through `pollBudgetGate`, and `collectBudget`) prices the seam as paid from then on. The doctor's opencode row does not read that predicate: `checkOpencode`'s price line is `entry.free ? "free" : ...` (src/doctor/doctor-opencode-checks.ts), so it still reads "free" for a model the gate now charges against the cap. An operator checking backend readiness is told their free tier is still free while it is billing, which is the unsafe direction on a money-spending surface; make the row report the demotion the gate already applies.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-opencode-checks.ts: extend the `../agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.js` import with `opencodeModelFree` beside `opencodeModelKey`/`readOpencodeCache`, and add `import { formatDate } from "../text/datetime.js"`. In `checkOpencode`'s per-model loop, replace `const price = entry.free ? "free" : ...` with the gate's predicate: `const free = opencodeModelFree(cache, key);` and price it as `free ? "free" : entry.billedAt !== undefined ? \`no longer free (billed ${formatDate(new Date(entry.billedAt))})\` : \`$${entry.inputPerM ?? 0}/$${entry.outputPerM ?? 0} per M\``. In the `entry.billedAt !== undefined` case also push a warn: `` `${pair.model} was free in the catalog but billed once on ${formatDate(new Date(entry.billedAt))} — the budget gate now prices it` ``. Extend the function's doc comment to say the freeness read is `opencodeModelFree`, the same call the budget gate and status use, so the row cannot drift from what the team is billed.
- docs/backends.md, the OpenCode section's "The catalog prices the model as free until an observed bill marks it priced." sentence: append that `tumwater doctor` then names the model, its billed date and that the budget gate prices it, instead of reading it as free.
