### A project with no declared check gets one automatically, part 2/2: the plan role plans the check, the feature role declares it, and the `no-check` alert says so (planned 2026-10-25 by user; requires part 1/2 landed, since the feature role's non-npm route is that part's request path and a running build without it discards the request with a warning; touches src/run/run-prompt.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts src/prompt/gate-notes.ts src/roles/role-guidance.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts src/backlog/backlog.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts docs/cli.md docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md test/run-prompt.test.ts test/gate-notes.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `detectBuildCheck(root, cfg) === null` (surfaced as `noDeclaredCheck`, src/status/status-data.ts) is the state in the 2026-10-25 screenshot: an amber alert and the doctor's `check` row that only ask the operator to declare a check by hand. The team should close the gap itself — the plan role writes the plan that declares this project's check, the feature role implements it, and the alert says so. Declaration is either a tracked diff (the verifying script added to package.json where the walked-up install root carries one) or `check.command` in the local tumwater.json through part 1/2's request path (no role writes tumwater.json). The alert clears the moment a check exists, by hand or automatically: `noDeclaredCheck` is recomputed from `detectBuildCheck` on every snapshot and holds no dismissal state, so this part adds none.

**Approach.**
- The detection signal is already in prompt assembly: src/run/run-prompt.ts computes `const check = detectBuildCheck(root, config) ?? undefined` and threads it to `buildRunPrompt`. Add a `noCheck` note built by a new `buildNoCheckNote(role)` in src/prompt/gate-notes.ts beside the other `build*Note` helpers, set by run-prompt when `check === undefined` and the base role is `plan` or `feature`; src/prompt/prompt.ts's `RunPromptInput` gains `noCheck?: string` and `buildRunPrompt` pushes it in the note slot right after `role.find` (where `planTargetNote` and `flakyChecks` already ride). Every other role's prompt is byte-unchanged.
- Exactly one of the two notes is in flight, decided by a marker rather than by prose: `CHECK_DECLARATION_MARKER = "**Declares the project check**"` (src/roles/role-guidance.ts, beside `NEEDS_REVIEW_NOTE`) is written as its own line under the declaration entry, and a new helper beside `plannedPlanEntries` (src/backlog/backlog.ts, `declarationPlanEntry(root)`) recognizes it among PLANS.md's `## Planned` entries only. No marker → the plan note; marker → the feature note. So the feature role never invents a declaration the plan role never wrote, and the plan note cannot stack a second declaration plan on one already waiting.
- The plan note: this project declares no deterministic check — before anything else, write the entry that declares one, headed `### Declare the project's deterministic check` and marked with `CHECK_DECLARATION_MARKER`, naming the exact command and the route it lands by (a `test`/`typecheck`/`build` script in package.json when the walked-up install root carries one, else `check.command`), with acceptance criteria that the doctor's `check` row reads ok and the `no-check` alert is gone. Writing it is the run's work even when the eligible-plan target is already met, so the in-prompt queue-full stop yields to it; a full plan backlog defers the plan role before this prompt is built, so the note only reaches a run already admitted past that stop — the note never claims to outrank the scheduling deferral. Its escape clause keeps the alert honest: a project with nothing to verify yet — no source, no script to wire — gets no plan, and the note says to end with `NOTHING_TO_DO`.
- The feature note: the entry marked `CHECK_DECLARATION_MARKER` is this run's task unless the run was handed another entry; implement its declaration so a merge makes it live (the doctor's `check` row ok, `tumwater status --json` without `noDeclaredCheck`). It does not demand an in-run re-read — while the change is unmerged both reflect the pre-declaration state, so live is confirmed on merge, and the run marks the plan done when the declaration is complete and correct rather than forcing an impossible verification. The two routes, chosen by the repo: (1) add the verifying script to package.json as `test`/`typecheck`/`build` (detection's preference order) — a tracked diff the reviewer sees, live the moment it merges; (2) otherwise write `{ "check": { "command": "…" } }` to `.tumwater-config-request.json` at the worktree root (never tumwater.json) — part 1/2 runs it green, applies it to the live config, and deletes the file. A marker entry held with a Needs-review note is not available to the feature role, so the note ends the run there rather than forcing it.
- src/roles/role-catalog.ts: the plan role's `find` text gains the rule pointing at the note (its task over adding another plan, its precedence over the in-prompt eligible-plan stop within an admitted run, and the marker to write — while acknowledging the scheduling deferral precedes the prompt); the feature role's gains the note as the first thing to check among `## Planned`'s entries, with both routes and the merge-confirmed live rule.
- Alert wording (src/ui/team-alerts.ts's `no-check` block): keep the title's `safety gates are off` and the detail's `check.command`, `build pre-check`, `red-main baseline` and `redeploy's green check` phrases (the pinned case matches all five), and add that the plan role will plan a check for this project and the feature role declare it — a `test`/`typecheck`/`build` npm script, or `check.command` — keeping the manual remedy as the way to skip the wait and noting that a project with nothing to verify yet stays as it is. `actions` stays `[]` (the Settings card's `Declared check (JSON)` row is the remedy, src/config/config-editable-keys.ts). The doctor's twin row (src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts's `checkBuildCheck` warn, whose detail the same `no-check` state mirrors) gains the same sentence, so the two surfaces cannot contradict.
- Auto-dismissal needs no code and gets no state: declaring a check by hand (`tumwater config set`, the dashboard's Settings row, or an npm script) or through part 1/2's request path makes `detectBuildCheck` non-null, which drops `noDeclaredCheck` from the next snapshot and with it the alert on all four surfaces (`tumwater status`, TUI, GUI, and the `--json` key). While a declaration is merely planned, the alert stays up — deliberately, since the gates really are off — and its wording is what tells the operator why.
- docs: docs/cli.md's `tumwater status` alert enumeration and docs/how-it-works.md's dashboard-alerts sentence describe the new wording; docs/config.md's `check` row and docs/how-it-works.md's role/planning section gain the one sentence that the plan and feature roles declare a missing check automatically.

**Goal.** Every `run_end` written by `finalizeRun` (src/run/run-finalize.ts) carries `cacheReadTokens` when the run read any prompt tokens from the provider cache, and `run-usage.ts`/`pi-stream.ts` fold it — but no surface reads it back: the name appears on the emitter and its stream parsers only, never in `report-data.ts`, `history-data.ts`, `event-format.ts`, `role-view.ts`, `status-model.ts` or the failure digest. The digest's `Prompt tokens by role` line (src/failure/failure-render.ts) already prices one prompt-budget metric — the median prompt and the pre-edit share — from the same `run_end` trail and the same `promptStatsFor` fold. Add the cache-read share to that line so an operator sees how much of each role's prompt bill its backend served from cache (the reason a role's effective per-token cost can sit far below its list price) without a second field to read it in isolation; its test fixture already carries `cacheReadTokens: 40` that today's fold ignores.

**Approach.**
- src/failure/failure-data.ts, `PromptStatRow`: add `cacheReadShare?: number;` with the comment `sum(cacheReadTokens) / sum(promptTokens), in [0, 1]; absent when no run in the role reported a cache read`.
- `promptStatsFor`'s `Acc`: add `cacheReadSum: number`, initialized `0` beside the other two sums. In the run loop, after `preEdit`, fold `const cacheRead = nonNegativeNumber(ev.cacheReadTokens, 0);` (same finite guard as `prompt`/`preEdit`, so a torn or hand-edited `1e999` reads as absent rather than reaching the ratio) and add it to `acc.cacheReadSum`. In the return literal, spread `...(acc.cacheReadSum > 0 ? { cacheReadShare: acc.cacheReadSum / acc.promptSum } : {})` beside `preEditShare` — so a role whose runs reported no cache reads keeps today's exact row and render, and the omission-when-zero convention the other `run_end` telemetry fields use holds.
- src/failure/failure-render.ts, the `## Prompt tokens by role` loop: build the line rather than one template — keep `` `- ${roleCell(row.role)}: median ${row.medianPromptTokens} prompt tokens/run · ${percent(row.preEditShare, 1)} before first edit` `` and, when `row.cacheReadShare !== undefined`, append `` ` · ${percent(row.cacheReadShare, 1)} cache reads` `` through the same `percent` helper (so 40/50 renders `80%`). Extend the section's doc comment one clause: the cache-read share appears only when some run reported cache reads.

### The e2e tier runs its files one at a time, so a loaded host cannot stretch their wall-clock waits (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan — no eligible plan and no blocked part touches `test/test-runner.ts`, `test/test-runner.test.ts` or `DEVELOPMENT.md`; it takes the concrete isolation step the open BUGS.md class entry "e2e/concurrency tests can fail on a loaded host…" names ("run the concurrency/e2e tests isolated from the full suite's load") without editing any of that entry's member tests or their sources; touches test/test-runner.ts test/test-runner.test.ts DEVELOPMENT.md) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `test/test-runner.ts` hands the whole selection to one `node --test`, which starts files concurrently up to `os.availableParallelism() - 1` (its own `orderByDuration` comment: "as many at once as its concurrency allows"). Run the pure e2e tier's files one at a time, which is the quiet host the tier's design already assumes.

**Approach.**
- `test/test-runner.ts`: add `isE2eTier(files: readonly string[]): boolean` (exported, pure) — true when `files.length > 0` and every `path.basename(file)` ends with the existing `E2E_SUFFIX` (`.e2e.test.js`). Extend `buildNodeTestArgs`'s `opts` with `concurrency?: number`; when it is set, insert `--test-concurrency=${opts.concurrency}` immediately after `--test` and before the `--test-reporter` flags, so the flag precedes the positional files. `main()` computes `concurrency: isE2eTier(sel.files) && nodeSupportsTestConcurrency() ? 1 : undefined` and passes it, so only the all-e2e selection (`npm run test:e2e`, `npm test <an-e2e-file>`) serializes; a mixed selection (`npm test orchestrator`) and the unit suite keep today's argv byte-for-byte.
- `nodeSupportsTestConcurrency(version: string = process.versions.node): boolean` beside `nodeSupportsTestCoverageExclude`, in the same shape: `--test-concurrency` arrived in Node v20.10.0, at the package's `>=20.3` engines floor, so nodes 20.3 through 20.9 must never be handed it but every node at or above 20.10 may; return true only for major `>= 21` or major `20` with minor `>= 10`, and false for an unparseable version.
- `buildNodeTestArgs`'s doc comment and the module header's "files run in parallel" sentence: a pure e2e selection runs its files one at a time on a node that knows `--test-concurrency`, so a loaded host cannot stretch one file's waits against its siblings; the unit suite and a mixed selection are unchanged.
- DEVELOPMENT.md's e2e paragraph ("The e2e tier stays out of the gating suite because its wall-clock waits are not load-proof") adds that the tier's files run one at a time so each waits against a quiet host, not its siblings.

- `npm test` (unit-only) produces exactly today's argv for the same selection, and `npm run test:e2e` on Node 20.10+ produces one `node --test --test-concurrency=1 … <the e2e files>` spawn; the `--repeat` and `--coverage` paths reuse the same argv builder.

### A project with no declared check gets one automatically, part 1/2: a role's config request may declare `check.command`, and the harness runs it green before it is written (planned 2026-10-25 by user; touches src/config/config-request.ts src/run/run-verdict.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts docs/config.md test/config-request.test.ts test/run-verdict.test.ts test/prompt-roles.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** Nothing turns the safety gates on except a declaration on disk — `check.command` in tumwater.json or a `test`/`typecheck`/`build` npm script (src/build/build-check-detect.ts's `detectBuildCheck`, which needs a package.json AND a node_modules in the same walked-up directory) — and no role may write tumwater.json: the director prompt's boundary note says so in as many words (`tumwater.json, which stays off-limits to you as to every role`, src/prompt/prompt.ts). The one role-reachable config path is the staged request file (`.tumwater-config-request.json` at the worktree root, src/config/config-request.ts's `applyConfigRequest`, consumed by src/run/run-verdict.ts and deleted on every path), and today it accepts exactly one key, `customRoles`. This part widens it to `check.command` — deliberately not the whole `check` section, so a role can declare a check but never turn the gates off (`gateCommand: ""`, `mergeCommand: ""`, `timeoutSeconds`) — and makes the declaration a *verified* claim: the harness runs the candidate check green before it writes.

**Approach.**
- src/config/config-request.ts: the permitted-key filter (the `for (const key of Object.keys(parsed)) if (key !== "customRoles") ignored.push(key)` loop) admits `check`, and the request's `check` object is read only for its `command` (a non-blank string, `isNonBlankString`); every other sub-key inside it is pushed into `ignored` (named by the caller's existing warning, whose wording gains the accepted-key names) and dropped, and a blank or absent command is rejected like any other malformed request. The write keeps the one trap — fresh `loadConfig` under `withConfigLock`, `{ ...current.check, command }`, `validateConfig`, `writeJsonAtomic(configPath(root))` — with the request's own `roles`-section handling untouched (`preserveFileRoles`' rule: the whole-config write must not expand a partial section).
- The guard against a false declaration, which is why this part may not be skipped: a declared check is fail-closed. The gate's pre-check rejects on a red run (src/review/review-precheck.ts's `gateBuildPrecheck`), and a failure that also reproduces on main leaves every queued pin kept with nothing landing (`mainRedNotMine`) — so a command that could never pass (a typo, `npm test` in a tree with no install, a toolchain the repo lacks) parks the whole queue behind a red main no role can repair by code. Before writing, run the declared command through `runBuildCheck` (src/build/build-check.ts) in the requesting worktree — and the gate command too when `check.gateCommand` is set and differs, since that is what the gate scope actually runs — each at `check.cwd` resolved against the worktree (default `.`), under the config-resolved timeout, the same install-first step the gate's own run takes (`runBuildCheck`'s `install` argument), and the same process-wide check permit (`maxConcurrentChecks`), so the guard rehearses exactly what the pre-check will do there. Only a `passed` outcome for every candidate writes; a `failed`, a timeout or a skip on any candidate writes nothing and returns an error naming what was observed (`check.command not declared: \`npm run lint\` failed in the worktree`), which run-verdict's existing `config request rejected: <error>` warning carries while the file is still deleted. The requested command must have been observed green — the role's own claim is not the evidence.
- `applyConfigRequest` becomes async (`runBuildCheck` is), and run-verdict.ts's call site awaits it. The guard costs one check run per declaration, never one per run.
- Consumer gate: run-verdict.ts consumes the request only for `DIRECTOR_ROLE`; widen it to the director or the feature role. The director keeps its `customRoles` power and gains the same check power, so a user's "declare the check as `pytest -q`" routes instead of being recorded as guidance; the feature role is the consumer part 2/2's note names.
- src/prompt/prompt.ts: the director's boundary note (the paragraph beginning `Note on one boundary in the rules below, director only`) names `check.command` among the keys the request may carry, and keeps naming every key it may not. docs/config.md's `check` row gains the same: a role may declare `check.command` through the staged config request, and a declared command is run green in the worktree before it is written.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A request `{ "check": { "command": "npm run lint" } }` whose command passes in the worktree lands `check.command` in the root's tumwater.json with any hand-set `gateCommand`/`mergeCommand`/`timeoutSeconds` preserved, applies nothing else, deletes the request file, and is announced by the existing `config_changed` live reload (no new logging path).
- A request whose command fails, times out, or cannot run writes nothing, returns an error naming the observed outcome, still deletes the file, and leaves the config byte-identical.
- A request naming `check.gateCommand`, `check.mergeCommand`, `check.timeoutSeconds` or `check.command: ""` changes nothing and warns naming the ignored key(s). `customRoles` behavior — replacement, the `roles.<id>` strip, the unchanged-array skip — is byte-for-byte as today.

Both use the existing count-desc/name-asc ranking, so the two shapes cannot order a shared test differently.

### The always-on `mainred` alert names the failing test and the merge the main watch blamed — from the `main_culprit` event no surface reads (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan — the in-flight status-table peak-ctx plan edits `src/status/status-roles.ts`, `src/text/format.ts`, `src/ui/status-render.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` and `docs/how-it-works.md`, the history peak-ctx plan edits `src/run/*`, `src/text/format.ts` and `src/events/events.ts`, the failure-digest plan edits `src/events/event-format.ts` and `src/failure/*`, and part 3k/3 edits `src/ui/status-model.ts` — no eligible plan touches `src/status/status-polls.ts`, `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`, `test/status-polls.test.ts` or `test/team-alerts.test.ts`; the blocked part 3f/3 (which waits on part 3e/3) also edits `src/status/status-polls.ts` to drop the merge slot's in-lock gate/batch check plumbing and `src/ui/status-model.ts`, so whichever of 3f and this plan lands second rebases in `status-polls.ts` at a different function; touches src/status/status-polls.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts test/status-polls.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role)

**Goal.** When main's check is failing, the always-on red `mainred` alert (`buildStatusAlerts`, `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`) tells the operator only that N roles are blocked; it names neither what failed nor whose change broke main. The data exists and no surface reads it: the main watch logs a `main_culprit` event carrying `commit`, `runner` and the tip's `failingTests` (`src/baseline/main-watch.ts`) that a grep of `src` outside the event/format/tone plumbing finds no reader for. An operator watching the dashboard or TUI therefore has to run `tumwater doctor` or open the raw feed to learn the failing test and the responsible role. Surface both on the alert.

**Approach.** Two source files carry the change; the alert reads only what the poll already scans.
- src/status/status-polls.ts: add `culprit?: HarnessEvent` to `MainCheckScan` and collect the newest `main_culprit` event in `scanMainCheck`'s existing single pass (beside the newest full-scope `build_check` and the `merge_done` events), so the stat-cached scan keeps its one log read per poll. Have `mainCheckScanFor`'s clone copy `culprit` the way it copies `check`, so a caller never receives the cached object itself. Add `red?: { failingTests: string[]; culprit?: { commit: string; runner?: string } }` to `MainCheckStatus` with a doc comment naming its readers. In `mainCheckForPoll`, derive `red` entirely from the newest `main_culprit` verdict — the only event that carries the red tip's failing tests (the `build_check` event never does) — and only when `status === "failed"` and the verdict's `commit` equals the sha this poll derived for the tip (so a newer `build_check` failure can't borrow a blame written for a different head). Populate `failingTests` only when the verdict's list is an array whose first element is a string (the event log is loose-typed), and `culprit` when its `commit` is the derived sha (`runner` when that too is a string) — so a passing or skipped check, or a red tip the watch hasn't blamed, keeps today's exact `MainCheckStatus` shape.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts, the `if (red.length)` block: build the detail from `snap.mainCheck?.red` when present — `A full check failed on main: <squash(first failing test, 80)><" (+N more)">` and, when `red.culprit?.runner`, `; the main watch blames <roleLabel(runner)>'s merge <shortSha(commit)>` — and keep `seeFailures()` as the action. With no `red` detail the alert's title and detail are byte-identical to today. No new alert key, tone, action or ordering.
- Deliberately unchanged: the alert's generic "Code roles stop authoring until main's check passes" sentence. Part 3k/3 sweeps the stale references the red-main authoring block's removal (part 3a/3) left behind in `src/ui/status-model.ts`, and the alert is the same sweep's business; correcting it here would cross into that in-flight part's judgment about what the red-main hold now means (a merge that adds no new failures still lands, `warnMainRedOnce` in `src/baseline/main-red.ts`). This plan adds the evidence, not a new reading of the hold.

**Files touched.** src/status/status-polls.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts test/status-polls.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With the newest full-scope check a failed `build_check` and a `main_culprit` whose `commit` is that tip's derived sha, carrying `failingTests: ["a", "b"]` and `runner: "feature"`, `mainCheckForPoll` returns `status: "failed"` and `red` naming both failing tests and the `feature`/commit culprit.
- A passing full-scope check returns a `MainCheckStatus` with no `red` key, as does a failed one whose red tip the watch hasn't blamed (no matching `main_culprit`), so every existing reader (`heldByMainRed`, the doctor's `main red` row, `tumwater status --json` via `statusPayload`) is unchanged.
- The `mainred` alert for a snapshot whose `mainCheck.red` is present names the first failing test and the culprit role in its detail; for a snapshot with no `mainCheck` (or no `red`), its title and detail are exactly today's strings.

### Self-redeploy runs no full check of its own while the main watch verifies main: its target is the watch's newest green commit, and its pre-warm never starts a second check (planned 2026-10-25 by user; evidence: the 2026-10-25 analysis of main's full-check load after Fast merge, AFTER window 2026-10-22 03:24 → 10-24 11:24 PDT plus the 37 h since; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — part 3i/3 edits `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts`'s `mergeStartHeld`, not `pollRedeploy`, and part 3k/3 edits `src/baseline/main-baseline.ts`'s module header, not `redeployTarget`; land it before "Check-permit priority, part 2/2" takes its week of `check_wait` data, so that week does not measure this waste; touches src/baseline/main-baseline.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts docs/invariants.md docs/how-it-works.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** Since the Fast merge defaults went live, nothing seeds main's verdict cache at merge time, so the full suite on main runs after the merge. Two pollers ran it, each on whatever head it saw. One is the main watch (`src/baseline/main-watch.ts`, single-flight). The other is self-redeploy's cooldown pre-warm (`PrewarmProbes.prewarm`, `src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts`). The pre-warm starts `mainIsGreen(head)` on every new head, even while its previous check is still running.

In the 56 h AFTER window there were 437 full `baseline` checks (26.1 h); the watch's own runs were 147 (7.8 h). Self-redeploy ran 285:
- 188 (10.7 h) were runs the watch shared in flight or read from the cache;
- 97 (7.3 h, 28% of all full-check time) produced a verdict nobody used;
- 202 overlapped another pre-warm run.

Since Saturday the unused share is 57 of 127 runs (5.3 of 10.1 h, 52%). Two or more full suites on main ran at once for 12% of AFTER and 22% since Saturday. 105 of AFTER's 251 `check_wait`s (4.3 of 10.9 h) waited while two or more "main baseline" checks held permits.

Each pre-warm check also hard-resets the shared `_main` mirror (`ensureDetachedWorktree`) to its head. An earlier pre-warm suite may still be running there or waiting for a permit, keyed to the sha it read before the reset. So a verdict can be recorded under a commit whose tree it did not test. plans/fast-merge.md part 5 already says the target is "the newest first-parent commit on main with a green full-check verdict", which needs no check of the redeployer's own. Make the code do that whenever the watch verifies main. Never re-point the mirror under a running pre-warm step.

**Approach.**
- src/baseline/main-baseline.ts, `redeployTarget(wt, tip, buildSha, watched = false)`:
  - With `watched` true, walk `tip`'s first-parent history (at most REDEPLOY_WALK_MAX) down to `buildSha`. Return the first commit whose cached verdict is green, observed or inherited.
  - With no green above the build, return `buildSha` itself. `buildStaleness` then reads it as not stale, so no episode, hold or pre-warm starts until the watch calls a newer commit green.
  - A cached red is walked past, never targeted. The watch's red has already had its confirming re-run.
  - A build that is not a first-parent ancestor of `tip` keeps today's answer (`tip`, which the redeployer checks), as does `watched` false.
  - Every target `watched` picks has a cached green, so `mainIsGreen` on it is a cache hit and the redeployer starts no suite.
  - Update the doc comment: the watch supplies the verdicts and the redeployer only reads them.
- src/baseline/main-baseline.ts: export `watchVerifiesMain(root, config): boolean`. It returns `detectBuildCheck(root, config) !== null && mergeCommandOf(config) !== undefined`: the configs where no merge seeds a green (`watchedBaseline`'s doc) and the watch has a check to run.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, `pollRedeploy`:
  - Pass `watchVerifiesMain(ctx.root, liveConfig)` as `redeployTarget`'s `watched`.
  - A project with no declared check, or with `check.mergeCommand: ""` (full check in the lock), keeps today's target.
- src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, `PrewarmProbes.prewarm`:
  - When `head` differs from the probe's head while its green check or its compile is still running (`!done`), return without resetting, so the mirror is not re-pointed under it.
  - The next poll after both settle takes the newest head as today.
  - Say so in the class comment, beside "the mirror worktree both run in must not serve two checks at once".
- docs/invariants.md INV-K1:
  - Guarantee: while the main watch verifies main (a declared check and a `check.mergeCommand` in effect), the target always carries a cached green and is never an unchecked tip. With no green newer than the build, nothing is targeted. Outside that mode an unchecked tip stays the target and the redeployer checks it.
  - Binds: `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts` (`pollRedeploy`), not `src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts`, which no longer calls it.
  - Pinned by: add the new tests' names.
- docs/how-it-works.md "## Updates": after "The commit it builds is main's newest one whose full check passed…", add one sentence. With the main watch on (the default whenever `check.gateCommand` is set), that verdict is the watch's: the update waits for the watch to call a newer commit green and runs no check of its own.

**Files touched.** src/baseline/main-baseline.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts docs/invariants.md docs/how-it-works.md test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `watched` true and main A (build) → B (cached green) → C (no verdict), `redeployTarget` returns B and `mainIsGreen` on B runs no check. With C cached red, it returns B. With no green above A, it returns A, and `buildStaleness(A, A)` reads not stale.
- With `watched` false, every existing `redeployTarget` case answers exactly as today, including "an unchecked tip is the target (the redeployer checks it)".
- `watchVerifiesMain` is true for a config with a declared check and `check.gateCommand` set and no `check.mergeCommand`. It is false for `check.mergeCommand: ""` and for a project with no declared check. `pollRedeploy` passes its answer as `watched`.
- A pre-warm whose head moves while its green check (or compile) is unsettled starts no second `mainGreen` (or `compile`) until the first settles, then runs the newest head.
- After deploy, almost every `baseline` `build_check` from source `tumwater` settles within 5 s of a `main_check` from the watch with `durationMs` > 0. The exception is the redeployer's rare witness check on the running build (`buildRed`, during a cooldown). Over 56 h of events, full-check runs no `main_check` used go from 97 to about 0.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts:
  - add `redeployTarget in watch mode targets the newest cached green and never an unchecked tip`: the A → B → C cases above, B seeded with `noteGreenBaseline`, C left unchecked and then cached red. Assert no check script ran (a manifest whose `test` script fails, so any run would turn up red).
  - add `redeployTarget in watch mode targets the build itself when nothing newer is green`.
  - add `watchVerifiesMain is true only with a declared check and a merge command in effect`: a gate command with no `mergeCommand` key gives true; `mergeCommand: ""` gives false; no declared check gives false.
  - The three existing `redeployTarget` tests stay as they are, pinning `watched` false.
- test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts: add `a head that moves while the pre-warm's green check runs starts no second check until it settles`. Use a fake `mainGreen` returning a held promise and count its calls. Then resolve it, poll on the newest head, and assert exactly one more call for that head.

### Every role may fix main's failing check: a role's prompt names main's failing tests, and any role may land the fix (planned 2026-10-25 by the operator; the `ci` healer stays the owner, so this only restores information the harness stopped giving — "Every commit is verified on main, part 3a/3" deleted the `<main-known-red>` note with the gate that built it — and relaxes the one-owner wording in plans/fast-merge.md "One owner for a red main"; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — parts 3i/3 and 3j/3 of that series edit `src/runner/runner-run.ts` at their own recovery arms and part 3k/3 edits `src/events/events.ts`'s comment, none of them the note append this part adds, no eligible plan touches `src/prompt/gate-notes.ts` or `test/gate-notes.test.ts`, and docs/how-it-works.md's red-main paragraph is a distant shared paragraph, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/prompt/gate-notes.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts src/baseline/main-red.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gate-notes.test.ts test/runner-red-main.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** "Every commit is verified on main, part 3a/3" removed the red-main authoring block and, with it, the `<main-known-red>` note every role's prompt carried; a role now starts on a red main without being told which tests fail, so only `ci` — handed the `<main-red>` heal note by `mainRedHealNote` — can act on them. The operator's 2026-10-25 decision (plans/fast-merge.md "One owner for a red main", revised) keeps `ci` as the owner of main's greenness but not as a lock: any role may fix main's failing build or tests in its own worktree and land the fix like any other change, and two roles fixing one break is an ordinary rebase conflict. This part restores the missing information — the failing tests, named on every role's prompt — and words it as permission rather than "leave them alone".

**Approach.**
- src/prompt/gate-notes.ts: re-add `buildMainKnownRedNote(tests: readonly string[]): string` beside `buildMainRedNote`, rendering a `<main-known-red>` block — one line per failing test, then the permission sentence: main's tip already fails these; the `ci` role owns them and fixes them on its own clock; a role whose change touches what they test, or that can land a fix for one, fixes it in its own worktree and lets the change land normally; never weaken or delete a test to make the suite pass. Its header comment says why it is back (this entry) and that `ci` owns the repair without monopolizing it.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: append the block for every role whose run does not already carry the red-main heal note (every role but `ci`), reading `watchedBaseline(wt)` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) — a pure read of the main watch's persisted verdict, so a role's start pays no check run — and rendering only while its status is `red` and it names failing tests (the `namedFailures` rule main-red.ts uses: empty when the list is empty or at `FAILING_TESTS_MAX`). `namedFailures` is exported from src/baseline/main-red.ts (its one home) so the rule cannot drift; the note rides the run's prompt string in the same `appendPromptNote` way the `<main-red>` heal note does — the notes are appended strings in runner-run.ts, not fields of a run-prompt type.
- docs/how-it-works.md: the red-main paragraph ("While main's check is failing, every role keeps working … a newly-verified red main queues a `ci` healer") gains one clause — every role's prompt names the failing tests, and a fix from any role lands like any other change, `ci` owning the repair without monopolizing it.

### The failure digest's Team state changes section replays every harness gate hold and lift — disk, quiet hours, the maintenance allowance, the subscription windows and the live model/concurrency edits (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan — no eligible plan and no blocked part touches `src/failure/failure-state-change.ts`, `src/events/event-format.ts`, `test/failure-state-change.test.ts` or `test/failure-render.test.ts`; part 3k/3 edits `src/events/events.ts`'s `run_end`/`main_red` comment lines, which this plan reads but does not touch, and the in-flight status-table and history plans touch status/ui/text and run/detail files, none of them `src/failure`; touches src/events/event-format.ts src/failure/failure-state-change.ts test/failure-state-change.test.ts test/failure-render.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `renderFailureMarkdown`'s Team state changes section is the evidence the selfcheck role judges its "was the harness's response wrong" rule against (plans/telemetry-role.md §"Fleet state changes"), but it replays only a subset of the harness's own decisions. `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES` lists the budget gates, the team/role pause and resume, the rate-limit/backend hold, the model fallback, `max_concurrent_changed`/`retention_changed`/`config_changed` and the restart lifecycle — yet the holds that stop and restart work for the other configured gates never appear: `disk_low`/`disk_ok`, `quiet_hours_started`/`quiet_hours_ended`, `maintenance_quota_hold`/`maintenance_quota_resumed`, `subscription_window_reserved`/`subscription_window_limited`/`subscription_window_reset`, the live-edit siblings `provider_concurrency_changed` and `model_changed`, and the one-time `bootstrap_complete` admission. `grep -n 'disk_low\|quiet_hours\|subscription_window\|maintenance_quota' src/failure/` prints nothing, so a window in which a disk floor or a subscription-window reserve stopped the team reads in the digest as if the team merely chose to idle: the `run_deferred`/`run_end` counts show the stop with no harness decision to explain it. Add the missing transitions with compact bounded lines, keeping the section's constant byte bound.

**Approach.** Two files carry the change; the wording helpers stay in their one home rather than being re-derived.
- src/events/event-format.ts: add `export` to the four private helpers the feed's own lines already use — `gigabytes(v)`, `windowSuffix(e)`, `windowResetPhrase(e)` and `backendLabel(e)`. Visibility only; no line or byte changes. The failure digest then reuses them, so a disk, quiet-hours or subscription line cannot drift between the feed and the digest.
- src/failure/failure-state-change.ts: add the twelve types to `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES` and one `case` per type in `describeStateChange`, each a compact (≤ `STATE_CHANGE_MAX`) version of the event feed's line, every free field through `field()` so no unbounded payload reaches the page:
  - `disk_low`: `waiting: low disk — ${gigabytes(ev.freeGB)} free (floor ${gigabytes(ev.holdGB)})`; `disk_ok`: `disk recovered — ${gigabytes(ev.freeGB)} free`.
  - `quiet_hours_started`: `waiting: quiet hours${windowSuffix(ev)}`; `quiet_hours_ended`: `quiet hours ended${windowSuffix(ev)}`.
  - `maintenance_quota_hold`: `waiting: maintenance allowance used — ${field(ev.maint)}/${field(ev.allowance)} in 24h (${field(ev.work)} work)`; `maintenance_quota_resumed`: `maintenance allowance reopened — ${field(ev.maint)}/${field(ev.allowance)} in 24h`.
  - `subscription_window_reserved`: `waiting: ${backendLabel(ev)} window ${field(ev.windowType)} at ${pct(ev.utilization)}% past its ${pct(ev.reserve)}% reserve`; `subscription_window_limited`: `waiting: ${backendLabel(ev)} window ${field(ev.windowType)} rejected${windowResetPhrase(ev)}`; `subscription_window_reset`: `${backendLabel(ev)} window reset — model jobs run again`.
  - `provider_concurrency_changed`: `${field(ev.provider)} concurrency ${field(ev.from)} → ${field(ev.to)}`; `model_changed`: `model changed — now ${field(ev.to)}`; `bootstrap_complete`: `bootstrap complete — ${field(ev.plansDone)}/${field(ev.untilPlansDone)} plans done`.
- `pct(v)` is `claudeUtilizationPct(finiteNumber(v, 0))` (import `claudeUtilizationPct` from `../agent/claude/claude-account.js`), the same percent format the feed's subscription lines use; the existing imports of `finiteNumber`, `formatGB` (from `../text/format.js`), `isNonBlankString` and the event-format helpers cover the rest.
- Extend `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES`'s doc comment to name the gate holds beside the existing list. Deliberately left out, and said so in the comment: `subscription_window_warning` (observational, gates nothing), `disk_reclaim` (an action, not a state transition), `image_blind` (a run outcome), and `permit_reserve`/`slot_wait`/`check_wait`/`provider_wait`/`claim` (per-run advisories or assignments).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES` holds each of the twelve types; `describeStateChange` returns the compact line above for each, and every free field is byte-sliced so a hand-edited payload cannot exceed `STATE_CHANGE_MAX` or emit `NaN`/`undefined` (a `disk_low` with no `freeGB` reads `0.0 GB` through `finiteNumber`).
- The existing set's lines and the section's newest-`STATE_CHANGE_TOP` cap/remainder behavior are unchanged, and `renderFailureMarkdown` prints a new type's line in the Team state changes section (the collector's `STATE_CHANGE_TYPES` filter is what admits it), so no render change is needed.

Two day lines remain missing from the window shape: `**Cost per commit:**` (`costPerCommitLine` over `costPerCommitPairs(data.series)`) and its notional sibling `**Estimated per commit:**`, both only the day render prints. **Approach.**
- src/report/report-render.ts: factor the ranking out of `costPerCommitPairs(series, pick)` into a map-based core `costPerCommitPairsFrom(cost: Record<string, number>, commits: Record<string, number>)` holding the existing mergeDone/idle construction and its sorts verbatim. `costPerCommitPairs` keeps its signature and becomes the day caller: fold `pick(d)` across the series through `baseRoleOf(id)` into `cost` and aggregate `d.commitsByRole ?? {}` into `commits` exactly as today, then `return costPerCommitPairsFrom(cost, commits)`. ### A brief file that exists without its `tumwater:prompt` block raises the always-on `no-brief` alert — the marker-less-README warning the doctor `brief` row prints today (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — the in-flight `backlog archive` alert is the only plan that edits src/ui/team-alerts.ts and src/ui/status-payload.ts, and it adds its own field and alert in the same status slice, so whichever lands second rebases at the `noDeclaredCheck`/`no-check` pair and the `…snap.noDeclaredCheck ? { noDeclaredCheck: true }…` spread; the in-flight `Every commit is verified on main` parts 3a/3 and 3l/3 edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/runner and the review tests, and the in-flight TUI History plan edits only src/ui/tui files — none of them touches this plan's files except that one rebase; touches src/brief/brief.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/brief.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Every role's prompt carries the project brief read from README.md or TUMWATER.md (src/brief/brief.ts's `readBrief`, markers `PROMPT_START`/`PROMPT_END`). When a brief file exists but its markers are gone — a hand edit that strips the block, or a README created as a directory or permission-lost file — `briefFile(root)` returns null (or throws) and every run reaches its model with no project prompt, so the team burns tokens producing work unrelated to the project. Today only `tumwater doctor`'s `brief` row (`checkBrief`, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) reports it; the operator must run doctor to see it, and the running team's own dashboards stay silent. The `no-check` alert already twins doctor's `check` warn on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI (src/ui/team-alerts.ts's `buildStatusAlerts`, `snap.noDeclaredCheck`); give the brief break the same always-on amber twin. The pre-init state (`checkBrief`'s own comment: a repo with no brief candidate "is exactly what a repo looks like between `git clone` and `tumwater init` on purpose") is deliberately out of scope: alerting on it would fire on every on-purpose pre-init repo.

**Approach.**
- src/brief/brief.ts: add `export function briefBlockMissing(root: string): boolean` beside `briefFile`. It returns false when no path in `briefCandidates(root)` exists (the pre-init state), else `true` when `briefFile(root)` is null; a `try`/`catch` around `briefFile` returns `true` on the unreadable-candidate throw, since a brief that cannot be read is one the roles cannot use. Doc comment states the condition is a subset of doctor's `brief` warn (the marker-less and unreadable states, not the bare-repo one) and names its one consumer.
- src/status/status-data.ts, the `StatusSnapshot` interface beside `noDeclaredCheck` (line ~377): add `noBrief?: boolean` with a doc comment mirroring `noDeclaredCheck`'s — the doctor `brief` row's marker-less-file warning state, present only in that state so the surfaces render as before when the brief resolves. In `snapshot()`, beside the `noDeclaredCheck: detectBuildCheck(root, cfg) === null ? true : undefined,` line, add `noBrief: briefBlockMissing(root) ? true : undefined,` and import `briefBlockMissing` from `../brief/brief.js`. Add no new file read beyond the brief candidates the run prompt already reads.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts, beside the `...(snap.noDeclaredCheck ? { noDeclaredCheck: true } : {}),` spread: add `...(snap.noBrief ? { noBrief: true } : {}),` so `tumwater status --json` scripts can read the same state the alert renders (the `noDeclaredCheck` precedent), and extend that spread's doc-comment sentence.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `"noBrief"` to BOTH `snap` Pick lists that carry `"noDeclaredCheck"` (`StatusAlertsInput` ~line 291 and `teamAlerts`' parameter ~line 1300). In `buildStatusAlerts`, directly after the `if (snap.noDeclaredCheck) { … key: "no-check" … }` block, add `if (snap.noBrief) { out.push({ key: "no-brief", tone: "amber", title: "The project brief has no prompt block — every role runs without its project prompt", detail: "A brief file exists but carries no well-formed tumwater:prompt block, so each run's prompt reaches the model with no project brief. Restore the block in the file the doctor `brief` row names, or re-run `tumwater init`.", actions: [] }); }`, matching the `no-check` alert's amber tone and empty actions.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater status` row that already names the `no-check` alert and the `--json` `noDeclaredCheck` key: add the parallel clause — a brief file that exists without the `tumwater:prompt` block surfaces a standing amber `no-brief` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI, and `--json` carries `noBrief`. docs/how-it-works.md, the brief paragraph near `tumwater init` (line ~5): add one sentence that the always-on surfaces raise the amber `no-brief` alert when a brief file loses its marker block.

**Files touched.** src/brief/brief.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/brief.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A repo whose README.md exists without the `tumwater:prompt` markers has `snapshot(root, …).noBrief === true`; `statusPayload` carries `noBrief: true` and one `no-brief` alert with tone `amber`; `renderStatus` (the TUI header) and the dashboard alert list carry its title.
- Adding the markers to that README.md (or replacing it with a file carrying the resolved brief) sets `noBrief` back to `undefined` and removes the alert; a repo with no README.md and no TUMWATER.md keeps `noBrief` absent and raises no `no-brief` alert (the pre-init state stays silent).
- A README.md that exists but cannot be read (a directory or chmod-0 file) raises `no-brief` rather than crashing the snapshot.
- The alert sits directly after `no-check` in `teamAlerts`' emission order, and `teamAlerts(base, …)` with `noBrief` absent still returns `[]` for a healthy team.
- `briefBlockMissing` returns false for no candidates, true for a marker-less candidate, false once a candidate carries the block, and true for an unreadable candidate.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/brief.test.ts (already imports `briefFile`, `makeRepo`): add "briefBlockMissing is true only when a candidate exists without a resolvable block" — a `makeRepo()` with neither file returns false; writing a marker-less `README.md` returns true; adding the `tumwater:prompt` block returns false; making README.md unreadable (`fs.chmodSync(…, 0o000)`, restored in a `finally`) returns true. Import `briefBlockMissing`.
- test/status-payload.test.ts, beside "the payload's noDeclaredCheck follows detectBuildCheck": add "the payload's noBrief follows briefBlockMissing and clears when the brief resolves" — a `makeRepo()` plus a marker-less README.md yields `snapshot(...).noBrief === true`, a `noBrief` payload key and a `no-brief` alert with tone `amber`; prefixing the README.md with `PROMPT_START`/`PROMPT_END` (imported from `../src/brief/brief.js`) clears both; a `makeRepo()` with no README.md yields `undefined` and no `no-brief` alert.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, beside "no declared check raises one amber no-check alert": add "a marker-less brief raises one amber no-brief alert right after no-check" — `teamAlerts({ ...base, noBrief: true }, …)` filtered to `no-brief` has length one, tone `amber`, a title matching `/prompt block/` and a detail matching `/tumwater:prompt/` and `/tumwater init/`, and `actions` deep-equal `[]`; `noBrief` absent, `false` and `undefined` each yield none; with both `noDeclaredCheck` and `noBrief` set, the emitted key order is `["no-check", "no-brief"]`.

### The `tumwater role <id>` view and the dashboard role drawer forecast when a role's own daily cap falls, the per-role twin of the team budget badge's `~cap at HH:MM` (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role; independent in files of every eligible plan — the in-flight `Every commit is verified on main` parts 3a/3 and 3l/3 edit `src/baseline`, `src/status`, `src/doctor`, `src/roles/roles.ts`, `src/runner`, `src/prompt` and their tests but not `src/roles/role-view.ts`, `src/roles/role-render.ts` or `test/role-view.test.ts`; the in-flight `no-brief` alert plan edits `src/brief`, `src/status/status-data.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/team-alerts.ts` and `docs/how-it-works.md`'s brief paragraph, and the in-flight dashboard `Cost per commit` plan edits `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts` and `test/gui-client-report.test.ts` — neither touches `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts` or `test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts`; the `tumwater report --since` plan and the in-flight TUI History and `backlog archive` plans touch other files; only `docs/how-it-works.md` is shared, the `no-brief` plan at the brief paragraph and this plan at the `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` bullet in `## Spend and pausing`, so whichever lands second rebases in that file at a distant paragraph; touches src/roles/role-view.ts src/roles/role-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/role-view.test.ts test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team's daily spend forecast already has one home and three readers: `projectCapHit` (src/budget/budget.ts) projects when today's linear burn reaches `maxDailyCostUsd`, the status snapshot's `budget.capHitAt` carries it, and the budget badge (`budgetBadge`, src/ui/badges.ts) and the dashboard sidebar spend card (`budgetCardHtml`, src/ui/gui/gui-client-operator.ts) render `· ~cap at HH:MM`. A role's own `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` cap has the spend-vs-cap half of that story everywhere an operator reads it — `rolePayload`'s `dailyCap` (`{ capUsd, spentUsd, over, roleIds }`, src/roles/role-view.ts), the CLI's `- Daily cap:` line (src/roles/role-render.ts) and the dashboard role drawer's Daily cap row (src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts) — but none of them says when the cap will fall, so the operator learns a role is capped only from the amber `role-cap` alert after the hold has started. Add the same projection to the per-role view: while a role is under its cap and burning, `tumwater role <id>` and the drawer name `~cap at HH:MM`, so the cap can be raised before the role sits idle. The projection is the already-accepted team rule, not a new estimate: same `projectCapHit`, same `~` forecast marker, same `clockHm` wall-clock hours-and-minutes.

**Approach.**
- src/roles/role-view.ts: import `projectCapHit` from `../budget/budget.js` beside the existing `roleCapVerdicts` import. Add `dailyCapHitAt?: number` to `RoleViewPayload`, directly after `dailyCap`, with a doc comment naming it the role's `projectCapHit({ spentUsd: verdict.spentUsd, capUsd }, now)` instant and stating it is present only while a forecast stands (so a capped-but-over, zero-spend, or no-cap payload keeps its current JSON shape). Declare `let dailyCapHitAt: number | undefined;` beside the existing `let dailyCap`. In the existing `if (verdict) dailyCap = …` branch, after assigning `dailyCap`, set `const hitAt = projectCapHit({ spentUsd: verdict.spentUsd, capUsd }, now.getTime()); if (hitAt !== null) dailyCapHitAt = hitAt;` — the base role's SUMMED `spentUsd` is the right burn, since the cap is base-level. In the returned object, directly after `...(dailyCap ? { dailyCap } : {})`, add `...(dailyCapHitAt !== undefined ? { dailyCapHitAt } : {})`.
- src/roles/role-render.ts: inside the existing `if (p.dailyCap)` block, after the `shared by …` suffix, append `if (p.dailyCapHitAt !== undefined) cap += ` · ~cap at ${clockHm(p.dailyCapHitAt)}`;`. `clockHm` is already imported at the top, so no new import.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts: the drawer is browser code and cannot import `../text/datetime.js` (the `quietWindowEnd` precedent's own note). Add a local `const capClock = (ms) => String(new Date(ms).getHours()).padStart(2, "0") + ":" + String(new Date(ms).getMinutes()).padStart(2, "0");` inside `drawerConfigHtml` beside its `fallbackLabel` local. In the `dc ? … : "no cap"` `capBody` expression, after the `shared by …` suffix, concatenate `(typeof view.dailyCapHitAt === "number" ? " · ~cap at " + capClock(view.dailyCapHitAt) : "")`. No backticks in this file (the whole module is a `String.raw` template).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` bullet in `## Spend and pausing`: add one sentence that `tumwater role <id>` and the dashboard role drawer state `~cap at HH:MM` while the role is under its cap — the same `projectCapHit` forecast the budget badge carries for the team cap — so the cap can be raised before the hold starts.

**Files touched.** src/roles/role-view.ts src/roles/role-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/role-view.test.ts test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A non-director role with a finite cap above 0 and today's spend below it carries `dailyCapHitAt` equal to `projectCapHit({ spentUsd, capUsd }, now.getTime())`, and `renderRoleMarkdown` prints `- Daily cap: $S of $C spent today (not holding) · ~cap at HH:MM` (zero-padded local wall clock, `clockHm`).
- A role at or over its cap, a role with 0 spend today, a role with cap 0, a role with no cap, and the director each carry no `dailyCapHitAt` and render exactly the line they render today (no `~cap at`).
- The dashboard role drawer's Daily cap row appends `· ~cap at HH:MM` when the payload carries `dailyCapHitAt`, and is byte-identical to today when it does not; the director still shows no Daily cap row.
- `dailyCap`'s shape stays `{ capUsd, spentUsd, over, roleIds }`, so `tumwater role <id> --json` keeps every existing key and only gains `dailyCapHitAt` when a forecast stands.
- No change to `projectCapHit`, the status snapshot's `budget.capHitAt`, `budgetBadge`, `budgetCardHtml`, or the amber `role-cap` alert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/role-view.test.ts, beside "role payload carries the daily cap verdict and renders a Daily cap line": add "role payload forecasts the daily cap hit while the role is under it" — `writeConfig(dir, { maxDailyCostUsdPerRole: { coverage: 1 } })`, `saveRunnerState(dir, { ...freshRunnerState("coverage"), dayStamp: today, dayCostUsd: 0.6 })` at `new Date(2026, 9, 16, 12, 0, 0)`; assert `p.dailyCapHitAt === projectCapHit({ spentUsd: 0.6, capUsd: 1 }, now.getTime())` (import `projectCapHit`) and `renderRoleMarkdown(p)` matches `/· ~cap at 20:00$/m`. Then `dayCostUsd: 1.2` (over) yields no `dailyCapHitAt` and a render with no `/~cap at/`; `dayCostUsd: 0` yields no `dailyCapHitAt`.
- test/role-view.test.ts, in the existing "daily cap sums instances, and is absent …" case: assert `"dailyCapHitAt" in rolePayload(dir, "coverage", NO_MODELS, now)` is false for cap 0, the director, and a no-cap repo (the forecast cannot outlive the `dailyCap` gate).
- test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts, in "the role drawer always renders a Daily cap row …": add a stub payload whose `dailyCap` is present with `over: false` and `dailyCapHitAt: new Date(2026, 9, 16, 20, 0, 0).getTime()`; assert the Daily cap `<dd>` matches `/· ~cap at 20:00/`. The existing over-cap stub carries no `dailyCapHitAt`, so its assertion stays as written and proves the absent case renders no forecast.

### Every commit is verified on main, part 3a/3: the red-main authoring block comes off — a code role authors on a red main and the `ci` healer is handed the failing tests (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held part 3/3; rewritten 2026-10-24 by the plan role, which split the stale-reference sweep off as part 3k/3, and revised 2026-10-24 by the plan role to move the heal-key green clear into the main watch and hand the `main_red_hold` event comment to part 3k/3 — this part is the behavior removal and its commit record must say so; the pre-merge blocks themselves come off in parts 3g/3–3j/3 and 3d/3–3f/3; touches src/baseline/main-red.ts src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts src/roles/roles.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts src/prompt/gate-notes.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/main-red.test.ts test/main-red-heal.test.ts test/runner-red-main.test.ts test/roles.test.ts test/runner-ids.test.ts test/runner-prompt-requeue.test.ts test/gate-notes.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 2**

**Goal.** Main's redness stops blocking authoring. `mainRedGate` (src/baseline/main-red.ts) and `baselineBlocked`/`BASELINE_BLOCKED_ROLES` (src/roles/roles.ts) exist only to keep a code role from spending an authoring run whose diff the pre-merge check would reject; with the pre-merge blocks coming off (parts 3g/3–3j/3 and 3d/3–3f/3) nothing is left to reject it, so the block only stalls every code role while main is red. The surviving information is the `ci` healer's hand-off (`mainRedHealNote`, `mainRedHealPrompt`) naming the failing tests and their owner, and the watch's and `main red` label's report of an unheld red. A code role no longer gets a `<main-known-red>` note: the gate that built it is gone. The gate also cleared the heal-dedup key on a green main; that clear moves to the main watch, which settles a green verdict on every new tip, so a failing set that returns after green still queues a fresh heal prompt (INV-AZ2).

**Approach.**
- Delete `mainRedGate` (src/baseline/main-red.ts) and its call in `runner-run.ts` (the `blocked` branch that reads `mainRedGate(ctx.root, ctx.role, wt, undefined, …)`), so a code role's run on a red main proceeds. Keep `mainRedHealNote`, `mainRedHealPrompt`, `queueCulpritHeal`, `baselineCheckLogger` and `warnMainRedOnce` — the healer hand-off the watch and the `ci` plan read. Reword `mainRedHealNote`'s "mainRedGate exempts ci" clause so the hand-off reads as independent of any gate, reword `mainTipVerdict`'s "the same per-SHA, team-wide cache mainRedGate reads" and "exactly as mainRedGate warns it" references to the surviving readers, and drop `main-red.ts`'s now-unused `baselineBlocked` import. Export `clearHealKeyOnGreen()` (sets `lastHealKey = null`), reword the `lastHealKey` doc comment ("a green main observed by the gate or the ci handoff clears it") to name the ci handoff and the main watch, and delete the gate's own `if (baseline.baseline?.status === "green") lastHealKey = null;` with the gate.
- src/baseline/main-watch.ts: in `watchOnce`, call `clearHealKeyOnGreen()` when the settled verdict is not red (a green, or a red naming only quarantined tests) before the `if (!red) return;` line, so a merge-turned-green main drops the dedup key.
- Delete `buildMainKnownRedNote` (src/prompt/gate-notes.ts) and its `test/gate-notes.test.ts` cases: its only caller is the gate's `onKnownRed` path in `runner-run.ts`, which goes with the branch. Drop `runner-run.ts`'s `knownRed` accumulation and the import. In gate-notes.ts's header change only the "a red main blocks every other code role" clause; its pre-merge "the gate's deterministic pre-check rejects any change that leaves the suite red" clause stays for parts 3g/3–3j/3 and 3d/3–3f/3.

If any comment here names the parts that remove the pre-merge blocks, cite exactly "parts 3g/3–3j/3 and 3d/3–3f/3" — `3c/3` no longer exists (it was split into 3g–3j).
- Delete `baselineBlocked` and `BASELINE_BLOCKED_ROLES` (src/roles/roles.ts) and every reader; reword the `CODE_MAINTENANCE_ROLES` header (no "red-main blocking"), the `DEFERRABLE_ROLES` writer comment and `baselineBlocked`'s doc. `DEFERRABLE_ROLES` and `OBSERVER_ROLES` (which keeps `ci`) stay, so the healer still schedules while main is red.

### The `backlog archive` rule gets an always-on alert, its finished-history rows stat-gated for the poll (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — the `Forward, never back` part 6/6 and the `Every commit is verified on main` parts 3a/3 and 3l/3 touch docs/how-it-works.md (whichever lands second rebases at the alert list sentence), but none touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts, src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, test/backlog-archive.test.ts or test/team-alerts.test.ts; the dashboard spend card edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-operator.ts and test/gui-client.test.ts only, so it shares nothing; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/backlog-archive.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** `checkLiveFinished` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) warns when PLANS.md's `## Done` or BUGS.md's `## Fixed` still holds finished history, but it is doctor-only: every other backlog-hygiene rule (stranded plans, duplicated headings, validation gaps, plan dependencies, stale bugs and questions) has an always-on amber team alert, and this one never reaches `tumwater status`, the dashboard or the TUI. Its call chain `checkLiveFinished` → `liveFinishedHistory` → `planArchiveAll` re-parses the live files and the unbounded archives (PLANS-DONE.md is ~5 MB) on every call, so it cannot simply join the poll path. This adds the alert, fed by a stat-gated row reader so a steady-state poll pays four stats, not a full re-parse.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts: add an exported `LiveFinishedEntry` interface (`file`, `section`, `archive`, `entries`, `bytes` — the shape `liveFinishedHistory` returns) and `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root): LiveFinishedEntry[]`, the always-on twin of `checkLiveFinished`, beside `duplicatedBacklogHeadings`. It builds a cache key from `statOrNull` (`../files/files.js`) over each `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` spec's `file` and `archive` under `root` (`${dev}:${ino}:${mtimeMs}:${size}`, `absent` when the stat is null), and serves the last `liveFinishedHistory(root)` rows from a module-level `Map<string, { key: string; rows: LiveFinishedEntry[] }>` (bounded like `backlogHeadingFileCache`: clear at 64 roots) when the key is unchanged, returning a copy; on a miss it recomputes, and returns `[]` uncached when `liveFinishedHistory` throws, so an unreadable file stays `checkLiveFinished`'s signal and never breaks a status poll. `checkLiveFinished` keeps calling `liveFinishedHistory` directly, so its wording and its unreadable-file throw are unchanged. Add `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` to the existing backlog-md import; no write path (planArchiveAll, archiveNewFinishedEntries, archiveFinishedOnMain) changes.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface LiveFinishedEntry` (the same five fields) beside `BacklogHeadingDuplicate`, add `liveFinished: readonly LiveFinishedEntry[]` to `BacklogAlertsInput`, destructure it, and emit the alert in `buildBacklogAlerts` immediately after the `duplicatedHeadings` block and before the `validationGaps` block: `key: "backlog-archive"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(liveFinished.length, "live backlog file still holds", "live backlog files still hold")} finished history` ``, detail `` liveFinished.map((l) => `${l.file} ## ${l.section} holds ${plural(l.entries, "finished entry", "finished entries")} (${Math.round(l.bytes / 1024)} KB)`).join("; ") + " — every run that reads the file pays for them; `tumwater archive` moves them to the archive files" ``, `actions: []` (the fix is a command, not a drawer row). Add `liveFinished: readonly LiveFinishedEntry[] = []` as the last parameter of `teamAlerts` and pass it into the `buildBacklogAlerts({ … })` object, so every existing positional caller keeps its meaning; the alert's emission position comes from `buildBacklogAlerts`, not the parameter order.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `liveFinishedEntriesFor` with `duplicatedBacklogHeadings` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and pass `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` as the last argument of the `teamAlerts(...)` call.
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the alert-list sentence, after "a duplicated backlog section heading," add "finished history still under a live backlog file's `## Done` or `## Fixed` (the `backlog-archive` alert, the always-on twin of the doctor's `backlog archive` warn),".
- No change to `liveFinishedHistory`, `planArchiveAll`, `checkLiveFinished`, `checkBacklogHeadings`, `duplicatedBacklogHeadings` or any archive write path.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/backlog-archive.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With PLANS.md's `## Done` (or BUGS.md's `## Fixed`) holding a finished entry, `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` returns the rows `liveFinishedHistory(root)` returns, and `statusPayload`/`renderStatus` carry one amber `backlog-archive` alert naming the file, section, entry count and KB, with no actions; with both live finished sections empty, no such alert.
- Two consecutive `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` calls with no file change return equal rows, and appending a finished entry to PLANS.md makes the next call report the new row without a process restart.
- An unreadable PLANS.md (or archive) makes `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` return `[]` instead of throwing, while `checkLiveFinished(root)` still returns its non-ok outcome for the same tree; no write path changed.
- The alert sits between `backlog-headings` and `validation-gaps` in emission order when all three are present.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/backlog-archive.test.ts (which already imports `checkLiveFinished`, `liveFinishedHistory`, `makeRepo`): add "liveFinishedEntriesFor caches the finished-history rows while the files are unchanged" — seed one entry under PLANS.md's `## Done`, assert `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` deep-equals `liveFinishedHistory(root)`, call it again and assert equality, then append a second finished entry and assert the count rises to two; add "liveFinishedEntriesFor stays silent on an unreadable file while the doctor still reports it" — make PLANS.md unreadable (`fs.chmodSync(..., 0o000)` restored in a `finally`), assert `liveFinishedEntriesFor(root)` returns `[]` and `checkLiveFinished(root).level !== "ok"`. Import `liveFinishedEntriesFor` alongside `checkLiveFinished`.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts (which already imports `makeRepo`, `writeBacklogFile` and drives `statusPayload`/`renderStatus`): add "the finished-history alert follows the duplicated-heading alert and names the archive command" — a repo with an entry still under PLANS.md's `## Done` yields a `backlog-archive` alert with tone `amber` whose detail names `PLANS.md`, `## Done`, the count and `tumwater archive`, and `renderStatus` carries the title; a clean pair of live files yields none; a duplicated heading plus finished history yields `["backlog-headings", "backlog-archive"]` in that order.

So a role with `provider: deepseek`, `model: deepseek-v4` and a resolved `thinking: high` on the `strong` tier reads `deepseek/deepseek-v4 (thinking: high) (strong tier)` from `tumwater role <id>` but only `deepseek/deepseek-v4 (strong tier)` in the dashboard drawer, even though both render the same `/api/role` payload (`rolePayload`, `src/gui/gui-history-endpoints.ts`). ### The role's `backend` override joins the model-override surfaces, part 1/2: `tumwater role <id> --backend` writes `roles.<base>.backend` and the payload carries `backendOverride` (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior — the in-flight TUI Transcript `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+K` and hint plans edit only src/ui/tui/* and docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table and Check-state row, and the `Every commit is verified on main` and `Forward, never back` series edit src/merge, src/review, src/baseline, src/orchestrator, src/prompt, src/report, src/runner and src/config/config-schema.ts/config-views.ts, none of which this part touches; this part shares docs/cli.md with the two TUI plans but edits the `tumwater role` vocabulary, a different section, and shares src/roles/role-view.ts with the blocked part 3d/3, which only deletes `review.afterMerge` surfaces from it and cannot run before its part 3j/3; part 2/2 below builds on this part, since it prefills from the `backendOverride` this part adds; touches src/roles/role-view.ts src/cli/cli-role-command.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md docs/config.md test/cli-operators.test.ts test/role-view.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `roles.<base>.backend` is a documented per-role field (docs/config.md's `roles.<id>` table): the backend (`pi`, `claude`, `opencode`, `codex`) that runs the role's model, with the id passed through as written. `config set roles.<id>.backend claude` writes it, and `tumwater role <id>` already renders the resolved backend on its Model line, but the write flags beside that line stop at `--provider`/`--model`/`--thinking`, so the command an operator uses to configure a role cannot route it to another backend. **Approach.**
- `src/roles/role-view.ts`: add `backendOverride?: string` to `RoleViewPayload` beside `providerOverride`/`modelOverride`/`thinkingOverride`, and compute it beside them from `rawRoleField(root, base, "backend")` (string-only, spread only when present), so a payload for a file with no backend override stays byte-identical.

Through `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey`, `validateConfig`'s `checkEntryBackend` owns the id (rejecting an unknown one, and a `model` that cannot pair with the named backend), and the write stays atomic.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: add `tumwater role <id> --backend <id>` and `tumwater role <id> --clear-backend` usage lines beside `--provider`/`--clear-provider`, naming the four backend ids and the model/backend pair rule.
- docs/cli.md: name `--backend`/`--clear-backend` in the `tumwater role` row's vocabulary, and docs/config.md: note that `tumwater role <id> --backend` writes the `backend` field (the row's description stays).

### Forward, never back, part 4/6: the revert subsystem is deleted — no `main_revert` is emitted and a red main is healed forward (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held part 2/2; requires part 3b/6 landed, since every surface must read the forward finding before the backward readers go; parts 5/6–6/6 then delete every reader of the historical events this part stops writing; touches src/baseline/main-revert.ts (deleted) src/baseline/main-red.ts src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts src/merge/merge-core.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/runner/revision.ts docs/invariants.md docs/how-it-works.md test/main-revert.test.ts (deleted) test/operator-revert.test.ts test/revision.test.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** With a rejection answered forward, the machinery that takes a commit off main has no caller but the red-main culprit, and this part removes that too: nothing is ever removed from main, including a red main's culprit, which the watch's already-queued heal prompt repairs forward. No new `main_revert` event is logged and no revision is handed back for a red main. The event type and its readers stay, reading history (parts 5/6–6/6 delete them).

**Approach.**
- Delete the revert subsystem: src/baseline/main-revert.ts (`runMainRevert`, `revertSkipReason`, `routeMainCulprit`) is deleted; src/merge/merge-drain.ts's revert slot (`startRevert`, `handBackReverted`, `handBackRevert`, `revertReasons`, `PendingRevert`, `pendingReverts`, and `assignPendingReverts`' revert loop) is deleted; src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts's `p.revert` is gone; src/merge/merge-core.ts's `recordRevertedChange` and `handBackChange` (the reverted hand-back) are deleted; and src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts's `routeMainCulprit` wiring now calls `queueCulpritHeal` directly. `MainCulprit` moves to src/baseline/main-watch.ts, whose `onCulprit` is its only remaining producer, and keeps only the fields a red-main heal needs (`commit`, `failingTests`, `tip`). `revertCommitIn` (src/operator/revert.ts) stays: `tumwater revert` is the operator's own act, and the `operator_revert` event with it.
- A red main heals forward: src/baseline/main-red.ts's heal path becomes the only one — the heal prompt the watch already queues, with the existing wording — and `main-watch.ts`'s `onCulprit` names the tip as the culprit without routing a revert.
- **Corrected against the code (2026-10-24, feature):** src/runner/revision.ts's re-apply chain (`applyRevision`/`applyWithConflicts`, `state.revision`, `rejectedRefName`) is NOT deleted — it is shared with the surviving revise-rejected and conflict-handback paths, which a pre-merge rejection still uses. Only `pickBase`'s revert-only special case (re-applying a commit already on main that a `Revert <sha>` landed) is removed; the surviving chain re-applies by merge-base alone.
- Docs: docs/invariants.md loses INV-L1, INV-C3, INV-BS1/2/3, INV-CO1 and INV-CR1 (the `reason: "post-review"` reading is parts 5/6–6/6's, with the readers); docs/how-it-works.md's revert paragraphs describe the red-main heal prompt instead.
- No change to the pre-merge deterministic checks, the main watch's own check, or the `main_revert` event type and its readers: this part removes the emission, not the verification, and parts 5/6–6/6 remove the readers.

**Files touched.** src/baseline/main-revert.ts (deleted) src/baseline/main-red.ts src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts src/merge/merge-core.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/runner/revision.ts docs/invariants.md docs/how-it-works.md test/main-revert.test.ts (deleted) test/operator-revert.test.ts test/revision.test.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts

Import `retireLeftovers`, `leftoverRetireLines` and `type LeftoverRetireReport` from `../doctor/doctor-contention-checks.js`; `retire` is injectable so a test needs no git.

"" : "error: ") + d.message`, and calling `fetchDoctor()`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts: add `if (clickClosest(ev, "button[data-action='doctor-retire-leftovers']")) { ev.preventDefault(); retireLeftoversClick(); }` beside the other Health-card dispatch lines.

"") === ""` and the Health view): the first press sets `session.retireLeftoversArmed` and flashes a press-again confirm; the second clears it, flashes `retiring every disabled role's leftovers …`, calls `session.retireLeftovers(session.root)`, flashes `leftoverRetireLines(report).join("; ")` or `no leftover roles to retire` when the report is empty, then re-runs `run()` and resets `session.paneScroll`. A rejection flashes instead of killing the TUI.
