### The doctor's stale workspace pin raises a standing amber `workspace-pins` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — the in-flight `tumwater doctor --retire-leftovers` plan shares only src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts (this plan exports a `staleWorkspacePins` helper beside `checkWorktreePool`, that plan extracts `retirableLeftoverRoles` and adds `retireLeftovers`) and test/doctor-checks.test.ts (additive cases), while `Forward, never back` part 3b/6 adds its own comment and wording blocks to src/ui/team-alerts.ts and src/ui/status-payload.ts at the `post-merge-churn` symbols and the two TUI editor plans append their own fields at the `teamAlerts` call in src/ui/tui/tui.tsx; every shared edit is additive and whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/status-render.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `workspaces` row (`checkWorktreePool`, src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts) warns on three things: legacy leftover checkout directories, slot contention over the last 24 h, and a pin older than `PIN_STALE_MS` (a checkout held out of the pool by a run that never resumed). Only the contention third has an always-on twin: `status-payload.ts`'s `capacityContention` feeds the amber `contention` alert. The leftover-directory half is transient — startup's `retireLegacyRoleWorktrees` removes those every team start — so the missing twin is the stale pin: a resumable run parked for over a day (or a paused role's checkout) silently shrinks the pool, and no observer surface names it until an operator runs `tumwater doctor`. Give the pin the validation-gaps/`ci-stale` treatment: one shared predicate, one standing amber alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI, so the row and the alert cannot drift on what a stale pin is.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts: beside `PIN_STALE_MS` export the one predicate the row and the alert share — `export interface StaleWorkspacePin { role: string; dir: string; ageMs: number }` (role is the slot's `pinnedFor`, dir is `path.basename(slot.dir)`, ageMs is `now - pinnedAt`) and `export function staleWorkspacePins(root: string, now = Date.now()): StaleWorkspacePin[]`, filtering `readSlotsState(root).slots` to `pinnedFor !== null && pinnedAt != null && now - pinnedAt > PIN_STALE_MS`. `checkWorktreePool` deletes its inline `pins`/`stale` filters and its `stale.map(...)` prose and renders the same `feature pinned on _slot-1 for 25h` line from `staleWorkspacePins(root, now)`, so the row's wording and the alert's selection cannot disagree. The legacy-leftover and slot-wait halves are untouched (the readiness doc comment gains one clause that the stale pin is now the alert's too).
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: add `staleWorkspacePins` to the existing import from `../doctor/doctor-contention-checks.js` and re-export it beside the `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS` re-export (`export { staleWorkspacePins };`), so `tui.tsx` keeps importing every alert feed from this one module. In the module's `teamAlerts(...)` call add `staleWorkspacePins(root, now)` as the new last argument after `qaCoverageAlert(root, now)`.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: import `type StaleWorkspacePin` from `../doctor/doctor-contention-checks.js`; add `workspacePins: readonly StaleWorkspacePin[] = []` as the trailing parameter of `teamAlerts` (documented as appended last), and add `workspacePins: readonly StaleWorkspacePin[]` to `TailAlertsInput`, passing it into `buildTailAlerts({ snap, now, contention, regressedFixes, roles, workspacePins })`. In `buildTailAlerts`, immediately after the `contention` block, push the amber alert `key: "workspace-pins"`, `title` `` `${plural(workspacePins.length, "workspace pinned past a day", "workspaces pinned past a day")}` ``, `detail` joining `` `${p.role} pinned on ${p.dir} for ${Math.round(p.ageMs / 3_600_000)}h` `` with `"; "` and appending `` ` — a pinned workspace is held out of the pool; resume the role, or retire its leftovers and run \`tumwater doctor\`` ``, and `actions: openRoleActions(workspacePins)` (the existing "Open <role>" buttons). The module's alert-list doc comment gains the stale pin. No other alert's key, tone, order or wording moves.
- src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `staleWorkspacePins` from `../status-payload.js` and pass `staleWorkspacePins(root, Date.now())` as the new last argument of the `teamAlerts(...)` call, so the TUI's attention lines carry the alert too (the dashboard reads it from the status payload unchanged).
- src/ui/status-render.ts: the CLI `tumwater status` surface renders the same `teamAlerts(...)` result via `renderStatus`, so it imports `staleWorkspacePins` and passes `staleWorkspacePins(root, Date.now())` as the new last argument there too — added so the acceptance criterion's `tumwater status` promise holds (the other two survivors each now land the same trailing arg).
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the Workspace pool paragraph, after the sentence that ends "naming the number to raise `worktreeSlots` above.", add that a workspace pinned longer than a day by a run that never resumed raises the same standing amber `workspace-pins` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI that the doctor's `worktree pool` row warns about, cleared by resuming the role or retiring its leftovers.
- No change to `checkWorktreePool`'s legacy-leftover and slot-wait prose, `capacityContention`, the retention/reap paths, `PIN_STALE_MS`'s value, or any CLI flag or key.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With one slot pinned for longer than a day, `tumwater status` (and the dashboard banner and TUI attention lines) shows exactly one amber alert keyed `workspace-pins`, naming the role, the slot directory and the whole-hour age, with an "Open <role>" action for the first three pinned roles; with no stale pin it shows none.
- The alert's roles, directories and ages equal `checkWorktreePool(root, now)`'s stale-pin clause for the same slots.json — the shared `staleWorkspacePins` predicate is the only selector.
- A fresh pin, an unpinned slot, a malformed/absent slots.json and a timeouted `pinnedAt` produce no alert and no throw (the same tolerance `checkWorktreePool` has today).
- Existing alerts keep their keys, tones and order; the `contention` alert is unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts: `staleWorkspacePins is the doctor row's stale-pin selector` — for the 25 h pin the existing `checkWorktreePool` case already writes, assert `staleWorkspacePins(root, now)` deep-equals one `{ role: "feature", dir: "_slot-1", ageMs: 25 * 3_600_000 }`, and that a fresh pin and an unpinned slot yield `[]`; the existing row case still passes unchanged on the rendered line.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts: `a stale workspace pin raises the workspace-pins alert` — call `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, …)` with `[{ role: "feature", dir: "_slot-1", ageMs: 25 * 3_600_000 }]` as the last positional argument (pinning the position, as the `primary-overwrite`/`notify` cases do) and assert exactly one amber alert keyed `workspace-pins` with a title matching `/workspace pinned past a day/`, a detail including `feature`, `_slot-1`, `25h` and `tumwater doctor`, and an `actions` entry opening `feature`; an empty list adds none; two pins title `/workspaces pinned past a day/` and name both.
- test/status-payload.test.ts: `the status payload carries the doctor's stale workspace pin` — seed the 25 h pin, call the payload builder (or `staleWorkspacePins` and `checkWorktreePool` on the same root) and assert the alert detail's role/dir/hour phrase matches the doctor row's phrase, the shared-predicate pin the `capacityContention` case uses.

### The TUI Health view's key hint and docs table name the same keys: the missing `Ctrl+S` drop-pins hint and `Ctrl+U` re-sync-install row (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — the in-flight TUI Transcript `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+K` plan and the in-flight `tumwater doctor --retire-leftovers` surface plan edit `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`'s `hintLine` branches and `docs/cli.md`'s TUI-keys table at neighbouring rows this plan also touches, so whichever lands second rebases there, and the retire-leftovers plan adds both a Health hint entry and a Health docs row, which this plan's new test expects to agree; no eligible plan edits `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts`; touches src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`'s `hintLine` is the TUI's in-app key reference (its Health branch is the `else if (view.kind === "health") keys = [...]` line), and `docs/cli.md`'s `## TUI keys` table is the written one. They disagree on the Health view in two places. The code handles `Ctrl+U` as re-sync install on Health (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts`, the `key.ctrl && key.name === "u" ... session.view === session.roleIds.length + 7` arm) and the Health hint lists `["Ctrl+U", "re-sync install"]`, but `grep -n 'Ctrl+U' docs/cli.md` matches only the combined prompt-line row and the Activity declared-check row — no Health row. In the other direction the docs carry a `Ctrl+S (twice) | Health` drop-broken-pins row and the code handles it, but the Health hint omits `Ctrl+S`, so a terminal operator never sees the key the row documents. `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` cannot catch either: it compares only the set of Ctrl letters across the whole code scan and the whole docs section, so a letter documented for the wrong view or missing from a view still passes. Make the Health view's two references agree on the same key set, and add the per-view check that holds them together.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`: in the `else if (view.kind === "health") keys = [...]` line of `hintLine`, add `["Ctrl+S", "drop broken pins"]` beside `["Ctrl+K", "kill orphans"]` — the same terse form the existing two-press arms use (they show `Ctrl+K`, not `Ctrl+K (twice)`). No other hint branch changes.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the `## TUI keys` table add a row `| \`Ctrl+U\` | Health | re-sync the root checkout's install now (the terminal twin of \`tumwater doctor --resync-install\` and the dashboard Health card's Re-sync install; the \`install\` row refreshes after it) |`, matching the wording of the existing Health `Ctrl+E` reclaim row. Leave the combined `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+K` prompt-line row and the Activity `Ctrl+U` declared-check row unchanged.
- `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts`: add one test, `the Health view's hint and docs rows name the same Ctrl keys`, that derives both sides from source rather than the whole-file set. Find the Health hint line (`tui-frame.ts` split on `\n` for a line containing `view.kind === "health") keys =`) and collect its `Ctrl+([A-Z])` letters. Slice the `## TUI keys` section of `docs/cli.md` as the existing `documentedCtrlKeys` does, and for each table line whose Key cell (the second `|`-split cell) has Ctrl letters, add them to `documentedHealth` when its Where cell (the third cell) matches `/\bHealth\b/` and to `documentedAny` when it matches `/\bany view\b/`. Assert `[...hinted].filter((k) => !documentedHealth.has(k) && !documentedAny.has(k)).sort()` is `[]` (every Health hint key is documented for Health or for any view; this catches the missing `Ctrl+U` row) and that `[...documentedHealth].filter((k) => !hinted.has(k)).sort()` is `[]` (no docs Health key is unhinted; this catches the missing `Ctrl+S` hint entry). The `any view` set is what keeps the hint's `Ctrl+T`/`Ctrl+D` out of the Health-only reverse check.
- No change to any handler: the Health pane's `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+S` arms, `tui-keys.ts`, `tui-panes.ts`, the dashboard, or the three existing tests in `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`'s Health branch lists both `Ctrl+U` and `Ctrl+S`; the other branches and every non-Ctrl entry are unchanged.
- `docs/cli.md`'s `## TUI keys` section has a `Ctrl+U | Health` row; the `Ctrl+U` Activity row and the combined `Ctrl+U / Ctrl+K` prompt-line row are byte-for-byte as before, and the `Ctrl+S (twice) | Health` row is unchanged.
- The new test passes; before the two source edits it fails on exactly the missing `Ctrl+U` docs row and the missing `Ctrl+S` hint entry.
- The existing `handledCtrlKeys` tests are unchanged and still pass, so the whole-section set comparison keeps guarding stray undocumented letters.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**

### The TUI Health view toggles a role's enabled state with `Ctrl+V`, the terminal twins of the dashboard Settings card's Enable and the role drawer's Disable (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — the in-flight TUI Health `Ctrl+S` plan (broken-pin drop) shares only src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and docs/cli.md with this plan, at its `Ctrl+S` routing arm and its TUI-keys table row respectively, while this plan touches none of that plan's src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts, tui-pane-session.ts or tui-panes.ts and that plan touches none of this plan's editor modules; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-enabled.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-ctx.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/cli.md test/tui-role-enabled.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater role <id> --enable`/`--disable` writes `roles.<base>.enabled`, and the dashboard carries both controls — the role drawer's two-click Disable and the Settings card's disabled-roles list with Enable (`POST /api/role-disable`/`/api/role-enable`). The TUI has neither: a `grep` of src/ui/tui for `roles.<id>.enabled`/`--enable`/`--disable` matches nothing, so a terminal operator must leave the TUI to permanently stop a role (pause and stop are transient). This also strands the TUI's own retire flow: `retireRole` (src/operator/retire.ts) refuses a role still `enabledInConfig` (`role <id> is still enabled in tumwater.json — disable it first`), so the Health view's existing `Ctrl+X` retire editor cannot be used on the live role the operator wants to remove. Add one Health-view editor: `Ctrl+V` on the prompt line types a role id, and Enter toggles its `roles.<base>.enabled` — enabling a disabled role at once, disabling an enabled one only on a second Enter (the drawer's two-click confirm), with the director refused.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-enabled.ts` (new) — `createRoleEnabledEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, modelled line-for-line on `createRetireEditor` (tui-editor-retire.ts): it owns its `roleEnabledMode` flag and saved-draft pair, and its `handleKey` opens on `key.ctrl && key.name === "v" && ctx.view === ctx.roleIds.length + 7` after `session.editorEntryDenied("roleEnabled")` (so another editor's hold flashes its subject), calls `session.takeDraft()`, blanks the line, and flashes `enable or disable a role: type the role id, Enter to toggle, Esc to cancel`. Esc, `Ctrl+V` again, and `Ctrl+T` exit by restoring the draft. On Enter it reads `role = session.input.trim()` (empty flashes `a role id is required` and stays), rejects an id outside `knownRoleIds(loadConfigSafe(session.root).config ?? defaultConfig())` with `unknownRoleMessage(role, knownRoleIds(...))`, maps `base = baseRoleOf(role)`, and refuses only a disable with `the director cannot be disabled` (`base === DIRECTOR_ROLE && enabled`; the CLI's and the GUI's rule — the director is always enabled, so no disable is ever offered — while a config-disabled director still enables at once below, since enabling stays allowed). It computes `enabled = cfg.roles[base]?.enabled !== false`: a disabled role is enabled at once, an enabled role arms `confirmBase = base` and flashes `press Enter again to disable <base> — any other role id or Esc keeps it enabled`, and a second Enter on the same base writes through the shared `setConfigKey(session.root, \`roles.${base}.enabled\`, enabled ? "false" : "true")` the CLI, the Settings card and the drawer all use. Success exits and flashes `` `${base}: disabled` ``/`` `${base}: enabled` `` (the CLI's words); a `setConfigKey` failure flashes its error and stays open so the id can be fixed. A changed id, or a key that edits it, re-arms rather than disabling, since the confirm is keyed to the base the line currently names.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts` — add `roleEnabled: boolean` to `TuiHeld` (beside `retire`), add `"roleEnabled"` to the `EditorEnterKey` union, add `["roleEnabled", "role state"]` to `HOLDER_SUBJECTS`, and initialize `roleEnabled: false` in `createTuiEditorSession`'s `held` literal. `heldEditorFlash`/`anyEditorHeld`/`editorEntryDenied` iterate that registry, so the mutual-exclusion contract and busy-guard flash need no other change.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` — import `createRoleEnabledEditor`, append `createRoleEnabledEditor(session)` to the `editors` array (after `createRetireEditor`), add `roleEnabledMode: boolean` to the `TuiEditorState` interface (beside `retireMode`), and return `roleEnabledMode: session.held.roleEnabled` from `state()`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` — add `roleEnabledMode: boolean` to `TuiKeysState` (beside `retireMode`); `state()` already spreads `editors.state()`, so no other change.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts` — add `roleEnabledMode?: boolean` to `TuiMode`; add the mode hint branch `else if (mode.roleEnabledMode) keys = [["Enter", "enable/disable role"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]];` beside the `retireMode` branch; add `if (mode.roleEnabledMode) return [{ text: "role state", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }];` to `promptPrefix` beside the retire label; and add `["Ctrl+V", "enable/disable role"]` to the Health view line in `hintLine`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx` — add `roleEnabledMode: s.roleEnabledMode` to the `mode` object it builds from `keys.state()` (the frame's hint/prefix input).
- docs/cli.md — in the TUI keys table add a `| Ctrl+V | Health | enable or disable a role's `roles.<base>.enabled` by typed role id (Enter enables a disabled role; an enabled one disables on a second Enter; the director cannot be disabled) — the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings card's Enable and the role drawer's Disable |` row, and extend the Control-the-roles row's existing `--enable`/`--disable` clause (which ends `re-enabling one stays on the Settings card`) with `, and the TUI's Health view `Ctrl+V` toggles either state from a typed role id`.
- No change to `setConfigKey`, `retireRole`, the CLI flags, the dashboard controls or their routes, and no new pane arm or routing in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts (the editor owns `Ctrl+V` before the panes; off the Health view `Ctrl+V` keeps its Activity attach, Pending top, History revert, Inbox top and Transcript reset-counters meanings).

### `tumwater doctor --retire-leftovers` retires every disabled role's leftover worktree, branch and merge ref in one pass, the reap for the `leftover role branches` row (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the in-flight TUI `--drop-broken-pins` plan imports `dropBrokenPins`/`brokenPinDropLines` from src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts but edits only src/ui/tui files, docs/cli.md and test/tui-keys.test.ts, so this plan's edit to that module and its src/cli.ts and src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts additions are its alone; src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md are shared with the blocked `A post-merge rejection stops reverting` part 2/3 and `Forward, never back` part 3b/6 at neighbouring clauses, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The `leftover role branches` doctor row already lists every disabled role that still keeps a `tumwater/<id>` branch and names `tumwater retire --role <id>` as its fix, but clearing those leftovers takes one command per role. The four other mutating doctor rows each have a one-pass reap: `--kill-orphans` (src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts), `--commit-backlog` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts), `--resync-install` (src/build/dep-install.ts) and `--drop-broken-pins` (src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts), each also offered by the dashboard Health card. Before this change, `grep -rn 'retireLeftovers\|retire-leftovers' src docs test` printed nothing, so a fleet that churned several roles (lowered `instances`, removed custom roles, disabled roles) still needs one `tumwater retire --role` per role. Add the missing reap: `tumwater doctor --retire-leftovers` retires each role the row lists as retirable, through the same `retireRole` core `tumwater retire --role <id>` uses, in one pass. The dashboard's per-role Retire buttons and the TUI Health Ctrl+X retire editor already cover the one-role case, so this is CLI-only and needs no new TUI key or dashboard button.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts: extract the retirable-id walk out of `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` (its `listBranches` loop over `knownRoleIds(config)`/`runnerEnabled`/`CUSTOM_NAME_RE`, skipping the director) into `export async function retirableLeftoverRoles(root: string, config?: TumwaterConfig | null): Promise<{ retirable: string[]; unknown: string[] }>`, and have `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` call it, so the row and the reap can never disagree on what a retirable leftover is. Add `export interface LeftoverRetireReport { retired: { role: string; removed: string[] }[]; failed: { role: string; reason: string }[] }` and `export async function retireLeftovers(root: string, config?: TumwaterConfig | null): Promise<LeftoverRetireReport>`: for each id in `retirable`, `await retireRole(root, role, {})` (never `force`, exactly the CLI's own refusal policy) and record `{ role, removed }`; a thrown rail refusal (still enabled, unmerged commits, dirty or unusable worktree, run in progress) is caught into `{ role, reason: errorMessage(err) }` and the loop continues. Add `export function leftoverRetireLines(report: LeftoverRetireReport): string[]`, one line per retired role naming its `removed` artifacts through the same `artifactPhrase`/plural wording the retire surfaces use, and one line naming each failed role and its reason; an all-empty report yields no lines. Import `retireRole`/`artifactPhrase`/`errorMessage` as needed.
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: add `export const RETIRE_LEFTOVERS_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--retire-leftovers"] };` beside `DROP_BROKEN_PINS_FLAG`, doc-commented as the fifth mutating doctor flag, value-less like the others.
- src/cli.ts: import `type LeftoverRetireReport` from `./doctor/doctor-contention-checks.js` beside `BrokenPinDrop`; add `RETIRE_LEFTOVERS_FLAG` to `rejectUnknownArgs("doctor", …)`'s allowlist; add a `let leftoverRetire: LeftoverRetireReport | undefined;` block that runs `retireLeftovers(root, config)` before `renderDoctor`, printing `leftoverRetireLines` under `if (!args.includes("--json"))` with the same blank-line discipline the `--drop-broken-pins` block uses, and pass it into the JSON payload under a `leftoverRetire` key beside `brokenPinDrop`.
- src/cli/help.ts: append `[--retire-leftovers]` to the `tumwater doctor` synopsis line and one clause to the flags paragraph (retire each disabled role's leftover worktree/branch/merge ref, like `tumwater retire --role <id>` per role, never `--force`).
- docs/cli.md: in the Audit row's `--drop-broken-pins` clause neighbourhood, add that `--retire-leftovers` first retires each role the `leftover role branches` row calls retirable through the same `retireRole` core `tumwater retire --role <id>` uses, never forcing, and that with `--json` the report gains a `leftoverRetire` field with `retired` and `failed` lists; name it in the disabled-roles clause the row already carries.

### Forward, never back, part 3b/6: every surface reads a rejected entry as the reviewer's recorded finding, not a pending revert (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split 2026-10-24 by the plan role from the held part 3/6; requires part 1/6 landed, since a rejected entry no longer fills the revert slot; independent of part 3a/6 and shares no file with it; docs/invariants.md's revert guarantees are part 4/6's and are left alone (INV-BT4 is touched here); touches src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/failure/failure-data.ts src/failure/failure-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts src/review/post-merge-review-accept.ts src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/roles/role-render.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/cli.md docs/invariants.md test/cli-reviews.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts test/gui-client-pending.test.ts test/gui-post-review-accept.test.ts test/post-merge-review-accept.test.ts test/post-merge-review-render.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** Part 1/6 made a rejected commit stop filling the revert slot: a rejection is answered by the reviewer's own landed fix, and a rejection whose reply carried no fix is a recorded finding, not a state waiting for a revert. The renderer, the CLI, the TUI, the dashboard, the churn alert and their docs still say "waiting to revert" and "the rejection starts a revert and a re-author". This part removes every such claim so the surfaces agree with the code: a rejected entry reads `[rejected — <reasons>]`, and `--accept` retires it like any other terminal entry.

**Approach.**
- Shared label: in src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts, `postReviewStatusLabel`'s `rejected` branch returns `` `[rejected — ${entry.rejected!.map((r) => squash(r, 60)).join("; ")}]` `` (drop "waiting to revert: "), and its doc comment loses "still waiting on the revert". In src/review/post-merge-review.ts, the `PostReview.rejected` comment loses "and its revert has not been started yet (the revert slot was busy)", and the `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN` comment's "the pre-revert signal" becomes "the reviewer-fix signal". The `fixed`, `failing` and `waiting` branches are unchanged — part 1/6's `[fixed — the repair <sha> already merged on main]` already reads the fix.
- GUI twin: src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts's hand-kept `postReviewStatusLabel` `rejected` branch takes the same text and its comments lose "still waiting on the revert".
- Accept: a rejected entry waits on nothing now, so it is acceptable. In src/review/post-merge-review-accept.ts, delete `removeAcceptedEntry`'s `if (entry.rejected) return { status: "rejected", commit: entry.commit };` guard and the `rejected` member of `AcceptPostReviewOutcome`, and reword the file's comments; in src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts, delete `cmdReviewsAccept`'s `outcome.status === "rejected"` branch and the doc-comment clause; in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts, drop the "stays on main with the reviewer's reasons — there is nothing to accept" row line and the `outcome.status === "rejected"` flash branch; in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, drop the `outcome.status === "rejected"` 409 branch and the comment naming it. In src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, the row's accept-button guard drops `!Array.isArray(e.rejected)` so a rejected row renders the two-click Accept like any pending row. The `fixed` guard (a landed repair is not acceptable) stays.
- Alert and payload: src/ui/team-alerts.ts's `post-merge-churn` comment block and detail string ("the pre-revert signal", "costs a revert and a re-author") say the rejection is answered by the reviewer's own fix and the remedy is to narrow `review.afterMerge`; src/ui/status-payload.ts's `postMergeChurnAlert` doc comment takes the same wording. The alert's key, tone, title, count and actions are unchanged.
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md's post-merge-review bullet (a rejection "goes to the revert slot as above … back to its role as a revision") describes the reviewer's fix on top of main, and its "pre-revert signal" phrase takes the reviewer-fix wording; its red-main revert paragraphs stay for part 4/6. docs/cli.md's `tumwater reviews` clause, its `--accept` sentence and the Pending pane's `Ctrl+A` key row lose "waiting on its revert". docs/invariants.md's INV-BT4 (a rejected entry is accepted like any pending one) is reworded, while its revert guarantees stay for part 4/6. src/cli/help.ts's `tumwater reviews` stanza takes the same wording.

### Forward, never back, part 3a/6: a post-merge review dropped at its failure cap files its commit as backlog work (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split 2026-10-24 by the plan role from the held part 3/6; requires part 1/6 landed, since the drop sites and the entries they leave are part 1/6's; independent of part 3b/6 and shares no file with it; touches src/merge/merge-post-review.ts src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts test/backlog-archive.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** A post-merge review that never reaches a verdict disappears today: in `startPostReview` (src/merge/merge-post-review.ts) a third failed run warns "stays on main unreviewed" and `settlePostReview(root, entry.commit, null)` drops the entry, and the failed-fix-merge cap in `mergeReviewerFix` drops it the same way. The commit stays on main with nothing but an event line naming it. This part leaves the commit on main *and* files one BUGS.md `## Open` entry naming it, so an unreviewed commit becomes ordinary backlog work a role can pick up.

**Approach.**
- src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts: extract the body of `fileQuarantineBugsOnMain` — the `withLock(mergeLockDir(root), …)` + `withPrimaryWorktreeLockAsync` wrapper, the primary-on-base-branch check, the `git status --porcelain -- BUGS.md` cleanliness check, the read and `restoreBugs`/`writeTextAtomic` rollback, the `appendBugEntryLocked` appends, and the `tumwater(operator):` `git commit` — into an exported `fileBugsOnMain(root, entries: readonly { title: string; body: string }[], subject: string, opts?: { lockTimeoutMs?: number })`. `fileQuarantineBugsOnMain` becomes a thin caller that maps each `{ test, tail }` to its `quarantineTitlePrefix(test) + date + ")"` title and its body and passes the existing "File N quarantined flaky tests in BUGS.md" subject, so its behavior and tests stay as they are.
- src/merge/merge-post-review.ts: add a best-effort `fileDroppedReview(root, entry, failure)`: build one entry (title `` `post-merge review of ${shortSha(entry.commit)} never reached a verdict (found by the review role ${formatDate(new Date())})` ``, body naming `entry.summary` and the `failure` text) and call `fileBugsOnMain(root, [entry], "File an unreviewed post-merge commit in BUGS.md")`; on `{ status: "skipped" }` or a throw, log one `warnEventBestEffort(root, entry.role, …)` and return, so a filing problem never stops the drop. Import `formatDate` from ../text/datetime.js and `fileBugsOnMain` from ../backlog/backlog-archive.js.
- Call `await fileDroppedReview(...)` before the two `settlePostReview(root, entry.commit, null)` drop sites: in `startPostReview` when `failures >= POST_REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT`, passing `outcome.detail`; in `mergeReviewerFix` when `failures >= POST_REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT`, passing `` `fix did not merge: ${result}` ``. File before settling, keep the existing warnings and the `deleteRef(reviewFixRef(...))` calls, and leave the `exhausted` (REVISION_BACKSTOP) arm alone — it records its own surviving findings.

### The `qa` observer's flow-coverage ledger goes stale silently: a `qa coverage` doctor warn and a standing amber `qa-stale` alert, the twin of `ci-stale` (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan, and adds one surface rather than changing an existing one — the in-flight `Forward, never back` part 3b/6 edits the same `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md`, `test/team-alerts.test.ts` and `test/status-payload.test.ts` in neighbouring blocks, and `Every commit is verified on main` parts 3a/3 and 3b/3-3j/3 edit `docs/invariants.md`/`docs/how-it-works.md` as neighbouring clauses, so whichever lands second rebases there; none of them edits `src/run/qa-coverage.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts`, `src/ui/status-render.ts` or `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`; touches src/run/qa-coverage.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/qa-coverage.test.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `qa` is the only role that exercises the product's own flows like a user, and each run records the one flow it exercised into `.tumwater/state/qa-coverage.json` (`recordFlow`, src/run/qa-coverage.ts, from the run's `FLOW:` verdict at src/run/run-verdict.ts). That ledger's only reads are on demand — `tumwater role qa` (`rolePayload`'s `flowCoverage`, src/roles/role-view.ts) and the dashboard role drawer — so if qa is disabled, paused, wedged, or failing before it records, nothing says so and the team silently loses its only flow-level observer. The `ci` role already has exactly this surface for its own ledger: a `ci parity` doctor row and the standing amber `ci-stale` alert, both reading the one `ciParityStalled` predicate (src/run/ci-parity.ts). Give the qa ledger the same: a ledger whose newest exercise is over three days old raises a `qa coverage` doctor warn and one standing amber `qa-stale` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI.

**Approach.**
- `src/run/qa-coverage.ts`: import `DAY_MS` from `../text/datetime.js` beside the existing `formatAge`; add `export const QA_COVERAGE_STALE_MS = 3 * DAY_MS` and `export function qaCoverageStalled(coverage: QaCoverage, now: number): boolean`. True only when the ledger has at least one well-formed entry and every entry's `lastRunAt` is older than the window (`now - max(lastRunAt) > QA_COVERAGE_STALE_MS`). An empty ledger (a missing file, or a project that never ran qa) is not a stall — the same "no record yet is not a stall" rule `ciParityStalled` applies to a missing parity record. This is the one stall predicate the row and the alert share.
- `src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts`: add `export function checkQaCoverage(root: string, now: number = Date.now()): CheckOutcome`: read with `readQaCoverage(root)`; an empty ledger is `okOutcome("no qa flow coverage recorded yet — the qa role has not completed a flow")`; a non-stalled ledger is an `okOutcome` naming the newest exercised flow and its age; a stalled one is a `warnOutcome` naming the newest flow, its age and that the qa role is disabled, paused, or unable to record (mirroring `checkCiParity`'s wording and shape). `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: register `{ name: "qa coverage", run: () => checkQaCoverage(root) }` immediately after the `ci parity` row, so the default `tumwater doctor` run, the Health card and the TUI Health tab all carry it.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: export `interface QaCoverageStale { newestFlow: string; newestAt: number; count: number }` and `export function qaCoverageAlert(root: string, now: number = Date.now()): QaCoverageStale | null` — read the ledger and return null unless `qaCoverageStalled`, else the newest flow name, its `lastRunAt` and the entry count (the `quarantineAlert` shape). Add `qaCoverage: QaCoverageStale | null = null` as the new trailing parameter of `teamAlerts` and pass it into `buildMergeAlerts` (`MergeAlertsInput`) beside `ciParity`; there push the alert exactly like the `ci-stale` block: `key: "qa-stale"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `qa's flow coverage has not advanced in over ${QA_COVERAGE_STALE_MS / DAY_MS} days` `` (import the constant from `../run/qa-coverage.js`), detail naming the newest flow and its age plus "the qa role is disabled, paused, or unable to record; resume or enable it, or check `tumwater doctor`", and no action button (the role drawer already carries the toggle). Pass `qaCoverageAlert(root, now)` as the trailing argument at the payload's own `teamAlerts(...)` call; `src/ui/status-render.ts` and `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx` do the same at their direct calls, so the CLI status, the TUI and the dashboard cannot disagree on whether qa has gone quiet.
- Docs: `docs/invariants.md`, under the existing "Observer run ledgers: a failed ledger write never fails a run" section, add `INV-BW3`: the `qaCoverageStalled` predicate is the one home of the stall decision, shared by `checkQaCoverage` and `qaCoverageAlert`, pinned by the tests below (mirroring `ci-stale`'s one-predicate rule). `docs/cli.md`'s Audit row: name the `qa coverage` row in the doctor list and the standing `qa-stale` alert beside the `ci-stale` mention. `docs/how-it-works.md`: the observer/qa paragraph gains one sentence that a coverage ledger whose newest exercise is over three days old raises the doctor warn and the standing alert.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `qaCoverageStalled({}, now)` is false; it is true only for a non-empty ledger whose newest `lastRunAt` is more than `QA_COVERAGE_STALE_MS` old; a ledger with one fresh entry among old ones is false.
- `tumwater doctor` reports an `ok` `qa coverage` row for a missing ledger or one exercised within three days, and a `warn` row naming the newest flow and its age for an older one; the row appears in the default doctor run and in the Health card/TUI Health list.
- With a stalled ledger, the alert list carries exactly one amber `qa-stale` alert on all three surfaces (`tumwater status`, the dashboard's alert banner, the TUI attention lines); inside the window, and with an empty ledger, there is none. Each of the three `teamAlerts(...)` call sites passes `qaCoverageAlert(root, now)`.

**Tests.**

**Goal.** `tumwater reviews --status <state>[,<state>...]` (landed 2026-10-24) keeps only the post-merge review entries in the listed states, and its accepted vocabulary is `POST_REVIEW_STATES` (`["waiting", "failing", "rejected", "fixed"]`, src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts), parsed by `parseReviewStatusList` (src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts). The generated completion scripts complete every other value-bearing flag — role ids after `--role`, result classes after `--result`, event-type codes after `--type`, summary groups after `--by`, thinking levels after `--thinking`, model selectors after `--model` — but `--status` completes nothing: `bashScript` (src/cli/completion.ts) has no `--status` arm and `fishFlagValue` has no `--status` branch, so `tumwater reviews --status wa<TAB>` offers nothing even though the flag itself is completed from `help.ts`'s stanza. Add the four-state vocabulary from its one export, with the same comma-list handling `--result`/`--type` already use.

**Approach.**
- src/cli/completion.ts: import `POST_REVIEW_STATES` from `../review/post-merge-review-render.js` and add `const REVIEW_STATE_WORDS = [...POST_REVIEW_STATES]` beside `THINKING_LEVEL_WORDS`, with a doc comment naming `reviews --status` as the consumer (one source, so a new state completes the moment `POST_REVIEW_STATES` grows).
- `bashScript`: add an arm beside the existing `--type` arm — `if [ "$prev" = "--status" ]; then _tumwater_list "${REVIEW_STATE_WORDS.join(" ")}" "$cur"; return 0; fi`. `_tumwater_list` is the comma-list helper the `--role`/`--result`/`--type` arms use, so a partial list keeps its earlier items (`waiting,r<TAB>` → `waiting,rejected`) and drops the states already listed, matching `parseReviewStatusList`'s comma-list shape.
- `fishFlagValue`: add `if (flag === "--status") return ` -x -a "(__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_review_states)"`;` before the final `return ""`.
- `fishScript`: define `__tumwater_review_states` beside `__tumwater_types` — `function __tumwater_review_states; printf '%s\n' ${REVIEW_STATE_WORDS.join(" ")} | __tumwater_unlisted; end` — so the fish comma-list path skips already-listed states the same way.
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` sentence's list gains "review states after `reviews --status`" beside its result-class and event-type clauses.
- No change to `POST_REVIEW_STATES`, `parseReviewStatusList`, `statusFlagSpec`, `cmdReviews`, or the command's flag set; the flag token is already completed from the help-derived spec.

### A stalled `ci` parity raises a doctor warn and a standing amber `ci-stale` alert, so main's full-suite verification silently going days without covering a new tip is surfaced on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior — the `Forward, never back` parts edit src/review, src/merge, src/verdict, src/runner, src/prompt and src/report, the `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/config, src/orchestrator and src/runner, and the bug-parked plan edits src/backlog, src/doctor/doctor.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog*.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts and rewords the two existing hold blocks in src/ui/team-alerts.ts. This plan edits src/run/ci-parity.ts and src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts, which none of them touches, and adds one `ciParity` field to teamAlerts's `Pick<StatusSnapshot, …>` plus one amber block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts; the bug-parked plan adds no `Pick` field and rewords neighbouring blocks, so whichever lands second rebases over that list; it edits no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/roles, src/backlog, src/gui or src/ui/gui file; touches src/run/ci-parity.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/ci-parity.test.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The `ci` role's parity ledger (src/run/ci-parity.ts) records the main tip and lock each of its full-suite runs covered. Its two always-on readers — the `ci parity` doctor row (`checkCiParity`, src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts) and the status-header badge (`ciParityBadge`/`ciParityTone`, src/ui/badges.ts) — both read a record whose tip no longer matches main as `stale`, and both treat that as harmless: the row is `ok` and the badge is a calm blue, because the role runs on its own 2-hour clock and main moves on every merge, so a post-merge gap is normal. But a `stale` verdict that stays stale for days is not normal: it means the role that is now the full suite's own runner — and, after the `Every commit is verified on main` parts land, the only full-suite verification — has silently stopped covering new tips (disabled, paused, wedged, or failing before it records). Every always-on surface still reads fine. Give that stall a doctor warn and one standing amber alert over a single shared threshold and predicate, so the row, the alert and the badge's own wording cannot disagree on when stale is a problem.

**Approach.**
- src/run/ci-parity.ts: add `export const CI_PARITY_STALE_MS = 3 * DAY_MS` (import `DAY_MS` from `../text/datetime.js`) and `export function ciParityStalled(parity: { state: "current" | "stale" | "failed"; lastRunAt: number } | undefined, now: number): boolean`, true only when a record exists, its `state` is `"stale"` (a `"failed"` record already warns, a `"current"` one is verified for the tip), and `now - parity.lastRunAt > CI_PARITY_STALE_MS`. The parameter is structural, not the `CiParityStatus` type from src/status/status-polls.ts, so the existing `status-polls.ts → ci-parity.ts` import edge stays one-way. Update the module doc to name the stall rule.
- src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts, `checkCiParity`: in the existing `stale` branch, when `ciParityStalled({ state: "stale", lastRunAt: entry.lastRunAt }, now)` return `warnOutcome` naming the covered tip and lock and their age, the current tip and lock, and the stall (no full-suite run has covered a tip in over three days, so the `ci` role is disabled, paused, or unable to record); otherwise keep the existing `okOutcome` stale wording. The `current` and `failed` branches are unchanged (a failed record already warns). This one change reaches `tumwater doctor`, the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab, which all render doctor rows.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `"ciParity"` to the `Pick<StatusSnapshot, …>` the `teamAlerts` `snap` parameter reads (src/status/status-data.ts already carries `StatusSnapshot.ciParity`; no new positional argument, so status-payload.ts's call site is untouched), import `ciParityStalled` and `CI_PARITY_STALE_MS` from ../run/ci-parity.js, and in the alerts list add one amber block with key `ci-stale`, emitted only when `ciParityStalled(snap.ciParity, now)`: title `plural`-shaped, e.g. `main's full suite has not covered a tip in over 3 days`, detail naming the covered sha (shortSha of `snap.ciParity.covered`) and its age (`humanAgo(snap.ciParity.lastRunAt, now)`) and the current main tip when one is resolvable, with the remedy naming the `ci` role (enable/resume it, or `tumwater doctor`) and no action button (the fix is a role toggle the role drawer already has). Place it beside the other verification alerts (after `main-diff-rules`, before the pause/quiet group) so a spent budget or red main still leads. Add `ci-stale` to the `ALERT_MARKS`-driven vocabulary and docs/how-it-works.md's dashboard-alerts list.
- src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, src/ui/gui/*: no change — the TUI attention lines, `tumwater status` attention lines and the dashboard alerts list already render whatever `teamAlerts` returns.
- docs/cli.md: the `ci parity` clause inside the `tumwater doctor` row gains the warn-past-three-days sentence. docs/how-it-works.md: the dashboard-alerts list sentence gains the `ci-stale` one.
- No change to `ciParityForPoll`, `parityIsCurrent`, `currentCiParityState`, `ciParityBadge`, `ciParityTone`, `readCiParity`/`recordParity`, `renderParityBlock`, or the `ci` role's prompt.

### A project with no declared check raises a standing amber `no-check` alert, so the review gate's pre-check, the red-main baseline and redeploy's green check silently being off is surfaced on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the `Forward, never back` parts edit src/review, src/merge, src/verdict, src/runner, src/prompt and src/report, the `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/config, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/status/status-polls.ts and src/ui/status-model.ts, and the `ci` parity plan edits src/run/ci-parity.ts, src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts, src/ui/team-alerts.ts and the two docs. This plan leaves src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts and src/run/ci-parity.ts untouched, and computes its rule in src/status/status-data.ts, which none of them edits; the only shared files are src/ui/team-alerts.ts (this plan and the `ci` parity plan each add one field to the `snap` `Pick` and one amber block, so whichever lands second rebases over the field list and the neighbouring block) and the two docs lines; touches src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `checkBuildCheck` (src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts) warns `none declared — the review gate's build pre-check, the red-main baseline, and redeploy's green check are all off (set \`check.command\` in tumwater.json for a non-npm repo)`, but only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. On the always-on surfaces there is no signal at all: the header's `mainCheckBadge` (src/ui/badges.ts) renders only from a `build_check` event and silently renders nothing when no check has run, and no alert names the absent safety layer. A team running on a non-npm project, or any tree where `detectBuildCheck` finds neither a `check.command` nor a qualifying npm `package.json`, therefore merges with all three deterministic gates off and nothing says so. Give the rule the doctor-twin treatment the other silent-state rows got: one shared rule, an always-on amber `no-check` alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI.

**Approach.**
- The rule's one home already exists: `detectBuildCheck(root, config)` (src/build/build-check-detect.ts) returns `null` exactly when no check is declared, and `checkBuildCheck` calls it. No new predicate is needed; the alert reads the same result through the snapshot so the two cannot disagree.
- src/status/status-data.ts: in `snapshot()`, compute `const noDeclaredCheck = detectBuildCheck(root, cfg) === null;` (import `detectBuildCheck` from `../build/build-check-detect.js`; `cfg` is the config the snapshot already loads and is structurally a `CheckConfigSlice`), and add `noDeclaredCheck: noDeclaredCheck ? true : undefined,` beside `ciParity: ciParityForPoll(root, cfg)`. Add `noDeclaredCheck?: boolean;` to `StatusSnapshot` with a doc comment naming the rule and the doctor `check` row it twins (present only when no check is declared, so the `snapshotWith` fixtures that omit it stay valid and render no alert). One compute serves both the dashboard (which calls `snapshot()` through `statusPayload`) and the TUI (whose `renderStatus` receives a `snapshot()`), so the surfaces cannot diverge.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `"noDeclaredCheck"` to the `snap` `Pick<StatusSnapshot, …>` in the exported `teamAlerts` parameter and in `StatusAlertsInput`, and in `buildStatusAlerts` push one amber block with key `no-check` immediately after the existing `install` block: title `No project check is declared — the safety gates are off`; detail naming the three gates and the fix (`The review gate's build pre-check, the red-main baseline and redeploy's green check have nothing to run. Set \`check.command\` in tumwater.json (or add a test/typecheck/build npm script) so merges are verified.`); `actions: []` (the fix is a config edit the Settings view already offers, and the dashboard Health card and TUI Health tab run the same doctor row). No new positional parameter is added, so `status-payload.ts`'s and `status-render.ts`'s `teamAlerts(...)` call sites are untouched.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: expose the raw field in the `statusPayload` object beside `mainCheck`/`ciParity` (`...(snap.noDeclaredCheck ? { noDeclaredCheck: true } : {})`), commented as the machine-readable twin of the alert, so `tumwater status --json` scripts can read it.
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater status` row's alert enumeration gains the no-declared-check alert, and the `tumwater doctor` row's `check` clause says the same state raises the standing alert. docs/how-it-works.md: the dashboard-alerts list sentence (the `The web dashboard opens on Team: alerts for whatever needs you (…)` paragraph) gains it.
- No change to `checkBuildCheck` (src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts stays untouched), `detectBuildCheck`, `mainCheckBadge`, the review gate, the baseline or redeploy.

### Forward, never back, part 2/6: the self-fix chain is counted and its dead end stops the fixes and clears the entry (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split from the held parts 1/2–2/2; requires part 1/6 landed, since the chain this counter bounds is the fix chain part 1/6 lands; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/merge/merge-post-review.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** A self-fix chain cannot loop forever, and its dead end is operator-visible. A landed fix enters the queue as a normal post-review entry (`addPostReview`, `summary` = the finding it answers), so the next iteration reviews it like any unreviewed commit; the entry carries the reviewed commit's round + 1 and stops at `REVISION_BACKSTOP` (src/runner/revision.ts), clearing the entry. The answered plan is deliberately NOT held at the stop: its implementation landed and was archived to PLANS-DONE.md before the reviewed commit, so it is never under `## Planned` when the stop runs — there is nothing left to hold (unlike a rejection's exhaustion, which holds a live `## Planned` plan). Without this part the forward path as written is counted by neither `state.lastReview` nor the backstop, so a fix that never converges is an unbounded loop with an invisible dead end (plans/post-merge-fix-forward.md "The machinery a forward arm can reuse").

**Approach.**
- Carry the round on the fix: when the harness commits the reviewer's fix (part 1/6), its body carries the `Revision: <n>` trailer one past the reviewed commit's round (`revisionRoundOf`, src/git/commit-message.ts), so the next review of that fix reads its own round from the same place a rejection's hand-back reads it.
- Stop at the backstop: in `reviewMergedCommit`/`startPostReview` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts, src/merge/merge-post-review.ts), when the reviewed commit's round reaches `REVISION_BACKSTOP`, the reviewer records its surviving reasons (a `revision`/`exhausted` event) instead of committing a fix, deletes the review-fix ref, returns `{ kind: "exhausted" }`, and the harness settles the entry null so nothing re-reviews it. No `holdEntryAfterExhaustion` and no **Needs review** hold: a rejection's exhaustion holds a live `## Planned` plan, but a post-merge answered plan is already archived under `## Done`, so the hold's `## Planned`-search would be a deliberate no-op — the stop only stops and clears.
- One counter: reuse `revisionRoundOf` and `REVISION_BACKSTOP` rather than a second counter, so the self-fix chain and the rejection chain share `REVISION_BACKSTOP` and cannot drift.
- A landed fix is a post-review entry, not a `state.revision`/`state.forwarded` hand-back: the round lives on the fix commit's body, and the stop writes no runner state beyond the review event. (Part 1b/6 deletes `state.forwarded`; this part does not write it.)

**Files touched.** src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/merge/merge-post-review.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts — the self-fix chain reuses `REVISION_BACKSTOP` (src/runner/revision.ts) and `revisionRoundOf` (src/git/commit-message.ts) without editing them, and the review-chain tests live in test/post-merge-review.test.ts (not test/revision.test.ts) because the chain's machinery is the post-merge review subsystem. There is no plan-claim carriage: the authoring role's plan is not carried onto the review entry, because the stop holds nothing.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The landed fix appears as a new post-review entry and is reviewed on a later iteration; its commit body carries `Revision: <n>` one past the reviewed commit's round.
- A chain of self-fixes stops at `REVISION_BACKSTOP`: the reviewer stops fixing, records the surviving findings, and the post-review entry is cleared — no fix commit, no review-fix ref, and no **Needs review** hold are produced.
- There is one backstop constant: the self-fix chain and the rejection chain both read `REVISION_BACKSTOP`, and no second counter is introduced.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/post-merge-review.test.ts: `a self-fix chain stops at the backstop and clears the entry` — walk the fix commits' `Revision` rounds to `REVISION_BACKSTOP` and assert the entry is cleared and no **Needs review** hold is fabricated.
- test/post-merge-review.test.ts: `a reviewer's fix commit carries the next revision round` — assert the landed `tumwater(reviewer): Fix` commit's body names one past the reviewed commit's round, and that a review at the backstop records reasons instead of committing a fix.

### Forward, never back, part 1b/6: the failed-forward hand-back machinery is deleted — a rejected commit is answered only by the reviewer's own fix (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split from the held part 1/6; requires part 1/6 landed, since the plumbing this part deletes is dead only once a rejection stops filling the revert slot; touches src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/merge/merge-core.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts src/runner/runner-state.ts src/runner/runner-state-load.ts src/run/run-verdict.ts src/run/run-stage.ts src/prompt/gate-notes.ts src/paths.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/main-revert.test.ts test/revision.test.ts test/merge-drain.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

### Forward, never back, part 1/6: the reviewer's fix-forward prompt replaces the revert slot, so a post-merge rejection never reverts (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; requires part 1a/6 landed, since the harness that commits and lands the reviewer's fix is part 1a/6, and the switch that asks for an edit merges only once that landing path is the running build; its scope split again 2026-10-24 by the plan role — part 1b/6 below deletes the failed-forward hand-back plumbing this part leaves with no caller; split from the held parts 1/2–2/2; supersedes the accounting plan and parts 1/3–3/3 of "A post-merge rejection stops reverting" above; design half: plans/post-merge-fix-forward.md "Decision"; part 2/6 below accounts and bounds the self-fix chain, part 3/6 files a review that never reaches a verdict and updates every surface, and parts 4/6–6/6 delete the revert machinery this part stops using; lands before "Every commit is verified on main" part 3/3 below, which removes the last pre-merge block; touches src/merge/merge-post-review.ts src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts test/gate-prompts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 3**

**Goal.** Nothing is ever taken off main for a post-merge finding. A rejection today pays a revert commit, a gate run on the revert inside the single merge slot, a hand-back to the author and a second review — 11 such cycles in the trailing day of 2026-10-23/24, every one a doc/claim slip (plans/post-merge-fix-forward.md "Measurement"), and 8 of 11 are the class a forward fix repairs on top of main in one run. With part 1a/6's landing path in place, this part makes the reviewer's own fix the only answer a rejection gets: `drainPostReviews` stops building the revert-slot culprit, and the post-merge review prompt tells the reviewer that a finding it can repair is the work — make the minimal fix in the worktree, leave the edit, and end with the verdict line plus `FIX: <files changed>`. Self-review is deliberate: at this project's 53% reject rate (plans/reviewer-as-role.md) the author and the reviewer were already rewriting the same text by turns, so the second reader was mostly nominal. The red-main revert is untouched here; parts 4/6–6/6 delete it.

**Approach.**
- A post-merge rejection stops filling the revert slot. src/merge/merge-post-review.ts `drainPostReviews` no longer builds a revert-slot culprit (`postReview: { reasons }` and the `skipChecks` WeakSet go): a rejected entry is answered by the reviewer's own fix (part 1a/6), never by a revert. The failed-forward fallback `sendReviewToRole` and the parked-forward plumbing it alone used are now unreachable and are deleted by part 1b/6 below, not here.
- What deliberately stays until part 4/6: `MainCulprit.postReview` (never set once `drainPostReviews` stops building the slot item, but still read by `runMainRevert` and `startRevert`), `startRevert`, `handBackReverted`, `revertReasons` and src/baseline/main-revert.ts itself, because the red-main revert still runs through them, and `revertCommitIn` (src/operator/revert.ts) with the `operator_revert` event, which is the operator's own act and stays for good.
- src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts `buildReviewPrompt` (its post-merge arm): the reviewer is told that a finding it can repair is the work — make the minimal fix in the worktree, leave the edit, and end with the verdict line plus `FIX: <files changed>`; a finding it cannot repair is recorded as the reasons are today. The clause renders only when the post-merge mode is set, so a pre-merge caller's prompt is byte-identical.
- The self-fix chain's accounting and bound, the failure cap and the surfaces are part 2/6 and part 3/6, not this part: this part only makes a repairable finding become a landed fix.

- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/post-merge-review.test.ts (this part's revert-slot cases live here, not in test/merge-drain.test.ts as the plan's anchor guessed): the `drainUntilRevert` helper and the tests that reverted and handed a rejection back (`a rejecting post-merge review reverts the commit and hands it back as a revision`, `a post-merge rejection of an already-archived entry restores the live entry and fetches the revision`, `a rejected entry stays queued until its revert ran`, `a queued rejection fills the revert slot …`) were replaced with forward assertions — a rejected entry never fills `p.revert` and stays recorded in post-review.json while its commit stays on main, and the torn-entry, failed-write and queueing cases are kept.

### The doctor's `claimed bugs` finding becomes a standing amber alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI — the always-on twin of the false-fix scan, made poll-cheap by a stat-keyed source haystack (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior — the `Forward, never back` parts edit src/review, src/merge, src/verdict/fix-claim.ts's `falseFixReason` callers and docs/invariants.md, but none of them edits `sourceHaystack`/`cachedSourceHaystack` or the doctor's fix-claim scan; the `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/config, src/orchestrator and src/runner; the post-merge-rejection parts edit src/merge, src/review and src/cli; the Ready-only Backlog plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts and its neighbours and no src/ui/team-alerts.ts. It shares src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx and docs/how-it-works.md with the in-flight `stale questions` plan, which appends its own trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and its own amber block in the same `buildBacklogAlerts` — both additions are additive and whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/verdict/fix-claim.ts src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/fix-claim.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `checkFixClaims` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) warns when a newest Fixed record is a false fix — its Fix paragraph names symbols, and **none** of them exist anywhere on the tree. This is the class the review chain has burned on (BUGS-FIXED.md's 105-run, 41-h fight over an already-fixed entry), and unlike its sibling `checkValidationGaps` — which got an always-on alert precisely because its scan runs no source-tree walk — it is visible only when an operator runs `tumwater doctor`. Its scan builds `sourceHaystack` (src/verdict/fix-claim.ts), which reads every non-markdown file under `src/`, `test/` and `scripts/` (~15 MB here), so it cannot run on the 1 Hz observer poll as it stands; `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`'s validation-gaps comment says as much. Give the rule the validation-gaps treatment: one shared scan, one amber alert, and a stat-keyed haystack cache so the poll reads the tree only when a file changed.

**Approach.**
- `src/verdict/fix-claim.ts`: add `export function cachedSourceHaystack(root: string): string` beside `sourceHaystack`, backed by a module-level `Map<string, { signature: string; text: string }>` (cleared past a small cap, like the other stat caches). It walks the same files `sourceHaystack` walks (the private `walkSourceFiles`, `node_modules`/`dist` skipped) plus `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`, builds a signature of each file's path + `mtimeMs` + `size` (`statSync`, which `sourceHaystack` already calls per file) sorted so the walk order cannot matter, and on a match returns the cached text with no file reads; on a miss it reads and stores. The cache is transparent — its return equals `sourceHaystack(root)` for the same tree — so the gate's `falseFixReason`, which keeps calling `sourceHaystack`, is untouched.
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts`: add `export interface FixClaimProblem { heading: string; missing: string[] }` and a private `classifyFixClaims(records: readonly BacklogEntry[]): FixClaimProblem[]` holding the loop currently inside `checkFixClaims` (skip records whose `fixSymbols(body)` is empty; build the haystack once via `cachedSourceHaystack(root)`, not `sourceHaystack`; keep a record when every symbol is `unbackedSymbols`). Add `export function fixClaimProblems(root: string): FixClaimProblem[]` over the same `fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)` scan `validationGapRecords` uses, and rewrite `checkFixClaims` to keep its `readBacklogChecked(root, "BUGS.md")` guard and then format its existing message from `fixClaimProblems(root)` (first row's `heading`/`missing`, `andMore` over the rest), so the row and the alert share the one scan exactly as `checkValidationGaps`/`validationGapProblems` do.
- `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`: import `type FixClaimProblem` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` beside `ValidationGapProblem`; add `fixClaims: readonly FixClaimProblem[]` to `BacklogAlertsInput` and `fixClaims: readonly FixClaimProblem[] = []` as the final `teamAlerts` parameter, threading it into `buildBacklogAlerts`. There, in a block beside `validation-gaps`, when non-empty emit an amber `false-fixes` alert: title `plural(fixClaims.length, "Fixed record names code that is not on this tree", "Fixed records name code that is not on this tree")`; detail `BUGS.md records "${first.heading}" as Fixed, but none of the symbols its Fix paragraph names exist on this tree: ${missingSymbolNames(first.missing)}` plus `joinWithMore(rest.map((p) => "\"" + p.heading + "\""), 3)`, then ` — land the fix or keep the bug Open / refresh a stale record` (the doctor's own wording, so the two say the same thing); `actions: []` (the fix is editing BUGS.md, like `validation-gaps`).
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/status-render.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`: import `fixClaimProblems` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and pass `fixClaimProblems(root)` as the final `teamAlerts(...)` argument (status-payload's `alerts:` call; the `renderStatus` and TUI attention calls).
- `docs/how-it-works.md`, the dashboard-alerts paragraph in "More controls": after the `validation gaps` item add "a Fixed record whose Fix paragraph names code that is not on the tree".
- No change to `checkFixClaims`'s rule, `fixSymbols`, `unbackedSymbols`, `sourceHaystack`, `falseFixReason`, `FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED`, or any backlog writer.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A repo whose newest Fixed record names only symbols absent from `src/`/`test/`/`scripts/`/`package.json`/`tsconfig.json` makes `tumwater status`, the dashboard payload's `alerts` and the TUI attention lines carry one amber `false-fixes` alert naming that record and its missing symbols; a repo whose newest Fixed records all name at least one live symbol carries none.
- The alert and `checkFixClaims` agree on the set because both read `fixClaimProblems(root)` (one `fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)` scan and one `cachedSourceHaystack(root)`): the doctor's message and the alert name the same first record.
- `cachedSourceHaystack(root)` returns the same string as `sourceHaystack(root)` on the same tree, and a steady-state poll of an unchanged tree performs no file reads (the signature walk is stat-only); after a source file's content changes, the next call reflects it.
- An empty `fixClaims` list (the existing short-argument `teamAlerts` calls) emits no `false-fixes` alert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/fix-claim.test.ts: `cachedSourceHaystack caches on the stat signature and re-reads on a change` — in a temp tree write a non-md source file; assert `cachedSourceHaystack(root)` equals `sourceHaystack(root)` and contains the file's text, a second call returns the same text, and after rewriting the file (a different mtime/size) the next call contains the new text and not the old. Plus `fixClaimProblems names a record whose symbols are all absent` — seed BUGS.md `## Fixed` with a record whose Fix paragraph names a symbol that exists nowhere; assert one row with that heading and the missing name, and that adding the symbol's text to a `src/` file (with the cache reset by the stat change) empties the row.
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: `checkFixClaims and fixClaimProblems agree on the false record` — the same seeded repo, assert the check's `warnOutcome` message contains the heading `fixClaimProblems(root)[0].heading` names.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts: `the false-fixes alert names the first record and folds the rest` — call `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, …, fixClaims)` (filling the intervening defaulted arguments) with two `FixClaimProblem` rows; assert one amber `false-fixes` alert whose title counts both, whose detail names the first heading and its missing symbols and folds the second, and whose `actions` is `[]`; an empty list yields no `false-fixes` alert.
- test/status-payload.test.ts: `the status payload carries the false-fixes alert` — a repo with a false newest Fixed record includes a `false-fixes` alert in `statusPayload(root).alerts`, and a repo without one omits it.

### The doctor's `stale questions` finding becomes a standing amber alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI — the always-on twin of its one backlog row with no twin yet (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent in behavior of every eligible plan — no eligible plan changes this rule or adds a backlog alert. It shares `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/status-render.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`, `test/team-alerts.test.ts` and `test/status-payload.test.ts` with the in-flight parallel-instances plan, which adds its own `stale-claims` alert through the same four modules and its own cases to the same two tests: both are additive alert modules and additive test cases, so whichever lands second rebases there. It shares `docs/how-it-works.md` with several waiting plans as a neighbouring sentence. It touches no other planning surface; touches src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `stale questions` row (`checkStaleQuestions`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog-bugs.ts) warns when an open QUESTIONS.md entry's `(asked by … YYYY-MM-DD)` stamp is at least `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS` (7) old, but unlike its sibling `stale bugs` row it has no always-on twin: `teamAlerts`' `questions` alert (src/ui/team-alerts.ts `buildBacklogAlerts`) is indigo and lists every open question with no age, and only an operator who runs `tumwater doctor` learns that one has waited a week. A question that waits too long is a role stuck behind a decision — the exact class every other backlog row already raises as an amber alert (`stale-bugs`, `waiting-bugs`, `stale-prompts`, `stale-merges`). Give it the same twin, computed from the one threshold and stamp parser the doctor uses so the alert and the row cannot disagree on which questions are stale.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`: add `export interface StaleQuestion { index: number; position: number; title: string; days: number; }` beside `StaleBug`, with `position` the 1-based `questions --list` / `tumwater questions answer <n>` number, `title` stamp-stripped for prose, `days` the whole-day age, and `index` the 0-based `## Open` position kept only as the file-order tiebreak for `byDaysThenIndex` (the `questions` action opens the Questions tab, so the alert carries no row address). Add `staleQuestions: readonly StaleQuestion[] = []` as the final parameter of `teamAlerts`, thread it into `buildBacklogAlerts`'s input object, and there emit one amber `stale-questions` alert directly after the `questions` alert (so existing key orders are unchanged when the list is empty, and a repo with both reads `questions, stale-questions, refused, …`). Title `${plural(staleQuestions.length, "open question waited", "open questions waited")} 7+ days for an answer`; detail `#${first.position} "${first.title}" has waited ${first.days}d for an answer` + the `moreDetail(rest.map((q) => q.title))` fold, then ` · answer it with \`tumwater questions answer ${first.position} "<decision>"\`, or close it in QUESTIONS.md`; action `[{ label: "Answer", act: "questions" }]` (the `questions` alert's own action). The comment names `checkStaleQuestions` as the shared row, like the `stale-bugs` comment names `checkStaleBugs`.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: add `export function staleOpenQuestions(root: string, now = Date.now()): StaleQuestion[]` beside `staleOpenBugs`, built exactly like it from `openQuestionEntries(root)`, `questionFilingDate(entry.title)` (src/backlog/question-answer.js), `ageInDays`, `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS` (import beside the existing `STALE_BUG_DAYS` from ../doctor/doctor-backlog.js) and `stripEntryStamp`, keeping only dated headings at or past the threshold and sorting through `byDaysThenIndex` (oldest-first, ties in file order) — no refused/waiting filter, because questions carry no such notes. Pass it as the final `teamAlerts(...)` argument in the payload builder's call.
- `src/ui/status-render.ts` and `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`: import `staleOpenQuestions` from `../status-payload.js` and pass `staleOpenQuestions(root, now)` as the final `teamAlerts(...)` argument, so `tumwater status`, the dashboard banner list and the TUI attention lines all carry it.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`, the dashboard-alerts paragraph in "More controls": after the existing "open questions" item, add "a question that has waited a week for an answer".
- No change to `checkStaleQuestions`, `openQuestionEntries`, `questionFilingDate`, `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS`, the `questions` alert or any backlog writer.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A repo whose QUESTIONS.md `## Open` holds a question stamped 7+ days ago makes `tumwater status`, the dashboard payload's `alerts` and the TUI attention lines carry one amber `stale-questions` alert naming that question's number, title and day count, with the `Answer` action; the same repo with only fresh or undated questions carries none.
- The alert is emitted right after `questions` and folds every question past the first through `moreDetail`, so two stale questions render `2 open questions waited 7+ days for an answer` and name the rest.
- The alert and `checkStaleQuestions` agree on the set because both read `STALE_QUESTION_DAYS` and `questionFilingDate`: a question exactly 7 days old is stale on both, and a 6-day-old or undated one is stale on neither.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/team-alerts.test.ts: `the stale-questions alert names the oldest and folds the rest` — call `teamAlerts(base, ["Q?"], [], now, …, staleQuestions)` (filling the intervening defaulted arguments) with two `StaleQuestion` rows; assert one amber `stale-questions` alert whose title counts both, whose detail starts `#<first.position> "<first.title>" has waited <first.days>d`, carries `tumwater questions answer <first.position>`, folds the second, and whose action is `[{ label: "Answer", act: "questions" }]`; an empty list (the existing short-argument calls) yields no `stale-questions` alert.
- test/status-payload.test.ts: `staleOpenQuestions picks the 7+ day set and the payload carries it` — seed a QUESTIONS.md `## Open` with a fresh dated question, an undated one, and one stamped 8 days before `now`; assert `staleOpenQuestions(dir, now)` returns only the old one with its `position` and `days`, and that the status payload for that repo includes a `stale-questions` alert while a repo whose only question is fresh omits it.

### Forward, never back, part 1a/6: the harness commits a reviewer's worktree edit as one fix commit and lands it on main, so a review run can repair what it found (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split from the held part 1/6; part 1/6 below turns on the fix-forward prompt this part makes landable; a change to how a commit reaches main, so the switch that depends on it is a separate part and merges only once this one is the running build; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/merge/merge-post-review.ts src/verdict/reply-contract.ts src/paths.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts test/reply-contract.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 3**

**Goal.** Give the harness a way to land a reviewer's edit as a commit on main. Today `reviewMergedCommit` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) runs the reviewer in a `--detach --force` checkout of the reviewed commit C and throws the worktree away: whatever the reviewer wrote is lost, which is why a post-merge finding can only be answered by a revert. This part makes a review run whose reply carries a `FIX:` line and whose worktree has edits produce one `tumwater(reviewer): Fix <short sha> — <first finding>` commit on C and land it through the ordinary change path (the gate on the fix tree, then the fast-forward under the merge lock), so the work survives. It changes no prompt and asks for no edits: until part 1/6 lands, a normal review run leaves the worktree clean and emits no `FIX:` line, so the path is inert.

**Approach.**
- src/review/post-merge-review.ts `reviewMergedCommit`: hold the worktree on a branch-backed checkout of C — create/reset `refs/tumwater/review-fix/<short sha>` with `setRef` (src/git/git.ts) at C and check that ref out instead of `--detach --force` — and parse the reply's `FIX:` line (below). When the verdict parses and the worktree has edited paths (`git status --porcelain`), commit them with the harness's own `git` call (never pi) as one commit whose subject is `tumwater(reviewer): Fix <short sha> — <first reason>` and whose body carries the numbered reasons; return a new `{ kind: "fixed"; fix: string; reasons: string[] }` outcome naming the fix's full sha, and log the reviewed commit's verdict so `review_rejected`/`review_verdict` still carry one record for C. A clean worktree, or a reply with no `FIX:` line, keeps today's `{ kind: "reject" }` / `{ kind: "approve" }` outcomes and deletes the ref.
- src/verdict/reply-contract.ts: `fixLine` beside `flowLine`/`ciResultLine` — `FIX: <comma-separated paths>` split and validated with `labeledLine`, so a bare `FIX:` or a reply truncated mid-verdict records nothing.
- src/merge/merge-post-review.ts `startPostReview`: on `outcome.kind === "fixed"`, merge the fix ref through the ordinary change path (`mergeApprovedChange`/`mergeToMain`, its gate over the fix tree and its `mergeLockDir` lock), then `settlePostReview(root, entry.commit, { ...entry, fixed: outcome.fix })` so the entry names both shas. A landing that fails (conflict, red gate, a refused fast-forward) leaves main at C, warns, and keeps the entry for the next poll, exactly as a failed run is kept today; a run with no edit and no finding still settles `approved`, and an unrepairable finding still settles `rejected`.
- src/paths.ts: add the durable ref name (`reviewFixRef(sha)`) beside the other `refs/tumwater/` paths, so the fix's ref has one home and the existing pin housekeeping sees it; delete the ref once the merge settles.
- No prompt change here — part 1/6 adds the clause that makes a reviewer emit the `FIX:` line. This part only makes an edit durable and merged.
