**Acceptance criteria.**
- A post-merge review run that carries a `FIX:` line and leaves an edited path in its worktree produces exactly one commit whose subject begins `tumwater(reviewer): Fix <short sha>` and whose parent is the reviewed commit; main fast-forwards to it and the entry settles `fixed` naming both shas.
- A run with no edit and no finding settles `approved`; a run whose finding is unrepairable (no edits, or no `FIX:` line) settles `rejected` as today; a bare or truncated `FIX:` line records nothing.
- A fix whose landing fails leaves main at the reviewed commit, keeps the entry in post-review.json with its failure recorded, and the next poll retries it.
- The reviewer's worktree is reset to the reviewed commit at the start of every review, so a leftover ref or edit from an earlier review cannot change what is reviewed.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/post-merge-review.test.ts: `the harness commits and lands a reviewer's edit as one fix` — seed a merged afterMerge change, have the fake review run write a file in the worktree and reply with a `FIX:` line and `VERDICT: reject`, and assert one `tumwater(reviewer): Fix <sha>` commit whose parent is the reviewed commit is on main and the entry settles `fixed` with both shas; `a run with no edit settles approved`, `a finding with no FIX line records reasons`, and `a failed landing keeps the entry and leaves main unmoved` cover the other arms. Keep the torn-entry, failed-write and git-could-not-start cases.
- test/reply-contract.test.ts: `fixLine` mirrors the FLOW cases — `FIX: a.ts, b.ts` parses to the two paths, a mid-sentence mention does not, and `FIX:` alone (or a reply truncated mid-verdict) records nothing.

**Goal.** `checkWorkInstances` (src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts, the doctor's `parallel instances` row) already names the two claim states an operator must act on: a claim whose key no longer appears in its role's backlog section (the instance is working on an entry that moved), and a claim idle longer than `CLAIM_IDLE_MAX_MS` (the scheduler releases these, so seeing one means the reader's view and the scheduler's disagree). But it runs only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`; on the always-on surfaces a stopped instance holding a vanished plan is invisible. This is the same missing-twin gap the `ci parity`, `stalled plans`, `plan dependencies` and `validation gaps` alerts close: give the doctor's claim rule an always-on amber alert, over one shared classifier so the row and the alert cannot drift.

**Approach.**
- New `src/scheduling/claim-entries.ts`: export `interface ClaimState { id: string; file: "PLANS.md" | "BUGS.md"; title: string; kind: "gone" | "idle"; hours: number }` and `staleClaimEntries(root: string, ids: readonly string[], now = Date.now()): ClaimState[]`. For each `id` in the given order, read `loadRunnerState(root, id).claim` (skip an id with no claim); a claim whose `key` is absent from `listedKeys(root, id)` is `gone` (hours 0, and `gone` wins over idle for the same claim); otherwise, when `now - claim.at > CLAIM_IDLE_MAX_MS`, it is `idle` with `hours = Math.round((now - claim.at) / 3_600_000)`; a fresh listed claim is omitted. - `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`: import the `ClaimState` type, add `staleClaims: readonly ClaimState[] = []` as the trailing parameter of `teamAlerts` and a `staleClaims` field on `StatusAlertsInput`, and in `buildStatusAlerts` push one amber alert (`key: "stale-claims"`) when the list is non-empty: title `${n} work-instance claim(s) is/are stale`, a detail that joins the claims like the doctor (`claimed plan "Alpha" (feature-2) has been idle 25h`, `claimed bug "Gone" (bugfix-2) names an entry no longer listed`), and actions the `Open <role>` buttons for the first three claim ids (the `openRoleActions` shape, labelled through `roleLabel`). Nothing when empty.
- Call sites add the trailing argument `staleClaimEntries(root, roles.map((r) => r.role), now)` beside the other readers they already compute: src/ui/status-payload.ts (`roles`, `now`), src/ui/status-render.ts (`roles`, `Date.now()`), src/ui/tui/tui.tsx (`status.roles`, `Date.now()`).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the "Parallel work instances" bullet: add one sentence — while a claim names an entry no longer listed, or has sat idle past `CLAIM_IDLE_MAX_MS`, `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI carry the same amber alert as `tumwater doctor`'s `parallel instances` row; it clears when the scheduler's next poll releases the claim.

### Every commit is verified on main, part 3b/3: a torn merge-queue head is dropped loudly and its change re-queued, so no landing waits forever on one unreadable file (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held part 3/3; independent of parts 3a/3 and 3c/3–3f/3; touches src/merge/merge-queue.ts src/merge/merge-verify.ts docs/invariants.md test/merge-queue.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** A torn or foreign queue head makes `headMerge` read null forever, and `dropTornHead` (src/merge/merge-verify.ts) drops it with a warning that names only the file. Nothing re-queues the change the file was meant to carry, so it waits for next-run leftover recovery while every healthy entry behind it is stranded for that poll. Drop the bad head loudly enough to name its role and put its change back on the queue, so the "nothing blocks a landing" rule holds even for a file the queue cannot read.

**Approach.**
- `staleHeadFile` (src/merge/merge-queue.ts) keeps returning the unreadable head; `dropTornHead` (src/merge/merge-verify.ts) reads the file's raw bytes before dropping it. `MergeEntry` serializes `role` first, so a torn write keeps a `"role":"<id>"` substring: recover it with a tolerant match (`/"role"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/`), not a JSON parse.
- When a role is recovered, read that role's merge pin with `mergeRefName(role)` (src/paths.ts, `refs/tumwater/merge/<role>`); when it resolves, enqueue a fresh `MergeEntry` for that sha with `enqueueMerge` (the shape leftover recovery builds) before dropping the torn file, so the same poll's `queuedMergeFiles` sees it. A torn head with no recoverable role or no pin drops with the existing warning plus the file's role when known.
- `readMergeQueue`/`dropMerge` and the rest of `drainVerify` are unchanged.

**Files touched.** src/merge/merge-queue.ts src/merge/merge-verify.ts docs/invariants.md test/merge-queue.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A torn head is dropped and its recovered change is re-queued in the same poll (a subsequent `headMerge` reads the re-queued entry, not null); the warning names the torn file and, when recovered, its role.
- A foreign or unrecoverable head is dropped with the file named and the queue advances; no healthy entry behind a torn head waits.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/merge-queue.test.ts: `a torn queue head is dropped and its change re-queued` — write a partially-serialized head carrying `role`/`sha`, run the drain's torn-head step, and assert the file is gone, a fresh entry for the same sha is queued, and one warning names the file; a head with no readable role drops with the warning and no re-queue.

### The watch's five diff-rule failures on main raise a standing amber alert on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI, so a diff the gate let through cannot sit on main unremarked (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the in-flight `ci parity` badge plan edits src/ui/status-payload.ts (badge fields) and src/ui/status-render.ts (the badge span), the `Forward, never back` parts edit src/review, src/merge, src/verdict and docs/invariants.md, the `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/config, src/orchestrator and src/runner (none adds a team alert or edits src/ui/team-alerts.ts), and the Ready-only plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts and its neighbours, not src/ui/tui/tui.tsx; it shares src/ui/status-payload.ts and src/ui/status-render.ts with the badge plan (additive: a badge field and span there, a `teamAlerts` reader and trailing argument here) and shares no file with any other waiting plan; touches src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/status-payload.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The main watch runs the review gate's five deterministic diff rules on every tip it covers (src/baseline/main-watch.ts `watchRules`), and a violation is logged as `warning` with the message `main's tip <short sha> fails the diff rules: <reason>` — the same reason text the gate rejects with. Nothing reads that warning: `tumwater doctor`'s `claimed bugs` row re-derives one rule (a false-fix claim) only on demand, the `mainred` alert is a build red, and the event log is the only surface. So a conflict marker, a protected edit, a leaked secret, a phantom fix claim or a broken backlog structure that reached main through a gate blind spot (the gate judges one change; the watch judges each first-parent commit's own diff) is invisible to an operator watching the dashboard. Add one read-only amber alert that surfaces the warning the watch already writes.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: beside `DROPPED_POST_REVIEW_WINDOW_MS` add `export const MAIN_RULE_FAILURE_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;` (the same trailing-day convention every event-reading alert uses) and `const MAIN_RULE_FAILURE_MARKER = "fails the diff rules";` (the exact substring `main-watch.ts`'s `watchRules` writes, so the alert cannot drift from the watch). Add `export interface MainRuleFailure { count: number; latestTs: number; latestMessage: string }` and `export function mainRuleFailures(root: string, now = Date.now()): MainRuleFailure | null`, shaped exactly like `droppedPostReviewsAlert`: `eventsSince(root, MAIN_RULE_FAILURE_WINDOW_MS, now, (e) => e.type === "warning" && typeof e.message === "string" && e.message.includes(MAIN_RULE_FAILURE_MARKER))`, then `{ count: hits.length, latestTs: latest.ts, latestMessage: String(latest.message) }` for the last hit, else `null`. `eventsSince` degrades an unreadable log, so no try/catch (the `droppedPostReviewsAlert` precedent). No git read and no rule re-run: the watch already paid for the check.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: append `mainRuleFailures(root, now)` as the **last** argument of the `teamAlerts(...)` call (`statusPayload`), after `droppedPostReviewsAlert(root, now)`.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `MainRuleFailure` to the `import type { … } from "./status-payload.js"` line beside `DroppedPostReviews`; add `mainRuleFailure: MainRuleFailure | null;` to `MergeAlertsInput`; append one amber block at the end of `buildMergeAlerts` (after the `dropped-post-reviews` block), and destructure `mainRuleFailure` from `input`: `key: "main-diff-rules"`, tone `amber`, title `` `${plural(mainRuleFailure.count, "diff-rule failure on main", "diff-rule failures on main")} in the last day` ``, detail `` `most recently ${humanAgo(mainRuleFailure.latestTs, now)}: ${squash(mainRuleFailure.latestMessage, 160)} — the gate approved a diff the watch's five rules reject, so main carries what the gate would refuse; repair the tip or revert it with \`tumwater revert <sha>\`` ``, `actions: seeFailures()`. Update the `buildMergeAlerts` doc comment and the `teamAlerts` doc comment's alert list to name a diff-rule failure on main.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: append `mainRuleFailure: MainRuleFailure | null = null,` as the **last** parameter of `teamAlerts` (after `droppedPostReviews`) and pass it through `buildMergeAlerts({ …, mainRuleFailure, now })`. The default keeps every existing positional caller and test unchanged; append, never insert, because the trailing order is load-bearing.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: add `mainRuleFailures` to each file's import from `./status-payload.js` and pass `mainRuleFailures(root, Date.now())` as the **last** `teamAlerts(...)` argument (after `droppedPostReviewsAlert(root)`), so `tumwater status` and the TUI attention lines carry the alert.
- docs/how-it-works.md: after the paragraph sentence that ends "…deterministically within one poll, with no confirming re-run.", add that a warning in the trailing day raises a standing amber alert naming the tip and the rule on `tumwater status`, the dashboard and the TUI, so a diff the gate let through cannot sit on main unremarked.
- No change to `main-watch.ts` (the warning is the source), to `diffRuleReasons`, to the doctor's `claimed bugs` row, or to any `main_red`/revert path.

### A `ci parity` doctor row says whether the full suite has covered main's tip, so `tumwater doctor`, the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab answer "is main verified by CI?" (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every waiting series — the `Forward, never back` parts edit src/review, src/merge, src/verdict and docs/invariants.md, the `Every commit is verified on main` parts edit src/baseline, src/merge, src/config, src/orchestrator, src/runner and docs/how-it-works.md, the post-merge-rejection parts edit src/merge, src/review and src/cli, the drop-broken-pins plan edits src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts, src/cli, src/gui and src/ui/gui, and the Ready-only plan edits src/ui/tui, src/ui/gui/gui-client-backlog.ts and docs/how-it-works.md. This plan edits src/run/ci-parity.ts and three src/doctor files none of them touch; it shares test/doctor-checks.test.ts and test/doctor.test.ts with the drop-broken-pins plan (that plan adds the drop-pins cases, this one the ci-parity cases) and docs/how-it-works.md with the `Every commit is verified` and Ready-only plans (neighbouring paragraphs), so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/run/ci-parity.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** The `ci` role runs the workflow's own full suite and e2e at main's tip and records what it covered in the CI-parity ledger (`readCiParity`, src/run/ci-parity.ts), but the only reader is the role's own next prompt (`parityBlockFor`): an operator has no surface answering "has the full suite covered main's current tip?". `tumwater doctor`'s `check` row names the command and its median, and `main's check` names red windows, but neither reads the ledger. Add a read-only `ci parity` doctor row — the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab render doctor rows, so one check reaches all three surfaces — that reports the ledger's verdict and whether it covers the current tip.

**Approach.**
- src/run/ci-parity.ts: extract the "current" decision out of `renderParityBlock` into `export function parityIsCurrent(entry: CiParityEntry, tip: string, lockHash: string): boolean` (result `passed`, `tip` non-empty and a prefix of `entry.tip`, `entry.lockHash === lockHash`) and have `renderParityBlock` call it, so the prompt block and the doctor row cannot disagree on what "current" means. Export the private `currentParityState` as `export function currentCiParityState(root, config): { tip: string; lockHash: string }` (it already resolves the tip and lock with no spawn). Export the `CiParityEntry` interface so the doctor can name the record's shape.
- src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts: add `export function checkCiParity(root: string, config?: { baseBranch?: string } | null, now: number = Date.now()): CheckOutcome`. Read `readCiParity(root)` and `currentCiParityState(root, config ?? undefined)`:
  - no record → `okOutcome("no CI parity recorded yet — the ci role has not completed a workflow run")`.
  - `entry.result === "failed"` → `warnOutcome` naming the covered tip and lock and the verdict (the ci role's contract is to fix or file what it finds, so a lingering failed record is actionable until the next green run); use `shortSha` from src/text/format.ts and an age phrase from `now - entry.lastRunAt`.
  - `parityIsCurrent(entry, tip, lockHash)` → `okOutcome("current — CI covered main at <tip> @ <lock>, passed <age> ago")`.
  - otherwise → `okOutcome("stale — the last run covered <tip> @ <lock> (<result>, <age> ago); main is now <tip> @ <lock>, so the ci role has not yet covered this tip")`. Stale is `ok`, never `warn`/`fail`: main moves on every merge and the ci role runs on its own clock, so a post-merge gap is normal and must not turn the Health card or the exit code red.
- src/doctor/doctor.ts: import `checkCiParity` and add `{ name: "ci parity", run: () => checkCiParity(root, config, Date.now()) }` immediately after the `check` row (before `root install`), so the report order groups it with main's verification.
- src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts: insert `"ci parity"` at the same position in `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` (the completion script lists doctor names from it, so no separate completion edit).
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater doctor` row's check enumeration gains the `ci parity` clause. docs/how-it-works.md: the paragraph that mentions the ci role/parity names the doctor row as its operator surface.

### `tumwater doctor --drop-broken-pins` drops the `refs/tumwater/` pins whose commit is gone, and the dashboard Health card does too — the reap for the one doctor row whose only remedy is a manual `git update-ref -d` (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior — the `ci` parts edit src/roles and src/run, the "Every commit is verified on main" parts edit src/baseline and src/merge, the `teamAlerts` parts edit src/ui/team-alerts.ts, the Pending Ctrl+O plan edits the TUI Pending pane, and the notable-cull plan edits the CLI `logs` feed and the TUI Activity pane; it shares src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts and src/cli.ts with the notable-cull plan (that plan adds `NOTABLE_FLAG` for `logs`, this one `DROP_BROKEN_PINS_FLAG` for `doctor` — additive sibling lines, so whichever lands second rebases there) and docs/cli.md's doctor row with the notable-cull and Pending plans (this one edits the `doctor` row only, they edit the `logs` and TUI-keys rows); touches src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts docs/cli.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-settings.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `checkTumwaterPins` (src/doctor/doctor-contention-checks.ts) fails the `tumwater pins` doctor row when a `refs/tumwater/` pin names a commit that is gone, because such a pin stops `git gc` and aborts a detached checkout, and its row names only a manual `git update-ref -d <ref>` as the fix. Every other mutating doctor action has an operator-facing reap: `--kill-orphans` (the orphans row), `--commit-backlog` (the dirty-checkout merges), `--resync-install` (the `root install` row), each reaching the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab (Ctrl+K, Ctrl+A and Ctrl+U). Give the `tumwater pins` row the same reach: one core drops each broken pin, and `tumwater doctor --drop-broken-pins` and the dashboard Health card call it, so a lone broken pin cannot hold the team's git housekeeping hostage with no in-product way to clear it.

**Approach.**

### A `ci` role runs the CI workflow's own jobs at main's tip and fixes what fails, part 3/3: its parity block and `CI:` result line make its no-op decision cheap (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held single `ci` plan; requires part 1/3 landed — the block is the role's own record and the `CI:` line is what it reads back — and lands before its repeated full-suite runs get expensive; touches src/config/config.ts src/run/ci-parity.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts src/verdict/reply-contract.ts src/runner/runner-outcome.ts src/run/run-verdict.ts docs/config.md test/reply-contract.test.ts test/qa-coverage.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** Without a record of what it covered, the role must run the whole CI job — minutes of suite plus e2e — every tick to answer a question its own history already holds. The parity block and the `CI:` result line make that decision cheap: the role reads the tip and the `package-lock.json` hash its last green run covered, and declares nothing-to-do when main has not moved since and the lock file is unchanged.

**Approach.**
- src/config/config.ts: seed `minRunIntervalSeconds` for `ci` at the observer trio's `7200` (docs/config.md's row), so parity costs at most one full suite plus e2e every two hours; the per-role override works as for every other role.
- src/run/ci-parity.ts (new) + src/prompt/prompt.ts (its `ciParity` field, :315): the same-shaped `ciParity` prompt field — the tip the last recorded green parity run covered, its `package-lock.json` hash, and how it went — rendered by a module of its own, and omitted entirely when the record is missing or unreadable, exactly as the qa coverage block is.
- src/verdict/reply-contract.ts: `extractCiResult` beside `extractFlow` (:194) — `CI: <sha> — passed|failed`, split and validated with the same `labeledLine`/verdict-required rules (a bare `CI: <sha>`, a non-hex id, or a reply truncated mid-verdict is not a result and is not recorded). The run outcome carries it (src/runner/runner-outcome.ts, src/run/run-verdict.ts) and the parity block reads it back, so a fresh session that remembers nothing still knows what the last run covered.
- docs: docs/config.md's `minRunIntervalSeconds` row names `ci` with `7200` (the `Observer` line in docs/glossary.md and the observer paragraph in docs/how-it-works.md belong to part 1/3).
- No change to `.github/workflows/*`, to `check.gateCommand`, to `npm run test:gate`'s definition, to the main watch's check or to the post-merge review. The merge gate stays fast and affected-only — that is the point of a role whose cadence is its own. An implementation that finds itself slowing the gate, or editing a workflow file, has gone off-plan.

**Files touched.** src/config/config.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts src/run/ci-parity.ts src/verdict/reply-contract.ts src/runner/runner-outcome.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts src/run/run-verdict.ts src/run/run-stage.ts src/paths.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts docs/config.md docs/invariants.md test/config.test.ts test/prompt-roles.test.ts test/reply-contract.test.ts test/ci-parity.test.ts test/run-verdict.test.ts test/run-resume.test.ts test/revision.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Its prompt carries a CI parity block naming the tip and lock hash of the last green run; with main unmoved since that run and the lock hash unchanged the role declares nothing-to-do without running the suite (one model run, no suite run).
- A `CI:` line is required on every run and a bare `CI: <sha>` records nothing, so the parity block cannot advance on a truncated reply (the `FLOW:` line's own rule).
- The merge gate is untouched: `npm run test:gate` still runs only the affected tests, and no test that pins its command changes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.**
- test/reply-contract.test.ts: `extractCiResult` mirrors the FLOW cases — `CI: abc1234 — passed` and `CI: abc1234 — failed` parse, a mid-sentence mention does not, and `CI: abc1234` alone (or a reply truncated mid-verdict, or a non-hex id) records nothing.
- test/ci-parity.test.ts (new): the parity block renders "current" for the recorded green tip with a matching lock hash, "stale" naming both shas and hashes when main moved or the lock hash changed (or the last run failed), and is omitted entirely for a missing or malformed record rather than rendering an empty verdict.

**Note (2026-10-24 by the feature role).** Implemented as planned; `npm run test:gate` passes. The plan's file list did not name every path the wired change touched, so they were added to it in the same change: src/run/runner-run.ts (extracts the `CI:` line for the `ci` role), src/run/run-stage.ts (a comment pins that the staged/merge path never records parity — a changed run has not verified main, so a written entry would leave a false `current` if the fix never landed; the sole recorder is resolveRunVerdict's no_change path), src/paths.ts (the ledger path builder, `ciParityPath`), src/roles/role-catalog.ts (the `ci` find text now names the parity block and the required `CI:` line — without it the role would never emit the line the whole mechanism reads back), docs/invariants.md (INV-BW2, the ci-parity twin of INV-BW1), and the tests whose observer-context literals gained the field (test/run-verdict.test.ts adds the parity-recording, cut-off, and failed-write cases; test/run-resume.test.ts/test/revision.test.ts compile-time `ci: null`). The qa-coverage-adjacent parity test is a new test/ci-parity.test.ts, and test/config.test.ts pins the new `ci` 7200 default to the slow-clock set.

### Every commit is verified on main, part 2/3: the newest head is the culprit — the bisect is deleted (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held single plan; requires part 1/3 landed, so a rule failure added there is attributed to the tip the same way a build red is; part 3/3 below then takes the pre-merge blocks off; touches src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/baseline/main-culprit.ts (deleted) docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/main-watch.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** A red is attributed without a search. The watch checks each new tip, so the tip is the culprit for whatever it finds; the first-parent walk, its fresh last-green re-check and its doc-only skip have nothing left to reconstruct. This part deletes that search. The confirming re-run that turns a one-off flake into a quarantine and the sleep-span skip stay; only the attribution search goes.

**Approach.**
- Delete src/baseline/main-culprit.ts: `findRedCulprit`, `CULPRIT_SEARCH_MAX`, `OWNER_EVENT_TAIL`, `RedCulprit`, and its imports. Remove the `findRedCulprit` import and call from src/baseline/main-watch.ts's `watchOnce`; keep the merged-event owner helper that part 1/3 added.
- Name the tip: on a red `baseline`, the watch logs one `main_culprit` event for `baseline.sha` carrying its `failingTests` and, when the newest `merged` event names it, its `runner`, then calls `onCulprit?.({ commit: baseline.sha, failingTests: baseline.failingTests ?? [], tip: baseline.sha, ...(runner ? { runner } : {}) })`. The `environment`/`unattributed` warning branches and their reasons go, because there is no search left to fail.
- Keep, unchanged: the confirming re-run (`reverifyRed`) and the `quarantineTests` call it feeds, the sleep-span skip, and the once-per-red-head guard (`lastWatched` already holds the head).
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md's culprit paragraph says the newest head is the culprit; docs/invariants.md's attribution guarantee is re-pointed (its pre-merge halves remain part 3/3's).

**Goal.** The dashboard's Activity card has opened on a Notable/All choice since it was built: `feedFilter` defaults to `"notable"` and culls `eventKind(it) === "routine"` rows (src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts). The two other surfaces of the same event feed cannot: `tumwater logs` prints every routine bookkeeping event (`run_start`, `wake`, `merge_queued`, a passing `build_check`) and the TUI Activity pane's only narrowing is Ctrl+O's exact-type cycle, so an operator watching the always-on feed in a terminal reads a wall of routine rows the browser hides by default. Give both the dashboard's cull, as one filter rule in one home: only routine events are hidden, the choice defaults to all on both so a `tumwater logs` script's output is unchanged, and it composes with the role scope, the text search, the type filter and the window each surface already has.

**Approach.**
- One rule: add `export function isNotableEvent(type: string, result: string | undefined): boolean { return eventKind(type, result) !== "routine"; }` to src/ui/tone.ts, beside `eventKind`. It is the harness-side spelling of the dashboard copy's `eventKind(it) !== "routine"` cull; the browser copy stays its own (it cannot import harness modules), pinned as it already is.
- `tumwater logs --notable`: in src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts add `NOTABLE_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--notable"] }` beside `COUNT_FLAG`; in src/cli.ts's `case "logs"` add it to `rejectUnknownArgs`'s allowlist. In src/cli/log-commands.ts read `const notable = rest.includes("--notable")` beside `count`/`json`; reject it with `--transcript` through `rejectTranscriptViewRival(rest, "--notable", notable)`; and add `(!notable || isNotableEvent(e.type, eventResult(e)))` to `feedFilter` so the `--since` window, the `-n` view, the `-f` follow and `--count` all cull through the one predicate. `eventResult` joins the existing event-format import, and `isNotableEvent` imports from `../ui/tone.js`.
- The `-n` view's guard must learn the new filter: today `const shown = grepLower !== null || type !== null || roleFilter !== null ? tail.events.filter(feedFilter) : tail.events;` bypasses `feedFilter` when `--notable` is the only filter — add `|| notable` to that condition. (`--since` and the follow callback already filter through `feedFilter` unconditionally.)
- Empty-match prose: when `--notable` is the only active filter and nothing matches, name it — `no notable events` in the `-n` view, `no notable events ${windowPhrase}` in the `--since` view, and the same line under `--count` (which already reuses the window's plain-view prose). Extend the three existing `shown.length === 0` / `filtered.length === 0` branches: add `notable` to their firing condition and a first branch `if (notable && grepPattern === null && type === null && roles === null)` that says the notable line. A notable feed composed with `--grep`/`--type`/`--role` keeps that filter's existing wording.
- TUI, one read: give `activityEvents` (src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts) a fifth `notable = false` parameter and add `(!notable || isNotableEvent(e.type, eventResult(e)))` to its filter — the same rule, so the CLI and the TUI cannot disagree. In `paneBody`'s Activity branch pass `pane.notable` for `preType` and the events read, so the tally line counts only notable rows while culled (the dashboard's rule that a Notable cull tallies only the notable rows), and add `!pane.notable` to the `(no events yet)` guard on `emptyNote`.
- TUI, one cycle: in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-activity.ts add `let activityNotable = false;` beside `activityType`. Its Ctrl+O arm builds `present` from the unchanged pre-type read and cycles a slot array `[{notable:false,type:null}, {notable:true,type:null}, ...present.map((t)=>({notable:false,type:t}))]`, finding the current slot by `notable` and `type` together, so the cycle is all → notable → each present type → all. The paging total and `applySearch` pass the new flag; `state()` returns `activityNotable`.

- Docs: src/cli/help.ts's `tumwater logs` usage line gains `[--notable]` beside `[--count]`; docs/cli.md's `tumwater logs` row describes `--notable` (`only non-routine events — the dashboard feed's Notable choice; composes with --since, --grep, --type, --role, -n, -f and --json`) and its TUI-keys Ctrl+O row adds Activity's notable stop; docs/how-it-works.md's Activity-feed sentence names the cull.

The operator reading the `post-merge-churn` / `dropped-post-reviews` alerts on the surface that raised them cannot tell a review queued four minutes ago from one queued four days ago. Import `humanAgo` from `../text/datetime.js` (the helper `renderMergeQueue` uses). Update the module doc comment to name the age and delete the "there is no age line" sentence. Keep the scope header and every status/`--status`/`--role` wording unchanged.

### Every commit is verified on main, part 1/3: the watch's per-tip check runs the deterministic diff rules, naming the rule and the head (decided by the user 2026-10-24; split from the held single plan; part 2/3 below then makes the newest head the culprit and deletes the bisect, and part 3/3 takes the pre-merge blocks off; this part leaves every pre-merge check in place and keeps the bisect; design half: plans/fast-merge.md "What stays"; touches src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/baseline/main-culprit.ts src/events/event-read.ts src/review/diff-rules.ts src/review/review.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/main-watch.test.ts test/review-precheck.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** A commit that lands is judged by the same deterministic rules the merge gate runs before it. Today the watch checks only the declared build command on a new tip, while the conflict-marker, secret-leak, protected-edit, false-fix and backlog-structure rules live only inside the gate (src/review/review.ts) — so a commit that leaves a conflict marker or breaks a backlog section is invisible until a reviewer or a user finds it. This part runs those rules on the tip within one poll and names the rule and the head. It removes nothing: the merge slot's in-lock gate run, the pre-merge model verdict and the red-main authoring block all still stand (part 3/3), and the bisect that names a build red's culprit stays (part 2/3).

**Approach.**
- One home for the rules: add `export async function diffRuleReasons(wt, baseRev, files, role, exempt): Promise<string[]>` to a NEW module src/review/diff-rules.ts — the gate's five deterministic calls in the gate's own order and scope: `conflictMarkerReason(wt, files)`, then `protectedEditReason(wt, baseRev, files, role)`, then `secretLeakReason(wt, baseRev, files)`, and, after the exempt branch, `falseFixReason(wt, baseRev, files)` only when `exempt` and `backlogStructureReason(wt, baseRev, files)` for every diff. The module lives apart from review-precheck.ts so the main watch can import it without a runtime import cycle (review-precheck.ts imports onlyKnownMainFailures from main-watch.ts); src/review/review.ts computes `const baseRev = await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch)` once, calls `diffRuleReasons(wt, baseRev, files, role, isExemptDiff(files, config.review.exemptPaths))`, rejects on `reasons[0]`, and keeps its exempt/code branch and `reviewResume` reset exactly as today. src/run/stage-check.ts is unchanged — it keeps its own calls.
- A base rev, not a branch: the four async rules resolve their base with `changeBaseRev(wt, baseRev)`, which is `git merge-base HEAD <baseRev>`; a commit sha works there exactly as a branch name does, so the watch passes a commit without changing the rule functions.
- The watch runs them per commit, on every tip it covers: in `watchOnce` (src/baseline/main-watch.ts), the diff rules run on a build green, a build red, a skipped/sleep-spanned head, and a repo with no declared build check. Each first-parent commit in the watched range (`git rev-list --first-parent base..tip`, or `[tip]` when base is undefined) is judged by its OWN diff (`treeDiffFiles(wt, commit^, commit)`) and its OWN merged-event role, so a legitimate director/steward PRINCIPLES.md edit in an intermediate commit is not blamed on whichever role merged the tip. The merged-event owner lookup is `mergingRoleOf` in src/events/event-read.ts, shared by main-watch.ts and main-culprit.ts — moved out of main-culprit.ts's inline copy and out of main-watch.ts so neither consumer imports the other (no runtime import cycle). A finding is reported as a `warning` naming `shortSha(tip)` and the reason; it is deterministic, so it takes no confirming re-run and never quarantines. The brief-block rule is role-independent and runs even when no merged event names a commit's role; only the PRINCIPLES.md half of the protected-edit rule needs an attribution.
- The rule check is deliberately *not* added to `checkMainBaseline`: that function is consulted by the merge path, the redeploy gate and main-red attribution, and a rule failure there would read main red for every consumer. The watch alone owns the per-tip rule judgement this part adds.
- The full suite and the e2e suite stay out of the watch's check: a full `npm test` plus `npm run test:e2e` on every landing would melt the host. They stay the `ci` role's job at its own cadence (the `ci` plan above), and this part does not change that plan.
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md's merge paragraph describes landing-then-verifying and names the deterministic rules the watch runs on the tip; docs/invariants.md re-points INV-G1 and the merge-check guarantees at the main watch (their pre-merge halves are part 3/3's to delete).

**Files touched.** src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/baseline/main-culprit.ts src/events/event-read.ts src/review/diff-rules.ts (new) src/review/review.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md test/main-watch.test.ts test/review-precheck.test.ts

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The deterministic rules run against main's tip: a commit that leaves a conflict marker, leaks a secret, edits a protected path or the brief block, or breaks the backlog structure is reported by the watch naming the rule and the head within one poll; a false-fix claim is reported when the diff is md-only, exactly as the gate scopes it.
- `diffRuleReasons` is the gate's one call site of those five rules: the gate still rejects a secret leak and a protected edit, still runs the false-fix and backlog checks on an exempt md-only diff, and the watch's report quotes the same reason text the gate would.
- The build check's red handling is unchanged: a red the confirming re-run turns green is still quarantined, and the bisect still names the culprit for a build red.
- Every pre-merge check is still in place when this part lands: the merge slot's gate run, the pre-merge model verdict and the red-main authoring block are part 3/3's to remove, and this part removes none of them.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `ci` role runs the CI workflow's own jobs at main's tip and fixes what fails, part 2/3: the red-main healer hand-off moves from `bugfix` to `ci` (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role, split from part 1/2 of the held `ci` plan; requires part 1/3 landed, since the hand-off names the role that part adds; touches src/baseline/main-red.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/main-red.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** Main's two broken signals — the watch naming a red culprit and a CI step failing — reach different roles today: `bugfix` owns the red-main repair (`queueCulpritHeal`'s prompt, `runner-run.ts`'s `<main-red>` note branch, and its exemption from the red-main authoring block), while a failing CI step has no owner until a human or a post-merge reviewer finds it. With part 1/3's `ci` role in place, this part routes the hand-off to it, so both signals land in one queue of main repairs and no second role races it for the same tree; `bugfix` returns to its own charter (BUGS.md's backlog) with no heal prompt and no red-main note.

**Approach.**
- src/baseline/main-red.ts: the watch-culprit branch (`enqueueRolePrompt(root, BUGFIX_ROLE, mainRedHealPrompt(red.sha))`, :106) and `queueCulpritHeal` (:141) name the ci role (`"ci"`) instead of `BUGFIX_ROLE`, and the `baseRoleOf(foundBy) !== BUGFIX_ROLE` guard (:104) becomes `!== "ci"`, so a red main the ci role itself found does not re-queue a heal prompt to itself. The prompt text is unchanged (`mainRedHealPrompt` already names the culprit, the failing tests and the output tail; only its recipient changes), and the `could not queue the heal prompt for bugfix` warning (:108) names the healer role.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: the `ctx.baseRole === "bugfix"` branch (:580) keys on the ci base role instead, so the role that receives the hand-off is the one whose prompt carries the `<main-red>` failure note; a `bugfix` run falls through to the ordinary `mainRedGate` path. Rename the note helper `bugfixMainRedNote` (src/baseline/main-red.ts:157, its one production caller at runner-run.ts:581, and its cases in test/main-red.test.ts) to `mainRedHealNote`, so the name stops naming a role it no longer serves.
- docs/how-it-works.md: every red-main hand-off sentence names `ci` — the merge-pipeline Check bullet's "the failure goes to bugfix", the merge bullet's "the bugfix note", the backlog paragraph's "queues a bugfix healer", and the watch's "queues bugfix's heal prompt naming the commit and the failing tests". The "one owner for a red main" paragraph lives in plans/fast-merge.md, not docs/how-it-works.md, and its D1 bullet already carries the 2026-10-24 supersede note naming the `ci` role, so both are read and left as-is.
- No change to the watch's check, `mainRedHealPrompt`'s wording, or `BASELINE_BLOCKED_ROLES`: `ci` is already exempt because part 1/3 puts it in `OBSERVER_ROLES`, not through a bugfix-specific branch. The "Every commit is verified on main" plan below removes the authoring block entirely.

### `tumwater plan|bug --release` reports which hold it lifted, and every surface names all three holds it can lift (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the `ci` series edits src/roles, docs/glossary.md and docs/how-it-works.md, the "Every commit is verified on main" series edits src/baseline, src/merge, src/config and docs/config.md, and the budget series edits src/gates, src/budget and docs/invariants.md; none of them edits src/backlog/backlog-release.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts or docs/cli.md, so this runs alongside all of them. **Goal.** One release lifts exactly one hold, and which hold is deliberate: `liftRefusal` (src/backlog/backlog-release.ts) tries the Refused note first, then the Waiting-for-the-next-failure note, then a held-for-operator Needs-review/Needs-replan note. Nothing reports which one it took, so after `tumwater plan --release` or `tumwater bug --release` the operator cannot tell a refusal lifted from a failure-wait lifted from an operator-hold lifted; the `--json` payload carries only `{file, title}`, and the TUI/GUI flashcards drop the third hold. The written surfaces disagree on the set, too: `tumwater plan --release` help says only "the Refused note" (src/cli/help.ts), while `tumwater bug --release` says "the Refused or Waiting for the next failure note"; the TUI's Ctrl+R `not_refused` flash says "no Refused or Waiting for the next failure note" while its other arm already names all three; and src/gui/gui-client-boot.ts's release flash says "no Refused or Waiting note". Name the lifted hold on every surface and state the full set wherever the command is described.

**Approach.** No behavior change to what a release does — the try order, the one-note-per-release rule, the commit and the wake are untouched.
- src/backlog/backlog-release.ts: export `type LiftableHold = "refused" | "waiting-for-failure" | "held-for-operator"`; make `liftRefusal` return the lifted kind (or `null` when it spliced nothing) instead of a boolean, by returning the kind whose `without…Notes` call shrank the slice. `releaseEntry`'s return and `ReleaseEntryOutcome`'s `"released"` variant gain `lifted: LiftableHold` (its `"not_refused"` variant is unchanged). ### A `ci` role runs the CI workflow's own jobs at main's tip and fixes what fails, part 1/3: the role exists as an observer that reads the workflow's steps (planned 2026-10-24 by the operator, split from the held single `ci` plan; part 2/3 below moves the red-main healer hand-off onto the same role and part 3/3 adds its cheap no-op decision — the poll interval, the parity block and the `CI:` result line; touches src/roles/role-catalog.ts src/roles/roles.ts src/roles/role-labels.ts docs/glossary.md docs/how-it-works.md test/roles.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** Nothing in the loop runs what CI runs. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s test job is `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` (`npm test` = eslint + tsc + the **whole** suite); the team's own check is `check.gateCommand = "npm run test:gate"` (`eslint` + `tsc` + the **affected** tests only, package.json:41, tumwater.json:92). So the full suite and the e2e suite execute only on GitHub, after a change has landed, and the gap has already been paid for twice: the after-merge reviewer in the 2026-10-23 window rejected a commit over "an e2e test the gate skips" (plans/fast-merge.md, "Review before merge for every role not listed in `review.afterMerge`"), and plans/qa-role.md's motivation names the same hole ("the broken-GUI-page incident shipped through a green suite precisely because no consumer of the page existed in CI"). A `ci` role whose one job is CI parity closes it: it runs the workflow's own steps against main's tip and fixes what fails, before a user, a release tag or a post-merge reviewer finds it. This part adds the role and its charter only: `ci` runs the workflow's steps and repairs a failing step's own cause, but it changes no existing routing — a red main's culprit keeps going to `bugfix` (`queueCulpritHeal` and `runner-run.ts`'s `<main-red>` note) until part 2/3 moves that hand-off, so `docs/how-it-works.md`'s merge-pipeline lines naming bugfix stay correct here. Part 3/3 makes its no-op decision cheap.

**Approach.**
- src/roles/role-catalog.ts: add the role after `qa` — `{ id: "ci", tier: "default", title: "CI parity runner", find: … }`. Its find text reads the workflow instead of carrying a hardcoded command list, so a step added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is picked up without a code change: run that job's own `run:` steps verbatim against main's tip in this worktree (`actions/checkout`, `setup-node` and the git identity are the worktree's own) — `npm ci`, then `npm test`, then `npm run test:e2e`, and `npm pack` (the workflow's package job) when the tip is a push-to-main tip. Part 3/3 below makes the first steps conditional on the parity block; this part runs them every tick, which is correct but expensive, and is exactly what part 3/3 fixes. A failing step is the work: reproduce it, fix the source/tests/docs it names, re-run that step until green, and commit the fix as the run's one change; a step that fails once and passes on the re-run is a flake — file ONE BUGS.md entry naming the test and the flake and change nothing else. Whatever it cannot fix is filed with the failing output. The role never edits `.github/workflows/*` (it reads them) and never weakens a test to make a step pass.
- src/roles/roles.ts: add `"ci"` to `OBSERVER_ROLES` — its product is a verdict and a fix, so `no_change` must mean "checked, green" and schedule at `minRunIntervalSeconds` rather than climbing the idle ladder (src/run/run-apply.ts:241), and the role must not ride every main move the way a maintenance role does: a full suite plus e2e per merge is exactly the load storm BUGS.md's e2e/concurrency class entry blames for flaking the concurrency tests. Do **not** add it to `CODE_MAINTENANCE_ROLES`/`BASELINE_BLOCKED_ROLES`: an observer carries no baseline block, and part 2/3's `ci` must be able to author while main is red (the exemption `bugfix` carries today). This part changes neither `src/baseline/main-red.ts` nor that exemption; every existing red-main path still names `bugfix`. The "Every commit is verified on main" plan below removes the block entirely. The md-only exemption list stays unchanged — `ci` authors code.
- src/roles/role-labels.ts and docs: the role's label renders as "CI" wherever role labels are shown (the shared label table, the scheduler's log lines), docs/glossary.md:61's "Observer" line and docs/how-it-works.md's observer paragraph ("`qa`, `selfcheck` and `feedback` are never deferred") add `ci`. In docs/how-it-works.md only that observer sentence changes: the merge-pipeline sentences that route the attributed main-check failure to bugfix ("the failure goes to bugfix", "the bugfix note", "queues a bugfix healer", "queues bugfix's heal prompt naming the commit and the failing tests") keep naming bugfix here, because this part moves no routing — part 2/3 renames them to `ci` when it moves the hand-off.

### The dashboard's Post-merge reviews card gains a State picker that keeps only the chosen states, the `tumwater reviews --status` twin (planned 2026-10-24 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the `ci` series edits src/roles and docs, the "Every commit is verified on main" series edits src/baseline, src/merge, src/config and docs/config.md, the budget series edits src/gates and src/budget, the `--release` plan edits src/backlog, src/cli/help.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts and docs/cli.md, and the role-drawer toggle plan edits src/roles/role-view.ts, src/gui and src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts; none of them edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts or test/gui-client-pending.test.ts, and only docs/how-it-works.md is shared, as a neighbouring sentence inside the Pending-view paragraph; the blocked part 3/3 of "A post-merge rejection stops reverting" later rewrites `postReviewStatusLabel` and this same card, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gui-client-pending.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater reviews --status <state>[,<state>...]` (src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts, `postReviewState`/`POST_REVIEW_STATES` in src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts) keeps only the entries in the named states, each under its whole-queue position, and the dashboard's Post-merge reviews card has its `--role` twin (the Role picker) but not its `--status` twin: the card prints every present state and the operator chasing the `post-merge-risk`/`post-merge-churn` reds must read past the waiting entries, exactly as the CLI had to before `--status` landed. Give the card the same state axis, through the same precedence the label already applies, so the browser and `tumwater reviews --status` cannot disagree on what `rejected`, `failing` and `waiting` mean.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts: add `let pendingReviewState = "";` beside `pendingReviewRole`.
- Same file, beside `postReviewStatusLabel`: add the browser twin of the server's `postReviewState` — `const POST_REVIEW_STATE_ORDER = ["waiting", "failing", "rejected"];` and `function postReviewState(e) { if (e && e.rejected !== undefined) return "rejected"; if (e && typeof e.failures === "number" && e.failures > 0) return "failing"; return "waiting"; }` — the exact precedence `postReviewState` (src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts) applies (rejected before failing before waiting) and its `rejected` branch is literal (`!== undefined`, pinned to the server predicate by test; statusPayload's entries come from `readPostReviews`, which only ever stores an array or leaves it off, so the two agree there), doc-commented as the browser twin. Refactor `postReviewStatusLabel` to branch on it (`rejected` reasons arm, `failing` count/last-failure arm, `waiting` empty string) so every rendered string is byte-identical; hand-kept copy as today, because the inline client script cannot import the server renderer.
- Same file, `postReviewsHtml(entries, armed = "", role = "", state = "")`: compute `const present = new Set(entries.map(postReviewState));` and `const states = POST_REVIEW_STATE_ORDER.filter((s) => present.has(s));`, then `const activeState = state && states.includes(state) ? state : "";` (a state no entry names falls back to all, exactly as `active` does for a role). Build the head's pickers as today's role select plus, when `states.length` is positive, a sibling state select `<label><span class='sr-only'>State</span><select class='field' id='pendingreviewstate'><option value=''>All states</option>` with one `<option value='<state>' [selected]>` per state in `POST_REVIEW_STATE_ORDER` order. Keep the Role select's markup byte-identical — the new select is its sibling inside the same card head, so the existing `/id='pendingreviewrole'…<\/select>/` pin still matches. Widen the kept filter to `(e) => (!active || (e && e.role === active)) && (!activeState || postReviewState(e) === activeState)`; the queue-head count stays `kept.length of entries.length` and the empty-list branch is untouched; a role and a state that are each present but disjoint leave no row, and that one filtered-empty case renders `post-merge reviews (0 of N):` followed by the sibling Overlapping files card's `No … matches the filters` empty message rather than a bare head.
- Same file, `renderPendingReviews(status)`: beside the `pendingReviewRole` prune add `const states = new Set(entries.map(postReviewState)); if (!states.has(pendingReviewState)) pendingReviewState = "";`, and pass `pendingReviewState` as `postReviewsHtml`'s fourth argument. The `$("pendingreviews")` `change` listener gains `else if (e.target.id === "pendingreviewstate") { pendingReviewState = e.target.value; renderPendingReviews(lastStatus); }`, mirroring the `pendingreviewrole` arm.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the Pending-view paragraph's Post-merge reviews sentence: after "with a Role picker that keeps only the chosen role's entries, the `tumwater reviews --role` twin" add "and a State picker that keeps only the chosen states — waiting, failing, rejected, each entry counted in the first state it matches — the `tumwater reviews --status` twin".
- No change to `postReviewStatusLabel`'s strings, the server renderer, `scopePostReviews`, `statusPayload.postReviews`, the TUI Pending pane (whose Ctrl+A accept addresses a whole-queue position, so a filter there would renumber it) or the Accept button. An implementation that finds itself editing anything else has gone off-plan.

### Split `pollBudgetGate`'s fallback-and-view half out of `src/gates/budget-gates.ts` (planned 2026-10-24 by the organize role) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** `src/gates/budget-gates.ts` is 692 lines (3.5× the project's 197-line median) and holds one responsibility too many in a single function: `pollBudgetGate` (lines 244–621, ~378 lines) first decides the gate and emits its edge-triggered events, then derives the fallback config view the roles run under, and both halves share the function's local state and reads. A change to one half (a new subscription-backend rule, a new window-move) forces a read of the other, and the view derivation — the purest, most testable piece — stays buried under the event half. Splitting the view+window derivation out gives each half a plain function boundary and its own tests, mirroring how `stage-path-checks.ts` split `stage-check.ts` and how the vote/failure guards live under `src/budget/`.

**Approach.** Do not start the split now; this entry is the plan. - `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts) keeps the spend read, the price/demotion resolutions, the breaker re-key, the `budgetGate` decision, the warning/transition events and `topDailySpenders` — its first ~110 lines unchanged — then calls the new module for the view fields, so the function shrinks to roughly its pre-view size and both modules compile against the same `BudgetGatePoll` shape.

Re-export what `budget-gates.ts` still exports so no importer's name changes.
- Docs: docs/invariants.md's budget-gate and fallback-view paragraphs re-point their `src/` bind lines at the new module where they name `pollBudgetGate`'s body.

**Goal.** `tumwater reviews` lists the post-merge review queue and `--role` narrows it to the listed roles, but every entry's state (shown by `postReviewStatusLabel`) is only readable, never selectable. An operator answering the `post-merge-churn`/`post-merge-risk` alerts wants just the entries the reviewer turned back, or just the entries whose review runs keep ending without a verdict (the backend-failure class the at-risk advice names), and today must read past every waiting entry. `tumwater history` already narrows its rows by outcome class (`--result`); give `tumwater reviews` the same axis over its entries' three states, preserving each kept entry's whole-queue position so `--accept <n>` still addresses the number the read prints.

**States (the precedence `postReviewStatusLabel` already applies).**
- `rejected`: `entry.rejected !== undefined` — the post-merge reviewer turned the commit back.
- `failing`: not rejected and `entry.failures > 0` — its review runs keep ending without a verdict.
- `waiting`: neither — awaiting its next review run.

Because the state is defined once and the label branches on it, an entry can never print `[rejected — …]` while filtering as `failing`.

**Approach.**
- src/review/post-merge-review-render.ts: add `export const POST_REVIEW_STATES = ["waiting", "failing", "rejected"] as const;`, `export type PostReviewState = (typeof POST_REVIEW_STATES)[number];`, and `export function postReviewState(entry: PostReview): PostReviewState` returning the state by the precedence above, doc-commented as the one home the status label and the `--status` filter share. Refactor `postReviewStatusLabel` to branch on `postReviewState(entry)` — `rejected` prints the existing reasons suffix, `failing` the existing failed-run count/last-failure suffix, `waiting` the empty string — so every rendered string is byte-identical.

It also gains a fourth optional parameter `filter?: string` and carries it on the returned `scope` (`{ roles, positions, total, filter? }`); the one position-computing loop is otherwise unchanged. `renderPostReviews`'s `scope` parameter gains `filter?: string`: the header's filter text is `scope.filter ?? `--role ${(scope.roles ?? []).join(",")}``, and the no-match line reads `no post-merge reviews matching ${scope.filter} (…)` when `filter` is set, else the existing `no post-merge reviews for ${scope.roles.join(",")} (…)`. Every existing three-argument `scopePostReviews` call (`tumwater reviews --role`, the TUI Pending-scope plan's call) passes no `filter`, so its header, no-match line and kept-entry numbering render exactly as today; a state filter passes `roles: []` and the filter text.

When `statusRaw` is null the existing path is untouched. [], keep, filterText)` and render that; `--json` prints `{ pending: entries }`.

### Every post-merge rejection reaches one accounted terminal state: the revert chain holds its plan at exhaustion like a rejection's does, and the forwarded hand-back carries the same round and backstop counters (reported by the user 2026-10-24) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Follow-up 2026-10-24 by the operator:** its terminal-state accounting survives — "Forward, never back" below keeps `holdEntryAfterExhaustion` and the `Revision`-trailer round/backstop counters for the reviewer's self-fix chain — while its subject (the reverted chain, the forwarded hand-back) is deleted by that plan. Feature runners claim this entry every minute and have landed nothing so far; leave whatever is in flight as it is, keep whatever lands, and let the newer plan absorb it when it lands rather than fighting it now.

**Goal.** Every post-merge rejection ends somewhere operator-visible when it never converges, and every hand-back path counts rounds the same way. Two gaps make that false today. (1) The plan hold: `recordRevertedChange` (src/merge/merge-core.ts:401-424) counts rounds and clears the chain at `REVISION_BACKSTOP` but never calls `holdEntryAfterExhaustion`, so an exhausted post-merge chain leaves its plan eligible for a fresh pick that restarts the same cycle — the asymmetry against `recordRejectedChange` (src/merge/merge-core.ts:354-390, which holds at its exhaustion via the call at :387). (2) The forwarded path: `sendReviewToRole` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts:129-140) enqueues an inbox prompt and records nothing — no `state.lastReview`, no round — so a rejection that keeps being handed back has no backstop and no terminal state. Design: plans/post-merge-fix-forward.md, "What could land" item 2.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-core.ts: `recordRevertedChange` calls `holdEntryAfterExhaustion(root, role, state.claim, reasons)` in its exhaustion branch, beside the existing `revision exhausted` log, exactly as `recordRejectedChange` does at :387 — so a post-merge chain that stops converging holds its PLANS.md plan for the plan role instead of re-picking. The existing "a BUGS.md claim is never held" rule inside `holdEntryAfterExhaustion` (no role resolves a Needs-review hold on a bug) stays the one home of that exemption.
- src/merge/merge-core.ts: add the one home of the forwarded record — `recordForwardedChange(root, role, state, commit, reasons)` — set beside `recordRevertedChange` and sharing its round arithmetic (the commit's `Revision` trailer read from `git log -1 --format=%B`, + 1) and its `REVISION_BACKSTOP` handling, so the two hand-back paths cannot drift on the counter. Its `state.lastReview` verdict must say what happened — the commit is still on main, not reverted — so no surface reads a revert that never ran (the BUGS-FIXED.md:24-31 class of defect).
- src/merge/merge-drain.ts `sendReviewToRole`: route through `recordForwardedChange` the way `handBackReverted` (:106) routes a revert — the commit's own runner when it is free, else the first free runner of the same base role — keeping the inbox prompt only for the no-free-runner case, where the round is counted at assignment (`assignPendingReverts`, :142) rather than at the first hand-back.
- Terminal state: an exhausted forwarded chain must be visible where rejections already are (`tumwater report`'s per-role maps, src/report/report-fold.ts) — a `revision exhausted` event is already logged for the reverted chain; the forwarded one logs the same event with its own action, so both read the same way on the report's revision line.
- No change to `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN`/`postMergeRejectionCounts` here: BUGS.md's filed churn entry (filed 2026-10-24, `tumwater bug`) owns the alert's row folding.

- A chain of post-merge rejections that never converges ends with the revision cleared, `refs/tumwater/rejected/<role>` deleted, a `revision exhausted` event logged, and its PLANS.md plan held as a **Needs review** note naming the surviving objections verbatim — the same end state a pre-merge rejection's exhaustion produces.

**Goal.** A `MergeEntry` the pipeline re-queues after a retriable result names its result in `retry` (`merge_blocked`, `review_error`, `merge_conflict` or `main_red`, `retryEntry` in src/merge/merge-requeue.ts) but not how many times the change has bounced, and every re-queue resets `enqueuedAt` to now (`retryEntry`) so it also loses its queue age. A change re-queued once and one re-queued forty times read identically on `tumwater queue`, the dashboard Pending card and the TUI Pending pane. On the day one dirty primary `PLANS.md` produced ~300 `merge_blocked` refusals across five roles (BUGS.md's 2026-10-23 entry), the surfaces showed a succession of apparently fresh single retries, not a change stuck in a loop; the landed `primary-overwrite` alert names that one cause after the fact, but nothing names a repeated bounce itself. Carry a count on the entry and show it wherever the retry reason is already shown, so "this change keeps coming back" is visible at a glance.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-queue.ts: add `retryCount?: number` to `MergeEntry` beside `retry`, doc-commented as how many times the pipeline has re-queued this change (absent for a fresh entry and a recovery's entry; informational, not an ordering key — the filename still orders the queue by the current attempt's `enqueuedAt`). A first re-queue gets 1.
- src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts `retryNote`: widen the `Pick` to `"retry" | "notBefore" | "retryCount"`, and when `(entry.retryCount ?? 0) > 1` append `` ` · ×${entry.retryCount}` `` after `re-queued after ${entry.retry}` and before the `eligible in` clause. A fresh entry (no `retry`) and a first re-queue (count 1) render byte-identically to today, so no existing queue line moves.
- src/status/status-data.ts: add `retryCount?: number` to the `mergeQueue.entries` element type and `...(typeof e.retryCount === "number" ? { retryCount: e.retryCount } : {})` to the `merges.map`, so the key stays absent for a fresh entry and the dashboards receive it.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts `queueEntryLineHtml`: inside the existing `retry` clause, append `(Number.isFinite(e.retryCount) && e.retryCount > 1 ? " · ×" + e.retryCount : "")` after the result and before the `eligible in` clause, matching `retryNote`'s wording.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater queue` clause (the sentence that already says a re-queued entry names why it is back): add that a change re-queued more than once also names how many times it has bounced (`re-queued after merge_blocked · ×3`).

### The merge-queue surfaces mark a high-friction change — the queued commit whose authoring run burned past the friction thresholds and which the reviewer scrutinizes hardest — on `tumwater queue`, the TUI Pending pane and the dashboard Pending card, so an operator can see which waiting change is likeliest to be turned back (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the in-flight `post-merge churn` doctor plan edits src/review/post-merge-review.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/doctor/doctor*.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and test/doctor*.test.ts, the role-view plan edits src/config/config-views.ts, src/review/review.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/roles/role-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts, docs/cli.md and its role-view/drawer tests, and the event-feed plan edits src/events/event-format.ts and test/event-format.test.ts; this touches none of those and shares only docs/how-it-works.md's merge-queue region with no waiting entry; touches src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/merge-queue.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts test/gui-client-pending.test.ts) — done 2026-10-24 by the feature role

**Goal.** A queued `MergeEntry` (src/merge/merge-queue.ts) carries `highFriction?: boolean` when its authoring run burned past `thrashTurns`/`thrashMinutes` (src/run/run-stage.ts sets it on the enqueue; `review.ts` passes it to the reviewer, which applies extra scrutiny — src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts). It never reaches a queue read surface: `renderMergeQueue` (src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts, behind `tumwater queue`, the TUI Pending pane and the TUI transcript) prints only the merge label, retry, revision and summary; status-data's `mergeQueue.entries` projection deliberately copies per-entry scalars but drops `highFriction` (src/status/status-data.ts); and the dashboard's `queueEntryLineHtml` (src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts) has no branch for it. So while a churn spell runs, the operator watches the queue without seeing which waiting change the reviewer will treat hardest — the settled class behind the open revert-ceiling bug. Surface the flag on every queue read surface, in one wording.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts, `renderMergeQueue`: beside `noteTag`/`retryTag` add `const frictionTag = e.highFriction === true ? " · high friction" : "";` and insert `${frictionTag}` in the line after `${tag}` and before `${retryTag}` (order: age, merge label, high friction, retry, revision, summary). `highFriction === true` is the discriminator the queue reader's `isMergeEntry` accepts and `review.ts` reads, so a hand-edited non-boolean does not fabricate the marker. An entry without the flag renders byte-identically to today (empty tag). This one change covers `tumwater queue`, the TUI Pending pane and the TUI transcript, since all three render through this function.
- src/status/status-data.ts, the `mergeQueue.entries` map: add `...(e.highFriction === true ? { highFriction: true as const } : {})`; add `highFriction?: true;` to the `entries` element type (beside `revisionRound`/`retry`); and correct the field's doc comment, which currently says the copies omit the "optional `body`/`highFriction`", to say only `body` is omitted (the boolean flag rides along as the queue line's marker). `status --json` and `/api/status` then carry it.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, `queueEntryLineHtml`: insert `(e.highFriction === true ? ### `tumwater doctor` gains a `post-merge churn` row, the audit twin of the amber `post-merge-churn` alert: the CLI audit names the roles whose already-merged commits the reviewer turned back, so a churn day can no longer make `tumwater doctor` report a false all-clear on main's check (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the in-flight `tumwater history` revert-reason plan edits src/run/run-detail-data.ts, src/run/run-detail-render.ts, docs/cli.md and test/run-detail*.test.ts, the time-spend plan edits src/failure/time-spend.ts, docs/invariants.md and test/failure-time-spend.test.ts, and the failure-digest plan edits src/failure/failure-data.ts, src/failure/failure-render.ts, docs/cli.md and test/failure-render.test.ts; this touches none of those and shares docs/how-it-works.md with no waiting entry; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A post-merge rejection — a `review_rejected` event with `afterMerge: true`, written by `reviewMergedCommit` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) — is an already-landed commit the reviewer turned back, the costly kind that starts a revert and a re-author. The always-on `post-merge-churn` amber alert fires when a trailing day holds at least `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN` (2) of them and names each role (src/ui/status-payload.ts `postMergeChurnAlert`, the block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts), but it renders only on the live dashboard/TUI/`tumwater status` surfaces. `tumwater doctor` has no row for it, and the row that audits main's reverts — `main's check` (`checkMainRed`, src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts) — reads `revertWarnings`/`revertGuardrail` (src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts), which deliberately count only `reason !== "post-review"`. So on a day of six post-merge rejections the doctor prints `no role waiting on main's check`: a false all-clear on the very cost the `review.afterMerge` tiering introduced. Give the doctor the audit twin, sharing the alert's window, threshold and event selection so the two cannot disagree on when churn fires.

**Approach.**
- src/review/post-merge-review.ts: move `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS` here from src/ui/status-payload.ts (beside `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN`), doc-commented as the 24 h window the churn rule reads. Add the one home of the trigger and selection: `export function postMergeChurn(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): { count: number; roles: readonly PostMergeRejection[] } | null` — `const roles = postMergeRejectionCounts(events); const count = roles.reduce((n, r) => n + r.count, 0); return count >= POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN ? { count, roles } : null;`.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS` and `postMergeChurn`; reduce `postMergeChurnAlert`'s body to `const events = eventsSince(root, POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS, now, (e) => e.type === "review_rejected"); return postMergeChurn(events);` inside its existing `try`; re-export the constant (`export { POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS };`) so test/status-payload.test.ts's import keeps working. `PostMergeChurn` and the alert's behavior are unchanged.
- src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts: add `export function checkPostMergeChurn(root: string): CheckOutcome { const churn = postMergeChurn(readEventsSince(root, POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS).events); if (churn === null) return okOutcome("no post-merge rejection burst in the last day"); return warnOutcome(...); }`, modelling `checkFlakyChecks` beside it (ok/warn only — a churn burst does not stop the team); the warn detail is `` `${plural(churn.count, "post-merge review rejection")} in the last day (${churn.roles.map((r) => `${roleLabel(r.role)} ×${r.count}`).join(", ")}) — each commit had already landed, so each cost a revert and a re-author; narrow \`review.afterMerge\` for the noisy role or raise the authoring bar` ``. It imports `postMergeChurn`/`POST_MERGE_REJECT_WINDOW_MS` from ../review/post-merge-review.js and `roleLabel` from ../roles/role-labels.js.
- src/doctor/doctor.ts: register `{ name: "post-merge churn", run: () => checkPostMergeChurn(root) }` immediately after `flaky checks`; import it from ./doctor-project-checks.js.
- src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts: add `"post-merge churn"` immediately after `"flaky checks"`.
- test/doctor.test.ts: add `"post-merge churn"` to the expected name list immediately after `"flaky checks"`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the post-merge-review paragraph: after "Two or more post-merge rejections in a day raise one standing amber alert naming each role on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`", add "— and a matching `post-merge churn` doctor row names the same roles on `tumwater doctor`".
- No change to `postMergeRejectionCounts`, `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN`, the `post-merge-churn` alert's trigger/wording/window, or `checkMainRed`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater doctor` prints a `post-merge churn` row: a trailing day holding at least `POST_MERGE_REJECT_WARN` `review_rejected` events with `afterMerge: true` makes it a warn naming each role with its count and `review.afterMerge`; a day with one such event, a day of only pre-merge `review_rejected` events, and a lone post-merge rejection 25 h old each make it ok.

### The event feed names the review tier — before merge or after merge — on the `review_start`, `review_verdict` and `review_rejected` lines, so a post-merge review no longer reads as a pre-merge one (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the in-flight `post-merge churn` doctor plan edits src/review/post-merge-review.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/doctor/doctor*.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and test/doctor*.test.ts, the Usage-chart plan edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and test/gui-client-report.test.ts, and the role-view plan edits src/config/config-views.ts, src/review/review.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/roles/role-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer-config.ts, docs/cli.md and its role-view/drawer tests; this touches only src/events/event-format.ts and test/event-format.test.ts, none of those) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A review runs either before a commit merges (the default) or after it (a role listed in `review.afterMerge`, whose `review_start`/`review_verdict`/`review_rejected` events carry `afterMerge: true` and are written by `reviewMergedCommit`, src/review/post-merge-review.ts). `formatEvent` (src/events/event-format.ts) renders the `review_start` line with a hardcoded `before merge`, so a post-merge review reads `reviewing <sha> before merge` — factually wrong — and its `review_verdict`/`review_rejected` lines name no tier, so the costly post-merge rejection that reverts an already-landed commit reads identically to a pre-merge one the gate caught in time. The event feed is the operator's first surface (`tumwater logs`, `logs -f`, the dashboard feed and the TUI Activity pane all go through `formatEvent`), and the report table, failure digest and churn alert already name the post-merge class; make the feed line name the tier too.

**Approach.**
- src/events/event-format.ts, `review_start`: replace the literal `before merge` with `${e.afterMerge === true ? "after merge" : "before merge"}`, so the existing pre-merge line is unchanged and a post-merge review reads `reviewing <sha> after merge` (`review resumed <sha> after merge` when `resumed`).
- src/events/event-format.ts, `review_verdict`: after `${shortSha(e.head)}` insert `${e.afterMerge === true ? " after merge" : ""}` before the optional reason, so a post-merge approval reads `review approved <sha> after merge — <reason>`.
- src/events/event-format.ts, `review_rejected`: after `${shortSha(e.head)}` insert the same `${e.afterMerge === true ? " after merge" : ""}`, so a post-merge rejection reads `review rejected <sha> after merge — <reason>`.
- Add a one-line comment on the first of the three that `afterMerge` is the tier flag `reviewMergedCommit` writes for a `review.afterMerge` role; keep `=== true` as the discriminator (the test `postMergeRejectionCounts` and the report fold use), so a hand-edited non-boolean field does not fabricate the tier.
- No docs change: no doc enumerates these event lines (docs/config.md documents the `review.afterMerge` policy, not the feed's wording), and docs/how-it-works.md is held by the in-flight churn plan.
- No change to `review_failed`, `notify.ts`, or any other line: a post-merge review's failures are warn events, not `review_failed` events.

- `formatEvent` renders `reviewing <sha8> after merge` for a `review_start` with `afterMerge: true`, and `review resumed <sha8> after merge` when `resumed` is also set; without the flag the line is byte-identical to today's `... before merge`.
- A `review_verdict` with `afterMerge: true` reads `review approved <sha8> after merge — <reason>` (and `review approved <sha8> after merge` with no reason); without the flag it is unchanged (`review approved <sha8> — <reason>`).
