### Interlock relief, part 1/4: The relief run holds its commit on the branch, and its row does not join the earlier change's verdict (planned 2026-10-23 by user; design in plans/interlock-relief.md "The decision" and "What lands"; split of the oversized Interlock relief part 1/2 — the scheduler admission is part 3/4, the recovery arms part 2/4; touches src/run/run-stage.ts src/run/run-outcome.ts src/run/run-finalize.ts src/history/history-queued.ts test/run-stage.test.ts test/history-data.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role
**Previously held 1**

**Goal.** A post-merge-review role the scheduler admits while its first change is queued (part 3/4) may author a second change. The queue's one-entry-per-role cap must hold: the new commit stays on the branch, unpinned and unqueued, until the first entry drains. Today `stageRunMerge` unconditionally pins and enqueues, which would put two changes on the queue for one role. Stop that, and keep the held run's `run_end` out of the queued-row join so the earlier change's merge verdict is not attributed to it.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-stage.ts (`stageRunMerge`): before `pinAndReset`, if the role already has a queued entry (`queuedMerges(ctx.root).some((e) => e.role === ctx.role)`) or an unmerged pin (`hasUnmergedPin(ctx.root, ctx.role)`), pin nothing, enqueue nothing, and leave the commit on the branch. End `{ result: "queued", summary: finalSummary, commit, highFriction, heldOnBranch: true }`. The commit message, events, flow/filed records and friction are unchanged; only the pin/enqueue block is skipped.
- src/run/run-outcome.ts: add `heldOnBranch?: true` to `RunOutcome`, documented as "the run committed but enqueued nothing because the role already had a queued change; its `run_end` must not join the queued-row verdict".
- src/run/run-finalize.ts: write `heldOnBranch` onto the `run_end` event when the outcome carries it.
- src/history/history-queued.ts (`resolveQueuedResult`): return `null` at the top when `end.heldOnBranch === true`, before the window/floor and bucket walks. The one guard covers all three call sites (`history-data.ts`, `time-spend.ts`, `run-detail-data.ts`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a queued entry already present for the role (`queuedMerges` non-empty), and separately with an unmerged pin and no queue entry, `stageRunMerge` pins nothing, enqueues nothing, leaves the commit on the branch, and ends `queued` with `heldOnBranch: true`; with neither present it pins and enqueues exactly as today.
- `resolveQueuedResult` returns `null` for a `run_end` carrying `heldOnBranch: true`, and the earlier queued run's row still resolves to its own pin's verdict; a `run_end` without the flag is unaffected.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Tests.** test/run-stage.test.ts (the held run pins and enqueues nothing, leaves its commit on the branch, and ends `queued` + `heldOnBranch`); test/history-data.test.ts (a `heldOnBranch` `run_end` is not joined, and the earlier queued run keeps its own pin's verdict).

### Root-install re-sync, part 1/2: `tumwater doctor --resync-install` re-syncs the root checkout's install on demand (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every waiting entry — it adds one value-less doctor flag beside `--commit-backlog`, the CLI's doctor arm, and an operator entry point in src/build/dep-install.ts, none of which any waiting entry touches; the two Health surfaces that call it are part 2/2; touches src/build/dep-install.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/dep-install.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** When a post-merge re-sync fails, the always-on `install` amber alert (src/ui/team-alerts.ts, the `install` block) tells the operator to "run npm install in the project's root checkout" — but only the merge path calls `syncRootInstall` (src/build/dep-install.ts), so the repair is manual, and a running team's next merge is the only automatic retry. Add `tumwater doctor --resync-install`: it runs the same `syncInstall` the merge path runs, under the merge lock, and reports the outcome, so the alert's advice is a harness verb that logs its own `dep_install` event.

**Approach.**
- src/build/dep-install.ts: keep `interface InstallResult` private (an export no other file uses fails the exports gate) and have `RootInstallResync` extend it so the new report names it: `export interface RootInstallResync extends InstallResult { attempted: boolean; packages: string[]; pinned: boolean }` and `export async function resyncRootInstall(root: string, install: InstallRunner = npmInstall): Promise<RootInstallResync>`. Inside `withLock(mergeLockDir(root), ...)` (the lock `tryMerge` holds around its own `syncRootInstall`, merge-to-main.ts, so a merge and the operator can never run two root installs at once), call `syncInstall(root, install)`: `null` (no drift) returns `{ attempted: false, ok: true, packages: [], durationMs: 0, pinned }`; otherwise log the same `dep_install` event `syncRootInstall` logs, but with `source: TUMWATER_SOURCE` (the `operator_revert` precedent in src/operator/revert.ts; import it from ../events/events.js) and a failed `warnEventBestEffort`, then return `{ attempted: true, ok: r.ok, packages: r.packages, durationMs: r.durationMs, pinned, ...(r.detail ? { detail: r.detail } : {}) }`. `pinned` is true when a readable package-lock.json names a top-level project, read inside the lock so an `attempted`-false run matches the lockfile the sync would have aligned against; the catch of a `withLock` timeout/throw returns `{ attempted: true, ok: false, packages: [], durationMs: 0, pinned: <a fresh read>, detail: errorMessage(err) }` so callers never throw. Add `export function rootInstallResyncLines(r: RootInstallResync): string[]` — the one renderer the CLI and part 2/2's surfaces share: `!attempted` and `pinned` gives `["node_modules already matches package-lock.json — nothing to re-sync"]`, `!attempted` and not `pinned` gives `["no package-lock.json to match — nothing to re-sync"]` (so a lockless tree never claims to match a lockfile); `ok` gives `` [`re-synced the root install (${r.packages.join(", ")}) in ${shortSpanPhrase(r.durationMs)}`] `` (import `shortSpanPhrase` from ../text/phrases.js); a failure gives `` [`the root install re-sync failed: ${r.detail ?? "unknown error"}`] ``.
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: add `export const RESYNC_INSTALL_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--resync-install"] }` beside `COMMIT_BACKLOG_FLAG`, value-less like it.
- src/cli.ts: import the flag in the `REPROBE_FLAG`/`KILL_ORPHANS_FLAG` group, add it to `rejectUnknownArgs("doctor", ...)`, and in the `doctor` case before `runDoctor` (beside the `--commit-backlog` block) dynamically import `resyncRootInstall`/`rootInstallResyncLines` from `./build/dep-install.js`, call it when the flag is present, and (text form only) `say` each line then a blank so `--json` stays one document. Carry the result into the payload as `resyncInstall`, chaining it with the existing `withBacklogCommit`/`withKill` wrappers. Like `--commit-backlog`, a failed re-sync does not change the exit code — the doctor's check rows decide it.
- src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md: add `[--resync-install]` to the `tumwater doctor` usage line and one clause to its paragraph naming the root re-sync and that it takes the merge lock.

**Tests.**
- test/dep-install.test.ts, `resyncRootInstall reports nothing to do, a re-sync and a failure, logging under tumwater`: a no-drift root returns `attempted: false` and appends no event; a drifted root with a fake `InstallRunner` returns `attempted: true, ok: true` and appends exactly one `dep_install` with `source: "tumwater"` and the drifted packages, and `rootInstallResyncLines` names them; a failing fake returns `ok: false` with its `detail` and warns. Model on the existing `syncRootInstall` cases (a fake runner keeps the suite off the registry).
- test/doctor.test.ts, `doctor --resync-install is accepted and reports nothing to do without a lockfile`: a repo with no package-lock.json prints the nothing-to-do line and (with `--json`) carries `resyncInstall.attempted === false`; a run without the flag carries no `resyncInstall` field, so the existing doctor payload is unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater doctor --resync-install` runs `syncInstall` under the merge lock; no drift spawns nothing and logs nothing; a re-sync logs one `dep_install` with `source: "tumwater"` and names the re-synced packages; a failure names its detail and does not throw.
- `--json` carries `resyncInstall` only when the flag is given; the doctor's check rows, its other flags and its exit-code rule are unchanged.
- The check and the CLI read one renderer (`rootInstallResyncLines`) and one core (`resyncRootInstall`).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Merges repeatedly refused by files uncommitted in the primary checkout raise a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the orchestrator/merge/CLI plans — Interlock 1/2, post-merge-review and Root-install 1/2 touch no src/ui file or docs/how-it-works.md; the in-flight notify alert shares this plan's three src/ui surfaces, docs/how-it-works.md and test/team-alerts.test.ts, so whichever of the two lands second rebases over a neighbouring argument and block; touches src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The merge path refuses a merge when the primary checkout holds uncommitted files the merge would overwrite (`primaryCheckoutBlockers`, src/merge/merge-git.ts, with `overwriteBlockedReason`): it warns `merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: <files>) — commit, stash or remove them there` and returns `merge_blocked` (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts `tryMerge`; the batch arm in src/merge/merge-stack.ts). On 2026-10-23 one uncommitted `PLANS.md` produced ~300 of these refusals and blocked the two PLANS-touching roles from landing all day (BUGS.md's 2026-10-23 entry). None of the three observer surfaces names this state: `stale-merges` reads a stalled queue, `skipped-merges` unreadable queue files, and the doctor's `uncommitted backlog` row runs only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor` (and its git read is async, so it never reaches the status poll). Add the always-on twin over the last day's overwrite-block warnings, so a fleet stuck retrying one dirty file is a single amber banner until the file is committed and the refusals age out.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface PrimaryOverwriteBlock { count: number; latestTs: number; message: string }` beside `StaleMerge`, documented as the status-payload read of the last day's primary-overwrite warnings. Append `primaryOverwrite: PrimaryOverwriteBlock | null = null` as the **last** parameter of `teamAlerts`, after `reverts: RevertWarning | null = null` (today's final optional parameter; after the notify plan's `notifyFailure` when that has landed), so existing 18-argument callers and tests keep compiling. Add one amber block after the `skipped-merges` block: `key: "primary-overwrite"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(primaryOverwrite.count, "merge was", "merges were")} refused by files uncommitted in your primary checkout` ``, detail `` `most recently ${humanAgo(primaryOverwrite.latestTs, now)}: ${squash(primaryOverwrite.message, 160)} — roles cannot commit your checkout; commit the file(s) on main with \`tumwater doctor --commit-backlog\` (or by hand) so merges can proceed` ``, `actions: []`. `plural`, `humanAgo` and `squash` are already imported, so this adds no import; update the module doc comment's alert list to name a dirty primary checkout refusing merges.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `eventsSince` from `../events/event-window.js` and `type PrimaryOverwriteBlock` beside the other team-alerts types. Add `export const PRIMARY_OVERWRITE_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;` and `const PRIMARY_OVERWRITE_MARKER = "would overwrite files in the primary checkout";` above `export function primaryOverwriteBlocks(root: string, now = Date.now()): PrimaryOverwriteBlock | null` (place it beside `skippedMergeFiles`): `const hits = eventsSince(root, PRIMARY_OVERWRITE_WINDOW_MS, now, (e) => e.type === "warning" && typeof e.message === "string" && e.message.includes(PRIMARY_OVERWRITE_MARKER)); const latest = hits[hits.length - 1]; return latest ? { count: hits.length, latestTs: latest.ts, message: String(latest.message) } : null`. `eventsSince` returns events in event order, so the last hit is the latest. Append `primaryOverwriteBlocks(root, now)` as the **last** `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call, after `revertAlert(root, now)` (after `notifyFailures(root, now)` when the notify plan has landed); it must not be inserted before `revertAlert`.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `primaryOverwriteBlocks` from `./status-payload.js`, and append `primaryOverwriteBlocks(root)` as the **last** `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx); both calls currently end in `revertAlert(root)`, so the new argument goes after it (after the notify plan's `notifyFailures(root)` when landed).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("a failing or stuck role, … a pause"): add "a dirty primary checkout refusing merges" so the documented list matches the alerts.
- No change to src/merge/*, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts or its `uncommitted backlog` check: the alert only reads the `warning` event the merge path already writes, so an implementation that finds itself editing either has gone off-plan.

**Tests.**
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, a unit test `a merge refused by an uncommitted primary file raises one standing amber alert`: `const blockObj = { count: 2, latestTs: now - 3600_000, message: "merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: PLANS.md) — commit, stash or remove them there" }; const alerts = teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [], [], [], null, [], [], [], null, [], [], [], null, blockObj);` — `primaryOverwrite` is the 19th positional argument, after `reverts` (passed `null`); passing it one position earlier silently lands it in `validationGaps` and raises no alert, so the test pins the position. Assert exactly one alert with `key: "primary-overwrite"`, tone `amber`, a title matching `/2 merges were refused/`, a detail including `1h ago`, `uncommitted: PLANS.md` and `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog`, and `actions` `[]`; one hit reads `/1 merge was refused/`; a null last argument adds no alert.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, an integration test `primaryOverwriteBlocks and the surfaces carry a primary-overwrite alert from overwrite-block warnings, and none without one`: seed a root with `writeEvents(root, [{ ts: now - 3600_000, source: "feature", type: "warning", message: "merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: PLANS.md) — commit, stash or remove them there" }])` and assert `primaryOverwriteBlocks(root, now)` has `count === 1` and a `message` containing `uncommitted: PLANS.md`, and `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "primary-overwrite"` while `renderStatus` shows the title; a warning without the marker (`{ type: "warning", message: "pi exited 1" }`) and a clean root each produce none; a marking warning older than the window (call `primaryOverwriteBlocks`/`statusPayload` with `now + 25 * 3600_000`) produces none.

### A failed notify page raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `notify` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every waiting entry — Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner, the post-merge-review plan edits src/orchestrator and src/merge, Root-install 1/2 edits src/build and src/cli, and Root-install 2/2 edits src/gui and src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts and tui-frame.ts, none of them this plan's files; only docs/how-it-works.md is shared, so whichever lands second rebases there; no change is needed in src/events/notify.ts or test/notify.test.ts, whose `isNotifyFailure`/`notifyExitWarning` already exist and are exported and already tested; touches src/doctor/doctor-notify.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md docs/config.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `notify` check (src/doctor/doctor-notify.ts, `checkNotify`) warns when the configured notify hook failed to page within the last day (`isNotifyFailure` events — a nonzero exit, a kill, or a failed start), but only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. The notify hook is the operator's paging channel — a spent budget, a red main — so a hook that silently stopped reaching them leaves the fleet unsupervised. Give the stale-bug rule's treatment to the notify rule: an always-on alert, at the same threshold and over the same `isNotifyFailure` window, so a dead webhook stays visible in the alert banners for the day after a failed page.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-notify.ts: change `const NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS = DAY_MS;` to `export const NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS = DAY_MS;` and widen its doc comment to say the always-on notify alert reuses this window (the `STALE_BUG_DAYS` precedent in src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts). `checkNotify` keeps its current filter and wording unchanged.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface NotifyFailure { count: number; latestTs: number; message: string }` beside `StaleBug`, documented as the doctor's `NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS` rule computed by src/ui/status-payload.ts's `notifyFailures`. Append `notifyFailure: NotifyFailure | null = null` as the **last** parameter of `teamAlerts`, after `reverts: RevertWarning | null = null` (today the final optional parameter), so the existing 18-argument callers and tests keep compiling and the argument cannot land in the `skippedMergeFiles` slot. Add one block immediately after the `stale-bugs` block (before `waiting-bugs`): `key: "notify"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(notifyFailure.count, "failed notify page", "failed notify pages")} in the last day` ``, detail `` `the notify hook could not reach you ${humanAgo(notifyFailure.latestTs, now)}: ${squash(notifyFailure.message, 160)} — check it with \`tumwater notify --test\`` ``, `actions: []`. `plural`, `humanAgo` and `squash` are already imported (../text/phrases.js, ../text/datetime.js, ../text/text.js), so this adds no import. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a failed notify page.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS` from `../doctor/doctor-notify.js`, `eventsSince` from `../events/event-window.js` and `isNotifyFailure` from `../events/notify.js`. Add `export function notifyFailures(root: string, now = Date.now()): NotifyFailure | null` beside `staleOpenBugs`: `const failures = eventsSince(root, NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS, now, isNotifyFailure); const latest = failures[failures.length - 1]; return latest ? { count: failures.length, latestTs: latest.ts, message: String(latest.message) } : null`. Append `notifyFailures(root, now)` as the **last** `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call, after `revertAlert(root, now)`; it must not be inserted before `skippedMergeFiles`.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `notifyFailures` from `./status-payload.js`, and append `notifyFailures(root)` as the **last** `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx); both calls currently pass 18 arguments ending in `revertAlert(...)`, so the new argument goes after it.
- No change to src/events/notify.ts or test/notify.test.ts: `isNotifyFailure`, `notifyExitWarning` and `notifyExitGloss` already exist and are exported in src/events/notify.ts, and test/notify.test.ts already pins them; the alert only reads them. An implementation that finds itself editing either file has gone off-plan.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("a failing or stuck role, … a stale bug, a pause"): add "a failed notify page" so the documented list matches the alerts.
- docs/config.md, the `notify` sentence ("a hook that exits nonzero logs a warning"): add "and raises a standing dashboard alert while a failed page is within the last day" — the window rule, not "until a page succeeds", because the notifier logs only failures and a later success does not clear them.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, both modeling the existing stale-bug tests:
- A unit test `a failed notify page raises a standing amber alert`: `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [], [], [], null, [], [], [], null, [], [], null, { count: 1, latestTs: now - 3600_000, message: "notify command exited with code 127 paging budget_paused" })` — `notifyFailure` is the 19th positional argument, after `reverts` (passed `null`); passing it one position earlier silently lands it in `skippedMergeFiles` and raises no `notify` alert, so the test pins the position. It gives exactly one alert with `key: "notify"`, tone `amber`, a title matching `/failed notify page/`, a detail including `1h ago`, `code 127` and `tumwater notify --test`, and `actions` `[]`; two failures title `/failed notify pages/`; a null last argument adds no alert; with both a stale bug and a notify failure, the keys are `["stale-bugs", "notify"]`.
- An integration test `notifyFailures and the surfaces carry a notify alert from failed pages, and none without one`: seed a root with `warnEvent(root, "tumwater", notifyExitWarning("budget_paused", 127, null) ?? "")` (test/doctor-notify.test.ts's pattern) and assert `notifyFailures(root, now)` has `count === 1` with a `message` starting `notify command exited with code 127`, and `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "notify"` while `renderStatus` shows the title; a `feature`-sourced warning and a clean root each produce none; a failure older than 24h (call `notifyFailures`/`statusPayload` with `now + 25 * 3600_000`) produces none.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A configured notify hook whose page failed within the last `NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS` produces one amber `notify` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the failure count, the age of the latest, its squashed message, and the `tumwater notify --test` fix; a hook with no failure in the window produces none.
- `notifyFailure` is the last `teamAlerts` parameter and the last argument at all three call sites and in the unit test; passing it before `reverts`/`skippedMergeFiles` fails the unit test.
- The alert and the doctor's `notify` check share `NOTIFY_CHECK_WINDOW_MS` and the same `eventsSince`/`isNotifyFailure` filter, so the rule and its threshold cannot drift; neither `src/events/notify.ts` nor `test/notify.test.ts` is modified.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A revert that looks false or a revert burst raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `main's check` revert rule (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except the shared alert files — the four in-flight alert plans each append one defaulted trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and one amber block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edit src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx and docs/how-it-works.md, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; it edits no src/doctor file because the doctor already runs this rule through `guardrailWarnings`, and no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/roles, src/review, src/report, src/cli or src/gui file; touches src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/main-guardrails.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The fast-merge guardrails' G2 rule (`revertWarnings`, src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts) warns when a `main_revert` in the trailing day looks false — its named test has been quarantined since, or its change merged again unchanged and main stayed green — or when more than `REVERT_RATE_LIMIT` (5) reverts land in a day. A revert is the main watch taking a merged change back off main (`main_revert`, src/baseline/main-watch.ts), so a false one is working code lost and a burst is a flaky-revert habit; both deserve the operator's eye while they are happening. Today G2 is visible only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor` or reads the selfcheck digest: the always-on alert model already carries its siblings — G1 red main as the `mainred` alert and G3 quarantine as the `quarantine` alert — but nothing on the dashboard, the TUI or `tumwater status` reads `revertWarnings`. Give G2 the same treatment, over the same rule and thresholds.

**Approach.**
- src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts: add `export interface RevertGuardrail { count: number; phrases: string[] }` (the trailing-day revert count and the `revertWarnings` phrases that fired). Extract `revertWarnings`'s body into `export function revertGuardrail(events, quarantine, now): RevertGuardrail | null` — the same cutoff/reverts select, the same rate-limit phrase and per-revert `revertLooksFalse` phrases, returning `null` when `reverts.length === 0` or `phrases.length === 0`, and `{ count: reverts.length, phrases }` otherwise. `revertWarnings` becomes `return revertGuardrail(events, quarantine, now)?.phrases ?? [];`, so its strings are byte-identical and the doctor and the selfcheck digest are unchanged.
- src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts: add `export function revertsFor(root: string, now: number = Date.now()): RevertGuardrail | null { return revertGuardrail(readEventsSince(root, DAY_MS).events, loadQuarantine(root), now); }` beside `guardrailWarnings` — the poll-path read (one trailing-day event read plus the quarantine file), the same material `guardrailWarnings` already reads. Leave `guardrailWarnings` as it is (it must read once and call the rule once, not twice).
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface RevertWarning { count: number; phrases: readonly string[] }` beside `QuarantinedTests`, documented as G2 computed by main-guardrails' `revertsFor`. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `reverts: RevertWarning | null = null` (append after `strandedPlans`, and after the in-flight plans' trailing parameters once those land) and add one amber block after the `quarantine` block: `key: "reverts"`, tone `amber`, title `` `${plural(reverts.count, "revert off main", "reverts off main")} in the last day` ``, detail `` `${reverts.phrases.join("; ")} — the main watch takes a change off main when main's full check flags it; fix the failing test or the revert repeats` ``, `actions: [{ label: "See failures", act: "view", arg: "failures" }]`. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a revert that looks false or a revert burst.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `revertsFor` beside `quarantineWarning` from `../baseline/main-guardrails.js` and add `type RevertWarning` to the `./team-alerts.js` import. Add `export function revertAlert(root: string, now = Date.now()): RevertWarning | null { return revertsFor(root, now); }` beside `quarantineAlert`, documented as the always-on feed for the `reverts` alert over the same rule. Pass `revertAlert(root, now)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call (after `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)`).
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `revertAlert` from the same module as each file's `quarantineAlert` import, and pass `revertAlert(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alertLines` call and the TUI attention call (after `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)`).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("… a stale or oversized flake quarantine, a plan filed under the wrong backlog section, a pause"): add "a revert off main that looks false or a revert burst".

**Tests.**
- test/main-guardrails.test.ts: using the existing `ev` helper, add `revertGuardrail returns the count and phrases, and null when nothing fires`: the quarantined-since revert fixture gives `{ count: 1 }` with the same `did not reproduce` phrase `revertWarnings` returns; six `main_revert` events inside the day give `count: 6` and the `over the 5-revert ceiling` phrase; a lone revert that is neither false nor over the limit gives `null` and `revertWarnings` returns `[]` for it. Assert `revertWarnings([revert], q, now)` deep-equals `revertGuardrail([revert], q, now)!.phrases` for the false-revert fixture, pinning that the strings cannot drift.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts: add unit test `a revert that looks false raises one amber alert after the quarantine one`: `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [], [], [], null, [], [], [], quarantined, [], { count: 1, phrases: ["revert abc blamed test/T.ts, which has been quarantined since — the failure did not reproduce"] })` (the `reverts` object as the 16th positional argument, after `strandedPlans`) gives exactly one `reverts` alert, tone `amber`, title `1 revert off main in the last day`, a detail matching `/did not reproduce/` and `/fix the failing test/`, and the failures action; `{ count: 6, phrases: ["6 reverts in the last 24 h — over the 5-revert ceiling"] }` titles `/6 reverts off main in the last day/`; a null argument (and the defaulted call) adds no `reverts` alert; with both a quarantine and a revert, `quarantine` precedes `reverts`. Add integration test `revertAlert and the surfaces carry a revert alert from a false revert, and none without one`: `makeRepo()`, then `writeEvents(root, [{ ts: now - 10 * 60_000, source: "tumwater", type: "main_revert", commit: "abcdef1234567890", failingTests: ["test/T.ts"] }])` (test/fixtures/log-fixtures.js) and a `.tumwater/state/quarantine.json` entry for `test/T.ts` whose `lastSeen` is at or after the revert (the `quarantinePath` + fs pattern the quarantine integration test uses); assert `revertAlert(root, now)` returns `{ count: 1 }`, `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "reverts"`, and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows its title; a clean `makeRepo()` produces none on either.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A `main_revert` in the trailing day that `revertWarnings` calls false, or more than `REVERT_RATE_LIMIT` reverts in the day, renders one amber `reverts` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the revert count and the doctor's own phrases; a day with no reverts, or only ordinary reverts under the limit, renders none.
- The alert and the doctor share one rule (`revertGuardrail`, the same `REVERT_RATE_LIMIT` and `revertLooksFalse` reached through `revertsFor`/`guardrailWarnings`), and `revertWarnings`' strings and `guardrailWarnings` are otherwise unchanged.
- docs/how-it-works.md names the alert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A Fixed record with a bad Validation gap trace raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `validation gaps` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the waiting series in behavior — it reads BUGS.md and edits src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts's `checkValidationGaps`, which the in-flight duplicated-headings alert also edits but only its neighbouring `checkBacklogHeadings`; the in-flight duplicated-headings alert (adds a `duplicatedHeadings` trailing parameter and a `backlog-headings` block), the in-flight post-merge-review-queue plan (adds a `postReviews` field to `statusPayload`) and the blocked notify alert (adds a `notifyFailure` parameter and block) all share src/ui/team-alerts.ts and src/ui/status-payload.ts, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring parameter/field/block; it touches no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/roles, src/review, src/report, src/cli, src/gui or src/ui/gui file; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `validation gaps` check (src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts, `checkValidationGaps`) warns when a newest `## Fixed` record in BUGS.md/BUGS-FIXED.md carries no `**Validation gap:**` line, an unrecognized tag, or an `unclear-invariant` tag with no `docs/invariants.md` section: a missing line makes that record invisible to every closed-vocabulary consumer, and a typo like `no-reprod` lands as its own key on `tumwater report`'s `Validation gaps` line. The check is a cheap, synchronous BUGS.md/BUGS-FIXED.md read (`fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)`, no `sourceHaystack` walk like `checkFixClaims`), so it is safe on the status-poll path — but it runs only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`, so a bad trace stays invisible to the observer surfaces that already show the stale-bug, waiting-bug, stranded-plan and plan-dependency twins. Give it the same treatment: an always-on amber alert over the same scan, so the newest Fixed records' traces stay visible until they are corrected.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts: keep the per-record `validationGapTag`/`VALIDATION_GAP_TAGS`/`docs/invariants.md` classification in a private `classifyValidationGaps(records)`, and export `interface ValidationGapProblem { title: string; kind: "missing" | "unrecognized" | "unpinned"; tag?: string }` plus `export function validationGapProblems(root: string): ValidationGapProblem[]` returning the problems of the ONE shared scan `validationGapRecords(root) = fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)` (empty when the file is unreadable). Order the returned rows suspects first, then `unpinned`, so the first row is the one the doctor's message names. `checkValidationGaps` keeps its `readBacklogChecked(root, "BUGS.md")` read for its no-file outcome, then classifies the same `validationGapRecords(root)` records, so the doctor and the alert literally share one scan; it then splits the problems into `suspects` (`kind !== "unpinned"`) and `unpinned` (`kind === "unpinned"`) and builds its two existing messages unchanged, so its wording, the `andMore`/`truncate` folding and the ok text are byte-for-byte (the existing test/doctor-backlog.test.ts assertions still pass).
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: import `type ValidationGapProblem` beside the other doctor types. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `validationGaps: readonly ValidationGapProblem[] = []`, appended after `strandedPlans` (and after the duplicated-headings alert's `duplicatedHeadings` when it has landed), so existing callers and tests keep compiling. Add one amber block after the `stranded-plans` block: `key: "validation-gaps"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(validationGaps.length, "Fixed record has a validation-gap problem", "Fixed records have validation-gap problems")}` ``, detail `` `BUGS.md "${first.title}" ${reason}${more} — every Fixed entry writes exactly one known **Validation gap:** tag (write \`none\` rather than omitting it), and an unclear-invariant fix pins its reconstructed guarantee in docs/invariants.md` `` where `reason` is `has no **Validation gap:** line` for `missing`, `names unrecognized Validation gap tag "${first.tag}"` for `unrecognized`, and `is an unclear-invariant fix but names no docs/invariants.md section` for `unpinned`, and `more` folds `validationGaps.slice(1)` through `joinWithMore(…, 3)` as `"<title>"`; `actions: []` (the fix is editing BUGS.md). `plural` and `joinWithMore` are already imported, so this adds no runtime import. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a Fixed record with a bad Validation gap trace.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `validationGapProblems` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and pass `validationGapProblems(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call (after `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)` and after the duplicated-headings plan's `duplicatedBacklogHeadings(root)` when that has landed).
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `validationGapProblems` from the same module and pass `validationGapProblems(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alertLines` call (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx), after each file's `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)` argument (and after `duplicatedBacklogHeadings(root)` when that plan has landed).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("a stale bug, a broken plan dependency clause, a stranded inbox prompt, a stalled merge queue, …"): add "a Fixed record whose Validation gap trace is missing or unrecognized".

**Tests.**
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, a unit test `validationGapProblems returns the doctor's rows and leaves its wording unchanged`: using the existing `validationGapsRepo` helper, assert `validationGapProblems(root)` has one row each of `kind: "missing"` (for `validationGapsRepo([null, "no-fake"])`), `kind: "unrecognized"` with `tag: "no-reprod"` (for `["no-reprod", "no-fake"]`), and `kind: "unpinned"` (for the single `unclear-invariant`-without-a-section body), each row's `title` starting `Entry 0: details`; a fully tagged repo returns `[]`, an out-of-window `unclear-invariant` record returns `[]`, and the unreadable-file case returns `[]` while `checkValidationGaps` still returns its unreadable outcome. Assert `checkValidationGaps`'s existing messages (`newest 2 Fixed record(s) carry a known Validation gap tag`, `has no **Validation gap:** line`, `unrecognized Validation gap tag "no-reprod"`, the `unclear-invariant … docs/invariants.md` nudge) still match.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, a unit test `a bad Validation gap trace raises one amber alert`: call `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, …, [{ title: "A fix", kind: "missing" }])` with the new trailing argument (the last positional, after `strandedPlans` and any landed `duplicatedHeadings`); assert exactly one alert with `key` `validation-gaps`, tone `amber`, title `Fixed record has a validation-gap problem`, and a detail matching `/BUGS\.md "A fix"/`, `/no \*\*Validation gap:\*\* line/`, `/every Fixed entry writes exactly one known/` and `/docs\/invariants\.md/`, with `actions` `[]`. An `unrecognized` row carries `/unrecognized Validation gap tag "no-reprod"/`, an `unpinned` row `/unclear-invariant.*docs\/invariants\.md/`; two rows title `/Fixed records have validation-gap problems/` and fold the second title; an empty array (and `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now)`) adds no `validation-gaps` alert; with a `strandedPlans` row and a validation problem, `stranded-plans` precedes `validation-gaps`.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, an integration test `statusPayload and renderStatus carry a validation-gaps alert from BUGS.md, and none without one`: `makeRepo()`, then write a BUGS.md whose newest `## Fixed` record has no `**Validation gap:**` line (the `validationGapsRepo` shape); assert `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "validation-gaps"` while `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title; a clean `makeRepo()` (no BUGS.md or fully tagged) produces none on either.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A newest Fixed record with no `**Validation gap:**` line, an unrecognized tag, or an `unclear-invariant` tag naming no `docs/invariants.md` section renders one amber `validation-gaps` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the record, the problem, and the closed-vocabulary/`docs/invariants.md` fix; a clean set renders none.
- The alert and the doctor share one scan (`validationGapProblems` over `classifyValidationGaps`/`validationGapRecords`, `fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)`, `validationGapTag`/`VALIDATION_GAP_TAGS`), and `checkValidationGaps`'s message and ok text are unchanged.
- The alert runs no `sourceHaystack` walk, so it adds only the same two backlog-file reads `checkValidationGaps` already makes to the poll path.
- docs/how-it-works.md names the alert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard's Failures view and the TUI's Failures pane list the flake quarantine below the digest, the read twin of the amber quarantine alert (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the four in-flight alert plans append one trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and one amber block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edit src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, docs/how-it-works.md and test/team-alerts.test.ts; Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner; the validation-gap and duplicated-heading alerts edit src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts. This plan edits none of those source files — src/review/quarantine-render.ts, src/gui, src/ui/gui and src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts are untouched by every waiting plan, and docs/how-it-works.md is the only shared file (a neighbouring sentence), so whichever lands second rebases there; it edits no src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, src/doctor, src/merge, src/orchestrator or src/runner file, and it leaves renderFailureMarkdown and the selfcheck digest unchanged; touches src/review/quarantine-render.ts src/gui/gui-report-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/quarantine-render.test.ts test/gui-report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts test/tui.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The review gate's flake quarantine (`.tumwater/state/quarantine.json`, `quarantinePath`) lists the tests that failed then passed on the same tree, and `onlyQuarantined` (src/review/known-flakes.ts) treats their failures as known so the gate stops re-rejecting them. Its only surfaces today are `tumwater quarantine` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts `cmdQuarantine`, over `quarantineRows`/`renderQuarantine` in src/review/quarantine-render.ts) and the amber `quarantine` alert, whose action is `{ label: "See failures", act: "view", arg: "failures" }`. That action lands on the dashboard Failures view and the TUI Failures pane, and both render only the failure digest, so the operator sees the alert's count and then no list. Add the current quarantine below the digest on both always-on surfaces, from the same `quarantineRows`/`renderQuarantine` rule the CLI uses, so the three cannot disagree.

**Approach.**
- src/review/quarantine-render.ts: add `export function renderQuarantineSection(rows: readonly QuarantineRow[], now: number): string`, documented as the Markdown section the Failures surfaces append (pure, no I/O). Return `""` when `rows.length === 0`; otherwise the lines `## Flake quarantine`, a blank line, the `quarantineWarning(rows, now)` phrase and a blank line when one fires, then one bullet per row: `` `- ${squash(r.test, 80)} — first seen ${humanAgo(r.firstSeen, now)}, last seen ${humanAgo(r.lastSeen, now)}, ${plural(r.count, "flake")} — ${r.bug ? `filed: ${squash(r.bug, 80)}` : "not filed"}` ``. `plural`, `squash`, `humanAgo` and `quarantineWarning` are already imported, so this adds no runtime import. Leave `renderQuarantine` (the CLI's text form) as it is.
- src/gui/gui-report-endpoints.ts: import `loadQuarantine` from `../review/known-flakes.js` and `quarantineRows`, `renderQuarantineSection` from `../review/quarantine-render.js`. In `handleFailures` (both the since branch and the day branch) add `quarantine: renderQuarantineSection(quarantineRows(loadQuarantine(root)), Date.now())` to the object sent with `sendJson`, and extend the doc comment to name the field: the digest's `markdown` is unchanged and `quarantine` is the current (not window- or role-scoped) list, `""` when empty. No route change: the field rides in the existing `GET /api/failures`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: add a `// report-quarantine:start` / `// report-quarantine:end` region holding `function quarantineCardHtml(md)`: `const q = String(md || "").trim(); return q ? "<article class='card md'>" + renderMarkdown(q, true) + "</article>" : "";` (`renderMarkdown` is a page global reached through the concatenation, like the report render already does). In the `failures` windowView's `render`, append `quarantineCardHtml(d.quarantine)` after the digest card, so a window with a digest but an empty quarantine is unchanged. Update the module doc comment to say the Failures view also paints the current flake quarantine below the digest.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts: import `loadQuarantine` from `../../review/known-flakes.js` and `quarantineRows`, `renderQuarantineSection` from `../../review/quarantine-render.js`. In `failuresPaneCache`, after the `renderFailureMarkdown(...)` body, append `\n\n` + the section when it is non-empty (both the day and the stepped-window branches). `usagePaneCache` is unchanged.
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the dashboard Failures/TUI Failures sentence, add that the view and the pane list the current flake quarantine below the digest, the read twin of `tumwater quarantine`.

**Tests.**
- test/quarantine-render.test.ts: add `renderQuarantineSection is empty for an empty list and a Markdown section otherwise`: `[]` gives `""`; two rows — one with `bug: "A filed flake"` and one with `bug: ""`, the first `firstSeen` older than `QUARANTINE_AGE_MS` so `quarantineWarning` fires — give a string starting `## Flake quarantine`, containing the warning phrase and exactly two `- ` bullets, the first naming the test, `first seen`, `last seen`, its flake count and `not filed`, the second ending `filed: A filed flake`.
- test/gui-report.test.ts: add `/api/failures carries the current flake-quarantine section`: `makeRepo()`, `writeFileDeep(quarantinePath(repo), JSON.stringify({ tests: [{ test: "test/T.ts", firstSeen: now - 5 * 86_400_000, lastSeen: now, count: 2, bug: "" }] }))` (the test/cli-quarantine.test.ts fixture pattern; import `quarantinePath` from ../src/paths.js), then through `withGui` fetch `/api/failures` and assert `d.quarantine` starts `## Flake quarantine` and names `test/T.ts`; a clean `makeRepo()` (no quarantine file) returns `quarantine: ""`. Assert the response's `markdown` is still exactly `renderFailureMarkdown(collectFailureReport(...))` for the same query.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: extract the `report-quarantine` region with the existing `clientScope` seam (a `renderMarkdown` stub returning a marked string) and assert `quarantineCardHtml("## Flake quarantine\n- test/T.ts")` returns one `card md` article wrapping the stub's output, while `quarantineCardHtml("")` and `quarantineCardHtml(undefined)` return `""`.
- test/tui.test.ts: with a seeded `.tumwater/state/quarantine.json` (`quarantinePath`), the Failures frame contains `## Flake quarantine` and the test name; a repo without one contains neither. Model it on the existing Failures-frame assertions (`assert.match(frame, /\[Failures\]/)`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The dashboard's Failures view and the TUI's Failures pane list the current quarantine under the digest, naming each test's first/last-seen ages, flake count and filed/not-filed bug; an empty quarantine adds nothing on either surface.
- `/api/failures` carries the section as a `quarantine` string (empty when the list is empty); its `markdown` field is byte-identical to `renderFailureMarkdown(collectFailureReport…)` for the same query, so `tumwater report --failures`, its `--json`, and the selfcheck digest are unchanged.
- The section and the CLI read one rule (`quarantineRows`/`quarantineWarning` in src/review/quarantine-render.ts), and the `quarantineWarning` phrase appears when it fires.

### Duplicated `## ` backlog section headings raise a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `backlog headings` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the in-flight series — only src/ui/status-payload.ts is shared, with the in-flight post-merge-review-queue plan adding its `postReviews` field and the blocked notify alert adding a `notifyFailure` parameter and block, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring field/block; it touches no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/roles, src/review, src/cli, src/report, src/gui or src/ui/gui file; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The doctor's `backlog headings` check (src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts, `checkBacklogHeadings`) warns when a `## ` section heading appears more than once in PLANS.md, BUGS.md, QUESTIONS.md or either archive file: every section reader takes the first section of a name, so later entries are invisible. The merge gate blocks a merge that *adds* another copy, but a duplicate already on main persists until a deliberate edit and nothing repairs it on its own — and the damage is silent and costly (on 2026-10-23 two archived BUGS-FIXED entries shared one normalized heading, hiding the other's body and rejecting every md-only BUGS.md edit for two days). The doctor warns only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`, so give the stale-bug rule's treatment to this one: an always-on alert over the same `duplicateHeadings`/`BACKLOG_FILES` scan, so a duplicated section stays visible on every observer surface until it is removed.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts: extract the per-file body of `checkBacklogHeadings` into `export interface DuplicatedBacklogHeading { file: string; heading: string }` and `export function duplicatedBacklogHeadings(root: string): DuplicatedBacklogHeading[]`, both fed by a private `scanBacklogHeadings(root): { duplicates: DuplicatedBacklogHeading[]; rows: string[] }` so the two public functions share one loop over `BACKLOG_FILES` and one `duplicateHeadings` call and cannot drift. Because the always-on alert polls the scan on every observer tick, the per-file read is stat-cached (`cachedByStat` over a module-level cache keyed by path): a steady-state poll pays one stat per file instead of re-reading every `BACKLOG_FILES` member, including the MB-scale archive files. `checkBacklogHeadings` reads `rows` (the `${file} "## ${heading}"` and `${file} (unreadable)` strings in `BACKLOG_FILES` order, interleaved as encountered) and keeps its message and `ok`/`warn` shape byte-for-byte.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface BacklogHeadingDuplicate { file: string; heading: string }` beside the other alert payload interfaces, documented as the doctor's `backlog headings` rule computed by `duplicatedBacklogHeadings` (structural twin: no mapping in status-payload). Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `duplicatedHeadings: readonly BacklogHeadingDuplicate[] = []`. Add one block after the `stranded-plans` block: `key: "backlog-headings"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(duplicatedHeadings.length, "duplicated backlog heading", "duplicated backlog headings")}` ``, detail `` `${first.file} "## ${first.heading}" appears more than once${more} — readers take the first section of a name, so later entries are invisible; remove the duplicate in a deliberate edit` `` where `more` folds `duplicatedHeadings.slice(1)` through `joinWithMore(..., 3)` as `\`"## <heading>" in <file>\``, `actions: []`. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a duplicated backlog section heading.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `duplicatedBacklogHeadings` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and pass `duplicatedBacklogHeadings(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call (after `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)`).
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `duplicatedBacklogHeadings` from the same module as each file's `strandedPlanEntriesFor` import (`../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and `../../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js`) and pass `duplicatedBacklogHeadings(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alertLines` call (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx); both currently end their argument list with `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("a stale bug, a broken plan dependency clause, a stranded inbox prompt, a stalled merge queue, …"): add "a duplicated backlog section heading".

**Tests.**
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, a unit test `duplicated backlog headings raise one amber alert folded like stranded plans`: call `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, …, [])` with `[{ file: "PLANS.md", heading: "Done" }]` as the new trailing argument (the last positional, after `strandedPlans`); assert exactly one alert with `key` `backlog-headings`, tone `amber`, title `1 duplicated backlog heading`, and a detail matching `/PLANS\.md "## Done"/`, `/appears more than once/` and `/remove the duplicate/`, with `actions` `[]`. Two rows title `/duplicated backlog headings/` and fold the second as `/— and 1 more/`; an empty array (and `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now)`) adds no `backlog-headings` alert; with a `strandedPlans` row and a duplicate, `stranded-plans` precedes `backlog-headings`.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, an integration test `statusPayload and renderStatus carry a duplicated-heading alert from the backlog files, and none without one`: `makeRepo()`, then `writeBacklogFile(root, "PLANS.md", [{ heading: "## Planned", body: "### A (planned 2026-01-01 by plan)" }, { heading: "## Planned" }, { heading: "## Done" }])`; assert `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "backlog-headings"` while `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title; a clean `makeRepo()` produces none on either.
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: in `checkBacklogHeadings warns on a duplicated heading and stays silent on a clean set` (or a sibling beside it), assert `duplicatedBacklogHeadings(dir)` deep-equals `[{ file: "PLANS.md", heading: "Done" }]` on the duplicated doc and `[]` on the clean one; on the unreadable-file case, assert it returns the readable files' duplicates `[{ file: "BUGS.md", heading: "Open" }]` (no unreadable row of its own) while `checkBacklogHeadings`'s row still names `PLANS.md (unreadable)` — pinning that the alert and the doctor share one scan and the doctor's wording is unchanged. The same case pins `BACKLOG_FILES` order in the doctor row when an unreadable file coexists with a duplicate heading: the detail starts with `PLANS.md (unreadable)` and that phrase precedes `BUGS.md "## Open"`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A `## ` section heading that appears more than once in PLANS.md, BUGS.md, QUESTIONS.md or either archive file renders one amber `backlog-headings` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the file, the heading, and the remove-the-duplicate fix; a clean set renders none.
- The alert selects the same files and headings as the doctor's `backlog headings` check (`BACKLOG_FILES` and `duplicateHeadings`, through `duplicatedBacklogHeadings`), and `checkBacklogHeadings`'s message — including the unreadable-file clause — is unchanged.
- docs/how-it-works.md names the alert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater report` gains a `Post-merge rejections by role` line, so the reviewer rejections of already-merged commits are visible per role (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — none of the four in-flight entries (queue move-to-top, doctor `--commit-backlog` surfaces, convergence-hold charter, post-merge review queue surfaces) touches src/report or test/report*.test.ts; only docs/cli.md is shared, as a neighbouring clause inside its one `tumwater report` row, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-render.ts docs/cli.md test/report.test.ts test/report-data.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `review.afterMerge` (landed 2026-10-23 with reviewer-as-role) moved the high-volume roles' changes to post-merge review, and `reviewMergedCommit` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) logs each verdict with `afterMerge: true`. A post-merge rejection is a different event from a pre-merge one: the commit already merged, so the rejection names it to the revert path off main (src/baseline/main-revert.ts's `MainCulprit.postReview`). The usage report folds every `review_rejected` into one `rejectionsByRole` map (src/report/report-fold.ts), so an operator reading `tumwater report` cannot tell how many of a role's rejections were returned after the change had already landed — the costly kind. Add that subset as its own ranked line, so the report shows the rejections that escaped to main beside the ones the gate caught.

**Approach.**
- src/report/report-fold.ts: `UsageFold` and `DayFold` each gain `postMergeRejectionsByRole: Record<string, number>` beside `rejectionsByRole`, documented as the `review_rejected` events whose `afterMerge` is true, per role id — a subset of `rejectionsByRole`, kept apart because a post-merge rejection turns back an already-merged commit. In `foldUsageEvent`'s `review_rejected` branch, after `addTo(target.rejectionsByRole, eventRole(ev), 1);` add `if (ev.afterMerge === true) addTo(target.postMergeRejectionsByRole, eventRole(ev), 1);`. `dayFoldFor` initialises it to `{}`.
- src/report/report-data.ts: `collectReportSince`'s `acc: UsageFold` literal gains `postMergeRejectionsByRole: {}`, and its returned object gains `postMergeRejectionsByRole: scopedByRole(acc.postMergeRejectionsByRole, bases),` beside `rejectionsByRole`. `collectReport`'s team branch sets `day.postMergeRejectionsByRole = fold.postMergeRejectionsByRole` only when non-empty (the zero-means-absent rule its siblings use); its scoped branch narrows with `narrowToRole(fold.postMergeRejectionsByRole, bases)` and sets it only when non-empty.
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains optional `postMergeRejectionsByRole?: Record<string, number>`; `SinceReport` gains required `postMergeRejectionsByRole: Record<string, number>` (always present, empty when none). Both doc comments say it is the `afterMerge: true` subset of that interface's `rejectionsByRole`.
- src/report/report-render.ts: in `renderSinceReportMarkdown`, after `pushRankedRoleLine(lines, "Rejections by role", rankedRoleMap(data.rejectionsByRole));` add `pushRankedRoleLine(lines, "Post-merge rejections by role", rankedRoleMap(data.postMergeRejectionsByRole));`. In `renderReportMarkdown`, after its `Rejections by role` push add `pushRankedRoleLine(lines, "Post-merge rejections by role", rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.postMergeRejectionsByRole ?? {}));`. Update both surrounding comments to say the new line is the `afterMerge: true` subset.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater report` row's ranked per-role list: after "rejections (from `review_rejected` events)" add "post-merge rejections (those `review_rejected` events that carried `afterMerge: true` — a merged commit the reviewer turned back, so it had to be reverted off main)".

**Tests.**
- test/report-data.test.ts, beside "collectReport folds review_rejected events into per-day per-role rejections": add `collectReport folds post-merge review_rejected events into their own map`: write a `review_rejected` with `afterMerge: true` for `feature` and one without for `clean`; assert the day's `rejectionsByRole` deep-equals `{ feature: 1, clean: 1 }` (both still count) and its `postMergeRejectionsByRole` deep-equals `{ feature: 1 }`; assert a day with no afterMerge rejection carries no `postMergeRejectionsByRole` key. Add `collectReportSince carries the post-merge rejection subset` asserting the same split over `collectReportSince(root, 6 * HOUR)` and `{}` when none.
- test/report.test.ts: in "renderReportMarkdown prints a Rejections by role line ranked by count, only when rejections exist", give a day a `postMergeRejectionsByRole` and assert the new line ranks like its sibling; in the zero-rejection pin (the `lines[15]` test) assert the new line reads `**Post-merge rejections by role:** -`. Add `postMergeRejectionsByRole: {}` to the `renderSinceReportMarkdown` literal fixtures (they build the full `SinceReport`), and add a since assertion that the line ranks when the map is non-empty.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater report` and `tumwater report --since <duration>` each print a `Post-merge rejections by role` line ranking, per role, every `review_rejected` whose `afterMerge` is true, beside the existing `Rejections by role` line; a window with none renders the shared `-` form.
- `rejectionsByRole` is unchanged: it still counts every `review_rejected`, so the new map is exactly its `afterMerge: true` subset and no JSON field is renamed or removed.
- The line is role-scoped like its siblings (`tumwater report --role <id>` narrows it), and `--json` carries the new map (per-day only when nonzero; always present on the window report).
- docs/cli.md names the new line.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The post-merge review queue is visible on the dashboard's Pending view and the TUI Pending pane, not only `tumwater reviews` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the in-flight queue-move-to-top plan's and the parked notify plan's edits except as noted — queue-move-to-top also adds a row button and Ctrl+V arm to `src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts` and `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts`, and the parked notify plan edits `src/ui/status-payload.ts`; whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring card/block/field; it touches no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/roles, src/doctor or src/cli file and no src/ui/team-alerts.ts file; touches src/review/post-review-render.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/cli.md test/post-review-render.test.ts test/status-payload.test.ts test/gui-client-pending.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater reviews` (landed 2026-10-23) lists the post-merge review queue `.tumwater/state/post-review.json` (`readPostReviews`, src/review/post-merge-review.ts) through `renderPostReviews`, but the two observer surfaces still do not read it: the dashboard's Pending view shows the pre-merge Merge queue card and the TUI Pending pane shows the merge queue and the change roster, and neither reads `readPostReviews` (a post-merge review that keeps ending without a verdict or a rejected commit still waiting on its revert is invisible until the operator runs the CLI). Surface the queue on both, in the same FIFO order and wording the CLI prints, so the reviewer-as-role pipeline is observable where operators watch merges.

**Approach.**
- src/review/post-review-render.ts: extract `export function postReviewStatusLabel(entry: PostReview): string` — the bracketed suffix `renderPostReviews` builds inline today (`[rejected — waiting to revert: <squashed reasons>]` when `rejected` is set, else `[N failed review runs]` when `failures` is positive, else `""`), reasons squashed to 60 as today. `renderPostReviews` calls it and appends `" · " + label` only when the label is non-empty, so the CLI, the dashboard and the TUI share one status wording and cannot drift.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `readPostReviews` from `../review/post-merge-review.js` and add `postReviews: readPostReviews(root),` to the object `statusPayload` returns, beside `mergeQueue: snap.mergeQueue` — raw data for the browser, exactly like the merge queue and for the same reason (the browser JS cannot import the TypeScript reader).
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts: add `function postReviewsHtml(entries)`: `"<div class='empty'>No merged commit is waiting for a post-merge review</div>"` when the array is empty; else a `<div class='queue-head'>post-merge reviews (N):</div>` and one `<div class='queue-entry'>` per entry carrying `<span class='mono'>${roleLabel(e.role)} ${shortSha(e.commit)}</span> · ${esc(e.summary)}` plus `esc(postReviewStatusLabel(e))` in a `mono` span when the label is non-empty (reuse the existing queue-entry/queue-head classes so no CSS change is needed). Add `function renderPendingReviews(status)` that reads `status && Array.isArray(status.postReviews) ? status.postReviews : []` and sets `$("pendingreviews").innerHTML`; add the card `<div class='card' id='pendingreviews'><div class='empty'>Loading…</div></div>` in `buildPendingView` between the `pendingqueue` and `pendingoverlaps` cards; call `renderPendingReviews(lastStatus)` wherever `renderPendingQueue(lastStatus)` is called in this module (`fetchPending`) and update the module doc comment to name the card.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, the status-poll repaint: beside the two existing `if (activeView === "pending") renderPendingQueue(...)` hooks (in the poll handler and the fetch-then-repaint path) add `if (activeView === "pending") renderPendingReviews(...)`, so the card repaints on every poll like the Merge queue card.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts: import `readPostReviews, type PostReview` from `../../review/post-merge-review.js` and `renderPostReviews` from `../../review/post-review-render.js`. Add `let lastReviews: PostReview[] = [];` set in `refresh()` from `readPostReviews(session.root)` (a cheap synchronous read, like `readMergeQueue`), and a `const reviewsHead = (): string => lastReviews.length === 0 ? "" : renderPostReviews(lastReviews);`. Define `const queueAndReviews = (): string => { const q = queueHead(); const r = reviewsHead(); return r === "" ? q : q + "\n\n" + r; };` and replace the `queueHead()` calls that compose `head` (in `refresh`, the Ctrl+G arm, and the Ctrl+N restore) with `queueAndReviews()`, so the post-merge review block paints under the merge queue and above the change roster and needs no new key or scope (the Ctrl+G scope narrows only the merge queue). Update the pane doc comment.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the Pending/merge-pipeline section: one sentence naming the dashboard's Post-merge reviews card and the TUI Pending pane's block as the observer twins of `tumwater reviews`.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater reviews [--json]` clause: add that the dashboard's Pending view shows the same queue in its Post-merge reviews card and the TUI Pending pane renders it above the change roster.

**Tests.**
- test/post-review-render.test.ts: add `a postReviewStatusLabel names the rejection or the failed-run count`: an entry with neither `rejected` nor `failures` gives `""`, one with `failures: 2` gives `"[2 failed review runs]"`, one with `rejected: ["a", "b"]` gives `"[rejected — waiting to revert: a; b]"`; the existing `renderPostReviews` cases still pass (they pin the same strings now built by the helper).
- test/status-payload.test.ts: add `statusPayload carries the post-merge review queue`: a `makeRepo()` root whose `postReviewPath(root)` is written with one well-formed entry puts that entry in `statusPayload(root).postReviews` (deep-equal), and a root with no file carries `[]`; a torn entry is dropped by `readPostReviews` as today.
- test/gui-client-pending.test.ts: add `postReviewsHtml is empty until a commit waits and names each entry otherwise`: `postReviewsHtml([])` matches `/No merged commit is waiting/`; two entries match `/post-merge reviews \(2\)/` and each row carries the role label, short sha and summary; a `rejected` entry carries `waiting to revert` and a `failures: 2` entry `2 failed review runs`; the role/summary text is escaped. Use the existing `clientScope` over `["format", "labels", "pending-table"]` with `postReviewsHtml` exposed.
