### The doctor's uncommitted-backlog repair runs from the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab, not only `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the waiting series — the alert plans edit src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx; Interlock 1/2 and the post-merge-review plan edit src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner; the reviews plan edits src/review, src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts, src/cli.ts and docs/cli.md; it shares with the in-flight queue-move-to-top plan only neighbouring additions in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts and src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, a neighbouring docs/cli.md clause and one test/tui-keys.test.ts case, so whichever lands second rebases there; it reads the landed `commitUncommittedBacklog` from src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts and edits no src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/review or src/ui/team-alerts.ts file; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/cli.ts src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts docs/cli.md test/doctor-backlog.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-settings.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` landed 2026-10-23 (src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, `commitUncommittedBacklog`) so an operator can commit the dirty tracked backlog/brief file that blocks merges from the primary checkout. Every other doctor recovery action reaches the observer surfaces — Kill orphans (dashboard button, TUI Ctrl+K twice), Re-probe models (dashboard button, TUI Ctrl+P), reclaim (dashboard button, TUI Ctrl+E), `notify --test` (dashboard Send test, TUI Ctrl+N) — but commit-backlog is CLI-only. The `uncommitted backlog` row warns in the dashboard Health card and the TUI Health tab, yet the repair it names is unreachable from either. Add the missing surface for the two recovery verbs that share the `commitUncommittedBacklog` core, so the checkout cannot drift between the CLI and the surfaces.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: export `backlogCommitLines(report: BacklogCommitReport): string[]` beside `commitUncommittedBacklog` — the CLI text form's three line groups, in order: `committed ${file} on ${base}` per committed file, `could not commit ${file} — commit it by hand` per failed file, the `skipped` sentence when set — so the CLI, the dashboard handler and the TUI flash share one wording and cannot drift. In `checkUncommittedBacklog`'s warn detail, change the tail `and commit them on ${base}` to `and commit them on ${base} (or run \`tumwater doctor --commit-backlog\`, or the Health card's Commit backlog, or the TUI Health tab's Ctrl+A)` — the same naming of its own recovery the orphans row carries.
- src/cli.ts: the `--commit-backlog` text branch prints `backlogCommitLines(backlogCommit)` instead of its inline `committed`/`failed`/`skipped` loops (the same lines in the same order); the `--json` field is unchanged.
- src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts: add `handleCommitBacklog(req, res, root, commit: (root: string) => Promise<BacklogCommitReport> = (r) => commitUncommittedBacklog(r, loadConfigSafe(r).config))` beside `handleKillOrphans`: `readPostBody(req, res, "{}")`, then `const report = await commit(root); const lines = backlogCommitLines(report); if (lines.length === 0) lines.push("nothing to commit — every watched backlog or brief file is committed"); sendJson(res, 200, { ok: report.failed.length === 0, message: lines.join("; "), committed: report.committed, failed: report.failed, skipped: report.skipped, base: report.base });`. `commitUncommittedBacklog` never throws, so an off-base or unreadable checkout lands as the `skipped` sentence, not a 500. Import `commitUncommittedBacklog, backlogCommitLines, type BacklogCommitReport` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog.js` and `loadConfigSafe` from `../config/config.js`; widen the module doc comment to name commit-backlog.
- src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts: add `handleCommitBacklog` to the `./gui-operator-commands.js` re-export list beside `handleKillOrphans`. src/gui/gui-server.ts: add `"POST /api/doctor-commit-backlog": (req, res) => handleCommitBacklog(req, res, root),` beside `/api/kill-orphans`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts (the `GUI_CLIENT_SETTINGS_JS` module): in `buildSettingsView`'s Health header, add `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-action='doctor-commit-backlog' title='Commit each uncommitted tracked backlog or brief file on main, like tumwater doctor --commit-backlog'>Commit backlog</button>` beside Kill orphans. Add `commitBacklogClick` beside `killOrphansClick` — a single click, because the commit is the doctor's own recommended repair and is reversible (unlike the process kill's two-click arm) — POSTing `/api/doctor-commit-backlog`, flashing `(d.ok ? "" : "error: ") + d.message`, then `fetchDoctor()` so the `uncommitted backlog` row repaints.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts (the `GUI_CLIENT_BOOT_JS` module): in the Health card's delegated click listener, add `if (clickClosest(ev, "button[data-action='doctor-commit-backlog']")) { ev.preventDefault(); commitBacklogClick(); }`.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add a `commitBacklog` seam beside `killOrphans` (`commitBacklog?(root: string): Promise<BacklogCommitReport>`, defaulting to `(r) => commitUncommittedBacklog(r, loadConfigSafe(r).config)`), so the arm is testable without committing on a throwaway root.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts: in `handleKey`, add a Ctrl+A arm guarded like its siblings (`key.ctrl && key.name === "a" && promptLineFree(ctx.es) && session.view === session.roleIds.length + 7`): flash `committing the uncommitted backlog/brief files …`, then `void session.commitBacklog(session.root).then((report) => { const lines = backlogCommitLines(report); session.flashMessage(lines.length ? lines.join("; ") : "nothing to commit — every watched backlog or brief file is committed"); void run(); session.paneScroll = 0; session.requestRender(); }, (err: unknown) => { session.flashError(err); session.requestRender(); })`. Import `backlogCommitLines` from `../../doctor/doctor-backlog.js` and update the pane doc comment to name the arm.
- src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: in `handleKey`, add an explicit Ctrl+A case routing to `health.handleKey` only when `session.view === session.roleIds.length + 7` (the `Ctrl+P` case's shape). The Backlog view's Ctrl+A (open the answer editor for the selected question) stays with `tui-editor-answer.ts`, which the key dispatcher consults before the pane router, so the new case never shadows it.
- docs/cli.md: the Audit row's `--commit-backlog` clause names the dashboard Health card's Commit backlog and the TUI Health tab's Ctrl+A; add a TUI key-table row `| Ctrl+A | Health | commit each uncommitted tracked backlog or brief file on the base branch ... |` beside the other Health rows.

**Tests.**
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: a unit test `backlogCommitLines names each committed and failed file and the skip sentence`: a report `{ base: "main", committed: ["PLANS.md"], failed: ["BUGS.md"], skipped: null }` deep-equals `["committed PLANS.md on main", "could not commit BUGS.md — commit it by hand"]`; a `skipped` report returns just that sentence; an empty report returns `[]`. The existing `checkUncommittedBacklog warns naming each modified backlog file` test's new clause is covered by extending its `/merge_blocked/` assertion to also match `/tumwater doctor --commit-backlog/`.
- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts: `handleCommitBacklog answers the commit lines and ok`, modelled on the `handleKillOrphans` test: inject `async () => ({ base: "main", committed: ["PLANS.md"], failed: [], skipped: null })` and assert 200 with `ok: true`, `message: "committed PLANS.md on main"` and the report arrays; a failed report gives `ok: false` and the could-not-commit line; an empty report gives the nothing-to-commit message; a `not json` body is 400 and the seam is never called.
- test/gui-client-settings.test.ts: `commitBacklogClick posts /api/doctor-commit-backlog and reruns the doctor`, modelled on the `killOrphansClick` test's JS harness: one click (no arming) posts once to `/api/doctor-commit-backlog` and refetches the doctor.
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: `Ctrl+A on the Health view commits the dirty backlog and flashes the lines`, using the new `commitBacklog` seam: navigate to Health, resolve a report with one committed file, press Ctrl+A, assert the flash joined the lines and the doctor re-ran; an empty report flashes the nothing-to-commit line; Ctrl+A on the Backlog view still answers the selected question (the existing test), and Ctrl+A off Health calls no commit.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The dashboard Health card's Commit backlog button POSTs `/api/doctor-commit-backlog`, which commits each dirty tracked backlog/brief file through `commitUncommittedBacklog` and answers the same lines `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` prints; a clean checkout answers the nothing-to-commit message; a file whose commit fails answers `ok: false` naming it; an off-base or unreadable checkout answers the skip sentence, not an error.
- The TUI Health tab's Ctrl+A does the same through the same core and flashes those lines (or the nothing-to-commit line), then re-runs the checks; Ctrl+A on the Backlog view still opens the answer editor, and Ctrl+A off Health commits nothing.
- `backlogCommitLines` is the one source of the committed/failed/skip wording the CLI, the handler and the TUI flash share, and `checkUncommittedBacklog`'s warn names the three repairs.
- docs/cli.md's `--commit-backlog` clause and the TUI key table name both surfaces; the `tumwater help`/docs parity test (cli-doc.test.ts) passes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The plan role acts on the automatic convergence hold, not only the feature's too-large Needs-review note (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every waiting series — Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge and src/runner/leftover.ts, the post-merge-review plan edits src/orchestrator and src/merge, the alert plans edit src/ui, the reviews plan edits src/review and src/cli, and the queue-top and commit-backlog plans edit src/merge, src/gui and src/ui/tui; this plan touches src/roles, src/runner/revision.ts, its tests and docs/invariants.md, and shares only the src/runner directory with Interlock 1/2's different file; touches src/roles/role-guidance.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts src/runner/revision.ts test/prompt-roles.test.ts test/role-guidance.test.ts test/revision.test.ts docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `holdEntryAfterExhaustion` (src/runner/revision.ts) holds a claimed PLANS.md plan when a change's revision chain stops converging, writing `**Needs review <date> by <role>: could not converge — <surviving objections>**` (INV-BH4). `entryHold` classifies it `needs-review`, the claim gate refuses it, and `checkStalledPlans` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) tells the operator "the plan role resolves it by splitting or replanning". But the plan role's charter (`find` in src/roles/role-catalog.ts) tells it only what to do with the feature's `**Needs review …: too large for one run (held N)**` note (split) and the `**Needs replan …: rejected after N review rounds (held H)**` note (rewrite); the automatic hold's `could not converge` text matches neither, so a run following its charter leaves it parked. Three plans sit that way right now (Interlock relief 1/2, the failed-notify alert, the post-merge-review role), each with its objections quoted in the note. Name the automatic hold's marker in the charter and tell the plan role to rewrite from those objections, so the hold reaches the one role that clears it.

**Approach.**
- src/roles/role-guidance.ts: export `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER = "could not converge"` with a doc comment naming the note it identifies (a `**Needs review … by <role>: could not converge — …**` line) and why it is shared: it sits between `holdEntryAfterExhaustion`, which writes the note, and the plan charter, which reads it. Add no second literal.
- src/runner/revision.ts: build the note's reason from `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER` instead of the inline `"could not converge"`, so the writer and the charter cannot drift. The note is otherwise unchanged.
- src/roles/role-catalog.ts, the plan `find`: add one bullet after the `NEEDS_REVIEW_NOTE` split bullet — a plan held by the automatic convergence hold (`CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER`) also outranks adding another plan: the text after the dash is the reviewer's surviving objections, so read the quoted objections and the code they name and rewrite the plan so an implementation answers each (correcting the approach or the anchors, tightening the acceptance criteria, or splitting it per PLAN_SIZING), then remove the note. Extend the existing lift paragraph so a note with no `(held N)` tag (the automatic hold) is lifted without writing a `**Previously held 0**` marker; a counted note still round-trips its count.
- test/role-guidance.test.ts: beside the existing plan-charter marker assertions, assert the plan `find` includes `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER` and that the constant is `"could not converge"`.
- test/prompt-roles.test.ts: in "the plan role prioritizes a Needs review plan …", assert the plan `find` matches the rewrite-from-quoted-objections clause and names `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER`.
- test/revision.test.ts: in "an exhausted chain holds the entry with the surviving objections, not a fresh pick", assert the hold line includes `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER` (the test checks only `startsWith("**Needs review")` today), pinning the note reason the charter now reads.
- docs/invariants.md, INV-BH4: state that the hold's `could not converge` marker is the one the plan charter names, so the plan role rewrites the plan from the quoted objections rather than leaving it parked; add the new test names to "Pinned by".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `CONVERGENCE_HOLD_MARKER` is the single source of the `could not converge` text: `holdEntryAfterExhaustion` builds its reason from it and the plan `find` references the same constant, and a test asserts it.
- The plan role's charter names the automatic hold and instructs a rewrite against the note's quoted objections (not a split), and says a note without a `(held N)` tag lifts without a `**Previously held 0**` marker; the `NEEDS_REVIEW_NOTE` split path and the counted-lift path are unchanged.
- test/revision.test.ts's exhausted-chain test asserts the hold line carries the marker; test/prompt-roles.test.ts and test/role-guidance.test.ts assert the charter carries it; the existing split and counted-lift assertions still pass.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A waiting merge can be moved to the front from the Pending pane and the dashboard's Merge queue card, not only `tumwater queue --top <n>` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the post-merge-review scoping plan edits src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, merge-verify.ts, merge-drain.ts and src/orchestrator, Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/orchestrator and src/runner, and the alert plans (quarantine, stranded-plans, blocked notify) edit src/ui/team-alerts.ts, status-payload.ts, status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx — none of them edits src/merge/merge-top.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts or src/ui/gui; the reviews and doctor --commit-backlog plans edit src/cli, src/review, src/doctor and docs/cli.md (this plan extends the existing `tumwater queue --top` clause in docs/cli.md, a neighbour of their new rows, so whichever lands second rebases there); it touches no src/cli, src/doctor, src/review or src/orchestrator file and no src/ui file the in-flight plans touch; touches src/merge/merge-top.ts src/events/events.ts src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts docs/cli.md test/merge-top.test.ts test/gui-queue-top.test.ts (new) test/gui-client-pending.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater queue --top <n>` (landed) moves a waiting merge to the front, and the merge queue has a Cancel on both observer surfaces (`tumwater queue --cancel <n>`, the Pending pane's Ctrl+X twice, the dashboard card's two-click Cancel) — but the reorder lives only in the CLI: an operator watching the Pending pane or the dashboard's Merge queue card can remove a waiting merge but cannot prioritize one. The other two queues already carry both verbs on their surfaces (the Backlog pane's Ctrl+V for plan/bug, the Inbox pane's Ctrl+V for prompts). Give the merge queue the same treatment: Ctrl+V on the Pending pane and a one-click Move to top on each dashboard Merge-queue row that is not already first, both through the landed `moveQueuedMergeToTop` core, so the surfaces, the CLI, and the event log cannot drift.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-top.ts: extract the post-position body of `moveQueuedMergeToTop` into a private `topQueuedFile(root, files, index): TopQueuedOutcome` (the already-first check, the stamp computation, the rename, the `merge_topped` event); `moveQueuedMergeToTop(root, position)` keeps its range check then delegates. Add `export type TopQueuedByShaOutcome = TopQueuedOutcome | { status: "gone" }` and `export function moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha(root: string, sha: string): TopQueuedByShaOutcome` — `const files = queuedMergeFiles(root); const i = files.findIndex((q) => q.entry.sha.toLowerCase() === sha.toLowerCase()); return i < 0 ? { status: "gone" } : topQueuedFile(root, files, i);` — the sha-addressed twin of `cancelQueuedMergeBySha` (src/merge/merge-cancel.ts), so a browser row that shifted between paint and click moves the entry it named or nothing. Document the `gone` race as merge-cancel.ts does.
- src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts: add `export async function handleQueueTop(req, res, root): Promise<void>` beside `handleQueueCancel`, modelled on it: `readPostBody(req, res, '{"sha": "1a2b3c4"}')` and the same 400 on a non-4-64-hex `sha`; the same `readMergeQueue`/`queueInFlight`/`orchestratorAlive` 409 when a live merge marker names the sha (with `handleQueueCancel`'s wait-then-revert wording); then `moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha`. Answer `{ status: "gone" }` 200 for a sha no longer queued, `{ ok: true, status: "already-first", role, commit, summary, message: \`${shortSha(sha)} is already at the front\` }` when the entry is position 1, and `{ ok: true, status: "topped", role, commit, summary, message: \`moved the merge of ${shortSha(sha)} to the front — ${outcome.summary}\` }` otherwise. Import `moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha, type TopQueuedByShaOutcome` from `../merge/merge-top.js`.
- src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts: add `handleQueueTop` to the `./gui-operator-commands.js` re-export list beside `handleQueueCancel` (the tests import this barrel, as gui-queue-cancel.test.ts does).
- src/gui/gui-server.ts: add `"POST /api/queue-top": (req, res) => handleQueueTop(req, res, root),` beside the `/api/queue-cancel` route, importing `handleQueueTop` beside its sibling.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts: in `queueEntryLineHtml`, add a sixth parameter `top` (a boolean); when `top && position > 1 && typeof e.sha === "string"`, prepend to the row's buttons `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-top='${esc(e.sha)}'>Move to top</button>`. Pass `true` from `pendingQueueHtml`'s `queueEntryLineHtml` call and leave `drawerQueueHtml`'s call without it (the drawer shows this role's merges, not the queue's order, so its rows have no reorder). In `buildPendingView`'s `$("pendingqueue")` click listener, before the `[data-cancel]` branch, handle `const t = e.target.closest("[data-top]"); if (t) { const sha = t.getAttribute("data-top"); if (sha) { await postAction("/api/queue-top", { sha }, (d) => d && d.status === "topped" ? "moved the merge of " + shortSha(d.commit) + " to the front" : d && d.status === "already-first" ? "that merge is already at the front" : "that merge already left the queue"); fetchPending(); } return; }` — a single click, because the move is reversible and non-destructive (unlike Cancel's two-click arm). Update the module doc comment to name the Move to top button beside Cancel.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts: import `moveQueuedMergeToTop` from `../../merge/merge-top.js`; in `mergeDetail`, change the header to `merge #${row.position} (Ctrl+X to cancel, Ctrl+V to top): …`; in `handleKey`, add a `key.ctrl && key.name === "v"` arm after the Ctrl+X arm, gated by the same `promptLineFree(ctx.es) && session.view === session.roleIds.length + 5` and the same "select a merge with ↑↓ first" list-mode flash. Resolve the row exactly as Ctrl+X does (`queueRows[Math.min(selectedQueue, queueRows.length - 1)]`); when `row.position === 1`, flash `merge #1 is already at the front` and change nothing; otherwise re-read `queuedMergeFiles(session.root)` and verify `files[row.position - 1]?.entry.sha === row.entry.sha` (a queue that shifted under the selection refuses with "the merge queue changed — try again"), call `moveQueuedMergeToTop(session.root, row.position)`, and on `topped` clear the selection and `queueDetail`, flash `moved merge #<position> to the front: <roleLabel> <shortSha> — <summary>`, and `refresh()`; `already-first` flashes `merge #<position> is already at the front`; `out-of-range` flashes "the merge queue changed — try again"; `gone` flashes "that merge already left the queue" — each followed by `refresh(); session.requestRender();`. No two-step arm (the move is reversible). Update the module doc comment to name the Ctrl+V arm.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater queue … --top <n>` clause in the Check-state row: add that the same move is the dashboard Merge queue card's per-row Move to top button and the TUI Pending pane's Ctrl+V, both through this core. In the TUI key table, add a row `| Ctrl+V | Pending | move the selected queued merge to the front (the terminal twin of `tumwater queue --top <n>`); position 1 reports already-first |` beside the `Ctrl+X` (twice) Pending row.

**Tests.**
- test/merge-top.test.ts: add by-sha cases to the existing suite: after three `enqueueMerge` calls, `moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha(root, thirdSha)` answers `topped` with role/sha/summary and the next `queuedMerges(root)` lists it first; the leading entry's sha answers `already-first` and renames nothing; an unknown sha answers `gone` with the order unchanged; and the by-sha move logs exactly one `merge_topped` event under the entry's role.
- test/gui-queue-top.test.ts (new, the gui-queue-cancel.test.ts pattern: `makeRepo`, `pinOffMain`, `enqueueMerge`, `handleQueueTop` through `captureJson`/`fakeReq`): a valid sha moves the named entry's queue file to the front (next `queuedMerges` order) and answers 200 `topped` with role/commit/summary; the leading sha answers 200 `already-first` and renames nothing; an unknown sha answers 200 `gone`; a sha a live merge marker names answers 409 and leaves the file; a missing or non-hex sha answers 400 and writes nothing.
- test/gui-client-pending.test.ts: extend the `pendingQueueHtml` suite: with two entries the second row carries `data-top='<sha>'` and reads `Move to top` while the first row carries none, and a one-entry queue carries none; role and summary markup stays escaped.
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: update the `selects a queued merge in full` assertion to the new `(Ctrl+X to cancel, Ctrl+V to top)` header; add `the Pending pane moves the selected queued merge to the front with Ctrl+V`: with a two-entry queue, select the second, press Ctrl+V, assert the flash names the move, `queuedMerges(root)` lists the second first with every entry field unchanged, one `merge_topped` event is logged, and the pane returns to list mode; Ctrl+V on position 1 flashes already-first and changes nothing; Ctrl+V in list mode flashes the select hint; and Ctrl+V still opens the attach editor on the Activity view (the new arm is scoped to the Pending view).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Ctrl+V on a selected Pending merge at position > 1 moves it to the head of the merge queue through `moveQueuedMergeToTop`, logs one `merge_topped`, and the pane's refreshed list shows it first with its entry JSON unchanged; position 1 answers already-first and changes nothing.
- The dashboard Merge queue card renders a Move to top button on every row but the first; clicking it posts `/api/queue-top` by sha through `moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha`, moving that entry to the front and refetching; an unknown sha reports it already left; a mid-merge sha is refused.
- The GUI and TUI reorder the same queue the CLI's `tumwater queue --top <n>` does, through the shared `moveQueuedMergeToTop` core, so the three cannot drift on the rename, the `merge_topped` event, or the already-first/out-of-range outcomes; the new `moveQueuedMergeToTopBySha` is the sha-addressed twin of `cancelQueuedMergeBySha` and follows the same `gone` race handling.
- docs/cli.md's queue `--top` clause and TUI key table name both new surfaces; `tumwater help`/docs parity (cli-doc.test.ts) passes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A plan filed under the wrong PLANS.md section raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `plans stuck in Planned` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except three in-flight alert plans that also append one defaulted trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and one amber block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edit src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, docs/how-it-works.md and test/team-alerts.test.ts — the stalled-plans alert appends `stalledPlans`, the notify alert `notifyFailure` and the quarantine alert `quarantined`, so whichever lands after the others rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; it reads the already-exported, stat-cached `strandedPlanEntriesFor` from src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts and changes nothing there, so it shares no source file with src/cli, src/doctor, src/review, src/merge or src/orchestrator; touches src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A plan heading filed under the wrong `## ` section is invisible to every reader that scans the right one: a `(planned …)` heading sitting under `## Done` never enters a Planned reader (the claim allocator never hands it out), and a done-dated heading still under `## Planned` invites a second implementation. The detector (`strandedPlanEntriesFor`, src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts) already reads PLANS.md and PLANS-DONE.md, is stat-cached so an unchanged file costs one stat, and is what the clean role's prompt block, the doctor's `plans stuck in Planned` row (`checkStrandedPlans`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) and the merge gate already share. The clean role repairs a stranded heading only when it happens to run, and the doctor warns only when the operator asks; give the state the stale-bug treatment so it stays on the always-on observer surfaces until it is repaired. Amber because a stranded plan is work that silently never runs.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: import `type StrandedPlanEntry` from `../backlog/backlog-structure.js` (beside the existing `stripEntryStamp` import) and document it as the doctor's `plans stuck in Planned` rule. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `strandedPlans: readonly StrandedPlanEntry[] = []` after `skippedMergeFiles` (and after the stalled-plans alert's `stalledPlans`, the notify alert's `notifyFailure` and the quarantine alert's `quarantined` when those have landed, so existing callers and tests keep compiling). Add one amber block after the `plan-dependencies` block: `key: "stranded-plans"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${strandedPlans.length === 1 ? "A plan sits" : "Plans sit"} under the wrong backlog section` ``, detail `` `${first.file ?? "PLANS.md"} has a plan stranded under ## ${first.section}: "${first.title}"${more} — move it under ## ${first.section === "Done" ? "Planned" : "Done"}${first.file === undefined || first.file === "PLANS.md" ? "" : " in PLANS.md"} (the clean role repairs these)` `` where `const [first, ...rest] = strandedPlans;` and `const more = rest.length ? ` · ${joinWithMore(rest.map((e) => `"${e.title}" in ${e.file ?? "PLANS.md"} ## ${e.section}`), 3)}` : ""`, and `actions: []` (the fix is editing a backlog file, and a `PLANS-DONE.md` entry has no PLANS.md drawer index). `joinWithMore` and `plural` are already imported. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a plan filed under the wrong section.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `strandedPlanEntriesFor` beside `finishedTitle` from `../backlog/backlog-structure.js` and pass `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call, after `skippedMergeFiles(root)`.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `strandedPlanEntriesFor` from `../backlog/backlog-structure.js` beside the existing backlog imports (`openQuestions`, `refusedEntries`) and pass `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx), after `skippedMergeFiles(root)`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("… a stale bug, a broken plan dependency clause, a stranded inbox prompt, a stalled merge queue, …"): add "a plan filed under the wrong backlog section" after "a broken plan dependency clause" so the documented list matches the alerts.
- No doctor change: `checkStrandedPlans` and the alert both read `strandedPlanEntriesFor`, so the selection cannot drift (only the prose differs).

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, modelling the plan-dependency alert tests:
- A unit test `plans filed under the wrong backlog section raise a standing amber alert`: pass `[{ title: "Split me (planned 2026-10-20)", section: "Done" }]` as the new last `teamAlerts` argument (filling any parameters the in-flight stalled-plans, notify and quarantine alerts added with their defaults first) and assert exactly one alert with `key: "stranded-plans"`, tone `amber`, title `A plan sits under the wrong backlog section`, a detail including `PLANS.md`, `## Done`, `Split me`, `move it under ## Planned` and `clean role`, and `actions` `[]`; a two-entry list (one with `file: "PLANS-DONE.md"`, section `Done`) titles `Plans sit under the wrong backlog section` and its detail names `PLANS-DONE.md` and `in PLANS.md`; an `[]` argument adds none; with a plan-dependency problem and a stranded plan, `plan-dependencies` precedes `stranded-plans`.
- An integration test `strandedPlanEntriesFor and the surfaces carry a stranded-plans alert from PLANS.md, and none without one`: `writeBacklogFile(root, "PLANS.md", [{ heading: "## Planned" }, { heading: "## Done", body: "### Stray plan (planned 2026-10-20)\n\nbody" }])`, then assert `strandedPlanEntriesFor(root)` names `Stray plan`, `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "stranded-plans"` and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title; a PLANS.md whose planned heading sits under `## Planned` and whose done-dated heading sits under `## Done` produces `[]` and no `stranded-plans` alert.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A plan heading filed under the wrong section of PLANS.md or PLANS-DONE.md produces one amber `stranded-plans` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the file, the current section, the heading and the section it belongs under; a correctly-sectioned PLANS.md and a missing PLANS.md each produce none.
- The alert fires exactly on the entries `strandedPlanEntriesFor` returns — the same call the clean role and `checkStrandedPlans` read — so the alert and the doctor cannot drift on the selection.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater reviews [--json]` lists the post-merge review queue, so an operator can see a merged commit still awaiting review, one whose review keeps failing, or a rejected one still waiting on the revert (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the post-merge-review scoping plan (in flight) edits src/orchestrator/scheduling-skip.ts, scheduling-scope.ts, orchestrator-poll.ts and src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, merge-verify.ts, merge-drain.ts, none of this plan's files; queue --top, doctor --commit-backlog and the quarantine plan each add a neighbouring stanza to src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md (this plan puts its command in its own src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts, so only those three are shared, and whichever lands second rebases there); it edits no src/ui, src/doctor, src/merge or src/orchestrator file; touches src/review/post-review-render.ts (new) src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts (new) src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/post-review-render.test.ts (new) test/cli-reviews.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The reviewer-as-role change (Reviewer as a regular role, part 1/4, landed 2026-10-23) moved the high-volume roles' changes to post-merge review through `review.afterMerge`, and the merge drain now parks each merged commit in `.tumwater/state/post-review.json` (`addPostReview`/`readPostReviews`, src/review/post-merge-review.ts) until `drainPostReviews` (src/merge/merge-post-review.ts) reviews it. That file is the one merge-pipeline queue with no operator read surface: `tumwater queue` shows the pre-merge queue, and neither `tumwater status`, the doctor, the TUI nor the dashboard reads `readPostReviews` (`grep -rn readPostReviews src/cli src/status src/doctor src/ui` matched nothing before this plan). Three states there are invisible and worth seeing: a commit still awaiting its review, a review that ended without a verdict `POST_REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT` times (the entry is then dropped and the commit stays on main unreviewed), and a rejected commit whose revert has not started yet (`rejected`, the entry the drain keeps until `startRevert` settles it). Add the missing read: `tumwater reviews` lists every well-formed entry in FIFO order with its role, short commit, summary and status; `--json` serves the same normalized list to scripts.

**Approach.**
- src/review/post-review-render.ts (new): `export function renderPostReviews(entries: readonly PostReview[]): string`. Empty renders `post-merge review queue empty` (the `merge queue empty` convention, src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts). Otherwise a header `post-merge review queue (${plural(entries.length, "entry", "entries")}):` then one line per entry in the given order: `  ${i + 1}. ${roleLabel(entry.role)} ${shortSha(entry.commit)} · ${squash(entry.summary, 80)}` with one status suffix — ` · [rejected — waiting to revert: ${entry.rejected.map((r) => squash(r, 60)).join("; ")}]` when `rejected` is set, else ` · [${plural(entry.failures, "failed review run")}]` when `entry.failures` is a positive number, else nothing. Import `roleLabel` from ../roles/role-labels.js, `shortSha` from ../text/format.js, `squash` from ../text/text.js, `plural` from ../text/phrases.js and `type PostReview` from ./post-merge-review.js. Pure — no I/O and no clock read (the entry carries no timestamp, so no age line; a reader wanting the commit's age uses `tumwater history <role>`).
- src/cli/cli-review-commands.ts (new): `export async function cmdReviews(root: string, args: string[]): Promise<void>` — `rejectUnknownArgs("reviews", args, [JSON_FLAG])`, then `const entries = readPostReviews(root); sayJsonOrRender(args, { pending: entries }, () => renderPostReviews(entries));`. No `requireReadyRepo`: `readPostReviews` reads a missing, torn or hand-edited file as the well-formed subset (or `[]`), so the command prints the empty line in any directory and is read-only (the `cmdBacklog` rationale; it writes no file, unlike `cmdQueue`'s `--cancel`). Give the module a doc comment saying it is `tumwater queue`'s post-merge twin and why it does not gate. Import `JSON_FLAG, rejectUnknownArgs` from ./cli-flag-specs.js, `sayJsonOrRender` from ./cli-output.js, `readPostReviews` from ../review/post-merge-review.js and `renderPostReviews` from ../review/post-review-render.js.
- src/cli.ts: `case "reviews": await (await import("./cli/cli-review-commands.js")).cmdReviews(root, args); break;` beside `case "queue"`.
- src/cli/help.ts: a stanza beside `tumwater queue`, `tumwater reviews [--json]`, saying it lists the post-merge review queue (`review.afterMerge`) in FIFO order — one line per merged commit with its role, short sha, summary and either its rejected reasons (waiting to revert) or its failed-review-run count — that an empty queue prints `post-merge review queue empty`, and that `--json` prints `{ pending: [...] }`. `helpStanzas` feeds completion.ts, so shell completion picks the command up with no further edit.
- docs/cli.md, the `Check state` row: a `tumwater reviews [--json]` clause after the `tumwater queue` clause, with the same meaning.

**Tests.**
- test/post-review-render.test.ts (new): `[]` renders `post-merge review queue empty`; two entries render the `post-merge review queue (2):` header and `  1. feature #2 <short sha> · <summary>` / `  2. …` in input order; an entry with `rejected: ["a", "b"]` carries `[rejected — waiting to revert: a; b]` and one with `failures: 2` carries `[2 failed review runs]`; an entry with neither carries neither suffix.
- test/cli-reviews.test.ts (new, the test/cli-queue.test.ts pattern: `makeRepo`, `initProject`, `cli`): with no post-review file, `reviews` prints `post-merge review queue empty` and exits 0; after writing `postReviewPath(root)` with `{ pending: [{ commit, role: "improve", summary: "seed" }, { commit: other, role: "clean", summary: "rejected", rejected: ["no tests"] }] }` (the test/post-merge-review.test.ts seeding pattern), `reviews` lists both in order with `improve` first and the second's `waiting to revert: no tests`; `reviews --json` prints `{ pending: [...] }` whose entries carry `commit`/`role`/`summary`/`rejected`; a file with a torn entry (`{ commit: 7 }`) drops only that entry; `reviews --bogus` exits nonzero naming the flag; `readPostReviews(root)` deep-equals the entries read before the command (read-only).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater reviews` lists every well-formed entry in `.tumwater/state/post-review.json` in FIFO order, numbered, each naming its role, short commit, summary and either its rejected reasons (waiting to revert) or its failed-review-run count; with no entries it prints `post-merge review queue empty`.
- `--json` emits `{ pending: [...] }` with the normalized entries; a missing or torn file degrades to the empty/well-formed list, exit 0.
- The command is read-only (it never writes `post-review.json`), and `tumwater help` and docs/cli.md name it (the `cli-doc.test.ts` parity).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A stuck dirty backlog file in the primary checkout can be committed from the doctor, not only by hand: `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` commits each uncommitted tracked backlog/brief file on main (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the notify alert edits src/doctor/doctor-notify.ts and src/ui/team-alerts.ts, status-payload.ts, status-render.ts and tui.tsx; the interlock and post-merge-review plans edit src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner; queue --top and the re-queued-merge plan edit src/merge, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts and src/events; the held-for-operator plan edits src/gui and src/ui/tui; this plan touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, which none of them edits, and it shares `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` and `docs/cli.md` with the queue --top and re-queued-merge plans only as neighbouring stanzas, so whichever lands second rebases there; it edits no `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/doctor-backlog.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A harness backlog write whose commit does not land leaves the tracked file dirty in the primary checkout, and every merge that touches it is refused at the pre-flight (`merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: PLANS.md) — commit, stash or remove them there`, src/merge/merge-stack.ts and merge-to-main.ts) and retried each poll — the 2026-10-23 case logged 303 refusals in one day (BUGS.md "The primary checkout's PLANS.md sat uncommitted all of 2026-10-23"). The doctor's `uncommitted backlog` row (`checkUncommittedBacklog`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts) already names the files and tells the operator to commit them, but no harness command does it; only hand-run git can. Add the missing recovery: `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` commits each dirty tracked backlog or brief file on the base branch through the same `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` core every operator backlog write already uses (src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts, under the primary-worktree lock), so the fleet unblocks without losing the write.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: extract the dirty-file discovery from `checkUncommittedBacklog` into `export interface DirtyBacklogFiles { base: string; primary: string | null; watched: string[]; dirty: string[] | null }` and `export async function dirtyBacklogFiles(root: string, config: TumwaterConfig | undefined): Promise<DirtyBacklogFiles>` — `base = targetBranch(config?.baseBranch, primary)`, `primary = await currentBranch(root)`, `watched` the `[...BACKLOG_FILES, ...(briefFile(root) ? [briefFile(root)] : [])]` list, `dirty` the non-`??` names from `gitTry(root, "status", "--porcelain", "--", ...watched)` (null when that read fails). Rewrite `checkUncommittedBacklog` to call it and return the SAME four outcomes and detail strings it returns today (off-base, unreadable, all-clean, warn), so its existing tests stay green unchanged.
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: add `export interface BacklogCommitReport { committed: string[]; failed: string[]; skipped: string | null }` and `export async function commitUncommittedBacklog(root: string, config: TumwaterConfig | undefined): Promise<BacklogCommitReport>`. `const d = await dirtyBacklogFiles(root, config)`; when `d.primary === null || d.primary !== d.base` return `{ committed: [], failed: [], skipped: \`your checkout is not on ${d.base}; nothing committed\` }`; when `d.dirty === null` return `{ committed: [], failed: [], skipped: "could not read git status; nothing committed" }`; otherwise, for each name in `d.dirty`, `await commitOperatorBacklogEdit(root, name, stampedSubject("operator", \`Commit uncommitted ${name}\`))` (import `stampedSubject` from ../git/commit-message.js and `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` from ../backlog/backlog-commit.js) and push the name to `committed` on true or `failed` on false; a file already staged or committed by a concurrent write simply returns false and lands in `failed`, and the function never throws.
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: add, beside `KILL_ORPHANS_FLAG`, `export const COMMIT_BACKLOG_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--commit-backlog"] };` with a doc comment saying it commits each dirty tracked backlog or brief file on the base branch before the report, under the primary-worktree lock, through the operator backlog commit path (the second mutating doctor flag, after `--kill-orphans`).
- src/cli.ts, the `doctor` arm: add `COMMIT_BACKLOG_FLAG` to the `rejectUnknownArgs("doctor", ...)` list; when `args.includes("--commit-backlog")`, `await commitUncommittedBacklog(root, undefined)` before `runDoctor` (undefined makes `targetBranch` treat the checked-out branch as the base, the same precedence `checkUncommittedBacklog(root, undefined)` uses), print its lines before the report unless `--json` (the `--kill-orphans`/`orphanKillLines` shape): `committed <file> on main` per committed file, `could not commit <file> — commit it by hand` per failure, and the `skipped` sentence alone when set; thread the report into the JSON payload as `backlogCommit` through the existing `withKill`-style spread, so `--problems` and `--json` both carry it and a plain `doctor --json` carries no such key.
- src/cli/help.ts, the `doctor` usage line and paragraph: add `[--commit-backlog]` and say it first commits each uncommitted tracked backlog or brief file (PLANS.md, BUGS.md, QUESTIONS.md, their archives, the brief) on the base branch under the primary-worktree lock, so a merge the dirty file blocks can proceed; `docs/cli.md`, the `tumwater doctor` section, the same sentence.

**Tests.**
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, beside the `checkUncommittedBacklog` block (the `backlogRepo()` helper): `commitUncommittedBacklog commits each dirty backlog file and the check reads ok afterwards` — append a line to PLANS.md and QUESTIONS.md, call `commitUncommittedBacklog(root, { baseBranch: "main" } as never)`, assert `committed` deep-equals `["PLANS.md", "QUESTIONS.md"]`, `failed` empty and `skipped` null, `git status --porcelain -- PLANS.md QUESTIONS.md` is empty, `checkUncommittedBacklog(root, undefined).level === "ok"`, and the newest commit subjects `stampedSubject("operator", ...)` prefix/sha shape; `commitUncommittedBacklog skips a primary that is not on the base branch` — `git checkout -b other`, append to BUGS.md, call with `{ baseBranch: "main" }`, assert every list empty and `skipped` matches `/not on/`, and BUGS.md is still dirty; `commitUncommittedBacklog reports a failed commit and keeps going` — write `.git/index.lock` to make `git commit` fail, dirty PLANS.md and QUESTIONS.md (or dirty only PLANS.md), and assert PLANS.md lands in `failed` while it stays dirty.
- test/doctor.test.ts, beside the `doctor --kill-orphans …` test (line ~573): `doctor --commit-backlog commits a dirty backlog file before the report; with --json it is the report's backlogCommit field` — in a seeded repo (the file's existing repo helper) make PLANS.md dirty, run `["doctor", "--commit-backlog"]`, assert the `committed PLANS.md on main` line precedes the report, the `uncommitted backlog` row is `ok`, the file is clean, `["doctor", "--commit-backlog", "--json"]` carries `doc.backlogCommit.committed` with `PLANS.md`, and a plain `["doctor", "--json"]` has no `backlogCommit` key.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With the primary on the base branch and a dirty tracked backlog or brief file, `tumwater doctor --commit-backlog` commits each such file on the base branch through `commitOperatorBacklogEdit` (one `tumwater(operator): Commit uncommitted <file>` commit each), leaves every other staged or dirty path alone, prints the committed lines before the report, and the report's `uncommitted backlog` row then reads ok; `--json` carries `backlogCommit` and a plain `doctor --json` omits it.
- A primary off the base branch, or one whose git status cannot be read, commits nothing and reports the skip sentence; a file whose commit fails stays dirty and is listed under `failed` while the other listed files are still attempted.
- The recovery reuses `checkUncommittedBacklog`'s existing discovery and branch precedence and never throws; the check's four detail strings are unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A stale or oversized flake quarantine raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `flaky checks` quarantine rule (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the post-merge-review scoping plan edits src/orchestrator, src/merge and src/review; queue --top, doctor --commit-backlog and the reviews plan edit src/cli and src/events; the in-flight `tumwater quarantine` plan adds src/review/quarantine-render.ts and edits src/review/known-flakes.ts (this plan reads the already-exported `loadQuarantine` and changes nothing there), src/cli, src/cli/help.ts, src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts and docs/cli.md; this plan shares src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, docs/how-it-works.md and test/team-alerts.test.ts with the in-flight stalled-plans alert (and the blocked notify alert) as one more trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and one more amber block, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; it edits no src/backlog, src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/cli or src/review file; touches src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The review gate's flake quarantine (`.tumwater/state/quarantine.json`, `quarantinePath`) lists the tests that failed and then passed on the same tree; `onlyQuarantined` (src/review/known-flakes.ts) treats a failure naming only quarantined tests as a known failure, so the main watch records a pass and the gate stops re-rejecting it. `quarantineWarning` (src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts) fires when the list holds more than `QUARANTINE_WARN_COUNT` (10) tests or any test's `firstSeen` is older than `QUARANTINE_AGE_MS` (3 days) — an old entry is a failure the team has stopped seeing, and an unfiled one never leaves — but the only surfaces that show it are the doctor's `flaky checks` row (`checkFlakyChecks`, run only when the operator asks) and, once it lands, the `tumwater quarantine` read command. A quarantine that quietly grows or ages means the fleet is merging on a suite whose red is being excused, and nothing on the always-on observer surfaces says so. Give the stale-bug rule's treatment to the quarantine rule: an amber alert while `quarantineWarning` fires, off the same function the doctor calls, so the alert and the doctor cannot disagree on when the list is a problem.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface QuarantinedTests { count: number; oldestTest: string; oldestFirstSeen: number; warning: string }` beside `StaleBug`, documented as the doctor's `quarantineWarning` rule computed by src/ui/status-payload.ts's `quarantineAlert`. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `quarantined: QuarantinedTests | null = null` after `skippedMergeFiles` (and after the stalled-plans alert's `stalledPlans` and the notify alert's `notifyFailure` when those have landed, so the existing callers and tests keep compiling). Add one amber block after the `skipped-merges` block: `key: "quarantine"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(quarantined.count, "test")} in the flake quarantine — the gate is excusing their failures` ``, detail `` `${quarantined.warning} · oldest: ${squash(quarantined.oldestTest, 80)} (${humanAgo(quarantined.oldestFirstSeen, now)}) — a quarantined test counts as a known failure until its filed bug leaves BUGS.md \`## Open\`, so fix the test or file the missing bug` ``, `actions: [{ label: "See failures", act: "view", arg: "failures" }]`. Import `squash` from `../text/text.js` and `humanAgo` from `../text/datetime.js`. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a stale flake quarantine.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `quarantineWarning` from `../baseline/main-guardrails.js`, `loadQuarantine` from `../review/known-flakes.js` and `type QuarantinedTests` from `./team-alerts.js`. Add `export function quarantineAlert(root: string, now = Date.now()): QuarantinedTests | null` beside `staleOpenBugs`: `const entries = loadQuarantine(root); const warning = quarantineWarning(entries, now); if (warning === null) return null; const oldest = entries.reduce((a, b) => (b.firstSeen < a.firstSeen ? b : a)); return { count: entries.length, oldestTest: oldest.test, oldestFirstSeen: oldest.firstSeen, warning };`. Pass `quarantineAlert(root, now)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `quarantineAlert` from the same module as `staleOpenBugs`, and pass `quarantineAlert(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("… a stalled merge queue, a merge-queue file the reader skips, a waiting bug held a week, a pause"): add "a stale or oversized flake quarantine" so the documented list matches the alerts.
- The doctor is unchanged: `checkFlakyChecks` keeps its combined row and both it and `quarantineAlert` call `quarantineWarning`, so the trigger and threshold are single-homed.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, modelling the existing stale-bug alert tests:

### `tumwater quarantine [--json]` lists the flake quarantine so an operator can see which tests the gate is excusing and why (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the post-merge-review scoping plan edits src/orchestrator, src/merge and the review section of docs/how-it-works.md; the notify alert (blocked) edits src/doctor/doctor-notify.ts and src/ui; Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner; the queue --top and doctor --commit-backlog plans share `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` (neighbouring `cmdQuarantine`/`cmdQueueTop` functions), `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` and `docs/cli.md` (neighbouring stanzas and rows) with this plan, so whichever lands second rebases there — none of them edits src/review; touches src/review/quarantine-render.ts (new) src/review/known-flakes.ts src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts src/doctor/doctor-project-checks.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md test/quarantine-render.test.ts (new) test/cli-quarantine.test.ts (new) test/doctor-checks.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role
