### A plan parked by a Needs review or Needs replan note raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `stalled plans` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the post-merge-review scoping plan edits src/orchestrator, src/merge and src/review; queue --top, doctor --commit-backlog and quarantines edit src/cli and src/review; the reviews plan adds its own src/cli command; none of them touches src/ui or src/backlog; only the notify alert (blocked, needs review) also edits src/ui/team-alerts.ts and src/ui/status-payload.ts, appending a trailing `notifyFailure` parameter and block, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A planned plan held by a **Needs review …** or **Needs replan …** note is parked until the plan role splits or replans it (`entryHold`, src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts; the claim allocator refuses it), and the state is visible only as the `[blocked: needs review]`/`[blocked: needs replan]` marks in `tumwater backlog` and the doctor's `stalled plans` row (`checkStalledPlans`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. A plan that stays parked means the plan role is not running or keeps deferring, and nothing on the always-on observer surfaces says so. The `refused` and `operator-held` alerts already cover the other two plan holds; give the same always-on treatment to the two role-resolvable holds: an amber alert while a `needs-review` or `needs-replan` plan waits, off the same `entryHold` classification the doctor uses, so the alert and the doctor cannot disagree on which entries are stalled.

**Approach.**
- src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts: add `export interface StalledPlan { index: number; title: string; hold: "needs-review" | "needs-replan" }` beside `RefusedEntry` and `export function stalledPlanEntries(root: string): StalledPlan[]` — the planned plans whose hold is exactly `needs-review` or `needs-replan`, in file order, from the same `backlogHolds(root)` + `plannedPlanEntries(root)` pair `operatorHeldEntries` uses, carrying the 0-based PLANS.md index and the hold. A `held-for-operator` plan is excluded (its own `operatorHeldEntries` feed and `operator-held` alert); a missing file yields `[]`.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: import `type StalledPlan` beside `type RefusedEntry`, widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `stalledPlans: readonly StalledPlan[] = []` after `skippedMergeFiles`, and add one amber block after the `operator-held` block: `key: "stalled-plans"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(stalledPlans.length, "plan is stalled", "plans are stalled")} in review` ``, detail `` `Plan ${entryListDetail(stalledPlans.map((p) => p.title))} — ${stalledPlans[0].hold === "needs-replan" ? "a Needs replan note parks it" : "a Needs review note parks it"}; the plan role splits or replans it, so a plan that keeps sitting here means the plan role is not running or keeps deferring` ``, `actions: [{ label: "Open backlog", act: "backlog", arg: `plans:${stalledPlans[0].index}` }]`. Update the module doc comment's alert list.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `stalledPlanEntries` beside `refusedEntries`/`operatorHeldEntries`, and pass `stalledPlanEntries(root)` as the new last `teamAlerts` argument in the `alerts:` call.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `stalledPlanEntries` from the same module as `refusedEntries`/`operatorHeldEntries` and append it as the new last `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx); both currently pass twelve arguments ending in `skippedMergeFiles(root)`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("… a stale bug, a broken plan dependency clause, … a waiting bug held a week, a pause"): add "a plan stalled by a Needs review or Needs replan note" so the documented list matches the alerts.
- The doctor is unchanged: `checkStalledPlans` keeps reporting all three holds (including held-for-operator) and both it and `stalledPlanEntries` classify through `entryHold`, so the hold decision is single-homed. The alert deliberately shows the two role-resolvable holds; held-for-operator stays the `operator-held` alert's.

**Tests.**
- test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts: `stalledPlanEntries lists the needs-review and needs-replan plans, excluding eligible and held-for-operator ones` — a PLANS.md with a ready plan, a `**Needs review …**` plan, a `**Needs replan …**` plan, and a `**Needs review … (held 3)**` plan yields exactly the middle two with their 0-based indexes and holds; `stalledPlanEntries(tmpdir())` is `[]`.
- test/team-alerts.test.ts, both modelling the operator-held and plan-dependency tests:
  - A unit test `stalled plans raise a standing amber alert naming the first plan and the plan-role fix`: `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [], [], [], null, [], [], [{ index: 2, title: "Split me (planned 2026-10-20)", hold: "needs-review" }])` (the new last argument) gives exactly one alert `key: "stalled-plans"`, tone `amber`, title `1 plan is stalled in review`, a detail including `Split me`, `Needs review`, and `plan role`, and `actions` `[{ label: "Open backlog", act: "backlog", arg: "plans:2" }]`; two rows title `2 plans are stalled in review`; a `needs-replan` row's detail says `Needs replan`; a `[]` argument adds none; with both an operator-held row and a stalled row, `operator-held` precedes `stalled-plans`.
  - An integration test `stalledPlanEntries and the surfaces carry a stalled-plans alert from PLANS.md, and none without one`: `writeBacklogFile(root, "PLANS.md", ...)` with a `**Needs review …**` plan and a `**Needs replan …**` plan, then `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "stalled-plans"` with an `Open backlog` action `plans:<index>` and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title; a `**Needs review … (held 3)**` plan produces the `operator-held` alert and no `stalled-plans` alert; a PLANS.md with only eligible plans produces neither.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A planned plan whose hold is `needs-review` or `needs-replan` produces one amber `stalled-plans` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the first such plan in file order, its note kind, and the plan role's fix, with an `Open backlog` action landing on its row; a plan whose hold is `held-for-operator` produces the `operator-held` alert and none from `stalled-plans`; a PLANS.md with no such hold produces none.
- The alert reads the same `entryHold` classification as the doctor's `stalled plans` row (`stalledPlanEntries` calls `backlogHolds`/`plannedPlanEntries`), so the two cannot disagree on which holds are role-resolvable and which is the operator's.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater queue --top <n>` moves a waiting merge to the front, so an operator can prioritize one change over a long queue (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — Interlock 1/2 reads src/merge/merge-queue.ts's `queuedMergeRoles` and edits src/orchestrator and src/runner, the post-merge-review scoping plan edits src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, merge-verify.ts, merge-drain.ts and src/orchestrator, and the in-flight notify alert edits src/doctor and src/ui; this plan adds a new src/merge module and touches src/cli, src/events and docs/cli.md only, none of them shared. It is the sibling of the landed `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (src/merge/merge-cancel.ts) and mirrors the landed `tumwater prompt --top <n>` (src/inbox/inbox-top.ts); touches src/merge/merge-top.ts (new) src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts src/events/events.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/events/event-format.ts docs/cli.md test/merge-top.test.ts (new) test/cli-queue.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The merge queue's order is its queue files' names (`queueFileName(enqueuedAt, …)`, src/merge/merge-queue.ts `queueFiles`), and the drain takes the oldest due entry first (src/merge/merge-verify.ts, the `notBefore` skip). `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (landed) lets an operator remove a waiting merge, and `tumwater prompt --top <n>` and `tumwater plan|bug --top <n>` move an entry to the front of the other two queues, but the merge queue has no reorder: with ten feature instances and a critical bugfix waiting behind them, the operator can only cancel it or wait. Add `tumwater queue --top <n>` — the sibling of `--cancel` — moving the Nth queued merge to the head by renaming its queue file to a stamp one below the queue's minimum, exactly as `movePromptToTop` does for the inbox.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-top.ts (new): `export type TopQueuedOutcome = { status: "topped"; role: string; sha: string; summary: string } | { status: "already-first"; role: string; sha: string; summary: string } | { status: "out-of-range"; depth: number }` and `export function moveQueuedMergeToTop(root: string, position: number): TopQueuedOutcome`. Resolve `queuedMergeFiles(root)` (the same readable, filename-ordered list `tumwater queue` renders and `--cancel` resolves against). Out-of-range (position < 1 or > length) returns `{ status: "out-of-range", depth }` and changes nothing; position 1 returns `already-first` and changes nothing. Otherwise read the target's basename stamp via `queueFileStamp` (src/files/file-queue.ts), compute `stamp = Math.min(...stamps) - 1` over the readable queue files' stamps (falling back to `Date.now()` when no stamp parses), and `renameSync` the file to `path.join(path.dirname(file), queueFileName(stamp, 0, ".json"))`, stepping the stamp one lower while the destination exists (the `inbox-top.ts` collision loop). The move is a rename, so the entry JSON is never rewritten and every field (`enqueuedAt`, `notBefore`, `retry`, `revisionRound`, `priorReview`) is unchanged; log one `merge_topped` event under `entry.role` with `commit: entry.sha` and `summary: entry.summary` via `logEventBestEffort`, and return `topped`. No lock and no pin write: the module mirrors merge-cancel.ts's "one file per entry, tolerant of a concurrent drop" stance.
- src/events/events.ts: add `| "merge_topped" // an operator moved a waiting merge to the front with tumwater queue --top; carries commit + summary` beside `merge_cancelled`. src/events/event-labels.ts: add `merge_topped: "merge moved to front"` (the `Record<HarnessEvent["type"], string>` makes the compiler demand it). src/events/event-format.ts: add `case "merge_topped": return \`moved the merge of ${shortSha(e.commit)} to the front — ${textOr(e.summary)}\`;` beside the `merge_cancelled` case.
- src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts: in `cmdQueue`, before the read gate and beside the `--cancel` branch, route `if (args.includes("--top")) { await cmdQueueTop(root, args); return; }`. `cmdQueueTop` is `cmdQueueCancel`'s twin: parse `--top <n>` (via `parsePositionFlag`; a repeat is refused) and `--json` (a repeat is refused), tolerate `--help`/`-h`, refuse `--role` and `-f`/`--follow` by name with `--top`-specific wording, reject anything else, then `requireReadyRepo`. Refuse the entry a live merge names, reusing `cmdQueueCancel`'s check (`readMergeQueue` + `queueInFlight` + `orchestratorAlive` + `mergeChanges`), so `--top` cannot rename the file a drain is merging. Call `moveQueuedMergeToTop`; `out-of-range` fails naming the current depth (as `--cancel` does); `already-first` prints and exits 0; `topped` prints `moved queue entry <n> to the front: <role> <shortSha> — <summary>`, or with `--json` prints `{ topped: { role, commit, summary } }`.
- src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md, the `tumwater queue` stanza/row: add `--top <n>` beside `--cancel`, saying it moves the Nth queued merge to the front of the execution order (so the next due entry the drain takes is that one), preserving any `notBefore` deferral, refusing an entry a live merge is merging and `--role`/`-f`, and answering "already first" for position 1.

**Tests.**
- test/merge-top.test.ts (new, modelled on test/merge-cancel.test.ts): after `initProject` and three `enqueueMerge` calls, `moveQueuedMergeToTop(root, 3)` makes the next `queuedMerges(root)` list the third entry first with its `role`/`sha`/`summary`/`enqueuedAt`/`notBefore` unchanged; position 1 answers `already-first` with no rename; positions 0 and 4 answer `out-of-range` with the depth and leave the order unchanged; a deferred entry moved to the front keeps its `notBefore`; the move logs exactly one `merge_topped` event under the entry's role carrying its sha and summary; with a torn head file present, the target still sorts first among the readable files.
- test/cli-queue.test.ts (extend the `--cancel` suite): `queue --top 3` prints the moved line and exits 0; `queue --top 1` prints the already-first line and exits 0; `queue --top 9` fails naming the depth; `--top` with `--role` or `-f` fails with the queue-specific wording; `--json` prints `{ topped: { role, commit, summary } }`; a `queue` read after `--top 3` lists the moved entry first; `--top` refuses an entry a live merge marker names (seed `mergeStatePath`/`queueInFlight` as the `--cancel` test does).
- test/event-format.test.ts: one `merge_topped` case asserting the line `moved the merge of <short sha> to the front — <summary>` and the label `merge moved to front`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater queue --top <n>` moves the Nth readable queued merge to the head of the execution order in one rename; `tumwater queue` lists it at position 1 on the next read, and its entry JSON is unchanged (the file is renamed, not rewritten).
- Position 1 is a no-op reported as already first; an out-of-range position fails naming the current depth; an entry a live merge is merging, `--role` and `-f/--follow` are refused; `--json` returns the documented shape.
- The move logs one `merge_topped` event under the entry's role, and that event renders and carries its label.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A re-queued merge names why it is back on every queue surface and in the event log (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/orchestrator and src/runner, the post-merge-review plan edits src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, merge-verify.ts, merge-drain.ts and src/orchestrator, the notify alert edits src/doctor and src/ui, and the queue --top plan edits src/merge/merge-top.ts (new), src/cli and src/events/events.ts/event-labels.ts; this plan reads the already-present `MergeEntry.retry`/`notBefore` fields without changing src/merge/merge-queue.ts and edits src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts and src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, none of which those plans touch; it shares src/events/event-format.ts and docs/cli.md with the queue --top plan as neighbouring additions, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts src/events/event-format.ts docs/cli.md test/merge-queue.test.ts test/status-data-inbox.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts test/gui-client-pending.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A merge entry the pipeline re-queues after a retriable result keeps its role, summary and revision fields but drops its old `enqueuedAt`, so it reads exactly like a fresh change: the queue file carries `retry` (`merge_blocked`, `review_error`, `merge_conflict` or `main_red`, src/merge/merge-requeue.ts `retryEntry`) and, for a `review_error`, a `notBefore` 60 s deferral the drain honours (src/merge/merge-verify.ts:117), yet `tumwater queue`, the dashboard's Merge queue card and the TUI's Pending pane render none of it — and `formatEvent`'s `merge_queued` line ignores the event's own `retry` field (src/events/event-format.ts). An operator watching a change come back cannot tell a retry from a fresh submission or from a stalled queue. Name the retry (and its deferral) wherever the queue is shown, so the reason for a re-queued change is visible without grepping the event log.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts: add `export function retryNote(entry: Pick<MergeEntry, "retry" | "notBefore">, now: number): string` beside `revisionNote`: `""` when `entry.retry === undefined`; else `` `re-queued after ${entry.retry}` ``, appending `` ` · eligible in ${humanSeconds(secondsUntil(entry.notBefore, now))}` `` while `entry.notBefore !== undefined && entry.notBefore > now` (import `secondsUntil` from `../text/datetime.js` beside `humanAgo`/`humanSeconds`/`secondsSince`). In `renderMergeQueue`, compute `const retry = retryNote(e, now);` and insert `retry ? ` · ${retry}` : ""` into the entry line immediately after the bracketed merge `tag` and before the revision `noteTag`, so a fresh entry's line stays byte-identical.
- src/status/status-data.ts: widen the `mergeQueue.entries` element type with `retry?: string; notBefore?: number`, and in the `merges.map` add `...(typeof e.retry === "string" ? { retry: e.retry } : {})` and `...(typeof e.notBefore === "number" ? { notBefore: e.notBefore } : {})` beside the existing `revisionRound`/`priorObjections` spreads, so a fresh entry's JSON keys stay absent and the dashboards receive both fields. (`status-payload.ts` re-exports the snapshot unchanged, so it needs no edit.)
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts: in `queueEntryLineHtml`, beside the inline revision `note`, build `const retry = typeof e.retry === "string" ? " · re-queued after " + e.retry + (Number.isFinite(e.notBefore) && e.notBefore > now ? " · eligible in " + humanSeconds(Math.max(0, Math.round((e.notBefore - now) / 1000))) : "") : ""` and splice it into the line after the merge-label clause and before the revision `note` (`humanSeconds`, `plural`, `roleLabel`, `shortSha` are already in the browser scope).
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts: in `mergeDetail`, add `const retry = retryNote(e, session.now());` and push it as its own blocked line (`if (retry) lines.push("", retry);`) after the revision note, so the selected-row detail carries it; the list body already gains it through `renderMergeQueue`.
- src/events/event-format.ts, the `merge_queued` case: append a suffix only when the event carries a retry — `const base = `waiting to merge ${shortSha(e.commit)} — ${textOr(e.summary)}`; return `${base}${typeof e.retry === "string" && e.retry ? ` (re-queued after ${textOr(e.retry)})` : ""}`;` — so a fresh event's line is byte-identical to today's.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater queue` command clause: after the revision-note sentence, add that a re-queued entry names why it is back (`re-queued after <result>`) and, while a `review_error` retry's 60 s deferral still holds, when it may start (`eligible in <duration>`).

**Tests.**
- test/merge-queue.test.ts: a `retryNote` unit block (`retryNote({}, now) === ""`; `retryNote({ retry: "merge_blocked" }, now) === "re-queued after merge_blocked"`; `retryNote({ retry: "review_error", notBefore: now + 42_000 }, now) === "re-queued after review_error · eligible in 42s"`; the same entry with `notBefore: now - 1` renders no eligibility clause); a `renderMergeQueue` case with a re-queued entry asserting the retry text lands between the age and the summary, and the existing fresh-entry lines unchanged.
- test/status-data-inbox.test.ts: extend the queue snapshot test with a second entry carrying `retry: "review_error"` and a future `notBefore`, asserting `snap.mergeQueue.entries` carries both fields; the existing fresh-entry `deepEqual` proves the keys stay absent otherwise.
- test/gui-client-pending.test.ts: a case modelled on "pendingQueueHtml names a re-submitted change's revision round…" asserting a row with `retry` and a future `notBefore` renders `re-queued after review_error · eligible in 42s`, and a row without them renders neither (no `undefined`/`NaN`).
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: seed a queued entry with `retry` and assert the selected-row `queueDetail` names `re-queued after <result>` (the list body through `renderMergeQueue` is covered by test/merge-queue.test.ts).
- test/event-format.test.ts: keep the existing fresh `merge_queued` assertion and add a retry-bearing event (`retry: "merge_blocked"`) asserting the ` (re-queued after merge_blocked)` suffix.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater queue`, the dashboard's Merge queue card, and the TUI's Pending list and selected-row detail render `re-queued after <result>` for an entry whose `retry` field is set, and append ` · eligible in <duration>` while its `notBefore` is in the future; a fresh entry's line is byte-identical to today's (the existing fresh-line assertions stay green).
- `status --json`'s `mergeQueue.entries` carries `retry` and `notBefore` only when present; a fresh entry's keys stay absent.
- `tumwater logs` renders a retry-bearing `merge_queued` line with the ` (re-queued after <result>)` suffix and a fresh one unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A held-for-operator plan can be released from the TUI and the dashboard drawer, not only from `tumwater plan --release` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except one shared test file — the in-flight "A re-queued merge names why it is back" plan also adds a case to test/tui-keys.test.ts (its queueDetail retry case), so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring test; it shares no source file with any waiting plan: Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge, src/orchestrator and src/runner, the post-merge-review plan edits src/merge and src/orchestrator, the notify alert edits src/doctor and src/ui/team-alerts.ts, status-payload.ts, status-render.ts and tui.tsx, and queue --top edits src/merge/merge-top.ts, src/cli and src/events; touches src/gui/gui-backlog-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts test/gui.test.ts test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Backlog hold convergence part 2/3 gave a held-for-operator plan an always-on amber alert naming `tumwater plan --release`, and made `--release` actually lift the note (the release core `liftRefusal`, src/backlog/backlog-release.ts, has the held-for-operator branch). The two observer surfaces still refuse to: the TUI's Ctrl+R gate in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts admits only `hold === "refused"` and `hold === "waiting-for-failure"` and flashes "carries no Refused or Waiting for the next failure note" for a held-for-operator plan, and `GET /api/backlog` (src/gui/gui-backlog-endpoints.ts) serves only `refused`/`waiting`, so the drawer's Release button (src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, `data-act='entry-release'`) renders for a refused or waiting entry only. An operator who sees the alert and opens the entry from its "Open backlog" action finds no way to act. This plan adds the missing trigger on each surface; the release itself is unchanged.

**Approach.**
- src/gui/gui-backlog-endpoints.ts: import `operatorHeldEntries` from `../backlog/backlog-eligibility.js`. In `handleBacklog`'s 200 payload add `...(file === "plans" && operatorHeldEntries(root).some((e) => e.index === index) ? { heldForOperator: true } : {})` after the `refused`/`waiting` fields. The key is present only on a held-for-operator plan, so every other entry's payload stays byte-identical to today's and the four `deepEqual` payload assertions in test/gui.test.ts need no change. Gating on `file === "plans"` keeps the button on exactly the `operatorHeldEntries` selection the `operator-held` alert and the doctor use (plans only). Extend the handler's doc comment with the new key.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts: the drawer's Release condition becomes `d.refused || d.waiting || d.heldForOperator`. Do not touch the Move-to-top, Edit or Cancel buttons.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts: in the Ctrl+R arm, widen the gate `selected.picked.hold !== "refused" && selected.picked.hold !== "waiting-for-failure"` to also admit `"held-for-operator"`. Update that arm's flash wording to name the held-for-operator note beside Refused and Waiting, and update its `// Ctrl+R twice releases …` comment. `releaseArmed`/`tryReleaseEntry` need no change: they already accept the note once the gate admits it, and `git`/commit/wake behavior is the same path a refused release takes.

**Tests.**
- test/gui.test.ts: a new test "gui /api/backlog marks a held-for-operator plan for the drawer's Release button": seed PLANS.md (through the existing `writeBacklogFile` helper) with a plain planned entry and one carrying `**Needs review 2026-10-16 by feature: too large for one run (held 3)**` plus `**Previously held 2**`; assert the held plan's payload has `heldForOperator: true` with its `body`, and the plain entry's payload has no `heldForOperator` key (read the raw JSON object and check `("heldForOperator" in body) === false`). Keep this in its own repo, not the existing two-entry fixture, whose `index 2` out-of-range assertions depend on the section holding exactly two plans.
- test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts: extend "the entry drawer offers Release this entry only on a refused or waiting entry" (rename it to name the held-for-operator case) with a held-for-operator response, e.g. `"/api/backlog?file=plans&index=3": { title: "Held", body: "**Needs review 2026-10-16 by feature: x (held 3)**", refused: false, waiting: false, heldForOperator: true }`, and assert `data-act='entry-release' data-arg='plans:3'` appears; keep the existing note-lessness assertion (`entry-release` absent when none of the three is set).
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: a new test beside the Ctrl+R cases, seeding a held-for-operator plan through the existing `backlogReleaseRig`, e.g. `backlogReleaseRig("## Planned\n\n### Held plan (planned 2026-10-01)\n\n**Needs review 2026-10-16 by feature: too large for one run (held 3)**\n\n**Previously held 2**\n")`; select it (`down(1)`), press Ctrl+R twice, and assert PLANS.md loses both the Needs-review and `**Previously held 2**` lines, the flash names the release, and the wake marker lists `["feature"]`. Add the boundary: the same rig with `(held 2)` still arms nothing and flashes the no-note message (the below-threshold entry stays `needs-review`, which the plan role owns).

**Acceptance criteria.**

A plan whose hold is `needs-review`/`needs-replan` below the threshold, or any entry with no hold, shows no Release button.
- Ctrl+R twice on a held-for-operator plan in the TUI releases it; a below-threshold Needs-review plan still flashes the no-note message and writes nothing.
- `GET /api/backlog` adds `heldForOperator: true` only for a held-for-operator plan; every other entry's payload carries no such key.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A run's trail names the model it started on in its summary header and its `--json` payload (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the four in-flight plans touch src/doctor, src/ui, src/merge, src/orchestrator, src/runner, src/cli and src/events, none of them src/run; it shares docs/cli.md with the queue --top and re-queued-merge plans as a neighbouring row (their "Check state" queue clauses vs this "Watch run history" clause), so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/run/run-detail-data.ts src/run/run-detail-render.ts docs/cli.md test/run-detail-data.test.ts test/run-detail.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history`'s run rows name the model each run started on — `RunRow.model`, the `runRowCells` model column between result and duration — and `--summary --by model`, the `history --model` listing filter and `history <role> --last --model` all key on it, but the one-run trail drops it: `RunDetail` (src/run/run-detail-data.ts) carries no model field, and `renderRunDetail`'s summary header (src/run/run-detail-render.ts) prints result, duration, usage, the commit sha, `merged as` and `reverted`, never the selector. So an operator who opens `history feature 12` — or the TUI History trail or the dashboard's History drill-down, all three of which render `renderRunDetail` — must read into the first event line to learn which model (a per-role override, a fallback, a reroute) the run actually used, and `history <role> <n> --json` gives a script no top-level field for it. Carry the `run_start`'s model onto `RunDetail` and into the header, so the summary line names what ran.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-detail-data.ts: add `model: string | null` to `RunDetail` beside `result`, documented as the agent-qualified selector the run's `run_start` carried (a per-role override, a fallback or the primary — the same string `RunRow.model` and the report's `runsByModel` use), or null when the run's start is outside the scanned window or carried none. In `detailFrom`, replace the trailing `startTs: number | null` parameter with `start: HarnessEvent | null` and compute `startTs: start === null ? null : start.ts` and `model: typeof start?.model === "string" && start.model.length > 0 ? start.model : null`; both call sites already have the value in hand — the paired read passes `start`, the rotation-unpaired read (`if (e.type === "run_end" …) return detailFrom(role, runNumber, all, events, [e], e, null)`) passes `null`. `cmdRunDetail`'s `--json` rides the existing `sayJson({ ...detail, ...footer })` spread (src/run/run-detail.ts), so the payload gains `model` with no change there.
- src/run/run-detail-render.ts, `renderRunDetail`: after `if (d.usage !== "") summary.push(d.usage);`, add `if (d.model !== null) summary.push(d.model);`. The model then reads between the usage and the `· commit <sha>` clause: `feature run #3 — merged · 1m · 12.3k tok · $0.41 · claude/claude-sonnet-5-5 · commit abc1234`. Extend the function's doc comment to name the model in the summary list and the absent-start rule.
- docs/cli.md, the "Watch run history" row's trail-header sentence (the clauses naming result, duration and usage): add that the header names the model the run started on when its `run_start` carried one (the selector `history --model` matches and the listing's model column shows), and that `--json` carries it as `model`, null when the start sits outside the scanned window or named none. No new flag, command or key.

**Tests.**
- test/run-detail-data.test.ts: a test "readRunDetail carries the run's model from its run_start, and null without one" — seed a paired run whose `start` sets `model: "claude/claude-sonnet-5-5"` and assert `d.model` equals it; the same fixture with no model asserts `d.model === null`; the existing rotation-unpaired fixture (only the `end` survives) asserts `d.model === null`. Existing cases keep passing: they `deepEqual` selected fields, not the whole payload.
- test/run-detail.test.ts: extend "renderRunDetail prints the summary header, the commit sha, and formatEvent lines" (or add a sibling) with `d.model` set, asserting `lines[0]` matches `/merged · 60s · .* · claude\/claude-sonnet-5-5 · commit abc1234/` and that `{ ...d, model: null }` renders no ` · claude` clause; in "cmdRunDetail --last --model picks the newest run on the listed models" add `assert.equal(JSON.parse(await out(["bugfix", "7"], {}, true)).model, "a")`, proving the `--json` field.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater history <role> <n>`, the TUI History trail and the dashboard History drill-down name the run's model in the summary header (after the usage, before the `· commit` clause) whenever the run's `run_start` carried one; a run with no model, or whose start is outside the scanned window, renders byte-identically to today.
- `tumwater history <role> <n> --json` carries `model` (the selector string, or null); no existing key changes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A merge-queue file the reader skips raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `merge-queue files` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior except three in-flight alert plans that also append one `teamAlerts` parameter and one stale block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edit src/ui/status-payload.ts — the notify plan appends `notifyFailure`, the waiting-bug plan appends `staleWaitingBugs`, the plan-dependency plan appends `planDependency` — so whichever lands after the others rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; the waiting-bug plan also edits test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, so the two test additions land as neighbouring cases; Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts and src/runner/leftover.ts (this plan reads the already-exported `unreadableMergeQueueFiles` from src/merge/merge-queue.ts and changes nothing there); `start --gui` edits src/cli, src/gui and src/process, and Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `readMergeQueue` (src/merge/merge-queue.ts) reads every durable queue file and skips any that is torn, foreign, or vanished mid-listing, counting them in `MergeQueueView.unreadable`; the drain repairs only an unreadable *head* (`staleHeadFile`), so a skipped file that sorts after a healthy entry sits in `.tumwater/merge-queue/` forever and its merge is stranded. `tumwater queue` prints only a count, and the doctor's `merge-queue files` row (`checkMergeQueueFiles`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts) warns only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. The just-landed `stale-merges` alert reads only *readable* entries, so it can never see a skipped file. Give the doctor's rule the stale-bug treatment: an always-on amber alert over the same `unreadableMergeQueueFiles` set, so a stranded queue file stays visible on all three observer surfaces until someone removes it.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: add `export function skippedMergeQueueFiles(root: string): string[]` beside `checkMergeQueueFiles`, returning `unreadableMergeQueueFiles(root).map((f) => path.relative(root, f))` — the one checkout-relative path list the doctor row and the alert share. Rewrite `checkMergeQueueFiles` to call it (`const files = skippedMergeQueueFiles(root);` then `andMore(rest, (f) => f, "file(s)")`), so the check's message stays byte-identical; `unreadableMergeQueueFiles` in src/merge/merge-queue.ts is unchanged. Its doc comment names it as the shared traversal.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `skippedMergeFiles: readonly string[] = []`, appended after `staleMerges` and after every parameter a landed in-flight plan has added before it (the notify plan's `notifyFailure`, the waiting-bug plan's `staleWaitingBugs`, the plan-dependency plan's `planDependency`), so the existing callers and tests compile. Add one amber block right after the `stale-merges` block: `key: "skipped-merges"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(skippedMergeFiles.length, "merge-queue file is", "merge-queue files are")} unreadable` ``, detail `` `the queue reader skips ${first} — a torn or foreign file never drains, so its merge is stranded; remove it (a crashed enqueue's merge ref still recovers on the next run)` `` plus, when others are skipped, `` ` · ${joinWithMore(rest, 3)}` ``, `actions: []`. `plural` is already imported and `joinWithMore` is imported from `../text/text.js`. Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a merge-queue file the reader skips.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `skippedMergeQueueFiles` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog.js` (the same import line as `staleQueuedMergeRows`); add `export function skippedMergeFiles(root: string): string[] { return skippedMergeQueueFiles(root); }` beside `staleMerges`, documented as the always-on feed for the skipped-merges alert, sharing the doctor's one list; pass `skippedMergeFiles(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call (after `staleMerges(root, now)`).
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `skippedMergeFiles` from the same `status-payload.js` module as `staleOpenBugs`/`stalePrompts`/`staleMerges`, and pass `skippedMergeFiles(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alerts` call and the TUI attention call, each currently ending `…, staleOpenBugs(root), stalePrompts(root), staleMerges(root))`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the Team alerts list (“… a stranded inbox prompt, a stalled merge queue, a pause”): add “a merge-queue file the reader skips” after “a stalled merge queue” so the documented list matches the alerts.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, modelling the existing stale-merge tests:
- A unit test `a skipped merge-queue file raises a standing amber alert right after the stale-merge alert`: pass `["000-torn.json"]` as the `skippedMergeFiles` argument (after whatever alert arguments have landed) and assert exactly one alert with `key: "skipped-merges"`, tone `amber`, title `1 merge-queue file is unreadable`, a detail matching `/000-torn\.json/` and `/crashed enqueue's merge ref/`, and `actions` `[]`; two paths title `/merge-queue files are unreadable/` and the second is folded into the detail through `joinWithMore`; an empty argument adds none; with both a stale merge and a skipped file, `stale-merges` precedes `skipped-merges`.
- An integration test `skippedMergeFiles and the surfaces carry a skipped-merge alert from the queue, and none without one`: a `makeRepo()` root with `fs.mkdirSync(mergeQueueDir(root), { recursive: true })` and `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(mergeQueueDir(root), "000-torn.json"), '{"role":')` plus `'{"nope":true}'` in `999-foreign.json`; assert `skippedMergeFiles(root)` equals those two checkout-relative paths, `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "skipped-merges"` with the title and a detail naming `000-torn.json`, and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title. A root holding only a readable `enqueueMerge` entry yields none, and an absent queue yields none.
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: add a `skippedMergeQueueFiles` test asserting the two checkout-relative paths for a queue with a torn and a foreign file and `[]` for an all-readable queue; the existing `checkMergeQueueFiles` tests pass unchanged (the refactor preserves its wording).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A `.tumwater/merge-queue/` file the reader skips (torn, foreign, or vanished mid-listing) produces one amber `skipped-merges` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts via `statusPayload`, the TUI attention lines via `teamAlerts`, and `tumwater status` via `renderStatus`), naming the count and the first skipped file's checkout-relative path; a queue whose files all read produces none.
- The alert and the doctor's `merge-queue files` row share `skippedMergeQueueFiles`, the one relative-path list over `unreadableMergeQueueFiles`, so the selection and the named paths cannot drift.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A waiting bug held a week raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `waiting bugs` rule (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except two in-flight alert plans that also append one `teamAlerts` parameter and one stale block — the notify alert appends `notifyFailure`, the stalled merge-queue alert appends `staleMerges`, so whichever lands after the others rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge and src/runner, `start --gui` edits src/cli, src/gui and src/process, Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles, and Split run-agent edits src/agent; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-bugs.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `waiting bugs` check (`checkWaitingBugs`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog-bugs.ts) warns when an open BUGS.md bug held by a `**Waiting for the next failure …**` note has outlived `STALE_WAIT_DAYS` (7) without a recurrence, but only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. Every other stale-backlog fact has an always-on twin on the three observer surfaces, and src/ui/status-payload.ts's `staleOpenBugs` doc comment already promises "the refused and waiting alerts name those" — but no waiting alert exists: `staleOpenBugs` skips a waiting bug, so a fleet whose flake never comes back shows no banner while the hold parks indefinitely. Give the doctor's rule the stale-bug/stale-prompt treatment: an always-on amber alert at the same threshold over the same held-bug selection and anchor, so a lapsed hold stays visible until it is released.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog-bugs.ts: factor the `held` build out of `checkWaitingBugs` into a module-private `heldWaitingBugs(root)` returning, in file order, `{ index, position, title, note, name, since, date }` (the same `openBugEntries` walk, `waitingNote`/`refusalNote` skip, `quotedTestName`, `waitingNoteDate` and `dayAfterMs` logic); `checkWaitingBugs` then calls it and is otherwise unchanged. Add `export function staleWaitingBugRows(root: string, now = Date.now()): Array<{ index: number; position: number; title: string; days: number }>`: over `heldWaitingBugs(root)`, `anchor = b.date ?? filingDate(b.title)`, skip a null anchor, `days = ageInDays(anchor, now)`, keep `days >= STALE_WAIT_DAYS`, return `{ index: b.index, position: b.position, title: stripEntryStamp(b.title), days }`, sorted most-days-first then file order (the `staleOpenBugs` order). Import `stripEntryStamp` from `../backlog/backlog-structure.js` (`STALE_WAIT_DAYS`, `ageInDays`, `filingDate`, `waitingNote` and `refusalNote` are already imported). Its doc comment says it shares the doctor's `STALE_WAIT_DAYS` threshold and the `heldWaitingBugs` selection/anchor, and that it deliberately omits `checkWaitingBugs`'s recurrence scan because that scan reads events back to the oldest hold and is too costly on the status poll path; the doctor still reports a recurrence first.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface StaleWaitingBug { index: number; position: number; title: string; days: number }` beside `StaleBug`, documented as the doctor's `STALE_WAIT_DAYS` rule computed by src/ui/status-payload.ts's `staleWaitingBugs`. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `staleWaitingBugs: readonly StaleWaitingBug[] = []`, appended after `stalePrompts` and after every parameter a landed in-flight plan has added before it (the notify plan's `notifyFailure`, the stalled merge-queue plan's `staleMerges`), so existing callers and tests compile. Add one amber block after the `stale-bugs` block: `key: "waiting-bugs"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(staleWaitingBugs.length, "waiting bug held", "waiting bugs held")} 7+ days` ``, detail `` `#${first.position} "${first.title}" has waited ${first.days}d for its next failure` `` plus, when others await, ` · ${entryListDetail(rest.map((r) => `#${r.position} "${r.title}"`))}`, plus `` ` · its flake has not come back — release it with \`tumwater bug --release ${first.position}\`, or keep the hold if the failure is still expected` ``, `actions: [{ label: "Open backlog", act: "backlog", arg: `bugs:${first.index}` }]` (the `stale-bugs` action shape). `plural` and `entryListDetail` are already local/imported, so this adds no import. Update the module doc comment's alert list.

A hold dated `${daysAgo(2, now)}` (under `STALE_WAIT_DAYS`) yields no row/alert; a bug carrying both a waiting note and a `**Refused …**` note yields none; a bug with no waiting note yields none.

### A broken plan-dependency clause raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `plan dependencies` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior except the in-flight alert plans that also append one `teamAlerts` parameter and one stale block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edit src/ui/status-payload.ts — the notify plan appends `notifyFailure`, the stalled merge-queue plan appends `staleMerges`, the waiting-bug plan appends `staleWaitingBugs` — so whichever lands after the others rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge and src/runner, `start --gui` edits src/cli, src/gui and src/process, Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles, and Split run-agent edits src/agent; none touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts or src/backlog/backlog-parts.ts; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `plan dependencies` check (`checkPlanDependencies`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts) warns when a planned heading's `requires … landed` clause is broken: a cycle that keeps a whole series blocked forever, a dangling ref naming a part no heading carries (which voids the hold and makes the dependent claimable now), a clause that parses to no part (which holds nothing), or a dependency verb like "blocked by part 1/2" that the claim allocator (`assignNext`, src/scheduling/claims.ts) ignores (BUGS.md 2026-10-14: such a part was handed out six times while its prerequisite was in flight). Every one of these is invisible until the operator runs `tumwater doctor`: the backlog listings show a normal `[blocked: …]` or no hold at all, and the allocator acts on the misread clause. This project has hit the class more than once — the 2026-10-23 plan-role rewrite of Interlock relief 1/2 had to drop a `requires reviewer-as-role part 1/4 landed` clause because no heading carried that series name, so the hold was void. Give the doctor's rule the stale-bug treatment: an always-on amber alert over the same `planDependencyProblems` set, so a broken clause stays visible on all three observer surfaces until someone fixes the heading.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.ts: factor the message construction out of `checkPlanDependencies` into `export function planDependencyProblem(root: string): { kind: "cycle" | "dangling" | "unparsed" | "misworded"; message: string } | null`. It computes `planDependencyProblems(plannedPlanEntries(root), donePlans(root))` and returns the first non-empty kind in the existing severity order (cycle, dangling, unparsed, misworded) with the byte-identical message the function builds today, including its `andMore`/`others` tails, or `null` when all four are empty. `checkPlanDependencies` becomes `const p = planDependencyProblem(root); return p ? warnOutcome(p.message) : okOutcome("every planned plan's requires clause names a known part, with no cycle or misworded dependency");`, so its existing tests pass unchanged. Give the new function a doc comment naming it as the one problem-set/severity/wording source the check and the alert share.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface PlanDependencyProblem { kind: "cycle" | "dangling" | "unparsed" | "misworded"; message: string }` beside `StaleBug`, documented as the doctor's `plan dependencies` rule computed by src/ui/status-payload.ts's `planDependencyAlert`. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `planDependency: PlanDependencyProblem | null = null`, appended after `stalePrompts` and after every parameter a landed in-flight plan has added before it (the notify plan's `notifyFailure`, the stalled merge-queue plan's `staleMerges`, the waiting-bug plan's `staleWaitingBugs`), so the existing callers and tests compile. Add one amber block right after the `operator-held` block: `key: "plan-dependencies"`, `tone: "amber"`, `title` map keyed on `kind` — `cycle` → `"Plan dependency cycle blocks a whole series"`, `dangling` → `"A plan requires a part no heading carries"`, `unparsed` → `"A plan's requires clause names no readable part"`, `misworded` → `"A plan's dependency wording holds nothing"` — `detail: planDependency.message`, `actions: []` (the fix is editing PLANS.md, and the message names the heading and ref). Update the module doc comment's alert list.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `planDependencyProblem` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog-plans.js` and `type PlanDependencyProblem` from `./team-alerts.js`; add `export function planDependencyAlert(root: string): PlanDependencyProblem | null { return planDependencyProblem(root); }` beside `stalePrompts` (the same reader-owns-the-rule seam the stale alerts use), and pass `planDependencyAlert(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `planDependencyAlert` from the same `status-payload.js` module as `staleOpenBugs`/`stalePrompts`, and pass `planDependencyAlert(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alerts` call and the TUI attention call, each currently ending `…, staleOpenBugs(root), stalePrompts(root))`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the Team alerts list (“… refused entries, a stale bug, a stranded inbox prompt, a pause”): add “a broken plan dependency clause” after “a stale bug” so the documented list matches the alerts.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, modelling the existing stale-bug tests:
- A unit test `a broken plan-dependency clause raises a standing amber alert`: pass `{ kind: "misworded", message: "PLANS.md plan \"S, part 2/2: b\" names S 1/2 as a prerequisite without a `requires … landed` clause — the claim allocator ignores that wording and hands the part out now; write it as `requires part 1/2 landed`" }` as the `planDependency` argument (after whatever alert arguments have landed) and assert exactly one alert with `key: "plan-dependencies"`, tone `amber`, title `"A plan's dependency wording holds nothing"`, `detail` equal to the message, and `actions` `[]`; the other three kinds map to their titles; a `null` argument adds no alert; with both a stale bug and a dependency problem, `plan-dependencies` precedes `stale-bugs`.
- An integration test `planDependencyAlert and the surfaces carry a plan-dependency alert from PLANS.md, and none without one`: a `makeRepo()` root with `writeBacklogFile(root, "PLANS.md", [{ heading: "## Planned", body: ... two planned entries whose second is headed `### S, part 2/2: b (blocked by part 1/2 above)` ... }, { heading: "## Done" }])`; assert `planDependencyAlert(root)` returns `{ kind: "misworded" }`, `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "plan-dependencies"` with the title and a detail naming `S 1/2`, and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title. A root whose planned series pairs a `(requires part 1/2 landed)` child with its `S, part 1/2` parent in `## Done` yields none.
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: a `planDependencyProblem` test asserting the returned `kind` for a misworded clause and `null` for the clean pair; the existing `checkPlanDependencies` tests pass unchanged (the refactor preserves its wording).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A PLANS.md whose planned entries hold a cycle, a dangling `requires` ref, an unparsed clause, or a misworded dependency produces one amber `plan-dependencies` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts via `statusPayload`, the TUI attention lines via `teamAlerts`, and `tumwater status` via `renderStatus`), titled by kind and carrying the doctor's exact message; a clean PLANS.md produces none.
- The alert and the doctor's `plan dependencies` row share `planDependencyProblem`, so the problem set, the severity order, and the wording cannot drift.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater start --gui` forwards `--all-interfaces` and `--token <secret>` to the dashboard child, so the one-command form can serve the LAN behind the auth gate (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan and of Interlock 1/2 — Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles, the stranded-inbox and notify alerts edit src/doctor, src/ui and docs/how-it-works.md, and Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge, src/runner and src/orchestrator; none touches src/cli/cli-start.ts, src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, src/cli/cli-args.ts, src/gui/gui-command.ts, src/cli/help.ts or docs/cli.md; completes the deferral PLANS-DONE.md "`tumwater start --gui --port <n>` picks the dashboard port" recorded as "widening those is out of scope and would need its own plan"; touches src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/cli-start.ts src/cli/cli-args.ts src/gui/gui-command.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-start.test.ts test/cli-start-guards.test.ts test/cli-gui.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater start --gui --port <n>` threads the dashboard port to the `tumwater gui` child through `guiChildPlan` → `guiArgs` → `spawnGuiChild` (src/cli/cli-start.ts, src/process/supervisor.ts), but `--all-interfaces` and `--token <secret>` still exist only on `tumwater gui`. So an operator who wants the dashboard reachable on the LAN, behind the token gate, cannot use the one-command form: `tumwater start --gui --all-interfaces --token s3cret` is refused by `START_FLAG_SPECS`, and there is no way to boot the team and the exposed dashboard together. This plan completes the deferral by threading the two flags onto the dashboard child exactly as `--port` is threaded, with the token validated before boot so a bad token fails loudly instead of leaving the team running behind a dashboard that exited.

**Approach.**
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: factor the two dashboard-only specs out of `GUI_FLAG_SPECS` into module consts `ALL_INTERFACES_FLAG` and `TOKEN_FLAG` (`{ names: ["--all-interfaces"] }` and `{ names: ["--token"], value: true, valueName: "<secret>", missingValue: TOKEN_VALUE_ERROR }`), declared before `START_FLAG_SPECS` so both `START_FLAG_SPECS` and `GUI_FLAG_SPECS` reference one definition; add both consts to `START_FLAG_SPECS`. Move the `TOKEN_VALUE_ERROR` declaration above `START_FLAG_SPECS` (it is currently between the two spec arrays) so the array literal can reference it at module load.
- src/cli/cli-args.ts: add `export function tokenValueProblem(args: string[], example: string): string | null`, the shared home for cmdGui's two token checks: `null` when `flagValue(args, "--token")` is null; `TOKEN_VALUE_ERROR` when it is the empty string; and the flag-looking message (import `TOKEN_VALUE_ERROR` from cli-flag-specs.js, `flagValue` is local) when it starts with `--`, wording `--token got the flag-looking value "<v>" instead of a secret — write the secret as its own argument (e.g. \`${example} --token s3cret --all-interfaces\`)`. The example names the command the operator typed, so the fix is copyable from either caller.
- src/gui/gui-command.ts: replace cmdGui's inline empty/flag-looking checks with `const problem = tokenValueProblem(args, "tumwater gui"); if (problem) fail(problem);` so the wording cannot drift from `start`'s. Behavior is unchanged.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts, `cmdStart`: generalize the existing `--port`-requires-`--gui` refusal to all three dashboard-only flags — refuse `--all-interfaces` and `--token` without `--gui` with the same shape (`--all-interfaces is only valid with --gui (e.g. \`tumwater start --gui --all-interfaces\`); the standalone dashboard is \`tumwater gui --all-interfaces\``), keeping the `--port` wording byte-identical (its guard test pins the phrase). Call `tokenValueProblem(args, "tumwater start --gui")` and `fail` its message when non-null, after the `--gui` guard and before `runStartupCheck`, so a bad token never boots.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts, `guiChildPlan`: collect the dashboard flags onto `guiArgs` in a fixed order — `--port <p>` when `flagValue(runArgs, "--port")` is present, then `--all-interfaces` when present, then `--token <secret>` when present — so the child receives the same flags it would get from a direct `tumwater gui` invocation. Strip `--all-interfaces` by name and `--token` plus its value token (the `portIdx` skip-set pattern already removes `--port` and its value) from `orchestratorArgs`, so the supervised generation and the self-redeploy hand-off never see a value-less or duplicated dashboard flag. Update the `guiArgs` doc comment to name all three.
- src/cli/help.ts: in the `--gui` clause of the `start` stanza, replace "(--port <n> picks another port, like `tumwater gui --port N`; its --all-interfaces and --token stay on that command)" with a clause saying `--port <n>`, `--all-interfaces` and `--token <secret>` all forward to the dashboard child, like the `tumwater gui` flags; in the `gui` stanza, say `tumwater start --gui` forwards `--port N`, `--all-interfaces` and `--token <secret>` the same way.
- docs/cli.md: under `tumwater start --gui`, add a continuation line naming `--all-interfaces`/`--token <secret>` as forwarded (the `tumwater gui` twins), and adjust the paragraph after the block that currently reads "`gui --all-interfaces` exposes the dashboard … pair it with `--token <secret>`" to say `tumwater start --gui` forwards both so the one-command start can serve the LAN behind the gate. Both flags already appear in docs/cli.md, so the cli-doc flag-coverage test is satisfied.

**Tests.**
- test/cli-start.test.ts, extend the `guiChildPlan` cases: `guiChildPlan(["--gui", "--all-interfaces", "--token", "s3cret"])` returns `guiArgs: ["--all-interfaces", "--token", "s3cret"]` and `orchestratorArgs: []`; `guiChildPlan(["--branch", "x", "--gui", "--port", "8123", "--all-interfaces", "--token", "s3cret", "--for", "2h"])` returns `guiArgs: ["--port", "8123", "--all-interfaces", "--token", "s3cret"]` and `orchestratorArgs: ["--branch", "x", "--for", "2h"]` (neither `--all-interfaces` nor the token value survives).
- test/cli-start-guards.test.ts: `run --all-interfaces` and `run --token s3cret`, each without `--gui`, exit 1 before any boot with the flag's "only valid with --gui" message; `run --gui --token --all-interfaces` exits 1 with the flag-looking-value message and writes no events (the `readEvents(repo).length === 0` assertion the sibling guards use); `run --gui --token` (valueless) exits 1 with the spec's `--token requires a non-empty secret` before boot.
- test/cli-gui.test.ts: the existing `gui --token` validation test must pass unchanged (it pins the shared helper's empty and flag-looking wording); do not change it except to keep it green.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater start --gui --all-interfaces --token s3cret` (and the `run` alias) boots the team and spawns the `tumwater gui` child with `--all-interfaces --token s3cret`, pinned by `guiChildPlan`; the supervised orchestrator generation and a self-redeploy receive neither flag.
- `--all-interfaces` or `--token` without `--gui` fails before boot with a message naming the flag and the `tumwater gui` form; a valueless or flag-looking `--token` fails before boot and no team boots.
- `tumwater gui`'s own `--all-interfaces`/`--token` behavior and its error wording are unchanged (its existing test passes).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A stalled merge queue raises a standing amber alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `stale merge-queue entries` row (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except the in-flight notify alert — it also appends a trailing `teamAlerts` parameter and block in src/ui/team-alerts.ts and edits src/ui/status-payload.ts, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring parameter and block; this plan reads the queue through the already-exported `queuedMerges`/`readMergeMarker`/`mergeChanges`, so Interlock 1/2's `queuedMergeRoles` stage change in src/merge does not collide; Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles and Split run-agent edits src/agent; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `stale merge-queue entries` check (`checkStaleQueuedMerges`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts) warns when a queued change waits past `MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS` (6 h) without starting — every other queued-change health fact is a hook into its own role or stage (a verify reads in the team row, a team hold gets a banner, the `STUCK`/`STALL_RE` alert catches a running stage frozen), but a change that quietly never starts reads healthy: the header's `merge queue: N` badge counts it and `tumwater queue` ages it, yet nothing calls it out on its own. The whole fleet drains through that queue, so a stalled drain is operational signal every bit as much as a stale bug or a stranded prompt. Give the doctor's rule the stale-bug/stale-prompt treatment: an always-on amber alert at the same threshold and over the same `queuedMerges`/`readMergeMarker`/`mergeChanges` filter, so a stuck queue stays visible on all three observer surfaces until it drains.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: widen `const MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS = 6 * HOUR_MS;` to `export const MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS = 6 * HOUR_MS;` and extend its doc comment to say the always-on `stale-merges` alert (src/ui/status-payload.ts) reuses this window (the `STALE_PROMPT_MS`/`STALE_BUG_DAYS` precedent). Factor the filter out of `checkStaleQueuedMerges` into an exported reader `staleQueuedMergeRows(root, now): Array<{ role: string; summary: string; waitedMs: number }>`: read `queuedMerges(root)`, build the in-flight role set from `readMergeMarker(root)`/`mergeChanges(marker)` (absent marker → empty set, the existing guard), keep `!inFlight.has(e.role) && now - e.enqueuedAt > MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS`, and map each to `{ role: e.role, summary: e.summary, waitedMs: now - e.enqueuedAt }` in queue-file order (oldest first). `checkStaleQueuedMerges` then calls the reader and keeps its current `withWait`/`mergeWaitPhrase` detail and byte-identical wording (`merge-queue entry of ${roleLabel(first.role)} — "${truncate(first.summary, FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX)}" — has waited ${humanSeconds(...)} to start…`), so its existing tests pass unchanged. Give the reader a doc comment naming it as the one traversal shared by the check and the alert.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface StaleMerge { role: string; summary: string; waitedMs: number }` beside `StalePrompt`, documented as the doctor's `MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS` rule computed by src/ui/status-payload.ts's `staleMerges`. Widen `teamAlerts` with one more defaulted trailing parameter `staleMerges: readonly StaleMerge[] = []` — appended after `stalePrompts` and after any parameter a landed in-flight plan has added before it (the notify plan appends `notifyFailure`), so the existing callers and tests compile. Add one amber block after the `stale-prompts` block: `key: "stale-merges"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(staleMerges.length, "queued merge waited", "queued merges waited")} 6+ hours to start` ``, detail naming the first `roleLabel(first.role)` and its summary, `duration(first.waitedMs)` of waiting, the rest folded via `joinWithMore(rest.map((m) => roleLabel(m.role)), 3)`, and the fix clause `` — the merge queue has stopped moving; run \`tumwater queue\` to see it, or drop the entry with \`tumwater queue --cancel <n>\` ``, `actions: []` (the header's `merge queue: N` badge and the Pending view already carry the drill-in). `roleLabel`, `plural`, `duration` and `joinWithMore` are already imported, so this adds no import. Update the module doc comment's alert list.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: add `staleQueuedMergeRows` to the existing `../doctor/doctor-backlog.js` import, and add `export function staleMerges(root: string, now = Date.now()): StaleMerge[]` beside `stalePrompts`, returning `staleQueuedMergeRows(root, now).map((m) => ({ role: m.role, summary: m.summary, waitedMs: m.waitedMs }))` (the stale-prompts seam: the reader owns the rule, this maps it to the alert shape). Import `type StaleMerge` from `./team-alerts.js` beside `StaleBug`/`StalePrompt`, and pass `staleMerges(root, now)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `staleMerges` from the same `status-payload.js` module as `staleOpenBugs`/`stalePrompts`, and pass `staleMerges(root)` as the next `teamAlerts` argument in `renderStatus`'s `alerts` call (status-render.ts) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx), each currently ending `…, staleOpenBugs(root), stalePrompts(root))`.
- docs/how-it-works.md, the Team alerts list ("… a stale bug, a stranded inbox prompt, a pause"): add "a stalled merge queue" after "a stranded inbox prompt" so the documented list matches the alerts.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, modelling the existing stale-bug/stale-prompt tests:
- A unit test `a stalled merge queue raises a standing amber alert`: `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [], [], [{ role: "feature", summary: "add the parser", waitedMs: 7 * 3600_000 }])` gives exactly one alert with `key: "stale-merges"`, tone `amber`, title `1 queued merge waited 6+ hours to start`, a detail matching `/feature/`, `/add the parser/`, `/7h/` and `/tumwater queue/`, and `actions` `[]`; two rows title `/queued merges waited/`; a `[]` argument adds none; with both a stale bug and a stale merge, `stale-bugs` precedes `stale-merges`.
- An integration test `staleMerges and the surfaces carry a stale-merge alert from the queue, and none without one`: a `makeRepo()` root with `fs.mkdirSync(mergeQueueDir(root), { recursive: true })` and `enqueueMerge(root, { role: "feature", summary: "add the parser", enqueuedAt: now - 7 * 3600_000, sha: "abc1234", run: 1 })`; assert `staleMerges(root, now)` is one row `{ role: "feature", summary: "add the parser" }`, `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "stale-merges"` with the title and a detail naming `feature` and `7h`, and `renderStatus(root, snapshot(root, undefined, now))` shows the title. A root whose only stale entry's role is in `writeMergeMarker(root, { … stage: "merging", changes: [{ role: "feature", … status: "merging" }] })` yields no `stale-merges`; a root whose only entry is enqueued exactly `now - 6 * 3600_000` (not strictly past) yields none (`enqueueMerge`, `mergeQueueDir` and `writeMergeMarker` imported from `../src/merge/merge-queue.js`, `../src/paths.js` and `../src/merge/merge-slot.js`).
- The existing `checkStaleQueuedMerges` tests in test/doctor-backlog.test.ts pass unchanged (they pin the check's wording, which the refactor preserves).

**Acceptance criteria.**

### A stranded inbox prompt raises a standing alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`: the always-on twin of the doctor's `stale prompts` rule (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan except one shared file — Backlog hold 2/3 adds its held-for-operator alert in the same `teamAlerts` function of src/ui/team-alerts.ts, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring block; Interlock 1/2, Cancel dashboard and Split run-agent touch no file here; touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/ui/team-alerts.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx docs/how-it-works.md test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The doctor's `stale prompts` check (src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts checkStalePrompts, STALE_PROMPT_MS) warns when a prompt has waited more than a day for its role to dequeue it, but only when the operator runs `tumwater doctor`. A paused, disabled or failing role never reaches the run that would dequeue it, so the prompt waits indefinitely and only the Inbox views show its age, and only when the operator looks. The stale-bug rule already has an always-on alert (`key: "stale-bugs"`, src/ui/team-alerts.ts) fed by `staleOpenBugs` on all three surfaces; give the stale-prompt rule the same treatment, at the same threshold and over the same inbox traversal, so a stranded prompt is visible in the alert banners until it is delivered or dropped.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: change `const STALE_PROMPT_MS = DAY_MS;` to `export const STALE_PROMPT_MS = DAY_MS;` and widen its doc comment to say the always-on stale-prompt alert reuses this threshold (the `STALE_BUG_DAYS` precedent). `checkStalePrompts` keeps its current filter and wording unchanged.
- src/ui/team-alerts.ts: add `export interface StalePrompt { role: string; position: number; waitedMs: number }` beside `StaleBug`, documented as the doctor's `STALE_PROMPT_MS` rule computed by `stalePrompts` (oldest-first). Widen `teamAlerts`' parameter list with a 7th `stalePrompts: readonly StalePrompt[] = []` (defaulted, so the existing six-argument callers and tests keep compiling), and add one block right after the `stale-bugs` block: `key: "stale-prompts"`, `tone: "amber"`, title `` `${plural(stalePrompts.length, "queued prompt waited", "queued prompts waited")} 1+ day for its role` ``, detail `` `inbox prompt for ${roleLabel(first.role)} #${first.position} has waited ${duration(first.waitedMs)} — the role is not dequeuing it (paused, disabled, or failing); resume or enable it, or drop the prompt with \`tumwater prompt --cancel ${first.position} --role ${first.role}\`` `` plus, when more than one, ` · ${entryListDetail(rest.map((p) => `${roleLabel(p.role)} #${p.position}`))}`, and `actions: [{ label: "Open inbox", act: "queued" }]` (the dashboard's backlog arm sets the Inbox tab). Update the module doc comment's alert list to name a stranded inbox prompt.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: import `STALE_PROMPT_MS` from `../doctor/doctor-backlog.js` beside `STALE_BUG_DAYS`, and `queuedListRows` + `listWideScope` from `../inbox/inbox.js` and `deliverableAt` from `../inbox/prompt-not-before.js`. Add `export function stalePrompts(root: string, now = Date.now()): StalePrompt[]` beside `staleOpenBugs`, using the exact doctor filter: `queuedListRows(root, null, listWideScope(root)).filter((p) => p.queuedAtMs !== null && deliverableAt(p.notBeforeMs, now) && now - p.queuedAtMs > STALE_PROMPT_MS)` sorted by `queuedAtMs` ascending, each mapped to `{ role, position, waitedMs: now - queuedAtMs }`. Pass `stalePrompts(root, now)` as `teamAlerts`' 7th argument in `statusPayload`'s `alerts:` call.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: import `stalePrompts` from the same module as `staleOpenBugs`, and pass `stalePrompts(root)` as the 7th `teamAlerts` argument in `alertLines` (status-render.ts line ~493) and the TUI attention call (tui.tsx line ~172).
- docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard alert list ("a failing or stuck role, … a stale bug, a pause"): add "a stranded inbox prompt" so the documented list matches the alerts.

**Tests.** test/team-alerts.test.ts, both modeling the existing stale-bug tests:
- A unit test `stale queued prompts raise a standing amber alert`: `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now, [], [], [{ role: "feature", position: 2, waitedMs: 25 * 60 * 60 * 1000 }])` gives exactly one alert with `key: "stale-prompts"`, tone `amber`, a title matching `/queued prompt waited/`, a detail that starts `inbox prompt for feature #2 has waited`, includes `tumwater prompt --cancel 2 --role feature` and `paused, disabled, or failing`, and `actions` `[{ label: "Open inbox", act: "queued" }]`; two entries fold the rest through `— and 1 more`; no entries adds no alert; with both arrays set, `stale-bugs` precedes `stale-prompts`.
- An integration test `stalePrompts and the surfaces carry a stale-prompt alert from the inbox, and none without one`: seed a root whose `tumwater.json` lists `feature`, `enqueueRolePrompt(root, "feature", …)` then rename its queue file to an old 13-digit stamp (the `promptRoot`/`stampPrompt` helpers in test/doctor-backlog.test.ts); assert `stalePrompts(root, now)` names `{ role: "feature", position: 1 }`, and `statusPayload(root, now).alerts` carries `key: "stale-prompts"`; a prompt stamped exactly 24 h ago (not strictly past it) and a `--at` prompt whose `notBefore` is still in the future each add no alert.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A prompt due-but-undelivered for more than `STALE_PROMPT_MS` produces one amber `stale-prompts` alert on all three surfaces (the dashboard's `GET /api/status` alerts, the TUI attention lines, and `tumwater status`), naming the oldest prompt's role and position, its wait, and the deliver-or-drop commands; a deferred prompt still counting down and a prompt at or under the threshold produce none.
- The alert and the doctor's `stale prompts` check share `STALE_PROMPT_MS` and the same `queuedListRows`/`listWideScope`/`deliverableAt` traversal, so the rule and its threshold cannot drift.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater start --for <duration> --json` prints the window's per-role summary as one JSON object, so a scripted window run does not parse the prose table (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — Interlock 1/2 edits src/merge and src/runner, Interlock 2/2 edits docs/how-it-works.md, Backlog hold 2/3 and the stranded-inbox alert edit src/ui/team-alerts.ts, Backlog hold 3/3 edits src/roles, and Split run-agent edits src/agent; none touches src/cli/cli-start.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md or these tests; touches src/cli/cli-start.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-start.test.ts test/cli-start-guards.test.ts test/cli-start-once.test.ts test/cli-start-window.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater start --once --json` prints a round as one JSON object for a cron/CI caller. The other scripted boot, `--for <duration>`, prints only a prose window line and the `history --summary` table (`windowSummary`, src/cli/cli-start.ts), so an overnight or CI window run whose caller wants the counts must scrape that table. **Approach.**
- src/cli/cli-start.ts, `cmdStart`: widen the `--json` gate from `if (json && !once) fail("--json is only valid with --once")` to `if (json && !once && forMs === null) fail("--json is only valid with --once or --for")` (`forMs` is already parsed above it).
- src/cli/cli-start.ts, `cmdStart`: refuse `--json` with the two interactive modes, which write their own banner to the stdout the JSON document must own — `if (json && args.includes("--gui")) failRivalShapes("--json", "--gui", "the dashboard writes its banner to the stdout a JSON document must own")`, and the same for `--tui` ("a TUI owns the terminal"). Place both right after the widened gate, so a `--for --json --gui`/`--tui` fails before any boot.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts: add `export interface WindowReport { window: string; covered: boolean; roles: HistorySummaryRow[]; total: HistorySummaryRow }` and `export function windowReport(label, summary, covered): WindowReport` beside `windowSummary`, returning `{ window: label, covered, roles: summary.roles, total: summary.total }`. Unlike `windowSummary` it does not append `SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE`; `covered: false` is the fact a script reads.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts, the `else if (forMs !== null && !exit.restart)` branch: build `const summary = summarizeRunRows(rows)` once, then `if (json) sayJson(windowReport(durationLabel(forMs), summary, covered)); else say(windowSummary(durationLabel(forMs), summary, covered))`.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts: guard the two stdout writes that would otherwise share the document — the deadline line becomes `if (!json) say("deadline reached — stopping")`, and `superviseStartCommand`'s `onRespawn` restart line gains `&& !runArgs.includes("--json")` (the supervisor process reads `--json` from `runArgs`). The banner and event subscription are already `json`-guarded.
- src/cli/help.ts: on the `--for` bullet add `--for --json prints the window's per-role summary as one JSON object on stdout at exit (no banner or event stream); --json with --gui or --tui is refused;`, and change the `--once --json` sentence's tail `; only valid with --once;` to ` (the --once report; --json is refused without --once or --for);`.
- docs/cli.md: line 26's `--for 2h` usage comment gains the `--json` form (`tumwater start --for 2h --json`), and line 29's `(only with --once)` becomes `(only with --once or --for)`.

**Tests.**
- test/cli-start.test.ts: a `windowReport` unit test beside the `windowSummary` tests — over `summarizeRunRows` of a two-row fixture, `windowReport("2h", summary, true)` deep-equals `{ window: "2h", covered: true, roles: summary.roles, total: summary.total }`; a `covered: false` call carries `covered: false` and no `SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE` text.
- test/cli-start-once.test.ts: the existing "run --json without --once is refused and boots nothing" test's regex becomes `/--json is only valid with --once or --for/`; its body is otherwise unchanged.
- test/cli-start-guards.test.ts: `run --for 1s --json --gui` and `run --for 1s --json --tui` each fail before boot with the rival-shapes message naming `--json` and the interactive flag (same `initProject` + `withPi("exit 0")` pattern as the neighbouring guards).
- test/cli-start-window.test.ts: a `run --for 3s --json` test mirroring the existing prose `--for 3s` one (including its pre-window `ghost` run), asserting after the exit-0 child that `JSON.parse(s.out().trim())` is an object with `window === "3s"`, `typeof runs === "number"`, `typeof covered === "boolean"` and `Array.isArray(roles)`, and that stdout carries no `tumwater running on branch`, no `deadline reached — stopping`, no `stopping — finishing current runs`, and no `ghost`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
