### Split run-agent.ts's run lifecycle from its post-run settlement (planned 2026-10-23 by the organize role; independent of every in-flight agent entry — the Codex write-guard parts (6/9–9/9) and the Codex backend parts (9a/9–9d/9) touch src/agent/codex/*, src/prompt/dialect.ts, src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts and scripts/smoke-codex.mjs, not src/agent/run-agent.ts directly, and the `prepare` step that binds this file to codex already landed in part 5/9, so its contract is settled; mirrors the runner-run → runner-outcome split (linked by design but widened to run-agent's stdout/stdin/process-group concerns); touches src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/run-settle.ts docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `runAgent` is a single ~555-line async function (src/agent/run-agent.ts, 760 lines total) that both drives a backend agent to completion and settles what happened after it dies: pre-spawn setup (raw/native append logs, per-run tmpdir, marker, blind-read state, notes shim, session ledger), the async `prepare` step, spawn (env, detached group, process title, stdin pipe), incremental stdout/stderr decoding, the translator→parser→raw-log pipeline, the two watchdog clocks, and — in the `error`/`exit`/`close` handlers — the spawn-error cause, the process-group and marker orphan sweeps, the backend's post-run reconciliation, the exit-cause classification, and building the `PiRunResult` from the parser. One function owning setup, live streaming and death-handling is the largest module in the tree; it is also the single biggest obstacle to understanding any one backend's run, because the settlement half is interleaved with the feed half that precedes it. Split it on the same seam the runner split used: the run lifecycle stays where it is, the post-run settlement moves out.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/run-settle.ts (new): the post-run settlement half — the spawn-`error` handling (setupFailureResult), the `close`-handler work (flushing the decoders' held-back bytes, the translator's pending canonical lines, the backend's post-run reconciliation — opencode's session export — skipped when a killed run already settled, the exit-cause classification merging the backend's stderr verdict with the parser's event-derived flags, the blind-read failure override, and `resultFromParser` building the `PiRunResult` so adding a field touches one place), plus the `exit` orphan sweeps (the process-group sweep, then the fire-and-forget marker sweep). Each handler's body moves verbatim into a function that takes the live run state it closes over as a parameter.
- src/agent/run-agent.ts: keeps the run lifecycle — pre-spawn setup, `prepare`, spawn, decoders, stream pipeline, watchdogs, and the feed — and keeps `runAgent`/`PiRunOptions` as its exported surface. It defines a `RunSettle` binder (the shared run state: child, rawLog, parsers, decoders, watchdogs, terminateRun, finish, backend id, run marker, and the flags the handlers read live) as a type-only import for run-settle, so there is no runtime cycle; run-agent registers the `error`/`exit`/`close` listeners that delegate to run-settle's handlers.
- Move any helper only the settlement half uses (setupFailureResult, and openAppendLog if the state it returns travels only into settlement) with it; keep the type of the returned `PiRunResult` and the run's external behavior identical.
- docs/invariants.md: update the section that describes `runAgent`'s death handling (the orphan-sweep and exit-cause guarantees) to name run-settle.ts, alongside the live-reference update, in the same commit.

**Files touched.** src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/agent/run-settle.ts (new), docs/invariants.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `runAgent` no longer contains the `close`/`exit`/`error` handler bodies; those live in run-settle.ts and run-agent imports them back, with no runtime import cycle (run-settle imports run-agent's binder type only).
- A grep over src/, test/ and the markdown docs for `setupFailureResult` and the moved settlement names finds no stale path or reference.
- The wipe, orphan-sweep, reconciliation and exit-cause tests that drive runAgent through the fake backend suites — test/claude-run.test.ts, test/codex-run.test.ts, test/opencode-run.test.ts, test/release-run.test.ts and test/agent-backend.test.ts — pass unchanged; `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Cancel a waiting merge from the dashboard Pending card: each merge-queue row gains a two-click Cancel, the browser twin of `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — Interlock relief 1/2 edits `queuedMergeRoles` in src/merge/merge-queue.ts and src/orchestrator, the pollRunnerReasons split edits src/orchestrator, the Codex parts edit src/agent and src/prompt, `start --once --json` edits src/cli/cli-start.ts, and the Backlog hold parts edit src/backlog and src/roles; none touches src/merge/merge-cancel.ts, src/gui or src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, and this plan leaves docs/cli.md to the `start --once --json` entry; touches src/merge/merge-cancel.ts src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/merge-cancel.test.ts test/gui-queue-cancel.test.ts (new) test/gui-client-pending.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** An operator who sees an unwanted change in the dashboard's Pending merge-queue card can only watch it. `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (just landed) gives the terminal operator a way to stop it, but the browser — the surface the README leads with — has no twin: the queues on the card are read-only and a cancel means reaching for a shell. Add a two-click Cancel to each merge-queue row, backed by `POST /api/queue-cancel` on the same domain core the CLI uses, so the browser, the CLI, and the TUI cannot drift on what cancelling means.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-cancel.ts: extract the removal body of `cancelQueuedMerge` (the `deleteRefIfAt` + `dropMerge` + `merge_cancelled` event + `cancelled` result) into a private `removeQueuedEntry(root, target)` so the two addressed variants cannot drift, then add `export async function cancelQueuedMergeBySha(root: string, sha: string): Promise<CancelQueuedByShaOutcome>` with `export type CancelQueuedByShaOutcome = CancelQueuedOutcome | { status: "gone" }`. It resolves the readable file in `queuedMergeFiles(root)` whose `entry.sha === sha`; none means `{ status: "gone" }` (a concurrent drain is data for the client, not an error, the `/api/prompt-cancel` gone idiom); otherwise it runs `removeQueuedEntry` and returns `cancelled`. `cancelQueuedMerge(root, position)` keeps its signature and result and calls the same helper.
- src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts: `export async function handleQueueCancel(req, res, root)` modeled on `handleRevert` beside it. `readPostBody(req, res, '{"sha": "1a2b3c4"}')`; require `body.sha` to match `/^[0-9a-f]{4,64}$/i` else `badRequest` 400 (the `handleRevert` sha rule). Then `readMergeQueue(root)` and find the entry by sha: an absent entry answers 200 `{ ok: true, status: "gone" }` without touching disk. In-flight guard, mirroring `cmdQueueCancel` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts): when `queueInFlight(root, view.entries, orchestratorAlive(root))` names the sha (`inFlight.sha` or a `mergeChanges(inFlight)` record), answer 409 `{ error: 'this merge is being merged right now — wait for it to land, then `tumwater revert <shortSha>`' }` and change nothing. Otherwise `await cancelQueuedMergeBySha(root, sha)` and, on `cancelled`, answer 200 `{ ok: true, status: "cancelled", role, commit, summary, message: 'cancelled the merge of <shortSha> — <summary>' }`; on `gone`, 200 `{ ok: true, status: "gone" }` (the drain raced the click). Imports the merge/status readers the CLI branch already uses (`readMergeQueue`, `queueInFlight`, `orchestratorAlive`, `mergeChanges`, `shortSha`); update the module doc comment to name queue cancel in its list.
- src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts: re-export `handleQueueCancel` from the gui-operator-commands barrel. src/gui/gui-server.ts: register `"POST /api/queue-cancel": (req, res) => handleQueueCancel(req, res, root)` beside `"POST /api/revert"`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts (within the `// pending-table:start` region, so `pendingQueueHtml` stays a pure function of its args and does not reference the splice's `confirmSlot`): add a fifth optional arg to `queueEntryLineHtml(e, position, now, label, cancel)` — when `cancel` is `{ sha, armed }`, append a `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-cancel='<esc(sha)>'>` reading `Confirm cancel` when `armed` else `Cancel`; the drawer's `drawerQueueHtml` keeps calling it with four args, so the drawer markup is unchanged. Add a fifth optional `cancelArmedSha = ""` to `pendingQueueHtml(mergeQueue, now, labels, role, cancelArmedSha)` and pass `{ sha: e.sha, armed: e.sha === cancelArmedSha }` for each card row.

"cancelled the merge of " + shortSha(d.commit) : "that merge already left the queue")`, then clears `pendingCancelSha`, disarms, and calls `fetchPending()` so the removed row disappears at once rather than on the next status poll. `confirmSlot` and `shortSha` reach the module through the assembled script (roles and format splices, both earlier).

### `tumwater start --once --json` prints the round's per-role outcomes as one JSON object, so a cron/CI caller does not parse the prose summary (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the interlock and pollRunnerReasons-split series touch src/orchestrator and src/merge, the Codex write-guard parts touch src/agent, src/prompt and docs/backends, and the merge-slot median touches src/report and src/ui/gui; the only shared file is docs/cli.md, where this edits the `Start the team` once block and that plan edits the `tumwater report` row, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/cli/cli-start.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-start.test.ts test/cli-start-once.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater start --once` is the README's cron/CI command: it does one round, prints a one-line prose summary (`onceSummary`) plus a `once: failed — …` line when the round failed, and exits 3 on such a failure. A CI step that wants per-role outcomes — which role merged, which errored, which was skipped and why — has to scrape that prose. Add `--json`, valid only with `--once`, that prints the same round facts as one JSON document on stdout with the banner and the event stream suppressed, so the caller parses the round directly.

**Approach.**
- src/cli/cli-start.ts: split `onceSummary` into a structured `onceReport(root, roles, runsBefore, settled, runsDone)` and a `renderOnceSummary(report)` that produces today's exact line; keep `onceSummary` as their composition so its exported signature and every existing test stay unchanged. `onceReport` walks the existing `onceRoundRoles`/`onceFailures` helpers and returns `{ runs, outcomes, skipped, failures }`:
  - `runs`: the round's total run count (the `ran > 0` sum).
  - `outcomes`: `{ [result: string]: number }`, one key per result a ran role ended on (`state.lastResult ?? "no_change"`), inserted in the `compareCodeUnits`-sorted order `onceSummary` uses.
  - `skipped`: `[{ role, reason }]` in role order, one entry per role with `ran === 0`, `reason` resolved exactly as `onceSummary` resolves it (the `settled` map, then the pause marker, then `stateSkipReason`).
  - `failures`: `onceFailures(...)` verbatim.
- In `cmdStart`, read `const json = args.includes("--json");` beside `once`, and beside the `--role` guard add `if (json && !once) fail("--json is only valid with --once");`. When `json` is true, skip the three banner `say(...)` lines and the `subscribeEvents((e) => say(formatEvent(e)))` subscription, and after the round print `sayJson(onceReport(...))` instead of the `onceSummary` line; the `onceFailures` line and the `ONCE_FAILED_EXIT_CODE` exit are unchanged. The orchestrator and merge pipeline record events through `logEvent` (file plus subscription), not stdout, and the supervisor prints nothing on stdout for a once round, so stdout then holds exactly the one JSON document.
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: add `JSON_FLAG` to `START_FLAG_SPECS` and widen the spec's doc comment to name `--once --json`.
- src/cli/help.ts: add `[--json]` after `[--once]` in the `tumwater start` synopsis, and under the `--once` stanza add one wrapped line: ``--once --json prints the round's totals, per-result counts, skipped roles and failures as one JSON object on stdout (no banner or event stream); only valid with --once;``.
- docs/cli.md: in the `Start the team` block, under the `tumwater start --once` comment line, add `# add --json to print the round's totals, per-result counts, skipped roles and failures as one JSON object (only with --once)`.

**Tests.**
- test/cli-start.test.ts: a new test for `onceReport` over the same seeded state the `onceSummary` tests use — one advanced run and one skipped role — asserting `runs`, the sorted `outcomes`, the `skipped` role/reason pairs, and `failures`; and that `onceSummary(...)` still equals `renderOnceSummary(onceReport(...))`.
- test/cli-start-once.test.ts: a new test `run --once --json prints one JSON object and no banner or event stream` — `withIdlePi`, `cli(repo, "run", "--once", "--json")`, `JSON.parse(r.stdout)` gives `runs: 1`, `outcomes: { no_change: 1 }`, empty `skipped` and `failures`, and `r.stdout` matches neither `/tumwater once on branch/` nor `/roles:/`; a second test `run --json without --once is refused` — `cli(repo, "run", "--json")` exits 1 with `/--json is only valid with --once/` and boots nothing.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater start --once --json` writes exactly one parseable JSON object to stdout (no banner, no event lines) and exits 0, or 3 when the round failed, carrying `runs`, `outcomes`, `skipped` and `failures`; `--once --role clean --json` carries only clean's work.
- `tumwater start --json` without `--once` exits 1 with `--json is only valid with --once`; the daemon and `--for` output are unchanged.
- `tumwater start --once` (no `--json`) prints the same banner, event stream and summary line as before.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### TUI Pending pane: up/down opens a queued merge and Ctrl+X twice cancels it, the terminal twin of `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the dashboard cancel entry edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, src/gui and src/merge/merge-cancel.ts but not the TUI, and this uses the already-landed `cancelQueuedMerge(root, position)` so it does not wait on that entry's sha-addressed refactor; Interlock 1/2, the Codex parts, `start --once --json` and the Backlog hold parts touch src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/orchestrator, src/agent, src/prompt, src/cli/cli-start.ts, src/backlog and src/roles — none touches src/ui/tui; the only shared file is docs/cli.md, where this edits the TUI keys table and `start --once --json` edits the Start block, so whichever lands second rebases there; touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The Pending pane renders the durable merge queue (`renderMergeQueue`) but its rows are inert: an operator who sees an unwanted change can only press Ctrl+R and watch. `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` (landed) and the planned dashboard per-row Cancel give the other two surfaces a way to stop it; the terminal is left out. Add row selection to the TUI's merge-queue block — up/down open one row's detail, Esc returns to the list — and cancel the selected entry with Ctrl+X pressed twice, through the same `cancelQueuedMerge` core the CLI uses, so all three surfaces remove the same queue file and pin and log the same `merge_cancelled` event.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts: keep the visible rows as `queueRows: { entry: MergeEntry; position: number }[]` (the whole queue's `lastQueue.entries`, or `scopeMergeQueue`'s kept entries paired with `scope.positions[i]` when `roleScope` is set), rebuilt by `refresh()` and the Ctrl+G scope arm. Add `selectedQueue: number | null` and `queueDetail: string` (the selected row's rendered detail — header `merge #<position> (Ctrl+X to cancel): <roleLabel> run #<run> · <shortSha> · <age>`, then the summary and, when present, the entry's `body` and `revisionNote`). The new arms, each guarded by `session.view === session.roleIds.length + 5` and `promptLineFree(ctx.es)`:
  - up/down (via `moveEntrySelection(queueRows.length, selectedQueue, arrow)` from src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts) set the selection, rebuild `queueDetail`, reset `session.paneScroll = 0`, and repaint; Esc clears both.
  - Ctrl+X: with no selection, flash `select a merge with ↑↓ first`; with a selection, arm or cancel. The first press stores `session.queueArmed = { position, sha }` and flashes `press Ctrl+X again to cancel merge #<position> — any other key keeps it`. The second press (when `session.armedQueue` names the same sha) re-reads `queuedMergeFiles(session.root)` and aborts with `the merge queue changed — try again` unless the entry at the armed position still carries the armed sha; then it runs the CLI's in-flight guard — `queueInFlight(session.root, lastQueue.entries, orchestratorAlive(session.root))` naming the sha (`inFlight.sha` or a `mergeChanges(inFlight)` record) flashes the CLI's `being merged right now — wait for it to land, then tumwater revert <shortSha>` and changes nothing — then `await cancelQueuedMerge(session.root, position)`. On `cancelled` it flashes the CLI's line (`cancelled queue entry <position>: <roleLabel> <shortSha> — <summary>`) and calls `refresh()` (clearing the selection and detail); `out-of-range` flashes `that merge already left the queue` and refreshes. `reset()` clears the selection and detail on a view cycle, like the Queued pane.
  - `state()` returns `{ selectedQueue, queueDetail }` beside nothing else (the pane keeps its own cache).
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: add `armedQueue: { position: number; sha: string } | null` and `queueArmed: { position: number; sha: string } | null` to `TuiPaneSession` and its initializer, and move `queueArmed` onto `armedQueue` in `beginKey` (mirroring `armedNotes`/`notesClearArmed`), so any other key disarms the second press.
- src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add `selectedQueue: number | null` and `queueDetail: string` to `TuiKeysState` (merged through `...panes.state()`).
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts: in the `pane.kind === "pending"` branch, when `state.queueDetail` is non-empty window it through `entryBodyWindow` and return it; otherwise keep today's `state.paneCache` path. The empty note is unchanged.
- src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: the Pending key list gains `["↑↓", "select merge"]` and `["Ctrl+X", "cancel merge"]`.
- docs/cli.md, TUI keys table: add a `Ctrl+X (twice) | Pending | cancel the selected queued merge ...` row naming `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` as its twin and the wait-then-revert refusal, and note the up/down selection on the existing Pending Ctrl+R row or a new row.

**Tests.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts (the framework-free factory's harness, which already seeds merge queues with `enqueueMerge`): seed two queued entries; up/down set `selectedQueue` and fill `queueDetail` with the selected entry's role/sha/summary; Esc clears it; the first Ctrl+X arms (no disk change), the second removes only that entry (its file gone, its pin deleted, the other entry and pin intact) and logs one `merge_cancelled`; a key between the two presses disarms and changes nothing; a queue re-read between arm and confirm that moved the entry flashes the changed-queue notice and cancels nothing; a live `writeOrchestratorMarker` naming the sha flashes the wait-then-revert notice and leaves the file and pin.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: the Pending pane's hint line names `select merge` and `cancel merge`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Pending pane, up/down open a queued merge's detail, Esc returns to the list, and Ctrl+X twice removes exactly the selected entry from the queue and deletes its role's merge pin, logging the same `merge_cancelled` shape `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` does; any key between the two presses cancels nothing.
- A selected entry the running team is mid-merge is refused with the CLI's wait-then-revert wording and nothing is removed; a queue that shifted under the selection is refused with the changed-queue notice.
- The pane goes through the shared `cancelQueuedMerge`, so criterion one's removal path cannot drift from the CLI's; the dashboard entry's sha-addressed variant, when it lands, is a separate addressing layer over the same removal.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Write guard on Codex, part 9/9: The live `smoke:codex` step for the guard, and the docs (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 6/9 and Codex backend 9c/9 and Codex backend 9d/9 landed; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "Visibility (parts 8–9)" and "Risks"; touches scripts/smoke-codex.mjs docs/how-it-works.md docs/backends.md plans/codex-backend.md) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** After a Codex upgrade, one live command proves the guard still blocks. Session-flag trust could stop working while the `hooks/list` lookup still succeeds ("Risks"). The docs should say which backends are guarded and how.

**Approach.**
- scripts/smoke-codex.mjs (added by Codex backend part 9d/9) gains a `write guard` step.
  - Build a throwaway team layout: a git repo `<T>/repo`, its worktree `<T>/repo/.tumwater/worktrees/_slot-1`, and the same `notes.md` text in both. Keep the session dir under `<T>/repo/.tumwater/sessions`, never outside a `.tumwater` root.
  - Run the production invocation through `runAgent`, asking the model to use `apply_patch` to change `notes.md` at the primary's absolute path, and to follow any refusal.
  - Assert three things: the primary's `notes.md` is unchanged, the worktree's `notes.md` changed, and the run's rollout holds "blocked by PreToolUse hook".
  - The step is listed by the script's `--help`/dry-run.
- docs/how-it-works.md, "A run" step 2: the guarded tools name codex's `apply_patch`, through a trusted hook. Shell writes stay unchecked on every backend.
- docs/backends.md, Codex section:

  - `codex-hook-trust.json` caches the hash;
  - `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` is never used.
- plans/codex-backend.md: under "never passes `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`", add one sentence: tumwater trusts only its own write-guard hook, through the session-flag layer (plans/codex-write-guard.md).

**Tests.** None beyond the script's dry-run listing. The live step runs by hand: `npm run smoke:codex`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `npm run smoke:codex -- --help` (or the script's dry-run flag) lists the `write guard` step.

### Backlog hold convergence, part 1/3: The held count and the held-for-operator hold (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role, split from the user's "Backlog hold convergence" plan; the read half of the convergence backstop — parts 2/3 and 3/3 surface and write the count; touches src/roles/role-guidance.ts src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A Needs-review/Needs-replan note gains a held count, and an entry whose count reaches three becomes `held-for-operator`: `entryHold` classifies it as its own hold, the plan role no longer takes it, and every surface can see why. This part is the data layer only.

**Approach.**
- src/roles/role-guidance.ts: export the two literals both halves share — `HELD_TAG_PREFIX = "(held "` (the tag text before the number, so the parser and the note templates cannot drift) and `PRIOR_HELD_PREFIX = "**Previously held "` — beside the existing note prefixes. Document that the live count is `(held N)` on the note and the surviving marker after a lift is `**Previously held N**`.
- src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts: export `OPERATOR_HOLD_THRESHOLD = 3`. Add `heldCount(body: string): number` — the integer in the first Needs-review or Needs-replan note line's `(held N)` tag, else the integer in a `**Previously held N**` line, else 0; a missing or non-numeric tag is 0 and never throws.
- In `entryHoldAgainst`, before returning `"needs-review"`/`"needs-replan"` for a present note, return `"held-for-operator"` when `heldCount(body) >= OPERATOR_HOLD_THRESHOLD`. Add `"held-for-operator"` to the `EntryHold` union; `holdMark` renders ` [blocked: held for operator]`.
- src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts: `holdWording` gains a `held-for-operator` branch (e.g. `held for the operator (tumwater plan --release)`) and `seriesInfos` counts it with `needs-review`, so the notes block does not fall through to the `blockedBy` wording for a string hold.
- No change to the plan-role wake gate (`planBacklogFull`, src/scheduling/claims.ts): it already tests only `"needs-review"`/`"needs-replan"`, so a held-for-operator entry neither keeps the plan role running nor counts as an eligible plan. Verify with a test rather than editing it.

**Tests.**
- test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts: `heldCount` reads `(held 3)` from a Needs-review line, `(held 2)` from a Needs-replan line, `2` from `**Previously held 2**` when no note is present, and `0` when neither; a `(held x)` tag is 0.
- An entry with a `**Needs review … (held 3)**` line yields `entryHold` `"held-for-operator"` and `holdMark` `[blocked: held for operator]`; the same note with `(held 2)` yields `"needs-review"` (today's behavior); a bare `**Needs review …**` still yields `"needs-review"`.
- `planBacklogFull` is true (the plan role stops) for a backlog whose only marked entry is held-for-operator.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `entryHold` returns `"held-for-operator"` exactly for a present Needs-review/Needs-replan note whose count is at least 3, and `"needs-review"`/`"needs-replan"` otherwise; an untagged note keeps today's classification.
- `heldCount` is pure over the body and never throws; `holdMark` words the new hold as ` [blocked: held for operator]`; the prompt notes block names it without falling through.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Write guard on Codex, part 6/9: Codex runs carry the trusted write-guard hook (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 5/9 landed; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "Runs (part 6)" and findings 1, 2 and 5; also edited by the open Codex backend part 9a/9 in other functions of src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts; touches src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts docs/invariants.md test/codex-args.test.ts test/codex-run.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Turn the guard on. A codex run whose `apply_patch` would land under the team root but outside its worktree is refused with the shared refusal, as pi, claude and OpenCode runs are.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts: `CodexArgOptions` gains `guardArgs?: string[]`. codexArgs inserts it after the harness's own `-c` keys and before `-m`, on fresh and resumed (`exec resume`) runs alike. The passthrough cannot override it, because part 3/9 reserved `hooks`.
- src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts: `invocation` reads the state `prepare` stored.
  - With `{ trust }` it passes `guardArgs: ["-c", codexHookArg(definition), "-c", codexHookTrustArg(trust)]`.
  - With `{ off }`, or no state, it passes neither. An untrusted hook would be skipped silently anyway.
  - It never passes `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`. That flag would run the target repo's own `.codex` hooks unreviewed and add an `error` item to every run's stream (findings 1 and 4).
- docs/invariants.md: the next free `INV-CW` id. It is "a codex run carries the guard's hook and its trust entry together or neither, and never `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`", pinned by the tests below.

**Tests.**
- test/codex-args.test.ts: `guardArgs` lands between the last harness `-c` and `-m` for both a fresh and a resumed run, and is absent when unset.
- test/codex-run.test.ts, on the fake:
  - a fresh run and a resumed run each carry both `-c` values with the fake's key and hash;
  - with the lookup failing, neither appears;
  - no argv ever contains `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With trust available, every codex run's argv carries the hook and its trust; without it, the argv is exactly today's.
- The codex stream translator is unchanged: a blocked patch adds no stream item (finding 5).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Split orchestrator-scheduling.ts's pollRunnerReasons, part 3/3: multi-runner claim assignment and stand-down in scheduling-admit.ts (planned 2026-10-23 by the organize role, plan-only; split 2026-10-23 by the plan role out of the too-large single split; requires part 1/3 landed; independent sibling of part 2/3 — either may land first after part 1/3; touches src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts src/orchestrator/scheduling-admit.ts (new) test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Lift the post-gate admission — the stand-down turn-down and the parallel-work-instance claim assignment — into one function.

### Write guard on Codex, part 5/9: An async `prepare` step on agent backends; codex's resolves the guard's trust before a run (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 4/9 landed; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "Trust (parts 4–5)"; also edited by the open Codex backend part 9a/9 in other functions of src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts, so whichever lands later rebases; touches src/agent/agent-backend.ts src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts test/agent-backend.test.ts test/codex-run.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** `AgentBackend.invocation()` is synchronous, but the trust lookup spawns `codex app-server`. Resolve it in an awaited step before the invocation is built, without blocking the event loop and without one `app-server` per run.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/agent-backend.ts: `AgentBackend` gains optional `prepare?(run: AgentRunSpec): Promise<void>`, documented as "work the invocation needs that cannot be synchronous; never throws a run away".
- src/agent/run-agent.ts: right before `backend.invocation(runSpec)` (today around line 304), `await backend.prepare?.(runSpec)` inside a try/catch. A throw is logged as a `warning` (source `tumwater`) through `logEventBestEffort` on the run's root (`nearestTumwaterRoot(opts.sessionDir)`, skipped with no root), and the run continues.
- src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts: `prepare(run)` resolves the guard's trust for `codexWriteGuardDefinition()` under the run's codex env (`CODEX_HOME` as `invocation` computes it).
  - It goes through `codexHookTrust` with `root = nearestTumwaterRoot(run.sessionDir)` and `cwd = run.cwd`.
  - It is single-flight: one in-flight promise per process per (home, definition), shared by concurrent runs.
  - The result is a module-level state that `invocation` reads synchronously: `{ trust }` or `{ off: reason }`.
  - A failed lookup records `off` and logs one `warning` per process per (home, definition): `codex write guard off: <reason>`.
- Nothing uses the stored trust yet. This part only warms it, so a codex run now starts one `app-server` per new build and Codex version, and none on a cache hit.

**Tests.**
- test/agent-backend.test.ts (or a run-agent test beside it): a backend whose `prepare` throws still spawns its run and logs one warning; a backend without `prepare` behaves as before.
- test/codex-run.test.ts, on the fake:
  - two codex runs started together start one `app-server`;
  - a hanging `app-server` lets both runs start after the bounded wait and logs `codex write guard off:` once across three runs;
  - a pi run and a claude run start no `app-server`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- No backend's argv changes.
- A failing lookup never fails or delays a run beyond the 15 s bound.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The day report's merge-slot median: how long the merge slot held each change it landed (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the queue-cancel plan touches src/merge, src/cli and src/events, the interlock and split series touch src/orchestrator, and this adds one folded field and one line beside the report's other per-day medians; touches src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts docs/cli.md test/report-data.test.ts test/report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role
**Goal.** The team day report and the dashboard Usage view print a per-day `Merge wait median` (a `merge_done`'s enqueue-to-merged `queuedMs`), but nothing says how much of that wait the merge slot itself spent: `merge_done.durationMs` runs from the verification's start to the outcome (`writeMergeOutcome`, src/merge/merge-slot.ts) and is folded nowhere. Add a per-day `Merge slot median` — the lower median of the day's `merge_done.durationMs` — beside the merge-wait median, so an operator reads the queue backlog (the merge wait minus the slot time) apart from the slot's own review/check/rebase/merge work.

**Approach.**
- src/report/report-fold.ts: `UsageFold` and `DayFold` each gain `mergeDurationsMs: number[]` beside `mergeWaitsMs`, seeded `[]` in `dayFoldFor` and in `collectReportSince`'s accumulator (src/report/report-data.ts). In `foldUsageEvent`'s `merge_done` branch, after the `mergeWaitsMs` push, add `pushPositiveMs(target.mergeDurationsMs, finiteNumber(ev.durationMs, 0))`. Only `merge_done` feeds it: like `mergeWaitsMs`, a `merge_failed` is an attempt that never reached main, and a pre-`durationMs` event (or 0) contributes nothing, so the median is over landed merges only.
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains `mergeSlotMedianMs?: number` beside `mergeWaitMedianMs`, its doc comment saying it is the lower median of the day's `merge_done.durationMs` (verification start to outcome, ms), team-only, absent when the day has none.
- src/report/report-data.ts: add `"mergeSlotMedianMs"` to the `DayMedianKey` union (and its doc comment's "seven `…MedianMs` cells" count), and in `collectReport`'s team branch beside the `mergeWaitMedianMs` line: `setLowerMedian(day, "mergeSlotMedianMs", fold.mergeDurationsMs);`.
- src/report/report-render.ts: in the team-only block, after the `Merge wait median` line, add `pushDayCameoLine(lines, data.series, "Merge slot median", (d) => d.mergeSlotMedianMs);`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts: add `chartMergeSlotMedian(data)` returning `medianBarChart(data, "mergeSlotMedianMs", "#64748b", "merge slot")`, and `seriesHasMergeSlotMedian(data)` returning `seriesHasScalar(data, "mergeSlotMedianMs")`; update the shared `medianBarChart` comment's chart count (it now serves one more median).
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: add a block beside `Merge wait median`: `(seriesHasMergeSlotMedian(d) ? block("Merge slot median", chartMergeSlotMedian(d), "per day · verification start to outcome") : "")`.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater report` row: in the sentence naming each day's median merge wait, add each day's median merge-slot time (verification start to outcome, from `merge_done.durationMs`; team report only).

**Tests.**
- test/report-data.test.ts, a new test mirroring "collectReport gives each day the lower median of its merge_done queuedMs, team scope only": `merge_done` events on one day with `durationMs` 60_000, 120_000 and 240_000 (lower median 120_000); a `merge_done` with `queuedMs` but no `durationMs` (skipped, not zero); a `merge_failed` with a large `durationMs` (not counted); assert the first day's `mergeSlotMedianMs` is 120_000, a day with only non-qualifying merges omits the key, and every day of `collectReport(root, 3, "feature")` omits it.
- test/report.test.ts: the rendered team report contains `Merge slot median` when a day carries one, and no such line when no day does.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: the Usage view renders the `Merge slot median` block when the series carries the field and omits it otherwise, mirroring the existing `Merge wait median` case.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A day whose landed merges carry `durationMs` shows one `Merge slot median` line in `tumwater report` and one chart block in the dashboard Usage view; a merge-free (or duration-less) window prints no line and no block, so its output is unchanged.
- The field and line are team-only: a role-scoped day report and `report --json --role <id>` carry no `mergeSlotMedianMs`, and the `--since` totals report is unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater queue --cancel <n>` cancels a waiting merge before it lands (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the waiting series — it adds src/merge/merge-cancel.ts and the queue stanzas of src/cli, src/events and docs, while Interlock relief part 1/2 edits src/merge/merge-queue.ts's queued-roles read and the split series edits src/orchestrator; whichever lands later rebases; touches src/merge/merge-cancel.ts (new) src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts src/events/events.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/events/event-format.ts docs/cli.md test/merge-cancel.test.ts (new) test/cli-queue.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** An operator who sees an unwanted change waiting in the durable merge queue has no way to stop it. `tumwater queue` only reads; the alternatives are to let the change merge and then `tumwater revert`, or `tumwater retire --force` — which deletes the branch and merge ref but leaves the queue entry, so the pinned sha can still merge. Add `tumwater queue --cancel <n>`, the merge-queue twin of `tumwater prompt --cancel <n>`: it removes the Nth entry `tumwater queue` lists and deletes that entry's merge pin, so next-run leftover recovery cannot silently re-enqueue the change, and it logs a `merge_cancelled` event naming the role, commit and summary.

**Why deleting the pin is the whole cancellation.** `pinAndReset` (src/run/run-stage.ts) resets the author's branch to main the moment the commit is pinned, so `refs/tumwater/merge/<role>` is the only holder of a queued change. With the pin gone and the branch at main, `recoverLeftover` (src/runner/leftover.ts) finds no pin and no branch-ahead commit and returns null, so no later run re-queues the change.

**Approach.**
- New `src/merge/merge-cancel.ts`: `export async function cancelQueuedMerge(root: string, position: number): Promise<CancelQueuedOutcome>`, with `CancelQueuedOutcome = { status: "cancelled"; role: string; sha: string; summary: string } | { status: "out-of-range"; depth: number }`.
  - Resolve `position` against `queuedMergeFiles(root)` — the same readable, filename-ordered list `readMergeQueue`/`renderMergeQueue` render, so the position matches the line `tumwater queue` printed.
  - Delete the pin first with `deleteRefIfAt(root, mergeRefName(entry.role), entry.sha)` (src/git/git.ts; a no-op when the ref is gone or names a different sha, so a newer pin is never removed), then `dropMerge(file)` (ENOENT is already a no-op).
  - Log one `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: entry.role, type: "merge_cancelled", commit: entry.sha, summary: entry.summary })`.
  - No lock: the queue is the inbox idiom (one file per entry, `dropMerge` tolerant of a concurrent drop) and the pin delete is value-guarded. The new module mirrors `merge-requeue.ts` so `merge-queue.ts` stays the pure queue reader/writer.
- `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `cmdQueue`: before `rejectUnknownArgs`, route an invocation containing `--cancel` to a small cancel branch. Parse exactly one `--cancel <n>` with `parsePositionFlag`/`rejectRepeatFlag` (src/cli/cli-args.ts, the `cancelAndAnnounce` shape in src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts), accept optional `--json`, and reject every other flag.
  - Refuse `--cancel` with `-f/--follow` (a live view repaints a read) and `--role` (position numbers come from the whole queue); the refusal names `tumwater queue` as where the positions are. `--json` prints `{ cancelled: { role, commit, summary } }`; otherwise print one line `cancelled queue entry N: <role> <short sha> — <summary>`.
  - Refuse the entry a live merge marker names before touching it: read `queueInFlight(root, view.entries, orchestratorAlive(root))` (already imported) and, when the target sha is the marker's `sha` or one of `mergeChanges(marker)` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts), fail with ``queue entry N is being merged right now — wait for it to land, then `tumwater revert <sha>` ``.
  - On `out-of-range`, fail naming the current readable depth (the `prompt --cancel` wording).
  - Do not touch RunnerState: the queued role's `queuedSummary` stash is cleared by that role's next run (run-apply.ts), which the released interlock now lets start.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: add `[--cancel <n>]` to the queue usage stanza with one sentence. `docs/cli.md`, the queue clause of the inspect row: add `--cancel <n>` and its meaning.
- Events: `src/events/events.ts` gains `| "merge_cancelled" // an operator cancelled a waiting merge with tumwater queue --cancel; carries commit + summary` beside `merge_queued`; `src/events/event-labels.ts` gains `merge_cancelled: "merge cancelled"`; `src/events/event-format.ts` gains a `case "merge_cancelled"` returning `cancelled the merge of <shortSha> — <summary>` with no warning prefix (routine, like `prompt_cancelled`).
- docs/invariants.md: no wording change — cancellation removes queue files through the same `removeQueueFile`/`dropMerge` path the queue-file invariants already pin; read the queue-file section and leave it if it holds.

**Tests.**
- New `test/merge-cancel.test.ts` (temp repo, `enqueueMerge` + `setRef` as test/merge-queue.test.ts does): cancelling position 2 removes only that file, leaves positions 1 and 3 in order, and deletes the role's pin; a pin that names a different sha survives; an already-gone file and an out-of-range position return `out-of-range`; one `merge_cancelled` event carries the role, commit and summary.
- `test/cli-queue.test.ts`: `queue --cancel 1` prints the cancelled line and an empty queue afterwards; `--json` prints the object; a follow or `--role` invocation is refused; an out-of-range position fails naming the depth; a target a live merge marker names is refused with the wait-then-revert message.
- `test/event-format.test.ts`: the `merge_cancelled` line renders `cancelled the merge of <sha> — <summary>` with no `warning`, and a payload missing its fields renders `?`, never `undefined`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- After `tumwater queue --cancel N`, position N is gone from `tumwater queue`, the other entries keep their order, and the role's merge pin no longer names that sha; the role starts its next run and `recoverLeftover` does not re-enqueue the change.
- Cancelling the in-flight entry is refused, and cancelling with `--role`, `--follow` or an out-of-range position changes nothing.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Feedback role, part 2/2: the FILED reply line, the per-install filing ledger, and the issue_filed event (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 1/2 landed; design in plans/feedback-role.md "Shape" → "Part 2" and "Invariants" 3-5; touches src/verdict/reply-contract.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts src/run/feedback-filings.ts (new) src/paths.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts src/run/run-prompt.ts src/run/run-verdict.ts src/run/run-stage.ts src/events/events.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts test/reply-contract.test.ts test/feedback-filings.test.ts (new) test/run-prompt.test.ts test/run-verdict.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts test/event-labels.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every feedback run starts a fresh session, so the only durable record of what this install already filed must live in harness state — exactly the qa flow-coverage problem (plans/observer-roles.md 2/2). Add the model-reported result line, the ledger it persists to, the next run's injected "previously filed" block, and the event that makes a filing visible in the operator's activity feed.

- src/prompt/prompt.ts: `RunPromptInput.filings?: string` rendered beside the digest block; src/run/run-prompt.ts injects it for feedback only, in the qa coverage block's try/catch shape.
- src/run/run-verdict.ts + src/run/run-stage.ts: record beside qa's `recordFlow` — a non-cut-off `ctx.filed` writes the ledger and logs the `issue_filed` event (best-effort; a failed ledger write warns and never fails the run); a feedback run that also changed the tree still records its filing.
- src/events: `issue_filed` joins the event type union, rendered `filed issue #<n> <title> on znation/tumwater` in the feed, label `issue filed`.
- src/roles/role-catalog.ts: the charter's dedupe step names the injected "previously filed" block.

**Tests.**
- test/reply-contract.test.ts: `extractFiled` parses `FILED: #12 — title`; a line without a number, a mid-sentence mention, and a truncated `FILED: #12 — tit` yield null.
- test/feedback-filings.test.ts (new): ledger round-trip, the 100-entry cap keeps the newest, a malformed file reads empty, an empty ledger renders no block, the block renders newest-first with ages.

### Codex backend, part 9b/9: Session retention — prune expired Codex sessions with `codex delete --force` (planned 2026-10-20 by user; split 2026-10-23 by the plan role out of the too-large part 9/9; requires part 8/9 landed; independent sibling of parts 9a/9, 9c/9 and 9d/9; design in plans/codex-backend.md "CODEX_HOME and sessions"; touches src/agent/session-ledger.ts src/orchestrator/retention.ts test/session-ledger-prune.test.ts test/retention.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

Without `--force` Codex refuses to delete without a terminal (design finding 21), so `--force` is part of the command.
- When a delete fails or the binary is unusable, remove that session's rollout file under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/` as the fallback (the OpenCode spill-file fallback's twin), so the ledger line and rollout do not outlive the window.

- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Write guard on Codex, part 4/9: Ask codex for the hook's trust key and hash through `hooks/list`, and cache them per build and Codex version (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 3/9 landed; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "Trust (parts 4–5)" and finding 3; touches src/agent/codex/codex-hook-trust.ts (new) src/paths.ts test/fakes/fake-codex.ts docs/invariants.md test/codex-hook-trust.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Codex runs a session-flag hook only with the right `trusted_hash`. The hash is opaque: no simple digest of the definition matched (finding 3). So tumwater asks Codex for it, once per build and Codex version.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-hook-trust.ts (new): `lookupCodexHookTrust({ bin, env, cwd, definition, timeoutMs = 15_000 }): Promise<{ key: string; hash: string }>`.
  - It spawns `<bin> -c <codexHookArg(definition)> app-server` in `cwd` with `env`, using the harness's own spawn helper with process-group kill. It kills the group when done, on timeout and on error.
  - Over stdio, one JSON object per line, it sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"tumwater","version":<tumwater version>}}}`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialized"}`, then `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"hooks/list","params":{"cwds":[cwd]}}`.
  - It reads the reply to id 2 and returns the first hook in `result.data[*].hooks` with `source: "sessionFlags"`, `eventName: "preToolUse"` and `command` equal to `definition.command`, giving `{ key, hash: currentHash }`. It never hardcodes the key, which was `/<session-flags>/config.toml:pre_tool_use:0:0` on 0.163.0.
  - It rejects on timeout, on child exit before the reply, on a JSON-RPC error, and on "codex listed no session-flag PreToolUse hook with this command". It needs no login and makes no model request (verified with an empty `CODEX_HOME`).
- `codexHookTrust({ root, bin, env, cwd, definition })` caches in `codexHookTrustPath(root)` (new in src/paths.ts: `.tumwater/state/codex-hook-trust.json`).
  - The cache key is the trimmed output of `<bin> --version` plus `JSON.stringify(definition)`, each entry `{ key, hash, checkedAt }`.
  - A hit returns without spawning `app-server`. A miss looks up and writes the entry through `writeJsonAtomic`.
  - With `root` undefined (a hand run with no `.tumwater` root) it looks up and caches nothing. It never creates a `.tumwater` directory: a hand run once minted a phantom `$TMPDIR/.tumwater` and reddened every suite on the host (plans/codex-write-guard.md "Visibility").
- test/fakes/fake-codex.ts: the shim answers `app-server`.
  - It reads the JSON-RPC lines and answers `initialize` with `{}` and `hooks/list` with one sessionFlags preToolUse hook whose `command` is parsed from the `-c hooks.PreToolUse=` argument and whose `currentHash` is `sha256:` plus the sha256 of that command.
  - It appends each app-server start to a calls file the test can count. A test switch makes it hang, for the timeout case.
- docs/invariants.md: the next free `INV-CW` id. It is "the trust key and hash come from Codex's own `hooks/list` for the exact definition, are cached per Codex version and definition, and a lookup that times out leaves no child behind", pinned by the tests below.

**Tests.** test/codex-hook-trust.test.ts, on the fake:
- a lookup returns the fake's key and `sha256:` hash;
- a second `codexHookTrust` with the same version and definition starts no `app-server` (the calls file has one line);
- a changed `timeout` or a changed `--version` output looks up again;
- a hanging fake rejects within `timeoutMs` (set to 500 ms in the test), and the child's pid is gone afterwards;
- a fake whose list holds no matching hook rejects with the message above;
- `root` undefined writes no file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- No Codex run's argv changes yet, and no code path calls the lookup outside the tests.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Reviewer as a regular role, part 2a/4: The merge poll keeps up at fleet scale — FIFO, exactly-once, and the failure limit (planned 2026-10-23 by user; split 2026-10-23 by the plan role out of the too-large part 2/4; design in plans/reviewer-as-role.md "What lands" item 2; requires part 1/4 landed; independent sibling of part 2b/4 — either may land first; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts src/merge/merge-post-review.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Post-merge review was built for three slow maintenance roles; part 1/4 moved bugfix's, readme's and organize's volume onto it. The one-at-a-time poll must drain the queue: every merged commit is reviewed exactly once, the oldest unreviewed commit goes first, and a busy permit delays a review rather than dropping or reordering it. A verdict-less review drops its commit after POST_REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT runs and leaves it on main, because the failure is the reviewer's, not the change's.

**Approach.**
- Pin the FIFO guarantee in test/post-merge-review.test.ts: `addPostReview` appends to `readPostReviews`' array order, and `drainPostReviews` (src/merge/merge-post-review.ts) picks `pending.find((e) => e.rejected === undefined)` — the first unreviewed entry. A test queues N=10 merged commits across 4 roles (seed `postReviewPath` directly) and drives the poll with a fake reviewer; assert each commit is reviewed exactly once (count `review_verdict`/`review_rejected` heads), reviews run in queue order, and the file empties.
- Pin the rejected-first branch: with both an unreviewed entry and a rejected one queued, the revert slot fills before the next review starts (the same file's `drainPostReviews`). Do not add a per-role cap: the merge interlock releases a role once its change merges, so a role can queue more than one review; bounding that is a scheduling decision owned by the interlock entries, not this one.
- Pin the failure limit the existing tests stop short of: seed an entry with `failures = POST_REVIEW_FAILURE_LIMIT - 1`, run one verdict-less review, and assert the entry is dropped with the "stays on main unreviewed" warning and no revert is started. The git-could-not-start exemption (not counted toward the limit) is already tested.
- No production change is expected: if a test shows FIFO or exactly-once broken, fix the minimal cause in src/merge/merge-post-review.ts, never by changing `addPostReview`'s write path.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The N=10 test passes: every queued commit is reviewed exactly once, in queue order, and `readPostReviews` is empty at the end.
- The failure-limit test passes: the third verdict-less run drops the entry, logs the warning, and starts no revert.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Reviewer as a regular role, part 2b/4: The revert path holds — a post-merge rejection of an already-archived entry hands its author a fixable revision (planned 2026-10-23 by user; split 2026-10-23 by the plan role out of the too-large part 2/4; design in plans/reviewer-as-role.md "What lands" item 2 and "Risks"; requires part 1/4 landed; independent sibling of part 2a/4 — either may land first; touches src/merge/merge-drain.ts src/baseline/main-revert.ts test/post-merge-review.test.ts — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A post-merge rejection must not strand a change whose PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry was archived on merge. The revert of the merged commit restores the live entry, and `handBackReverted` → `recordRevertedChange` gives the author a revision carrying the reviewer's reasons, so the next run fixes the change instead of re-deriving it.

**Approach.**
- Extend test/post-merge-review.test.ts with the archive race end to end: make a repo, have the role's commit move a `## Planned` entry to the finished section (the `archiveNewFinishedEntries` shape, src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts), queue it with `addPostReview`, drive a rejecting review, then `drainMerge` through the revert and `handBackReverted`. Assert the heading is back under `## Planned` and absent from the finished section, `runner.state.lastReview` carries the reviewer's reasons, and `runner.state.revision.sha` is the reverted commit.
- Cover the failed-revert fallback only by asserting the existing path: `runMainRevert`'s `onFailed` → `sendReviewToRole` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) leaves the commit on main and enqueues a role prompt naming the reviewer's reasons. test/main-revert.test.ts already covers the throwing hand-off; add the archive-free case only if it is cheap, and do not build a second revert harness.
- If the archive-race test exposes a gap (an entry left only in the finished section, or a revision with nothing to apply), fix the minimal cause in the revert or hand-back path; do not widen the poll.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The archive-race test passes: after the revert the live entry is back under `## Planned` and the author holds the revision with the reviewer's reasons.
- The failed-revert fallback assertion passes: the commit stays on main and the role prompt names the reviewer's reasons.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Feedback role, part 1/2: the opt-in `feedback` observer — files one tumwater bug per run as a GitHub issue on znation/tumwater (planned 2026-10-23 by user; independent of every Planned entry; design in plans/feedback-role.md "The decision", "Invariants" and "Shape" → "Part 1"; touches src/roles/role-catalog.ts src/roles/roles.ts src/run/run-prompt.ts src/run/selfcheck-digest.ts src/config/config.ts src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts test/fakes/fake-gh.ts (new) README.md docs/config.md docs/glossary.md docs/how-it-works.md test/roles.test.ts test/config.test.ts test/prompt-roles.test.ts test/run-prompt.test.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Bring back the telemetry concept with the destination fixed: a new default-off observer role `feedback` that reads the same injected `<failure-digest>` selfcheck reads, applies the same response-was-wrong and rank-by-loss rules, and files ONE bug per run as a GitHub issue on github.com/znation/tumwater via the model's own shell running `gh` — never into the local BUGS.md, never editing the repo. The charter mirrors selfcheck's five rules verbatim where shared (rule 1 — a cluster is a bug ONLY when tumwater's RESPONSE to it is wrong; rank by loss; dedupe via `gh issue list --repo znation/tumwater --search` before every create) with the destination swapped: file with `gh issue create --repo znation/tumwater --title … --body …`, verify the issue URL in the command's output, cite the cluster key, the correlated merged commit, and `tumwater version` in the body, and redact absolute paths and secrets. Closing rule: "You never edit files in this repo — `gh` is your only write"; a fulfilled run ends with the nothing-to-do sentinel; a run that cannot file (gh missing/unauthenticated/failed) ends without the sentinel so the existing finished-without-changes warning (src/run/run-verdict.ts:321-326) surfaces the failure in the digest.

- src/config/config.ts: `roles.feedback = { enabled: false, minRunIntervalSeconds: 7200 }` beside the selfcheck entry, with the opt-in comment rewritten for the two roles. tumwater.example.json stays selfcheck-only (dogfood).

### Reviewer as a regular role, part 4/4: Reviewer feedback the author cannot miss — the rejection note leads the next run, and the commit body acknowledges each reason (planned 2026-10-23 by user; design in plans/reviewer-as-role.md "What lands" item 4; evidence: the same reason text recurring across 27 consecutive rejections of bugfix-2 (10-22T08:29→14:35Z), so the injected `lastReview` note is not changing the author's next run; touches src/prompt/prompt.ts src/prompt/gate-notes.ts src/run/run-prompt.ts src/git/commit-message.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Close the broken feedback loop that makes rejections cheap to repeat: when a run starts with a rejected change's reasons, those reasons — not the general charter — organize the run; and the resulting commit's body says, per numbered reason, what was done about it, so the re-review's prior-objection check (plans/revise-rejected.md) reads an answer, not a shrug.

- A revision commit's body carries one Objection line per prior reason; the existing commit-body tests are updated for the new template, and a non-revision commit body is unchanged.

### Write guard on Codex, part 3/9: The hook's definition and its two `-c` flags, and `hooks` keys reserved from the passthrough (planned 2026-10-23 by user; requires part 2/9 landed; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "The flags (part 3)" and findings 1–2; touches src/agent/codex/codex-write-guard.ts src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts src/config/config-validation.ts test/codex-write-guard.test.ts test/codex-args.test.ts test/config-validation.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** Build the exact `-c` values that install the hook and trust it, without wiring them into runs yet. Make sure an operator's `backends.codex.args` cannot replace either.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-write-guard.ts gains three exports:
  - `codexWriteGuardDefinition(nodeBin = process.execPath)` returns `{ matcher: "^apply_patch$", command, timeout: 30 }`. `command` is `n=<nodeBin quoted>; [ -x "$n" ] || n=node; exec "$n" <hook quoted>`, built like claude-write-guard.ts's `writeGuardSettings`. The hook path comes from `fileURLToPath(new URL("./write-guard-hook.js", import.meta.url))`, so a staged build runs its own copy.
  - `codexHookArg(definition)` returns the value `hooks.PreToolUse=[{matcher=<s>,hooks=[{type="command",command=<s>,timeout=30}]}]`.
  - `codexHookTrustArg(trust: { key: string; hash: string })` returns `hooks.state={<key>={trusted_hash=<hash>}}`, in the inline-table spelling. The dotted `hooks.state."<key>".trusted_hash=` spelling is ignored by Codex because the key contains dots (finding 2).
  - One `tomlString(s)` helper writes every TOML basic string, escaping `\`, `"` and control characters.
- Reserve `hooks`: a `-c`/`--config` passthrough whose key is `hooks` or starts with `hooks.` is refused. Codex is last-wins, so it could otherwise replace the guard or its trust.
  - Add a prefix rule beside `HARNESS_CODEX_CONFIG_KEYS` in codex-args.ts, for example `HARNESS_CODEX_CONFIG_KEY_PREFIXES = ["hooks"]` and an `isHarnessCodexConfigKey(key)` that both screens call.
  - The screens are config-validation.ts's `checkCodexConfigKeys` and any check codexArgs makes on its passthrough.
  - The problem text names the key as the existing one does ("…passes the config key hooks.PreToolUse, which tumwater manages — drop it or use another key").

**Tests.**
- test/codex-write-guard.test.ts:
  - `codexHookArg` and `codexHookTrustArg` produce the exact strings for a fixed definition and trust;
  - a `nodeBin` and hook path containing `'`, `"` and a space round-trip: the definition's `command` run through `sh -c` with a stray payload on stdin still prints the deny JSON;
  - `tomlString` escapes `\`, `"` and a control character.
- test/codex-args.test.ts: `isHarnessCodexConfigKey` is true for `hooks`, `hooks.PreToolUse` and `hooks.state` and false for `hooksy` and `model_provider`. The existing reserved keys stay true.
- test/config-validation.test.ts: `backends.codex.args` of `["-c", "hooks.PreToolUse=[]"]`, `["--config=hooks.state={}"]` and `["-c", "hooks={}"]` each report the key. `["-c", "model_provider=\"x\""]` still passes.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Nothing in a run's argv changes in this part.
- The three passthrough spellings above are refused at config validation.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Cooldown scope: A pending stale-build restart holds the redeploy, not the team (planned 2026-10-23 by user; design in plans/cooldown-scope.md "The decision"; evidence: the live instance paused 2026-10-23T09:51Z with all 30 roles stopped and auto-restart blocked by the cooldown until 13:04Z — 3 h 13 m of full stop over a stale build 15 commits ahead; the team pause and the error-streak breaker are deliberately out of scope (a pause is the operator's explicit command; the streak breaker already pauses only the failing role); touches src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts src/redeploy/redeployer.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The restart cooldown is a rate limit against restart storms, and it should limit restarts — not hold every role's runs and merges while it runs. A team whose build is merely stale (the common case: work landed, build didn't move) keeps working; the redeploy happens when its cooldown lapses or the operator forces it (the dashboard's restart button and `tumwater restart` already waive it — the escape hatch exists).

**Approach.**
- The cooldown-scoped hold was ALREADY in place in src/redeploy/redeployer.ts: inside the post-restart cooldown `poll` returns `none` (not `hold`), so orchestrator-scheduling's `holdForRestart` stays false and new runs and merges proceed on the running build while only the redeploy waits — confirmed against the code and the existing redeployer unit tests ("still inside the cooldown: deferring" → `none`; a forced restart starts the episode). No scheduling or policy change was needed; the plan's redeploy-policy/redeployer/orchestrator-scheduling anchors were already satisfied.
- The build-stale language updated on every surface that shows it — the alert (src/ui/team-alerts.ts), the badge (src/ui/badges.ts), the event feed (src/events/event-format.ts), and the digest (src/failure/failure-state-change.ts): "restarts when idle" becomes "restarts after cooldown; work continues", and the alert detail now says work continues on the running build until the restart lands or is forced.
- docs/how-it-works.md's Updates section states the narrowed scope (the cooldown limits restarts, not work); docs/glossary.md's `update available` row gains "work continues while the restart waits".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The pending-restart-inside-cooldown behavior (new runs start and merges proceed on the running build; the restart fires at the cooldown's lapse or on `restart_forced`, with the drain as today) was already pinned by test/redeployer.test.ts's cooldown/forced-restart cases; the team-alerts/badge/event-format/failure-state tests now assert the new language.
- The red-running-build carve-out and the swap's safety conditions are untouched (no scheduling/policy change); existing tests unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The day report's backlog lag median: how long a finished plan or bug waited from filing to done (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; shares src/report/report-types.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts and the src/ui/gui report files with the in-flight `tumwater report` main-red and review-duration entries — it adds a different field, line and chart beside theirs, so whichever lands later rebases; touches src/backlog, which no waiting entry touches; touches src/backlog/backlog-md.ts src/backlog/backlog.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts docs/cli.md test/backlog.test.ts test/report-data.test.ts test/report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The usage report shows each day's throughput (`features done` / `bugs fixed`) but never how long the items it closed had waited since filing, so a day that closes two stale plans looks the same as one that closes two fresh ones. Add `backlogLagMedianDays` per day: the lower median, over the entries completed that day whose heading carries both a filing and a completion stamp, of the filing-to-done span in whole calendar days. (`tumwater backlog --list` already shows an open entry's age; nothing shows the age at which entries were closed.)

**Approach.**
- src/backlog/backlog-md.ts: add `entryLags(md, sectionTitle, dateRe, filingRe): { done: string; lagDays: number }[]`, walking exactly the lines `entryDates` counts (the `### ` headings and `- ` epitaphs that close a trailing `(…; commit …)`) with the same `headingMetadata`/`trailingParenthetical` rules: `done = lastDate(meta, dateRe)`, `filed = firstDate(meta, filingRe)`, and push `{ done, lagDays: daysBetween(filed, done) }` only when both exist and `lagDays >= 0`. `firstDate` stays module-local; `filingRe` is a parameter so `STAMP_DATE_RE` (backlog.ts) keeps its one home. Import `daysBetween` from src/text/datetime.ts (a pure text helper, like this module). Update `firstDate`'s doc comment: `entryDates` and `entryLags` are now both callers.
- src/backlog/backlog.ts: add `sectionCompletionLags(root, fileName, sectionTitle, dateRe): { date: string; lagDays: number }[]` beside `sectionCompletionDates`, the same stat-cached file reader with its own `lagCache` (key `${file}\u0000${sectionTitle}\u0000${dateRe.source}\u0000${dateRe.flags}`), calling `entryLags(md, sectionTitle, dateRe, STAMP_DATE_RE)`. A missing or unreadable file yields `[]`.
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains `backlogLagMedianDays?: number` (team-only, absent when the day has none, like `checkMedianMs`), documented as the lower median of the whole-day filing-to-done lags of the entries completed that day.
- src/report/report-data.ts: in `collectReport`'s team branch (`role === undefined`), beside the `validationGaps` loop, collect a `Map<string, number[]>` from `sectionCompletionLags` over `finishedFiles("PLANS.md")` with `DONE_DATE_RE` and `finishedFiles("BUGS.md")` with `FIXED_DATE_RE`; for each `{ date, lagDays }` whose `date` is a `byDate` key, push into that day's list, then set `day.backlogLagMedianDays = lowerMedian(lags)`. (`collectReportSince` has no day series, so the `--since` report is unchanged, like the other day-granular backlog tallies.)
- src/report/report-render.ts: in `renderReportMarkdown`, after the `**Commits:**` line, under its own `data.role === undefined` guard, push `**Backlog lag median:** ${cells}` where `cells` joins `` `${monthDay(d.date)} ${d.backlogLagMedianDays}d` `` for each day that carries the field (no line when none); values are whole days from `daysBetween`, so a plain `${n}d` is exact where `medianLine`'s `shortSpanPhrase` would print minutes.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts: add `chartBacklogLagMedian(data)` = `reportSvg(data.series, (d) => [{ value: Number(d.backlogLagMedianDays) || 0, color: "#0891b2", title: d.date + ": " + (Number(d.backlogLagMedianDays) || 0) + "d median backlog lag" }], (v) => Math.round(v) + "d", false)` and `seriesHasBacklogLagMedian(data)` = `data.series.some((d) => d.backlogLagMedianDays != null)` (a defined-value check: a 0 backlog lag for a same-day filing and completion is real data, not absence), beside their siblings.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: append `(seriesHasBacklogLagMedian(d) ? block("Backlog lag median", chartBacklogLagMedian(d), "per day · filing to done") : "")` to the day-report block chain, beside the `Backlog items done` block.
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater report` row names the new `Backlog lag median` line (per day, whole days from each finished entry's filing stamp to its done/fixed stamp, team report only).

**Tests.**
- test/backlog.test.ts: `entryLags` over a `## Done` fixture returns `{ done: "2026-10-04", lagDays: 3 }` for a heading `(planned 2026-10-01 …; done 2026-10-04)`; a heading with no filing stamp and one whose filing is after its done yield nothing; a `- ` epitaph bullet is read the same way; a wrapped heading whose stamp continues on the next line still pairs.
- test/report-data.test.ts: a `## Done`/`## Fixed` fixture with two entries completed the same day (lags 2 and 4) gives that day `backlogLagMedianDays === 2` (the lower median) and no other day; a completion with no filing stamp still counts toward `featuresDone` but leaves the day's median unset when it is the day's only completion; a role-scoped `collectReport` leaves every day unset.
- test/report.test.ts: `renderReportMarkdown` prints `**Backlog lag median:** <MM-DD> <N>d` for the day that carries one and omits the line when no day does, and on a role-scoped report.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: the day-report block chain contains the `seriesHasBacklogLagMedian`/`chartBacklogLagMedian` gate, and `seriesHasBacklogLagMedian(d)` is false for a lag-free series and true for a day carrying a 0-lag median.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A day on which a finished plan or bug that carries both stamps completed reports the lower median of those completions' filing-to-done spans in whole days as `backlogLagMedianDays`; a day with no such entry carries no field and the line is omitted. A 0-day lag (a same-day filing and completion) is real data, so the field is present — `seriesHasBacklogLagMedian` checks definedness (`!= null`), not positivity.
- Entries with no filing stamp or a filing later than completion contribute nothing; `- ` epitaph bullets count like `### ` headings, matching the entry detection `featuresDone`/`bugsFixed` uses.
- The field and line are team-only: a role-scoped day report and `report --json --role <id>` carry no `backlogLagMedianDays`; the `--since` report is unchanged.
- The dashboard renders the `Backlog lag median` chart only when a day carries the field.
- The existing per-day lines render unchanged (their tests pass untouched); `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Reviewer as a regular role, part 3/4: The convergence rule — an objection that survives its revisions blocks the entry for the operator instead of rounds 3–6 (planned 2026-10-23 by user; design in plans/reviewer-as-role.md "What lands" item 3; evidence in plans/revise-rejected.md's motivation (a 14% reject rate consumed 21% of authoring spend) and the 2026-10-21→23 audit (21 items exhausted the cap; bugfix-2 exhausted the round-6 cap twice on one entry — the cap stops one cycle, the entry re-picked starts another); touches src/runner/revision.ts src/merge/merge-core.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The reject→revise loop converges. Today REVISION_BACKSTOP (6) bounds one cycle and REVISION_FINAL_ON_REPEAT (2) ends a chain early only when a reason is tagged `(prior N)`; nothing stops the re-pick that restarts an exhausted entry's cycle from scratch. End state: an objection that survives its revisions converts the entry to `[blocked: needs review]`-style operator handoff, and the author moves to other work.

**Approach.**
- src/runner/revision.ts: on exhaustion (round cap or repeated-objection final), instead of leaving the entry eligible for a fresh pick, mark it held. The hold lifts the same ways `needs-review` does today: the plan role (for PLANS.md) or a rewrite; for BUGS.md, the operator (`tumwater bug --release`) or the plan role's split — the existing `EntryHold` machinery (src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts) carries the new kind.
- The hold's reason text names the surviving objections verbatim (they are already in `RunnerState.lastReview`), so the operator or plan role sees exactly what would not converge.
- Keep the revision path itself unchanged for converging chains: each round fixes the last objection, the re-review sees the prior objections and the interdiff (plans/revise-rejected.md part 2/2), and a converging chain still lands.
- Considered and left out: teaching the *reviewer* to weight a repeated objection lower. That is verdict-quality work on the model side, not process; the hold is the process answer.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A chain whose objection survives its revisions ends with the entry held and the surviving reasons in the hold text, not with a fresh unheld pick; the author's next run takes a different entry.
- A converging chain (each round fixes the last objection) still lands through the normal revision path — its tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Reviewer as a regular role, part 1/4: Widen `review.afterMerge` to the low-blast-radius roles and document the tiering (planned 2026-10-23 by user, from the flow audit; design in plans/reviewer-as-role.md "The decision" and "What lands"; config + example + docs — the post-merge review machinery (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) already exists for clean/dedupe/coverage, so this part widens the default in src/config/config.ts and the dogfood example, updates docs/config.md and adds a test; the live tumwater.json is left to the operator, config changes no longer ride the commit path) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The reviewer stops being a pre-merge gatekeeper for the high-volume, low-blast-radius roles. bugfix, readme and organize join clean, dedupe and coverage in `review.afterMerge`: their changes merge on the deterministic gates (build pre-check, conflict markers, protected edits, secret leaks, backlog structure — all unchanged, all fail-closed) and the reviewer examines the merged commit when a permit is free, routing a rejection through the revert slot back to the author as a revision. feature, director, perf, improve and custom roles keep the pre-merge verdict. The 58-h audit (events.jsonl 2026-10-21→23) shows the cost of the current shape: 213 rejections vs 185 approvals, 21 items exhausted the revision cap unlanded, and serial reject streaks of 27 and 18 rounds on single small md-only entries — hours of reviewer and gate capacity against minutes-long edits.

**Approach.**
- The default (src/config/config.ts) and the tracked dogfood example (tumwater.example.json) carry `review.afterMerge: ["bugfix", "clean", "coverage", "dedupe", "organize", "readme"]`, so a fresh project inherits the tiering; the gitignored live tumwater.json is left to the operator (config changes no longer ride the commit path, plans/portability.md).
- docs/config.md: the `review.afterMerge` section gains the tiering rationale (post-merge for high-volume low-blast-radius roles, pre-merge for feature/director and by default for custom roles) and the tradeoff named: at the fleet's reject rate, roughly half of the listed roles' changes land-then-revert before a fix lands — the main baseline watcher and fast-merge's "a red main stops nobody" carry that churn.
- No review-machinery change in this part (src/review/post-merge-review.ts is untouched): the tiering is config plus the dogfood example; a fresh project inherits it from src/config/config.ts's widened default. Parts 2/4–4/4 (post-merge review hardening for fleet scale, the convergence rule, reviewer-feedback delivery) land separately and are pickable in any order after this one.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A bugfix change to a non-exempt file merges without a reviewer run first, and the merged commit's review (review_start with afterMerge, then verdict or rejection with reasons) appears in the event log; the rejection routes to the revert slot and back to bugfix as a revision with the prior objections carried.
- A feature change to the same kind of file still runs the pre-merge reviewer (review before merge_queued/merge_done, no afterMerge events for feature).
- `npm run test:gate` passes (config validation accepts the widened list; a list naming the director still fails as today).
