### Write guard on Codex, part 1/9: List the paths an `apply_patch` text writes (planned 2026-10-23 by user; independent of every Planned entry; design in plans/codex-write-guard.md "The hook (parts 1–2)"; touches src/agent/codex/codex-patch-paths.ts (new) test/codex-patch-paths.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The codex write guard has to know which files a patch writes before Codex applies it. Codex's PreToolUse payload carries the patch text, not a path (plans/codex-write-guard.md finding 4). This part adds the pure parser the hook will use; nothing calls it yet.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-patch-paths.ts (new): `patchWritePaths(patch: string): string[]`.
- It returns the path after each line that begins at column 0 with `*** Add File: `, `*** Delete File: `, `*** Update File: ` or `*** Move to: `, trimmed of trailing whitespace and `\r`, in order and without duplicates.
- Paths are kept as written. The caller resolves relative ones against the run's directory.
- Only a line starting exactly with `*** ` is a header. A hunk line (`+`, `-`, a space, `@@`) never counts, even when its text reads `*** Update File: …` after its prefix.
- A text without `*** Begin Patch` or `*** End Patch` is still scanned. A truncated patch still writes the files it names, so the guard must not trust the markers.

**Tests.** test/codex-patch-paths.test.ts:
- the live payload's patch, `*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /abs/repo/notes.md\n@@\n-primary\n+GUARD_TEST\n*** End Patch`, yields `["/abs/repo/notes.md"]`;
- one patch with an Add, a Delete, and an Update followed by `*** Move to: b/new.ts` yields all four paths in order;
- a hunk line `+*** Update File: evil.ts` is not counted;
- CRLF line endings and trailing spaces are stripped;
- a repeated path is listed once;
- empty text yields `[]`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `patchWritePaths` is pure: no filesystem and no imports beyond node built-ins.
- Every case above passes.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The day report's review-duration median: how long the reviewer ran each day (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of the Codex parts; adds only a new per-day median beside the existing ones, so a merge with the in-flight main-red entry rebases; touches src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts docs/cli.md test/report-data.test.ts test/report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team day report and the dashboard Usage view show each day's median reviewer-run wall-clock — how long the review gate actually took — beside the existing check/merge-wait/run medians. Today the reviewer's time is hidden inside `mergeWaitMedianMs` (enqueue through review to merged), so a slow review cannot be told apart from queue latency.

**Approach.**
- src/report/report-fold.ts: add `reviewDurationsMs: number[]` to `UsageFold` and `DayFold`, seeded `[]` in `dayFoldFor` beside `checkDurationsMs`. In `foldUsageEvent`, push `finiteNumber(ev.durationMs, 0)` into it when `> 0` from both a new `else if (ev.type === "review_verdict")` branch and the existing `review_rejected` branch (`review_rejected` carries `durationMs` only when a reviewer actually ran; the build pre-check and a duration-less event contribute nothing). The rule stated in one comment: the median is every reviewer run that reached a verdict, approval or rejection. `review_failed` stays out — it has no verdict.
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains `reviewMedianMs?: number` (team-only, absent when the day has none, like `checkMedianMs`), documented as the lower median of the day's reviewer-run durations.
- src/report/report-data.ts: add `reviewDurationsMs: []` to `collectReportSince`'s `acc` initializer (the shared `UsageFold` shape now requires it — the `--since` render draws no median, so the field is folded but not surfaced there). In `collectReport`'s team branch, `if (fold.reviewDurationsMs.length > 0) day.reviewMedianMs = lowerMedian(fold.reviewDurationsMs);`. A review belongs to the merge slot/reviewer, not the author role, so the team-only gate mirrors `checkMedianMs`.
- src/report/report-render.ts: after the `Run duration median` line, `const reviewDurations = medianLine(data.series, "Review duration median", (d) => d.reviewMedianMs); if (reviewDurations !== undefined) lines.push(reviewDurations);` — `medianLine` already omits a line when no day carries one.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts: `chartReviewMedian(data)` = `medianBarChart(data, "reviewMedianMs", <color distinct from the six existing median charts>, "review")`, a `seriesHasReviewMedian(data)` wrapper over `seriesHasScalar(data, "reviewMedianMs")`, beside their siblings in the `report-chart:end` region.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: add `(seriesHasReviewMedian(d) ? block("Review duration median", chartReviewMedian(d), "per day · reviewer runs that reached a verdict") : "")` to the day-report block chain.
- docs/cli.md: the `tumwater report` row names the new `Review duration median` line (per day, review approval or rejection durations, team report only).

**Tests.**
- test/report-data.test.ts: seed a day with `review_verdict` durations 2 min, 4 min and 6 min; assert `day.reviewMedianMs` is 4 min (the lower median) on that day and absent on a review-free day; a `review_rejected` carrying `durationMs: 5 * 60_000` joins the same median; a `review_rejected` with no `durationMs` and a `review_failed` are not counted; a role-scoped `collectReport` leaves every day's `reviewMedianMs` unset.
- test/report.test.ts: `renderReportMarkdown` prints `**Review duration median:** <MM-DD> <span>` for a day that carries one and omits it when no day does, and a role-scoped report prints no line.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: the day-report block chain contains the `seriesHasReviewMedian`/`chartReviewMedian` gate, and `seriesHasScalar(d, "reviewMedianMs")` is false for a review-free series.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A day whose reviewer runs reached verdicts reports the lower median of their durations as `reviewMedianMs`; a day with no review carries no field and the line is omitted (zero means absent).
- Both an approval (`review_verdict`) and a rejection with a positive `durationMs` count; a duration-less rejection, a `review_failed`, and a `durationMs: 0` event count for nothing.
- The field and line are team-only: a role-scoped day report and `report --json --role <id>` carry no `reviewMedianMs`.
- The dashboard renders the `Review duration median` chart only when a day carries a nonzero value.
- The existing check/merge-wait/run/provider-wait/slot-wait/check-wait medians render unchanged (their tests pass untouched); `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater report` prices main's red time per day: how long main had no passing full check (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; shares src/report and src/ui/gui/gui-client-report*.ts with the in-flight `Reverts by role` entry and the blocked Codex part 3d/9, but only adds new fields, lines and a chart beside theirs, so whichever lands second rebases over them; src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts is touched by no waiting entry; touches src/report/report-main-red.ts (new) src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts docs/cli.md test/report-main-red.test.ts (new) test/report-data.test.ts test/report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The usage report shows each day's count of failed full-suite checks (`checkFailures`) and its passing-check medians, but never the wall-clock time main spent red — the span every code role was held and every merge blocked. `redMainWarning` (src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts) already derives the current spell, but only for the doctor/selfcheck "right now" warning; the report had no main-red walk of its own (this plan's src/report/report-main-red.ts adds it). After this plan `tumwater report`, `report --since`, `report --json`, the TUI's Usage pane and the dashboard's Usage view name main's red time per day (`**Main red:** 10-22 1h 3m · 10-23 12m`), from the same `main_check`/`main_red_hold` rule G1 uses.

**Approach.**
- src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts: extract the predicates `redMainWarning` builds inline, without behavior change (its existing tests pass untouched): `ranFullMainCheck(ev)` (a `main_check` with numeric `durationMs` > 0 — the `relevant` filter's check half; stays module-private so no unused export dangles), `isRedMain(ev)` (`main_red_hold`, or a failed `main_check` that ran), and `isPassingMainCheck(ev)` (a `main_check` that ran and passed) — the latter two exported for the report caller. `redMainWarning`'s `relevant`/`red`/`passes` filters call them; their doc comments name the new report caller and say the rule is one home so the report and G1 cannot disagree about whether main is red.
- New src/report/report-main-red.ts: pure `mainRedMinutesByDay(events, fromMs, toMs): Map<string, number>`. Keep the events with a numeric `ts` in `[fromMs, toMs)` in ts order; a spell opens at a red event while none is open (a further red while open keeps the earliest start) and closes at the next `isPassingMainCheck` event; a spell still open at the end runs to `toMs`. Split every spell across local calendar days (`dayKey`) with Date-field midnight arithmetic (the `dayAt` walk, so a DST shift cannot leak an hour into the next day), summing ms per `YYYY-MM-DD`; return only nonzero entries. Doc comment: the rule is G1's; a spell already open before `fromMs` is not counted because its opener lies outside the window; this is main's own red time, not any role's.
- src/report/report-fold.ts: `ReportFoldEntry` gains `redEvents: HarnessEvent[]` (seeded `[]` on the full read), and `foldEventInto` appends the event when `isRedMain(ev) || isPassingMainCheck(ev)` — only the two shapes the interval walk needs, so the retained list stays tiny across the append-only fold (`foldLineInto` reaches the same `foldEventInto`, so an appended pass closes a spell a cache rebuild would have closed).
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains `mainRedMs?: number` (team-only, absent when zero, like `checkMedianMs`); `SinceReport` gains `mainRedMs: number` (always present, 0 when none).
- src/report/report-data.ts: `collectReport` calls `mainRedMinutesByDay(foldEntry.redEvents, dayAt(days - 1, now).getTime(), now.getTime())` once and sets `day.mainRedMs` on each series day that has one, in the team branch only (a role-scoped report leaves it unset, exactly as `checkFailures` is team-only). `collectReportSince` calls the same helper over `raw.events` with `[cutoff, end)` and returns the summed map as `mainRedMs`.
- src/report/report-render.ts: in `renderReportMarkdown`'s per-day block, after the `Red merge checks` line, push `**Main red:** ${days.map((d) => `${monthDay(d.date)} ${durationLabel(ms)}`).join(" · ")}` for the days that carry `mainRedMs` (no line when none, team-only); in `renderSinceReportMarkdown`, push `**Main red:** ${durationLabel(data.mainRedMs)}` when `data.mainRedMs > 0`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts: add `chartMainRedMs(data)` = `reportSvg(data.series, (d) => [{ value: Number(d.mainRedMs) || 0, color: "#dc2626", title: d.date + ": " + fmtSpan(Number(d.mainRedMs) || 0) + " main red" }], (v) => fmtSpan(v), false)`, gated by `seriesHasScalar(data, "mainRedMs")`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: append `(seriesHasScalar(d, "mainRedMs") ? block("Main red time", chartMainRedMs(d), "per day · no passing full check") : "") +` after the `Red merge checks` block chain.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater report` rows: name the `Main red` line and that it is main's own red wall-clock from `main_check`/`main_red_hold` (team-only).

**Tests.**
- test/report-main-red.test.ts (new): hand-built events — a `main_red_hold` at T closed by a passing `main_check` 40 min later yields 40 min on that day; a spell crossing local midnight splits across two day keys summing to the span; an open spell counts to `toMs`; a failed `main_check` with `durationMs: 0` opens nothing and a passed one with `durationMs: 0` closes nothing; a second red while open keeps the first start; events at or outside the bounds are ignored.
- test/report-data.test.ts: seed a `main_red_hold` plus a later passing `main_check` in one day; assert that day's `mainRedMs` and its absence on the other day; a role-scoped `collectReport` leaves every day unset; `collectReportSince` sums it.
- test/report.test.ts: `renderReportMarkdown` prints `**Main red:** <MM-DD> <span>` only for days that carry one and omits it on a role-scoped report (the `Red merge checks` pattern); `renderSinceReportMarkdown` prints the line for a positive window total and omits it at zero.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: the day-report block chain contains the gated `block("Main red time", chartMainRedMs(d))` call when `mainRedMs` is present, and `seriesHasScalar(d, "mainRedMs")` is false for a red-free series.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A day whose `main_red_hold` is closed by a later passing full `main_check` reports the elapsed wall-clock as that day's `mainRedMs`; a spell crossing midnight splits across both days summing to the whole span; a spell still open at the window end counts to the end.
- A `main_check` that did not run (`durationMs: 0`, cached or inherited) neither opens nor closes a spell; a `main_red_hold` alone still counts to the window end.
- The line and field are team-only: a role-scoped day report and `report --json --role <id>` carry no `mainRedMs`, and a red-free window renders no line; `--since` carries the window total.
- The dashboard's Usage view renders the `Main red time` chart only when a day carries a nonzero `mainRedMs`.
- `redMainWarning`'s output is unchanged by the predicate extraction (its tests pass untouched); `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Codex backend, part 3d/9: The report's API-equivalent line names each subscription backend (planned 2026-10-20 by user, split 2026-10-23 by the plan role from part 3/9 after a feature Needs-review; requires part 3a/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 3; touches src/events/events.ts src/run/run-finalize.ts src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts test/report.test.ts test/report-data.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The report prints one "<label> subscription, API-equivalent: $X estimated" line per subscription backend with notional spend, instead of one hardcoded "claude subscription" line.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-finalize.ts: the `run_end` event carries `agent: usage.agent` when the run reported billing or rate windows (the same condition that writes the account file), so the fold can attribute notional spend to a backend; document the new field in src/events/events.ts's `run_end` comment.
- src/report/report-fold.ts: a `notionalByBackend` map beside `notionalByProvider`, accumulated from each `run_end`'s `agent` — falling back to `"claude"` when `agent` is absent and `billing === "subscription"`, the same legacy default old window events get.
- src/report/report-types.ts and src/report/report-data.ts: carry `notionalByBackend` through the fold → day → totals exactly as `notionalByProvider` is carried; absent when empty.
- src/report/report-render.ts: `notionalLine` becomes one line per backend with notional spend, `${backendDisplayName(backend)} subscription, API-equivalent: $X estimated`; keep a single generic line for the total when only old-log totals are known.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A report over runs of two subscription backends prints two labeled notional lines; a claude-only report's line is byte-identical to today; the totals' `notionalCostUsd` still equals the sum.
- Old `run_end` events without `agent` still count their notional under claude (the legacy default).
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 3b/9: The status header and the GUI budget tile name each backend's window (planned 2026-10-20 by user, split 2026-10-23 by the plan role from part 3/9 after a feature Needs-review; requires part 3a/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 3; touches src/ui/badges.ts src/ui/status-render.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-operator.ts test/badges.test.ts test/status-header.test.ts test/gui-client.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The header badge and the GUI budget tile render each subscription backend's window under that backend's name; a claude-only team's text is byte-identical.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/badges.ts: `claudeWindowBadge(claudeWindow, now, moved)` becomes `subscriptionWindowBadge(blocks, now, moved)`, rendering `${block.label} ${windowLabel(block.primary.type)}` + utilization percent or status word + the "<backend id> model jobs wait until HH:MM" hold clause. The hold clause names the backend by its lowercase id (`block.backend`), not the display label, so a claude-only team keeps the byte-identical `claude model jobs wait` the old badge rendered (the acceptance pins that exact string); the label replaces hardcoded "claude" only in the window's opening `<label> <type>` label. The badge shows `blocks[0]` (the list is already most-constrained-first). `budgetBadge(budget, claudeWindow, now, chain)` becomes `budgetBadge(budget, windows, only, now, chain)`: the `if (only) return window` replacement and the "beside the spend" join are unchanged over the new arguments. `claudeWindowTone(claudeWindow)` becomes `subscriptionWindowTone(blocks)` reading `blocks[0]`.
- src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/status-payload.ts: pass `snap.subscriptionWindows` and `snap.subscriptionOnly` to `budgetBadge` and the tone; the payload's preformatted `budgetBadge` string is that same function's output.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-operator.ts: `budgetCardHtml(b, cw, chain)` becomes `budgetCardHtml(b, blocks, only, chain)` and `windowLinesHtml` takes the block list and `only`; they emit one window line per block (same per-line markup), each opening under `block.label`, and the held line names the block's label (`<label> model jobs wait until HH:MM`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Existing badge and status-header tests for a claude-only snapshot pass with byte-identical strings.
- With a `sub` block ordered first, the header badge reads `Sub 7d · 40%` and the tile lists both `Claude 5h …` and `Sub 7d …`; with claude first, the header keeps `Claude 5h …`.
- `npm test` passes.

### An operator `tumwater revert` logs an `operator_revert` event, so the reverted run's trail and history name the revert and the role it undid (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan and of the Codex backend series; touches src/events/events.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/operator/revert.ts src/run/run-detail-data.ts src/run/run-detail-render.ts docs/cli.md test/operator-revert.test.ts test/run-detail-data.test.ts test/run-detail.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** An operator who runs `tumwater revert` on a merged change leaves a trace the team can read. Today only the automatic main-watch revert logs an event (`main_revert`), and the run trail matches only `main_revert`; `revertedOf`'s doc comment says so in as many words ("an operator `tumwater revert` logs no `main_revert` and stays uncovered"). After this plan, `tumwater history <role> <n>`, the TUI's History trail and the dashboard's History drill-down all show `· reverted <sha> (by operator)` for a change an operator took back, and the event feed names it.

**Approach.**
- `src/events/events.ts`: add `"operator_revert"` to `HarnessEvent["type"]` with a comment that names its writer (an operator `tumwater revert`, src/operator/revert.ts) and its payload: `commit` (the reverted commit), `revert` (the inverse commit), `runner` (the role the reverted commit's stamp names, omitted for a hand-made, director or harness commit) and `subject`. It is deliberately distinct from `main_revert`: the revert guardrails and doctor warnings (`revertWarnings`, src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts; `test/doctor-holds.test.ts`) count `main_revert` and must not count an operator's deliberate revert.
- `src/events/event-labels.ts`: add `operator_revert: "operator revert"`. The file's `Record<HarnessEvent["type"], string>` makes the compiler demand it.
- `src/events/event-format.ts`: add a `case "operator_revert"` in the same shape as the existing `main_revert` case: `reverted <short commit> (by operator) as <short revert>`, naming the runner when the event carries one.
- `src/operator/revert.ts`:
  - Extract the stamped-role check `revertFollowUp` already performs into a helper `revertedRole(subject): string | null` (null when `stampedRole` is undefined, `operator` or `tumwater`) and use it in both `revertFollowUp` and the new log site.
  - In `revertMergedCommit`, after `revertCommitIn` succeeds and while the primary lock is held, call `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "operator_revert", commit: full, revert: reverted.sha, subject, ...(role === null ? {} : { runner: role }) })`. Best-effort, so a failed event write never turns a successful revert into a refusal. No import cycle: `src/events/events.ts` imports no operator module.
- `src/run/run-detail-data.ts`: `RunDetail["reverted"]` gains `kind: "main" | "operator"`; `revertedOf` accepts `operator_revert` beside `main_revert`, keeping the same `runner`-and-`commit` match (the run's role, and its `mergedSha` or `runCommitSha`), and returns `failingTests: []` with `kind: "operator"` for it. Update the two doc comments that say operator reverts stay uncovered.
- `src/run/run-detail-render.ts`: keep the `· reverted <sha>` clause, append ` (failing: <test>)` for a `main` revert that names one, and ` (by operator)` for an `operator` revert.
- `docs/cli.md`, the "Watch run history" row: after the existing `main_revert` clause, add the operator twin — a change an operator reverted adds `reverted <sha> (by operator)`.

**Tests.**
- `test/operator-revert.test.ts`: a new test seeds a `tumwater(feature): …`-stamped commit, reverts it, and asserts one `operator_revert` (`eventsOfType`, test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts) with the reverted sha as `commit`, the new HEAD as `revert`, and `runner: "feature"`; a second reverts a normal commit and asserts the event has no `runner`.
- `test/run-detail-data.test.ts`: the two existing `deepEqual` expectations gain `kind: "main"`; a new test matches an `operator_revert` to the run's landed sha (with `failingTests: []`, `kind: "operator"`), and a wrong runner or wrong commit leaves `reverted` null.
- `test/run-detail.test.ts`: the existing render literal gains `kind: "main"`; a new assertion renders an operator revert's `· reverted <sha> (by operator)` header.
- `test/event-format.test.ts`: one case for the new type's line.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater revert <sha>` logs exactly one `operator_revert` carrying the reverted commit, the inverse, the subject, and the stamped role when there is one; the CLI, the GUI and the TUI all reach it through `revertMergedCommit`, so all three log it once.
- An operator revert of a role's landed change makes that run's `readRunDetail(...).reverted` non-null with `kind: "operator"` and `failingTests: []`, and its rendered header line ends `(by operator)`; an automatic `main_revert` still yields `kind: "main"` and its first failing test.
- `main_revert` guardrail and doctor counts are unchanged by an operator revert (nothing that matches `main_revert` matches the new type).
- The updated run-detail-data and run-detail render tests, plus the new operator-revert and event-format tests, pass; `docs/invariants.md` is edited only if its run-trail/revert section pins the match (check INV-L1 before finishing).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater report` gains a `Reverts by role` line and per-day series: which role's merged changes the main watch took back off main (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — it folds the existing `main_revert` event and no waiting entry touches src/report; touches src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts docs/cli.md test/report.test.ts test/report-data.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The usage report names whose merged changes had to be reverted off main. Today `renderReportMarkdown` / `renderSinceReportMarkdown` count rejections, revisions, refusals, failed runs, fallbacks and image reroutes per role, but a revert — the most expensive merge outcome — appears nowhere in `src/report` (a grep for `main_revert` under it finds nothing); only doctor's `checkMainReverts`-family warnings and the selfcheck digest read `main_revert`. After this plan the day report and `report --since` print `Reverts by role: feature — 2 · bugfix — 1`, `report --json` carries the per-day/per-window map, and the dashboard's Usage view gains a `Reverts by role` chart gated like its siblings.

**Approach.**
- `src/report/report-types.ts`: `ReportDay` gains `revertsByRole?: Record<string, number>` (doc comment: `main_revert` events per base role, keyed by the culprit's `runner`; absent when the day has none — zero means absent, like its siblings). `SinceReport` gains `revertsByRole: Record<string, number>` (always present, empty when none, like `mergeFailedByRole`), so the `--since` render can gate on the window's own reverts.
- `src/report/report-fold.ts`: add `revertsByRole: Record<string, number>` to `UsageFold` and `DayFold`, seed `{}` in `dayFoldFor`, and fold the event in `foldUsageEvent`:
  - `else if (ev.type === "main_revert") { if (typeof ev.runner === "string" && ev.runner !== "") addTo(target.revertsByRole, baseRoleOf(ev.runner), 1); }`
  - Read `ev.runner` directly: `eventRole(ev)` returns `ev.source`, and a `main_revert` is written by the harness (`source: TUMWATER_SOURCE`, `src/baseline/main-revert.ts`), so the role that merged the culprit is only in `runner`. A revert with no `runner` (a hand-made or director commit) adds nothing — no `(unknown)` key — matching the zero-means-absent rule of the other role maps.
  - Key by `baseRoleOf(ev.runner)` so `feature-2`'s revert counts under `feature`, the same base-role rule `commitsByRole`/`mergedByRole` follow (a revert is a commit/merge outcome, not a run).
- `src/report/report-data.ts`: seed `revertsByRole: {}` in `collectReportSince`'s `acc`, return `revertsByRole: scopedByRole(acc.revertsByRole, bases)`; in `collectReport` set `day.revertsByRole = fold.revertsByRole` in the team branch when non-empty, and `narrowToRole(fold.revertsByRole, bases)` when non-empty in the role-scoped branch, beside the rejections/refusals pair.
- `src/report/report-render.ts`: one `Reverts by role` line in each render, beside `Refusals by role` and formatted with `String` like the other count lines:
  - `renderSinceReportMarkdown`: `rankedRoleLine("Reverts by role", rankedRoleMap(data.revertsByRole).filter(([, n]) => n > 0), String)`.
  - `renderReportMarkdown`: `rankedRoleLine("Reverts by role", rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.revertsByRole ?? {}).filter(([, n]) => n > 0), String)`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts`: add `chartRevertsByRole(data)` = `roleStackChart(data, "revertsByRole", (n) => plural(n, "revert"), countAxis, true)` beside `chartRefusalsByRole`, and add `"revertsByRole"` to the `reportRoleOrder` fallback list so the legend order matches the other role charts.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`: add `(seriesHasAny(d, "revertsByRole") ? block("Reverts by role", chartRevertsByRole(d)) : "") +` beside the refusals block in the day-report section list.
- `docs/cli.md`, the `tumwater report` row: after the refusals clause add each role's reverted merges (`Reverts by role`, from `main_revert` events), so the docs name the line.

**Tests.**
- `test/report-data.test.ts`: seed a `main_revert` with `runner: "feature"` and one without a `runner`; assert `collectReport(...).series` carries `revertsByRole: { feature: 1 }` only on that day (absent on a revert-free day), and `collectReportSince(...).revertsByRole` sums it; a `runner: "feature-2"` event folds to `feature`.
- `test/report.test.ts`: assert the day and `--since` Markdown carry the `Reverts by role` line, and the `--json` day carries `revertsByRole`; a role-scoped report narrows it.
- `test/gui-client-report.test.ts`: assert `seriesHasAny(d, "revertsByRole")` is false for a revert-free series and true for one carrying a nonzero map, and that the day-report block chain contains the new gated `block("Reverts by role", chartRevertsByRole(d))` call, mirroring the existing refusals-chart case.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A day with one `main_revert` whose `runner` is `feature` renders `**Reverts by role:** feature — 1` in both the day report and `report --since`; that day's `--json` carries `revertsByRole: { feature: 1 }`; a revert-free day carries no `revertsByRole` key (zero means absent).
- A `main_revert` with no `runner` adds no entry, and a `runner` of `feature-2` counts under `feature`.
- `report --role feature` narrows `revertsByRole` to `feature`; a role with no reverts renders `-`.
- The dashboard Usage view shows a `Reverts by role` chart only when some day carries a nonzero `revertsByRole`.
- Operator reverts are deliberately not folded here (that event does not exist yet); a later entry can add `operator_revert` to the same branch.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater report --failures` prices a main-watch revert as its own loss cause, so the digest names the agent-hours a `main_revert` threw away (planned 2026-10-23 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the Codex parts and the two revert entries edit src/report, src/run, src/events and src/ui, none of them src/failure; touches src/failure/time-spend.ts src/failure/failure-data.ts src/failure/failure-render.ts docs/cli.md docs/invariants.md test/failure-time-spend.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** The failure digest's `Top loss causes by time` ranking says where the fleet burned agent-hours on work that did not stick: an error cluster, a role's `no_change` total, a review-rejected authoring span, a merge-conflict/merge-blocked span, a refusal. It omits the most expensive outcome of all — a change that merged and was then reverted off main by the main watch (`main_revert`, src/baseline/main-revert.ts). That run's `run_end` resolved to a merge, so it priced as `merged` progress in the role × outcome table and appeared in no loss cause at all — before this plan `grep -rn 'main_revert\|revert' src/failure` matched nothing. After this plan a window containing an automatic revert ranks a `reverted` cause carrying the authoring span and the revert's first failing test, in both the Markdown digest and `report --failures --json`.

**Approach.**
- `src/failure/time-spend.ts`:
  - `LossCause.kind` and `LossDraft.kind` gain `"reverted"` (both unions are hand-written; the compiler flags both sites), and the two doc comments naming the kinds gain the reverted arm.
  - In `timeAndSpend`, before the run loop, build the reverted landings from `allEvents`: a `Set<string>` keyed `${runner}\u0000${commit}` for every event where `e.type === "main_revert"` and both `e.runner` and `e.commit` are non-empty strings. Key by the exact role id the event names (not `baseRoleOf` — the run_end's `eventRole` is the same instance id) so the join matches one run, the way `revertedOf` in src/run/run-detail-data.ts matches `runner` and the landed sha.
  - In the run loop, after the `merge_conflict`/`merge_blocked` branch and before `if (key === null) continue`, add: when `ev.result === "queued"` and `resolvedOutcome?.outcome.type === "merge_done"`, join on the sha main actually holds — `mergedShaOf` (the newest `merged` event for the role inside the merge's own span, `merge_done` ts minus its `durationMs`, else the pin sha for a no-op fast-forward) — and when the pair `${role}\u0000${mergedSha}` is in the map, set `key = \`reverted\u0000${role}\``, `kind = "reverted"`, and `example = truncateExample(first string of the matching main_revert's failingTests)` or `""` when it names none. The join is revertedOf's (src/run/run-detail-data.ts), not the pin: a verification rebases its pin onto main before landing, so `main_revert.commit` (the landed `merged` sha) is matched against the landed sha or a rebased landing is silently missing from the loss ranking. The matching `main_revert` is found from `allEvents` by the same runner+landed-sha key; keep a `Map<string, HarnessEvent>` instead of a `Set` so the example is available.
  - The run's span stays in the `merged` class of the time-and-spend table: it did merge. The loss ranking is the separate `what did not survive` lens, so this cause is additive, exactly as a review-rejected span is both error-class in the table and its own loss. Note this in the `timeAndSpend` doc comment.
  - An operator `tumwater revert` logs no `main_revert` today and is deliberately not folded; `operator_revert` is a later entry's concern.
- `src/failure/failure-data.ts`: the `FailureReportData.lossCauses` field comment (the `top LOSS_TOP causes by time` line) names the reverted arm.
- `src/failure/failure-render.ts`: in the loss-cause label chain, add a `c.kind === "reverted"` arm rendering `reverted off main on ${roleCell(c.roles[0] ?? "?")}<example clause>` (the example, when present, is the first failing test); update the section comment listing the causes.
- `docs/cli.md`, the `tumwater report --failures` clause inside the report row: after `the top five loss causes ranked by agent-hours` add that the ranking prices a change the main watch later reverted off main (`main_revert`) by its authoring span, named by the revert's first failing test.
- `docs/invariants.md`: add `### INV-C3: a change the main watch reverted off main prices its authoring span as a `reverted` loss cause` after INV-C2 (or extend INV-C2's guarantee, whichever reads truer once the code is in): the classifier prices the merged run whose landed sha a `main_revert` names as a `reverted` cause with its authoring span, while the role × outcome table keeps it `merged`; binds `timeAndSpend`; pinned by the new test below.

**Tests.**
- `test/failure-time-spend.test.ts`, new test `a main-reverted merge prices its authoring span as a reverted loss cause`, built like the existing queued→merged fixture (`merge_queued` + `run_end result "queued"` + `merge_done`): with a matching `main_revert` (`runner` and `commit` the merged sha, `failingTests: ["a.test.ts flaked"]`) the digest carries a loss cause `kind: "reverted"`, `roles: ["feature"]`, `example: "a.test.ts flaked"`, and the run's own duration ms/cost; a second `main_revert` with a different `commit` or a different `runner` adds no `reverted` cause. Assert the role's `timeSpend` row still shows `classes.merged` for that run (the table is unchanged) and that `renderFailureMarkdown(data)` matches `/reverted off main on feature — a\.test\.ts flaked/`. Follow the file's existing `atLocalTs`/`tmpdir`/`writeEvents` fixtures.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A window whose `main_revert` names the landed sha of a run that ended `queued` ranks one `reverted` loss cause for that role, carrying the run's `run_start`→`run_end` ms and cost and the revert's first failing test; `report --failures --json` carries `kind: "reverted"`.
- The same run still appears in the `merged` column of the time-and-spend table (unchanged), and a revert whose culprit run is outside the window adds no cause (no authoring span is known).
- A `main_revert` naming a different commit or a different runner leaves the digest's loss causes unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Codex backend, part 3c/9: The role view and its billing line name the job's own subscription backend (planned 2026-10-20 by user, split 2026-10-23 by the plan role from part 3/9 after a feature Needs-review; requires part 3a/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 3; touches src/roles/role-view.ts src/roles/role-render.ts test/role-view.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** A role running a subscription backend shows that backend's window label and "window used up" phrase instead of always saying Claude.

**Approach.**
- src/roles/role-view.ts: `claudeInPlay` becomes "a subscription backend is in play": the role's own seam backend when it is not `pi`, else the reviewer's backend when the review gate is on (today's precedence, generalized off the literal "claude"). Read its account with `readAccount(root, backend)`, keep `billingWindow` as the account's primary window type, and carry the backend id as a new view field beside it.
- src/roles/role-render.ts: the "window used up" phrase and the billing line use `backendDisplayName(billingBackend)` with `windowLabel(windowType)` ("Codex 7d window"), falling back to today's "Claude" wording when no backend is known.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A role on a codex subscription account renders "Codex 7d window" and "Codex window used up"; a claude role's render is byte-identical to today; a pi role with a claude reviewer still shows claude.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 3a/9: The subscription-window block is per backend, and `status --json` gains `subscriptionWindows` (planned 2026-10-20 by user, split 2026-10-23 by the plan role from part 3/9 after a feature Needs-review; requires part 2e/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 3; touches src/agent/subscription-account.ts src/agent/backend-traits.ts src/status/status-budget.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/ui/status-payload.ts test/status-budget.test.ts test/status-data-models.test.ts) — done 2026-10-23 by the feature role

**Goal.** One status-poll read yields one subscription-window block per subscription backend in use, not only claude's, and hands the ordered list to every display surface. This is the shared model parts 3b/9–3e/9 consume; a claude-only snapshot is unchanged apart from the added list.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/backend-traits.ts: add `backendDisplayName(id)` = `id.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + id.slice(1)` ("claude" → "Claude", "codex" → "Codex"), the one home of a backend's display name.
- src/agent/subscription-account.ts: extract the comparator inside `windowEntries` into an exported `compareWindowEntries(a, b)` and call it from `windowEntries` (output byte-identical), so a list of blocks can be ordered by its primary entry the same way.
- src/status/status-budget.ts: `claudeWindowBlock` becomes `windowBlocks(cfg, providers, accounts, catalog)` returning `{ blocks, only }`. `blocks: SubscriptionWindowBlock[]` (`{ backend, label: backendDisplayName(backend), windows: windowEntries(account), primary: windows[0]!, heldUntil }`) carries one entry for every distinct non-`pi` backend the enabled seams (roles, review, resolver) route to whose `accounts(backend)` reads `billing === "subscription"` with at least one window. Blocks sort by `compareWindowEntries(a.primary, b.primary)` then `backend`. `only` is team-global: `!seams.some((s) => !seamFree(providers, s, accounts, catalog))`.
  - `BudgetSlice` replaces `claudeWindow` with `subscriptionWindows: SubscriptionWindowBlock[]` and `subscriptionOnly: boolean`. `collectBudget` builds `accounts` as a per-poll memoized `readAccount(root, backend, now)` Map (one read per backend per poll, today's one-claude-read cost) and returns both new fields.
- src/status/status-data.ts: `StatusSnapshot` gains `subscriptionWindows?: SubscriptionWindowBlock[]` (present only when non-empty) and `subscriptionOnly: boolean`; it derives the existing `claudeWindow?: {windows, primary, only, heldUntil}` from the claude block (`only: subscriptionOnly`), with a doc comment saying it is kept for one release. Its presence rule is unchanged.
- src/ui/status-payload.ts: the payload spreads `subscriptionWindows` and `subscriptionOnly` beside `claudeWindow` (the preformatted `budgetBadge` stays on `claudeWindow` until part 3b/9).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With two subscription accounts (`claude` and a fake `sub`): `status --json` lists both `subscriptionWindows` entries, ordered most-constrained-first; each carries `backend`, `label`, `windows`, `primary`, `heldUntil`.
- A claude-only team: `snap.claudeWindow` is unchanged (same `windows`, `primary`, `heldUntil`; `only` as before), and the only `status --json` delta is the added keys.
- `snap.claudeWindow` is absent exactly when no claude subscription seam has a window (today's rule).
- `windowEntries` output is byte-identical to before.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 7/9: The codex adapter runs model jobs, with stream-minted sessions, the rollout read after each run, a PATH fake and its prompt dialect (planned 2026-10-20 by user; requires parts 5/9 and 6/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "CODEX_HOME and sessions", "The stream translator and the rollout read that completes it" and "The prompt dialect"; touches src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts (new) src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/session-ledger.ts src/prompt/dialect.ts src/paths.ts test/fakes/fake-codex.ts (new) test/test-runner.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** Codex model jobs run end to end. Fresh runs record their stream-minted session id; continues resume it; the rollout supplies this run's usage and windows; the reviewer's suite-rerun detection sees Codex's commands; and the prompt carries Codex's dialect.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-backend.ts (new): `codexBackend`, with `id: "codex"`, `label: "Codex"`, `defaultBin: "codex"` and `binEnv: "TUMWATER_CODEX_BIN"`. Its hooks:
  - `resolveBin` goes through `resolveBinForBackend`.
  - `invocation`:
    - For a continue, it takes the newest ledger record of this kind that is `agent: "codex"`, has this cwd and a UUID id, and whose rollout `findRollout` finds under the run's home. Otherwise the run is fresh.
    - It builds the args with `codexArgs` and the env with `codexEnv(withNotesPath(backendBaseEnv(…)), {home})`. The home is `backends.codex.configDir` expanded, else none.
    - It returns `sessionId` only for a resume.
  - `translator` returns `codexTranslator()`.
  - `resumable` makes the same check as the continue.
  - `afterRun` reads `findRollout` plus `rolloutLines` for the run's thread id: the resumed id, or else `translator.sessionId()`. On [] it flags `codex_usage_partial`, and a fresh run then emits `run_usage` from `turnCompletedUsage()`. A reported model switch warns `codex_model_switched {requested, ran}` once.
  - `classifyExit` handles the stderr half of a CLI that died before `turn.failed`. A killed run returns {} (design finding 12).
  - `imageInput` returns true for now. Part 8/9 reads the catalog.
- src/agent/run-agent.ts:
  - It registers `codexBackend`.
  - After each translated batch, when `translator.sessionId?.()` first returns an id the pre-spawn ledger record lacked, it appends one more `recordSession` line with that id (same kind, name, cwd, model, `at` now).
- src/agent/session-ledger.ts: `resumableSession` already takes the newest record of a kind. Add a test that the stream-minted record wins over its own pre-spawn record.
- src/prompt/dialect.ts: `CODEX_DIALECT` per design §6 (readRange, the `…N tokens truncated…` oversized-output wording, and the rule to keep polling `write_stdin` until a command reports its exit code), and an entry in `DIALECTS`.
- test/fakes/fake-codex.ts (new), the twin of fake-opencode.ts:
  - a PATH shim named `codex` that replays a canned `--json` stream;
  - it writes a matching rollout under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/…`;
  - it records argv and stdin per run;
  - on `exec resume <id>` it appends to that rollout.
- test/test-runner.ts strips `TUMWATER_CODEX_BIN` and `CODEX_*` from the suite environment.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/codex-run.test.ts (new), on fake-codex:
  - A fresh author run exits success with the fake's final text and usage.
  - The run's ledger holds a pre-spawn record and a second record whose id is the fake's thread id.
  - A follow-up with `continueSession` runs `exec resume <that id>` with `-m`.
  - With the rollout deleted, the follow-up runs fresh, and the resume path logs its usual handoff.
  - A fake rollout reporting `seven_day` at 72% puts a `seven_day` reading with utilization 0.72 on the result, and `billing: "subscription"`.
  - A reviewer run whose fake stream runs `npm test` is seen as a suite rerun.
  - The harness's SIGTERM mid-command ends with no marked process left. (run-agent's marker
  sweep, which every backend rides, is already unit-pinned in run-marker.test.ts; the
  codex-specific end-to-end orphan demonstration was deferred to keep this part focused.)
- Prompt: a codex run's prompt carries `CODEX_DIALECT`'s rules (test/prompt-rules.test.ts, beside the OpenCode rule cases).
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 5/9: The Codex invocation and environment: argv for fresh and resumed runs, isolation flags, and the scrubbed env (planned 2026-10-20 by user; requires part 4/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "The invocation" and "Findings, verified live" 6–10, 13 and 20; touches src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts src/agent/codex/codex-env.ts (new) and their tests) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** Build, as pure functions, the argv, stdin and environment of one Codex run, fresh or resumed. A Codex run then gets only the flags design §3 lists, the prompt on stdin, and an environment with no host Codex or Claude Code session state and no OpenAI API key.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts gains `codexArgs({model, effort?, resumeId?, args?, prompt})`. It returns `{args, stdin}`.
  - A fresh run: `exec --json --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules`, then the `--disable` list (`plugins`, `apps`, `goals`, `image_generation`, `browser_use`, `computer_use`, `tool_suggest`, `skill_search`), then `-c agents.enabled=false`, `-c web_search="disabled"`, `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false`, `-c analytics.enabled=false`, `-c feedback.enabled=false`, `-c history.persistence="none"`, `-c 'project_doc_fallback_filenames=["CLAUDE.md"]'`, `-m <model>`, `-c model_reasoning_effort=<effort>` when one is given, the passthrough args (through `appendPassthroughArgs`, src/agent/agent-args.ts), and `-`.
  - A resume: `exec resume <resumeId>` with the same flags, `-m` included (design finding 6). It has no `--sandbox` and no positional prompt besides `-`.
  - It throws on an unknown effort, as `claudeArgs` does.
  - It also exports `codexEffort(thinking, levels)`, which maps through `EFFORT_BY_THINKING` and returns undefined when the model's catalog `levels` (passed in) lack the result. Part 8/9 supplies the levels; until then the caller passes undefined, which means no clamp.
- src/agent/codex/codex-env.ts (new): `codexEnv(base, {home?})`.
  - It deletes every `CODEX_*`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `CLAUDECODE` and every `CLAUDE_CODE_*`.
  - It sets `CODEX_HOME` to `home` when one is given.
  - It keeps everything else, including `TUMWATER_RUN`, `TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH` and the PATH that carries the notes shim.
- Doc comments cite the design findings behind each flag. Every `-c` key in the argv was checked with `--strict-config` on Codex 0.163.0 (design finding 20).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/codex-args.test.ts (new):
  - The fresh argv for `{model: "gpt-6.1-sol", effort: "high"}` equals the full expected list, and stdin is the prompt.
  - The resume argv starts `exec resume <id>` and still carries `-m gpt-6.1-sol`.
  - A passthrough `--sandbox` throws, naming it.
  - `codexEffort("minimal", ["low","medium"])` is `low`. `codexEffort("max", ["low","medium","high"])` is undefined. `codexEffort("high", undefined)` is `high`.
- test/codex-env.test.ts (new):
  - From a base holding `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `TUMWATER_RUN` and `HF_TOKEN`, the result keeps only `TUMWATER_RUN` and `HF_TOKEN` of those.
  - `CODEX_HOME` is set when `home` is given and absent otherwise.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 4/9: `codex` becomes a backend id, with `backends.codex`, tier defaults, the effort mapping, reserved flags and traits (planned 2026-10-20 by user; requires part 2e/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Config and routing" and "CODEX_HOME and sessions"; touches src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/model-selector.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/agent/backend-traits.ts src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts (new) src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts docs/config.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make `codex` a valid backend wherever config is read: `backend: "codex"` beside a `model`, a top-level `backend: "codex"`, and `backends.codex` with `bin`, `args`, `configDir` and `windowReserve`. There is no adapter yet (part 7/9). The startup gate's existing rule ("backend X is configured but this build has no adapter for it") refuses a team that routes a job to codex until then.

**Approach.**
- src/config/config-schema.ts:
  - `BACKEND_IDS` gains `"codex"`.
  - `CODEX_BACKEND_KEYS` is `[...BACKEND_KEYS, "configDir", "windowReserve"]`, and validation picks the key list per backend. `configDir` has claude's rule: a leading `~` expands, and the value must be absolute after expansion.
  - The `BackendConfig.configDir` doc comment says it becomes `CODEX_HOME` on codex.
- src/config/model-selector.ts: `BACKEND_DEFAULT_MODELS.codex` is `{ small: "gpt-6-luna", default: "gpt-6.1-sol", strong: "gpt-6-astra" }` (design decision 4). A comment names the catalog descriptions they come from (design finding 14).
- src/agent/codex/codex-args.ts (new) holds only two things in this part:
  - `HARNESS_CODEX_FLAGS`: the flags listed in design §2 "Reserved passthrough flags".
  - `HARNESS_CODEX_CONFIG_KEYS`: `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`, `web_search`, `agents.enabled`, `check_for_update_on_startup`, `analytics.enabled`, `feedback.enabled`, `history.persistence`. A `-c <key>=…` or `--config <key>=…` passthrough whose key is one of these is refused.
  - Part 5/9 adds the builder beside them.
- `EFFORT_BY_THINKING` lives in codex-args.ts: `off` and `minimal` → `low`; `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max` pass. `ultra` is not a value it can produce.
- src/agent/backend-traits.ts: a `codex` entry.
  - `streamsToolOutput` false.
  - `usesPiModels` false.
  - `reservedPassthroughFlag` uses `HARNESS_CODEX_FLAGS`, plus the config-key check, with the reason "it is managed by tumwater".
  - `modelLabel` gives the bare model, or "codex default".
- src/config/config-validation.ts: the `-c` key check above, with the message naming the arg and the key.
- src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts: codex jobs skip the models.json lookup, as claude and opencode do.
- docs/config.md:
  - `backend` accepts `"codex"`, and `backends` is keyed by `pi`, `claude`, `opencode` or `codex`.
  - `backends.codex.configDir` is the Codex home, which needs one `CODEX_HOME=<dir> codex login`.
  - `backends.codex.windowReserve` is the reserve.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `routeModel`:
  - `{ backend: "codex", model: "gpt-6.1-sol" }` routes to `{agent: "codex", model: "gpt-6.1-sol"}`.
  - A top-level `backend: "codex"` with no `model` resolves `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` for the strong, default and small tiers.
  - `{ backend: "codex", model: "gpt-6-luna", thinking: "high" }` keeps thinking `high`.
- Validation:
  - `backends.codex: { configDir: "~/.codex-tumwater", windowReserve: { "seven_day": 0.7 } }` loads.
  - `configDir: "relative/dir"` is refused.
  - `backends.codex.args: ["--sandbox", "read-only"]` is refused, naming `--sandbox`.
  - `backends.codex.args: ["-c", "model=x"]` and `["--config=model_reasoning_effort=high"]` are refused, naming the key.
  - `backends.codex.args: ["-c", "model_verbosity=low"]` loads.
  - `backends.opencode.configDir` is still refused.
- test/backend-traits.test.ts: codex streams no tool output, uses no pi models, and labels `gpt-6.1-sol` as `gpt-6.1-sol` and an undefined model as `codex default`.
- Startup gate: with `backend: "codex"` and no codex adapter registered, the problem names codex. A pi-only config is unaffected.
- `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater start --gui --port <n>` picks the dashboard port (planned 2026-10-22 by user; touches src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/cli-start.ts src/process/supervisor.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater start --gui` (and its `run` alias) accepts `--port <n>` and serves the dashboard there, instead of only on the hard-coded 7180. Today `--port`, `--all-interfaces` and `--token` exist only on `tumwater gui`; `START_FLAG_SPECS` rejects `--port`, and the dashboard child is spawned as a bare `["gui"]` (`spawnGuiChild` in src/process/supervisor.ts), so the one-command form is stuck on the default. Only `--port` is added: `--all-interfaces` and `--token` stay on `tumwater gui` (widening those is out of scope and would need its own plan).

**Approach.**
- src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts: extract the existing GUI `--port` entry into one shared `PORT_FLAG` (`names: ["--port"]`, `value: true`, `valueName: "<n>"`, `validate` calling `parsePortFlag`) and use it in both `START_FLAG_SPECS` and `GUI_FLAG_SPECS`, so the shape check and error rendering cannot drift between the two commands. Update the `--gui` comment in `START_FLAG_SPECS`, which currently states port selection stays on `tumwater gui`.
- src/cli/cli-start.ts:
  - In `cmdStart`, beside the existing `--once` rival checks, refuse `--port` without `--gui`: `fail("--port is only valid with --gui (e.g. `tumwater start --gui --port 8080`); the standalone dashboard is `tumwater gui --port <n>`")`.
  - In `guiChildPlan`, parse the port with `flagValue(runArgs, "--port")` + `parsePortFlag` (null when absent) and return it as a new `guiArgs` field — `["--port", String(port)]` when given, else `[]`. Strip both `--port` and its value token from `orchestratorArgs` (alongside `--gui`/`--tui`), so the supervised orchestrator generation and the self-redeploy hand-off never receive it and never hit the `--port`-requires-`--gui` refusal.
  - Thread `plan.guiArgs` through `superviseDashboard(signal, stdio, guiArgs)` into `spawnGuiChild`.
- src/process/supervisor.ts: give `spawnGuiChild` a trailing `extraArgs: string[] = []` parameter, mirroring `spawnStartChild`, and spawn `["gui", ...extraArgs]`; update its doc comment.
- src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md: show `tumwater start --gui [--port <n>]`, and say next to `gui --port N` that booting with `start --gui --port N` does the same.
- Tests: extend `guiChildPlan` cases in test/cli-start.test.ts (subject returns `guiArgs`, strips `--port` and its value, leaves other args); extend the vocabulary test and valid-flags list in test/cli-args.test.ts (`--port <n>` accepted by `run`, `gui`'s list unchanged); add the `--port`-without-`--gui` refusal to test/cli-start-guards.test.ts; and extend the live `run --gui` case in test/cli-start-window.test.ts to spawn with a free `--port` (skip when taken) and fetch the dashboard on it. A bad `--port abc` is covered by the spec's `validate` in test/cli-args.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `guiChildPlan(["--gui", "--port", "8123"])` returns `guiArgs: ["--port", "8123"]` and `orchestratorArgs: []`; `guiChildPlan(["--gui"])` returns `guiArgs: []`; `guiChildPlan(["--branch", "x", "--gui", "--port", "8123", "--for", "2h"])` keeps `--branch x --for 2h` and no `--port`.
- `tumwater start --gui --port 8123` on a ready repo serves the dashboard on 8123: the live test fetches it there, the default 7180 is not bound by this run, and the process still frees 8123 on shutdown.
- `tumwater start --port 8123` (no `--gui`) exits nonzero with the message above; `tumwater start --gui --port abc` exits nonzero with `parsePortFlag`'s invalid-port wording before the ready-repo gate.
- `tumwater gui --port 8123`, `--all-interfaces` and `--token` behave exactly as before; `gui`'s valid-flags error text still names all three.
- `tumwater help start` and docs/cli.md show the `--port` form; `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater diff [-f/--follow]` repaints the pending-change view (the team roster, a role's change, or the `--overlaps` list) every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits, the last snapshot command's live twin (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; shares `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` and `docs/cli.md` with the in-flight `tumwater report -f/--follow` entry — when that entry has landed this widens `followView` in `src/cli/follow-view.ts`, otherwise it widens the local helper and report rebases; the in-flight fast-merge, gateCommand and Codex entries edit src/merge, src/baseline, src/build, src/config, src/doctor, src/events, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent, none of them these files. Touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new) and src/cli/follow-view.ts only when it exists) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `status`, `queue`, `backlog`, `report`, `logs` and `history` all have `-f/--follow`; `tumwater diff` is the last read-only query without a live form. An operator watching what roles hold pending — above all which files two roles both touch (`--overlaps`) — wants the same view to update as runs commit and land. Add `-f/--follow` to every `diff` shape: the team roster (no `--role`), one or more roles' change views (`--role`, composing with `--stat` and `--path`), and the `--overlaps` list (composing with `--role` and `--path`). Each frame repaints exactly the text the snapshot prints, every couple of seconds, until Ctrl+C or the parent process exits (the `status -f` rule). `--json` is refused — it prints one document — with the wording the sibling follow commands use.

**Approach.**

1. `followView` learns async frames. Widen its `frameText` seam from `() => string` to `() => string | Promise<string>`, make `frame` asynchronous (`const frame = async (): Promise<void> => { const text = await frameText(); process.stdout.write(tty ? "\x1b[H\x1b[2J" + text + "\n" : text + "\n\n"); }`), `await frame()` for the first paint, and drive the interval with `setInterval(() => { void frame(); }, interval)`. Guard against a slow read stacking frames with `let painting = false; if (painting) return; painting = true; try { … } finally { painting = false; }`. The sync callers (`cmdStatus`, `cmdQueue`, `cmdBacklog`, `cmdReport`) and their emitted bytes are unchanged, and the `startParentDeathWatch` end is untouched. Edit the helper where it lives: `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` today, or `src/cli/follow-view.ts` if the in-flight `tumwater report -f/--follow` entry has landed.
2. `cmdDiff` gains the flag and the seams. Signature becomes `export async function cmdDiff(root: string, args: string[], seams: FollowViewSeams = {}): Promise<void>` (cli.ts's call site passes no seams). Add `FOLLOW_FLAG` to its `rejectUnknownArgs` list, then after `requireReadyRepo`: `const follow = args.includes("-f") || args.includes("--follow");` and `if (follow && args.includes("--json")) fail("diff --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`.
3. Factor each shape's read into a thunk returning the view and its zero-arg `render`, used by both the follow frame and the snapshot, so a frame's text is exactly the snapshot's:
   - `--overlaps` (after the existing `--overlaps --stat` refusal, with `scope`/`path` already parsed): `const readOverlaps = async () => { let view = await collectChangeOverlaps(root); if (scope === null && path === undefined) return { view, render: () => renderChangeOverlaps(view) }; if (scope !== null) view = scopeChangeOverlaps(view, scope); if (path !== undefined) view = scopeChangeOverlapsToPath(view, path); return { view, render: () => renderChangeOverlaps(view, scope ?? undefined, path) }; };` then `if (follow) { await followView(async () => (await readOverlaps()).render(), seams); return; }` and the snapshot as `const { view, render } = await readOverlaps(); sayJsonOrRender(args, view, () => render());`.
   - The non-overlaps path, after `roles`/`path` are resolved: `readChange` returns the roster read (`collectTeamChanges` + `renderTeamChange`) with the existing `--stat needs --role` and `--path needs --role` refusals kept ahead of the read, the single-role read (`collectRoleChange` + `renderRoleChange`), or the multi-role read (`collectRoleChanges` + `renderRoleChanges`). The same `if (follow) { await followView(async () => (await readChange()).render(), seams); return; } ; const { view, render } = await readChange(); sayJsonOrRender(args, view, () => render());` shape.
   The `--json` payloads and every snapshot's output stay byte-identical.
4. `src/cli/help.ts` — add `[-f/--follow]` to the three `tumwater diff` stanza synopses (the roster stanza, the `--role` stanza, and the `--overlaps` stanza) and, after the roster stanza's description, one wrapped line: `-f/--follow repaints the same view every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent; it refuses --json;`.
5. `docs/cli.md` — in the `See a role's pending change` row, add the same `-f/--follow` sentence (the `status -f` wording), naming that it composes with `--role`, `--stat`, `--path` and `--overlaps` and refuses `--json`.

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts (cmdDiff, and `followView` while it is still local), src/cli/follow-view.ts (only when the report entry has landed), src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new), driving `cmdDiff` in-process with the follow seams exactly as test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts drives `cmdQueue` (`makeRepo`, `initProject`, `ensureWorktree` + `commitIn` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js to seed a pending change; `captureStdout`/`expectFailAsync` from ./helpers/exit-capture.js; `sleep` from ./helpers/wait.js; a `withDiffFollow` wrapper that always flips the parent to 1 and restores stdout in `finally`):
  - "diff -f repaints the roster until its parent exits, then prints nothing": a seeded feature worktree holding one commit; run `["-f"]` with `{ ppid: () => parent, intervalMs: 5, tty: false }`; poll the capture (bounded loop, generous) until it holds at least two `feature: ` roster lines; flip the parent; the follow resolves and a fresh capture stays empty over a settle.
  - "diff -f --role repaints that role's change view": `["--role", "feature", "-f"]`; the capture holds `/1 commit ahead of main/` at least twice; it then stops.
  - "diff -f --overlaps repaints the shared-file list": two roles whose worktrees both touch `widget.md`; `["--overlaps", "-f"]`; the capture holds `/widget\.md: feature, feature-2/` at least twice.
  - "diff -f --json is refused": `expectFailAsync(() => cmdDiff(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` rejects matching `/diff --json prints one document/`, and the capture holds no frame and no clear-screen.
  - "diff -f clears the screen only on a TTY": with `tty: true` a frame starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; with `tty: false` the capture never contains it.
- test/cli-diff.test.ts passes unchanged: the roster, `--role`, `--stat`, `--path`, `--overlaps` and `--json` snapshot paths are untouched.
- test/status-follow.test.ts, test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts and test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts pass unchanged: the widened `followView` still emits the same frames for a sync frame text.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### Codex backend, part 2e/9: The poll loop reads each subscription backend in use for its window move, hold, reserve and warning (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; requires parts 2c/9 and 2d/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 2; touches src/gates/gate-polls.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts test/gate-polls.test.ts test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** `pollTeamGates` reads every backend in `backendsInUse(liveConfig)` instead of claude alone, so a second subscription backend gets its own hold, reserve crossings, warning and window-move roles, and the window handback names the backend whose window resumed. No behavior change for a claude-only team. Closes the 2c series.

**Approach.**
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts: import `backendsInUse` from `./startup-gate.js` and `readAccount` from `../agent/subscription-account.js`; drop `readClaudeAccount` and the `seamIsClaude` import. Keep `TeamGateStates.claudeWindowWarned`/`claudeWindowReserved` as one `ReadonlySet<string>` of `backend:type:resetsAt` keys (the shape `logWindowEventOnce` builds and orchestrator's `loggedWindowKeys` seeds) — no per-backend map is needed, because every key already carries its backend.
- Replace the single `readClaudeAccount` block with a loop over `backendsInUse(liveConfig)`: for each `backend`, `const account = readAccount(root, backend, now)`, collect `windowObservation(backend, account, now, windowReserveFor(liveConfig, backend))`, and advance `states.claudeWindowReserved = pollClaudeWindowReserve(root, states.claudeWindowReserved, account, now, reserve, backend)` and the warning poll with `backend`. Pass the collected observations to one `pollTeamHold`.
- `windowMovedRoles`: replace `seamIsClaude(configForRole(liveConfig, r.role))` with a per-backend check, where `accounts = (b) => readAccount(root, b, now)`: a role on a moved tier is added only when its OWN backend is the tier's moved backend (`subscriptionBackendOf(configForRole(liveConfig, r.role), accounts) === subscriptionBackendOf(withModelOverrides(liveConfig, tier, {}), accounts)`), so a healthy backend's role riding the same tier is not dragged over.
- Handback: `const handBack = gateResumed || (windowResumedBackends.length > 0 && !budgetActive);` and, when the resumption is a window, name the backend whose window resumed on the `budget_handback` event beside `reason: "window"` — mapped per pair from the resumed backends (`windowResumedBackends`) whose tiers' price-resolved pair it is, not from the fallback pair itself (which for claude-only carries no backend, and for two subscription backends names the opposite one).
- src/gates/budget-gates.ts: delete the `seamIsClaude` shim part 2c kept for this call site.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The gate-polls and orchestrator-budget e2e tests pass with only their event `backend` expectations updated; a claude-only team's holds, events and moves are unchanged, and its window handback event gains `backend: "claude"`.
- A test registers a fake subscription backend `sub` whose account reports a rejected `five_hour` window: its roles enter `windowMovedRoles`, a hold keyed `sub` is placed, `subscription_window_limited { backend: "sub" }` is logged once, and claude's roles, hold and account are untouched. With claude rejected and `sub` healthy, only claude's roles move.
- A test with a `sub` reserve logs `subscription_window_reserved { backend: "sub" }` once per window, and claude's own reserve memory is unaffected.
- A test with a sub and a claude role riding the SAME tier, sub's window used up and claude healthy, moves only the sub role — the healthy claude role on the moved tier is not dragged over.
- `grep -n 'seamIsClaude\|pairIsClaude' src` and `grep -n 'readClaudeAccount' src/gates/gate-polls.ts` print nothing.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 2c/9: The budget gate's window move, chain reasons and director move read each subscription backend's own used-up window (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; requires parts 2a/9 and 2b/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 2; touches src/gates/budget-gates.ts test/budget-gates.test.ts test/budget-chain-info.test.ts) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** Part 2c was too large for one run, so it is split into 2c (this part, the gate), 2d/9 (the hold observation and the once-per-window polls) and 2e/9 (the poll loop). This part makes the budget gate read each subscription backend's own used-up window instead of one claude `windowOut`, so a job moving down its chain, the director's move and each tier's chain reason name the backend that actually reported the window. No behavior change for a claude-only or pi-only team.

**Approach.**
- `pairIsClaude` goes; `seamIsClaude` stays a thin exported `seamAgent(seam) === "claude"` shim (part 2e removes it). The per-backend lookup `subscriptionBackendOf(x, accounts)` is a module-private helper (kept unexported by the exports-invariant; part 2e/9 exports it when its poll loop calls it): for a resolved seam it reads the routed `agent`, else a fallback pair's `backend`, and returns the id only when its account reads `billing === "subscription"`, else null.
- Replace the single `readClaudeAccount`/`windowOut`/`directorWindowOut` with `windowOutFor(backend)` / `directorWindowOutFor(backend)` over the existing `accounts = (backend) => readAccount(root, backend)` lookup, each calling `claudeWindowUsedUp(accounts(backend), now, …, windowReserveFor(liveConfig, backend))` (no reserve for the director reading). `BudgetGatePoll.windowOut` becomes a `Partial<Record<string, { type: string; resetsAt: number; reserve?: true }>>` keyed by backend; `windowResumed` stays the boolean "any backend's move ended this poll" and a new `windowResumedBackends: readonly string[]` names them; `BudgetGateState.prevWindowMoved` becomes a `ReadonlySet<string>`.
- `pairFreeAt` keys its subscription branch on the pair's own backend; the `extraUsage` and overage rules stay claude-only. `available`, `windowTiers`, `movedTiers`, `directorMoved` and `windowMove` (any subscription seam's own window stands, with a fallback pair to move to) use the lookup.
- `chainInfo`'s `windowOut`/`account` params become the `windowOutFor`/`accounts` lookups, so its `"window"`/`"reserve"` reason reads the prior step's own backend; the `"overage"` reason stays claude-only.
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts is untouched by this part, but it is NOT done with the series: it still gates `windowMovedRoles` through `seamIsClaude`, so a non-claude subscription window move this part creates is not yet honored by the poll loop — part 2e/9 replaces that gate with the per-backend `subscriptionBackendOf` lookup. (This part changes `windowOut` to a backend-keyed record and adds `windowResumedBackends`; their meaning at the poll loop is unchanged.)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The budget-gates and budget-chain-info tests pass with only their account/windowOut shape expectations updated; a claude-only team's decision is unchanged.
- A test seeds a `sub` subscription account (a rejected `five_hour` window) and a config whose strong tier names that backend; `pollBudgetGate` moves only that tier's seams to fallback, `windowOut` names `sub`, and claude's account and window are untouched. With claude rejected and `sub` healthy, only claude's seams move.
- `grep -n 'pairIsClaude' src` prints nothing; `windowOut` is a backend-keyed record and `windowResumedBackends` names the resumed backend.
- `npm test` passes.
