### Merge on `check.gateCommand` when `check.mergeCommand` is unset, and review clean, dedupe and coverage after merging by default (planned 2026-10-21 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Defaults"; touches src/build/build-check-detect.ts src/config/config.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md DEVELOPMENT.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Fast merge parts 6/14 and 14/14 shipped `check.mergeCommand` and `review.afterMerge` as opt-in keys. tumwater.json is gitignored, so no team commit could set them. On 2026-10-21 the merge lock still ran the full `npm test` on every code merge (142–330 s each, the latest at 02:24), and every role was still reviewed before merging. Make both on by default (decided 2026-10-21 by you): a project that declared `check.gateCommand` merges on it, and clean, dedupe and coverage are reviewed after merging, unless the config opts out. This repo's tumwater.json sets `gateCommand`, so both switches take effect here at the next redeploy.

**Approach.**
- `mergeCommandOf` (src/build/build-check-detect.ts) is the one accessor every merge-path reader uses; `gateCommandOf` beside it is unchanged. Change `mergeCommandOf` alone, distinguishing an absent key from a blank one:
  - `check.mergeCommand` absent → `gateCommandOf(config)` — the new default, so a project with only `check.gateCommand` set merges on it;
  - a non-blank string → that string;
  - a blank string (`""`) → undefined: the explicit opt-out, which keeps the full check in the merge lock even when a gate command is set.

  The merge-path readers that call `gateCommandOf` directly keep their behavior through their own `mergeCommandOf` checks: in `verifyMerge` (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts) a verified no-op rebase now takes the `mergeCommandOf !== undefined` skip and seeds nothing, and `onlyExemptDriftFromVerified` returns before seeding. Update both doc comments — `mergeCommandOf`'s and the `check.mergeCommand` comment in src/config/config-validation.ts — to say the absent key falls back to `gateCommandOf`.
- `review.afterMerge`: add `afterMerge: ["clean", "dedupe", "coverage"]` to `defaultConfig().review` (src/config/config.ts). `overlayDefaults` already merges `review` key by key, so a config that omits the key inherits it, and `"afterMerge": []` opts out. The readers (src/review/review.ts ~350, src/review/post-merge-review.ts ~36) need no change.
- Never write a default into tumwater.json. `afterMerge` is a real default in `defaultConfig().review`, so the writer expands it into the file exactly like every other default (writeConfigMutation persists the defaults-merged load; INV-B3 covers only `roles`). What an unrelated-key write must keep out is `mergeCommand`, which is not a default at all — the fallback to `gateCommandOf` lives in `mergeCommandOf` at read time. A config write through the existing writers (the TUI and dashboard editors, the director's config requests) leaves an absent `mergeCommand` absent. Add a test for that (INV-B3 binds none of the changed keys, so it does not need an invariants pin).
- `tumwater doctor`'s `check` row (`checkBuildCheck`, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) gains the facts a reader cannot get today: the in-lock command from `mergeCommandOf(config)`, so the row reads `npm test · merge lock runs npm run test:gate, full check after merging`, or `… full check in the merge lock` when it is undefined. `CheckConfigSlice` already carries `check`, so no new plumbing is needed; do not name the after-merge roles here — they live under `review`, which that slice does not hold, and the `review` row in docs/config.md already documents them.
- Docs:
  - docs/how-it-works.md: rewrite the `**Check.**` bullet's sentence "The full check then still runs once per merge, over the batch or the single change, and a failing result there blocks the merge" — the pre-change rule the objection named. It should say that with a gate command set the in-lock command is that gate command, unless `check.mergeCommand` names another or `""` opts back into the full check in the lock, and that main's full check runs on the tip after the merge via the main watch. Keep the paragraph's later `check.mergeCommand` sentences, adjusting only what the new default makes stale; the `review.afterMerge` bullet lower in the file already describes the after-merge review and needs no change.
  - docs/config.md's `check` row: `mergeCommand` defaults to `gateCommand`, and `""` keeps the full check in the lock. The `review` row's default gains `"afterMerge":["clean","dedupe","coverage"]`, and the row says `[]` opts out.
  - DEVELOPMENT.md's "The gate runs the affected tests" paragraph: "The full `npm test` still runs once per merge, on the rebased tree, and on main's baseline, unless `check.mergeCommand` is set" becomes "…unless a gate or merge command is set (`check.mergeCommand` defaults to `check.gateCommand`)".
- Tests that assumed the old defaults change only their fixture config, not their assertions:
  - Merge tests that set `gateCommand` and expect the full check in the lock set `mergeCommand: ""`.
  - Tests that expect clean, dedupe or coverage to be reviewed before merging set `afterMerge: []`.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/build/build-check-detect.ts, src/config/config.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts (comment only), src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts.
- Docs: docs/config.md, docs/how-it-works.md, DEVELOPMENT.md.
- Tests: test/build-check-detect.test.ts (the `mergeCommandOf: on for a real string, off for blank or missing` case gains an absent key plus `gateCommand` set → the gate command, and `""` plus `gateCommand` set → undefined), test/config-validation-check.test.ts, test/config-write.test.ts, test/post-merge-review.test.ts, the doctor tests for `checkBuildCheck`, and the fixture configs of merge and review tests that relied on the old defaults.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `check.gateCommand` set and no `mergeCommand`, `mergeCommandOf` returns the gate command. A fake merge runs it in the lock, not the full check, and the main watch runs the full check afterwards.
- With `"mergeCommand": ""` and a gate command, the in-lock check is the full check, as before Fast merge part 6/14.
- With neither key set, the full check runs in the lock, as today.
- With no `review.afterMerge` in the file, a clean change merges with no `review_start` before its `merged` event, and gets an `afterMerge` review. With `"afterMerge": []`, it is reviewed before merging.
- Writing an unrelated key through the config writer leaves an absent `check.mergeCommand` absent (`afterMerge`, being a default, is expanded like every other default).
- doctor's `check` row names the in-lock command and where the full check runs.
- docs/how-it-works.md's `**Check.**` bullet and DEVELOPMENT.md's "The gate runs the affected tests" paragraph no longer say the full check runs once per merge when a gate command is set.
- `npm test` passes.

### A run's trail names the main-watch revert that took its merged change off main, so `tumwater history <role> <n>`, the TUI History trail and the dashboard drill-down say why a merged run is no longer on main (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the in-flight `report -f` and `diff -f` entries edit src/cli and different docs/cli.md rows, the in-flight run-duration entry edits src/report and the report charts, the in-flight merge-on-gate entry edits src/build, src/config and src/doctor, and the Codex parts edit src/gates, src/team, src/config, src/agent and src/report/report-render.ts (part 3/9, blocked) — none touches src/run/run-detail-data.ts, src/run/run-detail-render.ts or these tests; docs/cli.md is shared at its "Watch run history" row only. Touches src/run/run-detail-data.ts src/run/run-detail-render.ts docs/cli.md test/run-detail-data.test.ts test/run-detail.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** The fast-merge machinery reverts a commit that turned main red (or a post-merge review rejected) and logs a `main_revert` event carrying the culprit `commit`, the inverse `revert`, the `runner` that merged the culprit, and the `failingTests` (src/baseline/main-revert.ts; the event's shape is pinned in src/events/events.ts). An operator reading that run's trail cannot tell: `tumwater history <role> <n>`, the TUI's Ctrl+N History trail and the dashboard's History drill-down all render `renderRunDetail` with only the run's own events, so they show `merged as <sha>` and say nothing about the later revert. Add the revert to the shared payload and header: the run's trail gains `· reverted <sha>` (and its first failing test), the same text on all three surfaces, so the operator sees that the main watch took the change back and why.

**Approach.**
- src/run/run-detail-data.ts: `RunDetail` gains `/** The automatic main-watch revert of this run's merged change, from a `main_revert` event whose `runner` is this role and whose `commit` is the run's landed or pinned sha; null when there is none (an operator `tumwater revert` logs no `main_revert` and stays uncovered). */ reverted: { sha: string; revert: string; failingTests: string[] } | null;`.
- src/run/run-detail-data.ts, `readRunDetail`: capture the unfiltered read before the role filter — `const all = readEvents(root, HISTORY_SCAN_MAX_EVENTS); const events = all.filter((e) => e.source === role);` — and pass `all` to both `detailFrom` call sites (the paired path and the surviving-`run_end` unpaired path).
- src/run/run-detail-data.ts, `detailFrom`: build the return value as now, then `reverted: revertedOf(detail, all)`, where `detail` is the object literal (so `runCommitSha`/`mergedShaOf` have already run). Add the pure helper `revertedOf(d: RunDetail, all: readonly HarnessEvent[]): RunDetail["reverted"]`: walk `all` newest-first and return the first `e.type === "main_revert"` with `typeof e.runner === "string" && e.runner === d.role` and `typeof e.commit === "string"` equal to `d.mergedSha` or `runCommitSha(d)`; its `revert` (a string; `""` when absent) and `failingTests` (`Array.isArray` guard, else `[]`). `d.reverted = null` when nothing matches.
- src/run/run-detail-render.ts, `renderRunDetail`: after the existing `merged as` clause, `if (d.reverted !== null) header += \` · reverted ${shortSha(d.reverted.sha)}\` + (d.reverted.failingTests[0] !== undefined ? \` (failing: ${d.reverted.failingTests[0]})\` : "");`. The clause names the culprit sha (which equals the landed sha when the merge was rebased) and the first failing test; `failingTests[1]` and beyond stay out of the one-line header. `shortSha` is already imported.
- docs/cli.md, "Watch run history" row: in the sentence describing the trail header, after the `merged as <sha>` clause, add that a change the main watch later reverted adds `reverted <sha> (failing: <test>)`, from the `main_revert` event. No new flag, command or key.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/run-detail-data.test.ts, a new test "a run's main_revert names the automatic revert of its landed sha": seed run 1 with a `merged` event `commit: "landed1"` (source `feature`) inside its block (the collector reads a direct run's `merged` from inside the block, after its start, at or before its `run_end`), then a `main_revert` event `{ source: "tumwater", ts: 1300, type: "main_revert", commit: "landed1", revert: "rev1", runner: "feature", failingTests: ["a.test.ts", "b.test.ts"] }`. Assert `readRunDetail(root, "feature", 1)!.reverted` deep-equals `{ sha: "landed1", revert: "rev1", failingTests: ["a.test.ts", "b.test.ts"] }`. In the same test: a `main_revert` whose `runner` is `"bugfix"` and one whose `commit` is `"other"` each leave `reverted` null, and a run with no `main_revert` at all leaves it null — so the match is on both runner and sha.
- test/run-detail-data.test.ts: the no-op fast-forward case is matched through the pinned commit too — a run whose block carries a `merge_queued`/`merge_done` `commit: "pin1"` and no `merged` event gets `reverted.sha === "pin1"` for a `main_revert` with `commit: "pin1"` and `runner` equal to the run's role. The existing tests' field-by-field assertions stay green (they compare chosen fields, not the whole payload).
- test/run-detail.test.ts: a new render case, "renderRunDetail names a reverted change and its first failing test", builds a `RunDetail` with `reverted: { sha: "abcdef1234", revert: "9999999", failingTests: ["a.test.ts", "b.test.ts"] }` and sees `/ · reverted abcdef12 \(failing: a\.test\.ts\)$/m` in the header (`shortSha` is 8 chars); a `RunDetail` with `reverted: null` renders exactly today's header (a second assertion, not a new test, that the `reverted` clause is the only difference).
- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts: the existing `handleRun` test's `assert.deepEqual(data, { ...detail, text, stat, revertSha, hasCommit })` stays green (both sides carry `reverted`); add one assertion that a run whose change was reverted serves `reverted.sha` equal to the culprit through `handleRun`.
- docs/invariants.md's INV-L1 section is unchanged: this plan adds no new writer of `main_revert` and no new revert rule, only a read of the existing event in the run-detail collector. Confirm the section needs no edit before finishing.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### `tumwater diff [-f/--follow]` repaints the pending-change view (the team roster, a role's change, or the `--overlaps` list) every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits, the last snapshot command's live twin (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; shares `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts` and `docs/cli.md` with the in-flight `tumwater report -f/--follow` entry — when that entry has landed this widens `followView` in `src/cli/follow-view.ts`, otherwise it widens the local helper and report rebases; the in-flight fast-merge, gateCommand and Codex entries edit src/merge, src/baseline, src/build, src/config, src/doctor, src/events, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent, none of them these files. Touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new) and src/cli/follow-view.ts only when it exists) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** `status`, `queue`, `backlog`, `report`, `logs` and `history` all have `-f/--follow`; `tumwater diff` is the last read-only query without a live form. An operator watching what roles hold pending — above all which files two roles both touch (`--overlaps`) — wants the same view to update as runs commit and land. Add `-f/--follow` to every `diff` shape: the team roster (no `--role`), one or more roles' change views (`--role`, composing with `--stat` and `--path`), and the `--overlaps` list (composing with `--role` and `--path`). Each frame repaints exactly the text the snapshot prints, every couple of seconds, until Ctrl+C or the parent process exits (the `status -f` rule). `--json` is refused — it prints one document — with the wording the sibling follow commands use.

**Approach.**

1. `followView` learns async frames. Widen its `frameText` seam from `() => string` to `() => string | Promise<string>`, make `frame` asynchronous (`const frame = async (): Promise<void> => { const text = await frameText(); process.stdout.write(tty ? "\x1b[H\x1b[2J" + text + "\n" : text + "\n\n"); }`), `await frame()` for the first paint, and drive the interval with `setInterval(() => { void frame(); }, interval)`. Guard against a slow read stacking frames with `let painting = false; if (painting) return; painting = true; try { … } finally { painting = false; }`. The sync callers (`cmdStatus`, `cmdQueue`, `cmdBacklog`, `cmdReport`) and their emitted bytes are unchanged, and the `startParentDeathWatch` end is untouched. Edit the helper where it lives: `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` today, or `src/cli/follow-view.ts` if the in-flight `tumwater report -f/--follow` entry has landed.
2. `cmdDiff` gains the flag and the seams. Signature becomes `export async function cmdDiff(root: string, args: string[], seams: FollowViewSeams = {}): Promise<void>` (cli.ts's call site passes no seams). Add `FOLLOW_FLAG` to its `rejectUnknownArgs` list, then after `requireReadyRepo`: `const follow = args.includes("-f") || args.includes("--follow");` and `if (follow && args.includes("--json")) fail("diff --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`.
3. Factor each shape's read into a thunk returning the view and its zero-arg `render`, used by both the follow frame and the snapshot, so a frame's text is exactly the snapshot's:
   - `--overlaps` (after the existing `--overlaps --stat` refusal, with `scope`/`path` already parsed): `const readOverlaps = async () => { let view = await collectChangeOverlaps(root); if (scope === null && path === undefined) return { view, render: () => renderChangeOverlaps(view) }; if (scope !== null) view = scopeChangeOverlaps(view, scope); if (path !== undefined) view = scopeChangeOverlapsToPath(view, path); return { view, render: () => renderChangeOverlaps(view, scope ?? undefined, path) }; };` then `if (follow) { await followView(async () => (await readOverlaps()).render(), seams); return; }` and the snapshot as `const { view, render } = await readOverlaps(); sayJsonOrRender(args, view, () => render());`.
   - The non-overlaps path, after `roles`/`path` are resolved: `readChange` returns the roster read (`collectTeamChanges` + `renderTeamChange`) with the existing `--stat needs --role` and `--path needs --role` refusals kept ahead of the read, the single-role read (`collectRoleChange` + `renderRoleChange`), or the multi-role read (`collectRoleChanges` + `renderRoleChanges`). The same `if (follow) { await followView(async () => (await readChange()).render(), seams); return; } ; const { view, render } = await readChange(); sayJsonOrRender(args, view, () => render());` shape.
   The `--json` payloads and every snapshot's output stay byte-identical.
4. `src/cli/help.ts` — add `[-f/--follow]` to the three `tumwater diff` stanza synopses (the roster stanza, the `--role` stanza, and the `--overlaps` stanza) and, after the roster stanza's description, one wrapped line: `-f/--follow repaints the same view every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent; it refuses --json;`.
5. `docs/cli.md` — in the `See a role's pending change` row, add the same `-f/--follow` sentence (the `status -f` wording), naming that it composes with `--role`, `--stat`, `--path` and `--overlaps` and refuses `--json`.

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts (cmdDiff, and `followView` while it is still local), src/cli/follow-view.ts (only when the report entry has landed), src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/cli-diff-follow.test.ts (new), driving `cmdDiff` in-process with the follow seams exactly as test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts drives `cmdQueue` (`makeRepo`, `initProject`, `ensureWorktree` + `commitIn` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js to seed a pending change; `captureStdout`/`expectFailAsync` from ./helpers/exit-capture.js; `sleep` from ./helpers/wait.js; a `withDiffFollow` wrapper that always flips the parent to 1 and restores stdout in `finally`):
  - "diff -f repaints the roster until its parent exits, then prints nothing": a seeded feature worktree holding one commit; run `["-f"]` with `{ ppid: () => parent, intervalMs: 5, tty: false }`; poll the capture (bounded loop, generous) until it holds at least two `feature: ` roster lines; flip the parent; the follow resolves and a fresh capture stays empty over a settle.
  - "diff -f --role repaints that role's change view": `["--role", "feature", "-f"]`; the capture holds `/1 commit ahead of main/` at least twice; it then stops.
  - "diff -f --overlaps repaints the shared-file list": two roles whose worktrees both touch `widget.md`; `["--overlaps", "-f"]`; the capture holds `/widget\.md: feature, feature-2/` at least twice.
  - "diff -f --json is refused": `expectFailAsync(() => cmdDiff(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` rejects matching `/diff --json prints one document/`, and the capture holds no frame and no clear-screen.
  - "diff -f clears the screen only on a TTY": with `tty: true` a frame starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; with `tty: false` the capture never contains it.
- test/cli-diff.test.ts passes unchanged: the roster, `--role`, `--stat`, `--path`, `--overlaps` and `--json` snapshot paths are untouched.
- test/status-follow.test.ts, test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts and test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts pass unchanged: the widened `followView` still emits the same frames for a sync frame text.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### `tumwater report` shows each day's run-duration median beside its merge-wait median, the authoring side of the fast-merge split (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the two in-flight follow entries widen `followView` in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts and edit docs/cli.md's watch/check rows, the in-flight merge-on-gate entry edits src/build, src/config and src/doctor, and the Codex parts edit src/gates, src/team, src/config, src/agent and src/report/report-render.ts (part 3/9, at the claude-window line, a different function, so whichever lands second rebases); this one edits src/report/report-fold.ts, src/report/report-types.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts, so docs/cli.md's report row is the only shared file with a waiting entry; touches src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-types.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/report/report-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts docs/cli.md test/report-data.test.ts test/report.test.ts test/gui-client-report.test.ts) — done 2026-10-22 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater report`'s team day view prints a per-day `**Merge wait median:**` (a `merge_done`'s enqueue-to-merged `queuedMs`), the pipeline half of plans/fast-merge.md's "Method", but has no authoring-side counterpart: the time a run itself took (`run_start` to `run_end`). Add `**Run duration median:**` per day beside it — the lower median of `run_end.durationMs`, the same duration `tumwater history <role> <n>` reports — and its dashboard Usage chart twin, so the fast-merge defaults and guardrails can be read day by day against the merge wait they moved work into. Team scope only, like the report's other per-day medians (`checkMedianMs`, `mergeWaitMedianMs`, `providerWaitMedianMs`, `slotWaitMedianMs`, `checkWaitMedianMs`); a role-scoped report and `report --since` (a totals-only render with no series) are unchanged, and a day with no `run_end` prints no line, so a run-free window's output is byte-identical.

**Approach.**
- src/report/report-fold.ts: `UsageFold` gains `/** ms of each run_end that carried a positive durationMs, unsorted — the day report's run-duration median beside its merge-wait median. */ runDurationsMs: number[];`. In `foldUsageEvent`'s `run_end` branch, after `const { tokens, costUsd, notionalCostUsd } = eventUsage(ev);`, add `const runMs = finiteNumber(ev.durationMs, 0); if (runMs > 0) target.runDurationsMs.push(runMs);` (a merge-slot run's `run_end` counts too, exactly as the day's `runsByRole` already includes it). Add `runDurationsMs: []` to both `UsageFold` literals: `dayFoldFor`'s per-day fold (src/report/report-fold.ts) and `collectReportSince`'s `acc` (src/report/report-data.ts), so the required field is complete on both collectors.
- src/report/report-types.ts: `ReportDay` gains `/** Lower median of the day's run durations (`run_end.durationMs`, ms); team-only like the other per-day medians, absent when the day has none. */ runMedianMs?: number;`.
- src/report/report-data.ts: in `collectReport`'s team branch (`bases === undefined`), beside the existing `if (fold.mergeWaitsMs.length > 0) day.mergeWaitMedianMs = lowerMedian(fold.mergeWaitsMs);`, add `if (fold.runDurationsMs.length > 0) day.runMedianMs = lowerMedian(fold.runDurationsMs);`. The role branch leaves it unset like every other median, so a role-scoped series carries no `runMedianMs`.
- src/report/report-render.ts: in the team block, immediately before the `Merge wait median` line, add `const runDurations = medianLine(data.series, "Run duration median", (d) => d.runMedianMs); if (runDurations !== undefined) lines.push(runDurations);`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts: add `function chartRunMedian(data) { return medianBarChart(data, "runMedianMs", "#14b8a6", "run duration"); }` beside `chartMergeWaitMedian`, and `function seriesHasRunMedian(data) { return seriesHasScalar(data, "runMedianMs"); }` beside `seriesHasMergeWaitMedian`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts: in the chart block's list, beside the Merge wait median `block(...)`, add `(seriesHasRunMedian(d) ? block("Run duration median", chartRunMedian(d), "per day · run_start to run_end") : "")`. `seriesHasRunMedian` already gates a role-scoped or run-free series off, so no `!d.role` guard is needed.
- docs/cli.md, the `tumwater report` row: in the sentence that names the per-day merge wait median, add the run-duration median beside it (team scope only, from `run_end.durationMs`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/report-data.test.ts: a new test, "collectReport gives each day the lower median of its run_end durationMs, team scope only", mirroring the merge-wait test. Write `run_end` events for one day with `durationMs` 10_000, 20_000 and 30_000 (lower median 20_000), one `run_end` with no `durationMs` (skipped, not zero), and one `merge_done` with a large `durationMs` (not a run). Assert `data.series[2]!.runMedianMs === 20_000`, that a day with only a duration-less `run_end` has no `runMedianMs` key, and that every day of `collectReport(root, 3, "feature")` has no `runMedianMs`.
- test/report.test.ts: a new test, "renderReportMarkdown prints Run duration median for the days that carry one, team scope only", mirroring the merge-wait render test: a two-day `ReportData` whose second day carries `runMedianMs: 95_000` renders `/^\*\*Run duration median:\*\* 09-10 95s$/m`; a series with no `runMedianMs` (and a `role: "feature"` variant) renders no such line.
- test/gui-client-report.test.ts: a new test, "the Run duration median chart draws one bar per timed day and seriesHasRunMedian gates it", mirroring the merge-wait chart test: `chartRunMedian` over `mkDay("2026-09-01", { runMedianMs: 95_000 })` and `mkDay("2026-09-03", { runMedianMs: 180_000 })` gives the titles `["2026-09-01: 95s median run duration", "2026-09-03: 3m median run duration"]` and the same label count as `chartCommits`; `seriesHasRunMedian` is false for days carrying only another median and true for the seeded series.

### `tumwater report -f/--follow` repaints the usage report (or, with `--failures`, the failure digest) every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits, the live twin of the dashboard Usage card and the TUI Usage and Failures panes (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; `tumwater queue -f/--follow` and `tumwater backlog -f/--follow` have landed and `followView` is still local to src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, so this lifts that loop into a new leaf module; the in-flight `tumwater diff -f/--follow` entry shares src/cli/follow-view.ts and src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, so whichever lands first, the other rebases the module and cli-query-commands.ts; the in-flight merge-on-gate and Codex parts edit src/build, src/config, src/doctor, src/events, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent, and Codex part 3/9 edits src/report/report-render.ts — none of them touches src/report/report.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md or test/report-follow.test.ts. Touches src/cli/follow-view.ts (new) src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/report/report.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/report-follow.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater status`, `tumwater queue`, `tumwater backlog`, `tumwater logs` and `tumwater history` have `-f/--follow`; `tumwater report` is the read-only snapshot without a live form (`tumwater diff -f/--follow` is planned separately). An operator watching spend, run counts, or the failure digest wants the same table to update as runs land, the way the dashboard's Usage card and the TUI's Usage and Failures panes already do. Add `-f/--follow` to the two day forms (`report` and `report --failures`): repaint the same text every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the parent process exits (the rule `status -f`, `queue -f`, `logs -f` and `history -f` use), composing with `--days` and `--role`. As with `history -f`, `--since` (and so `--until`) is refused — follow means the window that ends now, not a bounded past one — and `--json` is refused because it prints one document.

**Approach.** The report collectors are synchronous (`collectReport`, `collectFailureReport`), so the existing `followView(frameText: () => string, seams)` shape fits with no async rework.

1. Lift the repaint loop into a leaf module. `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` already holds it as the local `followView` (`followStatus` is only the thin `status -f` wrapper around it; the `queue -f`/`backlog -f` entries landed). Create `src/cli/follow-view.ts` and move that function there unchanged — header comment, `stripTerminalControls(frameText())` and all — exporting:
   - `export const FOLLOW_VIEW_INTERVAL_MS = 2000;`
   - `export interface FollowViewSeams { ppid?: () => number; intervalMs?: number; tty?: boolean; }`
   - `export async function followView(frameText: () => string, seams: FollowViewSeams): Promise<void>`, exactly the body at cli-query-commands.ts's `followView` today: `const tty = seams.tty ?? process.stdout.isTTY;`, `const interval = seams.intervalMs ?? FOLLOW_VIEW_INTERVAL_MS;`, the `frame()` that writes `stripTerminalControls(frameText())` as `tty ? "\x1b[H\x1b[2J" + text + "\n" : text + "\n\n"`, one immediate `frame()`, then the `setInterval` plus `startParentDeathWatch(() => { clearInterval(timer); resolve(); }, { …seams })` promise. It imports `startParentDeathWatch` from `../process/supervisor.js` and `stripTerminalControls` from `../text/text.js` (both leaf modules; no cycle). Its header comment says it is the repaint loop every `-f` view shares. If the in-flight `tumwater diff -f/--follow` entry landed first it has already widened `frameText` to `() => string | Promise<string>` and made `frame` async; move that widened version instead, so the diff entry need not rebase.
   - In `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, import `{ followView, type FollowViewSeams }` from `./follow-view.js`, drop the local interval constant, seams interface and `followView`, and drop the now-unused `startParentDeathWatch`/`stripTerminalControls` imports (each is used only inside `followView` today) while keeping `errorMessage` in the `../text/text.js` import. Keep `followStatus` as the call `followView(() => renderStatus(root, scope ? scopeSnapshotToRoles(snapshot(root), scope) : snapshot(root), tty ? process.stdout.columns : undefined, scope !== null), seams)`. `status -f`, `queue -f` and `backlog -f` emit the same frames.
2. src/report/report.ts: `cmdReport` gains the flag.
   - Signature becomes `export async function cmdReport(root: string, args: string[], seams: FollowViewSeams = {}): Promise<void>`; import `{ followView, type FollowViewSeams }` from `../cli/follow-view.js`.
   - After the role parse: `const follow = args.includes("-f") || args.includes("--follow");` and `if (follow && args.includes("--json")) fail("report --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`.
   - In the `ms !== null` branch, before its `--days` rival check: `if (follow) failRivalShapes("report --since", "-f/--follow", 'follow means "from now on"; --since shows a bounded past window');` — the exact `history -f` rule; `--until` can only ride `--since`, so it is covered.
   - After `days` is parsed and before the `--json` branches: `if (follow) { await followView(() => args.includes("--failures") ? renderFailureMarkdown(collectFailureReport(root, days, role ?? undefined)) : renderReportMarkdown(collectReport(root, days, role ?? undefined)), seams); return; }`. The frame string is exactly what the snapshot branch would `say`, so the snapshot forms keep today's bytes.
3. src/cli.ts, the `report` case's `rejectUnknownArgs` list: add `{ names: ["-f", "--follow"] }` (value-less; the case still does no ready-repo gate).
4. src/cli/help.ts: add `[-f/--follow]` to the first stanza's synopsis (`tumwater report [--days N] [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [-f/--follow] [--json]`) and, after that stanza's description, add `-f/--follow repaints the report, or with --failures the failure digest, every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent; it refuses --json and --since;`, wrapped to the stanza's column. Leave the three `--since`-shaped synopses alone.
5. docs/cli.md, the Audit row: in the `tumwater report` clause, immediately before the `tumwater report --json` clause, insert ``-f/--follow` on the day forms (`tumwater report`, `tumwater report --failures`) repaints that report every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent process exits (a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent, like `status -f`), and refuses `--json` and `--since`;`. Leave the other report clauses alone.

**Files touched.** src/cli/follow-view.ts (new), src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/report/report.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/report-follow.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/report-follow.test.ts (new), driving `cmdReport` in-process with the follow seams the way test/status-follow.test.ts drives `cmdStatus` and test/history-follow.test.ts drives `cmdHistory` (a `makeRepo()` repo — report has no ready-repo gate and its collectors degrade to zeros — `captureStdout`/`expectFailAsync` from ./helpers/exit-capture.js and `sleep` from ./helpers/wait.js):
  - "report -f repaints until its parent exits, then prints nothing": run `["-f"]` with `{ ppid: () => parent.value, intervalMs: 5, tty: false }`; poll the capture until it holds at least two `# tumwater usage report` headings; flip the parent to 1; the follow resolves and a fresh capture stays empty over a settle.
  - "report -f --failures repaints the failure digest": run `["--failures", "-f"]`; the frames match `/# tumwater failure digest/` at least twice.
  - "report -f --json is refused": `expectFailAsync(() => cmdReport(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` rejects matching `/report --json prints one document/`, and the capture holds no report heading and no clear-screen.
  - "report -f --since is refused": the same with `["-f", "--since", "1d"]`, rejecting matching `/report --since/`.
  - "report -f clears the screen only on a TTY": with `tty: true` the output starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; with `tty: false` it never contains that sequence.
- test/report.test.ts and the CLI report tests pass unchanged: the `--days`, `--failures`, `--since`/`--until`, `--role` and `--json` snapshot paths are untouched.
- test/status-follow.test.ts, test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts and test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts pass unchanged: the moved `followView` emits the same frames and `status -f` still refuses `--json`.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### Fast merge guardrails, part 2/3: `tumwater doctor` and the selfcheck digest warn on a revert that looks false and on more than 5 reverts a day (planned 2026-10-21 by user; requires part 1/3 landed; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Guardrails" G2; touches src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts src/baseline/main-revert.ts src/merge/merge-to-main.ts src/merge/merge-stack.ts src/events/events.ts src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts docs/how-it-works.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make a misfiring revert visible. Today a `main_revert` that blamed a flaky test, or that removed a change which later merged again unchanged with main green, leaves no trace beyond the event, and a burst of reverts reads the same as one.

**Approach.**
- Events: `main_revert` gains `patchId`, the culprit's (`patchId(wt, C^, C)` in `runMainRevert`, src/baseline/main-revert.ts). `merged` gains `patchId`, the merged commit's, on the single path (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts; `patchId(wt, mainBefore, commit)` computed after the fast-forward, so a conflict-resolved merge carries the resolved change's id too) and on the batch path (src/merge/merge-stack.ts, `patchId(root, sha^, sha)` per stacked entry). A failed patch-id omits the field. src/events/events.ts's comments for both types name it.
- src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts: `revertWarnings(events, quarantine, now)` with G2's two tests per `main_revert` in the last 24 h, and the rate test (more than 5). `guardrailWarnings` includes it, so the digest section from part 1/3 carries it.
- src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts `checkMainRed` adds the revert phrases to its row.
- docs/how-it-works.md: the revert bullet says what doctor warns about.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/main-revert.test.ts: a successful revert logs `main_revert` with the culprit's patch-id.
- test/merge-to-main.test.ts and test/merge-stack.test.ts: `merged` carries the merged commit's patch-id on both paths.
- test/main-guardrails.test.ts:
  - a revert naming test T, with T in quarantine with `lastSeen` after the revert, warns that the failure did not reproduce;
  - a later `merged` with the revert's `patchId`, then a passed `main_check` with `durationMs` > 0, warns that the change merged again unchanged and main stayed green;
  - the same with that `main_check` failed, or with a different `patchId`, or with no `patchId`, does not warn;
  - 6 reverts in 24 h warn naming 6; 5 do not.
- test/doctor-holds.test.ts: the "main's check" row carries a revert phrase.
- `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater backlog -f/--follow` repaints the backlog every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits, the snapshot command's live twin of the TUI Backlog pane and the dashboard Backlog card (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; shares src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts and the `tumwater backlog` clause of docs/cli.md with the in-flight `tumwater queue -f/--follow` entry ahead of this one in `## Planned` and reuses the `followView` helper that entry's step 1 introduces, so whichever lands second rebases there; the in-flight TUI Activity tally plan edits `sayTally` in src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/events/event-tally.ts, docs/cli.md's `logs --count` sentence and docs/how-it-works.md's Activity paragraph; the in-flight TUI Pending Ctrl+G plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts, test/tui-keys.test.ts and docs/how-it-works.md's Pending paragraph; the Codex parts edit src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent. Touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater backlog` prints the planned features, open bugs, and open questions once (`cmdBacklog`, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts), with `--ready` hiding the held entries and counting them and `--grep` filtering them. The dashboard's Backlog card and the TUI's Backlog pane repaint as the team claims and finishes entries, but the CLI snapshot has no live form. Add `-f/--follow`: repaint the same text every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the parent process exits (the rule `status -f`, `queue -f`, `logs -f` and `history -f` use), composing with `--ready` and `--grep` so each frame reflects the current backlog; `--json` is refused with a follow because it prints one document.

**Approach.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts unless named otherwise.

1. Share the follow loop: call `followView(frameText, seams)` and take its `FollowViewSeams` argument type (both are introduced by the `tumwater queue -f/--follow` entry ahead of this one in `## Planned`: its step 1 renames the local `StatusFollowSeams` to `FollowViewSeams`, renames `STATUS_FOLLOW_INTERVAL_MS` to `FOLLOW_VIEW_INTERVAL_MS`, and lifts `followStatus`'s body into `followView`). If that entry has not landed yet, do that extraction exactly as it prescribes first, then use the helper here; both live in this file already, so neither is exported for the test.
2. `cmdBacklog` gains the flag and the follow branch:
   - Reuse the shared follow flag beside `BACKLOG_GREP_VALUE_ERROR`: `rejectUnknownArgs("backlog", args, [JSON_FLAG, READY_FLAG, grepFlagSpec(BACKLOG_GREP_VALUE_ERROR), FOLLOW_FLAG])` (the same shared `FOLLOW_FLAG` `status`/`queue` gate).
   - Change the signature to `export async function cmdBacklog(root: string, args: string[], seams: FollowViewSeams = {}): Promise<void>` (cli.ts's call site passes no seams and needs no change).
   - Add `const follow = rest.includes("-f") || rest.includes("--follow");` (over `rest`, the `--grep` token removed, so a flag-shaped pattern like `--grep -f` greps for the literal "-f" rather than entering follow mode) and, beside the flag gate, `if (follow && rest.includes("--json")) fail("backlog --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`.
   - Factor today's `sayJsonOrRender` value thunk into `const readBacklog = () => { const view = { ...backlogPayload(root), holds: backlogHolds(root), inProgress: backlogInProgress(root) }; const filtered = pattern === null ? view : grepBacklog(view, pattern); if (!ready) return { view: filtered, hidden: 0 }; const kept = readyBacklog(filtered); return { view: kept, hidden: filtered.plans.length + filtered.bugs.length - kept.plans.length - kept.bugs.length }; };` and `const renderBacklogText = (r) => renderBacklogMarkdown(r.view) + (r.hidden > 0 ? \`\n\n_(${r.hidden} held entries hidden; run \\\`tumwater backlog\\\` to see them)_\` : "");`. The factored `readBacklog` reproduces the thunk's `view` and its `hidden` side effect exactly, so the render text is byte-identical to today's.
   - Before the snapshot, `if (follow) { await followView(() => renderBacklogText(readBacklog()), seams); return; }`. Then `const result = readBacklog(); sayJsonOrRender(rest, result.view, () => renderBacklogText(result));` — the `--json` branch prints `result.view`, the text branch `renderBacklogText(result)`, matching today.
3. src/cli/help.ts, the `tumwater backlog` stanza: synopsis becomes `tumwater backlog [--ready] [--grep <text>] [-f/--follow] [--json]`, and after the `--grep` sentence add `-f/--follow repaints the backlog every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent; it refuses --json;`. Wrap to the stanza's column.
4. docs/cli.md, the `tumwater backlog` clause of the "Check state" row: add `[-f/--follow]` to its synopsis and, after the `--grep` sentence, add ``-f/--follow` repaints the backlog every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent process exits (a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent, like `status -f` and `queue -f`); it refuses `--json` ``. Leave the surrounding clauses untouched.

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts (new), test/backlog-render.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/cli-backlog-follow.test.ts (new), driving `cmdBacklog` in-process with the follow seams the way test/status-follow.test.ts drives `cmdStatus` (a `makeRepo()` + `initProject` repo, PLANS.md seeded with `writeBacklogFile` and BUGS.md with `seedOpenBug` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, `captureStdout` from ./helpers/exit-capture.js, `sleep` from ./helpers/wait.js, and a `runFollow(t, repo, args, seams, waitForFrames, count, flipParent)` helper that mocks setInterval with `t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["setInterval"] })`, waits in real time only for the first synchronous frame (the readiness gate, a git read), then drives the repaint and parent-death cadence deterministically with `t.mock.timers.tick(5)` per frame, and `flipParent()` (setting the seam's `ppid` to 1) followed by one more tick makes the death-watch resolve the follow; a `finally` flips and ticks again so a failure never leaves the follow's interval running, and a final `tick(60_000)` asserts nothing repaints once the follow has ended):
  - "backlog -f repaints until its parent exits, then prints nothing": seed a `### Alpha (planned 2026-01-01 by operator)` plan entry and the open bug; run `["-f"]` at `intervalMs: 5` non-TTY (`tty: false`, so no clear-screen); once two frames have ticked, `cap.out()` matches `/Alpha/` at least twice and contains `/An open bug/`; `flipParent()` then the follow resolves and no further tick repaints.
  - "backlog -f --ready keeps only ready entries and names the hidden count": seed a held plan (`**Refused 2026-10-07 by feature: no**`) and a ready one; run `["--ready", "-f"]`; the frames match `/### Ready plan/`, never `/Refused plan/`, and end with the `_(\(\d+ held entries hidden; run `tumwater backlog` to see them\)_` note.
  - "backlog -f --grep keeps only matching entries": seed a matching and a non-matching heading; the frames match the match and never the other.
  - "backlog -f --json is refused": `expectFailAsync(() => cmdBacklog(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` rejects matching `/backlog --json prints one document/`, and the captured stdout has no backlog heading and no clear-screen.
  - "backlog --grep -f does not enter follow mode over its own pattern": running `cli(repo, "backlog", "--grep", "-f")` prints one matched snapshot frame and exits 0 (the pattern "-f" is read over `rest`, never consumed as the follow flag; it is bound by cli()'s 20 s run, so a hang fails the test).
  - "backlog -f clears the screen only on a TTY": with `tty: true` the output starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; with `tty: false` it never contains that sequence.
- test/backlog-render.test.ts's flag-gate and help-synopsis assertions are updated to name `-f/--follow` (the unknown-flag list, the `help backlog` synopsis and the `tumwater help` backlog row); the rest of the backlog tests pass unchanged: `tumwater backlog`, `--ready`, `--grep` and their `--json` forms print the same bytes as today (the factored `readBacklog` returns the same view and hidden count).
- test/status-follow.test.ts passes unchanged: the reused `followView` emits the same frames and still refuses `status -f --json`.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### A role's notes are shown beside the live backlog state of every entry and series they name, so a note cannot keep a hold the backlog has lifted (planned 2026-10-21 by user; independent of every eligible plan; the structural fix for BUGS.md "Role notes keep a hold belief after the hold is lifted", and it also gives BUGS.md "A refusal can rest on another entry's refusal …" the current state to check against; touches src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts (new) src/prompt/prompt.ts src/run/run-prompt.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/notes-backlog.test.ts (new) test/prompt.test.ts test/run-prompt.test.ts) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Role notes are free text, carried into every later run of the role and rewritten from the previous note. When a note states something about the backlog (an entry is refused, a series is dead, a part is done), nothing checks that claim again. On 2026-10-21, plan run 414 wrote "Codex 2b/9 carry Refused — never re-add or re-author them; the Codex theme is dead". Four minutes later both Refused notes became Needs-replan notes, which the plan role exists to act on, but its notes kept telling it to skip them, and the series stalled. feature-4's notes needed the same hand correction. Make every run prompt say what is currently true of each entry and series the notes name, next to the notes, so the live state wins without anyone editing a notes file.

**Approach.**
1. New pure module src/prompt/notes-backlog.ts: `notesBacklogBlock(notes, backlog)`.
   - `backlog` is `{ planned: BacklogEntry[], openBugs: BacklogEntry[], donePlanTitles: string[] }`.
   - It returns the block's text, or undefined when the notes name nothing live.
2. **What counts as naming a series.** For each series among the planned entries (`seriesPart` in src/backlog/backlog-parts.ts), its tokens are the full series name and, when no other live series shares it, its first word. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries.
   - A line that holds a token and a part ref `i/n` that is one of that series' parts names that part. "Codex 2b/9" names Codex backend, part 2b/9.
   - A token alone names the series. "the Codex theme" names the Codex backend series.
3. **What counts as naming a standalone entry or bug.** A line that contains, in order, the first six words of a planned entry's or Open bug's title (`entryKey` normalization) names that entry.
4. **The state of each named item.**
   - A planned entry or bug gets `entryHold` (src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts): `eligible`, `refused (only the operator clears it)`, `needs review`, `needs replan (the plan role rewrites it)`, `waiting for the next failure`, or `waits on <parts>`.
   - A part found in `donePlans` reads `done`. A part found nowhere reads `not in the backlog`.
   - A series gets one summary line: its planned-part count, how many need a replan or review, how many wait on an earlier part, and how many are refused.
5. **The block.** It is at most 12 lines, series first:
   `What the backlog says now about entries your notes name (PLANS.md and BUGS.md as of this run; where your notes disagree, this is current):`
   followed by one `- <name> — <state>` line each.
6. **src/prompt/prompt.ts.**
   - `roleNotesBlock`'s caption changes from "check against the code before relying on them" to "check against the code, and against the backlog state below, before relying on them".
   - `buildRunPrompt` takes an optional `notesBacklog` and pushes it right after the notes block.
7. **src/run/run-prompt.ts.** Where it reads `notes` (`readRoleNote`), it builds the backlog argument from `plannedPlanEntries(root)`, `openBugEntries(root)` and `donePlans(root)`, all of which are already stat-cached, and passes `notesBacklogBlock(notes, …)` through. The director carries no notes, so it gets no block.
8. **docs/how-it-works.md**, the notes paragraph: a run also sees the current backlog state of each entry and series its notes name, and that state wins where they disagree.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/notes-backlog.test.ts (new):
  - The 2026-10-21 plan.md lines against a PLANS.md where Codex backend parts 2b/9 and 6/9 carry Needs-replan notes, and parts 2c/9–9/9 require earlier parts, yield `Codex backend — 9 parts planned: 2 need a replan, 7 wait on an earlier part, none refused`, plus `Codex backend, part 2b/9 — needs replan (the plan role rewrites it)` and the same for 6/9.
  - "Codex" alone resolves to the Codex backend series only while no other live series starts with "Codex". With a second such series, the bare word names neither.
  - A part listed in PLANS-DONE.md reads `done`. A refused entry reads `refused (only the operator clears it)`.
  - Notes that name no live entry or series give undefined.
  - Forty named parts render at most 12 lines.
- test/prompt.test.ts: with notes and a `notesBacklog` block, the block follows `</role-notes>` and the caption mentions the backlog state. Without a block, the prompt equals today's apart from the caption.
- test/run-prompt.test.ts: a run whose notes file names a planned part gets the block; the director's prompt has none.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 2b/9: Window events are `subscription_window_*` with a `backend`, and the reserve is `backends.<id>.windowReserve` (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; requires part 1/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 2; touches src/events/events.ts src/events/event-legacy.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/events/notify.ts src/team/team-polls.ts src/gates/gate-polls.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/config/config-write.ts docs/config.md docs/backends.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** The four window events are named for claude and carry no backend, and the only reserve key is the top-level `claudeWindowReserve`. Rename them to `subscription_window_{warning,reserved,limited,reset}`, each with a `backend: string` field (`"claude"` today), and let `backends.<id>.windowReserve` hold a reserve while `claudeWindowReserve` keeps working as claude's older spelling. Crucially the new key is live at the end of THIS part, not dead until part 2c: every production reader of `claudeWindowReserve` switches to `windowReserveFor(config, "claude")` here (part 2c generalizes the literal). No behavior change for a claude-only team. The TUI and GUI reserve editors and `config-editable-keys` are deliberately untouched — `claudeWindowReserve` stays a valid editable key and those editors keep writing it, so this rename does not span them.

**Approach.**
- Events. src/events/events.ts: rename the four union members (keeping their payload comments) and add `backend: string` to each. src/events/event-labels.ts: rename the four keys; their labels are backend-neutral ("usage window reserved", "waiting: usage window"). src/events/event-format.ts: rename the four cases and name the backend from the event through a small `backendLabel(e.backend)` helper that maps `"claude"` to `"claude"` and any other id to itself, so a claude-only team's lines read exactly as today. src/events/event-legacy.ts's `normalizeLegacyEvent` maps each old `claude_window_*` name to its new one with `backend: "claude"`. src/events/notify.ts renames its two defaulted entries.
- Emitters. src/team/team-polls.ts and src/gates/gate-polls.ts use the new names and write a literal `backend: "claude"` on each event. They do NOT gain a `backend` parameter — part 2c adds one when a second backend exists, so this part leaves no half-used parameter for 2c to redo. `loggedWindowKeys(root, type, now)` (src/team/team-polls.ts) reads each event's own `backend` (falling back to `"claude"` for an event written before this rename) and keys by `${backend}:${windowType}:${resetsAt}`; src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts passes the two new type names.
- Config. `BackendConfig` (src/config/config-schema.ts) gains `windowReserve?: Record<string, number>`, and `CLAUDE_AGENT_KEYS` gains `"windowReserve"` — claude only now (part 4/9 adds it for codex), so pi and opencode still refuse it as an unknown key. src/config/config-validation.ts validates each `backends.claude.windowReserve` value with the existing `0 < f <= 1` rule and rejects a file that holds both `claudeWindowReserve` and `backends.claude.windowReserve`, naming both. src/config/config-views.ts exports `windowReserveFor(config, backend)`: `backends[backend].windowReserve`, else `claudeWindowReserve` when `backend === "claude"`, else undefined.
- Live wiring. Replace the three direct `claudeWindowReserve` reads — src/gates/gate-polls.ts (`pollTeamHold` and `pollClaudeWindowReserve`) and src/gates/budget-gates.ts (`claudeWindowUsedUp`) — with `windowReserveFor(liveConfig, "claude")`, so the nested key drives the same reserve hold, the same `subscription_window_reserved` event and the same budget window move.
- Write path. src/config/config-write.ts's `setConfigKey`: setting `claudeWindowReserve` deletes `backends.claude.windowReserve`, and setting `backends.claude.windowReserve` deletes `claudeWindowReserve`, mirroring the `agentBin`/`piArgs` single-spelling arms, so a supported `config set` never writes the rejected pair; `validateConfig` (which `writeConfigMutation` already runs before writing) still refuses a hand-edited file that holds both.
- Docs. docs/config.md: the `backends` row names `backends.claude.windowReserve`, and the `claudeWindowReserve` row reads "The older top-level spelling of `backends.claude.windowReserve`; either may be set, but not both." docs/backends.md's "Reserve." paragraph gets the same full sentence, with the nested spelling as the current one.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/notify.test.ts, test/event-format-team.test.ts, test/gate-polls.test.ts and test/team-polls.test.ts pass with the new names and the added `backend`; the event-format lines for a `backend: "claude"` event render the same text as today's `claude_window_*` lines.
- `normalizeLegacyEvent({ type: "claude_window_limited", … })` yields `subscription_window_limited` with `backend: "claude"`; `tumwater logs --type claude_window_limited` still finds old lines.
- `loggedWindowKeys` returns one key per `backend:type:resetsAt`: two still-open windows whose types and `resetsAt` match but whose `backend` differ produce two keys, and a `backend: "codex"` warning does not suppress claude's own key.
- The nested key is live: a test with `backends.claude.windowReserve: { "seven_day": 0.8 }` and no `claudeWindowReserve` counts that window used up and logs `subscription_window_reserved { backend: "claude" }`, exactly as `claudeWindowReserve` did before this part.
- `windowReserveFor` reads the nested claude key, falls back to `claudeWindowReserve`, and returns undefined for a backend with neither; both keys set is a load error naming both; `backends.pi.windowReserve` is refused as an unknown key.
- A `config set` of either reserve spelling over a config holding the other leaves only the set spelling on disk, with no error; a hand-written file holding both fails `loadConfig`.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### Codex backend, part 6/9: The Codex stream translator and the rollout reader, with fixtures from the H1 captures (planned 2026-10-20 by user; independent of parts 1/9–5/9; design in plans/codex-backend.md "The stream translator and the rollout read that completes it" and "Findings, verified live" 3–5, 11, 15, 18, 19, 23 and 24; touches src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts (new) src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts (new) src/agent/agent-backend.ts test/fixtures/codex-events.ts (new) and their tests; reads test/fixtures/codex-captures/) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Translate `codex exec --json` into tumwater's canonical stream, and read the rollout file for what the stream lacks: this run's own token usage, the billing and the two usage windows. Both are pure over text, so the adapter (part 7/9) only wires them in.

**Approach.**
- src/agent/agent-backend.ts: `StreamTranslator` gains an optional `sessionId?(): string | undefined`, the backend session id once the stream has named it. This part only declares it; part 7/9's run-agent reads it.
- src/agent/codex/codex-stream.ts (new): `codexTranslator()`, which follows design §5's table row by row.
  - `bash` tool calls carry the inner command with the `/bin/zsh -lc` (or `bash -lc`) wrapper and its quoting removed.
  - A `command_execution`'s `aggregated_output` reaches `tool_execution_end` capped at `outputLimits(window).bash` (src/pi-extension/bounded-output.ts; 16,000 characters at 128k and above): head and tail around a marker naming the cut. The stream can carry a megabyte (design finding 18).
  - A `file_change` becomes one `edit` toolCall per changed path, `{path, kind}`, with `isError` when its `status` is not `completed`.
  - A `command_execution` still open at `turn.completed` is closed with `tool_execution_end {isError: true}` and the result "abandoned: the run ended while this command was still running", and `codex_command_abandoned` is warned once (design finding 19).
  - Repeated `error` items warn once per distinct message.
  - "Reconnecting... n/m" becomes `auto_retry_start`.
  - `turn.failed` is parsed through its JSON-string message to `status`, `error.type` / `code` and the message text, and classified per §5's table. The classifier tests the context-window signal **before** the generic 400 `invalid_request_error` branch (as src/agent/claude/claude-stream.ts's `classifyResult` tests "prompt is too long" before `CONFIG_STATUS`): a `context_window_exceeded` code, or a 400 whose message names the context window, is `contextExceeded`, never `configError`.
  - `item.started` and `item.completed` for `todo_list` and `web_search` are dropped silently: no canonical event and no `warnings()` entry, matching design §5's `item.*` row.
  - `finalize()` reports "codex exited without finishing its turn" when the stream saw neither `turn.completed` nor `turn.failed`.
  - `warnings()` lists unmapped event and item types once each, plus `codex_usage_partial` when the adapter flags it.
  - `turnCompletedUsage()` returns the stream's own figure, for the fallback.
- src/agent/codex/codex-rollout.ts (new):
  - `findRollout(home, id)` returns the path of `sessions/**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`, or null. It takes no third parameter and does no date math: it walks the `sessions` tree, matching file names that end with `-<id>.jsonl`. (Earlier text promised walking "the date dirs from the run's start date onward", but a `(home, id)`-only function has no reliable start date, and Codex's rollout name carries local time rather than UTC (finding 5), so a UTC-derived date bound can miss the file. The tree is one directory per active day, so the walk stays small; only the id match decides.)
  - `rolloutLines(text, {sinceTurnStart, requestedModel})` reads only the records after this run's `task_started`. It returns the canonical `run_usage`, `billing` and `rate_limit` lines of design §5, or [] when the turn's records are missing or malformed. A turn with no `token_count` (a killed run, design finding 23) yields `run_usage` without any `rate_limit`.
  - When the turn's `turn_context.model` differs from `requestedModel`, it also reports `{switchedTo: <model>}` so the adapter can warn `codex_model_switched` (design finding 24).
  - It never returns or logs `session_meta` fields.
- test/fixtures/codex-events.ts (new): loaders for the scrubbed captures in test/fixtures/codex-captures/ (its README.md maps each file to a finding), plus small builders for what no capture has:
  - a used-up window, built from the binary's message ("You've hit your usage limit. … Try again at …") and a `usage_limit_reached` code;
  - a `turn_context` whose model differs from the requested one.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/codex-stream.test.ts (new):
  - edit-run.jsonl yields `session`, `agent_start`, a `message_end` with text, an `edit` toolCall for `/work/repo/a.txt` with its start and end, then a `bash` toolCall whose `command` is `cat a.txt && git status --short` (not the `/bin/zsh -lc` form), with its start and end.
  - oversized-output.jsonl: the `tool_execution_end` result is at most 16,000 characters plus the marker, and keeps the first and last lines.
  - abandoned-command.jsonl: the open `sleep 90; echo ok` call is closed as an error before the final message, and `warnings()` holds `codex_command_abandoned` once.
  - long-command.jsonl: one call open for the whole run, closed with exit code 0.
  - Fed through `PiStreamParser`, the final text is the last agent message.
  - `sessionId()` is undefined before `thread.started` and the thread id after.
  - Classification: unknown-model.jsonl is `configError`; not-logged-in.jsonl is `configError` and its nine reconnect lines are nine `auto_retry_start`; the built used-up window is `transientRateLimit` with a `rejected` `five_hour` reading and `retryAfterSeconds`; a built 400 `invalid_request_error` carrying `context_window_exceeded` (or a message naming the context window) is `contextExceeded`, not `configError`.
  - Synthetic `item.started` and `item.completed` events for `todo_list` and `web_search` produce no canonical events and add nothing to `warnings()`.
  - sigterm-mid-command.jsonl, which ends after `item.started` with no turn event, finalizes to an error message.
  - An unknown item type is listed once in `warnings()`.
- test/codex-rollout.test.ts (new), on edit-run-and-resume-rollout.jsonl:
  - The first turn's `run_usage.input` is its last `turn_token_usage.input_tokens − cached_input_tokens`. The second turn's (the resume) is its own turn figure, not the thread total.
  - A `requestedModel` other than `gpt-6-luna` reports the switch.
  - The 300- and 10080-minute windows map to `five_hour` and `seven_day`, with `utilization` 0 and `resetsAt` the capture's `resets_at`.
  - `billing` is `subscription`.
  - `findRollout` finds a rollout placed at `sessions/2026/10/21/rollout-<time>-<id>.jsonl` from `home` and `id` alone, and returns null for an unknown id.
  - A truncated file yields [].
  - The output contains no `creator_user_id` or `creator_account_id` value.
- `npm test` passes.

### Fast merge guardrails, part 1/3: `tumwater doctor` and the selfcheck digest warn when main stays red over 30 minutes and when quarantine holds a test over 3 days or more than 10 tests (planned 2026-10-21 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Guardrails" G1, G3 and "Where the warnings show"; touches src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts (new) src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts src/run/selfcheck-digest.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts docs/how-it-works.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Make two quiet failures of the post-merge machinery visible: main staying red while merges go on, and quarantine growing or keeping a test long enough to hide it. Today the "main's check" row only names roles the red-main gate holds, and since roles keep working on a red main with known failures, it reads "no role waiting on main's check" while main is red. Nothing reads quarantine.json's age or size.

**Approach.**
- src/baseline/main-guardrails.ts (new), pure and synchronous:
  - `redMainWarning(events, now)`: G1's rule over the last 24 h of events. Only `main_check` events with `durationMs` > 0 and `main_red_hold` events count; a pass with `quarantined` tests is a pass. Returns the phrase, or null when main is green or red for 30 minutes or less.
  - `quarantineWarning(entries, now)`: G3's rule over `loadQuarantine` (src/review/known-flakes.ts). Returns the phrase naming the count when over 10 and the oldest tests over 3 days (age, BUGS.md heading or "not filed"), or null.
  - `guardrailWarnings(root, now)`: both phrases that fire, reading `readEventsSince(root, DAY_MS)` and quarantine.json. Each phrase is bounded (`squash`, as the doctor rows do).
- src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts `checkMainRed`: warns when roles are held, when `redMainWarning` fires, or both, joining the phrases in one row. Its ok detail is unchanged.
- src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts `checkFlakyChecks`: warns when today's flake count does or `quarantineWarning` fires; ok/warn only, as today.
- src/run/selfcheck-digest.ts: `selfcheckDigest` appends `## Fast merge guardrails` with one line per warning from `guardrailWarnings`, and nothing when none fires. A throw there drops only the section, never the digest.
- src/roles/role-catalog.ts, selfcheck's charter: a line under `## Fast merge guardrails` is tumwater's own response failing (rule 1), so it is fileable as it stands.
- docs/how-it-works.md: the main watch and quarantine bullets say what doctor warns about.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/main-guardrails.test.ts (new), on synthetic events with an injected `now`:
  - a `main_red_hold` 31 min ago warns, naming its sha and 31 min; 29 min ago does not;
  - that hold followed by a passed `main_check` with `durationMs` 0 still warns; followed by one with `durationMs` 120000, it does not;
  - a pass 60 min ago, then reds 40 and 20 min ago, warns "for 40 min";
  - a passed `main_check` carrying `quarantined` ends the red;
  - reds and no pass in the 24 h reads "more than 24 h".
- Quarantine: an entry with `firstSeen` 4 days ago warns with its age and heading; with `bug: ""` it says "not filed"; 11 fresh entries warn naming 11; 10 fresh entries do not.
- test/doctor-holds.test.ts: `checkMainRed` warns on a 31-min red with no role held, and gives one row with both phrases when roles are held too.
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts: `checkFlakyChecks` keeps its flake results and warns on an old quarantine entry.
- test/selfcheck-digest.test.ts: a 31-min red puts `## Fast merge guardrails` and the phrase at the digest's end; a green main leaves no such heading.
- `npm test` passes.

### Dashboard History gains a Newest failure button that opens the team's newest failing run, the `history --last --result problems` twin (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the TUI Inbox `/` search plan and the TUI Transcript change step Ctrl+Y plan change only src/ui/tui, src/inbox and docs/cli.md's TUI keys table. This plan changes only src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, test/gui-client-history.test.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and docs/cli.md's History row. Touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/cli.md) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history --last --result problems` opens the team's newest failing run in one command (PLANS-DONE.md "`history <role> --last --result <class>[,…]`"), and `GET /api/run?last=1&result=problems` with no role serves exactly that run (PLANS-DONE.md "`GET /api/run?last=1` with no role…", whose own text says "A dashboard button that uses it is a separate, later plan"). The dashboard's History view has Summary / By model modes, an outcome filter, and a per-row drill-down, but no way to jump to the newest failure: the operator must guess the role and scroll. Add a **Newest failure** button that opens that run's detail card above the table, regardless of the current role, window or count. It is the dashboard twin of the CLI command and the last missing consumer of the role-less `last` endpoint.

**Approach.** Everything below is in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts unless named otherwise.
1. Toolbar: in `buildHistoryView`, add `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' id='histnewest'>Newest failure</button>` immediately before the `#histrefresh` button, and wire `$("histnewest").addEventListener("click", () => openHistNewest());` beside the refresh listener.
2. State and fetch, all inside the `// history-detail:start` … `// history-detail:end` region (so `clientScope` over `HISTORY_REGIONS` reaches them):
   - Add `let histNewest = null;` beside `const histDetails = new Map();`.
   - `async function openHistNewest()`: set `histNewest = { state: "loading" }`, call `renderHistory()`; `const d = await getJson("/api/run?last=1&result=problems")`; reject a body without a string `text` or string `role` with the same "answered … without a text field" sentence the drill-down fetch uses, naming the endpoint and the run; then `const key = histDetailKey(d.role, d.run)`, `histDetails.set(key, { state: "ok", text: d.text, stat: typeof d.stat === "string" ? d.stat : "", revertSha: typeof d.revertSha === "string" ? d.revertSha : null, hasCommit: d.hasCommit === true })`, and `histNewest = { state: "ok", key }`. Catch → `histNewest = { state: "error", message: err && err.message ? err.message : "Newest failure unavailable" }`. Always end with `renderHistory()`. (The entry's real `role#run` key is what makes the card's own patch/transcript/revert buttons work: `toggleHistPatch`, `toggleHistTranscript`, `searchHistTranscript` and `histRevertStep` all look the entry up with `histDetails.get(key)` and parse the role and run back out of that key, exactly as they do for a row card.)
   - `function closeHistNewest()`: `histNewest = null; renderHistory();`
   - `function histNewestHtml()`: return `""` when `histNewest` is null; for `state: "loading"` return `<div class='empty'>Loading newest failure…</div>`; for `state: "error"` return `<div class='empty'><strong>Newest failure unavailable</strong>` + `esc(histNewest.message)` + `</div>`; for `state: "ok"` return `<div class='hist-newest'><div class='hist-detail-head mono'>Newest failure of any role <button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-hist-newest-close='1' title='Close'>×</button></div>` + `histDetailCardHtml(histDetails.get(histNewest.key), histNewest.key)` + `</div>`. Reuse the existing `hist-detail` / `hist-detail-head` classes so no CSS change is needed.
3. Render: change `renderHistory`'s innerHTML line to `body.innerHTML = historyNoteHtml(histNote) + historyStepHtml(histSinceKey, histStep) + histNewestHtml() + bodyHtml;`, so the pinned card sits above the window note's table.
4. Close and reset: add one more `$("histbody")` delegated click listener for `button[data-hist-newest-close]` that calls `closeHistNewest()`. In `fetchHistory`, set `histNewest = null;` beside `histDetails.clear();` so a refresh or a role/window/count change drops the pinned card together with the drill-down cache, like the row cards.
5. Docs: docs/how-it-works.md, in the dashboard History drill-down paragraph (the one that ends with the `GET /api/history?result=` sentence), add: "A Newest failure button opens the newest failing run of any role through `GET /api/run?last=1&result=problems`, the run `tumwater history --last --result problems` opens, as a card above the table." docs/cli.md, end of the "Watch run history" row: after "clicking a model in By model lists its runs, the `--model` twin" add "; its Newest failure button opens the newest failing run of any role, the `history --last --result problems` twin".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/gui-client-history.test.ts, new test "the Newest failure button loads the newest failing run as a pinned card": a `clientScope` over `HISTORY_REGIONS` exposing `openHistNewest`, `histNewest`, `histDetails`, `histNewestHtml`, `closeHistNewest`, with a recording `getJson` answering `{ role: "clean", run: 9, text: "clean run #9 — problems · 46s\nevent one", stat: " a.ts | 2 +-", revertSha: null, hasCommit: true }` and a `renderHistory` stub. Before the call `histNewestHtml()` is `""`. `openHistNewest()` synchronously makes `histNewest.state === "loading"` and the html match `/Loading newest failure/`. After `await sleep(0)`, the sole call is `/api/run?last=1&result=problems`, `histNewest.state === "ok"`, `histDetails.get("clean#9").state === "ok"`, and the html matches `/Newest failure of any role/`, `/event one/`, `/hist-detail-stat/` + `/a\.ts \| 2 \+-/`, `/data-hist-patch='clean#9'/` and `/data-hist-newest-close='1'/`. `closeHistNewest()` sets `histNewest` null and the html back to `""`.
- Same file, new test "a Newest failure miss renders the server's message instead of a stuck loading state": `getJson` rejects with `Error('no completed run with result "problems" in the scanned window (the retained log may have rotated past it)')`; after `await sleep(0)` `histNewest.state === "error"` and `histNewestHtml()` matches `/Newest failure unavailable/` and the message and not `/Loading newest failure/`.
- Same file, the toolbar test: `GUI_CLIENT_HISTORY_JS` contains `id='histnewest'` with the label `Newest failure`, and wires its click to `openHistNewest` (`/id='histnewest'[\s\S]*?openHistNewest/`).
- Same file, extend the whole-blob `historyFetchScope` harness (or a sibling) to also return `histNewest`, and assert `fetchHistory(false)` resets a previously set `histNewest` to null. (The harness runs the served blob with injected `getJson`/`renderHistory`; set `histNewest = { state: "error", message: "x" }` through returned state, then `await scope.fetchHistory(false)`.)
- The existing History tests pass unchanged: the drill-down toggle/caching tests, `histDetailCardHtml`, `fetchHistory`, and the toolbar/search persistence tests. `npm run test:gate` is green.

### Fast merge guardrails, part 3/3: The event log keeps five rotated generations instead of one (planned 2026-10-21 by user; independent of parts 1/3 and 2/3, sharing src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts with part 1/3 and src/events/events.ts with part 2/3 at other functions; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Guardrails" G4; touches src/files/files.ts src/events/events.ts src/paths.ts src/events/event-window.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts docs/config.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** Stop losing history at every rotation. events.jsonl rotates at 16 MB into events.jsonl.1 and the next rotation deletes it. The first rotation, on 2026-10-20, put 2026-08-20 → 2026-10-20 into events.jsonl.1; the next, about a week later, deletes it. The guardrails' 24 h windows do not need more, but every by-hand audit of the team does.

**Approach.**
- src/files/files.ts: `rotateIfLarge(file, maxBytes, keep = 1)`. Over the size it removes `<file>.<keep>`, renames `.<k-1>` → `.<k>` from oldest to newest, then the file to `.1`. Missing generations are skipped. With `keep` 1 it behaves as today, so role pi logs (src/agent/run-agent.ts) are unchanged.
- src/events/events.ts: `EVENTS_KEEP = 5` beside `EVENTS_MAX_BYTES`, passed by `logEvent`. `eventsRotationLabel()` reads "rotated at 16 MB, 5 kept".
- src/paths.ts: `eventsArchivePath(root, generation = 1)`; its comment no longer says one archive.
- src/events/event-window.ts: `readWindowEvents` continues into `.2`…`.5` while no file read so far covers the window, prepending each older file's events. `coversFullWindow` follows the same rule. `eventLogState` still reads the live file and `.1`.
- src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts `checkEventLog`: the ok detail adds "history from <date>, <n> files", from the first complete line of the oldest generation present.
- docs/config.md: the `logMaxBytes` row covers role logs only and says the event log rotates at a fixed 16 MiB and keeps five generations.

**Acceptance criteria.**
