### README and every GitHub release open with a token-consumption warning, so nobody enables the team without knowing it burns tokens continuously (planned 2026-10-21 by the director role; independent of every eligible plan: the three in-flight follow-mode/doctor plans edit src/cli, src/ui/tui, src/merge and src/doctor; the Codex series edits src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent, and its part 9/9 README change is the Backends paragraph, not the top of the file. None touches test/packaging.test.ts or .github/workflows/release.yml. Touches README.md .github/workflows/release.yml test/packaging.test.ts) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

> Note: the acceptance criterion pins `/### ⚠️ …/` in raw README, so the README blockquote uses `> ### ⚠️`; release.yml keeps the approach copy's `> ## ⚠️` (its test pins only the billion figure and `--notes`).

**Goal.** A user can install tumwater, read the README, or read any GitHub release's notes without being told that the team runs models continuously and consumes tokens at a scale that is easy to underestimate. Put one prominent warning at the very top of README.md and prepend the same warning to every GitHub release's auto-generated notes, so the cost is stated before the install line and before the changelog. The amount the user named is on the order of a billion tokens a day or more; both copies must say that figure and name `tumwater report` and `maxDailyCostUsd` as the ways to see and cap it.

**Approach.**

1. README.md — insert this exact block between the `# tumwater` H1 (line 1) and the intro paragraph that begins `tumwater is an opinionated autonomous development team`, with one blank line on each side, so it is the first thing under the title and above the npm install line:

   ```
   > ## ⚠️ Warning: tumwater eats tokens
   >
   > tumwater runs models continuously, all day, on every role. A busy team can burn through
   > **on the order of a billion tokens a day or more**. On pay-per-token API keys that is real,
   > unbounded money; on subscription backends it burns through your plan's usage windows just as
   > fast. Set `maxDailyCostUsd` before you start, and watch actual spend with `tumwater report`
   > and `tumwater status`.
   ```

   Do not touch the brief block between `<!-- tumwater:prompt:start -->` and `<!-- tumwater:prompt:end -->`; the warning goes above it. README.md is in the package's `files` allowlist (test/packaging.test.ts), so the same warning reaches npmjs.com — plain blockquote Markdown is used deliberately instead of GitHub's `> [!WARNING]` alert syntax, which npm renders literally as `[!WARNING]`.
2. .github/workflows/release.yml — in the `Attach the packed tarball to a GitHub release` step, add a `RELEASE_WARNING: |` block scalar to the step's `env:` holding the warning below, and add `--notes "$RELEASE_WARNING"` to the `gh release create` arguments, keeping `--generate-notes` and `--title`. `gh release create --help` documents that `--notes` is prepended to automatically generated notes, so the warning leads every release body and the generated changelog follows it:

   ```yaml
   RELEASE_WARNING: |
     > ## ⚠️ Warning: tumwater eats tokens
     >
     > tumwater runs models continuously, all day, on every role. A busy team can burn through
     > **on the order of a billion tokens a day or more**. Set `maxDailyCostUsd` before you
     > start, and watch actual spend with `tumwater report`.
   ```

   The existing `gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --generate-notes tumwater-*.tgz` line becomes `gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --generate-notes --notes "$RELEASE_WARNING" tumwater-*.tgz`. No `scripts/release.mjs` change: that script never creates the GitHub release; the workflow does.
3. test/packaging.test.ts — the file already reads both workflow YAMLs and pins their invariants, so pin both warnings there rather than adding a test file. Keep the existing two workflow tests unchanged.

**Files touched.** README.md, .github/workflows/release.yml, test/packaging.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/packaging.test.ts, "the README leads with the token warning": read `../../README.md`, and assert the block matches `/### ⚠️ Warning: tumwater eats tokens/`, matches `/billion tokens a day or more/`, and that its index is greater than the index of `# tumwater` and less than the index of `<!-- tumwater:prompt:start -->`, so the warning cannot drift below the intro or into the brief.
- New test in test/packaging.test.ts, "every release prepends the token warning": read `../../.github/workflows/release.yml`, and assert the text matches `/--generate-notes/`, matches `/--notes "\$RELEASE_WARNING"/`, and matches `/billion tokens a day or more/`, so removing `--generate-notes`, detaching the warning env var, or dropping the billion figure fails the gate.
- README.md and release.yml carry the warning copy verbatim as written above; `npm test` passes and test/docs-links.test.ts stays green (the warning adds no link).
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### `tumwater doctor` gains a `merge-queue files` row that warns and names every durable-queue file the reader skips, so a stranded queue entry is a health signal instead of a count on one command's output (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the in-flight `tumwater queue -f/--follow` and `tumwater backlog -f/--follow` entries edit src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md; the in-flight TUI Activity tally plan edits src/ui/tui and src/cli/log-commands.ts; the Codex parts edit src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent. None touches src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts or test/doctor.test.ts. Touches src/merge/merge-queue.ts src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `readMergeQueue` (src/merge/merge-queue.ts) reads every queue file once and skips any that is torn, foreign, or vanished mid-listing, counting them in `MergeQueueView.unreadable`; `tumwater queue` prints a trailing line counting the files it skipped (`merge-queue-render.ts`) and the status badge folds the count into the queue depth. The drain repairs only an unreadable *head* (`staleHeadFile`), so a skipped file that sorts after a healthy entry stays in `.tumwater/merge-queue/` forever. Nothing calls it out by name or level: the `stale merge-queue entries` doctor row reads only readable entries and `merge lock` only the lock. Add a `merge-queue files` row that warns and names each skipped file, so a stranded queue entry is visible to `tumwater doctor` (and `doctor --problems`) instead of only as a number on one command's output.

**Approach.**

1. src/merge/merge-queue.ts: add `export function unreadableMergeQueueFiles(root: string): string[]` beside `readMergeQueue`, returning the full paths of every file `queueFiles(root)` lists whose `readEntry` is null, in filename order. One doc comment: it names the files `readMergeQueue` counts, through the same skip policy, so the count and the list cannot drift.
2. src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts: add `export function checkMergeQueueFiles(root: string): CheckOutcome` immediately after `checkStaleQueuedMerges`. `const files = unreadableMergeQueueFiles(root);`; empty → `okOutcome("the queue reader skips no merge-queue file")`. Otherwise `const [first, ...rest] = files;` and `warnOutcome` with the detail `the merge queue holds ${plural(files.length, "file")} the reader skips — ${path.relative(root, first)}${andMore(rest, (f) => path.relative(root, f), "file(s)")}; a torn or foreign file is never drained, so nothing ages it or surfaces its merge — remove it (a crashed enqueue's merge ref still recovers on the next run)`. Warn, never fail, like `checkStaleQueuedMerges` and the module's other document checks. Add `unreadableMergeQueueFiles` to the existing `../merge/merge-queue.js` import; `path`, `plural`, `andMore`, `okOutcome` and `warnOutcome` are already imported. Extend the module header's list ("… stale queued merges, stale queued prompts …") with the files the queue reader skips, and give the check a header comment saying why it exists: `tumwater queue` counts the skips but does not name them, and the drain drops only an unreadable head, so a non-head skip is otherwise silent.
3. src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts: add `"merge-queue files"` to `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` immediately after `"stale merge-queue entries"`.
4. src/doctor/doctor.ts: add `checkMergeQueueFiles` to the `./doctor-backlog.js` import list and add `{ name: "merge-queue files", run: () => checkMergeQueueFiles(root) }` immediately after the `stale merge-queue entries` row.

No docs/invariants.md change: the new row is read-only and changes no guarantee (INV-AG1, the queue-file listing rules, is untouched). No docs/cli.md change: no user-facing doc enumerates the doctor rows.

**Files touched.** src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor-check-names.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/doctor-backlog.test.ts: widen the existing `../src/merge/merge-queue.js` import to `{ enqueueMerge, queuedMergeFiles, readMergeQueue, unreadableMergeQueueFiles }` and import `checkMergeQueueFiles` from `../src/doctor/doctor-backlog.js`; add a `checkMergeQueueFiles` block after the `checkStaleQueuedMerges` block, reusing its `queueRoot()` and `advice()` helpers:
  - "checkMergeQueueFiles reads ok for an absent, an empty, and an all-readable queue": a bare `tmpdir("doctor-merge-queue-files-")` → `ok`; `queueRoot()` → `ok`; `queueRoot()` plus `enqueueMerge(root, advice("improve", "tidy parser"))` → `ok`.
  - "checkMergeQueueFiles warns naming every file the reader skips": `queueRoot()` plus one `enqueueMerge`, then `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(mergeQueueDir(root), "000-torn.json"), '{"role":')` and `fs.writeFileSync(path.join(mergeQueueDir(root), "999-foreign.json"), '{"nope":true}')`. The outcome is `warn`; its detail contains `000-torn.json`, `999-foreign.json` and `2 files`; and it does not contain `path.basename(queuedMergeFiles(root)[0]!.file)`, the readable entry's own file.
  - "checkMergeQueueFiles names the extras via andMore": seed four unreadable files (`0.json`…`3.json` holding `{"nope":true}`); the detail names the first and contains `and 3 more`.
  - "unreadableMergeQueueFiles matches readMergeQueue's count": on the mixed root, `assert.equal(unreadableMergeQueueFiles(root).length, readMergeQueue(root).unreadable)`, and every returned path ends in `.json`.
- test/doctor.test.ts: the hardcoded name array in "the report lists every check in order" gains `"merge-queue files"` immediately after `"stale merge-queue entries"`, so both `assert.deepEqual` assertions (the literal and the `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES.filter((n) => n !== "funes")` one) pass; the all-`ok` loop passes because an absent merge-queue directory yields no skipped files. "doctor <check>... runs the named checks" continues to pass: `merge-queue files` matches a `DOCTOR_CHECK_NAMES` entry, and test/completion.test.ts's `/^[a-z0-9' -]+$/i` admits the hyphen and space.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### `tumwater queue -f/--follow` repaints the durable merge queue every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits, the snapshot command's live twin of the TUI Pending pane and the dashboard Merge queue card (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the in-flight TUI Activity tally plan edits `sayTally` in src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/events/event-tally.ts, docs/cli.md's `logs --count` sentence and docs/how-it-works.md's Activity paragraph; the in-flight TUI Pending Ctrl+G plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts, test/tui-keys.test.ts, docs/cli.md's `Ctrl+G` row and docs/how-it-works.md's Pending paragraph; the Codex parts edit src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent. None touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts's `queue` stanza or test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts; docs/cli.md is shared with the other two only at neighbouring clauses, so whichever lands second rebases there. Touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater queue` prints the durable merge queue once (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts `cmdQueue`), and `status` just gained `-f/--follow`; the queue itself has no live form. An operator watching the team merge wants the queue to update as entries land, the way the TUI Pending pane and the dashboard Merge queue card already do. Add `-f/--follow`: repaint the queue every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the parent process exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent (the same rule `status -f`, `logs -f` and `history -f` use). `--role` composes with it, each frame keeping only the listed roles' merges under their whole-queue positions; `--json` is refused with a follow because it prints one document.

**Approach.** The first three bullets are in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts unless named otherwise.

1. Share the status follow's loop instead of copying it:
   - Rename the local `interface StatusFollowSeams` to `interface FollowViewSeams` and `const STATUS_FOLLOW_INTERVAL_MS = 2000` to `const FOLLOW_VIEW_INTERVAL_MS = 2000`, updating `cmdStatus` and `followStatus`.
   - Extract `async function followView(frameText: () => string, seams: FollowViewSeams): Promise<void>` holding exactly today's `followStatus` loop: `const tty = seams.tty ?? process.stdout.isTTY;`, `const interval = seams.intervalMs ?? FOLLOW_VIEW_INTERVAL_MS;`, a `frame()` that writes `tty ? "\x1b[H\x1b[2J" + text + "\n" : text + "\n\n"`, the immediate first `frame()`, then the `setInterval` plus `startParentDeathWatch(() => { clearInterval(timer); resolve(); }, { ppid, intervalMs })` promise. `followStatus` becomes a call to `followView(() => renderStatus(root, scope ? scopeSnapshotToRoles(snapshot(root), scope) : snapshot(root), tty ? process.stdout.columns : undefined, scope !== null), seams)`, reading `tty` the same way for the column count; its emitted bytes are unchanged.
2. `cmdQueue` gains the flag and the follow branch. Its doc comment becomes `queue [-f/--follow]`, noting the repaint and the parent-death end.
   - Add local `const QUEUE_FOLLOW_SPEC = { names: ["-f", "--follow"] };` beside the other local specs; `rejectUnknownArgs("queue", args, [ROLE_FLAG, JSON_FLAG, QUEUE_FOLLOW_SPEC])`.
   - Change the signature to `export async function cmdQueue(root: string, args: string[], seams: FollowViewSeams = {}): Promise<void>` (cli.ts's call site passes no seams and needs no change).
   - `const follow = args.includes("-f") || args.includes("--follow");`, and beside the `status` refusal: `if (follow && args.includes("--json")) fail("queue --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`.
   - After `requireReadyRepo` and `parseRoleListScope`, factor the scoped read into `const readQueue = () => { const whole = readMergeQueue(root); const scoped = roles ? scopeMergeQueue(whole, roles, (r) => roles.includes(r) || roles.includes(baseRoleOf(r))) : undefined; const view = scoped ? scoped.view : whole; return { view, inFlight: queueInFlight(root, view.entries, orchestratorAlive(root)), scope: scoped?.scope }; };` — the exact body of today's snapshot read, one clock read for the render's age. Then `if (follow) { await followView(() => { const { view, inFlight, scope } = readQueue(); return renderMergeQueue(view, Date.now(), inFlight, scope); }, seams); return; }` beside the snapshot branch. The snapshot branch calls `readQueue()` once and keeps its `sayJsonOrRender(args, inFlight ? { ...view, inFlight } : view, () => renderMergeQueue(view, Date.now(), inFlight, scope))` exactly as today, so `tumwater queue` output is byte-identical.
3. src/cli/help.ts, the `tumwater queue` stanza: synopsis becomes `tumwater queue [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [-f/--follow] [--json]`, and after the existing `--json then lists only those entries` sentence add `-f/--follow repaints the queue every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent; it refuses --json;`. Wrap to the stanza's column.
4. docs/cli.md, the `tumwater queue` clause of the "Check state" row: change its synopsis to `tumwater queue [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [-f/--follow] [--json]` and, after the `--role` sentence, add: ``-f/--follow` repaints the queue every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent process exits (a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent, like `status -f`); it refuses `--json``. Leave the surrounding clauses untouched.

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/cli-queue-follow.test.ts (new), driving `cmdQueue` in-process with the follow seams the way test/status-follow.test.ts drives `cmdStatus` (a `makeRepo()`/`initProject` repo, entries seeded with `enqueueMerge`, `captureStdout` from ./helpers/exit-capture.js, `sleep` from ./helpers/wait.js, and a `withQueueFollow(args, intervalMs, tty, drive)` helper whose `stop()` sets the seam's parent to PID 1 and whose `finally` awaits the follow promise under a restored stdout):
  - Test "queue -f repaints until its parent exits, then prints nothing": seed `improve` run #3; run `["-f"]` at 5 ms non-TTY; after ~60 ms `cap.out()` matches `/merge queue \(1\):/` at least twice and contains `/1\. improve run #3/`; `stop()` then the follow resolves and stdout stops growing.
  - Test "queue -f --role keeps only the listed role's entries in every frame": seed `improve` and `clean`; run `["--role", "clean", "-f"]`; the captured frames match `/1\. clean run/` and never `/improve/`.
  - Test "queue -f --json is refused": `expectFailAsync(() => cmdQueue(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` rejects matching `/queue --json prints one document/`, and the captured stdout has no `merge queue` line and no clear-screen.
  - Test "queue -f clears the screen only on a TTY": with `tty: true` the output starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; with `tty: false` it never contains that sequence.
- test/cli-queue.test.ts passes unchanged: the snapshot, `--json` and `--role` tests see the same bytes as today.
- test/status-follow.test.ts passes unchanged: the extracted `followView` emits the same frames and still refuses `status -f --json`.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### TUI Activity pane shows a per-event-type tally line above the feed, the terminal twin of `tumwater logs --count` and the dashboard feed's tally chips (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Transcript change step Ctrl+Y plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-frame.ts and tui.tsx; the dashboard Newest failure plan edits src/ui/gui and docs; the `logs --transcript` completion plan edits src/cli/completion.ts and docs. None touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/events/event-tally.ts or `sayTally` in src/cli/log-commands.ts, so the only shared edits are neighbouring docs lines. Touches src/events/event-tally.ts (new), src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/cli/log-commands.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/how-it-works.md, test/tui-activity.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** The TUI Activity pane (`paneBody`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts) lists the event tail and cycles an exact event type with Ctrl+O, but shows no per-type counts. `tumwater logs --count` prints them (`sayTally`, src/cli/log-commands.ts: one `N × <label> (<type>)` per present type, most-frequent first with ties in type-name order), and the dashboard feed shows them as tally chips (`tallyChips`, src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts: `N × <label>`, the id as the chip title). The pane's Ctrl+O cycle already builds its options from the pre-type read, so an operator scrolling Activity cannot see which types are present or how many. Add one dim tally line above the feed, built from the role- and grep-filtered but type-unfiltered rows, so every type stays visible (and one Ctrl+O step away) while a type is selected.

**Approach.**
1. New src/events/event-tally.ts: `export function eventTypeTally(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): Array<[string, number]>`. It `increment`s a `Map` over `e.type`, then returns `sortByValueDesc([...counts.entries()])` (src/collections.ts), so the count-descending/type-ascending order has one home. Its doc comment says it is the ordering `sayTally` and the TUI tally share, and that the dashboard's browser tally chips keep their own copy because they run where harness modules cannot be imported (the `reportRoleOrder` exception src/ui/gui/gui-client-report-chart.ts documents).
2. src/cli/log-commands.ts, `sayTally`: replace its local `increment`/`sortByValueDesc` text branch with `eventTypeTally(events)`; the JSON branch keeps its own alphabetical key sort. The rendered lines are byte-identical because the helper reproduces exactly the `increment` + `sortByValueDesc` step it replaces.
3. src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, the activity branch of `paneBody`:
   - Add imports `eventTypeLabel` from `../../events/event-labels.js` and `eventTypeTally` from `../../events/event-tally.js`.
   - Read the type-unfiltered rows once: `const preType = activityEvents(root, pane.role, pane.grep, null);` then `const events = pane.type === null ? preType : activityEvents(root, pane.role, pane.grep, pane.type);`.
   - Build the line only when the feed is non-empty: `const tallyLine = events.length === 0 ? [] : [toneLine(eventTypeTally(preType).map(([type, n]) => `${n} × ${eventTypeLabel(type)} (${type})`).join(" · "), width, "dim")];`.
   - Give the tally one line of the body budget: `const rows = Math.max(1, eventBudget - tallyLine.length);` and use `rows` where the branch's `maxStart`/`start` math currently uses `eventBudget`, so `body` is `[...tallyLine, ...events.slice(start, start + rows).map(...)]` and stays at `eventBudget` lines at most.
   - Keep the existing `emptyNote` expression unchanged. No tally is added when `events.length === 0`, so the renderer still paints `emptyNote` (a role/grep scope with no events keeps `(no events match this filter)`, an empty log keeps `(no events yet)`). The Ctrl+O cycle can only select a type present in `preType`, so a selected type never empties `events` in the steady state; a rotation race is covered by the `events.length === 0` guard rather than a special case.
   - Extend the branch's comment to name the tally and to say it is built from `preType` so every type the Ctrl+O cycle offers stays counted.
4. Docs. docs/cli.md, the `logs --count` sentence in the "Check state" row: after "with `--json`, one object mapping type to count" add ", the same tally the TUI's Activity pane prints as one line above its event feed (the dashboard feed's tally chips carry the counts too)". docs/how-it-works.md, the Activity pane paragraph: add one sentence naming the tally line, its count-descending/type-name order, and that Ctrl+O selects one of the types it counts.

**Files touched.** src/events/event-tally.ts (new), src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-activity.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/how-it-works.md, test/tui-activity.test.ts (new), test/tui-keys.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/tui-activity.test.ts (new; a repo from `makeTuiRepo()` in test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js, events seeded with `logEvent` from ../src/events/events.js as test/tui.test.ts does, and a `TuiPaneState` literal like test/tui-backlog.test.ts's). Seed two `run_start` events and one `merge_failed` event.
  - `paneBody({ kind: "activity", role: null, grep: null, type: null }, { root, width: 200, eventBudget: 10, entryBudget: 5, state }).body` has length 4; its first line's text is exactly `2 × run started (run_start) · 1 × merge failed (merge_failed)`, and the next three lines are the formatted event lines oldest first.
  - The same call with `type: "merge_failed"` keeps that same first tally line and then only the merge_failed line: the tally is built from the type-unfiltered rows, so the filtered-out `run_start` count stays visible.
  - With `role` scoped to the role that only logged `merge_failed`, the tally line is `1 × merge failed (merge_failed)`.
  - With `grep: "nomatch"`, `body` is `[]` and `emptyNote` is `(no events match this filter)`.
  - With no events seeded, `body` is `[]` and `emptyNote` is `(no events yet)`.
  - Budget: the three-event seed with `eventBudget: 3` gives a three-line body, the tally line plus the newest two event lines, so the tally consumes one line of the tail budget.
- test/tui-activity.test.ts also pins `eventTypeTally` directly: inputs `a, a, b, c` return `[["a", 2], ["b", 1], ["c", 1]]` (count-descending, equal counts in type-name order), and `[]` returns `[]`.
- The existing `logs --count` tests pass unchanged (the tie-break and `--json` key-order cases), and the rendered `logs --count` text is byte-identical before and after the `sayTally` change.
- The existing TUI tests pass unchanged: the activity frame tests use `assert.match`, and "queued prompts render numbered above the activity pane and shrink its budget" computes its `full` from the same new frame shape before it asserts the two-line shrink.

### TUI Pending pane's Ctrl+G role scope also narrows the durable merge queue, each kept merge under its whole-queue position: the terminal twin of `tumwater queue --role <id>` (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the in-flight TUI Activity tally plan edits src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/events/event-tally.ts, src/cli/log-commands.ts and test/tui-activity.test.ts (new); the in-flight dashboard Pending Merge queue Role picker edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, test/gui-client-pending.test.ts and docs/how-it-works.md; the Codex parts edit src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent. None touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts or test/tui-keys.test.ts; docs/cli.md and docs/how-it-works.md are shared with those entries only at neighbouring sentences, so whichever lands second rebases there. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md; done 2026-10-21 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The Pending pane (`createPendingPane`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts) paints the durable merge queue above the roster, and its Ctrl+G already narrows the overlapping-files block to one holding role (the `diff --overlaps --role <id>` twin). The CLI narrows the queue too (`tumwater queue --role <id>[,<id>...]`, through `scopeMergeQueue` in src/merge/merge-queue-render.ts — the same helper src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts already calls for one role's change view), and the dashboard's Merge queue card is getting a Role picker, but the TUI queue itself always lists every role. Extend the pane's one Ctrl+G role scope so it narrows the merge queue as well as the overlapping files, cycling through the roles the queue names, then the overlap holders not already in that list, then back to all. Each kept merge keeps its whole-queue position and each kept overlap still names every holder. No new key and no `tui-panes.ts` routing change: Ctrl+G already reaches the Pending pane, and one role scope per pane beats two scopes fighting over keys.

**Approach.** All in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts unless named otherwise.

1. Exports and imports:
   - Add `export function mergeQueueRoles(view: MergeQueueView): string[]` beside `overlapHolders`: the distinct `entry.role` values in first-seen (queue) order, `[]` for an empty queue. Import the `MergeQueueView` type from `../../merge/merge-queue.js` and `scopeMergeQueue` beside `renderMergeQueue` from `../../merge/merge-queue-render.js`.
2. State: rename `let overlapScope: string | null = null;` to `let roleScope` and update its comment to say the one scope covers the queue and the overlaps. Add `let lastQueue: MergeQueueView | null = null;` and `let rosterText = "";` beside `head`.
3. Render:
   - Add `function queueHead(): string`: return `""` when `lastQueue` is null; else `const inFlight = queueInFlight(session.root, lastQueue.entries, orchestratorAlive(session.root));` and, when `roleScope === null`, return `renderMergeQueue(lastQueue, session.now(), inFlight)`; otherwise `const { view, scope } = scopeMergeQueue(lastQueue, [roleScope], (r) => r === roleScope);` and return `renderMergeQueue(view, session.now(), inFlight, scope)`.
   - In `refresh()`, replace the inline `readMergeQueue`/`renderMergeQueue` pair with `lastQueue = readMergeQueue(session.root); rosterText = ""; const queueText = queueHead();`, keeping the existing `head`/`base`/`paneCache` writes. On resolve, set `rosterText = "\n\n" + renderTeamChange(team); head = queueHead() + rosterText; compose();` where it once set `head = queueText + "\n\n" + renderTeamChange(team)`. `compose()` is unchanged, so the queue text with no scope stays byte-identical to today.
4. Ctrl+G arm: replace the holder-only cycle with `const queueRoles = lastQueue ? mergeQueueRoles(lastQueue) : []; const holders = lastOverlaps?.state === "ready" ? overlapHolders(lastOverlaps) : []; const roles = [...queueRoles, ...holders.filter((h) => !queueRoles.includes(h))];`. When `roles.length === 0`, set `roleScope = null`, recompute `head = queueHead() + rosterText`, `compose()`, `session.paneCache = base`, flash `no queued merges or overlapping files to scope`, and keep the pane. Otherwise cycle `roleScope` through `[null, ...roles]` exactly as the holder cycle does today, then recompute `head = queueHead() + rosterText`, `compose()`, `session.paneCache = base`. Keep the existing `overlapIndex = -1; ++drillGen;` reset (an open drill-down closes) and the `session.paneScroll = 0`.
5. Extend the file's top doc comment to say the Ctrl+G scope covers the merge queue too.
6. docs/cli.md, the `Ctrl+G` row: extend its Pending clause to "on Pending, keep only the queued merges and the overlapping files one role touches (each merge under its whole-queue position, each file still naming every holder), cycling through the roles the queue names and the overlap holders and back to all (the twin of `queue --role <id>` and `diff --overlaps --role <id>`)".
7. docs/how-it-works.md, the Pending pane paragraph: after the existing Ctrl+G sentence, add that the same scope also narrows the merge queue to that role's waiting merges, each under its whole-queue position (the `tumwater queue --role` view), and that the cycle includes the queued roles before the overlap holders.

**Acceptance criteria.** (test/tui-keys.test.ts, driving `createTuiKeys` over a `makeRoot()` temp root and seeding the queue through `enqueueMerge` from ../src/merge/merge-queue.js, both already imported there; Ctrl+T five times enters Pending as in the existing tests)
- New test "Ctrl+G on the Pending pane narrows the merge queue to each queued role under its whole-queue position": seed `feature` (run 1), `feature-2` (run 2) and `clean` (run 3) with distinct `enqueuedAt`s, `collectPending` resolving `{ mainBranch: "main", roles: [] }` and `collectOverlaps` a `no-base` view. The first press makes it start `merge queue (1 of 3, --role feature):` and contain ` 1. feature run #1 ` but neither ` 2. ` nor ` 3. `; the second `merge queue (1 of 3, --role feature-2):` with ` 2. feature #2 run #2 `; the third `merge queue (1 of 3, --role clean):` with ` 3. clean run #3 `; the fourth returns to the unscoped `merge queue (3):`. The match is exact, so `--role feature` does not pull `feature-2`'s entry (matching the transcript pane's queue scope, not the CLI's base-plus-instances rule).
- New test "the Pending pane's Ctrl+G scope filters the queue and the overlapping files from one cycle set": seed one `clean` queue entry and `collectOverlaps` a `ready` view with `{ path: "src/a.ts", roles: ["feature", "clean"] }`. The third returns to the whole queue and all overlaps.
- Unit test "mergeQueueRoles lists each queued role once in queue order": a `MergeQueueView` whose entries name `feature`, `clean`, `feature` yields `["feature", "clean"]`, and one with no entries yields `[]`.
- Update "Ctrl+G on the Pending pane with no overlaps flashes" (empty queue, no overlaps) to expect the flash `no queued merges or overlapping files to scope` and the unchanged pane.
- The rest of the existing Pending tests pass unchanged: with an empty queue the Ctrl+G cycle set is still `overlapHolders`, so "Ctrl+G on the Pending pane cycles the overlap scope through each holder and back", "Ctrl+N under a Pending overlap scope steps through only the scoped files" and "Ctrl+G on the Pending pane closes an open drill-down and survives Ctrl+R" keep their assertions.

### Dashboard Pending view's Merge queue card gets a Role picker that keeps only the chosen role's waiting merges, each under its whole-queue position: the dashboard twin of `tumwater queue --role <id>` (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the TUI Activity tally plan edits `sayTally` in src/cli/log-commands.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, the Transcript change step Ctrl+Y plan edits src/ui/tui, the `status -f` plan edits src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts and src/cli/help.ts, and the Codex parts edit src/events, src/config, src/gates, src/team, src/orchestrator and src/agent; none touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, test/gui-client-pending.test.ts or the Pending paragraph of docs/how-it-works.md. docs/how-it-works.md is shared with the TUI Activity tally plan's Activity paragraph, so whichever lands second rebases over a neighbouring paragraph. **Goal.** The Pending view's Merge queue card (`pendingQueueHtml`, src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts) lists every role's waiting merges in execution order. The CLI narrows that queue with `tumwater queue --role <id>[,<id>...]` (a base id taking its instances too), and the role drawer already lists one role's waiting merges, but the card itself has no such control. Add a Role picker to the card's head: choosing a role keeps only that role's queued merges, each under its position in the whole queue; "All roles" (the default) shows every line. Filtering stays client-side over the `/api/status` payload the card already paints (`status.mergeQueue.entries` with `status.mergeQueueLabels` parallel to it), so no endpoint and no server change is needed.

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts:
   - Beside `pendingOverlapRole`, add `let pendingQueueRole = "";`.
   - Change `pendingQueueHtml(mergeQueue, now, labels, role = "")` — an optional fourth parameter, so every existing three-argument caller and test is unchanged:
     - Keep the existing depth/entries/malformed branches, and after building the head append, when the entries name at least one string role, a `<label>` holding `<select class='field' id='pendingqueuerole'>`: `<option value=''>All roles</option>` then each distinct role id sorted, `esc`-escaped, labelled through `roleLabel`, and marked `selected` when it equals the active role.
     - `const roles = entries.map((e) => e && e.role).filter((r) => typeof r === "string")` de-duplicated and sorted; `const active = role && roles.includes(role) ? role : ""`.
     - Filter while keeping each entry's whole-queue index: `entries.map((e, i) => ({ e, i })).filter(({ e }) => !active || e.role === active)` and render each with `queueEntryLineHtml(e, i + 1, now, Array.isArray(labels) ? labels[i] : undefined)`.
   - `renderPendingQueue(status)`: before painting, set `pendingQueueRole = ""` when the current payload's entries name no such role (the same staleness reset `fetchPendingOverlaps` does), then paint `pendingQueueHtml(status && status.mergeQueue, Date.now(), status && status.mergeQueueLabels, pendingQueueRole)`.
   - In `buildPendingView`, add a `change` listener on `#pendingqueue`: when `e.target.id === "pendingqueuerole"`, set `pendingQueueRole = e.target.value` and call `renderPendingQueue(lastStatus)`.
   - Extend the file's top doc comment to name the Merge queue card's Role picker beside the overlapping card's pickers.
2. docs/how-it-works.md, the Pending paragraph: after "the Pending view also paints the merge queue as a card mirroring `tumwater queue`", add "with a Role picker that keeps only the chosen role's waiting merges, each under its whole-queue position, the `tumwater queue --role` twin".

### `tumwater status -f/--follow` repaints the team's status table every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent exits: the snapshot command's live twin of the TUI header and the dashboard Team card (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the TUI Activity tally plan edits `sayTally` in src/cli/log-commands.ts and docs/cli.md's `logs --count` sentence, the Transcript change step Ctrl+Y plan edits docs/cli.md's TUI keys table, and the dashboard Newest failure plan edits src/ui/gui; none touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts's `status` stanza, the `tumwater status` clause of docs/cli.md's "Check state" row or a new test/status-follow.test.ts. Touches src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/status-follow.test.ts (new) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater status` prints one snapshot and exits. `logs -f` and `history -f` stream, and the TUI header and the dashboard Team card update live, but a terminal operator watching from a shell has no way to keep the status table current. Add `-f/--follow` to `status`: render the current table, sleep, re-collect and repaint, until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits — the same parent-death rule `logs -f` uses, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent. The `--json` and `--role` surfaces stay as they are.

**Key choice.** Repaint in place on a TTY with `\x1b[H\x1b[2J` before each frame (the `watch` shape), and print frames separated by a blank line when stdout is not a TTY, so a piped follow stays readable and scriptable. `renderStatus` (src/ui/status-render.ts) is reused unchanged; the interval is a fixed default (no knob).

**Approach.**
1. src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts:
   - Import `startParentDeathWatch` from `../process/supervisor.js`.
   - Add beside the other local specs: `const STATUS_FOLLOW_SPEC = { names: ["-f", "--follow"] };` (unannotated like the neighbouring local specs, so no new import), `const STATUS_FOLLOW_INTERVAL_MS = 2000;`, and `interface StatusFollowSeams { ppid?: () => number; intervalMs?: number; tty?: boolean; }`.
   - `cmdStatus(root, args, seams: StatusFollowSeams = {})`: add `STATUS_FOLLOW_SPEC` to the `rejectUnknownArgs("status", args, …)` list; compute `const follow = args.includes("-f") || args.includes("--follow");` and, before `requireReadyRepo`, `if (follow && args.includes("--json")) fail("status --json prints one document; -f/--follow repaints a live view — drop one of them");`. After `requireReadyRepo` and `parseRoleListScope`, insert `if (follow) { await followStatus(root, scope, seams); return; }` ahead of the existing json/text branches.
   - `async function followStatus(root: string, scope: string[] | null, seams: StatusFollowSeams): Promise<void>` (the return type `parseRoleListScope` in src/cli/cli-args.ts gives): `const tty = seams.tty ?? process.stdout.isTTY === true;` and `const interval = seams.intervalMs ?? STATUS_FOLLOW_INTERVAL_MS;`. A `frame()` closure re-collects `snapshot(root)`, renders `renderStatus(root, scope ? scopeSnapshotToRoles(snap, scope) : snap, tty ? process.stdout.columns : undefined, scope !== null)` and writes `tty ? "\x1b[H\x1b[2J" + text + "\n" : text + "\n\n"` to stdout. Call `frame()` once, then `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { const timer = setInterval(frame, interval); startParentDeathWatch(() => { clearInterval(timer); resolve(); }, { ...(seams.ppid ? { ppid: seams.ppid } : {}), ...(seams.intervalMs !== undefined ? { intervalMs: seams.intervalMs } : {}) }); });`.
   - Extend `cmdStatus`'s doc comment with the `-f/--follow` line and its stop rule.
2. src/cli/help.ts, the `status` stanza: change the usage line to `tumwater status [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [-f/--follow] [--json]` and add `; -f/--follow repaints the table until Ctrl+C or the process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent` before the trailing team-wide-header sentence.
3. docs/cli.md, the `tumwater status` clause of the "Check state" row: add `[-f/--follow]` after `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]` and, after "works with `--json`", add: "-f/--follow repaints the table every couple of seconds until Ctrl+C or its parent process exits (a backgrounded follow does not outlive its parent, like `logs -f`); it refuses `--json`".

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/status-follow.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/status-follow.test.ts (new), modelled on test/history-follow.test.ts's in-process follow with the `ppid`/`intervalMs` seams and test/cli.test.ts's status setup: `const repo = makeRepo(); await initProject(repo, "status follow");` then the runner-flush delay, then `captureStdout()`.
  - "status -f repaints until its parent exits, then prints nothing": start `cmdStatus(repo, ["-f"], { ppid: () => parent, intervalMs: 5, tty: false })` with a local `let parent = 4242; let done = false;`, wait about 60 ms, and assert the captured output has at least two `tumwater ·` header occurrences (two or more frames) and the tells of the non-TTY shape (no `\x1b[H\x1b[2J`). Then set `parent = 1`, poll (the test/helpers/wait.js `sleep`) until `done`, record `const before = cap.out()`, wait about 30 ms, and assert `cap.out() === before` (nothing printed after the follow ended). `cap.restore()` in `finally`.
  - "status -f --role keeps only the listed role's rows": the same harness with `["--role", "feature", "-f"]`, wait about 60 ms, and assert the captured output contains `feature` and does not contain `clean` (the fresh project has no attention banner naming another role); then stop via the parent flip.
  - "status -f --json is refused": `await expectFailAsync(() => cmdStatus(repo, ["-f", "--json"], { ppid: () => 4242, intervalMs: 5 }))` and assert the message matches `/-f\/--follow repaints a live view/`; assert the captured stdout holds neither a table header nor a frame.
  - "status -f clears the screen only on a TTY": run once with `tty: true` (wait about 20 ms, stop) and assert the output starts with `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`; run once with `tty: false` and assert the output does not contain `"\x1b[H\x1b[2J"`.
  - The existing test/cli.test.ts `status` and `status --json` tests pass unchanged (bare status and `--json` keep their current shapes), and `rejectUnknownArgs` still refuses an unknown status flag.
- `npm run test:gate` is green.

### TUI Transcript change step Ctrl+Y shows the viewed role's diffstat instead of its full patch, and the full patch again on a second press: the terminal twin of `tumwater diff --role <id> --stat` and the dashboard drawer's Stat only toggle (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; replanned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the TUI Inbox `/` search plan edits the `/` plumbing and the Inbox hint line, and the TUI Pending Ctrl+G plan edits the Ctrl+G route and the Pending hint line, both in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts. This plan edits only the Ctrl+Y route and the transcript hint line there, so at most a neighbouring-line rebase. The role-less `/api/run?last=1` plan touches src/gui and src/run only. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, docs/cli.md, test/tui-keys.test.ts and test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-21 by the feature role

**Goal.** A role's Transcript view cycles transcript → notes → change with Ctrl+N (`createTranscriptPane` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts). The change step always renders the full patch (`session.collectChange(session.root, target)` then `renderRoleChange`). The CLI has `diff --role <id> --stat`, and the dashboard drawer gained a Stat only toggle (`GET /api/diff?role=<id>&stat=1`, PLANS-DONE.md). The terminal has neither. A large pending change fills many pages in the TUI, but the first question is usually just "which files does it touch". `collectRoleChange` (src/change/change-data.ts) already takes `opts.stat`, and `renderRoleChange` renders that view unchanged, so only the TUI plumbing is missing.

**Key choice.** Ctrl+Y (mnemonic: summar**Y**, as in the History pane's summary toggle). On a Transcript view it does nothing useful today. The Activity-only claude-reserve editor (`tui-editor-claude-reserve.ts`, built by `createTeamConfigKeyEditor`, which returns false off view 0) lets the key fall through. The `tui-panes.ts` router then sends it to `history.handleKey`, which flips the History pane's `historySummary` behind the scenes. The other Transcript keys are taken (see docs/cli.md's TUI keys table).

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: widen the `collectChange` seam's `opts` type in all three declarations (`TuiPanesDeps` and `TuiPaneSession` in tui-pane-session.ts, and `TuiKeysDeps`' optional one in tui-keys.ts) from `{ path?: string }` to `{ path?: string; stat?: boolean }`. The default `collectRoleChange` already accepts it. No other change there.
2. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts, `createTranscriptPane`:
   - Add `let changeStat = false;` and `let changeGen = 0;` beside `changeMode`/`changeCache`.
   - Pull the merge-queue header and collector call out of the notes → change arm into a local `loadChange(role: string)`. It starts `changeCache = null;` then `const gen = ++changeGen;`, computes `queueText` with the same try/catch, and calls `session.collectChange(session.root, target, changeStat ? { stat: true } : undefined)`. Both `.then` arms start `if (gen !== changeGen) return;`: that single staleness check replaces the old `changeMode`/same-role guards and also drops a load that Ctrl+Y, leaving the step, or `reset()` has superseded. The notes → change arm sets `changeMode = true; changeStat = false;` then calls `loadChange(role)`.
   - `changeGen`'s declaration comment must say exactly when it is bumped — `loadChange` on every change-step load (a Ctrl+Y toggle included), the change → transcript branch, and `reset()` — and why: a collector a newer load or a leave superseded must not paint the pane. Do not claim a bump the code does not perform.
   - The change → transcript branch (Ctrl+N while `changeMode`) sets `changeMode = false; changeGen += 1; changeCache = null;` so a load still in flight cannot paint the pane after the step is left.
   - A new arm: `key.ctrl && key.name === "y" && changeMode && promptLineFree(ctx.es) && session.view >= 1 && session.view <= session.roleIds.length`. It flips `changeStat`, sets `session.paneScroll = 0`, calls `loadChange(role)` (which clears `changeCache`, so the pane paints its loading note), requests a render, and returns true. With any of those conditions false it returns false, so the router falls through.
   - `reset()` adds `changeGen += 1` and `changeStat = false` beside clearing `changeMode`/`changeCache`, so cycling the view drops an in-flight load. Every fresh entry to the change step then starts on the full patch, like the drawer, which refetches without stat on reopen.
   - `state()` adds `changeStat`.
3. src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: the Ctrl+Y route becomes `if (transcript.handleKey?.(key, ctx)) return true; return history.handleKey?.(key, ctx) ?? false;`, with a one-line comment saying the transcript change-step arm goes first and falls through off it. Add `changeStat: tra.changeStat` to the aggregated state beside `changeCache`. Add the matching `changeStat: boolean` field, with a doc comment, to `TuiKeysState` in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts beside `changeCache`.
4. src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: the transcript view kind gains `changeStat?: boolean`. On the transcript hint line, when `view.change` is true, add `["Ctrl+Y", view.changeStat ? "full patch" : "stat only"]` after the Ctrl+N pair. src/ui/tui/tui.tsx passes `changeStat: s.changeStat` where it builds the transcript view.
5. docs/cli.md: in the TUI keys table's `Ctrl+N` | Transcript row, append "; on the change, `Ctrl+Y` shows the diffstat instead of the full patch, and the patch again on a second press (the `diff --role <id> --stat` text and the dashboard drawer's Stat only)".

**Acceptance criteria** (test/tui-keys.test.ts, modelled on "Ctrl+N cycles transcript → notes → change and back, caching the collector's render" and "Ctrl+T leaves change mode, and a resolution after a cycle away does not cache"; the collector stub records each call's `opts` and returns a fresh pending promise per call so a test controls resolution order):
- New test "Ctrl+Y on the Transcript change step toggles the diffstat". Enter the change step (Ctrl+T on a role view, then Ctrl+N twice). The first collector call has no `stat`, and `state().changeStat` is false. Ctrl+Y sets `changeStat` true and makes a second collector call with `{ stat: true }`. Once that resolves, `changeCache` equals `renderRoleChange(statView)`. A second Ctrl+Y makes a call without `stat` and sets `changeStat` back to false.
- New test "a superseded change-step load never paints over the newer one": enter the change step and hold its full-patch promise; Ctrl+Y issues the stat load; resolve the stat load, then resolve the older full-patch promise. `changeCache` is still `renderRoleChange(statView)` and `changeStat` is still true. This is the case the old guard missed and `changeGen` exists for.
- In the toggle test, Ctrl+Y on the stat step, then Ctrl+N (change → transcript), then Ctrl+N twice back to the change step: `changeStat` is false and the newest collector call has no `stat`.
- The existing "Ctrl+T leaves change mode, and a resolution after a cycle away does not cache" test passes unedited, so `reset()`'s staleness still holds with the new `changeStat` state, and the existing Ctrl+N cycle test passes unedited.
- Ctrl+Y on the live transcript step (not the change step) leaves `changeStat` false and makes no collector call. That keeps the History fallthrough intact. Assert the router still reaches History: on the History view, Ctrl+Y still cycles the summary, and the existing History Ctrl+Y tests pass unedited.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: the transcript hint with `change: true` contains `Ctrl+Y stat only`, and with `changeStat: true` contains `Ctrl+Y full patch`. With `change: false` it contains no `Ctrl+Y`.

### Codex backend, part 2a/9: The free-ness callers pass a per-backend account lookup (planned 2026-10-21 by the plan role; requires part 1/9 landed; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 2; touches src/pi/pi-models.ts src/agent/image-input.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/status/status-budget.ts src/roles/role-view.ts src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts and their tests; done 2026-10-21 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Every free-ness predicate takes one `account: ClaudeAccount | null`. Part 1/9 already made the store per backend (`readAccount(root, backend)` in src/agent/subscription-account.ts) but left the five exported pi-models predicates on one account, so a later part cannot judge a second backend without another signature sweep. This part converts them to `accounts: (backend: string) => SubscriptionAccount | null` and builds the lookup where they are called. No behavior change: `accounts("claude")` returns the same account, and no caller asks for another backend yet. This is the mechanical half the feature role split out of part 2/9, one theme applied everywhere it holds.

**Approach.**
- src/pi/pi-models.ts: `seamFree(providers, seam, accounts = () => null, catalog = null)`, and the same lookup in place of `account` in `piPairFree`, `fallbackModelPair`, `fallbackModelFree` and `teamModelsFree`. `seamFree`'s claude arm becomes the generic subscription arm — `const account = accounts(seamAgent(seam)); if (account?.billing === "subscription") return !accountUsesOverage(account);` ahead of the unchanged `pi` and `opencode` arms and the NOT-free default.
- src/gates/budget-gates.ts: `pollBudgetGate` builds `const accounts = (backend: string) => readAccount(root, backend)` once per poll and threads it into `seamFree`/`piPairFree` and `chainInfo`'s `isPriced`; keep the existing `account` value for the claude-only window and overage logic.
- The other callers pass the lookup derived from the one account they hold: `const accounts = (b: string) => (b === "claude" ? account : null)` in src/status/status-budget.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts and src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts; src/agent/image-input.ts's `piPairFree` call does the same.
- Leave `claudeWindowUsedUp`, `extraUsage`/`claudeOverageRefused`, `claudeWindowBlock` and every display on claude; they are not free-ness lookups (part 2c/9 and part 3/9 own them).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The existing tests pass with only the argument updated where they pass an account: test/pi-models.test.ts, test/image-input.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/status-budget.test.ts, test/role-view.test.ts and test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts.
- A new test calls `seamFree(providers, { agent: "claude" }, (b) => (b === "claude" ? subscriptionAccount : null))` and sees free, and with an API-billed account sees not free — the predicate reads the lookup, not a captured value.
- `grep -n 'account: ClaudeAccount | null' src/pi/pi-models.ts` prints nothing.
- `npm test` passes.

### Codex backend, part 1/9: The subscription account store is per backend, and a run's result names its backend (planned 2026-10-20 by user; independent of every eligible Planned entry; design in plans/codex-backend.md "Groundwork: the subscription account is per backend" item 1; touches src/agent/subscription-account.ts (new) src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/paths.ts src/pi/pi-run-result.ts src/agent/run-agent.ts src/run/run-usage.ts src/run/run-finalize.ts src/merge/merge-slot.ts and their tests; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Make the account file (billing plus the newest usage-window reading per window type) per backend, so a second subscription backend never writes into claude's file. Today `observeClaudeAccount` is called for any run that reports `billing` or `rateWindows` (src/run/run-finalize.ts, src/merge/merge-slot.ts), and `PiRunResult` does not say which backend ran. There is no behavior change for claude: its file, its shape and every caller's answer stay the same.

**Approach.**
- New src/agent/subscription-account.ts holds the generic half of src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, renamed:
  - the types `SubscriptionBilling` (`"subscription" | "api"`), `SubscriptionWindow` (today's `ClaudeWindow`, with the overage fields kept optional) and `SubscriptionAccount {billing, plan?, observedAt, windows}`, where `plan` is today's `subscriptionType`, kept under that file key on read and write for claude's file;
  - `accountPath(root, backend)`, which is `.tumwater/state/<backend>-account.json`. For claude that is today's `claudeAccountPath` file, and src/paths.ts keeps `claudeAccountPath` as `accountPath(root, "claude")`;
  - `readAccount(root, backend, now?)`, `writeAccount(root, backend, account)` and `observeAccount(root, backend, run)`, with today's torn-file healing, the reset-on-`resetsAt` rule and the unix-seconds-to-ms conversion;
  - `windowUsedUp`, `windowReserved`, `windowEntries`, `windowLabel` and `utilizationPct`;
  - `subscriptionWindowRejected`. Its `isUsingOverage` test is harmless for a backend that never reports overage.
- src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts keeps:
  - its exported names as thin wrappers (`readClaudeAccount(root)` is `readAccount(root, "claude")`, and so on);
  - the claude-only half: `seedClaudeAccount`, `parseClaudeAuthStatus`, `claudeAuthUsesSubscription`, and the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and third-party-provider checks;
  - `ClaudeAccount`, `ClaudeWindow`, `ClaudeBilling` and `ClaudeWindowEntry` as type aliases of the generic types.
- src/pi/pi-run-result.ts: `PiRunResult` gains `agent?: string`, the backend id that ran. src/agent/run-agent.ts sets it from `backend.id` in every result it builds, the spawn-error result included.
- src/run/run-usage.ts: `RunUsage` gains `agent` (the backend that last reported billing/windows), so run-finalize, which folds the run's account at run end from the usage accumulator (not a live run object), can name the backend. 
- src/merge/merge-slot.ts calls `observeAccount(root, run.agent ?? "pi", run)`; src/run/run-finalize.ts calls `observeAccount(root, usage.agent ?? "pi", {...})`. A run without `billing` or `rateWindows` skips the write, as today. A pi run never reports either, so in practice only claude writes until Codex part 8/9.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/subscription-account.test.ts (new) covers these cases:
  - `readAccount(root, "codex")` reads `.tumwater/state/codex-account.json`, and a missing file reads null.
  - An `observeAccount(root, "codex", run)` with a `five_hour` reading writes only the codex file; claude's file is untouched.
  - The reset-on-`resetsAt` and torn-file cases of test/claude-account.test.ts, run against `readAccount(root, "claude")`, give the same answers.
- test/claude-account.test.ts passes (its two `subscriptionType` references — the seed's `seeded.subscriptionType` and the writeClaudeAccount `before` literal — read the renamed `plan` field).
- A run-finalize test: a run with `agent: "codex"` and a rate window writes codex-account.json and not claude-account.json; a run with `agent: "claude"` writes claude's as today.
- Every `PiRunResult` built by run-agent carries `agent`. The fake-pi and fake-claude tests assert `pi` and `claude`.
- `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater logs --transcript <TAB>` completes role ids in bash, zsh and fish, like `--role` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the TUI Transcript change step Ctrl+Y plan edits src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md's TUI keys table, and the dashboard Newest failure plan edits src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, test/gui-client-history.test.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and docs/cli.md's "Watch run history" row; neither touches src/cli/completion.ts, test/completion.test.ts or docs/cli.md's completion line. Touches src/cli/completion.ts, test/completion.test.ts, docs/cli.md) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** The generated completion scripts complete role ids after `--role` and as the first argument of `role`, `history` and `revert` (docs/cli.md's completion line). `tumwater logs --transcript <id>` is the one role-id flag left out. In `bashScript` (src/cli/completion.ts) the role arm fires only when `prev` is `--role`; in `fishFlagValue` the role completion is returned only for `flag === "--role"`. So `tumwater logs --transcript fe<TAB>` offers nothing.

**Approach.**
1. src/cli/completion.ts, `bashScript`: in the role-id `if`, make the first disjunct also fire for a value after `logs --transcript` — i.e. `[ "$prev" = "--role" ] || { [ "$prev" = "--transcript" ] && [ "${COMP_WORDS[1]}" = logs ]; }`. Keep the rest of the condition (`$COMP_CWORD -eq 2` and the `ROLE_POSITIONAL_COMMANDS` positional arm) as it is. The `logs` guard is required because `history --transcript` is a boolean flag: `history --transcript <TAB>` must stay a no-value position, not get a role.
2. src/cli/completion.ts, `fishFlagValue`: before its final `return ""`, add `if (flag === "--transcript" && command === "logs") return ` -x -a "(__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_roles)"`;`. `fishFlagValue` is already called per command, so the `command === "logs"` guard gives the same boolean-flag protection.
3. docs/cli.md: in the completion line (the `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` sentence), change "completing role ids after `--role` and as the first argument of `role`, `history` and `revert`" to "completing role ids after `--role` and `logs --transcript`, and as the first argument of `role`, `history` and `revert`". Leave the comma-list parenthetical alone: `--transcript` takes one id, not a comma list.

**Files touched.** src/cli/completion.ts, test/completion.test.ts, docs/cli.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/completion.test.ts, the bash test "the bash script completes role ids after --role and for role/history/revert": add `assert.deepEqual(await complete(script, ["tumwater", "logs", "--transcript", "fe"], 3), ["feature", "feature-2"]);` and, in the same test, `assert.deepEqual(await complete(script, ["tumwater", "history", "--transcript", "fe"], 3), []);` (the `complete` helper stubs `tumwater completion --roles` to feature, feature-2 and qa; the `[]` proves the `logs` guard keeps `history --transcript` from getting a value).
- test/completion.test.ts, the fish static test "the fish script completes values after --role, path flags, --template, and --result, and config keys at word 3": with `flagLines("transcript")`, assert the `logs` line includes both `__fish_seen_subcommand_from logs` and `__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_roles`, and the `history` line includes `__fish_seen_subcommand_from history` and does not include `__tumwater_roles`.
- The existing completion tests pass unchanged, including the positional role-id tests, the comma-list tests, and `completionSpec over the real help`. `npm run test:gate` is green.

### TUI Inbox pane `/` search keeps only the queued prompts whose text contains the text, each under its unfiltered per-role number: the terminal twin of `tumwater prompt --list --grep <text>` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: Backend/model split part 5/5 changes src/config and test configs, bare `history --last` changes the history trail command and src/run/run-detail.ts, and the Overlapping files Folder picker changes src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts. No waiting plan touches src/ui/tui, src/inbox or docs/cli.md's TUI keys table. Touches src/inbox/inbox.ts src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-queued.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts test/inbox.test.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater prompt --list --grep <text>` keeps only the queued prompts whose text contains the text, case-insensitively, each under its unfiltered per-role number (`cmdPrompt`'s list mode, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, which filters `row.text.toLowerCase().includes(needle)` inline). The TUI's Inbox pane (`createQueuedPane`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-queued.ts, view `roleIds.length + 6`) lists every queued prompt with no way to narrow it. The shared `/` search editor (`createSearchEditor`, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts) already serves Activity, History, Backlog and a role's Transcript. Add the Inbox pane as its fifth target, so an operator with a long queue can find the prompt to cancel (Ctrl+X), edit (Ctrl+E) or move to the top (Ctrl+V).

**Approach.**
1. src/inbox/inbox.ts: add `export function queuedRowsMatching(rows: readonly QueuedListRow[], grep: string | null): QueuedListRow[]`. `null` returns a copy of `rows`; otherwise it keeps the rows whose `text.toLowerCase()` includes `grep.toLowerCase()`. In prompt-commands.ts, replace the inline `needle` filter with `queuedRowsMatching(scoped, parsed.grep ?? null)`. Output is unchanged.
2. tui-pane-queued.ts: add `let queuedGrep: string | null = null;`. `refreshQueued` builds `queuedRows` as `queuedRowsMatching(queuedListRows(...), queuedGrep)`, so `renderQueuedList` prints each kept row under its own `position` (its unfiltered per-role number). Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V and the Ctrl+E editor (tui-editor-queued.ts reads `ctx.queuedRows`) keep addressing the right role and position with no change. Add `applySearch(pattern)`: set `queuedGrep`, set `selectedQueued = null`, call `refreshQueued()`, and request a render. `state()` also returns `queuedGrep`. Add `applySearch` to the `satisfies` type. `reset()` stays as is, so the pattern persists across Ctrl+T cycles, as `backlogGrep` does.
3. Plumbing, mirroring `backlogGrep`/`applyBacklogSearch` at each site: `queuedGrep` in `TuiEditorCtx` (tui-editor-ctx.ts), in tui-panes.ts `editorCtx()` and its state object (`que.queuedGrep`), and in the state type in tui-keys.ts. `applyQueuedSearch` goes in the session deps interface and its wiring (tui-editor-session.ts), in the tui-editors.ts deps doc, in tui-panes.ts's return (`queued.applySearch`), and in tui-keys.ts's deps wiring.
4. tui-editor-search.ts: add `ctx.view === ctx.roleIds.length + 6` to the `/` open guard. Add `"queued"` to the `searchFor` union and pick it on that view. Add `queued: ctx.queuedGrep` to the pre-fill map and `queued: "inbox"` to the noun map. On Enter, call `session.applyQueuedSearch(applied)`. Update the comments that list the targets.
5. Render: in tui-frame.ts the `queued` `TuiView` becomes `{ kind: "queued"; grep?: string | null }`. tui.tsx passes `grep: s.queuedGrep`. The queued footer in `hintLine` adds `["/", view.grep ? `search: ${view.grep}` : "search"]` after Ctrl+X. In tui-pane.ts's `queued` branch, list mode with `pane.grep` set prepends a `search: "<grep>"` line. When no row matches, the body is that line plus `(no queued prompt matches "<grep>")`, so the operator can see why the pane is empty. With no grep and in selection mode, rendering is unchanged.
6. Docs: in docs/cli.md, the `/` row of the TUI keys table adds Inbox to its views column, plus the clause "on Inbox, keep only the queued prompts containing the text, each under its unfiltered number, like `prompt --list --grep`". In docs/how-it-works.md, the Inbox pane paragraph gets one sentence on the `/` search.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/inbox.test.ts: `queuedRowsMatching` over rows with texts `Fix Widget`, `other` and `widget two` and grep `WIDGET` keeps the first and third rows with their `position`s. A `null` grep keeps every row.
- test/tui-keys.test.ts, a new test modeled on "the `/` search filters the Backlog pane's active entries, clears, and persists across view cycling". Queue `director alpha` and `director widget` with `enqueuePrompt`, and `clean widget` with `enqueueRolePrompt`. Ctrl+T to the Inbox view, then `/` opens with an empty line. Typing `widget` + Enter sets `state().queuedGrep` to `"widget"`, `state().queuedRows` holds two rows (director position 2 and clean position 1), `paneCache` contains `2. director widget` and not `director alpha`, and the flash is `search: "widget"`. Down selects row 0. Ctrl+X then cancels the director's #2 file (alpha is still queued per `queuedListRows`). Re-opening `/` pre-fills `widget`, and Esc leaves it applied. A Ctrl+T cycle away and back keeps it. An empty line + Enter clears it, and every remaining row shows again.
- The existing test "`/` opens a search on Activity and History with an empty line, types elsewhere, and search mode owns the line" still passes (it types `/` on Usage, not Inbox).
- tui-frame: `hintLine({ kind: "queued", grep: "x" }, …)` names `search: x`. The `queued` pane render with `grep` and no rows shows `(no queued prompt matches "x")`.
- `tumwater prompt --list --grep` output is unchanged: its existing tests pass unchanged, test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts passes, and `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `GET /api/run?last=1` with no `role` serves the newest completed run of any role, and `result`/`model` narrow it the same way: the dashboard API twin of bare `tumwater history --last` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan: none of them edits `handleRun` or src/run/run-detail.ts. Touches src/run/run-detail.ts src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-server-api.test.ts)

**Goal.** `tumwater history --last` with no role opens the newest completed run of any role, and `--result`/`--model` narrow it (PLANS-DONE.md "`tumwater history --last` with no role"). `cmdRunDetail` (src/run/run-detail.ts) resolves it with `newestRunRow(root, null, classes, models)` and takes the role from the row. `GET /api/run` (`handleRun`, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) cannot do this. Its first step is `rejectBadRole(root, res, role)`, so `?last=1` with no role is a 400 "role required". A script asking "what was the newest failed run, whoever ran it" has to fetch `/api/history` and pick a row itself. This plan lets `last` stand without a role. It resolves the run through the same `newestRunRow`, so the CLI and the endpoint cannot pick different runs. It is API-only. A dashboard button that uses it is a separate, later plan.

**Approach.**
1. src/run/run-detail.ts: export `newestRunRow` (today it is module-private). Do not change its body. Extend its doc comment's last sentence with: "Also GET /api/run?last=1 with no role."
2. src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, `handleRun`:
   - Add `newestRunRow` to the existing `../run/run-detail.js` import.
   - Change the role check to `const bareLast = role === null && q.get("last") !== null; if (!bareLast && rejectBadRole(root, res, role)) return;`. A missing role without `last` is still the shared 400. A present role, including an empty one, is still validated as today.
   - Make `role` a `let` binding typed `string | null`. In the `last` branch, replace the `newestRunNumber` call with `const row = newestRunRow(root, role, classFilter, modelFilter);`, then `if (row !== null) role = row.role; run = row?.run ?? null;`. The 404 stays `runNotFoundLastMessage(role, classFilter, modelFilter)`. With no role, `role` is still `null` there, which gives the "any role" wording `cmdRunDetail` prints.
   - After the `last`/numbered branches, `role` is a string, so the existing `role as string` casts stay valid. Remove `newestRunNumber` from the import if nothing else in the file uses it. Check with `grep -n newestRunNumber src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts`. Keep the export in run-detail.ts if any other file still imports it. Check with `grep -rn newestRunNumber src test`, and if nothing uses it, delete it.
   - Doc comment: append to the `last` paragraph: "With no `role`, `last` opens the newest completed run of any role (newestRunRow with a null role, the run bare `tumwater history --last` opens), and the payload's `role` is that run's; `result`/`model` narrow it the same way, and a miss is a 404 worded for any role."
3. docs/how-it-works.md: after the sentence ending "the run `tumwater history <role> --last [--result] [--model]` opens (`newestRunNumber`, shared)." add: "Without `role`, `GET /api/run?last=1` serves the newest completed run of any role, the run bare `tumwater history --last` opens, with the same `result`/`model` narrowing." If step 2 deleted `newestRunNumber`, change that parenthetical to `(newestRunRow, shared)`. `grep -n 'api/run' docs/invariants.md` printed nothing when this was planned, so the plan claims no invariant ID.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts: add a new test, "handleRun ?last with no role serves the newest run of any role". Use the same five-event fixture as "handleRun ?last serves the newest run, narrowed by result and model":
  - `?last=1` answers 200 with `role` "feature" and `run` 5. Its body deep-equals `?role=feature&run=5`'s body.
  - `?last=1&result=problems` answers `role` "clean", `run` 4.
  - `?last=1&model=m-a` answers `role` "clean", `run` 3.
  - `?last=1&model=m-b&result=merged` answers 404 with error equal to `runNotFoundLastMessage(null, ["changes"], ["m-b"])`.
  - `?last=1&result=bogus` is a 400 matching `/result must be one of/`.
  - `?last=1&run=3` is a 400.
- The existing "handleRun's error cases" test passes unchanged. That shows `?run=3` with no role is still a 400. The existing "handleRun ?last serves the newest run…" test also passes unchanged.
- test/gui-server-api.test.ts, "gui /api/run serves one run's detail over the live route, 404 when the scan misses": add that `/api/run?last=1` answers `role` "clean" and `run` 9. That is the newest `run_end` in `historySeedEvents`, so this proves the live route forwards a role-less request.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### TUI Pending pane Ctrl+G cycles the overlapping-files block through each holding role, keeping only the shared files that role holds, each still naming every holder: the terminal twin of `tumwater diff --overlaps --role <id>` and the dashboard Overlapping files card's Role picker (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: Backend/model split part 5/5 changes src/config and test configs, bare `history --last` changes src/run/run-detail.ts and the history CLI, the dashboard Inbox search and `diff?stat=1` plans change src/gui and src/ui/gui. The TUI Inbox `/` search plan also edits src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, but in different arms: its `/` search plumbing and the Inbox hint line, while this plan adds one Ctrl+G routing line and edits the Pending hint line) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The TUI Pending pane (`createPendingPane`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts) lists every file two or more roles' pending changes touch, and Ctrl+N steps through them. It cannot narrow that list to one role. The CLI can (`diff --overlaps --role <id>`, through `scopeChangeOverlaps` in src/change/change-data.ts), and so can the dashboard's Role picker. With several feature instances running, an operator asks "what does feature-3 collide with?", and the terminal should answer it without leaving the TUI. Ctrl+G is free on the Pending view: today the `tui-panes.ts` Ctrl+G router sends it to the report pane's scope arm, which only changes the Usage/Failures scope behind the scenes, and docs/cli.md's Ctrl+G row does not list Pending.

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-pending.ts:
   - `pendingOverlapsText(view, scope?: string)`: with no `scope`, behave exactly as today. With a `scope`, narrow first through `scopeChangeOverlaps(view, [scope])`. A no-base view still returns `""`. An empty narrowed list returns `renderChangeOverlaps(narrowed, [scope])`, which gives the CLI's `no file held by <id> is touched by another pending change`. A non-empty one is headed `overlapping files held by <id> (N):` and then lists `renderChangeOverlaps(narrowed)`.
   - New `export function overlapHolders(view: ChangeOverlapsView): string[]`. It returns the distinct roles named across `view.overlaps` in first-seen order (paths are already sorted, and roles keep holdings order), and `[]` for a no-base view.
   - In `createPendingPane`, add `let overlapScope: string | null = null` and `let head = ""`. `head` is the queue text plus the roster, which today is everything in `base` before the overlaps block. Add a `compose()` helper that sets `base = head + (block ? "\n\n" + block : "")` with `block = pendingOverlapsText(lastOverlaps, overlapScope ?? undefined)`. `refresh()` sets `head = queueText` up front and `head = queueText + "\n\n" + renderTeamChange(team)` on resolve, then calls `compose()`. The painted text with no scope must equal today's text, so the existing Pending tests pass unchanged. `refresh()` does not reset `overlapScope`, so the scope survives Ctrl+R and leaving and re-entering the pane. The module is created once per session in `createTuiPanes`.
   - The Ctrl+N arm steps through the narrowed list: `overlapScope === null ? lastOverlaps : scopeChangeOverlaps(lastOverlaps, [overlapScope])`. `overlapDrillHeading`'s total is the narrowed count. When the narrowed list is empty it flashes the existing "no overlapping files to step through".
   - New Ctrl+G arm, guarded the way the Ctrl+N arm is (`promptLineFree(ctx.es) && session.view === session.roleIds.length + 5`). When `lastOverlaps` is not `ready` or `overlapHolders` is empty, set `overlapScope = null`, call `compose()`, and flash `no overlapping files to scope`. Otherwise cycle `overlapScope` through `[null, ...overlapHolders(lastOverlaps)]`: the next slot after `indexOf(overlapScope)`, so a scope whose role no longer holds a shared file after a refresh goes back to `null`. Then close any open drill-down (`overlapIndex = -1`, `++drillGen`), call `compose()`, set `session.paneCache = base` and `session.paneScroll = 0`, and request a render.
   - Extend the module's doc comment and the Ctrl+N comment to name the Ctrl+G scope.
