### Backend/model split, part 5/5: Retire the namespace spellings as load errors and drop the scalar budget backend (planned 2026-10-19 by user, split 2026-10-19 by the plan role, test migration split out into parts 4b/5 and 4c/5 2026-10-20 by the plan role; requires parts 3/5–4/5, part 4b/5 and part 4c/5 landed; touches src/config/model-selector.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/config/config-fallbacks.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/config/config-aliases.ts src/status/status-budget.ts src/ui/badges.ts docs/config.md docs/backends.md docs/glossary.md test/model-selector.test.ts test/config-validation.test.ts test/config-validation-model.test.ts test/config-views.test.ts test/config-aliases.test.ts test/badges.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**User decision 2026-10-20 (recorded by the director role): merge this without waiting for the operator to migrate tumwater.json first. The break when the live config reloads is accepted; the operator fixes it after the merge. The migration is: `model` drops the namespace (`"claude-sonnet-5-5"`, `"strong": "claude-opus-5-5"`) under the existing `"backend": "claude"`, and the pi fallback becomes `{ "backend": "pi", "model": "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b" }`. Each load error must name that exact edit, because the operator works from those messages.**

**Goal.** A model id never names a backend: each retired spelling fails the load with a message naming the exact edit (the operator chose no shims), and the fleet-wide scalar `BudgetSlice.backend` goes. Series goal and siblings: part 1/5.

**Approach.**
- `routeModel` (src/config/model-selector.ts) loses rule 1 (its `isBackendId(provider)` branch) and rule 3a (`startsWith("claude-")`): the backend is the explicit backend ?? the top-level `backend` ?? `"pi"`, and claude/opencode take the id verbatim on both paths. `seamKeyedFallbackProvider` (src/config/config-fallbacks.ts) follows the same rule (its `isBackendId(provider)` branch goes); a fallback step with no `backend` inherits its tier primary's resolved backend (the tier entry's, else the top level's). `seamAgent` keeps its `agent` read; its `isBackendId(seam.provider)` fallback goes (part 4c/5 moved the seam fixtures that relied on it). The fallback pair (`fallbackPair`, src/config/config-views.ts) carries only `provider: "claude"` for a non-pi backend today and no explicit `agent`, so retiring the `isBackendId(provider)` branch needs that pair to carry its backend first (found by part 4c/5's probe: the fallback-pair tests failed once the namespace spelling was gone). `BACKEND_IDS`' doc comment (src/config/config-schema.ts) drops "doubles as the selector provider namespace", and `isBackendId`'s drops "the reserved selector provider namespace".
- `validateConfig`'s raw pass rejects, each naming the value and the fix: a selector whose first segment is a backend id (`claude/claude-opus-5-5` → write `backend: "claude"` beside `model: "claude-opus-5-5"`); a bare `claude-…` id resolved to pi (add `backend: "claude"`, or write `anthropic/claude-…` to keep it on pi); `opencode/…` resolved to pi (write `backend: "opencode"`). Drop the `agent → backend` row from `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` (src/config/config-aliases.ts) so a top-level `agent` key is an unknown-key error naming `backend`; `agents → backends` stays.
- Delete `BudgetSlice.backend` (src/status/status-budget.ts, its interface field and `backend: cfg.backend ?? "pi"`); src/ui/badges.ts's `agentDefault` uses the constant `pi default`, and the test/badges.test.ts case passing `backend: "claude"` drops that field and asserts the new label.
- docs/config.md, docs/backends.md and docs/glossary.md drop part 3/5's "still load until part 5/5" sentences and the `agent → backend` rename rows; test/config-aliases.test.ts asserts the `agent` error.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n 'isBackendId(provider)\|isBackendId(seam.provider)\|startsWith("claude-")' src/config/model-selector.ts src/config/config-fallbacks.ts` finds nothing; each retired spelling (`claude/<id>`, `opencode/<id>` under pi, bare `claude-…` under pi, top-level `agent`) fails `validateConfig` with a message naming the offending value and the edit.

- `backend: "claude"` with no `model` still resolves claude's three tier defaults and `CLAUDE_GATED_MODELS` still lists exactly those three.
- `BudgetSlice` has no `backend` field. Parts 4b/5 and 4c/5 moved the other test fixtures, so the test files this part edits are the ones its heading lists; `npm test` passes.

**Done note.** Beyond the files above: a fallback pair now carries `backend` (`FallbackModelConfig`, set for a non-pi pair, `provider` staying its seam key), `pairOverrides` (config-views) turns a pair into `withModelOverrides` overrides with an explicit backend, `piPairFree` takes the pair, `applyFallbackModel` writes object tier entries naming the pair's backend on a non-pi team, and the image-reroute marker stores its `backend`. The legacy `fallbackModel` object's own `provider` pins its pair to pi. `BudgetSlice` and the status payload's `budget` lose `backend`. The doctor's "reserved provider" warnings and their two tests are gone, since a pi provider named like a backend now routes to pi. Test fixtures that relied on retired spellings (gate, status, TUI, CLI tests) moved to the `backend` form.

### `GET /api/diff?role=<id>&stat=1` serves the role's diffstat instead of its full patch, and the dashboard drawer's Pending change section gets a Stat only toggle: the twin of `tumwater diff --role <id> --stat` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: none of them touch `handleDiff` in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts or src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts — the Inbox Search plan edits only `handleBacklogMatch` in gui-endpoints.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater diff --role <id> --stat` prints a role's unmerged change as one `git diff --stat` line per file. The dashboard has no twin. `handleDiff` ignores `stat`, so the role drawer's Pending change section always fetches and paints the full patch. A large pending change then fills the drawer when the operator only wants to know which files it touches.

**Approach.**
1. src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts `handleDiff`. Read `const stat = q.get("stat") !== null;`, the same presence test `overlaps` uses.
   - In the `?overlaps` branch, when `stat` is set, send `badRequest(res, "overlaps lists paths, not patches; drop stat")` before collecting. This mirrors `cmdDiff`'s `diff --overlaps prints paths, not patches; drop --stat`.
   - In the team branch (`role === null`), when `stat` is set, send `badRequest(res, "stat needs role (the team roster carries no patch)")`. This sits beside the existing `path needs role` refusal and runs before it.
   - In the role branch, pass `{ ...(path === undefined ? {} : { path }), ...(stat ? { stat: true } : {}) }` to `collectRoleChange`. With `stat` absent, the call matches today's call, so the existing tests' `deepEqual` against `collectRoleChange(root, "feature")` still holds. `stat` combines with `path`, exactly as `diff --role <id> --stat --path <path> --json` does.
   - Extend the doc comment: `&stat=1` serves both halves as the `git diff --stat` summary, exactly `tumwater diff --role <id> --stat --json`.
2. src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts.
   - Add `let drawerChangeStat = false;` beside `drawerChange`. In `openRole`, reset it to false next to the existing `transcriptPrompts = false;`, so each drawer opens on the full patch as the transcript opens with prompts hidden. It is not stored.
   - `loadDrawerChange(role)` fetches `"/api/diff?" + (drawerChangeStat ? "stat=1&" : "") + "role="`, because `loadDrawerSection` appends the encoded role. With the toggle off, the URL stays `/api/diff?role=<id>`.
   - `drawerChangeSection()`: the `sec-head` div gets a `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-change-stat>` after the `<h3>`. Its label is `Stat only` when `drawerChangeStat` is false and `Full patch` when it is true.
   - `drawerChangeHtml` is unchanged. Under stat the `diff` and `uncommittedDiff` fields hold the stat text, which `diffPre` paints.
   - Add `function toggleDrawerChangeStat()`: flip `drawerChangeStat`, then call `loadDrawerChange(openRoleId())`. `loadDrawerSection` already ignores a null role and drops a stale answer.
   - In the `$("drawer")` click listener, before the `button.rowaction` lookup, add `if (clickClosest(ev, "button[data-change-stat]")) { toggleDrawerChangeStat(); return; }`.
3. Docs.
   - docs/how-it-works.md, Pending view paragraph: change "shows a role's full unmerged patch in its drawer" to "shows a role's full unmerged patch in its drawer (its Stat only toggle shows the diffstat instead, `GET /api/diff?role=<id>&stat=1`, the twin of `diff --role --stat`)".
   - docs/invariants.md, the change-data.ts paragraph that names `collectRoleChange`: add that `GET /api/diff?role=<id>&stat=1` serves `collectRoleChange(…, { stat: true })`.

**Files touched.** src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/invariants.md, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test "handleDiff with ?role&stat serves the diffstat view, matching collectRoleChange with stat" in test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, built like "handleDiff with ?role&path serves the path-scoped view…". Feature commits `feature.md` plus an edit to `notes.txt`, then appends uncommitted text to `notes.txt`.
  - `?role=feature&stat=1` answers 200 and deep-equals `collectRoleChange(root, "feature", { stat: true })`.
  - Its `diff` matches `/feature\.md \| /` and does not contain `diff --git`. Its `uncommittedDiff` matches `/notes\.txt \| /`.
  - `?role=feature&stat=1&path=notes.txt` deep-equals `collectRoleChange(root, "feature", { stat: true, path: "notes.txt" })`, and its `diff` does not contain `feature.md`.
- New test "handleDiff refuses stat without role and with overlaps". `?stat=1` answers 400 with an error matching `/stat needs role/`. `?overlaps=1&stat=1` answers 400 with an error matching `/drop stat/`.
- The existing handleDiff tests pass unchanged.
- New test in test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts, modeled on "the role drawer for a role the team no longer has…". Its responses serve `/api/diff?role=gone` (a full patch `diff --git a/x b/x`) and `/api/diff?stat=1&role=gone` (diff ` x | 1 +`).
  - After `toggleRole("gone")` and `flush()`, `drawermeta` contains `data-change-stat`, the label `Stat only` and the full patch.
  - Clicking `button[data-change-stat]`, or calling `toggleDrawerChangeStat()` if the harness cannot dispatch the click, then `flush()`, repaints `drawermeta` with ` x | 1 +`, the label `Full patch`, and no `diff --git`.
  - A second toggle restores the full patch and `Stat only`.
  - Toggling back to stat and then calling `toggleRole("gone")` twice (close, reopen) fetches `/api/diff?role=gone` again and shows `Stat only`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard Inbox tab's Search matches each queued message's full text, not only its 80-character preview, through `GET /api/backlog-match`'s new `queued` key: the dashboard twin of `tumwater prompt --list --grep` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the TUI Inbox `/` search entry edits src/inbox/inbox.ts, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts and src/ui/tui, the Folder picker entry the Pending card, `history --last` src/run/run-detail.ts and src/cli, and part 5/5 config loading — none touches handleBacklogMatch or the Backlog card's Inbox rows; touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-backlog.ts test/gui.test.ts test/gui-client-team.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** The Backlog card's Search box filters Inbox rows by `q.preview + " " + q.role` only (`renderBacklog`'s `hit` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-backlog.ts). `q.preview` is `promptPreview`, which truncates at `PROMPT_PREVIEW_MAX` (80 chars, src/inbox/inbox.ts). So a word past the 80th character of a queued message never matches on the dashboard, while `tumwater prompt --list --grep` (cmdPrompt, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts) matches the full text. The Plans/Bugs/Questions tabs already search entry bodies through `/api/backlog-match`; the Inbox tab should do the same.

**Approach.**
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, `handleBacklogMatch`**: after the `BACKLOG_FILE_READERS` loop, add `out.queued`, the queued messages whose full text contains the trimmed needle, case-insensitively. Each item is `{ role, file }`, where `file` is the queue-file basename. Build it from `queuedListRows(root, null, knownRoleIds(root))` (import from ../inbox/inbox.js; the director comes first, then each catalog role). That list already strips the not-before marker line from `text`, so the matching is exactly what cmdPrompt's `--grep` does: `row.text.toLowerCase().includes(needle.toLowerCase())`. Widen the `out` type to `Record<string, number[] | Array<{ role: string; file: string }>>`. Extend the doc comment to cover the `queued` key and say it is the match `prompt --list --grep` uses.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-backlog.ts, `renderBacklog`**: an Inbox row also counts as a hit when `backlogBodyHits` is current (`backlogBodyHits.needle === backlogGrep`) and `(backlogBodyHits.queued || [])` holds an item with the row's `role` and `file`. Implement this as a small local `queuedHit(q)` beside `hit`, used in the Inbox branch as `if (!hit(q.preview + " " + q.role) && !queuedHit(q)) return "";`. Don't change `hit`'s signature. Update the "Search narrows rows…" comment to say Inbox rows also match full text from /api/backlog-match. `fetchBacklogMatch` and `setBacklogGrep` stay as they are: they already refetch while the Search box has text, including the 5 s refresh in `renderBacklog`.
- No new route, flag or setting. The status poll still carries previews only.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/gui.test.ts, extend "gui /api/backlog-match lists the indexes whose heading or body matches" (or add a sibling test). Queue a director message (`enqueuePrompt`) and a role message (`enqueueRolePrompt` for a catalog role such as `feature`), each with more than 80 characters before the word `zebra`, plus one more message without it. `GET /api/backlog-match?grep=ZEBRA` answers a `queued` array that lists both matching `{ role, file }` pairs (file = basename of the path the enqueue returned), director first, and leaves out the third. The existing keys are unchanged, and the existing deepEqual is updated to include `queued` (an empty array when no messages are queued).
- test/gui-client-team.test.ts, a new test that uses `backlogScope("queued", …)`. The status queues a director message whose preview does not contain `zebra`. With `backlogGrep: "zebra"` and `backlogBodyHits: { needle: "zebra", ...noHits, queued: [{ role: "director", file: <its file> }] }`, the row is painted. With a stale needle (`needle: "zeb"`), it shows "Nothing matches this search". Add `queued: []` to `noHits` so the existing tests keep their shape.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard Pending view's Overlapping files card gets a Folder picker that keeps only the shared files at or under the chosen directory, each still naming every holder: the dashboard twin of `tumwater diff --overlaps --path <dir>` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: no waiting plan touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, test/gui-client-pending.test.ts or docs/how-it-works.md. Touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts test/gui-client-pending.test.ts docs/how-it-works.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `tumwater diff --overlaps --path <path>` and `GET /api/diff?overlaps=1&path=<path>` keep only the shared files at or under a path (`scopeChangeOverlapsToPath`, src/change/change-data.ts, through the private `inPath` rule). The dashboard's Overlapping files card (`pendingOverlapsHtml`, src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts) only has the Role picker. An operator who owns one area cannot narrow the card to it. Add a Folder picker beside the Role picker. Its options are every directory that holds an overlapping file, so it needs no text input. A text input would also lose focus on every repaint, because `paintPendingOverlaps` replaces the card's `innerHTML`. Filtering stays client-side over the one `/api/diff?overlaps=1` document, as the Role picker does.

**Approach** (all in the `GUI_CLIENT_PENDING_JS` string, inside the `pending-table:start`/`pending-table:end` markers for the pure functions):
1. Add `function pendingOverlapDirs(view)`. It returns the sorted, de-duplicated directories of every overlap path. For each overlap whose `path` is a string, strip one trailing `/`, split on `/`, and add each proper prefix (`a`, `a/b` for `a/b/c.ts`). When the path ended in `/` (an untracked-directory entry such as `src/new/`), also add the stripped path itself (`src/new`). A malformed document (not an object, or `overlaps` not an array) returns `[]`, as `pendingOverlapHolders` does. A root-level file such as `README.md` adds nothing.
2. Add the module-level `let pendingOverlapDir = "";` beside `pendingOverlapRole`.

### `GET /api/history?result=<class>[,...]` keeps only the runs in those outcome classes: the dashboard API twin of `tumwater history --result` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the `diff --overlaps --path` plan edits `handleDiff` in the same file, a different function; the Overlapping files Role picker plan changes src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts; part 5/5 of the Backend/model split changes src/config and test configs; touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `tumwater history --result <class>[,...]` narrows the run listing to outcome classes (merged/none/refused/problems), and `GET /api/run?last=1&result=` already accepts the same list (PLANS-DONE.md "`GET /api/run?role=<id>&last=1…`"). `GET /api/history` (`handleHistory`, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) takes `role`, `n`/`sinceMs`/`untilMs`, `grep`, `model` and `summary`, but no `result`. A script asking "feature's failed runs in the last day" has to fetch every row and reclassify them itself, copying `historyClass`. This plan adds `result` to `/api/history`, parsed by the same code `/api/run` uses, so the two endpoints accept and reject the same values.

**Approach.**
1. src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts: extract the class-list loop in `handleRun`'s `last` branch (the `splitCommaList(q.get("result") ?? "")` loop over `parseHistoryResultClass`, with its `result must be one of …${gotSuffix(piece)}${typoSuffix(piece, names)}` 400) into a module-level `function resultClassesQuery(q: URLSearchParams, res: http.ServerResponse): HistoryResultClass[] | null`. It returns the deduplicated classes in first-seen order (`[]` when `result` is absent, empty, or only commas, meaning "filter nothing"), or `null` once it has sent the 400. Give it a one-line doc comment naming both callers. `handleRun` calls it and returns on `null`. Its `classFilter = classes.length ? classes : null` line and its 404 wording stay as they are.

A bad class is then a 400 in both shapes, and it comes before any other 400 that `handleHistory` sends. Add `historyClass` to the existing `../history/history-data.js` import. Define `const inClasses = (rows: RunRow[]): RunRow[] => (classes.length ? rows.filter((r) => classes.includes(historyClass(r.result))) : rows);` beside `onModels`. Apply it after grep and before `onModels` in both the window branch and the count branch, which is the CLI's order (`cmdHistory`: grep, then `--result`, then `--model`). `summary`/`modelSummary` then fold the narrowed rows. With `result` absent the response is the same as today's. Add one sentence to the doc comment: "`result=<class>[,...]` keeps only the runs in those outcome classes (the `history --result` rule, parsed by resultClassesQuery like /api/run's), after `grep` and before `model`; an unknown class is a 400."

**Goal.** `tumwater diff --overlaps` lists every file two or more roles' pending changes touch, and `--role` keeps the files a listed role holds (PLANS-DONE.md "`tumwater diff --overlaps --role`"). This plan replaces both refusals with a filter. Overlaps are still computed across every file, so each kept line still names every holder. Only the printed set narrows, as `--role` does today. The repeat check `rejectRepeatFlag` already runs before the branch. Apply `scopeChangeOverlaps` when `--role` is given, then `scopeChangeOverlapsToPath` when a path is given. Render with `(v) => renderChangeOverlaps(v, scope ?? undefined, path)`. With neither flag, keep calling `renderChangeOverlaps` with one argument, as today. Update `cmdDiff`'s doc comment (`--path` keeps the files at or under that path).

Then `roleListQuery`, then `collectChangeOverlaps`, then scope by roles (when given) and by path (when given). ### `GET /api/run?role=<id>&last=1[&result=<class>[,...]][&model=<selector>[,...]]` serves the role's newest matching run: the dashboard API twin of `tumwater history <role> --last [--result] [--model]` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the `/api/diff?overlaps&role` plan edits `handleDiff` in the same file, a different function; touches src/run/run-detail.ts src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-server-api.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `tumwater history <role> --last` opens a role's newest completed run, and `--result <class>[,...]` / `--model <selector>[,...]` pick the newest run in those outcome classes or on those models (PLANS-DONE.md "`history <role> --last --model`"). `GET /api/run` (`handleRun`, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) only takes an explicit `run=N`, so a script or the dashboard has to fetch `/api/history` and pick a row itself to answer "show me feature's newest failed run". This plan adds `last` to `/api/run`. The run is resolved by the same code the CLI uses, so the two cannot pick different runs. When this was planned, `grep -n '"last"' src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` printed nothing.

**Approach.**
1. src/run/run-detail.ts:
   - Extract the `last` branch of `cmdRunDetail`'s `runNumber` expression into `export function newestRunNumber(root: string, role: string, classes: HistoryResultClass[] | null, models: string[] | null): number | null`. Move the expression as it stands: `readRunRows(root, 1, role)[0]` when both lists are null, else the HISTORY_MAX_RUNS scan through `runRowsOnModels` when `models` is set, then `.find` on `historyClass`; return `?.run ?? null`. `cmdRunDetail` calls it, and its output does not change.
   - Export `runNotFoundLastMessage` and rewrite its doc comment. It currently says the 404 "only ever serves the numbered form, so this wording has no second consumer"; it gets a second consumer here.
2. src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts `handleRun`. Keep the `rejectBadRole` check first. Then set `const last = q.get("last") !== null` (the flag's presence, whatever its value, like `patch`/`transcript`).
   - When `!last`: `q.get("result") !== null` → `badRequest(res, "result needs last")`, and `q.get("model") !== null` → `badRequest(res, "model needs last")` (the CLI's "--result needs --last" rule). Otherwise the existing `intQuery(q, res, "run", "positive")` path runs unchanged.
   - When `last`: `q.get("run") !== null` → `badRequest(res, "last cannot be combined with run (a number and the newest run are rival selectors)")`. `result` is parsed with `splitCommaList` (src/text/text.ts) plus `parseHistoryResultClass` (src/history/history-data.ts), deduplicated. A piece that is not a class → `badRequest` with `` `result must be one of ${Object.values(HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES).join(", ")}${gotSuffix(piece)}${typoSuffix(piece, Object.values(HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES))}` ``, which is the CLI's `parseHistoryResultList` wording without the `history --` prefix. `model` is parsed with `splitCommaListUnique`. For both, an absent value, `""`, or a list with no non-empty piece means null (filter nothing), as `handleHistory`'s `model` does. Do not call `parseHistoryResultList`/`parseHistoryModelList` (src/history/history.ts): they `fail()` (exit the process).
   - Call `newestRunNumber(root, role, classes, models)`. A null result → 404 `{ error: runNotFoundLastMessage(role, classes, models) }`. Otherwise use that number as `run` for the rest of the handler: `readRunDetail`, the existing 404, and `transcriptText`. The 200 payload has the same shape as the numbered form; the resolved number is in `detail.run`.
   - Extend `handleRun`'s doc comment with the `last`/`result`/`model` contract.
3. docs/how-it-works.md: after the "Its search box (applied on Enter) reloads it through `GET /api/run?…&transcript=1&grep=<text>` … toggling prompts clears it." sentence, add: "`GET /api/run?role=<id>&last=1` serves the role's newest completed run instead of a numbered one, and `&result=<class>[,...]` / `&model=<selector>[,...]` narrow it to the newest run in those outcome classes or on those models, the run `tumwater history <role> --last [--result] [--model]` opens (`newestRunNumber`, shared)." `grep -n 'api/run' docs/invariants.md` printed nothing when this was planned, so the plan claims no invariant ID.

- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, new test "handleRun ?last serves the newest run, narrowed by result and model". Use `serveRun` and `source:` events. Seed clean run 3 with `run_start` model `m-a` and result `changed`, then clean run 4 with `run_start` model `m-b` and result `error`, then a feature run 5 (`no_change`). Assert:
  - `?role=clean&last=1` → 200 with `run` 4. Its body `deepEqual`s `serveRun(root, "?role=clean&run=4")`'s body.
  - `&result=merged` → run 3, and so does the hidden class alias `&result=changes` (`parseHistoryResultClass` accepts both); `&result=problems` → run 4; `&model=m-a` → run 3; `&model=m-b&result=merged` → 404 whose error equals `runNotFoundLastMessage("clean", ["changes"], ["m-b"])`; `&result=` → run 4.

### `tumwater prompt --list --grep <text>` keeps only the inbox messages whose text contains the text, each under its unfiltered number, the inbox twin of `questions --grep` and `plan --list --grep` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Backend/model split parts change test configs and src/config, the completion plans change src/cli/completion.ts, the `history --last --result` plan changes the history trail command, and the `diff --path` plan changes `cmdDiff`; this one changes only the prompt command's list mode, its help stanza and docs/cli.md's "Steer the project" row) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `logs`, `history`, `backlog`, `plan --list`, `bug --list` and `questions` each take `--grep <text>`. `tumwater prompt --list` does not, and `prompt --list --grep deploy` fails at `rejectUnknownDoubleDash` (src/cli/cli-command-args.ts) as an unknown flag. An operator who queued several prompts with `--at`, or whose roles are paused with inboxes piling up, has to scan every section to find the message to `--cancel`, `--top` or `--edit`. Add `--grep <text>` to `--list` (and `--list --json`). It keeps the rows whose prompt text contains the text, case-insensitively. Each kept row stays under its own role section with its unfiltered position, so the number printed is still the one `--cancel <n>`, `--top <n>` and `--edit <n>` consume.

**Approach.**
1. `src/cli/cli-command-args.ts`:
   - Add `{ names: ["--grep"], value: true, valueName: "<text>" }` to `PROMPT_FLAG_SPECS`. The unknown-flag gate and the equals-form refusal then admit it, and `rejectDuplicateFlags` refuses a repeat.
   - Add `grep: string | null` to the `mode: "list"` arm of `PromptArgs`.
   - In `parsePromptArgs`, read `const grepFlag = args.indexOf("--grep")` beside the other flag indices. A missing, empty or `--`-leading value fails with `--grep needs text (usage: tumwater prompt --list --grep <text>)`, the wording the backlog list view uses.
   - `--grep` outside list mode fails with `--grep only applies to --list`, checked next to the existing `--json only applies to --list` refusal and before any branch writes. Without this, enqueue mode would refuse it as an unknown flag only by accident.
   - In the list branch, pass `grepFlag, grepFlag + 1` (only when present, like `roleClaim`) to `failStrayArg` and return `grep`.
   - Extend the parser's doc comment flag list with `--grep <text>`.
2. `src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts`, `cmdPrompt`'s `parsed.mode === "list"` branch. After the `--role` filter, also keep rows where `row.text.toLowerCase().includes(parsed.grep.toLowerCase())` when `parsed.grep !== null`. `QueuedListRow.text` is already stripped of the not-before marker, so the marker never matches. Filtering the list-wide rows keeps each row's `position`, the same reason the `--role` filter filters `allRows`.
   - `--json` prints `{ prompts }` with the filtered rows.
   - Empty output: when the role-scoped rows (before the grep) are empty, keep the existing empty-inbox lines unchanged; when they are non-empty but no row matches, print `no queued prompt matches "<text>"`.
3. `src/cli/help.ts`: change the stanza `tumwater prompt --list [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--json]` to `... [--grep <text>] [--json]`. Append `; --grep <text> keeps only the messages containing the text, case-insensitively, under the same numbers` to its description. Completion derives the flag from this stanza; check that `tumwater completion bash` output then lists `--grep` for `prompt` (or note it in VERIFIED if the derivation filters it).
4. `docs/cli.md` "Steer the project" row: after `` `--role <id>[,<id>...]` keeps only the listed roles' sections, under the same numbers `` add `` , `--grep <text>` keeps only the messages containing the text `` (edit with python; the row is one long line).

Queue `director task`, then qa prompts `qa one` and `Deploy the qa fix`, then readme prompt `docs deploy note` (the `submitPrompt`/`submitRolePrompt` helpers). `prompt --list --grep deploy` exits 0. ### TUI History trail Ctrl+W shows the shown run's full commit patch below its stat, and hides it on a second press: the terminal twin of `tumwater history <role> <n> --patch` and the dashboard History drill-down's Show patch button (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight Pending pane Ctrl+N plan also adds a field beside `collectChange` in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts, a neighbouring-line rebase at most; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** The History pane's run trail (Ctrl+N, `createHistoryPane` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts) shows the run's detail and its per-file stat (`loadTrailStat` through the `session.runStat` seam). With Ctrl+R it can also show the agent transcript. It cannot show the patch. The CLI prints it with `history <role> <n> --patch` (`runDetailPatch` in src/run/run-detail.ts), and the dashboard has the drill-down's Show patch button (`GET /api/run?…&patch=1`). So reading what a run actually changed means leaving the TUI. Ctrl+W is free on the History view: the Activity worktree-slots editor (`openCtrl: "w"`, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts) returns false when `ctx.view !== 0`, and the pause editor's Ctrl+W arms in src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts fire only on role views or while that editor is open.

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add `runPatch?(root: string, detail: RunDetail): Promise<string>` to `TuiKeysDeps`, beside `runStat`, with a doc comment that mirrors it. Default it to `runDetailPatch` (`const runPatch = deps.runPatch ?? runDetailPatch;`) and pass it into the session deps next to `runStat`. Add `trailPatch: boolean` to the state interface after `trailTranscript`, with a one-line doc comment (whether the trail shows the run's commit patch, toggled by Ctrl+W).
2. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts: add `runPatch(root: string, detail: RunDetail): Promise<string>` to both interfaces that list `runStat`, and copy it in the session builder (`runPatch: deps.runPatch`).
3. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts, inside `createHistoryPane`:
   - Add closure state next to the trail fields: `let trailPatch = false` and `let trailPatchText: string | null = null`.
   - `composeTrail`: compose `[trailText, trailStat, trailPatchText, trailTranscriptText]`. This is the CLI's order (`renderRunDetail`, then the stat and patch footer, then the transcript) in `cmdRunDetail`'s join (src/run/run-detail.ts).
   - Add `loadTrailPatch(detail)`, shaped exactly like `loadTrailStat`. It captures `trailGen`, calls `session.runPatch(session.root, detail)` and, only while `trailMode && trailPatch && gen === trailGen`, sets `trailPatchText`, calls `composeTrail()` and requests a render. On a rejection it does `session.flashError(err)` under the same guard.
   - `loadTrail`: reset `trailPatchText = null` beside `trailStat = null`. After `loadTrailStat(detail)`, call `loadTrailPatch(detail)` when `trailPatch` is set. This way the patch follows Ctrl+P, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+X and search re-reads, the way the transcript level already does.
   - Turning the trail off (the Ctrl+N toggle-off branch) and `reset()` also set `trailPatch = false` and `trailPatchText = null`, beside the existing `trailTranscript = "off"`.
   - A new `handleKey` arm `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "w")`. It returns false off the History view (`session.view !== session.roleIds.length + 4`). When `!promptLineFree(ctx.es)`, it requests a render and returns true. With no trail (`!trailMode || trailRun === null`), it does `session.flashMessage("open a run's trail with Ctrl+N to show its patch")`. Otherwise it flips `trailPatch`. On: `loadTrailPatch(trailRun.detail)`. Off: bump `trailGen`, then set `trailPatchText = null` and call `composeTrail()`. The bump keeps an in-flight patch from repainting. It also drops an in-flight stat, so re-issue `loadTrailStat(trailRun.detail)` when `trailStat === null`. Either way it sets `session.paneScroll = 0`, requests a render and returns true.
   - Expose `trailPatch` in `state()`. Update the pane's doc comment to list Ctrl+W beside Ctrl+R and Ctrl+V.
4. src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts `handleKey`: add `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "w") return history.handleKey?.(key, ctx) ?? false;` next to the Ctrl+S/Ctrl+Y one-line routes. Add `trailPatch: hist.trailPatch` to the state snapshot beside `trailTranscript`.
5. src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: pass `trailPatch: s.trailPatch` into the history view object. src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: add `trailPatch?: boolean` to the `history` view kind. In the trail-only part of the `history` footer, put `["Ctrl+W", view.trailPatch ? "hide patch" : "patch"]` after the Ctrl+R entry and before Ctrl+V.
6. Docs:
   - docs/cli.md: add a TUI key-table row after the `Ctrl+V` (twice) History row: `Ctrl+W` | History (on a run trail) | show or hide the shown run's full commit patch below its stat (the `history <role> <n> --patch` text and the dashboard History drill-down's Show patch).
   - docs/how-it-works.md: in the History trail paragraph (the one starting "`Ctrl+N` swaps the pane for the newest completed run's full event trail"), add one sentence: `Ctrl+W` adds the run's commit patch below the stat through `runDetailPatch`, the text `history <role> <n> --patch` prints.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/tui-keys.test.ts are built like "the History trail appends the run commit's stat once it resolves". They use `historyTrailRoot`, `openHistory`, and `makeKeys` with a `runStat` stub and a `runPatch` stub passed through its `seams` argument.
- "Ctrl+W on a History trail appends the run's patch after the stat, and a second press hides it": after Ctrl+N, the stat resolves to `" a.ts | 1 +"`. Then Ctrl+W, and the patch stub resolves to `"diff --git a/a.ts b/a.ts"`. `trailCache` then equals `renderRunDetail(detail)` + `"\n\n a.ts | 1 +\n\ndiff --git a/a.ts b/a.ts"`, and `state().trailPatch` is true. A second Ctrl+W restores `renderRunDetail(detail) + "\n\n a.ts | 1 +"`, and `trailPatch` is false.
- "the History trail composes detail, stat, patch, then transcript": Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+R, with both stubs resolved, give the four parts in that order joined by `"\n\n"`.

- "the trail patch follows Ctrl+P, and a late patch from the left run is dropped": with the patch on, Ctrl+P calls the stub again for the older run. Resolving the first call's promise after that leaves `trailCache` without its text. Resolving the second appends it.
- "Ctrl+N off and back on starts the trail without its patch": `trailPatch` is false after re-entering, and the stub is not called again.
- The existing History trail tests ("Ctrl+N on the History pane swaps the rows…", "Ctrl+R on the History trail cycles…", "Ctrl+V twice on a History trail…", "a late stat never overwrites…") pass unchanged. So does "Ctrl+W on Activity edits the pool size; Ctrl+W on a role's Transcript still opens the wake editor".

The default stays `collectRoleChange`, which already takes `opts`. Existing callers that pass two arguments do not change. Do not add a new seam.

   - Add closure state: `let base = ""` (the last full pane text), `let lastOverlaps: ChangeOverlapsView | null = null`, `let overlapIndex = -1` and `let drillGen = 0`.

### `tumwater diff --overlaps --role <id>[,<id>...]` keeps only the shared files a listed role holds, e.g. `diff --overlaps --role feature-2` answers "which of feature-2's files does another role also touch?" (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. It changes the `--overlaps` branch of `cmdDiff`, src/change/change-data.ts and src/change/change-render.ts, which no waiting plan touches. Only src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md are shared with `prompt --list --grep` and `history --last --model`, in other stanzas) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `diff --overlaps` lists every file two or more roles' pending changes touch, and `cmdDiff` (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts) refuses `--role` beside it ("diff --overlaps reads every role; drop --role"). An operator about to review or revert one role's work wants that role's collisions only. Accept `--role` with `--overlaps`: overlaps are still computed across every role (a listed role's file shared with an unlisted role still counts), then only the entries whose `roles` include a listed id are kept. Each kept entry still names all of its holders. Role ids match exactly, the same as `diff --role`: `feature` does not take in `feature-2`.

**Approach.**
- src/change/change-data.ts: add and export `scopeChangeOverlaps(view: ChangeOverlapsView, roles: string[]): ChangeOverlapsView`. It returns `{ ...view, overlaps: view.overlaps.filter((o) => o.roles.some((r) => roles.includes(r))) }`. A `no-base` view passes through with its empty list. The JSON document keeps its `{mainBranch, state, overlaps}` shape, with no new field.
- src/change/change-render.ts: `renderChangeOverlaps(view, scope?: string[])`. When the overlap list is empty and `scope` is given, it prints `no file held by <scope joined ", "> is touched by another pending change`. Without `scope`, it keeps its existing wording. `no-base` wording stays the same in both cases. The existing callers pass no scope: tui-pane-pending.ts `pendingOverlapsText`, and the `sayJsonOrRender` call in `cmdDiff`.
- src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts `cmdDiff`: in the `--overlaps` branch, remove the `--role` refusal (keep the `--stat` and `--path` refusals). Read `parseRoleListScope(root, args)`, which already fails on an empty or unknown piece. When it is non-null, print `scopeChangeOverlaps(view, roles)` and render with `(v) => renderChangeOverlaps(v, roles)`. Otherwise print the unscoped view as today. Update the doc comment on `cmdDiff`.
- src/cli/help.ts: the stanza becomes `tumwater diff --overlaps [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--json]`. Add one sentence: `--role keeps only the files a listed role holds, each still naming every holder`. Completion flags derive from the stanza, so `--role` completes after `--overlaps` with no further change. Check this by running `node dist/cli.js completion bash` after the build and grepping its output.
- docs/cli.md: the `diff --overlaps` row or sentence gets the same addition. docs/invariants.md: in the change-view paragraph that names `tumwater diff --overlaps`, add that `--role` filters the computed overlaps to entries that name a listed role (`scopeChangeOverlaps`). Add `scopeChangeOverlaps` to INV-AU5's **Binds** and the new tests to its **Pinned by**.

**Files touched.** src/change/change-data.ts, src/change/change-render.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/invariants.md, test/cli-diff.test.ts, test/change-render.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/change-render.test.ts, new test "scopeChangeOverlaps keeps entries naming a listed role, each with every holder". It uses overlaps `a.md: feature, clean, bugfix` and `b.md: clean, bugfix`. Scope `["feature"]` → only `a.md`, with all three roles. Scope `["bugfix"]` → both entries. Scope `["qa"]` → empty, and `renderChangeOverlaps(that, ["qa"])` returns `no file held by qa is touched by another pending change`. A `no-base` view with any scope still renders `main branch main does not exist`.
- test/cli-diff.test.ts, new test "diff --overlaps --role keeps the listed roles' shared files". Start from `seededFeatureRepo` (feature holds widget.md). Give `clean` widget.md and solo.md and `bugfix` solo.md, each through `ensureWorktree` with uncommitted files, as the existing overlaps test does. Then:
  - `diff --overlaps` prints both lines.
  - `--overlaps --role feature` prints exactly `widget.md: feature, clean`.
  - `--overlaps --role bugfix` prints exactly `solo.md: bugfix, clean`.
  - `--overlaps --role feature,bugfix` prints both lines in path order.
  - `--overlaps --role feature --json` deep-equals `{mainBranch: "main", state: "ready", overlaps: [{path: "widget.md", roles: ["feature", "clean"]}]}`.
- The existing test "diff --overlaps with no shared file says so, and rejects --role and --stat" is renamed "... and rejects --stat". Its `--role feature` case now expects exit 0 and `no file held by feature is touched by another pending change`. `--overlaps --role nope` exits non-zero with `nope` in stderr.
- The existing `diff --overlaps` tests, the `--path` misuse test, and test/tui-keys.test.ts "the Pending pane lists overlapping files below the roster, through the CLI's renderChangeOverlaps" pass with only the rename above.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### TUI History trail Ctrl+V, pressed twice after a dry-run preview, reverts the shown run's merged change: the terminal twin of `tumwater revert <role> <n>` and the dashboard History drill-down's Revert button (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. The Backend/model split part changes src/config and test configs, `prompt --list --grep` changes the prompt parser and src/inbox, `history --last --model` changes src/run/run-detail.ts and the history CLI, and the overlap drill-down changes src/gui and src/ui/gui. The TUI Health Ctrl+P plan shares tui-keys.ts, tui-pane-session.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-frame.ts and docs/cli.md with this one, but only in neighboring hunks: the deps seams, the Ctrl+P router and the Health footer, where this plan adds new seams, the Ctrl+V router and the History footer; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** An operator who spots a bad merge has three ways to undo it: `tumwater revert <sha>|<role> <n>` (`cmdRevert`, src/operator/operator-commands.ts), the dashboard History drill-down's preview-then-Revert button (`histRevertStep` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts → `handleRevert` in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts), and nothing in the TUI. The TUI already opens a run's full trail on the History view (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P steps to older runs; `createHistoryPane` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts holds the shown run in `trailRun`), so the operator reads the bad run and must then leave for a shell. Add Ctrl+V on a History run trail (mnemonic: re**V**ert). The first press runs `previewRevert` and flashes what it would undo, and arms only when the revert applies cleanly to a clean checkout. A second Ctrl+V right after it commits the revert through `revertMergedCommit`, the same cores the CLI and the dashboard call. Any other key in between disarms it. Ctrl+V is free on the History view. `handleKey`'s Ctrl+V router (src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts) only reaches the queued and backlog arms, which return false off their own views. The attach editor's Ctrl+V is guarded to view 0, and the Transcript pause editor's to views 1..N (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts).

**Approach.**
1. src/operator/revert.ts: export `runRevertSha(role: string, run: number, detail: RunDetail): { ok: true; sha: string } | { ok: false; error: string }`. It moves the two refusals out of `revertRunSha` (src/operator/operator-commands.ts), wording unchanged:
   - `detail.result !== "merged"` gives `` `${role} run #${run} did not merge (result: ${detail.result ?? "unknown"}); there is nothing to revert` ``.
   - A null `runMergedSha(detail)` (src/run/run-detail.ts) gives the "merged but the event log no longer names its commit; pass the sha from git log instead" sentence.
   - Otherwise `{ ok: true, sha }`.

   `revertRunSha` calls it and `fail`s on `!ok`, so the CLI's output is unchanged and the TUI cannot drift from it. Also export the `RevertPreview` interface, for the seam types. If importing `runMergedSha` from src/run/run-detail.ts into revert.ts creates an import cycle (check with `npm run test:gate`'s lint), put `runRevertSha` in src/run/run-detail.ts instead and import it from there in both places.
2. src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add two optional seams to the deps type, each with a doc comment in the style of `killOrphans?`:
   - `previewRevert?: typeof previewRevert`
   - `revertCommit?: typeof revertMergedCommit`

   In `createTuiKeys`, default them to the real cores (`deps.previewRevert ?? previewRevert`, `deps.revertCommit ?? revertMergedCommit`) and pass both into `createTuiPanes`.
3. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts:
   - Add `previewRevert` and `revertCommit` to `TuiPanesDeps`, to the session interface, and to `createTuiPaneSession`'s object.
   - Add the armed pair beside `armedKillOrphans`/`killOrphansArmed`: `armedRevert: string | null` (the full sha a second Ctrl+V reverts) and `revertArmed: string | null` (the pending arm), both initialized null, with doc comments in the same style.
4. src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts:
   - `beginKey`: add `session.armedRevert = session.revertArmed; session.revertArmed = null;`.
   - `handleKey`'s Ctrl+V router: put `if (history.handleKey?.(key, ctx)) return true;` first, ahead of the queued arm, and update the router comment.
5. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts, `createHistoryPane`:
   - Add `let reverting = false;`.
   - Add a Ctrl+V arm. It returns false off view `session.roleIds.length + 4`. On that view it always returns true after `session.requestRender()`, and acts only when `promptLineFree(ctx.es)`:
     - With the trail off, flash `open a run's trail with Ctrl+N to revert its change`.
     - While `reverting` is set, flash `a revert is already running`, so a held key never starts a second git operation.
     - Otherwise, `runRevertSha(trailRun.role, trailRun.run, trailRun.detail)` with `!ok` flashes its error.
     - **Second press** (`session.armedRevert === sha`): set `reverting = true` and flash `` `reverting ${shortSha(sha)} …` ``. Then `void session.revertCommit(session.root, sha)`:
       - On `ok`, flash `` `reverted ${shortSha(sha)}: main is now ${shortSha(r.headSha)}` `` plus `` `; ${followUp}` `` when `revertFollowUp(r.subject)` is non-null. These are the CLI's lines joined with "; ".
       - On `!ok`, flash `r.error`.
       - A rejection goes through `session.flashError`.
       - In `finally`, clear `reverting` and `session.armedRevert`, and request a render.
     - **First press**: set `reverting = true`, capture `const gen = trailGen`, and flash `` `previewing the revert of ${shortSha(sha)} …` ``. Then `void session.previewRevert(session.root, sha)`. When it resolves, apply its result only if `gen === trailGen`, so a trail closed or stepped since gets no stale arm. Each outcome flashes:
       - `!p.ok` flashes `p.error`.
       - `!p.applies` flashes `` `would conflict on ${p.primary} (HEAD ${shortSha(p.head)}); nothing was written` ``.
       - `p.dirty` flashes the CLI's "the checkout has staged or unstaged changes, so tumwater revert would refuse until they are committed or stashed; nothing was written".
       - Otherwise set `session.revertArmed = p.sha` and flash `` `press Ctrl+V again to revert ${shortSha(p.sha)} ${p.subject} (${p.paths.length} file${p.paths.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}) on ${p.primary} — any other key keeps it` ``.

       A rejection goes through `session.flashError`. In `finally`, clear `reverting` and request a render.
   - `reset()` also clears `session.revertArmed` and `session.armedRevert`.
   - Add a comment on the arm naming the CLI and dashboard twins and the two-press rule.
   - Extend the factory doc comment to mention Ctrl+V.
6. src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: in the `view.kind === "history"` footer, in the `view.trail ? [...]` spread that holds Ctrl+P/Ctrl+R, add `["Ctrl+V", "revert run"]` after the Ctrl+R entry.
7. Docs:
   - docs/cli.md TUI key table: add a row after the `Ctrl+R` | History (on a run trail) row: `` | `Ctrl+V` (twice) | History (on a run trail) | preview, then revert the shown run's merged change on main (the terminal twin of `tumwater revert <role> <n>` and the dashboard History drill-down's Revert; the first press arms only when the revert applies cleanly to a clean checkout, and any other key disarms it) | ``.
   - docs/cli.md Steer row (a long line, so edit it with python): after "the dashboard's History drill-down offers the same revert, preview first", add ", and so does the TUI History trail's Ctrl+V (twice)".

**Files touched.** src/operator/revert.ts, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, docs/cli.md, test/operator-revert.test.ts, test/tui-keys.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/operator-revert.test.ts, new case "runRevertSha refuses an unmerged run and a merged run naming no commit, and returns the merged sha": a `RunDetail` with `result: "changed"` gives the did-not-merge error naming the role and run, a merged detail with no `mergedSha` and no commit-bearing merge event gives the no-longer-names error, and one with `mergedSha` returns it.
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: write the events with a merged run (`run_end` `result: "merged"` and a `merge_done` carrying `commit`), open History and its trail with Ctrl+N, and inject `previewRevert`/`revertCommit` fakes that record their calls and resolve on demand. New cases:
  - "Ctrl+V twice on a History trail previews then reverts the run's merged commit": the first Ctrl+V calls the preview fake with the commit and flashes `/previewing/`. After a preview resolves with `applies: true, dirty: false`, the flash matches `/press Ctrl+V again/`, and the next Ctrl+V calls the revert fake once with the same sha. When that resolves, the flash matches `/main is now/`.
  - "a key between the two Ctrl+V presses disarms the revert": Ctrl+V, resolve the preview, any other key (e.g. PgDn), Ctrl+V. The second Ctrl+V calls the preview fake again and never the revert fake.
  - "a conflicting or dirty preview never arms": a preview with `applies: false` flashes `/would conflict/`, one with `dirty: true` flashes `/staged or unstaged/`, and a following Ctrl+V previews again rather than reverting.
  - "Ctrl+V on an unmerged run's trail flashes the CLI's refusal": a trail of a `result: "changed"` run flashes `/did not merge/` and calls neither fake.
  - "Ctrl+V off a History trail never reverts": on the History rows (trail off) it flashes `/Ctrl\+N/` and calls neither fake. On the Backlog and Queued views the existing Ctrl+V cases still pass unchanged.
- The existing History trail cases (the "Ctrl+N on the History pane swaps…", "Ctrl+P steps the trail back…" and "Ctrl+R on the History trail cycles…" tests) and the existing Ctrl+V cases pass unchanged.

### TUI Health tab Ctrl+P re-probes every image-input model: the terminal twin of the dashboard Health card's Re-probe models button and `tumwater doctor --reprobe` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Backend/model split part changes src/config and test configs, `prompt --list --grep` changes the prompt parser and src/inbox, `history --last --model` changes src/run/run-detail.ts and the history CLI, and the overlap drill-down changes src/gui and src/ui/gui. This one touches only the TUI Health pane, its key routing and footer, and docs) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The image-input check's failure says to fix the endpoint and then run `tumwater doctor --reprobe`. The dashboard can do this with its Health card's Re-probe models button (`handleDoctorReprobe` in src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, which runs `runDoctor` with `probeImages` `"all"`). Add Ctrl+P on the Health view (mnemonic: **P**robe). It re-runs the doctor checks with every claimed image-input model re-probed and paints the result. Ctrl+P is free on Health: the provider-caps editor's Ctrl+P opens on view 0 only, the Transcript pause editor's on views 1..N only, the report arm in `handleKey` (src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts) is routed for Usage/Failures only, and History's Ctrl+P arm (`tui-pane-history.ts`) returns false off view N+4. While `reprobing` is set, it flashes `a re-probe is already running` and returns true without calling the seam, so a held key never spends a second round of probes. ### Dashboard overlap drill-down: clicking a path on the Pending view's "Overlapping files" card shows each holding role's pending change limited to that path, served by `GET /api/diff?role=<id>&path=<path>`, the dashboard twin of `tumwater diff --role <id> --path <path>` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Backend/model split part changes src/config and test configs, `prompt --list --grep` changes the prompt command, `history --last --model` changes run detail, and the Re-probe button changes the Health card and gui-operator-commands.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `diff --role <id> --path <path>` (`diffPathArg` and `cmdDiff` in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, `opts.path` on `collectRoleChange` in src/change/change-data.ts) shows what each role did to a file that `diff --overlaps` names. The dashboard has no twin. Its Pending view's "Overlapping files" card (`pendingOverlapsHtml` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts) prints one `path: role, role` line per shared file, and nothing on it opens. The operator has to open each role's drawer and scroll its whole patch to find the hunks for that one file. `handleDiff` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) ignores a `path` query. This plan has two parts. The endpoint learns `?path=`. Each overlap line becomes a toggle that expands, under the line, every listed role's change scoped to that path.

**Approach.**
1. src/change/change-data.ts: export `normalizeDiffPath(raw: string): string | null`. Move the body of `diffPathArg`'s rule into it unchanged: strip leading `./` pieces and trailing `/`, and return null for an empty, `.`, absolute (`isAbsolute` from node:path) or `..`-bearing result. `diffPathArg` (cli-query-commands.ts) calls it and keeps its `fail(...)` message byte-for-byte. The `isAbsolute` import moves with the rule if nothing else in cli-query-commands.ts uses it.
2. src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts `handleDiff`: read `const rawPath = q.get("path")`.
   - In the `overlaps` branch, after the existing role refusal: `rawPath !== null` → `badRequest(res, "overlaps reads every file; drop path")`.
   - When `role === null` and `rawPath !== null` → `badRequest(res, "path needs role (the team roster carries no patch)")`.
   - With a role, after `rejectBadRole`: when `rawPath !== null` and `normalizeDiffPath(rawPath)` is null → `badRequest(res, "path takes a repo-relative path such as src/cli.ts (as overlaps lists it)")`. Otherwise call `collectRoleChange(root, role, { path })`, passing `{}` when there is no path so the unscoped document is unchanged.
3. src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts `drawerChangeHtml`: make it read a path-scoped view.
   - After the `no-base` check, when `typeof view.path === "string"` and both `commits` and `dirty` are empty, return `<p class='muted'>No pending change to <esc path>.</p>`. This mirrors `renderRoleChange`'s `no pending change to <path>` rule.
   - The note line gains ` · limited to <esc path>` when `view.path` is a string.
   - Unscoped views render exactly as now.
4. src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, inside the `// pending-table:start` … `// pending-table:end` region:
   - Add a pure `overlapDetailHtml(rows)`. `rows` is an array of `{ role, state: "loading" | "ok" | "error", view?, message? }`. Each row renders `<h3 class='mono'>` + `esc(roleLabel(role))` + `</h3>`, then `Loading…` for loading, the escaped message (fallback `Pending change unavailable`) for error, or `drawerChangeHtml(view)` for ok. Both functions live in the one spliced client script, so the call resolves the way `pendingTableHtml` already reaches `roleLabel`.
   - `pendingOverlapsHtml(view, open)` gains an optional second argument `open` (`{ path, rows }` or null). Each overlap line becomes `<button type='button' class='li-open mono clamp1' data-overlap='<index>'>` holding the same `esc(path) + ": " + roles` text, so the existing text assertions still match. The line whose `path === open.path` is followed by `<div class='overlap-detail'>` + `overlapDetailHtml(open.rows)` + `</div>`. With no `open` the output is the current markup except for the button wrapper.
5. Same file, outside the region:
   - Add module state `let pendingOverlapOpen = null`.
   - Add `async function togglePendingOverlap(index)`. It reads `pendingOverlaps.overlaps[index]` and returns when that entry is missing. When the entry's path is the open one, it sets `pendingOverlapOpen = null` and repaints. Otherwise it sets `{ path, rows }` with every role `loading` and repaints. Then it fetches each role in parallel with `getJson("/api/diff?role=" + encodeURIComponent(role) + "&path=" + encodeURIComponent(path))` and stores each result as `ok` or `error` (`err.message`). A reply is dropped when `pendingOverlapOpen` no longer holds that path, the same stale-answer rule as `loadDrawerSection`. It repaints after each reply.
   - The repaint is a `paintPendingOverlaps()` helper that sets `$("pendingoverlaps").innerHTML = pendingOverlapsHtml(pendingOverlaps, pendingOverlapOpen)`. `fetchPendingOverlaps` uses it too, and sets `pendingOverlapOpen = null` before its fetch, so Refresh closes the detail rather than showing a stale patch.
   - `buildPendingView` attaches one delegated `click` listener on `$("pendingoverlaps")`: `const b = e.target.closest("[data-overlap]"); if (b) togglePendingOverlap(Number(b.dataset.overlap));`.
6. Docs:
   - docs/how-it-works.md, the dashboard paragraph that cites `GET /api/diff?overlaps=1`: add that clicking a listed file shows each role's change to it (`GET /api/diff?role=<id>&path=<path>`, the twin of `diff --role --path`).
   - docs/invariants.md, the change-data paragraph that ends "`diff --role <id> --path <path>` scopes `collectRoleChange` …": add "and so does the dashboard's `GET /api/diff?role=<id>&path=<path>`, both normalising the path through `normalizeDiffPath`".

**Files touched.** src/change/change-data.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui-client-pending.test.ts, test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/invariants.md.

Build the setup of "handleDiff with ?overlaps serves collectChangeOverlaps's document…": feature commits `feature.md` and edits `notes.txt`. `serveDiff(root, "?role=feature&path=notes.txt")` is 200 and deep-equals `await collectRoleChange(root, "feature", { path: "notes.txt" })`. ### Dashboard Health card "Re-probe models" button: `POST /api/doctor-reprobe` runs the doctor with every claimed image-input model re-probed and answers the report, the dashboard twin of `tumwater doctor --reprobe` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Backend/model split part changes src/config and test configs, `diff --path` changes cmdDiff and src/change, `prompt --list --grep` changes the prompt parser and src/inbox, `history --last --model` changes src/run/run-detail.ts and the history CLI, and the comma-list completion plan changes src/cli/completion.ts. This one touches only the GUI doctor path and docs/backends.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The image-input check's failure tells the operator to fix the endpoint and then run `tumwater doctor --reprobe`. The dashboard's Settings → Health card runs the same checks through `GET /api/doctor`, but `handleDoctor` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) always passes `probeImages` `"never"`, so the card only shows the cached verdicts. That is deliberate: a refresh or Re-run must never spend a model call. As a result, an operator working in the dashboard has to go to a terminal to clear a stale or failed probe verdict. Add an explicit, separate action that spends the probe on purpose: a "Re-probe models" button on the Health card. It POSTs to a new `/api/doctor-reprobe`, which runs `runDoctor` with `probeImages` `"all"` (what `--reprobe` passes) and answers the same `DoctorReport`, and the card paints that report. `GET /api/doctor`, Re-run and the TUI Health tab keep `"never"`.

**Approach.**
1. src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts: beside `handleKillOrphans`, add
   `export async function handleDoctorReprobe(req, res, root, run: (root: string, probeImages: "all") => Promise<DoctorReport> = (r, p) => runDoctor(r, undefined, undefined, p))`.

4. src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts:

Otherwise it sets the flag, calls `buildSettingsView()`, shows `Re-probing…` in `#doctorbody` (the `Checking…` empty-panel shape), and calls `showFlash("Re-probing image-input models…")`. Then it runs `const report = await postJson("/api/doctor-reprobe", {})`, sets `lastDoctor = report` and paints `renderDoctorReport(report, doctorProblems)`. On a throw it paints `errorPanel("Health checks could not run", err, "empty")` and calls `showFlash("error: " + clientErrorMessage(err))`. A `finally` clears the flag.

### Comma-list completion skips the items already typed: `--role qa,<TAB>` offers `feature` and `feature-2` but not `qa` again, for every comma-list flag in bash, zsh and fish (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the `diff --path` plan also edits src/cli/completion.ts, but only its flag/path tables, not `_tumwater_list` or the fish value functions) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `--role`, `--result`, `--type` and `history --model` take comma lists, and completion fills in the item after the last comma ("Shell completion past the comma", PLANS-DONE.md). It still offers items the list already holds: today `history --role qa,<TAB>` offers `qa,qa` (pinned by test "the bash script completes the item after the last comma of --role, --result and --type lists"), and `history --result merged,<TAB>` offers `merged,merged`. A repeated item is never useful. Completion should offer only the items not yet in the list.

**Approach.**
1. src/cli/completion.ts `bashScript`, the `_tumwater_list` helper: build the word list from `$1` minus the items in `head`, then pass that list to `compgen`. Use exactly this body:
   ```
   _tumwater_list() {
     local head="" word words=""
     [[ "$2" == *,* ]] && head="${2%,*},"
     for word in $(printf '%s\n' "$1"); do
       [[ ",$head" == *",$word,"* ]] || words+="$word "
     done
     COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -P "$head" -W "$words" -- "${2##*,}") )
   }
   ```
   Write `$(printf '%s\n' "$1")`, not `$1`: the zsh script runs this function under bashcompinit, and zsh does not word-split a bare `$1`, but it does split a command substitution. The plan run checked this body in bash and in zsh with `bashcompinit`. Both gave `qa,feature qa,feature-2` for `qa,`, and `feature,feature-2 feature,qa` for `feature,`. The `,$head` / `,$word,` framing matches whole items, so `feature,` still offers `feature-2`. Update the helper's `#` comment to say it also drops the items already listed. The four call sites (`--role`/role positional, `--result`, `--type`, `history --model`) do not change. The role-positional case never holds a comma, so `head` is empty and nothing is dropped.
2. src/cli/completion.ts `fishScript`: add a filter function next to `__tumwater_argc`:
   ```
   function __tumwater_unlisted; set -l typed (string split , -- (string match -r '^.*,' -- (commandline -ct))); while read -l word; contains -- $word $typed; or echo $word; end; end
   ```
   Emit it as one TS template-string line like the others, escaping `\` as the neighbouring lines do. `string match -r '^.*,'` yields the token up to its last comma, or nothing when the token has no comma. Then pipe the four list sources through it: `__tumwater_roles` becomes `tumwater completion --roles 2>/dev/null | __tumwater_unlisted`. Do the same for `__tumwater_models`, and for `__tumwater_results` and `__tumwater_types` (pipe their `printf`). `__fish_complete_list` calls these functions while the commandline still holds the token, so `commandline -ct` reads the list being typed. Out of scope: the `--role=qa,` spelling. Its first item reads `--role=qa`, so nothing is dropped, and completion behaves as it does today.
3. Update the `fishFlagValue` doc comment to say the per-item completion skips the items already listed.
4. docs/cli.md, the `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` paragraph: change "a comma-list value (`--role`, `--result`, `--type`) completes its last item, keeping the items before it" to "a comma-list value (`--role`, `--result`, `--type`, `history --model`) completes its last item, keeping the items before it and skipping those already listed".

**Files touched.** src/cli/completion.ts, docs/cli.md, test/completion.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test "the bash script completes the item after the last comma of --role, --result and --type lists", the last assertion changes to `["tumwater", "history", "--role", "qa,"]` → `["qa,feature", "qa,feature-2"]`. The other four assertions there are unchanged and still pass.
- New test "the bash script skips the items a comma list already holds". It uses the existing `complete` helper, whose fake `tumwater` prints `feature feature-2 qa` for roles and `hf/m-a:deepinfra hf/m-b` for `--models`:
  - `history --role feature,` gives `["feature,feature-2", "feature,qa"]`, so a prefix-sharing id is kept.
  - `logs --role feature,qa,feature-2,` gives `[]`.
  - `history --result merged,` gives the three other class names from `HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES`, each prefixed `merged,`.
  - `logs --type run_start,run_` holds no `run_start,run_start`, and holds `run_start,run_end`.
  - `history --model hf/m-b,` gives `["hf/m-b,hf/m-a:deepinfra"]`.
- In the fish test "the fish script completes values after --role, path flags, --template, and --result, and config keys at word 3", or a new one: the script has a `function __tumwater_unlisted` line, and each of the `function __tumwater_roles`, `__tumwater_results`, `__tumwater_types` and `__tumwater_models` lines contains `| __tumwater_unlisted`.
- New test, `{ skip: !fishInstalled }`: `complete -C 'tumwater history --result merged,'` lists no `merged,merged`.
- "the fish script parses under fish when fish is installed", "fish completes the item after the last comma of a --result list", "the zsh script wraps the bash script in bashcompinit", and the existing bash role/result/type/model completion tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater diff --role <id>[,<id>...] --path <path>` limits each listed role's pending view to one file or directory: its commits that touch the path, the patch and the uncommitted edits under it. This is the follow-up to `diff --overlaps`, which names a shared file but cannot show what each role did to it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. It shares src/cli/completion.ts with the in-flight "Shell completion past the comma" plan only through a one-word `PATH_FLAGS` addition, so rebase onto it if that one lands first; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater diff --overlaps` prints `src/cli.ts: feature, bugfix`. To see what each role did to that file, the operator today reads both roles' whole patches (`diff --role feature,bugfix`), which can be up to `DIFF_MAX_BYTES` each. `--path <path>` keeps only the part of each view under one repo-relative path. The diff is git's, through a literal pathspec, so a directory path covers everything below it. `tumwater diff --role feature,bugfix --path src/cli.ts` then shows exactly the two edits that will meet at merge.

**Approach.**
1. **Flag.** In src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, beside `OVERLAPS_FLAG`, add `DIFF_PATH_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--path"], value: true, valueName: "<path>", missingValue: DIFF_PATH_VALUE_ERROR }`, with `DIFF_PATH_VALUE_ERROR = "diff --path needs a path (e.g. \`--path src/cli.ts\`)"`. Give each a doc comment in the style of its neighbours. No other command accepts `--path` today (grep `"--path"` in src finds nothing).
2. **cmdDiff** (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts): add `DIFF_PATH_FLAG` to its `rejectUnknownArgs` list. Read the value with `flagValue(args, "--path")` (src/cli/cli-args.ts) and fail a repeat through `rejectRepeatFlag` (count the `--path` tokens). Then normalise the value: strip leading `./` pieces and trailing `/` characters. Fail with `diff --path takes a repo-relative path such as src/cli.ts (as diff --overlaps prints it)` when the result is empty, when `path.isAbsolute` holds, or when any `/`-separated segment is `..`. Order the checks this way:
   - In the `--overlaps` branch, `--path` fails with `diff --overlaps reads every file; drop --path`, beside the existing `--role`/`--stat` rejections.
   - In the team branch (`roles === null`), `--path` fails with `diff --path needs --role <id> (the team roster prints no patch)`, the `--stat` wording's twin.
   - Otherwise pass `path` into the opts of `collectRoleChange`/`collectRoleChanges` next to `stat`.
3. **Collector** (src/change/change-data.ts): widen both opts types to `{ stat?: boolean; path?: string }`. In `collectRoleChange`, when `opts.path` is set, let `spec = ["--", \`:(literal)${opts.path}\`]`. Then:
   - `commits` comes from `git log --oneline ${mainBranch}..HEAD ...spec`, so only commits touching the path are listed. `ahead` and `behind` stay whole-branch counts.
   - The committed patch: the `--stat` branch appends `spec`, and the patch branch calls `aheadOfMainDiff(wt, mainBranch, DIFF_MAX_BYTES, spec)`. Compute either one only when `commits.length > 0`, not when `ahead > 0`.
   - `dirtyFiles` keeps an entry `f` when `f === path`, or `f.startsWith(path + "/")`, or `f` ends with `/` and `path.startsWith(f)`. The last case is porcelain's untracked-directory entry.
   - The uncommitted patch: give `cappedWorkingDiff(wt, spec: string[] = [])` the same spec, appended to both its `git diff HEAD` and its over-cap `--stat` call. Apply it to the `--stat` branch too.
   - Return `path: opts.path` on the view. In `RoleChangeView`, add `path?: string` with a doc comment: present only under `--path`, so the unscoped JSON (`diff --json`, the dashboard's /api/diff) is unchanged.
4. **aheadOfMainDiff** (src/git/git-diff.ts): add a 4th parameter, `pathspec: string[] = []`, appended to both its `git diff ${range}` and its over-cap `git diff --stat ${range}` calls. Its other caller, `src/review/review-run.ts`, passes nothing and keeps its behavior.
5. **Render** (src/change/change-render.ts `renderRoleChange`): when `view.path` is set and `view.commits.length === 0 && view.dirtyFiles.length === 0` (state ready), return `no pending change to ${view.path} for ${view.role}`. Otherwise, the first line gains `; limited to ${view.path}` after `workSummary(...)`. That summary's commit count stays the branch's; its uncommitted-file count is the scoped one. The other lines are unchanged.
6. **Help and completion.** In src/cli/help.ts, the `tumwater diff --role` stanza's usage line gains `[--path <path>]`, plus one clause: "--path keeps only the commits, patch and uncommitted edits under that repo-relative file or directory (composes with --stat, --json and a comma list)". Add `"--path"` to `PATH_FLAGS` in src/cli/completion.ts so its value completes file names. Flag-name completion comes from the help stanza.
7. **Docs.** In the docs/cli.md "See a role's pending change" row, add the same clause after the `--stat` parenthetical, and say that a path with nothing pending prints `no pending change to <path> for <id>`. ### `history <role> --last --result <class>[,...]` opens the role's newest run in the listed outcome classes, e.g. `history feature --last --result problems` jumps straight to its latest failure's trail (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: the Backend/model split parts change test configs and src/config, the two completion plans change src/cli/completion.ts, and the `--list --ready` plan changes the backlog list view; this one changes the one-run trail command, the history `--result` parser and the CLI arg helpers) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** To read a role's last failure today, you run `tumwater history --role feature --result problems -n 1`, copy the run number, then run `tumwater history feature <n>`. `history <role> --last` jumps to the newest run of any outcome. Add `--result` to the `--last` form so one command does it: `history <role> --last --result <class>[,<class>...]` prints the trail of the role's newest completed run whose outcome class is listed. It uses the same classes and spellings as the listing's `--result` (merged, none, refused, problems; `changes` stays a hidden alias), and it composes with `--stat`, `--patch`, `--transcript [--prompt] [--grep]` and `--json` exactly as `--last` does.

**Approach.**
1. src/history/history.ts: move the body of cmdHistory's `--result` validation (from the empty-value check through the deduplicating `parseHistoryResultClass` loop) into an exported `parseHistoryResultList(raw: string | undefined): HistoryResultClass[]`. It fails with `HISTORY_RESULT_VALUE_ERROR` on a missing, empty or all-commas value, and with the existing `history --result must be one of …` wording (gotSuffix + typoSuffix) on an unknown piece. cmdHistory calls it in place of the inline loop, and the listing behaves as before.
2. src/cli/cli-args.ts: add `parseResultFlag(args, missingValueError): { rest: string[]; raw: string | null }` beside `parseTypeFlag`, built on the module-local `takeValuedFlag` the same way. It removes the value token so `peelPositionals` cannot read `problems` as a run number.
3. src/cli.ts `runTrailCommand`: after `parseGrepFlag`, call `parseResultFlag(ungrepped, HISTORY_RESULT_VALUE_ERROR)` (import the constant alongside `HISTORY_GREP_VALUE_ERROR`), and peel positionals from its `rest`. Add `{ names: ["--result"] }` to that call's `rejectUnknownArgs` spec list, matching the `--grep` entry. Pass `result: raw` to cmdRunDetail. `historyTrailForm` (cli-command-args.ts) already skips `--result`'s value through `HISTORY_LISTING_VALUED_FLAGS`, so `history feature --last --result problems` already routes to the trail form. Do not change it.
4. src/run/run-detail.ts `cmdRunDetail`: add an option `result?: string | null` (default null).
   - After the `--grep needs --transcript` check, fail with `history --result needs --last on a one-run trail (usage: ${RUN_DETAIL_USAGE})` when `result !== null && !last`.
   - Otherwise parse it with `parseHistoryResultList(result)`.
   - With classes, the `--last` scan becomes `readRunRows(root, HISTORY_MAX_RUNS, role).find((r) => classes.includes(historyClass(r.result)))?.run ?? null`. Without them, keep today's `readRunRows(root, 1, role)[0]`.
   - A miss stays exit 0, printing `null` under `--json`. In prose, the wording comes from `runNotFoundPhrase(role, \`completed run with result "${flagNames}"\`)`, where `flagNames` is the classes mapped through `HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES` and joined with `,`. It reads, for example, `no completed run with result "problems" for bugfix in the scanned window (the retained log may have rotated past it)`. Keep this wording module-local beside `runNotFoundLastMessage`, and give that message an optional classes argument instead of adding a third helper.
   - `RUN_DETAIL_USAGE` becomes `tumwater history <role> [<n>] [--last [--result <class>[,...]]] [--stat] [--patch] [--transcript [--prompt] [--grep <text>]] [--json]`. Update the cmdRunDetail doc comment's synopsis and add one sentence on `--result`.
5. src/cli/help.ts: update the trail stanza's synopsis to the new usage. After the `--last` sentence, add `--result <class>[,...] (with --last) picks the newest run in the listed outcome classes instead (the listing's --result classes; scans the role's last 200 runs);`, wrapped to the stanza's column.
6. docs/cli.md "Watch run history" row: after "`tumwater history <role> --last` shows the newest completed run's trail instead of numbering one", add "; `--last --result <class>[,...]` picks the newest run in the listed outcome classes (`history feature --last --result problems` opens its latest failure)".

Out of scope: shell completion of `--result` after a trail form (src/cli/completion.ts is held by two in-flight plans), and the TUI/GUI trail views.
