### Shell completion past the comma: `--role a,<TAB>`, `--result merged,<TAB>` and `--type run_end,<TAB>` complete the next list item (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the Backend/model split parts change test configs and src/config, and the TUI History model filter touches only src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md's TUI keys table; it shares src/cli/completion.ts with the in-flight "Shell completion for `history --model`" plan, see step 4) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `--role`, `--result` (history) and `--type` (logs) take comma lists (`parseRoleListFlag`, src/cli/cli-args.ts, and the help text for `history` and `logs` in src/cli/help.ts). Shell completion only completes the first item. In bash, `compgen -W … -- "$cur"` matches the whole word, so `history --role qa,fe<TAB>` offers nothing because no role id starts with `qa,fe`. In fish, the `-a` lists offer only bare words. After this change, the item after the last comma completes, and the items already typed stay in front of it: `qa,fe<TAB>` gives `qa,feature qa,feature-2`.

**Approach.**
1. src/cli/completion.ts `bashScript`: emit a helper function before `_tumwater() {`:
   ```
   _tumwater_list() {
     local head=""
     [[ "$2" == *,* ]] && head="${2%,*},"
     COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -P "$head" -W "$1" -- "${2##*,}") )
   }
   ```
   Give it a one-line `#` comment saying it completes the item after the last comma of a comma-list value and keeps the items before it as the prefix. bash's default `COMP_WORDBREAKS` does not contain `,`, so `cur` holds the whole list. zsh's bashcompinit `compgen` also accepts `-P` (checked in /usr/share/zsh/5.9/functions/bashcompinit). Then change three arms so they call `_tumwater_list "<words>" "$cur"` instead of setting `COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W … -- "$cur") )`:
   - the `--role` / role-positional arm, with words `$(tumwater completion --roles 2>/dev/null)`. The positional case never holds a comma, so it behaves as it does now.
   - the `--result` arm.
   - the `--type` arm.
   Leave `--template`, `--thinking`, `--by` and `role --model` as they are, because they take one value.
2. src/cli/completion.ts `fishScript`: next to `__tumwater_doctor_checks`, push three function lines:
   - `function __tumwater_roles; tumwater completion --roles 2>/dev/null; end`
   - `function __tumwater_results; printf '%s\n' <HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES values>; end`
   - `function __tumwater_types; printf '%s\n' <EVENT_TYPE_CODES>; end`
   
   Write each `printf` as a TS template string in the same way as the doctor-checks line. In `fishFlagValue`, return `` ` -x -a "(__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_roles)"` `` for `--role`, and the same with `__tumwater_results` and `__tumwater_types` for `--result` and `--type`. `__fish_complete_list` is fish's own helper in share/functions: it splits the token on the separator and prefixes each candidate. The role-positional `complete` line keeps `(tumwater completion --roles 2>/dev/null)` unchanged.
3. Update the `EVENT_TYPE_CODES` doc comment, or add a short comment above the three call sites, to say these three flags take comma lists and so complete per item.
4. `history --model` is also a comma list. If the "Shell completion for `history --model`" plan has merged when you start (`grep -n 'completion --models' src/cli/completion.ts` prints its arm), route its bash arm through `_tumwater_list "$(tumwater completion --models 2>/dev/null)" "$cur"`. Also give fish a `function __tumwater_models; tumwater completion --models 2>/dev/null; end` with `(__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_models)`, and add the matching assertions below. Then drop that plan's "Comma lists are not completed past the first item" remark wherever it was copied into a code comment. If that plan has not merged, skip this step.
5. docs/cli.md, in the `tumwater completion bash|zsh|fish` paragraph: after "and check names after `doctor`", add "; a comma-list value (`--role`, `--result`, `--type`) completes its last item, keeping the items before it". Put it inside the parenthesis.

**Files touched.** src/cli/completion.ts, docs/cli.md, test/completion.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test "the bash script completes the item after the last comma of --role, --result and --type lists". It uses the existing `complete` helper, whose fake `tumwater` prints `feature feature-2 qa`:
  - `["tumwater", "history", "--role", "qa,fe"]` at cword 3 gives `["qa,feature", "qa,feature-2"]`.

- The existing bash tests "the bash script completes role ids after --role and for role/history/revert", "…result classes after their flags" and "…event-type codes after logs --type" pass without edits.
- In the fish test "the fish script completes values after --role, path flags, --template, and --result, and config keys at word 3":
  - every `-l role` line includes `__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_roles`.
  - a `-l result` line includes `__fish_complete_list , __tumwater_results`.

  - the script has a `function __tumwater_results` line that includes `problems`, and a `function __tumwater_types` line that includes `merge_failed` and `run_start`. These replace the old `includes("problems")` and `includes("merge_failed")` checks on the flag lines.

### Backend/model split, part 4c/5: Move test configs off namespaced and prefix-routed model ids to an explicit `backend` (planned 2026-10-19 by user, split 2026-10-20 by the plan role from part 5/5 after the feature role's trial run; independent of every eligible plan — it changes only test files; part 4b/5 edits some of the same files for the `agent` key, a rebase either way; touches test/budget-gates.test.ts test/config-write.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-boot.test.ts test/team-hold.test.ts test/team-polls.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/pi-models.test.ts test/role-view.test.ts test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts test/opencode-catalog.test.ts test/config-live.test.ts test/startup-gate.test.ts test/runner-pi-claude.test.ts test/doctor.test.ts and any further test file the probe below names; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** Part 5/5 removes the two routing rules where the model id picks the backend. Both live in `routeModel` (src/config/model-selector.ts): a `claude/…` or `opencode/…` provider runs that backend (the `isBackendId(provider)` branch), and a bare `claude-…` id runs on claude (the `startsWith("claude-")` branch). 5/5 also removes the matching `isBackendId(provider)` branch in `seamKeyedFallbackProvider` (src/config/config-fallbacks.ts) and `seamAgent`'s `isBackendId(seam.provider)` fallback (model-selector.ts). Part 4/5 moved the `model: "claude/…"` literals. The trial run found these spellings still relied on:
- bare `claude-…` ids with no `backend: "claude"` in scope;
- `claude/<id>` and `opencode/<id>` strings in `fallback` values and chains;
- resolved-seam fixtures that name the backend only through `provider: "claude"` / `"opencode"`.

This part rewrites them first. Series goal and siblings: part 1/5; part 4b/5 handles the `agent` key.

**Approach.** Mechanical, one theme, no src change. Each rewrite resolves to the same backend and model as before, so assertions stay as they are.
- A bare `claude-…` id resolved with no explicit backend (top-level `backend` unset or `pi`): add `backend: "claude"` to its section. A tier-map entry becomes the object form `{ backend: "claude", model }`, and a role or review section gains the key.
- A `"claude/<id>"` or `"opencode/<id>"` fallback string or chain step: becomes `{ backend: "claude" | "opencode", model: "<id>" }`, the part 2/5 step form.
- A resolved seam or pair fixture that names the backend only through `provider: "claude" | "opencode"`: gains `agent: "<id>"`, and its `provider` is dropped, the shape `routeModel` produces for these backends.
- Leave alone the cases part 4/5 already left: rendered display labels (`claude/claude-sonnet-5-5`), OpenCode argv (`--model opencode/<id>`), opencode catalog keys, event/history fixtures, and the legacy-rule pins in test/model-selector.test.ts, test/config-views.test.ts and test/config-validation*.test.ts. Each pin you touch gets the `// legacy spelling, retired in part 5/5` comment.
- **Probe** (local only, never committed):
  1. In `routeModel`, make `backend` = `provider === undefined ? configBackend : "pi"`.
  2. In `seamKeyedFallbackProvider`, make it `provider === undefined ? config.backend : "pi"`.
  3. In `seamAgent`, return `seam.agent ?? "pi"`.
  4. Run `npm run test:gate` into a scratch log and migrate each failing test whose cause is one of the three spellings above.
  5. Restore with `git checkout -- src/config` and re-run the gate.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `git diff --stat main` names only files under test/.
- With the probe applied, the gate's failures are confined to the legacy-pin files part 5/5 rewrites: test/model-selector.test.ts, test/config-views.test.ts, test/config-validation.test.ts, test/config-validation-model.test.ts and test/badges.test.ts. The run's VERIFIED line names the probe's remaining failing files.
- `npm run test:gate` passes on the committed tree (src restored).

The other listed files needed no edit: their `provider: "claude"` values are payload passthroughs, not routing, and no probe run failed in them. **Finding for part 5/5:** the probe still fails five tests outside the legacy-pin files — doctor-model-checks (two fallback-seam checks), doctor, role-view (a claude model-fallback episode) and startup-gate (a claude seam only as a fallback) — and, with `seamAgent`'s probe step applied, more in budget-gates and pi-models. ### `plan --list --ready` and `bug --list --ready` keep only the entries a role could claim, each under its unfiltered number, the numbered twin of `tumwater backlog --ready` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the Backend/model split parts change test configs and src/config, the TUI History model filter touches src/ui/tui, and the two completion plans touch src/cli/completion.ts; this one touches the backlog list view, help and docs only; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater backlog --ready` hides held entries (`readyBacklog`, src/backlog/backlog-render.ts), but it prints no position numbers. `plan --list` and `bug --list` print the numbers that `--top`/`--edit`/`--cancel`/`--show` take, but they cannot hide held entries. A long backlog with blocked series and refused bugs buries the claimable ones. With `--ready`, `plan --list` and `bug --list` keep only the entries whose hold is null. Each entry keeps its unfiltered position, so `plan --list --ready` followed by `plan --top <n>` acts on the entry that was printed.

**Approach.**
1. src/backlog/backlog-cli-view.ts `listAndAnnounce`: add a `ready` boolean to the argument loop, parsed like `--done`, with `rejectRepeatFlag(ready, "--ready")`. After the `-n needs --done` check, add `if (ready && done) fail("--ready needs the active list (finished entries carry no holds)")`.
2. In the active branch, after `matches` is computed (the grep filter), add `const kept = ready ? matches.filter((m) => (entryHolds[m.position - 1] ?? null) === null) : matches;` and `const hidden = matches.length - kept.length;`. Then use `kept` instead of `matches` in the JSON branch, the prose rows, and the bug lines. An entry a role is working on has no hold, so it stays with its `[working on it: …]` mark, as `readyBacklog` keeps it. Positions stay the unfiltered `position` values. The JSON shape does not change; it just has fewer entries.
3. Prose endings:
   - The existing `no …s` and `no …s match "<grep>"` lines keep their conditions.
   - Add a new case after them: `kept.length === 0` with `ready` set prints `no ${noun}s ready (${hidden} held; run \`tumwater ${command} --list\` to see them)`.
   - When `hidden > 0` and something is kept, push a last line after the rows (and after the grouped-series footnote when there is one): `(${hidden} held entries hidden; run \`tumwater ${command} --list\` to see them)`. This matches `cmdBacklog`'s wording.
4. Update the `listAndAnnounce` doc comment with one sentence on `--ready`: it keeps entries with no hold under their unfiltered numbers, composes with `--grep` and `--json`, and is refused with `--done`.
5. src/cli/help.ts: change the `tumwater plan --list [--grep <text>] [--json]` and `tumwater bug --list [--grep <text>] [--json]` stanzas to `[--ready] [--grep <text>] [--json]`. Add to each stanza's description: "--ready keeps only the entries no hold keeps from being picked (entries a role is working on stay), under their unfiltered numbers".
6. docs/cli.md: in the "Steer the project" row's `--list` sentence, after the `--grep <text>` clause on the active `--list`, add "; `--ready` keeps only the entries no hold keeps from being picked, under their unfiltered numbers (composes with `--grep` and `--json`; not with `--done`)".

**Files touched.** src/backlog/backlog-cli-view.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/backlog-write-list.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria** (in test/backlog-write-list.test.ts, reusing `seededPlansForList` and `seededBugsForList`; part 2/2 is blocked, and bug 1 is refused):
- New test "plan|bug --list --ready keeps the claimable entries under their unfiltered numbers":
  - `plan --list --ready` prints `planned features in PLANS.md:`, then `1. <p1><age suffix>`, then `(1 held entries hidden; run \`tumwater plan --list\` to see them)`.
  - `bug --list --ready` prints `open bugs in BUGS.md:`, then `2. <b2><age suffix>`, then the same hidden line naming `bug --list`.

- "help topics name the --list forms" now matches `tumwater bug --list \[--ready\] \[--grep <text>\] \[--json\]` and the plan equivalent.

### Shell completion for `history --model`: a `tumwater completion --models` hook prints the model selectors recent runs started on, and the bash/zsh/fish scripts complete them after `history --model` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan — the Backend/model split parts change test configs and src/config, and the TUI History model filter touches only src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md's TUI keys table) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `tumwater history --model <selector>[,...]` keeps only the runs that started on the listed selectors. Those selectors are long, exact strings (`huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:deepinfra`), and you can only find them by running `history --summary --by model` first. Shell completion offers role ids after `--role` through the dynamic `tumwater completion --roles` hook, and config keys through `--config-keys`. For `history --model` it offers nothing: `fishFlagValue` (src/cli/completion.ts) says "`history --model` takes run selectors read from the log", and the test "the bash script completes summary groups after --by and tier names after role --model" asserts `tumwater history --model ""` completes `[]`. Add a third dynamic hook that reads those selectors from the log.

**Approach.**
1. src/cli/completion.ts: add an exported `completionModels(root: string): string[]` beside `completionRoleIds`. It returns the distinct non-null `model`s of `readRunRows(root, HISTORY_MAX_RUNS, null)` (src/history/history-data.ts), sorted with `compareCodeUnits` (src/collections.ts). That is the same order `summarizeRunRowsByModel` lists them. Wrap the read in `try { … } catch { return []; }`, with a doc comment in the `completionRoleIds` style: an unreadable or absent log must not write errors into the operator's prompt, and outside a repo it prints nothing.
2. src/cli.ts, `case "completion"`: after the `--config-keys` arm, add `if (args.length === 1 && args[0] === "--models") { for (const m of completionModels(root)) say(m); break; }`, and import `completionModels` beside `completionRoleIds`.
3. src/cli/completion.ts `bashScript`: after the `role --model` arm, add a `history --model` arm: `if [ "$prev" = "--model" ] && [ "${COMP_WORDS[1]}" = history ]; then COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$(tumwater completion --models 2>/dev/null)" -- "$cur") ); return 0; fi`. zsh gets it through the bashcompinit wrapper (`completionScript`). `fishFlagValue`: replace the comment and add `if (flag === "--model" && command === "history") return \` -x -a "(tumwater completion --models 2>/dev/null)"\`;`. Keep the `role` tier arm first. The new comment says `role --model` completes the closed tier set and `history --model` completes the log's selectors.

Leave a one-line comment on the bash arm saying so. Do not add colon-rejoining logic. Comma lists are not completed past the first item, which is the same behavior as `--role`.

Change "`tumwater completion --roles` and `tumwater completion --config-keys` print the role ids and config keys that script completes" so it also lists `tumwater completion --models` and the model selectors.

### TUI Usage and Failures past windows: `Ctrl+P` on the Usage or Failures pane steps the Ctrl+E trailing window back one window length at a time, wrapping to the trailing window after the 7-day cap. This is the terminal twin of the dashboard Usage/Failures ◀ Earlier buttons and `tumwater report --since --until` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan in behavior. It shares src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-frame.ts and the docs/cli.md `Ctrl+P` rows with the in-flight "TUI History past windows", so rebase onto it if that one lands first; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `collectReportSince(root, sinceMs, role, untilMs)` (src/report/report-data.ts) and `collectFailureReportSince(root, sinceMs, role, untilMs)` (src/failure/failure-data.ts) already collect a bounded past window. `renderSinceReportMarkdown` and `renderFailureMarkdown` already label that window with `boundedWindowLine` (src/text/datetime.ts): `window: 2h to 1h ago (since …, until …)`. `tumwater report --since 2d --until 1d` and the dashboard's Usage/Failures step buttons (PLANS-DONE.md "Dashboard Usage and Failures past windows") use them. The TUI's Usage and Failures panes only have the Ctrl+E cycle of trailing windows (`REPORT_WINDOWS`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts), so the terminal cannot show "yesterday's spend". This plan adds a step that moves the window back by its own length.

**Key choice.** `Ctrl+P` has no meaning on Usage (view N+2) or Failures (N+3) today. `createTuiPanes`'s `handleKey` (src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts) sends every Ctrl+P to `history.handleKey`, whose arm returns false off the History view. The provider-caps editor's Ctrl+P (`createProviderCapsEditor`, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts) only acts on view 0. The transcript pause arm (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts) only acts on views 1..N. "Previous" means an earlier window here, as it will on History. The step wraps like every other TUI cycle, so no "later" key is needed.

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts: beside `REPORT_WINDOWS`, export a pure helper `steppedWindowBounds(windowMs: number | null, step: number): { sinceMs: number | null; untilMs: number | undefined }`.
   - It returns `{ sinceMs: windowMs, untilMs: undefined }` when `windowMs` is null or `step` is 0.
   - Otherwise it returns `{ sinceMs: (step + 1) * windowMs, untilMs: step * windowMs }`.
   - If "TUI History past windows" has landed, its `historyWindowBounds` (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts) computes the same thing. Make it call this helper or replace it, so the two panes cannot drift.
2. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts, `createReportPane`:
   - Add `let reportStep = 0;` next to `reportWindow`. Its comment says how many window lengths back the window ends; it is session-only, and 0 means the trailing window.
   - `usagePaneCache` and `failuresPaneCache` gain a trailing `step: number` parameter. When `sinceMs !== null`, they take `const b = steppedWindowBounds(sinceMs, step)` and pass `b.sinceMs!` and `b.untilMs` to `collectReportSince` / `collectFailureReportSince` as the 4th argument. With step 0, `untilMs` is `undefined`, so the call matches today's call. `recompute` passes `reportStep`.
   - The Ctrl+E arm sets `reportStep = 0` before `nextInCycle`.
   - Add a Ctrl+P arm. It applies when `key.ctrl && key.name === "p"`, the view is `session.roleIds.length + 2` or `+ 3`, and `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` holds. Restate the same editor guards as the Ctrl+E arm.
     - If `reportWindow === null`, call `session.flashMessage("pick a window with Ctrl+E to step back through earlier windows")`.
     - Else if `(reportStep + 2) * reportWindow <= REPORT_SINCE_MAX_MS` (src/events/event-window.ts), do `reportStep += 1`.
     - Otherwise set `reportStep = 0` and flash `"oldest window reached; back to the last " + cycleLabel(REPORT_WINDOWS, reportWindow)`.
     - In the last two cases call `recompute()`, which resets the scroll as Ctrl+E does. Return true with `session.requestRender()`. Off those two views, return false.
   - Ctrl+G and `dropScopes` keep the step, as they keep the window. Update the module's top doc comment to name Ctrl+P.
   - `state()` gains `reportStep`.
3. src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts:
   - Change the Ctrl+P routing line so that on views `roleIds.length + 2` and `+ 3` it returns `report.handleKey?.(key, ctx) ?? false`. Every other view still goes to `history.handleKey`. Add a one-line comment.
   - Map `reportStep: rep.reportStep` beside `reportSince`.
   - src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add `reportStep: number` to the state type beside `reportSince`, with a doc comment.
4. src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: in the usage/failures hint list, right after the Ctrl+E pair, add `["Ctrl+P", "earlier window"]` when `view.window` is non-null. The view type does not change; the pane body's window line names the stepped span.
5. Docs:
   - docs/cli.md TUI key table: add a row `| `Ctrl+P` | Usage, Failures | with a window chosen (Ctrl+E), step it back one window length (the `report --since --until` window), wrapping to the trailing window after the 7-day cap |`. Put it after the `Ctrl+P` History row. Read the rows with `grep -n` and `cut -c1-200` first.
   - docs/how-it-works.md: after the sentence "`Ctrl+E` cycles a session-only trailing window for the Usage and Failures panes …", add one sentence. It says that `Ctrl+P` steps that window back by its own length through the same `--until` bound `tumwater report --since --until` uses, that the body's window line names the span, and that Ctrl+E returns to the trailing window.

**Tests.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts, beside "Ctrl+E cycles the Usage and Failures panes' trailing report window and resets the scroll", using its `makeKeys(root, () => now)` / `writeEvents` setup:
  - "Ctrl+P on Usage steps the report window back one window length, and Ctrl+E resets it". Seed `feature` `run_end` events with `result: "error"`: run 1 at `now - 30m` with `tokens: 100`, run 2 at `now - 90m` with `tokens: 200`, and run 3 at `now - 2.5d` with `tokens: 300`. Keep the existing test's `// retired-name-ok` comments on the `loop:` fields.
    - Open Usage and press Ctrl+E for 1h. Ctrl+P gives `reportStep` 1, and `paneCache` matches `/window: 2h to 1h ago/` and `/200 output tokens/`, and does not match `/100 output tokens/`.
    - Ctrl+E three times (6h, 1d, 7d) then once more wraps to default with step 0. Ctrl+E twice more reaches 6h, then once more 1d. Two Ctrl+P presses give step 2, `/window: 3d to 2d ago/` and `/300 output tokens/`.
    - Ctrl+T to Failures keeps step 2, and the digest matches `/window: 3d to 2d ago/` and `/· 1 runs/`.
  - "Ctrl+P wraps the stepped report window after the 7-day cap". On 1d, after six Ctrl+P presses `reportStep` is 6 and `paneCache` matches `/window: 7d to 6d ago/`. A seventh press sets step 0, and the flash matches `/oldest window reached; back to the last 1d/`. On 7d, one Ctrl+P leaves step 0 and flashes the same wording with `7d`. Read the flash the way neighbouring flash tests in that file do.
  - "Ctrl+P on the default report window only flashes the Ctrl+E hint": `reportStep` stays 0, `paneCache` is unchanged, and the flash matches `/Ctrl\+E/`.
  - The existing Ctrl+E test and every History Ctrl+P test must pass unchanged.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts, beside the usage hint assertion: `hint({ kind: "usage", scope: null, window: "1h" })` and the failures twin match `/Ctrl\+P earlier window/`. With `window: null` they do not.
- A unit test of `steppedWindowBounds`, in the test file that already tests tui-pane-session.ts exports (find it with grep), or in test/tui-keys.test.ts: `(3_600_000, 0)` → `{ sinceMs: 3_600_000, untilMs: undefined }`, `(86_400_000, 2)` → `{ sinceMs: 259_200_000, untilMs: 172_800_000 }`, `(null, 3)` → `{ sinceMs: null, untilMs: undefined }`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On Usage or Failures with a trailing window chosen, each Ctrl+P moves the body to the window `(k+1)·len` to `k·len` ago. It is collected through `collectReportSince` / `collectFailureReportSince` with `untilMs`, and the body's window line reads `window: X to Y ago`. The hint shows `Ctrl+P earlier window`.
- The step wraps to 0, with a flash, once the next window's start would pass `REPORT_SINCE_MAX_MS`. So 1h steps up to 167 times, 6h up to 27, 1d up to 6, and 7d never.
- Ctrl+E resets the step. Ctrl+G and a view change keep it. With the default window, Ctrl+P only flashes the Ctrl+E hint. Step 0 calls the collectors exactly as today.
- Ctrl+P on every other view behaves as before: Activity caps, Transcript pause, History trail.
- docs/cli.md and docs/how-it-works.md describe the key. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard Activity past windows: "◀ Earlier" and "Later ▶" buttons on the Activity card step a Last hour / 6 hours / day window back one window length at a time through `GET /api/logs?sinceMs=&untilMs=` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. It touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, test/gui-client-team.test.ts and docs/how-it-works.md's Activity sentence. "TUI History past windows" touches only TUI files, their tests, docs/cli.md and docs/how-it-works.md's History sentence; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `handleLogs` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) already serves a bounded past window, `?sinceMs=S&untilMs=U` validated by `untilMsQuery` (src/gui/gui-args.ts). The Activity card's `#feedwindow` select (PLANS-DONE.md "Dashboard Activity window picker") only asks for trailing windows. So "the last hour" can never become "the hour before that", although the History, Usage and Failures views all step this way. This plan gives the Activity card the same ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ buttons, the twin of `tumwater logs --since --until`.

**Behavior, decided** (all logic in src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts, inside the `// activity:start` / `// activity:end` region):
- State: `let feedStep = 0;` beside `feedWindow`. It is view state and is not persisted, like History's `histStep`, so a reload returns to the trailing window. Its comment says: how many window lengths back the window ends.
- Helpers beside `FEED_WINDOWS`:
  - `const FEED_MAX_MS = 604_800_000;` mirrors the server's `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` (src/events/event-window.ts). A comment says the two must agree, and a test pins it.
  - `feedCanStepEarlier(windowMs, step)` returns true exactly when `windowMs` is non-zero and `(step + 2) * windowMs <= FEED_MAX_MS`. So Last day steps back at most 6 times, 6 hours 27 times and Last hour 167 times. It takes the number (`Number(feedWindow)`).
  - `feedSpan(ms)`: "1 hour"/"N hours", or "1 day"/"N days" for a whole number of days. It uses the same rule as `histSpan` (src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts). That helper lives in another region, which `feedScope` does not load, so the feed keeps its own copy.
  - `feedWindowPhrase()`: at step 0 it returns the window's FEED_WINDOWS phrase ("the last hour"). Otherwise it returns `"between " + feedSpan((feedStep + 1) * w) + " and " + feedSpan(feedStep * w) + " ago"`, where `w = Number(feedWindow)`. This is the History view's wording.
- `feedLogsQuery()`: when `feedWindow` is set and `feedStep > 0`, the first params are `"sinceMs=" + (feedStep + 1) * w` and `"untilMs=" + feedStep * w`, followed by grep and role in their current order. In every other case the URL is exactly what it is today.
- renderFeed:
  - The re-arm key becomes `feedRole + "\u0000" + feedText + "\u0000" + feedWindow + "\u0000" + feedStep`, so a step change re-arms `searchFeed()` the way a window change does.
  - The live-window refetch branch also requires `feedStep === 0`. A stepped window ends in the past, so a new event can never fall inside it, and polls never refetch it.
  - The two windowed empty states use `feedWindowPhrase()` in place of `windowPhrase`. So a stepped empty window reads "No events between 2 hours and 1 hour ago", and with a filter set it reads "No events match this filter between 2 hours and 1 hour ago". Build each head as `"No events " + (feedStep ? "" : "in ") + phrase` and `"No events match this filter " + (feedStep ? "" : "in ") + phrase`, so step 0 keeps today's exact wording.
  - When `feedStep > 0` and `feedResults !== null`, paint `"<li class='empty muted feed-note'>Showing events " + feedWindowPhrase() + ".</li>"` first in the panel, ahead of the sparse note.
  - At the end of renderFeed, set the controls: `$("feedstep").style.display = feedWindow ? "" : "none"`, `$("feedearlier").disabled = !feedCanStepEarlier(Number(feedWindow), feedStep)`, and `$("feedlater").disabled = feedStep === 0`.
- Listeners, registered at load next to the `#feedwindow` one:
  - A `click` listener on `$("feedearlier")` does `feedStep += 1` only when `feedCanStepEarlier(Number(feedWindow), feedStep)`.
  - A `click` listener on `$("feedlater")` does `feedStep = Math.max(0, feedStep - 1)`.
  - Each then calls `renderFeed(lastStatus)` when `lastStatus` is set.
  - The `#feedwindow` change listener and `clearFeedFilter()` set `feedStep = 0`. The Role picker, Search box, Notable/All choice and type chips keep the step.
- Update the region's head comment and the module doc comment with one clause each: on a window, ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ step it back by its own length through `?sinceMs=&untilMs=`, the twin of `tumwater logs --since --until`.

**Page.** In src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, directly after the `#feedwindow` `<label>`, add `<span id="feedstep" style="display:none"><button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" id="feedearlier">◀ Earlier</button><button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" id="feedlater">Later ▶</button></span>`.

**Docs.** In docs/how-it-works.md, after the sentence ending "…the twin of `tumwater logs --since`, refreshing when a new event arrives.", add this sentence: its ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ buttons step that window back by its own length through `/api/logs?sinceMs=&untilMs=`, the twin of `logs --since --until`, and a stepped window does not refresh.

**Tests** (test/gui-client-team.test.ts):

### TUI History past windows: `Ctrl+P` with the run trail off steps the History pane's trailing window back one window length at a time, wrapping to the trailing window after the 7-day cap, the terminal twin of the dashboard History ◀ Earlier buttons and `tumwater history --since --until` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan: it touches only TUI files, their tests and the TUI key docs, while "Dashboard Activity window picker" and "Dashboard Usage and Failures past windows" touch src/ui/gui/ files) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `readRunRowsSince(root, sinceMs, role, untilMs)` (src/history/history-data.ts) already serves a bounded past window. `tumwater history --since 2d --until 1d` and the dashboard History view's ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ buttons (PLANS-DONE.md "Dashboard History past windows") use it. The TUI History pane's Ctrl+S window cycle (`HISTORY_WINDOWS`, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts) only offers trailing windows, so the terminal can never show "yesterday". This plan adds a step that moves the pane's window back by its own length, one press at a time.

**Key choice.** `Ctrl+P` on the History view with the trail off currently falls through to nothing. In `createHistoryPane`'s Ctrl+P arm (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts), the `!trailMode` case returns false. The Activity caps editor's Ctrl+P is guarded to view 0 (`createProviderCapsEditor`, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts), and the Transcript pause editor only acts on a role's view. Off the trail, "previous" means an earlier window; on a trail it keeps its existing meaning, an older run. Like every other TUI cycle it wraps, so no "later" key is needed. Every other free Ctrl letter is already bound on some view (docs/cli.md TUI table). Ctrl+B and Ctrl+F both fire from History today.

**Approach.**
1. src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts, `createHistoryPane`:
   - Add `let historyStep = 0;` next to `historyWindow`. Its comment: how many window lengths back the window ends. It is session-only like the window, and 0 means the trailing window.
   - Add a module-level pure helper `historyWindowBounds(windowMs: number | null, step: number): { sinceMs: number | null; untilMs: number | null }`. It returns `{ sinceMs: windowMs, untilMs: null }` when `windowMs` is null or `step` is 0. Otherwise it returns `{ sinceMs: (step + 1) * windowMs, untilMs: step * windowMs }`. Export it for the tests.
   - `selectPaneRows` gains a trailing `step: number` parameter. The windowed branch calls `readRunRowsSince(session.root, bounds.sinceMs, role, bounds.untilMs)`. `historyPaneCache` gains a `step` parameter and passes it on. Both `historyPaneCache(...)` call sites and the trail's `selectPaneRows(...)` call pass `historyStep`, so Ctrl+N opens, and Ctrl+P on a trail walks, the stepped window's runs.
   - Header: when `sinceMs !== null && step > 0`, the window line reads `"window: between " + durationLabel((step + 1) * sinceMs) + " and " + durationLabel(step * sinceMs) + " ago"`. That is the wording `tumwater logs --since --until` prints (src/cli/log-commands.ts). Import `durationLabel` from src/cli/cli-args.ts, which TUI files already import from (tui-input.ts, tui-editor-pause.ts). It prints whole units, so 30 hours is `30h`; do not use `humanSeconds`, which rounds that to `1d`. When `step` is 0 the line stays `window: last <label>`. The sparse-window note keeps its current condition.
   - Ctrl+P arm: keep the trail branch exactly as it is. When the view is History, the trail is off and `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` holds:
     - If `historyWindow` is null, flash `"pick a window with Ctrl+S to step back through earlier windows"`.
     - If `(historyStep + 2) * historyWindow <= LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` (src/events/event-window.ts, the cap `history --since` rides), do `historyStep += 1`.
     - Otherwise set `historyStep = 0` and flash `"oldest window reached; back to the last " + cycleLabel(HISTORY_WINDOWS, historyWindow)`.
     - In the last two cases call `recompute()`, which resets the scroll as Ctrl+S does.
     - The arm then returns true with a render. Off the History view it still returns false.
   - The Ctrl+S arm sets `historyStep = 0` before cycling. Ctrl+G, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+Y, `/` and `reset()` keep the step, the way they keep the window.
   - `state()` gains `historyStep`.
2. src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add `historyStep: number` to the state type, with a doc comment, beside `historySince`. src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: map `historyStep: hist.historyStep` beside `historySince`.
3. src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: in the History hint list, when `!view.trail && view.since`, add `["Ctrl+P", "earlier window"]` right after the Ctrl+S pair. The view type does not change.
4. Docs:
   - docs/cli.md TUI key table: change the `Ctrl+P` History row's Where cell to `History`. Its text becomes: "on a run trail, the next older run's trail among the pane's filtered runs, wrapping to the newest after the oldest; with the trail off and a window chosen (Ctrl+S), step the window back one window length (the `history --since --until` window), wrapping to the trailing window after the 7-day cap". Read the row with `grep -n` and `cut -c1-200` first.
   - docs/how-it-works.md: after the sentence "On History, `Ctrl+S` cycles the pane's trailing window …", add one sentence. It says that with the trail off, `Ctrl+P` steps that window back by its own length through the same `readRunRowsSince` bound `tumwater history --since --until` uses, that the header names it as `window: between X and Y ago`, and that Ctrl+S returns to the trailing window.
   - Extend `createHistoryPane`'s top doc comment the same way.

**Tests.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts, next to "Ctrl+S cycles the History pane's trailing window…", using `makeKeys(root, () => now)` and `writeEvents` as that test does:
  - "Ctrl+P off the trail steps the History window back one window length, and Ctrl+S resets it". Seed `run_end` rows for `feature` run 1 at `now - 30m`, run 2 at `now - 90m` and run 3 at `now - 2.5d`. Open History and press Ctrl+S to get 1h. Ctrl+P gives `historyStep` 1, and `paneCache` matches `/window: between 2h and 1h ago/`, contains `feature #2` and not `feature #1`. Ctrl+P again gives step 2. Ctrl+S three times gives `1d` with step 0 and `/window: last 1d/`. Ctrl+P twice gives step 2, `/window: between 3d and 2d ago/` and `feature #3`.
  - "Ctrl+P wraps the stepped History window after the 7-day cap". On `1d`, after six Ctrl+P presses `historyStep` is 6 and the header says `between 7d and 6d ago`. A seventh press sets step 0 and the flash matches `/oldest window reached; back to the last 1d/`. On `7d`, one Ctrl+P leaves step 0 and flashes the same wording with `7d`.
  - "Ctrl+P on the default History window only flashes the Ctrl+S hint": `historyStep` stays 0, `paneCache` is unchanged and the flash matches `/Ctrl\+S/`.
  - "Ctrl+N on a stepped History window opens that window's newest run": on 1h with step 1, Ctrl+N gives a `trailCache` naming run 2.
  - The existing "Ctrl+P with the trail off does nothing…" test (default window) must pass unchanged.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts, beside the history hint assertion: `hint({ kind: "history", since: "1h", result: null, role: null, grep: null, trail: false })` matches `/Ctrl\+P earlier window/`. With `since: null`, and with `trail: true`, it does not.
- A unit test of `historyWindowBounds`: `(3_600_000, 0)` → `{ sinceMs: 3_600_000, untilMs: null }`, `(86_400_000, 2)` → `{ sinceMs: 259_200_000, untilMs: 172_800_000 }`, `(null, 3)` → `{ sinceMs: null, untilMs: null }`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the History view with the trail off and a trailing window chosen, each Ctrl+P moves the rows to the window `(k+1)·len` to `k·len` ago, read through `readRunRowsSince(…, untilMs)`. The pane header names it `window: between X and Y ago`, and the hint shows `Ctrl+P earlier window`.
- The step wraps to 0, with a flash, once the next window's start would pass `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS`. So 1d steps up to 6 times, 1h up to 167, and 7d never.
- Ctrl+S resets the step. The trail (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P on a trail) follows the stepped window's rows. Ctrl+P on a trail behaves as before.
- With no window chosen, Ctrl+P on History only flashes the Ctrl+S hint. Step 0 renders exactly as today.
- docs/cli.md and docs/how-it-works.md describe the key. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard Usage and Failures past windows: "◀ Earlier" and "Later ▶" buttons step a 1h/6h/1d window back one window length at a time through `/api/report` and `/api/failures` `?sinceMs=&untilMs=` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. It touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts, test/gui-report.test.ts and the History-step sentence of docs/how-it-works.md. "Dashboard Activity window picker" touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, test/gui-client-team.test.ts and docs/how-it-works.md's Activity paragraph; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `handleReport` and `handleFailures` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) already serve a bounded past window: `?sinceMs=S&untilMs=U`, validated by `untilMsQuery` (src/gui/gui-args.ts). They render it as Markdown whose window line comes from `boundedWindowLine` (src/report/report-render.ts, src/failure/failure-render.ts). No dashboard control uses that window yet. The Usage and Failures toolbars offer trailing windows only (`REPORT_SINCE_CHOICES` 1h/6h/1d in src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts), so "the last day" can never become "yesterday". This plan gives both views the step buttons that "Dashboard History past windows" (PLANS-DONE.md) gave History. A `1d` window stepped back once asks for `?sinceMs=172800000&untilMs=86400000`, the browser twin of `tumwater report --since 2d --until 1d` (and `report --failures --since 2d --until 1d`). The change is client-only. Both views are configurations of the one `windowView` scaffold, so a single change covers both.

**Approach** (all in src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts, inside the `// view-scaffold:start` / `:end` region):
1. Pure helpers next to `REPORT_SINCE_CHOICES`:
   - `const REPORT_MAX_MS = 604_800_000;` mirrors the server's `REPORT_SINCE_MAX_MS` (src/events/event-window.ts), the cap `sinceMs` rides on both endpoints. A comment says the two must agree, and a test pins it.
   - `reportCanStepEarlier(sinceMs, step)` is true exactly when `sinceMs` is truthy and `(step + 2) * sinceMs <= REPORT_MAX_MS`, so the next earlier window's `sinceMs` stays under the cap. `1d` steps back at most 6 times, `6h` 27 times and `1h` 167 times.
   - `reportEndpoint(resource, days, role, sinceMs, step)` gains a trailing `step`. When `sinceMs` is set and `step > 0`, the window part is `"/api/" + resource + "?sinceMs=" + (step + 1) * sinceMs + "&untilMs=" + step * sinceMs`. Otherwise the URL is exactly what it is today (step `0` or `undefined`, and the `?days=` shape always ignores the step). `&role=` follows as now.
2. `viewHead`: when `sinceChoices` is non-empty, render a `<span id='<pickerId>step' style='display:none'>` right after the segmented control (before Refresh). It holds `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-step='earlier'>◀ Earlier</button><button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-step='later'>Later ▶</button>`. A view without `sinceChoices` renders nothing new.
3. `windowView`:
   - Add `let step = 0;`, view state that is not persisted (like History's `histStep`), so a reload returns to the trailing window.
   - `fetchView` passes `step` as a fourth argument to `o.endpoint`. Both configs become `endpoint: (days, role, sinceMs, step) => reportEndpoint("report"|"failures", days, role, sinceMs, step)`.
   - After `buildOnce` and the `markActive` calls, `fetchView` does `const stepEl = $(o.pickerId + "step"); if (stepEl) { … }`. Inside it sets `stepEl.style.display = sinceMs ? "" : "none"` and sets each of the span's two buttons' `.disabled` (found with `stepEl.querySelector("[data-step='earlier']")` / `"[data-step='later']"`): Earlier to `!reportCanStepEarlier(sinceMs, step)`, Later to `step === 0`. The `if (stepEl)` guard keeps the existing tests' `$` stubs working, as `renderHistory` does for `#histstep`.
   - In `wireClicks`' click handler, check `clickClosest(ev, "[data-step]")` first. `earlier` does `step += 1` only when `reportCanStepEarlier(sinceMs, step)`. `later` does `step = Math.max(0, step - 1)`. Either then calls `fetchView()` and returns. The `[data-since]` and `[data-days]` branches reset `step = 0` before they fetch. The Role change, Refresh and Usage's throttled event-driven refetch keep the step.
4. Extend the module's top doc comment and the `windowView` comment with one sentence each: on a trailing window, ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ step it back by its own length through `?sinceMs=&untilMs=`, the twin of `report --since --until`.
5. docs/how-it-works.md: directly after the sentence "On a trailing window, the dashboard History toolbar's ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ buttons step that window back…", add the sentence: the dashboard Usage and Failures toolbars carry the same buttons on their 1h/6h/1d windows, through `/api/report` and `/api/failures` `?sinceMs=&untilMs=`, the twin of `report [--failures] --since --until`.

**Tests** (test/gui-report.test.ts):
- Update "the Usage and Failures views fetch their window on activation, never on a timer". Its two `GUI_PAGE` regexes pin `endpoint: (days, role, sinceMs) => reportEndpoint(…)` and must now pin the `(days, role, sinceMs, step)` form.
- New "reportEndpoint steps a since window back by its own length with untilMs". Use `clientScope(["panel-build", "view-scaffold"], ["reportEndpoint", "reportCanStepEarlier", "REPORT_MAX_MS"], inject)` with the same `document`/`$`/`recall`/`store`/`markActive`/`clickClosest`/`icon` stubs as the blurb test, because the region wires both views' clicks at load. Assert:
  - `reportEndpoint("report", 14, "", 86400000, 1)` → `"/api/report?sinceMs=172800000&untilMs=86400000"`.
  - `reportEndpoint("failures", 14, "clean", 3600000, 2)` → `"/api/failures?sinceMs=10800000&untilMs=7200000&role=clean"`.
  - Step `0` and `undefined` with `sinceMs` 86400000 → `"/api/report?sinceMs=86400000"`.
  - `reportEndpoint("report", 7, "", null, 3)` → `"/api/report?days=7"`.
- New "reportCanStepEarlier stops at the server's sinceMs cap". Import `REPORT_SINCE_MAX_MS` from `../src/events/event-window.js` and assert it equals the scoped `REPORT_MAX_MS`. Then assert `(86400000, 5)` → true, `(86400000, 6)` → false, `(21600000, 26)` → true, `(21600000, 27)` → false, and `(null, 0)` → false.
- New "the report step buttons walk a since window back and a since or day click resets it", modelled on "the Usage trailing-window control fetches ?sinceMs…" with the same whole-blob `new Function` seam and `recall` returning `"3600000"` for `usage-since`. Add a `usagewindowstep` element whose `querySelector` returns two stub buttons with a `disabled` field, and let `clickClosest` answer `[data-step]` from a per-phase variable. Assert:
  - The first fetch is `/api/report?sinceMs=3600000`, the span's `style.display` is `""`, Later is disabled and Earlier is not.
  - An `earlier` click fetches `/api/report?sinceMs=7200000&untilMs=3600000` and enables Later.
  - A `later` click fetches `/api/report?sinceMs=3600000` again.
  - After another `earlier`, a `[data-days]` click (`7`) fetches `/api/report?days=7` and leaves the span's `style.display` at `"none"`.
  - The head HTML (`els.report.innerHTML`) contains `id='usagewindowstep'` and `data-step='earlier'`.
- The existing tests in the file pass unchanged apart from the two regexes above.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a 1h/6h/1d window active, the Usage and Failures toolbars show ◀ Earlier / Later ▶. Earlier refetches `?sinceMs=(k+1)·len&untilMs=k·len` on that view's endpoint, with the role scope kept. Later steps back toward the trailing window and is disabled at step 0. Earlier is disabled once the next step's `sinceMs` would pass the server's 7-day cap. With a day window active, the buttons are hidden.
- Choosing a since or day button resets the step to 0. Role, Refresh and Usage's throttled refetch keep it. The step is never persisted.
- The stepped body is the server's bounded Markdown, whose window line already names the bounds, so the client adds no note of its own. Step 0 requests and renders exactly as today.
- No server file changes. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard Activity window picker: a `#feedwindow` select (Recent / Last hour / Last 6 hours / Last day) on the Activity card serves the feed of a trailing window through `GET /api/logs?sinceMs=` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. It touches src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, test/gui-client-team.test.ts and docs/how-it-works.md's Activity paragraph. "Dashboard window end on the last two windowed endpoints" touches only server files (gui-args.ts, gui-endpoints.ts, test/gui-endpoints.test.ts). "Dashboard History past windows" touches gui-client-history.ts, its test, and a different docs/how-it-works.md paragraph, the one starting "The dashboard's History drill-down adds…") — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** "Dashboard event-log window" (PLANS-DONE.md) taught `handleLogs` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) to answer `?sinceMs=S[&grep=][&role=]` with `{ events, covered, note }`, the twin of `tumwater logs --since`. That plan named the feed's window picker as later work, and the dashboard's Activity card still cannot ask for "every event in the last 6 hours": `feedLogsQuery` (src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts) only ever builds `/api/logs?grep=&role=` (the `n`-scanned slice), and only once a Role or Search filter is set. This plan adds a window select to the card head. A chosen window fetches `/api/logs?sinceMs=…` even with no filter, and the card paints that window instead of the carried status-poll events. The change is client-only.

**Behavior, decided:**
- Choices: `const FEED_WINDOWS = [["", "Recent", ""], ["3600000", "Last hour", "the last hour"], ["21600000", "Last 6 hours", "the last 6 hours"], ["86400000", "Last day", "the last day"]];` (value, option label, phrase), the dashboard's REPORT_SINCE_CHOICES lengths. `""` is today's behavior.
- State: `let feedWindow = …` recalled from `"feed-window"`. A recalled value that is not a `FEED_WINDOWS` value falls back to `""`. It persists through `store("feed-window", …)` like feed-role/feed-grep/feed-type.
- `feedLogsQuery()`: when `feedWindow` is set, `"sinceMs=" + feedWindow` is the first param, followed by grep and role in their current order. So role qa + grep boom + 1h gives `/api/logs?sinceMs=3600000&grep=boom&role=qa`, and 1h alone gives `/api/logs?sinceMs=3600000`. With no window the URL is exactly what it is today.
- `searchFeed()`'s early return becomes `if (!feedRole && !feedText && !feedWindow) return;`. renderFeed's re-arm key becomes `feedRole + "\u0000" + feedText + "\u0000" + feedWindow`.
- Live window: a server search today is fetched once per filter change. A window must not freeze, so add `let feedTailTs = 0;`. In renderFeed, take `tail` = the `ts` of the last element of `d.eventItems` (oldest-first), or 0 when there is none. When the key changed, set `feedTailTs = tail` before `searchFeed()`. Otherwise, when `feedWindow` is set, `feedResults !== null` and `tail !== feedTailTs`, set `feedTailTs = tail` and `void fetchFeedSearch(++feedSeq)`. This refetch skips the debounce and does not clear `feedResults`, so the old slice stays painted until the new answer lands, and a poll with no new event fetches nothing. A filter-only search (no window) keeps today's fetch-once behavior.
- Sparse note: add `let feedNote = "";`. `fetchFeedSearch` sets `feedNote = (d && d.note) || ""` on success. `searchFeed` and the catch branch reset it to `""`. renderFeed paints `"<li class='empty muted feed-note'>" + esc(feedNote) + "</li>"` first in the panel, ahead of the tally chips, when `feedNote` is non-empty and `feedResults !== null`.
- Empty states when `feedWindow` is set and the server slice is empty, with phrase P = the window's FEED_WINDOWS phrase: no role/grep/type gives `emptyFeedRow("No events in " + P, "Pick a longer window to look further back. ")`. Otherwise it gives `emptyFeedRow("No events match this filter in " + P, "Widen the Search or Role picker, clear the type chip, or pick a longer window. ")`. With no window, every empty state keeps its current wording.
- Row cap: a day of All events can run to thousands of rows. Add `const FEED_MAX_ROWS = 500;`. renderFeed paints `shown.slice(0, FEED_MAX_ROWS)` (shown is newest-first). When `shown.length > FEED_MAX_ROWS` it appends `"<li class='empty muted'>Showing the newest 500 of " + shown.length + " events — narrow the window or add a filter.</li>"`. The tally chips still count every pre-type row. Today the slice is at most `LOGS_SEARCH_EVENTS` (500) scanned rows, plus the carried window, so no current render reaches the cap.
- Control: gui-page.ts ships `<label><span class="sr-only">Window</span><select class="field" id="feedwindow"></select></label>` between the `#feedrole` and `#feedgrep` labels. The activity region fills it at load: `$("feedwindow").innerHTML = FEED_WINDOWS.map(([v, label]) => "<option value='" + v + "'>" + label + "</option>").join("")`, then `$("feedwindow").value = feedWindow`. Its `change` listener validates `ev.target.value` against FEED_WINDOWS (falling back to `""`), stores it, and calls `renderFeed(lastStatus)` when `lastStatus` is set, mirroring the `#feedrole` listener.
- `clearFeedFilter()` also resets `feedWindow = ""`, stores it, and sets `$("feedwindow").value = ""` when the element exists, so the empty state's Clear button returns the card to its default feed.

**Approach.** All of the logic lives in src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts, inside the `// activity:start` / `// activity:end` region. Update the region's head comment and the module doc comment so they name the window select. In src/ui/gui/gui-page.ts, add the one `<label>` described above. In docs/how-it-works.md, in the Activity sentence that ends "…persisted like the Notable/All choice", add a clause: a Window picker (last hour / 6 hours / day) shows that trailing window's events through `/api/logs?sinceMs=`, the twin of `tumwater logs --since`, refreshing when a new event arrives.

**Tests** (test/gui-client-team.test.ts, through the existing `feedScope` helper and `feedSettle`):
- "a chosen window fetches /api/logs?sinceMs= even with no filter": `feedScope({ "feed-window": "3600000" }, { getJson: (records path, returns { events: [{ ts: 1, source: "qa", type: "merged", message: "window row" }], covered: true, note: "" }), lastStatus: payload })`, where payload carries one "carried row". With a window chosen, the card fetches `/api/logs?sinceMs=<ms>[&grep=][&role=]` and paints that window's events, with the Notable/All cull and the type chips applied as for any server slice. It refetches without a debounce flash when a status poll carries a new event, and never on a poll without one.

### Dashboard window end on the last two windowed endpoints: `GET /api/failures?sinceMs=&untilMs=` and `GET /api/logs?sinceMs=&untilMs=` serve a bounded past window that ends before now, the twins of `report --failures --since --until` and `logs --since --until` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. "TUI History trail transcript search" touches only TUI files, none of these. Touches src/gui/gui-args.ts (doc comment only) + src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts + test/gui-endpoints.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** "Dashboard API window end" (PLANS-DONE.md) gave `/api/report` and `/api/history` an `untilMs` bound through `untilMsQuery` (src/gui/gui-args.ts). It left `/api/failures` alone until "Failure digest window" (PLANS-DONE.md) landed. That plan has now landed: `collectFailureReportSince(root, sinceMs, role?, untilMs?)` (src/failure/failure-data.ts) takes the bound, and `renderFailureMarkdown` prints the bounded `boundedWindowLine` header. `/api/logs?sinceMs=` (PLANS-DONE.md "Dashboard event-log window") said its `untilMs` would be a later plan. The CLI already bounds it: `cmdLogs` (src/cli/log-commands.ts) filters `readEventsSince`'s events with `e.ts < cutoff + ms - untilMs`. Today `handleFailures` and `handleLogs` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) never read `untilMs`. A script asking `/api/failures?sinceMs=345600000&untilMs=259200000` or `/api/logs?sinceMs=…&untilMs=…` silently gets the whole window up to now. Fixing both endpoints is one theme: the same helper applied to the two windowed endpoints still missing it. After this, `grep -n untilMsQuery src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` shows a call in every handler that calls `sinceMsQuery` or `reportScope`.

**Approach.**
1. `handleFailures`: right after `reportScope`, add `const untilMs = untilMsQuery(q, res, scope.sinceMs); if (untilMs === null) return;`. This is the same two lines `handleReport` uses. Then pass `untilMs` as the 4th argument of `collectFailureReportSince`. The days shape has no `sinceMs`, so `?days=7&untilMs=…` becomes the helper's "requires sinceMs" 400 instead of being ignored. Add `[&untilMs=<ms>]` to the doc comment's sinceMs shape.
2. `handleLogs`, in the `sinceMs` branch: after `sinceMsQuery`, add `const untilMs = untilMsQuery(q, res, sinceMs); if (untilMs === null) return;`. Destructure `cutoff` from `readEventsSince` as well. When `untilMs` is defined, keep only events with `e.ts < cutoff + sinceMs - untilMs` before `keep`, the CLI's exact edge. `covered` and `note` are unchanged, because coverage is about the window's far edge either way, as in handleHistory. In the count branch, call `if (untilMsQuery(q, res, undefined) === null) return;` before the `n` parse, so `?n=5&untilMs=…` and a bare `?untilMs=…` are 400s, the handleHistory count-branch rule. Update the handler's doc comment to show `sinceMs=S[&untilMs=U]`.
3. src/gui/gui-args.ts `untilMsQuery` doc comment: change "the report and history endpoints'" to name all four endpoints (report, failures, history, logs). The code does not change.
4. No dashboard client change. gui-client-feed.ts keeps calling `?n=`, and the Failures tab keeps its trailing windows. A past-window UI is a separate later plan, and it is a design choice that plan must settle.

**Tests** (test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, using the existing `serveFailures`/`serveLogs` helpers and `writeEvents`, placed beside "handleFailures serves the windowed digest as { markdown } when ?sinceMs is set" and "handleLogs ?sinceMs serves the trailing window's events, composing grep and role"):
- New test "handleFailures' ?untilMs ends the since window that long ago". Seed a `run_end` `result: "error"` event for `bugfix` at now−30 min (`error: "recent boom"`) and one for `feature` at now−3 h (`error: "old boom"`). `?sinceMs=14400000&untilMs=3600000` → 200, and `markdown` matches `/window: 4h to 1h ago/` and `/feature/` and does not match `/bugfix/`. The digest table names each role that ran (the existing sinceMs test asserts `/bugfix/`), and bugfix's run lies in neither the window nor its prior window `[now − 7 h, now − 4 h)`. Compare shapes, not bytes: each call reads its own `Date.now()`. 400 cases, each with the error matched: `?untilMs=3600000` and `?days=7&untilMs=3600000` → /requires sinceMs/; `?sinceMs=3600000&untilMs=3600000` → /must be shorter than sinceMs/; `?sinceMs=3600000&untilMs=abc` → /untilMs/.
- New test "handleLogs' ?untilMs drops the window's newer events". Seed the same three events as the existing sinceMs test (now−3 h, now−30 min, now−20 min) plus one at now−5 min. `?sinceMs=3600000&untilMs=600000` → `events` ts are `[now − 30 min, now − 20 min]`, with `covered: true` and `note: ""`. `&role=bugfix` added → `[now − 20 min]`. 400s: `?untilMs=600000`, `?n=5&untilMs=600000` → /requires sinceMs/; `?sinceMs=600000&untilMs=600000` → /must be shorter than sinceMs/.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `/api/failures?sinceMs=S&untilMs=U` (U < S) serves `{ markdown: renderFailureMarkdown(collectFailureReportSince(root, S, roles, U)) }`, with the bounded header and only the failures in `[now − S, now − U)`.
- `/api/logs?sinceMs=S&untilMs=U` serves `{ events, covered, note }` holding only the window's events older than `now − U`, and `grep` and `role` still compose.
- `untilMs` without `sinceMs`, with `days` or `n`, `untilMs >= sinceMs`, or a non-positive-integer `untilMs` is a 400 on both endpoints. Nothing ignores it silently.
- Requests without `untilMs` answer as before: the existing handleFailures and handleLogs tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard History past windows: "◀ Earlier" and "Later ▶" buttons step the History view's window back one window length at a time through `/api/history?sinceMs=&untilMs=` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. "TUI History trail transcript search" touches only TUI files and docs/cli.md, and "Dashboard window end on the last two windowed endpoints" touches only src/gui/gui-args.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts and test/gui-endpoints.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20
**Goal.** "Dashboard API window end" (PLANS-DONE.md) taught `/api/history` to serve a bounded past window (`sinceMs` plus `untilMs`, both validated by `untilMsQuery`, src/gui/gui-args.ts), but no dashboard control uses it. The History toolbar's `#histcount` select (src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, `HIST_WINDOWS`) offers only trailing windows: "the last day" can never become "yesterday". This plan adds two step buttons next to that select. They shift the chosen window back or forward by its own length, so `1d` stepped back once asks for `?sinceMs=172800000&untilMs=86400000`, the browser twin of `tumwater history --since 2d --until 1d`. This plan changes only the client. The endpoint already serves the shape.

**Approach** (all in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts):
1. View state: add `let histStep = 0;` beside `histModel`. It counts how many window lengths back the window ends. It is view state and is not persisted, like `histModel`, so a reload returns to the trailing window.
2. Inside the `history-table:start`/`:end` region, add these pure helpers next to `HIST_WINDOWS`:
   - `const HIST_MAX_MS = 604_800_000;` — the server's `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` (src/events/event-window.ts), the cap `/api/history`'s `sinceMs` rides. Add a comment saying the two must agree. A test pins it.
   - `histSpan(ms)`: `"1 day"`/`"N days"` when `ms` is a whole number of days (`ms % 86_400_000 === 0`), otherwise `"1 hour"`/`"N hours"`. Every window and step length is a whole number of hours.
   - `histCanStepEarlier(sinceKey, step)`: true exactly when `HIST_WINDOWS[sinceKey]` exists and `(step + 2) * w[0] <= HIST_MAX_MS`. That means the next earlier window's `sinceMs` is still under the cap. So `7d` never steps, `1d` steps up to 6 times, and `1h` up to 167.
   - `histWindowPhrase(sinceKey, step)`: `HIST_WINDOWS[sinceKey][1]` when `step` is 0 (for example "the last day"). Otherwise `"between " + histSpan((step + 1) * w[0]) + " and " + histSpan(step * w[0]) + " ago"`, which mirrors cmdLogs' `between X and Y ago` wording (src/cli/log-commands.ts). Returns `""` for an unknown key.
   - `historyQuery(count, role, sinceKey, grep, model, step)`: when a window is set and `step > 0`, the window part becomes `"/api/history?sinceMs=" + (step + 1) * w[0] + "&untilMs=" + step * w[0]`. Otherwise the URL is exactly what it is today. Role, grep, model and `&summary=1` follow in their current order.
   - `historyStepHtml(sinceKey, step)`: `""` when `step` is 0 or the key is unknown. Otherwise `"<p class='muted window-note'>Showing runs " + histWindowPhrase(sinceKey, step) + ".</p>"`.
3. In `historyTableHtml`, add a trailing `step` parameter. The empty-window branch then says `"No runs " + (step ? histWindowPhrase(sinceKey, step) : "in " + w[1])`, so step 0 keeps the current text unchanged.
4. Toolbar (`buildHistoryView`): right after the `#histcount` label, add `<span id='histstep' style='display:none'>` holding `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' id='histearlier'>◀ Earlier</button>` and `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' id='histlater'>Later ▶</button>`. The click handlers do `histStep += 1` (earlier) or `histStep = Math.max(0, histStep - 1)` (later), then `fetchHistory()`. The `#histcount` change handler resets `histStep = 0` before it fetches. Role, grep, model, refresh and the status-poll refetch keep the step.
5. `fetchHistory` passes `histStep` to `historyQuery`. `renderHistory` passes it to `historyTableHtml` and paints `historyNoteHtml(histNote) + historyStepHtml(histSinceKey, histStep) + bodyHtml`. It also sets `$("histstep").style.display` to `""` exactly when `HIST_WINDOWS[histSinceKey]` exists, `$("histearlier").disabled = !histCanStepEarlier(histSinceKey, histStep)` and `$("histlater").disabled = histStep === 0`.
6. docs/how-it-works.md: in the paragraph that starts "The dashboard's History drill-down adds…", add one sentence before it: on a trailing window, the dashboard History toolbar's ◀ Earlier / Later ▶ buttons step that window back by its own length, through `/api/history?sinceMs=&untilMs=`, the twin of `history --since --until`. Extend the module's top doc comment the same way.

**Tests** (test/gui-client-history.test.ts, using `clientScope(HISTORY_REGIONS, …)` and `iconStub` as the neighbouring tests do):
- "historyQuery steps a window back by its own length with untilMs": `historyQuery(50, "", "1d", "", "", 1)` → `"/api/history?sinceMs=172800000&untilMs=86400000&summary=1"`. `historyQuery(50, "clean", "1h", "x", "", 2)` → `"/api/history?sinceMs=10800000&untilMs=7200000&role=clean&grep=x&summary=1"`. Step 0 and step `undefined` with `"1d"` → `"/api/history?sinceMs=86400000&summary=1"`. `historyQuery(50, "", "", "", "", 3)` → `"/api/history?n=50&summary=1"` (no window, so the step is ignored).
- "histCanStepEarlier stops at the server's sinceMs cap": import `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` from `../src/events/event-window.js` and assert it equals the scoped `HIST_MAX_MS`. Then `("7d", 0)` → false, `("1d", 5)` → true, `("1d", 6)` → false, `("6h", 26)` → true, `("6h", 27)` → false, `("", 0)` → false.
- "histWindowPhrase and historyStepHtml name a stepped window": `("1d", 0)` → `"the last day"`, `("1d", 1)` → `"between 2 days and 1 day ago"`, `("6h", 1)` → `"between 12 hours and 6 hours ago"`, `("6h", 4)` → `"between 30 hours and 1 day ago"` (30 h is not a whole day, 24 h is). `historyStepHtml("1d", 0)` → `""`. `historyStepHtml("1d", 1)` contains `Showing runs between 2 days and 1 day ago.`
- "historyTableHtml's empty stepped window names its bounds": `historyTableHtml([], "all", new Set(), "", "1d", "", 1)` matches `/No runs between 2 days and 1 day ago/`. The same call with step 0 still matches `/No runs in the last day/`.
- Extend the toolbar test "the History toolbar carries the four trailing-window options in the #histcount select" (or add a sibling built the same way) so it asserts that the built toolbar HTML contains `id='histearlier'` and `id='histlater'` inside `id='histstep'`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a trailing window chosen, the History toolbar shows ◀ Earlier / Later ▶. Earlier refetches `/api/history?sinceMs=(k+1)·len&untilMs=k·len`. Later steps back toward the trailing window and is disabled at step 0. Earlier is disabled once the next step's `sinceMs` would pass the server's 7-day cap. With a run count chosen, the buttons are hidden.
- Changing the window select resets the step to 0. Role, search, model chip, Refresh and the status-poll refetch keep the step.
- A stepped window shows "Showing runs between X and Y ago." above the table, and its empty state names the same bounds. Step 0 renders exactly as today, and the existing gui-client-history tests pass unchanged.
- No server file changes. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### TUI History trail transcript search: `/` on a run trail whose transcript is showing keeps only the transcript entries that contain the text, the terminal twin of `tumwater history <role> <n> --transcript --grep <text>` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; the CLI and the dashboard History drill-down's transcript search box already narrow one run's transcript through `runTranscriptLines`' `grep` option, but the TUI History trail's Ctrl+R transcript (`loadTranscript` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts) never passes `grep`, and `/` on that view only sets `historyGrep`, which filters the run rows. Independent of every eligible plan. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-editor-ctx.ts, tui-editor-search.ts, tui-frame.ts, tui.tsx, test/tui-keys.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts and docs/cli.md's TUI key table. "Failure digest window" also edits docs/cli.md, but in its "Audit" row, not the key table) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** On the TUI History trail (Ctrl+N), Ctrl+R shows the run's agent transcript, but nothing can search it. Today `/` on that view sets `historyGrep`, so it filters the runs the trail steps through. The fix follows the CLI's own rule: `history <role> <n> --grep` needs `--transcript` and then filters the transcript (`cmdRunDetail` in src/run/run-detail.ts). So while a trail's transcript is showing (`trailTranscript !== "off"`), `/` searches that transcript. Otherwise `/` keeps today's run-row search. This settles which pane state `/` targets: the transcript search exists only while the transcript is visible. To change the run filter from a trail, press Ctrl+R until the transcript is off, then press `/`.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`:
  - Add `let trailGrep: string | null = null;` beside `trailTranscript`, with a comment saying it is set only while `trailTranscript !== "off"`.
  - `loadTranscript` passes `grep: trailGrep ?? undefined` to `runTranscriptLines`. On no match, its existing `found`/`note` fallback then shows the miss note `(no transcript entries matching "<text>" in <role> run <n>)`.
  - `applySearch`: when `trailMode && trailTranscript !== "off"`, set `trailGrep = pattern`, call `loadTranscript()` then `composeTrail()`, set `session.paneScroll = 0`, and return. Leave `historyGrep` and `session.paneCache` alone (the run rows stay as they are). Otherwise keep the current body unchanged.
  - Clear `trailGrep = null` everywhere `trailTranscript` goes back to `"off"`: the Ctrl+N toggle-off branch, `reset()`, and the Ctrl+R arm when its cycle lands on `"off"`. Ctrl+P (`loadTrail` → `loadTranscript`) and the plain↔prompts step keep the pattern, so the same search follows older runs and the prompts level.
  - `state()` returns `trailGrep`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`: add `trailGrep: string | null` to the state interface next to `trailTranscript`, with a doc line. `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`: copy `trailGrep: hist.trailGrep` in the state aggregation next to `trailTranscript`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts`: add `trailSearch: boolean` (true when `/` on History targets the trail's transcript) and `trailGrep: string | null`, each with a doc line. `editorCtx` in tui-panes.ts sets `trailSearch: s.trailMode && s.trailTranscript !== "off"` and `trailGrep: s.trailGrep`. That function is the only place that builds a `TuiEditorCtx`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts`, at the `/` open arm: for `searchFor === "history"`, pre-fill from `ctx.trailSearch ? ctx.trailGrep : ctx.historyGrep`. The flash noun becomes `"transcript"` instead of `"runs"` when `ctx.trailSearch` is true. Enter still calls `session.applyHistorySearch(applied)`, and the pane routes it. `searchFor` and the editor's other arms stay as they are. The trail state cannot change while the editor holds the line, because Ctrl+N/P/R all check `promptLineFree`.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`: add `trailGrep?: string | null` to the `history` view kind. In the History hint, the `/` entry becomes `view.trail && view.trailTranscript !== undefined && view.trailTranscript !== "off" ? (view.trailGrep ? \`transcript search: ${view.trailGrep}\` : "search transcript") : (view.grep ? \`search: ${view.grep}\` : "search")`. `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`: pass `trailGrep: s.trailGrep` in the history view object.
- `docs/cli.md`, TUI key table: the `/` row's parenthetical adds "on a History run trail whose transcript is showing (Ctrl+R), keep only that run's transcript entries containing the text, like `history <role> <n> --transcript --grep`". The `Ctrl+R` History row adds "turning the transcript off drops its search".
- Anchors are symbol-level; no line numbers.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/tui-keys.test.ts`, `test/tui-frame.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New tests in `test/tui-keys.test.ts` use the existing `historyTrailRoot`, `writeTrailPiLog` and `openHistory` helpers, plus `readRunDetail`/`runTranscriptLines`/`renderRunDetail` the "Ctrl+R on the History trail cycles…" test already imports:
  - Open the trail (Ctrl+N) and press Ctrl+R (plain). Then `/`, type `said-one`, Enter. `state().trailGrep` is `"said-one"`, `state().historyGrep` stays `null`, and `trailCache` equals `${renderRunDetail(detail)}\n\n${runTranscriptLines(root, "clean", 1, detail, { grep: "said-one" }).found.join("\n")}`.

With `trailGrep: "x"` it matches `/transcript search: x/`. With `trailTranscript: "off"` and `grep: "y"` it still matches `/search: y/`.
- The existing `/` History tests ("the Activity and History `/` searches are independent…") pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Dashboard event-log window: `GET /api/logs?sinceMs=` serves the event feed of a trailing time window, the twin of `tumwater logs --since <duration>` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan. Touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts `handleLogs` + test/gui-endpoints.test.ts. "Dashboard API window end" edits `handleReport`/`handleHistory` in the same file and src/gui/gui-args.ts; this plan edits neither of those functions nor gui-args.ts) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `tumwater logs --since 2h` (`cmdLogs`, src/cli/log-commands.ts) prints every event of a time window through `readEventsSince` (src/events/event-window.ts), with the sparse-window note when the log does not reach back that far. The dashboard's event search, `handleLogs` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts), only knows `?n=` — the newest N events, clamped to `LOGS_SEARCH_MAX_EVENTS` — so "which events matched `land` in the last 6h" cannot be asked of the server, and a busy log's 6h can exceed any count. `/api/history` already has the window shape (`?sinceMs=`, `sinceMsQuery`, `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS`, `covered`/`note`); `/api/logs` gets the same one.

Behavior, decided:
- `?sinceMs=S` answers `{ events, covered, note }`: `events` are `readEventsSince(root, S).events` filtered by the existing `role` and `grep` rules, oldest-first as `eventFeedItem` objects; `covered` is `readEventsSince`'s `covered`; `note` is `SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE` when `covered` is false, else `""` — the `/api/history` window shape.
- `sinceMs` with `n` is a 400 with `handleHistory`'s wording: `"sinceMs cannot be combined with n (a count and a window are rival shapes)"` (the CLI's "-n and --since are rival shapes").
- `sinceMs` parses through `sinceMsQuery(q, res, LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS, (ms) => \`sinceMs is capped at ${humanSeconds(LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS / 1000)} (got ${ms})\`)` — the same call `handleHistory` makes, so the cap and wording match `logs --since`/`history --since`.
- No row cap in the window branch: `logs --since` prints the whole window, and `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` already bounds its span.
- Without `sinceMs`, the response is unchanged (`{ events }`, n-scanned).
- No dashboard client change (src/ui/gui/gui-client-feed.ts keeps calling `?n=`); a window picker for the feed is a later plan. `untilMs` on this endpoint is also a later plan, once "Dashboard API window end" has landed `untilMsQuery`.

**Approach.** src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts:
1. Import `readEventsSince` from ../events/event-window.js (extend an existing event-window import line) and `sinceMsQuery` from ./gui-args.js if not already imported (`handleHistory` uses it, so it is; verify with grep). `humanSeconds` is already in scope (used by `handleHistory`).
2. In `handleLogs`, read `role`, `grep` and `needle` first, and build `const keep = (e: HarnessEvent) => (role === null || eventRole(e) === role) && (needle === null || eventMatchesGrep(e, needle));` (import the `HarnessEvent` type if it is not in scope). Then, before the `n` parse: `if (q.get("sinceMs") !== null) { if (q.get("n") !== null) { badRequest(...); return; } const sinceMs = sinceMsQuery(...); if (sinceMs === null) return; const { events, covered } = readEventsSince(root, sinceMs); sendJson(res, 200, { events: events.filter(keep).map(eventFeedItem), covered, note: covered ? "" : SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE }); return; }`. The existing n branch then filters with `keep`, unchanged in behavior.
3. Update the doc comment's first line to `GET /api/logs?n=N|sinceMs=S[&grep=<text>][&role=<id>]` and add a sentence describing the window branch (readEventsSince, the rival-shape 400, the LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS cap, covered/note as /api/history's window answers).

Seed with `ts: Date.now() - …`: a feature `run_end` summary "landed old" at now−3h, a feature `run_end` summary "landed new" at now−30min, a bugfix `run_end` summary "landed other" at now−20min. `?sinceMs=3600000` → status 200, two events (the 30min and 20min ones, oldest-first), `covered === true`, `note === ""`. `?sinceMs=3600000&role=feature` → only the 30min one. `?sinceMs=3600000&grep=other` → only the bugfix one. Assert on each item's `ts` (`eventFeedItem` returns `{ ts, source, type, result?, message }`).

- `sinceMs` with `n`, a non-positive or malformed `sinceMs`, or one above `LOGS_SINCE_MAX_MS` is a 400.
