### OpenCode catalog seed: the startup seed's failed fetch or failed cache write logs a warning instead of staying silent (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/gates/startup-gate.ts + test/startup-gate.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `runStartupCheck` (src/gates/startup-gate.ts) seeds the opencode models catalog once per root per process with `await seedOpencodeCatalog(root, config, opencodeSeed)`, and passes no `warn`. `refreshOpencodeCatalog` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) reports both of its failures only through `opts.warn?.(…)`: "open code model catalog fetch failed; keeping the cached copy" and "could not save the open code model catalog: …". So when a team boots offline, or cannot write `.tumwater/state/opencode-models.json`, nothing is logged. With no cache, every opencode seam prices as NOT free, so the budget gate counts its runs against the cap as paid spend, and the log never says why. `newOpencodeCatalogRefresh` starts its throttle at construction, so the first warning can come up to `OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS` (an hour) later. The plan that added the write warning (PLANS-DONE.md, "Leave startup-gate.ts alone. It passes no `warn` today, and wiring that up is a separate change") left this undone on purpose. This plan wires it up, so the startup seed's failures show up in the event log the way the live-reload and poll seeds' failures already do.

**Approach.**
1. src/gates/startup-gate.ts, `runStartupCheck`: change the seed call to `await seedOpencodeCatalog(root, config, { ...opencodeSeed, warn: (message) => warnEventBestEffort(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, message) })`. Import `warnEventBestEffort` and `TUMWATER_SOURCE` from ../events/events.js. Use the best-effort form because `runStartupCheck` promises never to throw, and it runs before the team's log necessarily exists. `warnEventBestEffort` falls back to stderr when the events log is unwritable. Keep the `opencodeSeedAttempted` guard as it is, so a process warns at most once, even though the supervisor and redeploy polls re-ask `runStartupCheck`.
2. Same file: update the comments that say startup is silent. In `seedOpencodeCatalog`'s doc comment, replace "`warn` receives the refresh's own warnings (startup passes none)" with wording saying every caller now passes one (startup logs through `warnEventBestEffort`). In the "Seed the opencode models catalog" comment in `runStartupCheck`, add that a failed fetch or cache write logs one warning event.
3. Leave `refreshOpencodeCatalog`, `newOpencodeCatalogRefresh` and src/config/config-live.ts unchanged.

### Quarantine filing: a test whose bug is already under `## Open` reuses that heading instead of filing a duplicate (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts + test/main-watch.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** main-watch's `settleQuarantine` (src/baseline/main-watch.ts) files the pending quarantined tests (`bug === ""`) with `fileQuarantineBugsOnMain` (src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts). That function commits BUGS.md on main, and only then does `settleQuarantine` record the headings with `markQuarantineFiled` (src/review/known-flakes.ts), which ends in a `saveQuarantine` with no try. If that write fails (full disk, read-only `.tumwater/state`), the outer catch warns `quarantine housekeeping failed: …`, but the entries keep `bug === ""`. On the next poll `fileQuarantineBugsOnMain` files them again. `appendBugEntryLocked` (src/backlog/backlog-write.ts) does no duplicate check, so every poll commits another identical `## Open` entry for the same test until the write works. Fix this at the filing step, so a filing that has already landed is never repeated, whatever made the bookkeeping fail.

**Approach.**
1. src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts, `fileQuarantineBugsOnMain`:
   - Add a module-private `function quarantineTitlePrefix(test: string): string` returning ``collapseWhitespace(`\`${test}\` failed, then passed on the same tree`) + " (quarantined by tumwater "``. Build the appended title from it as `` `${quarantineTitlePrefix(test)}${date})` `` so both use one spelling. `appendBugEntryLocked` collapses whitespace in the title, so the prefix has to be collapsed the same way to match what it wrote. Collapse only the test part, because `collapseWhitespace` trims and would drop the trailing space.
   - After `const before = readTextOrNull(file);`, compute `const open = before === null ? [] : parseEntryDetails(before, "Open").map((e) => e.title);`. Import `parseEntryDetails` from ./backlog-md.js, which the module already imports from.
   - In the loop, when `open.find((t) => t.startsWith(quarantineTitlePrefix(test)))` finds a title, `bugs.set(test, title)` and append nothing. Otherwise append as today and keep the test in a local `appended` count.
   - When nothing was appended, return `{ status: "filed", bugs }` before the `git add`/commit, so no empty commit is attempted. Otherwise, name the commit subject's count after the appended tests, not `tests.length`.
   - Extend the doc comment: a test whose quarantine entry is already under `## Open` (a filing whose `markQuarantineFiled` failed after the commit) gets that heading back and is not filed again.
2. Leave `markQuarantineFiled` and `settleQuarantine` unchanged. The existing catch already warns, and the next poll now records the reused heading.

### Doctor: one throwing check becomes a fail row instead of aborting the whole report, and a failed image-probe cache write keeps the fresh verdicts (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/doctor/doctor.ts + src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts + test/doctor.test.ts + test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `runDoctor` (src/doctor/doctor.ts) runs its checks in a loop with `const outcome = await step.run();` and no try. So when any one check throws, the whole report rejects. `tumwater doctor` (src/cli.ts), the dashboard's doctor endpoint (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) and the TUI Health pane (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts) then get no rows at all, not even the checks that passed. Most checks catch their own errors (`checkBrief`, `checkStateDir`, `findOrphans`). One known site does not: `checkImageInput` (src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts) ends its probe loop with `if (probedAny) writeImageProbeCache(root, probes);`, which has no try. With `--reprobe` or "missing", that write comes after the live model probes have already run (and been paid for). If the write fails (`writeJsonAtomic` on a full disk or a read-only `.tumwater/state`), the fresh verdicts are lost and `tumwater doctor` crashes.

**Approach.**
1. src/doctor/doctor.ts:
   - Add `export async function runDoctorCheck(run: () => CheckOutcome | null | Promise<CheckOutcome | null>): Promise<CheckOutcome | null>`. It returns `await run()`. When the call throws synchronously or rejects, it returns `failOutcome(\`the check threw: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` instead. Import `failOutcome` from ./outcome.js (the module already imports `CheckOutcome` there as a type) and `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js.
   - In `runDoctor`'s loop, replace `await step.run()` with `await runDoctorCheck(step.run)`. A throw is reported as `fail`, not `warn`, because a check that crashed verified nothing, and the CLI's exit code should say so.
   - Add one sentence to `runDoctor`'s doc comment: a check that throws becomes its own fail row, and every other check still runs.
2. src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, `checkImageInput`:
   - Wrap the `writeImageProbeCache` call in try/catch. On failure, set `let saveProblem: string | null` to `errorMessage(err)` (import it from ../text/text.js).
   - Move the verdict-building tail (everything after the write, through the final `return okOutcome(details)`) into a local `const verdict = (): CheckOutcome => { … }`. Then end the function with `const outcome = verdict(); if (saveProblem === null) return outcome;` followed by `return { level: outcome.level === "ok" ? "warn" : outcome.level, detail: \`${outcome.detail} — could not save the image-probe cache (${saveProblem}), so the next doctor probes again\` };`.
   - The in-memory `probes` map still feeds `seamImageInput` below the write, so this run's verdicts are unchanged.
3. test/doctor.test.ts: add the test "runDoctorCheck turns a throwing or rejecting check into a fail row and passes other outcomes through". It asserts:
   - a sync throw `() => { throw new Error("boom"); }` gives `{ level: "fail", detail: "the check threw: boom" }`;
   - an `async () => { throw new Error("late"); }` gives `detail: "the check threw: late"`;
   - `() => null` gives `null`;
   - `() => okOutcome("fine")` gives the same object (deepEqual).
4. test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts: add the test "checkImageInput keeps a fresh probe's verdict when the probe cache cannot be saved, and warns". Use `probeConfig()` and a passing probe, as in "checkImageInput with missing probes only uncached claimed models once, and caches the pass". Before the call, set `const undo = failRenameSyncOn(imageProbesPath(root), "disk full")` (from ./helpers/fs-faults.js), and call `undo()` in a `finally`. Assert:
   - `doesNotReject` on the call;
   - `level === "warn"`;
   - the detail still matches `/local\/vision \(verified \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\)/` and also matches `/could not save the image-probe cache \(disk full\)/`;
   - `readImageProbeCache(root)` is `{}` afterwards (nothing was saved).
5. docs/invariants.md: append the section "## Doctor: one failing check never takes down the report" after the last section, in the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout, with `### INV-CE1: a doctor check that throws becomes its own fail row, and a failed image-probe cache write keeps the run's verdicts`. Binds: `src/doctor/doctor.ts` (`runDoctorCheck`, `runDoctor`) and `src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts` (`checkImageInput`). Pinned by: the two new tests, cited by full name. On 2026-10-20, CC had merged and CD was reserved by the OpenCode catalog refresh plan, so CE was free. Re-check with `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and the Planned entries, and take the next free prefix if CE is gone.

### OpenCode catalog: a running team refetches a stale or missing models catalog, at most once an hour (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/gates/startup-gate.ts + src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts + test/startup-gate.test.ts + docs/invariants.md)

**Goal.** The opencode models catalog (`.tumwater/state/opencode-models.json`) is fetched at only two points: `runStartupCheck`, once per root per process (`opencodeSeedAttempted`), and a live edit that first routes a seam to opencode (`liveOpencodeSeedAttempted` in src/config/config-live.ts). Both go through `seedOpencodeCatalog` (src/gates/startup-gate.ts). Nothing fetches it again while the team runs. `CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_MS` (24 h) in src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts is consulted only at those two points. This causes two problems:
- A team whose startup fetch failed (a network blip at boot) has no cache. `refreshOpencodeCatalog` returns an empty catalog and writes nothing. `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts) reads `readOpencodeCache(root)` every poll, and its comment says an absent catalog makes every opencode seam read NOT free. So at the daily cap, the budget gate holds the team's free opencode runs until someone restarts it.
- A team that runs for days prices by a catalog that is days old, although the cache claims a 24 h trust window.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts:
   - Add `export function opencodeCatalogStale(cache: OpencodeCatalogCache, now: number): boolean`. It returns `cache.fetchedAt === 0 || now - cache.fetchedAt >= CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_MS`.
   - Use it for the age half of `fresh` in `refreshOpencodeCatalog`, so the rule lives in one place. Keep the version comparison where it is.
2. src/gates/startup-gate.ts:
   - Add `export const OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000`.
   - Add `export function newOpencodeCatalogRefresh(root: string, seed: OpenCodeSeedOptions, warn: (message: string) => void): { poll(config: TumwaterConfig): void }`. Its clock is `const clock = seed.now ?? Date.now`. It holds `let lastAttempt = clock()`, set at construction because the startup check has just tried, so the first polls after boot do not refetch.
   - `poll(config)` is synchronous and returns early in three cases: `!backendsInUse(config).includes("opencode")`; `clock() - lastAttempt < OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS`; or `!opencodeCatalogStale(readOpencodeCache(root), clock())`.
   - Otherwise `poll` sets `lastAttempt = clock()` and calls `void seedOpencodeCatalog(root, config, { ...seed, warn }).catch((err: unknown) => warn(\`open code model catalog refresh failed: ${errorMessage(err)}\`))`. Import `readOpencodeCache` and `opencodeCatalogStale` from the catalog module, and `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js if it is not already imported.
   - Doc comment: the poll path checks only the cache's age. It skips the `opencode --version` comparison, so no binary is spawned on every poll; the version check still runs inside `refreshOpencodeCatalog` once a refresh is due. A fetch that keeps failing warns at most once per `OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS`, through `refreshOpencodeCatalog`'s existing "open code model catalog fetch failed; keeping the cached copy" warning.
3. src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts: after `const { emit, warn } = bestEffortEventLogger(root)`, build `const opencodeCatalogRefresh = newOpencodeCatalogRefresh(root, {}, warn)` and add it to the poll context object.
4. src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts: add `opencodeCatalogRefresh: ReturnType<typeof newOpencodeCatalogRefresh>` to `PollContext` (a type-only import). Call `ctx.opencodeCatalogRefresh.poll(liveConfig)` right after `ctx.retentionPruner.poll(...)`. It is unconditional, so `--once` passes too: the throttle starts at construction, and a short round never reaches the hour.
5. test/startup-gate.test.ts: add two tests. Both share this setup:
   - `const root = makeRepo()` and a clock `let t = 1_000`.
   - A config `const config = structuredClone(defaultConfig())` (import `defaultConfig` from ../src/config/config.js), with `config.backends = { opencode: { bin: <a writeScript "exit 0" opencode in a tmpdir> } }` and `config.review = { ...config.review, enabled: true, backend: "opencode", model: "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free" }`. This is the same routing `opencodeRouting` in test/config-live.test.ts uses.
   - Collect the warnings in an array.
   - A `settle()` that awaits `new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r))`.

   Test "newOpencodeCatalogRefresh refetches a missing or stale catalog at most once per retry interval, only while opencode is routed". The fetch counts `calls` and returns `{ opencode: { models: { "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free": { cost: { input: 0, output: 0 } } } } }`. Build the refresher with `{ fetch, now: () => t }`, then:
   - (a) Poll at `t = 1_000` with no cache on disk, then settle: `calls === 0` (the retry throttle).
   - (b) Set `t = 1_000 + OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS`, poll, settle: `calls === 1`, and `readOpencodeCache(root).fetchedAt === t`.
   - (c) Set `t += OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS`, poll, settle: `calls === 1` (the cache is fresh).
   - (d) Set `t = readOpencodeCache(root).fetchedAt + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`, poll a pi-only `structuredClone(defaultConfig())`, settle: `calls === 1` (opencode is not routed).
   - (e) Poll `config` at the same `t`, settle: `calls === 2`.

   Test "a failing periodic catalog refresh warns once per retry interval and never throws out of poll". The fetch throws `new Error("offline")`. Set `t = 1_000 + OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS`, then assert `doesNotThrow(() => r.poll(config))` and settle. Poll again at the same `t` and settle. Assert that exactly one collected warning starts with `open code model catalog fetch failed`.
6. docs/invariants.md: append the section "## OpenCode catalog refresh: a running team re-fetches a stale catalog" after the last section, in the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout, with `### INV-CD1: the poll refetches a missing or stale opencode catalog at most once per OPENCODE_CATALOG_RETRY_MS, only while opencode is routed, and never throws`. Binds: `src/gates/startup-gate.ts` (`newOpencodeCatalogRefresh`) and `src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts` (`opencodeCatalogStale`). Pinned by: the two new tests, cited by full name. On 2026-10-20 CA had merged, CB was merged, and CC was reserved by the worktree-pool release plan, so CD was free. Re-check with `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and the Planned entries, and take the next free prefix if CD is gone.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Each of these mutations fails the first new test: dropping the `lastAttempt` throttle fails step (a); dropping the `opencodeCatalogStale` check fails step (c); dropping the `backendsInUse` check fails step (d).
- With `lastAttempt` set only after a success (not on every attempt), the second new test fails, because it sees two warnings.
- The existing opencode tests in test/startup-gate.test.ts, test/config-live.test.ts and test/opencode-catalog.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- Each test name cited in INV-CD1 exists verbatim (`grep -rF` it in test/).

### Worktree pool: a release whose slots.json write fails warns instead of throwing, and the next claim reclaims the slot (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/git/worktree-pool.ts + test/worktree-pool.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** A lease handle's `release` (the handle `prepareLeased` builds in src/git/worktree-pool.ts) calls `releaseSlot`. `releaseSlot` is an `updateSlotsState` read-modify-write (src/git/slots-state.ts), and its `writeJsonAtomic` and the slots lock's `withStateLock` timeout run with no try. A failed write (ENOSPC, EACCES, a lock timeout) causes three problems:
- `release` throws. `wakeWaiters` and `removeDroppedSlots` never run.
- The slot stays leased on disk under this live pid. `clearDeadLeases` only clears another pid's lease, so the pool loses that slot until the team restarts.
- The callers release in a `finally` (`runOnceInLeasePhase` in src/runner/runner-run.ts, and `.finally(() => lease.release())` in src/review/review.ts). A throw there replaces the run's own outcome or error.

`prepareLeased`'s prepare-failure path calls `releaseSlot` before `throw err`, so a failed write there also masks the real checkout error. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed this with a scratch test (since deleted). It took `leaseSlot` on a `worktreeSlots: 1` repo, installed `failRenameSyncOn(slotsStatePath(root), "EACCES fake")` and called `release()`. The call threw `Error: EACCES fake`, slots.json still held the lease with `process.pid`, and a following `tryLeaseSlot` returned null. The precedent is "a release whose use-record write fails still frees the slot" (test/worktree-pool.test.ts), which guarded the use-registry half of the same release.

**Approach.**
1. src/git/worktree-pool.ts:
   - Add a module-level `const unsavedReleases = new Map<string, Set<string>>()`, keyed by `rootKey(root)`. It holds the slot dirs whose release write failed in this process.
   - Add `function freeSlot(root, dir, role, count, pin): string[]`. It returns `releaseSlot(...)`. On a catch, it adds `dir` to the root's set, calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, \`could not free slot ${path.basename(dir)}: ${errorMessage(err)}; the next lease reclaims it\`)` and returns `[]`. All three imports already exist in the file.
   - In `prepareLeased`, replace both `releaseSlot(` calls (the prepare-failure path and the handle's `release`) with `freeSlot(`. `wakeWaiters` and `removeDroppedSlots` then run on every path.
   - In `tryClaim`, inside the `updateSlotsState` callback and before `chooseSlot`, read the root's set. For each `state.slots` entry whose `dir` is in it and whose `lease?.pid === process.pid`, set `lease = null`. After `updateSlotsState` returns, delete the root's key: the write landed, so the reclaim is on disk. If it throws, the set stays and the next claim retries.
   - Note in the doc comment that the pin and `lastRole` the failed release would have recorded are not replayed. A lost pin only means the next resume gets a fresh checkout.
2. test/worktree-pool.test.ts: add the test "a release whose slots.json write fails warns instead of throwing, and the next lease reclaims the slot". Import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `warningMessages` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js. The test does the following:

### Flake quarantine: a failed `quarantine.json` write warns instead of throwing out of a check whose re-run just passed (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/review/known-flakes.ts + test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `quarantineTests` (src/review/known-flakes.ts) ends with `saveQuarantine(root, entries)`, a bare `writeJsonAtomic(quarantinePath(root), …)` with no try. It has three callers, and each one runs it right after a re-run of the same tree **passed** (checked with `grep -rn 'quarantineTests(' src`):
- src/merge/merge-to-main.ts `verifyMerge`: the in-lock merge check failed, then passed on the immediate retry. A throw here rejects `mergeToMain` before `setMergeStage(…, "merging")`, so a change whose check is green fails its merge attempt.
- src/review/review-precheck.ts `gateBuildPrecheck`: the gate check failed, then passed on the retry. A throw rejects the gate, so the review attempt errors instead of going on with `outcome = retry.outcome`.
- src/baseline/main-watch.ts `watchOnce`: main's confirming re-run turned a red green. A throw skips the rest of `watchOnce` (the baseline transition handling after the re-run). The poll's `.catch` then logs a misleading "main watch could not check main" and marks the head watched.
Each caller ignores the return value. A full disk or a read-only `.tumwater/state` costs only the quarantine record, so it should not undo a passing check. This is the same best-effort contract `writePostReviews` (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) and the bootstrap latch write (src/gates/bootstrap-gates.ts) already follow.

**Approach.**
1. src/review/known-flakes.ts: in `quarantineTests`, replace the trailing `saveQuarantine(root, entries); return added;` with a try around `saveQuarantine`. On a catch, call `warnEventBestEffort(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, \`could not write quarantine.json: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` and `return []`, because nothing was recorded. Otherwise return `added` as before. Import `warnEventBestEffort` and `TUMWATER_SOURCE` from ../events/events.js (known-flakes.ts already imports a type from there, and events.ts imports nothing from src/review, so no cycle) and `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js. Add a sentence to the doc comment: "A failed write warns and returns no tests: the callers run this after a re-run passed, so a lost record must not fail that check." Leave `saveQuarantine`, `markQuarantineFiled` and `releaseQuarantine` unchanged. The latter two run only inside main-watch's `settleQuarantine`, whose try/catch already turns a throw into a "quarantine housekeeping failed" warning.
2. test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts: append the test "quarantine: a failed quarantine.json write warns and records nothing instead of throwing". Import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `warningMessages` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js. With `root = tmpdir()`, `const undo = failRenameSyncOn(quarantinePath(root), "disk full")`. In a try/finally that calls `undo()`, assert `quarantineTests(root, ["a"], "out")` deep-equals `[]`, which also proves it did not throw. After the finally, assert `quarantinedTests(root)` deep-equals `[]`. Assert `warningMessages(root)` holds exactly one message starting with `could not write quarantine.json` that includes `disk full`. Then call `quarantineTests(root, ["a"], "out")` again (the fault is undone) and assert it returns `["a"]`.
3. docs/invariants.md: in the existing section "## Flake quarantine: a test that failed then passed on one tree is quarantined until its filed bug leaves ## Open, and a possibly truncated list never counts", add `### INV-BI5: a failed quarantine write warns and never throws out of the check that passed` after INV-BI4, in the same Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. No new letter pair is needed. Guarantee: `quarantineTests` never throws on a failed store write. It warns once per failed call, records nothing, and returns `[]`, so the gate's re-run, the in-lock merge check's re-run and main-watch's confirming re-run go on with their passing result. Binds `quarantineTests`. Pinned by the step-2 test, cited by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 1's try/catch removed, the new test fails (the call throws `disk full`). With `return []` replaced by `return added`, it fails (it returns `["a"]`).
- The existing tests in test/known-flakes.test.ts, test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts and test/main-watch.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows src/review/known-flakes.ts as the only changed src/ file.
- The test name cited in INV-BI5 exists verbatim (`grep -rF` it in test/).

### Live config reload: a live edit that first routes a seam to opencode seeds the models catalog, as startup does (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/gates/startup-gate.ts + src/config/config-live.ts + test/config-live.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The only place that calls `refreshOpencodeCatalog` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) is `runStartupCheck` in src/gates/startup-gate.ts (checked with `grep -rn refreshOpencodeCatalog src`), and it calls it only when the *startup* config routes a seam to opencode. The live reload in src/config/config-live.ts (`newLiveConfigReload`'s `poll`) already loops over each backend a live edit newly routes to. For each one it checks the binary, and for claude it seeds the account (`seedClaudeAccount`, guarded by `liveClaudeSeedAttempted`) "exactly as startup would". It does nothing for opencode. So a pi team that live-edits a seam onto opencode gets no `.tumwater/state/opencode-models.json` until it restarts. The budget gate (`readOpencodeCache` in src/gates/budget-gates.ts) reads an absent cache as "every opencode seam NOT free". That means a free DeepSeek seam gets priced against the daily cap and is refused as a free fallback, and the role view and doctor show no catalog for it. This is the opencode half of the newly-routed-backend check that plans/provider-concurrency.md §9 gap 1 added for claude.

**Approach.**
1. src/gates/startup-gate.ts: pull the seed call out of `runStartupCheck` into an exported `seedOpencodeCatalog(root: string, config: TumwaterConfig, opts: OpenCodeSeedOptions & { warn?: (message: string) => void } = {}): Promise<unknown>`. It returns `refreshOpencodeCatalog(root, { providers: opencodeProviders(config), cliBin: resolveBackendBin(config, "opencode").bin, fetch: opts.fetch, now: opts.now, warn: opts.warn })`. Move the "Probe the configured opencode binary" comment into it. `runStartupCheck` keeps its `opencodeSeedAttempted` guard and calls `await seedOpencodeCatalog(root, config, opencodeSeed)`. Startup still passes no `warn`, so startup behavior is unchanged.
2. src/config/config-live.ts: add an optional dep `opencodeSeed?: OpenCodeSeedOptions` to `newLiveConfigReload` (tests only; production callers leave it out), plus a `liveOpencodeSeedAttempted` set next to `liveClaudeSeedAttempted`, with a matching comment. In the newly-routed-backend loop, after the claude branch: `if (backend === "opencode" && !liveOpencodeSeedAttempted.has(deps.root)) { liveOpencodeSeedAttempted.add(deps.root); void seedOpencodeCatalog(deps.root, reloaded.config, { ...deps.opencodeSeed, warn }).catch((err) => warn(\`open code model catalog seed failed: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)); }`. Import `errorMessage` from src/text/text.ts, `seedOpencodeCatalog` from src/gates/startup-gate.ts, and its type `OpenCodeSeedOptions`. Do not await it. `poll()` is synchronous and runs once per scheduler cycle, so a models.dev fetch (bounded by `CATALOG_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`) must not stall the loop. The `.catch` stops a rejected refresh from becoming an unhandled rejection, whether or not the in-flight "OpenCode catalog seed" plan has merged. Add opencode to the block comment above the loop: "for claude its account seeded" becomes "its account (claude) or models catalog (opencode) seeded".
3. test/config-live.test.ts: append two async tests. Each builds its reload with `newLiveConfigReload({ root, config: start, mainBranch: "main", runnerSignal: new AbortController().signal, runners, semaphore: new Semaphore(1), opencodeSeed: { fetch, now: () => 1_000 } })`, where `root = makeRepo()`, `writeConfig(root, start)`, `runners = [makeRoleRunner(root, "improve", start)]`. `start` is `defaultConfig()` with `review.enabled = true`. After one `live.poll()` of the unchanged file, each writes `next` with `backends = { opencode: { bin: <tmpdir script "exit 0"> } }` and `review = { ...review, backend: "opencode", model: "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free" }`, calls `live.poll()`, then `await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r))` so the fire-and-forget refresh settles (an `async` fetch stub plus synchronous cache I/O leaves only microtasks).
   - "a live edit routing a seam to opencode seeds the models catalog once": the fetch counts calls and returns `{ opencode: { models: { "deepseek-v4.1-flash-free": { cost: { input: 0, output: 0 } } } } }`. Assert `calls === 1`, `readOpencodeCache(root).fetchedAt === 1_000` and `.models["opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free"]?.free === true`. Poll again, settle again, and assert `calls` is still 1.
   - "a failed live catalog seed warns instead of crashing the poll": the fetch throws. Assert `poll()` returned without throwing, and that `warnMessages(root)` holds exactly one message starting with `open code model catalog fetch failed` (refreshOpencodeCatalog's existing warning, now routed to the live reload's `warn`).
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## Live config reload: a newly routed opencode backend gets its catalog" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20 BY had merged and BZ (OpenCode catalog seed) and CA (Claude account seed) were planned, so CB was free. Write one guarantee: the first successful reload that routes a seam to opencode, when the previous config did not, starts one catalog refresh per root per process. That refresh never blocks or throws out of `poll()`, and a failed fetch warns through the reload's event log. Binds `newLiveConfigReload` and `seedOpencodeCatalog`. Pinned by the two new tests, each cited by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 2's opencode branch removed, the first new test fails (`calls === 0`, `fetchedAt === 0`). With `warn` dropped from the seed options, the second fails (no warning).

### OpenCode catalog seed: a malformed models.dev body or a failed cache write no longer rejects `tumwater start` — done 2026-10-20 (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts + test/opencode-catalog.test.ts + docs/invariants.md)

**Goal.** `runStartupCheck` (src/gates/startup-gate.ts) awaits `refreshOpencodeCatalog` with no catch whenever a model job routes to opencode. Its comment says "a failed fetch keeps the last good cache (or an empty one) and never blocks startup". That holds only for a fetch that throws. Two other failures reject the refresh, and with it `runStartupCheck`, so `tumwater start` (src/cli/cli-start.ts awaits `runStartupCheck` with no catch) dies on a stack trace:
- `parseOpencodeCatalog` casts the fetched body instead of checking it. `Object.entries(providerInfo.models)` throws when a kept provider's `models` is `null`. `m.modalities.input.includes` throws when `input` is not an array or string, and `m.reasoning_options?.filter` throws when `reasoning_options` is not an array. A wrong-typed field passes through silently instead. `cost: { input: "0", output: 0 }` yields `inputPerM: "0"`, which the cache then holds, typed as a number, until the next read drops it.
- `writeOpencodeCache(root, cache)` in `refreshOpencodeCatalog` has no guard, so an unwritable `.tumwater/state/opencode-models.json` rejects the refresh. The cache stays stale, so every later start fails the same way.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed all of these with a scratch test (since deleted). Each of `{ opencode: { models: null } }`, `{ opencode: { models: { m: { modalities: { input: 5 } } } } }` and `{ opencode: { models: { m: { reasoning_options: { type: "effort" } } } } }` made `parseOpencodeCatalog(body, [])` throw a TypeError. The `cost` body above returned `{"opencode/m":{"free":false,"inputPerM":"0","outputPerM":0}}`. `refreshOpencodeCatalog` rejected when a directory sat at `opencodeModelsPath(root)`. "OpenCode catalog cache" in PLANS-DONE.md guarded the read side and deliberately left the parse out of scope; this plan covers the parse.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts, `parseOpencodeCatalog`: make it total over any `body`. Skip a provider unless `isJsonObject(providerInfo?.models)`, and skip a model entry unless `isJsonObject(raw)`. Read `cost` only when `isJsonObject(m.cost)` and `limit.context` only when `isJsonObject(m.limit)`, as today otherwise. Set `images` only when `Array.isArray(m.modalities?.input)`, with `modalities` checked by `isJsonObject` first. Compute `efforts` only when `Array.isArray(m.reasoning_options)`: keep the elements that pass `isJsonObject` and have `type === "effort"`, and flatMap each one's `values` when `Array.isArray`, else `[]`. Finally store the model only when `isOpencodeCatalogModel(model)` holds (the existing guard the cache read uses). That drops a model with a non-finite or non-number price, context or effort, so it reads as missing from the catalog, which means "not free", the safe direction for the budget gate. Add one sentence to the doc comment: the body is untrusted network data, and a malformed provider or model is skipped, never thrown on.
2. Same file, `refreshOpencodeCatalog`: wrap `writeOpencodeCache(root, cache)` in `try`/`catch`. The `catch` calls `opts.warn?.(\`could not save the open code model catalog: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` and the function still returns `cache`. Import `errorMessage` from wherever the other src/ files take it (`grep -rn 'export function errorMessage' src`). Extend the function's doc comment: a failed cache write warns and returns the fetched catalog, so the next start fetches again. Leave startup-gate.ts alone. It passes no `warn` today, and wiring that up is a separate change.
3. test/opencode-catalog.test.ts: append two tests.
   - "parseOpencodeCatalog skips a malformed provider or model instead of throwing": the body is `{ opencode: { models: { a: { modalities: { input: 5 } }, b: { reasoning_options: { type: "effort" } }, c: { cost: { input: "0", output: 0 } }, d: null, ok: { cost: { input: 0, output: 0 } } } }, "opencode-go": { models: null } }` with providers `["opencode-go"]`. `assert.deepEqual` the result to `{ "opencode/a": { free: false }, "opencode/b": { free: false }, "opencode/ok": { free: true, inputPerM: 0, outputPerM: 0 } }`.
   - "a failed catalog write warns and still returns the fetched catalog": on `tmpdir()`, `fs.mkdirSync(opencodeModelsPath(root), { recursive: true })` so a directory blocks the atomic rename. Call `refreshOpencodeCatalog` with `providers: []`, `fetch: fetchOf(catalogCapture())`, `cliVersion: "2.0.32"`, `now: () => 1_000` and a `warn` that collects messages. It resolves with `fetchedAt` 1_000 and `models["opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free"]?.free === true` (the model "a failed fetch keeps the old cache and logs one warning" already reads). Exactly one warning starts with `could not save the open code model catalog`.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## OpenCode catalog seed: a refresh never rejects the startup check" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BU, BV and BW had merged, BX (Merge write-back) and BY (Run end) were planned, and BZ was free. Write one guarantee: `refreshOpencodeCatalog` resolves for any fetched body and any cache-write failure. It drops a malformed upstream model rather than storing it or throwing, and a failed write warns through `opts.warn`. Binds `parseOpencodeCatalog`, `refreshOpencodeCatalog` and `isOpencodeCatalogModel`. Pinned by the two new tests plus "a failed fetch keeps the old cache and logs one warning". Cite each test by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 1 reverted, the first new test fails with a TypeError. With step 2 reverted, the second new test fails because the refresh rejects.
- The existing parse tests (the 2.0.32 capture) still pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts as the only changed src/ file.
- Each test name cited in the new section exists verbatim (`grep -rF` each one in test/).

### Run end: a failed role-state save in `finalizeRun` warns and still logs `run_end`, instead of rejecting the run task and skipping the breaker fold (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/run/run-finalize.ts + src/runner/runner-state.ts + test/run-finalize.test.ts + docs/invariants.md)

**Goal.** `finalizeRun` (src/run/run-finalize.ts) runs after the pi run, and for a `queued` result after the change is already in the merge queue. It folds the outcome with `applyRunOutcome`, releases a finished claim, calls `restoreMidRunWake`, then calls `saveRunnerState(root, s)` with no guard. After that come the streak warnings, the `observeClaudeAccount` fold and the `run_end` event. `runPhase` (src/runner/runner-run.ts) says it "Never throws", but a failed save rejects it: the `run_end` event is never logged (so the run's spend, duration and result never reach the feed the report and the failure digest read), and `ctx.setRunPair(undefined)` never runs. The rejection also skips the rest of the launch task in `launchDueRuns` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts): the fallback breaker's `recordFallbackRunAt` evidence fold and, for a probe, `abandonFallbackProbeAt`. That task's `.catch` only sets `running = false` and warns "run task rejected: …", so a probe run whose save fails leaves its claim on the pair. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the rejection with a scratch test (since deleted) in a copy of test/run-finalize.test.ts. It installed `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "feature-2"), "EACCES fake")` and called the file's `run(root, "feature-2", freshRunnerState("feature-2"), { result: "queued", summary: "x" })` helper. The call rejected with `Error: EACCES fake`, `s.running` was false (the fold had already happened in memory), and `eventsOfType(root, "run_end")` was empty. The in-memory state already holds everything the save would write, and the runner's next save (a skip reason, a merge write-back, the next run's end) writes it to disk. So a best-effort save loses nothing the team needs. This narrows the Poll-loop runner state plan's (PLANS-DONE.md) "run-end and CLI callers keep their errors": `saveRunnerState` itself stays strict, and CLI callers keep their errors.

**Approach.**
1. src/run/run-finalize.ts, `finalizeRun`: replace `saveRunnerState(root, s)` with `saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root, s)`. Swap the import from ../runner/runner-state.js (keep `hasOutstandingWork` and the `RunnerState` type, and drop `saveRunnerState` once `grep -n 'saveRunnerState(' src/run/run-finalize.ts` finds no other call). Add one sentence to the comment above the save, or to `finalizeRun`'s doc comment: a failed save warns and the run still ends normally, because the in-memory state already holds the fold and the runner's next save writes it.
2. src/runner/runner-state.ts, `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`'s doc comment: it now names two callers, not just "the orchestrator's poll loop, which has no catch". ### Merge write-back: a failed role-state save in `writeMergeOutcome` warns and still drops the settled queue entry, instead of leaving a merged change queued for a second review (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts + test/merge-slot.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) runs after a merge has settled, often after the change is already on main. Its order is `applyMergeOutcome`, then `saveRunnerState(root, state)` with no guard, then the streak warning, the best-effort `merge_done`/`merge_failed` event, and finally `dropMerge(file)`. Its doc comment says an unwritable feed "must not skip the drop, or the settled entry would stay queued and be re-verified and re-merged on the next drain". A failed state save skips the drop in exactly that way. The throw also skips the rest of `settleMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts): `removeMergeChange` and `requeueKeptChange` never run. `guardMergeTask` catches it and logs "merge task for <role> could not settle". On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed this with a scratch test (since deleted) in a copy of test/merge-slot.test.ts. It queued an entry with the file's `queued(root)` helper, installed `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "EACCES fake")`, and called `writeMergeOutcome(root, entry, state, "changed", 7, { tokens: 0, cost: 0, providerCost: {} }, file)`. The call threw `Error: EACCES fake`, `queueDepth(root)` was 1, the queue file still existed, and the log held no events. The live `state` object is the runner's own state, so the outcome is already applied in memory, and the runner's next save writes it to disk.

**Approach.**
1. src/merge/merge-slot.ts, `writeMergeOutcome`: replace `saveRunnerState(root, state)` with `saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root, state)`. It is already imported, and on failure it warns under the role's id with "could not save the role's state: <message>". Add one sentence to the doc comment: a failed state save warns and does not skip the drop either, because the in-memory state already holds the outcome and the runner's next save writes it. Leave `saveRunnerState` in `requeueKeptChange` alone (its caller `settleMergeOutcome` already wraps it in a `try`). Leave merge-core.ts alone (its verdict save runs before the merge, not after a durable step). Keep the `saveRunnerState` import only while some other call in the file still uses it (`grep -n 'saveRunnerState(' src/merge/merge-slot.ts`).
2. test/merge-slot.test.ts: after "an unwritable events feed still drops the settled entry — the queue never retries", add "a failed role-state save still logs the outcome and drops the settled entry". Use `queued(root)` and `freshRunnerState("improve")`. Install `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "EACCES fake")` (add `failRenameSyncOn` to the existing ./helpers/fs-faults.js import and `statePath` to the ../src/paths.js import), call `writeMergeOutcome(root, entry, state, "changed", 7, { tokens: 0, cost: 0, providerCost: {} }, file)`, and undo the fault in a `finally`. Assert that `queueDepth(root)` is 0, that `fs.existsSync(file)` is false, that `state.commits` is 1 (the in-memory fold), that `readEvents(root, 10)` has one `merge_done` event, and that `warningMessages(root)` (from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js) is exactly one entry matching `/could not save the role's state: EACCES fake/`.
3. docs/invariants.md: append "## Merge write-back: a settled entry is always dropped" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BU had merged, BV (OpenCode catalog cache) and BW (QA flow coverage) were planned, and BX was free. Write one guarantee: `writeMergeOutcome` drops the entry's queue file for every result, even when the role's state save or the event write fails; each failure warns and nothing throws. Binds `writeMergeOutcome` and `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`. Pinned by the new test plus "an unwritable events feed still drops the settled entry — the queue never retries" and "a merge's nonzero usage rides its merge_done event and the entry is dropped". Cite each test by its full name.

### OpenCode catalog cache: a foreign entry in `opencode-models.json` is dropped on read instead of throwing out of the poll loop's budget gate and `tumwater status`, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts + test/opencode-catalog.test.ts + test/status-budget.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `readOpencodeCache` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) checks that `fetchedAt` is a number and that `models` is an object (`isJsonObject`). It does not check the entries, so anything inside `models` reaches callers typed as `OpencodeCatalogModel`. `opencodeModelFree` reads `entry.free` after testing only `entry !== undefined`, so a `null` entry throws a TypeError. `opencodeModelFree` is reached from `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts, through `piPairFree` in src/pi/pi-models.ts; `pollTeamGates` in src/gates/gate-polls.ts calls it with no try), which means the throw escapes the poll loop. It is also reached from `collectBudget` (src/status/status-budget.ts), so it breaks `tumwater status` and the dashboards. `observeOpencodeRun` reads `entry.free` the same way. A wrong-typed field is quietly wrong instead of throwing. `free: "yes"` reads as free to the budget gate, which is the unsafe direction. `efforts: "high"` is a string, and the opencode backend's `entry?.efforts?.includes(thinking)` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts) matches substrings of it. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed all three with a scratch test (since deleted). The test wrote `{"fetchedAt":1,"models":{"opencode/m":null,"opencode/s":{"free":"yes"},"opencode/e":{"free":false,"efforts":"high"}}}` and read it back with `readOpencodeCache`. Then `opencodeModelFree(c, "opencode/m")` and `observeOpencodeRun(root, { model: "opencode/m", costUsd: 1 }, …)` threw TypeError, `opencodeModelFree(c, "opencode/s")` returned true, and the `efforts` value's `.includes("hi")` returned true. The cache file is a hand-editable state file, and a failed catalog fetch keeps whatever it holds (`refreshOpencodeCatalog`), so one bad entry stays in place until a fetch succeeds.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts: add an unexported `isOpencodeCatalogModel(value: unknown): value is OpencodeCatalogModel`. It requires `isJsonObject(value)` and `typeof value.free === "boolean"`. Each optional field must be absent or well typed: `inputPerM`, `outputPerM`, `context` and `billedAt` must each be a number with `Number.isFinite`, `images` must be a boolean, and `efforts` must be an array whose every element is a string. Any other field rides along unchecked. `readOpencodeCache` keeps its top-level checks. It returns `models` as a new object that keeps only the entries passing the guard, so a dropped entry reads as a model missing from the cache. That is "not free", the safe direction `opencodeModelFree`'s doc comment already names. Extend `readOpencodeCache`'s doc comment to say so in one sentence. Leave `opencodeModelFree`, `observeOpencodeRun`, `refreshOpencodeCatalog` and `parseOpencodeCatalog` unchanged. The parse of OpenCode's own fetched body is a separate concern and out of scope.

   - foreign entries `"opencode/null": null`, `"opencode/num": 7`, `"opencode/yes": { free: "yes" }`, `"opencode/nofree": { context: 1000 }`, `"opencode/ctx": { free: true, context: "big" }`, `"opencode/eff": { free: false, efforts: "high" }`, `"opencode/eff2": { free: false, efforts: ["high", 3] }` and `"opencode/billed": { free: true, billedAt: "soon" }`

   Assert that `readOpencodeCache(root).models` deep-equals `{ "opencode/ok": { free: true, context: 1000, efforts: ["high"], extra: 1 } }`. Assert that `opencodeModelFree(readOpencodeCache(root), "opencode/null")` and the same call for `"opencode/yes"` both return false. Assert that `observeOpencodeRun(root, { model: "opencode/null", costUsd: 1 }, { source: "feature", log: () => {} })` returns null. Import `readOpencodeCache`.

### QA flow coverage: a failed `qa-coverage.json` write warns instead of failing a run whose merge is already queued (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/run/run-stage.ts + src/run/run-verdict.ts + test/run-stage.test.ts + test/run-verdict.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `recordFlow` (src/run/qa-coverage.ts) writes the qa ledger with `writeJsonAtomic` and does not catch a write failure. Its two callers do not catch it either:
- `stageRunMerge` (src/run/run-stage.ts) calls `recordFlow` after the merge is queued, after the pin, and after the best-effort `merge_queued` event.
- `resolveRunVerdict` (src/run/run-verdict.ts) calls it on the no-change path, before returning `no_change`.

So a full disk, a read-only `.tumwater`, or any other failed ledger write throws out of the run. The catch in `runPhase` (src/runner/runner-run.ts) then turns the outcome into `error` and sets `lastError`. `finalizeRun` (src/run/run-finalize.ts) counts that toward the role's error streak, even when the work was committed and queued. The test was a copy of "a qa flow record from the reply is written into the coverage file" with `failRenameSyncOn(qaCoveragePath(root), "EACCES fake")` installed. `stageRunMerge` rejected with `Error: EACCES fake` while `queueDepth(root)` was 1. Without the fault it returned `no_change` and recorded the flow. With the same fault installed it rejected with `Error: EACCES fake`. The ledger only orders the qa role's flow menu. The run-stage comment beside `logEventBestEffort` already says that observability must not reject a run whose work is queued, and the ledger is in the same position.

Import `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js. Add a one-line comment saying the merge is already queued and the ledger only orders the qa menu, so a failed write warns rather than failing the run. Its return value and every other step stay as they are.

Assert that `outcome.result` is `"queued"`, that `queueDepth(root)` is 1, that `readQaCoverage(root)` deep-equals `{}`, and that `calls.warnings` holds exactly one entry matching `/qa flow "unit tests" not recorded: EACCES fake/`.

   - "a no_change run records its qa flow": the outcome is `no_change` and `readQaCoverage(root).status?.result` is `"passed"`.
   - "a failed qa coverage write warns and the no_change run stands": run with `failRenameSyncOn(qaCoveragePath(root), "EACCES fake")` installed and undone in a `finally`. The outcome is `no_change`, `readQaCoverage(root)` deep-equals `{}`, and `warns` is exactly one entry matching `/qa flow "status" not recorded: EACCES fake/`.
5. docs/invariants.md: append "## QA flow coverage: a failed ledger write never fails a run" after the last section. ### Post-merge reviews: a torn `post-review.json` entry or a failed `post-review.json` write warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop or wedging the merge slot, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts + test/post-merge-review.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `drainMergeQueue` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) calls `drainPostReviews` (src/merge/merge-post-review.ts) on every poll that is not held. The poll loop is a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so a throw there ends the team. The post-review file (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) can break the pipeline in three places:
- `readPostReviews` returns `saved.pending` without checking its entries. With `{"pending":[null]}`, `drainPostReviews` throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'rejected')` from `pending.find`, and it throws again on every later poll.
- `startRevert` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) calls `settlePostReview` in the revert task's `.finally`, before `p.merge = null`. When that write throws, `guardMergeTask` swallows the rejection, but `p.merge` stays set, so `drainMerge` never starts another merge or revert.
- In `drainPostReviews`, the revert skip check's `.then` calls `settlePostReview` before its warning. When that write throws, the chain rejects with no handler (`void`), and the "not reverting" warning is never logged.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the first two with scratch tests (since deleted). The first wrote `{"pending":[null]}` and called `drainPostReviews`, which threw. So does `addPostReview`, which `startMerge`'s `settleOne` calls before `settleMergeOutcome`: a throw there would skip writing back the merged change's outcome. This plan fixes the reader and that one writer, and does not edit src/merge/merge-drain.ts (the in-flight "Pending reverts" plan edits that file).

What that costs: a missed add leaves the commit unreviewed, with the warning naming the failure. A missed settle after an approval or a failed run means the commit is reviewed again. A missed settle after a revert keeps the rejected entry, and the next poll's `revertSkipReason` finds that its revert already merged and settles it.

### Pending reverts: a torn `reverted.json` entry, a failed hand-back save or a failed `reverted.json` rewrite warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/merge/merge-drain.ts + test/main-revert.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** Every poll that is not held runs `pollMergeDrain` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts) → `drainMergeQueue` → `assignPendingReverts` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts). The orchestrator's poll loop is a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so a throw there ends the team. `assignPendingReverts` has three unguarded throws:
- `pendingReverts` returns `saved.reverted` without checking its entries. An entry of `null` makes `handBackRevert` throw on `pending.role`. An entry whose `reasons` is not an array throws in `recordRevertedChange` (`reasons.map`, src/merge/merge-core.ts).
- `handBackRevert` calls `saveRunnerState(ctx.root, taker.state)` with no guard.
- The `writeJsonAtomic(revertedPendingPath(ctx.root), { reverted: left })` rewrite has no guard.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the first two with a scratch test (since deleted). In a temp root with no git repo, with runners `[fakeRunner("improve")]` (test/main-revert.test.ts's helper), `assignPendingReverts` rejects when reverted.json holds `{"reverted":[null]}`. It also rejects with "state write refused" when the file holds one well-formed entry for `improve` and `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "state write refused")` is installed.
A save that fails after `recordRevertedChange` has set `taker.state.revision` leaves the in-memory runner holding the revision. A failed rewrite then leaves the entry in the file. Today nothing stops the next poll from handing that same commit to a free sibling instance as well, so this plan also makes the hand-back skip a commit some runner already took.

**Approach.** All code changes are in src/merge/merge-drain.ts, which already imports `warnEventBestEffort`, `TUMWATER_SOURCE`, `errorMessage` and `writeJsonAtomic`.
1. `pendingReverts`: keep only entries that are JSON objects (use `isJsonObject`; find its module with grep and import it) with a string `commit`, a string `role`, and an array `reasons`. Rebuild `reasons` from its string elements only. Extend the doc comment: a torn or hand-edited entry is dropped, and the next rewrite leaves it out.
2. `handBackRevert`: wrap `saveRunnerState(ctx.root, taker.state)` in `try`/`catch`. The `catch` calls `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, taker.role, \`could not save the reverted change's revision: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)`, and the function still returns `true`. The in-memory state holds the revision, and the runner's next successful save writes it. If `saveRunnerStateBestEffort` exists in src/runner/runner-state.ts by then (the in-flight "Poll-loop runner state" plan adds it), call that instead of writing the `try`.
3. `assignPendingReverts`: before handing a pending entry back, skip it as already assigned when some runner in `ctx.runners` has `state.lastReview?.verdict === "reverted"` and `state.lastReview.head === pending.commit`. `recordRevertedChange` sets exactly that on every hand-back, the exhausted path included. Such an entry goes into neither `left` nor a hand-back, so the rewrite drops it. Then wrap the final `writeJsonAtomic` in `try`/`catch` that calls `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, \`could not rewrite the pending reverted changes: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)`. Add one sentence to the function's doc comment: it never throws, because the poll loop calls it with no catch, and step 3's check keeps a retry after a failed rewrite from handing a commit out twice.
4. Leave `handBackReverted`'s own `writeJsonAtomic` alone. It runs inside the revert's merge task (`runMainRevert(...)` in `drainMerge`), not in the poll body. It does share `handBackRevert`, so it gets step 2's guard too.
5. test/main-revert.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` and `patchFsMethod` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `statePath` from ../src/paths.js (`revertedPendingPath` is already imported). Write the cases on a temp root (`fs.mkdtempSync`), creating `path.dirname(revertedPendingPath(root))` first. Use ctx `{ root, mainBranch: "main", runners } as unknown as MergePipelineContext` with `fakeRunner`, the way `revertWith` builds it. There is no git repo, so `recordRevertedChange`'s git calls fail soft (`gitTry`) and the hand-back still sets `state.revision`. Use a commit of `"a".repeat(40)`. Undo every fault in a `finally`. Append:
   - "a torn reverted.json entry is dropped and the well-formed one is still handed back": the file holds `[null, {"commit": 7}, {"commit": "<sha>", "role": "improve", "reasons": "x"}, {"commit": "<sha>", "role": "improve", "reasons": ["first", 3]}]`. `assignPendingReverts` resolves. `improve`'s `state.revision?.sha` is the sha, and its `state.lastReview?.reasons` deep-equals `["first"]`. The file then reads `{ reverted: [] }`.
   - "a hand-back whose state save fails warns and still counts as assigned": one well-formed entry, with `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "state write refused")` installed. The call resolves, `state.revision?.sha` is the sha, the file reads `{ reverted: [] }`, and one `warning` event (`eventsOfType`, already imported) has source `improve` and a message containing `state write refused`.
   - "a failed reverted.json rewrite warns, and the next poll does not hand the commit out twice": runners `feature` and `feature-2`, both free, and one entry for role `feature`. Patch `renameSync` with `patchFsMethod` so that a rename whose destination equals `revertedPendingPath(root)` throws `new Error("pending write refused")` (check `FsCall`'s type in fs-faults.ts and match the wrapper's signature to it). The first call resolves, `feature` holds the revision, and a `warning` event's message contains `pending write refused`. Undo the patch. `feature` now holds a revision, so `hasOutstandingWork` keeps it from being free. The second call resolves, `feature-2.state.revision` is undefined, and the file reads `{ reverted: [] }`.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) drop step 1's filter — the torn-entry test rejects; (ii) remove step 2's `try` — the save test rejects; (iii) remove step 3's `try` — the rewrite test rejects; (iv) remove step 3's already-assigned check — the rewrite test's `feature-2.state.revision` is set. Put in VERIFIED only what you saw.
6. docs/invariants.md: append "## Pending reverts: a hand-back from reverted.json never throws and never hands a commit out twice" after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BQ had merged, BR (Poll-loop runner state) was planned, and BS was free. Use the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout:
   - 1: a reverted.json entry that is not an object with a string commit, a string role and an array of reasons is dropped, and the reasons keep only their strings. Binds `pendingReverts`. Pinned by the torn-entry test.
   - 2: `assignPendingReverts` never throws. A failed state save warns under the taker's id and the entry still counts as assigned, and a failed rewrite warns under `tumwater`. Binds `handBackRevert`, `assignPendingReverts`. Pinned by the save and rewrite tests, plus "with no free runner the revision waits in reverted.json and is assigned once one frees" (the healthy path still rewrites the file).
   - 3: a commit some runner's `lastReview` records as reverted is never handed out again. Binds `assignPendingReverts`. Pinned by the rewrite test.

### Poll-loop runner state: a skip-reason, claim-release or main_red re-queue save that fails warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/runner/runner-state.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts + src/merge/merge-slot.ts + test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts + test/merge-requeue.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The orchestrator's poll loop (`while (!signal.aborted)` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) runs inside a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so any throw from a poll step ends the team (`stopCause` stays `"error"`). Three poll-step writes of a runner's state file call `saveRunnerState` (src/runner/runner-state.ts, a `writeJsonAtomic`) with no guard:
- `noteSkip` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, which `pollRunnerReasons` calls whenever a role's skip reason changes;
- the claim-release save in `pollRunnerReasons` (`r.state.claim = undefined; saveRunnerState(root, r.state)`);
- both saves in `requeueMainRedPin` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts), which `pollMergeDrain` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts) calls for every runner, plus its `enqueueRetry` → `enqueueMerge` queue write.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted): in the existing claim-hold setup ("a sibling held by an unclaimed mid-entry runner records claim-hold, cleared once admitted"), making the rename of `statePath(root, "feature-2")` fail with `failRenameSyncOn` (test/helpers/fs-faults.ts) makes `pollRunnerReasons` reject with that error. A full disk (ENOSPC), a read-only `.tumwater/state` (EACCES) or a state path replaced by a directory reaches the poll loop the same way. The in-memory state is already updated before each of these saves, and the next successful save of that runner (its run end, or the next change) writes it, so a failed save loses nothing the team needs to keep running. The events feed beside these saves is already best-effort ("a claim release survives an unwritable events feed").

**Approach.**
1. src/runner/runner-state.ts: add `export function saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root: string, state: RunnerState): void` beside `saveRunnerState`. It calls `saveRunnerState` in a `try`; the `catch` calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, state.role, \`could not save the role's state: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` (import `warnEventBestEffort` from ../events/events.js and `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js; events.ts does not import runner-state, so there is no cycle). Doc comment: for writes in the orchestrator's poll loop, which has no catch; the in-memory state stays ahead of the file until the runner's next successful save. Leave `saveRunnerState` itself strict: run-end and CLI callers keep their errors.
2. src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts: `noteSkip` and the claim-release save in `pollRunnerReasons` call `saveRunnerStateBestEffort` instead of `saveRunnerState`. If `saveRunnerState` is then unused in the file, drop it from the import.
3. src/merge/merge-slot.ts, `requeueMainRedPin`: both `saveRunnerState(root, state)` calls become `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`. Wrap the final `enqueueRetry(root, retryEntry(kept.entry, sha, "main_red"))` in `try`/`catch` that calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, kept.entry.role, \`the kept main_red change could not be re-queued: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` (import what is missing; check the file's existing imports first). Do not restore `state.mainRedRetry` on that failure: the role's leftover recovery re-queues a kept pin with no record, as `requeueKeptChange`'s doc says ("leftover recovery stays the backstop"). Extend `requeueMainRedPin`'s doc comment with one sentence: it never throws, since the poll loop calls it with no catch. Leave `requeueKeptChange` alone: it runs when a merge settles, not in the poll body.
4. test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `eventsOfType` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js (that module is already imported for `unwritableEvents`/`writeEvents`). Append two tests; undo each fault in a `finally`:
   - "a skip reason that cannot be saved warns and leaves the poll running": the claim-hold setup above, with `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "feature-2"), "state write refused")` installed before the poll. `pollRunnerReasons` resolves; `feature2.state.skipReason` is `"claim-hold"`; one `warning` event has source `feature-2` and a message containing `state write refused`.
   - "a claim release that cannot be saved warns and leaves the poll running": the "a claim release survives an unwritable events feed" setup (first poll assigns `beta` to feature-2, then `config.roles.feature = { enabled: true, instances: 1 }`), with the same fault on feature-2's state path before the second poll. It resolves and `feature2.state.claim` is undefined. `failRenameSyncOn` fails only the first matching rename, so do not assert on the file's contents.
5. test/merge-requeue.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` and `patchFsMethod` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js, `statePath` and `mergeQueueDir` from ../src/paths.js. Append two tests built like "a main_red pin is re-queued once main's head moves, and not before" (`pinnedEntry`, `settleMergeOutcome(..., "main_red", ...)`, `noteGreenBaseline` on a moved head); install each fault after the settle and undo it in a `finally`:
   - "a main_red re-queue whose state save fails still queues the change": `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "state write refused")`. `requeueMainRedPin` resolves, `queuedMerges(root)` holds the entry with `retry: "main_red"`, and `state.mainRedRetry` is undefined.
   - "a main_red re-queue whose queue write fails warns instead of throwing": `patchFsMethod("renameSync", (orig) => (a, b) => { if (typeof b === "string" && b.startsWith(mergeQueueDir(root))) throw new Error("queue write refused"); return orig(a, b); })` (check `FsCall`'s type in fs-faults.ts and adapt the wrapper's signature to it). `requeueMainRedPin` resolves, `queuedMerges(root)` is empty, and a `warning` event's message contains `queue write refused`.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) `noteSkip` back to `saveRunnerState` — the skip-reason test rejects; (ii) the claim release back to `saveRunnerState` — the claim-release test rejects; (iii) `requeueMainRedPin`'s clearing save back to `saveRunnerState` — the state-save test rejects; (iv) the enqueue `try` removed — the queue-write test rejects. 6. docs/invariants.md: append "## Runner state in the poll loop: a failed save costs only that save" after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. ### Session retention: an OpenCode DB directory that cannot be created skips only the OpenCode session deletes instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a session-retention section (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/orchestrator/retention.ts + test/retention.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `RetentionPruner.prune` (src/orchestrator/retention.ts) calls `ensureParentDir(dbPath)` for `opencodeDbPath(root)` first, before any pruning, with no catch. It runs from the `RetentionPruner` constructor at startup (`new RetentionPruner(root, config.sessionRetentionDays)` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) and from `RetentionPruner.poll` in the poll loop (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts). The `pruneOldFiles` doc comment in src/files/files.ts says a throw escaping this pass "would end the whole team". On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted): when `.tumwater/opencode` is a regular file, `new RetentionPruner(root, 7)` throws EEXIST, and so does `poll(root, 7)` on a pruner built with 0. A 30-day-old file in `toolOutputDir(root)` survives, because the throw comes before the file pass. A read-only `.tumwater` (EACCES) or a full disk (ENOSPC on the mkdir) leaves through the same call. A team that has never run OpenCode still pays this cost, because the directory is created unconditionally. If that directory cannot be created, the OpenCode DB cannot exist either, so no `opencode session delete` could succeed. Skipping the deletes loses nothing. docs/invariants.md has no section on retention.ts: `grep -n -i retention docs/invariants.md` finds nothing.

**Approach.**
1. src/orchestrator/retention.ts, `RetentionPruner.prune`: make `bin` a `let`. Wrap `ensureParentDir(dbPath)` in `try { … } catch { bin = undefined; }`. With no `bin`, `pruneOpencodeSessions` skips the session deletes but still prunes the spill dir. The file pass and the ledger line pass then run as before. Add a short comment: the directory cannot be created, so no OpenCode DB is there to delete from, and this pass runs in the poll loop, where a throw ends the team. Use plain vocabulary (no "tick", no "loop" for role). Change nothing else in src/.
2. test/retention.test.ts: append one test, "RetentionPruner: an OpenCode DB dir that cannot be created skips the session deletes and still prunes the rest". Write a regular file at `path.dirname(opencodeDbPath(root))` (import `opencodeDbPath` from ../src/paths.js; create its parent first). Add a 30-day-old file in `toolOutputDir(root)` with the existing `staleFile` helper. Record a 30-day-old `opencode` session with `recordSession`, as the idle-role test does, and point `TUMWATER_OPENCODE_BIN` at a `writeScript` capture bin, deleting the variable in a `finally`. Then:
   - `assert.doesNotThrow(() => new RetentionPruner(root, 7))`. The tool-output file is gone, and the capture log does not exist (no delete was attempted).
   - Make a new stale tool-output file. `const p = new RetentionPruner(root, 0)`, then `assert.doesNotThrow(() => p.poll(root, 7))`. The file is gone.
   Do not assert on the spill dir: `opencodeSpillDir` points under `os.homedir()` and is `""` for a root without commits.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) remove the try/catch. The constructor throws EEXIST. (ii) Keep the catch but leave its body empty, so `bin` is not cleared. The capture log then holds `session delete`, and the test fails. Check whether any other test in test/retention.test.ts catches either mutation, and claim in VERIFIED only what you saw.

### Session ledger: a retention trim that cannot rewrite a ledger leaves it as it was instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a session-ledger section (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/session-ledger.ts + docs/invariants.md + a new test/session-ledger-prune.test.ts)

**Goal.** `pruneSessionLedgers` (src/agent/session-ledger.ts) rewrites each ledger that lost a line with `writeTextAtomic`, and nothing catches a failure of that write. Its one caller is `RetentionPruner.prune` (src/orchestrator/retention.ts). That runs from the `RetentionPruner` constructor at startup (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) and from `RetentionPruner.poll` inside the poll loop (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts). The loop "and its finally run with no catch" (the `bestEffortEventLogger` comment in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts), and `walkFiles`' doc comment in src/files/files.ts says that a throw escaping the retention pass "would end the whole team". So a full disk (ENOSPC on the temp file) or a read-only session dir holding one stale ledger line stops the team, or keeps it from starting. A full disk is the case where retention matters most. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted):
- a stale line in a session dir chmodded 0o555 makes `pruneSessionLedgers` throw EACCES;
- with `withThrowingFs("writeFileSync", errnoError("ENOSPC"), …)` (test/helpers/fs-faults.ts) it throws ENOSPC, and the ledger's bytes are unchanged and no temp file is left behind (`writeAtomic` removes it);
- a ledger with nothing past the window is not rewritten: its mtime and inode are unchanged;
- a ledger whose every line ages out stays in place as an empty file; a line whose `at` is not a number (`"x"`) counts as pruned;
- `hasResumableSession` is false for a missing dir and for a dir holding only `sessions.jsonl`, and true once another `.jsonl` file exists;
- `recordSession` into a path under a regular file does not throw, and `readSessions` of it is `[]`;
- `pruneOpencodeSessions` with no `bin` returns 0 and still deletes an old spill file; with a `bin` that exits 1 it returns 0; with a `bin` path that does not exist it returns 0 and does not throw.
docs/invariants.md names none of session-ledger.ts's functions. test/session-ledger.test.ts covers the record/read round trip, the resume selection and the main prune path, but none of the points above.

A ledger that cannot be rewritten keeps all its lines and adds nothing to the count, so the `pruned N stale session ledger line(s)` warning in retention.ts never claims lines that are still there. Extend the doc comment by one sentence: a ledger that cannot be rewritten (a full disk, a read-only dir) is left as it was and not counted, because this pass runs in the orchestrator's poll loop, where a throw ends the team. Use plain vocabulary (no "tick", "loop" for role, "landing"); src/agent/ is already under the vocabulary guard. Change nothing else in src/.
