### docs/invariants.md gains an orchestrator-info section, and one new test file pins that a publish writes once for a changed batch, never for an unchanged one, and warns rather than throws when the file cannot be written (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/orchestrator-info-publish.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `publishInfoFields` (src/team/orchestrator-info.ts) is the only way the orchestrator's poll publishes the info file that status, the TUI, the GUI and `tumwater start`'s second-team check read. Its callers are src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts (permits, check permits, slot pool, build) and src/gates/gate-polls.ts (the budget fields, disk). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name orchestrator-info.ts or any of its functions, and no test imported `publishInfoFields`. test/orchestrator-info.test.ts pins the tolerant reader, the atomic writer and `orchestratorAlive`, but not the publish rules the function's doc comment promises:
- an unchanged batch leaves the file untouched and returns false (the comparison is by JSON serialization, so a fresh but equal object is not a change);
- every field in a batch is staged, with no short-circuit, and a changed batch is one write that holds all of them;
- publishing `undefined` for a present field removes it from the file;
- a write that fails (for example, the path is a directory) does not throw. It logs one `warning` reading "could not publish orchestrator info: …", the in-memory `info` keeps the new value, and the function still returns true. Publishing the same value again returns false and does not retry. The doc comment says the field "is retried the next time its value changes".
The plan role confirmed all four behaviors on 2026-10-20 with a scratch test, then deleted it. The scratch test made the write fail by `fs.mkdirSync` on `orchestratorStatePath(root)`; on darwin the rename failed with EISDIR.

**Approach.**
1. New test/orchestrator-info-publish.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/orchestrator-info.test.ts. Import `publishInfoFields`, `readOrchestratorInfo`, `writeOrchestratorInfo` and the `OrchestratorInfo` type from ../src/team/orchestrator-info.js, `orchestratorStatePath` from ../src/paths.js, `tmpdir` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js and `warningMessages` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js. Each test starts from `const info: OrchestratorInfo = { pid: 1, startedAt: 2, roles: ["feature"] }` and calls `writeOrchestratorInfo(root, info)`.
2. Test "publishInfoFields writes every field of a changed batch in one publish". Publish `[["stopsAt", 5], ["slotPool", { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`. Expect a return of true, and expect `readOrchestratorInfo(root)` to deep-equal `{ ...base, stopsAt: 5, slotPool: { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 } }`. Then publish `[["stopsAt", 5], ["slotPool", { leased: 2, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`, where only the second field changes, and expect the file to carry `leased: 2`. Mutation: replace the loop with `const changed = fields.some(([field, value]) => assignInfoFieldIfChanged(info, field, value));`. The first batch then stages only `stopsAt`.
3. Test "publishInfoFields leaves the file untouched when no field changed". After the step-2 style publish, `fs.rmSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))`. Then publish the same values again as fresh object literals, plus `["disk", undefined]` for a field that was never present. Expect a return of false, and expect `fs.existsSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))` to be false. Mutations: (a) `if (changed)` → `if (true)` before the write, which recreates the file; (b) in `assignInfoFieldIfChanged`, compare `value === info[field]` instead of the two `JSON.stringify` calls, which makes the fresh `slotPool` object a change.
4. Test "publishInfoFields removes a field published as undefined". Publish `[["slotPool", { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`, then `[["slotPool", undefined]]`. Expect the second call to return true, and expect the read-back file to have no `slotPool` key (`assert.equal("slotPool" in readOrchestratorInfo(root)!, false)`). Mutation: in `assignInfoFieldIfChanged`, add `if (value === undefined) return false;` as its first line.
5. Test "publishInfoFields warns instead of throwing when the info file cannot be written". `fs.rmSync` the file and `fs.mkdirSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))`. Publish `[["stopsAt", 9]]`, wrapped in `assert.doesNotThrow`. Expect a return of true, `info.stopsAt === 9`, and exactly one message in `warningMessages(root)` that starts with "could not publish orchestrator info: ". Publish `[["stopsAt", 9]]` again. Expect false, with still exactly one such warning. Mutation: add `throw err;` after the `warnEventBestEffort(...)` call in `writeOrchestratorInfoBestEffort`. This type-checks and keeps every import used.
   Run the new file once. Before writing VERIFIED, apply each mutation by hand, check that it fails its new test, and check that the test passes again once you revert it. Also run test/orchestrator-info.test.ts and test/gate-polls.test.ts under each mutation, and drop any claim that only the new tests catch a mutation that one of them also catches.
6. docs/invariants.md: append "## Orchestrator info: a publish writes once for a changed batch and never for an unchanged one, a failed write warns rather than throws, and a reader drops a wrong-shaped field" at the end, after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BK had merged, BL, BM and BN were planned, and BO was free. Follow the existing Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout:
   - 1: A publish stages every field, compares each by JSON serialization, writes once when any changed and not at all otherwise, and a field published as `undefined` leaves the file. Binds `publishInfoFields` and `assignInfoFieldIfChanged`. Pinned by the step 2–4 tests.
   - 2: A publish never throws: a failed write logs one `warning`, keeps the new value in memory, and is not retried until the value changes again. Startup's `writeOrchestratorInfo` stays strict and atomic. Binds `publishInfoFields`, `writeOrchestratorInfoBestEffort`, `writeOrchestratorInfo`. Pinned by the step-5 test plus "writeOrchestratorInfo leaves the previous file intact when a write is killed mid-flight" (test/orchestrator-info.test.ts).
   - 3: `readOrchestratorInfo` returns null for a missing, torn or non-object file, and drops each nested field whose shape is foreign while it keeps well-formed ones; `orchestratorAlive` is false with no info. Binds `readOrchestratorInfo`, `normalizeInfoFields`, `orchestratorAlive`. Pinned by "readOrchestratorInfo returns null for missing, torn, and non-object files", "readOrchestratorInfo drops nested fields with a foreign shape and keeps well-formed ones", "readOrchestratorInfo round-trips a well-formed providerHolds and drops foreign entries" and "orchestratorAlive is false with no info and reflects pid liveness otherwise" (test/orchestrator-info.test.ts), and "pollTeamGates publishes the measured disk state for observers" (test/gate-polls.test.ts).
   Cite each test by its full name.

### docs/invariants.md gains a fallback-chain-reason section, and one new test file pins the four chain reasons no test reaches: demoted, step-cap, reserve and overage (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/budget-chain-info.test.ts — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `chainInfo` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts) builds the `chain` block the orchestrator publishes for each tier the budget gate moved off its primary. "demoted", "step-cap", "reserve" and "overage" are therefore unpinned, and so is their order. The plan role ran a scratch probe that called `chainInfo` directly on 2026-10-20 and confirmed every behavior below. The probe was then deleted.

1. Create test/budget-chain-info.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/budget-gates.test.ts. Import `chainInfo` from ../src/gates/budget-gates.js, `defaultConfig` from ../src/config/config.js, `IDLE_FALLBACK_BREAKER` from ../src/budget/fallback-breaker.js, `todayStamp` from ../src/budget/budget.js, and the `TierFallbackMap` type from ../src/config/config-fallbacks.js. Write a local helper that calls `chainInfo` with these defaults: `resolved` = `{ default: <the case's resolution>, small: { pair: null, from: null }, strong: { pair: null, from: null } }`, `moved: new Set(["default"])`, `breakers: {}`, `states: []`, `windowOut: null`, `account: null` and `isPriced: () => true`. Each case overrides what it needs. States are `{ dayStamp: todayStamp(now), dayCostByPair: { … } }`. No temp directory is needed: `chainInfo` is pure.
   - Config "pi two-step": `defaultConfig()` with `provider = "paid"`, `model = "gpt-x"` and `fallback = [{ model: "free/qwen-free", maxDailyCostUsd: 1 }, "free/llama-free"]`. The resolution is `{ pair: { provider: "free", model: "llama-free" }, from: null, step: 1 }`.
   - Config "claude primary": `provider = undefined`, `backend = "claude"`, `model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` and `fallback = [{ backend: "claude", model: "claude-opus-5-5" }, { model: "free/qwen-free", maxDailyCostUsd: 3 }]`. ### docs/invariants.md gains a git-diff-paths section, and one new test file pins that a tree diff tells an unreadable answer from an empty one, lists both ends of a move, and decodes non-ASCII names (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/git-diff-paths.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** src/git/git-diff.ts turns git's diff output into paths and capped diffs. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name git-diff.ts or any of its functions. test/git-diff.test.ts covers `changedFiles`, `unquotePorcelainPath`, `aheadOfMainDiff` and the range of `aheadOfMainFiles`, but before this entry no test called `treeDiffFiles` directly. The merge path depends on it: `exemptTreeDelta` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) decides whether a stack is review-exempt, and the overwrite-blocker check in src/merge/merge-git.ts reads it. Three documented guarantees have no test that would catch them breaking:
- `treeDiffFiles` returns null when git fails (an unknown commit), and `[]` for identical trees. `exemptTreeDelta` relies on this, because "an unreadable diff is not exempt" only holds while null is kept separate from `[]`.
- `treeDiffFiles` passes `--no-renames`, so a file moved from `src/` to `docs/` lists both its old and its new path. With git's default rename detection, `git diff --name-only` lists only `docs/x.md`. The plan role checked this in a scratch repo on 2026-10-20. A code-to-docs move would then read as a docs-only, review-exempt delta.
- `treeDiffFiles` and `aheadOfMainFiles` decode git's C-quoted names. Under the default `core.quotePath`, `héllo.md` comes out as `"h\303\251llo.md"` (checked the same way), which is not a real path and does not match a `*.md` exemption.

**Approach.**
1. New test/git-diff-paths.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/git-diff.test.ts. Import `treeDiffFiles` and `aheadOfMainFiles` from ../src/git/git-diff.js, `commitAll` from ../src/git/git.js and `ensureWorktree` from ../src/git/worktree.js. Import `makeRepo`, `seedCommit` and `sh` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js. Use real git throughout, as test/git-diff.test.ts does.
2. Test "treeDiffFiles is null for an unknown commit and empty for identical trees". Use `makeRepo()`. Assert that `await treeDiffFiles(repo, "deadbeef", "HEAD")` is `null`, and that `await treeDiffFiles(repo, "HEAD", "HEAD")` deep-equals `[]`. Mutation: replace `out === null ? null : gitLines(out).map(unquotePorcelainPath)` with `gitLines(out).map(unquotePorcelainPath)`. This type-checks and returns `[]` for the unknown commit.
3. Test "treeDiffFiles lists a moved file under both its old and its new path". Use `makeRepo()` and `seedCommit(repo, "src/x.ts", ...)`, after first creating `src/` with `fs.mkdirSync`, because seedCommit writes the file directly. Then `fs.mkdirSync(docs)` and run `sh(repo, "git", "mv", "src/x.ts", "docs/x.md")` and `sh(repo, "git", "commit", "-m", "move")`. Assert that `(await treeDiffFiles(repo, "HEAD~1", "HEAD"))!.sort()` deep-equals `["docs/x.md", "src/x.ts"]`. Mutation: delete the `"--no-renames"` argument. Git then reports only `docs/x.md`.
4. Test "treeDiffFiles and aheadOfMainFiles decode a non-ASCII name to its real path". Use `makeRepo()` and `const wt = await ensureWorktree(repo, "improve", "main")`. Write `héllo.md` in `wt` and run `commitAll(wt, "add")`. Assert that `await aheadOfMainFiles(wt, "main")` deep-equals `["héllo.md"]`, and that `await treeDiffFiles(wt, "main", "HEAD")` deep-equals `["héllo.md"]`. Mutations: (a) drop `.map(unquotePorcelainPath)` from `aheadOfMainFiles`; (b) drop it from `treeDiffFiles`. Both type-check (`gitLines` returns `string[]`, and `unquotePorcelainPath` stays used elsewhere in the file).
   Run the new file once. Before you write VERIFIED, apply each mutation by hand. Check that it fails its new test and that the test passes again once you revert it. Mutations: (a) replace `Promise.allSettled(inFlight.map((t) => t.promise)).then(() => {})` with `Promise.race(inFlight.map((t) => t.promise))`; (b) replace `inFlight.flatMap((t) => t.roles)` with `inFlight[0]!.roles`. ### docs/invariants.md gains a staging self-check section, and one new test file pins that each git-level finding stops at its cap and says how many it left out (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/stage-path-caps.test.ts)

**Goal.** `gitLevelFindings` (src/run/stage-path-checks.ts) is the git-level half of the pre-commit self-check: `stageCheckFindings` (src/run/stage-check.ts) calls it, and the findings go back to the author's still-open session. Each finding is meant to stay bounded however large the change is. The caps are `MAX_STALE_PATHS` (stale-reference findings per change), `MAX_STALE_HITS` (`file:line` hits per stale reference), `MAX_MISSING_PATHS` and `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES` (all 10). `cappedList` appends `moreSuffix` (src/text/phrases.ts, ` (+N more)`) for what a missing-path or lost-newline finding leaves out. Before this entry, no test in test/stage-check.test.ts makes a change that exceeds any of these caps, and docs/invariants.md named neither stage-path-checks.ts nor `gitLevelFindings`. A regression that dropped a cap would send a 40-file rename's whole reference list into the session's prompt, and none of the tests would notice.

**Approach.**
1. New test/stage-path-caps.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/stage-check.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files. Call `gitLevelFindings(wt, "main")` directly. Use two-digit, zero-padded names (`00`…`11`) so git's path order matches the numeric order and no name is a prefix of another.
2. Test "a missing-path finding names the first ten paths and counts the rest". Base: `src/keep.ts` and `README.md` (`Start.\n`). 3. Test "a lost-final-newline finding names the first ten files and counts the rest". Base: `src/n00.ts` … `src/n10.ts`, each `export const n = 1;\n`. In the worktree, rewrite each without its trailing newline. Assert one finding matching `/removes the final newline from: /`. It contains `src/n09.ts`, does not contain `src/n10.ts`, and ends with ` (+1 more)`. Mutation: `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES = 11`.
4. Test "a change deleting more referenced paths than the cap reports only the cap's worth". ### docs/invariants.md gains a batch-merge section, and one new test file pins that a stack seeds main's baseline only when a full check passed on exactly the merged tip (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/merge-stack-seed.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `mergeStack` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) merges a batch of approved changes. It cherry-picks them onto main's tip, runs ONE scope-`batch` check over the combined tree, and fast-forwards main through the captured shas (`ffStackToMain`). When main moves mid-check, it re-stacks, up to `BATCH_RESTACK_ATTEMPTS` times. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named neither file nor function (`grep -c 'merge-stack\|mergeStack' docs/invariants.md` gave 0). After a merge, `mergeStack` calls `noteGreenBaseline(seed)` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts). That records the tip as green in the cache the main watch and the redeployer read. `seed` is set only when the batch check status is `"passed"` and `mergeCommandOf(ctx.config) === undefined`. A doc-only stack, a stack whose failures are all main's known failures (`onlyKnownMainFailures`), and a `check.mergeCommand` green seed nothing. Before this entry, no test read `cachedBaselineVerdict` after a batch merge: `grep -n cachedBaselineVerdict test/merger-*.test.ts test/merge-stack.test.ts` gave nothing. A regression that seeded a known-red or unchecked tip as green would skip the main watch's check on that tip and go unnoticed.

### docs/invariants.md gains a review-verdict and revision-finality section, and two tests pin that only a leading `(prior N)` with N ≥ 1 is a repeat tag and that a tag with no matching prior count still counts one revision (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md, a comment in src/merge/merge-core.ts + a new test/revision-prior-tags.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** The review gate depends on two things. First, src/review/review-verdict.ts's `parseVerdict` turns the reviewer's reply into a verdict and its reasons. It fails closed when no verdict line exists, and the last VERDICT line wins. It caps the reasons at `MAX_REASONS` and drops a leading prior-objection resolution from a rejection. Second, src/merge/merge-core.ts's `recordRejectedChange` uses `priorObjectionNumber` to decide when a revision chain ends. Each reason gets a persistence count: 0 for an untagged reason, and `1 + prior[n - 1] ?? 0` for a `(prior N)` restatement. The rejection is final when any count reaches `REVISION_FINAL_ON_REPEAT` or the round reaches `REVISION_BACKSTOP` (both in src/runner/revision.ts). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named none of `parseVerdict`, `priorObjectionNumber`, `recordRejectedChange` or the two constants. Two edges are untested:
- No test calls `priorObjectionNumber` directly. Its only coverage is the `(prior 1)` reply in test/revision.test.ts's "a rejection whose objection has survived two revisions is final and deletes the rejected ref". Nothing pins the `^` anchor (a tag mid-line is not a tag), the case-insensitive match, the leading-whitespace trim, or the `n >= 1` guard.
- Two cases are untested: a `(prior N)` tag whose N is beyond the prior list, and a tag with no `priorCounts` at all (a recovery merge, or a first rejection). In both, `prior[n - 1] ?? 0` gives a count of 1. That is not final this round, but one more restatement makes it final. The doc comment on `recordRejectedChange` says such a tag "reads as a fresh objection", which a reader takes to mean count 0. The code gives 1, so the comment is corrected to match the code. The behavior does not change.

**Approach.**
1. New test/revision-prior-tags.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/revision.test.ts or test/review-verdict.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files. Import `priorObjectionNumber` from ../src/review/review-verdict.js. Import `verifyRequest` from ../src/merge/merge-batch.js, `refSha` from ../src/git/git.js, `rejectedRefName` from ../src/paths.js and `freshRunnerState` from ../src/runner/runner-state.js. Import `withPi` from ./fakes/fake-pi.js, and `batchWiring`, `makeCtx`, `pinnedFixture`, `request`, `reviewerPi` and `ROLE` from ./fixtures/merger-fixtures.js. These are the same imports test/revision.test.ts uses.
2. Test "priorObjectionNumber reads only a leading (prior N) tag with N of at least one". `"(prior 3) still wrong"` → 3. `"  (PRIOR 2) still wrong"` → 2 (trimmed, case-insensitive). `"(prior 0) still wrong"` → null. `"prior to the change, x"` → null. `"see (prior 1) above"` → null. `"(prior one) x"` → null. Mutations: drop the `^` from the regex (the mid-line case returns 1); drop `&& n >= 1` (the zero case returns 0).
3. Test "a (prior N) tag beyond the prior list, or with no prior list, counts one revision and is not final". (a) Under `withPi(reviewerPi("VERDICT: reject\n1. (prior 3) a stale number"), …)`, take `pinnedFixture()`, `freshRunnerState(ROLE)`, `makeCtx` and `batchWiring` as the sibling tests do. Call `verifyRequest(ctx, request(sha, { revisionRound: 1, priorReview: { sha, reasons: ["the bug"], counts: [1] } }), w)`. Assert `verdict.kind` is `"result"`, `state.revision?.round` is 2, `state.revision?.reasonCounts` deep-equals `[1]`, `state.lastReview?.exhausted` is undefined, and `refSha(root, rejectedRefName(ROLE))` equals `state.revision?.sha`. (b) Do the same with a fresh fixture and state, the reply `"VERDICT: reject\n1. (prior 1) still wrong"` and `request(sha, { revisionRound: 1 })` (no `priorReview`). Assert the same: round 2, `reasonCounts` `[1]`, not exhausted. Mutation: in `recordRejectedChange`, change `prior[n - 1] ?? 0` to `prior[n - 1] ?? 1`. Both cases then reach count 2 and go final (`state.revision` undefined).
   Run the new file once. Before you write VERIFIED, check by hand that each named mutation fails its new test and that the test passes again once the mutation is reverted. Tests compile through tsc first, so a mutation must type-check. Also run test/revision.test.ts and test/review-verdict.test.ts under each mutation. If one fails there too, drop any claim that only the new tests catch it.
4. src/merge/merge-core.ts, comments only. In `recordRejectedChange`'s doc comment, replace "a `(prior N)` tag then reads as a fresh objection" with wording that matches the code: the tag counts as having survived one revision (count 1), so it is not final that round. Make the same correction to the inline comment's "An out-of-range or missing tag (a stale prior list, no prior round) reads as a fresh objection". Change no code.
5. docs/invariants.md: append "## Review verdict and revision finality: a reply without a verdict never approves, and a rejected change revises until one objection survives two revisions or the backstop" at the end, after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BD (disk hold) had merged, and BE (backlog index), BF (merge strikes) and BG (team hold) were planned, so BH was free. Take the letter pair after the highest one taken or planned. Reread each test before you cite it. Guarantees:
   - 1: a reply with no VERDICT line at line start is no verdict, and the gate fails closed on it, never approving. When a reply carries several verdict lines, the last one wins. Binds `parseVerdict`. Pinned by "parseVerdict returns null when no verdict line exists", "parseVerdict ignores a VERDICT mention that is not at line start", "parseVerdict reads the verdict from the LAST verdict line" (review-verdict.test.ts) and "gate fails closed on a verdict-less reply: commit kept for re-review" (review.test.ts).
   - 2: at most `MAX_REASONS` reasons are recorded, each clipped to the shared per-line cap. A rejection drops only leading lines that state prior objections resolved and carry no outstanding signal. Binds `parseVerdict`. Pinned by "parseVerdict caps recorded reasons at ten", "parseVerdict clips an over-long reason to the shared per-line cap", "a leading prior-objection resolution is not recorded as a rejection's first reason", "a line mixing a resolution with an open objection is kept whole".
   - 3: a repeat tag is exactly a leading `(prior N)`, case-insensitive, with integer N ≥ 1. Anything else is an untagged reason. Binds `priorObjectionNumber`. Pinned by the step-2 test.
   - 4: an untagged reason counts 0, and a tagged one counts 1 plus the prior round's count for objection N, taking that count as 0 when the prior list has no entry N. The rejection is final, with the ref deleted and `exhausted` set, when any count reaches `REVISION_FINAL_ON_REPEAT` or the round reaches `REVISION_BACKSTOP`. Otherwise the ref points at the judged head and the round advances. The director never revises. Binds `recordRejectedChange`, `REVISION_FINAL_ON_REPEAT`, `REVISION_BACKSTOP`. Pinned by "a gate rejection points the rejected ref at the judged head and records round 1", "a rejection whose objection has survived two revisions is final and deletes the rejected ref", "a converging chain whose revisions raise only new objections keeps revising", "a chain whose objections never repeat ends at the backstop", "the director never gets a revision: a rejection leaves no revision state" (revision.test.ts) and the step-3 test.

### docs/invariants.md gains a flake-quarantine section, and three tests pin that a list at the parser's cap is never quarantined nor counted as only-quarantined, that the store keeps the 100 most recently seen tests and reads malformed entries as defaults, and that a missing BUGS.md releases nothing (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md, src/review/known-flakes.ts (one `export`) + a new test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** src/review/known-flakes.ts keeps the flake quarantine in `.tumwater/state/quarantine.json` (`quarantinePath`). `quarantineTests` adds a test that failed and then passed on the same tree. `onlyQuarantined` returns the failing tests when every one is quarantined. `markQuarantineFiled` and `releaseQuarantine` take a test out once its BUGS.md entry leaves `## Open`. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named none of these functions (`grep -c known-flakes docs/invariants.md` gave 0, and no heading mentions quarantine). test/known-flakes.test.ts covers the basic add/repeat/release path, but these edges have no direct test:
- The `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` guard (src/build/build-check-report.ts) in both `quarantineTests` and `onlyQuarantined`. A list of that length may have been cut short, so it is neither recorded nor counted as only-quarantined. test/main-watch.test.ts's "a failing list at the parser's cap is never counted as only known failures" pins the same guard in main-watch's own `onlyKnownMainFailures`, not in `onlyQuarantined`. `onlyQuarantined` is called from src/baseline/main-watch.ts and src/baseline/main-culprit.ts.
- `saveQuarantine` keeps the `QUARANTINE_MAX` (100) entries with the newest `lastSeen` and drops the rest.
- `loadQuarantine` reads a malformed file as an empty list. It skips an entry without a string `test`, defaults a missing or zero `count` to 1, and defaults a non-string `bug` to `""`. `quarantineTests` counts a test named twice in one call once.
- `releaseQuarantine` releases nothing when BUGS.md is missing, even for a filed test.

**Approach.**
1. src/review/known-flakes.ts: export `QUARANTINE_MAX` so the test does not repeat the literal. Change nothing else.
2. New test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/known-flakes.test.ts. Import `tmpdir` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, `quarantinePath` from ../src/paths.js, `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` from ../src/build/build-check-report.js, and from ../src/review/known-flakes.js import `QUARANTINE_MAX`, `loadQuarantine`, `quarantinedTests`, `quarantineTests`, `onlyQuarantined`, `markQuarantineFiled` and `releaseQuarantine`. Write a fixture file with `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(quarantinePath(root)), { recursive: true })` and then `fs.writeFileSync`.
3. Test "quarantine: a failing list at the parser's cap is neither quarantined nor counted as only quarantined". Let `names` be `t0`…`t${FAILING_TESTS_MAX - 1}`. Assert `quarantineTests(root, names, "out")` deep-equals `[]`, `quarantinedTests(root)` deep-equals `[]` and `fs.existsSync(quarantinePath(root))` is false. Then call `quarantineTests(root, names.slice(0, -1), "out")` and `quarantineTests(root, names.slice(-1), "out")`, so that every name is listed. Assert `onlyQuarantined(root, names.slice(0, -1))?.length` is `FAILING_TESTS_MAX - 1` and `onlyQuarantined(root, names)` is null. Mutations: drop `|| tests.length >= FAILING_TESTS_MAX` from `quarantineTests` (the first call returns every name); drop `|| failingTests.length >= FAILING_TESTS_MAX` from `onlyQuarantined` (the last assertion gets the list).
4. Test "quarantine: the store keeps the most recently seen tests, reads malformed entries as defaults, and counts a name once per call". (a) Write `{ tests: [...] }` with `QUARANTINE_MAX` entries `{ test: "q" + i, firstSeen: i, lastSeen: i, count: 1, bug: "" }` for i = 1…QUARANTINE_MAX. Call `quarantineTests(root, ["new"], "")`. Assert `loadQuarantine(root).length` is `QUARANTINE_MAX`, `quarantinedTests(root)` includes `"new"` and `"q2"` but not `"q1"`, and the `"new"` entry has no `tail` key (empty output keeps none). Mutations: drop `.slice(0, QUARANTINE_MAX)` (length QUARANTINE_MAX + 1); sort ascending (`a.lastSeen - b.lastSeen`, which drops `"new"`). (b) In a fresh root, write `{ tests: [{ test: "a", count: 0 }, { test: 5 }, "x", { test: "b", bug: 3, firstSeen: "y" }] }`. Assert `loadQuarantine` deep-equals `[{ test: "a", firstSeen: 0, lastSeen: 0, count: 1, bug: "" }, { test: "b", firstSeen: 0, lastSeen: 0, count: 1, bug: "" }]`. Then write `not json` and assert `loadQuarantine` deep-equals `[]`. Mutation: `count: num(e.count) || 1` → `count: num(e.count)`. (c) In a fresh root, call `quarantineTests(root, ["d", "d"], ["l1", "l2"])`, which returns `["d"]`. Assert the entry's `count` is 1 and its `tail` is `"l1\nl2"`. ### docs/invariants.md gains a team-hold section, and two tests pin that the first provider+kind to storm in a poll wins and that a failure stamped at the re-open poll never re-trips the hold (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/team-hold-edges.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** src/team/team-hold.ts holds the team's backend-failure policy. `teamHold` steps one provider's `TeamHold` per poll. Two distinct roles (`HOLD_STORM_ROLES`) failing on the same provider and kind within `HOLD_STORM_WINDOW_MS` trip a hold. The hold lasts `HOLD_BASE_MS`, doubles on a same-provider, same-kind relapse within `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS`, honors a 429's Retry-After, and is capped at `HOLD_CAP_MS`. It re-opens by itself at its deadline. A rejected subscription window holds its provider until `resetsAt`. `heldProviders`, `standingHolds` and `windowHeldProviders` read the map. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name the module, `teamHold` or any `HOLD_*` constant (`grep -n -i 'team hold\|teamHold\|storm' docs/invariants.md` printed nothing). test/team-hold.test.ts covers most clauses. Two clauses of `teamHold` have no test:
- Pick order. The doc comment says "the first qualifying kind in observation order wins", which the `break` in the `byProviderKind` loop implements. "two roles on the same backend kind storm even while others fail differently" has only one kind with two roles behind it, so it would still pass if the loop kept the last qualifying group.
- The strict re-open boundary. `o.at > prev.reopenedAt` drops a failure stamped at or before the re-open. "a held team stays held until its deadline, then re-opens by itself" only feeds failures from before the deadline, so it would still pass under `>=`.

This plan adds both tests in a new file, then a section that cites them and the existing tests. No change to src/.

**Approach.**
1. New test/team-hold-edges.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Import `TEAM_OPEN`, `teamHold`, `HOLD_BASE_MS` and the `HoldKind`/`HoldObservation` types from ../src/team/team-hold.js. Define the same small `obs(role, at, kind)` helper test/team-hold.test.ts uses. Do not edit test/team-hold.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files.
2. Test "when two provider+kind groups both storm in one poll, the first one seen wins": at T0, observations `obs("dedupe", T0, "connection")`, `obs("perf", T0, "server")`, `obs("qa", T0, "connection")`, `obs("readme", T0, "server")`. Assert `kind` is `"connection"`, `roles` deep-equals `["dedupe", "qa"]`, and `until` is `T0 + HOLD_BASE_MS`. Then `obs("perf", T0, "server")`, `obs("dedupe", T0, "connection")`, `obs("readme", T0, "server")`, `obs("qa", T0, "connection")` (the server pair seen first) yields `kind` `"server"` and `roles` `["perf", "readme"]`. Mutation: delete the `break;` in `teamHold`'s `for (const entry of byProviderKind.values())` loop. The first assertion then sees `"server"`.
3. Test "a failure stamped at the re-open poll never re-trips the hold; one a millisecond later does": `held = teamHold(TEAM_OPEN, [obs("bugfix", T0), obs("coverage", T0)], T0)`, `U = held.until!`. `reopened = teamHold(held, [obs("perf", U), obs("steward", U)], U)` has `until` null and `reopenedAt` `U`. Then `teamHold(reopened, [obs("perf", U + 1), obs("steward", U + 1)], U + 1)` trips with `escalation` 1 and `until` `U + 1 + 2 * HOLD_BASE_MS` (a same-kind relapse inside `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS`). Mutation: change `o.at > prev.reopenedAt` to `o.at >= prev.reopenedAt`. The first poll then holds again.
   Run the file once. Before you write VERIFIED, check by hand that each named mutation fails its new test and that the test passes again once the mutation is reverted. Tests compile through tsc first, so a mutation must type-check. Also run test/team-hold.test.ts and test/team-polls.test.ts under each mutation. If a mutation fails a test there too, drop any claim that only the new tests catch it.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## Team hold: two roles failing alike on one provider hold that provider, and the hold re-opens by itself" at the end, after the last section. For the INV prefix, check `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BD (disk hold) had merged and BE (backlog index) and BF (merge strikes) were planned, so BG was free. Take the letter pair after the highest one taken or planned. Reread each test before you cite it. Guarantees:
   - 1: a hold trips only when `HOLD_STORM_ROLES` distinct roles failed on the same provider and kind within `HOLD_STORM_WINDOW_MS` (the edge counts). One role never trips it, and different kinds or providers never add up. When two groups qualify in one poll, the first one seen wins. Binds `teamHold`, `HOLD_STORM_WINDOW_MS`. Pinned by "one role's 429s never trip the hold — the per-run retry already answers them", "two distinct roles' 429s within the window trip a base hold naming them", "429s further apart than the storm window do not add up", "failures of different kinds are different incidents: neither storms alone", "pollTeamHold separates the same kind at different providers: no cross-provider storm" (team-polls.test.ts), and the step-2 test.
   - 2: the hold lasts the longer of `HOLD_BASE_MS` doubled once per relapse and the furthest Retry-After, measured from its own 429, and never more than `HOLD_CAP_MS`. A relapse is the same provider and kind re-tripping within `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS` of the re-open; anything else starts at the base. Binds `HOLD_BASE_MS`, `HOLD_RELAPSE_MS`, `HOLD_CAP_MS`. Pinned by "the hold honors the largest Retry-After seen, measured from its own 429, and caps it", "backend failures of one kind trip the same hold, but carry no Retry-After", "a storm that resumes right after re-open doubles the hold; one after a calm spell starts fresh", "a relapse is per kind: the same kind escalates, a different kind starts at the base" and "a storm that outlasts every re-open escalates to the cap and stays there".
   - 3: a held provider stays held until its deadline and then re-opens by itself. No failure stamped at or before the re-open counts toward the next storm. A lifted hold stays in the map as relapse memory, but `heldProviders` does not read it as held. Binds `teamHold`, `heldProviders`. Pinned by "a held team stays held until its deadline, then re-opens by itself", the step-3 test, and "a lifted provider's hold stays in the map with its relapse memory but stops reading as held" (team-polls.test.ts).
   - 4: a rejected subscription window holds its provider until `resetsAt`, however many roles failed, and a window with no future `resetsAt` holds nothing. A reserve hold is re-checked every poll, and the director is held only by a rejected window (`windowHeldProviders`). `standingHolds` lists neither lifted nor subscription-window holds. Binds `windowHeldProviders`, `standingHolds`. Pinned by "a rejected subscription window holds its provider until resetsAt, whatever the role count", "a standing reserve hold is re-evaluated: a rejected window replaces it, a vanished one drops it", "standingHolds names each standing provider hold and skips lifted and subscription-window ones", "a subscription-window hold stops the director too, while a 429-storm hold still exempts it" (orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts) and "a reserve crossing holds claude but not the director, and logs claude_window_reserved once per window" (team-polls.test.ts).

### docs/invariants.md gains a merge-strikes section, and two tests pin that an unreadable patch-id never counts as a strike and that an old strike on another patch does not add to a new one (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/merge-check-strikes.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts decides when a merge that keeps failing is blamed on the change. `tallyCheckFailure` counts strikes on `RunnerState.mergeCheckFailures`, keyed by patch-id. `pinKept` keeps the pin while the count is under `MERGE_CHECK_FAILURE_LIMIT` (2). At the limit, `mergeCheckRed` hands the change to `attributeRedCheck` and `mergeBlocked` hands it to `rejectChange`. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name the module, `MERGE_CHECK_FAILURE_LIMIT`, `mergeBlocked` or `attributeRedCheck` (a `grep -n` printed nothing). test/merger.test.ts covers the limit for one patch: "a single merge's red in-lock check retries once, then …" and "a fix-claim-blocked merge retries once, then rejects with the block reason". test/attribute-red-check.test.ts covers `attributeRedCheck`. Two branches of `tallyCheckFailure` have no test:
- An unreadable patch-id. `patchId` (src/git/git.ts) returns null for an empty `main...head` diff. The doc comment says such a pin is never counted, so no stored strike can ever reach the limit, and it is never wrongly blamed. Nothing tests that this pin stays kept on every attempt and leaves no strike stored.
- An old strike on another patch. `prior?.patchId === patch` makes a different change start counting from 1 ("a different change starts fresh"). The one test that seeds a strike on another pin, "a stale red strike of another pin is not recorded as a flake when a different pin merges", merges green and never reaches the tally.

This plan adds both tests in a new file, then a section that cites them and the existing tests. No change to src/.

**Approach.**
1. New test/merge-check-strikes.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). It calls `mergeBlocked` from ../src/merge/merge-check-failures.js directly with `makeCtx`, `pinnedFixture`, `ROLE` and `REF` from ./fixtures/merger-fixtures.js, `freshRunnerState` from ../src/runner/runner-state.js, `refSha` from ../src/git/git.js, `sh` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, and `eventsOfType` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js (check that helper's signature before using it). `mergeBlocked` runs no model and no check, so neither test needs a pi shim. Do not edit test/merger.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch it.
2. Test "mergeBlocked keeps a pin whose patch-id cannot be read on every attempt and stores no strike": `pinnedFixture()` leaves the role worktree `wt` clean at main, so `patchId(wt, "main", HEAD)` sees an empty diff and returns null. Call `mergeBlocked(ctx, ROLE, wt, "the block")` three times. Each call returns `"merge_blocked"`, `state.mergeCheckFailures` stays `undefined`, `state.lastError` matches `/merge_blocked — the block/`, `refSha(root, REF)` is still the pinned sha, and no `review_rejected` event is logged. Mutation: in `tallyCheckFailure`, replace `patch === null ? undefined : { patchId: patch, count }` with `{ patchId: patch ?? "unreadable", count }`. This type-checks, and the strike assertion fails.
3. Test "mergeBlocked starts a new patch's count at one when the stored strike belongs to another patch": take `pinnedFixture()`, then `sh(wt, "git", "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", sha)` so that `wt`'s head carries the pinned change and its patch-id is readable. Seed `state.mergeCheckFailures = { patchId: "another-pin", count: 1 }`. The first `mergeBlocked` call returns `"merge_blocked"` and leaves `state.mergeCheckFailures` with `count` 1 and a `patchId` other than `"another-pin"`. The ref is still there. The second call returns `"rejected"`, `refSha(root, REF)` is null, `state.mergeCheckFailures` is `undefined`, `state.lastReview?.verdict` is `"reject"`, and `state.lastReview!.reasons[0]` is `"merge blocked: the block"`. Mutation: in `tallyCheckFailure`, replace `patch !== null && prior?.patchId === patch ? prior.count : 0` with `prior ? prior.count : 0`. The first call then returns `"rejected"`.
   Run the file once. Before you write VERIFIED, check by hand that each named mutation fails its new test and that the test passes again once the mutation is reverted. Guarantees:
   - 1: one patch's red in-lock check, or its deterministic cross-check block, keeps the pin (`merge_blocked`) under `MERGE_CHECK_FAILURE_LIMIT`. ### docs/invariants.md gains a backlog-index section, and two tests pin that the newest closed entries spill from the live section into its archive file and that a long heading is clipped to 160 characters (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/backlog-index-edges.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `renderBacklogIndexBlock` (src/backlog/backlog-index.ts) builds the `<backlog-index>` block in every role's prompt (called from src/run/run-prompt.ts). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name the module (`grep -c backlog-index docs/invariants.md` printed 0). test/backlog-structure.test.ts has tests for it, all named "renderBacklogIndexBlock …", but none puts an archive file in the fixture root (`grep -c PLANS-DONE test/backlog-structure.test.ts` matches only the stranded-heading and `backlogStructureReason` tests), and none renders a heading longer than `INDEX_TITLE_MAX`. So two behaviors are unpinned, although the archive path is the one this repository uses on every run (its PLANS.md `## Done` is empty and the closed lines come from PLANS-DONE.md):
- `CLOSED_SECTIONS` reads the live file's closed section first, then its archive (`FINISHED_ARCHIVES` in src/backlog/backlog-md.ts), and lists at most `RECENT_CLOSED_MAX` (5) in total across the two through the `room` counter. Changing `files: [a.file, a.archive]` to `files: [a.file]` drops every archive line. Replacing `?.slice(0, room)` with `?.slice(0, RECENT_CLOSED_MAX)` lists up to ten per kind. As far as a grep shows, no test fails on either change.
- `indexTitle` clips a title to `INDEX_TITLE_MAX` (160) characters through `truncate` (src/text/text.ts), which ends the clipped title with `…`. Raising the constant to 1000 changes no test result.

### docs/invariants.md gains a maintenance-allowance section, and two tests pin that the in-flight figure skips disabled and work roles while counting a legacy-id merge, and that a vanished or replaced events log keeps the window's counted merges (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/maintenance-quota-gate.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `src/gates/maintenance-quota.ts` caps code-maintenance merges in a rolling 24 h window (`maintenanceQuota`, `pollMaintenanceQuotaGate`, `countMaintenanceWindow`). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name the module (`grep -c maintenance-quota docs/invariants.md` printed 0). test/maintenance-quota.test.ts covers the verdict arithmetic, the incremental fold, rotation, torn lines and the hold/resume transitions, but these branches fail no test when broken:
- The `!o.enabled` skip in `pollMaintenanceQuotaGate`. The only disabled observer in the suite (`clean-2` in "pollMaintenanceQuotaGate computes the allowance verdict and logs one hold per transition") is neither running nor holding a queued merge, so deleting `if (!o.enabled) continue;` changes no result.
- The tier filter on in-flight roles. No test has a running work role (feature) beside a maintenance one, so deleting the `commitTier(...) !== "maintenance"` skip only fails if a work observer is in flight — none is.
- A merged event under a legacy role id (`dry`, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts) counts on the maintenance side only because `parseEventLine` normalizes `source` through `normalizeLegacyEvent` (src/events/event-legacy.ts) before `tierOfEvent` calls `commitTier`; no maintenance-quota test writes a `dry` merge.
- The `!counter.seeded` clause in `countMaintenanceWindow`'s `else if (stat === null && !counter.seeded)`. When the events log disappears after a first count, the memo's records keep counting. Dropping the clause reseeds an empty window and the count falls to zero; no test deletes the log after a count ("a missing events log counts zero and seeds an empty memo" only starts without one). A directory in the log's place likewise folds nothing and must not throw.

This plan adds the tests in a new file, then the section that cites them. No change to src/.

**Approach.**
1. New test/maintenance-quota-gate.test.ts. Reuse the imports test/maintenance-quota.test.ts uses (`writeEvents` from test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts, `tmpdir` from test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts, `HOUR` from test/helpers/oracles.ts, `eventsLogPath` from src/paths.ts). Event fixtures use the `loop` field with the trailing `// retired-name-ok: legacy event field in a fixture` comment, as that file does. Do not edit test/maintenance-quota.test.ts.
2. Test "the in-flight figure skips disabled and work roles, and a legacy dry merge counts as maintenance". Events: one `{ ts: now - HOUR, loop: "dry", type: "merged", commit: "d" }`. Observers: `{ role: "clean-2", enabled: true, running: true, hasQueuedMerge: false }`, `{ role: "dedupe", enabled: false, running: true, hasQueuedMerge: true }`, `{ role: "feature", enabled: true, running: true, hasQueuedMerge: false }`. `pollMaintenanceQuotaGate(root, newMaintenanceQuotaGateState(), observers, 2, now)` deep-equals `{ allowance: 12, used: 2, held: false }` (1 merged maintenance + the enabled `clean` role; `clean-2` is not a runner id, so the test uses bare `clean`). Mutations: delete `if (!o.enabled) continue;` gives used 3; delete the `commitTier(baseRoleOf(o.role)) !== "maintenance"` skip gives used 3. Before writing the expected value, confirm `countMaintenanceWindow` on that log returns `{ work: 0, maint: 1 }`; if the `dry` merge counts as neither, stop and file it in BUGS.md instead of pinning it.
3. Test "a vanished or replaced events log keeps the window's counted merges and does not throw". Write one `{ ts: now - HOUR, loop: "clean", type: "merged", commit: "a" }`; with one `newMaintenanceWindowCounter()`, `countMaintenanceWindow(root, counter, now)` is `{ work: 0, maint: 1 }`. `fs.rmSync(eventsLogPath(root))`; the next count is still `{ work: 0, maint: 1 }`. Mutation: change `stat === null && !counter.seeded` to `stat === null` gives `{ work: 0, maint: 0 }`. Then `fs.mkdirSync(eventsLogPath(root))`; the next count does not throw and is still `{ work: 0, maint: 1 }`. Do not recreate the log as a file afterwards: an inode reused by the new file would make the fold read from the old offset and the result would depend on the filesystem.
   Run each case once and confirm each named mutation flips it before writing VERIFIED.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## Maintenance allowance: maintenance merges stop at the rolling-day allowance, counted from the event log" at the end. Take the next free INV prefix: check `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, AX (false-fix gate) was the highest merged, AY (backlog conflicts) and AZ (red-main healer) were planned, so BA was free. Take the letter pair after the highest one taken or planned. Guarantees (cite only tests in test/maintenance-quota.test.ts, test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts and the new file; reread each before citing it):
   - 1: the allowance is `maintenancePerWorkMerge × work merges + MAINTENANCE_DAILY_FLOOR` over the trailing 24 h, and the gate holds while merged maintenance plus enabled maintenance roles in flight reach it. Binds `maintenanceQuota`, `pollMaintenanceQuotaGate`. Pinned by "maintenanceQuota computes the allowance, used, and held verdict", "the floor keeps the allowance at 12 when no work merged", "a run in progress and a queued merge both count as in flight toward the used figure" and the step-2 test.
   - 2: the window counts `merged` events by tier (legacy ids under their canonical role), folds only appended complete lines, reseeds after rotation, and a missing, vanished or non-file log never throws and never drops counted merges. Binds `countMaintenanceWindow`. Pinned by "countMaintenanceWindow counts merged events by tier inside the last 24 h", "a rotated log is reseeded from the live file and its archive, not folded from the old offset", "a torn trailing merged line is counted once, not again when its newline arrives", "a missing events log counts zero and seeds an empty memo" and the step-3 test.
   - 3: the gate logs one `maintenance_quota_hold` per open-to-held transition and one `maintenance_quota_resumed` per re-open, and the scheduler spends the headroom one maintenance role at a time. Pinned by "pollMaintenanceQuotaGate computes the allowance verdict and logs one hold per transition" and "the allowance's in-flight headroom starts at most one of two due maintenance roles per poll".

### docs/invariants.md gains a red-main healer section, and two tests pin that a failing set returning after a green main is healed again, order-blind, and that the culprit heal prompt drops the clauses it has nothing for (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/main-red-heal.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `src/baseline/main-red.ts` decides when a red main pages the team (`main_red_hold`, once per SHA through `lastMainRedSha`) and when it queues a heal prompt for bugfix (once per failing set through `lastHealKey`). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name the module (`grep -c main-red docs/invariants.md` printed 0). test/main-red.test.ts covers the once-per-SHA warning, the same-set dedup across two red commits, and bugfix's own red queueing nothing. Three branches fail no test when broken:
- Green clears the heal key. `mainRedGate` sets `lastHealKey = null` on a green baseline (as does `bugfixMainRedNote`), so a failing set that comes back after main went green queues a fresh heal prompt. No test runs red → green → red. Deleting the clear in `mainRedGate` fails no test.
- The heal key is order-blind. `warnMainRedOnce` keys on `[...named].sort().join("\n")`. `parseFailingTests` (src/build/build-check-report.ts) keeps output order, so the same set printed in another order on the next red commit would queue a second prompt without the sort. Dropping `.sort()` fails no test.
- The culprit prompt's optional clauses. `mainRedHealPrompt(sha, detail)` adds ` Failing: …` only when `detail.failingTests` is non-empty and ` Output tail: … | …` only when a tail is given. test/main-revert.test.ts "a revert that conflicts leaves main alone and queues the heal prompt naming the culprit" checks only the culprit's short SHA and a test name. The orchestrator's `queueCulpritHeal` call passes no tail, and a culprit can carry no failing tests. Dropping the `failingTests.length > 0` guard (the prompt then reads `Failing: .`) fails no test.

This plan adds the tests in a new file, then the section that cites them. No change to src/.

**Approach.**
1. New test/main-red-heal.test.ts (a new file, so its module-level `lastHealKey`/`lastMainRedSha` start fresh in their own process). Reuse `baselineFixture`, `fakeNpm` (test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts), `mainRedHolds` (test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts), `queuedRolePrompts` (src/inbox/inbox.ts), `sh`, `tmpdir` (test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts), `shortSha` (src/text/format.ts), as test/main-red.test.ts does. Do not edit test/main-red.test.ts.
2. Test "a failing set queues one heal prompt in any order, and queues another after main turns green". Role `coverage` (a blocked role, as in main-red.test.ts). The npm script reads two flag files under a `tmpdir()` outside the repo: if `green` exists, `exit 0`; else if `swap` exists, print `✖ heal-beta (1ms)` then `✖ heal-alpha (1ms)`, otherwise alpha then beta; then `exit 1`. Pass `() => {}` as `onKnownRed`. Between steps, make a new main commit that changes a tracked code file (write a counter into `index.js`, `git add`, `git commit`), then `sh(wt, "git", "reset", "--hard", "main")`. An empty or doc-only commit after a green can inherit that green (`inheritedGreen`, src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) and never run the check.
   - Red (alpha, beta): `queuedRolePrompts(root, "bugfix").length` is 1.

**Goal.** `src/verdict/fix-claim.ts` is the only check on an md-only diff that moves a bug to Fixed: `falseFixReason` rejects a Fixed entry, or a one-line record, whose Fix paragraph names code that exists nowhere on the tree. `fixedEntriesAt` feeds the doctor's newest-Fixed checks in src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts. - `fixedEntriesAt` order and input. It returns BUGS.md's Fixed entries (from the `bugsMd` text when given) and then BUGS-FIXED.md's, newest first. The doctor keeps the first `FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED`, so swapping the order, or ignoring `bugsMd`, changes which records the doctor checks, and no test notices.

### docs/invariants.md gains a worktree-reclaim section, and two tests pin that a pass reports freed space clamped at zero and that reclaimWorktree refuses an in-use worktree without deleting (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/reclaim-guards.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `src/team/reclaim.ts` deletes the gitignored files in idle harness worktrees (`git clean -fdX`) when the disk runs low, when a worktree goes idle, and on `tumwater reclaim`. It is the only code in the harness that deletes files across every role's worktree. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name reclaim.ts (`grep -c reclaim.ts docs/invariants.md` printed 0), and no `## ` section heading there mentions disk or reclaim. test/reclaim.test.ts covers it well, but two rules have no test:
- Freed space. `reclaimPass` reports `freedGB` as `max(0, after - before)` and `freeGB` as the last sample, and logs both in `disk_reclaim`. No test in test/reclaim.test.ts reads `freedGB` (`grep -n freedGB test/reclaim.test.ts` printed nothing before this entry). Dropping the `Math.max(0, …)` clamp fails no test, and then a pass during which another writer used up space reports a negative "freed" figure in the event, in `ReclaimController.lastReclaim` and in the disk status.
- In-use refusal. `reclaimWorktree` returns false without cleaning when `claimForReclaim` refuses (the worktree is in use by a run). The existing test that uses `beginWorktreeUse` covers only `reclaimCandidates` leaving an in-use worktree out of the list. If the `if (!claimForReclaim(resolved)) return false;` guard were removed, no test would fail, and a direct call (the `candidates` a caller passes in, or a list that went stale while the pass ran) would delete a running role's `node_modules/` or `dist/` mid-build.

This plan adds both tests in a new file, then the section that cites them. No change to src/.

Use it instead of importing test/reclaim.test.ts's unexported `seedWorktree`.

### docs/invariants.md gains a pause-marker section, and two tests pin that a paused-roles marker naming a legacy id pauses and resumes the canonical role, and that an empty role set carries no deadline (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/team-state-pause-read.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `src/team/team-state.ts` holds both operator pause markers (the team marker `pauseTeam`/`resumeTeam` and the per-role set `pauseRole`/`resumeRole`) and every read side the scheduler (`pollPauseGates`, src/gates/pause-gates.ts), the dashboards and the CLI share. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named team-state.ts once, for the scheduled stop only (`scheduleStop`, `scheduledStopAt`, `cancelScheduledStop`); no section states the pause guarantees. test/team-state.test.ts covers the writers, expiry, reasons and the cross-process lock well. Two read-side rules in `readPausedRoles`/`standingRolePause` have no test (`grep -n '"dry"\|"telemetry"\|standingRolePause' test/*.ts` printed no pause test before this entry):
- Legacy ids. `readPausedRoles` maps each stored id through `canonicalRoleId` (src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts: `dry` → `dedupe`, `telemetry` → `selfcheck`), so a marker written before a rename still pauses the renamed role, and `pauseRole`/`resumeRole` see it. ### docs/invariants.md gains a detached process-group runner section, and three tests pin runScriptGroup's per-stream output cap, its spawn-failure result, and groupAlive's EPERM branch (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry: no waiting entry edits src/process/process-group.ts or test/process-group.test.ts (checked with `grep -n 'process-group' PLANS.md`, which, before this entry, matched nothing). **Goal.** `src/process/process-group.ts` owns the detached process-group runner (`runScriptGroup`) behind the build check and the lockfile install, plus the group-wide deadline (`armGroupDeadline`, `groupAlive`, `KILL_GRACE_MS`, `GROUP_POLL_MS`) that git-run's `execGitBounded` also uses. docs/invariants.md does not mention the module (`grep -c 'process-group\|runScriptGroup\|armGroupDeadline' docs/invariants.md` gave 0 on 2026-10-20). The deadline behaviour is tested end to end in test/build-check-process.test.ts and test/build-check.test.ts. Three of the runner's own guarantees have no direct test. First, each stream stops accumulating once it reaches `maxBuffer`. The only test passing `maxBuffer` uses 1 MiB with a few bytes of output. Second, a command missing from PATH resolves with `spawnError` set, not with the `close` event's code. Node fires `error` (ENOENT) and then `close` with code -2, checked on 2026-10-20 with a scratch `spawn("no-such-cmd-xyz")`. Third, `groupAlive` counts EPERM as a member still existing. test/build-check-process.test.ts defines its own local `groupAlive` and never calls the exported one.

**Approach.**
- test/process-group.test.ts: import `groupAlive` too, and add three tests at the end of the file:
  1. "runScriptGroup caps each stream at maxBuffer, dropping later chunks". Run `sh -c 'printf a; printf x >&2; sleep 0.3; printf b; printf y >&2'` with `maxBuffer: 1`, `timeoutMs: 30_000`, `killGraceMs: 1_000`. The sleep makes `a` and `b` arrive as separate chunks (Node delivered them as `["a","b"]` in the same scratch check). Assert `code === 0`, `stdout === "a"`, `stderr === "x"`. Mutation check: remove the `if (stdoutSize < opts.maxBuffer)` guard on the stdout handler; stdout then reads `ab` and the test must fail.
  2. "runScriptGroup reports a command missing from PATH as spawnError, never a code, and resolves". Run `tumwater-no-such-command-xyz` with no args and the same options. Assert `r.spawnError?.code === "ENOENT"`, `r.code === undefined`, `r.timedOut === false`. Mutation check: in the `child.on("error", …)` handler, drop the `finish({ spawnError: err })` call; the run then settles from `close` with code -2 and no spawnError, so the test must fail.
  3. "groupAlive: no pid is no group, EPERM is a live member, any other error is gone". Use `t.mock.method(process, "kill", …)` (node:test restores it when the test ends). Assert `groupAlive(undefined) === false` and that the mock saw no call for it. Then assert true when kill returns normally, true when it throws an error with `code: "EPERM"`, and false when it throws `code: "ESRCH"`. Also assert the mock received `-pid` and signal `0`. Mutation check: change the catch to `return false`; the EPERM case must fail.
  Check each mutation by hand, then revert it.

**Goal.** `src/process/launch-services.ts` owns the launchservicesd Mach-port facts: the thresholds, the warning text, and the warn-once-per-step rule (`nextLaunchServicesWarning`). Two behaviours of `LaunchServicesWatch.poll` have no test. First, a `null` sample (count unreadable) returns before `this.lastWarned` is touched, so an unreadable sample in the middle of an episode neither ends it nor warns. The only null test, "the watch never overlaps samples and stays quiet on an unreadable count", feeds null as the first sample, where `lastWarned` is already null, so it cannot tell "kept" from "reset". **Approach.**
- test/launch-services.test.ts: add two tests at the end of the file. They use only what the file already has (`portsProbe`, `LaunchServicesWatch`, `LAUNCH_SERVICES_SAMPLE_MS`, `launchServicesWarning`, `harnessWarnings`, `tmpdir`).   1. "an unreadable sample mid-episode neither warns nor ends the episode". `portsProbe(120_000, null, 125_000, 170_000)`, four polls. Assert `probe.reads === 4` and warnings deep-equal `[launchServicesWarning(120_000), launchServicesWarning(170_000)]`. Mutation check: change `if (ports === null) return;` in `poll` to also set `this.lastWarned = null`; 125k then warns and the test must fail.
  2. "the watch re-arms once the count drops under the threshold, warning on the next climb past it". `portsProbe(120_000, 90_000, 110_000)`, three polls. Assert warnings deep-equal `[launchServicesWarning(120_000), launchServicesWarning(110_000)]`; 110k is within a step of 120k, so only the re-arm makes it warn. Mutation check: change `this.lastWarned = next.lastWarned;` to `this.lastWarned = next.lastWarned ?? this.lastWarned;`; 110k then stays quiet and the test must fail.
  Check each mutation by hand, then revert it.

Its failure contracts differ per method, and they matter. `cwds` must reject when no lookup could run, because a silent empty map would read as "no orphans". `runMarkers` and `launchServicesPorts` must never reject, so a dead reader cannot turn doctor red. docs/invariants.md does not mention the module yet (`grep -c process-table docs/invariants.md` gave 0 on 2026-10-20). Two behaviours have no test. First, `parseLsofCwds` drops an `n` line whose opening `p` line was not a number (`Number.isInteger(pid)`), and no test feeds it one. Second, `cwds` and `runMarkers` return an empty map at once for an empty pid list. Only `runMarkers([])` is asserted (in "systemProcessProbe.runMarkers reads a live child's mark and skips vanished pids"). Inside the same `try`, empty PATH with `pathReplace(tmpdir("no-lsof-"))` and restore it in the `finally` too. Assert `await systemProcessProbe.cwds([])` deep-equals `new Map()`. As the control, assert `systemProcessProbe.cwds([process.pid])` rejects under the same PATH, which shows the empty-list answer did not come from a lookup. Mutation check: delete `if (pids.length === 0) return new Map();` at the top of `cwds`; the first assertion then rejects, and the test must fail.

**Goal.** `src/process/run-marker.ts` decides which processes belong to which run. If membership is loose, one run's sweep kills a sibling run's processes. If the sweep throws, a finished run fails. docs/invariants.md does not mention the module yet (`grep -c run-marker docs/invariants.md` gave 0 on 2026-10-20). Two behaviours have no test. First, the ps-side readers (`runMarkersInPs`, `pidsMarkedInPs`) have no test showing that a mark which is a prefix of another run's mark does not match; only the /proc reader `procEnvironCarriesMarker` has one. Second, nothing tests the `try`/`catch` around `findMarkedPids` in `sweepRunMarker`, which turns an unreadable table into "0 signaled".

**Approach.**
- test/run-marker.test.ts: add two tests at the end of the file. They use the imports the file already has (`errnoError`, `fs`, `TestContext` mocks):
  1. "the ps readers match a mark as a whole comma-separated run id, never as a prefix, and drop empty values". Use the marker `4242-deadbeefcafe`. Build ps output with these rows: `  111 node a.js TUMWATER_RUN=4242-deadbeefcafe0`, `  222 node b.js TUMWATER_RUN=x4242-deadbeefcafe`, `  333 node c.js TUMWATER_RUN=` and `  444 node d.js TUMWATER_RUN=,4242-deadbeefcafe,`. Assert that `pidsMarkedInPs(stdout, "4242-deadbeefcafe")` is `[444]`. Assert that `pidsMarkedInPs(stdout, "4242-dead")` is `[]`. Assert that `runMarkersInPs(stdout)` has no key 333 (an empty value is not a mark) and maps 444 to `["4242-deadbeefcafe"]`. Also assert `runMarkersInEnviron(["TUMWATER_RUN=,a,,a,"])` is `["a"]`. Check each row against `psMarkerAssignments`, `runMarkersInEnviron` and `runMarkersInPs` before asserting it.

Pin `process.platform` to `"linux"` the same way "sweepRunMarker on Linux walks /proc environ and signals only the marked pid" does: save the descriptor, `Object.defineProperty`, and restore it in `finally`. Mock `fs.readdirSync` to throw `errnoError("EACCES", "EACCES: permission denied")`. Assert that `await sweepRunMarker(makeRunMarker())` equals 0 and that the mock was called once, with `/proc`.

### docs/invariants.md gains a deferred-prompt marker section, and one unit test pins that the parser, the stripper and the due check agree on what counts as plumbing (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. It appends after whatever invariants section is last, so it only needs a rebase over the queue-file and queue-file-name sections if those merge first; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** src/inbox/prompt-not-before.ts owns the `tumwater:not-before <iso-utc>` line that `tumwater prompt --at` writes at the top of a queue file. `notBeforeMs` decides whether a prompt is held back, and `stripNotBeforeMarker` decides what the operator and the role see. If the two drift, a prompt is held back while its marker still shows, or the marker is stripped from a prompt that is not deferred. `grep -c prompt-not-before docs/invariants.md` printed 0 on 2026-10-20. The existing tests (test/inbox.test.ts "operator content that merely starts with a marker-shaped line is never treated as plumbing", "a marker line without the writer's blank separator is content, not a deferral", "a malformed or missing not-before marker reads as deliverable") go through the inbox store. None calls `stripNotBeforeMarker` or `deliverableAt` directly: `grep -n 'stripNotBeforeMarker\|deliverableAt' test/*.ts` printed nothing on 2026-10-20. So nothing pins three behaviours. (1) A stamp in the writer's shape that `Date.parse` rejects (month 13) is neither held back nor stripped. (2) The due check accepts a stamp equal to now. (3) Only the leading marker is stripped.

**Approach.**
- Create test/prompt-not-before.test.ts in the style of the other unit tests (`import test from "node:test"`, `import assert from "node:assert/strict"`), importing `notBeforeMarker`, `notBeforeMs`, `stripNotBeforeMarker`, `deliverableAt` and `deliverableNow` from `../src/inbox/prompt-not-before.js`. It needs no tmpdir and no fs. Use a new file, not test/inbox.test.ts, because the queue-file-name plan appends to that file. Add these tests:
  - "notBeforeMarker round-trips through notBeforeMs to the millisecond and strips to the body". With `at = 1_700_000_000_123`, `notBeforeMs(notBeforeMarker(at) + "body")` equals `at`, and `stripNotBeforeMarker(notBeforeMarker(at) + "body")` equals `"body"`. A body that itself starts with a second marker (`notBeforeMarker(at) + notBeforeMarker(at + 1) + "body"`) loses only the first marker.
  - "a writer-shaped stamp that Date.parse rejects is neither deferred nor stripped". Use `const text = "tumwater:not-before 2030-13-45T25:61:00.000Z\n\nbody"`. Assert `notBeforeMs(text)` is null, `stripNotBeforeMarker(text)` equals `text`, and `deliverableNow(text, 0)` is true. (On node, `Date.parse("2030-13-45T25:61:00.000Z")` is NaN. Do not use a 30 February date: node rolls it over to March and parses it.)
  - "deliverableAt delivers at the stamp's own millisecond, not before". `deliverableAt(null, 0)` is true, `deliverableAt(5, 5)` is true, `deliverableAt(6, 5)` is false. Also assert that `deliverableNow(notBeforeMarker(5) + "x", 4)` is false and `deliverableNow(notBeforeMarker(5) + "x", 5)` is true.

Pinned by the round-trip test, the Date.parse test, and test/inbox.test.ts "operator content that merely starts with a marker-shaped line is never treated as plumbing" and "a marker line without the writer's blank separator is content, not a deferral".
  - `INV-AI2: the stripper removes exactly what the parser accepts, once, and passes every other text through unchanged`. Binds `stripNotBeforeMarker`. Name its consumers from `grep -n 'stripNotBeforeMarker(' src -r` at the time of writing (on 2026-10-20: inbox.ts, inbox-edit.ts and run-prompt.ts). Pinned by the round-trip test and the Date.parse test.

### Plain terms code run, part 19/20: Rename the start command code and convert CLI and team and doctor and status modules (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 18/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names" and "Commands and config"; touches src/cli/ + src/cli.ts + src/process/supervisor.ts + src/build/build-stage.ts + src/team/ + src/doctor/ + src/status/ + src/backlog/ + src/brief/ + src/change/ + src/redeploy/ + root modules + their tests; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The `tumwater start` command's code is named for it (`cmdStart`, `START_FLAG_SPECS`, `superviseStart`, `spawnStartChild`). The CLI, team, doctor, status, backlog, brief, change and redeploy modules lose their tick wording.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run"; in src/cli/cli-start.ts, "this run" meaning the whole `tumwater start` process → "this session". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- Start-command names: in src/cli/cli-start.ts, `cmdRun` → `cmdStart` and `superviseRunCommand` → `superviseStartCommand`; in src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, `RUN_FLAG_SPECS` → `START_FLAG_SPECS`; in src/process/supervisor.ts, `superviseRun` → `superviseStart` and `spawnRunChild` → `spawnStartChild`, with their uses in src/cli.ts, src/cli/cli-start.ts and src/build/build-stage.ts and their tests. Plain terms commands may already have renamed some of these; rename whichever remain.
- Do not change any argv. The supervisor spawns its child as `["run", …extraArgs]` (in `spawnStartChild`), and that literal `run` must stay. `run` stays a hidden alias of `tumwater start`, so a rollback to an older build, whose CLI only knows `run`, can still respawn the child. Add a one-line comment at the spawn site saying so.
