### docs/invariants.md gains a text-shaping section, so a fixer touching label truncation, prompt caps, count parsing or terminal-control stripping reads what src/text/text.ts promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Appends after whatever invariants section is last, so it only rebases over the display-format section if that merges first. Touches docs/invariants.md and test/text.test.ts only, not src/text/text.ts — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Replanned 2026-10-20 by the plan role:** the refusal's blocker is gone. test/invariants-doc.test.ts's `ID_RE` is now `/^INV-[A-Z]{1,2}\d+$/`, and `grep -n 'INV-AD' docs/invariants.md` found nothing on 2026-10-20 (INV-AB and INV-AC are taken), so `INV-AD` is a valid, free prefix.

**Goal.** src/text/text.ts holds the one-line text rules that every display surface, prompt cap and input parser uses: `truncate` and `squash` bound a label, `truncateWithNote` caps text injected into a prompt with a visible marker, `parsePositiveInt`/`parseNonNegativeInt` define a valid count across CLI flags and GUI query params, and `stripTerminalControls` keeps untrusted text from driving the operator's terminal. `grep -n 'squash\|truncateWithNote\|parsePositiveInt\|stripTerminalControls' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing today. The terminal-text section only mentions `truncate` in passing. test/text.test.ts pins most rules directly, but `squash` has no direct test. Its doc comment says it collapses whitespace before it truncates, and that the order matters. Nothing fails today if the order is reversed. This plan adds that test and the section.

**Approach.**
- Add one test to test/text.test.ts, next to the truncate tests, and add `squash` to the existing import from `../src/text/text.js`. Title it "squash collapses whitespace before it bounds the line". Assert `squash("a\n\n\n\nbcd", 5) === "a bcd"`. Reversed (`collapseWhitespace(truncate(s, 5))`) that input gives `"a…"`, so the test catches a swapped order. Also assert `squash("  x  ", 10) === "x"`, and that `squash` of a long multi-line string with max 20 has no `\n` and is at most 20 characters long. Do not edit any existing test.
- Append a new section at the very end of docs/invariants.md, after whatever section is last at that point. Title it `## Text shaping: a bounded line never overflows or splits a character, and a count is plain decimal`. Give it a two-sentence intro in the register's style: text.ts is the single home of these rules so consumers cannot drift, and it is presentation and parsing only (node built-ins, importable from any layer). Use the id prefix `INV-AD`. Run `grep -n 'INV-AD' docs/invariants.md` first, and if it finds something, use the next free two-letter prefix.
- Add five entries, each with **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.** like the existing ones. Before writing each guarantee, read the cited test and the matching code, and state only what the code does. Where a detail below is wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-AD1: a truncated line is at most max characters and never ends on a lone surrogate`. Guarantee: `truncate` returns `s` unchanged when it fits. Otherwise it cuts to `max - 1` code units, backing off one more when the cut would split a surrogate pair (`cutSplitsSurrogatePair`), drops trailing whitespace the cut leaves behind, and appends `…`. A non-positive `max` gives `""`. Binds: src/text/text.ts (`truncate`, `cutSplitsSurrogatePair`). Pinned by: test/text.test.ts "truncate leaves a string unchanged when it fits, including the exact boundary", "truncate cuts to at most max characters, ellipsis included", "truncate drops a trailing space the cut leaves behind before appending the ellipsis", "truncate never splits a surrogate pair (no lone surrogates in clipped labels)", "truncate never returns a string longer than max (the display-width invariant)" and "truncate with a non-positive max fits nothing and returns the empty string".
  - `### INV-AD2: a squashed detail is one line, collapsed before it is bounded`. Guarantee: `squash` is `truncate(collapseWhitespace(s), max)`. Every whitespace run becomes one space and both ends are trimmed before the cut, so the budget is spent on words, not on newlines. Binds: src/text/text.ts (`squash`, `collapseWhitespace`). Pinned by: test/text.test.ts "collapseWhitespace folds runs of spaces, tabs, and newlines to single spaces" and the new "squash collapses whitespace before it bounds the line".
  - `### INV-AD3: a capped prompt text keeps a plain prefix and always says it was cut`. Guarantee: `truncateWithNote` returns text of at most `max` characters unchanged. Past that it keeps exactly the first `max` code units (`max - 1` when that cut would split a surrogate pair), with no ellipsis or trim, and then appends `\n…[<label> truncated at <max> chars]`, which names `max`, not the number of units kept. Binds: src/text/text.ts (`truncateWithNote`, `cutSplitsSurrogatePair`). Pinned by: test/text.test.ts "truncateWithNote passes short text through and appends its marker past the cap" and "truncateWithNote never splits a surrogate pair at the cut boundary".
  - `### INV-AD4: a count parses only as a plain decimal digit run that is a safe integer`. Guarantee: both parsers accept only `^\d+$` with no leading zero (a lone `"0"` is allowed) that `Number()` gives as a safe integer. Hex, exponent, sign, whitespace padding, a decimal point, zero-padding and an overflowing run all give null. `parsePositiveInt` also rejects 0, and `parseNonNegativeInt` accepts it. Binds: src/text/text.ts (`parsePositiveInt`, `parseNonNegativeInt`). Pinned by: test/text.test.ts "parsePositiveInt accepts plain decimal only — hex, scientific, signed, and padded forms are null" and "parseNonNegativeInt accepts plain decimal only and allows zero".
  - `### INV-AD5: untrusted text reaches the terminal without control characters except newline and tab`. Guarantee: `stripTerminalControls` removes every C0 control except `\n` and `\t`, plus DEL and the C1 block U+0080–U+009F. ESC goes with the rest, so no OSC or CSI sequence survives. Name the two display boundaries the doc comment gives (the CLI's `say` and the composed TUI frame) only after confirming them with `grep -rn 'stripTerminalControls' src`, and state that event JSON is not stripped only if that grep supports it. Binds: src/text/text.ts (`stripTerminalControls`). Pinned by: test/text.test.ts "stripTerminalControls removes ESC/C0/C1/DEL and keeps only newline and tab".
- Do not cover `textOr` (the display-format section's INV-AA2 binds it), `gotSuffix`, `errorMessage`, the blank-line trimmers or `tooLongMessage`. Keep the words "tick", "loop" and "notebook" out of the new prose and the new test title.
- Before citing it, check every quoted title with `grep -nF '<title>' test/text.test.ts`. The guard in test/invariants-doc.test.ts fails on a title that is not in the cited file.

**Files touched.** docs/invariants.md, test/text.test.ts (one new test and the `squash` import).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n '^### INV-AD' docs/invariants.md` lists INV-AD1 through INV-AD5 (or the fallback prefix), all under the new section, each with the three field labels.
- The new test fails when `squash`'s body is changed to `collapseWhitespace(truncate(s, max))` (check this locally, then restore the line), and passes as the code stands.

### docs/invariants.md gains a shared-phrases section, so a fixer touching count wording, hold spans, the budget phrase, tool-call labels or the fallback wordings reads what src/text/phrases.ts promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Appends after whatever invariants section is last, so it only rebases over the display-format, text-shaping and Markdown-builder sections if they merge first. Touches docs/invariants.md and test/phrases.test.ts only, not src/text/phrases.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** src/text/phrases.ts is the single home of the team's shared wording: `plural`/`agree` pick a count's number form, `shortSpanPhrase`/`holdPhrase` word a hold's span, `budgetPhrase` words a spend against its cap, `describeToolCall` builds the one-line tool-call label, and `firstReason`/`backendKindPhrase` fall back to fixed wording on an unreadable field. `grep -n 'phrases' docs/invariants.md` found nothing on 2026-10-20. test/phrases.test.ts pins the label, the budget phrase, the span rounding and the two fallbacks, but it does not import `plural`, `agree` or `holdPhrase`, and `grep -n "text/phrases" test/*.ts` shows no other test file importing them (only test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, for `shortSpanPhrase`). So nothing pins the plural rule (`n === 1` is singular, 0 and every other count are plural), or `holdPhrase`'s clamp of a negative or unreadable hold to `0s` and its relapse tail. This plan adds those two tests and the section.

**Approach.**
- Add two tests at the end of test/phrases.test.ts, and add `agree`, `holdPhrase` and `plural` to the existing import from `../src/text/phrases.js`. Do not edit any existing test.

**Goal.** src/text/datetime.ts is the single home of the local calendar-day rule and the relative-time phrasing. The event log's day key, the daily-budget stamp, both reports' windows, the history and transcript timestamps, and every "ago" and countdown cell all render through it. A wrong rule there buckets an event into the UTC day instead of the local one, lets two reports select different days, prints `NaN-NaN-NaN` for a corrupt stamp, or shows a negative countdown or a "60m" label. `grep -n 'datetime' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing today. test/datetime.test.ts pins most of the rules below. `humanAgo` and `secondsSince` have no direct test (`grep -rn 'humanAgo\|secondsSince' test` finds nothing), so this plan adds one small test for them rather than citing a test that does not check them.

  - `humanAgo(now - 120_000, now)` is `"2m ago"`, `humanAgo(now - 3 * 3600_000, now)` is `"3h ago"`, and `humanAgo(now + 60_000, now)` is `"0s ago"`.

### docs/invariants.md gains a status-poll section, so a fixer touching the observer reads in src/status/status-polls.ts reads what they promise instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. **Goal.** `tumwater status`, `tumwater queue`, `tumwater doctor`, the TUI and the GUI all poll through src/status/status-polls.ts every second. Its rules are what keep an observer from throwing or misreporting: main's badge comes from the newest merge-scope check only, a stale `main_red` hold is retired by a newer passed check (BUGS.md 2026-09-30), an in-flight merge marker displays only while the orchestrator is alive and a queued change it names is unfinished, a broken tumwater.json keeps the last valid config, and each poll gets its own copy of the cached runner state. `grep -n 'src/status\|heldByMainRed\|liveMergeMarker\|mainCheckForPoll' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing today. The record filtering in `liveMergeMarker` has no direct test: test/cli-queue.test.ts "queue prints the in-flight label only while an orchestrator is alive" only covers a single-change marker from the older format. So this plan adds the section, plus one small test file that pins the per-change filter before the section cites it. No source changes.

**Approach.**
- Add test/status-polls.test.ts (node:test, the same imports style as test/status-data-team.test.ts). It calls `liveMergeMarker` (src/status/status-polls.ts) directly with in-memory `MergeInFlight` values (src/merge/merge-slot.ts). It needs no repo. Write three tests with these exact titles:
  - "liveMergeMarker shows a single-change marker only while its sha is queued": a marker without `changes` comes back as-is when its sha is in the set, and undefined when it is not.
  - "liveMergeMarker keeps only the queued records and hides a marker whose queued records are all done": take a marker with three records, one queued `merging`, one queued `done`, and one `approved` whose sha is not queued. The result's `changes` holds the two queued records only. When only the `done` record is still queued, the result is undefined.
  - "liveMergeMarker drops a null or malformed record instead of throwing": `changes: [null, 7, {role: "x"}, <one valid queued merging record>]` returns a marker whose `changes` is just the valid record. Cast the fixture through `unknown`, since the type forbids it.

Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style: the dashboards and CLI read status-polls.ts's cached readers every second, in a process separate from the orchestrator, so every reader must tolerate torn, foreign or stale files. Use the letter `T`. `grep -n 'INV-T' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first; if it finds something, use the next free letter.

### docs/invariants.md gains a usage-report fold section, so a fixer touching the memoized event fold reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches docs/invariants.md only; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `foldWindowEvents` (src/report/report-fold.ts) memoizes the event-log half of the usage report per (root, fromKey), so a dashboard polling /api/report folds only appended lines. A memo like this is only correct if every warm answer equals the cold one, and its fallback arms (torn tail, rotated or shrunken log, a moved window) are where a fix goes wrong. Only test/report-fold-cache.test.ts and a few test/report-data.test.ts tests pin this. `grep -n 'src/report\|foldWindowEvents' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing. This plan adds the section, as the 2026-10-20 claims, backlog-archive, fallback-breaker and provider-concurrency sections did. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes. It is independent of the init invariants plan above; both append a section, so whichever merges second appends after the other.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the very end of docs/invariants.md, after whatever section is last at that point. Title it `## The usage report fold: a warm read equals a cold one`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intro under the backlog-archive section): `collectReport` and `collectReportSince` (src/report/report-data.ts) both fold through `foldWindowEvents`, which keeps a bounded memo (`reportFoldCache`, `REPORT_FOLD_CACHE_MAX`) and either reuses it, folds the appended complete lines, or falls back to a full `readWindowEvents` pass. Use the letter `R`. `grep -n 'INV-R' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first; if it finds something, use the next free letter.
- Add five entries, each with **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.** like the existing ones. Before writing each guarantee, read the cited tests and the matching part of `foldWindowEvents`, and state only what the code does. Where a detail below turns out to be wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-R1: a warm fold equals the cold read, and an appended event counts once`. Guarantee: a cache hit on an unchanged log (same dev, ino, mtime and size, `sameStatIdentity`) returns the stored fold; growth on the same file folds only the lines past the stored offset, and the offset a full pass seeds is the scan's own end (`raw.liveEnd`), not the earlier stat's size, so an event is never folded twice. A legacy `merged` line appended to a warm fold folds as `merge_done`. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`, `foldLineInto`, `foldEventInto`), src/files/files.ts (`sameStatIdentity`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "warm collectReport equals the cold read before and after appends", "a merge appended after a warm fold counts once, including in the role split" and "a legacy `merged` line appended after a warm fold folds as merge_done".
  - `### INV-R2: a torn trailing write folds only once its newline lands`. Guarantee: the append arm reads through `readCompleteLines`, which holds back a newline-less tail; a grown log with no complete new line returns the stored fold unchanged, and the next call folds the completed line whole. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`), src/files/tail.ts (`readCompleteLines`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "a torn trailing write is ignored until its newline lands".
  - `### INV-R3: a replaced or shrunken log refolds from scratch`. Guarantee: the append arm runs only when the size grew and dev and ino match; a log replaced by a different file (even one larger than the stored offset) or a shrunken one takes the full `readWindowEvents` pass, so no fold mixes two files' bytes. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`, `ReportFoldEntry`'s `dev`/`ino`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "a rotated log replaced by a fresh larger one refolds instead of folding the new log's bytes" and "a shrunken log (rotation) refolds instead of misaligning the byte offset".
  - `### INV-R4: the coverage proof follows the window`. Guarantee: the memo key includes `fromKey`, so a moved window gets a fresh entry and its own `fileCovers` instead of carrying an older window's proof; an empty or missing log reads as fully covered, not truncated, and the proof updates when the first event is appended. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`), src/report/report-data.ts (`collectReport`, `collectReportSince`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "the coverage proof follows the window, not the memo's seed: empty-log vacuous arm flips on first append"; test/report-data.test.ts "collectReportSince treats an empty or missing event log as fully covered, not truncated" and "collectReportSince proves coverage on a same-day log start and notes a log born inside the window".
  - `### INV-R5: both reports aggregate through one fold, with the merge share named`. Guarantee: `collectReport` and `collectReportSince` fold every event through `foldUsageEvent`, so a trailing window and a same-seed day slice agree; merge-slot tokens and cost go into `mergeTokens`/`mergeCostUsd`, never into `tokensOut`/`costUsd` inside the fold, and each collector adds the merge share to its surfaced totals once; a role-scoped window excludes the merge share. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldUsageEvent`, `UsageFold`), src/report/report-data.ts (`collectReport`, `collectReportSince`). ### Self-redeploy's restart cooldown drops from 12 h to 4 h, so fixes merged on main reach the running team the same working day (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/redeployer.test.ts, test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts and test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS` (src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts) allows at most one completed auto-restart per 12 h. It was set for BUGS.md 2026-09-11, when a drain's measured p50 was 46 min and its p75 82 min, so back-to-back drains halted the team. Drains are now short. The `restart` events' `finishedMs` for the last eight restarts (2026-10-17T17:51Z to 2026-10-20T12:42Z) were 2 s, 487 s, 835 s, 1562 s, 1596 s, 385 s, 363 s and 44 s. That is a median of about 7 min, and only one of them aborted runs (two, on 2026-10-19). The 12 h wait now costs more than the drains it prevents. On 2026-10-20 the team ran build 9a8ff490 (05:40 PDT) from 12:42Z. Two fixes that landed after it waited for the next restart, allowed only at 2026-10-21T00:42Z:
- 36d70ba86 (06:15 PDT), "Stand down a primary whose eligible entries siblings all hold". Until it ran, the primary `feature` runner kept paying for model runs that could only end in nothing-to-do. There were 58 `run_end` `no_change` results on `feature` that day, mostly 3–10 s runs started on a `main moved` wake or right after its own claim was released.
- 5aed15103 (05:56 PDT), "Merge PLANS.md, BUGS.md and QUESTIONS.md conflicts entry by entry". Until it ran, 23 `conflict_handback` events that day named PLANS.md as the only conflicted file. `git merge-file --diff3` reproduces the conflict for each of the seven sampled.

Each self-check extension merged that day also waits up to 12 h before it can stop a rejection. A 4 h cooldown allows at most six restarts a day. At the median drain, that holds new runs for about 42 min a day, against about 14 min today. In return, a merged fix runs within 4 h instead of within 12 h.

**Approach.**
- src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts: set `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS = 4 * 60 * 60_000`. Rewrite its doc comment: keep the 2026-09-11 reason, then add the 2026-10-20 re-derivation with the drain figures above. Add `export const RESTART_COOLDOWN_HOURS = RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS / 3_600_000;` beside it, with a one-line doc comment modelled on `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MIN`'s: the one home of the ms→h division the operator-facing warning uses. In the `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MS` doc comment and in the red-build doc comment that names "the 12 h deferral", say "the ordinary cooldown" instead of "12 h".
- src/redeploy/redeployer.ts: in `poll`'s cooldown warning, replace the literal `" (at most one completed restart per 12 h)"` with `` ` (at most one completed restart per ${RESTART_COOLDOWN_HOURS} h)` `` and import the constant beside `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS`. Change the three comments that say "12 h": the `urgentLapseWarnedFor` doc, the `effectiveCooldownUntil` doc, and the comment above the urgent-lapse warning. Each should say "the ordinary cooldown" or "the announced deadline" in place of the hour count.
- src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts: in `prewarm`'s doc comment, "the 12 h rate limit" becomes "the restart rate limit".
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the self-redeploy paragraph, "at most once every 12 hours" becomes "at most once every 4 hours", and "the 12-hour clock" becomes "the 4-hour clock".
- Tests. The timing assertions already derive from `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS`, and every hard-coded offset in test/redeployer.test.ts and test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts is 1 h or 2 h, which stays inside a 4 h cooldown. Do not change any offset. In test/redeployer.test.ts:
  - Change the two `assert.match(..., /per 12 h/)` to `/per 4 h/`.
  - Retitle "a red RUNNING build cuts the cooldown to the urgent window: the episode starts minutes, not 12 h, after the swap" so that it ends "…starts minutes, not the ordinary cooldown, after the swap".
  - Change the present-tense comments and assertion messages that say "12 h" (the waive-the-cooldown comment, "the urgent lapse starts the episode — not 12 h later", "the ordinary 12 h deadline stands", "keeps the full 12 h cooldown", "still inside the ordinary 12 h cooldown", "skips the 12 h cooldown", "its announced 12 h deadline") to say "the ordinary cooldown" or "its announced deadline".
  - Do the same for "inside the 12 h window" in test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts and "must not cut a 12 h cooldown" in test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.
  - Leave the two dated past-tense incident lines unchanged, since they describe what happened then: the "BUGS.md 2026-09-30 (urgency carve-out)" comment in test/redeployer.test.ts, and "The 2026-09-30 shape" in test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts.
- Out of scope: `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MS`, `STALE_ESCALATE_AFTER_MS`, the drain window, the forced-restart path, and any new config knob. This is a default change, not a setting.

**Files touched.** src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/redeployer.test.ts, test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts, test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.

### docs/invariants.md gains a provider-concurrency section, so a fixer touching the semaphore or the provider lease reads what they promise instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches docs/invariants.md only; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `maxConcurrent` and `maxConcurrentPerProvider` are enforced by the counting semaphore (src/concurrency/semaphore.ts) and the provider lease that follows a run across providers (src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts). Their callers are src/merge/merge-drain.ts, src/merge/merge-verify.ts, src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, src/git/worktree-pool.ts, src/config/config-live.ts and src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts. Their guarantees (no deadlock on re-key, no preemption on a cap change, a full key never delaying another key) are pinned only by tests: `grep -n -i 'semaphore\|provider-lease\|maxConcurrent' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing. The register exists so a fixer reads a subsystem's contract before changing its code; the 2026-10-20 claims, backlog-archive and fallback-breaker sections did this for their subsystems. This plan adds the section. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after `## The backlog archive: finished entries move once, and only the ones a change added`. Title it `## Provider concurrency: every run holds one team permit and at most one provider slot`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intro under the backlog-archive section): what the semaphore bounds, and that a lease moves with its run. Use the next free letter, `P`; `grep -n 'INV-P' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first.
- Add five entries, each with **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.** like the existing ones. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions' doc comments and the cited tests, and state only what the code does: where a detail below turns out wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-P1: admission needs both a team permit and the provider key's headroom, and a full key never delays another`. Binds: src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (`Semaphore.acquireLease`, `enforcedKeyCaps`), src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts. Pinned by: test/semaphore.test.ts "semaphore bounds concurrency" and "two keys fill independently: a full key never delays a free key, FIFO within a key"; test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts "maxConcurrentPerProvider caps role-run admission per provider while others run beside (part 2/5)" and "a verify's reviewer and a role run on the same capped provider never overlap, while another provider runs beside (part 3/5)".
  - `### INV-P2: a cap change never preempts, and permits never leak`. Guarantee: growing a cap wakes parked waiters up to the new headroom and no further; shrinking below in-use stops nothing already running and grants nothing until releases drain under the cap; repeated resizes leave the counts whole. Binds: src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (`setCapacity`, `setKeyCaps`), src/config/config-live.ts. Pinned by: test/semaphore.test.ts "growing capacity wakes queued acquirers up to the new headroom, never beyond it", "shrinking below current in-use admits no new work until releases drain under the cap", "shrinking a key below its in-use preempts nothing and grants nothing until releases drain", "repeated grow/shrink cycles leak no permits and starve no waiter" and "capacity fully restores after a burst: no slot leak".
  - `### INV-P3: wait order is by tier, FIFO within a tier, and the reserve holds a permit for work roles`. Binds: src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (`acquire`, `acquireLease`). Pinned by: test/semaphore.test.ts "a lower-tier arrival jumps ahead of parked higher-tier waiters, FIFO within a tier", "tier ordering never starves a higher tier: once no lower-tier waiter is parked, it drains FIFO", "a reserve keeps a permit free for a work acquirer while maintenance sits at its cap" and "the verify and merge tiers ignore the reserve"; test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts "the director's run starts immediately while every maxConcurrent slot is busy".
  - `### INV-P4: a lease follows its run to the provider it actually uses, and a re-key cannot deadlock`. Guarantee: a run on another key re-keys the lease (old key returned first); a parked re-key keeps only its team permit and is granted ahead of admission waiters for that key; releasing a lease whose re-key is parked cancels the grant without taking the target slot; a forced lease may exceed a full key by one holder and blocks grants until it drains. Binds: src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts (`withProviderLease`, `ensureProviderLease`), src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (`SemaphoreLease.rekey`, `forceLease`), src/merge/merge-drain.ts, src/merge/merge-verify.ts. Pinned by: test/provider-lease.test.ts "ensureProviderLease is a no-op without a lease in context", "a run on a different key re-keys: it releases the old key and takes the new one" and "a re-key to a full provider parks (holding no key) and is granted when it drains"; test/semaphore.test.ts "rekey gives the old key back first, and a parked re-key beats a parked admission for the key", "releasing a lease while its re-key to a full key is parked cancels the grant and never steals the target", "a forced lease overshoots a full key by one holder, blocking grants until it drains under the cap" and "re-key waiters hold a team permit only, so the key always drains (no deadlock)".
  - `### INV-P5: no provider slot is held while waiting for a worktree pool slot`. Binds: src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts (`dropProviderLeaseKey`), src/git/worktree-pool.ts (its `acquire`). Pinned by: test/provider-lease.test.ts "dropProviderLeaseKey returns the held key without giving up the team permit"; test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts "two runs on one provider and a single worktree slot both finish (pool-slot wait rule, part 4/5)".
- Leave src/concurrency/check-permit.ts (the build-check cap) and src/concurrency/lock.ts (the cross-process mutex) out: they are separate subsystems, and this section covers only the run semaphore and the lease.
- Cite only test titles that do not contain "tick" or "loop", and keep both words out of the new prose. The Plain-terms series (PLANS.md parts 16/20–20/20 and cleanup 1/7–7/7) sweeps those words, and this keeps the section out of its way. Watch the series' wording rules in prose too: no "run … running" stacks.
- Before citing it, check every quoted title with `grep -nF '<title>' <file>`; replace any that has changed with the test's exact current title. The guard in test/invariants-doc.test.ts fails on a title that is not in the cited file.

**Files touched.** docs/invariants.md only.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n '^### INV-P' docs/invariants.md` lists INV-P1 through INV-P5, all under the new section, each with the three field labels.
- Every quoted title in the new section is found by `grep -F` in its cited test file.
- `sed -n '/^## Provider concurrency/,$p' docs/invariants.md | grep -n -w -i 'tick\|loop'` prints nothing.

### The pre-queue self-check runs a finished plan's "prints nothing" acceptance greps, so a change stops being rejected for an acceptance grep that still matches (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Adds src/run/acceptance-greps.ts and test/acceptance-greps.test.ts and wires them into `stageCheckFindings` in src/run/stage-check.ts, which also holds the merged garbled-wording self-check (`garbledWordingFindings`); leave it unchanged; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Plans state acceptance criteria as grep commands: PLANS.md and PLANS-DONE.md hold over 40 criteria of the form "`grep …` finds nothing / prints nothing / is empty". Today nothing runs them before review. Between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-20, 42 `review_rejected` events cite an acceptance or VERIFIED grep that still matched. One example is the 2026-10-20 05:00Z feature-3 rejection: "`grep -rn "logs --role" src docs/cli.md` still matches `docs/cli.md:40`". Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue. If the self-check runs the grep, the fix-up turn sees the hits and fixes them first. This plan covers only the strict "matches nothing" form. Criteria worded "prints only …" / "lists only …" need judgement: handing their hits to the fix-up turn would invite it to rename the serialized names those criteria deliberately keep. So they stay out.

**Approach.**
- **New module src/run/acceptance-greps.ts.** Give it a module doc comment, plus a doc comment on each export.
  - `export function emptyGrepCriteria(body: string): string[]`. Collapse the body's whitespace to single spaces. Return each backticked span (`` `…` ``) that:
    - starts with `grep ` or `git grep `;
    - is followed, after optional spaces, by one of: `finds nothing`, `prints nothing`, `returns nothing`, `outputs nothing`, `matches nothing`, `lists nothing`, `is empty`, `lists none`, or `prints|finds|lists|returns|gives|shows` followed by `no` and then `lines?|hits?|matches?|output`. Match case-insensitively.
    - Drop a criterion whose text from that phrase to the next `.` or `;` contains `apart from`, `except`, `excluding`, `other than`, `besides` or `beyond`. Such a criterion allows some hits.
    - Return the spans' inner text without duplicates, in body order, at most 5.
  - `export function grepArgv(cmd: string): { file: "grep" | "git"; args: string[] } | undefined`. A minimal shell-word splitter. Single quotes are literal. In double quotes, only `\"` and `\\` are escapes. Outside quotes, a backslash keeps the next character. Return undefined when an unquoted `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `$`, `(`, `)` or backtick appears, or when a quote is left open. `git grep …` gives `{ file: "git", args: ["grep", …] }`; `grep …` gives `{ file: "grep", args: […] }`. Nothing goes through a shell, so `*` stays literal (grep's own `--include=*.ts` handles it).
  - `export async function acceptanceGrepFindings(wt: string, entries: { title: string; body: string }[]): Promise<string[]>`. For each entry and each criterion with a non-undefined argv, run `execFileAsync(file, args, { cwd: wt, timeout: 20_000 })` (src/process/process.ts).
    - An exit code of 1 with empty stdout is a pass. Any other failure (exit 2, a timeout, a spawn error) skips that criterion: an unrunnable command is not evidence.
    - Exit 0 with non-empty stdout yields one finding: `PLANS.md's finished entry "${truncate(title, 160)}" says \`${cmd}\` matches nothing, but it prints ${n} line(s): ${first 5 lines, each cut to 200 chars, joined with "; "}${more suffix} — fix those lines, or correct the claim if the criterion is wrong`.
    - Give at most one finding per entry: the first failing criterion's. `truncate` is in src/text/text.ts.
- **Wiring in src/run/stage-check.ts.** In `stageCheckFindings`, the `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` block already reads head and base text for `PLANS.md`/PLANS-DONE.md. For the `PLANS.md` spec only, collect the entries this change finished:
  - `## Done` entries of the head `PLANS.md` whose `finishedKey` (the existing helper) is not among the base `## Done` keys;
  - plus PLANS-DONE.md `## Done` entries whose key is not among the base archive's keys.

  Run `acceptanceGrepFindings(wt, entries)` on them, inside the existing `.catch(() => [])` pattern, and push its findings. Add a sentence to the module header doc comment's staging-only paragraph: `acceptanceGrepFindings` runs only at staging and runs the strict "matches nothing" greps of the plan entries the change finished. The gate does not run it.
- **No prompt change.** `buildStageFixPrompt` (src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts) already passes each finding's text to the fix-up turn.

**Files touched.** src/run/acceptance-greps.ts (new), src/run/stage-check.ts, test/acceptance-greps.test.ts (new). docs/invariants.md stays unchanged: no Binds list there pins a staging-only finding of this kind. Check with `grep -n "finishedDuplicateFindings\|strayPlaceholder" docs/invariants.md`, which finds nothing.

**Acceptance criteria.** In test strings, build the trigger phrases (for example "finds" + " nothing") by concatenation. That way this change's own PLANS.md Done entry is the only text that matters to its own self-check. That entry's criteria must hold on the finished tree.
- "emptyGrepCriteria picks the matches-nothing greps and skips qualified or only-kind ones": a body holding `` `grep -rn foo src` finds nothing``, `` `git grep -n bar` is empty``, `` `grep -rn baz src` prints only kept names`` and `` `grep -rn qux src` prints nothing apart from a fixture`` gives exactly the first two commands.
- "grepArgv splits quotes and refuses shell syntax": `grep -rnE 'a|b' "src dir" --include=*.ts` gives `["-rnE", "a|b", "src dir", "--include=*.ts"]`; `git grep -n x` gives file `git` and args `["grep", "-n", "x"]`; `grep x | wc -l` and `grep 'x` give undefined.
- "acceptanceGrepFindings reports a matches-nothing grep that still matches": in a temp dir holding `src/a.ts` with the text `leftoverName`, an entry whose body says `` `grep -rn leftoverName src` `` + " finds nothing" yields one finding that names the entry's title and contains `src/a.ts:1`. Removing the text yields no finding. An entry whose grep exits 2 (a missing path) yields no finding.
- A test in test/stage-check.test.ts, "a finished plan whose matches-nothing grep still matches yields the acceptance-grep finding": use `repoWith` with a base PLANS.md and a `src/a.ts` containing `oldName`. In the worktree, add a `## Done` entry to PLANS.md whose body says the grep for `oldName` over `src` finds nothing. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` then includes a finding that contains `src/a.ts:1`. The same entry already present under `## Done` on the base yields no acceptance-grep finding.
- `grep -rn "acceptanceGrepFindings" src` lists the definition in src/run/acceptance-greps.ts and its call and doc mention in src/run/stage-check.ts.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

The plain-terms rename parts kept being rejected after that for shapes it misses.
