The shapes: "run" directly followed by "run"/"runs" ("the role's next run" + " runs", "while the role's runs" + " run off-model"); "run" directly followed by "running" ("no director run" + " running"); a possessive "run's"/"runs'" followed, with at most one word between, by "run"/"runs" ("this run's pi" + " run", "the authoring run's" + " run", "the run's own" + " runs'"); "runs and runs"; and the same phrases split across a line break inside a comment ("the role's next run" / "runs and clear only", src/ui/status-model.ts in the 14:27Z rejection). Eleven parts of the series are still to come (16/20–20/20 and cleanup 1/7–7/7). Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue; a finding costs one fix-up turn.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Append three patterns to `GARBLED_WORDING`, in this order:
  - `/\bruns?\s+run(?:s|ning)?\b/i` ("run" stacked on "run", "runs" or "running");
  - `/\bruns?'s?\s+(?:(?!agent\b)[a-z]+\s+)?runs?\b/i` (a possessive run followed by run, with at most one word between; "agent" is excluded because "this run's agent run" is the wording the rename series prescribes);
  - `/\bruns?\s+(?:and|or)\s+runs?\b/i`.
  The first covers both the "run" + "runs" and the "run" + "running" shapes. Extend the doc comment above `GARBLED_WORDING` to describe them in words, without writing a garbled phrase out in full: the change's own self-check reads its added lines, so a comment that spells out one of these phrases flags itself. (The existing comment already does this, and the patterns' own source text does not match, because `\s+` is not whitespace.)
- In `garbledWordingFindings`, also check a phrase split across two lines. While walking a hunk, remember the previous added line's text (`prevAdded`; reset it to null on each `diff --git` header, on each `@@` hunk header and on any line that is not an added line). For an added line with no single-line hit and a non-null `prevAdded`, build `joined = prevAdded.trimEnd() + " " + cur.replace(/^\s*(?:\/\/+|\*|#)\s*/, "")`. For the first `GARBLED_WORDING` match in `joined` that starts before `prevAdded.trimEnd().length` and ends after it (so it spans the join and was not already reported for the earlier line), push `${file}:${lineNo - 1}-${lineNo} "${m[0]}"`. Use a global copy of each regex (`new RegExp(re.source, re.flags + "g")`) with `matchAll` to find a spanning match. Record prose stays skipped as before.
- Fix the module header doc comment: the paragraph that starts "A fifth check, `garbledWordingFindings`" repeats "fifth" (the detached-doc paragraph above it is the fifth, `movedSourceFindings` the sixth). Make it "A seventh check", and extend its parenthetical list with the new shapes (described in words, as above) and "including a phrase split across two added lines".

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts. The gate does not run this check, and no docs/invariants.md Binds list names `garbledWordingFindings` (check with `grep -n garbled docs/invariants.md`; it was empty when this was planned), so that file stays unchanged. Main already holds lines with these shapes (`grep -nE "\bruns?\s+runs?\b" src` hits src/runner/runner-run.ts and src/run/run-resume.ts); the check reads only added lines, so they are not reported unless a change rewrites them. Leave them alone; the series parts reword them.

**Acceptance criteria.** Build every garbled sample in the tests by string concatenation (as the existing garbled-wording tests do), so test/stage-check.test.ts's own added lines do not match.
- A new test, "added lines that stack run on runs or running, or a run's run, yield the garbled-wording finding": in `src/a.ts`, add the lines `// while the role's next run` + ` runs`, `// with no director run` + ` running`, `// the authoring run's` + ` run`, `// this run's pi` + ` run` and `// across runs and` + ` runs`. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` gives one garbled-wording finding that names each of those five `src/a.ts:N` lines.
- A new test, "a garbled phrase split across two added comment lines yields the garbled-wording finding": two added lines `// the alert stays up while the role's next run` and `// runs and clears after`, with the garbled part concatenated as above. The finding contains `src/a.ts:2-3`.
- A new test, "the prescribed agent-run wording yields no garbled-wording finding": the added lines `// this run's agent run`, `// the role has run twice; it ran once` and `// a run, and then the next` give no garbled-wording finding.
- The existing garbled-wording tests ("added lines with a broken participle…", "added lines that stack run on run…", "garbled wording in record prose…", "garbled wording already on the base…") pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a `_None yet._` placeholder the change added to a backlog section that still holds entries (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. The in-flight moved-source self-check plan also adds a check to src/run/stage-check.ts, so whichever merges second rebases over a neighbouring hunk; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A feature run that finishes the last entry under `## Planned` sometimes writes `_None yet._` where that entry used to be, even though the section still holds other entries. `_None yet._` is the skeleton placeholder that marks an empty section (init-templates.ts, `PLACEHOLDER` in src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts), so the file then says `## Planned` is empty while it lists open plans. Reviewers rejected this five times: 10-09 13:12, 10-16 18:30, 10-19 14:47 (feature-4, head 97f625eee), 10-20 00:20 (feature-3) and 10-20 13:43 (feature-3, head 8c45509f9). In both heads checked, the PLANS.md hunk adds `+_None yet._` directly above `## Done`. Each rejection cost a review round and a re-queue for a one-line deletion. No current check catches it: `grep -n 'None yet' src/run/stage-check.ts src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` is empty. A staging finding gives the fix-up turn the exact line to delete before the change is queued.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `const PLACEHOLDER_LINE = "_None yet._";` with a one-line doc comment ("the skeleton placeholder that marks an empty backlog section"). Also add `const PLACEHOLDER_FILES = ["PLANS.md", "BUGS.md", "QUESTIONS.md"] as const;` (the live backlog files; the archives have no placeholder sections).
- Add a module-private helper `placeholderSections(md: string): Map<string, number>`. For each `## ` section title in `md` (`fenceAwareHeadingLines(md, "## ").map((l) => headingTitle(l, "## "))`), when `sectionBodyLines(md, title).some((l) => l.trim() === PLACEHOLDER_LINE)` and `parseEntryDetails(md, title).length > 0`, it maps the title to that entry count. Import `fenceAwareHeadingLines`, `headingTitle` and `sectionBodyLines` from `../backlog/backlog-md.js`, where `parseEntryDetails` is already imported. Fenced lines are excluded because `sectionBodyLines` strips them, so a quoted placeholder never counts.
- Add an exported `strayPlaceholderFinding(file: string, head: string, base: string): string | undefined`. It returns undefined unless some section is in `placeholderSections(head)` but not in `placeholderSections(base)`, so damage already on main is not blamed on this change. For the first such section in file order, it returns `` `${file}'s "## ${title}" section holds ${n} entr${n === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}, but this change left the empty-section placeholder ${PLACEHOLDER_LINE} in it — delete that line: it marks a section with no entries` `` followed by `moreSuffix(count - 1)`, the way `waitingNoteFinding` reports the rest. Give it a doc comment in the style of `waitingNoteFinding`'s.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the `waitingNoteFinding` block, add a loop over `PLACEHOLDER_FILES` that skips files not in `files`. For each file, read `head` with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, file)) ?? ""` and `base` with `(await fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), file).catch(() => undefined)) ?? ""`, then push `strayPlaceholderFinding(file, head, base)` when it is defined. Every role gets this check, not only feature.
- In the module's header doc comment, add a sentence after the `finishedDuplicateFindings` one: `strayPlaceholderFinding` is staging-only too. It flags a `_None yet._` line the change left in a PLANS.md, BUGS.md or QUESTIONS.md section that still holds entries.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts. The gate and `backlogStructureReason` stay unchanged. No docs/invariants.md section pins the staging-only findings (its stage-check.ts Binds cover the protected-edit, secret-leak and plan-dependency checks, which this plan does not change), so that file stays unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/stage-check.test.ts, add `strayPlaceholderFinding` to the existing import from `../src/run/stage-check.js`. Add the test "strayPlaceholderFinding flags a placeholder added to a section that still holds entries". With `base = "# Plans\n\n## Planned\n\n### A\n\nBody.\n\n### B\n\nBody.\n\n## Done\n\n_None yet._\n"` and `head` equal to base with `### B\n\nBody.\n\n` replaced by `_None yet._\n\n`, the finding matches `/PLANS\.md's "## Planned" section holds 1 entry, but this change left the empty-section placeholder _None yet\._/`. The `## Done` placeholder in an entry-less section adds nothing to the finding.
- In the same test: `strayPlaceholderFinding("PLANS.md", head, head)` is undefined, because the damage is already on the base. A head whose `## Planned` holds only `_None yet._` and no entries gives undefined. A head whose only placeholder sits inside a fenced block (a ```` ``` ```` fence) in an entry's body gives undefined.
- A new test, "a placeholder added to a non-empty BUGS.md section yields the stray-placeholder finding", uses `repoWith({ "BUGS.md": "# Bugs\n\n## Open\n\n### One bug\n\nBody.\n" })`. It writes the file with `\n_None yet._\n` appended, calls `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "docs")`, and asserts that exactly one finding matches `/BUGS\.md's "## Open" section holds 1 entry/`.
- The existing test "a clean change yields no findings" still passes unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a reference to a file that the change moved code out of, so a split stops being rejected for a doc that still says the moved code lives in the old file (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, like the garbled-wording and detached-doc self-check plans above; whichever lands later rebases onto the others' `gitLevelFindings` line and header paragraph; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Three organize changes were rejected on 2026-10-20 for the same defect. Each one moved code out of a file that still exists, and left a reference elsewhere saying the moved code lives in the old file. At 11:28 (head 7fe012b38), tests moved from test/gate-prompts.test.ts to the new test/gate-notes.test.ts, but the `entryRangeLines` doc in src/prompt/gate-notes.ts still said "pinned in tests (test/gate-prompts.test.ts)". At 13:37 (head 9c1bbe9f2), the `eventMessage` cases moved out of src/events/event-format.ts into new `event-message-*.ts` modules, but the **Binds** list in docs/invariants.md still named `src/events/event-format.ts` for the `image_reroute` lines. At 03:31, an open PLANS.md entry still named src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts as the home of moved code. The existing checks miss this shape. `staleReferenceFindings` only greps `D` and `R` paths, and the old file here is `M`. `staleNameFindings` exempts a name the change re-declares (a move), and neither stale line named a moved declaration. A move can be read from the `-U0` diff that `gitLevelFindings` already builds: lines removed from one file and added verbatim to another. Grepping the staged tree for the old file's full path then lists the lines to re-check, so the author's fix-up turn can repoint them before a review is spent. The 11:28 and 13:37 cases would both have been caught. The 03:31 case sits in record prose, which every path check deliberately skips (`isRecordProse`).

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `movedSourceFindings(wt: string, diff: string, entries: NameStatusEntry[]): Promise<string[]>`. Call it in `gitLevelFindings` after `staleNameFindings`. Give it a `/** (f) … */` doc in the style of the `(a)`–`(d)` docs, and add one sentence to the module header's paragraph on the git-level checks. Letter it after the last existing check letter: (f) if the detached-doc plan's (e) has landed, else (e).
- Collect moves from the diff. Walk it like `staleNameFindings`, tracking the current file from `diff --git a/.* b/(.*)`. For each file, keep `removed: string[]` and `added: Set<string>` of lines with the `-`/`+` marker stripped and `.trim()` applied. Keep only trimmed lines of at least `MOVED_LINE_MIN_CHARS = 12` characters, so braces, `});` and blank lines never count. A source is a file whose `entries` status is `M`. Its moved count is the number of its `removed` lines found in some other file's `added`. Its receivers are those other files, in diff order. A source qualifies when its moved count is at least `MOVED_LINES_MIN = 10`. Add both constants beside `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES`, each with a one-line doc.
- For each qualifying source, stopping after `MAX_STALE_PATHS` sources, run `gitTry(wt, "grep", "-n", "-F", "-I", "--cached", "-e", source)`. Parse hits with the same `^([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)$` regex that `staleReferenceFindings` uses. Skip a hit that is in the source file itself, in record prose (`isRecordProse`), or whose line fails `hasStandalonePathOccurrence(text, source)`. Keep up to `MAX_STALE_HITS`. Do not exclude receivers: the 11:28 stale line was itself a moved line, so it sat in the receiver. Emit nothing for a source with no remaining hits.
- Wording, one finding per source: `` `${source} had ${n} lines moved to ${cappedList(receivers, MAX_STALE_PATHS)}, but it is still named at: ${hits.join(", ")} — check each still describes what stays in ${source}, and point any that describes the moved code at its new file` ``. A correct reference is answered in RISK, as `buildStageFixPrompt` already allows.
- Out of scope: basename-only or extension-swapped references (`gate-prompts.ts`, `./event-format.js`), record prose, and moves into a file the change does not touch.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. No docs/invariants.md section covers the self-check's advisory findings (`grep -n "self-check" docs/invariants.md` is empty), so it stays unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts under a `// Moved-source check: …` comment. Each builds with `repoWith`, edits the worktree with `fs.writeFileSync`, and calls `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`. `BODY` is 12 distinct lines such as `export const valueNumber${i} = ${i} * 1000;`.
- "moving code out of a file that a doc still names yields the moved-source finding". Base: `src/big.ts` = `export const keep = 1;\n` + BODY, `docs/x.md` = `The bodies live in src/big.ts.\n`. Head: `src/big.ts` = `export const keep = 1;\n`, new `src/small.ts` = BODY. Exactly one finding matches `/src\/big\.ts had 12 lines moved to src\/small\.ts, but it is still named at: docs\/x\.md:1/`. After rewriting `docs/x.md` to name `src/small.ts`, no finding matches `/lines moved to/`.
- "a reference inside the receiving file is reported too". Same move, with no docs/x.md, but the receiver's head starts with `// pinned in tests (src/big.ts)\n`. The finding names `src/small.ts:1`.
- "a move below the line threshold, a pure deletion, or a reference in record prose yields no moved-source finding". Three repos, each giving no finding that matches `/lines moved to/`. (a) Move only 5 BODY lines. (b) Delete BODY from `src/big.ts` with no receiver. (c) The full move, with the reference only in `PLANS.md`.
- "a basename-only reference is not reported". The full move, with `docs/x.md` = `See big.ts.\n`. No finding matches `/lines moved to/`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The self-check's outcome warning carries the finding texts, so the log shows which checks fire and which ones a fix-up turn leaves open (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/run-stage.ts, test/run-stage.test.ts and the `"warning"` line of the event-type union in src/events/events.ts. The two in-flight self-check plans edit src/run/stage-check.ts only, so neither conflicts)

**Goal.** `stageRunMerge` (src/run/run-stage.ts) ends the pre-queue self-check with one `warning` event. Its message holds counts only: "stage self-check: N findings — fixed by the follow-up turn", "…; M still open, queued for the gate", or "the follow-up turn left no change; nothing to land". The events log holds 49 of these in the seven days before this plan. Several of them read "10 findings; 10 still open" or "11 findings; 11 still open" (feature-3 on 10-18, others on 10-17), and nothing records what those findings were. That leaves three questions the log cannot answer. Which checks fire? Which findings does an author ignore? Did a check miss the defect a reviewer later rejected? For example, the 13:36 rejection on 2026-10-20 named `deferTick` and `restoreMidTickWake` comments left in tests. The log has no self-check warning for that run, so it cannot show whether the staleName check, merged at 13:22, was part of the running build. The plan role picks its self-check work from rejection themes, and it is planning more checks now (garbled wording, detached doc comments). Recording the finding texts lets it measure a check after it lands instead of guessing.

**Approach.** All in src/run/run-stage.ts:
- Add a module-level constant `SELF_CHECK_LOGGED_FINDINGS = 12` (the most findings one outcome event carries) and `SELF_CHECK_FINDING_CHARS = 300` (the cap on each finding's text), each with a one-line doc. Add a module-private helper `findingDigest(findings: readonly string[]): string[]` that returns `findings.slice(0, SELF_CHECK_LOGGED_FINDINGS).map((f) => squash(f, SELF_CHECK_FINDING_CHARS))`. Import `squash` from `../text/text.js`.
- In `stageRunMerge`'s self-check block, the three outcome `ctx.warn(...)` calls become `logEventBestEffort(ctx.root, { source: ctx.role, type: "warning", message, findings: findingDigest(findings) })`. `message` is the exact string each one passes today. The "still open" outcome also carries `open: findingDigest(remaining)`. `findings` is the list handed to `requestStageFix`, so it includes the `assignedMoved` and `heldMoved` findings pushed onto it. Every other `ctx.warn` call in the file stays as it is. Add a one-line comment saying why these three bypass `ctx.warn`: they carry fields beyond a message, and `ctx.warn` only takes a message. The runner's `warn` → `warnEventBestEffort` writes the same `{ source: role, type: "warning", message }` shape, so feeds, `formatEvent`'s `warning: <message>` line and any warning counter see an unchanged event. Only the extra fields are new.
- In src/events/events.ts, add a trailing comment to the union's final `| "warning";` line: `// something is off but the loop continues: message; the stage self-check's outcome warnings (run/run-stage.ts) also carry findings (the finding texts, capped) and, when some stayed open after the fix-up turn, open`.

**Files touched.** src/run/run-stage.ts, src/events/events.ts (one comment), test/run-stage.test.ts. No docs/invariants.md section covers the self-check's warnings (`grep -n "self-check" docs/invariants.md` is empty), so it stays unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/run-stage.test.ts, import `readEvents` from `../src/events/event-read.js`. Update the five tests that now assert one of these messages through `calls.warnings`. They are "a self-check finding triggers one follow-up and queues with the fixed warning", "a finding the follow-up leaves unfixed still queues, with the still-open warning", and the other still-open and no-change tests that assert those exact strings (`grep -n '"stage self-check' test/run-stage.test.ts`). Each one reads `readEvents(root, 50).filter((e) => e.type === "warning")` and asserts:
  - the fixed case: one event with the same message, `source: "improve"`, `findings` deep-equal to `["md-only BUGS.md edit moves X to Fixed, but none of its symbols exist"]`, and no `open` key;
  - the still-open case: the same message, `findings: ["a finding"]` and `open: ["a finding"]`;
  - the no-change case: message "stage self-check: the follow-up turn left no change; nothing to land" with `findings: ["a finding"]`.
  Where a test's `calls.warnings` had held only that message, it now asserts `calls.warnings` is `[]`.
- A new test, "the self-check outcome warning caps the logged findings and their length", sets `stageChecks: [Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, i) => \`finding ${i} \` + "x".repeat(400)), []]`. It asserts that the warning's `findings` has length 12, that each entry has at most 300 characters and ends with `…`, and that the first one starts with `finding 0 `.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a doc comment that the change detached from its declaration (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, like the garbled-wording self-check plan above; whichever lands second rebases onto the other's `gitLevelFindings` line and header paragraph; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Ten `review_rejected` events between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-20 name the same mechanical defect: a JSDoc block that no longer sits on the declaration it documents. Two edits cause it. (1) New code is inserted between an existing `/** … */` block and its declaration. The doc then describes the inserted code, and the old declaration is left with none. Examples: `postReviewDue` between `drainMergeQueue`'s doc and its declaration (feature-5, 10-20), `quietHoursLine` inside `scheduleLine`'s doc (10-16), `entryRevisionFields` under `enqueueMerge`'s doc (dedupe, 10-18), `outcomeOrBadRequest` in src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts (dedupe, 10-18). (2) A declaration is deleted but its doc is kept, so the doc lands on the next declaration. Example: the `/** @deprecated Use …. */` line left above `export async function mergeHead` in test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts (feature, 10-20 13:12), which marked a live fixture deprecated. Both shapes can be read straight from the `-U0` diff the self-check already builds in `gitLevelFindings`, so the author's fix-up turn can repair them before a review is spent.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `detachedDocFindings(wt: string, diff: string): string[]`. Call it in `gitLevelFindings` after `newlineFindings(diff)`. Put a `/** (e) … */` doc on it in the style of `newlineFindings`'s `(c)` doc, and add a sentence about it to the module header's paragraph on the fourth check.
- Walk the diff like `newlineFindings`: `diff --git` starts a file, and `+++ ` gives the path through `diffPlusPath`. Consider only paths matching the existing `JS_FILE` and not `/dev/null`. For each such file, read the head text once with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, file))`, split it on `"\n"`, and collect every hunk as `{ c, d, removed: string[], added: string[] }`. The header is `@@ -a[,b] +c[,d] @@`, and an omitted count means 1. `-` lines go into `removed` and `+` lines into `added`, without the marker. Lines are 1-based into the head file.
- Two module-level helpers:
  - `DOC_TARGET`: a regex for a line that can carry a doc comment. It is either a keyword declaration, `^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:abstract\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:function\b|const\b|let\b|var\b|class\b|interface\b|type\b|enum\b)`, or a class member or field, `^\s*(?:(?:public|private|protected|static|readonly|async|get|set|override)\s+)*#?[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\??\s*[(<:=]`. Combine them with `|` into one regex.
  - `closesDocComment(lines: string[], i: number): boolean` (0-based `i`). It is true when `lines[i].trim()` ends with `*/` and the nearest line at or above `i` that contains `/*` has a trimmed form starting with `/**`. This covers one-line blocks like `/** @deprecated Use b. */`.
- Rule (1), insertion. The hunk has `removed.length === 0` and `d > 0`. Head line `c - 1` must exist, closes a doc comment, and is not an added line of any hunk in this file. At least one `added` line matches `DOC_TARGET`. Head line `c + d` exists and matches `DOC_TARGET`. Report the site as `` `${file}:${c - 1}` ``.
- Rule (2), deletion. The hunk has `d === 0` and at least one `removed` line matching `DOC_TARGET`. Head line `c` (git's convention: the line before the deleted range) closes a doc comment and is not an added line. Report `` `${file}:${c}` ``.
- Emit at most one finding per rule, each listing its sites with `cappedList(sites, MAX_DETACHED_DOCS)`. Add the constant `MAX_DETACHED_DOCS = 10` beside `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES`, with a one-line doc. Wording:
  - (1) `code was inserted between a doc comment and the declaration it documents, so the doc now describes the inserted code: ${list} — move the inserted code above the doc comment or below that declaration`
  - (2) `a declaration was deleted but its doc comment was kept, so the doc now documents the next declaration: ${list} — delete the doc comment with it`
- Out of scope: a doc that disagrees with its own declaration's text, `//` line comments, and non-JS files.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. No invariants section names these findings (the self-check findings are advisory), so docs/invariants.md is unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts. Each builds with `repoWith`, edits the worktree with `fs.writeFileSync`, and calls `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`:
- "code inserted between a doc comment and its declaration yields the detached-doc finding": base `src/a.ts` is `/** Doc A. */\nexport function a() {}\n`. Head is `/** Doc A. */\n\nfunction ins() {}\n\nexport function a() {}\n`. There is exactly one finding matching `/inserted between a doc comment/`, and it names `src/a.ts:1`.
- "a documented helper inserted under another doc also yields it": the same base, with head `/** Doc A. */\n\n/** Doc ins. */\nfunction ins() {}\n\nexport function a() {}\n`. The finding names `src/a.ts:1`.
- "a deleted declaration whose doc comment stays yields the finding": base `test/f.ts` is `/** @deprecated Use b. */\nexport const old = b;\n\nexport function c() {}\n`. Head deletes only line 2. One finding matches `/its doc comment was kept/` and names `test/f.ts:1`.
- "deleting a declaration with its doc, adding a function after a declaration, or editing a declaration line yields no detached-doc finding": three edits on the Doc A base, each giving no finding that matches either regex. (a) Delete both lines of the deprecated alias in the `test/f.ts` base. (b) Append `\n/** Doc z. */\nexport function z() {}\n` after `a`. (c) Change `export function a() {}` to `export function a(x = 1) {}`.
- "a line comment inserted between a doc and its declaration yields no finding": the head inserts `// eslint-disable-next-line no-console` between `/** Doc A. */` and `export function a() {}`. No finding matches `/inserted between a doc comment/`.
- "a detached doc in a non-JS file is not reported": the rule (1) shape in `docs/a.md` gives no detached-doc finding.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags the garbled wording a word-swap rename leaves in added lines (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts test/stage-check.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The plain-terms rename series swaps "tick" words for "run" words by rote, which leaves two kinds of garbled English that reviewers reject change after change. One is a broken past participle: an auxiliary followed by "ran" ("would have" + " ran", "has actually" + " ran"), or "ran" hyphenated onto another word ("never" + "-ran", "least-recently" + "-ran", "stale" + "-ran"). The other is "run" stacked on "run": "the run is" + " running", "a run already" + " running", "run the" + " run", "running a" + " run", "runs no" + " run". In the events log, 11 `review_rejected` events quote one of these phrases in their reasons, and ten of them are from 2026-10-20 alone (feature, feature-2, feature-4, on parts 13–15). Twelve parts of the series are still to come (16/20–20/20 and cleanup 1/7–7/7). Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue. The pre-queue self-check (`stageCheckFindings`, src/run/stage-check.ts) already gives the author one bounded fix-up turn for heuristic findings like path drift and stale names, and any finding left open still goes to the gate (run-stage.ts "…still open, queued for the gate"). So a mechanical check for these phrases can turn most of those rejections into a fix-up turn, and a false positive costs only that turn.

**Approach.**
- src/run/stage-check.ts:
  - Add `function garbledWordingFindings(diff: string): string[]`, and call it in `gitLevelFindings` right after `newlineFindings(diff)`. It reads the `-U0` diff that function already has.
  - Walk the diff by line. On `diff --git a/… b/<path>`, set the current file to `<path>`. On `@@ … +<c>[,<d>] @@`, set the next new-side line number to `c`. On a `+` line that is not a `+++ ` header, test the text after the `+`, then add 1 to the line number. Skip files where `isRecordProse(file)` holds: history in the backlog quotes old wording.
  - Use one case-insensitive pattern list, `GARBLED_WORDING`, with a doc comment saying what each pattern catches and why (rote "tick → run" swaps):
    - `/\b(?:has|have|had|having)\s+(?:\w+ly\s+|never\s+|not\s+|already\s+|just\s+)?ran\b/i`
    - `/[A-Za-z]-ran\b/i`. Keep the character class: if it were written as `\w-ran\b`, this source line would match itself.
    - `/\bruns?\s+(?:is|are|was|were|already|still)\s+(?:still\s+|already\s+)?running\b/i`
    - `/\b(?:run|runs|running)\s+(?:a|the|no)\s+run\b/i`
  - Record a hit as `<file>:<line> "<matched text>"`. Keep at most one hit per line (the first pattern that matches). The check returns at most one finding: ``added lines carry garbled rename wording (reword them; a rote "tick" → "run" swap reads wrong here): `` followed by `cappedList(hits, MAX_STALE_HITS)`.
  - In the module's top doc comment, add a sentence after the `staleNameFindings` paragraph: a fifth check, `garbledWordingFindings`, reports added lines (outside record prose) that carry the broken participles and doubled "run" wording a word-swap rename leaves. Like the path checks, the gate does not run it. Describe the phrases with ellipses (for example "has/have/had … ran"), never as a literal phrase, so the comment does not match its own check.
- No docs/invariants.md change: like the path-drift and lost-newline findings, this is a staging heuristic and not a gate guarantee (the "merge gate's deterministic rejections" section binds stage-check.ts only for the protected-edit and secret checks).

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/stage-check.test.ts, write each fixture the way "removing a file's final newline yields the finding" does: `repoWith({...})`, write the file, then `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`. Build every garbled phrase by string concatenation (for example `"would have " + "ran"`), so the test file's own lines do not match the check:
  - "added lines with a broken participle yield the garbled-wording finding": base `src/a.ts` holds `export const a = 1;\n`. Append a comment line `// the role would have ` + `ran twice` and a second line `// a never` + `-ran role`. There is exactly one finding matching `/garbled rename wording/`, and it names `src/a.ts:2` and `src/a.ts:3`.
  - "added lines that stack run on run yield the garbled-wording finding": an added `test/b.test.ts` line `assert.ok(x, "no run was ` + `running");` gives a finding that names `test/b.test.ts:1`.
  - "garbled wording in record prose, and a correct participle, yield no finding": the same broken-participle phrase added to `PLANS.md`, and a `src/a.ts` comment `// the role has run twice; it ran once today`, give no finding matching `/garbled rename wording/`.
  - "garbled wording already on the base is not reported": a base file that already holds the phrase, plus an unrelated added line elsewhere in that file, gives no garbled-wording finding.
- `grep -nE "(has|have|had|having) ran|[A-Za-z]-ran\b" src/run/stage-check.ts test/stage-check.test.ts` prints nothing. Neither file trips the new check.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `main_red`-kept change stays parked while main's new head is still red, instead of re-queuing on any move of main (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts src/runner/runner-state.ts test/merge-requeue.test.ts test/runner-state.test.ts)

**Goal.** A merge ends `main_red` when the change's check failed on tests main does not already know about and main's tip was red (`attributeRedCheck`, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts, and merge-core.ts's `gate.mainRed` branch). Both comments say the kept pin is re-merged "once main is green". But `requeueMainRedPin` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) puts the pin back on the queue on the first poll where main's head differs from `RunnerState.mainRedRetry.head`. Any merge onto a red main counts as a move, even a docs-only plan merge or a fix that does not fix, so the retry pays a full gate check (224–754 s per `main_red` attempt in the 10-18..10-20 log) and gets `main_red` again. The log shows repeat attempts on one commit: ccf1224e three times on 10-20 07:07–07:28, 313597d9 three times on 10-18 07:04–07:16, and 08eb565e, 6ac7a001 and 1fb03be5 twice each. Today those repeats come mostly from leftover recovery, which the in-flight plan "A change kept by a `main_red` merge waits for main to move…" fixes; once it lands, `requeueMainRedPin` is the only re-queue path, and its "any move" rule is what remains. The main watch (src/baseline/main-watch.ts) runs the full check on every new main head and records the verdict in the baseline cache, so the poll can ask that cache instead of guessing. This change only touches `requeueMainRedPin` and the state record, not leftover.ts, so the two plans can merge in either order.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-slot.ts:
  - Import `cachedBaselineVerdict` from `../baseline/main-baseline.js`.
  - Add `export const MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS = 15 * 60_000;` with a doc comment: the longest a kept `main_red` pin waits for the main watch's verdict on a moved head before it is re-queued anyway. This bounds the wait when no verdict ever arrives, for example after a watch check that timed out or a restart's cold cache.
  - `requeueMainRedPin` gains a trailing parameter `now = Date.now()`. Keep the early return when there is no record, `mainHead === ""`, or `mainHead === kept.head`. After it, read `const verdict = cachedBaselineVerdict(mainHead)`:
    - `"red"`: return. The record stays unchanged (original `head`, no save), so every later poll asks again, and a re-verified green for the same SHA, or a further move, releases the pin.
    - `undefined`: if `kept.waitingSince === undefined`, set `state.mainRedRetry = { ...kept, waitingSince: now }`, call `saveRunnerState(root, state)` and return. Otherwise return while `now - kept.waitingSince < MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS`. Past that, fall through.
    - `"green"`, or the wait bound passed: re-queue exactly as today (clear the record, save, `pinnedRetrySha`, skip when the role already has a queued entry, `enqueueRetry(... "main_red")`).
  - Rewrite the doc comment to describe the three outcomes. In `requeueKeptChange`'s doc, change "for requeueMainRedPin to re-queue once main moves" to "once main moves to a head whose verdict is not red".
- src/runner/runner-state.ts: `mainRedRetry` becomes `{ head: string; entry: Omit<MergeEntry, "sha">; waitingSince?: number }`. Document `waitingSince` as the ms epoch of the first poll that saw main moved with no cached verdict for its head. Update the field's doc comment: it is re-queued on the first poll whose main head differs and is not cached red, or once `MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS` has passed with no verdict. In the torn-record check, also require `s.mainRedRetry.waitingSince === undefined || typeof s.mainRedRetry.waitingSince === "number"`.
- Make the two comments that promise "once main is green" match the code: `attributeRedCheck`'s doc in src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts and the `gate.mainRed` comment in src/merge/merge-core.ts. Each should say the orchestrator poll's `requeueMainRedPin` re-queues the pin once main's head moves and the watch has not found the new head red. If the in-flight leftover plan has already rewritten `attributeRedCheck`'s sentence, extend its wording rather than replacing it.
- Out of scope: comparing the change's own failing tests with main's new failures. The record does not carry them, and a still-red main produces `main_red` again either way.

**Files touched.** src/merge/merge-slot.ts, src/runner/runner-state.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts (comment), src/merge/merge-core.ts (comment), test/merge-requeue.test.ts, test/runner-state.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/merge-requeue.test.ts "a main_red pin is re-queued once main's head moves, and not before": before the `"f".repeat(40)` call, seed a green with `noteGreenBaseline("f".repeat(40))` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts). The rest of its assertions stay as they are.
- New test "a main_red pin stays parked while main's new head is cached red": settle `main_red` as the existing test does. Seed a red for `"e".repeat(40)` by writing `baselineVerdictsPath(root)` (src/paths.ts) with `{ reds: [{ sha: "e".repeat(40), script: "test", failingTests: ["t"] }] }` and calling `persistBaselineVerdicts(root)`, as test/main-baseline-persist.test.ts "a restart reloads a saved red…" does. `requeueMainRedPin(root, "main", state, "e".repeat(40), Date.now() + 2 * MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS)` queues nothing, and `state.mainRedRetry` keeps its original `head` with no `waitingSince`.
- New test "a main_red pin waits for a moved head's verdict, then re-queues past MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS": with a head no verdict is cached for (`"d".repeat(40)`), a call at `now = 1_000` queues nothing and sets `waitingSince` to 1_000. `loadRunnerState(root, "improve").mainRedRetry?.waitingSince` is 1_000, so the value was saved. A call at `1_000 + MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS - 1` queues nothing. A call at `1_000 + MAIN_RED_VERDICT_WAIT_MS` queues one entry with `retry: "main_red"` and clears `state.mainRedRetry`.
- test/runner-state.test.ts, new test "loadRunnerState drops a mainRedRetry with a foreign-typed waitingSince", written like "loadRunnerState heals and validates the reviewResume marker" (no test covers the torn `mainRedRetry` record yet): a record whose `waitingSince` is a string reads as `undefined`, and one with a numeric `waitingSince` survives the load.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 14/20: Convert the event and report and file and text helpers (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 13/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/events/ + src/report/ + src/files/ + src/text/ + their tests + test/fakes/log.ts + test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The event readers, report fold, file helpers and text helpers use run names: `eventRun`, `runSpanMs`, `runStartMap`, `runStart` and `runEnd`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message. `normalizeLegacyEvent`'s map from `tick_*` types to `run_*` types is a legacy reader: its old names stay.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/events/ and src/files/: `eventTick` → `eventRun`, `tickSpanMs` → `runSpanMs`, `tickStartMap` → `runStartMap`, the helpers `tickStart`/`tickEnd` → `runStart`/`runEnd`, and `tickDurationMs` → `runDurationMs`, each aliased where src/history/, src/roles/ or src/ui/ still use it. Check each new name with `grep -rnw` first, because `runStart` must not collide with a local in the same module. Comments in events.ts, event-format.ts, event-read.ts, event-window.ts and notify.ts.
- src/report/ (report-data.ts, report-render.ts): locals such as `totalTicks` → `totalRuns`, and comments. The report JSON keys are Plain terms scripting's.
- src/text/ (phrases.ts, datetime.ts, text.ts, format.ts): comments.
- Tests: test/event*.test.ts, test/events.test.ts, test/notify*.test.ts, test/report*.test.ts, test/cli-logs*.test.ts, test/log-commands*.test.ts, test/datetime.test.ts, test/fakes/log.ts (`seedTickEvents` → `seedRunEvents`) and test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts.

**Files touched.** src/events/*.ts, src/report/*.ts, src/files/*.ts, src/text/*.ts, and the tests listed above.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `eventRun`, `runSpanMs`, `runStartMap`, `runStart` and `runEnd` are declared; old names survive only as aliases still used elsewhere.
- `grep -rnE '[Tt]ick[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Tick|TICK_|\bticks?\b' src/events src/report src/files src/text` lists only the legacy event-type map, aliases and serialized names.

### A change kept by a `main_red` merge waits for main to move instead of being re-queued by its author's next run (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20 feature-4's change ccf1224e went through three full gate checks against a red main in 22 minutes. Its `merge_failed main_red` events came at 07:07:06, 07:16:04 and 07:28:47, and the next attempt merged at 07:31. Each failure was followed within 2 s by a `run_start` and a `merge_queued` "recovered leftover work from feature-4: …". feature-5 (07:12, 07:22) and the 10-18 07:04–07:20 cluster (feature-2, feature-3, dedupe) show the same loop. The design already has a wait for this: `requeueKeptChange` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) records a `main_red` pin as `RunnerState.mainRedRetry = { head, entry }`, and the orchestrator poll's `requeueMainRedPin` re-queues it only once main's head differs. But `recoverLeftover` (src/runner/leftover.ts) never reads `mainRedRetry`. The author's next run, which starts at once because roles keep authoring while main's red names its failing tests, finds the pin with nothing queued and enqueues it straight away, against the same red head. The two comments that promise a wait are wrong today: `attributeRedCheck`'s doc comment (src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts) says "recovery re-merges it once main-red.ts's repair turns main green", and `gateBuildPrecheck`'s main-red branch (src/review/review-precheck.ts) says "the author's next tick re-merges the change once main is green again".

**Approach.**
- src/runner/leftover.ts:
  - `LeftoverContext` gains `mainRedRetry?: RunnerState["mainRedRetry"]`, documented as the record of a `main_red` pin waiting for `requeueMainRedPin`.
  - `LeftoverRecovery` gains `| { kind: "main_red_wait"; sha: string; message: string }`.
  - In `recoverLeftover`, put the new check right after the `reviewHold` check, so the stale and dangling pin drops still run first. When `ctx.mainRedRetry` is set, return `{ kind: "main_red_wait", sha, message: \`kept change ${shortSha(sha)} waits for main to move past red ${shortSha(ctx.mainRedRetry.head)} before its next merge\` }`. Nothing is enqueued and the pin is kept. Add a comment saying that `requeueMainRedPin` owns this re-queue and why: re-queuing against the same red head pays a full gate check whose result is already known.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: pass `mainRedRetry: s.mainRedRetry` in the `recoverLeftover({...})` call. The new kind reaches `ctx.finishRecoveryRun` through the existing `else if (recovered)` arm, so that arm needs no change.
- src/runner/runner-recovery.ts `finishRecoveryRunPhase`: add a branch after the `held` one. When `recovered.kind === "main_red_wait"`, set `ctx.state.lastError = recovered.message` and return `{ result: "main_red", summary: recovered.message, error: recovered.message, recoveredLeftover: true }`. Do not reset the worktree. `main_red` schedules on the idle ladder (the final `else` in src/run/run-apply.ts). The role's status reads "main red" through `heldByMainRed` (src/status/status-polls.ts), and the run's cause is itemized like the authoring gate's `main_red` (INV-C1). Do not use `error`: that would put a wait on the error ladder and count it as a failure.
- No change to `requeueMainRedPin`. It still clears the record and enqueues the entry under its original summary once main's head moves. After that, the role's next run sees `already_queued`, as it does today. If the poll finds the pin gone, the record is cleared, so recovery goes back to its normal path.
- Make the two comments match the code: in `attributeRedCheck`'s doc and `gateBuildPrecheck`'s main-red comment, say the kept pin is re-queued by the orchestrator poll (`requeueMainRedPin`) once main's head moves, and leftover recovery holds it until then.
- Out of scope: waiting for a green verdict rather than any move of main's head. The baseline cache (`cachedBaselineVerdict`, src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) is per process and often has no verdict for a new head yet, so that would be a separate change.

**Files touched.** src/runner/leftover.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/runner/runner-recovery.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts (comment), src/review/review-precheck.ts (comment), test/leftover.test.ts, test/runner-recovery.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/leftover.test.ts, new test "a pin waiting on a main_red retry is held, not re-queued": pin a commit as the existing "a pinned commit not in main is put on the merge queue, not merged" test does. Call `recoverLeftover` with `mainRedRetry: { head: <main's sha>, entry: { role, run: 1, summary: "x", enqueuedAt: 0 } }`. It returns kind `main_red_wait` with the pinned sha, and its message contains `waits for main to move past red`. `queuedMerges(root)` is empty, the merge ref still points at the sha, and no `merge_queued` event is logged. The same call without `mainRedRetry` returns `enqueued`.
- test/leftover.test.ts: with `mainRedRetry` set and a pin that main already contains, the stale pin is still deleted and the call returns null.
- test/runner-recovery.test.ts, beside "finishRecoveryRunPhase ends error on a held pin and keeps its message": a new test "finishRecoveryRunPhase ends main_red on a pin waiting for main to move". The outcome's `result` is `main_red`, its `summary` and `error` are the message, `recoveredLeftover` is true, `state.lastError` is the message, and the worktree reset is not called.
- The existing test/merge-requeue.test.ts test "a main_red pin is re-queued once main's head moves, and not before" passes unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The gate stops rejecting a change for a test that its base commit already failed and main has fixed since (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/review/review-precheck.ts, which the blocked Plain terms code run part 18/20 also edits; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20, between 07:31 and 07:36 UTC, three changes were rejected for one test that their own diffs did not touch: feature (ab6d53e2), feature-2 (c671a472) and feature-5 (08eb565e). Each rejection had 13 reasons, all "check failed (`npm run test:gate`): ✖ report --role takes a comma list and sums the listed roles". Main 13c3c497 was red on that test (`main_red_hold` 07:16). Bugfix's "Make the report --role comma-list test immune to the midnight hour" merged at 07:26, so main's tip a23befe4 was green. The three branches still sat on the red base, so their gate check failed the old test twice. `gateBuildPrecheck` (src/review/review-precheck.ts) then asks only main's tip: `mainTipVerdict(..., true)` returned green, so the failure was blamed on the change and went through `reject`. Main's known-failure excuse (`onlyKnownMainFailures`, src/baseline/main-watch.ts) did not help either. The watch's newest verdict was the green tip, so the known list was empty. The verdict that answers the question is the one for the change's base, and the baseline cache already holds it: the main watch recorded 13c3c497 red, with its `failingTests`.

**Approach.** Only src/review/review-precheck.ts.
- Add a module-private `async function staleBaseFailures(wt: string, mainBranch: string, head: string, mainTip: string, failingTests: readonly string[] | undefined): Promise<{ base: string; tests: string[] } | null>`:
  - Return null when `failingTests` is empty or undefined, or its length is at least `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` (src/build/build-check-report.ts). A list that long may have been cut short, which is the same rule `onlyKnownMainFailures` uses.
  - Take `base = await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch, head)` (src/git/git.ts). Return null when `base === mainTip`, because then the tip verdict already judged the same base.
  - Take `verdict = await watchedBaseline(wt, base)` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts). That is the cached verdict for the base or its nearest first-parent ancestor, and it runs nothing. Return null unless `verdict?.status === "red"` and every failing test is in `verdict.failingTests ?? []`. Otherwise return `{ base, tests: [...failingTests] }`.
  - Wrap the body in try/catch and return null on a throw, so a git problem falls back to today's attribution.
- In `gateBuildPrecheck`, in the main-green branch (after the `main.status === "red"` block, before the `return { resolved: await reject(...) }`), add: when `main.status === "green"`, call `staleBaseFailures(wt, mainBranch, head, main.sha, outcome.failingTests)`. When it returns a result, `warnEventBestEffort(root, role, \`gate check fails only tests its base ${shortSha(base)} already failed, and main ${shortSha(main.sha)} is green: ${tests.join(", ")}; going on to review\`)` and `return { knownMainFailures: tests }`. This is the same hand-off the known-failure branch uses: no `verifiedHead`, so nothing seeds a green. The merge path rebases onto main, and its own merge check judges the rebased tree. If that tree still fails, `attributeRedCheck` sees a green main and rejects as it does today. ### docs/invariants.md gains a backlog-archive section, so a fixer touching the archive sweep reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. They go above the archive's existing entries, in their live order. Entries the base already held stay in the live section. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". ### A commit body's WHY, RISK and VERIFIED lines are kept whole up to 1000 characters, so a reviewer stops rejecting a change because the harness cut its own RISK line mid-sentence (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/git/commit-message.ts and test/commit-message.test.ts, which no Planned entry names; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `extractCommitBody` (src/git/commit-message.ts) caps each of WHY, RISK and VERIFIED at `COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX = 200` characters with `truncate`, which ends a cut line with "…". At that size the cap cuts ordinary answers, not just verbose ones. In the 1306 commits on main since 2026-10-13, 1554 of the 3741 `WHY:`/`RISK:`/`VERIFIED:` lines end in "…". 1344 of them are exactly 200 characters long and 210 are 199 (`truncate` trims a trailing space before the ellipsis). Reviewers read that commit message and reject the change over it. Between 2026-10-19 08:58 and 2026-10-20 00:57 UTC there were seven `review_rejected` reasons from feature-3 and feature-5 like "WHY, RISK and VERIFIED each end mid-sentence with "…" in the commit message itself" and "the RISK list stops at `` (`src/… ``". They came from Plain-terms parts whose series rules ask for any leftover name to be listed in the commit message. The author cannot fix this in a revision: each new round truncates the line again. The cap exists so that a verbose model cannot bloat every commit. 1000 characters still does that job and fits a full list of leftovers.

**Approach.**
- **src/git/commit-message.ts.** Set `COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX` to `1000`. Reword its doc comment to give the reason: the cap only bounds a runaway reply, and at 200 it cut almost half of all body lines, which reviewers rejected as incomplete claims. Change "capped at 200 chars" in `extractCommitBody`'s doc comment to name the constant. Leave the rest as it is: `truncate` still cuts a field that is over the cap. `parseCommitMetadata` re-extracts the body through `extractCommitBody`, so leftover recovery reads a whole field back under the same cap. Leave `COMMIT_SUMMARY_MAX`, `summaryOverCap` and `SUMMARY_BLOCK` (src/verdict/reply-contract.ts) alone. This plan adds no follow-up turn for an over-long body field.
- **test/commit-message.test.ts.** Rename "extractCommitBody caps each field at 200 chars with an ellipsis" to "extractCommitBody caps each field at 1000 chars with an ellipsis". Feed it a 1500-character WHY, and assert the result is exactly 1000 characters long, ends in "…", and leaves RISK untouched. Add "extractCommitBody keeps a 600-character field whole": a 600-character RISK made of words and spaces comes back unchanged, with no "…".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n 'COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX = ' src/git/commit-message.ts` shows `1000`. `grep -rn '200 chars' src/git/commit-message.ts` finds nothing.
- Both tests named above pass. Every other test in test/commit-message.test.ts passes without edits, including "extractCommitBody pulls all three fields, trimmed" and "extractCommitBody tolerates any subset and returns null when none are present".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### docs/invariants.md gains a fallback-breaker section, so a fixer touching the breaker reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The fallback breaker (src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts) decides whether the engaged free fallback is still allowed to serve. That register exists so a fixer reads a subsystem's contract before changing its code. Without a section, a breaker fix has no guarantee to check against, and a change that breaks one is caught only if its test happens to fail. This plan adds the section. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after `## Main's red culprit`. Title it `## The fallback breaker: a free fallback that cannot serve is demoted, not retried forever`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intros under `## Bounded waits…` and `## Hermetic, deterministic gating tests`). Use the next free letter, `M`; `grep -n 'INV-M' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first.
- Add three entries. Each has **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.**, matching the existing entries. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions' doc comments and the cited tests. State only what the code does: if a detail below turns out wrong, correct the sentence to match the code rather than the plan.
  - `### INV-M1: consecutive fallback failures demote the fallback, and a demoted fallback admits one probe run per cool-down`. Guarantee: `FALLBACK_BREAKER_POLICY.failureLimit` consecutive `error` outcomes on an engaged fallback pair demote it. The count is team-wide; any served run in between resets the streak. While the pair is demoted, `fallbackServing` is false and roles on it are paused. After the cool-down, exactly one probe run is admitted while other due roles wait. A served probe closes the breaker. A failed probe re-opens it with the cool-down doubled, capped at `maxCooldownMs`. A probe that never ran, or produced no evidence, hands its slot back. Binds: src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts (`fallbackServing`, `fallbackProbeDue`, `startFallbackProbe`, `abandonFallbackProbe`), src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts.   - `### INV-M2: a change of subject re-trusts the fallback`. Guarantee: editing the cap, changing the fallback pair, or the gate leaving the fallback (local midnight) replaces a demoted breaker with a fresh, trusted one on the next poll. ### The pre-queue self-check flags a finished entry that the archive already holds under another done date, so a revision stops being rejected for leaving the same plan twice in PLANS-DONE.md or in both PLANS.md and its archive (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, which the in-flight stale-name self-check plan also edits; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Between 2026-10-19 08:58 and 2026-10-20 13:22 UTC, seven `review_rejected` events from feature instances were for one finished entry recorded twice. Three examples: "`PLANS-DONE.md` now has the same plan entry twice. Line 8 says "done 2026-10-20 by the feature role" and line 23 says "done 2026-10-19 by the feature role"" (feature, 10-20 07:38); "`PLANS-DONE.md` has the "Pi built-in image capability, part 2/2" entry twice (lines 8 and 38), left over from this revision's `PLANS.md` conflict resolution" (feature-2, 07:40); "The finished plan entry "A window move's runs feed the fallback breaker…" appears in both `PLANS.md` `## Done` and `PLANS-DONE.md`, and the two copies disagree" (feature-2, 13:22). Each one cost a review round and a revision. Today's guards miss both shapes because they compare whole headings (src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts `archiveKey`, src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts `readdedHeadings`):
- A revision re-finishes its plan with a new `done` date. The heading differs from the archived copy's, so the commit-time sweep (`archiveNewFinishedEntries`, called in src/run/run-stage.ts after the self-check) moves it as a new entry, and `readdedHeadings` sees no repeat.
- The heading matches but the text differs. `entryFates` then gives the entry the `stay` fate, which is by design: the sweep leaves it in `PLANS.md ## Done` for the reviewer to see, and the reviewer rejects it.

The self-check runs before the sweep, while the author can still fix the change in one fix-up turn, so it is the place to catch both.

**Approach.** Only src/run/stage-check.ts.
- Add `finishedKey(title: string, dateRe: RegExp): string`, which returns `collapseWhitespace(finishedTitle(title, dateRe))`. `finishedTitle` is in src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts and `collapseWhitespace` is in src/text/text.ts. The key drops the completion stamp and the `(planned …)`/`(found …)` parenthetical, so "X (planned …; done 2026-10-19 …)" and "X (planned …; done 2026-10-20 …)" key equal. It also handles a heading whose done date wraps onto the next line: an unclosed `(` is cut.
- Add the exported pure function `finishedDuplicateFindings(spec: FinishedArchive, live: { head: string; base: string }, archive: { head: string; base: string }): string[]`. `FinishedArchive` comes from src/backlog/backlog-md.ts. Use `DONE_DATE_RE` for PLANS.md and `FIXED_DATE_RE` for BUGS.md (both from src/backlog/backlog.ts). Read entries with `parseEntryDetails(md, spec.section)`. It returns at most one finding per rule:
  - **Live copy of an archived entry.** Find the first entry under the head live file's `spec.section` whose key is (1) absent from the base live file's `spec.section` keys and (2) held by an entry under the head archive's `spec.section`. Skip it when one of those archived entries has the same whitespace-collapsed heading and the same `body`, because the sweep drops that exact copy (`drop` fate). Wording: `` `${spec.file}`'s "## ${spec.section}" entry "${truncate(title, 160)}" is already archived in ${spec.archive} — the commit-time sweep would leave two copies; edit the archived entry in place (its text and its stamp) and delete this copy ``.
  - **Second archive copy.** Find the first key whose count under the head archive's `spec.section` is above 1 and above its count in the base archive. Skip this rule when `readdedHeadings(archive.base, archive.head)` is non-empty, because `backlogStructureReason` already reports that case. Wording: `` `${spec.archive} holds "${truncate(title, 160)}" ${n} times — this change added a copy under a different heading or stamp; keep the archived entry once, edited in place, and delete the other copies` ``. Use the first head copy's title. `truncate` comes from src/text/text.ts.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the `PLANS.md` dependency block, loop over `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts). For each `spec` where `files` includes `spec.file` or `spec.archive`, read both heads with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, …)) ?? ""` and both bases with `fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), …)`. Wrap the whole block in `.catch(() => [])`, matching the module's rule that a git hiccup yields no finding. Push the returned findings.
- Add a sentence to the module header comment: like `planDependencyFinding`, `finishedDuplicateFindings` runs only at staging. The gate does not run it, because the sweep that creates the second copy runs after it.
- Out of scope: changing the sweep's `archiveKey` or `entryFates` (an edited archived entry legitimately stays visible to the reviewer), and repairing duplicates already on main. Checked 2026-10-20: PLANS-DONE.md has none under this key, and BUGS-FIXED.md has one pair, which the base-count comparison never flags.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts:
- A unit test, "finishedDuplicateFindings flags a re-finished plan that the archive holds under another done date", calls `finishedDuplicateFindings(FINISHED_ARCHIVES[0], …)` on hand-built markdown. The head PLANS.md `## Done` holds "### X (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)" with some body. The base live file is empty. Both the head and base archives hold "### X (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)" with another body. Exactly one finding matches `/PLANS\.md's "## Done" entry "X .*" is already archived in PLANS-DONE\.md/`.
- In the same test: when the live copy has the archived copy's exact heading and body, the result is `[]`. When the base live file already had X under `## Done`, the result is `[]`.
- "finishedDuplicateFindings flags a second archive copy under a new stamp, and leaves an exact re-paste to the structure check": the head archive holds X twice with two different done dates, and the base holds it once. Exactly one finding matches `/PLANS-DONE\.md holds "X .*" 2 times/`. A head that adds an exact copy of the base heading gives `[]`. A base that already held two copies and a head that still holds two gives `[]`.
- A BUGS.md case: a head `## Fixed` entry "### Y (found by the qa role 2026-10-18) — fixed 2026-10-20 by the bugfix role", while BUGS-FIXED.md holds Y "— fixed 2026-10-19 by the bugfix role". It yields the live-copy finding naming BUGS-FIXED.md.
- An integration test, "a re-finished plan the archive already holds yields the finished-duplicate finding". It is built with `repoWith` like "a duplicated ## Done heading yields the structure finding". The repo commits PLANS.md (empty `## Done`) and PLANS-DONE.md holding X under `## Done`. The worktree pastes X with a new done date into PLANS.md `## Done`. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` returns exactly one finding, the live-copy one.
- The existing stage-check tests pass unedited, including "a duplicated ## Done heading yields the structure finding" and "a clean change yields no findings".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 12/20: Rename the scheduler's deferral and wake names and convert the gates (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 11/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/scheduling/ + src/gates/ + their tests + test/fixtures/gate-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The scheduler and the gates use run names: `deferRun`, `deferRunReason`, `restoreMidRunWake` and `runOnPair`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/scheduling/: `deferTick` → `deferRun` and `deferTickReason` → `deferRunReason`, both aliased (orchestrator, roles and tests use them); `restoreMidTickWake` → `restoreMidRunWake`; the `exitReady` argument members `roleTicks` → `roleRuns` and `directorTicks` → `directorRuns` (rename the call in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts too); the local `tickSnapshots` → `runSnapshots`. Comments in scheduling.ts, backoff.ts, once-round.ts, claims.ts, quiet-hours.ts and the work-merged cache module ("the min-tick-interval clock" → "the min-run-interval clock").
- src/gates/: `tickOnPair` → `runOnPair` (aliased if src/budget still uses it); comments in gate-polls.ts, budget-gates.ts, streak-gate.ts, pause-gates.ts, maintenance-quota.ts, startup-gate.ts, role-cap-gates.ts, disk-gate.ts and bootstrap-gates.ts.
- Tests: test/scheduling.test.ts (about 90 lines), test/once-round.test.ts, test/backoff.test.ts, test/claims.test.ts, test/quiet-hours.test.ts, test/gate-polls.test.ts, test/gate-event-best-effort.test.ts, test/streak-gate.test.ts, test/maintenance-quota.test.ts, test/disk-gate.test.ts, test/role-cap-gates.test.ts, test/pause-gates.test.ts, test/bootstrap-gates.test.ts, test/startup-gate.test.ts and test/fixtures/gate-fixtures.ts.
