### A window move's runs feed the fallback breaker, so a dead window fallback is demoted and its tier held instead of failing every run until the window resets (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** At 06:11 UTC on 2026-10-20 the claude usage window ran out, and `fallback_switched` (reason `window`) moved the small, default and strong tiers to `qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b`. That endpoint was down. For the next 29 minutes the moved runs kept failing with "Connection error.", and the team-wide `rate_limit_hold` on `qwenrunner` escalated through holds of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 minutes. The tiers stayed on that step until the window reset at 06:40 (`fallback_switched` reason `available`). The fallback breaker (src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts) exists to demote a free fallback whose runs keep failing, then let a probe through after a cool-down. But it only learns from runs made while the daily cap is reached. In `launchDueRuns` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts), `ranPair` is non-null only when `budgetActive`. The input's own doc comment gives the reason: "only a budget hold puts role runs on fallback pairs". A window move below the cap also puts role runs on fallback pairs, so its runs never reach the breaker. Every price-free chain step already has a breaker entry (`chainPairs` in `pollBudgetGate`, src/gates/budget-gates.ts), and the `chain` block already resolves through `servingResolved`. A demotion would therefore already log `fallback_switched` with reason `demoted`. The only missing pieces are the evidence and the per-tier hold.

**Approach.**
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts, `pollTeamGates`: compute `windowMovedRoles`. It is the set of non-director runners whose `roleSeamTier(liveConfig, r.role)` is a key of the budget gate's `windowTiers`, and it is empty while `windowTiers` is empty. A role whose own seam is not claude (pinned to another model) keeps its model through the move, so it is left out. Return it beside `budgetActive`, with a doc comment on the result type: the roles a window move put on a fallback pair, whose run outcomes fold into the breaker even below the cap.
- In the same function, extend the `budgetPausedRoles` loop. Today it runs only `if (budgetActive)`. Keep that branch as it is, and add an `else` branch: a role in `windowMovedRoles` whose `servingResolved[roleSeamTier(liveConfig, r.role)].pair === null` joins `budgetPausedRoles`. Below the cap a role on an unmoved tier is never added. The scheduling pass already folds `budgetPausedRoles` and lets `probeRoles` pierce it (`pollDeferralInputs` and the `budgetPausedRoles.has(role) && !probeRoles.has(role)` check in src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts), so the probe needs no change. Update the `budgetPausedRoles` doc comment to cover the window case.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts: add `windowMovedRoles: ReadonlySet<string>` to `LaunchContext` beside `budgetActive`. Change the `ranPair` condition to `(budgetActive || windowMovedRoles.has(runner.role)) && cfg?.model !== undefined`, and leave the rest of the fold unchanged. A pair with no breaker entry is still skipped by `ranOn !== undefined`. Update the `budgetActive` doc comment, which says only a budget hold puts runs on fallback pairs. src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts passes `gates.windowMovedRoles` next to `gates.budgetActive`.
- Out of scope: `reviewStrongPaused` stays cap-only, so a demoted strong window step still serves the reviewer until the window resets. Leave the breaker's rekey and policy, `budget_paused`/`budget_fallback` (cap-only events) and the hand-back alone.

**Files touched.** src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, test/gate-polls.test.ts, test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/gate-polls.test.ts, "pollTeamGates: a used-up window's demoted fallback holds the moved tier's roles below the cap". Set it up like "a used-up claude window moves claude roles to the fallback and hands them back at the reset": `writeClaudeAccount` with a rejected `five_hour` window, a claude tier, a free fallback, and spend under the cap. Seed `states.budget.breakers[<fallback pair>]` as demoted (`failures: 3, probeAt: <now + 60_000>`), the way "budgetPausedRoles holds the tiers that resolved to pause…" seeds its breaker. Assert that the moved role is in `windowMovedRoles` and in `budgetPausedRoles`, and that the director is in neither. With the breaker entry trusted (`IDLE_FALLBACK_BREAKER`), the moved role is in `windowMovedRoles` but not in `budgetPausedRoles`. With no used-up window, `windowMovedRoles` is empty.
- New e2e test in test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts, "a window move's failing fallback is demoted and its tier held, below the cap". Model it on "a free fallback whose ticks keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves". Use a tier `{ provider: "claude", model: "claude-opus-5-5" }`, the fallback `local/local-free` (failing until `healed`), a cap that is never reached, and a rejected `five_hour` window written with `writeClaudeAccount`. Use `fallbackBreakerPolicy: { failureLimit: 2, cooldownMs: 1500, maxCooldownMs: 1500 }`. Assert that after two failed fallback runs a `fallback_switched` event with a tier `to: null` appears (reason `demoted` needs a further chain step: with a lone fallback the tier resolves to no pair, so the event reads `to: null`) and no further role run starts while demoted. After `healed` is written, one probe run on `model=local-free` serves and the tier is back on the fallback. If startup refuses because the claude binary is missing, put the fake claude from test/orchestrator-mixed.e2e.test.ts on PATH. The moved roles never run on it.
- The existing tests "a free fallback whose ticks keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves" and "budgetPausedRoles holds the tiers that resolved to pause, and every demotion is published" pass unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The invariants register's guard checks each quoted test title against the cited test file, so a renamed test can no longer leave a **Pinned by.** citation pointing at nothing (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches test/invariants-doc.test.ts and docs/invariants.md; a Plain terms part that also edits docs/invariants.md only rebases) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** docs/invariants.md's "Keep it honest" paragraph promises that "a stale citation is a visible broken link, not silent drift". `invariantProblems` (test/invariants-doc.test.ts) keeps that promise only for paths: it reports a missing field, a malformed or duplicate id and a cited path that does not exist. It never reads the quoted test titles that each **Pinned by.** field names after its `test/*.test.ts` path, and the tick→run renames have already broken two of them. INV-C1 quotes "a main_red tick's cause is clustered with the tick errors, not left a bare count", but test/failure-render.test.ts now titles that case "a main_red tick's cause is clustered with the run errors, not left a bare count". INV-J1 quotes "a blind image read fails the tick with an error naming the file and the model", but test/run-verdict.test.ts now says "fails the run". The remaining Plain terms parts rename many more test titles, so a guard is needed before more citations drift.

**Approach.** Test file and doc only. No src change.
- In test/invariants-doc.test.ts, add `TITLE_RE`, which matches a `test(`, `it(` or `describe(` call (optionally `.skip`/`.only`/`.todo`) whose first argument is a `"…"`, `'…'` or `` `…` `` literal, and `testTitles(source: string): string[]`, which returns each title with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. A template-literal title keeps its `${…}` placeholders. test/run-stage.test.ts titles its cases `` `a commit made in the ${label} follow-up folds into the harness commit` ``, and INV-H1 cites two expansions of that title.
- Add `titleMatches(cited: string, title: string): boolean`. It returns true when the two are equal. It also returns true when `cited` ends with `…` and `title` starts with the text before the ellipsis, because INV-L1 cites "a named culprit is reverted on main…". Finally, it returns true when `title` has `${…}` placeholders and `cited` matches the title with each placeholder read as a non-empty wildcard (the literal parts regex-escaped and the match anchored at both ends).
- Add `citedTitles(pinned: string): { file: string; title: string }[]` over the text from `**Pinned by.**` to the entry's end. Scan it with one alternation, `` /`([^`]*)`|"([^"]+)"/g ``. A backtick code span is consumed whole: if it is a `test/….test.ts` path it becomes the current file, otherwise it is skipped. This keeps the quotes inside a span such as INV-A4's `` `helpTopic("config")` `` from counting as a title. A `"…"` quote after a current file is a cited title, with its whitespace collapsed, since titles wrap across doc lines. A quote before any test path is ignored.
- `invariantProblems` takes an optional `readTest: (rel: string) => string | undefined`, which defaults to reading `path.join(ROOT, rel)` and returning `undefined` when the file is missing. For each cited title whose file reads, and where no `testTitles` entry satisfies `titleMatches`, it pushes `` `${label}: cited test title not found in ${file}: "${title}"` ``. A missing file is already reported by the path check, so no title problem is added for it.
- Fix the citations that the new check finds in docs/invariants.md, using the titles the tests carry when the change is made. Today those are the INV-C1 and INV-J1 citations quoted above. Run the guard to get the current list, because an in-flight Plain terms part may rename more.
- Extend the "Keep it honest" paragraph in docs/invariants.md by one sentence: each title quoted after a cited test path must name a test in that file, and a trailing `…` cites by prefix.

**Files touched.** test/invariants-doc.test.ts, docs/invariants.md.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/invariants-doc.test.ts, built with the file's `register`/`entry` helpers or with hand-built markdown as "a test path cited outside **Pinned by.** does not satisfy the pin check" does, and passing a `readTest` stub so no fixture file is written:
- "a quoted title that no test in the cited file carries is reported": the stub serves `test("the real title", …)`, and the entry cites "the old title". There is exactly one problem, and it names the entry, the file and "the old title". Citing "the real title" yields `[]`.
- "a wrapped, truncated or template-expanded citation matches its test": a citation split across two lines matches. A citation of "the real…" matches `test("the real title", …)`. A citation of "a commit made in the missing-SUMMARY follow-up folds" matches `` test(`a commit made in the ${label} follow-up folds`, …) ``, and a citation of "a commit made in the  follow-up folds" (empty placeholder) does not.
- "quotes inside a code span and before any test path are not titles": a **Pinned by.** field reading `` `test/x.test.ts` — "the real title" (reads `helpTopic("config")`) `` yields `[]`. So does a quote placed before the first test path.
- The existing test "this repo's docs/invariants.md is honest" passes against the corrected doc, with its assertion unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a removed identifier that a comment or doc still names, so a rename stops being rejected for a comment pointing at a name that no longer exists (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts; a blocked Plain terms part that also edits them only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** In the 48 hours to 13:15 UTC on 2026-10-20 there were 205 `review_rejected` events. Several were for a leftover name that a mechanical check could have caught before the change queued. Two from 2026-10-20: "`src/run/run-timing.ts:233` still says `tickStartHeld`, which this change renamed to `runStartHeld`" (feature-2, 11:45), and "`src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts:91` … still says … `abortedTicks`. The field the redeployer emits is `abortedRuns`" (feature-2, 11:56). The 11:52 review of the same change rejected it for "a comment points at a name that no longer exists". The compiler catches code that still uses a removed name, but nothing catches a comment, an assertion message or a doc that still names it. Each one costs a gate check, a review and a revision. The pre-queue self-check (`stageCheckFindings`, src/run/stage-check.ts) already does this for paths: `staleReferenceFindings` reports a renamed or deleted path that is still named in the tree, and `requestStageFix` (src/run/run-stage.ts) gives the author one fix-up turn while its session is still open. This plan adds the same check for identifiers.

**Approach.** Only src/run/stage-check.ts.
- Add `staleNameFindings(wt: string, diff: string): Promise<string[]>`. Call it from `gitLevelFindings` on the `-U0` cached diff that function already computes, after `newlineFindings`. It is best-effort like its siblings: a git failure contributes nothing.
- Candidates: walk the diff, tracking the current file from `+++ ` headers as `missingPathFindings` does. Removed lines start with `-` but not `---`. A removed line belongs to the file named by the b-path of the last `diff --git a/<x> b/<y>` header. That path is used rather than `+++ `, which reads `/dev/null` for a deleted file, and only its extension matters. Only removed lines in `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js` and `.mjs` files count. Take the names declared there with an exported `declaredNames(line: string): string[]`, which uses two patterns:
  - keyword declarations `\b(?:function\*?|const|let|var|class|interface|type|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)`;
  - property or field signatures at the start of the line, `^\s*(?:(?:readonly|public|private|protected|static)\s+)*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\??\s*:`.

  Keep a name only if it is compound, so common words never count: it contains a lowercase letter followed by an uppercase letter (`tickStartHeld`, `RunnerState`), or it is UPPER_SNAKE with at least one underscore (`MAX_STALE_HITS`). Drop every name that `declaredNames` also finds on an added `+` line anywhere in the diff, because the change re-declared it, for example by moving it. Cap the candidate set at `MAX_STALE_NAMES = 40` in first-appearance order.
- One `gitTry(wt, "grep", "-n", "-w", "-I", "--cached", "-e", n1, "-e", n2, …)` call covers every candidate. Attribute each hit line to the candidates it contains as a whole word. A candidate is still live, and is dropped, when any hit line in a `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` file declares it according to `declaredNames`. Another module may still own the name. For each remaining candidate, keep the hits that pass all three filters:
  - the file is not record prose (`isRecordProse`);
  - the line does not carry `retired-name-ok`;
  - the occurrence is not inside a `"…"` or `'…'` string literal. Legacy-name tables and serialized keys spell old names as strings on purpose. Backticked names in comments and markdown still count.
- Emit one finding per name, at most `MAX_STALE_PATHS` names and `MAX_STALE_HITS` hits each, worded like the path finding: `` `tickStartHeld` was removed by this change but is still named at: src/run/run-timing.ts:233 ``. Use `cappedList` for the hits.
- Extend the module's header comment (the "Part 2/2 appends git-level … findings" paragraph) with this fourth check and the reasons for its exemptions.
- Out of scope:
  - test titles that docs quote (docs/invariants.md citations are test/invariants-doc.test.ts's concern);
  - non-JS languages;
  - the review gate (like the other git-level checks, this one is a staging-time heuristic and the gate does not run it).

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts, built with `repoWith` and `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` like "a remaining reference to a renamed path yields the stale-reference finding":
- "a comment still naming a renamed function yields the stale-name finding": `src/a.ts` holds `export function tickStartHeld() {}` and `src/b.ts` holds `// see tickStartHeld\n`. The worktree renames the function to `runStartHeld` in a.ts. Exactly one finding matches `` /`tickStartHeld` was removed by this change but is still named at: src\/b\.ts:1/ ``. Updating the comment as well leaves `[]`.
- "a removed interface field still named in a doc yields the finding": the field `abortedTicks: number;` is renamed in an interface, and README.md still names it. The finding names README.md.
- "a removed name that is still declared elsewhere, quoted as a string, marked retired-name-ok or named in record prose yields no stale-name finding": four sub-cases, each giving `[]`. In the first, the name is still declared in another src file. In the second, the remaining hit is `"tickStartHeld"` in a string. In the third, the hit line carries `// retired-name-ok: …`. In the fourth, the hit is in PLANS.md.
- "a removed single-word name is never a candidate": removing `const status = 1;` while a comment says "status" gives `[]`.
- A `declaredNames` unit test covers `export const FOO_BAR`, `async function fooBar(`, `interface FooBar {`, `  readonly fooBar?: string;`, and a call line `fooBar(x);`, which yields nothing.
- The existing stale-reference, missing-path and newline tests pass unedited. So does "the git-level check leaves the index clean, so change detection still sees the worktree".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI's per-key editor guards ask the session's held registry instead of hand-listing editors, so a newly added editor can no longer be typed over by Ctrl+P/A/W/V, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+N or Ctrl+E (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `createTuiEditorSession` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`) already keeps a registry of which editors hold the prompt line: `heldEditorFlash` walks the six special holders plus `HOLDER_SUBJECTS`, and `anyEditorHeld` wraps it. Five key-entry guards still list `!session.held.<x>` flags by hand, though, and each list has fallen behind the editors added since it was written:
- `createPauseEditor`'s per-role Ctrl+P/A/W/V arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`) and `createPromptEditor`'s Ctrl+R arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-prompt.ts`) run on the transcript views. Neither checks `held.instances`, even though `createInstancesEditor`'s Ctrl+G opens on those same views. With the instances editor open, Ctrl+P therefore opens the pause editor on top of it, and Ctrl+R opens the role-prompt editor on top of it. The pause arm also skips `attach`, `brief`, `providerCaps`, `slots`, `backends`, `fallback`, `model` and `claudeReserve`. The prompt arm also skips `retire`, `attach`, `brief`, `providerCaps`, `slots`, `fallback`, `model` and `claudeReserve`.
- The answer editor's Ctrl+A arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-answer.ts`), the entry editor's new-entry Ctrl+N arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-entry.ts`) and the queued editor's Ctrl+E arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-queued.ts`) each check at most eight holders.

Every new editor plan has had to find and patch these lists. Reviewer rejections in the 24 hours to 13:00 UTC 2026-10-20 include "missed this sibling" findings of exactly this kind: a `held.slots` or `held.concurrency` left out of some guards but added to others.

**Approach.**
- **`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`**: widen `anyEditorHeld(except?: "pause")` to `anyEditorHeld(...except: ReadonlyArray<"pause" | "rolePromptFor" | "search">)`. It returns true when any holder `heldEditorFlash` checks is set and is not named in `except`. The holders are `search`, `pause`, `queued`, `answer`, `entry`, `rolePromptFor` and every `HOLDER_SUBJECTS` mode. Implement it as its own walk over those flags, so `heldEditorFlash`'s ordering and wording stay unchanged. The existing `anyEditorHeld()` / `anyEditorHeld("pause")` call sites keep their meaning. `quietTeam` and the `pauseEdit*` fields are sub-state, not holders, and stay out. Update its doc comment.
- **`tui-editor-pause.ts`**: replace the per-role arm's hand list with `!session.anyEditorHeld("rolePromptFor", "search")`. Role prompt and search stay excepted because the arm deliberately still lets Ctrl+P resume a paused role and Ctrl+A/Ctrl+V act while they are held, and its inner branches already flash `busyFlash("role prompt"/"search")` for the editor-opening cases. Leave those inner branches as they are.
- **`tui-editor-prompt.ts`**: replace the Ctrl+R arm's list with `!session.anyEditorHeld("rolePromptFor")`. A second Ctrl+R still has to reach the arm to exit role-prompt mode.
- **`tui-editor-answer.ts`, `tui-editor-entry.ts`** (the new-entry branch only, after the existing plan↔bug flip branch), **`tui-editor-queued.ts`**: replace each list with `!session.anyEditorHeld()`. In the entry and queued arms, the module-local `entryEditFor`/`queuedEditFor` checks are mirrored in `session.held.entry`/`session.held.queued`, so the registry covers them.
- A blocked key keeps today's behaviour at every site: the arm returns false and the key falls through. No new flash is added.
- Out of scope: `onArrow`'s history-recall list in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`. It deliberately leaves out holders such as `rolePromptFor`, whose mode keeps its own recall pair, so it is not the same guard.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`, `tui-editor-pause.ts`, `tui-editor-prompt.ts`, `tui-editor-answer.ts`, `tui-editor-entry.ts`, `tui-editor-queued.ts`; tests in `test/tui-instances.test.ts` (the fixture `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` from `test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`, as in "Ctrl+G is mutually exclusive with the other prompt-line editors, flashing the way out").

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test: on clean's transcript, after Ctrl+G opens the instances editor, Ctrl+P does not open the pause editor (no `pause clean:` prompt in the frame) and Ctrl+R does not open the role-prompt editor. The frame still shows the instances editor's prompt, and Esc then exits it as before.
- The existing tests that cover the per-role pause/wake/abort keys, Ctrl+R role-prompt toggling, Ctrl+A answer, Ctrl+N new entry and Ctrl+E queued edit pass unchanged. That includes the role-prompt/search cases where Ctrl+P on a paused role still resumes it.
- After the change, `grep -n '!session.held\.' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-{pause,prompt,answer,entry,queued}.ts` finds no multi-flag guard chain.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A feature or bugfix primary whose eligible entries are all held by siblings stands down instead of running a model run that can only end in nothing-to-do (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** In the 24 hours to 13:11 UTC on 2026-10-20, the primary `feature` runner ended 52 runs with `no_change`. Their median length was 4.5 s, and together they cost $1.65 notional on the claude subscription window. A typical one: at 09:00:32 a `wake` ("main moved") was followed by `run_start` with no `claim` event and then `run_end` `no_change` 5.7 s later. In a multi-runner group, `pollRunnerReasons` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts) skips an extra instance with no free entry ("no-free-entry"). The feature stand-down added 2026-10-12 skips the primary only when `eligible.length === 0`. When eligible entries exist but siblings hold every one, the claim block finds no `pick`, sets `runner.state.heldElsewhere`, and admits the primary unassigned. `buildHeldEntriesNote` (src/prompt/gate-notes.ts) then tells the run to "treat the backlog as having nothing to do for you". The run is paid for, but the only outcome it can have is no change. That is the waste the 10-12 stand-down was meant to remove, and the same holds for a bugfix primary whose open bugs are all held by siblings.

**Approach.** Only `pollRunnerReasons`, in the claim block's `else if (instanceIndex(runner.role) >= 2)` branch:
- Widen the condition to `!pick && (instanceIndex(runner.role) >= 2 || (heldTitles.length > 0 && !freshlyWoken(runner.state)))`. The branch body stays as it is: `noteSkip(root, runner, "no-free-entry")`, the `once.settle(runner.role, "no free entry")` call, and `continue`. `nextRunAt`/`backoffSeconds` are untouched, so the first poll after a sibling releases its entry or main moves starts the primary again.
- Keep `runner.state.heldElsewhere` as the line above sets it. The branch is reached only for reasons other than inbox/resume, but a later inbox or resume run reuses the stored list in its `<held-entries>` note.
- Without `heldTitles`, behavior does not change: a bugfix primary with no open bugs (an empty `claimGroup.eligible`) still runs in search mode, and so does any multi-runner role whose `eligibleEntries` is empty. An operator wake (`freshlyWoken`) still gets its run, the same exemption the stand-down above uses. A runner with a claim or outstanding work never reaches this branch.
- Update the claim block's comment ("the primary runs unassigned only while some eligible entry exists (all of them held by siblings)") to say the primary now stands down in that case too, unless an operator wake is fresh.

**Files.** `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts`, `test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts`, `docs/how-it-works.md` (the "Parallel work instances" bullet: an instance, the first included, also skips while every eligible entry is held by a sibling, and an operator wake still runs).

**Acceptance criteria.** In `test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts`:
- Rename "an unassigned primary is told the entries its siblings hold, and the prompt names them" to say the primary stands down. Keep its `heldElsewhere` and prompt assertions, and add these: `reasons.has(feature)` is false, `feature.state.skipReason` is `"no-free-entry"`, and `nextRunAt`/`backoffSeconds` are unchanged.
- A new test with the same three-feature setup, where the primary carries `wokenAt` later than `lastRunEndedAt`: the primary is admitted unassigned, with `heldElsewhere` set.
- A new bugfix case: with two bugfix runners, BUGS.md holding one open eligible bug, and `bugfix-2` holding its claim, the primary `bugfix` is not admitted and records `"no-free-entry"`. With BUGS.md holding no open bugs, the primary is still admitted (search mode).
- The existing tests "an extra instance with no free entry is skipped and keeps its schedule", "a once round settles an extra feature instance with no free entry" and the bugfix held-only tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A per-run provider-failure warning names the provider/model it failed on, so a mixed-provider team can tell which backend is down from the feed alone (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20 the claude window fallback (`fallback_switched`, 06:11 UTC) moved every tier to `qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b`. That endpoint was unreachable, and from 06:11 to 07:20 UTC the feed carried 14 `run_end` "Connection error." failures and 26 warnings reading only `provider backend failure (connection error) — the transient retry does not cover this kind; the team-wide wait watches for a storm`. Claude, huggingface and qwenrunner seams were all in use that week, and the per-run warnings in src/runner/runner-pi.ts name none of them. The team-wide `rate_limit_hold` does carry `provider`, but it forms only on a storm. A single role's failure, or a retry line ("provider rate-limited the request (429 …) — retrying the agent run once"), leaves the operator guessing which backend misbehaved. `runWithTransientRetry` already knows the seam: `opts.config` is the config this agent run actually ran on (a fallback pair included; see its `seamHoldKey(opts.config)` comment). So naming it costs one string.

**Approach.**
- In `runWithTransientRetry` (src/runner/runner-pi.ts), compute once `const on = opts.config.model !== undefined ? \` on ${seamPairName(opts.config)}\` : "";`. With no model (pi's own saved default), `seamPairName` would print `?/?`, so the label is omitted rather than guessed.
- Insert `on` into each retry-branch warning right after its leading phrase and parenthetical, before the ` — ` separator. The results: `pi crashed on malformed JSON (<detail>)${on} — resuming the session once`, `provider rate-limited the request (429…)${on} — retrying the agent run once`, `provider severed the in-flight stream (terminated)${on} — …`, `provider request timed out after accepting the connection${on} — …`, `model server timed out an idle predict stream (e.g. machine sleep)${on} — …`.
- `warnBackendKindFloor(run)` takes the same label as a second parameter (`warnBackendKindFloor(run: PiRunResult, on: string)`), passed at both call sites. Its text becomes `provider backend failure (${backendKindPhrase(run.backendKind)})${on} — the transient retry does not cover this kind; …`. The retry runs on the same `opts` (`runPi({ ...opts, continueSession: true })`), so one label serves both attempts.
- Do not touch the `fallbackClone` warning (it names its model already), the 429/backend folds, or any event shape. These are `warning` messages only.
- Update the `warnBackendKindFloor` docblock to say the line names the seam's pair.

**Files touched.** src/runner/runner-pi.ts, test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Existing assertions keep matching with no edit, because the label lands after the substrings they test. That covers test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts's `/provider backend failure \(connection error\)/` and `/rate-limited the request \(429, retry after 3s\)/`, test/runner-2.test.ts's pi-crash regex, and the `retrying the agent run once` substring checks in test/runner-4.test.ts and test/runner-transient-retry.test.ts. `defaultConfig()` sets no model, so those tests' warnings carry no label.
- New test in test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts, "the backend-kind floor warning names the seam's provider/model pair". A `cfg` with `agent = "pi"`, `provider = "omlx"`, `model = "qwen"` (the shape of "a 429 agent run folds its seam hold key …") and a first run of `errorLine("Connection error.")` produce exactly one warning that starts with `provider backend failure (connection error) on omlx/qwen — `.
- New test in the same file, "a retry warning names the seam's provider/model pair": the same cfg with a 429 first run (retry after 3s) yields `warns[0]` matching `/^provider rate-limited the request \(429, retry after 3s\) on omlx\/qwen — retrying the agent run once$/`.
- New assertion: "a backend-kind failure the retry does not cover warns once and earns no retry" (default config) also asserts `!warns[0]!.includes(" on ")`, so no `?/?` label appears.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `budget_paused` or `budget_fallback` page names the roles spending most today, so a cap reached without a prior warning still says where the money went (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The 2026-10-20 plan gave `budget_warning` a `topRoles` list and on purpose left the cap events alone. But the warning fires only while the gate is open (`warn = gate === "open" && …` in `pollBudgetGate`, src/gates/budget-gates.ts). So a poll that goes from under 80% straight past the cap logs only the transition event. The live log has this case: on 2026-09-30 a `budget_paused` ($15.04 of $15) and on 2026-10-01 three `budget_fallback` events had no `budget_warning` before them that day. `budget_paused` is on the notify allowlist (`NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`, src/events/notify.ts) and stops the team, so it is the page where knowing who spent the money matters most. Today the operator has to run `tumwater report` to find out.

**Approach.**
- In `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts), the `gate !== state.prevGate` emission adds `topRoles: topDailySpenders(states, now)` to `budget_fallback` and `budget_paused` when the list is not empty. It uses the same omit-when-empty spread as the warning. `budget_resumed` does not get it: a midnight resume reads zero spend, and a cap raise is the operator's own act. Compute the list once per poll, before the warning branch, only when the warning or a transition fires. Both branches then share one `const topRoles`.
- In src/events/event-format.ts, move the warning case's inline `topRoles` read into a module-level helper `mostByPhrase(value: unknown): string`. It returns ` (most by feature $30.00, plan $10.01)`, or `""` for a missing, empty, or all-malformed array, using the same `isJsonObject`/`Number.isFinite` checks it has now. `budget_warning` calls it with no change to its output. `budget_paused` puts the phrase right after "daily cost reached", before the refused/demoted parenthetical. `budget_fallback` puts it right after "daily cost reached", before "; roles continue on", in both its tiered and single-pair returns.
- Document `topRoles` on the `budget_paused` and `budget_fallback` comments of the `HarnessEvent` union in src/events/events.ts, and in docs/config.md's `budget_paused` row (the table has no `budget_fallback` row; do not add one).

**Acceptance criteria.**

### A backlog conflict where each side finished or added different whole entries settles without a model run, so a revision stops getting PLANS.md conflict markers handed back (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/merge/backlog-conflicts.ts, test/backlog-conflicts.test.ts, docs/how-it-works.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** In the three days to 2026-10-20 the event log holds 73 `conflict_handback` events with `reason: "revision"` whose `conflicted` list is only `["PLANS.md"]`, plus a dozen more where PLANS.md is one of the files. Each one hands a feature run conflict markers to clean up by hand. I rebuilt the six newest of them (`git -c merge.conflictStyle=diff3 merge-tree --merge-base=<merge-base> <main at the event> <sha>`, in a scratch clone). All six have the same shape. The base holds entries A, B, C under `## Planned`. Main finished some of them, and sometimes added a new plan. The change finished a different one, usually its own plan. No entry was edited on both sides. The settler `resolveInsertOnlyText` (src/merge/backlog-conflicts.ts) cannot settle these, because git's hunk boundaries cut through entries: one side of a hunk is a lone `### ` heading line, with the rest of that entry's body outside the hunk. So `settledLines` matches none of its three shapes, and the file goes to the pi resolver (merge path) or keeps its markers (revision path, `pickSettlingBacklog` in src/runner/revision.ts). This plan adds a second deterministic pass that merges entry by entry instead of hunk by hunk.

**Approach (src/merge/backlog-conflicts.ts).**
- New exported `mergeBacklogEntries(base: string, ours: string, theirs: string): string | null`, where ours is main and theirs is the change, the same convention as the hunk sides. It parses each text into blocks: a preamble (lines before the first `## ` line), then per `## ` section one header block (the heading line plus its lines before the first `### `), then one block per `### ` entry (heading line plus body up to the next `### `/`## `). Classify lines with `fenceTracker` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts), so a heading inside a fenced block is body text. Compare and emit every block with its trailing blank lines removed. An entry's key is its heading line, verbatim, within its section.
- Return null, so the file stays conflicted as today, when: any version's tracker is still `open()` at EOF; a section holds two entries with the same key in any version; the three versions' `## ` heading sequences differ; or a preamble or section header block changed on both sides to different text.
- Per section, walk main's entry order and keep each entry that main has, by these rules:
  - In all three versions: if main's copy equals base, take the change's copy. If the change's copy equals base, or both copies are equal, take main's. Otherwise return null.
  - In base and main, but the change deleted it: drop it if main's copy equals base, else return null.
  - Not in base (main added it): keep it. If the change also added the same key, the two texts must be equal, else return null.
  - An entry main deleted is never kept, but if it is in base and the change edited it (its text differs from base), return null.
  - Then insert each entry only the change added (not in base) right after the nearest entry before it in the change's order that is already in the result, or first in the section when there is none.
- Emit the blocks in order, joined by one blank line, with the file ending in exactly one `\n`.
- In `resolveBacklogInsertConflicts`, when `resolveInsertOnlyText` returns null and the file is `PLANS.md`, `BUGS.md` or `QUESTIONS.md` (not the two archive files), read the three index stages with `gitTry(wt, "show", `:1:${file}`)` and the same for `:2:` and `:3:`. A null stage (a file added or deleted on one side) leaves the file in `remaining`. Pass the stages to `mergeBacklogEntries`. On a non-null result, write it with `writeTextAtomic` and `git add` it, the same as the hunk path. This one change covers both callers: the merge's first pass (`mergeToMain`, src/merge/merge-to-main.ts) and the revision pick (`pickSettlingBacklog`). Both stop with the stages in the index, and stage 2 is main in each.
- Extend the module comment with the fourth shape. Note there that a same-entry edit on both sides still goes to the resolver.

**Tests (test/backlog-conflicts.test.ts).**
- Unit tests on `mergeBacklogEntries`, each building three `# Plans\n\n## Planned\n\n…\n\n## Done\n` texts from entries:
  - Base [A, B, C], main [B], change [A, C] gives [].
  - Base [B, C], main [B, D], change [C] gives [D].
  - Base [A, B], main [A, B, N], change [A] gives [A, N] (the change deleted B; the entry first said [B, N]).
  - Base [A, B], change adds M after A and main deletes B, giving [A, M].
  - The change edits A's body while main deletes B gives [A′].
- Each of these returns null: both sides editing A differently; main editing A while the change deletes it; a duplicate heading; a section heading only one side renamed; an unclosed fence.
- A `### ` line inside a fenced block in an entry's body stays body text.
- An integration test in the style of `resolveBacklogInsertConflicts settles a real rebase where …`, built on `makeRepo`/`seedCommit`/`rebaseOntoMainLeaveConflicts`. Seed [A, B, C]. The change finishes B. Main finishes A and C and adds D. Assert the rebase reports "conflict", that `resolveBacklogInsertConflicts` returns `[]`, that PLANS.md reads [D], and that it is staged. Before writing the assertions, check that the seeds really conflict: this test only proves anything when the old hunk settler alone leaves PLANS.md conflicted.
- The existing hunk-shape tests still pass unchanged.

**Docs.** In docs/how-it-works.md's backlog paragraph (the one that starts "PLANS.md, BUGS.md and QUESTIONS.md hold open work"), add one sentence: when a merge or a revision conflicts in one of those files and each side only added, removed or edited different `### ` entries, tumwater merges the entries itself, and the same entry edited on both sides still goes to the conflict resolver.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `mergeBacklogEntries` returns the results listed under Tests, and null for each bail-out case listed there.
- The integration test's rebase settles with no pi run, and the resolved PLANS.md holds exactly D under `## Planned`.
- A conflicted `PLANS-DONE.md`/`BUGS-FIXED.md` is handled exactly as before: only the hunk pass runs on it.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 10a/20: Rename the orchestrator's run launch and timing names, src prose included (planned 2026-10-16 by user, split 2026-10-20 by the plan role from part 10/20 after two rejected reviews; requires parts 9a/20 and 9b/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/orchestrator/ + src/cli/cli-start.ts + src/scheduling/once-round.ts + src/redeploy/ + test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts + identifier uses in the non-e2e test/orchestrator-*.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The orchestrator launches and times runs by run names: `launchDueRuns`, `ROLE_RUN_DURATION_SAMPLES`, `roleRunDurationsMs` and `runsDone`. Its src/ comments read as sentences after the swap. Part 10b/20 converts the prose in the orchestrator's non-e2e tests.

**Why the split.** Part 10/20 was rejected twice on 2026-10-20 for one thing: a blanket tick → run swap in comments and assertion messages produced nonsense, e.g. "a switch that moves a mid-run run" (orchestrator-launch.ts, the provider-lease comment in `launchDue*`), and "ran its run" / "runs exactly one run" pairs (orchestrator-scheduling.ts once-mode comments; test/orchestrator-defer.test.ts and orchestrator-director.test.ts assertion messages). Over the old part's files, about 80 comment, title or message lines put "tick" next to "run"/"runs"/"ran". Splitting the identifier rename and src prose (10a) from the test prose (10b) makes each part small enough to reread line by line.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message. The `restart` event's `abortedRuns` field is Plain terms event log's.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- Prose rule (the review objection): never substitute a "tick" word in a comment by find-and-replace. Before editing a file's prose, list its collision lines with `grep -niE 'tick.*\b(run|runs|ran|running)\b|\b(run|runs|ran|running)\b.*tick'` and rewrite each one by hand as a sentence that says one thing once. Change the verb or the agent-run noun, not just the tick word. For example, "in-flight ticks always run to completion" → "in-flight runs always finish"; "The tick's own run time (null when it never ran …)" → "The run's own duration (null when it never started …)"; "a switch that moves a mid-tick run to another provider" → "a switch that moves an agent run to another provider mid-run"; "every run it makes re-keys it to the provider that run actually uses" → "every agent run it makes …"; "a role that already ran its tick" → "a role that already had its run"; "runs exactly one tick" / "at most one tick" → "gets exactly one run" / "at most one run"; "a paused role runs no tick" → "a paused role gets no run"; "roles ticking on that provider" → "roles running on that provider". Reread every changed comment line in the diff as a sentence before finishing.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts (the poll steps split out of `runOrchestrator`) reads `tickStartHeld` and `roleTickDurationsMs`: rename those uses with the members below.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts: `launchDueTicks` → `launchDueRuns`, `ROLE_TICK_DURATION_SAMPLES` → `ROLE_RUN_DURATION_SAMPLES`, member `roleTickDurationsMs` → `roleRunDurationsMs`, `tickStartHeld` → `runStartHeld` and `roleTickP75Ms` → `roleRunP75Ms` (a member read by src/redeploy/; rename those uses here). Locals `tickIdx`, `tickCalls` and `roleTicksInFlight` → run forms.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts: the exit-info member `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, renamed with its uses in src/cli/cli-start.ts (`onceSummary`/`onceFailures` parameters) and src/scheduling/once-round.ts (the `ticksRun(runner)` method → `runsDone(runner)`); `recordFallbackTickAt` and `deferTick` uses as they stand. orchestrator-scheduling.ts, orchestrator-poll.ts and retention.ts: comments, under the prose rule.
- test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts: `awaitSettledTick` → `awaitSettledRun` (aliased: the e2e tests in part 11/20 use it about 38 times), `timedTickHarness` → `timedRunHarness`, `awaitFirstTick` → `awaitFirstRun`; its comments under the prose rule.
- Identifier uses only in test/orchestrator-{launch,seams,scheduling,probe,defer,director,redeploy,once,fallback,divergence,start-event-best-effort}.test.ts: the renamed members and fixtures (`exit.ticksRun` → `exit.runsDone`, `roleTickDurationsMs`, `awaitSettledTick` call sites and so on) so the suite compiles; leave those files' comments, titles, assertion messages and locals to part 10b/20.

**Files touched.** src/orchestrator/*.ts, the `ticksRun`/`roleTickP75Ms` uses in src/cli/cli-start.ts, src/scheduling/once-round.ts and src/redeploy/, test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts, and identifier uses in the non-e2e orchestrator tests listed above.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `launchDueRuns`, `ROLE_RUN_DURATION_SAMPLES` and `awaitSettledRun` are declared, and `runsDone` replaces `ticksRun` everywhere in src/ and test/.
- `grep -rnE '[Tt]ick[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Tick|TICK_|\bticks?\b' src/orchestrator` prints only serialized names and the legacy readers named above.
- `grep -rniE "mid-run run|\bran (its|a|the|no) run\b|\bruns? (no|one|exactly one) run\b|at most one run\b.*\bran\b|run's own run\b|\bruns? runs?\b" src/orchestrator src/scheduling/once-round.ts test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts` prints nothing.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.

### A `budget_warning` names the roles spending most today, so the 80% page says where the money went (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `budget_warning` is on the notify allowlist (`NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`, src/events/notify.ts), and docs/config.md says it means "time to raise the cap or fix the fallback before the pause". But the page carries only the team total: the live log's two warnings in the last three days read `spentUsd` 12.01 of `capUsd` 15 and 16.02 of 20, with no role named. To decide whether to raise the cap, pause one role, or lower one role's `maxDailyCostUsd`, the operator then has to run `tumwater report`. The poll that logs the warning already holds every role's state, and each one has its daily window (`dailyCost`, src/budget/budget.ts), so the event can name the top spenders itself.

**Approach.**
- In src/budget/budget.ts, add `export function topDailySpenders(states: RunnerState[], now = Date.now(), limit = 3): { role: string; spentUsd: number }[]` beside `teamDailyCost`. It returns today's `dailyCost(s, now)` per state, keeps only spend above 0, sorts by spend descending (ties by `role` ascending, so output is deterministic), and keeps the first `limit`. Each state counts as its own role, so `feature` and `feature-2` are listed apart, the same way `RunnerState.role` names them.
- In `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts), the `budget_warning` emission adds `topRoles: topDailySpenders(states, now)` when that list is not empty (omit the field when empty, the codebase's omit-when-absent idiom). Use the poll's own `now` and `states`. No other budget event changes: `budget_paused`/`budget_fallback` already name the fallback, and this plan keeps to the warning.
- In src/events/event-format.ts, `case "budget_warning"` renders a valid `topRoles` array as ` (most by feature $5.20, plan $3.10, director $1.40)` between "of the daily cap spent" and "; runs still start". Money goes through `usd` (src/text/format.ts). Entries that are not an object with a string `role` and a finite `spentUsd` are skipped, the same defensive reads the other cases use (`textOr`/`finiteNumber`). A missing, empty, or all-invalid array renders today's line unchanged, so older logged events read the same.
- Document `topRoles` in the `budget_warning` comment of the `HarnessEvent` type union in src/events/events.ts. In docs/config.md's `budget_warning` row, say the event names up to three roles that spent the most today.

**Files touched.** src/budget/budget.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, src/events/events.ts, docs/config.md, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/event-format-team.test.ts, test/budget.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A new test for `topDailySpenders` covers four cases. Four roles with today's spend come back as the top three, highest first. A tie is ordered by role name. A role with a stale `dayStamp` or zero spend is left out. No spend at all returns `[]`.
- In test/budget-gates.test.ts, the existing "exactly one budget_warning" case also asserts that `events[0]!.topRoles` deep-equals `[{ role: "feature", spentUsd: threshold }]`. A new case with two roles spending asserts both appear, highest first.
- test/event-format-team.test.ts: a `budget_warning` with `topRoles` renders `budget warning — $40.01 of $50.00 of the daily cap spent (most by feature $30.00, plan $10.01); runs still start`. The existing test without `topRoles` still renders the current line unchanged, and a `topRoles` holding only malformed entries renders that same line too.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A claude usage window warns once per window across restarts and window overlaps, so the notify page stops re-paging the same `claude_window_warning` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `claude_window_warning` is on the notify allowlist (`NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`, src/events/notify.ts), and docs/backends.md promises that `claude_window_reserved` "is logged once per window". In practice the same window is logged again and again. From 10-17 to 10-20 the live log shows `seven_day` warnings for one window (`resetsAt` 1792450800000) logged 9 times. 8 of them came less than a second after an `orchestrator_start`. The next `seven_day` window (`resetsAt` 1793055600000) was logged 4 times in one day. Each repeat followed a `five_hour` warning. There are two causes, both in `logWindowEventOnce` (src/team/team-polls.ts):
1. The memory is one `type:resetsAt` string in `TeamGateStates.claudeWindowWarned` / `claudeWindowReserved` (src/gates/gate-polls.ts), and it starts at `null` on each start (`newTeamGateStates`, called by src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts). So every restart re-announces a window that is still warning.
2. It logs only the first matching window per poll and then keeps only that window's key. With `five_hour` and `seven_day` both warning, a `five_hour` warning's key replaces the `seven_day` key. When the `five_hour` warning ends, `seven_day` no longer matches the stored key and is logged again.

**Approach.**
- src/team/team-polls.ts, `logWindowEventOnce`: replace `prevKey: string | null` with `logged: ReadonlySet<string>` and return a `ReadonlySet<string>`. Walk every window in `account.windows`, not only the first match. Each window whose `eventFor` is non-null, whose `resetsAt` is not past, and whose `` `${type}:${w.resetsAt ?? ""}` `` key is not in `logged` is logged and gets its key added. The returned set also drops keys whose numeric suffix is `<= now`, so the set stays bounded. A key with an empty suffix is kept. When nothing was added or dropped, return the input set itself so a quiet poll allocates nothing. A non-subscription account returns `logged` unchanged.
- `pollClaudeWindowWarning` and `pollClaudeWindowReserve`: take and return `ReadonlySet<string>` in place of the key. Update their doc comments: once per window key across polls, and several windows crossing in one poll each log their own event.
- New export in team-polls.ts: `loggedWindowKeys(root, type: "claude_window_warning" | "claude_window_reserved", now): ReadonlySet<string>`. It reads `eventsSince(root, CLAUDE_WINDOW_LOOKBACK_MS, now, (e) => e.type === type)` from src/events/event-window.ts, with `CLAUDE_WINDOW_LOOKBACK_MS = 7 * 24 * 3600_000` (the longest window claude reports is `seven_day`, so any window still open was warned within that span). It collects `` `${windowType}:${resetsAt}` `` for events whose `windowType` is a string and whose `resetsAt` is a number `> now`. Events without a numeric `resetsAt` are skipped, because they cannot name their window.
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts: `TeamGateStates.claudeWindowWarned` / `claudeWindowReserved` become `ReadonlySet<string>`. `newTeamGateStates` seeds both with `new Set()` and stays config-only. Update the field doc comments.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts: right after `const gateStates = newTeamGateStates(config)`, set `gateStates.claudeWindowWarned = loggedWindowKeys(root, "claude_window_warning", Date.now())` and the same for `claudeWindowReserved` with `"claude_window_reserved"`. Add a one-line comment saying a restart must not re-announce a window that is still open.
- docs/config.md, the `claude_window_warning` notify row: add "once per window, also across restarts".

**Files.** src/team/team-polls.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, docs/config.md, test/team-polls.test.ts.

**Out of scope.** No new state file: the event log is already the record of what was logged. The warning's wording and `claude_window_reserved`'s payload do not change. If a past event was pruned by log retention, its window may be announced once more; that is acceptable.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/team-polls.test.ts "pollClaudeWindowWarning logs the first allowed_warning once per window" and the `pollClaudeWindowReserve` tests pass with sets in place of keys: `new Set()` in place of `null`, and checks like `set.has(\`five_hour:${resetsAt}\`)` in place of key equality.
- New test: start from an account where only `seven_day` warns, then poll with `five_hour` and `seven_day` both warning, then only `seven_day` again, threading the returned set each time. The log ends up with exactly one `seven_day` and one `five_hour` `claude_window_warning`.
- New test: after one key is in the set and its `resetsAt` passes, the next poll's returned set no longer contains it.
- New test: `loggedWindowKeys` on a root whose log holds a `claude_window_warning` with a future `resetsAt`, one with a past `resetsAt`, one with no `resetsAt`, and a `claude_window_reserved` returns only the future warning's key. A `pollClaudeWindowWarning` seeded with that set, for the same window, logs no new event.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `role_paused` event carries a timed role pause's deadline, so `logs` and the failure digest say until when a role is paused (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater pause --role <id> --for <duration>` writes one shared deadline into the paused-roles marker. `team_paused` already carries a timed pause's `until`, and `role_resumed` already says `expired` when that shared deadline ran out. `role_paused` carries only `role`, so `logs` and the failure digest show `role docs paused — it starts no new runs` with no hint that the pause lifts by itself. `pollPauseGates` (src/gates/pause-gates.ts) already reads the deadline each poll (`standingRolePause(root).until`) but only stores it in `state.prevRolesUntil` for the `expired` mark. Put it on the event too.

**Approach.**
- src/gates/pause-gates.ts, `pollPauseGates`: the `role_paused` event spreads `...(rolesUntil !== undefined ? { until: rolesUntil } : {})`, the same shape as `team_paused`. `standingRolePause` returns `until` only while the set is non-empty, and `readPausedRoles` reads an expired marker as empty, so a logged `until` is the live deadline. Update the doc comment on `pollPauseGates` to say so.
- src/events/events.ts: extend the `role_paused` union comment to "carries role, and `until` (ms epoch, the set's shared deadline, timed pause only) — events logged before carry no `until`".
- src/events/event-format.ts, `case "role_paused"`: render `${rolePausePhrase(role)}${pauseSuffix(e.until, undefined)} (the rest of the team keeps running)`. `pauseSuffix` already drops a missing or non-numeric `until`.
- src/failure/failure-state-change.ts, `case "role_paused"`: append ` until ${formatTime(new Date(until))}` when `finiteNumber(ev.until, null)` is non-null, the same as the `team_paused` case.

**Out of scope.** A `--for` that moves the deadline of an already-paused set (re-pausing a member, or a timed join that overwrites the shared deadline) crosses no edge, so it logs no new event for the roles already paused; this plan adds no event for a deadline change. A per-role pause reason stays out (refused earlier). The streak breaker's pauses still log `role_streak_paused`, not `role_paused`: the fold in `pollTeamGates` (src/gates/gate-polls.ts) is unchanged. ### A startup migration logs only what it changed, so a "kept … both exist" collision stops logging `state_migrated` twice on every start (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts src/merge/merge-queue.ts src/events/events.ts test/startup-migrations.test.ts test/legacy-role-migration.test.ts. The Plain terms parts leave these legacy readers alone; a part that renames an identifier in merge-queue.ts only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `runStartupMigrations` (src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts) logs one `state_migrated` event for each step that returns any notes. Its doc comment promises "A second call moves and logs nothing". That is false when a step keeps something. The `legacyRoleIds` step (`migrateLegacyRoleIds`, src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts) returns a `kept <from> and <to>: both exist` note for every artifact present under both ids. It returns that note again on every start, and those notes count as `moved`. In this team's event log, each of the six `orchestrator_start`s from 2026-10-18 06:00 to 2026-10-20 00:41 UTC sits between two `state_migrated step:legacyRoleIds moved:2` events. The detail of each is `kept …/state/dry.json and …/state/dedupe.json: both exist; kept …/state/telemetry.json and …/state/selfcheck.json: both exist`, and nothing had moved. The event comes twice because src/cli/cli-start.ts and `runOrchestrator` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) each call `runStartupMigrations`. The `mergeRefs` step (`kept <ref> and <target>: they name different commits`) and the `mergeQueueDir` step (`legacyMigrateLandQueueDir`'s `<name> already in merge-queue, left in place`) have the same shape. After this change, a step logs only when it changed something, and a kept collision is reported only alongside a change.

**Approach.**
- **src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts.**
  - Export `interface MigrationNotes { moved: string[]; kept: string[]; failed: string[] }`. `moved` lists what the step changed (moved, renamed, or removed). `kept` lists what it left in place because both names exist. `failed` lists artifacts that hit an error, which the step retries at the next start.
  - `StartupMigration.run` returns `Promise<MigrationNotes>`.
  - In `runStartupMigrations`, when `moved.length > 0`, log the `state_migrated` event with `moved: moved.length` and `detail: [...moved, ...kept].join("; ")`. A step with only `kept` notes logs nothing. When `failed.length > 0`, log one warning per step via `warnEventBestEffort`: `` `startup migration ${step.name}: ${failed.join("; ")}` ``. Like a thrown step, it repeats each start until the step succeeds. The thrown-step warning stays as it is.
  - Update the doc comments on `StartupMigration` and `runStartupMigrations`.
- **src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts, `migrateLegacyRoleIds`.** Return `MigrationNotes`. The `renamed branch …` and `moved …` notes go to `moved`, every `kept …: both exist` note goes to `kept`, and `attempt`'s `could not move <what>: …` catch goes to `failed`. Note texts stay the same. Update the doc comment's "Returns one line per artifact".
- **src/merge/merge-queue.ts, `legacyMigrateLandQueueDir`.** Return `MigrationNotes`, with `moved <name>` in `moved` and `<name> already in merge-queue, left in place` in `kept`. `failed` stays empty, because a non-ENOENT error still throws. Import the type from src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts, or declare a structurally identical one locally if that import would create a cycle (check with the existing lint/compile).
- **src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts.** `mergingMarker` returns `{ moved: ["removed the old landing.json marker"], kept: [], failed: [] }`, or all three lists empty on ENOENT. In `mergeRefs`, `moved …` and `removed …: … already names the same commit` go to `moved`, and `kept … they name different commits` goes to `kept`.
- **src/events/events.ts.** The `state_migrated` union comment: `moved` counts what the step changed, and `detail` lists the changes followed by any collisions the step kept. A step that only kept things logs nothing. Events logged before this change may count kept collisions in `moved`.
- Leave both `runStartupMigrations` call sites in place. With this change the second call logs nothing, because the first one already moved everything it could.

**Out of scope.** Resolving a kept collision (deleting or archiving the old-id artifact): that would discard state and is the operator's call. A doctor row for kept collisions. The `backlogArchive` `state_migrated` event (src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts `archiveAtTeamStart`), which already logs only on an actual move.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/legacy-role-migration.test.ts "a legacy role id's branch, refs and files move to the new id; logs stay": `notes.moved` has 8 entries and `notes.kept` and `notes.failed` are empty. The second call deep-equals `{ moved: [], kept: [], failed: [] }`.
- test/legacy-role-migration.test.ts "an artifact already under the new id is kept and reported": the `kept branch tumwater/oldy` note is in `notes.kept`, and no entry of `notes.moved` starts with `kept`.
- test/startup-migrations.test.ts "mergeRefs moves a legacy pin once, keeps a differing pair, and retire sees a legacy-only pin": after the run that removes `same` and keeps `diff`, exactly one new `mergeRefs` `state_migrated` event has `moved: 1` and a `detail` containing `kept`. One more `runStartupMigrations` call adds no `mergeRefs` event, and the `diff` legacy ref still names `other`.
- test/startup-migrations.test.ts, new test: a fresh repo whose only legacy artifact is a differing `diff` pair (a legacy pin and a current pin naming different commits). Two `runStartupMigrations` calls log no `state_migrated` event with `step: "mergeRefs"`, and both refs keep their commits.
- test/startup-migrations.test.ts "a basename already in the new directory is left in the old one": the `mergeQueueDir` event's `moved` equals the number of files actually moved, which is one less than the fixture's file count.
- The existing "logs one state_migrated" and "a second start logs nothing" tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater doctor`'s "check contention" row names which checks held the slots, so an operator can tell merge-check queueing from a main-baseline run or gate checks crowding each other (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md. Plain terms cleanup part 6/7 renames other doctor-checks.ts symbols; whichever lands second only rebases) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `check_wait` events now carry `heldBy`, the labels of the permit holders when the check parked: `<role> <scope>` from `runScopedBuildCheck` (src/build/build-check-scoped.ts), `main baseline` from src/baseline/main-baseline.ts, and `a check` for an unlabeled caller (`withCheckPermit`, src/concurrency/check-permit.ts). They also carry `limit`. `checkCheckContention` (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) still only counts and sums the waits: `3 waits for a check slot in the last 24h, 15m total, longest 10m — raise maxConcurrentChecks above 2`. Raising the cap is the wrong fix when the waits sat behind the main baseline or behind merge checks, which go first by design. The sibling `checkProviderContention` already names its busiest bucket. The plan for `heldBy` explicitly left this row out of scope. This change makes the row say what the waits sat behind.

**Approach (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, `checkCheckContention` only).**
- Add a small private helper, `checkHolderKind(label: string): string`. It maps `"main baseline"` to `"the main baseline"`. It maps a label whose last space-separated word is `gate`, `merge` or `batch` to `"gate checks"`, `"merge checks"` or `"batch checks"`. Anything else, including `"a check"`, maps to `"other checks"`.
- While summing, read each event's `heldBy` with `stringList` (src/files/json-object.ts). Map the labels to kinds and dedupe them, then add the event's `waitedMs` once to each distinct kind in a `Map<string, number>`. A wait behind two merge checks counts once toward `merge checks`. Events without `heldBy`, which were logged before the field existed, add nothing to the tally but still count in `count`, `total` and `longest`, as today.
- When the tally is non-empty, rank the kinds by total descending, breaking ties by kind name, and insert ` (behind <kind> <shortSpanPhrase(ms)>, <kind> <span>…)` right after the `longest …` clause. On a warning, the existing ` — raise maxConcurrentChecks above N` suffix stays after it. When no event in the window carries `heldBy`, the detail is unchanged byte for byte.
- The level logic (`CHECK_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS`) and the advice stay unchanged. Update the function's doc comment to describe the parenthetical.

**Docs.** In docs/cli.md's `tumwater doctor` row, the `check contention` clause gains "naming what the waits sat behind (merge, gate or batch checks, or the main baseline)". In docs/how-it-works.md's `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet, the sentence about the doctor row gets the same words.

**Out of scope.** Changing the advice by holder kind (for example, not suggesting a higher cap when the main baseline held every wait). The report's "Check wait median". The live `checkPermits` badge. Per-role holder names.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts "checkCheckContention sums the last day of check_wait events and warns at ten minutes" passes unchanged, because its events carry no `heldBy`.
- New test in test/doctor-checks.test.ts, "checkCheckContention names what the waits sat behind, busiest first". Log three `check_wait` events:
  - 240 000 ms, `heldBy: ["feature merge", "dedupe merge"]`
  - 120 000 ms, `heldBy: ["main baseline", "clean gate"]`
  - 60 000 ms, no `heldBy`
  The detail equals `3 waits for a check slot in the last 24h, 7m total, longest 4m (behind merge checks 4m, gate checks 2m, the main baseline 2m)`. Merge checks count once at 4m, not 8m, and the 2m tie sorts `gate checks` before `the main baseline`. The level is `ok`.
  A fourth event of 600 000 ms with `heldBy: ["a check"]` makes the level `warn`. The detail then contains `other checks 10m` ranked first, followed by ` — raise maxConcurrentChecks above 2`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `team_resumed` and `role_resumed` say when a timed pause ran out, so `logs` and the failure digest tell an expired `pause --for` from an operator's `resume` (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/gates/pause-gates.ts src/team/team-state.ts src/text/phrases.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/failure/failure-state-change.ts src/events/events.ts test/pause-gates.test.ts test/event-format-team.test.ts test/failure-render.test.ts)

**Goal.** Since the merged team_paused plan, a timed pause logs `team paused … until HH:MM:SS`. When the pause ends, the line is always `team resumed — roles run again`. That is true whether the deadline passed (`standingMarker` in src/team/team-state.ts reads an `until` in the past as no pause) or the operator typed `tumwater resume` early. The per-role pair behaves the same way: `readPausedRoles` returns no roles once the shared `until` has passed, and `pollPauseGates` logs a bare `role_resumed`. Someone reading `logs` or the failure digest's Team state changes can't tell "the freeze ran out" from "someone lifted it". All 5 `team_resumed`/`role_resumed` events in the live log carry no field beyond `ts`, `source`, `type` and `role`. This plan adds `expired: true` to a resume event the deadline caused, and the event's lines say so.

**Approach.**
- **src/team/team-state.ts.** Export `standingRolePause(root): { roles: string[]; until?: number }`, a thin wrapper over `readPausedRoles(pausedRolesPath(root))` that drops `until` when `roles` is empty. This is the same rule `pausedRolesUntil` applies, so one read gives a consistent set and deadline. `pausedRoles` and `pausedRolesUntil` stay as they are.
- **src/gates/pause-gates.ts.**
  - `PauseGateState` gains `prevTeamUntil?: number` and `prevRolesUntil?: number`, the deadlines the previous poll saw. `newPauseGateState` leaves both undefined.
  - In `pollPauseGates`, on the paused→unpaused crossing, compute `const expired = state.prevTeamUntil !== undefined && state.prevTeamUntil <= Date.now()` and log `{ source, type: "team_resumed", ...(expired ? { expired: true } : {}) }`. After the crossing check, set `state.prevTeamUntil = marker?.until` on every poll, not only at a crossing. A re-pause that moves the deadline is then followed, and an early `resume` (deadline still in the future) logs no `expired`.
  - Replace the `pausedRoles(root)` call with `standingRolePause(root)`. A role that leaves the set while `state.prevRolesUntil !== undefined && state.prevRolesUntil <= Date.now()` logs `role_resumed` with `expired: true`. Then set `state.prevRolesUntil` to this poll's `until`. A role resumed individually before the shared deadline logs no `expired`. Drop the `pausedRoles` import if nothing else in the file uses it.
  - A restart mid-pause starts with both undefined, so a resume on the restart's first crossing is never marked expired. That is the conservative reading, and the `PauseGateState` doc comment must say so.
  - The streak-gate fold in src/gates/gate-polls.ts (`states.pause.prevPausedRoles.add(role)`) is unchanged.
- **src/text/phrases.ts.** Add `export const PAUSE_EXPIRED_SUFFIX = " (its timed pause ran out)"`. Its doc comment names its two readers. `teamResumePhrase` and `roleResumePhrase` are unchanged, because `tumwater resume`'s confirmation (src/operator/operator-commands.ts) and src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts also use `teamResumePhrase`.
- **src/events/event-format.ts.** In `case "team_resumed"` and `case "role_resumed"`, append `PAUSE_EXPIRED_SUFFIX` only when `e.expired === true`; any other value, absent included, renders today's line exactly. Example: `team resumed — roles run again (its timed pause ran out)`.
- **src/failure/failure-state-change.ts.** In the `team_resumed` and `role_resumed` cases, apply the same `ev.expired === true` rule.
- **src/events/events.ts.** Extend the `team_resumed` and `role_resumed` union comments: they carry `expired: true` when the pause's `until` deadline lifted it rather than `tumwater resume`; events logged before this change, or a resume on a restarted orchestrator's first crossing, carry no `expired`.

**Implementation note.** The expiry tests let a short real deadline (40 ms) pass between polls instead of rewriting the marker with a past `until`: the poll keeps the deadline it last saw, and a rewrite to a past value never shows the poll a deadline that has passed.

**Out of scope.** `role_paused` carrying the shared `until` is a separate follow-up. Notify paging is out too: the resume events stay off `NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`. Nothing deletes an expired marker file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/pause-gates.test.ts. Add a test: `pauseTeam(root, Date.now() + 60_000)`, poll once, then rewrite the marker with an `until` in the past by calling `pauseTeam(root, Date.now() - 1)`; `pauseTeam` overwrites a standing pause whenever it is given an `until`. The next poll returns `userPaused === false` and logs exactly one `team_resumed` whose `expired` is `true`. The existing "team pause logs team_paused once, resume logs team_resumed once" test also asserts that its `team_resumed` has no `expired` key. Add a timed-pause-then-early-`resumeTeam` case whose `team_resumed` also has no `expired` key.
- test/pause-gates.test.ts, per role. `pauseRole(root, "tests", <future>)`, poll, then make the deadline pass by writing a past `until` (`pauseRole` with a past `until` if it overwrites the shared deadline, otherwise a direct `writeJsonAtomic` to `pausedRolesPath(root)`). The next poll logs one `role_resumed` for `tests` with `expired: true`. The existing "a per-role pause that expires while no poll runs reads as resumed" test asserts that its `resumeRole`-driven `role_resumed` has no `expired` key.
- test/event-format-team.test.ts. `team_resumed` with `expired: true` matches `/team resumed — roles run again \(its timed pause ran out\)$/`. `role_resumed` with `role: "docs", expired: true` matches `/role docs resumed — it runs again \(its timed pause ran out\)$/`. `expired: "yes"` renders the existing line unchanged, and the existing bare assertions still match.
- test/failure-render.test.ts. The table holding `[{ type: "team_resumed" }, "team resumed — roles run again"]` gains rows for `{ type: "team_resumed", expired: true }` and `{ type: "role_resumed", role: "docs", expired: true }`, each ending in `(its timed pause ran out)`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `main_red_hold` names the failing tests it lets past, so the notify page and `logs` say which test is red, not only how many (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/baseline/main-red.ts src/events/events.ts docs/config.md test/main-red.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** Since Fast merge part 8/14, a red main whose check names its failing tests logs `main_red_hold` with the message `main <sha> is red (<n> failing tests); changes that add no new failures still merge` (built in `warnMainRedOnce`, src/baseline/main-red.ts). The event carries only `sha`, `script` and `message`. The live log's newest two holds both read `(1 failing tests)`: the count is mis-pluralized, and neither the notify page nor `logs` says which test is failing. The names are already in hand, since `namedFailures(red)` computes them for the heal key. This plan puts them on the event and the first one in the message. The no-names branch (`redMainMessage(red, "code merges blocked until main is green")`) is unchanged.

- **src/baseline/main-red.ts, `warnMainRedOnce`.**
  - When `named.length > 0`, the event gains `failingTests: named`. `namedFailures` already caps the list below `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` (50). With no named failures the event has no `failingTests` key.

Example: `main 1645a5c0 is red (1 failing test: startParentDeathWatch takes a SIGKILLed supervisor's grandchild down with it); changes that add no new failures still merge`.
  - The heal-key logic and the once-per-SHA guard stay as they are.
- **src/events/event-format.ts.** No change: `case "main_red_hold"` renders `message`, so `logs`, the dashboards and the notify line pick up the new wording.
- **src/events/events.ts.** Extend the `main_red_hold` union comment: it carries `failingTests` (the named failures, fewer than `FAILING_TESTS_MAX`) when the red names them, and its message then names the first one. Events logged before this change carry no `failingTests`.
- **docs/config.md.** Fix the `main_red_hold` row in the notify event table. It says every code role is held until a fix merges, which has been false for a red that names its failing tests since Fast merge part 8/14. New text: "Main's own check is failing. When the check names its failing tests, the message names the first and roles keep working on changes that add no new failures; otherwise every code role is held until a fix merges."

**Out of scope.** Listing every name in the message: the event's `failingTests` carries the full list. The failure digest, the doctor, and `main_check` events.

- test/main-red.test.ts, "mainRedGate lets a role run on a red main that names its failing tests, once per failing set". Replace the `(2 failing tests); …` substring check with an assertion that the message contains `(2 failing tests: known-red-alpha, +1 more); changes that add no new failures still merge`. Also assert the hold's `failingTests` deep-equals `["known-red-alpha", "known-red-beta"]`.
- test/main-red.test.ts. Add a test with one named failure (script `echo '✖ known-red-alpha (1.2ms)'; exit 1`). Its message contains `(1 failing test: known-red-alpha); changes that add no new failures still merge` and does not contain `failing tests`.
- test/main-red.test.ts. Add a test, or an assertion in an existing red-with-no-named-tests test, that the hold logged by the unnamed branch has no `failingTests` key and its message still ends `code merges blocked until main is green`.
