### A `check_wait` event names the checks that held the check slots and the cap, so `logs` says what a gate check waited behind (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/concurrency/check-permit.ts src/build/build-check-scoped.ts src/build/build-check-events.ts src/baseline/main-baseline.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/events/events.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/check-permit.test.ts test/build-check-events.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A scoped check that waits `CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS` or more for a `maxConcurrentChecks` permit logs `check_wait` with `role`, `scope` and `waitedMs` (`logCheckWaitEvent`, src/build/build-check-events.ts). `formatEvent` renders `waited 2m10s for a check slot (feature-3 gate check)`. The line doesn't say what held the slots or what the cap was. In the last 80,000 lines of the live event log, all 30 `check_wait` events carry no fields beyond `ts`, `source`, `type`, `role`, `scope` and `waitedMs`, and two gate checks there waited 130 s each. An operator can't tell whether a gate check waited behind merge checks (expected, since merges go first), behind a main-baseline run, or behind other gate checks. The cap is live-editable, so the cap in force at the time is gone too. This plan records the labels of the permit holders and the cap at the moment the check parked, and the line names them.

**Approach.**
- **src/concurrency/check-permit.ts.**
  - Add a module-level `const permitHolders = new Map<symbol, string>()`. Insertion order is acquisition order.
  - `withCheckPermit` gains a trailing optional `label?: string` parameter, after `hooks`. Once the permit is held, by either `tryAcquire` or `acquire`, set `permitHolders.set(token, label ?? "a check")` with a fresh `Symbol()` token. Delete the token in the existing `finally`, before `checkPermits.release()`. The reentrant early return (`holdingPermit.getStore()`) registers nothing, because it takes no permit.
  - When `tryAcquire` fails, capture `const parked = { heldBy: [...permitHolders.values()], limit: checkPermits.limit }` before `hooks?.waiting()`. Comment that the snapshot is taken at park time and isn't revised if holders change mid-wait.
  - Change `PermitWaitHooks.waited` to `waited?(waitedMs: number, parked: { heldBy: string[]; limit: number }): void` and pass `parked`. Update its doc comment.
  - `checkPermitSnapshot` is unchanged.
- **src/build/build-check-scoped.ts**, `runScopedBuildCheck`'s `withCheckPermit` call. Pass `` `${role} ${scope}` `` as the label. Forward `parked` through the `waited` hook to `logCheckWaitEvent`.
- **src/baseline/main-baseline.ts**, `checkMainBaseline`'s `withCheckPermit` call. Pass `undefined` hooks and the label `"main baseline"`.
- **src/build/build-check-events.ts**, `logCheckWaitEvent`. Add a trailing optional `parked?: { heldBy: string[]; limit: number }` and spread `heldBy` and `limit` into the event when it is given. Callers that omit it log today's shape.
- **src/events/event-format.ts**, `case "check_wait"`. When `e.heldBy` is a non-empty array of strings, append `; held by <labels joined with ", ">` inside the parentheses. When `limit` is a finite number (read through `finiteNumber`), also append ` of maxConcurrentChecks <limit>`. Example: `waited 2m for a check slot (feature-3 gate check; held by feature-2 merge, main baseline of maxConcurrentChecks 2)`. When `heldBy` is absent, empty or malformed, render today's line exactly, so older log lines read as before. Update the case's comment.
- **src/events/events.ts**: extend the `"check_wait"` union member's comment. It carries `heldBy`, the holders' labels at park time (`<role> <scope>`, `main baseline`, or `a check` for an unlabeled caller), and `limit`, the cap at park time. Events logged before this change carry neither.
- **docs/how-it-works.md**, the `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet. Change "(role, scope, waitedMs)" to also name the checks that held the slots and the cap when the check parked.

**Out of scope.** `checkCheckContention` (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) and the report's check-wait median stay as they are. The live `checkPermits` badge doesn't list holders.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/check-permit.test.ts, "withCheckPermit calls its wait hooks only when the permit is not free". The first caller passes the label `"feature merge"`. The `waited` hook records its second argument, and the test asserts it deep-equals `{ heldBy: ["feature merge"], limit: 1 }`. After all three settle, a fourth caller with a free permit calls no hooks.

### A `provider_wait` event names the cap that held the run, so `logs` and `tumwater doctor` stop blaming a provider slot when `maxConcurrent` was full (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts src/events/events.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A role run's admission waits on `Semaphore.acquireLease(tier, key)` (src/concurrency/semaphore.ts) until BOTH the team total (`maxConcurrent`, less the tier's reserve) and its provider key (`maxConcurrentPerProvider[key]`, when one is set) have room. When that wait reaches `PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS`, `launchDueTicks` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts) logs `provider_wait` with `role`, `waitedMs`, and the seam's `key`. The key is present whenever the seam has one, whichever cap was full. So `formatEvent` renders `waited 10m for a huggingface slot (plan)`, and `checkProviderContention` (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) files that wait under "the huggingface slot". That happens even when huggingface has no cap and the team-wide `maxConcurrent` held the run. In the live log, every recent `provider_wait` carries `key: "huggingface"` (one waited 643 s). An operator reading the line would look at the per-provider knob, which may not be what held the run. This plan records which cap was full when the run parked, and the line and the doctor row name that cap.

**Approach.**
- **src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts**, in the `usesSlot` admission closure inside `launchDueTicks`. Just before `lease = await semaphore.acquireLease(roleTier(runner.role), key)`, take `const pool = semaphore.snapshot()` and work out the cap that would hold the run:
  - `const keyed = key !== undefined ? pool.byKey[key] : undefined;`
  - `const providerFull = keyed?.limit !== undefined && keyed.inUse >= keyed.limit;`
  - `const heldBy = providerFull ? { cap: "provider" as const, limit: keyed!.limit! } : { cap: "team" as const, limit: pool.limit };`

  When both caps are full, the provider wins. The run's own key is the narrower knob, and both knobs are named in docs/how-it-works.md. The snapshot is taken at park time and isn't revised if the caps change mid-wait; say so in a one-line comment. Spread `...heldBy` into the `provider_wait` event beside `waitedMs` and `key`. Nothing else in the admission changes: the snapshot is read-only, and it's taken once per launched role run.
- **src/events/event-format.ts**, `case "provider_wait"`. When `e.cap === "provider"` and `e.key` is a non-empty string, render `waited <span> for a <key> slot (<role>; maxConcurrentPerProvider.<key> is <limit>)`. When `e.cap === "team"`, render `waited <span> for a run slot (<role>; maxConcurrent is <limit>)`, with no key named even when one is present. Read `limit` through `finiteNumber`; when `limit` isn't a finite number, drop the `; … is <limit>` part. An event with no `cap`, or an unknown one, renders today's line exactly, so older log lines read as before. Update the case's comment to say this.
- **src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts**, `checkProviderContention`. Bucket a wait under `""` ("the run cap") when `ev.cap === "team"`, whatever its key. Otherwise keep today's bucketing by key. On a warn, when the `""` bucket is non-empty and `config` is defined, add `raise maxConcurrent above <config.maxConcurrent>` to the advice list, after the per-provider entries and joined with the same `" and "`. Update the function's doc comment: a team-cap wait counts toward "the run cap" bucket.
- **src/events/events.ts**: extend the `"provider_wait"` union member's comment. It carries `cap` (`"provider"` when the run's provider key was at its cap when it parked, else `"team"`) and `limit` (that cap's value). Events logged before this change carry neither.
- **docs/how-it-works.md**, the `maxConcurrentPerProvider` bullet. The event names which cap held the run, and the doctor row files a team-cap wait under the run cap.

**Out of scope.** `report-fold.ts`'s `providerWaitMedianMs` stays one median over every wait. `tumwater doctor`'s "check contention" and "workspaces" rows are unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts, "a role tick that waits for its provider slot logs a provider_wait event; an at-once admission and a director do not". That test's existing wait (`Semaphore(1)`, `setKeyCaps({ omlx: 1 })`, held omlx lease) now also asserts `cap === "provider"` and `limit === 1`. Add a test of the same shape: `new Semaphore(1)` with no key caps, the team permit held by `semaphore.acquireLease(0, "other")`, and an omlx runner. Its `provider_wait` has `key === "omlx"`, `cap === "team"` and `limit === 1`.
- test/event-format.test.ts, "formatEvent renders provider_wait naming the key and the run cap when none". The two existing cap-less assertions still match. Add a `cap: "provider", limit: 2, key: "omlx"` event that matches `/waited 2m for a omlx slot \(feature; maxConcurrentPerProvider\.omlx is 2\)/`. Add a `cap: "team", limit: 3, key: "omlx"` event that matches `/waited 2m for a run slot \(feature; maxConcurrent is 3\)/` and does not contain `omlx`. Add a `cap: "team"` event with `limit: "x"` that matches `/for a run slot \(feature\)/`.
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts, "checkProviderContention sums the last day of provider_wait events and warns at ten minutes". Its existing assertions still hold, since those events carry no `cap`. Add a test: two waits with `key: "omlx"`, `cap: "team"`, 600_000 ms each, and a config with `maxConcurrent: 3` and no `maxConcurrentPerProvider`. The row warns, its detail contains `(the run cap)`, it contains `raise maxConcurrent above 3`, and it does not contain `omlx`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `team_paused` event carries the operator's pause reason and a timed pause's deadline, so `logs` and the failure digest say why the team was paused and until when (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/gates/pause-gates.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/failure/failure-state-change.ts src/events/events.ts test/pause-gates.test.ts test/event-format-team.test.ts test/failure-state-change.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater pause --for <dur> --reason <text>` (and the TUI's pause editor) writes both `until` and `reason` into the team pause marker through `pauseTeam` (src/team/team-state.ts), and `standingTeamPause` reads them back, folded and capped. `pollPauseGates` (src/gates/pause-gates.ts) logs the transition as a bare `{ source, type: "team_paused" }`. `formatEvent` (src/events/event-format.ts) and `describeStateChange` (src/failure/failure-state-change.ts) can therefore only render the fixed `teamPausePhrase()` line. Someone reading `logs` or the failure digest later can't tell a deploy-freeze pause from an indefinite one, or when a timed pause lifts. The TUI flash shows the reason only at the moment of pausing.

**Approach.**
- **src/gates/pause-gates.ts.** In `pollPauseGates`, read `const marker = standingTeamPause(root)` once and set `userPaused = marker !== null`. This replaces the `isTeamPaused` call, so the marker is still read once per poll. Import `standingTeamPause` and drop `isTeamPaused` if nothing else in the file uses it. On the paused transition, log `{ source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "team_paused", ...(marker.until !== undefined ? { until: marker.until } : {}), ...(marker.reason ? { reason: marker.reason } : {}) }`, so an untimed, reasonless pause logs the same line as before. `team_resumed` and the per-role branch stay unchanged. A re-pause that only changes the reason while the team is already paused still logs nothing; that edge-trigger behavior stays as it is.
- **src/events/event-format.ts.** In the `team_paused` case, build the line as `teamPausePhrase()`, then ` until ${formatTime(new Date(until))}` when `finiteNumber(e.until, null)` is a number, then `: ${reason}` when `e.reason` is a non-blank string, then the existing ` (director keeps running)`. Example: `team paused — roles start no new runs until 14:05:00: deploy freeze (director keeps running)`. A non-numeric `until` or a non-string `reason` renders as if absent, the same corrupt-field rule `windowResetPhrase` applies.
- **src/failure/failure-state-change.ts.** In the `team_paused` case, add the same two suffixes to `teamPausePhrase()`. Pass the reason through the file's `field()` and import `formatTime` from src/text/datetime.ts. Keep it inline in the case (two optional suffixes): a shared helper would cross the event-format ↔ digest import boundary for six lines.
- **src/events/events.ts.** Extend the `"team_paused"` union member's trailing comment: it carries `until` (ms epoch, timed pause only) and `reason` (the operator's `--reason`, when given). Events logged before the change carry neither.
- Do not change `team_resumed`, `role_paused`, src/events/event-labels.ts or the notify allowlist. `team_paused` is the operator's own action and stays unpaged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/pause-gates.test.ts: a new test. After `pauseTeam(root, Date.now() + 3_600_000, "deploy freeze")`, the first `pollPauseGates` logs exactly one `team_paused` event whose `reason` is `"deploy freeze"` and whose `until` equals the marker's. The existing "team pause logs team_paused once, resume logs team_resumed once" test also asserts that its plain `pauseTeam(root)` event has neither an `until` nor a `reason` key.
- test/event-format-team.test.ts "formatEvent renders the team pause and resume events plainly": the existing bare event still matches its regex. Add an event with `until` and `reason: "deploy freeze"`; it renders `team paused — roles start no new runs until ${formatTime(new Date(until))}: deploy freeze (director keeps running)`, with the expected value computed in the test so it holds in any time zone. An event with `until: "soon"` and `reason: 7` renders the bare line.
- test/failure-state-change.test.ts "team and role pauses render fixed and role-named lines": the bare `team_paused` assertion stays as is. Add one: `describeStateChange` of an event carrying both fields equals `team paused — roles start no new runs until <formatTime(new Date(until))>: deploy freeze`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### An `orchestrator_stop` event names why the team stopped (a restart onto a new build, a settled `--once` round, a stop signal, or a poll-loop error), so `logs` and the failure digest no longer read a bare "tumwater stopped" (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/text/phrases.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/failure/failure-state-change.ts src/events/events.ts test/event-format.test.ts test/failure-state-change.test.ts test/orchestrator.e2e.test.ts test/orchestrator-redeploy.e2e.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `runOrchestrator` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) emits `{ type: "orchestrator_stop" }` from its `finally` with no other field. `formatEvent` (src/events/event-format.ts) and `describeStateChange` (src/failure/failure-state-change.ts) both render it as the constant `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED` (src/text/phrases.ts), "tumwater stopped". The poll loop leaves its `while` in four ways, and each one means something different to an operator: `pollRedeploy` returns true (a self-redeploy drained and swaps builds), `pollReserveAndExit` returns true (the `--once` round settled and fired `internalStop`), the caller's signal aborted (Ctrl+C or SIGTERM, which is also how `tumwater stop` and the `--for` window's end reach the child), or a poll step threw. The orchestrator knows which one happened, but the event does not record it. Six `orchestrator_stop` events in the live log since 10-18 carry only `source`.

**Approach.**
- **src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts.** Before the `try`, declare `let stopCause: "restart" | "once" | "signal" | "error" = "error";`. Set it to `"restart"` immediately before the `pollRedeploy` break and to `"once"` immediately before the `pollReserveAndExit` break. After the `while` exits normally (the signal aborted), set `"signal"` only when `stopCause` is still `"error"`, as the last statement inside the `try`. A throw therefore leaves `"error"`. The `finally` emits `{ source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "orchestrator_stop", cause: stopCause }`. Change nothing else in the loop or the drain.
- **src/text/phrases.ts.** Make `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED` module-private (the exports test rejects an unused export) and add `orchestratorStopPhrase(cause: unknown): string`. It returns `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED` followed by ` to restart onto the new build` for `"restart"`, ` — the --once round settled` for `"once"`, ` on a stop signal` for `"signal"`, and ` — its polling failed` for `"error"`. Any other value, including undefined from every pre-change event, returns the bare `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED`. Give it a doc comment that names both callers, like the constant's.
- **src/events/event-format.ts** and **src/failure/failure-state-change.ts.** Their `orchestrator_stop` cases return or assign `orchestratorStopPhrase(e.cause)` / `orchestratorStopPhrase(ev.cause)` in place of the constant. Drop the `ORCHESTRATOR_STOPPED` import from a file that no longer uses it, because lint flags unused imports.
- **src/events/events.ts.** Add a trailing comment on the `"orchestrator_stop"` union member: it carries `cause` (`restart`, `once`, `signal` or `error`), and events logged before the field existed carry none.
- Do not change `src/events/event-labels.ts`. Its `orchestrator_stop` label is the type's short name, not the event line.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/event-format.test.ts "formatEvent renders wake reasons and warning messages operators rely on": the existing cause-less `orchestrator_stop` still matches `/tumwater stopped/`. Add an assertion that `{ type: "orchestrator_stop", cause: "restart" }` renders exactly `tumwater stopped to restart onto the new build`.
- test/failure-state-change.test.ts "run_deferred, orchestrator lifecycle, and supervisor_exit render their payloads": the existing assertion that the cause-less event renders `"tumwater stopped"` stays as it is. Add exact-string assertions for `cause: "once"`, `"signal"` and `"error"`, and one for `cause: "bogus"` that renders the bare `"tumwater stopped"`.
- test/orchestrator.e2e.test.ts "runOrchestrator ticks enabled roles and cleans up on shutdown" (the caller aborts its controller) asserts that the logged `orchestrator_stop` event has `cause: "signal"`.
- test/orchestrator-redeploy.e2e.test.ts "a stale self-hosted build drains the team, swaps, and returns restart" asserts that the logged `orchestrator_stop` event has `cause: "restart"`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `claude_window_warning` event carries the window's utilization, so the notify page and `logs` say how full the window is, not only "near its limit" (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

### A `merge_failed` event carries why the merge failed, so a notify page, `logs` and the failure report name the reason, not only the outcome code (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The blocked Plain terms parts rename identifiers in src/merge/ and src/events/ later, which is only a rebase. Touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts src/events/event-format.ts src/failure/failure-data.ts docs/config.md test/merge-slot.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts test/failure-render.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) logs `merge_failed` with `commit`, `result`, `summary`, duration and usage, but no reason. Across the live team's last 523 `merge_failed` events, none carries a reason field. The notify hook's page is `formatEvent(event)` (`spawnNotifyCommand`, src/events/notify.ts), and `merge_failed` is on `NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`. So a paged operator reads `merge of ab6d53e2 failed (review error) (in 54m) — Reject misspelled tier names…` and has to open `tumwater logs` to learn why. `mergeFailureSection` (src/failure/failure-data.ts) works around the same gap by pairing each blocked or conflicted `merge_failed` with the role's last earlier `warning`. Put the reason on the event itself.

**Approach.**
- **src/merge/merge-slot.ts.** Add an exported pure helper, `mergeFailureReason(state: RunnerState, result: TickResult, startedAt: number): string | undefined`. `writeMergeOutcome` calls it after `applyMergeOutcome`, with `startedAt = Date.now() - durationMs`. When the helper returns a string, `writeMergeOutcome` adds `reason: truncate(reason, 300)` to the `merge_failed` event (`truncate` from src/text/text.ts). The helper's rules:
  - `changed` and `aborted` have no reason, so the helper returns undefined.
  - `rejected`: return `state.lastReview.reasons[0]` (trimmed) only when `state.lastReview.at >= startedAt`. That is the review this merge recorded (`run-apply.ts` writes it on a reject; `merge-core.ts` writes the `reverted` one). An older review is stale, so return undefined.
  - Any other result (`review_error`, `main_red`, `merge_blocked`, `merge_conflict`): take `state.lastError`. Every merge path that ends with one of these sets `lastError` first: merge-core.ts's `gate check failed:` and `review failed:` lines and its `merge failed: ${result}` catch-all, merge-check-failures.ts, and the drain/batch/verify `errorMessage(err)` catches. Strip a leading `merge failed: `, then a leading `${result} — `. Return undefined when what remains is empty or equals `result`, which is the catch-all's bare `merge failed: merge_conflict`.
  - Extend `writeMergeOutcome`'s doc comment with one sentence: the failed event carries the reason the helper derives.
- **src/events/event-format.ts.** In the `merge_failed` case, a non-empty string `e.reason` renders inside the outcome parenthesis as `failed (rejected: <truncate(reason, 120)>)`. An event without `reason` (every old log line) renders exactly as today. Update the case comment: the event now names its reason itself, and the review/check events still carry the full text.
- **src/failure/failure-data.ts.** In `mergeFailureSection`, prefer a non-empty string `ev.reason` over `lastWarning.get(role)`. Old events keep the warning pairing and the `NO_MERGE_REASON` fallback. Mention the preference in the function's doc comment.
- **docs/config.md.** Change the notify table's `merge_failed` row to say the message names the change's summary and why the merge failed: the review's first reason, or the check, block or error that stopped it.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/merge-slot.test.ts adds cases that call `writeMergeOutcome` and read the event back. (1) `rejected` with `state.lastReview = { verdict: "reject", reasons: ["no test covers the new flag", "other"], at: Date.now() }` gives `reason: "no test covers the new flag"`. (2) `rejected` with a `lastReview.at` older than the merge's start gives no `reason` key. (3) `merge_blocked` with `lastError = "merge failed: merge_blocked — check failed (\`npm run test\`): ✖ x"` gives `reason: "check failed (\`npm run test\`): ✖ x"`. (4) `merge_conflict` with `lastError = "merge failed: merge_conflict"` gives no `reason` key. (5) `changed` gives no `reason` key.

The existing reason-less assertions stay unchanged.

- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A red check's reasons drop Node's own `node:internal` stack frames and the lines the headline already repeats, so the clipped tail keeps more of the assertion's diff (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/build/build-check-report.ts and test/build-check-report.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A red check's output becomes `outputTail` through `clipBuildTail` (src/build/build-check-report.ts): the last 10 meaningful lines, plus a rescued failed-test name line and error-message line. `checkFailureReasons` turns that tail into the reasons a rejection records in `state.lastReview`, the author's next-run note, and the `review_rejected` event. Today the 10-line window spends lines on node:test's own plumbing frames (`at async Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1409:7)`, `at async Test.processPendingSubtests (node:internal/…)`). Those frames are the same in every failure and say nothing about the code under test. In the event log's last 200,000 lines (2026-10-16 18:28Z to 2026-10-20), 20 of 24 `review_rejected` events whose first reason starts `check failed` carried such frames: 50 of their 283 reason lines. Because the window is cut from the end, these frames push out the lines just above the stack, which is where a failed `strictEqual` or `deepStrictEqual` prints its diff. Example: node:test prints `1 !== 0` between `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:` and the stack. In the spec-output fixture of the test "failureHeadline names the failed test even when the stack and assertion dump crowd its name out of the window", that diff line is cut today. Dropping the two internal frames keeps it. Separately, when the headline is `<test name> — <message>`, `checkFailureReasons` removes only a tail line equal to the whole headline. So the `✖ <test name> (510.9ms)` line and the message line both appear again right below the headline, which already says both (seen in the 2026-10-20 `report --role` rejections).

**Approach.**
- src/build/build-check-report.ts:
  - Add `const NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME = /^at\s(?:.*\()?node:internal\//;` with a doc comment: a stack frame inside Node's own runtime (the test runner, the task queue). It matches both `at fn (node:internal/…)` and a bare `at node:internal/…`. It does not match frames in other built-in modules such as `node:fs` or `node:async_hooks`, nor frames in project files.
  - `clipBuildTail`: after the existing blank/banner filter, drop every line `NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME` matches, before taking the 10-line window and the `cut` prefix. If that leaves no lines, use the unfiltered lines, so output made only of internal frames still yields a tail and a headline. When the dropped frame is `at async Test.processPendingSubtests (…) {`, the property dump's opening `{` goes with it; that is accepted. Add one sentence to the doc comment.
  - `checkFailureReasons`, the verified (non-`unverified`) branch: after the headline, drop each tail line the headline already carries, not only the line equal to the whole headline. That means a line equal to the headline; a line that, with its trailing duration removed (the same ` \([\d.]+m?s\)$` replace `failureHeadline` uses), equals the headline or plus ` — ` starts it (the test-name or ⚠ marker line, including node:test's second copy under `✖ failing tests:`); and a line with which the headline ends after a ` — ` (the message line). Every other line keeps its order. The `unverified` branch is unchanged. Update the doc comment.
- No other file changes: `failureHeadline`, `parseFailingTests` (which reads the full output, not the tail), and the callers in src/review/review-precheck.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts and src/baseline/main-baseline.ts read the new tail as is.

**Tests** (test/build-check-report.test.ts):
- Update "failureHeadline names the failed test even when the stack and assertion dump crowd its name out of the window". `tail.length` becomes 11: the rescued name, then a window that now contains the message and `1 !== 0`. Assert `tail.includes("1 !== 0")`, and that no tail line contains `node:internal/`. The headline assertion is unchanged. (A standalone simulation of the change on this fixture gave exactly that 11-line tail.)
- New, "clipBuildTail drops node:internal frames but keeps project and other built-in frames". Use output of: an `AssertionError …` line, `at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///w/dist/test/x.test.js:3:35)`, `at Test.runInAsyncScope (node:async_hooks:226:14)`, `at Test.run (node:internal/test_runner/test:1397:25)`, `at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)`, `actual: 1,`. The tail is those lines without the two `node:internal` frames, in order.
- New, "clipBuildTail keeps an all-internal output rather than returning nothing": two `node:internal` frames in, the same two out.
- New, "a red check's reasons do not repeat the test name or message the headline carries". Pass a tail of `✖ t (1.5ms)`, `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: boom`, `actual: 1,` to `checkFailureReasons`. Expect `["check failed (\`npm run test\`): ✖ t — AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: boom", "actual: 1,"]`.
- The existing "a red check's reasons lead with the headline and drop it from the tail" passes unchanged: it calls `checkFailureReasons` on a hand-built tail, which `clipBuildTail` never filters. So does test/review-precheck.test.ts "gate pre-check names the failing assertion, not the stack frame the tail opens on": its `at TestContext` and `node:async_hooks` frames survive, so `reasons.some((r) => r.startsWith("at "))` still holds.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- No `outputTail` produced by `clipBuildTail` from output that holds any other meaningful line contains a frame `NODE_INTERNAL_FRAME` matches. Frames in project files and in other `node:` modules are kept.
- For the spec-output fixture above, the tail holds `1 !== 0`, and `failureHeadline` still reads `✖ the wake was restored — AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:`.
- A verified red check's reasons hold the headline once. No later reason is the test-name line or the message line the headline already contains.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A merge whose files are dirty in the primary checkout is blocked before its merge check runs, instead of after a full check and three fast-forward attempts (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-git.ts, src/merge/merge-stack.ts, src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, src/merge/merge-batch.ts and their tests. The in-flight entry "A merge blocked by a dirty primary checkout names the files git refused to overwrite…" also edits src/merge/merge-git.ts and adds `overwriteBlockedReason`; this entry prints the same wording, and whichever lands second only rebases)

**Goal.** When the primary checkout is on main, `ffMainToOrWhy` (src/merge/merge-git.ts) fast-forwards it with `git merge --ff-only`. git refuses when the checkout holds uncommitted edits to a file the merge changes, or an untracked file the merge would create. Today tumwater learns this only at the fast-forward, after the expensive step. On 2026-10-19 between 21:26 and 21:39 UTC the event log shows the cost. In the batch path, `mergeStackIn` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) ran a 258 s `build_check` and then failed the fast-forward. The re-stack loop retried twice more, because a re-stack onto an unchanged tip skips the check (`docOnlyRestack`), so the 3 `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: …` warnings came within 0.8 s. The loop then returned `blocked`, and `mergeApproved` (src/merge/merge-batch.ts) emitted `merge_blocked` for every change. Leftover recovery re-merges each such change through its own gate and `tryMerge` (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts), whose in-lock check runs before the same doomed fast-forward. Over those 13 minutes plan, director, feature-2 and bugfix-3 logged `merge_failed merge_blocked` with durations of 152–548 s. A dirty checkout can be seen with one `git status` before any check runs.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-git.ts: add `export async function primaryCheckoutBlockers(root: string, mainBranch: string, tip: string): Promise<{ uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] } | null>`.
  - Return null when `currentBranch(root)` is not `mainBranch`, because the ref-push arm touches no working tree.
  - Otherwise read the paths the merge changes with `gitTry(root, "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-only", mainBranch, tip)`, and the checkout's state with `gitTry(root, "--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")`. `--no-optional-locks` keeps a read-only status from taking `index.lock` under an operator's own git.
  - Split the `-z` output on NUL. Each record is `XY<space>path`. A rename or copy record (X `R` or `C`) is followed by one more record holding the source path; consume it and treat both paths as uncommitted.
  - Put a changed path from a `??` record in `untracked`, and one from any other record in `uncommitted`. Keep the diff's order, and keep only paths in the diff's set.
  - Return null when both lists are empty, or when either git call fails (`gitTry` returns null). This pre-flight never blocks on a read error; the fast-forward still decides.
- The reason text, `the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: a.txt, b.txt; untracked: c.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`. Leave out an empty group, and list at most 5 names per group, then `, +N more`. If `overwriteBlockedReason` already exists in merge-git.ts when you start, call it. Otherwise add it there as `export function overwriteBlockedReason(blockers: { uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] }): string`, with exactly that output, so the sibling entry finds it.
- src/merge/merge-stack.ts `mergeStackIn`: right after `assembleStack` returns and `tip` is known, before `docOnlyRestack`, call `primaryCheckoutBlockers(ctx.root, ctx.mainBranch, tip)`. On non-null, `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, mergeDone.at(-1)!.role, \`merge blocked: ${overwriteBlockedReason(b)}\`)` (the role `ffStackToMain` warns under) and return `{ kind: "blocked" }`. No check runs, and no re-stack follows. Add a sentence to the function's doc comment.
- src/merge/merge-batch.ts: in `mergeApproved`'s `outcome.kind === "blocked"` arm, reword the comment to cover both causes: a race lost on every attempt, or a dirty primary checkout found before the check. The code there is unchanged.
- src/merge/merge-to-main.ts `tryMerge`: after `const target = await headOf(wt, "HEAD")` and before `verifyMerge`, make the same call with `target`. On non-null, warn `merge blocked: <reason>` under `ctx.role` and return `"merge_blocked"`. The in-lock check is skipped. The gate check that ran before the lock is not saved; this entry does not try to save it.
- `ffFailureReason` and `ffMainToOrWhy` stay unchanged. A checkout that turns dirty between the pre-flight and the fast-forward still fails there, as it does today.

**Tests.**
- test/merge-git.test.ts, "primaryCheckoutBlockers names only the dirty paths the merge changes". Use `initializedWorktree()`. In `wt`, commit an edit to a tracked `shared.txt` (committed on main first, then `git reset --hard main` in `wt`) and a new `fresh.txt`. In `root`, overwrite `shared.txt` without committing, write an untracked `fresh.txt` and an untracked `other.txt`. Expect `{ uncommitted: ["shared.txt"], untracked: ["fresh.txt"] }`; `other.txt` is not in the diff. A clean `root` returns null. A `root` checked out on another branch returns null.
- test/merge-git.test.ts, "overwriteBlockedReason caps each group at 5 names": 7 uncommitted names list the first 5, then `, +2 more`, and no `untracked:` group. Skip this case if the sibling entry already landed an equivalent test.
- test/merger-restack.test.ts, "a batch whose files are dirty in the primary checkout is blocked before its check". Use `batchFixture(["alpha", "beta"])`, whose default edit creates `alpha.txt` and `beta.txt`. Write an untracked `alpha.txt` in `root`, then run `runBatch` with `withApprovePi`, as the neighbouring tests do. Expect results `["merge_blocked", "merge_blocked"]` and `batchChecks(root).length === 0`. `warningMessages(root)` holds exactly one `merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (untracked: alpha.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there` and no `fast-forward failed` line. Both refs are kept, and main has not moved.
- The existing tests in test/merge-git.test.ts, test/merge-stack.test.ts, test/merger-restack.test.ts and test/merger.test.ts pass unchanged. Their primary checkouts are clean, so the pre-flight returns null.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a file the merge changes left uncommitted or untracked in a primary checkout that is on main, a batch merge runs no `build_check`, logs one `merge blocked: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (…) — commit, stash or remove them there`, and keeps every change's ref as `merge_blocked`. A single-change `tryMerge` returns `merge_blocked` with the same warning and runs no in-lock check.
- A dirty path the merge does not change, a primary checkout off main, and a clean checkout all merge exactly as today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A merge blocked by a dirty primary checkout names the files git refused to overwrite, instead of cutting git's error off at "would be overwritten by merge:" (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-git.ts and test/merge-git.test.ts. Plain terms code run 18/20 later renames code in src/merge/ but no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases)

**Goal.** When the primary checkout is on main, a merge fast-forwards it with `git merge --ff-only` (`ffMainToOrWhy`, src/merge/merge-git.ts). If the checkout holds uncommitted edits to a file the merge changes, or untracked files the merge would create, git refuses. It lists the files on tab-indented lines below a `… would be overwritten by merge:` header. `ffFailureReason` keeps only the first line of the error, so both callers' warnings (`mergeToMain` in src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, the stacked fast-forward in src/merge/merge-stack.ts) end at that colon. Between 21:26 and 21:39 UTC on 2026-10-19 the event log held 10 such `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: … Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:` warnings, from plan, director, feature-3 and feature-2. None of them said which file to commit or remove. The warning should name the files.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-git.ts: add `export function overwriteBlockers(gitError: string): { uncommitted: string[]; untracked: string[] }`. It walks the error's lines. A line containing `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:` starts the uncommitted group, and a line containing `untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge:` starts the untracked group. Each following line that starts with a tab adds its trimmed text to the current group. Any other line ends the group. git can print both groups in one error, as `git merge --ff-only` does when one file is dirty and another is untracked.
- `ffFailureReason`: after the main-moved test, compute `overwriteBlockers(errorMessage(err))`. If either group is non-empty, return `fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: a.txt, b.txt; untracked: c.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`. Leave out a group that is empty. Each group lists at most 5 names and then `, +N more`. If both groups are empty, return the first line of the error as today. Update the doc comment: a dirty primary checkout is reported with its files, and any other cause still reports git's first line.
- The `merge blocked: ` prefix and both callers stay unchanged, so the warnings in merge-to-main.ts and merge-stack.ts pick up the new wording with no edits.

**Tests.** In test/merge-git.test.ts, beside "ffMainToOrWhy names main having moved off the ref's base, with its new head":
- "overwriteBlockers reads both of git's would-be-overwritten lists". Input: the error text `git merge --ff-only abc failed (1): error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:\n\tf.txt\n\tg.txt\nPlease commit your changes or stash them before you merge.\nerror: The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge:\n\tnew.txt\nPlease move or remove them before you merge.\nAborting`. Expected: `{ uncommitted: ["f.txt", "g.txt"], untracked: ["new.txt"] }`. An error without either header gives two empty lists.
- "ffMainToOrWhy names the primary checkout's files the fast-forward would overwrite". Use `initializedWorktree()`. Commit `shared.txt` on main in `root`, then `sh(wt, "git", "reset", "--hard", "main")`. In `wt`, change `shared.txt`, add `fresh.txt` and commit. In `root`, overwrite `shared.txt` without committing and write an untracked `fresh.txt`. `ffMainToOrWhy(root, headSha(wt), "main")` returns exactly `fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (uncommitted: shared.txt; untracked: fresh.txt) — commit, stash or remove them there`, and main's head has not moved.
- A unit case for the cap: 7 uncommitted names list the first 5, then `, +2 more`. Export the message builder as `overwriteBlockedReason(blockers)` so this case needs no repo.
- The existing `ffMainToOrWhy` tests pass unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A merge blocked by uncommitted or untracked files in the primary checkout logs `merge blocked: fast-forward failed: the merge would overwrite files in the primary checkout (…) — commit, stash or remove them there`, naming up to 5 files per group.
- Every other fast-forward failure (main moved outside the merge lock, or any other git error) reads exactly as it does today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A tool call's label drops a leading `cd <dir> &&`, so a stalled command's warning names the command and not the worktree path (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/text/phrases.ts and test/phrases.test.ts. Plain terms code run 14/20 edits comments in src/text/phrases.ts but renames no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `describeToolCall` (src/text/phrases.ts) builds the one-line label of a tool call: `<toolName> <detail>`, with the detail squashed to 32 characters. Three places use it: the stall warning (src/pi/pi-stream.ts builds the label, and src/pi/pi-watchdogs.ts logs `tool call stalled: <label> — …`), the dashboards' last-tool cell and stall flag (src/ui/progress-data.ts), and transcript rendering (src/ui/transcript.ts). Agents often start a bash command with `cd <their worktree> && …`. The absolute worktree path then fills all 32 characters. In the event log from 2026-10-17 15:58 to 2026-10-19 22:51 UTC, 46 of the 60 `tool call stalled` warnings read exactly `tool call stalled: bash cd /Users/zach/tumwater/.tumwat… — …`, and none of those 46 says which command hung. The label should skip the leading `cd` and show the command that runs after it.

**Approach.**
- src/text/phrases.ts: add a module-private `withoutLeadingCd(command: string): string`. It removes leading segments that match `^\s*cd\s+("[^"]*"|'[^']*'|\S+)\s*(?:&&|;)\s*`, repeatedly, so `cd a && cd b && npm test` becomes `npm test`. Remove a segment only when it ends in `&&` or `;`. A bare `cd dir`, or `cd dir || …`, stays unchanged. If removing would leave the string empty, return the original.
- `describeToolCall`: apply `withoutLeadingCd` only when the candidate came from `args.command` or `args.cmd`, before `squash`. Paths, patterns and urls are unchanged. Add one sentence to the doc comment: a leading `cd <dir> &&` is dropped from a command, because the run's cwd is implied and the path would use up the 32-character budget.
- No caller changes. The stall classifier reads the raw `call.command` (`commandBuffersOutput(call.command || call.label)` in pi-watchdogs.ts and `stalledToolLabel`), not the label, so INV-A2's threshold behavior does not change. A `cd x && sleep 999 | tail` command still classifies as buffered through its raw command.

**Tests.** In test/phrases.test.ts, add the test "describeToolCall drops a leading cd so the label names the command":
- `describeToolCall("bash", { command: "cd /Users/zach/tumwater/.tumwater/worktrees/_slot-10 && npm run test:gate > x.log 2>&1" })` returns `bash npm run test:gate > x.log 2>&1`. A remainder longer than 32 characters is squashed as today: `cd /w && ` followed by 40 `x` gives `bash ` followed by 31 `x` and `…`.
- `cd "/a b" && ls` gives `bash ls`. `cd a; cd b && make` gives `bash make`. `{ cmd: "cd a && ls" }` gives `bash ls`.
- These stay unchanged: `cd /tmp` gives `bash cd /tmp`, and `cd a || exit 1` gives `bash cd a || exit 1`. `{ path: "/x/cd y && z" }` still basenames to `cd y && z`.
- The existing describeToolCall tests and the `tool call stalled` assertions in test/pi.test.ts pass unchanged (none of their commands starts with `cd`).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A stalled `cd <worktree> && <cmd>` call logs `tool call stalled: bash <cmd…> — …`. The dashboards' last-tool cell and the transcripts show the same label.
- A command with no leading `cd … &&`/`;` segment gets exactly the label it gets today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 8/20: Rename the runner's run pipeline phases (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 7/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/runner.ts + src/runner/runner-run.ts + test/runner.test.ts + test/runner-2.test.ts through test/runner-5.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The runner's run pipeline (`runPhase`, `runOncePhase`, `runOnceInLeasePhase`, `runWithWorktreePhase`) and the runner's comments and core tests use run wording throughout.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: `tickPhase` → `runPhase`, `runTickPhase` → `runOncePhase` (it pairs with `RoleRunner.runOnce`), `runTickInLeasePhase` → `runOnceInLeasePhase`, `tickWithWorktreePhase` → `runWithWorktreePhase`, and the locals `quietKilledTick`, `tickBase`, `nTick` and `tickOutcome` → run forms. This file has about 150 tick lines; most are comments describing the pipeline, and most of its "run" nouns mean the agent run, so apply the "agent run" rule here with care.
- src/runner/runner.ts: comments ("one full tick of this role" → "one full run of this role"), and uses of `RunOutcome`, `RunUsage`, `runPhase` and `runOncePhase`.
- Tests test/runner.test.ts and test/runner-2.test.ts through test/runner-5.test.ts: migrate names, comments and titles. docs/invariants.md quotes test/runner-2.test.ts titles ("a tick whose agent reads an image on a blind model stops and fails", "a blind read on a text-only …"); update the quotes to the renamed titles.

**Files touched.** src/runner/runner.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, test/runner.test.ts, test/runner-2.test.ts, test/runner-3.test.ts, test/runner-4.test.ts, test/runner-5.test.ts, docs/invariants.md (quotes only).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `runPhase`, `runOncePhase`, `runOnceInLeasePhase` and `runWithWorktreePhase` are declared, and no tick-named function remains in src/runner/runner-run.ts.
- `grep -nE '[Tt]ick|TICK'` over this part's seven code files prints nothing except kept senses.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Kill orphans, part 2/2: the TUI Health pane's Ctrl+K twice kills the orphaned processes, the terminal twin of the dashboard's Kill orphans (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; requires part 1/2 landed for `orphanKillLines` and the `OrphanKillReport` export. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, docs/cli.md, test/tui-keys.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts. Plain terms code run 15/20 later renames code in src/ui/tui/; this entry renames nothing, done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The TUI's Health pane already has Ctrl+R (re-run), Ctrl+E (reclaim) and Ctrl+N (test notify) as twins of dashboard actions. It has no twin for the Kill orphans button from part 1/2. A terminal operator who sees the orphans row fail should be able to reap the processes without leaving the TUI.

**Approach.**
- src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add a `killOrphans?(root: string): Promise<OrphanKillReport>` seam to the deps beside `runDoctor`, defaulting to `(r) => killOrphans(r)` from src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts, and pass it into the session deps the same way `runDoctor: runDoctorSeam` is passed.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts: add `killOrphans(root)` to `TuiPanesDeps` and to the session, beside `runDoctor`. Add the armed pair `armedKillOrphans: boolean` and `killOrphansArmed: boolean`, both initially false and documented like `armedNotes`/`notesClearArmed`.
- src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: `beginKey` moves `killOrphansArmed` into `armedKillOrphans` and clears `killOrphansArmed`, the same as the other armed pairs. Extend its doc comment to say that only the Health Ctrl+K branch reads `armedKillOrphans`.
- src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts: in `handleKey`, add a `key.ctrl && key.name === "k" && promptLineFree(ctx.es) && session.view === session.roleIds.length + 7` branch. If `session.armedKillOrphans` is false, set `session.killOrphansArmed = true` and flash `press Ctrl+K again to kill the orphaned processes the orphans check lists — any other key keeps them`. If it is true, flash `killing orphaned processes …` and call `session.killOrphans(session.root)`. When that resolves, flash `orphanKillLines(report).join("; ")`, then `run()`, `session.paneScroll = 0` and `requestRender()`, the same order Ctrl+E uses. A rejection goes to `session.flashError`. Write the comment block in the style of the Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N blocks. Ctrl+K is not bound on any view outside the prompt-line editor (src/ui/tui/tui-input.ts), and `promptLineFree` keeps that editor's kill-line binding.
- src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: the `health` hint list gets `["Ctrl+K", "kill orphans"]` after `["Ctrl+N", "test notify"]`.
- docs/cli.md: add a `Ctrl+K` row to the TUI key table (Health: twice kills the orphaned processes, like `tumwater doctor --kill-orphans` and the dashboard Health card's Kill orphans). The Audit row's `doctor` text names the TUI's Health Ctrl+K beside the dashboard button.

**Tests.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts, beside "Ctrl+N on the Health view runs the notify hook once and flashes the outcome": "Ctrl+K twice on the Health view kills the orphans and flashes the lines". With an injected `killOrphans` that counts calls and resolves `{ killed: [{ pid: 4242, command: "node x", descendants: 0 }], failed: [] }`, the first Ctrl+K makes no call and flashes the press-again note. The second makes one call, flashes `killed pid 4242 node x`, and calls the injected `runDoctor` again.
- Same file: "a key between two Ctrl+K presses on the Health view disarms the kill". The sequence Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+K makes no call.
- Same file: "Ctrl+K off the Health view never kills". Ctrl+K twice on Activity makes no call.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: the health hint matches `/Ctrl\+K kill orphans/`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Health pane, Ctrl+K arms and a second consecutive Ctrl+K runs `killOrphans` once. The flash shows the same lines `doctor --kill-orphans` prints (joined with `; `), and the checks re-run.
- Any other key between the two presses cancels the kill. Ctrl+K on other views, and in the prompt-line editor, behaves as it does today.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A run whose end-of-run sweep had to kill processes it left running logs a warning naming the role and the count, so a leaking role shows up in the event feed instead of the sweep's count being discarded (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/process/run-marker.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts, test/run-marker.test.ts and test/pi-process.test.ts. The blocked Plain terms code parts reword src/runner/runner-pi.ts and src/agent/run-agent.ts, but they rename no identifier this entry uses or adds; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** When pi exits, the exit hook in `runAgent` (src/agent/run-agent.ts) calls `sweepRunMarker(runMarker)` (src/process/run-marker.ts). That sends SIGTERM to every process still carrying the run's `TUMWATER_RUN` mark and returns how many it signaled, but the hook throws the number away (`void sweepRunMarker(runMarker).catch(() => {})`). So nobody can tell which role's runs leave servers, watchers or `logs -f` followers running. BUGS.md's open entry about two leaked `logs -f` processes had to be traced by hand. When a run that tumwater did not kill leaves marked processes running, the run should log one warning under its role, giving the run kind and how many processes the sweep signaled. Runs that tumwater kills (abort, deadline, quiet watchdog, blind image read) are excluded: their process group got SIGTERM moments before the sweep scans, so members that are still exiting would be counted and every killed run would raise a false leak.

**Approach.**
- src/process/run-marker.ts: add `export function leftoversSweptMessage(kind: PiRunKind, count: number, killed: boolean): string | undefined`. It returns undefined when `count === 0` or `killed` is true. Otherwise it returns `run sweep: ${plural(count, "process", "processes")} the ${kind} run started ${count === 1 ? "was" : "were"} still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`, using `plural` from src/text/phrases.ts. Import `PiRunKind` as a type from src/pi/pi-event-line.ts. In the doc comment, explain why killed runs are excluded (see Goal).
- src/agent/run-agent.ts:
  - Add an optional `onLeftoversSwept?: (message: string) => void` to `PiRunOptions`. Its doc comment goes beside `onToolCallStalled` and `onAgentWarning`.
  - Put the killed test in one place: declare `const wasKilled = (): boolean => aborted || wd.timedOut || wd.quietKilled || blindRead !== undefined;` right after `let aborted = false;` (below the `startPiWatchdogs` call that sets up `wd`). The `close` handler's `const killed = …` becomes `const killed = wasKilled();`.
  - The `exit` hook becomes `void sweepRunMarker(runMarker).then((n) => { const msg = leftoversSweptMessage(opts.kind, n, wasKilled()); if (msg) opts.onLeftoversSwept?.(msg); }).catch(() => {});`. The sweep is still not awaited, so the run resolves exactly when it did before.
- src/runner/runner-pi.ts (`RunnerPi.runnerPiOpts`): set `onLeftoversSwept: (message) => this.host.warn(message)` beside `onToolCallStalled`. This one site covers the author run, its follow-ups and the gate (review/resolver) runs, because each of them builds its options here. A gate run's warning is filed under the authoring role, the same as its usage.

**Tests.**
- test/run-marker.test.ts, "leftoversSweptMessage words the sweep's count and stays silent for a killed or clean run": `("author", 1, false)` gives `run sweep: 1 process the author run started was still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`. `("gate", 2, false)` contains `2 processes the gate run started were`. `("author", 0, false)` and `("author", 3, true)` give undefined.
- test/pi-process.test.ts, "the end-of-run sweep reaches a detached tool call's cross-group orphan (regression)": pass `onLeftoversSwept: (m) => messages.push(m)` through `runPiFixture(dir, { config, onLeftoversSwept })`. After the existing `waitFor` that the orphan is gone, also `waitFor` `messages.length === 1` (the callback fires after the sweep's scan resolves) and assert that `messages[0]` starts with `run sweep: 1 process the author run started`. `runPiFixture` (test/helpers/pi-run-harness.ts) already passes `kind: "author"`. The existing finally that kills the orphan stays.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A run that ends without being killed and leaves N ≥ 1 marked processes running logs one `warning` event under its role, reading `run sweep: N process(es) the <author|gate> run started … still running after pi exited; sent SIGTERM`.
- A run that leaves nothing running logs no sweep warning. A run that tumwater aborted or killed (deadline, quiet watchdog, blind read) logs none whatever the sweep counts.
- The run's result, its resolve timing and the sweep's SIGTERM/SIGKILL behavior do not change: `sweepRunMarker`'s signature and body stay as they are, and the existing tests in test/run-marker.test.ts and test/pi-process.test.ts pass.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Kill orphans, part 1/2: the dashboard Health card's Kill orphans button runs `doctor --kill-orphans`, so an operator does not need a terminal to reap leaked processes (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every Planned entry. Touches src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts, src/cli.ts, src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts. **Goal.** `tumwater doctor --kill-orphans` kills the processes the orphans check fails on, and the check's detail names that command. The dashboard's Health card (Settings view) shows the same failing row but offers no way to act on it, so the operator has to switch to a terminal. Add a two-click Kill orphans button to the Health card. It runs the same `killOrphans`, toasts what was killed in the CLI's wording, and re-runs the checks.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-orphans.ts: export the report type as `OrphanKillReport` and add `export function orphanKillLines(report: OrphanKillReport): string[]`. Move the CLI's wording into it unchanged: `could not scan the process table — <error>; nothing killed`; `killed pid <pid>` plus ` (+N descendant(s))` when there are descendants, then ` <command>`; `could not kill pid <pid>: <reason>`; and `no orphaned processes to kill` when both lists are empty. Import `plural` from src/text/phrases.ts, as src/cli.ts does.
- src/cli.ts: the `doctor --kill-orphans` branch prints `orphanKillLines(await killOrphans(root))` one line per `say`, then the blank line it prints now. CLI output does not change.

It follows `handleReclaim`'s body discipline (`readPostBody(req, res, "{}")`, body ignored) and answers `sendJson(res, 200, { ok: !("error" in report) && report.failed.length === 0, message: orphanKillLines(report).join("; ") })`. Re-export it from src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts beside `handleReclaim`. Route it in src/gui/gui-server.ts as `"POST /api/kill-orphans"` beside `"POST /api/reclaim"`.
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts: `buildSettingsView`'s doctorcard header gets `<button type='button' class='btn btn-sm' data-action='doctor-kill-orphans'>Kill orphans</button>` after Re-run. Add `const killSlot = confirmSlot(paintKillButton)` and a `killOrphansClick()`. The first click arms the slot and the button reads `Confirm kill`. A second click within the window disarms the slot, shows `showFlash("Killing orphaned processes…")`, posts `/api/kill-orphans`, and then shows `showFlash((d.ok ? "" : "error: ") + d.message)` and calls `fetchDoctor()`. A post failure flashes `"error: " + clientErrorMessage(err)`, the same as `testNotify`. `paintKillButton` sets the button's text from `killSlot.armed("orphans")`.

An injected `kill` resolving `{ killed: [{ pid: 4242, command: "node x", descendants: 1 }], failed: [] }` answers `{ ok: true, message: "killed pid 4242 (+1 descendant) node x" }`. One resolving `{ error: "boom" }` answers `ok: false` with the scan wording.
