### A slot reset drops a dangling pin under any `refs/tumwater/` namespace and logs a `warning` event naming the ref, its sha and its file age, so the next occurrence leaves evidence for the open object-pruned-before-ref question (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** BUGS-FIXED.md's 2026-10-19 "dangling `refs/tumwater/merge/feature-5`" fix made `checkoutDetached` (src/git/worktree.ts) delete a `refs/tumwater/merge/<role>` ref whose object is gone and retry the checkout. Two gaps remain:

1. The heal only matches `refs/tumwater/merge/`. A `refs/tumwater/rejected/<role>` pin (`rejectedRefName`, src/paths.ts), written by `recordRejectedChange` in src/merge/merge-core.ts, wedges `git checkout --detach` the same way, because git walks every ref to report orphaned commits. So does a leftover legacy `refs/tumwater/landing/<role>` (`legacyLandingRefName`). Both are harness-owned pins and useless once their object is gone.
2. The heal deletes the ref without a trace. That fix's entry ends "The object-pruned-before-ref ordering was not investigated", and the live ref was already gone when it was looked at. If it happens again, the operator needs the ref name, the sha it named, and when that ref file was last written, to compare with the merge events in `events.jsonl`. Today that evidence is deleted silently.

**Approach.**
- In `checkoutDetached`, widen the match to `/fatal: bad object (refs\/tumwater\/\S+)/`. Refs outside `refs/tumwater/` (branches, tags, the operator's own refs) still throw unchanged, because tumwater does not own them.
- Give `checkoutDetached` the repository `root` as a new first parameter. Thread it through `hardResetWorktree` as an optional argument that is used only when `detach` is true. `ensureDetachedWorktree(root, dir, ref)`, the only `detach` caller, already has it. `resetWorktreeToMain` keeps calling `hardResetWorktree(wt, mainBranch)` without it.
- Before the `update-ref -d`, read what the bad ref named: `refShaFromFiles(root, ref)` from src/git/git.ts, which reads the loose file or packed-refs without needing the object. When the loose file exists under the common dir (`resolveGitDir`/the commondir `refShaFromFiles` uses), also read its mtime with `fs.statSync(...).mtimeMs`. Then call `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "warning", message, ref, sha, refWrittenAt })` from src/events/events.ts. Here `message` is `dropped dangling ref <ref> (<shortSha>, object missing) so a worktree checkout could proceed`, and `refWrittenAt` is an ISO string, or the field is omitted when the ref was packed. The existing `case "warning"` in src/events/event-format.ts already renders `warning: <message>`, so this needs no new event type or label. Check that src/events/events.ts does not import src/git/ (today it imports only paths, files, event-legacy and text), so the new import adds no cycle.
- Update the `checkoutDetached` doc comment to say it covers every `refs/tumwater/` pin and logs the drop.

**Files touched.** src/git/worktree.ts (`checkoutDetached`, `hardResetWorktree`, `ensureDetachedWorktree`); test/worktree.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The existing "ensureDetachedWorktree drops a dangling merge ref that makes `checkout --detach` exit 128" test still passes. It now also asserts that `readEvents(repo)` (src/events/event-read.ts) holds one `warning` event whose `ref` is `refs/tumwater/merge/feature-5`, whose `sha` is the 40-character `1…1` value it wrote, and which has a `refWrittenAt` string.
- New test "ensureDetachedWorktree drops a dangling rejected pin too": the same setup with `refs/tumwater/rejected/feature-5` ends with the slot at main's head, the ref file gone, and one `warning` event naming that ref.
- New test "ensureDetachedWorktree still throws on a dangling ref outside refs/tumwater/": a loose `refs/heads/broken` pointing at a missing object makes `ensureDetachedWorktree` reject with `bad object`. The ref file stays and no `warning` event is logged.
- `resetWorktreeToMain` callers compile unchanged. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Leftover recovery drops a merge pin whose commit is gone, with a warning, instead of re-queuing it on every author run (done 2026-10-19; planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. It sits beside "A slot reset drops a dangling pin under any `refs/tumwater/` namespace", which heals the slot checkout. This plan heals the role's own pin and touches different files)

**Goal.** BUGS-FIXED.md's 2026-10-19 "dangling `refs/tumwater/merge/feature-5`" entry shows that a `refs/tumwater/merge/<role>` pin can outlive its commit. Leftover recovery does not handle that case:

- `refSha` (src/git/git.ts) reads the ref from files, so it returns the dangling sha.
- `dropStalePin` (src/runner/leftover.ts) asks `isMergedInto`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <missing> main` exits 128, so `gitTry` returns null and the pin reads as "not merged".
- `recoverLeftover` then enqueues a `MergeEntry` for a sha that cannot merge.
- `verifyRequest` (src/merge/merge-batch.ts) cannot lease a slot at that sha and degrades to a terminal `error`. Its comment says so: "The queue entry outlived its pinned commit". The drain drops the entry, but no path deletes the pin.
- The role's next run calls `recoverLeftover`, which finds the same pin and queues it again.

So the role re-queues a dead sha on every run, ends each run on `error`, and never authors again. `pinnedRetrySha` shares `dropStalePin`, so the merge slot's own re-queue (`requeueKeptChange`, `requeueMainRedPin` in src/merge/merge-slot.ts) can queue the same dead sha after a retriable result. A scratch repo checked the git side: with `.git/refs/tumwater/merge/feature` holding `1111…1` (no such object), `merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 128, `log -1 --format=%B` exits 128, `cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` exits 128, and `update-ref -d refs/tumwater/merge/feature <sha>` exits 0 and removes the file.

**Approach.**
- src/git/git.ts: add `export async function commitExists(root: string, sha: string): Promise<boolean>`. It returns `(await gitTry(root, "cat-file", "-e", \`${sha}^{commit}\`)) !== null`. Give it a one-line doc comment. `isSelfHosted` in src/build/build-info.ts already runs this same command inline, so switch it to call `commitExists(root, info.sha)`, which keeps one home for the idiom.
- src/runner/leftover.ts: add a private `dropDanglingPin(root, role, ref, sha): Promise<boolean>` next to `dropStalePin`. When `commitExists(root, sha)` is false, it:
  - runs `deleteRefIfAt(root, ref, sha)`, guarded by the old value so it cannot remove a pin a concurrent write has just repointed;
  - logs `warnEventBestEffort(root, role, \`dropped merge pin ${shortSha(sha)}: its commit is missing from the repository, so it can never merge\`)`;
  - returns true.
  
  Otherwise it returns false. Call it first in `pinnedRetrySha` (return null when it returns true) and in `recoverLeftover`'s `if (sha)` branch (return null when it returns true), each time before `dropStalePin`. Recovery then reads "nothing to salvage", and the run goes on to author on a fresh main, as it does after a stale pin.
- Extend `recoverLeftover`'s doc comment: a pin whose commit is missing is deleted with a warning and nothing is queued. `hasUnmergedPin` stays as it is ("ref presence is the whole answer"), because recovery now clears the dangling pin on the role's next run.

**Files touched.** src/git/git.ts (`commitExists`); src/build/build-info.ts (`isSelfHosted`); src/runner/leftover.ts (`dropDanglingPin`, `pinnedRetrySha`, `recoverLeftover`); test/leftover.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/leftover.test.ts, "a pin whose commit is missing is dropped with a warning and nothing is queued". It uses `makeRepo` and writes `refs/tumwater/merge/<ROLE>` as a loose ref file holding `"1".repeat(40)` under `.git/refs/tumwater/merge/`, so `setRef` does not reject the missing object. It checks:
  - `recoverLeftover(makeCtx(root, wt))` returns null;
  - `queuedMerges(root)` is `[]`;
  - `refSha(root, mergeRefName(ROLE))` is null;
  - `warningMessages(...)` (test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts) holds one message containing `dropped merge pin 1111111` and `missing`.
- New test, "pinnedRetrySha drops a pin whose commit is missing". The same setup run through `pinnedRetrySha(root, ROLE, "main", {})` returns null, and the ref is gone.
- The existing tests "a pinned commit not in main is put on the merge queue, not merged" and "a stale ref already contained in main is deleted without queuing anything" still pass, so a live pin still gets no warning and is still queued.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI History trail follows the pane's window, outcome filter and search, so Ctrl+N opens the newest run the rows show and Ctrl+P steps through only those runs (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight plans touch src/cli/, src/gui/, src/ui/gui/ and src/tick/, none of the source files below; the in-flight Show transcript plan also edits docs/how-it-works.md, but a different paragraph (the History drill-down), so whichever lands second just rebases; the blocked plain-terms parts rename identifiers in src/ui/tui/ later, which is only a rebase. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/cli.md) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** On the TUI History pane, `Ctrl+O` filters the rows to an outcome class (say, `problems`), `Ctrl+S` sets a trailing window and `/` sets a search. `Ctrl+N` and `Ctrl+P` ignore all three. `loadTrail` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts reads `readTickRows(session.root, index + 1, historyRole)[index]`, scoped only by `Ctrl+G`. So an operator who filters to `problems` and presses `Ctrl+N` reads the newest run of any outcome, usually a success, and has to step through the successes with `Ctrl+P`. The Ctrl+P plan (PLANS-DONE.md, "The TUI's History trail steps back through older runs with Ctrl+P") left this as a separate change. This plan makes the trail use the same selection as the rows.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- The trail's run list is the pane's selection: scope (`Ctrl+G`), then window (`Ctrl+S`), then search (`/`), then outcome class (`Ctrl+O`). Search and class are applied in the same order `historyPaneCache` uses today. `Ctrl+N` opens entry 0 and `Ctrl+P` steps to entry `trailIndex + 1`. It wraps to entry 0 with the existing `oldest run reached; back to the newest` flash when the list has no further entry or `next` reaches `HISTORY_MAX_TICKS`.
- With no window, the trail reads up to `HISTORY_MAX_TICKS` rows before filtering, not the rows view's `HISTORY_DEFAULT_TICKS`. Ctrl+P already steps past the 20 rows shown, and a filter must not hide a matching run that is only slightly older. With a window, it reads `readTickRowsSince(...).rows`, as the rows view does. When no window, search or class is set, the read stays `readTickRows(root, index + 1, role)`, so the unfiltered path does no extra work.
- Changing a filter while a trail is on re-reads the trail at index 0, the same way `Ctrl+G` calls `refreshTrail` today. This covers `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+O` and a finished search (`applySearch`). An empty new selection leaves `trailCache` null, so the pane shows its existing no-trail note, as after `Ctrl+G` onto an empty scope. `Ctrl+Y` (summary) does not touch the trail.
- `Ctrl+N` on an empty selection flashes `no completed runs match the pane's filters` when a window, search or class is set. Otherwise it keeps today's `no completed runs to inspect`.

**Approach (src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts only).**
- Extract the read-and-filter head of `historyPaneCache` into a closure, `selectPaneRows(sinceMs, resultClass, role, grep, limit)`. It returns `{ rows, covered, afterGrep, filtered }`: the raw read (`readTickRows(session.root, limit, role)` when `sinceMs === null`, else `readTickRowsSince`), its coverage flag, the count after `tickRowsMatchingGrep`, and the class-filtered rows. `historyPaneCache` calls it with `HISTORY_DEFAULT_TICKS` and keeps its body and empty-state wording. The rows view must render exactly what it renders today.
- `loadTrail(onEmpty, index = 0)` picks its row from `selectPaneRows(historyWindow, historyResult, historyRole, historyGrep, limit).filtered[index]`, where `limit` is `index + 1` when all three filters are null, else `HISTORY_MAX_TICKS`. Keep its `trailGen++`, its try/catch, its `trailIndex = index` and its stat load. Update its doc comment and the `trailMode`/`trailIndex` comments: the trail now follows the pane's selection, not only its scope.
- In the `Ctrl+S` and `Ctrl+O` arms and in `applySearch`, add `if (trailMode) refreshTrail();` before the recompute, as the `Ctrl+G` arm does.
- In the Ctrl+N arm, pick the flash text from whether `historyWindow`, `historyResult` or `historyGrep` is non-null.
- **docs/how-it-works.md**: in the History paragraph, change "the role's newest when `Ctrl+G` scopes the pane, else the team's" so it says the trail is the newest run among the pane's rows (scope, window, result and search). Add to the Ctrl+P sentence that it steps through those same runs. **docs/cli.md**: change the TUI-keys rows for History `Ctrl+N` ("the newest completed run's event trail") and `Ctrl+P` to say "among the pane's filtered runs".

**Acceptance criteria (test/tui-keys.test.ts, beside "Ctrl+G while a trail is shown re-reads the new scope's newest tick" and the Ctrl+P stepping tests that use `steppingRoot`).**
- Use a team log with, oldest to newest, clean 1 `failed` (class `problems` under `historyClass`), qa 1 `changed`, clean 2 `changed`. With `Ctrl+O` advanced to `problems` (pressed as many times as `HISTORY_RESULTS` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-session.ts needs), `Ctrl+N` shows clean 1's trail (`renderTickDetail(readTickDetail(root, "clean", 1)!)`) with `trailIndex` 0. `Ctrl+P` then wraps back to clean 1 and flashes `/oldest run reached/`.
- With the trail on and no filter, `Ctrl+O` to `problems` swaps the trail to clean 1. Advancing `Ctrl+O` to a class with no rows leaves `trailMode` true and `trailCache` null.
- With the trail on, a History search for `qa work` (type `/`, then the text, then Enter, as the Activity search test types it) shows qa 1's trail. `Ctrl+P` from there wraps and does not show a clean run.
- `Ctrl+N` with a class that matches nothing flashes `/match the pane's filters/` and leaves `trailMode` false. With no filter on an empty log it still flashes `/no completed runs to inspect/`.
- The existing History rows, summary, Ctrl+G trail and Ctrl+P tests pass unchanged. That covers the rows view: `historyPaneCache`'s output does not change.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI's History trail steps back through older runs with Ctrl+P, so the terminal can read any recent run's trail, not only the newest (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight dashboard and CLI history plans touch src/gui/, src/ui/gui/, src/history/history.ts, src/cli/ and src/tick/, none of the files below; the blocked plain-terms parts rename identifiers in src/ui/tui/ later, which is only a rebase. Touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts docs/cli.md docs/how-it-works.md) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** On the TUI History pane, `Ctrl+N` swaps the rows for a run's event trail, but only ever for the newest completed run in the pane's scope (`loadTrail` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts reads `readTickRows(session.root, 1, historyRole)[0]`). To read any older run, the operator has to leave the TUI and type `tumwater history <role> <n>`, or open the dashboard drill-down. This plan lets `Ctrl+P` step the on-screen trail back one run at a time.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- `Ctrl+P` works only while the History pane shows a trail (`trailMode`). It replaces the trail with the next older completed run in the same scope as `Ctrl+N`: the exact role `Ctrl+G` set (`historyRole`), else the whole team. The trail is rendered the same way, through `readTickDetail`/`renderTickDetail`, with the async stat footer.
- Steps go through `readTickRows(session.root, trailIndex + 2, historyRole)`, whose rows are newest first, and take row `trailIndex + 1`. When there is no older row, or the next index would reach `HISTORY_MAX_TICKS` (src/history/history-data.ts), the trail wraps back to the newest run (index 0) and flashes `oldest run reached; back to the newest`. This wraps like the pane's other cycle keys (`Ctrl+G`, `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+O`).
- Stepping ignores the pane's window (`Ctrl+S`), outcome filter (`Ctrl+O`) and search (`/`), as `Ctrl+N` already does. One rule covers both keys. Making the trail follow the filters is a separate change.
- No "newer" key. `Ctrl+N` returns to the rows, and pressing `Ctrl+N` again reopens the newest run. Every nearby Ctrl key already means something else on some view (`Ctrl+F` pauses the team, `Ctrl+B` edits the budget), and wrap-around reaches the newest run anyway.
- `Ctrl+P` with the trail off, or on any other view, keeps today's behavior. The router returns false, so the Activity provider-caps editor (view 0) and the Transcript pause editor (role views), which both run in the editors ahead of the panes, are unaffected.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts** (`createHistoryPane`):
  - Add `let trailIndex = 0`, the 0-based newest-first position of the shown run, documented beside `trailMode`.
  - Generalize `loadTrail(onEmpty)` to `loadTrail(onEmpty, index = 0)`. It reads `readTickRows(session.root, index + 1, historyRole)[index]`. When that row is `undefined`, it behaves as today, which is the only case at index 0. On success it sets `trailIndex = index`. Keep its `trailGen++` and try/catch.
  - `refreshTrail` (the Ctrl+G and roster-drop path), the Ctrl+N toggle in both directions and `reset()` all set or return to index 0, so a scope change still shows the new scope's newest run.
  - Add a `key.ctrl && key.name === "p"` arm. It returns false unless `session.view === session.roleIds.length + 4` and `trailMode`. When `!promptLineFree(ctx.es)`, it consumes the key with a render, as the Ctrl+N arm does. Otherwise it computes `next = trailIndex + 1`. When `next < HISTORY_MAX_TICKS` and `loadTrail(null, next)` returns true, the step is done. Otherwise it calls `loadTrail(null, 0)` and flashes the wrap message. Either way it sets `session.paneScroll = 0` and requests a render.
  - Expose `trailIndex` in `state()`. Update the module and `trailMode` doc comments to name Ctrl+P.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts** `handleKey`: add `if (key.ctrl && key.name === "p") return history.handleKey?.(key, ctx) ?? false;` beside the Ctrl+S/Ctrl+Y history routes.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts**: add `trailIndex: number` to the state type beside `trailMode`/`trailCache`, with a doc comment. **src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts** copies it into the aggregated state as `trailIndex: hist.trailIndex`, beside `trailCache: hist.trailCache`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts**: in the history hint, when `view.trail` is true, insert `["Ctrl+P", "older run"]` after the Ctrl+N pair.
- **docs/cli.md**: add a TUI-keys row: `Ctrl+P` | History (on a run trail) | the next older run's trail in the pane's scope, wrapping to the newest after the oldest. **docs/how-it-works.md**: append a sentence after "`Ctrl+N` again returns to the rows." that says the same.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts, new tests beside "Ctrl+G while a trail is shown re-reads the new scope's newest tick":
  - With clean runs 1 and 2 (run 2 newest) and a qa run between them, Ctrl+N shows clean 2. With the pane scoped to clean, Ctrl+P shows `renderTickDetail(readTickDetail(root, "clean", 1)!)` and `trailIndex` is 1. A second Ctrl+P wraps to clean 2, `trailIndex` is 0, and the flash matches `/oldest run reached/`. Team-scoped, Ctrl+P steps from clean 2 to qa's run.
  - Ctrl+P with the trail off on History leaves `trailMode` false and `trailCache` null. Ctrl+N after a Ctrl+P (off, then on again) shows the newest run with `trailIndex` 0. Ctrl+G after a Ctrl+P shows the new scope's newest run.
  - A late stat from the run that Ctrl+P left does not overwrite the stepped-to trail, with the `resolves` pattern of "a late stat never overwrites a trail that was exited or re-read".
  - The existing test "Ctrl+P opens the provider-caps editor on Activity and the pause editor on a role's Transcript" still passes unchanged.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: the history hint contains `Ctrl+P older run` with `trail: true` and does not contain it with `trail: false`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history <role> <n> --transcript` appends that one run's agent transcript to its trail, so you can read what the agent did in a past run without scrolling the role's whole log (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight `history <role> <n> --patch` plan edits the same `cmdTick`/`runTrailCommand`/HELP line/docs row, so whichever lands second rebases and keeps both flags. The blocked runner-rename parts rename identifiers in src/tick and src/ui only as rebases. Touches src/agent/run-agent.ts src/ui/transcript-run.ts (new) src/tick/tick-detail.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/transcript-run.test.ts (new) test/tick-detail.test.ts test/pi.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater history <role> <n>` prints a run's harness events: start, verdict, merge, usage. It does not show what the agent itself said or ran. The only CLI view of that is `tumwater logs --role <id>` (`cmdLogsTranscript`, src/cli/log-commands.ts). It prints the last N entries of `.tumwater/log/<role>.pi.jsonl` (`piLogPath`), so reading run 412 when the role is on run 430 means guessing `-n` and scrolling through 18 other runs. The dashboard drawer shows only the live tail too (`/api/transcript`). `--transcript` appends exactly the agent runs that started inside the run's `[startTs, endTs]` window, rendered the way `logs --role` renders them.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- **Run start times.** Each agent run in the raw log begins with the harness's `tumwater_run` marker (`runAgent` in src/agent/run-agent.ts), which carries `kind`, `agent` and an optional `label` but no time. Add `ts: Date.now()` to that marker. For a marker written before this change (no numeric `ts`), the segment's start is the `timestamp` of its first `message_end` whose `message.role` is `"user"` (the same field `createTranscriptRenderer` already stamps its separator from). A segment with neither is skipped.
- **Which runs are included.** A segment is included when `detail.startTs <= start <= (detail.endTs ?? Infinity)`. That covers the authoring run, its retries and fallbacks, and any review or gate run the role logged inside the window (they render with their `── review @ … ──` separator). A merge review that runs after the run's `run_end` is outside the window and is not shown. `detail.startTs === null` (the start was rotated out of the event log) prints a note instead of a guess.
- **Files read.** `piLogPath(root, role)` + `".1"` (the one generation `rotateIfLarge` keeps), then `piLogPath(root, role)` itself, oldest first, each only if it exists. Each file is read whole. This is a one-shot command, and each file is bounded by `logMaxBytes`. Lines before a file's first marker are skipped.
- **Prompts.** No `--prompt` companion: the transcript renders with `includePrompts: false`, like plain `logs --role`. The run's prompt is already on `tumwater role <id>`.
- **Composition.** `--transcript` is accepted with `--last` and with `--stat` (and with `--patch` if that has landed). The stat block, then any patch block, then the transcript block, each separated by a blank line. With `--json`, a `transcript` field (an array of strings, one per rendered line) is added beside `stat`, and only when the flag is given.
- **Nothing found.** When no segment matches, the block is the single line `(no transcript for <role> run <n>: rotated out of .tumwater/log/<role>.pi.jsonl, or the run started no agent)`. The exit code is 0, as for `--stat`'s missing-commit texts. With `--json`, the field is `[]`.
- No dashboard or TUI change.

**Approach.**
- **src/agent/run-agent.ts**: add `ts: number` to the marker object type and literal (keep the `label` only-when-set rule). Update its comment.
- **src/ui/transcript-run.ts (new)**: `export function readRunTranscript(file: string, fromTs: number, toTs: number | null): string[]`. It reads `file + ".1"` and `file` if they exist and splits their lines into segments, a segment starting at each line that parses (`parsePiEventLine` with a `tumwater_run`-only set, as `MARKER_ONLY` in src/ui/transcript-tail.ts does) as a `tumwater_run` marker. Each segment's start is marker `ts`, else the first user `message_end`'s `message.timestamp`. It keeps the segments whose start is in the window, concatenates their lines (markers included, so labels render), and returns `formatTranscript(lines).flat()` (src/ui/transcript.ts). Keep this small and synchronous. Add a header comment naming the marker-ts / user-timestamp fallback.
- **src/tick/tick-detail.ts**: `cmdTick` gains a `transcript` boolean. Because the boolean list is growing, convert its trailing flags to one options object `{ last, stat, transcript }` (plus `patch` if that has landed) and update the one caller. When the flag is set and `detail.startTs !== null`, call `readRunTranscript(piLogPath(root, role), detail.startTs, detail.endTs)`. For a null `startTs`, use the note `(no transcript: run <n>'s start rotated out of the event log)`, or `[]` under `--json`. Then append the block, or the empty-result line, as described above. Update `TICK_USAGE` to `... [--stat] [--transcript] [--json]`.
- **src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts**: `export const TRANSCRIPT_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--transcript"] };`, documented like `STAT_FLAG`.
- **src/cli.ts**: `runTrailCommand` admits `TRANSCRIPT_FLAG` in its `rejectUnknownArgs` list and passes `rest.includes("--transcript")`.
- **src/cli/help.ts**: the `tumwater history <role> [<n>] ...` line gains `[--transcript]`. Completion derives from HELP.
- **docs/cli.md**: in the "Watch run history" row, after the `--stat` clause, add: "`--transcript` appends the agent transcript of the runs that started inside that run's window (the role's `logs --role` rendering, rotated-out runs noted; `--json` adds a `transcript` array)".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/transcript-run.test.ts (new), against temp files:
  - Three markers with `ts` 1000, 2000 and 3000, each followed by an `agent_start` and an assistant `message_end` with distinct text. Window `[1500, 2500]` returns only the second run's text.
  - Window `[1500, null]` returns the second and third.
  - A `.1` file holding the first run and a live file holding the next two: window `[0, null]` returns all three, oldest first.
  - A legacy marker without `ts` whose run has a user `message_end` with `timestamp: 2000` is included by `[1500, 2500]`.
  - A missing file returns `[]`.
  - A labeled marker (`label: "review"`) renders a `── review` separator.
- test/tick-detail.test.ts: seed run_start/run_end events for `clean` runs 1 and 2 (`writeEvents`, test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts) and a `clean.pi.jsonl` with one marker-stamped segment inside each run's window.
  - `history clean 2 --transcript` prints the trail and then only run 2's assistant text, not run 1's.
  - `--json` carries a `transcript` array with that text, and omits the key without the flag.
  - A run with no matching segment prints the `(no transcript for clean run 2: …)` line and exits 0.
  - `--last --transcript` shows the newest run's text.
  - `--transcript --stat` prints the stat block before the transcript block.
- test/pi.test.ts: the assertions on the marker's exact bytes are updated to parse the line and check `kind`/`agent`/`label` plus a numeric `ts` between the before and after `Date.now()` of the call. Grep test/ for other exact `{"type":"tumwater_run",` byte assertions on *written* logs and update them the same way. Fixtures that only *feed* markers to renderers stay as they are.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history -f/--follow` prints the last runs, then one row per run as it finishes, a quiet live feed beside `logs -f` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19; no dependency on any Planned entry — it touches cmdHistory's flag handling, which the in-flight By-model drill-down plan also edits, so whichever merges second rebases onto the other)

**Goal.** An operator who wants to watch outcomes, not every event, has no live view on the CLI:
`tumwater logs -f` streams every event (run_start, merge_queued, inbox lines, model changes …)
and `tumwater history` is a one-shot listing. `tumwater history -f` prints the usual last-N rows,
then keeps following the event log and prints one history row each time a run ends, through the
same row filters (`--role`, `--grep`, `--result`, `--model`) — `tail -f` for run outcomes. It
ends on Ctrl+C or once its parent process is gone, exactly as `logs -f` does.

**Approach.**
- src/cli/log-commands.ts: export `followUntilParentGone` and its `FollowSeams` interface
  unchanged, so history's follow shares the one follow-plus-parent-death-watch helper.
- src/history/history.ts `cmdHistory(root, args, seams: FollowSeams = {})`:
  - `-f`/`--follow` (same spellings as logs). Rival shapes fail through `failRivalShapes` with
    logs' wording style: `--since` ("follow means \"from now on\"; --since shows a bounded past
    window", the logs wording), `--summary` ("a summary tallies a bounded set; -f follows from now
    on"), and `--json` ("--json prints one document; -f streams rows"). `-n`, `--role`, `--grep`,
    `--result` and `--model` compose with it.
  - Build one row predicate from the parsed `--grep`/`--result`/`--model` values (the same
    `tickRowsMatchingGrep`, `historyClass`, and model-membership rules the current inline filters
    apply — if the By-model plan's `tickRowsOnModels` has landed, reuse it) and use it for the
    followed rows; the non-follow path keeps its current filters and empty-state wording
    unchanged.
  - With `-f`: before the normal `readTickRows` read, take `readEventsTailWithEnd(root,
    HISTORY_FOLLOW_BUFFER_EVENTS)` (new module constant, 2000; not exported) as the seed buffer and offset.
    Print the initial filtered rows **oldest first** (so newer rows append below, as in any
    follow), padded by `widestWidths`; print no empty-state prose (`logs -f` prints none either).
  - Follow `eventsLogPath(root)` from `tail.coveredEnd` with `followUntilParentGone`. Each parsed
    event (`parseEventLine`) is appended to the buffer (drop the oldest beyond
    `HISTORY_FOLLOW_BUFFER_EVENTS`); on a `run_end`, `tickRows(buffer, 1, roleScope)[0]` is that
    run's row (the buffer supplies its run_start for duration and model; a start that fell out of
    the buffer renders the dash, history's existing unpaired rule). Skip the row when its
    `role#run` key was among the initial rows (an end appended between the tail read and the
    `readTickRows` read is delivered twice), or when the predicate rejects it; otherwise print
    `renderRow(row, widths)` where `widths` is a running maximum: add `widenWidths(a, b)` (the
    column-wise max) to src/history/history-render.ts beside `widestWidths`.
  - A run whose change is waiting to merge prints `queued`, its result at run_end; the follow
    does not print a second line when the merge resolves (`tumwater history` shows the
    resolved result afterwards).
- src/cli.ts `case "history"`: add `{ names: ["-f", "--follow"] }` to its `rejectUnknownArgs`
  list (the logs spec spelling).
- src/cli/help.ts: add `[-f/--follow]` to the `tumwater history` usage line and one sentence to
  its stanza ("-f prints the last N rows oldest first, then one row per run as it ends, until
  Ctrl+C or its parent exits; not with --since, --summary or --json"). Completion derives from
  HELP (completionSpec), so no completion.ts edit. docs/cli.md: the "Watch run history" row's
  synopsis and text gain the same.

**Files touched.** src/history/history.ts, src/history/history-render.ts,
src/cli/log-commands.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, a new
test/history-follow.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/history-follow.test.ts, in-process with the `{ ppid, intervalMs: 10 }` seams and
  `captureStdout`, appending events with `fs.appendFileSync(eventsLogPath(repo), …)` the way
  test/log-commands.test.ts's `assertFollowEndsWithParent` does:
  - two runs already in the log print oldest first; then a `run_start`+`run_end` pair appended
    while following prints one row naming that run, its result, and its model from the
    run_start;
  - `--role clean -f` does not print an appended `feature` run, and `--result merged -f` does not
    print an appended `no_change` run, while each prints a matching one;
  - no run prints twice: across the whole captured output each `#<run>` of a role appears on
    one line only;
  - the follow resolves once the fake ppid turns 1, and an event appended after that prints
    nothing.
- `history -f --since 1h`, `history -f --summary` and `history -f --json` each fail with a
  message naming both flags (assert through the existing exit-capture helper).
- The existing tests in test/cli-history.test.ts, test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts,
  test/cli-history-views.test.ts and test/log-commands.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard's History drill-down gets a "Show patch" button that loads the run's full commit patch below its stat, the dashboard twin of `tumwater history <role> <n> --patch` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight By-model drill-down plan edits `handleHistory` and src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts's table/query code, and this entry edits `handleTick` and the `history-detail` region, so the two meet only as a rebase. The blocked runner-rename parts rename `readTickDetail`/`TickDetail` later, also only a rebase. Touches src/tick/tick-detail.ts src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/gui-server-api.test.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The dashboard's History drill-down (`histDetailCardHtml` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, fed by `GET /api/run`, `handleTick` in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) shows a run's trail and its commit's per-file stat. It also offers "Revert this change…". It never shows what the change actually was. The CLI got `history <role> <n> --patch` (`tickDetailPatch` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts), and that plan kept the dashboard on the stat only. As a result, a dashboard user who is about to revert a change cannot read it first. This plan adds the patch to the drill-down, loaded only on demand, because a patch can be large and most expanded cards never need one.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- `GET /api/run` takes an optional `patch` flag, which counts when present whatever its value (the rule `handleHistory` uses for `summary`). With the flag, the payload gains `patch: await tickDetailPatch(root, detail)`, the same text `history --patch` prints, placeholders included, with no byte cap. Without the flag, the payload carries no `patch` key, so the default expand costs no extra `git show`.
- Every `/api/run` payload also gains `hasCommit: boolean`, which is `tickCommitSha(detail) !== null`. The client shows the button only when `hasCommit === true`. A run that sent nothing to merge gets no dead button, and a server too old to send the field gets no button either.
- The button reads "Show patch". The first click fetches `/api/run?role=<id>&run=<n>&patch=1` and shows "Loading patch…" while the fetch runs. The answer renders as `<pre class='mono hist-detail-patch'>` directly under the `hist-detail-stat` block and above the revert control. Once loaded, the button reads "Hide patch" and toggles the block's visibility without refetching. A failed fetch shows the error message in an `err` div under the button, and the next click retries. The patch lives on the card's cache entry, so `fetchHistory`'s `histDetails.clear()` drops it with the trail.
- No TUI change. The TUI History trail keeps its stat footer. A full patch in a fixed-height pane is a separate decision.

**Approach.**
- **src/tick/tick-detail.ts**: export `tickDetailPatch` (it is module-private today) and `tickCommitSha`. Neither body changes. Extend `tickDetailPatch`'s doc comment to name GET /api/run as its second caller.
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts** `handleTick`: import both, add `hasCommit` to the payload, and add `patch` when `q.get("patch") !== null`. Extend the doc comment with both fields.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts**, inside the `history-detail:start`…`end` region:
  - `fetchHistDetail` stores `hasCommit: d.hasCommit === true` on the ok entry.
  - Add `histPatchHtml(entry, key)`, which returns the button (`data-hist-patch='<key>'`) plus the sub-state from `entry.patch`, a value of `{ state: "loading" | "ok" | "error", text?, message?, open? }`. `histDetailCardHtml` calls it after the stat block when `entry.hasCommit`.
  - Add `async function toggleHistPatch(key)`. On an entry with a loaded patch, it flips `open`. Otherwise it sets `{ state: "loading" }`, calls `renderHistory()`, then `getJson` with `&patch=1`, and stores `ok` with `open: true` (or `error` when the fetch fails or the answer has no string `patch`), then calls `renderHistory()` again. `role` and `run` come from splitting the key on its last `#` (`histDetailKey` builds it as `role + "#" + tick`).
  - Wire one more delegated `#histbody` click listener for `button[data-hist-patch]`, beside the revert listener.
  - Update the cache-state comment above `histDetails` to list `hasCommit` and `patch`.
- **docs/how-it-works.md**: after the "Revert this change…" sentence, add one sentence: the drill-down's "Show patch" button loads the run's commit patch on demand through `GET /api/run?…&patch=1`, the same `tickDetailPatch` text `tumwater history <role> <n> --patch` prints.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/gui-server-api.test.ts, a new test beside "gui /api/run carries revertSha only for a run whose commit is on main". For a run with a real commit, `/api/run?role=…&run=…` has `hasCommit: true` and no `patch` key, and the same request with `&patch=1` has a `patch` string that matches `diff --git`. For a run with no commit, the payload has `hasCommit: false`, and `&patch=1` gives `patch` equal to `(no commit: this run sent nothing to merge)`.
- test/gui-client-history.test.ts:
  - `histDetailCardHtml` renders a `data-hist-patch` button only for an ok entry with `hasCommit: true`, and none for `hasCommit` false or absent.
  - A new test drives `toggleHistPatch` through `clientScope` with a stubbed `getJson`, as "the drill-down's revert button previews, then reverts, through /api/revert" does. The first toggle requests a URL that ends `&patch=1`. ### The dashboard's By model summary drills into the runs: clicking a model shows the History table of that model's runs, through a new `GET /api/history?model=<selector>`, the dashboard twin of `tumwater history --model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. The in-flight revert-button entry also edits src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts and src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, but different functions (`handleTick`, the drill-down card); this entry edits `handleHistory`, the toolbar, `historyQuery`, `histModelSummaryHtml` and `renderHistory`, so whichever merges second only rebases. The logs -f entry edits src/cli/log-commands.ts only. The blocked plain-terms parts rename `TickRow` and the `tickRows…` family later, which is also a rebase. Touches src/history/history-data.ts src/history/history.ts src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts docs/cli.md test/history-data.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history --model <selector>[,...]` lists the runs behind one line of `history --summary --by model`. The dashboard's History view has the same "By model" mode (`histModelSummaryHtml` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts), but you can't go from a model's line to its runs: `handleHistory` (src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) reads `role`, `grep`, `n`/`sinceMs` and `summary`, and has no `model` query. The table has no model filter either, and the search box (`grep`) matches model names as substrings, not exact selectors. This plan makes each model label in the By model table a link. Clicking it switches to the Table view, filtered to runs whose `run_start` named exactly that selector.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- One shared filter rule. Add `tickRowsOnModels(rows: TickRow[], models: string[]): TickRow[]` to src/history/history-data.ts, next to `tickRowsMatchingGrep`. It keeps rows with `r.model !== null && models.includes(r.model)` (exact, case-sensitive; a null-model row never matches). Give it a doc comment naming its two call sites. `cmdHistory` (src/history/history.ts) replaces its inline `rows.filter((r) => r.model !== null && pieces.includes(r.model))` with this call. Its flag parsing, errors and empty-state messages stay as they are.
- `handleHistory` reads `model` like `role`: `""` and absent filter nothing. The value is a comma list, split, trimmed and deduplicated as `cmdHistory` does. A list with no non-empty pieces (e.g. `","`) filters nothing (no 400, matching the "" rule). An unknown selector is not an error and keeps no rows, matching the CLI. The filter applies after `grep` in both the count and `sinceMs` shapes, before `summary`/`modelSummary` are folded, so both summaries fold exactly the rows served. `n` still bounds the rows read before filtering, the same as `history -n N --model`.
- The client sends a single selector, the one clicked. The `(unknown)` bucket and the total row are not clickable, because the CLI can't select a null model either.
- The model filter is view state, not a persisted preference: a new `let histModel = ""` is not passed to `store`/`recall`, so a reload starts unfiltered. When it is set, the toolbar shows a chip button `id='histmodel'` reading "Model: <selector> ×". Clicking the chip clears `histModel` and refetches. When it is empty, the chip is hidden (`style.display = "none"`).

**Approach.**
- **src/history/history-data.ts**: add `tickRowsOnModels` as above.
- **src/history/history.ts**: call it from `cmdHistory`'s `--model` branch.
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts** `handleHistory`: parse `model` as above and apply `tickRowsOnModels` after the grep filter in both arms. Extend the doc comment's query list.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts**:
  - `historyQuery(count, role, sinceKey, grep, model)`: append `&model=<encodeURIComponent(model)>` when `model` is non-empty, placed after grep and before `&summary=1`. Existing calls without a fifth argument keep their URLs, because an `undefined` model appends nothing.
  - `fetchHistory` passes `histModel`.
  - `histModelSummaryHtml`: when a model row's model is non-null, its label cell holds `<button type='button' class='linkish mono' data-histmodel='<esc(model)>'>` around the label. `.linkish` already exists in src/ui/gui/gui-styles.ts and is used by gui-client-team.ts; no new CSS. To keep the shared renderer unchanged for the role table, give `summaryTableHtml` an optional per-entry `labelHtml` that it uses instead of `esc(e.label)` when present.
  - `buildHistoryView`: add the chip button to the toolbar after the role picker. Its click handler clears `histModel` and calls `fetchHistory()`. The existing `#histbody` click listener gains a branch: `ev.target.closest("button[data-histmodel]")` sets `histModel = b.dataset.histmodel`, sets `histMode = "table"`, calls `store("hist-mode", "table")` and then `fetchHistory()`.
  - `renderHistory` shows or hides the chip and sets its text from `histModel`. In `historyTableHtml`'s empty state, an active model filter with zero rows shows "No runs on this model". Add a `model` parameter, appended last.
- **docs/cli.md**: in the Watch run history row, extend the clause about the dashboard's By model mode to say that clicking a model lists its runs (the `history --model` twin).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/history-data.test.ts: `tickRowsOnModels` keeps exact matches for one and for two selectors, drops a null-model row, and treats a case-different selector as no match.
- test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, beside "handleHistory ?summary also folds the served rows per model" and using the same fixture: `?n=50&model=m-a` serves only clean's row. `?n=50&model=m-a,m-b&summary=1` serves two rows, with `modelSummary` deep-equal to `summarizeTickRowsByModel` of the served rows. `?sinceMs=3600000&model=m-a` filters the window arm. `?n=50&model=` and `?n=50&model=,` serve all three rows. `?n=50&model=nope` serves `rows: []` with status 200.
- test/gui-client-history.test.ts: `historyQuery(50, "", "", "", "m-a")` returns `/api/history?n=50&model=m-a&summary=1`. A selector with `/` and `:` is URL-encoded. The existing four-argument assertions still pass. `histModelSummaryHtml` renders a `data-histmodel` button for a named model and none for the `(unknown)` bucket or the total row. Through the existing fetchHistory/clientScope harness, clicking a `data-histmodel` button fetches a URL containing `&model=` and switches the mode to table. Clicking `#histmodel` refetches without `model=`.
- The existing `history --model` tests in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater revert <role> <n>` and `tumwater revert <role> --last` revert the change a run merged, without copying a sha out of its trail (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight `history --patch` entry edits `TICK_USAGE`/`cmdTick` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts and src/cli.ts's `history` case, and this entry edits only `cmdRevert` and the `revert` case, so the two meet only as rebases. The blocked plain-terms parts rename `readTickDetail`/`TickDetail` later, which is also only a rebase) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater revert <sha> [--dry-run]` (`cmdRevert` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts) takes only a sha. The dashboard's History drill-down now reverts a run directly: `handleTick` in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts resolves `tickMergedSha(detail)` through `resolveRevertTarget`. From a terminal, the operator still runs `tumwater history <role> <n>` and copies the `merged as <sha>` or pinned sha into `revert`. This plan lets `revert` take the same run address `history` takes: `tumwater revert <role> <n> [--dry-run]` and `tumwater revert <role> --last [--dry-run]`. It goes through the same cores (`previewRevert`, `revertMergedCommit` in src/operator/revert.ts) and the same sha rule (`tickMergedSha`), so the CLI and the dashboard pick the same commit for the same run.

**Approach.**
- The forms are told apart by arity, so nothing is ambiguous. One positional and no `--last` is a sha, as today. Two positionals are `<role> <n>`. `--last` plus one positional is `<role>`. A sha form with `--last`, or any other count, fails with the usage `revert needs a commit or a run (usage: tumwater revert <sha>|<role> <n>|<role> --last [--dry-run])`. The existing flag-shaped-token gate (`revert takes only --dry-run (got …)`) becomes `revert takes only --dry-run and --last (got …)` and still runs before any lookup.
- Add a module-local `revertRunSha(root, positionals, last): string` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts, next to `cmdRevert`. It resolves the run the way `cmdTick` does:
  - role: `canonicalRoleId`, then checked against `knownRoleIdsCached(root)`. An unknown role fails with `unknownRoleMessage(role, ids)` plus the revert usage.
  - number: `parseCountFlag("revert <n>", positionals[1])` for the numbered form. For `--last` it is `readTickRows(root, 1, role)[0]?.run`, which is the run `tumwater history <role> --last` shows, so an operator can inspect it and then revert that same run. `--last` does not skip ahead to the newest *merged* run; a non-merged newest run gets the refusal below.
  - `readTickDetail(root, role, n)`. A missing run fails with `tickNotFoundMessage(role, n)`, or for `--last` with no runs, `no completed run of <role> in the event log`. Unlike `history`, revert exits 1 here because it is an action that did not happen.
  - `detail.result !== "merged"` fails with `<role> run #<n> did not merge (result: <result ?? "unknown">); there is nothing to revert`. This covers rejected, refused, no-commit and still-queued runs before git is asked anything.
  - Otherwise return `tickMergedSha(detail)`. If it is null (a merged run whose log lost every sha event), fail with `<role> run #<n> merged but the event log no longer names its commit; pass the sha from git log instead`.
  - The returned sha then goes into the unchanged `previewRevert` / `revertMergedCommit` path, so the base-branch, not-on-main, dirty-tree and conflict refusals keep their current wording.
- Under the run forms, the dry-run output adds one first line, `run <role> #<n> merged as <short sha>`, before the `would revert …` lines. A real revert prints the same line before `main is now …`. The sha form's output does not change.
- Every helper is already exported, so src/tick/ does not change: `tickNotFoundMessage` and `tickMergedSha` (src/tick/tick-detail.ts), `readTickDetail` (src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts), `readTickRows` (src/history/history-data.ts), `canonicalRoleId` (src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts), `knownRoleIdsCached` (src/config/config.ts), `unknownRoleMessage` (src/roles/roles.ts) and `parseCountFlag` (src/cli/cli-args.ts).
- src/cli.ts's `revert` case keeps calling `cmdRevert(root, args)`. Update its comment to say the positionals select a sha or a run.

**Files touched.** src/operator/operator-commands.ts (`cmdRevert`, new `revertRunSha`, doc comment), src/cli.ts (comment only), src/cli/help.ts (the `tumwater revert` entry: `tumwater revert <sha>|<role> <n>|<role> --last [--dry-run]`, plus one line saying the run forms revert the commit the run merged as, the sha `history <role> <n>` names; completion derives from HELP), docs/cli.md ("Steer the project" row: the run forms, and that `--last` is the run `history <role> --last` shows), test/cli-operators.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/cli-operators.test.ts, beside the existing revert tests, a repo from `initProject` + `seedCommit` with `writeEvents` (test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts) seeding `clean` run 1 (`merge_done` with `commit: <seeded sha>`, `run_end` `result: "merged"`), run 2 (`run_end` `result: "rejected"`, pinned commit on a side branch) and run 3 (`merged`, `commit: "0".repeat(40)`). The same shape as "gui /api/run carries revertSha only for a run whose commit is on main" in test/gui-server-api.test.ts. Cases:
  - "revert <role> <n> reverts the commit that run merged as": `cli(repo, "revert", "clean", "1")` exits 0. stdout starts `run clean #1 merged as <short>`, HEAD's subject is `tumwater(operator): Revert <short>`, and the tree is clean.
  - "revert <role> <n> --dry-run previews the run's commit and writes nothing": exit 0, the `run clean #1 merged as` line and then `would revert <short>`, and HEAD is unchanged.
  - "revert <role> --last takes the newest completed run": with run 3 the newest, `revert clean --last --dry-run` exits 1 with the core's `no such commit` refusal for the zero sha. A repo whose newest clean run is run 1 previews run 1's sha.
  - "revert refuses a run that did not merge, an unknown run and an unknown role, writing nothing": `revert clean 2` → exit 1, stderr matches `did not merge \(result: rejected\)`. `revert clean 9` → exit 1 with `tickNotFoundMessage("clean", 9)`'s text. `revert nosuchrole 1` → exit 1 naming the unknown role. HEAD is unchanged after each.
- The existing "revert with zero or multiple positionals fails with usage and writes no commit" test is updated. Zero positionals and three positionals fail with the new usage text. `revert <sha> extra` now fails as an unknown role (`extra`), and HEAD is unchanged. The existing "revert rejects a flag-shaped token…" test matches the new `--dry-run and --last` wording. The success and `--dry-run` sha-form tests pass unchanged.
- test/help.test.ts's revert assertions (if any match the old signature) are updated to the new HELP line.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history <role> <n> --patch` appends the run's full commit patch to its trail, the patch twin of `--stat` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight `history -f` plan edits src/history/history.ts and src/cli/log-commands.ts, the dashboard Revert plan adds one exported `tickLandedSha` to src/tick/tick-detail.ts, and a blocked runner-rename part renames identifiers there, so these meet only as rebases; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater history <role> <n> --stat` (`cmdTick` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts) appends the per-file `git show --stat` summary of the commit a run pinned. To see what the run actually changed, though, you still have to copy the `commit <sha>` out of the header and run `git show` yourself. `tumwater diff --role <id>` already prints the patch of a role's *pending* change. This plan gives a *finished* run the same view: `--patch` appends that commit's full patch. Like `--stat`, it shows the commit the run pinned (`tickCommitSha`), not the `merged as` sha: a rebased merge carries the same changes under a new sha, and the stat and the patch should describe the same commit.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- `--patch` is accepted with `--stat`. Then the stat block comes first and the patch block follows, each separated by a blank line, in the same order as `git show --stat --patch`. With `--last`, it applies to the newest finished run, just as `--stat` does.
- The patch is printed whole, with no byte cap, the same as `diff --role`'s patch. The reviewer-facing truncation in `aheadOfMainDiff` (src/git/git-diff.ts) is for a model's context window, not for a terminal that can page.
- A run with no commit, or with a commit that is not in the repository, prints the same `(no commit: this run sent nothing to merge)` / `(commit <short> is not in this repository)` texts `--stat` prints. A missing commit is not a failure, and the exit code is 0.
- `--json` adds a `patch` string field beside `stat`, and only when the flag is given. No dashboard or TUI change: the dashboard's `GET /api/run` (`handleTick`) and the TUI's History trail (`tickStat` in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts) keep the stat footer only.

**Approach.**
- **src/tick/tick-detail.ts**:
  - Generalize `tickCommitStat(root, sha)` into `tickCommitShow(root, sha, what: "--stat" | "--patch")`, which runs `gitTry(root, "show", what, "--format=", sha)`. It keeps both placeholder texts and the `trimEnd()`. Keep `tickDetailStat` exactly as it is now, on top of the new helper.
  - Export `tickDetailPatch(root, d)` beside it, with a doc comment that names the pinned-commit rule.
  - `cmdTick` gains a trailing `patch = false` parameter. It collects the stat and patch blocks (each only when its flag is given) into one footer list. Plain text joins the trail and the footer with `\n\n`. `--json` spreads `{ stat?, patch? }` into the detail. Update the doc comment and `TICK_USAGE` to `tumwater history <role> [<n>] [--last] [--stat] [--patch] [--json]`.
- **src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts**: add `PATCH_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--patch"] }` beside `STAT_FLAG`, value-less.
- **src/cli.ts** `runTrailCommand`: add `PATCH_FLAG` to its `rejectUnknownArgs` list, and pass `rest.includes("--patch")` to `cmdTick`. Update its doc comment's admitted-flag list.
- **src/cli/help.ts**: the `history <role>` usage line gains `[--patch]`, plus the phrase "--patch appends the commit's full git show patch (after --stat's summary when both are given)". Completion derives from HELP.
- **docs/cli.md** "Watch run history" row: after the `--stat` clause, add "`--patch` appends that commit's full patch (after the `--stat` summary when both are given)".

**Files touched.** src/tick/tick-detail.ts, src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/tick-detail.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/tick-detail.test.ts, "tick --patch appends the pinned commit's patch, text and JSON", built like "tick --stat appends the pinned commit's per-file summary, text and JSON":
  - Its text output starts with the plain trail and contains `diff --git a/README.md b/README.md` plus a `+` line from the commit.
  - With `--stat` and `--patch` together, the `README.md | ` stat line comes before the `diff --git` line.
  - `--json --patch` carries a `patch` field that matches `diff --git`, and it has no `stat` key unless `--stat` is given too.
  - `cli(repo, "tick", "bugfix", "3", "--patch")` exits 0.
- A case beside "tick --stat names a missing or foreign commit instead of failing" checks that `--patch` prints `(no commit: this run sent nothing to merge)` for a run with no commit and `(commit 00000000 is not in this repository)` for a foreign sha.
- The two existing usage assertions in test/tick-detail.test.ts that match `\[--stat\] \[--json\]` are updated to match the new `TICK_USAGE`. The existing `--stat` tests pass with no change.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard's History drill-down gets a "Revert this change" button that previews, then reverts, the run's merged commit through the same cores as `tumwater revert` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight entries edit src/cli/log-commands.ts, `history --model` and the rename series, and none touches src/operator/revert.ts, `handleTick` or the drill-down card; a blocked part of the runner rename series renames identifiers in src/tick/tick-detail.ts, where this plan adds only one exported function; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater revert <sha> [--dry-run]` (`cmdRevert` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts) undoes one merged change on main. The dashboard's History drill-down (`histDetailCardHtml` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, fed by `GET /api/run`, `handleTick` in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts) already shows which sha a run landed under (`merged as <sha>`, added by the finished plan "A run's trail names the sha its change landed under on main"). To undo it, though, the operator has to copy that sha into a terminal. This plan adds the button that the finished plan was laying the groundwork for. It runs the same two cores (`previewRevert`, `revertMergedCommit` in src/operator/revert.ts), so the dashboard and the CLI cannot drift on what a revert refuses or how it commits.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- The button shows only on a run whose change is on the base branch. The server decides which runs those are, not the client.
- It is a two-step control and never reverts on the first click. The first click fetches a dry-run preview and shows it in the card: subject, paths, and whether it applies cleanly. The second click (a "Revert" button in that preview) commits. If the preview says it would conflict, or that the checkout is dirty, it shows no commit button.
- After a revert, the card shows `main is now <short sha>` plus the redo warning that `cmdRevert` prints. The card does not track "already reverted". Previewing a second time shows git's verdict (normally a conflict).
- There is no TUI key. The TUI has no drill-down card to hang it on (its `Ctrl+N` is the newest run only).

**Approach.**
- **src/tick/tick-detail.ts**: export a `tickMergedSha(d: TickDetail): string | null` that returns `d.mergedSha ?? tickCommitSha(d)`. A no-op fast-forward logs no `merged` event, so its pinned commit is what landed. Give it a doc comment saying that.
- **src/operator/revert.ts**: export `resolveRevertTarget`, unchanged. Its doc comment adds that `handleTick` also uses it, to decide whether a run's commit is on the base branch.
- **src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts** `handleTick`: add `revertSha` to the 200 payload. It is the full sha from `resolveRevertTarget(root, landed)` when `landed = tickMergedSha(detail)` is non-null and the target is ok, else null. A rejected or unmerged run's pinned commit is not on main, so it gets null, and so does a primary checkout that is off the base branch. Update the doc comment.
- **src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts**: add `handleRevert(req, res, root)` for `POST /api/revert`. Its body is `{"sha": "<hex>", "dryRun"?: true}`, read with `readPostBody(req, res, '{"sha": "1a2b3c4"}')`.
  - A `sha` that is not a string matching `/^[0-9a-f]{4,64}$/i` gets a 400 and nothing runs. That also rules out a flag-shaped or ref-name value. A `dryRun` that is neither absent nor a boolean also gets a 400.
  - With `dryRun: true`, call `previewRevert`. Success answers 200 `{ ok: true, preview }`, the RevertPreview object. A refusal answers 409 `{ error }`.
  - Otherwise call `revertMergedCommit`. Success answers 200 `{ ok: true, headSha, beforeSha, message }`, where `message` is `main is now <short> — the reverted role may redo the work, so cancel or edit its PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry if it should not`. A refusal answers 409 `{ error }` with the core's wording.
  - Add `handleRevert` to the module's doc-comment list. It is barrelled through src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts like `handleRetire`.
- **src/gui/gui-server.ts**: add the route `"POST /api/revert": (req, res) => handleRevert(req, res, root)` next to `/api/retire`. It inherits the router's shared Origin/token gate for POSTs.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts**:
  - The ok cache entry also keeps `revertSha` (a string, or null when the field is absent, as with an older server). It gains an optional `revert` sub-state: `{ state: "previewing" | "preview" | "reverting" | "done" | "error", preview?, message? }`.
  - `histDetailCardHtml` appends a `<button type='button' data-hist-revert='<role>#<run>'>Revert this change…</button>` when `revertSha` is set. Below it, it renders the sub-state:
    - `previewing`: "Checking…"
    - `preview`: `would revert <short> <subject>`, the paths as a list, then either a `data-hist-revert-go` "Revert" button styled `btn-danger` (applies && !dirty) or the CLI's would-conflict / dirty-checkout sentence.
    - `done`: the server's message.
    - `error`: the server's error.
  - Add `previewHistRevert(key)` and `runHistRevert(key)`, which `postJson("/api/revert", …)` and then `renderHistory()`. Wire them through one delegated click handler in `buildHistoryView`, next to its `data-hist` listener.
  - `fetchHistory` already clears `histDetails`, so a refetch drops every stale preview.

**Files touched.** src/tick/tick-detail.ts, src/operator/revert.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts (barrel export), src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts, docs/how-it-works.md (one sentence on the dashboard's History drill-down, beside the existing drill-down mention), docs/cli.md ("Steer the project" row: "the dashboard's History drill-down offers the same revert, preview first"), and the new test file test/gui-revert.test.ts plus test/gui-client-history.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test/gui-revert.test.ts, built on the `fakeReq`/`captureJson` shape of test/gui-retire.test.ts with `makeRepo`/`seedCommit` from test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts:
  - "POST /api/revert dryRun previews and writes nothing": 200, and `preview.applies` is true. HEAD and `git status --porcelain` are unchanged.
  - "POST /api/revert reverts a merged commit": 200. HEAD moved, and its subject is `tumwater(operator): Revert <short>`.
  - "POST /api/revert refuses a sha not on main with 409 and writes nothing" (a commit on a side branch).
  - "POST /api/revert rejects a non-hex sha and a non-boolean dryRun with 400": `"--json"`, `"main"`, `42`, and `dryRun: "yes"`.
- The test file that covers `handleTick` (test/gui-server-api.test.ts's "gui /api/run serves one run's detail…" seed, or a new case beside it) checks two things. `revertSha` is the full sha for a run whose `merge_done` commit is on main. It is null for a run whose pinned commit is not in the repo.
- test/gui-client-history.test.ts covers three cases. (1) An ok entry with `revertSha` renders the `data-hist-revert` button, and one without it does not. (2) Clicking the button posts `{sha, dryRun: true}` and renders the preview's subject and paths plus a `data-hist-revert-go` button. A preview with `applies: false` renders no go button. (3) Clicking go posts `{sha}` with no `dryRun` and renders the server's message.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater logs -f` ends itself once the process that started it is gone, so a follow orphaned at PPID 1 stops instead of polling for days (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry: the in-flight entries edit status, prompt, history, src/tick and the GUI backlog, and none touches src/cli/log-commands.ts's follow loops) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** Both follow loops in src/cli/log-commands.ts, the event feed's `followFile(...)` at the end of `cmdLogs` and the transcript's in `cmdLogsTranscript`, end with `await new Promise(() => {}); // Follow until Ctrl+C.`. A follow whose parent shell exits is reparented to launchd/init. Its 500 ms `followFile` poll then keeps it alive forever, because nothing ever sends it Ctrl+C. BUGS.md's open entry "Two `logs -f` processes leaked out of a slot's run and stayed alive for 3½ days" is that shape: two `node …/_slot-8/dist/src/cli.js logs -f` sat at PPID 1 from 2026-10-16 until the doctor flagged them. That bug waits on the spawner's identity before adding any reaper. This plan does not reap anything. It makes `logs -f` itself end when its parent goes, which is the same parent-death watch the run generation (`startParentDeathWatch` in src/process/supervisor.ts) and the dashboards (`watchReloadSupervisor` in src/redeploy/self-reload.ts) already arm. Whoever turns out to spawn a leaked follow, the follow cleans itself up. Leave the bug entry open: its spawner question still stands. The implementer adds one **Progress 2026-MM-DD (feature)** line under it naming this change.

**Decided scope (no open question).**
- Only `-f`/`--follow`, in both views (the event feed and `--role <id>` transcripts). The bounded views (`-n`, `--since`, `--count`) already return on their own.
- "Gone" means `process.ppid` differs from its value when the follow started, the rule `startParentDeathWatch` already applies. When it fires, the follow stops its `followFile` poll and `cmdLogs` resolves, so the CLI exits 0 through its normal path in src/cli.ts. Nothing calls `process.exit` from the log module.
- A deliberate `nohup tumwater logs -f > file &` whose shell then exits also ends. That is intended: the events stay in `.tumwater/events.jsonl` and `tumwater logs --since` reads them back. docs/cli.md says so.
- The poll uses `startParentDeathWatch`'s default interval (`PARENT_POLL_MS`, 5 s, timer unref'd). No new knob.

**Approach.**
- **src/cli/log-commands.ts**:
  - Add an exported `interface FollowSeams { ppid?: () => number; intervalMs?: number }` with a doc comment saying it exists so tests can drive the parent-death watch without reparenting a real process.
  - Add a module-private `followUntilParentGone(file: string, offset: number, onLines: (lines: string[]) => void, seams: FollowSeams): Promise<void>`. It calls `const stop = followFile(file, offset, onLines)`, then returns a promise. That promise arms `startParentDeathWatch(() => { stop(); resolve(); }, { ...(seams.ppid ? { ppid: seams.ppid } : {}), ...(seams.intervalMs !== undefined ? { intervalMs: seams.intervalMs } : {}) })`. Import `startParentDeathWatch` from ../process/supervisor.js. Its doc comment says the follow runs until Ctrl+C or until its parent is gone, and names the leaked-`logs -f` bug's shape.
  - `cmdLogs(root, args, seams: FollowSeams = {})` passes `seams` to `cmdLogsTranscript` (a new last parameter). Each of the two `followFile(...)` + `await new Promise(() => {})` pairs becomes `await followUntilParentGone(file, <offset>, <same callback>, seams)`. Each callback body stays byte-for-byte the same.
  - Update `cmdLogs`'s doc comment: `-f` follows until Ctrl+C or until its parent process exits.
- **src/cli.ts**: unchanged (`cmdLogs(root, args)` takes the default seams).
- **docs/cli.md**: in the "Check state" row, after `tumwater logs -f` (`--follow`), add: "(ends on its own once the shell or process that started it exits, so a backgrounded follow does not outlive it)".
- **BUGS.md**: one Progress line under the open leaked-`logs -f` entry, as above. Leave its Waiting note and everything else as they are.

**Files touched.** src/cli/log-commands.ts, docs/cli.md, BUGS.md, test/log-commands.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/log-commands.test.ts, "logs -f ends once its parent is gone": in a fresh repo (the existing follow test's setup), `cmdLogs(repo, ["-f"], { ppid: () => parent, intervalMs: 10 })` with `let parent = 4242`. The promise is still pending after an event is appended and printed. After `parent = 1`, it resolves within a bounded wait (poll for up to 5 s). A further appended event is not printed.
- test/log-commands.test.ts, "logs --role -f ends once its parent is gone": the same shape with `["--role", "clean", "-f"]`.
- The existing follow tests in test/log-commands.test.ts and test/cli-logs.test.ts pass unchanged (their parent never changes).
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history --model <selector>[,<selector>...]` keeps only the runs that started on the listed models, the row view behind `history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the in-flight part 11/14 renames comments and local names under src/cli/, and src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts and src/cli.ts's `history` case may meet it as a rebase; the status and prompt entries touch `cmdStatus`, src/ui/status-* and src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, not src/history; touches src/history/history.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` (`summarizeTickRowsByModel`, src/history/history-data.ts) counts runs per model, for example how many runs a role spent on the fallback. Nothing lists the runs behind one of its lines. Every `TickRow` carries `model`, the agent-qualified selector its `run_start` named, or null. Today the closest filter is `--grep <model>`, which also keeps rows whose summary or error happens to mention the text. Add `--model <selector>[,<selector>...]`. It keeps the rows whose `model` equals one of the listed selectors exactly, so a line from the `--by model` table can be copied straight into the filter. Out of scope: the dashboard's and the TUI's History views, and value completion for the flag.

**Decided semantics (no open question).**
- A row matches when `row.model` is one of the listed selectors, compared exactly and case-sensitively. A row with a null model never matches. `(unknown)` is only the summary's label for null, so it is not accepted as a selector.
- The value is split on commas, each piece trimmed, empty pieces dropped and duplicates removed, as `--result` does. A missing value, an empty value, or a value made only of commas fails with `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR = "history --model needs a model selector"`.
- An unknown selector is not an error. Models have no closed vocabulary, and an old log holds models the config has since dropped. An unknown selector just keeps no rows.
- The flag composes with `--role`, `-n`, `--since`, `--grep`, `--result`, `--summary`, `--by` and `--json`. It runs on the collected rows after the `--result` filter and before the `--json`, summary and table branches, so all three render the same narrowed set. `-n` still bounds the scanned window, not the printed rows, which is the `--grep` rule.

**Approach.**
- **src/history/history.ts**:
  - Export `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR` beside `HISTORY_RESULT_VALUE_ERROR`, with a doc comment in the same style.
  - In `cmdHistory`, right after the `--result` block, save `const afterResult = rows.length;`. Then read `flagValue(rest, "--model")` and parse it into `models: string[] | null` as described above. When `models` is set, filter with `rows = rows.filter((r) => r.model !== null && models.includes(r.model))`. Add a comment in the file's style naming the exact-match rule and why an unknown selector is not an error.
  - In the empty-state `say(...)` chain, put a new first arm before the `--result` arm: when `models !== null && afterResult > 0`, print `` `no runs on model "${models.join(",")}"` ``. This keeps the existing rule that the message blames the filter that actually emptied the set. `--json` still prints `{"rows":[]}`.
  - Update the `cmdHistory` doc comment's flag list to name `--model`.
- **src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts**: add `export function modelFlagSpec(missingValue: string): FlagSpec`, returning `{ names: ["--model"], value: true, valueName: "<selector>", missingValue }`, beside `resultFlagSpec`/`byFlagSpec`, with a matching doc comment.
- **src/cli.ts** `case "history"`: import `HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR` with the other history errors and add `modelFlagSpec(HISTORY_MODEL_VALUE_ERROR)` to the `rejectUnknownArgs("history", …)` list. The trail form (`history <role> <n>`) is untouched.
- **src/cli/help.ts**: in the `tumwater history` usage line, add `[--model <selector>[,...]]` after the `--result` bracket. In the description, after the `--result` sentence, add: `--model <selector>[,...] keeps only the runs that started on the listed models (the exact selectors --by model prints);`.
- **docs/cli.md** "Watch run history" row: add `[--model <selector>[,...]]` after the `--result` bracket in the synopsis. After the `--result none,refused,problems` clause, add `, `--model` keeps only the runs that started on the listed models, the exact selectors `--summary --by model` prints (`--model acme/m1 --summary` tallies just that model's runs by role)`.

**Files touched.** src/history/history.ts, src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts. Also touch test/cli-help.test.ts or test/cli-doc.test.ts, but only if their help/doc flag-parity checks need the new flag listed.

**Acceptance criteria.** All new tests go in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts and reuse the event fixture from "history --summary --by model tallies runs per model": feature #1 and #3 on `acme/m1`, clean #2 on `acme/m2`, and bugfix #9 with no start.
- "history --model keeps only the runs that started on the listed models":
  - `history --model acme/m1` prints exactly two rows, feature #3 and feature #1, newest first.
  - `history --model acme/m1,acme/m2 --json` gives `rows` with roles `["feature", "clean", "feature"]`.
  - `history --model acme/m1,acme/m1` prints the same as `--model acme/m1`.
  - `history --model acme/M1` prints `no runs on model "acme/M1"` and exits 0, which shows the match is case-sensitive.
  - `history --model m1` prints the same empty-state line, which shows the match is exact, not a substring.
- "history --model composes with --role, --result and --summary":
  - `--model acme/m1 --result merged` keeps only feature #1.
  - `--model acme/m1 --role clean` prints `no runs on model "acme/m1"`.
  - `--model acme/m1 --summary --by model` gives the model column `["acme/m1", "total"]`.
  - `--model acme/m1 --summary` gives one `feature` line plus `total`.
  - `--model nosuch --json` prints `{"rows":[]}`.
- "history --model fails with its own wording when the value is missing or empty": a trailing `history --model`, `history --model ""` and `history --model ","` each exit non-zero, and stderr matches `history --model needs a model selector`.
- "an empty log keeps its own wording under --model": a repo with no events, run with `--model acme/m1`, prints `no runs yet`.
- The existing tests in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts, test/cli-history.test.ts and test/cli-history-views.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A run's trail names the sha its change landed under on main, so a rebased merge's run says which commit `tumwater revert` takes (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry — the blocked plain-terms parts rename src/tick/ and history-data.ts names later and will rebase over this; the status, prompt and history --model entries touch none of these files; touches src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts src/tick/tick-detail.ts docs/cli.md test/tick-detail-data.test.ts test/tick-detail.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater history <role> <n>` (and the dashboard History drill-down and TUI History
pane, which render the same `renderTickDetail` text) shows only the commit the run *pinned*
(`tickCommitSha` in src/tick/tick-detail.ts: the `merge_queued`/`merge_done` event's
`commit`). When the merge rebased, main holds that change under a different sha, so the
pinned sha is not what `tumwater revert` accepts (`revertMergedCommit` in src/operator/revert.ts
refuses a commit that is not on main), and nothing in the trail names the landed one. The
landed sha is already logged: `merged` events carry it (`logEventBestEffort(... type: "merged",
commit ...)` in src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, source = the role). This plan pairs that event into
the run's payload and header. It is also the prerequisite for a later dashboard "Revert this
change" button, which is not part of this plan.

**Approach.**
- src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts: add `mergedSha: string | null` to `TickDetail` (doc it beside

    event inside `block` whose `commit` is a non-empty string.
  - `merge?.type === "merge_done"` (a queued run whose merge finished): the newest `merged`
    event in `scoped` (already this role's events only) whose `commit` is a non-empty string and

    merge-to-main logs `merged`, and `durationMs` runs from the verification's start. If
    `durationMs` is not a finite number, the value is null. This window also covers a
    leftover-recovery run, whose merge sits before its block.
  - Every other case is null: no merge, a failed or pending merge, or a `merged` event that
    rotated out. A no-op fast-forward logs no `merged` event, so it also reads null.
- src/tick/tick-detail.ts `renderTickDetail`: after the ` · commit <short>` segment, append
  ` · merged as <shortSha(mergedSha)>` when `mergedSha !== null && mergedSha !== sha` (when

  resolves to its merge's verdict and outcome event; a pending merge stays queued", asserts:
  - a queued run with `merged` (commit `landed1`) logged inside its `merge_done`'s
    `durationMs` window reads `mergedSha === "landed1"`;
  - a direct `changed` run with a `merged` event in its block reads that event's commit;
