### Fast merge, part 4a/14: The main watch names the first-parent commit that turned main red (planned 2026-10-19 by user, split 2026-10-19 by the plan role from part 4/14; requires part 3/14 landed; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 2: merge on the gate, full check after the merge"; touches src/baseline/main-watch.ts src/baseline/main-culprit.ts src/events/events.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Part 3's watch records a red tip but not which commit broke it. This part finds that commit and records it, without acting on it yet. Parts 4b/14 (revert) and 4c/14 (hand-back) act on this event. Splitting the search out keeps each part one run.

**Approach.**
- New module src/baseline/main-culprit.ts exporting `findRedCulprit(root, wt, config, red)`, where `red` is the watch's confirmed red `MainBaseline` at tip T. It runs inside the watch's existing `withMainTipWorktree` callback, so every check goes through `gateMainQueue` in `_gate-main`. Re-point the mirror per candidate with `ensureDetachedWorktree(root, gateMainWorktreePath(root), sha)`, and re-point it back at T before returning.
- Last green G: walk `git rev-list --first-parent T` (T excluded) and take the newest commit whose `cachedBaselineVerdict` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) is `"green"`. Cap the walk at a constant `CULPRIT_SEARCH_MAX = 50`. When none is found, return `{ kind: "unattributed", reason: "no green commit within 50 first-parent commits" }`.
- Environment guard: check G with `checkMainBaseline(…, forceFresh = true, …, CHECK_TIER.merge)`. If G is red now, return `{ kind: "environment", green: G }`.
- Bisect: the candidates are the first-parent commits in G..T, minus those whose diff touches only `review.exemptPaths` (`isExemptDiff`, src/review/exemptions.ts). Binary-search for the first red candidate C. Use `checkMainBaseline` with observedOnly = true, so cached verdicts answer without a run. Then confirm C once with `reverifyRed = true`; if it comes back green, return `unattributed` ("red did not reproduce at <C>").
- New failures: T's `failingTests` minus G's (G's are empty when its cached verdict is green, so this is T's list; keep the subtraction for a G that carried known failures).
- Owner: the newest `merged` event whose `commit` is C (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts and src/merge/merge-stack.ts log it; its `source` is the runner). Read it with `readEvents` (src/events/event-read.ts); a commit whose `merged` event has left the read tail counts as having none. Return `{ kind: "culprit", commit: C, runner?: string, failingTests }`. `runner` is absent for a commit with no `merged` event (an operator or hand commit).
- `createMainWatch` (src/baseline/main-watch.ts): after it logs a `main_check` with status `failed`, it calls `findRedCulprit` and logs exactly one event:
  - culprit → `main_culprit` `{ commit, runner?, failingTests, green }`. Register `main_culprit` in the event-type union in src/events/events.ts with a comment in the style of `main_check`'s.
  - environment → a `warning` `main's last green commit <short G> is red now too — not attributing`.
  - unattributed → a `warning` naming the reason.
- Search only once per red head: a later poll on the same T does not search again. Update the module comment ("nothing acts on what it sees yet" still holds; add that the watch names the culprit).

**Files touched.** src/baseline/main-culprit.ts (new), src/baseline/main-watch.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-labels.ts and src/events/event-format.ts (the new event type needs a label and a line), docs/how-it-works.md, test/main-watch.test.ts (the culprit cases live here, not in a new test/main-culprit.test.ts).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In a fake repo with a fake check: G is green, A merges green, B makes a test fail, D is doc-only. The watch on D logs `main_culprit` with commit B, B's `merged` runner, and the failing test.
- With the check made red at G too, no `main_culprit` is logged and the "red now too" warning is.
- A red culprit with no `merged` event yields `main_culprit` with no `runner`.
- No green within the cap gives the unattributed warning.
- `npm test` passes.

**Changed from the plan.** The subset rule lives in `onlyKnownMainFailures` beside `knownMainFailures` (src/baseline/main-watch.ts, which keeps the newest verdict's failing tests per root in memory); the merge-lock rule sits in `verifyMerge` (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts) and, for a batch, in `mergeStack` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts), so a known-only red stack merges in its one check instead of bisecting. src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts also changed: `mergeCheckRed` and `attributeRedCheck` keep the pin (`merge_blocked`, no strike) for a red naming only known failures, covering a main whose known set grew after the check ran. src/baseline/main-red.ts needed no change. ### Fast merge, part 2/14: A runner waiting on its change no longer counts toward its role's `instances` (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 1: roles stop waiting on their own change"; touches src/roles/runner-ids.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/scheduling/claims.ts src/ui/status-model.ts src/status/status-roles.ts docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md and their tests); done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** A runner with a change in the merge pipeline never runs (plans/merge-queue.md invariant 3), so `instances: 5` means five runners that are each idle while their change merges. From 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-19 the five feature runners wrote code for 77.5 h and waited on their own changes for 129.5 h. On average only 1.4 of them were writing code at any moment. Keep the one-change-per-runner rule, and let the role use more runners: a runner waiting on its change no longer holds one of the role's `instances` places.

**Approach.**
- Only the roles in `INSTANCE_ROLES` (feature, bugfix) change. Single-runner roles stay exactly as they are.
- src/roles/runner-ids.ts:
  - `runnerIds` and `runnerEnabled` allow runner ids up to `2 × instances`: `feature` … `feature-10` at `instances: 5`. Name the factor once as `RUNNERS_PER_INSTANCE = 2`.
  - `configuredInstances` keeps its meaning: the role's limit on concurrent runs.
- Admission, in the poll (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts):
  - A runner of an instance role may start a run only while fewer than `instances` of that role's runners are running (a run in flight, not a queued change).
  - A runner with a queued change is still skipped by the interlock.
  - Among eligible runners, first admit one with a pending revision or conflict hand-back, then the lowest-index runner with neither.
- Claims (src/scheduling/claims.ts):
  - Each runner keeps its own claim. A waiting runner keeps the entry its change carries, and the next admitted runner is assigned the next eligible entry.
  - The claim-group hold (`busy`, orchestrator-scheduling.ts ~176-180) and `workReserveCount` count running runners, not runner ids.
- Lowering `instances` keeps today's resize behavior: surplus runners finish what is queued and start nothing new.
- Status: a runner with index above `instances` that has no run, no queued change, no claim and no pending revision does not get its own row. This covers `tumwater status` (src/status/status-roles.ts), the dashboard and the TUI (src/ui/status-model.ts), so the table does not show ten idle feature rows.
- docs/config.md `instances` row: the number of runs writing code at once; tumwater keeps up to twice as many runners, so a runner waiting on its change does not hold a place. docs/how-it-works.md: the same, in the parallel-instances paragraph.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/roles/runner-ids.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/scheduling/claims.ts, src/ui/status-model.ts, src/status/status-roles.ts.
- Docs: docs/config.md, docs/how-it-works.md.
- Tests: test/runner-ids.test.ts (or wherever `runnerIds` is tested), the scheduling and claims tests, and an orchestrator e2e test with a fake agent.
- Keep the interlock assertions in test/orchestrator-3.e2e.test.ts true per runner.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `instances: 2` and a fake reviewer that blocks: while one feature change waits in the pipeline, a second feature runner starts a run on the next planned entry. No third run starts while two are running.
- A change rejected for revision runs on its own runner before a free runner starts new work, once a place is free.
- No two runners ever hold the same claim.
- An idle surplus runner does not appear in `tumwater status`.
- plan, clean and every other single-runner role schedule exactly as before.
- `npm test` passes.

**Deviations.** `instances: 1` keeps its single bare runner (the 2× pool applies from `instances: 2`); src/ui/status-model.ts needed no change because the row filter lives in src/status/status-roles.ts, which feeds the TUI too.

### Fast merge, part 13/14: The run prompt names the gate command for verification and says tumwater runs the full check (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 6: agents run the tests for what they touched"; touches src/prompt/prompt.ts src/tick/tick-prompt.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The run prompt says "verify with `npm run test` (the project's declared check) — run it after your change and fix what you broke" (src/prompt/prompt.ts ~147). From 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-19 agents ran the full suite in 70 of 162 sampled author runs, 12% of author run time. Tumwater runs the gate command on every change and the full check itself, so the agent only needs the gate command.

**Approach.**
- src/tick/tick-prompt.ts (~127): pass `gateCommandOf(config)` to the prompt builder alongside the detected check.
- src/prompt/prompt.ts: with a gate command, the verify text becomes: "verify with `<gate>` (lint, compile and the tests your change affects) — run it after your change and fix what you broke. Tumwater runs the full check (`<check>`) itself; do not run it." The "Leave the project working" rule's scratch-file advice names the gate command. Without a gate command the wording is unchanged.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts.
- Tests: test/prompt.test.ts (~125, ~129, ~411), test/tick-prompt.test.ts (~117), plus a new case with `check.gateCommand` set.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `check.gateCommand: "npm run test:gate"`, a feature prompt names `npm run test:gate` and does not contain "verify with `npm run test`".
- Without a gate command, the existing wording tests (`pytest -q`, `make check`, the fallback) pass unchanged.
- `npm test` passes.

### Fast merge, part 10/14: An approval survives a rebase, a requeue and a restart while the change's own lines are unchanged (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 5: a diff is reviewed once"; touches src/git/git.ts src/review/review.ts src/runner/runner-state.ts src/tick/tick-apply.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** 42% of review time from 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-19 went to reviewing a diff that had not changed: 66 reviews after a requeue (14.3 h) and 40 after a clean rebase (3.5 h). The approval key is a patch-id that hashes context lines (src/git/git.ts ~487-513), so main moving next to a hunk invalidates it. PLANS.md and BUGS.md hunks, in nearly every change, are the usual case. Only one approval is remembered per role (`lastApprovedPatchId`, src/runner/runner-state.ts).

**Approach.**
- The approval patch-id hashes the change's own lines only: `git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary -U0 main...head | git patch-id --verbatim`. Update the comment that says context lines count.
- Remember up to 8 approved patch-ids per runner (`approvedPatchIds`), persisted with the runner state so they survive a restart.
  - Clear them when the change merges (`changed`) or is finally rejected (src/tick/tick-apply.ts).
  - `lastApprovedHead` stays.
- The reuse check in src/review/review.ts (~274-281) matches any remembered id.
- The gate pre-check still runs before reuse on a tree that moved; only the reviewer is skipped.
- A conflict resolution that changes the change's own lines gets a different id and is reviewed, as today.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/git/git.ts, src/review/review.ts, src/runner/runner-state.ts, src/tick/tick-apply.ts.
- Tests: test/git.test.ts (or test/git-diff.test.ts) and the review tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A change is approved. Main then edits a PLANS.md line next to the change's PLANS.md hunk, and the change is verified again. No `review_start` is logged, the gate runs, and the change merges.
- A change whose own lines changed is reviewed.
- After a restart, an approved change that is still queued is verified again without a review.
- `npm test` passes.

### Fast merge, part 1/14: The merge pipeline re-queues a kept change itself, so a retry needs no author run (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 1: roles stop waiting on their own change"; touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts src/merge/merge-queue.ts src/merge/merge-verify.ts src/runner/leftover.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts docs/how-it-works.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** A merge attempt that ends `merge_blocked`, `review_error`, `merge_conflict` or `main_red` drops its queue entry and keeps its pin. Only the author's next run puts it back, through `recoverLeftover` (src/runner/leftover.ts), and that run waits for its scheduling gap. After `main_red` it also waits on the idle backoff, which doubles from 120 s up to 10 h. From 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-19, 79 `merge_blocked` attempts alone held 60 h of pipeline time. The pipeline should re-queue such a change itself, at once.

**Approach.**
- Factor the eligibility checks of `recoverLeftover` into one exported helper that both the author path and the pipeline call, so the two cannot drift. The checks are:
  - a pin that main already contains is stale and gets deleted;
  - the `mergeReviewError` hold;
  - `MERGE_CONFLICT_LIMIT`, at which the conflict hand-back stays the author's job.
- After `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) drops the entry, handle a result in `RETRIABLE_MERGE_RESULTS` (src/merge/merge-core.ts) whose pin still exists and that the helper allows:
  - enqueue a new entry for the same runner;
  - copy the dropped entry's `run`, `summary`, `body`, `highFriction`, `revisionRound` and `priorReview` unchanged, so the summary is not the "recovered leftover work from …" label;
  - use the pin's current sha;
  - log `merge_queued` with a new `retry` field naming the result.
- A `review_error` re-queue waits 60 s. Add an optional `notBefore` (epoch ms) to `MergeEntry` (src/merge/merge-queue.ts) and have `drainVerify` (src/merge/merge-verify.ts) skip an entry until then. A dead reviewer backend is already held team-wide by `reviewHeld`.
- `main_red` keeps the pin, as today. The orchestrator poll (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, where it reads `mainHead`) re-queues such a pin on the first poll whose main head differs from the head when the attempt settled. Record that head on the runner's state, beside the pin.
- The interlock (`queuedRoles`, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts) is unchanged: the runner still does not run while its re-queued entry exists. Leftover recovery at run start stays as the backstop after a restart or a crash.
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the paragraph about merge retries, say the pipeline re-queues a kept change itself.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/merge/merge-slot.ts, src/merge/merge-queue.ts, src/merge/merge-verify.ts, src/runner/leftover.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, and src/runner/runner-state.ts for the head field.
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md.
- Tests: test/merge-requeue.test.ts (new), test/orchestrator-once.e2e.test.ts (an orchestrator test with a fake agent), and test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A change whose first in-lock merge check is red, then green, merges with no `run_start` for its runner between its `merge_failed merge_blocked` and its `merge_done`. The re-queue's `merge_queued` carries the original summary and `retry: "merge_blocked"`.
- A `review_error` attempt re-queues once, no sooner than 60 s later. A held reviewer configuration error does not re-queue.
- A `main_red` pin re-queues once main's head moves, and not before.
- At `MERGE_CONFLICT_LIMIT` the hand-back still goes through the author's run, as today.
- `npm test` passes.

### Fast merge, part 5/14: Self-redeploy runs main's newest green commit, not only a green tip (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 2: merge on the gate, full check after the merge"; touches src/redeploy/redeployer.ts src/redeploy/redeploy.ts src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/baseline/main-baseline.ts docs/how-it-works.md docs/invariants.md and their tests); done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Self-redeploy only ever runs a commit whose full check is green (decided 2026-10-19 by you). Today it targets only main's tip (`mainHead`, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts ~355). When the tip is red it deploys nothing until main moves (`blockedHead`, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts ~317 and ~411). Once part 6 lets main be briefly red between merges, that would stall redeploys. The target should be the newest green commit instead.

**Approach.**
- Choose the target before `redeploy.poll`, or as a `RedeployDeps` method (src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts):
  - Walk main's first-parent history from the tip back to the running build's commit, at most 64 commits.
  - Take the newest commit with a green full-check verdict in the cache; observed and inherited greens both count.
  - An unchecked tip is checked as today (`mainIsGreen`, src/redeploy/redeploy.ts). If it is red, fall back to the newest older green commit that is newer than the running build.
- `staleness`, `mainGreen`, `compile`, `swap` and the prewarm probe (src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts) already take a sha; pass the target.
- `blockedHead` blocks only the red commit itself.
- Only full-check verdicts count. A green from a cheaper command (part 6's `check.mergeCommand`) never makes a commit deployable.
- docs/invariants.md: an entry stating that self-redeploy only runs a commit with a green full-check verdict, pinned by this part's test. docs/how-it-works.md: the redeploy paragraph.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/baseline/main-baseline.ts.
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md, docs/invariants.md.
- Tests: test/redeployer.test.ts, test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.

**As built.** `redeployTarget` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) picks the target and src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts passes it to `redeploy.poll` as the head, so the redeployer, probes and policy files needed no change; tests are in test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Running build A, main A → B (green) → C (red): the redeploy targets B.
- Running build A, main A → B (red): no redeploy.
- A green tip is deployed as today.
- A commit with only a non-full-check green is never deployed.
- `npm test` passes.

### Fast merge, part 3/14: Main watch runs the full check on main's tip after merges and records each verdict with its failing tests (planned 2026-10-19 by user; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 2: merge on the gate, full check after the merge"; touches src/baseline/main-baseline.ts src/baseline/main-red.ts src/build/build-check-report.ts src/build/build-check.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts src/events/events.ts docs/how-it-works.md and their tests, plus a new src/baseline/main-watch.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Parts 4–8 need a full-check verdict for main's commits, with the names of the failing tests, without any run or merge waiting for it. Today a full check runs on main only when something needs one right away: a fresh run's red-main gate, the gate's re-attribution, a merge's attribution, or the redeployer. A red verdict keeps only its script and a clipped output tail. This part adds the watch and records what it sees. Nothing acts on it yet.

**Approach.**
- New src/baseline/main-watch.ts, called from the orchestrator poll beside `redeploy.poll` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts ~448) with the poll's `mainHead`. When the head differs from the last watched head and no watch run is in flight:
  - Run main's full check on the tip through `gateMainQueue` in `_gate-main` (src/baseline/main-red.ts), at merge-tier check priority.
  - Cached verdicts count, so do not force a fresh run.
  - A red runs once more before it is final (`reverifyRed`).
  - One run covers every commit since the last watched head; a head that moves during a run is watched next.
- Doc-only commits inherit green, as `inheritedGreen` already does.
- Skip while the team is held for a restart or for disk space, and when the project has no check.
- Failing tests:
  - Add `failingTests?: string[]` to `MainBaseline` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts).
  - Parse them from the complete check output, before `clipBuildTail` cuts it (src/build/build-check-report.ts, src/build/build-check.ts): every line `FAILED_TEST_LINE` matches, with the trailing duration stripped, deduplicated, in output order, at most 50.
  - Export the parser for parts 7 and 9.
- Persist reds: `.tumwater/state/baseline-verdicts.json` gains `reds: [{ sha, script, failingTests }]` (newest 64) beside `greens`, loaded at start like the greens.
- Log a `main_check` event: `{ sha, status, durationMs, covered, failingTests? }`. `covered` counts first-parent commits since the previous watched head. Register it in the event catalog (src/events/events.ts) so `tumwater logs` renders it.
- docs/how-it-works.md: a short paragraph on the watch.

**Files touched.**
- Source: new src/baseline/main-watch.ts; src/baseline/main-baseline.ts, src/baseline/main-red.ts, src/build/build-check-report.ts, src/build/build-check.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/events/events.ts.
- Docs: docs/how-it-works.md.
- Tests: a new test/main-watch.test.ts, test/main-baseline-persist.test.ts, and a parser case in the build-check report tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- After a fake merge, exactly one `main_check` with status `passed` is logged for the new head.
- Two merges in quick succession produce at most two watch runs. A run that covers both reports `covered: 2`.
- A red tip logs `main_check` status `failed` with `failingTests` parsed from a node:test fixture output holding three `✖` lines. The red was re-run once first.
- A restart reloads the red verdict and its failing tests.
- A doc-only commit inherits green without a run.
- No run, gate or merge waits on the watch.
- `npm test` passes.

### Give the director an own-clock retry for its unmerged change, not only a prompt-driven one (planned 2026-10-19 by user; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the TUI-editor entries and the check-wait pair (src/build, src/events, src/doctor, src/config) and the backend/model split (src/config, src/status, src/roles) touch none of this part's files; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/scheduling (runner 9/14, run 12/20), src/orchestrator (runner 8/14, run 10/20-11/20), src/runner (run 8/20-9/20) and src/tick (run 1/20-5/20) only in far-behind parts, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/scheduling/scheduling.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts + src/runner/leftover.ts + src/runner/runner-run.ts + src/tick/tick-resume.ts + docs/how-it-works.md + test/scheduling.test.ts + test/leftover.test.ts + test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts + test/orchestrator-director.test.ts + test/runner-leftover-recovery.test.ts + test/orchestrator.e2e.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** A change whose merge fails non-terminally keeps its merge ref and is retried by "next-tick leftover recovery, never the queue" (`src/events/events.ts:41`): `docs/how-it-works.md:281-283` promises "a commit left unmerged (a merge error that kept it, or a crash before it was queued) goes back in the merge queue at the role's next run, which ends there instead of authoring". Thirteen roles get that next run from their own min-run clock; the director is the only role with no clock — `isEligible` returns a run for it only when `inboxCount > 0` (`src/scheduling/scheduling.ts:60-63`), so after a `merge_blocked` (`src/tick/tick-apply.ts:290-296` sets `lastResult`, so the dashboard reads "Merge blocked") a director with an empty inbox sits on the kept pin **forever** and nothing retries it. The exemption that creates this is a *cost* argument — an explicit human prompt outranks any autonomous gate, `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts:217-235` — but a leftover-recovery run spends nothing: it authoring-runs no pi and ends in about a second (`finishRecoveryTickPhase`, `src/runner/runner-recovery.ts:94-136`). **Goal:** a director holding a kept merge pin is due on the same min-run clock a `queued` outcome already schedules (`scheduleAtMinInterval`, `src/tick/tick-apply.ts:157-169`; default 20 s), and that promptless run re-enqueues the pin exactly as a prompt-driven leftover-recovery run does today.

**Approach.**
- **The due reason.** `src/scheduling/scheduling.ts`: add `leftoverPending?: boolean` to `EligibilityOptions` (documented as "the role holds a kept merge pin a previous merge failed to land") and the director branch becomes `if (inboxCount > 0) return { run: true, reason: "inbox" }; if (opts.leftoverPending) return now >= s.nextRunAt ? { run: true, reason: "leftover" } : { run: false }; return { run: false };`. The inbox arm stays first, so a queued prompt never waits the clock. The `nextRunAt` gate is what keeps the retry from spinning: a persistently blocked fast-forward (a dirty primary checkout, or main moving under the ff) is never counted (`src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts:113-115`), so without the clock every poll would re-queue the same pin and pay a full gate+merge check per cycle; `nextRunAt` is the interval the `queued` outcome already wrote, the same cadence every other role retries its kept pin at. The director is never yield-scaled (`docs/how-it-works.md:184-190`), so the plain clock — not `yieldMultiplierFor` — is the right one.
- **The predicate.** `src/runner/leftover.ts`: add `export async function hasUnmergedPin(root: string, role: string): Promise<boolean>` — true when `refSha(root, mergeRefName(role))` (`src/paths.ts:467-469`) resolves. Placed beside `recoverLeftover`, the one reader of that same ref, so the poll and the recovery path cannot disagree on what "unfinished" means. A pin main already holds is left to `recoverLeftover` (it deletes the stale ref and returns null), so the cheap ref-presence answer is enough and no `isMergedInto` probe is added to the poll.
- **The poll.** `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts`: beside the one-list-per-poll `queuedRoles` snapshot (`:141-146`), compute `const pinnedDirector = !queuedRoles.has(DIRECTOR_ROLE) && (await hasUnmergedPin(root, DIRECTOR_ROLE))`. The `!queuedRoles` clause keeps the merge-queue interlock authoritative (`:330-338`): while the pin is queued or in flight the interlock already holds the role, and the leftover reason must not read as operator demand. Pass `leftoverPending: pinnedDirector` into the `isEligible` call. The gates above it (subscription-window hold, per-role pause, disk hold, restart hold) already cover the new reason, so no gate decision changes; `commitTier(DIRECTOR_ROLE)` is "work" (`src/roles/roles.ts:116-121`), so the maintenance allowance never holds it. The reason rides into the `wake` event (`src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts:139-141`) and renders as `woke (leftover)` (`src/events/event-format.ts:213`).
- **Reachability — the real seam.** Recovery sits inside the prompt-bearing path: `planTickStart` returns null for a null prompt (`src/tick/tick-resume.ts:187`) and `runTickPhase` returns `{ result: "skipped" }` before any worktree work (`src/runner/runner-run.ts:348`). Add one input to `planTickStart` — `recoveryOnly?: boolean`, set by the runner when `ctx.pending.get() === null` and the shared `hasUnmergedPin` predicate holds — and, when set, return a plan with `prompt: null`, `resuming: false`, `handoff: false`, `userPrompt: null` instead of the null-plan early return. `TickStartPlan.prompt` widens to `string | null` and its doc comment (`src/tick/tick-resume.ts:15-34`) changes from "Never null" to "null only for a promptless recovery run".
- **The promptless tick.** `src/runner/runner-run.ts`: `tickWithWorktreePhase`'s leftover-recovery block already runs first and returns via `ctx.finishRecoveryTick` when it salvaged the pin. Add the other arm: when recovery found nothing (or deleted a stale pin) **and** `prompt === null`, end there — `await resetWorktreeToMain(wt, ctx.mainBranch); return { result: "skipped" };` — immediately after the recovery block and before the red-main gate, so a run that authors nothing never reaches `ctx.pi.runAuthoringPi(wt, prompt, …)` with a null prompt.
- **Do not consume the pending reroute.** `runTickPhase`'s director branch clears `s.imageReroute` once the tick is confirmed to run (`:349-363`), so the image-reroute one-shot is delivered with exactly one prompt. Gate that clear on `plan.prompt !== null`: a promptless recovery run must leave a pending reroute for the prompt that follows it. The director's dedicated worktree hold (`useWorktree`, same branch) is unchanged and still wraps the recovery run.
- **What it deliberately does not change.** Scope is the director only. Every other role already gets a next tick from its own clock, and after a `queued` result that clock is the role's own min interval, so their pins already retry "at the role's next run". Widening the rule to every role would let a steward retry a blocked merge on a ~20 s clock instead of its 6 h one — a team-wide pacing change this entry does not make. The director still authors nothing without a prompt: a recovery-only tick's outcomes are `queued` (pin salvaged), `skipped` (nothing to salvage), or `error` (the pin is held on a permanent reviewer-config error, `recoverLeftover`'s `held` arm, which stays on the error ladder). With a prompt queued the flow is today's exactly: recovery salvages the pin, `finishRecoveryTick` hands the prompt back (`ctx.pending.requeueUnfulfilled`, `src/runner/runner-recovery.ts:101-103`) and the tick ends `queued`; the next poll's tick runs the prompt.
- **Docs.** `docs/how-it-works.md`: the Interruptions bullet at `:281-283` gains the director clause (its next run is otherwise only ever an operator prompt, so it is also due on its own min-run clock while a pin is kept); the Scheduling director bullet at `:174` gains the same sentence, naming the `woke (leftover)` wake event.

**Tests.**
- **test/scheduling.test.ts** — the director arm, beside the existing inbox case: `isEligible(director, now, head, 0, { leftoverPending: true })` is `{ run: false }` before `nextRunAt` and `{ run: true, reason: "leftover" }` at/after it; `{ leftoverPending: false }` with an empty inbox stays `{ run: false }`; a non-empty inbox stays `{ run: true, reason: "inbox" }` whatever `leftoverPending` is (the inbox arm never waits the clock).
- **test/leftover.test.ts** — `hasUnmergedPin` is false with no ref and true with one; a stale pin (the sha contained in main) reads true until `recoverLeftover` deletes it, then false — pinned beside the existing stale-pin recovery case.
- **test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts** — a director whose state holds a kept merge ref and an empty inbox appears in the poll's reasons map with `"leftover"`; while a merge-queue entry for the director exists, it does not (`queuedRoles` wins and no demand is counted).
- **test/runner-leftover-recovery.test.ts** — the promptless run: with a kept pin, an empty inbox and `recoveryOnly`, the tick logs `merge_queued` for the same sha, ends `queued` with `recoveredLeftover`, runs no pi (the fake-pi records zero authoring calls), logs no `prompt_taken`, and leaves a pending `imageReroute` marker in place; with no pin and no prompt it ends `skipped` and touches nothing.
- **test/orchestrator.e2e.test.ts** — mirror the file's "a queued prompt wakes the idle director (reason: inbox)" case at `:272-313`: pin `refs/tumwater/merge/director` to a commit off main with an empty inbox, run the fast team, and require a director `wake` event with `reason: "leftover"`, a tick that re-enqueues the same sha and runs no authoring pi, and — the control — no director tick at all when the ref is absent and the inbox is empty.
- **test/orchestrator-director.test.ts** — the once-round twin: `run --once` recovers the director's kept pin and still drains the merge queue before exit; an idle director with neither prompt nor pin still settles as idle (the existing `test/orchestrator-once.test.ts:124` case stays green unchanged).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A director holding `refs/tumwater/merge/director` and an empty inbox ticks on its own min-run clock (`reason: "leftover"`), logs `merge_queued` re-enqueueing the pin, runs no pi, and ends `queued` — the end state a prompt-driven leftover-recovery run reaches today — with no `prompt_taken` event.
- A promptless director with no kept pin still skips: no tick, no wake, `nextRunAt` untouched (byte-identical to today's idle behavior, `test/orchestrator-once.test.ts:124` included).
- The retry never beats `nextRunAt`: after a `merge_blocked` the director waits the min interval the `queued` outcome scheduled, so a persistently blocked fast-forward cannot spin the merge queue, and a held pin (permanent reviewer-config error) stays on the error ladder rather than the min-interval one.
- With a prompt queued and a pin kept the behavior is today's exactly: one recovery tick that hands the prompt back, then the authoring tick (the existing double-`prompt_taken` pin in `test/pending-prompt.test.ts` stays green).
- A recovery-only tick consumes no pending image reroute; the next prompted director tick still starts on the reroute's target.
- Every other role's eligibility and retry cadence are unchanged: `leftoverPending` reaches only the director arm, and no non-director schedule changes.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`'s Interruptions and Scheduling director bullets name the director's own-clock recovery and the `woke (leftover)` wake.
- `npm test` passes.

### Check-wait observability, part 2/2: `tumwater doctor` names check-slot contention and the dashboard Settings edits `maxConcurrentChecks` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; requires part 1/2 landed; independent of every other eligible Planned entry — the TUI-editor entries touch src/ui/tui and its seams, which this part does not, and the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/doctor and src/config only in far-behind parts; touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts src/config/config-editable-keys.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts docs/cli.md docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/gui-client-settings.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Part 1/2 records `check_wait` events, but nothing reads them: an operator sees a check wait only by grepping the feed. The two sibling waits already have a consumer: `checkWorktreePool`'s workspace row sums `slot_wait` and names `worktreeSlots`, and `checkProviderContention` sums `provider_wait` and names `maxConcurrentPerProvider`; both knobs are dashboard-editable because `tumwater doctor` names them (the rationale on `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS`). `maxConcurrentChecks` is the third such cap, documented in docs/config.md and `TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`, validated by `validateConfig`'s `checkNumber(r, "", "maxConcurrentChecks", POSITIVE_INTEGER)`, but editable only by hand in `tumwater.json` — it is in neither `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` nor the dashboard's `SETTINGS_KEYS`. This part adds the missing consumer and surface: a `check contention` doctor row that warns over a 24 h window and names the cap, and a dashboard Settings row for it.

**Approach.**
- **src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts** — add `const CHECK_WAIT_CHECK_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 3600_000;` and `const CHECK_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS = 10 * 60_000;` beside `SLOT_WAIT_*`/`PROVIDER_WAIT_*`, and `export function checkCheckContention(root: string, config: TumwaterConfig | undefined, now = Date.now()): CheckOutcome`, mirroring `checkProviderContention` minus the per-key grouping: read `eventsSince(root, CHECK_WAIT_CHECK_WINDOW_MS, now, (ev) => ev.type === "check_wait")` inside a try/catch that returns `okOutcome("could not read the event log for check waits: " + errorMessage(err))` on a read error; accumulate `count`, `total` and `longestMs` from `finiteNumber(ev.waitedMs, 0)`; return `okOutcome("no check waits")` when `count === 0`; build `detail = `${plural(count, "wait")} for a check slot in the last 24h, ${shortSpanPhrase(total)} total, longest ${shortSpanPhrase(longestMs)}``; when `total >= CHECK_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS`, append ` — raise maxConcurrentChecks above ${config?.maxConcurrentChecks ?? defaultConfig().maxConcurrentChecks}` and return `warnOutcome(detail)`, else `okOutcome(detail)`. Import `defaultConfig` from `../config/config.js` (not yet imported in this file) and `TumwaterConfig` is already in scope.
- **src/doctor/doctor.ts** — register `{ name: "check contention", ...checkCheckContention(root, config) },` directly after the `{ name: "provider contention", ... }` row, and add `checkCheckContention` to the existing `./doctor-checks.js` import list.
- **src/config/config-editable-keys.ts** — add `"maxConcurrentChecks"` to `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` in the run-concurrency group with `maxConcurrent`/`maxConcurrentPerProvider`/`worktreeSlots`, and extend the block comment so the trio becomes a quartet and it names `checkCheckContention` beside `checkWorktreePool`/`checkProviderContention` as the check that advises this key.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts** — add `["maxConcurrentChecks", "Max concurrent checks"],` to `SETTINGS_KEYS` directly after the `maxConcurrentPerProvider` row; the existing `test/gui-client-settings.test.ts` pin (`SETTINGS_KEYS.map(([key]) => key)` equals `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS`) then covers it.
- **docs/config.md** — extend the `maxConcurrentChecks` table row (currently "The most runs of the project's check in flight at once across the whole team.") to name the dashboard Settings field, like the `worktreeSlots`/`provider` rows.
- **docs/cli.md** — in the `Configure` row's list of dashboard-edited keys, add `maxConcurrentChecks` beside the run-concurrency caps; in the `Audit` row's `tumwater doctor` sentence, add the new `check contention` row: sums the last 24 h of `check_wait` events and warns at 10 minutes, naming `maxConcurrentChecks` to raise.
- **docs/how-it-works.md** — extend the `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet (part 1/2 already added the `check_wait` sentence) to say `tumwater doctor`'s `check contention` row sums the last 24 h and warns at 10 minutes, the way the `provider contention` sentence reads.

**Tests.**
- **test/doctor-checks.test.ts** — mirror the existing `checkProviderContention` tests: with `check_wait` events logged via `logEvent` in a temp root, `checkCheckContention(root, config, now)` reports no warns for a total below 10 minutes, and a warn whose detail names the total, the longest wait, and `raise maxConcurrentChecks above 2` when `config` omits the key; with `config = { maxConcurrentChecks: 5 }` the advice says `above 5`; an empty event log yields "no check waits"; an unreadable log yields a non-warn "could not read the event log" outcome.
- **test/gui-client-settings.test.ts** — the existing `SETTINGS_KEYS`-equals-`EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` assertion covers the new row; extend the label assertion so `maxConcurrentChecks` maps to `Max concurrent checks`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater doctor` includes a `check contention` row after `provider contention`: it reports `no check waits` with an empty log; a 24 h total below 10 minutes is ok and names the count, total and longest; a total at or above 10 minutes is a warn naming the count, total, longest and `maxConcurrentChecks` to raise. `--problems` keeps only that warn row when it is the only warn.
- The advice names the live cap when `tumwater.json` sets `maxConcurrentChecks` and the default (2) otherwise, and the row reads nothing but `check_wait` events (doctor stays read-only).
- `maxConcurrentChecks` is in `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` and the dashboard Settings view renders a `Max concurrent checks` row backed by it, editable through the same `/api/config-set`/`/api/config-unset` routes; the `SETTINGS_KEYS`-equals-`EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` test passes.

### `tumwater logs --type` takes a comma-separated list of event types, so one feed or tally shows every event of the kinds an operator is chasing (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — touches only `src/cli/log-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, docs/cli.md and `test/cli-logs-filtering.test.ts`) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `logs --type` filters the event feed by ONE exact type today (`cmdLogs`, `src/cli/log-commands.ts`), so a question that spans kinds — "every `merge_failed` and `review_rejected` in the last day", "count the `run_deferred` and `run_end` events" — takes one command per type or a loose `--grep` that also matches lines quoting those words. Accept `--type a,b,c`: an event passes when its type equals any listed type (after `canonicalEventType`), in every view `--type` already composes with (`-n`, `--since`, `-f`, `--grep`, `--count`, `--json`). A single type behaves exactly as now.

**Approach.**
- **src/cli/log-commands.ts** — after `parseTypeFlag` (unchanged: it still returns the raw value), split `type` on `,`, trim each piece and drop empty pieces; when that leaves none (e.g. `--type ,`), `fail(TYPE_VALUE_ERROR)`. Build `wantedTypes = new Set(pieces.map(canonicalEventType))` and make `typeFilter` test `wantedTypes.has(e.type)`. Replace the `--since` branch's inline `events.filter((e) => e.type === wantedType)` with `events.filter(typeFilter)` so the window, the `-n` view, the tally and the follow share the one predicate (`feedFilter` already threads `typeFilter`). Rework `typeEmpty(type)` to take the raw value and its pieces: the prose stays `no events matching "<raw value as typed>"`, and the did-you-mean hint is `typoSuffix` of the FIRST piece whose canonical form is not an `EVENT_TYPE_LABELS` key (no hint when every piece is valid). The single-type output is then unchanged character for character. Update the `--type` comment block above `parseTypeFlag`'s call to say a comma list matches any of its types.
- **src/cli/help.ts** — the `logs` usage reads `[--type <event type>[,<event type>...]]` and the prose says `--type shows only events of the listed exact event types (comma-separated)`; keep the `--type <event type>` substring so `test("tumwater help logs documents --type")` still matches.
- **docs/cli.md** — the `Check state` row's `tumwater logs --type <event type>` clause names the comma list (`--type merge_failed,review_rejected` shows events of either type).
- Completion is untouched: `src/cli/completion.ts` keeps offering single codes, which still complete the first piece of a list.

**Tests** (in `test/cli-logs-filtering.test.ts`, beside `test("logs --type prints only events of exactly that type, where --grep substrings")`, reusing its event-seeding helpers):
- `logs --type merge_failed,review_rejected -n 50` prints both types' rows in log order and omits other types; ` merge_failed , review_rejected ` (spaces around the pieces) behaves the same.
- `--since 1h --type a,b` filters the window to both types, and `--count --type a,b` tallies only those two types.
- `--type merge_faild,review_rejected` matching nothing prints `no events matching "merge_faild,review_rejected"` plus the did-you-mean hint naming `merge_failed`; `--type merge_failed,review_rejected` with neither present prints the prose with no hint.
- `--type ,` fails with `TYPE_VALUE_ERROR`'s wording and a non-zero exit.
- The existing single-type `--type` tests pass unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater logs --type a,b` shows exactly the events whose canonical type is `a` or `b`, in the `-n`, `--since`, `-f`, `--count` and `--json` views, and composes with `--grep` (type-list AND text) as the single type does; an older event name in the list matches its current one.
- A single `--type <t>` produces output identical to today's, including the empty-match prose and its hint (the existing single-type tests pass untouched).
- An empty-match list names the value as typed and hints only for the first invalid piece; a list with no non-empty piece fails with `TYPE_VALUE_ERROR`.
- `tumwater help logs` and docs/cli.md document the comma list; `npm test` passes.

**Goal.** The status table renderer, the status payload builder and the team alerts use role and runner names, and `AlertLoop` becomes `AlertRole`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):

Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.

Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. ### Check-wait observability, part 1/2: Record check-permit waits as `check_wait` events (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the in-flight TUI-editor entries (model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, role model Ctrl+X, instances Ctrl+G) and the planned claude-reserve entry touch src/ui/tui and src/config, which this part does not; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/build and src/events only in far-behind parts; touches src/concurrency/check-permit.ts src/build/build-check-events.ts src/build/build-check-scoped.ts src/events/events.ts src/events/event-labels.ts src/events/event-format.ts docs/how-it-works.md test/check-permit.test.ts test/build-check-events.test.ts test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Two of the three process-wide concurrency waits are observable: a pooled worktree lease that waits 30 s or more logs a `slot_wait` event (`src/git/worktree-pool.ts`'s `logSlotWait`, `SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_MS`), and a role tick's semaphore admission that waits 30 s or more logs a `provider_wait` event (`src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts`, `PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS`); `tumwater doctor`'s `workspaces` and `provider contention` rows sum them (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`'s `checkWorktreePool`, `checkProviderContention`). The check permit — the third process-wide bound, `maxConcurrentChecks` (`src/concurrency/check-permit.ts`'s `withCheckPermit`, default 2) — records nothing. A scoped check parked behind a full permit only flips the merge cell's stage to `check-wait` (`src/merge/merge-slot.ts`'s `checkWaitStage`, `MergeStage`), a transient per-role record with no event, so `tumwater logs`, `tumwater history` and `tumwater report` cannot show a check wait and no consumer can act on one. `src/merge/merge-drain.ts` documents a real 2.5-minute wait on 2026-10-12. This part records the wait as a `check_wait` event, the signal the follow-up part 2/2 sums and names `maxConcurrentChecks` for; it changes no gate and no merge decision.

**Approach.**
- **src/concurrency/check-permit.ts** — add an optional `waited?(waitedMs: number): void` to `PermitWaitHooks`, documented as called once with how long the wait took, after `granted()`, only when the permit was not free. In `withCheckPermit`'s existing `if (!checkPermits.tryAcquire())` branch, capture `const waitStarted = Date.now()` immediately before `hooks?.waiting()`, and after `await checkPermits.acquire(tier)` call `hooks?.granted(); hooks?.waited?.(Date.now() - waitStarted);`. The free-permit path calls neither. The `waited` member is optional, so `merge-slot.ts`'s `waitStageHooks`/`checkWaitStage`/`resolveWaitStage`/`providerWaitStage` (which set only `waiting`/`granted`) keep type-checking unchanged.
- **src/build/build-check-events.ts** — add `export const CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS = 30_000;`, documented like `SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_MS`/`PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS` as the threshold a wait must reach to be worth an event, and add `export function logCheckWaitEvent(root: string, role: string, scope: BuildCheckScope, waitedMs: number): void` that returns without logging when `waitedMs < CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS` and otherwise calls `logEventBestEffort(root, { source: role, type: "check_wait", role, scope, waitedMs })`. This is the one home of the event's shape, beside `buildCheckEvent`, so the feed's second check event cannot drift a field. Add the runtime import of `logEventBestEffort` from `../events/events.js` (events.js imports nothing from build/, so no cycle).
- **src/build/build-check-scoped.ts** — in `runScopedBuildCheck`, replace the pass-through `permitWait` argument to `withCheckPermit` with a wrapper hooks object: `waiting` and `granted` forward to `permitWait?.waiting?.()`/`permitWait?.granted?.()`, and `waited: (waitedMs) => logCheckWaitEvent(root, role, scope, waitedMs)`. `runScopedBuildCheck`'s single `role` parameter is the event's `role`/`source` — for a `batch` scope the caller already passes `roles[0]` as `role` (`src/merge/merge-stack.ts`), exactly as the `build_check` event's `source` is `roles[0]` today, so the event fires once per check, not once per batched role. `main-baseline.ts`'s direct `withCheckPermit` call (no hooks) does not log — the signal is scoped to the gate/merge/batch checks a merge pipeline runs, which is where `maxConcurrentChecks` contention matters.
- **src/events/events.ts** — add `| "check_wait" // a scoped check (gate, merge, or batch) waited CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS or more for a process-wide check permit (build-check-events.ts's logCheckWaitEvent); carries source/role, scope and waitedMs — the signal to raise maxConcurrentChecks` to the event-type union, beside `slot_wait`/`provider_wait`.
- **src/events/event-labels.ts** — add `check_wait: "waited for a check slot",` to `EVENT_TYPE_LABELS` beside `slot_wait`/`provider_wait`; the `Record<HarnessEvent["type"], string>` type already makes the compiler demand it.
- **src/events/event-format.ts** — add a `case "check_wait":` beside the `slot_wait`/`provider_wait` cases, returning a routine-with-explanation line in the same style: the wait (`shortSpanPhrase(finiteNumber(e.waitedMs, 0))`), the role (`textOr(e.role)`), and the scope.
- **docs/how-it-works.md** — extend the `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet (the one that ends "... the rest queue, and merges go first.") to say that a scoped check whose permit wait reaches 30 s logs a `check_wait` event (role, scope, waitedMs).

**Tests.**
- **test/check-permit.test.ts** — extend the existing "withCheckPermit calls its wait hooks only when the permit is not free" test (or add beside it): with a free permit, a hooks object recording `waited` is never called; with a held permit, after release `waited` was called exactly once with a number `>= 0` and after `granted` in the call order. Keep the file's "every test lets its work finish" discipline (a leaked permit parks every later acquire).
- **test/build-check-events.test.ts** — new tests for `logCheckWaitEvent`: with a temp repo root, a call at `CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS - 1` writes no event and a call at `CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS` writes exactly one `check_wait` whose fields are `source` = role, `role`, `scope`, `waitedMs`, read back with `readEvents`.
- **test/event-format.test.ts** — a `check_wait` event with `role`, `scope`, `waitedMs` renders a line naming the wait and the role (mirror the existing `slot_wait`/`provider_wait` cases).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A scoped check (gate, merge, or batch) whose permit wait reaches `CHECK_WAIT_EVENT_MS` logs one `check_wait` event carrying its role, scope and `waitedMs`; a wait below the threshold logs nothing; a free permit logs nothing.
- One `check_wait` fires per scoped check, including a `batch` check over several roles (`runScopedBuildCheck`'s single `role` argument), never one per batched role.
- `main-baseline.ts`'s direct `withCheckPermit` call, which passes no hooks, logs no `check_wait`.
- `withCheckPermit` calls its `waited` hook once, after `granted`, only on a real wait; existing `PermitWaitHooks` implementations that omit `waited` still type-check and behave unchanged.
- `EVENT_TYPE_LABELS` and `eventTypeLabel("check_wait")` resolve, and the event-format line names the wait and role; `npm test` passes.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's claude subscription-window reserve (`claudeWindowReserve`) with Ctrl+Y, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Claude window reserve (JSON)` field and `tumwater config set claudeWindowReserve` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the in-flight TUI editors (model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, role model Ctrl+X, instances Ctrl+G) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; the dashboard half touches only src/config/config-editable-keys.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts and test/gui-client-settings.test.ts, which no eligible Planned entry edits; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-claude-reserve.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts src/config/config-editable-keys.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-claude-reserve.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts test/gui-client-settings.test.ts — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The team's claude subscription-window reserve — the top-level `claudeWindowReserve` (`Record<string, number>`, `src/config/config-schema.ts`), mapping a window type to the fraction at or past which the team counts the claude.ai window used up until it resets and moves the subscription Claude jobs down the fallback chain (`src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts`'s reserve handling, `src/gates/budget-gates.ts`, the `claude_window_reserved` event) — is documented in docs/config.md and docs/backends.md (which recommends `{ "seven_day": 0.8 }` to leave a fifth of the week for you), validated by `validateConfig`'s block in src/config/config-validation.ts (`claudeWindowReserve must be an object mapping window types to fractions`, `claudeWindowReserve.<type> must be a fraction above 0 and at most 1`), and writable through `tumwater config set claudeWindowReserve`, but neither visual surface edits it: it is absent from `EDITABLE_CONFIG_KEYS` (`src/config/config-editable-keys.ts`) and the dashboard's `SETTINGS_KEYS` (`src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`), and `grep -rn claudeWindowReserve src/ui/tui` finds no editor. Every other operator knob the dashboard Settings and TUI already edit — the run-concurrency caps, quiet hours, notify hook and agent backends — has both surfaces, so add the reserve beside them. `Ctrl+Y` is free on the Activity view: `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` routes Ctrl+Y to the History pane's summary toggle (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`, `promptLineFree`-guarded), and the prompt-line editors run before every pane arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`), so the new arm consumes Ctrl+Y only on `ctx.view === 0` and returns false everywhere else. `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` compares only the set of handled Ctrl letters to docs/cli.md's table, and Ctrl+Y is already documented (the History summary row), so no new letter is needed — only that row's text gains the Activity meaning.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-claude-reserve.ts** (new) — `createClaudeReserveEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, a thin call to `createTeamConfigKeyEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts`) like `createProviderCapsEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts`), whose `TeamConfigKeySpec.mode` union gains `"claudeReserve"`: `mode: "claudeReserve"`, `openCtrl: "y"`, `configKey: "claudeWindowReserve"`, a `prefill` reading `loadConfigSafe(s.root).config?.claudeWindowReserve` (`JSON.stringify(existing)` when set, `""` when unset), the open flash `edit the team's claude subscription-window reserve (claudeWindowReserve, a JSON object like {"seven_day":0.8}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`, and the cleared/set flashes `claude window reserve cleared` / `claude window reserve set to <text>`. The factory owns the mode flag, saved-draft pair, Activity-only scope pin, held-registry guard, and the Enter arm (empty line `unsetConfigKey`, otherwise `setConfigKey`; `validateConfig`'s block owns the value's truth; an `{ok:false}` flashes and stays open). Only `loadConfigSafe` is imported here.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-pane-ctx.ts** — add `claudeReserveMode: boolean` to `TuiPaneEditorState` and `!es.claudeReserveMode` to `promptLineFree`, so the Activity pane's Ctrl+G and Ctrl+O cycles do not fire while the editor holds the prompt line. Also `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-config.ts` (the `mode` union).
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `claudeReserve: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface (documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+Y claude-reserve editor) and initialize it `false`; add `"claudeReserve"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. Add the sibling early clause `if (h.claudeReserve && entering !== "claudeReserve") return session.busyFlash("claude reserve");`, and add an `entering === "claudeReserve"` bottom clause that returns the busy flash for whichever of the accumulated flags is set (`h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions`/`h.providerCaps`/`h.concurrency`/`h.slots`/`h.notify`/`h.backends`), with the same nested-ternary wording the latest sibling (`entering === "backends"`) uses; the clause is required because the guard body has no generic `h.budget && entering !== "budget"` early clause.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's model (`model`) with Ctrl+A, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Model` field and `tumwater config set model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the plan-rerun entry edits src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling, src/orchestrator and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, the queue-order entry src/roles and src/prompt, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; the in-flight run-cap (Ctrl+N), worktree-slots (Ctrl+W) and provider-caps (Ctrl+P) entries — plus the landed quiet-hours (Ctrl+S) editor — also edit src/ui/tui and share src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx and tui-frame.ts with this one — each adds one editor module, one held flag, one state field and one frame branch — and share docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table as different rows, a rebase either way; when those concurrency entries have landed, this plan's `onArrow` no-editor condition and its new `heldEditorFlash` clause include their `concurrency`/`slots`/`providerCaps` flags, as noted below; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-model.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-model.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts)

**Goal.** The team's model — the top-level `model` key, a selector string or a map by tier (`small`/`default`/`strong`), validated by `checkModelTripleField` (`src/config/config-field-checks.ts`) and the `checkSelectorHalves`/per-entry `checkSelectorValue` block in `validateConfig` (`src/config/config-validation.ts`; the scalar shape message is `model must be a model id or a map by tier (small, default, strong)`, verified at `config-field-checks.ts`) — is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Model`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose field renders an object as compact JSON through `settingsFieldValue`) and `tumwater config set model '{"strong":"..."}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: no `tui-editor-model.ts` exists and no TUI editor writes the top-level `model` (the `model` occurrences under `src/ui/tui` are the History pane's per-run model cell in `tui-history.ts` and "model-written text" comments in `tui-frame.ts`/`tui.tsx`). The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`) and its quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`, `createQuietEditor`), and its run cap, worktree slots and provider caps once the in-flight Ctrl+N/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+P entries land. `model` is the most fundamental of the dashboard Settings rows still without a TUI twin (the others are `provider`, `fallback`, `notify` and `backends`), so add it beside the rest. `Ctrl+A` is free on the Activity view: the answer editor's `Ctrl+A` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-answer.ts`) is guarded to a selected open backlog question, the pause editor's per-loop abort `Ctrl+A` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`, guarded by `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length`) is a role's Transcript, and `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`), so the new arm must enter only on `ctx.view === 0` and return false everywhere else. `Ctrl+M` is deliberately not used: ink's key bridge maps `key.return` before `key.ctrl` (`src/ui/tui/tui-keymap.ts`), so Ctrl+M arrives as the `return` key and cannot be told from Enter.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-model.ts** (new) — `createModelEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring the team half of `createQuietEditor` (src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts) but with no role scope: a private `modelMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitModelMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.model` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "a"`: enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (a role's Transcript keeps `Ctrl+A` for abort, Backlog keeps it for answer), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("model")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `modelMode` and `session.held.model`, pre-fill from one fresh `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.model` — a string as-is, an object as `JSON.stringify(...)`, `""` when unset — place the cursor at the end, and flash `edit the team's model (model, a model id or a JSON map by tier like {"strong":"..."}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "model")` and, on `ok`, flashes `team model cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "model", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `team model set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a bare `huggingface/...` becomes the literal selector string, while `{"strong":"..."}` becomes the map), and `validateConfig` owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitModelMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitModelMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the quiet and budget editors do; import no `baseRoleOf` (the team key owns no role).
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `model: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+A team-model editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"model"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. Extend the guard body with the two clauses the existing per-editor entries use: first, beside `h.quiet && entering !== "quiet"`, add `if (h.model && entering !== "model") return session.busyFlash("model edit");`, which covers entering any other editor while the model editor holds the line; second, beside the existing `entering === "instructions"` clause, add an `entering === "model"` clause that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions` is set (naming that editor's subject, the same nested-ternary wording those clauses use). The second clause is required, not redundant: the guard body has no generic `h.budget && entering !== "budget"` early clause, so entering a value the bottom clauses do not list while the budget editor holds the shared line would otherwise let the new editor overwrite it. If the in-flight Ctrl+N/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+P concurrency entries have landed, add their `concurrency`/`slots`/`providerCaps` flags to this plan's `entering === "model"` subject list exactly as they extend each other's, and add their flags to this plan's `onArrow` list below.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `modelMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createModelEditor` and add `createModelEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createBudgetEditor(session)`; return `modelMode: session.held.model` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.model` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.budget`), adding `!session.held.concurrency`/`!session.held.slots`/`!session.held.providerCaps` there too if those in-flight entries have landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `modelMode: s.modelMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `modelMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "model", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.modelMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.modelMode) keys = [["Enter", "save the model"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+A", "model"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table gains a `| Ctrl+A | Activity | edit the team's model (`model`, a model id or a JSON map by tier like `{"strong":"..."}`; empty clears it) |` row, one row per (key, view), distinct from the Transcript `Ctrl+A` (abort an in-flight run) and Backlog `Ctrl+A` (answer the selected question) inside the existing `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+V` and backlog rows.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-model.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+A opens with the footer `model ›` and the line pre-filled from `tumwater.json`'s `model` (the bare string when it is a string, compact JSON when it is a map, empty when unset); Enter on a selector string writes that string to `tumwater.json` and flashes `team model set to <text>`; Enter on a JSON tier map writes the object; Enter on the number `42` flashes the validator's `model must be a model id or a map by tier (small, default, strong)` message, leaves the editor open with the text kept and the file byte-identical; Enter on an empty line unsets the key (it disappears from the file) and flashes `team model cleared`, leaving the file bytes unchanged when it was already absent; Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with another editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+A flashes the busy message and leaves it open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+A on Activity opens the model editor (`session.held.model`, and `session.held.budget` stays false); on a role's Transcript, Ctrl+A still aborts that role's run (the existing per-loop control, unaffected because the new arm returns false off view 0); and the existing "Ctrl+E is inert in the prompt-line modes and off the report views only moves the label" test stays green unchanged (this plan binds Ctrl+A, not Ctrl+E).
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, modelMode: true })` reading `model ›` and the hint branch's `save the model`; and the Activity hint line naming `Ctrl+A model`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+A opens the editor; the footer reads `model › `, the line pre-fills the file's `model` (a bare string as-is, a map as compact JSON, empty when unset) and the open flash names `model`, the model-id-or-tier-map shape and the empty-clears rule. On a role's Transcript, Ctrl+A still aborts the in-flight run; on Backlog with a question selected, Ctrl+A still opens the answer editor.

- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line, and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, modelMode: true })` reads `model › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s model branch names `save the model`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+A model`.
- `test/tui-keys.test.ts`'s existing Ctrl+E report-window test is unchanged and still passes (this plan does not bind Ctrl+E).

### Plain terms code runner, part 4/14: Rename the status model's role phase and rank (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/status-model.ts + src/ui/tone.ts + src/ui/badges.ts + test/status-model.test.ts + test/badges.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The shared display model names what it describes, a role's row: `rolePhase`, `roleRank`, `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortRolesByState`, `roleRowCells` and `roleWakeMarker`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/ui/status-model.ts: `loopPhase` → `rolePhase`, `loopRank` → `roleRank`, `LOOP_RANK_RULES` → `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortLoopsByState` → `sortRolesByState`, `LoopSortRow` → `RoleSortRow`, `loopRowCells` → `roleRowCells`. Each export used outside this part keeps an alias: `loopPhase` is named in src/merge/, src/runner/, src/tick/, src/ui/ and src/ui/gui/; `LOOP_RANK_RULES` is interpolated by src/ui/gui/gui-client-model.ts.
- src/ui/badges.ts: `loopWakeMarker` → `roleWakeMarker` (alias; src/ui/status-render.ts uses it). src/ui/tone.ts: migrate its `loopRank` import and comments.
- test/status-model.test.ts (about 130 `loopPhase` calls and 69 `freshLoopState` calls) and test/badges.test.ts: migrate to the new names, including `freshRunnerState`, and convert comments and test titles.
- The browser twin of the rank (`loopRank` inside gui-client-model.ts's template) is part 7/14's; only the server export's name changes here.

**Files touched.** src/ui/status-model.ts, src/ui/tone.ts, src/ui/badges.ts, test/status-model.test.ts, test/badges.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `rolePhase`, `roleRank`, `ROLE_RANK_RULES`, `sortRolesByState`, `roleRowCells` and `roleWakeMarker` are the declared names; old names exist only as deprecated aliases, and only while another file still uses them.
- `grep -nE '[Ll]oop[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Loop|LOOP_|\bloops?\b'` over this part's five files lists only aliases and kept senses.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

**Note.** Also migrated this part's use of part 2/14's earlier rename inside status-model.ts: its nine `LoopState` type references became `RunnerState` (the deprecated `LoopState` alias still has live users in src/runner, e.g. `freshlyWoken(s: LoopState)`). ### The TUI's Transcript view edits the viewed role's model override (`roles.<base>.model`) with Ctrl+X, the terminal twin of `tumwater role <id> --model` and the dashboard role drawer's Model overrides editor (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 3/14 moves src/runner and its tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight TUI editors (run cap Ctrl+N, worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, notify Ctrl+E, backends Ctrl+X) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-role-model.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A role's model override (`roles.<base>.model`, resolved per tier by `configForRole` in `src/config/config-views.ts` and printed by `tumwater role <id>` as its `Model:` line, `src/roles/role-render.ts`) is writable from two surfaces: the CLI (`tumwater role <id> --model <id>` / `--clear-model`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`) and the dashboard role drawer's Model overrides editor (`POST /api/role-model` → `handleRoleModel`, `src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts`), both through `setRoleModelFields(root, base, { model })` (`src/config/config-write.ts`), whose `checkModelTripleField` (shape `"tier-name"`, `src/config/config-field-checks.ts`) accepts a non-empty model id or a bare tier name (`small`/`default`/`strong`) and owns the `roles.<id>.model …` rejection messages. The TUI cannot: no `tui-editor-role-model.ts` exists and `grep -rn model src/ui/tui` finds no per-role write (the `model` hits are the History pane's per-run cell and the team-wide editors). The Transcript view already edits the sibling per-role holds — daily cap Ctrl+B, quiet hours Ctrl+O, min run interval Ctrl+S, standing instructions Ctrl+L, notes Ctrl+E, counters Ctrl+V — so add the last per-role override beside them. `Ctrl+X` is free on the Transcript view: the transcript pane consumes it only in notes mode (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-transcript.ts`'s `noteMode` arm, which clears notes), the backlog cancel and Health retire arms are guarded to their own views, and the editors run before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`), so the new arm enters only when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length && !ctx.noteMode` and returns false everywhere else. (`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+L`/`Ctrl+E`/`Ctrl+X` are the in-flight team editors' keys on Activity; the view guards keep them disjoint.)

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-role-model.ts** (new) — `createRoleModelEditor(session: TuiEditorSession): TuiEditorModule`, mirroring `createIntervalEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-interval.ts`): a private `roleModelMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitRoleModelMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.roleModel` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "x"`. Enter only when `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length && !ctx.noteMode` (notes mode keeps Ctrl+X for clear-notes; every other view falls through unchanged), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("roleModel")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, pin `lockedRole = ctx.roleIds[ctx.view - 1]!` so a roster shift cannot redirect the write, set `roleModelMode` and `session.held.roleModel`, pre-fill from `rawRoleField(session.root, baseRoleOf(lockedRole), "model")` (a string as-is, `""` when unset — the FILE's own override, so clearing a role that only has the catalog's tier never looks like an operator override), place the cursor at the end, and flash `edit ${lockedRole}'s model override (a model id or tier name like strong; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. Success and cancel both `exitRoleModelMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitRoleModelMode }`. Import `setRoleModelFields` from `../../config/config-write.js`, `baseRoleOf` from `../../roles/runner-ids.js`, and `rawRoleField` from `../../roles/role-view.js` — the shared write the CLI's `--model` and the dashboard's `handleRoleModel` use, not a hand-rolled `setConfigKey`.
