### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's per-provider concurrency caps (`maxConcurrentPerProvider`) with Ctrl+P, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Provider concurrency caps (JSON)` field and `tumwater config set maxConcurrentPerProvider` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the plan-rerun entry edits src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling, src/orchestrator and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, the queue-order entry src/roles and src/prompt, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; the in-flight quiet-hours (Ctrl+S), run-cap (Ctrl+N) and worktree-slots (Ctrl+W) entries also edit src/ui/tui and share src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx and tui-frame.ts with this one — each adds one editor module, one held flag, one state field and one frame branch — and share docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table as different rows, a rebase either way; when the Ctrl+N entry has landed, this plan's `onArrow` clause and `heldEditorFlash` union/guard include its `concurrency` flag, and likewise the slots entry's `slots` flag, as noted below; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-provider-caps.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts, done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The team's per-provider run caps `maxConcurrentPerProvider` (an optional JSON object mapping a provider key to a positive integer, validated by `checkProviderConcurrencyCap` (`src/config/config-keys.ts`) and the map block in `validateConfig` (`src/config/config-validation.ts`)) is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Provider concurrency caps (JSON)`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose field renders an object as compact JSON) and `tumwater config set maxConcurrentPerProvider '{"key":2}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: `grep -rn maxConcurrentPerProvider src/ui/tui` finds nothing. `tumwater doctor`'s `checkProviderContention` (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) names the exact cap to raise. The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`) and, once the in-flight entries land, its run cap (`Ctrl+N`), worktree slots (`Ctrl+W`) and quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`). Add the provider caps beside them, completing the run-concurrency knob set the doctor points at. `Ctrl+P` is free on Activity: the only `Ctrl+P` arm today is the shared pause editor's pause key, guarded by `pauseEditRole !== null` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`), and `pauseEditRole` is null on Activity (the team pause is `Ctrl+F`), so the key falls through there while a role's Transcript keeps it.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts** (new) — `createProviderCapsEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createBudgetEditor`/`createQuietEditor`: a private `providerCapsMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitProviderCapsMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.providerCaps` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "p"`: enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (the team scope; a role's Transcript keeps its pause/resume key), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("providerCaps")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft(...)`, set `providerCapsMode` and `session.held.providerCaps`, pre-fill `session.input` with `JSON.stringify(loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.maxConcurrentPerProvider)` when that map is defined and `""` when it is not, place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's provider concurrency caps (maxConcurrentPerProvider, a JSON object like {"anthropic":2}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "maxConcurrentPerProvider")` and, on `ok`, flashes `provider concurrency caps cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "maxConcurrentPerProvider", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `provider concurrency caps set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so `{"anthropic":2}` becomes the object, while `anthropic` falls back to the literal string) and `validateConfig` (whose map message is `maxConcurrentPerProvider must be an object mapping provider names to concurrency caps`) owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitProviderCapsMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitProviderCapsMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and quiet editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `providerCaps: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+P provider-caps editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"providerCaps"` to the `heldEditorFlash(entering: ...)` union; extend the guard body with `if (h.providerCaps && entering !== "providerCaps") return session.busyFlash("provider caps");` — that holds any other editor out while this one holds the line — and, because `budget` is only excluded through the bottom `entering === "..."` clauses (the guard body has no generic `h.budget && entering !== "budget"` early clause), also add an `entering === "providerCaps"` clause that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use). The bottom clause is required, not redundant: without it, Ctrl+P while the budget editor holds the shared line would not flash busy and would open over it. If the in-flight Ctrl+N run-cap entry has landed, prefix its `concurrency` flag (and, when landed, the Ctrl+W slots entry's `slots` flag) to this clause's subject list the same way, since those editors add flags to the same `TuiHeld`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `providerCapsMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createProviderCapsEditor` and add `createProviderCapsEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createBudgetEditor(session)`; return `providerCapsMode: session.held.providerCaps` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.providerCaps` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.budget`), adding `!session.held.concurrency`/`!session.held.slots` there too if those in-flight entries have landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `providerCapsMode: s.providerCapsMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `providerCapsMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "provider caps", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.providerCapsMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.providerCapsMode) keys = [["Enter", "save provider caps"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+P", "provider caps"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table gains a `| Ctrl+P | Activity | edit the team's per-provider concurrency caps (`maxConcurrentPerProvider`, a JSON object like `{"anthropic":2}`; empty clears it) |` row, one row per (key, view), distinct from the Transcript `Ctrl+P` inside the `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+V` row.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-provider-caps.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+P opens with the footer `provider caps ›` and the line empty when `tumwater.json` leaves the key unset, and pre-filled with compact JSON when it holds `maxConcurrentPerProvider`; Enter on valid JSON writes the object to `tumwater.json` and flashes `provider concurrency caps set to <text>`; Enter on a non-object (`anthropic`) or a cap of `0` flashes the validator's `maxConcurrentPerProvider …` message, leaves the editor open with the text kept and the file byte-identical; Enter on an empty line removes the key and flashes the cleared wording; Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with another editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+P flashes the busy message and leaves it open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+P on Activity opens the provider-caps editor (`session.held.providerCaps`), while Ctrl+P on a role's Transcript still opens the pause editor (`session.held.pauseEditRole`), so the new arm does not swallow the pause key.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, providerCapsMode: true })` reading `provider caps ›` and the hint branch's `save provider caps`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+P opens the editor; the footer reads `provider caps › `, the line pre-fills compact JSON from a set `maxConcurrentPerProvider` (empty when unset) and the open flash names `maxConcurrentPerProvider`, the JSON-object shape and the empty-clears rule. On a role's Transcript, Ctrl+P still opens the pause editor.
- Enter with a JSON object writes `maxConcurrentPerProvider` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `provider concurrency caps set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `provider concurrency caps cleared`; a non-object or a non-positive-integer cap flashes the validator's `maxConcurrentPerProvider …` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line, and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, providerCapsMode: true })` reads `provider caps › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s provider-caps branch names `save provider caps`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+P provider caps`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+P | Activity` row naming the per-provider caps and `maxConcurrentPerProvider`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm test` passes.

### The plan loop reruns after a productive plan tick while PLANS.md still has planning room (planned 2026-10-19 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the git-author entry edits src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts, src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts and src/operator/revert.ts, the dashboard-settings entry src/config/config-editable-keys.ts and src/ui/gui, the TUI-instructions entry src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md, and the backlog-grep entry src/backlog, src/cli and docs/cli.md, none of which is src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts or docs/config.md; touches src/brief/brief.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/scheduling/scheduling.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts plans/work-ratio.md docs/config.md test/brief.test.ts test/scheduling.test.ts test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts test/main-red.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The plan loop's tight loop is keyed on whether the product still needs plans, not on the brief's placeholder status. Today the plan role schedules a zero min gap only while `briefStatusIncomplete(root)` is true — `scheduleConfigForRole`'s `descriptionIncomplete` flag, read in `orchestrator-scheduling.ts` and `runner-run.ts`. The readme role replaces the placeholder early, so the zero gap turns off while the project is still being planned: the plan role drops to its 3600 s slow clock (or bootstrap's 20 s) even right after a productive run. The user's rule: "If the product is not yet finished, and the plan role produced a change last time it ran, the plan loop should run again." The plan role's own machine signal that it still has planning work is `planBacklogFull` (`src/scheduling/claims.ts`): PLANS.md's `## Planned` holds at least `planBacklogTarget` eligible plans and no needs-review/needs-replan mark. While it is false there is planning room, so a productive (`changed`/`queued`) plan tick should rerun on the next poll (zero gap) and an unproductive (`no_change`) tick should drop to the idle backoff; once the backlog reaches target, `planDeferral` already holds the plan tick (`plans-full`) until work frees a slot. This subsumes both current triggers — a fresh project's empty backlog is not full — so `bootstrapActive` and `briefStatusIncomplete` no longer need to reach `scheduleConfigForRole`.

**Approach.**
- **src/config/config-views.ts** — change `scheduleConfigForRole(config, role, bootstrapActive, descriptionIncomplete = false)` to `scheduleConfigForRole(config, role, planBacklogOpen = false)`: when `planBacklogOpen && baseRoleOf(role) === "plan"`, return `{ ...configForRole(config, role), minRunIntervalSeconds: 0 }`; every other role and the closed case return `configForRole(config, role)`. Rewrite the doc comment to state the rule — the plan role's zero gap is on while PLANS.md still has planning room (below `planBacklogTarget`, or holding a marked plan) — replacing the bootstrap and placeholder wording.
- **src/scheduling/scheduling.ts** — in `EligibilityOptions`, delete `bootstrapActive` and `descriptionIncomplete` and add `planBacklogOpen?: boolean` with the new doc comment; in `isEligible`'s `minGapSeconds`, call `scheduleConfigForRole(runner.config, runner.role, opts.planBacklogOpen === true)` and update the comment above it.
- **src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts** — delete the `briefStatusIncomplete` import and the `const descriptionIncomplete = briefStatusIncomplete(root);` read; at the `isEligible` call pass `{ once: once.active, planBacklogOpen: !planBacklogFull }` (`planBacklogFull` is already destructured from `ctx`). Also remove the now write-only `bootstrapActive` from `SchedulingPassCtx`, break it out of `orchestrator.ts`'s two poll context objects, delete it from `gate-polls.ts` (no reader left after the above), and drop it from the test ctx fixtures.
- **src/runner/runner-run.ts** (formerly src/loop/loop-tick.ts) — delete the `bootstrapStatus` and `briefStatusIncomplete` imports and their two reads; import `planBacklogFull` from `../scheduling/claims.js`; compute `const planBacklogOpen = !planBacklogFull(ctx.root, ctx.config);` and pass it as `scheduleConfigForRole(ctx.config, ctx.role, planBacklogOpen)`; update the comment.
- **src/brief/brief.ts** — delete `briefStatusIncomplete` (its only callers are the two scheduling sites above); `EMPTY_STATUS` and `managedSections` stay. Deviation: `EMPTY_STATUS` keeps as a module-private constant (the exports-unused guard, test/exports.test.ts, flags an export no other file references, and its only external consumers were `briefStatusIncomplete` and the two removed test imports), so the `export` is dropped while the constant and `managedSections` stay.
- **docs/config.md** — in the `minRunIntervalSeconds` row, replace the placeholder clause: while PLANS.md's `## Planned` still has planning room (`planBacklogFull` false) the plan role schedules with a zero gap, so a productive plan run reruns on the next poll and an unproductive one drops to the idle backoff; once the target is met the plan loop defers (`plans-full`) and this interval applies.

**Tests.**
- **test/brief.test.ts** — remove the "briefStatusIncomplete is true for the templates…" test and the now-unused `briefStatusIncomplete`/`EMPTY_STATUS` imports (line 11/13; `EMPTY_STATUS` has no other use in the file).
- **test/scheduling.test.ts** — replace "bootstrap schedules plan on the global gap…" and "a placeholder-status brief schedules plan on a zero gap…" with: `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", true).minRunIntervalSeconds === 0`, `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", false).minRunIntervalSeconds === configForRole(cfg, "plan").minRunIntervalSeconds`, and `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "feature", true)` equal to `configForRole(cfg, "feature")`; then a plan runner ticked `changed` under the two-argument zero-gap config leaves `nextRunAt - Date.now() < 1000` and `isEligible(r, afterChanged + 1, "", 0, { planBacklogOpen: true })` returns `{ run: true, reason: "scheduled" }`; a following `no_change` tick moves `nextRunAt` at least `cfg.idleBackoff.initialSeconds` into the future and, with `lastMainHead` unchanged, `isEligible(..., { planBacklogOpen: true }).run` is `false`. Keep the closed case: `isEligible` without `planBacklogOpen` holds a just-productive plan on its 3600 s clock.
- **test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts** — replace "a plan runner is admitted while the brief status is the placeholder…" with one that keeps a due-now plan runner (`runs = 1`, `lastRunEndedAt = T0`, `nextRunAt = T0`, non-empty `lastMainHead`) and, via `ctx.planBacklogFull`, asserts `pollRunnerReasons` admits it when `planBacklogFull` is false and skips it when true; drop the `EMPTY_STATUS`/`readmeTemplate` imports if no longer used elsewhere in the file. The bootstrap-held test's `ctx.bootstrapActive = true` line and the ctx builder's `bootstrapActive: false` are dropped with the field.
- **test/main-red.test.ts** — the queued-healer test's `isEligible` call drops the removed `descriptionIncomplete: false` flag (now the empty `{}`), the only edit the scheduling-option rename forces here.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", true).minRunIntervalSeconds === 0`; `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", false)` and every non-plan role equal `configForRole(...)`.
- After a `changed` plan tick under `planBacklogOpen`, a plan runner whose `lastRunEndedAt` is that tick is admitted immediately by `isEligible` with reason `"scheduled"`; after a `no_change` tick, with `lastMainHead` unchanged, it is not admitted and `nextRunAt` is the idle backoff out.
- `pollRunnerReasons` admits a due-now plan runner with `ctx.planBacklogFull` false and skips it with `ctx.planBacklogFull` true.
- `briefStatusIncomplete` is gone and no source file imports it.
- `npm test` passes.

**Files touched.** Source: src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts. Docs: docs/config.md, plans/work-ratio.md. Tests: test/brief.test.ts, test/scheduling.test.ts, test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts, test/main-red.test.ts.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team-wide quiet-hours window with Ctrl+S, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `quietHours` field and `tumwater config set quietHours` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the healer entry edits src/baseline/main-red.ts, the plan-rerun entry src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; none touches src/ui/tui. It shares src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts and the shared editor seams (tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts) and docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table with the in-flight backlog-search and Ctrl+L instructions entries, which each add one editor target/leaf and one hint token — a rebase either way; the blocked plain-terms runner/run/cleanup series renames identifiers in src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase. touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-quiet.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The per-role quiet-hours window is editable from the TUI (Ctrl+O on a role's Transcript, `createQuietEditor`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts`) and the dashboard role drawer, and the team-wide top-level `quietHours` window is editable from the dashboard Settings view (the `quietHours` row, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`) and `tumwater config set quietHours`. The TUI has no team-wide editor: `grep -n quietHours src/ui/tui/*.ts` finds only `quietHoursPerRole` in `tui-editor-quiet.ts`, and Ctrl+S is free on the Activity view (view 0) — the view that already owns the team-wide daily cap (Ctrl+B) and pause/stop (Ctrl+F/Ctrl+Q). Add the team-wide window to the existing quiet editor, so an operator can put the whole team to sleep for a nightly window without leaving the terminal.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts** — `createQuietEditor` gains a `let quietTeam = false` scope flag, cleared by `exitQuietMode`. Split the entry arms so each key toggles its own scope and neither steals the other: the Ctrl+O arm enters only `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` and, while open, exits only the per-role scope (Ctrl+O in team mode is consumed and does nothing); the new Ctrl+S arm, added after it, enters only when `ctx.view === 0` and closed, and while open exits only the team scope. Both arms keep the `session.heldEditorFlash("quiet")` busy guard, set `session.held.quiet` and `session.held.quietTeam`, save/restore the draft through `session.settleDraft`/`session.restorePromptFrom`, and open with the flash `edit the team's quiet hours (e.g. 23:00-07:00, empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The team arm pre-fills `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.quietHours ?? ""` (the per-role arm keeps `quietHoursPerRole.<base>`), and `lockedRole` stays null. The Enter arm computes `const cfgKey = quietTeam ? "quietHours" : \`quietHoursPerRole.${baseRoleOf(lockedRole!)}\`` and words the success flash `team: quiet hours set to <window>` / `team: quiet hours cleared` for the team scope, keeping the existing role wording. `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` and `validateConfig` (whose `parseQuietHours` error names `quietHours` for the top-level key) own the window's truth; an invalid window flashes and stays open.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `quietTeam: boolean` to `TuiHeld` beside `quiet`, documented as the quiet editor's scope, and initialize it `false`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `quietTeam: boolean` to `TuiEditorState`, and return `quietTeam: session.held.quietTeam` from `state()` beside `quietMode`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `quietTeam: s.quietTeam` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — both inline mode types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix` gain `quietTeam?: boolean`; `promptPrefix` returns `team quiet hours › ` when `quietMode && quietTeam` (else the existing `quiet hours › `), and `hintLine`'s quiet branch says `save team quiet hours` when `quietTeam`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys `Ctrl+S` row gains Activity with `edit the team's quiet-hours window (quietHours; an empty line clears it)`.

### Plain terms code runner, part 1/14: Move the loop modules to src/runner and their tests to runner names (done 2026-10-19 by the feature role; requires Plain terms code merge 11a/11, Plain terms code merge 11b/11, Plain terms code merge 11c/11, Plain terms code merge 11d/11, Plain terms code merge 11e/11 and Plain terms code merge 11f/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/loop/ + src/roles/loop-ids.ts + src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts + test/loop*.test.ts + test/fixtures/loop-*.ts + every importer + docs/invariants.md + DEVELOPMENT.md)

**Goal.** Mechanical. The per-instance worker's modules and their tests move to `runner` names, with every import path and path citation updated and no identifier changed, so later parts rename symbols inside files that already carry their final names.

**Approach.**
- `git mv` only (keeps history), then fix paths. No identifier, comment wording or test title changes beyond the paths themselves.
- Leave record prose alone: do not edit BUGS.md, PLANS.md, QUESTIONS.md, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS-FIXED.md or any `plans/*.md`. Their old paths are correct as written. Finished entries record files as they were, and open plans (this series' own entries included) name both sides of the moves they describe, so a find-and-replace over them turns `src/loop/` → `src/runner/` into `src/runner/` → `src/runner/`. That sweep got this part rejected five times on 2026-10-18 and -19 (bullet added 2026-10-19 by user). The pre-queue self-check no longer lists these files; a review objection asking for them to be swept is outside this part's scope, so say so in RISK.
- Source moves: `src/loop/` → `src/runner/`; inside it `loop.ts` → `runner.ts`, `loop-state.ts` → `runner-state.ts`, `loop-pi.ts` → `runner-pi.ts`, `loop-fallback.ts` → `runner-fallback.ts`, `loop-recovery.ts` → `runner-recovery.ts`, and `loop-tick.ts` → `runner-run.ts` (its final name: it holds the run pipeline phases, so Plain terms code run does not move it again); `leftover.ts`, `model-fallback.ts` and `revision.ts` keep their names. `src/roles/loop-ids.ts` → `src/roles/runner-ids.ts`. `src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts` → `src/ui/gui/gui-client-roles.ts` (it renders the Roles card).
- Test moves: every `test/loop*.test.ts` → `test/runner*.test.ts` with the same suffix (`loop.test.ts` → `runner.test.ts`, `loop-2.test.ts` → `runner-2.test.ts`, `loop-pi-retry.test.ts` → `runner-pi-retry.test.ts`, `loop-ids.test.ts` → `runner-ids.test.ts`, …); `test/gui-client-loops.test.ts` → `test/gui-client-roles.test.ts`; `test/fixtures/loop-fixtures.ts` → `test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts`; `test/fixtures/loop-pi-fixtures.ts` → `test/fixtures/runner-pi-fixtures.ts`.

The enforcement is that grep, not a hand-list: run it and clear every hit. ### New plans join the back of the `## Planned` queue, so the plan role appends instead of inserting at the top (planned 2026-10-19 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the plan-rerun entry edits src/scheduling, src/orchestrator and src/config, the git-identity entry src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog and src/operator, the backlog-grep entry src/backlog and src/cli, the TUI entries src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md, and the blocked plain-terms series src/loop/src/runner, none of which is src/roles/role-guidance.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts, test/role-guidance.test.ts or test/prompt-roles.test.ts; touches src/roles/role-guidance.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts test/role-guidance.test.ts test/prompt-roles.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Claim assignment is the first free entry in file order — `assignNext` (`src/scheduling/claims.ts`) returns `free[0]`, and `src/prompt/prompt.ts`'s index lists entries in that same order — so the order of entries under `## Planned` is the work queue. The plan role's charter says only "Write it as a short markdown section under `## Planned`" (step 5, `src/roles/role-catalog.ts`) and names no position; a new plan lands at the top of the section, ahead of every older plan already waiting, including the plan-rerun and blocked-series entries. The operator's `tumwater plan` already appends filed entries at the section's end (`appendEntryLocked`, `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`, pinned by `test/backlog-write.test.ts` "filePlan appends to ## Planned …"), so the two write paths disagree. The user's ruling: a new plan joins the back of the queue. State the rule once in a shared constant and embed it wherever a role is told to write a plan.

**Approach.**
- **src/roles/role-guidance.ts** — export `PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE`, a short paragraph in the style of `PLAN_SIZING`/`DECOMPOSITION_GUIDANCE`: append the new entry at the END of `## Planned`, after every existing entry, never at the top; file order is the queue and claim assignment takes the first free entry (`assignNext`, `src/scheduling/claims.ts`), so an entry inserted at the top jumps ahead of work already waiting. Give it a doc comment naming its consumers.
- **src/roles/role-catalog.ts** — import `PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE` and interpolate it in the plan role's step 5, right after "Write it as a short markdown section under `## Planned` in PLANS.md: goal, approach, files touched, acceptance criteria." Embed it once in the organize role's find text, after the step 1 sentence that sends an oversized split to a `## Planned` entry; the later "write it as a plan in PLANS.md under ## Planned" sentence in the same find is covered by that one paragraph.
- **src/prompt/prompt.ts** — append `${PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE}` to the director's "A feature request or substantial change: write a concrete plan for it in PLANS.md" routing bullet, so a plan the director files also lands at the back. Import it beside `PLAN_SIZING`/`DECOMPOSITION_GUIDANCE`.
- No change to `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts`: `appendEntryLocked` already writes before the section's next `## ` heading, i.e. at the end; do not touch it.

**Files touched.** Source: src/roles/role-guidance.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts. Tests: test/role-guidance.test.ts, test/prompt-roles.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE` is exported from `src/roles/role-guidance.ts`, is longer than one sentence, and its text says the new entry is appended at the end of `## Planned` / the back of the queue and that file order is the queue.
- The constant is embedded verbatim in `roleById("plan")!.find`, in `roleById("organize")!.find`, and in `buildDirectorPrompt("add a feature", "a project")`: each of those strings `.includes(PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE)`.
- `test/role-guidance.test.ts` pins those three embeddings with `assert.ok(...includes(PLAN_QUEUE_GUIDANCE))`, following the file's existing "director routing includes the shared … guidance" pattern.
- `test/prompt-roles.test.ts`'s plan-role test asserts the plan find matches the back-of-queue wording (e.g. `/at the END of `## Planned`/`).
- No other role find text sends an entry to `## Planned` without embedding the constant: `grep -n '## Planned' src/roles/role-catalog.ts` shows the guidance beside each plan-writing sentence.
- `npm test` passes.

### The TUI's Backlog pane searches the active entries with `/`, the terminal twin of the in-flight `tumwater backlog --grep <text>` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the backlog-grep entry edits src/backlog/backlog-render.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md's Check-state and Steer rows, and this reuses the already-landed `entryMatches` (`src/backlog/backlog.ts`) without editing any of them; the concurrency-settings entry edits src/config/config-editable-keys.ts and src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts, and the git-identity entry src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts and src/operator/revert.ts, none of which is src/ui/tui; the Ctrl+L instructions entry overlaps this only in the shared TUI plumbing both extend — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui-editor-search.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-pane-backlog.ts, tui-frame.ts — each adding one editor target/leaf and one hint token, a rebase either way; docs/cli.md is shared only as different rows (this edits the TUI-keys `/` and Backlog rows); the blocked plain-terms runner/run/cleanup series renames identifiers in src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-backlog.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The TUI already opens a prompt-line `/` search on the Activity and History views (`createSearchEditor`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts`): typing text and Enter filters that view, Esc cancels, and the applied pattern persists across view cycling. The Backlog pane has no such filter, so on a repo whose `PLANS.md` holds thousands of lines an operator can only step entry by entry. The in-flight CLI plan gives `tumwater backlog` and `plan|bug --list` a `--grep <text>` over the *active* entries; this adds the same active-entry text search to the TUI through the existing `/` editor, matching each entry's heading or body case-insensitively via the exported `entryMatches` (`src/backlog/backlog.ts`, the rule the finished-entry listings already use). The answered/done/fixed rows the pane shows are not part of the active backlog and are hidden while a search is applied.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts** — add pure `export function visibleBacklogIndexes(entries: ReadonlyArray<{ label: string } & BacklogEntry>, pattern: string | null): number[]`: with no pattern, every open entry's index (label `plan`, `bug` or `question`); with a pattern, only those whose `entryMatches(entry, pattern)` holds. Extend `moveEntrySelection` with an optional `visible: number[]` list (default: `0..count-1`) so up/down step within the matching indexes and wrap there, returning an unfiltered index; a stale selection outside `visible` restarts at the first (down) or last (up) match, and an empty list returns null. Keep the existing two-argument callers/tests valid.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts** — own `let backlogGrep: string | null = null`; expose `grep()` and `applySearch(pattern)`, which sets `backlogGrep`, clears `selectedEntry`/`entryScroll` so the next frame starts in list mode, and leaves the pattern applied across view cycles (like `historyGrep`). The up/down arrow arm reads `session.flat()` plus `backlogGrep` through `visibleBacklogIndexes` and steps with `moveEntrySelection`. `state()` returns `backlogGrep` beside the existing fields. **Write arms are unchanged**: `selectedEntry` stays an index into the unfiltered flat list, so Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+R / Ctrl+E / Ctrl+A keep their existing position math and act on the entry the filter shows.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts** — merge the pane's `backlogGrep` into `state()`, add it to `editorCtx()`, and expose `applyBacklogSearch: backlog.applySearch` beside `applyHistorySearch`/`applyActivitySearch`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts** — add `backlogGrep: string | null` to `TuiEditorCtx` (the pre-fill source and the search target guard).
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts** — add `"backlog"` to the `searchFor` union and `ctx.view === ctx.roleIds.length + 1` to the `/` open guard; pre-fill `ctx.backlogGrep`; flash `search backlog: Enter to filter, Esc to cancel`; the Enter branch sets `applyBacklogSearch(pattern === "" ? null : pattern)` and flashes `search: "<pattern>"` / `search cleared`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** / **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add the `applyBacklogSearch(pattern: string | null): void` leaf/dep and pass it through, exactly as `applyHistorySearch` is today.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts** — the `pane.kind === "backlog"` render branch keeps `const flat = browsableBacklogEntries(root)` and derives `const shown = grep === null ? flat : flat.filter((e) => (e.label === "plan" || e.label === "bug" || e.label === "question") && entryMatches(e, grep))`; list mode builds `planListLines`/`listed` from `shown`, prepends a `search: "<grep>"` line, omits the answered/done/fixed sections, and renders `(no entries match "<grep>")` when nothing matches; entry mode still opens `flat[sel]`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — the Backlog hint-key list (the `view.kind === "backlog"` branch) gains `["/", "search entries"]`, so the hint names the key the way Activity and History already do.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI keys table's `/` row gains Backlog ("filter the active entries by heading or body"), and the Backlog row names `/`.

**Files touched.** Source: src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane-backlog.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-ctx.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts. Docs: docs/cli.md. Tests: test/tui-backlog.test.ts, test/tui-keys.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `visibleBacklogIndexes(entries, pattern)` returns every open entry's index with `pattern: null` and only the heading-or-body matches (case-insensitively, using `entryMatches`) otherwise; it never returns an answered/done/fixed index.
- `moveEntrySelection` with a `visible` list steps to the next/previous matching index and wraps at that list's ends, returns the unfiltered index, and returns null for an empty list.
- On the Backlog view with an empty prompt line, `/` opens the search editor; Enter with text filters the list to matching open entries under a `search: "<pattern>"` header with the answered/done/fixed sections hidden; Enter with an empty line clears the search and restores the full list; Esc leaves the applied pattern unchanged.
- Up/down while a search is active open only matching entries, and Ctrl+X on a matching entry that is not first in its section cancels that entry (the position it reports matches the entry shown), because the selection is still an index into the unfiltered list.
- Leaving the Backlog view with Ctrl+T and returning keeps the applied search, and `/` reopens it pre-filled; a pattern with no match shows `(no entries match "<pattern>")`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI keys table names `/` for Activity, History and Backlog, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm run test` passes.

### A verified-red main queues a bugfix heal run, so the healer ticks on the next poll instead of waiting out its own clock (planned 2026-10-19 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the backlog-grep and Ctrl+L entries edit src/ui/tui, the concurrency-settings entry src/config and src/ui/gui, the git-identity entry src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog and src/operator, the plan-rerun entry src/scheduling, none of which is src/baseline/main-red.ts; the blocked plain-terms runner series reaches src/baseline/main-red.ts and test/main-red.test.ts only in far-behind parts (runner 12/14–13/14, run 5/20), so implement under whichever identifier names are on main; touches src/baseline/main-red.ts test/main-red.test.ts docs/how-it-works.md) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** On a red main the only repairer is `bugfix` — `mainRedGate` (`src/baseline/main-red.ts`) exempts it, and `bugfixMainRedNote` hands its tick the failing check when it runs. But red discovery by any other path (a blocked role's `mainRedGate`, the review gate's `mainTipVerdict`) only logs the team-wide `main_red_hold` warning and blocks/keeps pins; it schedules nothing. Bugfix is a work role, but with no open bugs it defers like a maintenance role, so a red main can sit unrepaired until bugfix's own interval or a coincidental wake brings it in. The user wants a verified red main to get a heal run promptly. Add the missing handoff: the first time a red SHA is verified by a path that is not bugfix's own tick, enqueue one bugfix prompt, which makes bugfix due on the orchestrator's next poll.

**Approach.**
- **src/baseline/main-red.ts** — change `warnMainRedOnce(root, red)` to `warnMainRedOnce(root, red, foundBy: string)`. Keep the `lastMainRedSha` once-per-SHA guard and the `main_red_hold` log exactly as they are; after the log, when `baseRoleOf(foundBy) !== BUGFIX_ROLE`, add one prompt to bugfix's own inbox with `enqueueRolePrompt(root, BUGFIX_ROLE, mainRedHealPrompt(red.sha))` (import `enqueueRolePrompt` from `../inbox/inbox.js`, and `BUGFIX_ROLE` beside the existing `baselineBlocked` import from `../roles/roles.js`). Skip when bugfix itself found the red: its running tick already appends the note and is the heal, and enqueuing from inside it would queue a second run. A comment beside the enqueue names why the queue is the mechanism: a queued per-role prompt makes the loop due by itself (`isEligible`, `src/scheduling/scheduling.ts`, returns `{ run: true, reason: "inbox" }` on a non-empty inbox before any interval, backoff, or deferral check), and `pollRunnerReasons` (`src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts`) skips the need-based deferral block for reason `inbox`, so no scheduler change is needed.
- **src/baseline/main-red.ts** — add `export function mainRedHealPrompt(sha: string): string`, a one-line, self-limiting directive: it says the check was reported red at the short SHA, tells bugfix to verify main is green now, and to reproduce and land the fix only if it is still red. The self-limiting wording is the green race's whole handling: if main turned green before bugfix consumes the queued prompt, `bugfixMainRedNote` returns undefined (no `<main-red>` note is appended) and the prompt's own "verify green" clause makes the tick a no-op. Import `shortSha` from `../text/format.js` if it is not already in scope.
- **src/baseline/main-red.ts** — pass the discovering role at every `warnMainRedOnce` call site: `bugfixMainRedNote` → `role`, `mainRedGate` → `role`, `verdictAtMainTipIn` → `role`. Update the `warnMainRedOnce` doc comment and the module header to state that the once-per-red-SHA handoff now also queues the healer (one prompt per newly-verified red SHA per process; a restart re-queues once, desirable because the cache is cold then too).
- **docs/how-it-works.md** — the "While main's check is failing" bullet ("Bugfix, the director, and markdown-only roles keep going.") gains that a verified-red main also queues the bugfix healer, so it starts on the next poll instead of waiting out its interval or deferral, and that the queued prompt no-ops if main turned green first.
- No BUGS.md change: the handoff is the fix mechanism itself, and an auto-filed bug would just be claimed by a second bugfix tick.

**Files touched.** Source: src/baseline/main-red.ts. Docs: docs/how-it-works.md. Tests: test/main-red.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `mainRedGate(root, "coverage", wt)` on a red main still returns the same `main_red` outcome and logs one `main_red_hold`, and leaves exactly one prompt in bugfix's inbox (`queuedRolePrompts(root, "bugfix")`, `src/inbox/inbox.js`) whose text names the red SHA's short form; a second blocked role's gate (`mainRedGate(root, "feature", wt)`) on the same SHA adds no second prompt and no second warning.
- `mainRedGate` on a green main, `mainRedGate` for a non-blocked role, and `bugfixMainRedNote` on a red main each leave bugfix's inbox empty; `bugfixMainRedNote` still returns the `<main-red>` note and logs the warning.
- `mainRedHealPrompt(sha)` returns one line naming the short SHA, pinned by a direct assertion.

### Harness commits set tumwater as the git author and the account running tumwater as the git committer (planned 2026-10-19 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the Ctrl+L instructions entry edits src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md, the backlog-grep entry src/backlog/backlog-render.ts, src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts and docs/cli.md, and the refused-history entry src/history, src/cli and src/ui/gui, none of which is src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts, src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts or src/operator/revert.ts; the blocked plain-terms runner/run/cleanup series reaches src/git in run 5/20 and src/merge in run 18/20, far behind, a rebase; touches src/git/git-run.ts src/git/git.ts src/init/init.ts src/merge/merge-git.ts src/merge/merge-stack.ts src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts src/operator/revert.ts test/commit-identity.test.ts (new) test/git.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every commit the harness authors is stamped `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>` as BOTH author and committer, because each commit/rebase/cherry-pick call passes `COMMIT_IDENT` (`["-c", "user.name=tumwater", "-c", "user.email=tumwater@localhost"]`, `src/git/git-run.ts`). `-c user.name`/`user.email` set the *committer*; the author defaults to it. The user asks that tumwater stay the git author while the committer becomes "the account running tumwater" — the ambient `user.name`/`user.email` git identity of whoever invokes the team, whether a human operator or a CI bot. So `git log --format='%an <%ae> | %cn <%ce>'` shows `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>` on the left and the operator's identity on the right, while blame-based classification (`docs/code-metrics.md` "Who wrote it" keys on author and trailer) and `INV-H1`'s "tumwater-stamped commit" wording stay correct. To preserve the property `COMMIT_IDENT`'s own doc comment names — ticks work with no global git config — a repo/machine with no ambient identity falls back to `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>` for the committer too.

**Approach.**
- **src/git/git-run.ts** — replace the `COMMIT_IDENT` const with the split identity. Add `export const COMMIT_AUTHOR = "tumwater <tumwater@localhost>"`. Add `export async function committerIdent(cwd: string): Promise<{ name: string; email: string }>`: read `git config user.name` and `git config user.email` through `gitTry` (ambient local+global config); return both trimmed when both are non-empty, otherwise `{ name: "tumwater", email: "tumwater@localhost" }`. Add `export async function committerIdentArgs(cwd: string): Promise<string[]>` = the two `-c` pairs alone for the committer (both `git commit` sites and rebase/cherry-pick), which rewrite the committer while preserving each source commit's (tumwater) author; and `export function commitAuthorArgs(): string[]` = `["--author", COMMIT_AUTHOR]`, appended right after the `commit` subcommand (`--author` is a commit option, not a global one) to pin the author. Update the module header and the removed const's doc comment to state the split and the no-config fallback. No process-global cache: identity is resolved per call against the command's `cwd`, so a test (or a repo) with its own local identity reads correctly and no cross-repo bleed is possible.
- **src/git/git.ts** — in `commitPathsAndDiscardRest` and `commitAll`, replace `...COMMIT_IDENT` with `...(await committerIdentArgs(wt))` and add `...commitAuthorArgs()` after the `commit` subcommand.
- **src/init/init.ts** — the init commit call uses `...(await committerIdentArgs(root))` plus `...commitAuthorArgs()`.
- **src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts**, **src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts**, **src/operator/revert.ts** — each `commit` call uses `...(await committerIdentArgs(<repo-or-worktree>))` plus `...commitAuthorArgs()`.
- **src/merge/merge-git.ts** (`attemptRebase`, `continueRebase`) and **src/merge/merge-stack.ts** (the `cherry-pick`) — replace `...COMMIT_IDENT` with `...(await committerIdentArgs(wt))`.
- **docs/invariants.md** — no change: `INV-H1`'s guarantee (agent commits fold into the run's single commit) is unaffected by which identity fields that commit carries, and its "tumwater-stamped commit" wording still holds because the author stays tumwater.
- Tests: **test/commit-identity.test.ts** (new) using `makeRepo` (whose `.git/config` fixture identity is `test <test@example.com>`): (a) after `commitAll`, `git log -1 --format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>` reads `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>|test <test@example.com>`; (b) with the repo's `[user]` section removed and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at a nonexistent file for the child (set/restore in the test, and pass through `childEnv`), the commit still succeeds with `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>` on both sides; (c) a merge-flow rebase (`rebaseOntoMain`/`continueRebase` over a moved main, using the existing `test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts` helpers) rewrites `%cn` to the ambient identity while `%an` stays `tumwater <tumwater@localhost>`. Extend **test/git.test.ts** only if a shared assertion helper is the cleaner home.

The terminal's finished-entry listings already search by text: `plan --list --done --grep <text>`, `bug --list --done --grep <text>` and `questions --answered --grep <text>` keep the entries whose heading or body contains the text, case-insensitively, under their unfiltered numbers (`entryMatches`, `src/backlog/backlog.ts`). The active listings have no text filter: `tumwater backlog` prints every planned plan and open bug with its full body (thousands of lines on this repo), and `plan --list`/`bug --list` print every entry. `--ready` narrows by hold, not by text, and an operator who greps the file loses the numbering and eligibility marks the CLI adds. `plan --list --grep x` is explicitly refused today (its parser fails `--grep needs --done`). Goal: let `--grep` search the active entries on both surfaces, through the same `entryMatches` haystack and the same unfiltered numbering, so a printed number still reaches `--show`/`--edit`/`--cancel`.

**Approach.**
- **src/backlog/backlog-render.ts** — add `export function grepBacklog(view: BacklogView, pattern: string): BacklogView`: keep plan `i`, bug `i` and question `i` only when `entryMatches(entry, pattern)`, and filter `holds.plans`/`holds.bugs` and `inProgress.plans`/`inProgress.bugs` by the same kept indexes so the parallel arrays stay aligned (reuse the `pick` shape `readyBacklog` already has; a view without `holds`/`inProgress` filters only the entry arrays). Questions carry no holds and filter by `entryMatches` alone. Its doc comment says it is the active-entry twin of the finished-entry `--grep`.
- **src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts** (`cmdBacklog`) — parse the flag with the shared `parseGrepFlag` (`src/cli/cli-args.ts`) and `grepFlagSpec`, exactly as `cmdLogs` does: `const { rest, pattern } = parseGrepFlag(args, BACKLOG_GREP_VALUE_ERROR); rejectUnknownArgs("backlog", rest, [JSON_FLAG, READY_FLAG, grepFlagSpec(BACKLOG_GREP_VALUE_ERROR)]);`, where `BACKLOG_GREP_VALUE_ERROR` is `backlog --grep needs text (usage: tumwater backlog --grep <text>)`; switch the `--ready`/`--json` reads to `rest`. In the payload thunk, apply `pattern === null ? view : grepBacklog(view, pattern)` before `readyBacklog`, so `--grep` composes with `--ready` and the hidden count counts only matching held entries; `--json` and the Markdown branch already share that thunk, so they cannot drift.
- **src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts** (`listAndAnnounce`) — drop the `grep !== null && !done` refusal. In the active (non-`--done`) branch build `const numbered = entries.map((entry, i) => ({ entry, position: i + 1 }));` and `const matches = grep === null ? numbered : numbered.filter((m) => entryMatches(m.entry, grep));`. The JSON branch maps `matches` (each keeps its original `position`, with `hold`/`inProgress` read by `m.position - 1`). The prose branch renders `matches` through the existing `line`/`groupBlockedSeries` path keyed on `m.position`, so each entry keeps its unfiltered number and a series with two or more matching blocked parts still compresses. Empty `entries` with no pattern keeps `no <noun>s`; a pattern with no match prints `no <noun>s match "<pattern>"` (mirroring the done branch's `no done plans match`). The `--done` branch and the `-n needs --done` refusal are unchanged.
- **src/cli/help.ts** — the `tumwater backlog [--ready] [--json]` stanza becomes `[--ready] [--grep <text>] [--json]` with the one-line clause `--grep keeps the entries whose heading or body contains the text, case-insensitively`; the `bug --list [--json]` and `plan --list [--json]` stanzas gain `[--grep <text>]` and that clause, beside the existing `--done --grep` wording.
- **docs/cli.md** — the Check-state row's `tumwater backlog` clause gains `--grep <text>`, and the Steer row's `plan|bug --list` clause names it as the active twin of `--list --done --grep`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater backlog --grep <word>` on a repo whose PLANS.md, BUGS.md and QUESTIONS.md each hold the word in one entry's body prints only those entries, case-insensitively, and every non-matching section renders its existing `_(none)_`; `--json`'s `plans`/`bugs`/`questions` arrays and their parallel `holds`/`inProgress` hold only the matches.

### The fixer records a reconstructed invariant in docs/invariants.md when it lands a `unclear-invariant` fix, so a guarantee is pinned once instead of reconstructed per bug (planned 2026-10-18 by the steward role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it extends src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts's landed `checkValidationGaps` and edits src/roles/role-guidance.ts's `VALIDATION_GAP_GUIDANCE`, files no in-flight or blocked entry touches; touches src/roles/role-guidance.ts src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

**Goal.** The gap tally ties `unclear-invariant` with `none` as the largest tag across BUGS.md and BUGS-FIXED.md (102 each), and its traces read almost uniformly "the intended guarantee had to be reconstructed from a doc comment / the design / an unused field because no test or doc pinned it first" — e.g. "The loop drawer's Configuration Model row omits pi's saved default model" (the drawer-vs-CLI "read identically" guarantee), "The role view's Schedule omits the yield multiplier" (a released lease owns no key slot), "The scheduler dispatches two roles onto the same open plan" (a landing supersedes a prior reject), and the "a test temp dir must live under the per-run root the exit hook reaps" guard. The gap machinery that has landed — the doctor's `checkValidationGaps`, the report/GUI Validation-gap tallies, and the coverage role's gap-from-traces target pick — records each unclear-invariant bug and routes coverage at its module, but none of it retires the tag: the fix lands, and the very invariant it had to reconstruct stays just as unpinned as before, so the next bug in the same area reconstructs it again. Retire the tag by making the unpinned invariant itself a product of the fix: when a fixer closes an `unclear-invariant` bug it writes the reconstructed guarantee into docs/invariants.md's matching section (a "Pinned by" line, or a new section when none exists) in the same commit.

**Approach.**
- **src/roles/role-guidance.ts** — in the `unclear-invariant` row of `VALIDATION_GAP_GUIDANCE`, append one sentence telling the fixer to record the reconstructed invariant in docs/invariants.md in the same commit, so the next bug in that area does not reconstruct it again.
- **src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts** — extend `checkValidationGaps` (not a new check): over the same bounded newest-full-body `## Fixed` window `checkFixClaims` uses, for each entry whose tag is `unclear-invariant`, warn when the body names no docs/invariants.md section, nudging the fixer to pin the reconstructed invariant. Keep it informational and bounded exactly like `checkFixClaims` so pre-convention history does not warn forever; a fix that pinned the invariant in code rather than the doc, or whose prose does not name the file, may warn spuriously — that is the accepted cost of a nudge, not a hard gate.
- **docs/invariants.md** — no mechanical change here; the criterion is that the unclear-invariant fix's own commit adds the "Pinned by" line (or a section) for the reconstructed guarantee.

- The `unclear-invariant` guidance sentence tells the fixer to record the reconstructed invariant in docs/invariants.md in the same commit.
- `checkValidationGaps` over a seeded BUGS.md whose `## Fixed` holds a recent `unclear-invariant` entry citing no docs/invariants.md section warns with that nudge; the same hook with the body naming a section does not; `unclear-invariant`-free and pre-window entries are unchanged.

### The plan role runs a tight loop while the brief still carries the placeholder status (planned 2026-10-18 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the doctor entry edits src/doctor, the coverage entry src/roles, the dashboards entry src/ui and src/roles/role-labels.ts, and the revert entry src/operator and src/cli, all disjoint from this entry's src/brief, src/config, src/scheduling and src/orchestrator edits; it shares src/loop/loop-tick.ts only with the registered Plain terms code runner part 1/14, which moves that file into src/runner without changing its content, so implement it under whichever name is on main — a rebase either way; touches src/brief/brief.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/scheduling/scheduling.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts src/loop/loop-tick.ts docs/config.md test/brief.test.ts test/scheduling.test.ts test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

**Goal.** A freshly seeded project's brief (README.md, or TUMWATER.md in an adopted repo) carries the initial prompt but its status section still holds the template placeholder `_No status yet. The readme role keeps this section up to date._` (`managedSections`, src/brief/brief.ts). The user's request for that state: "the plan role should run in a tight loop until it has no changes." Today plan still sleeps — it has a 3600 s slow clock (src/config/config.ts), and even the new-project bootstrap only lowers it to the team-wide `minRunIntervalSeconds` (20 s) rather than running back-to-back (`scheduleConfigForRole`, src/config/config-views.ts). While the brief's status is still the placeholder, plan should schedule its next run with a ZERO min gap: a productive (`changed`/`queued`) plan tick reruns on the next poll, and a `no_change` tick drops to the idle backoff ladder, so the burst ends at the first run that changes nothing (a later main move can still wake it, as for every role). The trigger is the placeholder status, not bootstrap: an adopted repo, or one whose `bootstrap` entry was removed, gets the same behavior, and the rule turns itself off the moment the readme role replaces the placeholder. The description's other half — the initial prompt — is always present (init rejects an empty one), so the placeholder status is the one machine-detectable "description not yet complete" signal; a malformed brief stays doctor's warning, not a tight loop.

**Approach.**
- **src/brief/brief.ts** — hoist the placeholder line into `export const EMPTY_STATUS = "_No status yet. The readme role keeps this section up to date._"` and use it in `managedSections`. Add `export function briefStatusIncomplete(root: string): boolean`: using the module's private `firstBriefText(root, ownsBrief)`, return `false` when there is no resolved brief or it carries no well-formed `STATUS_START`/`STATUS_END` pair (a malformed brief is doctor's warning); otherwise slice between the markers, trim, and return `body === "" || body === EMPTY_STATUS`. One small file read, like `readInitialPrompt`.
- **src/config/config-views.ts** — give `scheduleConfigForRole` a fourth parameter `descriptionIncomplete = false` (after `bootstrapActive`): when `baseRoleOf(role) === "plan"`, `descriptionIncomplete` returns `{ ...resolved, minRunIntervalSeconds: 0 }` (tighter than bootstrap); the existing bootstrap branch and every non-plan role are unchanged. Extend the doc comment to name the zero-gap rule and that the flag means the brief's status section is still the placeholder.
- **src/scheduling/scheduling.ts** — add `descriptionIncomplete?: boolean` to `EligibilityOptions` and pass `opts.descriptionIncomplete === true` as `scheduleConfigForRole`'s fourth argument in `isEligible`, so the admitted gap and the tick's `nextRunAt` come from one rule.

### `tumwater history` and both dashboards give `refused` runs their own outcome class, so a deliberate refusal stops counting as a problem and becomes filterable (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the refusals-report entry edits src/report and src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts, the config near-miss entry src/config and src/text, the tight-loop entry src/brief, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling and src/orchestrator, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop to src/runner and touches docs/invariants.md and DEVELOPMENT.md, none of which is src/history or src/cli/cli-run.ts; it meets the refusals-report entry only at docs/cli.md's history vs report row, a rebase; the blocked plain-terms runner/run/cleanup series renames identifiers in src/history and src/cli only in far-behind parts (runner 13/14, run 6/20 and 14/20), a rebase either way; touches src/history/history-data.ts src/history/history-render.ts src/cli/cli-run.ts src/cli/help.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts docs/cli.md test/history-data.test.ts test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts test/cli-run.test.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/tui-keys.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

The history surfaces still fold it into the generic `problems` bucket, however: `historyClass` (`src/history/history-data.ts`) returns `problems` for every result that is not `changes` or `none`, so a role that deliberately declined a harmful task (`TUMWATER_REFUSED`) is counted and filtered exactly like a crashed or rejected run, and the per-role `problems` column in `history --summary`, the `--for`/`--once` window line, the dashboard History filter and Summary table, and the TUI's Ctrl+O outcome cycle all overstate failures and hide refusals. `tumwater report` (a separate in-flight plan) adds a per-role refusals tally; this entry fixes the classification its history siblings share. Give `refused` its own outcome class beside `changes`, `none` and `problems`, and apply it to every surface that speaks the class list.

**Approach.**
- `src/history/history-data.ts` — the one canonical rule. Make `HISTORY_RESULT_CLASSES = ["changes", "none", "refused", "problems"]` (refused before problems so the TUI cycle reads merged, none, refused, problems). Add `refused: "refused"` to `HISTORY_RESULT_FLAG_NAMES`. In `historyClass`, return `"refused"` for `result === "refused"` and leave every other branch unchanged (`error`/`rejected` stay `problems`; `no_change`/`skipped`/`user_aborted` stay `none`). Add `refused: number` to `HistorySummaryRow`, initialize it to `0` in `summarizeTickRows`'s `blank()`, and let the existing `t[cls] += 1` tally it. - `src/cli/cli-run.ts` — the `windowSummary` line (`for <label>: N runs — …`) appends `${total.refused} refused` between the none and problems counts.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts` — add `["refused", "Refused"]` to `HIST_FILTERS` after `none`; add the `result === "refused"` branch to the `historyClass` mirror so `test/gui-client-history.test.ts`'s pin against the canonical rule holds; add a `Refused` `<th>` and `cell(r, "refused")` to `histSummaryHtml` between None and Problems, and update the column comment there.
- `src/cli/help.ts` — the `history` usage line becomes `[--result <merged|none|refused|problems>]`; its `--result` sentence names the new class (a deliberate decline, no longer folded into problems).
- `docs/cli.md` — the Watch-run-history row's `--result <merged|none|problems>` becomes `--result <merged|none|refused|problems>` and its `--summary` clause names the refused column.
- Tests: in `test/history-data.test.ts` add `refused: 0` to the `summarizeTickRows` `deepEqual` literals and add a case proving a `refused` row lands in `refused` while `error`/`rejected` stay in `problems`; in `test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts` add a `--result refused` case (its own seeded rows, so the shared fixture's other assertions are untouched); in `test/cli-run.test.ts` update the `windowSummary` first line and header regex (`1 changes, 1 none, 1 refused, 1 problems` style); in `test/gui-client-history.test.ts` add `"refused"` to `bucketCases` mapping to `"refused"`, update the expected array, and add `refused: 0` to the summary literals; in `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts` add `refused: number` to the summary type annotation; in `test/tui-keys.test.ts` add the `refused` step to the Ctrl+O cycle assert (merged → none → refused → problems → all).

**Goal.** plans/repair-traces.md's invariant 2 is "the vocabulary is closed and lives in one place" and the shared guidance (src/roles/role-guidance.ts `VALIDATION_GAP_GUIDANCE`) tells every bugfix run to "never invent a tag" and to write `none` rather than omit the line. A Fixed entry with no line at all is equally invisible. **Approach.**
- **src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts** — import `validationGapTag` from `../backlog/backlog-md.js` (beside `BACKLOG_FILES`/`lastDate`) and `VALIDATION_GAP_TAGS` from `../roles/role-guidance.js`. ### The bugfix healer's red-main note carries the failing check's output tail (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the revert entry edits src/operator, src/cli and docs/cli.md, and the blocked plain-terms runner series reaches src/baseline, src/prompt and their tests only in far-behind parts (runner 12/14–13/14, run 5/20) — no shared file; touches src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts src/baseline/main-red.ts test/gate-prompts.test.ts test/main-red.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

**Goal.** On a red main the only repairer is `bugfix` (`mainRedGate` exempts it), and the only signal it gets is `buildMainRedNote`'s `<main-red>` block. A red baseline already computes the check's bounded clipped tail — `checkMainBaseline` returns `red.outputTail`, set from `clipBuildTail(output)` in src/build/build-check.ts (≤12 meaningful lines: the failing test's name, the error-message line, then the stack) — but `bugfixMainRedNote` passes only `failureHeadline(red.outputTail)` to the note, so the healer starts with a single line that is often just the test name (`✖ <test>`), not the assertion or stack, and must spend its run reproducing the failure before it can fix it. Pass the tail it already holds, bounded and verbatim, so the healer begins from the actual error.

**Approach.**
- **src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts** — extend `buildMainRedNote(sha, script?, headline?, tail?: readonly string[])`: keep the first four body lines and the existing `what` line byte-identical, and when `tail` is an array with at least one non-blank string, append a labeled block before the closing `</main-red>` — one line naming how many lines follow and a fenced body of those lines (trim each, drop empty ones) so the failure's own text cannot read as instructions. `tail` absent, `[]`, or all-blank renders today's exact string.
- **src/baseline/main-red.ts** — `bugfixMainRedNote` passes `red.outputTail` as the fourth argument. Leave `redMainMessage` and `mainRedGate`'s `main_red` outcome unchanged: that text is folded into `LoopState.lastError`, which single-line surfaces squash (`checkMainRed` squashes to 160 chars), so the tail belongs only in the prompt block.

### `tumwater revert <sha>` undoes one merged change on main, under the primary-worktree lock (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the merge-queue entry edits src/merge, src/status and src/ui/gui/gui-client-pending.ts, the drawer entry edits src/gui, src/ui/gui and src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts, and the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/operator and src/cli only in far-behind parts; meeting docs/cli.md's Steer-the-project row, a rebase; touches src/operator/revert.ts src/operator/operator-commands.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/operator-revert.test.ts test/cli-operators.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

**Goal.** When a merged change turns out bad — most visibly by reddening main, where the red-main gate holds every code loop but `bugfix` and pages the operator through `main_red_hold` — recovery is either the `bugfix` healer patching forward or running `git revert` by hand in the primary checkout. The harness owns every git operation (PRINCIPLES.md) and already commits operator edits on main under the primary-worktree lock (`commitOperatorBacklogEdit`, src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts). Add the matching operator command: `tumwater revert <sha>` reverts one commit already on the base branch and commits the inverse on main as `tumwater(operator): Revert <short sha>`, fail-closed — off the base branch, an unknown ref, a ref not on main, or a revert that conflicts writes no commit and restores the checkout.

**Approach.**
- **src/operator/revert.ts** (new, beside retire.ts) — `export async function revertMergedCommit(root: string, ref: string): Promise<{ ok: true; headSha: string; beforeSha: string } | { ok: false; error: string }>`, mirroring `commitOperatorBacklogEdit`'s lock-and-branch discipline: yield once (`setImmediate`) then run the body inside `withStateLockAsync(primaryWorktreeLockPath(root), …)` (src/concurrency/lock.ts, src/paths.ts). Under the lock:
  - `const primary = await currentBranch(root)`; when it is null or `targetBranch(loadConfigSafe(root).config?.baseBranch, primary) !== primary`, return `{ ok: false, error: "the primary checkout is not on " + <base> + " — run from a checkout of it" }`, writing nothing.
  - `const full = await gitTry(root, "rev-parse", "--verify", ref + "^{commit}")`; null → `{ ok: false, error: "no such commit: " + ref }`.
  - `const head = await headOf(root, "HEAD")`; `!(await isMergedInto(root, full, primary))` → `{ ok: false, error: shortSha(full) + " is not on " + primary }` (src/git/git.ts, src/text/format.ts).
  - Refuse when `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is non-empty (staged or unstaged changes to a tracked path): the tree must be clean before the inverse commit is written, and clean before a failed revert may call `revert --abort` (whose hard reset would otherwise discard the operand's pre-existing staged changes) — `{ ok: false, error: "the worktree has staged or unstaged changes; commit or stash them first, nothing was committed" }`.
  - `await gitTry(root, "revert", "--no-commit", full)`; null → `await gitTry(root, "revert", "--abort")` (safe: the guard kept the tree clean), then `{ ok: false, error: "reverting " + shortSha(full) + " conflicted; nothing was committed and the checkout is unchanged" }`.
  - `await gitTry(root, ...COMMIT_IDENT, "commit", "--only", "-m", stampedSubject("operator", "Revert " + shortSha(full)), "--", …)` with the revert's own staged paths (`git diff --cached --name-only --no-renames`), mirroring `commitOperatorBacklogEdit`'s `--only` so an unrelated staged path can never ride into the inverse commit, and saying `--no-renames` so a rename revert lists both halves (default name-only collapses a rename to its destination, inverting only one half and leaving the other staged); null → `revert --abort`, then `{ ok: false, error: "the revert of " + shortSha(full) + " did not commit; nothing was committed" }`.
  - `{ ok: true, headSha: await headOf(root, "HEAD") , beforeSha: head }`. `head` is captured before the revert so a future caller can compare, and the resolved full sha is what the commit message shortens.
- **src/operator/operator-commands.ts** — add `export async function cmdRevert(root, args)`: no flags; require exactly one positional (none → `fail("revert needs a commit (e.g. run tumwater revert 1a2b3c4)")`, more than one → the same usage error); refuse a flag-shaped token (`args[0].startsWith("-")`) as a flag before any lookup, so a lone `--json` is rejected as a flag rather than misread as the ref; `const r = await revertMergedCommit(root, ref)`; `!r.ok` → `fail(r.error)`; else `say(...)` naming the new main head and one line that the role may redo the work, so cancel or edit its PLANS.md/BUGS.md entry if it should not.
- **src/cli.ts** — add `case "revert":` beside `"retire"`, routing to `cmdRevert`.
- **src/cli/help.ts** — add a `tumwater revert <sha>` stanza beside `tumwater abort`/`tumwater retire` (completion.ts derives its command list from HELP's stanzas, so it needs no edit).
- **docs/cli.md** — in the "Steer the project" row, beside `tumwater abort`/`tumwater retire`, add that `tumwater revert <sha>` reverts one merged change on main, committing `tumwater(operator): Revert <short sha>` under the primary-worktree lock, and that it refuses off the base branch, on an unknown or unmerged ref, and on a conflict.

**Files touched.** Source: src/operator/revert.ts (new), src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts. Docs: docs/cli.md. Tests: test/operator-revert.test.ts (new), test/cli-operators.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `revertMergedCommit(repo, "HEAD")` on a clean repo checked out on its base branch returns `ok: true`, moves HEAD to the inverse commit, leaves `git status --porcelain` empty, and `git log -1 --format=%s` reads `tumwater(operator): Revert <short sha>` for the reverted head.
- Reverting a non-tip commit whose paths no later commit touched succeeds and leaves the tree clean; reverting a commit a later commit edited in the same region returns `ok: false`, leaves HEAD exactly where it was, leaves `git status --porcelain` empty, and the error names the conflict.
- An unknown ref and a ref that exists but is not on the base branch each return `ok: false`, name the ref or say it is not on the base branch, and change neither HEAD nor the worktree.
- Checked out on a non-base branch, `revertMergedCommit` returns `ok: false` naming the base branch even when the ref resolves, and commits nothing (mirroring `commitOperatorBacklogEdit`'s branch guard).
- `cli(repo, "revert", <sha>)` exits 0 and prints the new main sha; `cli(repo, "revert")` and `cli(repo, "revert", <a>, <b>)` each exit nonzero with the usage error, writing no commit.
- docs/cli.md's Steer-the-project row names `tumwater revert <sha>`.
- `npm test` passes.

- `rolePayload` omits `providerOverride`/`modelOverride`/`thinkingOverride` for a role the file gives no overrides, and carries them for `feature-2` when the file holds `roles.feature.model` (the base role's value).

### The dashboard role drawer sets a role's instance count, the last per-role hold with no dashboard control (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the blocked plain-terms series and of the in-flight CLI/TUI plans — it edits src/gui and the drawer/bootstrap pair, meeting doc src at docs/cli.md's role row; reads `view.instances` from role-view's payload, which the in-flight `tumwater role <id> --instances` plan lands first (its role-view.ts field and role-render.ts Instances line rebase in cleanly), so this consumer rides that payload with no role-view edit of its own; touches src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts docs/cli.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts test/gui-client-boot.test.ts) — done 2026-10-18 by the feature role

**Goal.** `roles.<base>.instances` is the count that makes `feature-2`…`feature-N` real runners (`configuredInstances`/`loopIds`, `src/roles/loop-ids.ts`); only `feature` and `bugfix` may split (`INSTANCE_ROLES`), the bound is `INSTANCE_COUNT` (an integer 1–8, `src/config/config-validation.ts`), and `validateConfig` refuses an `instances` key on any other role with `roles.<id>.instances is only valid for feature and bugfix`. Every per-role knob already has a dashboard role-drawer editor — Daily cap, Quiet hours, Min run interval, Instructions override, Notes — and the in-flight `tumwater role <id> --instances` plan gives the key a CLI write and a role-page `- Instances:` line, but the drawer, where an operator changes one role's holds, has no control for it. Add the drawer's instance editor, so the count that spawns parallel runners is set where the runner is inspected.

**Approach.**
- **src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts** — add `handleRoleInstances(req, res, root)` modelled on `handleRoleInterval` (not `handleRoleCap`: with no director exemption, `validateConfig` owns which roles may set it). Body `{ role, instances }`; a missing/empty/non-string `role` → 400 `role required`; `instances === undefined` → 400 `instances required`; `base = baseRoleOf(role)`. A `null`, `""` or whitespace-only value clears: `if (rejectBadRole(root, res, role)) return;` then `unsetConfigKey(root, `roles.${base}.instances`)` (the explicit guard because `unsetConfigKey`'s no-op map path skips `validateConfig` — the clear-arm gap `handleRoleInterval`'s comment records) and 200 `{ ok: true, role: base, message: `${base}: instances cleared` }`. Otherwise `setConfigKey(root, `roles.${base}.instances`, JSON.stringify(value))` and, on `ok`, 200 `{ ok: true, role: base, instances: value, message: `${base}: instances set to ${value}` }`; a failure is `configKeyError(res, key, result)`'s 400 naming the dotted key. No own range or role check: `setConfigKey` runs the candidate through `validateConfig`, whose `INSTANCE_COUNT` rejects `0`, `9`, `1.5` and `abc` and whose `!INSTANCE_ROLES.has(id)` branch rejects a non-feature/bugfix id (the director and custom roles included).
- **src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts** — add `handleRoleInstances` to the barrel export line beside `handleRoleInterval`.
- **src/gui/gui-server.ts** — add `"POST /api/role-instances": (req, res) => handleRoleInstances(req, res, root),` beside the `role-interval` route.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts** — add `let instancesEditing = null; // { role, value }` beside `intervalEditing`, `startInstancesEdit(role, value)`/`stopInstancesEdit()` beside the interval pair, and clear it in `closeDrawer`'s editing-state reset. In `drawerConfigHtml`, after the Min run interval row, add an `Instances` row rendered only when the role may split (its base, `role.replace(/-\d+$/, "")`, is `"feature"` or `"bugfix"`): body from `typeof view.instances === "number" ? view.instances : 1`, tagged `(set)` when the payload carries the field and `(default)` otherwise, plus a `Set instances`/`Edit` control; while open, `<input id='instanceseditinput' type='number' min='1' max='8' step='1' value='...'>` prefilled with the count (empty when the payload has none) and Save/Discard, mirroring the interval editor's markup.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts** — add `instances-edit` (`startInstancesEdit(arg, drawerRole?.view?.instances ?? "")`), `instances-discard` (`stopInstancesEdit()`) and `instances-save` beside the interval arms. `instances-save` reads `#instanceseditinput`, keeps the interval arm's `validity.badInput` guard (a rejected `"2.5"` is an error, not a clear), and posts `/api/role-instances` `{ role: arg, instances: input.value.trim() === "" ? null : Number(input.value) }`; on success it clears `instancesEditing`, calls `loadDrawerRole(arg)`, and flashes the server's `message`.
- **src/roles/role-view.ts** — no change: the in-flight `tumwater role <id> --instances` plan landed first and already carries `instances?: number` in `RoleViewPayload`, populated from the config when set and absent when not, so `/api/role` gives the drawer the real count to display and seed.
- **docs/cli.md** — in the `tumwater role <id>` row's drawer sentence (which ends with the min run interval clause), add "and sets the role's instance count, writing `roles.<base>.instances` (an integer 1–8; only `feature` and `bugfix` may split)".

**Files touched.** Source: src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-server.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts. Docs: docs/cli.md. Tests: test/gui-endpoints.test.ts, test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts, test/gui-client-boot.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
