### The TUI's Ctrl+B edits the viewed role's daily cap on its Transcript pane, the terminal control for the amber role-cap alert (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the eligible Planned entries — the dashboard per-role-cap entry shares only docs/cli.md with this one, editing the `tumwater role <id>` row while this edits the TUI-keys `Ctrl+B` row, and neither Notes command 3/4, Notes command 4/4 nor the plain-terms series touches src/ui/tui; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-budget.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** `teamAlerts` (src/ui/team-alerts.ts) raises the amber `role-cap` alert with the detail "Raise the cap to resume it", and the TUI paints it as an attention line (src/ui/tui/tui.tsx calls `teamAlerts` and `alertLines`). The terminal has no control for it: `Ctrl+B` edits only the team cap (`tui-editor-budget.ts` writes through `setDailyBudgetUsd`, src/config/config-write.ts), so a role's own `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.<role>` is settable only from `tumwater config set` — or from the dashboard's role drawer once the in-flight dashboard plan lands. Make `Ctrl+B` edit the cap in scope: the team cap on the Activity view as today, the viewed role's cap while a role's Transcript pane (or its notes view) is up, so the TUI's own alert path ends at a control.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-budget.ts** — rename the unused `_ctx` parameter to `ctx` and branch on the pane inside the existing `key.ctrl && key.name === "b"` arm, before the `heldEditorFlash("budget")` guard's effects. One `budgetMode` flag, one `session.held.budget` slot and one saved-draft pair serve both scopes: only where the editor reads its pre-fill and writes differ.
  - A role view is `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` (the same in-range guard `tui-editor-notes.ts` carries, which also keeps `roleIds[ctx.view - 1]` safe when `syncRoster` shrinks the roster). The role is `ctx.roleIds[ctx.view - 1]!`; otherwise the arm takes the team branch below unchanged.
  - Refuse the director: `if (role === DIRECTOR_ROLE) { session.flashMessage("the director has no daily cap"); return true; }` (`DIRECTOR_ROLE` from src/roles/roles.ts; the cap exempts the director, the rule `role-view.ts` applies and the dashboard plan words).
  - Pre-fill from the file at entry: `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.maxDailyCostUsdPerRole?.[baseRoleOf(role)] ?? 0` (`loadConfigSafe` from src/config/config.ts; src/roles/loop-ids.ts maps `feature-2` → `feature`, the map's key). Empty for none, exactly as the team branch blanks a disabled cap. The snapshot carries `capPaused` but no cap values, so one fresh read per open is the smallest honest source; a broken config degrades to no pre-fill and the write reports the real error.
  - On `Enter`, parse through the team branch's own `parseBudgetInput` (src/ui/tui/tui-input.ts), then write `setConfigKey(session.root, `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.${baseRoleOf(role)}`, JSON.stringify(parsed.value))` — the one dotted-key write `tumwater config set` uses, whose `checkDailyBudgetUsd` screen and `validateConfig` role-id check are the same the dashboard plan relies on. On `!result.ok` flash `result.error` and stay in edit mode (the team branch's broken-config contract); on success `exitBudgetMode()` and flash `` `${role}: cap set to ${usdCap(parsed.value)}` `` for a positive value or `` `${role}: cap removed` `` for `0`.
  - Leave the team branch byte-for-byte as it is: the `currentCapUsd` snapshot pre-fill, the `currentBudgetFree` all-free guard, the `setDailyBudgetUsd` write, and the `budget set to …` / `budget disabled` wording. The all-free guard stays team-only: a team-wide free verdict is not a per-role fact.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]` to the `view.kind === "transcript"` hint row (beside the existing Ctrl+P/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+A/Ctrl+V entries); the Activity branch already names `Ctrl+B daily cap`, and the budget-mode hint wording stays generic ("save the daily cap"), since the shared `budget` mode flag does not carry the scope.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys `Ctrl+B` row becomes "edit the daily cost cap: the team's on Activity, the viewed role's (`maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.<role>`) on its Transcript; empty means no cap".

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/ui/tui/tui-editor-budget.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts.
- Docs: docs/cli.md.
- Tests: test/tui-keys.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts, test/tui-operator-keys.test.ts, test/tui.test.ts.

### Notes command, part 4/4: Keep funes and other operator extensions out of team runs: pi skips discovered extensions, Claude Code can use a config dir of the team's own, and doctor says where funes could reach the team (planned 2026-10-17 by user; design in plans/notes-command.md "Keeping funes out of team runs"; touches src/pi/pi-args.ts src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/agent/claude/claude-backend.ts src/agent/claude/claude-env.ts src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts docs/backends.md docs/config.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** funes, the transcript-recall tool you use for your own sessions, must never run in or index the team. Today it doesn't run inside team runs, but:

- **It indexes team transcripts from outside.** funes's Claude Code hook sweeps every changed session under `~/.claude/projects`, so team Claude Code runs make up 59% of the sessions in your personal funes memory.
- **pi would load it.** Team pi runs load anything pi discovers: installed packages, `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, and pi's built-in MCP extension reading `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`. A `funes add pi` would put funes in every team pi run.

This part closes the pi path, offers an opt-in fix for the Claude Code path, and has doctor report all three backends.

**Approach.**
- **src/pi/pi-args.ts:** pass `--no-extensions`, then `-e builtin:llama.cpp -e builtin:codemode -e builtin:tool-search`.
  - Those are pi 1.2.0's built-ins other than `mcp`, kept so behavior is otherwise unchanged. tumwater's own `-e` extensions still load.
  - Keep the three names in one exported constant with a comment naming the pi version they were read from (pi's `dist/extensions/index.js`).
  - Add `--no-extensions` to `HARNESS_PI_FLAGS`, so `piArgs` passthrough cannot repeat it.
- **Config:** `backends.claude.configDir` (string, optional), in src/config/config-schema.ts and config-validation.ts.
  - A leading `~` expands; the value must be an absolute path after expansion.
  - When set, src/agent/claude/claude-env.ts sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to it for every claude process tumwater spawns: runs, the `claude auth status` seed in src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, and doctor.
  - `claudeConfigDir()` in src/agent/claude/claude-backend.ts reads the configured dir before the env, so the resume check and doctor's transcript sizes follow it.
  - Unset, behavior is exactly today's.
- **Doctor** (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts):
  - A `pi extensions` row, shown when a model job runs on pi, lists what team runs now skip: installed packages (`pi list`, bounded), files in `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, and servers in `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json`. Each is named, so a package meant for the team does not vanish silently.
  - A `funes` row, shown when `funes` is on PATH:
    - It warns when a Claude Code model job runs with no `backends.claude.configDir` while `~/.funes/integrations/claude-plugin` exists: "team Claude Code transcripts are indexed into your personal funes memory — set backends.claude.configDir and log in there once (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth login`)".
    - It notes an OpenCode global config `plugin` entry that names funes.
    - Otherwise it is ok.
  - With `backends.claude.configDir` set, the existing claude login check runs against that dir.
- **docs/backends.md and docs/config.md:**
  - `backends.claude.configDir`, and its one-time login (a fresh config dir reports `loggedIn: false`, verified 2026-10-17);
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` as the alternative;
  - pi runs skipping discovered extensions, including a target repo's own `.pi/extensions` (design decision 5).

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/pi/pi-args.ts, src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-backend.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-env.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md, docs/config.md.
- Tests: test/pi-args.test.ts, test/config-validation.test.ts, test/claude-env.test.ts, test/claude-run.test.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **pi argv** has `--no-extensions` and the three `-e builtin:` flags before tumwater's own `-e` extensions; a `piArgs` entry `--no-extensions` is refused.
- **`backends.claude.configDir`:**
  - With it set, a Claude Code run's env and the account seed's env both carry `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` = the expanded path.
  - `claudeTranscriptPath` resolves under it.
  - A relative path is refused at load.
  - Unset, the env is byte-identical to before.
- **Doctor with a fake `funes` on PATH and a temp HOME holding `.funes/integrations/claude-plugin`:**
  - It warns for a Claude Code team with no config dir, and is ok once one is set.
  - No `funes` on PATH gives no row.
  - A temp HOME with `.pi/agent/mcp.json` naming a server gets that server listed in the pi row.

### OpenCode backend, part 6f/7: OpenCode runs cap tool output at pi's window-scaled limits (planned 2026-10-17 by user; requires part 6e/7 landed; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "Small-window parity with pi" item 2; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-config.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** OpenCode's tool results stop entering the context at up to 51,200 bytes (its `tool_output` default, finding 13) and come in at the same budget as a pi run's. The free model's window is 200K, against the 1M window it replaces, and every turn re-sends what a tool returned.

**Approach.**
- `opencodeConfigContent` takes an optional `toolOutput: { maxLines, maxBytes }` and, when given, writes `"tool_output": { "max_lines": …, "max_bytes": … }` into the injected config.
  - The key and its shape were checked in the 2.0.32 binary. It bounds the shell tool's cut (which keeps the tail) and the `@opencode/ToolOutput` service, which cuts every other tool result (keeping the head and saving the full text to a file).
- The adapter (`opencodeBackend.invocation`) passes:
  - `maxBytes` = `outputLimits(window).bash` from src/pi-extension/bounded-output.ts, which is 16,000 at 128k and above and scales down below that;
  - `maxLines` = `Math.round(maxBytes / 40)`, the ~40 characters a line that pi's "12k chars ≈ 300 lines" read cap implies (400 at 16,000 bytes).
  - The window is part 6e/7's `seamContextWindow` for the run's model. An unknown window gives the 128k values, which is what the 200K free model gets.
- Without `toolOutput`, the config is byte-identical to today's.
- The dialect's `oversizedOutput` already tells the model that shell output keeps its last lines and to read the spill file in ranges. The other tools' cut keeps the head, so add that to the dialect text if a test or the smoke check shows the model misreading it.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/opencode/opencode-config.ts, src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts.
- Tests: test/opencode-config.test.ts, and the adapter's invocation test.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `opencodeConfigContent({ ..., toolOutput: { maxLines: 400, maxBytes: 16000 } })` parses to a config whose `tool_output` is `{ "max_lines": 400, "max_bytes": 16000 }`, and the same call without `toolOutput` returns today's string unchanged.
- An adapter invocation for a model whose catalog window is 65,536 injects `max_bytes` 8000 and `max_lines` 200. An unknown window injects 16000 and 400.
- `npm test` passes.

### The dashboard role drawer sets one role's daily cap: the control the amber "over its daily cap" alert's Open-role action leads to (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it touches src/gui/ and src/ui/gui/ and docs/cli.md, none of which Notes command 2/4, Notes command 4/4 or OpenCode 6f/7 touch; touches src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts src/gui/gui-server.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** A role over its `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` cap raises the amber `role-cap` team alert, whose detail says "Raise the cap to resume it" and whose action is `openRoleActions` (`{ act: "role", arg: <id> }`, src/ui/team-alerts.ts) — the dashboard opens that role's drawer. The drawer shows the cap read-only (`drawerConfigHtml`'s "Daily cap" row in src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, landed 2026-10-16), so the advertised remedy names no control: raising the cap today means `tumwater config set maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.<role> <usd>` in a terminal, while the team-wide cap already has a browser editor (`/api/budget`). Give the drawer that same editor for one role, so the alert's path ends at a control.

**Approach.**
- **Server — `handleRoleCap` in src/gui/gui-config-commands.ts,** mirroring `handleBudget`. Body `{ role, maxDailyCostUsd }` (`readPostBody`). Require `role` to be a non-empty string; refuse `DIRECTOR_ROLE` with 400 `"the director has no daily cap"` (the wording `handleRoleNotes` uses for notes, src/gui/gui-operator-commands.ts), because the cap exempts the director (`role-view.ts`'s `role !== DIRECTOR_ROLE` guard). Screen the value with `checkDailyBudgetUsd(value, "maxDailyCostUsdPerRole." + baseRoleOf(role))` (src/roles/loop-ids.ts maps `feature-2` → `feature`, the map's key; a custom or bare id is the identity), then write through the CLI's own dotted-key path: `setConfigKey(root, "maxDailyCostUsdPerRole." + baseRoleOf(role), JSON.stringify(value))`, so the per-key validator and whole-config `validateConfig` (which rejects an unknown role id) own the final truth. Answer `{ ok: true, role: baseRoleOf(role), maxDailyCostUsd }`; a write failure is `configKeyError`'s 400 exactly as `handleConfigSet` reports it. `setConfigKey` already imports cleanly; add the `baseRoleOf` and `DIRECTOR_ROLE` imports.
- **Wire:** add `handleRoleCap` to the export in src/gui/gui-endpoint-commands.ts and the route `"POST /api/role-cap"` beside `"POST /api/budget"` in src/gui/gui-server.ts.
- **Drawer — src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts:**
  - Add `let capEditing = null; // { role, value }` beside `noteEditing`, with `startCapEdit(role, capUsd)` / `stopCapEdit()` that set it and call `repaintDrawerRole()`, the Notes editor's shape. Also clear `capEditing` in `closeDrawer`.
  - In `drawerConfigHtml`, for a non-director role render a Daily cap row **always** (today it appears only when the payload carries `dailyCap`): with `dailyCap`, today's read-only sentence plus an `Edit cap` button; without one, `<dd>no cap</dd>` plus a `Set a cap` button. While `capEditing && capEditing.role === role`, render instead an `<input id='capeditinput' type='number' min='0' step='0.01'>` prefilled with the cap (empty for none) and `Save`/`Discard` buttons, mirroring the Notes editor's `data-act` markup. A director shows no row (`canEdit`'s existing rule).
- **Boot dispatch — gui-client-boot.ts's `runAct`:** add `cap-edit` (`startCapEdit(arg, drawerRole?.view?.dailyCap?.capUsd ?? 0)`), `cap-discard` (`stopCapEdit()`), and `cap-save`: read `#capeditinput`, apply the team editor's `badInput` guard and `parseBudgetField` (both in scope from the operator blob, concatenated earlier), `showFlash("error: " + error)` and post nothing on an invalid field, else `postAction("/api/role-cap", { role: arg, maxDailyCostUsd: value }, (d) => { capEditing = null; loadDrawerRole(arg); return value > 0 ? "Daily cap set to " + fmtCap(value) : "Daily cap removed"; })` — the team editor's flash wording (src/ui/gui/gui-client-operator.ts `saveBudget`).
- **docs/cli.md:** in the `tumwater role <id>` row, extend the clause that says the dashboard's role drawer "edits or clears the notes" to say it also sets the role's daily cap (`maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.<role>`).

**Files touched.**

### Notes command, part 1/4: A `tumwater-notes` command writes a run's own role note, and every run finds it on its PATH (planned 2026-10-17 by user; design in plans/notes-command.md "The `tumwater-notes` command" and "Reaching it from a run"; touches src/notes-cli.ts (new) src/agent/notes-shim.ts (new) src/agent/run-agent.ts src/process/run-marker.ts src/paths.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts package.json and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Give every backend the same way to write a role's notes: a shell command, `tumwater-notes`, that acts only on the note `TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH` names. Today each backend has its own carrier: a pi extension, and an MCP server for Claude Code and for OpenCode.
This part only adds the command and puts it on every run's PATH. Nothing tells a model to use it until part 2/4.

**Approach.**
- **src/notes-cli.ts** (new, `#!/usr/bin/env node` like src/cli.ts, `// vocabulary: plain`), with a second bin entry in package.json: `"tumwater-notes": "dist/src/notes-cli.js"`.
  - `write` replaces the note with stdin (read to EOF); `write --file <path>` uses that file instead.
  - `show` prints the current note; a missing note prints nothing.
  - `clear` empties the note.
  - It validates and writes through `validateRoleNote` / `writeRoleNote` (src/agent/role-notes-write.ts): the same 4 KB cap and atomic write as the existing carriers.
  - Success prints `notes saved (<n> bytes)` or `notes cleared`, and exits 0.
  - `write` with empty input exits 1: "nothing to write — use `tumwater-notes clear` to empty the note". A heredoc that lost its body must not wipe the note.
  - An over-cap note exits 1 with `validateRoleNote`'s message.
  - No `TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH` exits 1: "this run keeps no notes".
  - Anything else exits 2 with a three-line usage.
  - The note path comes only from the env, never from an argument.
- **src/paths.ts:**
  - Move `teamRootOf(sessionDir)` here from src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts, exported, and make the adapter import it.
  - Add `notesShimDir(root)` = `<tumwater dir>/bin`.
- **src/agent/notes-shim.ts** (new): `ensureNotesShim(root)` writes `<tumwater dir>/bin/tumwater-notes`, the two-line `sh` script `exec "<process.execPath>" "<dist>/src/notes-cli.js" "$@"`.
  - `<dist>` is resolved from this module's own URL, as src/pi/pi-args.ts resolves the bundled extensions, so a staged build points at its own copy.
  - It is written atomically with mode 0755, only when the content differs.
  - It returns the directory.
- **src/process/run-marker.ts:** `agentBaseEnv(marker, base, binDir?)` prepends `binDir` to `PATH` when given.
- **src/agent/run-agent.ts:** before building the invocation, call `ensureNotesShim(teamRootOf(sessionDir))`. Hand the dir to the backend through a new optional `AgentRunSpec.binDir`; the pi, Claude Code and OpenCode adapters pass it to `agentBaseEnv`.
  - A failure to write the shim logs one warning, and the run goes on without it.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/notes-cli.ts (new), src/agent/notes-shim.ts (new), src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/agent/agent-backend.ts, src/pi/pi-backend.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-backend.ts, src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts, src/process/run-marker.ts, src/paths.ts, package.json.
- Tests: test/notes-cli.test.ts (new), test/notes-shim.test.ts (new), test/run-marker.test.ts, test/opencode-run.test.ts, test/claude-run.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **`tumwater-notes`, run as a child process with a temp `TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH`:**
  - `write` from stdin saves the note and prints its byte count.
  - `write --file` saves the file's text.
  - `show` prints it back.
  - `clear` empties it.
  - Empty stdin exits 1 and leaves the old note in place.
  - A 4097-byte note exits 1 and leaves the old note in place.

  - An unknown subcommand exits 2.

  - It writes an executable script whose run of `show` prints the note.

  - A different dist path rewrites it.
- **Runs:** a run through each backend's fake (pi, Claude Code, OpenCode) has `<tumwater dir>/bin` first on its env's `PATH`.

### The day report and Usage view tally deferred runs by reason (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the "provider contention" row touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts and the `tumwater doctor` Audit row of docs/cli.md, and OpenCode 6b/7 and 6d/7 touch src/pi, src/gates, src/status and src/agent/opencode, none of them src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts or src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts (this plan's docs/cli.md edit is the `tumwater report` row, a different row from that plan's Audit row); touches src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts, test/report-data.test.ts, test/report.test.ts, test/gui-client-report.test.ts and docs/cli.md) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** A due maintenance tick that stands down logs `run_deferred` with a reason (`DeferReason` in src/scheduling/scheduling.ts: `"backlog"`, `"no-work"`, `"plans-full"`), and the event feed, live status cell and failure digest each render that reason. No report tallies them, so an operator reading `tumwater report` or the dashboard Usage view sees a day's runs, tokens, cost, rejections and fallbacks but not how many maintenance ticks deferred, nor why — an idle day reads the same whether the backlog was open, nothing had merged, or the plan target was met. Tally each day's `run_deferred` events by reason and show them beside the other per-role breakdowns.

**Approach.**
- **src/report/report-data.ts:** add `deferredByReason: Record<string, number>` to `UsageFold` (~line 44) and `DayFold` (~line 231), and initialize `deferredByReason: {}` in `dayFoldFor` (~line 354) and in `collectReportSince`'s `acc` (~line 666) — those are the only two fold constructors. In `foldUsageEvent`, add a branch after the `image_reroute` one: `else if (ev.type === "run_deferred") { const reason = ev.reason === "backlog" || ev.reason === "plans-full" ? ev.reason : "no-work"; addTo(target.deferredByReason, reason, 1); }`. A missing, foreign or torn `reason` folds as `no-work`, the same fallback `deferredReasonText` (src/events/event-format.ts) applies in the feed, so the tally and the feed agree on `no-work`'s meaning; bucketing by the raw code keeps the collector free of a presentation import and lets the render print the code the event carried, as `Runs by model` prints raw selectors. Add `deferredByReason?: Record<string, number>` to `ReportDay` (set only when a day has deferrals, zero-means-absent) and to `SinceReport` (absent when empty, like `notionalByRole`). In `collectReport`'s team branch, after the `runsByModel` assignment, add `if (Object.keys(fold.deferredByReason).length > 0) day.deferredByReason = fold.deferredByReason;`; the role branch leaves it unset (a reason is not a role). In `collectReportSince`, compute `const deferred = scopedByRole(acc.deferredByReason, base);` and spread `...(Object.keys(deferred).length > 0 ? { deferredByReason: deferred } : {})` — `scopedByRole` empties a role-scoped window (no reason code is a role), the same team-only rule `runsByModel` follows.
- **src/report/report-render.ts:** in `renderReportMarkdown`, after the `Image reroutes by role` line, add `const deferred = rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.deferredByReason ?? {}).filter(([, n]) => n > 0); if (data.role === undefined && deferred.length > 0) lines.push(rankedRoleLine("Deferred runs by reason", deferred, String));`. In `renderSinceReportMarkdown`, the same line from `rankedRoleMap(data.deferredByReason ?? {}).filter(([, n]) => n > 0)`, gated on `data.role === undefined`. A deferral-free window prints no line, so its output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts:** add `reportDeferredOrder(data)` beside `reportModelOrder` (window totals per reason code, count desc then name asc, `Object.hasOwn` reads/seeds like `reportModelOrder`), `chartDeferredByReason(data)` calling `stackChart(data, reportDeferredOrder(data), "deferredByReason", (n) => plural(n, "deferral"), countAxis, true)` beside `chartRunsByModel`, and one block in the Usage render chain, gated like the model chart: `(!d.role && seriesHasAny(d, "deferredByReason") ? block("Deferred runs by reason", chartDeferredByReason(d), "per day · backlog, no-work, plans-full") : "")`. The reason codes are the legend labels, as raw provider keys and model selectors already are.
- **docs/cli.md:** in the `tumwater report` row, after the `image reroutes (image_reroute hops to a tier that can read images)` clause, insert `, and deferred maintenance ticks tallied as ``Deferred runs by reason`` by the `run_deferred` event's reason (`backlog`, `no-work` or `plans-full`; team report only)` (wording may be tightened; keep it one clause in that row).

### The dashboards and `tumwater status` name a standing provider failure hold (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; the doctor `provider hold` row landed 2026-10-14 and the plan that added it said no status surface names the hold, so this closes that half — `grep -rn "rate_limit\|teamHold" src/status src/ui` is empty; independent of the eligible report plans (no src/report, src/ui/gui or src/ui/tui file) and of OpenCode 7/7 (src/doctor, src/agent/opencode); it shares src/gates/gate-polls.ts and src/status/status-data.ts with the in-flight OpenCode 6b/7, which touches src/gates and src/status, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms code run part 19/20 also reaches src/status, src/team, src/gates and src/orchestrator, far behind part 1/20; touches src/team/team-hold.ts, src/team/orchestrator-info.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/team-alerts.ts, test/team-hold.test.ts, test/orchestrator-info.test.ts, test/status-data-team.test.ts and test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** When a provider storms — two roles' runs end on the same provider and failure kind inside a short window — `pollTeamHold` (src/team/team-polls.ts) opens a per-provider hold, logs one `rate_limit_hold` event, and the roles on that provider start no new ticks until it re-opens. Three surfaces name it today: the event feed, the failure digest, and `tumwater doctor`'s `provider hold` row. The live status snapshot, the dashboard alert banners, the TUI attention lines and `status --json` say nothing, so an operator watching idle loops with no log open sees no reason for them. Publish each provider's standing failure hold in the orchestrator info file and raise one team alert naming it, the way the disk, maintenance and quiet holds are named.

**Approach.**
- **src/team/team-hold.ts:** add `standingHolds(holds: ReadonlyMap<string | undefined, TeamHold>): Array<{ provider?: string; until: number; kind: HoldKind }>`, the structured sibling of `heldProviders`: iterate the map, skip an entry whose `until` is null (a lifted hold kept only for relapse memory) and one whose `kind` is `"subscription-window"` (that hold already has the snapshot's `claudeWindow` block and its header badge), and emit `{ ...(provider !== undefined ? { provider } : {}), until, kind }`, sorted by provider name so two reads of one map agree. `undefined` provider means pi's default backend, the same meaning `heldProviders` gives it, so it is omitted from the JSON rather than written as null.
- **src/team/orchestrator-info.ts:** add `providerHolds?: Array<{ provider?: string; until: number; kind: string }>` to `OrchestratorInfo`, documented as the standing per-provider failure holds, absent while none stands. Validate it in `normalizeInfoFields` the way `disk` is validated: drop the field when it is not an array, and drop each entry that is not an object with a finite `until` and a string `kind`, or whose `provider` is present but not a string, keeping the well-formed siblings.
- **src/gates/gate-polls.ts:** right after `states.teamHold = pollTeamHold(...)`, compute `const providerHolds = standingHolds(states.teamHold);` and `publishInfoFields(root, info, [["providerHolds", providerHolds.length > 0 ? providerHolds : undefined]]);` — the `chain`/`disk` omit-when-empty idiom, so an open team leaves the file untouched and a change writes once.
- **src/status/status-data.ts:** add `providerHolds?: OrchestratorInfo["providerHolds"]` to `StatusSnapshot` (documented, like `chain`), and in the returned object beside `chain` add `...(running && info?.providerHolds && info.providerHolds.length > 0 ? { providerHolds: info.providerHolds } : {})`, so the field appears exactly while a live orchestrator publishes a standing hold.
- **src/ui/team-alerts.ts:** add `"providerHolds"` to the `Pick` and, after the maintenance-allowance alert, push one blue (self-clearing, no operator action — the quiet and maintenance alerts' tone) `provider-hold` alert when `snap.providerHolds` is non-empty: title `Provider limit is holding new runs` / `Provider limits are holding new runs` (via `plural`), detail naming each hold as `<provider or "pi's default backend"> (<kind>) until it re-opens in <humanSeconds(secondsUntil(until, now))>` joined by `"; "`, then `Runs in progress finish; roles on a held provider start no new runs until it re-opens.`, `actions: []`. Import `humanSeconds` and `secondsUntil` from `../text/datetime.js`. Both observer surfaces read it for free: the dashboard ships `alerts` from `status-payload.ts` and the TUI draws them with `alertLines`.

### The day report and Usage view tally merge failures by reason (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the blocked plain-terms series and of OpenCode 6b/7 and 6d/7, which touch src/pi, src/gates, src/status and src/agent/opencode; it shares src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and the `tumwater report` row of docs/cli.md with the eligible "deferred runs by reason" plan, so whichever lands second rebases) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every `merge_failed` event carries the tick result that produced it (`result`, a `TickResult` from src/tick/tick-outcome.ts: `rejected` for a review rejection, `merge_conflict`, `merge_blocked` for a failed fast-forward, `aborted` for a shutdown, and so on), and `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) always logs it. The report folds those events into `mergeFailed` and `mergeFailedByRole` only, so the day report and `--since` say how many merges failed and which authoring roles wrote them, never *why* — an operator cannot tell a review rejection (fix the change) from a conflict or a block (rebase) from a shutdown abort (capacity). The failure digest's "Merge failures" section (src/failure/failure-data.ts `mergeFailureSection`) clusters only `merge_blocked`/`merge_conflict` in a transient window; the report's permanent per-day record has no reason breakdown. Tally each window's `merge_failed` events by `result` and render them beside "Merge failures by role".

**Approach.**
- **src/report/report-data.ts:** add `mergeFailedByReason: Record<string, number>` beside `mergeFailedByRole` in `UsageFold` and `DayFold`, and initialize `mergeFailedByReason: {}` beside each `mergeFailedByRole: {}` (the two fold constructors, `dayFoldFor` and `collectReportSince`'s `acc`). In `foldUsageEvent`'s `merge_done`/`merge_failed` branch, in the `else` that already does `addTo(target.mergeFailedByRole, role, 1)`, also `addTo(target.mergeFailedByReason, typeof ev.result === "string" && ev.result.length > 0 ? ev.result : "unknown", 1)` (a module-local `const reason = ...` reads better; a legacy event with no `result` folds under `unknown`, so the buckets always sum to `mergeFailed`). Add `mergeFailedByReason?: Record<string, number>` to `ReportDay` beside `mergeFailedByRole?` (zero-means-absent). In `collectReport`'s team branch, after the `mergeFailedByRole` assignment, add `if (Object.keys(fold.mergeFailedByReason).length > 0) day.mergeFailedByReason = fold.mergeFailedByReason;`; the role branch leaves it unset (merge runs are the merge slot's). In `collectReportSince`, add `mergeFailedByReason: scopedByRole(acc.mergeFailedByReason, base)` beside `mergeFailedByRole` (always present, empty for a role scope — a result code is not a role), and add the same field to `SinceReport` with a doc comment mirroring `mergeFailedByRole`'s.
- **src/report/report-render.ts:** in the day render's `if (data.role === undefined)` merge block (beside the `Merge failures by role` line), add `const mergeFailureReasons = rankedRoleMap(data.mergeFailedByReason ?? {}).filter(([, n]) => n > 0); if (mergeFailureReasons.length > 0) lines.push(rankedRoleLine("Merge failures by reason", mergeFailureReasons, String));`. In the `--since` render's matching block, the same line from `rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.mergeFailedByReason ?? {})`. Both reuse `rankedRoleLine`/`rankedRoleMap`/`rankedRoleTotals` (rank count desc then name asc); a reason-free window prints no line, so its output is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts:** add `reportMergeFailureOrder(data)` beside `reportModelOrder` (window totals per reason code, count desc then name asc, `Object.hasOwn` reads/seeds like `reportModelOrder`), `chartMergeFailuresByReason(data)` calling `stackChart(data, reportMergeFailureOrder(data), "mergeFailedByReason", (n) => plural(n, "merge failure"), countAxis, true)` beside `chartMergeFailuresByRole`, and one block in the Usage render chain after the "Merge failures by role" block: `(seriesHasAny(d, "mergeFailedByReason") ? block("Merge failures by reason", chartMergeFailuresByReason(d)) : "")`.
- **docs/cli.md:** in the `tumwater report` row, after the `image reroutes (image_reroute hops to a tier that can read images)` clause, insert `, and merge failures tallied as `Merge failures by reason` by each `merge_failed`'s result (a review rejection, a conflict, a blocked fast-forward or a shutdown abort; team report only)` (wording may be tightened; keep it one clause in that row).

### OpenCode backend, part 7/7: Doctor checks the OpenCode install, models and leaks; session retention; docs; and an opt-in `smoke:opencode` live check (planned 2026-10-17 by user; revised 2026-10-17 by user after the live probe; requires parts 6b/7, 6c/7 and 6d/7 landed; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "Sessions", "Spend, free-ness, image input and doctor" and "Hand steps"; touches src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts src/agent/session-ledger.ts src/orchestrator/retention.ts docs/backends.md docs/config.md scripts/smoke-opencode.mjs (new) package.json and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Before any OpenCode run starts, `tumwater doctor` says everything that would make one fail or leak:

- an OpenCode that is missing, V1, or too old;
- a model OpenCode does not know;
- a provider with no credential;
- the operator's global opencode config, which still loads into team runs.

The team's OpenCode sessions and spill files are pruned like its other session files. docs/backends.md explains the backend and the free model's catch. `npm run smoke:opencode` re-verifies the exact production invocation against the real CLI.

**Approach.**
- **Doctor**, when any model job routes to opencode:
  - **Version** (src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts): parse `opencode --version` (`opencode v2.0.32`).
    - A 1.x version fails, naming `brew install opencode`.
    - Below `OPENCODE_MIN_VERSION` = `2.0.32` (a constant in src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts, the H1-verified version) fails.
  - **Models:** each model is in the catalog cache, with "free" or its per-M prices and its context window.
    - An unknown model fails.
    - A thinking level the model has no effort for is noted as dropped.
    - A non-gateway provider (`opencode/anthropic/…`) warns unless `opencode auth list --format json` (bounded) lists it.
  - **Leaks:** the operator's global opencode config files and `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`. Each of these warns, naming the file and key:
    - an MCP server (disabled for team runs);
    - a `plugin`, `agent` or `instructions` entry;
    - the AGENTS.md file.
  - **Sizes:** `.tumwater/opencode/opencode.db`, and the shell spill dir for this repo's root commit (`~/.local/share/opencode/shell/<root commit>/`, finding 17).
- **Retention:** the session pruning that applies `sessionRetentionDays`:
  - also runs `opencode session delete <id> --standalone` (bounded) for each OpenCode ledger record older than the window;
  - deletes spill files older than the window in this repo's spill dir.
- **docs/backends.md:** a new "OpenCode (`opencode/…` model ids)" section:
  - the config from plans/opencode-backend.md "Goal";
  - the free model's catch: OpenCode's own client only, no login, time-limited, intermittent refusals that move work to the fallback;
  - Go, which pi already reaches as `opencode-go/…`;
  - what tumwater turns off and denies, and why `read` must stay allowed;
  - role notes ride the role-notes MCP server; a run's first model request cannot see MCP tools (upstream issues 51812 and 56240), and notes are written at a run's end, after that;
  - XDG left alone, and why;
  - where sessions and spill files live.
- **docs/config.md:** `backends.opencode`, `TUMWATER_OPENCODE_BIN` and `maxConcurrentPerProvider.opencode`.
- **scripts/smoke-opencode.mjs** (`npm run smoke:opencode`, **not in `npm test`**), the twin of scripts/smoke-claude.mjs. It drives the real `opencode` through the compiled `runAgent`, in a throwaway git repo:
  - a three-step run on `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` that reads, edits and checks a file;
  - a resume of that session that recalls something from the first run;
  - a SIGTERM during a long `node` shell command, then a check that no marked process survives;
  - a run carrying a notes file that reads a file and runs a command, then saves a role note before it ends; the notes file must then hold the note. This is the real usage pattern, and it is the guard on OpenCode's MCP timing (finding 21);
  - checks that the run's tokens came from `run_usage` (the export) and its cost is 0, and that the catalog cache calls the model free.

  It prints a named PASS or FAIL for each check and exits nonzero on the first failure. A free-tier 403 gets its own FAIL line saying the gate refused the exact production invocation, so a stricter gate is seen here before the team sees it.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts, src/agent/session-ledger.ts, src/orchestrator/retention.ts.
- Scripts: scripts/smoke-opencode.mjs (new), package.json.
- Docs: docs/backends.md, docs/config.md.
- Tests: test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/session-ledger.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **Doctor with a fake `opencode`:**
  - `opencode v1.19.3` fails, naming the install command.
  - `opencode v2.0.31` fails; `opencode v2.0.32` passes.
  - A model missing from the catalog fails, and the free model reads "free".
  - A non-gateway model with no listed credential warns.
  - A temp HOME whose `.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` has an MCP server and an `instructions` entry gets one warning naming both.
  - A pi-only config shows no opencode rows.
- **Pruning:** with an OpenCode ledger record older than the window, pruning calls the fake's `session delete` with its id, and leaves a fresh one alone.
- `npm run smoke:opencode` exists, includes the end-of-run note check, and is not reachable from `npm test`.
- `npm test` passes.

### The "provider contention" doctor row names every provider key that waited, not just the busiest (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the provider-wait median plan touches src/report, src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and the report tests, and OpenCode 6b/7 and 6d/7 touch src/pi, src/gates, src/status and src/agent/opencode, none of them src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts or its test (the blocked OpenCode 7/7 does edit src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts for its install/models/leaks checks, so whichever lands second rebases); touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts and docs/cli.md) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor`'s "provider contention" row (`checkProviderContention`, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) already sums the last 24 h of `provider_wait` events into `perKey` totals — one bucket per `ev.key`, plus a key-less bucket for the team cap — but its detail renders only the single largest bucket ("…(the omlx slot)") and, on a warn, advises raising only that one cap. On a team mixing providers (a headline feature: `maxConcurrentPerProvider` caps each key), a second contended key and its cap are invisible: the operator raises `omlx` and the other provider keeps parking runs. Name every bucket that waited, ranked, and advise each key with a configured cap.

**Approach.**
- **src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts `checkProviderContention`:** after the existing `perKey` loop and the `if (count === 0)` return, rank the buckets: `const ranked = [...perKey.entries()].map(([key, total]) => ({ key, total })).sort((a, b) => b.total - a.total || a.key.localeCompare(b.key));` (ties break on key name, so the detail is deterministic). Add local helpers `const bucketLabel = (key: string) => (key === "" ? "the run cap" : `the ${key} slot`);` and a bucket cell `${bucketLabel(key)} ${shortSpanPhrase(total)}`.
- **The parenthetical:** one bucket keeps today's exact wording, `(${bucketLabel(ranked[0].key)})`, so a single-provider team's row is unchanged. With two or more, print the busiest first and the rest as "also": `(${cells[0]}, also ${cells.slice(1).join(", ")})` — e.g. `(the omlx slot 4m, also the run cap 60s)`.
- **The warn advice:** replace the single `bestKey` clause (and the `let bestKey`/`bestTotal` scan that fed it) with one clause per ranked bucket that is keyed and has a configured cap, in rank order: `raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.${key} above ${cap}` for `config?.maxConcurrentPerProvider?.[key] !== undefined`, joined with ` and ` and appended as `` ` — ${advice}` `` when `total >= PROVIDER_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS`. The key-less bucket never gets advice, exactly as today. Keep the `longest` phrase, the count, the total, the thresholds and the read-error branch (`okOutcome("could not read the event log for provider waits: …")`) as they are.
- **Doc comment:** update the function's comment (lines naming "the key of the largest per-key wait total") to say it names every key that waited, busiest first, and each key's cap to raise.
- **docs/cli.md:** the `tumwater doctor` Audit row's clause `provider slots that runs waited for, calling for a larger maxConcurrentPerProvider` becomes `provider slots that runs waited for, naming each provider key that waited and calling for a larger maxConcurrentPerProvider`.

**Files touched.** Source: src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts. Docs: docs/cli.md. Tests: test/doctor-checks.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Extend "`checkProviderContention` sums the last day of `provider_wait` events and warns at ten minutes": its two-bucket ok case now reads `…longest 4m (the omlx slot 4m, also the run cap 60s)`; after the third wait pushes it to `warn`, the detail still names `raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.omlx above 2` when the config carries `{ omlx: 2 }`.
- A new case with waits on two keyed providers under a warn (e.g. `maxConcurrentPerProvider: { omlx: 2, acme: 1 }`, totals over the threshold) asserts the detail ranks the busier bucket first and names both `raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.omlx above 2` and `raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.acme above 1`.
- A waits-on-one-key case keeps the single-bucket wording `(the omlx slot)` (no `also`); a wait whose key has no configured cap contributes its bucket cell but no advice clause; the zero-wait case still reads `no provider waits`.
- `npm test` passes.

### The team alert banner names the per-role daily-cap hold and the maintenance-allowance hold, so an operator sees why roles are idling without reading every row (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the two eligible Planned entries — the OpenCode 6a/7 plan touches src/agent/opencode/ and src/paths.ts, and the day-report model plan touches src/report/ and src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts — while this touches only src/ui/team-alerts.ts; the blocked plain-terms series renames `AlertLoop`→`AlertRole` in the same file, so whichever merges second rebases; touches src/ui/team-alerts.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every hold the scheduler enforces has a per-row label in the status table, but only some reach the team's alert banner — `teamAlerts` in src/ui/team-alerts.ts is the one source behind the dashboard's alert band, the TUI's attention lines and the `tumwater status` banner (src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts and src/ui/tui/tui.tsx all call it with the whole snapshot). Two holds stop whole roles and never produce a banner today: a role over its `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` cap (`snap.capPaused`; an idle loop's own row reads `waiting: daily cap spent`, src/ui/status-model.ts) and the maintenance allowance (`snap.maintenanceQuota.held`; an idle loop reads `waiting: maintenance allowance used <used>/<allowance>`). An operator watching roles sit idle gets no team-level explanation, unlike the team budget, the disk floor, the quiet-hours window and the rate-limit hold, which each already have one. Add one alert for each hold.

**Approach.**
- `teamAlerts`'s `Pick<StatusSnapshot, …>` (src/ui/team-alerts.ts) gains `"capPaused"` and `"maintenanceQuota"`; both are required on the snapshot, so no other signature change and no caller changes.
- Right after the budget block, when `snap.capPaused.length > 0`, push a `role-cap` alert: tone `"amber"` (it asks for a raise); title names the held roles through `listRoleIds` and agrees the verb — `${listRoleIds(snap.capPaused)} is over its daily cap` / `… are over their daily caps` — so the banner names who is held, not just how many; detail names the held loops and says they start no new runs until local midnight, and that raising `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` resumes them; actions `openRoleActions(<those loops>)` so the dashboard buttons open each paused role, the `openRoleActions` shape the failing and stuck alerts already use. Build the loop slice with `loops.filter((l) => snap.capPaused.includes(l.role))` — the `snap.capPaused.includes(s.role)` predicate status-model.ts already uses — and fall back to the raw ids through `listRoleIds` if a stale id matches no loop.
- Right after the quiet-hours block, when `snap.maintenanceQuota.held.length > 0`, push a `maintenance` alert: tone `"gray"` (by design and self-clearing, not something the operator acts on — the quiet alert's tone, not the amber failed/refused ones); title `Maintenance is held at its rolling allowance`; detail gives `snap.maintenanceQuota.used` of `snap.maintenanceQuota.allowance` of the maintenance allowance used (not commits — `used` also counts in-flight maintenance loops) over the last 24 h, names the held loops, and says they resume as work merges (the verb agrees: `resumes`/`resume`); no actions.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/team-alerts.test.ts`'s `base` gains `capPaused: []` and `maintenanceQuota: { allowance: 0, used: 0, held: [] }`, and `teamAlerts(base, [], [], now)` still yields no alerts.
- `teamAlerts({ ...base, capPaused: ["feature"] }, [], [{ role: "feature", phase: "idle: daily cap spent", errorStreak: false, inFlight: false }], now)` yields one alert with key `role-cap`, tone `amber`, a title naming `feature`, a detail containing `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` and `midnight`, and an action `{ label: "Open feature", act: "role", arg: "feature" }`; a snapshot with `capPaused: []` has no `role-cap` alert.
- `teamAlerts({ ...base, maintenanceQuota: { allowance: 3, used: 3, held: ["organize", "clean"] } }, [], [<organize loop>, <clean loop>], now)` yields one alert with key `maintenance`, tone `gray`, a detail containing `3 of 3` and both role names; a `held: []` snapshot has no `maintenance` alert. `alertNeedsYou` is true for `role-cap` and false for `maintenance`.

### OpenCode backend, part 6a/7: The models.dev catalog fetch, parse and cache answer whether an OpenCode model is free (planned 2026-10-17 by user; revised 2026-10-17 by user after the live probe; split 2026-10-17 by the plan role from part 6/7 into parts 6a/7–6d/7; requires part 5b/7 landed; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "Spend, free-ness, image input and doctor" and "Findings, verified live" 9, 10; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts (new) src/paths.ts test/opencode-catalog.test.ts (new)) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The data half of OpenCode free-ness, with no seam wired yet: a bounded fetch of the catalog OpenCode itself caches, a parse that keeps only the models the config routes through OpenCode, a cache that survives a failed fetch, and `opencodeModelFree(cache, model)` as the one predicate part 6b/7's seam reads.

**Approach.**
- **src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts (new):**
  - `fetchOpencodeCatalog()` GETs `https://models.dev/api.json`, bounded at 30 s (finding 10); V2's `opencode models` prints ids only.
  - `parseOpencodeCatalog(body, providers)` keeps the `opencode` provider plus any provider the config routes through OpenCode (`opencode/<provider>/…`). For each model it records: `free` (input and output cost both 0); `inputPerM`, `outputPerM`; `context` (`limit.context`); `images` (`modalities.input` includes `"image"`); `efforts` (the `values` of the `reasoning_options` entry with `type: "effort"`).

It is refreshed when older than 24 h or when `opencode --version` changed; a failed fetch keeps the old cache and logs one warning; `billedAt` survives a refresh.
  - `opencodeModelFree(cache, model)` = `free && billedAt === undefined`; a model missing from the cache is not free.

### A role run that waits for a provider slot is recorded, and `tumwater doctor`'s new "provider contention" row sums those waits and names the binding key, so `maxConcurrentPerProvider` can be sized from real waits (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — OpenCode part 6a/7 touches src/agent/opencode/ and src/paths.ts, and the blocked plain-terms series is refused — while this touches src/events/, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts and src/doctor/; touches src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-labels.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, docs/how-it-works.md, test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/event-format.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Worktree-pool contention is already measured and surfaced: `logSlotWait` (`src/git/worktree-pool.ts`) logs a `slot_wait` event when a pooled lease waits `SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_MS` (30 s) or more, and `checkWorktreePool` (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) sums the last 24 h and warns at 10 minutes, naming the number to raise `worktreeSlots` above. Provider-slot contention is not: a role tick's admission parks on `Semaphore.acquireLease` (`src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts`), the live status shows `awaiting <key> slot` while it parks, but once the tick starts the wait leaves no record. `grep -rn "provider_wait\|provider contention\|permit wait" src test` finds nothing, and `checkProviderConcurrency` only audits the caps for typos, unused keys and non-binding values. So an operator cannot tell whether `maxConcurrentPerProvider` (or `maxConcurrent`) is the binding limit or is set too high. This plan records one `provider_wait` event per role-tick admission that waited 30 s or more, and adds a `provider contention` doctor row that sums the last 24 h and warns at 10 minutes, naming the key and the cap to raise.

**Approach.**
- **src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts:**
  - Add `export const PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS = 30_000;` beside `ROLE_TICK_DURATION_SAMPLES`, with a comment mirroring `SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_MS` in src/git/worktree-pool.ts: the wait threshold below which no event is logged, so a tick that starts at once stays silent.
  - `LaunchContext` gains an optional `providerWaitMs?: number` — the test seam mirroring `breakerNow`, documented as such; the launch reads `ctx.providerWaitMs ?? PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS`.
  - In the `usesSlot` tick closure, hoist the key the acquire already computes once (`const key = cfg ? seamConcurrencyKey(cfg, piDefault) : undefined;`), wrap the acquire in `const admittedAt = Date.now();`, keep the existing `lease = await semaphore.acquireLease(roleTier(runner.role), key);`, and immediately after it, when `Date.now() - admittedAt >= providerWaitMs`, `logEventBestEffort(ctx.root, { source: TUMWATER_SOURCE, type: "provider_wait", role: runner.role, waitedMs: Date.now() - admittedAt, ...(key !== undefined ? { key } : {}) })`. Add `TUMWATER_SOURCE` to the existing `../events/events.js` import (it already imports `logEventBestEffort`). Measure only the admission await — the role tick's own wait; re-key waits (`ensureProviderLease`) and the merge/verify leases (`merge-drain.ts`, `merge-pipeline.ts`) are out of scope, so this is one signal in one place, not a change to the semaphore.
  - A tick admitted at once logs nothing, even with `providerWaitMs` at its default; the event is written best-effort like the launch pass's other events, so an unwritable log never blocks a start.
- **src/events/events.ts:** add the union member `"provider_wait" // a role tick's semaphore admission waited PROVIDER_WAIT_EVENT_MS or more for its provider/team slot; carries role, waitedMs, and key when the tick's authoring seam has one (orchestrator-launch.ts) — the signal to raise maxConcurrentPerProvider or maxConcurrent`.
- **src/events/event-labels.ts:** `provider_wait: "waited for a provider slot"`. The `Record<HarnessEvent["type"], string>` type makes the compiler demand this, so the family cannot ship half-labelled.
- **src/events/event-format.ts:** a `case "provider_wait"` beside `slot_wait`, routine-with-explanation and with no warning prefix: `` return `waited ${shortSpanPhrase(finiteNumber(e.waitedMs, 0))} for a ${typeof e.key === "string" && e.key.length > 0 ? `${e.key} slot` : "run slot"} (${textOr(e.role)})` ``. (`finiteNumber`, `shortSpanPhrase` and `textOr` are the helpers the `slot_wait` case already uses.)
- **src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts:** next to the slot-wait constants, add `PROVIDER_WAIT_CHECK_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 3600_000` and `PROVIDER_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS = 10 * 60_000`, then `export function checkProviderContention(root: string, config: TumwaterConfig | undefined, now = Date.now()): CheckOutcome` modelled on `checkWorktreePool`'s slot-wait half: `readEventsSince(root, PROVIDER_WAIT_CHECK_WINDOW_MS).events`, keep `ev.type === "provider_wait" && ev.ts >= now - PROVIDER_WAIT_CHECK_WINDOW_MS`; with none return `okOutcome("no provider waits")`; otherwise count them, total `finiteNumber(ev.waitedMs, 0)`, and find the largest total per key (the key-less bucket reads "the run cap"). Detail: `` `${plural(count, "wait")} for a provider slot in the last 24h, ${shortSpanPhrase(total)} total, longest ${shortSpanPhrase(longestMs)} (${keyLabel})` ``, appending `` ` — raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.${key} above ${cap}` `` (the cap from `config?.maxConcurrentPerProvider?.[key]`, omitted when absent or key-less) when `total >= PROVIDER_WAIT_WARN_TOTAL_MS`, which also makes the row `warnOutcome`. A read throw pushes `could not read the event log for provider waits: ${errorMessage(err)}` and leaves the level unchanged, like the slot-wait branch.
- **src/doctor/doctor.ts:** register `{ name: "provider contention", ...checkProviderContention(root, config) }` immediately after the existing `{ name: "provider concurrency", … }` row.
- **docs/how-it-works.md** §Scheduling's `maxConcurrentPerProvider` bullet: after the sentence naming the key, add that a run whose admission waits 30 s or more for its slot logs a `provider_wait` event, and `tumwater doctor`'s "provider contention" row sums the last 24 h and warns at 10 minutes, naming the key to raise.
- **docs/cli.md**'s `tumwater doctor` Audit row: add "provider slots that runs waited for, calling for a larger `maxConcurrentPerProvider`" to the list of what doctor names.

**Files touched.** Source: src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-labels.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts. Docs: docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md. Tests: test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/event-format.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts`: a due role whose config keys to `omlx` and a real `new Semaphore(1)` whose only permit another `acquireLease` already holds — with `providerWaitMs: 0` in the test's ctx — logs exactly one `provider_wait` event (read back through `readEvents`/`eventsOfType`) carrying `role` and `key: "omlx"`, with `waitedMs >= 0`; the same launch against an unheld semaphore (default `providerWaitMs`) logs none; a director launch (`forceLease`, never waiting) logs none.
- `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, beside the "`checkWorktreePool` sums the last day of `slot_wait` events and warns at ten minutes" test: synthetic `provider_wait` events (`role`, `key`, `waitedMs`) totalling under 10 minutes read ok; totalling at or above it warn and the detail names the key and, with a config carrying `maxConcurrentPerProvider: { omlx: 2 }`, the `raise maxConcurrentPerProvider.omlx above 2` clause; an empty log reads ok with `no provider waits`.
- `test/event-format.test.ts`: `formatEvent` over a keyed `provider_wait` reads `waited 2m for a omlx slot (feature)` and over a key-less one `waited 30s for a run slot (feature)` (the same phrasing family as the `slot_wait` case).
- `npm run test` passes.

With per-role `roles.<id>.model` overrides, a model fallback, a budget fallback and the OpenCode backend, an operator cannot see how much of a day ran on the fallback or on an override. **Approach.**
- **src/report/report-data.ts:**
  - `UsageFold` and `DayFold` gain `runsByModel: Record<string, number>`; seed it `{}` in `dayFoldFor` and in `collectReportSince`'s `acc` literal.

It tallies the window's `run_start` events — the same event whose `model` the CLI's `run #N started on <model>` line prints, and the only event that carries a model (`run_end` has none) — so a run that started with no configured model contributes no key. Both collectors route through this one function, so the day and trailing windows cannot drift.

In `renderSinceReportMarkdown`, inside its `if (data.role === undefined)` provider gate, push the same line from `rankedRoleMap(data.runsByModel)`. Zero-means-absent like the provider lines: no modelled start prints no line, so a team whose `run_start`s carry no model keeps today's output unchanged.

### OpenCode backend, part 5b/7: OpenCode runs carry the role-notes MCP server, so roles keep their notes on OpenCode (planned 2026-10-17 by user; requires part 5/7 landed; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "The invocation", "The prompt dialect and role notes" and "Findings, verified live" 21; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-config.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts src/prompt/dialect.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Part 5/7 ships OpenCode with role notes off. It was planned when OpenCode's MCP tools looked unreliable.

A follow-up probe found they are missing only from a run's **first** model request (finding 21). OpenCode connects MCP servers in the background and rebuilds the tool list on every request. A note saved at the end of a multi-step run, which is how roles use notes, was written 6 times out of 6.

This part turns notes on. An OpenCode run that carries notes gets tumwater's role-notes MCP server, and its prompt asks for the note the way pi's and claude's prompts do.

**Superseded 2026-10-17 by Notes command part 3/4:** this part's carrier — the `notesServer` option, the `mcp.servers.tumwater` entry, and `notesTool: "tumwater_role_notes"` — was deleted once every backend wrote its note through the `tumwater-notes write` command. The approach and acceptance below record the interim mechanism only.

**Approach.**
- **src/agent/opencode/opencode-config.ts:**
  - `OpencodeConfigOptions` gains an optional `notesServer?: { command: string[]; notesPath: string }`.
  - When it is given, `opencodeConfigContent` adds `mcp.servers.tumwater = { type: "local", command, codemode: false, environment: { TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH: notesPath } }`.
    - `codemode: false` makes it a direct tool. Code Mode (`execute`) is denied, and MCP tools would otherwise only be reachable through it.
  - An operator server also named `tumwater` is not given `{ disabled: true }`. This entry replaces it, because a later config replaces a server object whole.
  - Without `notesServer` the output is unchanged.
  - Update the module comment that says no server of tumwater's own is configured.
- **src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts:** when `run.notesPath` is set, `invocation` passes `notesServer`.
  - Its command is `[process.execPath, <dist role-notes-server.js>]`, resolved the way claude-backend.ts's `roleNotesMcpConfig` resolves it (`new URL("../mcp/role-notes-server.js", import.meta.url)`).
  - Pass it on every invocation that carries notes: fresh, resumed, a transient retry, a SUMMARY follow-up. OpenCode's config is per process.
  - The run env also carries `TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH`, as the pi and claude adapters' envs do.
  - This replaces part 5/7's "a run's notesPath is ignored".
- **src/prompt/dialect.ts:** `OPENCODE_DIALECT.notesTool` becomes `"tumwater_role_notes"`, so `roleNotesInstruction` asks for the note "before you end".
  - Nothing in the prompt mentions the first-request gap (design §5): the note is written after it has passed.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/opencode/opencode-config.ts, src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts, src/prompt/dialect.ts.
- Tests: test/opencode-config.test.ts, test/opencode-run.test.ts, test/prompt-dialect.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **`opencodeConfigContent` with `notesServer`**, parsed back:
  - `mcp.servers.tumwater` has `type: "local"`, the given command, `codemode: false`, and `environment.TUMWATER_NOTES_PATH` set to the notes path.
  - Operator servers are still `disabled: true`.
  - An operator server named `tumwater` is replaced, not disabled.
  - Without `notesServer`, the output is byte-identical to before.
- **An authoring run with a notebook, on the fake:**
  - Its recorded `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` has the `tumwater` server, pointing at dist's role-notes-server.js and at the role's notes path.
  - A continue of that run carries the server too.
  - A run without `notesPath` has no `tumwater` server.
- **Prompts:**
  - The opencode prompt carries the notes instruction naming `tumwater_role_notes`.
  - The pi and claude prompts are byte-identical to before.
- **The capture:** test/fixtures/opencode-captures/mcp-notes-end-of-run.jsonl, through part 4/7's translator, gives a tool execution named `tumwater_role_notes` after the run's `read` and `bash` calls.
- `npm test` passes.

### OpenCode backend, part 5/7: The opencode adapter runs model jobs, with minted sessions, the export after each run, a PATH fake and its prompt dialect (planned 2026-10-17 by user; revised 2026-10-17 by user after the live probe; requires part 3/7 and part 4/7 landed; design in plans/opencode-backend.md "Sessions", "The prompt dialect and role notes" and "The stream translator, and the export that completes it"; touches src/agent/agent-backend.ts src/agent/run-agent.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts (new) src/prompt/dialect.ts src/prompt/prompt.ts src/paths.ts src/agent/opencode/opencode-stream.ts test/fakes/fake-opencode.ts (new) test/test-runner.ts test/doctor-checks.test.ts test/startup-gate.test.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** Register an `opencode` backend that runs real model jobs through `opencode run`: authoring, review, follow-ups and resolver runs.

- Its cost and usage are complete: they come from the session export, not only from the lossy stream.
- A session resumes only when it really exists.
- The prompts describe OpenCode's real tool surface.

**Approach.**
- **The seam hook.** `AgentBackend` (src/agent/agent-backend.ts) gains an optional `afterRun?(run: AgentRunSpec, invocation: AgentInvocation, translator: StreamTranslator): string[]` — the translator goes in so the hook can add `opencode_usage_partial` to the run's warnings, which `finish()` drains after the hook returns.
  - It returns canonical lines. src/agent/run-agent.ts calls it in the child `close` handler, exactly once, only when `!settled` and the run was not killed (`!killed`), before the parser's final fold, and writes and parses the lines like streamed ones.
  - The `!settled` guard is load-bearing: the spawn `error` handler calls `finish()`, which sets `settled` before `close` fires, so a run whose binary never started must not spend a 10 s export on a session that was never created.
  - pi and claude do not implement it.
- **`opencodeBackend`** in src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts:
  - `id: "opencode"`, `label: "OpenCode"`, `defaultBin: "opencode"`, `binEnv: "TUMWATER_OPENCODE_BIN"`.
  - `resolveBin` goes through `resolveBackendBin`.
  - `invocation`:
    - the database is `opencodeDbPath(root)` = `<tumwater dir>/opencode/opencode.db` (a new helper in src/paths.ts; the tumwater dir is the `.tumwater` that contains `run.sessionDir`);
    - `title` = `run.sessionName`;
    - the passthrough from `resolvedAgentConfig(run.config, "opencode").args`;
    - `operatorMcpNames(process.env, os.homedir())`;
    - part 3/7's builders, with the env layered on `agentBaseEnv(run.runMarker)`.
    - It returns the `sessionId`, which the runner records in the session ledger before spawning.
    - A run's `notesPath` is ignored (design decision 8).
  - **Sessions:**
    - A fresh run calls `mintOpencodeSessionId()`.
    - A continue takes the ledger's newest record of this run's kind (`resumableSession`). It resumes that id only when the record is OpenCode's, has this run's `cwd`, and `opencode session export <id> --standalone` (spawnSync with the run env, 10 s timeout) exits 0. Otherwise it mints a fresh id.
    - `resumable` answers through the same helper.
  - `afterRun` runs the same export, bounded at 10 s, and returns `opencodeExportLines(json)`. On failure or empty lines it returns `[]`, and the translator's warnings gain `opencode_usage_partial`.
  - `classifyExit`: a run the harness killed is never classified. On a nonzero exit, stderr naming `FreeTierError` → `transientBackend`, and `Model unavailable` / `Variant unavailable` → `configError`.
- **Registration:** src/agent/run-agent.ts registers `opencodeBackend` beside pi and claude.
- **Dialect** (src/prompt/dialect.ts, the `DIALECTS` table):
  - `PromptDialect` gains an optional `backendRules?: string[]`. src/prompt/prompt.ts renders it after the oversized-output rule. `roleNotesInstruction` returns `""` when `notesTool` is empty.
  - `OPENCODE_DIALECT` has:
    - `notesTool: ""`;
    - `readRange`: "the read tool's offset/limit (or `sed -n 'A,Bp'`)";
    - `oversizedOutput`: "Oversized shell output keeps only its last lines, followed by a note naming the file with the full output — read that file in ranges (the read tool's offset/limit) instead of re-running the command.";
    - `backendRules`: the two rules in plans/opencode-backend.md §5 (pass `timeout` for long commands such as the check; never set `background`).
  - The pi and claude prompts stay byte-identical.
- **`test/fakes/fake-opencode.ts`**, the twin of fake-claude.ts: a PATH shim named `opencode`.
  - For `run`, it replays a capture from part 4/7's fixtures, records argv, stdin and the `OPENCODE_*` env, and stores the session id in a per-test ledger file.
  - For `session export <id>`, it prints a canned export when it knows the id, and exits 1 otherwise. It also handles `session delete <id>`.
  - It supports a scripted exit code and a scripted hang.
- **test/test-runner.ts** strips `TUMWATER_OPENCODE_BIN`, `OPENCODE` and every `OPENCODE_*` from the suite environment.

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/agent/agent-backend.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts (new), src/agent/opencode/opencode-stream.ts, src/prompt/dialect.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/paths.ts.
- Tests: test/fakes/fake-opencode.ts (new), test/opencode-run.test.ts (new), test/agent-backend.test.ts, test/prompt-dialect.test.ts, test/test-runner.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/startup-gate.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **An authoring run with `model: "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free"`, through `runAgent` on the fake:**
  - It spawns `opencode` with part 3/7's argv (a minted `--session`, `--title` = the session name) and the prompt on stdin.
  - It appends an opencode ledger record before the spawn.
  - It writes canonical lines to the raw log and native lines to `.tumwater/log/<role>.opencode.native.jsonl`.
  - Its result's tokens equal the canned export's `info.tokens`, and `costUsd` is 0.
- **With the fake's export failing:** the result keeps the streamed tokens, and the run logs `opencode_usage_partial`.
- **Continue:**
  - With the id known to the fake's export, the same `--session` id is passed.
  - With an unknown id, or a record from another cwd, a new id is minted and `resumable` answers false.
- **A run on the hanging fake that the quiet watchdog kills:** its group is killed, the fake's export is never invoked (assert `fake.exportsFile` is absent or empty), and no classifier overrides the result.
- **A failed spawn never calls `afterRun`.** Register a stub `AgentBackend` (the shape test/agent-backend.test.ts already uses: id, label, defaultBin, binEnv, resolveBin, invocation, translator, classifyExit) whose `resolveBin` returns a nonexistent binary and whose `afterRun` increments a counter and returns `[]`; await `runAgent` and assert the result is not ok and the counter is 0. The counter is the assertion: `finish()` drains translator warnings in the spawn `error` handler before `close` runs, so a `!warnings.includes("opencode_usage_partial")` check would pass even with the `!settled` guard removed and must not be used.
- **Prompts:** the opencode prompt has no notes instruction and carries both backend rules. The pi and claude prompts are byte-identical to before.
- `npm test` passes.

### The director honors its `roles.director.instructions` override, so the standing instructions a `tumwater role director` page shows reach its runs (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; `roles.<id>.instructions` is documented as "Extra instructions appended to this role's prompt" (docs/config.md), accepted for every id `allRoleIds()` returns — the director included — and `rolePayload` surfaces it for any id (`instructions: cfg.roles[role]?.instructions ?? null`, src/roles/role-view.ts), so `tumwater role director` renders the `Instructions override` block and computes its `Next run's prompt` preview through `assembleTickPrompt` — yet `buildDirectorPrompt` (src/prompt/prompt.ts) takes no `extraInstructions`, and `assembleTickPrompt`'s director branch (src/tick/tick-prompt.ts) passes none, unlike its role branch (`extraInstructions: config.roles[base]?.instructions`). So `config set roles.director.instructions "…"` is stored, validated and displayed, but no director run receives it: the role page shows an override that does nothing. This plan also makes the in-flight `--instructions-file` plan's director acceptance criterion true, since that plan writes `roles.director.instructions` and expects it to reach the director's runs. Independent of every eligible Planned entry: the instructions-file plan (src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/completion.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md) and the context-window plan (src/roles/role-view.ts, src/roles/role-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts) touch none of this plan's files; the in-flight OpenCode 5/7 also edits src/prompt/prompt.ts for its dialect work, so whichever lands second rebases over adjacent lines there. Touches src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts, docs/config.md, test/prompt-roles.test.ts and test/tick-prompt.test.ts — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A `roles.director.instructions` override reaches every director run exactly as it reaches a catalog role's runs: `buildDirectorPrompt` appends the same `Additional standing instructions from the user:` block `buildTickPrompt` already appends, so the `tumwater role director` page and its `Next run's prompt` preview — both computed from `assembleTickPrompt` — name the same standing text the run receives. An unset override changes nothing: the block is omitted exactly as today.

**Approach.**
- `src/prompt/prompt.ts` (`buildDirectorPrompt`): add a trailing optional parameter `extraInstructions?: string` after `compact?: boolean`, doc-commented as the director's `roles.director.instructions` override (its run prompt is otherwise the user's request). After the routing-rules `parts.push(...)` and before the director-only boundary note (`Note on one boundary in the rules below, director only`), push `Additional standing instructions from the user:\n${extraInstructions.trim()}` when it is non-empty — the exact literal and shape `buildTickPrompt` uses (`if (extraInstructions) parts.push(…)`), so the two builders present the text identically and before the closing reply contract stays last.
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts` (the `role === DIRECTOR_ROLE` branch): pass `config.roles[DIRECTOR_ROLE]?.instructions` as the new final argument to `buildDirectorPrompt`, mirroring the role branch's `config.roles[base]?.instructions`. `defaultConfig()` already seeds a `director` entry (`allRoleIds()` includes it), so the lookup is defined for every config.
- `docs/config.md`: the `roles.<id>` `instructions` row gains a clause that the director's entry is honored like any role's (its notes stay unset, the `role` command's `--clear-notes` refusal).

**Files touched.** Source: src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts. Docs: docs/config.md. Tests: test/prompt-roles.test.ts, test/tick-prompt.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/prompt-roles.test.ts` beside the existing `buildDirectorPrompt` tests: `buildDirectorPrompt("add dark mode", "a project", undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, "Prefer small plans.")` contains `Additional standing instructions from the user:\nPrefer small plans.`, and the same call without the last argument does not contain `Additional standing instructions` (the unset case stays byte-identical).
- New test in `test/tick-prompt.test.ts` beside "a director's prompt is built from the dequeued request, returned as userPrompt": a `defaultConfig()` whose `roles.director` carries `{ enabled: true, instructions: "Prefer vitest." }`, with `enqueuePrompt(dir, "add dark mode")`, assembles a non-null prompt whose text carries `Additional standing instructions from the user:\nPrefer vitest.`
- The preview seam agrees: the same config with `assembleTickPrompt({ …, role: DIRECTOR_ROLE, preview: true })` carries that block and still peeks rather than consumes the queued prompt (`inboxSize(dir, DIRECTOR_ROLE)` stays 1) — the property the existing preview tests pin.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater role <id>` and the dashboard role drawer name the resolved model's context window and the compact prompt it selects (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; the compact-prompt change (commit b1eb00a9) makes a run's prompt and its read/cap scaling depend on the model's declared window through `compactPromptWindow` (src/pi-extension/context-window.ts) and `seamContextWindow` (src/pi/pi-models.ts), but no surface shows the window: `rolePayload` (src/roles/role-view.ts) computes `compactPromptWindow(seamContextWindow(configForRole(cfg, role), root, modelsPath))` inline only to build the `nextPrompt` preview, and `grep -rn "seamContextWindow\|contextWindow" src/roles/role-render.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` finds no rendering — so an operator reading `tumwater role <id>` or the drawer sees `Model: …` and peak-context tokens but cannot see that a 64k local model gets the shortened prompt and smaller read caps while a 200k model does not. Both surfaces already consume the one `rolePayload`, so one field pair renders in both. Independent of every eligible Planned entry: OpenCode part 5/7 touches src/agent, src/prompt and src/paths only; the TUI Health retire plan touches src/ui/tui only; the blocked plain-terms series is far behind. Touches src/roles/role-view.ts, src/roles/role-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/cli/help.ts, test/role-view.test.ts, test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** `tumwater role <id>` (its Markdown page and its `--json` document) and the dashboard role drawer name the resolved primary seam's declared context window and whether a run on it gets the compact prompt — `64k tokens (compact prompt)` for the local Qwen at 64k, `256k tokens (full prompt)` for a large model. When the window cannot be known (a non-pi seam, an unresolvable provider/model pair, or a model pi's definitions declare no window), both say `unknown (full prompt)` rather than guessing, which is exactly the compact-prompt decision `seamContextWindow`/`compactPromptWindow` already make. The line names the same seam the page's `- Next run:` preview is assembled from, so the window, the compact flag and the preview cannot disagree; a run currently on the model fallback may use a different window, which is the fallback's own documented state.

**Approach.**
- `src/roles/role-view.ts`: add two fields to `RoleViewPayload`, beside the model fields:
  - `contextWindow: number | null` — "The resolved primary seam's declared context window in tokens, or null when it cannot be known (a non-pi seam, an unresolvable pair, or a model with no declared window)."
  - `compactPrompt: boolean` — "Whether a run on that seam gets the compact prompt (compactPromptWindow): a known window of at most 128k. False when the window is unknown."
  - In `rolePayload`, compute once before building the payload object: `const contextWindow = seamContextWindow(configForRole(cfg, role), root, modelsPath);` and `const compactPrompt = compactPromptWindow(contextWindow);`. Replace the inline `compact: compactPromptWindow(seamContextWindow(configForRole(cfg, role), root, modelsPath))` in the `nextPrompt` preview with `compact: compactPrompt` (same call, one read), and add `contextWindow, compactPrompt` to the returned object. `seamContextWindow` and `compactPromptWindow` are already imported.
