### The dashboard composer recalls recently sent prompts with Up and Down, restoring the draft you were typing — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The composer keeps one unsent draft per target (`drafts`), but a sent prompt is gone:
re-sending a nudge means retyping it. The TUI's prompt line recalls recent prompts
(`tui-prompt-history.ts`); give the dashboard composer the same recall — Up steps back through
the prompts you have sent, Down steps forward and restores the draft you were typing.

**Approach.** All changes are inside the `gui-client-composer` blob in
`src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts`, beside the existing `drafts`/`promptInput`/keydown/submit
code; no server or page change.

1. Beside `drafts` add the recall state: `const promptHistory = [];` (oldest first, the text of
   each successfully sent prompt), `let recallIndex = null;` (null means the live draft, an
   index means browsing `promptHistory`), `let recallDraft = "";` (the live draft saved when
   browsing starts), and `const PROMPT_HISTORY_MAX = 50;`.
2. Add one helper, `recallSentPrompt(step)` where `step` is `-1` for Up and `1` for Down, that
   returns true when it changed the box. Up with `recallIndex === null` saves
   `recallDraft = promptInput.value` and moves to the newest entry; otherwise it steps one older
   while it can. Down at the newest restores `recallDraft` and resets `recallIndex` to null.
   Down while already live is a no-op. On a change it sets `promptInput.value` to the entry (or
   `recallDraft`), then calls `autosize()`, `updateCount()` and
   `promptInput.setSelectionRange(value.length, value.length)` so the recalled text is ready to
   send. Doc it as the composer's mirror of the TUI's `recallPromptHistory`.
3. In the existing `promptInput.addEventListener("keydown", …)`, add an `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`
   arm: when `!ev.isComposing` and (scouting already browsing, or the current value has no
   newline — `recallIndex !== null || !promptInput.value.includes("\n")`), call
   `recallSentPrompt(ev.key === "ArrowUp" ? -1 : 1)` and `ev.preventDefault()` when it returns
   true. The newline guard applies to the live draft only: a recalled multi-line entry keeps
   its Up/Down recallable (Down always walks back to the saved draft), while an untouched
   multi-line draft keeps the textarea's own Up/Down line movement, like the TUI keeps its
   arrows for other panes.
4. Record a send in the existing submit handler's success path (the code after the
   `try`/`finally` that is reached only when the server accepted the prompt, where the input is
   cleared): push the trimmed `text` unless it equals `promptHistory`'s last entry, drop the
   oldest entry past `PROMPT_HISTORY_MAX`, and reset `recallIndex = null; recallDraft = "";`.
   On `setTarget`, hand the saved draft to the old target's slot when a switch happens
   mid-recall (`drafts[promptTarget] = recallIndex !== null ? recallDraft : promptInput.value`,
   the TUI's `settlePromptRecall` swap) and reset `recallIndex`/`recallDraft`, so a target swap
   never saves the recalled entry over the unsent draft or discards it; `draftForDirector`
   resets the same two after routing through `setTarget`, so a prefilled answer is never left
   mid-recall.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts`, `test/gui-client-composer.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-client-composer.test.ts`: a new test "the composer recalls sent prompts with Up and
  Down and restores the live draft", modelled on the existing submit test. Submit `first`, then
  `second` (the `s.fire(s.form(), "submit", SUBMIT)` + `await s.flush()` pattern), type
  `draft in progress`, then fire `keydown` `ArrowUp`: the box reads `second`; a second `ArrowUp`
  reads `first`; a third stays `first` (the oldest end); `ArrowDown` reads `second`; a second
  `ArrowDown` restores `draft in progress`; a third is a no-op. `preventDefault` was called on
  each recall. With the value `line one\nline two`, `ArrowUp` leaves it unchanged and does not
  call `preventDefault`. Submitting the same text twice in a row adds one history entry (one
  `ArrowUp` reaches it, the next stays).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Each day's red full-suite merge checks are counted in the `tumwater report` day report (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the plain-terms series and of the in-flight problems-only Health view plan; the report half of a red-check signal whose GUI chart is left to a later plan, as the project did for `Merge check median`; touches src/build/build-check-events.ts, src/report/report-data.ts, src/report/report-render.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The day report shows `**Merge check median:**` — how long the passing full-suite
merge checks took — but not how often that check went red. A flaky or broken suite is the
team's biggest merge bottleneck: a red merge check keeps its pin and retries, so it usually
produces no `merge_failed` and no `Merge failures by role` row, and the median happily reports
a fast pass on a day when half the checks failed first. Count each day's failed full-suite
`build_check` events (the merge, batch and baseline scopes `isPassingFullCheck` already
counts) and print them as a `**Red merge checks:**` line beside the medians, so a spike shows
a flaky or broken suite without reading the failure digest.

**Approach.**

1. `src/build/build-check-events.ts`: add `export function isRedFullCheck(ev: HarnessEvent): boolean`
   right after `isPassingFullCheck` (line 23). Body:
   `ev.type === "build_check" && ev.status === "failed" && ["merge", "batch", "baseline"].includes(String(ev.scope))`.
   Doc it as the red sibling of `isPassingFullCheck`: the same three scopes and the failed
   status; a `skipped` check made no verdict about the tree, and a merge-scope timeout is
   already remapped to `failed` by `runScopedBuildCheck` (`MERGE_SCOPES`), so `failed` alone is
   the rule. The two predicates are mutually exclusive on `status`, so the fold branch below
   never sees the other's events.
2. `src/report/report-data.ts`:
   - `UsageFold` (starts line 37): add `checkFailures: number;` beside `checkDurationsMs`, with
     a doc comment: a count of failed full-suite build_check events (`isRedFullCheck`), so a day
     whose checks went red before passing is visible beside its passing-check median.
   - `foldUsageEvent` (line 121): after the `isPassingFullCheck(ev)` branch that pushes
     `checkDurationsMs`, add `else if (isRedFullCheck(ev)) { target.checkFailures++; }` with a
     one-line comment, and import `isRedFullCheck` beside `isPassingFullCheck`.
   - `DayFold` (line 199): add `checkFailures: number;` beside `checkDurationsMs`.
   - `dayFoldFor` (line 308): initialize `checkFailures: 0,` beside `checkDurationsMs: []`.
   - `collectReportSince`'s `acc` initializer (line ~603): initialize `checkFailures: 0,`
     beside `checkDurationsMs: []` (the field is part of `UsageFold`, so the shape must satisfy
     it).
   - `ReportDay` (line ~420): add
     `/** Failed full-suite build_check events that day (isRedFullCheck); absent when the day has none (zero means absent). */ checkFailures?: number;`
     beside `checkMedianMs`.
   - The day assembly's team branch (beside
     `if (fold.checkDurationsMs.length > 0) day.checkMedianMs = …`, line ~731): add
     `if (fold.checkFailures > 0) day.checkFailures = fold.checkFailures;`. Leave the
     role-scoped branch alone — checks belong to the merge slot, so a scoped series carries
     none, exactly like `checkMedianMs`.
3. `src/report/report-render.ts`: in the team branch of `renderReportMarkdown`, right after the
   `**Merge check median:**` push (line ~293), push a `**Red merge checks:**` line when any day
   has `checkFailures`, each day rendered `${monthDay(d.date)} ×${d.checkFailures}` and joined
   with ` · `. Zero-absent: no line when no day carries the field.
4. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater report` parenthetical (line 47), extend the
   merge-check clause to say the team report also names each day's count of red full-suite
   merge checks beside the merge check median.

### Plain terms code merge, part 11a/11: Rewrite the merge family in the pipeline modules' comments (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; split 2026-10-17 by the plan role from part 11/11, siblings parts 11b/11, 11c/11 and 11d/11; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches comments in src/merge/ src/events/ src/review/ src/verdict/ src/git/ src/tick/ src/failure/ src/change/ src/build/ src/process/ and src/loop/) — done 2026-10-17 by the feature role

**Goal.** The merge family's identifiers and file names are already renamed and guarded (`RETIRED` in test/retired-names.test.ts carries the family; part 11/11's identifier half landed). What remains is comment prose. This part rewrites the merge family in the comments of the pipeline modules, so a reader sees `merge`, `merged` and `approved` where the code merges.

**Approach.**
- Work only in the listed paths, and only on comments (line and block). Apply plans/terminology.md "Code names": the pipeline `landing`/`land` → `merge`; `land queue` → `merge queue`; `landed` (now on main) → `merged`; `unlanded` → `unmerged`; `lander` → `merger`; `vet`/`vetting` → `verify`; `vetted` → `approved`. Name event types by their current names (`merge_queued`, `merge_done`, `merge_failed`).
- Keep four kinds of match: the `requires … landed` backlog grammar; a quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md title, kept verbatim; a legacy name kept on purpose (an old event type, an old state key, `_land-<role>`, `refs/tumwater/landing/`, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES`, `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS`, the startup migrations); and the ordinary English verb `land`/`lands`/`landed` meaning "arrive", which is not the merge pipeline (e.g. "the write landed", "the signal lands").
- Do not rename identifiers or touch string literals.

**Files touched.** Comments in src/merge/, src/events/, src/review/, src/verdict/, src/git/, src/tick/, src/failure/, src/change/, src/build/, src/process/ and src/loop/. plans/terminology.md is read, not edited.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `git grep -nE '[Ll]and(ings?|es|ed|ers?|s)?[^a-z]|[Ll]and(ings?|s|ed|ers?)?$|LAND|[Vv]et(ted|ting|s)?[^a-z]' -- src/merge src/events src/review src/verdict src/git src/tick src/failure src/change src/build src/process src/loop` lists only the four kept kinds above, and the run's summary names each remaining match and its kept kind.
- The diff changes comment lines only.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Split the TUI prompt-line editor monolith `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` into per-editor modules beside a shared prompt-line session (planned 2026-10-17 by the organize role; the natural second half of the landed "split the TUI key-handling monolith" series — part 1/2 made `tui-editors` the prompt-line editors and part 2/2 split the pane state into `tui-panes`, both merged 2026-10-16, so the single largest source file left is this one factory closure. Independent of every other Planned entry. It touches only `src/ui/tui/` and the existing `test/tui-*.test.ts` suites; the in-flight Health tab plan edits `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`/`tui-panes.ts` and `src/ui/gui/`, not `tui-editors.ts`, so the two do not overlap) — done 2026-10-17

**Why.** `tui-editors.ts` is 1121 lines, the largest source file in the repo at ~5.8× the ~193-line median, and it is one factory closure, `createTuiEditors`, that owns the one shared prompt line (`input`/`cursor`/`promptHistory`) plus eight mutually-exclusive modal editors — budget Ctrl+B, per-role prompt Ctrl+R, defer Ctrl+L, pause Ctrl+F/stop/wake, the inbox row's in-place editor Ctrl+E, the backlog answer editor Ctrl+A, the backlog new-entry/title editor Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N, and the `/` search editor — each with its own saved-draft pair, exit helper, and handleKey arms, all tangled in one ~700-line `handleKey`. A reviewer cannot hold one editor's behavior (its key, its pre-fill, its Enter/Esc guards) without the whole file. Part 2/2 of the monolith split already cut the pane side; this is the same split applied to the editor side, so each modal editor has one module boundary. This is a restructure only; it changes no behavior.

**Goal.** `createTuiEditors` becomes a thin aggregator. The shared mutable prompt line moves into one small session module, and each modal editor becomes its own module owning its mode flag, saved-draft pair, exit helper, and the handleKey arms for its keys. The mutually-exclusive invariants the file currently states "hold here once, at the module boundary" move into the session module, which exposes the shared `input`/`cursor`/`promptHistory`, `restorePromptFrom`, `settleDraft`, `busyFlash`, `heldEditorFlash`, and the exit-all routine.

**Approach.** Restructure only, no behavior change. Move code verbatim wherever possible; `test/tui-*.test.ts` (tui-budget, tui-role-prompt, tui-keys, tui-frame, tui-input, tui-prompt-history, tui-reload, tui-notebook, tui-operator-keys, tui-history, tui-backlog) is the regression net. Suggested target modules, all under `src/ui/tui/`:
- **`tui-editor-session.ts`** — the shared prompt line. Owns `input`, `cursor`, `promptHistory` and the shared helpers `restorePromptFrom`, `settleDraft`, `busyFlash`, `heldEditorFlash` and `exitAll` (which today just calls every per-editor exit helper in order). Exposes a plain mutable session object and the shared deps (`root`, `now`, `flat`, `flashMessage`, `flashError`, `commitBacklogEdit`) so the editor modules take only the session + the per-key `TuiEditorCtx`, not the whole `TuiEditorsDeps`.
- **`tui-editor-budget.ts`** and **`tui-editor-defer.ts`** — the budget Ctrl+B and defer Ctrl+L editors; each owns its mode flag, its saved-pair, `exitBudgetMode`/`exitDeferMode`, and the arms for its key (including its `heldEditorFlash(entering)` guard clause, which keeps the shared guard priority in the session module).
- **`tui-editor-prompt.ts`** — the per-role prompt Ctrl+R editor with its own saved pair and exit helper.
- **`tui-editor-pause.ts`** — the pause/stop/wake editor Ctrl+F (team) and per-loop pause/wake, owning `pauseEditMode`/`pauseEditRole`/`pauseEditWake`/`pauseEditStop`, its save pair, and the parse/dispatch leaves (`parsePauseInput`, `parseRolePauseInput`, `parseStopInInput`, `parseRoleWakeInput`, `parseBudgetInput` sits with budget).
- **`tui-editor-queued.ts`** — the inbox row's in-place editor Ctrl+E, owning `queuedEditFor` + pair and the `readQueuedPromptBody`/`editQueuedFile` arms.
- **`tui-editor-answer.ts`** — the backlog answer editor Ctrl+A, owning `answerFor` + pair and the `tryAnswerQuestion` arm.
- **`tui-editor-entry.ts`** — the backlog new-entry/title editor Ctrl+E/Ctrl+N, owning `entryEditFor` + pair, its plan↔bug flip, the `fileEntryWithBody`/`commitBacklogEdit` arms, and the position math that counts `plan`/`bug` labels.
- **`tui-editor-search.ts`** — the `/` search editor, owning `searchMode`, `searchFor`, its pair, and the `applyHistorySearch`/`applyActivitySearch` arms.
- **`tui-editors.ts`** shrinks to the aggregator: build the session, register the editors, and expose the unchanged `TuiEditors` surface. Its `handleKey` routes each key to the editors in today's priority order (each module returns true when it consumed the key and false to fall through, so the mutually-exclusive/busy-guard ordering is preserved exactly); `state()` returns `{ input, cursor, budgetMode, rolePromptFor, deferMode, defer, pauseEditMode, pauseEditRole, pauseEditWake, pauseEditStop, queuedEditFor, searchMode, answerFor, entryEditFor }` exactly as today; `onArrow`/`apply`/`exitAll`/`sync` move with the session or stay as the aggregator's thin tail. `TuiEditors`, `TuiEditorCtx`, `TuiEditorsDeps` and every `TuiEditorState` field name and type stay unchanged.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` (shrinks) and the new `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-*.ts` modules above. `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` (which scans the editor source for the Ctrl keys the docs table must name) got its hardcoded file list extended to the new per-editor modules; the rest of `test/tui-*.test.ts` (which covers these editors through the `TuiKeys` surface) passes unmodified.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `TuiEditors`, `TuiEditorCtx`, `TuiEditorsDeps`, and every `TuiEditorState` field name and type are unchanged; `createTuiKeys` in `tui-keys.ts` and `tui.tsx`/`tui-app.tsx` pass unmodified.
- Every editor consumes and leaves the prompt line exactly as today: the same keys open it, the same Esc/repeat-key exits it, the same saved draft is restored byte-for-byte, and the busy-guard flash wording and priority are unchanged.
- No behavior change: `npm run test` passes, with `test/tui-*.test.ts` unmodified (apart from the `tui-keys-doc` scan list) as the regression net.

### The TUI Health tab and the dashboard Health card take `tumwater doctor --problems`' problems-only view (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the plain-terms series and of the blocked runner/run/cleanup parts; touches only src/ui/tui/, src/ui/gui/, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor` prints well over 50 rows and `--problems` (`problemsOnly` and
`renderDoctorProblems` in src/doctor/doctor-render.ts) trims them to the warn and fail rows.
The two dashboards still paint every `ok` row: the TUI's Health tab renders `renderDoctor` into
its cached pane, and the dashboard's Health card renders every check through
`renderDoctorReport`. Give both surfaces the same problems-only view so an operator can hide
the ok rows without leaving the surface. The checks that run and the default full view stay as
they are.

**Approach.**

TUI (the Health tab is `kind === "health"` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts, painted from the
`paneCache` the Ctrl+T arm in src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts fills):
- src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts: import `renderDoctorProblems` beside `renderDoctor`. Add
  `let healthProblems = false;` and `let lastDoctorReport: DoctorReport | null = null;` beside
  `paneCache`. In the Health arm (`view === roleIds.length + 7`), set `lastDoctorReport = null`
  at entry and `lastDoctorReport = report` on resolution, painting
  `paneCache = (healthProblems ? renderDoctorProblems : renderDoctor)(report)`. Add a Ctrl+O arm
  before the existing History outcome arm: when `view === roleIds.length + 7` and
  `promptLineFree()`, flip `healthProblems`, repaint `paneCache` from `lastDoctorReport` (reset
  `paneScroll = 0`; leave the loading note when it is null), `deps.requestRender()`, `return
  true`. Every other view keeps the existing History Ctrl+O behavior. Expose `healthProblems`
  from `state()`.
- src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts: add `healthProblems: boolean` to `TuiKeysState`; the
  `...panes.state()` spread already carries the value.
- src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: pass `problems: s.healthProblems` in the Health pane literal.
- src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts: make the Health variant `{ kind: "health"; problems?: boolean }`;
  in `hintLine` split Health from the Brief branch and add
  `["Ctrl+O", view.problems ? "problems only" : "all checks"]`.
- docs/cli.md: the `Ctrl+O` TUI row's Where becomes `History, Health`, noting that on Health it
  toggles the problems-only view.

Dashboard (the Health card in src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts):
- Add `let lastDoctor = null; let doctorProblems = false;`. Change
  `renderDoctorReport(d, problems = false)`: when `problems`, keep only checks whose
  `level !== "ok"` and append a `<p>` line counting the hidden ok rows (mirroring `problemsOnly`
  and `renderDoctorProblems`). The Health card header gains a `<label>` holding
  `<input type='checkbox' data-action='doctor-problems'> Problems only`. `fetchDoctor` stores
  `lastDoctor = report` and paints `renderDoctorReport(report, doctorProblems)`. Add
  `toggleDoctorProblems(checked)`: set `doctorProblems = checked` and repaint `doctorbody` from
  `lastDoctor` (a no-op while it is null).
- src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts: a delegated `change` listener beside the doctor-rerun click arm
  calls `toggleDoctorProblems(box.checked)` for `input[data-action='doctor-problems']`.

**Files touched.** src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx,
src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts,
docs/cli.md, test/tui-keys.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts, test/gui-client-settings.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/tui-keys.test.ts: a test modelled on "the Health tab caches renderDoctor of the seam's
  report", with a seam report holding one `ok` and one `warn` check. On entry `state().paneCache`
  is `renderDoctor(report)`; after one Ctrl+O it is `renderDoctorProblems(report)` (holds the
  warn row and the hidden-ok count, not the ok row's name); after a second Ctrl+O it is
  `renderDoctor(report)` again. Ctrl+O on the History view still cycles the outcome filter.
- test/tui-frame.test.ts: `hintLine` for `{ kind: "health", problems: false }` names `Ctrl+O`
  with `all checks`; for `{ kind: "health", problems: true }` with `problems only`.
- test/gui-client-settings.test.ts: `renderDoctorReport(report, true)` keeps only the warn and
  fail rows and appends the hidden-count line; `renderDoctorReport(report)` still renders every
  row; a test calling `toggleDoctorProblems(true)` after `fetchDoctor` repaints `doctorbody`
  with the filtered report. Add `toggleDoctorProblems` to the scope's extracted names.
- `npm run test` passes, including `tui-keys-doc.test.ts` (Ctrl+O is already a documented key).

### The GUI Usage view charts each day's `Merge wait median` as a bar element beside `Merge check median`, so the operator sees merges queueing longer on the dashboard as well as in `tumwater report` (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the in-flight plain-terms merge part 11/11, which leaves src/ui/gui/ alone after part 10/11, and of the in-flight `tumwater doctor --problems` — touches only src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts and its test) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater report` prints a `Merge wait median` line (`renderReportMarkdown`, `src/report/report-render.ts`). Each series day already carries the figure to the dashboard as the optional `ReportDay.mergeWaitMedianMs` (`src/report/report-data.ts`). `collectReport` sets it in the team branch only. It is absent on days with no merge that carried `queuedMs` and on every day of a role-scoped report (pinned in `test/report-data.test.ts`). The GUI Usage view (`src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`) draws `Merge check median` but not the merge wait, so a merge queue that grows slower over days shows only in the CLI. Add one single-series bar chart for it, built exactly like `chartCheckMedian` (PLANS.md Done: "The GUI Usage view charts each day's `Merge check median` as a bar element"; the Done plan "`tumwater report` shows each day's median merge wait" left charting to a later plan).

**Approach.** All code changes go in the browser script `GUI_CLIENT_REPORT_JS`, inside the `report-chart:start` … `report-chart:end` region, so `clientScope` in the tests can load the builders. `fmtSpan` is already reachable there, since `chartCheckMedian` uses it.
- Add `chartMergeWaitMedian(data)` right after `chartCheckMedian`:
  `reportSvg(data.series, (d) => [{ value: Number(d.mergeWaitMedianMs) || 0, color: "#f59e0b", title: d.date + ": " + fmtSpan(Number(d.mergeWaitMedianMs) || 0) + " median merge wait" }], (v) => fmtSpan(v), false)`.
  A day without the field gives a zero segment. `reportSvg` already skips zero segments but keeps the day's slot, so the x-axis lines up with the other charts. Add a one-line comment in the style of `chartCheckMedian`'s: the lower median of the day's merge waits, enqueue to merged on main, from `mergeWaitMedianMs`.
- Add `seriesHasMergeWaitMedian(data)` right after `seriesHasCheckMedian`: `data.series.some((d) => Number(d.mergeWaitMedianMs) > 0)`, with a one-line comment like its sibling's.
- In the view's `render`, right after the `Merge check median` block, append `block("Merge wait median", chartMergeWaitMedian(d), "per day · enqueue to merged on main")` only when `seriesHasMergeWaitMedian(d)`. A window with no timed merge renders the same elements as now. A role-scoped report renders no such block, because `report-data.ts` never sets the field there, so this needs no extra code.
- No server, `report-data.ts`, `report-render.ts`, CLI or docs change: `/api/report` already serializes the optional field, and docs/cli.md does not list the GUI's charts.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`, `test/gui-client-report.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A new test in `test/gui-client-report.test.ts`, "the Merge wait median chart draws one bar per timed day and seriesHasMergeWaitMedian gates it". It is modelled on "the Merge check median chart draws one bar per checked day and seriesHasCheckMedian gates it", with the same `mkDay`/`mk` helpers, and loads `chartCommits`, `chartMergeWaitMedian` and `seriesHasMergeWaitMedian` through `clientScope(["format", "report-chart"], …)`. It checks:
  - A three-day series where only days 1 and 3 carry `mergeWaitMedianMs` (95 000 and 180 000) draws exactly two `<rect>`s, titled `2026-09-01: 95s median merge wait` and `2026-09-03: 3m median merge wait`.
  - The chart's SVG has as many day-label `<text … text-anchor='middle'>` elements as `chartCommits` has on that series, so the empty day keeps its slot.
  - `seriesHasMergeWaitMedian` is false for a series where only `checkMedianMs` is set, and true for the three-day series.

### `tumwater doctor --problems` prints only the warn and fail rows (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor` now prints well over 50 rows and a routing table. On a healthy team
almost every row is `ok`, so the one `warn` that explains a slow or stuck team is easy to miss.
Add `--problems` so the operator sees only what needs attention: the header, the warn and fail
rows, one line counting the hidden ok rows, and the verdict. The checks that run, the exit-code
contract, and the default output stay as they are. This is independent of the plain-terms
series. Its only overlap with the in-flight merge rename part 10/11 is the few lines of the
`doctor` case in `src/cli.ts`.

**Approach.**
1. `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`: add `export const PROBLEMS_FLAG: FlagSpec = { names: ["--problems"] };`
   beside `REPROBE_FLAG`. Give it a doc comment in the same style: a value-less flag accepted by
   `doctor`.
2. `src/doctor/doctor-render.ts`:
   - Pull the check-row loop out of `renderDoctor` into a private
     `checkLines(checks: DoctorReport["checks"]): string[]`. It keeps the current name-column
     rule: the width is the longest name, at least 12. `renderDoctor`'s output must stay
     byte-for-byte the same; the existing `renderDoctor` tests in `test/doctor.test.ts` pin
     this.
   - Add `export function problemsOnly(report: DoctorReport): DoctorReport`. It returns
     `{ ...report, checks: report.checks.filter((c) => c.level !== "ok") }`, keeping header,
     routing, and verdict unchanged. `--problems --json` prints this.
   - Add `export function renderDoctorProblems(report: DoctorReport): string`, which takes the
     full report. It prints the header, then `checkLines` over the non-ok checks (their width is
     computed over the shown rows only), then the line
     `<n> ok checks hidden — run tumwater doctor for the full report` (singular `check` when
     n is 1, using `plural` from `src/text/phrases.ts`; the line is left out when n
     is 0), then the verdict. It never prints the routing table. A report with no warn or fail
     rows prints the header, the hidden-count line, and `ready to run`.
3. `src/cli.ts`, `case "doctor"`: add `PROBLEMS_FLAG` to the `rejectUnknownArgs` list. With
   `--problems`, call `sayJsonOrRender(args, args.includes("--json") ? problemsOnly(report) : report, renderDoctorProblems)`.
   `sayJsonOrRender` in `src/cli/cli-output.ts` takes one payload, so the JSON branch gets the
   filtered report and the render gets the full one. Without the flag the call is unchanged.
   The exit-code line keeps reading the full `report`.
4. `src/cli/help.ts`: change the usage line to `tumwater doctor [--json] [--reprobe] [--problems]`
   and add one sentence to the stanza: `--problems prints only the warn and fail rows (and how
   many ok rows it hid), the same verdict and exit code; with --json the checks array holds
   only those rows`. Shell completion reads its words from this usage line through
   `usageWords` in `src/cli/completion.ts`, so it needs no edit.
5. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` parenthetical, add `--problems` after the
   `--json` clause with the same meaning.

**Files touched.** `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor-render.ts`, `src/cli.ts`,
`src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/doctor.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/doctor.test.ts`: a unit test that calls `renderDoctorProblems` on a hand-built
  `DoctorReport` with three ok rows, one warn, one fail, and a non-empty `routing`. The output
  holds the header, exactly the warn and fail rows, `3 ok checks hidden`, and the verdict, in
  that order. It contains no `routing:` line and none of the ok rows' names.
- A unit test with all-ok checks: the output is the header, `<n> ok checks hidden …`, and the
  verdict. A test with `checks: []` gets no hidden-count line.
- A unit test that `problemsOnly` keeps header, routing, and verdict and drops only the ok
  checks.
- The existing `renderDoctor` tests pass unchanged.
- A CLI test modelled on "doctor --reprobe is accepted and wired". On an initialized repo,
  `tumwater doctor --problems` exits 0, prints `ready to run`, and does not match
  `/^ok\s+git binary/m`. `doctor --problems --json` is one `JSON.parse`-able document whose
  `checks` contain no `level: "ok"` entry.
- A CLI test reusing the failing-environment fixture of "doctor --json keeps the exit-code
  contract" with `--problems` added: it still exits 1.
- `tumwater help doctor` shows `--problems`, and `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` says how long merges waited over the last 24 h, from enqueue to merged on main (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `tumwater report` now shows each day's median merge wait, and `tumwater doctor` says how
long passing merge checks took over the last 24 h. But doctor, the pre-flight an operator runs
when the team feels slow, says nothing about how long finished work waited to reach main. Its
"stale merge-queue entries" row only warns about one entry stuck for 6 hours. Add a 24 h
merge-wait phrase to that row. It is information only and adds no new warning threshold.
Independent of the plain-terms series: it touches only `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, its test,
and docs/cli.md.

**Approach.**
1. `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`: add an exported
   `mergeWaitPhrase(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): string | undefined` beside
   `checkStaleQueuedMerges`, modelled on `checkDurationPhrase` in `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`.
   - It takes `merge_done` events only, mapped through `finiteNumber(ev.queuedMs, 0)` and kept
     when > 0. A merge logged before `queuedMs` existed is skipped, the same rule as
     `foldUsageEvent` in `src/report/report-data.ts`. A `merge_failed` is not a wait that
     ended on main.
   - It sorts the values and takes the lower median, `values[Math.floor((n - 1) / 2)]`, and the
     longest.
   - It returns `merges in the last 24h waited <median> median, <longest> longest (<plural(n,
     "merge")>)`, with spans from `shortSpanPhrase` and `plural` from `src/text/phrases.ts`.
     It returns undefined when no event qualifies.
   - Its doc comment says the wait runs from the entry's last enqueue to its outcome and
     includes the merge check.
2. `checkStaleQueuedMerges(root, now)`: read
   `readEventsSince(root, MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS).events`, already imported in this file, and keep
   `ev.ts >= now - MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS`. `MERGE_WAIT_WINDOW_MS = 24 * 3600_000` is a new module
   constant. Pass the result to `mergeWaitPhrase`. When it returns a phrase, append
   ` · <phrase>` to the detail of both the ok and the warn outcome. Wrap the read in try/catch.
   On an error, omit the phrase and keep the outcome otherwise unchanged, so an unreadable event
   log never changes this row's level. Leave the level rules, the row name in
   `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, and every existing detail text as they are.
3. `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` description, after "the declared check
   and how long its passing merge checks took over the last 24 h", add "how long merges waited
   from enqueue to merged on main over the last 24 h (median and longest)".

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`, `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/doctor-backlog.test.ts` has a new test, "mergeWaitPhrase reports the lower median and
  longest of merge_done waits". Given `merge_done` events with `queuedMs` 60_000, 180_000 and
  600_000, it asserts the result equals
  `merges in the last 24h waited ${shortSpanPhrase(180_000)} median, ${shortSpanPhrase(600_000)} longest (3 merges)`.
  With two values it asserts the lower one is the median. It also checks that `merge_failed`
  events, `merge_done` events without `queuedMs` or with 0, and other event types give
  `undefined`.
- Another new test, "checkStaleQueuedMerges appends the last 24h merge wait to its detail",
  writes events with `logEvent` into a `queueRoot()`: two `merge_done` events with `queuedMs`
  within the window and one with `ts` 48 h ago. It asserts that the ok detail ends with
  ` · merges in the last 24h waited … (2 merges)`, so the 48 h-old one is excluded. It also
  asserts that a stale entry's warn detail carries the same suffix and stays `warn`.
- The existing `checkStaleQueuedMerges` tests pass unchanged. With no `merge_done` in the
  window, the detail has no ` · merges` suffix.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `plan|bug --list --done` and `questions --answered` take `--grep <text>` to find an old finished entry by its text (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** PLANS.md ## Done, BUGS.md ## Fixed, and QUESTIONS.md ## Answered keep every finished
entry, and they grow by several a day. The CLI shows only the newest N, and `-n` widens the
list without searching it. So "did we already do X?" or "how was that bug fixed?" means
scrolling hundreds of titles or grepping the raw file. Add a `--grep <text>` filter to the three
finished-entry lists, matching like `history --grep` and `logs --grep` do (case-insensitive
substring). Each match keeps its number from the unfiltered newest-first list, so the
number printed beside a match is the one `--show <n> --done` / `--show <n> --answered` takes.

**Approach.**
1. `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts` `listAndAnnounce`: in the arg loop, accept `--grep <text>` once
   (`rejectRepeatFlag`; take `args[++i]`, and when it is missing or empty, fail with
   `--grep needs text (usage: tumwater <command> --list --done --grep <text>)`). After the
   loop, fail with `--grep needs --done (it searches the finished entries)` when `--grep` is
   given without `--done`, beside the existing `-n needs --done` check. In the `done`
   branch: number `all` first (`{ entry, position: i + 1 }`). Then, when a pattern is set,
   keep only the entries whose `` `${title}\n${body}` `` lowercased includes the lowercased
   pattern. Then apply the limit (`count ?? 10`) to the matches. `older` counts matches left
   out, not all entries. Prose lines print `${position}. ${title}`, not `i + 1`.
   With a pattern and no match, print `no ${what} match "<text>"`. With a pattern, the
   header reads `${what} in ${fileName} matching "<text>", newest first:`. The trailing
   hint keeps its form but names the match count (`-n ${matches.length} shows more`).
   `--json` entries gain `position` (the unfiltered number) with or without a pattern,
   and `older` counts matches left out. Without `--grep`, every prose line and key the
   command prints today is unchanged. Update the function's doc comment.
2. `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`: give `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst` an optional
   `pattern?: string` and have it return each kept entry with its unfiltered newest-first
   `position`, filtered by the same title+body case-insensitive substring rule.
   `answeredQuestionList(root, count, pattern?)` prints `${position}. …` and, with a pattern,
   the header `answered questions in QUESTIONS.md matching "<text>", newest first:`, or
   `no answered questions match "<text>"` when none do.
   `answeredQuestionPayload(root, count, pattern?)` gives each question its `position`.
   `answeredQuestionAt` is unchanged.
   Put the one matcher in `src/backlog/backlog.ts` as an exported
   `entryMatches(entry: BacklogEntry, pattern: string): boolean`, used by both files.
3. `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts` `cmdQuestions`: accept `--grep <text>` under the same
   `!numbered` guard as `-n` (once; a missing or empty value fails like step 1's). Add
   `--grep` to the unknown-argument error's flag list and to the `rejectEqualsForm`
   specs. Fail with `--grep needs --answered (it searches the answered questions)` when
   `--grep` is given without `--answered`, and refuse it beside `--show`. Pass the pattern
   to `answeredQuestionList`/`answeredQuestionPayload`.
4. `src/cli/help.ts`: add `[--grep <text>]` to the `bug --list --done`, `plan --list --done`,
   and `questions --answered` stanzas, with one line saying it keeps the entries whose
   heading or body contains the text, case-insensitively, numbered as without it.
   `docs/cli.md`: name `--grep` in the Steer row's `--list --done` clause and the Answer
   row's `--answered` clause.

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog.ts`, `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`,
`src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`,
`docs/cli.md`, `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`, `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/backlog-write-list.test.ts`: a new test beside "plan --list --done lists the newest
  done plans, and bug --list --done an empty Fixed". From a ## Done holding entries whose
  bodies (not only titles) carry a word in mixed case: `plan --list --done --grep <word>`

- The same file: `plan --list --grep x` exits 1 with `--grep needs --done`, a repeated

### Plain terms code merge, part 10/11: Rename the merge identifiers in the status and dashboard and TUI and report and history and failure modules (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 9/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/ src/status/ src/report/ src/history/ src/failure/ src/gui/ and their tests, done 2026-10-17)

**Goal.** The presentation and reporting modules' merge-related identifiers say merge, including the dashboard's browser code. So do their comments and test names. A mechanical rename of about 540 lines with no behavior change.

**Approach.**
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `vet` → `verify`, `vetted` → `approved`;
  - a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`, and `Landed` inside a name that counts or carries the old `landed` event → `MergeDone`;
  - comments, test names and assertion messages follow the Glossary;
  - comment lines wrap at 100 columns.
- **Renames:**
  - ui/status-model.ts: `landingForRole` → `mergeForRole`, `LandingCell` → `MergeCell`, local `landing` → `merge`.
  - ui/status-render.ts: `lastLandedCell` → `lastMergedCell` (it renders `lastMergedAt`, so `Merged`).
  - status/status-polls.ts: `liveLandingMarker` → `liveMergeMarker`, local `landed` → `mergeDone`.
  - history/history-data.ts: `bucketLandingEvents` → `bucketMergeEvents`, and the member `landQueuedByLoop` → `mergeQueuedByLoop`. Rename both at every use, including src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts, src/failure/time-spend.ts and src/cli.ts.
  - failure/failure-data.ts: `LANDED_TOP` → `MERGE_DONE_TOP`, `LandedCommit` → `MergeDoneCommit`, `allLanded` → `allMergeDone`.
  - failure/time-spend.ts: `ResolvedLanding` → `ResolvedMerge`.
  - report/report-data.ts: `zeroLandingCounts` → `zeroMergeCounts`.
  - report/report-render.ts: `landingShareLine` → `mergeShareLine`, `landingFailures` → `mergeFailures`.
  - ui/badges.ts: `landingBadge` → `mergeBadge`, if the scripting series left the function's name.
  - Test locals: `landedRow`, `landedBefore`, `landedAfter`, `landedBeforeCommit`, `landedAfterCommit` and `landedFailed` → `mergeDone…`.
- **Browser code.** The dashboard's browser code in `String.raw` templates is not typechecked: `landingSummary` → `mergeSummary` (gui-client-drawer.ts and gui-client-loops.ts) and the test scope stub `landingTitle` → `mergeTitle`. Grep src/ui/gui/ and test/ for each one, scope stubs and expected call logs included.
- **Serialized fields.** `report --failures --json` and `/api/failures` serialize `landed`, `landedTotal` and the `landed` time class, so they belong to the scripting series. If any is still present, rename it by "Script interfaces" (`landed` → `merged`, `landedTotal` → `mergedTotal`; decision 3 allows the break) and say so in the commit body.
- **Move off the aliases.** These files still use aliases from parts 2–6, such as `readMergeQueue`, `renderMergeQueue`, `queueEntryMergeLabel`, `MergeInFlight`, `MERGE_STAGE_LABELS`, `isMergeChange`, `MergeChange`, `mergeStatePath`, `RETRIABLE_MERGE_RESULTS` and `applyMergeOutcome`. Move them to the new names, and delete each alias that test/exports.test.ts then reports unused.
- **docs/invariants.md:** `LANDED_TOP` and `landedTotal`. Also update the quoted test names "… price into error-class, not landed" and "a landed list over the newest-10 cap …" when this part renames those tests.
- **Leave alone:**
  - user-visible strings and expected-output literals;
  - event type names;
  - PLANS.md and BUGS.md titles quoted in comments, kept verbatim (test/plan-citations.test.ts).
- Skip any name that an earlier series already renamed.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/` (status-model.ts, status-render.ts, status-payload.ts, badges.ts, progress-data.ts, tone.ts, gui/*.ts, tui/*.ts), `src/status/`, `src/report/`, `src/history/`, `src/failure/`, `src/gui/`; the `landQueuedByLoop` uses in `src/tick/tick-detail-data.ts` and `src/cli.ts`. Tests: `test/gui*.test.ts`, `test/tui*.test.ts`, `test/status*.test.ts`, `test/report*.test.ts`, `test/history*.test.ts`, `test/failure*.test.ts`, `test/time-spend.test.ts`, `test/badges.test.ts`, `test/progress.test.ts`. Docs: docs/invariants.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**

**Done notes.** Also renamed the status snapshot field `landQueue` → `mergeQueue` (and its fixtures); internal phase/EventKind keys marked `vocabulary-ok` (`landing`, `vetted`), the user-visible "Landed today" tile and "No unlanded work." text, the `lander` event loop id and the retired-key lists in test/script-keys.test.ts and test/status-payload.test.ts were left. ### `tumwater report` shows each day's median merge wait, from a merge's enqueue to its commit on main (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** The report shows how long the merge check takes ("Merge check median") but not how
long a finished run's commit waits before it reaches main: queued behind other merges, reviewed,
checked, and fast-forwarded. When merges back up, every role's work sits finished but unmerged,
and nothing in `tumwater report` or its `--json` says so. Add a per-day "Merge wait median" line
beside the existing "Merge check median", fed by a new `queuedMs` field on the merge outcome
event.

**Approach.**
1. `src/merge/merge-slot.ts` `writeMergeOutcome`: add
   `queuedMs: Math.max(0, Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt)` to the `merge_done`/`merge_failed`
   event it logs (both types, the same payload; `entry.enqueuedAt` is the `MergeEntry` field
   already set at enqueue in `src/merge/merge-queue.ts`). It is the span from this entry's
   enqueue to its outcome and includes the slot's own `durationMs`. A leftover-recovery
   re-enqueue writes a new entry with its own `enqueuedAt`, so a retried change's wait counts
   from its last enqueue; say so in the comment. Update the `merge_done` and `merge_failed`
   comments in `src/events/events.ts` to name `queuedMs`.
2. `src/report/report-data.ts`: add `mergeWaitsMs: number[]` to `UsageFold` and `DayFold` (and
   initialize it to `[]` everywhere `checkDurationsMs: []` is initialized now). In
   `foldUsageEvent`'s `merge_done`/`merge_failed` branch, for `merge_done` only, push
   `finiteNumber(ev.queuedMs, 0)` when it is > 0, so a merge logged before this change (no
   field) is skipped rather than counted as zero. Add an optional `mergeWaitMedianMs?: number`
   to `ReportDay` with a doc comment like `checkMedianMs`'s. In `collectReport`, set it inside
   the `role === undefined` block with the same lower-median rule as `checkMedianMs`. Move
   the two-line lower-median computation into a small local `lowerMedian(values)` helper in
   report-data.ts and use it for both fields. Leave the field absent when the day has no
   measured merge. The `--since` report (`collectReportSince`) is not changed.
3. `src/report/report-render.ts`: right after the `**Merge check median:**` line in the
   team-scope block, print `**Merge wait median:** <MM-DD> <span> · …` using the same
   `monthDay` + `shortSpanPhrase` formatting. Print it only when some day carries
   `mergeWaitMedianMs`.
4. `docs/cli.md`: in the `tumwater report` description in the Audit row, add that the team
   report shows each day's median merge wait (enqueue to merged on main) beside the merge
   check median.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-slot.ts`, `src/events/events.ts`,
`src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, `docs/cli.md`,
`test/merge-slot.test.ts`, `test/report-data.test.ts`, `test/report.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/merge-slot.test.ts`: extend "a merge's nonzero usage rides its merge_done event and
  the entry is dropped" (or add a sibling test) to assert that `mergeDone.queuedMs` is a
  number ≥ 0 and at most `Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt` taken after the call. A
  `merge_failed` outcome carries `queuedMs` too.
- `test/report-data.test.ts`: a new test beside "collectReport gives each day the lower median
  of its passing full-suite checks, team scope only". From `merge_done` events with `queuedMs`
  values on two days, plus one `merge_done` without the field and one `merge_failed` with one,
  assert that each day's `mergeWaitMedianMs` is the lower median of only the `merge_done`
  values that carry the field. A day with none must not have the key at all
  (`!("mergeWaitMedianMs" in day)`), and a role-scoped `collectReport(root, n, "feature")`
  sets it on no day.
- `test/report.test.ts`: a new test beside "renderReportMarkdown prints Merge check median for
  the days that carry one, team scope only". It asserts that
  `/^\*\*Merge wait median:\*\* 09-10 12m$/m` (or whatever `shortSpanPhrase` prints for the
  fixture value) appears for a day carrying the field, and that the line is absent when no day
  carries one and on a role-scoped report.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater questions --show <n> --answered` prints the Nth newest answered question in full, context and recorded answer (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the waiting plain-terms rename series — touches only src/backlog/question-answer.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `questions --answered` prints each answered question as a `- <title> — <answer line>` bullet, the answer line truncated. To reread a question's full context or a multi-line decision, the operator must pipe `--answered --json` through a JSON tool or scroll QUESTIONS.md. `plan --show <n> --done` and `bug --show <n> --done` already print a finished entry in full, and the dashboard drawer and TUI backlog pane open answered questions read-only; only the CLI lacks it — today `questions --show 1 --answered` fails with `--show and --answered cannot be combined`. Let that combination print the Nth newest answered question, and number the `--answered` lines so `<n>` can be read off the list.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`:
  - Add `export function answeredQuestionAt(root: string, n: number): { position: number; title: string; body: string; answeredOn: string | null } | null`, reading `answeredQuestionEntries(root).reverse()` (newest first, the order `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst` uses) and returning entry `n - 1` with `answeredOn: answerDate(e.body)`, or null past the end. Also export `answeredQuestionCount(root: string): number` (`answeredQuestionEntries(root).length`) for the error message.
  - `answeredQuestionList`: render each line as `${i + 1}. ${e.title}${…preview}` instead of `- ${e.title}…`. Keep the header and the `(N older; -n <count> shows more)` line unchanged; `answeredQuestionPayload` and `answeredQuestionSummaries` are unchanged. Rewrite its doc comment: the lines are numbered by `--show <n> --answered` position, newest first, a numbering separate from the `## Open` positions `questions answer <n>` takes.
- `cmdQuestions` in `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, the `show !== undefined` branch: drop the `--show and --answered cannot be combined` refusal. When `answeredFlag`, call `answeredQuestionAt(root, show)`; on null `fail(\`no answered question at position ${show} (${count} in QUESTIONS.md)\`)`, mirroring the open-question wording (a missing file or empty `## Answered` reads `(0 in QUESTIONS.md)`). Otherwise `--json` prints the object via `sayJson`, prose prints `renderShownQuestion({ title, body })` — heading verbatim, blank line, body (the body holds the `**Answered …**` stamp and decision). Keep the existing `words.length > 0` and `--file` refusals ahead of it for both forms; `-n` together with `--show` fails with `-n does not apply to --show` (check it in the `show` branch before the lookup, since `-n` with `--answered` otherwise passes the `-n needs --answered` check). Without `--answered` the branch behaves as today.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: after the `questions --show <n> [--json]` stanza add `tumwater questions --show <n> --answered [--json]`: "Print the Nth entry of `questions --answered` (newest first) in full, context and recorded answer; --json prints {position, title, body, answeredOn}". In the `--answered` stanza change "List the newest answered questions, newest first" to "List the newest answered questions, numbered, newest first".
- `docs/cli.md`, "Answer open questions" row: after "`tumwater questions --answered [-n <count>]` lists the newest answered questions with their answer lines, newest first" add ", numbered, and `--show <n> --answered` prints the Nth one in full".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/question-answer.ts`, `src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/question-commands.test.ts`, `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/question-commands.test.ts` "answeredQuestionList shows the newest answers first with their answer lines" expects `^1\. Q12 — Answered 2026-10-12 by operator: decision 12$` and `^10\. Q3 — …$` in place of the bullets; "answeredQuestionList handles an entry without a stamp and empty sections" expects `…newest first:\n1. Bare`. A new unit test there checks `answeredQuestionAt(root, 1)` on `twelveAnswered()` is `{position: 1, title: "Q12", answeredOn: "2026-10-12", …}` with the body containing `decision 12`, and `answeredQuestionAt(root, 13)` is null.
- `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts` "questions --answered lists the newest answers and refuses misuse" expects `newest first:\n1\. New`.
- New test in `test/cli-questions-list.test.ts`, "questions --show <n> --answered prints one answered question in full": with QUESTIONS.md holding one open and two answered entries (the newer with a multi-line context and decision), `questions --show 1 --answered` exits 0 and prints exactly the newer heading, a blank line, and its body; `--show 2 --answered` prints the older; `--answered --show 1 --json` parses to `{position: 1, title, body, answeredOn: "<its date>"}`; `--show 3 --answered` exits 1 matching `no answered question at position 3 \(2 in QUESTIONS\.md\)`; `--show 1 --answered -n 2` exits 1 matching `-n does not apply to --show`; `--show 1` still prints the open entry.
- In "questions --show refuses misuse", the `[["--show", "1", "--answered"], /cannot be combined/]` case is removed (that form now succeeds); the other cases are unchanged.

### The TUI backlog pane's up/down reach the "answered recently" rows and open each answered question's full context and recorded answer read-only (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; done 2026-10-17 by the feature role; independent of the waiting plain-terms rename series and of the in-flight GUI "Answered recently" drawer plan — touches only src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts, tui-pane.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-editors.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests)

**Goal.** The TUI's backlog pane lists the 5 newest answered questions under `answered recently (K):`, but they are text only: a title and a truncated `**Answered …` preview. The done Done/Fixed browse plan made up/down continue from the open entries into the `done recently` / `fixed recently` rows and skipped the answered rows, so the operator still cannot reread an answered question's context or the full answer the director acted on without leaving the TUI. (The GUI gets the same capability in the in-flight "Answered recently" drawer plan.) Let up/down walk the answered rows too, in the list's visual order, and show each one's full body in entry mode, read-only.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, `browsableBacklogEntries`: between `...labeledBacklogEntries(root)` and the `done` rows, insert the newest answered questions as `label: "answered"` rows: `answeredQuestionEntries(root).reverse().slice(0, DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS)`, mapped through the same `finished` helper (give the helper a `count` argument, or slice before calling it, so answered rows use `DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS` and done/fixed rows keep `DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED`). Import `answeredQuestionEntries` from `src/backlog/backlog.ts` and `DASHBOARD_ANSWERED_QUESTIONS` from `src/ui/status-payload.ts` (already exported). `answeredQuestionEntries` returns `## Answered` in file order, oldest first. The list's rows come from `answeredQuestionSummaries` → `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst` (src/backlog/question-answer.ts), which reverses and slices the same list. So browse row `k` is the list's `k`th answered row. Rewrite the doc comment: the browse order is now exactly the list's visual order (open entries, answered, done, fixed). Answered, done and fixed rows are read-only, and the open entries keep their indexes.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, the `backlog` branch of `paneBody`: no logic change. List mode filters `flat` by label (`plan`, `bug`, `question`), so the answered rows (label `answered`) do not double into the open-questions section. The `answered recently` rows keep coming from `answeredQuestionSummaries`, so the list text does not change. Entry mode's header reads `answered: <verbatim title>`. Update the two comments: the opening "then the newest done plans and fixed bugs" becomes "then the newest answered questions, done plans and fixed bugs", and the "they stay out of `flat`, so selection and the edit keys never reach them" note becomes "they are in `flat` (up/down open their bodies), but no edit key acts on them".
- Guard the keys that act on the selection, so an answered row never reaches their plan/bug `else` arm:
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` Ctrl+X: extend `picked.label === "done" || picked.label === "fixed"` to include `"answered"`.
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` Ctrl+E: extend the same condition the same way.
  - In both, change the flash to `a done plan, fixed bug or answered question is read-only`.
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` Ctrl+A needs no change. Its `entry?.label !== "question"` refusal ("only an open question can be answered here") already covers answered rows, and its position math counts only `plan`/`bug` labels.

- `docs/cli.md`, "Answer open questions" row: change "(the TUI's backlog pane lists them too, read-only, under the open ones)" to "(the TUI's backlog pane lists them too, under the open ones, where up/down open each one's full context and answer read-only)".

### Plain terms code merge, part 9/11: Rename the merge identifiers in the gates and doctor and backlog and git and operator and concurrency and check modules (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 8/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/gates/ src/doctor/ src/backlog/ src/git/ src/operator/ src/concurrency/ src/baseline/ src/build/ and their tests, done 2026-10-17)

*Replanned 2026-10-17 by the plan role after two rejected reviews: the last objection was a
rewritten comment paragraph in test/worktree.test.ts that still said "the merge pipeline's
concurrent vets". This plan now gives the rule for the noun "vet", names the call sites outside
the listed directories, and adds a grep for leftover words to the acceptance criteria.*

**Goal.** These modules' merge-related identifiers, comments and test names say merge. The backlog heading grammar keeps its word. A rename of about 360 lines with no behavior change.

**Approach.**
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `vet` → `verify`, `vetted` → `approved`, and a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`;
  - comments, test names and assertion messages follow the Glossary ("unlanded" → "not yet merged");
  - **the noun "vet" in prose becomes "verify", plural "verifies"**: test/worktree.test.ts's two
    prune/add-race comments ("the landing pipeline's concurrent vets", "the loser's vet") become
    "the merge pipeline's concurrent verifies" and "the loser's verify". Use the same word in
    src/baseline/main-red.ts ("the landing pipeline's vets"), src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts
    ("a vet task", "the vet: providerWaitStage", "or vet waiting"), src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts
    ("A vet plus a merge", "a vet under way"), src/gates/disk-gate.ts ("landing vets") and
    src/gates/gate-polls.ts ("the land queue starts no new vet" → "the merge queue starts no new
    verify"). Rewrite every comment sentence that holds a retired word, including ones you only
    reflow;
  - comment lines wrap at 100 columns.
- **Prose after the rename** (an earlier attempt was rejected three times on these alone): read each
  edited comment, test name and assertion message as a sentence, not as a word swap.
  - **Reflow every edited comment paragraph** so only its last line is short. A rename that
    shortens a line (e.g. `checkStaleQueuedLandings` → `checkStaleQueuedMerges` in
    doctor-backlog.ts's `LAND_QUEUE_STALE_MS` and `checkStaleQueuedLandings` doc comments) pulls
    the following words up; never leave a mid-paragraph stub line or an early break.
  - **No doubled or garbled words.** Where the swap would produce "merged merge", "merge merge" or
    similar, reword: maintenance-quota.ts's "One merged landing the window keeps" becomes "One
    merged change the window keeps".
  - **Compound adjectives take "unmerged",** matching retire.ts's own "unmerged commit(s)": test
    strings such as test/retire.test.ts's "unlanded-commit refusal removes nothing" become
    "unmerged-commit refusal removes nothing", and "unlanded work"/"unlanded branch commits"
    become "unmerged work"/"unmerged branch commits". "not yet merged" is for predicate use
    ("work not yet merged").
- **Renames:**
  - doctor-backlog.ts: `checkStaleQueuedLandings` → `checkStaleQueuedMerges`, `LAND_QUEUE_STALE_MS` → `MERGE_QUEUE_STALE_MS`, local `landed` → `mergeDone`.
  - backlog-eligibility.ts: `prerequisitesLanded` → `prerequisitesMerged`. The heading keyword stays: `requiredParts`' `/requires\s+(.+?)\s+landed\b/` and the "requires … landed" prose are backlog grammar that every PLANS.md heading uses, not identifiers.
  - operator-requests.ts: `AbortableLanding` → `AbortableMerge`, including its uses in src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts. Locals `landing`/`landings` → `merge`/`merges`.
  - retire.ts: the member `landingRefPresent` → `mergeRefPresent`, local `landing` → `mergeRef`.
  - maintenance-quota.ts: `perWorkLanding` → `perWorkMerge`, and the member `hasQueuedLanding` → `hasQueuedMerge` (in src/gates/gate-polls.ts too).
  - Tests: `pinnedUnlanded` → `pinnedNotMerged`, and `vetA`/`vetB`/`vetGranted` → `verifyA`/`verifyB`/`verifyGranted`.
  - Comments that list tiers (src/concurrency/semaphore.ts: "LANDING_TIER, MERGE_TIER") → `VERIFY_TIER`, `MERGE_TIER`.
  - src/baseline/ and src/build/ (the main check and the build checks): mostly comments and test names. src/baseline's `landStack` call becomes `mergeStack`, and the comments' `verifyLanding` mentions become `verifyMerge`.
- **git/worktree.ts's `removeLegacyLandWorktrees` keeps its name.** It removes the legacy `_land-<role>` worktrees, which "State and git" keeps.
- **Collisions.** test/operator-requests.test.ts and test/check-permit.test.ts already bind a local `merge` near the `landing` locals. If a renamed local would share a scope with it (tsc reports the clash), use `inFlightMerge` or `mergeCheck` instead.
- **Move off the aliases.** These files still use aliases from parts 2–6, such as `queuedMergeRoles`, `readMergeQueue`, `readMergeMarker`, `mergeChanges`, `mergeRefName`, `VERIFY_TIER` and `ApprovedMerge`. Move them to the new names, and delete each alias that test/exports.test.ts then reports unused.
- **Leave alone:**
  - user-visible strings and expected-output literals (doctor check titles were set by the text series);
  - event type names;
  - legacy readers;
  - PLANS.md and BUGS.md titles quoted in comments, kept verbatim (test/plan-citations.test.ts).
- Skip any name that an earlier series already renamed.

**Files touched.** `src/gates/`, `src/doctor/`, `src/backlog/`, `src/git/`, `src/operator/`, `src/concurrency/`, `src/baseline/`, `src/build/`. Call sites outside them, renamed and nothing else: `src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts` (`AbortableMerge` uses), `src/status/status-polls.ts` (the `perWorkLanding` parameter and its pass to `maintenanceQuota`), and `test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts` (a `hasQueuedLanding: false` literal). Tests: `test/maintenance-quota.test.ts`, `test/*gate*.test.ts`, `test/doctor-*.test.ts`, `test/backlog-*.test.ts`, `test/git*.test.ts`, `test/worktree*.test.ts`, `test/operator-*.test.ts`, `test/retire.test.ts`, `test/check-permit.test.ts`, `test/semaphore.test.ts`, `test/provider-lease.test.ts`, `test/main-baseline*.test.ts`, `test/main-red.test.ts`, `test/attribute-red-check.test.ts`, `test/build-*.test.ts`, `test/dep-install.test.ts`.

- test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts still parses `requires part 2/5 landed` headings unchanged.
- In the listed directories, no identifier, comment or test name uses a retired merge word, except `removeLegacyLandWorktrees`, the grammar keyword and quoted backlog titles. Check it with
  `git grep -nwiE 'vet|vets|vetted|vetting|unlanded|landing|landings|land|landed' -- src/gates src/doctor src/backlog src/git src/operator src/concurrency src/baseline src/build test/worktree.test.ts`
  plus the test files listed above, run through `grep -v 'vocabulary-ok'`. It may print only

  expected-output literals this part leaves alone. In particular, no comment in

- `git grep -nE '\b(merged?|merging) merge' -- src test` prints no line this part introduced, and

### The TUI backlog pane's up/down reach the "done recently" and "fixed recently" rows and open each finished entry's full body read-only (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; done 2026-10-17 by the feature role; independent of the waiting plain-terms rename series and of the in-flight GUI drawer and `--show <n> --done` plans — touches only src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts, tui-pane.ts, tui-keys.ts, tui-panes.ts, tui-editors.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests)

**Goal.** The TUI's backlog pane lists the 5 newest Done plans and Fixed bugs under `done recently (N):` / `fixed recently (N):`, but they are text only. Up/down walk `labeledBacklogEntries` (open plans, bugs, questions), so the operator sees a finished entry's title and date and cannot read what the plan specified or how the bug was fixed without leaving the TUI. The GUI is getting the same capability in the in-flight "Done recently"/"Fixed recently" drawer plan. Let up/down continue past the open entries into those finished rows, and show each one's full body in entry mode, read-only. Answered questions stay text only: their newest-first order comes from `answeredQuestionsNewestFirst` (src/backlog/question-answer.ts), not file order, so they are out of scope here.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: export `DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED` (today it is a module-private `const`) so the TUI slices the same 5 rows `recentFinished` shows.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`: add `browsableBacklogEntries(root)`, which returns the same element type as `labeledBacklogEntries`: `[...labeledBacklogEntries(root), ...donePlanEntries(root).slice(0, DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED).map(done), ...fixedBugEntries(root).slice(0, DASHBOARD_RECENT_FINISHED).map(fixed)]`. Each finished row is `{ label: "done" | "fixed", mark: "", hold: null, claimer: undefined, ...e }`, with its title kept verbatim (stamp included). The open entries keep their indexes, so every plan/bug/question position computed from a selection index is unchanged. Doc comment: browsing order is the list's visual order minus the answered rows, and finished rows are read-only.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, the `backlog` branch of `paneBody`: read `browsableBacklogEntries(root)` once as the list (replacing the `labeledBacklogEntries` call), and clamp `sel` against its length. List mode filters it by label exactly as today (`listed("bug")`, `plans`), and the finished list rows keep coming from `recentFinished`, so the list text does not change. Entry mode works as today. Its header line `${e.label}: ${e.title}${e.mark}` reads `done: <verbatim title>` / `fixed: <verbatim title>` for finished rows. Update the "read-only for the same reason … stay out of `flat`" comments: answered rows stay out, while done/fixed rows are browsable but no edit key acts on them.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`: define `flat` as `() => browsableBacklogEntries(root)`, and update its comment. Both `createTuiPanes` and `createTuiEditors` receive it, so the arrow handler (`moveEntrySelection(flat().length, …)`) and the PgUp/PgDn entry-scroll handler in `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` reach the finished rows with no change. Keep the `flat()` type annotations in tui-panes.ts/tui-editors.ts as `ReturnType<typeof labeledBacklogEntries>`, since the element type is identical.
- Guard the keys that act on the selection, because a finished row must never fall into their `else` (plan/bug) arm:
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` Ctrl+X: before the `picked.label === "question"` branch, add `else if (picked.label === "done" || picked.label === "fixed") flashMessage("a done plan or fixed bug is read-only")`, leaving `cancelArmed` unset.
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` Ctrl+E: the same branch, with the same message, leaving `entryEditFor` null.
  - `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` Ctrl+A: the existing `entry?.label !== "question"` refusal already covers finished rows. Its position math `sel - entries.filter((e) => e.label !== "question").length + 1` would now also count the finished rows and give a wrong (negative) position, so change the filter to count `e.label === "plan" || e.label === "bug"`.
  - The Enter-to-save edit path (`entries[target.kind === "plan" ? … : plans + target.position - 1]`) indexes only plan/bug positions, which come before the appended rows, so it needs no change.
- `docs/cli.md`, the "Steer the project" row: change "and the TUI's backlog pane lists them too, read-only, after the answered questions" to "and the TUI's backlog pane lists them too, after the answered questions, where up/down open each one's full body read-only".

**Files touched.** `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-backlog.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-pane.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`, `test/tui-keys.test.ts`.

- New test in `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`, "browsableBacklogEntries appends the newest five done plans, then the newest five fixed bugs, after the open entries". With one Planned entry, one open bug, one open question, six Done entries and one Fixed entry, it returns 9 rows: the three open ones exactly as `labeledBacklogEntries` gives them, then five `done` rows (newest first, verbatim titles and bodies, `mark: ""`, `hold: null`), then one `fixed` row.
- `test/tui-backlog.test.ts`, "paneBody's backlog list shows the newest done plans and fixed bugs, read-only": its list-mode assertions are unchanged, as is the `selectedEntry: 0` assertion (`plan: Open plan`, no finished titles). New assertions: `selectedEntry: 1` paints `done: D6 (planned 2026-09-01, done 2026-10-06)` then `Body.`; `selectedEntry: 6` paints `fixed: Old bug (fixed 2026-10-02)`; `selectedEntry: 99` clamps to that same fixed row.

### `tumwater plan --show <n> --done` and `tumwater bug --show <n> --done` print the Nth newest Done plan or Fixed bug in full (planned 2026-10-17 by the plan role; independent of the waiting plain-terms rename series — touches only src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-17

**Goal.** `--list --done` prints only the titles of the newest finished entries, as `- <title>` bullets. To read what a done plan specified or how a bug was fixed, the operator has to pipe `--list --done --json` through a JSON tool or scroll PLANS.md/BUGS.md past every open entry. `--show <n>` already prints an open entry in full (`showAndAnnounce`), and `questions --show` does the same for questions. Let `--show <n> --done` print the Nth newest finished entry the same way, and number the `--list --done` lines so `<n>` can be read off the list.

**Approach.** All logic goes in `src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts`, using the readers it already imports (`donePlanEntries`, `fixedBugEntries`, `completionDate`, `DONE_DATE_RE`, `FIXED_DATE_RE`).
- `showAndAnnounce(root, args, command)`: accept `--done` once (`rejectRepeatFlag(done, "--done")`, the same as `listAndAnnounce`). With `--done`:
  - Read `all = command === "bug" ? fixedBugEntries(root) : donePlanEntries(root)`. These are in file order, which is newest first, the same order `--list --done` uses.
  - When `position > all.length`, `fail(\`no ${command === "bug" ? "fixed bug" : "done plan"} at position ${position} (${all.length} in ${command === "bug" ? "BUGS.md" : "PLANS.md"})\`)`. This mirrors the wording `locateEntry` (src/backlog/backlog-write.ts) uses for open entries, and an empty or missing section reads `(0 in …)`.
  - Otherwise `entry = all[position - 1]`. Prose prints `renderShownEntry({ title: entry.title, body: entry.body })`. Unlike `showEntry`, the title is kept verbatim: the `(done …)`/`fixed …` stamp is what the operator is looking for. `--json` prints `{ position, title, body, completedOn: completionDate(entry.title, dateRe) }`, with `dateRe` chosen as `listAndAnnounce`'s done branch chooses it. There is no `hold` key, because finished entries have no hold.
  - Without `--done` the function behaves as it does today. `cli.ts` already routes any `--show` invocation to `showAndAnnounce`, so `src/cli.ts` needs no change.
- `listAndAnnounce`'s done branch: render the prose lines as `${i + 1}. ${e.title}` instead of `- ${e.title}`, so the list numbers match `--show <n> --done`. Keep the header and the `(N older; -n M shows more)` line as they are, and leave `--json` unchanged. Update the doc comment above `listAndAnnounce` ("bullets" becomes "numbered") and the one above `showAndAnnounce` to name `--done`.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: under both the `bug --show <n>` and `plan --show <n>` stanzas, add a stanza `tumwater <cmd> --show <n> --done [--json]` reading "Print the Nth entry of `<cmd> --list --done` (newest first) in full; --json prints {position, title, body, completedOn}". ### `tumwater report`'s day report gains a `Merge check median` line giving each day's median passing merge-check time, so the operator sees the suite slowing over days (planned 2026-10-16 by the plan role; independent of the waiting plain-terms rename series and the in-flight GUI failed-runs chart — touches src/report/, src/build/build-check-events.ts and tests only, and leaves src/doctor/ and src/ui/ alone) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** `tumwater doctor`'s `check` row (`checkDurationPhrase` in `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) says how long passing merge checks took over the last 24 h. That is one number, with no history. The merge lock waits on the declared check, and a test suite tends to grow slower a little every day. That trend is what tells an operator to act before a check times out, and nothing shows it. The day report (`renderReportMarkdown` in `src/report/report-render.ts`) already has a day series built from the event log, so give it one more per-day figure: the median wall clock of that day's passing full-suite checks.

**Approach.**
- `src/build/build-check-events.ts`: export `isPassingFullCheck(ev: HarnessEvent): boolean`. It is true when `ev.type === "build_check"`, `ev.status === "passed"`, and `String(ev.scope)` is one of `merge`, `batch`, `baseline`. These are the scopes `checkDurationPhrase` counts: a `gate` check can run a subset of the suite. Import `HarnessEvent` as a type only, so the module keeps its no-runtime-cycle note true. Leave `checkDurationPhrase` as it is in this change, because the in-flight merge-rename part 9/11 edits the doctor modules. A later cleanup can switch it over to the predicate.
- `src/report/report-data.ts`:
  - Add `checkDurationsMs: number[]` to `UsageFold` and `DayFold`, with a short doc comment, and seed it `[]` wherever a fold seeds `revisionsByRole: {}`.
  - In `foldUsageEvent`, add a branch: when `isPassingFullCheck(ev)` is true and `finiteNumber(ev.durationMs, 0) > 0`, push that duration. The `build_check` type matches none of the existing branches, so add this as one more `else if`.
  - Add the optional field `checkMedianMs?: number` to `ReportDay`. Its doc comment says it is the lower median of the day's passing full-suite check durations and is absent when the day has none.
  - In `collectReport`, only in the team branch (`role === undefined`), set `day.checkMedianMs` to the lower median when `fold.checkDurationsMs` is non-empty: sort a copy ascending and take index `Math.floor((n - 1) / 2)`, the same rule as `checkDurationPhrase`. The role-scope branch leaves it unset, because checks belong to the merge slot, not to a role, just as the merge fields stay unset there.
  - `SinceReport` gets no new field: `collectReportSince` ignores `checkDurationsMs`.
- `src/report/report-render.ts`, `renderReportMarkdown`: inside the existing team-only `if (data.role === undefined)` block, after the `Merge failures by role` line, collect the series days that carry `checkMedianMs`, in series order. When there is at least one, push `**Merge check median:** 10-14 95s · 10-16 2m`: each part is `monthDay(d.date)` and `shortSpanPhrase(d.checkMedianMs)` (from `src/text/phrases.ts`), joined with ` · `. Days without a check are left out. When no day has one, print no line (zero means absent, like `Merge failures by role`). Add a one-line comment in the style of its neighbours. `renderSinceReportMarkdown` is unchanged.
- The GUI and the `report --json` output carry the new optional field through the existing serialization, so nothing changes there. Charting it is a separate later plan.

**Files touched.** `src/build/build-check-events.ts`, `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, `test/build-check-events.test.ts`, `test/report-data.test.ts`, `test/report.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/report-data.test.ts`, logging events the way the existing `collectReport` tests do. On one day, log passing `build_check` events with scope `merge` (60 000 ms), `batch` (120 000 ms) and `baseline` (90 000 ms), plus a passing `gate`-scope check and a `failed` merge-scope check that must both be ignored. `collectReport(root, 2)` gives that day `checkMedianMs === 90000`. The other day has no `checkMedianMs` key. With `role` set, no day carries the key.
- New test in `test/report.test.ts`, on hand-built `ReportData`:

  - A series where no day has the field renders no `Merge check median` line.
  - The same series with `role` set renders no line either.
