### The dashboards raise an amber `install` alert while the root checkout's `node_modules` is behind `package-lock.json` (planned 2026-10-16 by the plan role; independent of the waiting plain-terms series and of the in-flight "Image reroutes by role" report plan — it adds one module under `src/status/`, one optional `StatusSnapshot` field, and one branch in `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** When a post-merge re-sync (`syncRootInstall` in `src/build/dep-install.ts`) fails, every check installs into its own tree until a later merge retries. Today the operator sees this only as a `warn` line in the feed or by running `tumwater doctor`, whose `root install` row (`checkRootInstall` in `src/doctor/doctor-install.ts`) reports the drift. The dashboard, the TUI, and `tumwater status` raise no alert. These surfaces should show the drift the way they show the disk floor: an amber alert that names the drifted packages and the fix, and clears once the drift is gone. Clearing on drift, not on a later `dep_install` event, also clears it when the operator fixes the install by hand.

**Approach.**
- New module `src/status/status-install.ts` (`// vocabulary: plain` header like its siblings) exporting `collectRootInstallDrift(root: string, now: number): string[]`. It returns `installDrift(root)` from `src/build/dep-install.ts`, throttled per root through a module-level `Map<string, { at: number; drift: string[] }>`. A cached value younger than `ROOT_INSTALL_POLL_MS = 60_000` (measured against the passed `now`) is returned as a copy. Otherwise it recomputes and stores. Cap the map like `MAX_STAT_CACHED` in `src/files/stat-cache.ts` does: clear it when it reaches 64 roots. Throttle rather than stat-key because the answer depends on two files (the lockfile and each installed manifest), and the dashboard polls every second, so it must not re-parse a large lockfile each time. Export a `resetRootInstallCache()` for tests. `installDrift` already returns `[]` when there is no lockfile or it cannot be read, so a non-node project costs one failed read per minute.
- `src/status/status-data.ts`: `StatusSnapshot` gains `rootInstallDrift?: string[]`, documented as "direct dependencies the root checkout's `node_modules` does not hold at `package-lock.json`'s pin (the doctor's `root install` row); absent when none drift". `snapshot()` sets it from `collectRootInstallDrift(root, now)` only when the result is non-empty. The value does not depend on the team running: a stopped team's worktrees still borrow the root install.
- `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`: add `"rootInstallDrift"` to `teamAlerts`'s `Pick<StatusSnapshot, …>` and push right after the `disk` branch:
  - key `"install"`, tone `"amber"`
  - title: "The root install is behind package-lock.json"
  - detail: `${plural(n, "direct dependency", "direct dependencies")} not installed as pinned (${names}). Run npm install in the project's root checkout; until then each check installs into its own tree, and \`tumwater doctor\` names the last re-sync failure.`
  - `actions: []`
  - Show at most 5 names, then `, +N more`. `plural` is already imported from `src/text/phrases.ts`. No change to `src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts` or `tui-frame.ts` alertLines: both render alerts generically. `status-render.ts` filters only `stopped`, so `tumwater status` shows it too.

**Files touched.** `src/status/status-install.ts` (new), `src/status/status-data.ts`, `src/ui/team-alerts.ts`, `test/team-alerts.test.ts`, and a new `test/status-install.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/team-alerts.test.ts`: a snapshot with `rootInstallDrift: ["ink", "typescript"]` raises exactly one alert with key `install` and tone `amber`, whose detail names both packages and "npm install". `base` (no field) and `rootInstallDrift: []` raise no `install` alert. Seven names show five, then "+2 more".
- `test/status-install.test.ts`, on a temp dir with a `package-lock.json` pinning one devDependency at `1.0.0` and `node_modules/<name>/package.json` at `0.9.0`:
  - `collectRootInstallDrift` returns `[name]`.
  - After the manifest is rewritten to `1.0.0`, a call with the same `now` still returns `[name]` (throttled), and a call with `now + 60_001` returns `[]`.
  - A dir with no lockfile returns `[]`.
  - Call `resetRootInstallCache()` between tests.
- `snapshot()` on a fixture repo with that drift carries `rootInstallDrift: [name]`. With matching versions the key is absent. Assert this in `test/status-install.test.ts` through `snapshot(root)` if the existing status tests' fixture helper makes that cheap; otherwise the two unit tests above suffice.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms code merge, part 8/11: Rename the merge identifiers in the orchestrator and scheduling modules (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 7/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/orchestrator/ src/scheduling/ and their tests and fixtures, done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The orchestrator's and the scheduler's merge-related identifiers, comments and test names say merge. A mechanical rename of about 420 lines with no behavior change.

**Approach.**
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `landings` → `merges`, `vet` → `verify`, `vetted` → `approved`, and a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`;
  - comments, test names and assertion messages follow the Glossary;
  - comment lines wrap at 100 columns.
- **"On main" names take `Merged`.** These mean "qualifying work is on main", so they take `Merged` rather than `MergeDone`:
  - src/scheduling/work-merged-cache.ts: `WorkLandedCache` → `WorkMergedCache`, `workLandedHeads` → `workMergedHeads`;
  - scheduling.ts: `workLanded` → `workMerged`, `workLandedSinceLast` → `workMergedSinceLast`;
  - the orchestrator-scheduling member `workLandedSince` → `workMergedSince`.
- **Other renames:**
  - the orchestrator option `handoffLandingWindowMs` → `handoffMergeWindowMs` (orchestrator.ts, test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts and the tests);
  - backoff.ts: `YIELD_LAND` → `YIELD_MERGE`;
  - test: `seedLandQueue` → `seedMergeQueue`;
  - locals: `landings` → `merges` (orchestrator.ts's pipeline instance, once-round.ts).
- **Keep calls to `removeLegacyLandWorktrees` as they are.** It removes the legacy `_land-<role>` worktrees, which "State and git" keeps recognizing.
- **Fixtures.** The rest of test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts and test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts belongs to this part (comments, locals and test-only names). Part 2/11 already renamed their three exported helpers.

### `tumwater report` gains an `Image reroutes by role` line counting each role's image reroutes (planned 2026-10-16 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** When a role's model can't read images, its runs move to a tier that can. Each move logs an `image_reroute` event: with `preflight: true` from `src/loop/loop-tick.ts`, where an attachment was routed before any run, or with `preflight: false` from `src/tick/tick-verdict.ts`, after a blind read stopped a run. Today these events reach only the event feed, as one line each through `eventMessage`. The usage report already ranks fallbacks, failed runs, rejections, and revisions per role. A role whose text-only model keeps getting image work spends a hop per image, and a failed run when the hop follows a blind read. The report shows neither. Add a ranked `Image reroutes by role` line to the day report and the `--since` report, with the counts in `--json`. The operator can then see which role should get a vision-capable primary.

**Approach.** Count one reroute per `image_reroute` event, keyed by loop id (`eventRole(ev)`, the event's `source`, which both emitters set to `ctx.role`). Count both values of `preflight`. A split by `preflight` is out of scope: one count answers "which role needs a vision model". Follow the `fallbacksByRole` counter (PLANS.md Done: "`tumwater report` gains a `Fallbacks by role` line") step for step:
- `src/report/report-data.ts`:
  - add `imageReroutesByRole: Record<string, number>` to `UsageFold` and `DayFold`. Doc comment: image_reroute events per loop id, so a role whose model keeps being handed images it can't read is visible beside its runs and cost;
  - in `foldUsageEvent`, add an `else if (ev.type === "image_reroute")` branch right after the `model_fallback_started` branch. It does `addTo(target.imageReroutesByRole, eventRole(ev), 1)`;
  - set `imageReroutesByRole: {}` everywhere `fallbacksByRole: {}` is initialised today (`dayFoldFor` and `collectReportSince`'s accumulator literal);
  - add `ReportDay.imageReroutesByRole?: Record<string, number>`, absent when the day has none (zero means absent). Set it in `collectReport` in both places that set `fallbacksByRole`. The team branch copies the fold map when it is non-empty. The role-scoped branch narrows it with `narrowToRole`;
  - add `SinceReport.imageReroutesByRole: Record<string, number>`, always present (an empty map when there are none). The returned object uses `base === undefined ? acc.imageReroutesByRole : narrowToRole(acc.imageReroutesByRole, base)`.
- `src/report/report-render.ts`: in both renders, push `rankedRoleLine("Image reroutes by role", …filter(([, n]) => n > 0), String)` directly **after** the `Fallbacks by role` line. The `--since` render reads `rankedRoleMap(data.imageReroutesByRole)`. The day render reads `rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.imageReroutesByRole ?? {})`. A window with none renders `-`, like its siblings. The new line follows every line that `test/report.test.ts` indexes up to `Fallbacks by role`, but it shifts the index of every later line by one. Check each `lines[N]` assertion and bump only the ones past the new line.
- `docs/cli.md`: the Audit cell's `tumwater report` description names "fallbacks (model-fallback episodes started)" among the ranked per-role lines. Add "image reroutes (image_reroute hops to a tier that can read images)" right after it.

The GUI report charts (`src/ui/gui/gui-client-report.ts`) are out of scope. The JSON field is there for a later chart.

**Files touched.** `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, `docs/cli.md`, `test/report-data.test.ts`, `test/report.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/report-data.test.ts`: a log with two `image_reroute` events from `feature` today (one `preflight: true`, one `preflight: false`) and one from `qa` today, plus one from `feature` yesterday, gives today's `ReportDay.imageReroutesByRole` = `{ feature: 2, qa: 1 }` and yesterday's = `{ feature: 1 }`. A day with no such events has no `imageReroutesByRole` key. An `image_blind` event or a `model_fallback_started` event adds nothing to it.
- `collectReportSince` over the same log returns `imageReroutesByRole` covering the window. With `role: "feature"` it narrows to `{ feature: … }`, and a `feature-2` source folds into `feature`, as `narrowToRole` does for the other maps.
- `test/report.test.ts`: the day render prints `**Image reroutes by role:** feature — 3 · qa — 1` for a two-day series with those counts, and `**Image reroutes by role:** -` when there are none. The `--since` render prints the same line from `SinceReport.imageReroutesByRole`. Every existing `lines[N]` assertion passes, updated only where the new line shifts its index.
- `tumwater report --json` carries `imageReroutesByRole` for both the day report and `--since`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor`'s `disk space` row says what reclaim passes freed over the last 24 h (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of the waiting merge-rename series and the in-flight report fallbacks plan — touches only `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`, `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, and `docs/cli.md`) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The `disk_reclaim` event (logged once per pass by `reclaimPass` in `src/team/reclaim.ts`, carrying `mode`, `worktrees`, `freedGB`, `freeGB`, `durationMs`) has no consumer except its feed line in `eventMessage` (`src/events/event-format.ts`). An operator who runs `tumwater doctor` sees how much space is free now, but not that the team has been running reclaim passes to stay above the floor. Pressure passes in particular show the volume is tight even when the row reads ok. Append a reclaim phrase to the `disk space` row, the same way `checkBuildCheck` appends `checkDurationPhrase`. The dashboard's Health card and the TUI's Health tab run the same checks, so they pick up the phrase too.

**Approach.**
- In `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`, add an exported pure `diskReclaimPhrase(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): string | undefined`, placed next to `checkDurationPhrase`. It keeps `type === "disk_reclaim"` events, sums `finiteNumber(e.freedGB, 0)`, and counts the passes and the passes whose `mode` is `"pressure"`. It returns undefined when no event qualifies. Otherwise it returns `reclaim in the last 24h freed ${formatGB(total)} over ${plural(n, "pass", "passes")}`, plus `, ${p} under pressure` when `p > 0`. Example: `reclaim in the last 24h freed 12.4 GB over 3 passes, 2 under pressure`. Summing is safe here, unlike fallback durations: each pass is a point event, so it cannot straddle the window edge. An event with no `mode` field counts as pressure, matching the feed line's `textOr(e.mode, "pressure")`.
- In `checkDiskSpace`, compute the phrase once from `readEventsSince(root, 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).events` (already imported, same window as `checkBuildCheck`). Append it as ` · ${phrase}` to the detail of the fail, warn, and ok outcomes that follow a successful sample. Leave the statfs-failure warning unchanged. The phrase is informational only and never changes the row's level. Keep `checkDiskSpace`'s signature as it is: the existing test passes a temp root with no event log, and `readEventsSince` on a missing log yields no events.
- Extend `checkDiskSpace`'s doc comment with one sentence naming the phrase.
- In `docs/cli.md`'s Audit cell, change "the root checkout's `node_modules` drifting …" so the clause just before it reads: "free disk space against the hold floor and what reclaim passes freed over the last 24 h, the declared check and how long …".

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`, `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A new test `diskReclaimPhrase sums freed space and counts pressure passes` in `test/doctor-checks.test.ts` covers four cases:
  - Three `disk_reclaim` events (two `pressure` at 4.0 and 6.0 GB, one `idle` at 2.4 GB) plus one unrelated `build_check` event give exactly `reclaim in the last 24h freed 12.4 GB over 3 passes, 2 under pressure`.
  - One `idle` pass gives `… over 1 pass` with no pressure clause.
  - An empty list gives undefined.
  - An event with a non-numeric `freedGB` adds 0 but still counts as a pass.
- A new test `checkDiskSpace appends the last 24h of reclaim passes` writes `disk_reclaim` events to a temp root's event log with the module's existing event-writing helper (`logEvent`, as the slot-wait and check-duration tests do). It asserts that the ok detail contains `· reclaim in the last 24h freed` and that the level stays `ok`. A second assertion logs a `disk_reclaim` event backdated 48 h with `logEvent(root, { ts: Date.now() - 48 * 3_600_000, … } as never)` (the backdating form `test/cli-run-window.test.ts` uses) and checks that the phrase still counts only the recent passes.
- The existing `checkDiskSpace fails below the floor, …` test passes unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Split the TUI key-handling monolith into a `tui-panes` module: extract the pane-navigation state out of `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` (planned 2026-10-14 by plan, replanned 2026-10-16 by user; part 2/2 of the too-large "split the TUI key-handling monolith" plan split on feature's review. Part 1/2 (the prompt-line editors, `tui-editors`) merged 2026-10-14 in 8fec1a2c and is in Done, so this part has no prerequisite left; cross-reference part 1/2. It touches only `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, the new `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, and doc comments in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`. The Plain terms code parts that rename identifiers under `src/ui/tui/` (code runner 6/14, code run 15/20, code cleanup 1/7) are each held behind earlier parts; they find their sites by grep, so whichever merges second greps `tui-panes.ts` too) — done 2026-10-16

**Why this was replanned (2026-10-16).** Feature refused this part at 08:11 on 2026-10-14 because part 1/2 had not merged; part 1/2 merged at 09:06 that day (8fec1a2c), so the refusal's premise no longer holds. Feature reached this part early because its heading carried a bare `requires part 1/2 landed` with no series prefix: the eligibility parser cannot resolve such a clause (`tumwater doctor`'s plan dependencies row reports it as `unparsed`), so nothing held this part behind part 1/2. This revision drops that clause. It also rewrites the approach against the merged code, which differs from what the 10-14 text assumed:
- The editors do not take `refreshPaneCache`/`refreshTrail` as deps. `createTuiEditors` takes `root`, `now`, `flat`, `refreshQueued`, `clearBacklogSelection`, `applyHistorySearch`, `applyActivitySearch`, `flashMessage`, `flashError` and `commitBacklogEdit`, plus a per-key `TuiEditorCtx` snapshot (`view`, `roleIds`, `selectedEntry`, `selectedQueued`, `queuedRows`, `historyGrep`, `activityGrep`).
- The History trail has since gained an async per-file stat: `trailGen`, `loadTrailStat` and the `tickStat` seam.
- `TuiKeysState` is not exported; `TuiKeys` is the module's only exported type.
- `tui-keys.ts` is 1205 lines and `tui-editors.ts` is 1117 (at f5be92b8).

**Goal.** Part 1/2 moved the prompt-line editors into `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`. `createTuiKeys` in `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` still holds the second concern: the pane-navigation state and every pane arm of the key dispatch. That is the `view` index; the per-pane mode, cache, scroll and selection locals; the two Ctrl+X arms; `refreshPaneCache`/`refreshTrail`/`refreshQueued`; the three other pane-side leaves the editors call; and the top-of-file window tables and cache builders. This part finishes the split, so each concern has one module boundary a reviewer can hold.

**Approach.** Restructure only, no behavior change. Move code verbatim wherever possible.
- **New module `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`** with a `createTuiPanes(deps)` factory. It owns:
  - **State:** `view`, `scopeRole`, `selectedEntry`/`entryScroll`, `cancelArmed`, `notesClearArmed`, `selectedQueued`/`queuedRows`, `paneCache`, `noteMode`/`noteCache`, `trailMode`/`trailCache`/`trailGen`, `changeMode`/`changeCache`, `paneScroll`, `activityScroll`/`activityRole`/`activityGrep`, `historyWindow`/`reportWindow`/`historyResult`/`historyRole`/`historyGrep`, `eventBudget`/`entryBudget`, and `roleIds`.
  - **Tables and builders** from the top of `tui-keys.ts`: `nextInCycle`, `cycleLabel`, `SESSION_WINDOW_TAIL`, `HISTORY_WINDOWS`, `scopeCycle`, `HISTORY_RESULTS`, `historyPaneCache`, `REPORT_WINDOWS`, `usagePaneCache`, `failuresPaneCache`, with the imports only they use.
  - **Cache functions and editor leaves:** `refreshPaneCache`, `loadTrailStat`, `refreshTrail`, `refreshQueued`, `clearBacklogSelection`, `applyHistorySearch` and `applyActivitySearch`. The factory returns the four leaves the editors take (`refreshQueued`, `clearBacklogSelection`, `applyHistorySearch`, `applyActivitySearch`), so `createTuiKeys` passes them to `createTuiEditors` unchanged.
  - **Pane arms:** a `handleKey(str, key, es): boolean` that returns true when it consumed the key. It holds every arm of today's `handleKey` that runs after the editors' routing, except Ctrl+T and the two editor fallbacks: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+E (report window), Ctrl+S, Ctrl+O, the three Ctrl+X arms (notebook clear, queued cancel, backlog cancel), the backlog and Queued arrow arms, the PgUp/PgDn arms, and Esc on the Queued pane. `es` is `editors.state()`, so `promptLineFree` and the `es.answerFor`/`es.entryEditFor` guards read the same flags they read today. Esc on Queued sits after `editors.onArrow` today; an Esc is never an arrow, so running it inside the panes' dispatch, before `onArrow`, is behavior-neutral.
  - **`cycleView()`:** the pane half of today's Ctrl+T arm, everything after `editors.exitAll()`: the mode/cache resets, the `view` advance, the selection and scroll resets, and the per-pane entry (report and History through `refreshPaneCache`, Pending's async collector, Queued, Health, Brief).
  - **`beginKey()`:** moves both arms into per-key locals (`armed`, `armedNotes`) and clears them, as the top of today's `handleKey` does; the Ctrl+X arms read those locals. The shell calls it first on every key, so "every key starts disarmed" still holds for keys the editors consume.
  - **`syncRoster(roles)`:** `syncSnapshot`'s roster shift, view clamp and three stale-scope drops (report, History with its trail re-read, Activity). **`setLineBudgets`** moves with the budget locals.
  - **`editorCtx(): TuiEditorCtx`** builds the snapshot the shell passes to `editors.handleKey`.
  - **`state()`** returns the pane slice of `TuiKeysState`, including the `historySince`/`reportSince`/`historyResult` labels computed with `cycleLabel`.
  - **Deps:** `root`, `now`, `requestRender`, `flat`, `flashMessage`, `flashError`, `commitBacklogEdit`, and the four async seams already resolved to their defaults (`collectPending`, `runDoctor`, `collectChange`, `tickStat`).
- **`createTuiKeys` shrinks to the outer shell.** It resolves `TuiKeysDeps` (unchanged, with the same seam defaults). It keeps `flash`/`flashUntil`/`flashMessage`/`flashError`, `flat`, `commitBacklogEdit` and `directorInFlight`. It constructs the panes first, because the editors take the panes' leaves. Its `handleKey` runs, in today's order: `panes.beginKey()`, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C, `editors.handleKey(str, key, panes.editorCtx())`, the Ctrl+T arm (`editors.exitAll(); panes.cycleView();`), `panes.handleKey(...)`, `editors.onArrow`, then `editors.apply`. None of the pane arms that preceded Ctrl+T matches Ctrl+T, so taking it before them changes nothing. `syncSnapshot` calls `editors.sync`, sets `directorInFlight`, and calls `panes.syncRoster`. `state()` returns `{ ...editors.state(), ...panes.state(), directorInFlight, flash }`.
- **Doc comments.** `createTuiKeys`'s doc comment, and the `createTuiEditors` and `TuiEditorsDeps` comments that put the pane state "on the tui-keys.ts side", name `tui-panes.ts` as its home. Keep the `TuiKeysState` declaration in `tui-keys.ts` as the outward surface.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, the new `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, and doc comments only in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`. No test file changes: a split asserts no behavior change, so `test/tui-keys.test.ts` and the other `test/tui-*.test.ts` suites are the regression net.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `TuiKeys`, `TuiKeysDeps`, and every `TuiKeysState` field name and type are unchanged. `tui.tsx`, `tui-app.tsx` and every `test/tui-*.test.ts` file pass unmodified.
- `createTuiEditors`'s deps and `TuiEditorCtx` keep their shape; `git diff` of `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` touches comment lines only.
- No behavior change: the same keypresses do the same things, including the per-key disarm of both Ctrl+X arms and Ctrl+T restoring an open editor's saved draft.
- `wc -l src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` drops from 1205 to below ~600.
- `grep -nwE 'let (view|scopeRole|selectedEntry|entryScroll|cancelArmed|notesClearArmed|selectedQueued|queuedRows|paneCache|noteMode|noteCache|trailMode|trailCache|trailGen|changeMode|changeCache|paneScroll|activityScroll|activityRole|activityGrep|historyWindow|reportWindow|historyResult|historyRole|historyGrep|eventBudget|entryBudget|roleIds)' src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` prints nothing (it prints 28 lines at f5be92b8). Run on `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, it prints 28 lines.
- `grep -nwE '(function|const) (nextInCycle|cycleLabel|scopeCycle|historyPaneCache|usagePaneCache|failuresPaneCache|refreshPaneCache|loadTrailStat|refreshTrail|refreshQueued|clearBacklogSelection|applyHistorySearch|applyActivitySearch|SESSION_WINDOW_TAIL|HISTORY_WINDOWS|HISTORY_RESULTS|REPORT_WINDOWS)' src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts` prints nothing (17 lines at f5be92b8). Run on `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`, it prints 17 lines.
- `npm run test` passes.

**As landed (2026-10-16).** `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` also changed: its scan of the Ctrl keys the TUI handles now reads `tui-panes.ts` too, because Ctrl+N/G/S/O moved there. `tui-panes.ts`'s `handleKey` takes `(key, es)` (no `str`: no pane arm reads it); `TuiKeysState` stays unexported, and `state()` in `tui-panes.ts` is typed by inference. Two `tui-editors.ts` comments were re-wrapped to fit the 100-column limit. `tui-keys.ts` is 324 lines.

### The event feed gives `backend_binary`, `quiet_hours_started`, `quiet_hours_ended`, and `restart_forced` their own lines, and a test makes every event type render one (planned 2026-10-16 by plan) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** `eventMessage` (`src/events/event-format.ts`) turns each `HarnessEvent` into the one line that `tumwater logs`, `formatEvent`, and the dashboards' activity feed (`eventFeedItem`) show. Four types in the `HarnessEvent["type"]` union (`src/events/events.ts`) have no `case` and fall through to `default`, which prints the bare code. So an operator sees `quiet_hours_started` with no window and no hint that roles have stopped starting runs. They see `restart_forced` with no build, and `backend_binary` without the backend's name. Each event already carries the fields a sentence needs (`window`; `build`; `agent` and `found`). This plan writes those sentences and adds a test so the next new event type cannot ship without a line. `EVENT_TYPE_LABELS` already does the same job for the short chip labels in `src/events/event-labels.ts`.

**Approach.**
- In `eventMessage`, add four cases next to their siblings. Use the existing helpers `textOr` and `shortSha`, and follow the sibling cases' wording style: a routine hold reads `waiting: …` with no warning prefix, as in `disk_low` and `maintenance_quota_hold`.
  - `quiet_hours_started` (next to `disk_low`): `waiting: quiet hours (<window>) — roles start no new runs until the window ends; the director still runs`. Drop the ` (<window>)` part when `e.window` is not a non-empty string. `pollQuietHoursGate` (`src/scheduling/quiet-hours.ts`) sets `window: undefined` when `quietHours` is not a string.
  - `quiet_hours_ended`: `quiet hours ended (<window>) — roles start runs again`. Handle a missing window the same way.
  - `restart_forced` (next to `restart_blocked`): `restart forced by you — the update skips its cooldown (running version <shortSha(e.build)>)`. `Redeployer.forceRestart` (`src/redeploy/redeployer.ts`) emits it with `build: this.build.sha`, which is the running build.
  - `backend_binary` (next to `model_changed`): when `e.found === false`, write `warning: newly routed <agent> backend — its binary was not found`. Otherwise write `newly routed <agent> backend checked — binary found`. The `<agent>` comes from `textOr(e.agent)`. ### `tumwater doctor` gains a `root install` row that warns when the root checkout's `node_modules` no longer matches `package-lock.json`'s direct pins, so an operator learns a failed post-merge re-sync is making every check install into its own tree (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — adds one new module under `src/doctor/` and one row to `src/doctor/doctor.ts`'s list, and leaves `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` alone, which the in-flight "check row … 24 h passing merge-check durations" plan edits) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** When a merge moves main's lockfile, `syncRootInstall` (`src/build/dep-install.ts`) re-installs the root checkout. If that install fails, it logs a `dep_install` event with `status: "failed"` plus a warning, and only tries again when a later merge calls it. Until then, every gate and merge check finds the drift through `installDrift` and runs its own `npm install` into its own tree. Each check pays for an install, and nothing tells the operator the root is behind. `src/build/dep-install.ts` and `src/events/event-format.ts` are the only places that reference `dep_install` or `installDrift` today, so no doctor row, alert, or report reads either one. Add a doctor row that checks the root live and names the fix.

**Approach.**
- New module `src/doctor/doctor-install.ts` exporting `checkRootInstall(root: string, now = Date.now()): CheckOutcome`, written in the same style as the other read-only checks (`okOutcome`/`warnOutcome` from `./outcome.js`):
  - No `package-lock.json` at `root` (`fs.existsSync(path.join(root, "package-lock.json"))` is false) → `okOutcome("no package-lock.json — nothing pinned")`.
  - `installDrift(root)` (imported from `../build/dep-install.js`) is empty → `okOutcome("node_modules matches package-lock.json")`.
  - Otherwise → `warnOutcome`. The detail reads: the count from `plural(n, "direct dependency", "direct dependencies")` (`src/text/phrases.ts`), then "not installed as package-lock.json pins (<names, comma-joined>) — run npm install in <root>; until then each check installs into its own tree". After it, add `; the last re-sync failed ${shortSpanPhrase(now - ev.ts)} ago: ${textOr(ev.error)}` when the newest `dep_install` event in `readEventsSince(root, 24 * 3600_000).events` has `status === "failed"`. Name the window constant `DEP_INSTALL_CHECK_WINDOW_MS`. Wrap the event read in try/catch the way `checkWorktreePool` does: a read error adds `could not read the event log: ${errorMessage(err)}` to the detail and still warns.
  - A failed `dep_install` event with no drift now (an operator already installed by hand) stays ok. The live drift is the truth, and the event only explains it.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import `checkRootInstall` and add `{ name: "root install", ...checkRootInstall(root) }` directly after the `check` row.
- Docs: in `docs/cli.md`'s `tumwater doctor` Audit cell, add "the root checkout's `node_modules` drifting from `package-lock.json`'s direct pins (naming the last failed post-merge re-sync)" to the list of what it flags.

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-install.ts` (new), `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, `test/doctor-install.test.ts` (new), `docs/cli.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/doctor-install.test.ts` (node:test, offline, temp dirs from `tmpdir` in `test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts`; build the lockfile and `node_modules` manifests by hand the way `writeLock`/`installPkg` in `test/dep-install.test.ts` do, either copied or moved into a shared fixture) pins these cases:
  - no lockfile is ok with "nothing pinned";
  - a lockfile whose pins are all installed is ok;
  - a missing pin and a version-skewed pin warn, with both names in the detail and the `npm install` fix text;
  - a drifting root with a `dep_install` `status: "failed"` event logged in the last 24 h (via `logEvent`) warns, and the detail includes that event's `error` text;
  - the same failed event with no drift is ok.
- `tumwater doctor` lists a `root install` row right after `check`. The row is ok on this repo's own healthy checkout, which `test/doctor.test.ts` covers only if it already asserts row names; otherwise do not add an assertion there.
- No `src/ui` import in `src/doctor/doctor-install.ts`. `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor`'s `check` row says how long the declared check's passing merge checks took over the last 24 h, so the operator sees the suite slowing the merge lock before it times out (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, docs/cli.md) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** Each merge runs the project's declared check inside the merge lock: the `merge` and `batch` scope `build_check` events, plus the `baseline` checks on main's tip. So the suite's wall clock sets an upper limit on how many changes merge per hour. Every one of those runs is logged with its `durationMs` (`buildCheckEvent` in src/build/build-check-events.ts), but no surface reads the number back. `MainCheckStatus` (src/status/status-polls.ts) carries status, counts and time but no duration. The `report` and failure digest do not price check time. Doctor's `check` row (`checkBuildCheck` in src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) names only the command. An operator first learns the suite slowed down when merges back up or a check hits its deadline. BUGS.md's open supervisor-flake entry cites one such run that took 145 s.

**Approach.**
- src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts: add an exported pure helper `checkDurationPhrase(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): string | undefined`.
  - It keeps the events whose `type` is `build_check`, whose `status` is `passed`, whose `scope` is `merge`, `batch` or `baseline`, and whose `durationMs` is a finite number above 0 (read it with `finiteNumber` from src/files/json-object.ts).
  - It skips `gate`-scope checks, because a scoped gate check can run a subset of the suite (src/build/build-check-scoped.ts). It skips failed, skipped and timed-out runs, because they do not measure a full passing run.
  - It returns `undefined` when no event qualifies.
  - Otherwise it sorts the durations in ascending order and takes the lower median, the element at index `Math.floor((n - 1) / 2)`, so the median is always a run that actually happened. It also takes the maximum.
  - It returns `passing merge checks in the last 24h took <median> median, <max> slowest (<plural(n, "run")>)`. Each duration is formatted with `shortSpanPhrase` from src/text/phrases.ts, which doctor-checks.ts already imports from. `plural` comes from the same file.
- `checkBuildCheck(root, config)`: keep its signature and its `warn` outcome for "none declared". For a declared check, read `readEventsSince(root, 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).events`, the helper `checkFlakyChecks` already uses, and pass them to `checkDurationPhrase`. When it returns a phrase, append ` · <phrase>` to the existing `ok` detail, for both the `command` form and the npm-script form. The level stays `ok`: this is information, and a slow suite is not a pre-flight failure. With no qualifying events, the detail stays exactly as it is today.
- docs/cli.md: in the Audit row's list of what `tumwater doctor` names, add the declared check and how long its passing merge checks took over the last 24 h.
- Out of scope: a warn threshold or config knob, a status/TUI/dashboard badge, durations in `tumwater report`, and any change to `build_check` events.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, docs/cli.md.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts, unit tests of `checkDurationPhrase` on hand-built event arrays:
  - passed `merge`, `batch` and `baseline` events of 60 000, 125 000 and 90 000 ms give `passing merge checks in the last 24h took 90s median, 2m slowest (3 runs)`;
  - a passed `gate` event, a `failed` `merge` event, a `merge` event with no `durationMs`, and a non-`build_check` event, alone or together, give `undefined`;
  - two qualifying events of 40 000 and 100 000 ms give a median of `40s` (the lower median).
- test/doctor-checks.test.ts: for a repo with a declared npm `test` script and two passed `merge`-scope `build_check` events written with `logEvent`, `checkBuildCheck(root)` returns level `ok` with a detail that starts `npm test · passing merge checks in the last 24h took` and ends `(2 runs)`. The existing "checkBuildCheck names the declared script and walks up from a worktree to the installed root" test passes unchanged; its repos log no events.
- `npm run test` passes.

### A refused plan or bug raises a standing `refused` team alert on the dashboard, the TUI and `tumwater status`, the way an open question does (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/ui/team-alerts.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx and their tests; no src/merge, src/tick, src/doctor or src/ui/gui edit) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A **Refused** note holds an entry until a human decides ("The objection stands until a human or the director edits the entry"). Today the operator hears about it in three places: one notify page when the refusal lands (`entry_refused`), the `refused` row in `tumwater doctor` (`checkRefusedEntries`, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts), and a `[blocked: refused]` mark inside the backlog lists. Once the page has scrolled away, nothing on the surfaces an operator watches says a decision is waiting. The tui-panes split in PLANS.md has been held this way since 2026-10-14. An open question gets a standing indigo banner (the `questions` alert in `teamAlerts`, src/ui/team-alerts.ts) until it is answered. This plan gives refused entries the same kind of standing alert. It is amber, because the operator has to act, and it carries a button that opens the backlog card.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: add an exported `refusedEntryTitles(root: string): string[]`. It returns the verbatim titles of the planned plans and then the open bugs whose hold is `"refused"`, in file order. Read `backlogHolds(root)` (cached) and pair `holds.plans[i]` with `plannedPlanEntries(root)[i].title` and `holds.bugs[i]` with `openBugEntries(root)[i].title`. These are the parallel readers `backlogInProgress` already walks. Give it a doc comment in the style of `backlogMarks`. A missing file yields `[]`, because the readers already return `[]`.

When `refused.length > 0`, push this alert directly after the `questions` alert:
  key `refused`, tone `amber`; title `<plural(refused.length, "refused entry waits", "refused entries wait")> on your decision`; detail `<stripEntryStamp(refused[0])>`, then ` — and <N-1> more` when there are several, then ` · no role takes it until you release it (tumwater plan|bug --release <n>, or the entry's drawer) or cancel it`; actions `[{ label: "Open backlog", act: "backlog" }]`.
  The dashboard already handles `act: "backlog"` in src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, where it scrolls to the backlog card, so no client change is needed. Update the module's alert-order comment if it lists the keys.
- Pass the titles at the three production call sites, each read fresh per poll like `openQuestions`:

  - `renderStatus` in src/ui/status-render.ts: the CLI banner call.
  - src/ui/tui/tui.tsx: the `attention` line's `teamAlerts(…)` call.
- Out of scope: notify changes (`entry_refused` already pages), doctor changes, a per-entry release button on the banner, and any change to how holds are decided.

A repo with neither file returns `[]`.

### `tumwater doctor` warns when a recently Fixed bug's quoted test has failed again since its fix and no Open bug names that test (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts and test/doctor.test.ts; no src/merge, src/tick, src/backlog or src/ui edit)

**Goal.** BUGS.md's ## Fixed section holds flake bugs whose headings quote the test name. Two of today's are `"runGit SIGKILLs a git that ignores SIGTERM, taking its grandchild with it"` (fixed 2026-10-16) and `"a later wake request leaves a pending scheduled wake standing"` (fixed 2026-10-14). When such a test fails again, nothing links the failure to the Fixed record. The open `startParentDeathWatch` bug was filed by hand, after its 10-01 and 10-09 Fixed entries, when an operator session happened to read improve's red merge check. `checkWaitingBugs` (src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts) already does this matching for Open bugs that carry a Waiting note: `quotedTestName` on the heading, then `failureMentions` over the event log since the day after the note. This plan applies the same matching to the newest Fixed records. It adds one doctor row, `regressed fixes`, which warns when a Fixed record's quoted test has failed since the day after its fix and no Open bug quotes the same test. Like every backlog check, it is a warn, never a fail, and doctor writes nothing to BUGS.md.

**Approach.** All logic is in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
- Extract the inline day-after computation in `checkWaitingBugs` (the `new Date(Number(date.slice(0, 4)), Number(date.slice(5, 7)) - 1, Number(date.slice(8, 10)) + 1).getTime()` expression) into an unexported `dayAfterMs(date: string): number` (local midnight after a `YYYY-MM-DD`). `checkWaitingBugs` calls it, and its behaviour is unchanged.
- Add an exported `checkRegressedFixes(root: string): CheckOutcome`:
  - Read BUGS.md with `readDocChecked(…, "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify")`, as `checkFixClaims` does.
  - Take `fixedEntries(doc).slice(0, FIX_CLAIMS_CHECKED)`, the same newest-10 window `checkFixClaims` uses and for the same reason: older records drift.
  - For each record, `name = quotedTestName(entry.title)` and `date = lastDate(entry.title, /(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/)` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts; the last date in the heading is the fix date in both heading shapes, `— fixed 2026-10-14` and `(fixed 2026-10-16)`). Skip a record whose `name` or `date` is null, or whose `dayAfterMs(date)` is NaN.
  - Skip a record when an Open bug's heading quotes the same test: `openBugEntries(root).some((e) => quotedTestName(e.title) === name)`. The regression is then already filed. This is why the open startParentDeathWatch bug stops the Fixed 10-09 record from warning.
  - When any record is left, read events once with `readEventsSince(root, Math.max(0, Date.now() - <earliest since>))`, exactly as `checkWaitingBugs` does. Keep the records where `failureMentions(events, name, since)` is non-empty, and remember each one's newest mention.
  - None left: `okOutcome("no recently Fixed bug's quoted test has failed since its fix")`.
  - Otherwise, warn on the first in file order (newest-first), with `andMore` over the rest (`#`-less, `"${truncate(title, FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX)}"`): `BUGS.md Fixed record "<title truncated to FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX>" quotes a test that failed again after its <date> fix (<formatTimestamp(ts)>: <truncate(text, REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX)>)<more> — file it as a new bug with \`tumwater bug\`, quoting the test name and citing the Fixed record`.
- Update the comment on `checkWaitingBugs`/`failureMentions` only where it says the matching serves Waiting bugs alone. Give `checkRegressedFixes` its own doc comment in the style of its neighbours.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import `checkRegressedFixes` and add `{ name: "regressed fixes", ...checkRegressedFixes(root) }` directly after the `"waiting bugs"` row.
- Out of scope: auto-filing or reopening the bug (doctor stays read-only), Fixed records older than the newest 10, one-line compressed records (`fixedEntries` returns `###` entries), and any team alert or dashboard change (dashboards already show doctor rows).

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, a fixture like `recurrenceRoot` writes a BUGS.md with an empty `## Open` and a `## Fixed` entry `### \`test/x.test.ts\` "${FLAKY_TEST}" flaked (found by bugfix <5 days ago>) — fixed <N days ago>`, and logs a `warning` event `${FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX}<failure>`:
  - N = 2 with failure `✖ ${FLAKY_TEST}`: `checkRegressedFixes` is `warn`, and the detail contains `failed again after its`, the failure text, and `tumwater bug`;
  - N = 0 (same-day failure): ok;
  - N = 2 with an unrelated failure: ok;
  - N = 2 with an Open entry whose heading quotes the same `FLAKY_TEST`: ok;
  - a Fixed heading with no quoted span of 12 or more characters, or with no date: ok;
  - no BUGS.md: ok with `no BUGS.md — nothing to verify`;
  - two regressed Fixed records: the warn names the first and carries the `andMore` count.
- The existing `checkWaitingBugs` tests pass unchanged after the `dayAfterMs` extraction.
- test/doctor.test.ts's row-name list gains `"regressed fixes"` right after `"waiting bugs"`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Staging asks a bugfix run that adds a Progress note to an open bug, but leaves no Waiting for the next failure note under it, to write that note (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/tick/stage-check.ts, docs/how-it-works.md and test/stage-check.test.ts; no src/merge, src/backlog, src/ui or src/doctor edit)

**Goal.** Step 2 of bugfix's find text (src/roles/role-catalog.ts, the `bugfix` entry) says that when a bug cannot be reproduced, the run records a Progress note, writes `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE` (src/roles/role-guidance.ts) as its own line under the heading, and ends. The note's hold then stops later bugfix runs from re-investigating without new evidence. Runs skip the second half. The open BUGS.md entry for the `startParentDeathWatch` flake gained four `**Progress 2026-10-16 (bugfix…)**` notes on one day. The fourth was a BUGS.md-only "no repro, no code change" run. None of them wrote the Waiting note, so the bug stayed eligible and each run spent a tick, a review and a landing. This plan adds a staging finding (the same one fix-up turn the other findings get, src/tick/tick-stage.ts) for a bugfix run whose diff adds a Progress note to an entry that stays under `## Open` with no Waiting note. The finding is advisory: the change commits and queues either way, and the gate does not run it (like `planDependencyFinding`).

**Approach.** All code is in `src/tick/stage-check.ts`:
- Add a pure, exported `waitingNoteFinding(head: string, base: string): string | undefined`. `head` is the edited BUGS.md and `base` is its text at the merge-base.
  - Parse both with `parseEntryDetails(text, "Open")` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts, already imported). Pair entries by `entryKey(title)` (src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts). Skip a head entry with no base entry: a newly filed bug is not a re-investigation.
  - Count the entry's Progress lines: lines whose trimmed text matches `/^-\s+\*\*Progress\b/`. That is the form today's open entry uses (`- **Progress 2026-10-16 (bugfix, second):** …`).
  - A head entry counts when its Progress count is greater than its base entry's, `waitingNote(body)` is null, and `refusalNote(body)` is null (both from src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts).
  - Return undefined when no entry counts. Otherwise name the first in file order, with `moreSuffix(<number of other counting entries>)` (src/text/phrases.ts, already imported) appended: `BUGS.md bug "<title>" gained a Progress note but stays open with no Waiting for the next failure note — if this run could not reproduce it, add ${WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_NOTE} as its own line under the heading so later runs wait for new evidence (bugfix's step 2); if it did reproduce, leave the entry as it is`. Quote `<title>` in full, as `heldMovedFinding` does.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the PLANS.md block, add: when `baseRoleOf(role) === "bugfix"` (src/roles/loop-ids.ts, so `bugfix-2` counts) and `files.includes("BUGS.md")`, read the head with `readTextOrNull` and the base with `fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), "BUGS.md").catch(() => undefined)`, exactly as the PLANS.md block does. Push the finding when it is defined. Every other role is unaffected. A run that moves the bug to `## Fixed` gives no finding, because the entry is no longer under Open in head.
- Update the module header comment: like `planDependencyFinding`, `waitingNoteFinding` is staging-only and bugfix-only.
- docs/how-it-works.md, in the hold-note bullet that begins "A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce": add one sentence. A bugfix run that adds a Progress note to an open bug without writing the note is asked to write it in its staging fix-up turn.
- Out of scope: role ids other than bugfix (selfcheck lifts notes, it does not write them); any gate or in-lock check; changing bugfix's find text.

**Files touched.** src/tick/stage-check.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit tests of `waitingNoteFinding` in test/stage-check.test.ts, over a two-entry `## Open` base where entry A has one Progress line:
  - head adds a second Progress line to A and no Waiting note: the finding names A's title and contains `Waiting for the next failure`;
  - the same head plus a `**Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: x**` line under A: undefined;
  - the same head plus a `**Refused …**` line under A: undefined;
  - head identical to base, or editing A's Symptom line only: undefined;
  - head moving A to `## Fixed` with a new Progress line: undefined;
  - a newly filed entry C carrying a Progress line: undefined;
  - Progress lines added to both A and B: the finding names A and carries the `moreSuffix` count.
- A `stageCheckFindings` test built with `repoWith` (as the "a duplicated ## Done heading" test is): BUGS.md on main has an Open entry with one Progress line, and the worktree adds a second. With role `"bugfix"` and with `"bugfix-2"`, the findings include the Waiting-note finding. With role `"feature"`, they do not.
- The existing stage-check and tick-stage tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` warns when a bug held by a Waiting for the next failure note has failed again, naming the failure and the release command (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md and test/doctor-backlog.test.ts) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce is held by a `**Waiting for the next failure …**` note until it fails again (docs/how-it-works.md). Two things lift the hold: whoever records a new occurrence deletes the note, or an operator runs `tumwater bug --release <n>`. In practice only selfcheck records occurrences, and selfcheck is opt-in (`roles.selfcheck.enabled`). On a default team, a waiting test can flake again in the gate or the merge check, and the event log records the failure. But nothing connects that failure to the held bug, so the bug stays parked with exactly the evidence it was waiting for. Doctor's `waiting bugs` row (`checkWaitingBugs`) already names each held bug and its release command, and today it always reports ok. This plan makes it warn when a held bug's test has failed in a gate or merge check since the day after its note was written. The warning names the failure and the release command. Doctor stays read-only: it writes nothing to BUGS.md.

**Approach.** All of the change is in `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
- Add a pure, exported `quotedTestName(title: string): string | null`. It returns the first span between straight double quotes in a bug heading that is at least 12 characters long (`/"([^"]{12,})"/`), or null. Today's open bug heading quotes its test name this way (`… "startParentDeathWatch takes a SIGKILLed supervisor's grandchild down with it" …`). The test-runner failure line that `failureHeadline` (src/build/build-check-report.ts) puts into flake warnings and rejection reasons carries the same text verbatim, after `✖ `. The 12-character floor stops a short quoted word from matching unrelated failures.
- Add a pure, exported `waitingNoteDate(note: string): string | null`. It returns the first `YYYY-MM-DD` in `waitingNote(entry.body)`'s text, or null.
- Add a pure, exported `failureMentions(events: readonly HarnessEvent[], name: string, sinceMs: number): { ts: number; text: string }[]`. It collects every event with numeric `ts >= sinceMs` that falls under either rule:
  - a `warning` whose string `message` includes `name`. This covers the gate's `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`, the merge check's `MERGE_FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX`, and the `merge check failed (kept for one retry): …` warning in src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts.
  - a `review_rejected` event whose `stringList(e.reasons)` (src/files/json-object.ts) has an entry that includes `name`. For this event, `text` is the first such reason.

  Results come back in event order.
- In `checkWaitingBugs`, for each held bug (a waiting note and no refusal note, as today), take `quotedTestName(entry.title)` and `waitingNoteDate(note)`. When both are non-null, compute `since` as local midnight starting the day after the note date. The note carries only a date, so a same-day failure cannot be told apart from the failure the note was written about, and the day after is the conservative cutoff. Read events once per check with `readEventsSince(root, Date.now() - firstSince)` from src/events/event-window.ts, using the earliest `since` across held bugs. Skip the read entirely when no held bug yields both values. A bug with any `failureMentions` has recurred.
- When any held bug recurred, return `warnOutcome`:
  - Text: `BUGS.md bug #<n> "<title>" failed again since its Waiting for the next failure note (<formatTimestamp(ts) of the newest mention>: <truncate(text, REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX)>)<more> — record the occurrence under the entry and release it with \`tumwater bug --release <n>\``.
  - `<more>` uses `andMore` over the other recurred bugs.
  - `formatTimestamp` comes from src/text/datetime.ts.
- With no recurrence, keep today's ok text unchanged.
- Update the function's doc comment: it is now ok, or warn when a held bug's quoted test failed again. A warn is never a fail.
- Docs:
  - docs/how-it-works.md, in the hold-note bullet that begins "A bug that bugfix cannot reproduce": add one sentence saying `tumwater doctor` warns when the held bug's quoted test has failed again in a gate or merge check since the day after the note.
  - docs/cli.md, in the Audit row's waiting-bugs clause (grep `open bugs held by a Waiting`): add "and warning when one has failed again since".
- Out of scope: lifting the note automatically (that is a harness write to BUGS.md, and the note is a human or role decision); matching bugs whose heading quotes no test name; the dashboard and TUI.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `quotedTestName('`test/x.test.ts` "startParentDeathWatch takes a grandchild down" flaked')` returns the quoted name. A heading with no quotes, or only a quoted span shorter than 12 characters, returns null.
- `waitingNoteDate("Waiting for the next failure 2026-10-16 by bugfix: x")` is `"2026-10-16"`. A note with no date gives null.
- `failureMentions` over synthetic events returns:
  - a gate flake warning, a merge flake warning and a `review_rejected` whose reasons include the name, all at or after `sinceMs`;
  - nothing for an event before `sinceMs`, a warning that does not include the name, or a `review_rejected` with no matching reason.
- `checkWaitingBugs` fixtures in test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, built with `logEvent` the way test/doctor-checks.test.ts's `checkFlakyChecks` tests are:
  - Recurrence: one held bug quotes a test name, its note is dated two days before today (`daysAgoStamp(2)`), and a `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` warning naming the test is logged now. The check returns `level: "warn"`, and the detail contains `failed again`, the warning's text and `tumwater bug --release 1`.
  - Same-day: the same fixture with the note dated today (`daysAgoStamp(0)`) stays ok with today's text.
  - Unrelated: the same fixture with a flake warning that does not include the name stays ok.
- The existing `checkWaitingBugs` and `checkStaleBugs` tests still pass, with no change to their expected text.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The dashboard's entry drawer offers "Release this entry" on a bug held by a Waiting for the next failure note, as `tumwater bug --release <n>` already does (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — touches only src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts (doc comment), src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts, docs/cli.md and their tests; no src/backlog, src/merge, src/tick or src/ui/tui edit) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A bug carrying a **Waiting for the next failure** note is held from bugfix until someone lifts it. `tumwater bug --release <n>` lifts it, and so does the dashboard's `POST /api/backlog-release`: `tryReleaseEntry` in `src/backlog/backlog-write.ts` goes through `liftRefusal`, which drops a Refused note or, failing that, the waiting note. But the entry drawer never shows the button for a waiting bug. `refreshEntry` in `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` renders "Release this entry" only when `d.refused` is true, and `handleBacklog` in `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` sends `{ title, body, refused }` with no waiting flag. An operator who sees a waiting bug in the dashboard has to switch to a terminal. Show the button for waiting entries too.

**Approach.**
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts` (the `GET /api/backlog?file=&index=` handler that sends `refused: refusalNote(entry.body) !== null`): also send `waiting: waitingNote(entry.body) !== null`. `waitingNote` is already exported from `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts` next to `refusalNote`. Keep `refused` and its meaning as they are. Questions entries get `waiting: false` the same way they get `refused: false`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts` `refreshEntry`: render the existing `entry-release` button when `d.refused || d.waiting`. Keep the same markup, label, and position. Use one click, with no arming, as for refused entries.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-boot.ts` `entry-release` handler: change the `not_refused` toast from "That entry carries no Refused note — refreshed" to "That entry carries no Refused or Waiting note — refreshed". The `not_refused` status name stays as it is, so no payload key is renamed.
- `src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts` `handleBacklogRelease` doc comment: say that an entry with neither a Refused nor a Waiting-for-the-next-failure note answers `not_refused`. That is what `liftRefusal` already does, so this is a comment-only change.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Steer row, where `--release <n>` is described, add that the dashboard's plan/bug drawer offers the same release on a refused or waiting entry. Grep for existing wording about the drawer's Release first, and extend it if it is there.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-client-drawer.test.ts` "the entry drawer offers Release this entry only on a refused entry" (rename it to "…only on a refused or waiting entry") also covers a fixture `{ title: "Wait", body: "**Waiting for the next failure …**", refused: false, waiting: true }`, which shows `data-act='entry-release'`. An entry with both flags false still shows no `entry-release`.
- `test/gui.test.ts`'s `/api/backlog` assertions include `waiting: false` in their `deepEqual` payloads. A bug fixture carrying a `**Waiting for the next failure` note line (the `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX` in `src/roles/role-guidance.ts`) reads back `waiting: true` and `refused: false`. Add that fixture beside the existing refused bug, or as a new test in `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`.
- `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`: either extend "handleBacklogRelease lifts the Refused note, …" or add a sibling test. Posting a release for a BUGS.md entry that carries only a waiting note answers `status: "released"`, removes the note line from the file, and writes the wake request. This pins the server half the drawer now relies on.
- `test/gui-client-boot.test.ts`: if any test asserts the `not_refused` toast text, it now matches the new wording.
- `npm run test` passes. `test/comment-width.test.ts` stays green on the edited doc comment.
- Out of scope: the TUI (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`), any change to how the note is written or lifted, auto-expiry, and a distinct button label for waiting entries.

### A red merge check whose failure matches a recorded flake keeps its pin once instead of being rejected on main's cached green (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts, src/loop/loop-state.ts, src/tick/tick-apply.ts and their tests) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** The review gate already skips a failure it has recorded as flaky. In `src/review/review-precheck.ts`, a red whose headline passes `isKnownFlake` (`src/review/known-flakes.ts`) keeps the commit and the pin and counts no strike (BUGS.md 2026-10-06). The merge side has no such check. When the in-lock merge check goes red twice on one patch (`MERGE_CHECK_FAILURE_LIMIT`), or a batch bisect narrows a red to one change (`src/merge/merge-batch.ts`), `attributeRedCheck` in `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts` asks `mainTipVerdict` for main's verdict. That verdict usually comes from the per-SHA cache, which an earlier merge seeded green, so the change is rejected. This applies even when the failing test is one the gate or the merge retry recorded as a flake within the last 24 h. The merge-check flake record (done 2026-10-16) now feeds that memory from merge retries too, so the merge side can use it. One excuse per headline per pin bounds the retry: a change that really breaks a flaky test is still rejected, after at most one extra round of retries.

**Approach.**
- `src/loop/loop-state.ts`: add `mergeFlakeExcused?: string` to `LoopState`, next to `mergeCheckFailures`. Its doc comment says it holds the normalized failure headline (`normalizeClusterKey`) that `attributeRedCheck` last excused as a known flake for this role's pinned change. It is cleared when the change merges or is rejected. In the heal function that heals `mergeCheckFailures`, delete `mergeFlakeExcused` when it is not a string.
- `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`: on the line `if (changeGone) s.mergeCheckFailures = undefined;`, also clear `s.mergeFlakeExcused`, so each new change starts with its one excuse available.
- `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `attributeRedCheck`: after the unverified-tree branch and before `mainTipVerdict`, compute `headline = failureHeadline(red.outcome.outputTail) ?? describeCheck(red.check)`. This is the expression `mergeCheckRed` and review-precheck.ts already use. Also compute `key = normalizeClusterKey(headline)` (import from `src/failure/failure-cluster.ts`). When `isKnownFlake(ctx.root, headline)` is true and `state.mergeFlakeExcused !== key`, do the following:
  - set `state.mergeFlakeExcused = key`;
  - set `state.lastError` to the template `` `${label} failed: known-flaky failure, merge kept: ${headline}` ``;
  - call `warnEventBestEffort(ctx.root, role, detail)`, where `detail` is the template `` `${label}: known-flaky failure, merge kept: ${headline}` ``;
  - call `saveLoopState`;
  - return `"merge_blocked"`.

  That is the return the unverified branch already uses: the ref stays and recovery merges it again. Otherwise, continue to main's verdict unchanged. Extend the function's doc comment with the known-flake branch, its once-per-headline limit and the reason (this plan, BUGS.md 2026-10-06).
- Same file, `mergeCheckRed`: today it logs `merge check failed (kept for one retry): …` whenever `keepPinOrAttribute` returns `"merge_blocked"`. With this plan, that result can also come from the attribution callback's flake excuse, which logs its own warning. Track whether the callback ran with a local `let attributed = false` set inside the callback, and log the kept-for-retry warning and store the strike headline only when `!attributed`.
- Leave unchanged: the gate side, `mainTipVerdict`'s cache use (a forced fresh run on the merge side would be a separate plan), and the batch caller in merge-batch.ts. It already passes the returned result through `emit`, and `"merge_blocked"` is an outcome it already handles from the unverified branch.
- The file is `// vocabulary: plain`: say "merge", never "landing", in new lines.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts`, `src/loop/loop-state.ts`, `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`, `test/attribute-red-check.test.ts`, `test/streak-gate.test.ts`, `test/loop-state.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/attribute-red-check.test.ts`, a new test named "attributeRedCheck keeps the ref once for a known-flake red, then attributes a repeat". Use the "rejects deterministically when main's own tip is green" fixture (a green fake npm) with a unique marker. Seed one warning event for the role whose message is `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX + "✖ the flaky test"`. Run the red with `outputTail: ["✖ the flaky test (1.2ms)", "expected 2 to be 3"]`.
  - The first call returns `"merge_blocked"`. The pin ref still exists, `state.lastReview` is unchanged (no reject), `state.lastError` contains `known-flaky failure, merge kept` and `the flaky test`, and `loadLoopState(root, ROLE).mergeFlakeExcused` is set.
  - A second call with the same state returns `"rejected"` and deletes the pin.
- The same file: a red whose headline matches no flake warning still returns `"rejected"` on a green main. The existing first test covers this, since it seeds no flake warning. It must still pass unchanged.
- A test in `test/streak-gate.test.ts`, which already drives `applyMergeOutcome` (`src/tick/tick-apply.ts`): `mergeFlakeExcused` is cleared on `"changed"` and on `"rejected"` and kept on `"merge_blocked"`.
- `test/loop-state.test.ts`: a saved state with a non-string `mergeFlakeExcused` loads with the field absent.
- `npm run test` passes, including `test/vocabulary.test.ts` and `test/comment-width.test.ts`.

**Note.** The seeded flake warning in the new test is the full headline `✖ the flaky test — expected 2 to be 3` (what `failureHeadline` yields for that outputTail), not `✖ the flaky test` alone: the key is the normalized whole headline.

### Plain terms code merge, part 5/11: Rename the merger core and batch and stack identifiers (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 4/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/merge/merge-core.ts merge-batch.ts merge-stack.ts and the merger tests)

**Goal.** The merger (the old lander), the batch verify-and-merge and the stack take merge, merger, verify and approved names in identifiers, comments, test names and fixtures. A mechanical rename of about 450 lines with no behavior change.

**Approach.**
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `lander` → `merger`, `vet` → `verify`, `vetted` → `approved`, and a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`;
  - comments, test names, temp-dir prefixes (`"lander-rec-"`, `"lander-rereview-rej-"` → `"merger-…"`) and assertion messages follow the same rule;
  - comment lines wrap at 100 columns.
- **merge-core.ts:**
  - `LanderContext` → `MergerContext`. merge-to-main.ts already has `MergeContext`, a different shape. Keep both, and start each doc comment by saying which one it is.
  - `LandRequest` → `MergeRequest`, `LandingScopeContext` → `MergeScopeContext`, `RETRIABLE_LANDING_RESULTS` → `RETRIABLE_MERGE_RESULTS`, `landApprovedChange` → `mergeApprovedChange`, `landApprovedChangeIn` → `mergeApprovedChangeIn`.
- **merge-batch.ts:** `landVetted` → `mergeApproved`, `vetRequest` → `verifyRequest`, `vetRequestIn` → `verifyRequestIn`, `VetVerdict` → `VerifyVerdict`, `landOne` → `mergeOne`, `landedCount` → `mergeDoneCount`, and the parameter `vetted` → `approved`.
- **merge-stack.ts:** `landStack` → `mergeStack`, `landStackIn` → `mergeStackIn`, local `landed` → `mergeDone`.
- **Fixtures and tests:** `vetAndLand` → `verifyAndMerge`, `vetThenMerge` → `verifyThenMerge`, `landerCtx` → `mergerCtx`, and `landWt` → `mergeWt`. If `mergeWt` is already bound in the same scope, use `mergeWorktree`.
- **Earlier callers move now:** `VetVerdict`, `vetRequest`, `landVetted` and `landApprovedChange` in part 4/11's files, and `LandRequest` and `LanderContext` in part 2/11's files.
- **Aliases.** None were kept: every caller of the renamed names (including those outside part 5/11's own files) moved in this part, so no `@deprecated` alias exists for `vetRequest`, `landVetted`, `LanderContext`, `RETRIABLE_LANDING_RESULTS`, `landStack` or `vetAndLand`.
- **Leave alone:**
  - user-visible strings and expected-output literals;
  - event type names;
  - the `_land-<role>` legacy worktree name;
  - PLANS.md and BUGS.md titles quoted in comments, kept verbatim (test/plan-citations.test.ts).
- Skip any name that an earlier series already renamed.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-core.ts`, `merge-batch.ts`, `merge-stack.ts`; `test/fixtures/merger-fixtures.ts`; `test/merger.test.ts`, `test/merger-bisect.test.ts`, `test/merger-errors.test.ts`, `test/merger-restack.test.ts`, `test/merge-stack.test.ts`; earlier-caller lines in the part 2/11 and 4/11 modules.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `MergerContext`, `MergeRequest`, `mergeApproved`, `verifyRequest`, `VerifyVerdict`, `mergeStack` and the other new names are exported. Each old name is either gone or a `@deprecated` alias of it.
- `MergeContext` (merge-to-main.ts) and `MergerContext` (merge-core.ts) both exist, and each doc comment names its role.
- After this part, no file under `src/merge/` has an identifier, comment or test name with a retired merge word, except aliases, `runLandingPi`/`foldLandingUsage`/`AbortableLanding`/`applyMergeOutcome` (parts 6, 7 and 9), quoted backlog titles and legacy-layout names.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater doctor` names open bugs held by a "Waiting for the next failure" note, and stops calling them stale (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts, src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md and test/doctor-backlog.test.ts)

**Goal.** The "Waiting for the next failure" hold (done 2026-10-16) parks an open bug until it fails again, but doctor does not know about it. `checkStaleBugs` (`src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`) skips only Refused bugs, so a bug held on purpose still warns "has waited N d for a fix — no role is fixing it: check that the bugfix role is enabled and not failing". That advice is wrong for a held bug. No doctor row lists which bugs are waiting or how to release one, so the only sign is the `[blocked: waiting for the next failure]` mark in the backlog listings. This plan makes `checkStaleBugs` skip waiting bugs and adds one doctor row, `waiting bugs`, that names them.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts`: next to `refusalNote`, export `waitingNote(body: string): string | null`. It applies the same rule to `WAITING_FOR_FAILURE_PREFIX` (already imported for `entryHoldAgainst`): it takes the first trimmed line that starts with the prefix and strips the leading `**` and the first closing `**`. Factor the shared body into a private `noteText(body, prefix)` that both functions call, so `refusalNote`'s behavior stays the same.
- `src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts`:
  - `checkStaleBugs`: skip an entry when `waitingNote(entry.body) !== null`, the same way it skips refused entries. Update its doc comment to say that a waiting bug is skipped too and that `checkWaitingBugs` names it.
  - New `export function checkWaitingBugs(root: string): CheckOutcome`, shaped like `checkStaleBugs`. Read BUGS.md with `readDocChecked(…, "no BUGS.md — nothing to verify")`. Walk `openBugEntries(root)` in order and keep `{ position: index + 1, title, note }` for each entry whose `waitingNote` is non-null and whose `refusalNote` is null; a Refused bug belongs to `checkRefusedEntries`. When none match, return `okOutcome("no open bug is waiting for its next failure")`. Otherwise return an **ok** outcome, never a warn: the hold is deliberate, and doctor only reports it. The detail is `` BUGS.md bug #<n> "<title>" is held until it fails again (<note, truncated to REFUSAL_NOTE_MAX>)<andMore> — selfcheck lifts the note when it records a new occurrence; release it now with `tumwater bug --release <n>` ``. Truncate titles with `FIX_CLAIM_HEADING_MAX` and render the rest with `andMore` as `` #<n> "<title>" ``, as `checkStaleBugs` does. Give the function a doc comment in the style of its neighbors.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: import `checkWaitingBugs` and register `{ name: "waiting bugs", ...checkWaitingBugs(root) }` right after the `stale bugs` row.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the `Audit` row's `tumwater doctor` list, after "open bugs unfixed 3 days or more after their filing stamp", add ", open bugs held by a Waiting for the next failure note (not counted as unfixed; released with `tumwater bug --release <n>`)".

A body that mentions the words only mid-line returns null. The existing `refusalNote` tests pass unchanged.

### Plain terms code merge, part 4/11: Rename the merge pipeline and drain and verify identifiers (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 3/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts merge-drain.ts merge-verify.ts, their tests and test/comment-width.test.ts) (done 2026-10-16)

*Replanned 2026-10-16 by plan after two rejected rounds: the earlier attempts rewrapped comments so that overflow words started a new line with a stray `/**` (e.g. `/** no` in test/fixtures/merge-fixtures.ts's `reviewers` doc), and test/comment-width.test.ts checks only width, so it could not catch that. This plan now adds that check first and states how to rewrap.*

**Goal.** The pipeline, the merge-queue drain and the verify stage take merge, verify and approved names in identifiers, comments and test names. Two names that would collide take explicit alternatives. A mechanical rename of about 480 lines with no behavior change, plus a guard that keeps rewrapped doc comments well formed.

**Approach.**
- **Comment guard first.** In `test/comment-width.test.ts`, extend `commentOffenders` so a line whose trimmed text starts with `/*` while `inBlock` is already true is also an offender. Mark it in `offendersInFile`'s output as `(nested)`, next to `(cols)`; return a `kind: "cols" | "nested"` field from `commentOffenders` to do that. Update the comment above `commentOffenders` and the first test's name ("every comment line in src/ and test/ fits in 100 columns and opens no block inside a block"). Add a case to `commentOffenders flags over-wide comment lines only`, or a sibling test, with a `/** a` line followed by `/** b` that asserts the second is flagged `nested`, and a closed `/** a */` followed by `/** b */` that is not flagged.
- **Fix the one existing nested opener.** On main, `src/config/config-fallbacks.ts` has an orphaned two-line fragment, "/** The `model` selector a run actually starts on, …", left before the doc comment of the team-level fallback pair when the organize split in e591b82ce copied it. The full comment and its function stay in `src/config/config-views.ts`. Delete the fragment, so the new guard passes on the tree as it is.
- **How to rewrap.** Rewrap each changed comment by editing it, not with a script that splits lines. A line pushed past 100 columns moves its last words to the start of the next line in the same comment. That line keeps the comment's continuation prefix (` * ` in a `/** … */` block, `// ` in a line comment), and `/**` appears only on a comment's first line. When the comment's last line overflows, add a new ` * ` line before the closing `*/`.
- **Rename rule**, as in this series:
  - in identifiers, `landing`/`land` → `merge`, `vet`/`vetting` → `verify` and `vetted` → `approved`; a bare `landed` → `mergeDone`;
  - in comments, "vet" → "verify" (as a noun, "verification"), "vetted" → "approved", "landing" → "merge";
  - test names and assertion messages follow the same rule. `vet` → `verify` adds three characters, so rewrap as above.
- **merge-pipeline.ts:**
  - `LandingPipeline` → `MergePipeline`, `LandingPipelineContext` → `MergePipelineContext`, `InFlightLanding` → `InFlightMerge`, `VettedLanding` → `ApprovedMerge`;
  - `landingTasks` → `mergeTasks`, `abortableLandings` → `abortableMerges`, `settleLandingOutcome` → `settleMergeOutcome`, `newLandingPipeline` → `newMergePipeline`, `guardLandingTask` → `guardMergeTask`;
  - the pipeline's members `vetting` → `verifying` (it holds the in-flight verifications) and `vetted` → `approved`. They are members, so rename them at every use, in the orchestrator and the tests too.
- **merge-drain.ts:**
  - `drainLandings` → `drainMergeQueue`, not `drainMerges`: the same file already has `drainMerge`, which starts the fast-forward.
  - `settleAbortedVetted` → `settleAbortedApproved`.
  - `drainMerge`, `startMerge` and `MERGE_TIER` keep their names.
- **merge-verify.ts:**
  - `LANDING_TIER` → `VERIFY_TIER`, not `MERGE_TIER`: merge-drain.ts already defines `const MERGE_TIER = LANDING_TIER - 1` for the fast-forward's conflict runs, which becomes `VERIFY_TIER - 1`.
  - `vetLimit` → `verifyLimit`, `drainVetting` → `drainVerify`, `startVet` → `startVerify`.
  - Locals: `vet` → `verify`, `vets` → `verifies`, `vetted` → `approved`, and the test's `alphaVet` → `alphaVerify`.
- **Earlier callers move now.** `VettedLanding` and `settleLandingOutcome` are called in part 3/11's files.
- **Aliases.** Keep two-line `@deprecated` aliases for the exports later parts call: `drainLandings`, `settleAbortedVetted`, `InFlightLanding`, `VettedLanding`, `LandingPipeline`, `LandingPipelineContext`, `newLandingPipeline`, `landingTasks`, `abortableLandings`, `settleLandingOutcome`, `LANDING_TIER`, `vetLimit` and `startVet`. Move these files off earlier parts' aliases. Delete any alias that test/exports.test.ts reports unused.
- **Leave for their parts:** `runLandingPi` (part 7/11), `AbortableLanding` (part 9/11), and `VetVerdict`, `landVetted` and `vetRequest` (part 5/11).
- **Leave alone:**
  - user-visible strings and expected-output literals;
  - event type names, including `slot_wait.purpose: "verify"`, which the events series set;
  - PLANS.md and BUGS.md titles quoted in comments, kept verbatim (test/plan-citations.test.ts).
- Skip any name that an earlier series already renamed.

**Files touched.** `src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts`, `merge-drain.ts`, `merge-verify.ts`; `test/fixtures/merge-fixtures.ts`; `test/merge-pipeline.test.ts`, `test/merge-drain.test.ts`, `test/merge-drain-verify.test.ts`, `test/merge-pipeline-seams.test.ts`; member and earlier-caller lines in `src/merge/merge-slot.ts`, `src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts` and tests; `test/comment-width.test.ts`; `src/config/config-fallbacks.ts` (the orphaned fragment only).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `drainMergeQueue`, `VERIFY_TIER`, `MergePipeline`, `ApprovedMerge` and the other new names are exported. Each old name is either gone or a `@deprecated` alias of it.
- `git grep -nE '\.vetting\b|\.vetted\b|\bvetting:|\bvetted:' -- src test` prints nothing.
- `MERGE_TIER` in merge-drain.ts is defined as `VERIFY_TIER - 1`. Neither `drainMerges` nor a second `MERGE_TIER` exists.
- test/comment-width.test.ts fails on a `/**` line inside an open block comment, and its new case shows it. The orphaned fragment is gone from `src/config/config-fallbacks.ts`.
- Every comment this change touches keeps a single `/**` opener on its first line. The comment-width test passing shows this, and the VERIFIED line cites it.
