### The `entry_refused` event names the refused plan or bug, so `tumwater logs` and the notify page say which entry is now held (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/verdict/refusal.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, src/events/events.ts, docs/config.md and their tests) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** When a refusal note lands, `handleRefusal` (`src/verdict/refusal.ts`) logs `{ type: "entry_refused", reason, files }`. `formatEvent` (`src/events/event-format.ts`) renders that as `entry refused: <reason> (PLANS.md)`. `notify.ts` pages that same line as `TUMWATER_EVENT_MESSAGE`, because `entry_refused` is in `NOTIFY_EVENT_TYPES`. The operator learns that some entry is now held until a human releases it, but not which one. To act (`tumwater plan|bug --release <n>`, the dashboard's release button, or an edit), they must open PLANS.md or BUGS.md and look for the note. The harness already holds both versions of the file in `handleRefusal`: main's copy (`fileContentAt(wt, ctx.mainBranch, "PLANS.md")`) and the worktree's. So it can name the entries whose Refused note is new and put their titles on the event.

**Approach.**
- `src/verdict/refusal.ts`:
  - Add and export `newlyRefusedTitles(baseMd: string, headMd: string, section: string): string[]`. Parse `headMd` with `parseEntryDetails(headMd, section)`. Keep each entry whose `refusalNote(entry.body)` is non-null and whose base entry is either missing from `parseEntryDetails(baseMd, section)` or has a null `refusalNote`. Match base and head entries by `entryKey(title)`. Return the kept entries' titles passed through `stripEntryStamp` (`src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`), in file order. Give it a one-paragraph doc comment in the style of `withoutBlockedPlanRefusals`.
  - In `handleRefusal`, compute the titles once `notes` is known and before `commitPathsAndDiscardRest`. That commit resets and cleans the worktree, but the committed notes stay at HEAD, so read before committing to keep the read simple. Do this for each of `[{ file: "PLANS.md", section: "Planned" }, { file: "BUGS.md", section: "Open" }]` whose file is in `notes`: call `newlyRefusedTitles(await fileContentAt(wt, ctx.mainBranch, file), fs.readFileSync(path.join(wt, file), "utf8"), section)` and concatenate the results into `entries`. Read PLANS.md after the `withoutBlockedPlanRefusals` rewrite, so a dropped note is never named. Wrap the reads in `try/catch`, falling back to `[]`: the event is best-effort, and naming must never fail the refusal.
  - Add `entries` to the existing `entry_refused` event: `{ source, type: "entry_refused", reason, files: notes, entries }`. Leave the `reason` and `files` keys unchanged.
- `src/events/event-format.ts`, `case "entry_refused"`: when `Array.isArray(e.entries)` and it is non-empty, render `` entry refused: "<first>"<more>: <reason> (<files>) ``. Here `<first>` is the first title clipped with `truncate(…, 80)` from `src/text/text.ts`, and `<more>` is ` (and N more)` when more than one title is listed. Otherwise keep today's exact line `entry refused: <reason> (<files>)`, so events logged before this change still render as they did.
- `src/events/events.ts`: extend the `entry_refused` union comment to say the event also carries `entries` (the stamp-free titles of the plans and bugs whose Refused note is new).
- `docs/config.md`: in the notify table's `entry_refused` row, say that the message names the held entry.

**Files touched.** `src/verdict/refusal.ts`, `src/events/event-format.ts`, `src/events/events.ts`, `docs/config.md`, `test/refusal.test.ts`, `test/event-format.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/refusal.test.ts`, new unit tests for `newlyRefusedTitles`. A Planned entry that gained a Refused note is returned with its `(planned … by …)` stamp stripped. An entry already refused on base is not returned. An entry that is new on head and carries a note is returned. A note on a `## Done` entry is not returned for section `Planned`. A `### ` line inside a fenced block is not taken as an entry.
- `test/refusal.test.ts`, the existing landed-note tests: the test "a refusal note on a plan whose prerequisite is Done lands as usual" also asserts that the one `entry_refused` event's `entries` equals the refused part's stamp-free title. A new handleRefusal test refuses one PLANS.md plan and one BUGS.md bug in the same run and asserts that `entries` lists both, plan first. The test "a refusal with a markdown note commits only the note and merges it directly" appends a note under no heading, and it asserts `entries` is `[]` and that the event still fires.
- `test/refusal.test.ts`: the test "only the blocked plan's note is dropped when an eligible entry is refused too" asserts that `entries` names only the eligible entry, not the blocked plan whose note was dropped.
- `test/event-format.test.ts`: the existing test "formatEvent renders entry_refused with the reason and files and no warning prefix" passes unchanged. A new test asserts that `{ reason: "too risky", files: ["PLANS.md"], entries: ["Add X", "Add Y"] }` renders `entry refused: "Add X" (and 1 more): too risky (PLANS.md)`, and that a single entry renders with no `(and … more)`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The backlog index lists the newest five `## Done` plans and `## Fixed` bugs with line ranges, so a run reads recent history by range instead of grepping for it (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry)

**Goal.** Every role's orientation rules say to read "Planned plus recent Done entries, Open plus recent Fixed ones" (`commonRules` in `src/prompt/prompt.ts`), but the `<backlog-index>` block that `renderBacklogIndexBlock` (`src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`) builds lists only the actionable sections (`INDEX_SECTIONS`: PLANS.md `## Planned`, BUGS.md `## Open`, QUESTIONS.md `## Open`). So each run that follows the rule first greps PLANS.md or BUGS.md for the `## Done`/`## Fixed` headings. Those sections hold thousands of lines, so a careless grep re-sends a lot of history on every later turn, which is the cost the index was built to remove (BUGS.md 2026-10-06). Both files keep their closed sections newest first, so the first entries in file order are the recent ones. Append those entries' ranges to the same block.

**Approach.**
- `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`:
  - Add `const RECENT_CLOSED_MAX = 5;` and `const CLOSED_SECTIONS: readonly { file: string; section: string }[] = [{ file: "PLANS.md", section: "Done" }, { file: "BUGS.md", section: "Fixed" }];` next to `INDEX_SECTIONS`, each with a one-line doc comment (closed sections, newest first by the files' convention).
  - Add `const closedSectionCache = new Map<string, StatKeyedValue<ActionableEntryRange[]>>();`. Use a separate map because `indexSectionCache` is keyed by the file path alone, and PLANS.md would collide.
  - In `renderBacklogIndexBlock`, after the `INDEX_SECTIONS` loop, loop over `CLOSED_SECTIONS`. For each, call `cachedTextByStat(closedSectionCache, full, full, (md) => actionableEntryRanges(md, section).slice(0, RECENT_CLOSED_MAX), (v) => v.slice())`. Skip a null or empty result. Otherwise push the line `` `${file} ## ${section} (newest ${entries.length})` `` and then one `` `- ${e.start}-${e.end}: ${indexTitle(e.title)}` `` line per entry. Closed entries get no hold mark, no claimer, and no series collapsing.
  - The block stays `undefined` only when the actionable and closed lists are both empty. Rewrite the block's lead sentence to: `Backlog index — each actionable entry, then the newest closed ones, with the 1-based line range it occupies in its file.` Keep the remaining two lead lines unchanged. Update the function's doc comment to say that it also lists the newest `RECENT_CLOSED_MAX` entries of PLANS.md `## Done` and BUGS.md `## Fixed`.
- `src/prompt/prompt.ts`: in the orientation bullet, change "lists the actionable entries (PLANS.md ## Planned, BUGS.md ## Open, QUESTIONS.md ## Open) with each entry's 1-based line range" to "lists the actionable entries (PLANS.md ## Planned, BUGS.md ## Open, QUESTIONS.md ## Open) and the newest few ## Done and ## Fixed entries, each with its 1-based line range". Keep the "Planned plus recent Done entries, Open plus recent Fixed ones" clause exactly as it is, because `test/prompt.test.ts` pins it. Both modules are `// vocabulary: plain`, so the new text must avoid the retired words (harness, operator, loop, tick, landing).
- `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`:
  - The test "renderBacklogIndexBlock lists actionable entries with ranges and strips stamp suffixes" asserts `doesNotMatch(block, /## Done/)` and `/## Fixed/`. Its fixtures hold `_None._` there, so those assertions still hold. Leave them and add the new tests below.
  - A PLANS.md whose `## Done` holds seven entries headed `### D1 (done 2026-10-0N; planned …)` … `### D7 …`: the block contains `PLANS.md ## Done (newest 5)`, lists D1–D5 with their exact ranges, has no D6/D7, and strips the stamps.
  - A BUGS.md whose `## Fixed` holds two entries: the block contains `BUGS.md ## Fixed (newest 2)` with both ranges, and the closed lines come after the `QUESTIONS.md ## Open` lines.
  - A backlog with empty actionable sections but one Done entry still returns a block that lists that entry.
  - A `### ` line inside a fenced block in a Done body is not listed. This comes for free from `actionableEntryRanges`, but pin it.
  - A rewrite of PLANS.md's Done section with a new size is re-read, mirroring "renderBacklogIndexBlock re-reads a backlog file whose stat changed".

**Files touched.** `src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts`, `src/prompt/prompt.ts`, `test/backlog-structure.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `renderBacklogIndexBlock` on this repo's root lists `PLANS.md ## Done (newest 5)` and `BUGS.md ## Fixed (newest 5)`, each with five ranges, and each range's start line is a `### ` heading in that file's closed section.
- Closed entries never carry `[blocked: …]` or `[in flight by …]` marks, and they never change `eligibleEntries` or the claim allocator. This change does not touch `INDEX_SECTIONS`, so these readers do not change.
- A backlog with no `### ` entries in any of the five sections still yields `undefined`.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The steward's prompt lists how many full entries PLANS.md `## Done` and BUGS.md `## Fixed` hold past the ten the compression policy keeps, with the oldest ones' line ranges (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry; touches a new src/backlog/records-overflow.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts and src/roles/role-catalog.ts. The in-flight bugfix flake plan also adds one field to `buildTickPrompt` and one line to `assembleTickPrompt`, so whichever lands second rebases over adjacent lines)

**Goal.** The steward charter (`id: "steward"` in src/roles/role-catalog.ts) keeps the ten most recent `## Done` / `## Fixed` entries verbatim and compresses older ones to one line each. On 2026-10-16, PLANS.md `## Done` held 272 full (`### `) entries and BUGS.md `## Fixed` held 304, so about 560 entries were past the line. The steward's recent compressions (`git log --grep='(steward)'`) each took ten entries. Every steward run also has to grep two files of several hundred KB to find out whether compression is due and where the oldest full entries sit, and nothing tells it how far behind it is when it weighs compression against its other moves. The harness can count this cheaply and synchronously from the files the `<backlog-index>` block already reads, the same way `renderBacklogStructureBlock` gives the clean role its evidence.

**Approach.**
- New `src/backlog/records-overflow.ts`, opted into the vocabulary guard with a `// vocabulary: plain` line (test/vocabulary.test.ts):
  - `export const RECORDS_KEPT_FULL = 10;` (the charter's "ten most recent") and `const OLDEST_LISTED = 10;`.
  - `export interface RecordsOverflow { file: string; section: string; full: number; refused: number; oldest: ActionableEntryRange[]; over: number }`.
  - `export function recordsOverflow(md: string, file: string, section: string): RecordsOverflow | null`. It is pure. It calls `actionableEntryRanges(md, section)` (src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts), whose `### ` entries in file order are newest first. `full` is their count. The first `RECORDS_KEPT_FULL` are kept. The rest are candidates, minus any entry whose body (lines `start` through `end - 1` of `md.split("\n")`, zero-based, i.e. after the heading) carries a Refused note, detected with `refusalNote(body) !== null` (exported from src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts). The charter says those stay full. `refused` counts the excluded ones, `over` counts the remaining candidates, and `oldest` is the last `OLDEST_LISTED` candidates in file order (the bottom of the section). Returns `null` when `over === 0`.
  - `export function renderRecordsOverflowBlock(root: string): string | undefined`. For `["PLANS.md", "Done"]` then `["BUGS.md", "Fixed"]` it reads `filePath = path.join(root, file)` through `cachedTextByStat` (src/files/stat-cache.ts) with a module-level `Map<string, StatKeyedValue<RecordsOverflow | null>>` keyed by `${filePath}#${section}`. The clone returns a copy with `oldest` sliced. This follows `strandedPlanEntriesFor`, so an unchanged file costs one stat. A missing or unreadable file, or a `null` result, contributes nothing. Returns `undefined` when neither file contributes. Otherwise it returns exactly:
    ```
    Closed backlog sections holding more full entries than the 10 most recent your compression policy keeps:
    <records-overflow>
    PLANS.md ## Done: 272 full entries, 262 past the 10 kept (1 more carries a Refused note and stays full). Oldest, by line range:
    - 10900-10975: <title>
    …
    </records-overflow>
    ```
    One paragraph per file, separated by a blank line. The parenthetical is present only when `refused > 0`. Its rows are `oldest` in file order, rendered `- ${start}-${end}: ${title}`, with the title passed through `truncate(title, 120)` from src/text/text.ts. Both `10`s in the block are rendered from `RECORDS_KEPT_FULL`.
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts` `assembleTickPrompt`: next to `backlogStructure`, add `const recordsOverflow = base === "steward" ? renderRecordsOverflowBlock(root) : undefined;` with a one-line comment, and pass `recordsOverflow` to `buildTickPrompt`. Because `base` is used, `steward-2` and the `tumwater role steward` preview (role-view's `rolePayload` goes through the same function) get the block too.
- `src/prompt/prompt.ts`: add `recordsOverflow?: string` to the `buildTickPrompt` input type. Its doc comment: rendered closed-section overflow block (see records-overflow.ts); steward only, omitted when both closed sections are within the policy or unreadable. Destructure it and push it right after `if (backlogStructure) parts.push(backlogStructure);`, before the backlog index.
- `src/roles/role-catalog.ts`, steward `find`: at the end of the paragraph that starts "Reading the backlog files:", add one sentence: "When a \`<records-overflow>\` block is present, it counts the full entries past the ten kept in each closed section and lists the oldest ones with their line ranges: read those by range instead of searching for them." No other charter text changes.

**Files touched.** src/backlog/records-overflow.ts (new), src/tick/tick-prompt.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts, test/records-overflow.test.ts (new), test/tick-prompt.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/records-overflow.test.ts, `recordsOverflow` over inline markdown:
  - a `## Done` with exactly 10 `### ` entries (and some `- ` one-liners below them) returns `null`;
  - 13 entries return `full: 13, over: 3, refused: 0`, and `oldest` holds entries 11–13 with their 1-based heading lines as `start`;
  - 25 entries list only the last 10 in `oldest`, with `over: 15`;
  - an over-the-line entry with an indented `**Refused 2026-10-12 by feature: x**` body line is excluded from `oldest` and counted in `refused`. A Refused note on one of the first ten changes nothing;
  - `### ` lines under `## Planned` or inside a fenced block in `## Done` are not counted;
  - the `Fixed` section of a BUGS.md-shaped document is counted the same way.
- test/records-overflow.test.ts, `renderRecordsOverflowBlock` over a temp root: both files past the line give one block with a `PLANS.md ## Done:` and a `BUGS.md ## Fixed:` paragraph in that order, between `<records-overflow>` tags; only one file past the line gives only that paragraph; neither, or a root with no files, gives `undefined`; rewriting PLANS.md with a changed size re-reads it (as the `renderBacklogStructureBlock re-reads PLANS.md whose stat changed` test does).
- test/tick-prompt.test.ts, with a temp root whose PLANS.md `## Done` holds 12 full entries: `promptFor(dir, "steward").prompt` contains `<records-overflow>` before `Your task this run:`; `promptFor(dir, "steward-2")` carries it too; `promptFor(dir, "clean")` does not; a steward prompt over a `## Done` with 10 entries does not.
- test/vocabulary.test.ts passes with the new module opted in.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms role ids, part 2/5: Rename a legacy role id's branch and refs and files once at startup (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 1/5 and Plain terms state 3/5 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Role names"; touches src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts and the startup migration hook plus a test) (done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** When a role's id changes, the first startup on the new build moves that role's on-disk artifacts to the new id before anything reads them. The role keeps its branch, pending merge, notes, inbox and sessions. The step is idempotent and does nothing while `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS` is empty.

**Approach.**
- New module `src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts` with `migrateLegacyRoleIds(root: string, legacy = LEGACY_ROLE_IDS): Promise<string[]>`. It returns one line per artifact moved or skipped. For each `[old, new]`:
  - **Branch:** when `branchName(old)` exists and `branchName(new)` does not, run `git branch -m tumwater/<old> tumwater/<new>`. git also repoints any worktree that has it checked out. When the new branch exists, leave both and report the skip.
  - **Refs:** the merge ref (`refs/tumwater/merge/<id>`, through the name helper Plain terms state left in src/paths.ts) and `rejectedRefName(id)`. When the old ref exists and the new one does not, run `git update-ref <new> <sha>` and then `git update-ref -d <old> <sha>`.
  - **Paths:** `statePath`, `roleNotesPath`, `roleInboxDir`, `sessionDir` and `reviewSessionDir` (src/paths.ts). When the old path exists and the new one does not, `fs.renameSync`. When both exist, leave both and report.
  - **Not moved:** pi and native logs stay where they are, because they are history.
  - Each artifact is its own try/catch. A failure is reported and never aborts startup or the other moves. Use the git helpers the codebase already has (`gitTry` and `runGit` from src/git/).
- Register the step by appending one line at the end of src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts (the hook Plain terms state part 3/5 added): `registerStartupMigration({ name: "legacyRoleIds", run: (root) => migrateLegacyRoleIds(root) })`. It goes after `mergeRefs`, so its ref rename sees `refs/tumwater/merge/<old>` and never a legacy `landing/` ref. Its returned lines become the step's `state_migrated` detail, the hook's logging convention.
- `cmdRun`'s once-mode path (src/cli/cli-run.ts) reads `loadLoopState` for its `ticksBefore` snapshot before `runOrchestrator` starts. Call `runStartupMigrations(root)` there first, so the snapshot reads the migrated `state/<new>.json`. The hook is idempotent, so the orchestrator's own call then moves nothing.
- New `test/legacy-role-migration.test.ts` on a fixture repo (test/fixtures/repo-fixtures.ts), with the map `{ oldy: "newy" }`. Build:
  - branch `tumwater/oldy` and both refs;
  - `state/oldy.json`, `state/notes/oldy.md` and `inbox/oldy/x.md`;
  - `sessions/oldy/` and `sessions/_review/oldy/`;
  - a pi log.
  - Then assert:
    - after one run each artifact is under `newy` with its content intact, and the log has not moved;
    - a second run moves nothing;
    - with `tumwater/newy` already present, `tumwater/oldy` stays and the skip is reported;
    - with the real, empty map, nothing happens.

**Files touched.** src/roles/legacy-role-migration.ts (new), src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts, src/cli/cli-run.ts, test/legacy-role-migration.test.ts (new). Reads (does not edit): src/paths.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the fixture, every listed artifact moves to the new id, and nothing that already exists under the new id is overwritten.
- A second run is a no-op.
- The step is registered in the startup hook and runs before the first per-runner state read, which the hook's own test pattern pins.
- With `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS` empty, startup does no new git or file work beyond the empty loop.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The bugfix run's prompt lists the checks the merge gate excused as flaky in the last 24 h, with counts, so a flapping test gets fixed (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry; touches src/review/known-flakes.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts and src/prompt/prompt.ts)

**Goal.** When a check fails at the merge gate and then passes on its one re-run, the gate logs a warning starting `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` (src/review/known-flakes.ts) and lets the change merge. Nothing rejects, so no role is told about it. `tumwater doctor`'s `flaky checks` check (`checkFlakyChecks` in src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts) warns the operator. The only role that reads the event log is `telemetry`, and it is opt-in. So by default a flapping test is fixed only after someone files a bug by hand. The open BUGS.md entry for `test/supervisor.test.ts` "startParentDeathWatch…", now flaking for the third time, is an example. The bugfix run should get the gate's own flake tally as a fact. Then it knows whether an open flaky-test bug is still firing, and with an empty `## Open` it has a confirmed latent bug to take instead of a ~10-call hunt. This follows the plan run's harness-computed eligible count (`planTargetNote` in src/tick/tick-prompt.ts).

**Approach.**
- `src/review/known-flakes.ts`: add `export function flakeCounts(events: readonly HarnessEvent[]): [string, number][]`. It tallies `flakeWarningKeys(events)` (no cutoff) into a `Map` with `increment` from src/collections.ts. It returns the entries sorted by count, highest first. Ties keep first-seen order (the sort is stable). The function is pure, with no I/O and no clock.
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` `checkFlakyChecks`: replace its inline `counts` map and sort with `const flapped = flakeCounts(events).filter(([, n]) => n >= 2);`. Its output does not change: the same order and the same detail strings. In its import from known-flakes.js, replace `flakeWarningKeys` with `flakeCounts`. Remove the `increment` import from src/collections.js, because this is its only use in the file. Update the doc comment above `checkFlakyChecks` to name `flakeCounts` where it names `flakeWarningKeys`.
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`: add a private `flakyChecksNote(root: string): string | undefined`. It reads `readEventsSince(root, KNOWN_FLAKE_WINDOW_MS).events` (src/events/event-window.ts) and calls `flakeCounts` on them. The read sits inside `try { … } catch { return undefined; }`, as the qa coverage read does, so an unreadable log never fails a run. With no counts it returns `undefined`. Otherwise it returns exactly:
  `Flaky checks: in the last 24h the merge gate excused these check failures as flaky (each failed, then passed on its one re-run), most frequent first: ${shown}${more}. An excused flake blocks no merge, so it stays unfixed until it has a BUGS.md entry. When an open bug names one of these, that bug is still firing. When \`## Open\` holds no entries, a check excused 2 or more times is a confirmed latent bug: take it as this run's latent-bug candidate.`
  Here `shown` is the first 5 entries rendered `"${key}" ×${n}`, joined with `"; "`. `more` is `` ` (and ${counts.length - 5} more)` `` when there are more than 5, else `""`. In `assembleTickPrompt`'s role branch, add `const flakyChecks = base === "bugfix" ? flakyChecksNote(root) : undefined;` next to `planTargetNote`, and pass it to `buildTickPrompt`. This way bugfix instances (`bugfix-2`) get the note, and so does the `tumwater role bugfix` preview, which goes through the same branch.
- `src/prompt/prompt.ts`: add `flakyChecks?: string` to the `buildTickPrompt` input type. Its doc comment says: the bugfix run's flake tally, rendered by tick-prompt.ts, omitted for every other role and when no flake was excused in the window. Destructure it in `buildTickPrompt` and push `flakyChecks.trim()` right after the `planTargetNote` push, so it follows the task text.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: in the merge pipeline's **Check** bullet, after "one that then passes is warned as a flake and proceeds", add one sentence: the bugfix run's prompt lists the checks excused as flakes in the last 24 h, with their counts.

**Files touched.** src/review/known-flakes.ts, src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/tick/tick-prompt.ts, src/prompt/prompt.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/known-flakes.test.ts, test/tick-prompt.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/known-flakes.test.ts: `flakeCounts([])` is `[]`. Three warnings, two of them with the same headline apart from a duration ("test failed after 3s" and "test failed after 9s") and one other headline, give `[["test failed after <dur>", 2], ["<other normalized key>", 1]]`. Two headlines with equal counts come back in first-seen order. Non-warning events and warnings without the prefix are not counted.
- test/tick-prompt.test.ts, using `logEvent(root, { source: "review", type: "warning", message: \`${FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX}…\` })` as test/doctor-checks.test.ts does:
  - after two warnings for one headline, the `bugfix` prompt contains `Flaky checks:` and `"<key>" ×2`, and the note comes after `Your task this run:`;
  - with the same log, the `feature` prompt does not contain `Flaky checks:`;
  - a `bugfix` prompt over an empty log does not contain `Flaky checks:`;
  - six distinct headlines show five entries and `(and 1 more)`;
  - a `bugfix-2` prompt carries the note.
- The existing `checkFlakyChecks` tests in test/doctor-checks.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes, including the plain-terms vocabulary guard on prompt text.

### Fallback chain, part 7a/7: A `tumwater doctor` "fallback chain" check lists each tier's steps and probes local servers (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; split 2026-10-16 by plan from part 7/7, siblings 7b/7, 7c/7 and 7d/7; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "Events and surfaces"; touches src/pi/pi-models.ts src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts src/doctor/doctor.ts and their tests)

**Goal.** Doctor's over-cap model row says "priced at zero (cost n/a), serving not verified" even when the local server is down. On 2026-10-16 neither `qwenrunner` (127.0.0.1:8090) nor oMLX (:8000) was listening. A new row lists every step of every tier's chain and says whether each one can run now. This part reads only config, pi's `models.json` and the loop states, so it needs no other part of 7/7.

**Approach.**
- src/pi/pi-models.ts: add `piProviderBaseUrl(modelsPath: string, provider: string): string | null`. It returns the provider's `baseUrl` string from `models.json`, or null when the file, the provider or the field is missing. Read the file with the same `readJsonFile` guard `readPiProviders` uses.
- src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts: add `async function checkFallbackChain(root: string, modelsPath = piModelsPath(), probe: (url: string) => Promise<boolean> = probeModels): Promise<CheckOutcome>`.
  - It loads the config with `loadConfigForCheck`, takes the steps from `tierChainSteps(config)`, and loads the states with `loadLoopStates(root, config)`. Export that function from src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts, where it is module-private today.
  - No steps: `okOutcome("none configured")`.
  - For each step it writes one fragment, `<tier> <step+1>: <provider>/<model> — <verdict>`. Fragments are joined with `; `. The verdict is decided in this order:
    1. A pi step whose `piProviderBaseUrl` host is `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`, and where `probe(<baseUrl>/models)` resolves false: `not running (GET <baseUrl>/models failed)`.
    2. A step with `maxDailyCostUsd` where `pairDailyCost(states, modelPairName(pair), now) >= maxDailyCostUsd`: `cap reached ($5.00/$5)`, written as `${usd(spent)}/${usdCap(cap)}` (src/text/format.ts).
    3. A pi step that `piPairFree` prices at zero: `free`, plus ` · server up` when rule 1 probed it.
    4. A claude step: `claude` and the billing (`subscription` or `extra usage` when `pair.extraUsage`), from `readClaudeAccount(root)`.
    5. Otherwise: `priced` and today's spend over its cap, or `priced, team cap only` when it has no step cap.
  - It warns when any step reads `not running`, and is ok otherwise.
  - `probeModels(url)` is a module-private `fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) })` that resolves `res.ok` and resolves false on any throw. It uses node's built-in fetch, so it adds no dependency.
- src/doctor/doctor.ts: add `{ name: "fallback chain", ...(await checkFallbackChain(root)) }` right after the `over-cap model` row.

**Files touched.** src/pi/pi-models.ts, src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor-holds.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** All of these are tests in test/doctor-model-checks.test.ts, with a temp `models.json` and an injected or real local probe:
- A local step whose `baseUrl` points at a port that was listened on and then closed (a `node:http` server on 127.0.0.1:0, then `close()`) warns and contains `not running`. The same step with the server listening reads ok and contains `free · server up`.
- A priced step with `maxDailyCostUsd: 5` and a state charging that pair $5 today contains `cap reached ($5.00/$5)`.
- A config with no fallback reads ok `none configured`.
- A non-local `baseUrl` never calls the probe: the injected probe counts zero calls.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Plain terms role ids, part 1/5: Read legacy role ids as their new ids through one alias table (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires Plain terms state 5/5 and Plain terms commands 6/6 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Role names"; touches src/roles/ and src/config/config-aliases.ts and src/cli/ and the event normalizer plus the persisted role readers) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** One table of retired role ids, and every place a role id enters tumwater reads an old id as its new one: typed ids, config keys, old events, and persisted state. This part ships the table empty, so nothing changes yet. Parts 3/5 and 4/5 each add one row and get every alias for free.

**Approach.**
- New module `src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts`. Each function takes an optional `legacy` map so tests can pass fixture ids.
  - `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {}`, old id → new id. Its doc comment says rows are added by the switch parts and never removed.
  - `canonicalRoleId(id: string, legacy = LEGACY_ROLE_IDS): string` — the own-property mapping, else `id`.
  - `legacyRoleIdsOf(id: string, legacy = LEGACY_ROLE_IDS): string[]` — the old ids that map to `id`.
  - `roleCommitGrep(id: string, legacy = LEGACY_ROLE_IDS): string` — `--grep="tumwater(<id>)"` followed by one more `--grep="tumwater(<old>)"` per legacy id. git ORs repeated `--grep`s, so a prompt's history search sees a role's commits under both ids.
- **Typed ids:** canonicalize before validating, so `--role <old>` behaves exactly like `--role <new>`.
  - `parseRoleFlag` (src/cli/cli-args.ts). This covers `parseRoleScope`, the operator commands, `start --role` and `cmdDiff`.
  - `cmdRole`'s id read in src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, its positional or its direct `flagValue(rest, "--role")`.
  - The prompt command's `--role` check in src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts.
  - `tumwater role <id>` in src/roles/role-view.ts `rolePayload`.
  - The `history <role> <n>` positional in src/tick/tick-detail.ts `cmdTick`.
  - The dashboard needs none: it sends ids from its own status payload.
- **Config:** extend `normalizeConfigKeys` and `canonicalConfigKey` in src/config/config-aliases.ts (Plain terms commands) with a role-id pass driven by `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS`, taking an optional `legacy` map.
  - An old id as a key of `roles`, `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` or `quietHoursPerRole` moves to the new id.
  - Both present records the problem `sets both roles.<old> and roles.<new> — keep roles.<new> (<old> is its old id)`.
  - Each move is added to `renamed`, so doctor's `config key names` check reports it with no new code.
  - `canonicalConfigKey` maps `roles.<old>.<field>` and `<map>.<old>`, so `config get|set|unset` accept the old id.
- **Events:** in `normalizeLegacyEvent` (Plain terms event log), pass `source`, and the `role` field of role events, through `canonicalRoleId`. History, the report, the failure digest and the feeds then fold an old id's events into the new id.
- **Persisted state:** each reader canonicalizes the role ids it returns. Writers already write the id they are given.
  - `readPausedRoles` and `scheduledWakes` in src/fleet/fleet-state.ts.
  - The merge-queue entry reader's `role`: `queuedLandingFiles` in src/landing/landing-queue.ts, or its Plain terms state successor.
  - The merging marker's role reader.
  - `readSlotsState`'s pinned role in src/git/slots-state.ts.
- **Prompts:** `searchGuidance(roleId)` in src/roles/role-guidance.ts uses `roleCommitGrep(roleId)` in place of its single `--grep`.
- New `test/legacy-role-ids.test.ts`, using a fixture map `{ oldy: "newy" }`:
  - `canonicalRoleId`, `legacyRoleIdsOf` and `roleCommitGrep`;
  - `normalizeConfigKeys` moves `roles.oldy`, `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole.oldy` and `quietHoursPerRole.oldy`, refuses a file with both ids, and lists each move;
  - `canonicalConfigKey("roles.oldy.model")`;
  - with the real, empty map, every function is the identity.

**Files touched.** src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts (new), src/roles/role-guidance.ts, src/roles/role-view.ts, src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/cli/cli-args.ts, src/cli/cli-query-commands.ts, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, src/tick/tick-detail.ts, the `normalizeLegacyEvent` module in src/events/, src/fleet/fleet-state.ts, src/landing/landing-queue.ts or its successor, src/git/slots-state.ts, the merging-marker reader; test/legacy-role-ids.test.ts (new).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `LEGACY_ROLE_IDS` empty, no existing test changes and no command output changes.
- With the fixture map, a config holding `roles.oldy` normalizes to `roles.newy` and reports `roles.oldy → roles.newy`, and one holding both is refused naming both.
- `roleCommitGrep("newy", { oldy: "newy" })` holds both `--grep` arguments, and `searchGuidance` uses it.

### Fallback chain, part 7b/7: The budget gate publishes each tier's step as a `chain` block and logs `fallback_switched` (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; split 2026-10-16 by plan from part 7/7, siblings 7a/7, 7c/7 and 7d/7; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "Events and surfaces"; touches src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/gates/gate-polls.ts src/fleet/orchestrator-info.ts src/events/ and their tests)

**Goal.** After parts 1/7–6/7, a tier can run on a later step of its chain because the window is used up, the reserve is reached, the team cap is reached, a step's own cap is spent, or a step was demoted. Nothing records which step each tier is on. This part publishes it for the surfaces in 7c/7 and 7d/7, and logs each change.

**Approach.**
- src/fleet/orchestrator-info.ts: export `interface ChainTierInfo { pair: string; step: number; of: number; reason: ChainReason; returnsAt?: number; spentUsd?: number; capUsd?: number }`, with `type ChainReason = "window" | "reserve" | "cap" | "step-cap" | "overage" | "demoted"`. Add `chain?: Partial<Record<ModelTier, ChainTierInfo>>` to `OrchestratorInfo`. The read-side sanitizer drops a `chain` that is not a JSON object, the same way it drops a malformed `budget`.
  - `step` is the 1-based position in the supplying tier's chain: `TierFallback.step ?? 0`, plus 1.
  - `of` is that chain's length, from `tierChainSteps`.
- src/gates/budget-gates.ts: `BudgetGatePoll` gains `chain: Partial<Record<ModelTier, ChainTierInfo>>`, built by a new exported pure helper `chainInfo(...)` from `servingResolved`. A tier gets an entry only when this poll moved it off its primary: every tier while `reached`, and while the window move is active, the tiers whose primary is a subscription claude seam. A tier the gate pauses (`pair: null`) gets no entry.
  - `reason` names why the position just before the active step cannot run, checked in this order:
    1. That position is a chain step whose breaker is demoted (`fallbackServingPair` false): `demoted`.
    2. It is a chain step at its own `maxDailyCostUsd`: `step-cap`.
    3. It is a claude step, or the tier's primary is claude, and `windowOut` is set: `reserve` when `windowOut.reserve`, else `window`.
    4. It is a claude `extraUsage` step and `claudeOverageRefused(account)`: `overage`.
    5. Otherwise: `cap`.
  - `returnsAt` is `windowOut.resetsAt` for `window` and `reserve`, and the next local midnight (`dayAt(-1, new Date(now)).getTime()`) for `cap` and `step-cap`. It is absent for `demoted` and `overage`.
  - `spentUsd` and `capUsd` are set for a priced active step that has `maxDailyCostUsd`, from `pairDailyCost`.
  - `BudgetGateState` gains `prevChain` (initially `{}`).
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts: add `["chain", chain]` to the existing `publishInfoFields` batch. When there are no entries, publish `undefined` so the field disappears. When any tier's `pair` or `step` differs from `state.budget.prevChain`, log one `fallback_switched` event carrying `tiers: { <tier>: { from: <pair|null>, to: <pair|null>, reason } }` for each changed tier. A tier returning to its primary has `to: null` and reason `available`. Then advance `prevChain`.

### A role's run prompt says when its notes were last saved, so the run can weigh how stale they are (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry. It touches only the notes block in `src/prompt/prompt.ts`, the note read in `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, their tests, and one docs sentence. No waiting entry edits `roleNotesBlock` or `TickPromptInput.notes`. Blocked Plain terms parts later rename `buildTickPrompt` and `initialPrompt` in the same file, and rebase over this change without touching it) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** Every role run sees its notes as `Notes your role wrote in earlier runs (yours, unverified — …)`, with no hint of their age. A note saved this morning and one last replaced three weeks and hundreds of merges ago look the same. So a run cannot tell whether "where things live" and "ruled out" still hold before it spends tool calls checking them. The note file's mtime is when the notes were last saved. `saveRoleNote` writes through `writeTextAtomic` (tmp + rename), so the mtime changes only when the file is replaced. A run that never calls `role_notes` leaves the date alone, which is the date the run should see.

**Approach.**
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`: next to `readRoleNote`, read the note file's last-saved day: `statOrNull(roleNotesPath(root, role))` (from `src/files/files.ts`), then `dayKey(stats.mtimeMs)` (from `src/text/datetime.ts`). Pass it as a new `notesSavedDay` field to `buildTickPrompt`. When `statOrNull` returns null, or the note is undefined, pass undefined. Do not change `readRoleNote` itself.
- `src/prompt/prompt.ts`: add `notesSavedDay?: string` to `TickPromptInput`. Its doc comment says it is the note file's mtime as a local `YYYY-MM-DD` and that omitting it keeps today's wording. In `buildTickPrompt`, resolve `const day = today ?? todayStamp()` once. Use `day` for both `sharedPreamble` and the notes block, so the age and the date line cannot disagree. Change `roleNotesBlock(notes)` to `roleNotesBlock(notes, savedDay?, today?)`. When both are given, the parenthetical opens with the age: `Notes your role wrote in earlier runs (last saved 2026-10-14, 2 days ago; yours, unverified — check against the code before\nrelying on them):`. Use `today` in place of the date clause when the days match, and `1 day ago` for one day. A saved day after today (clock skew or a hand-set mtime) renders just `last saved <day>`, with no age. Count days with a small pure helper, `daysBetween(fromKey: string, toKey: string): number`, added to `src/text/datetime.ts`. It parses both `YYYY-MM-DD` keys with `Date.UTC`, so a DST shift cannot make the count off by one, and returns the whole-day difference. Without `savedDay`, the block is byte-identical to today's.
- Tests:
  - `test/prompt.test.ts`, next to "a role's run prompt carries the role-notes block only when a note exists": pin `today: "2026-10-16"` and check the rendered phrase for `notesSavedDay` values `"2026-10-16"` (`last saved today;`), `"2026-10-15"` (`2026-10-15, 1 day ago;`), `"2026-09-30"` (`2026-09-30, 16 days ago;`) and `"2026-10-20"` (`last saved 2026-10-20;`, with no "ago"). Also check that a prompt without `notesSavedDay` contains `(yours, unverified` with no `last saved`.
  - `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`, next to "a role run prompt reads the note from roleNotesPath…": write the note, then `fs.utimesSync` it to a fixed past local date (for example `new Date(2026, 8, 30, 12)`). Assert the prompt carries `last saved 2026-09-30,`. A missing note file still gives no block.
  - `test/datetime.test.ts`: a `daysBetween` unit test. Cover the same day (0), a span across a DST change such as `2026-03-01` → `2026-04-01` (31), and a negative span.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`, in the notes paragraph ("A run sees the note when one exists…"): add that the run is also told the day the note was last saved and how many days ago that was.

**Files touched.** `src/prompt/prompt.ts`, `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, `src/text/datetime.ts`, `test/prompt.test.ts`, `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`, `test/datetime.test.ts`, `docs/how-it-works.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A run whose note file was last written on 2026-09-30, building its prompt on 2026-10-16, shows `last saved 2026-09-30, 16 days ago; yours, unverified` in the `<role-notes>` heading (test/prompt.test.ts and test/tick-prompt.test.ts).
- A same-day note reads `last saved today;`, and a future mtime shows the date with no age.
- With no note, or with no `notesSavedDay`, the notes block and the write instruction are unchanged, and the existing role-notes tests pass as written.
- The date line and the notes age come from the same resolved day: a test passing `today` sees both use it.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The plan role's stop-target line also gives the harness's count of eligible plans, so the run does not recount the index by hand (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; done 2026-10-16)

**Goal.** A plan run decides whether to stop by comparing the eligible plans in `## Planned` with its stop target. Today the prompt states only the target: `planTargetNote` in `assembleTickPrompt` (`src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`) renders "This run's stop target: when PLANS.md `## Planned` already holds N or more eligible plans…". The model then counts the `<backlog-index>` lines not marked `[blocked: …]` itself, every run. It can miscount, for example by leaving out in-flight entries or counting a whole blocked series as one plan. The harness already computes this count: `planBacklogFull` (`src/scheduling/claims.ts`) compares `eligibleEntries(root, "feature").length` with `planBacklogTarget(config)` to decide whether a plan run is deferred. The prompt should give that same number, so the model and the scheduler use one count.

**Approach.**
- `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, in the `base === "plan"` branch that builds `planTargetNote`: compute `const eligible = eligibleEntries(root, "feature").length`. `eligibleEntries` is already imported from `../backlog/backlog-eligibility.js`. Append one sentence to the note: `` It holds ${eligible} now (the harness's count of entries feature could take, the same count that decides whether a plan run is deferred).`` Use the bare number as shown, not `plural` from `src/text/phrases.ts`: "It holds N now" reads correctly for any N, and it keeps the test regexes simple. The existing sentence stays word for word, so the current `/2 or more eligible plans/` matches keep passing.
- Leave `src/roles/role-catalog.ts`'s charter text alone. Its rule, "count only eligible entries — those the index block does not mark blocked", stays the definition. The new sentence only gives the result.
- The preview path (`tumwater role plan`'s next prompt, via `rolePayload`) builds its prompt through `assembleTickPrompt`, so it shows the same count with no extra code.
- `docs/how-it-works.md`, in the paragraph that says the plan role keeps `instances(feature) + 1` eligible plans ahead: add that the plan run's prompt gives both the target and the current count, the same count the deferral uses.

**Files touched.** `src/tick/tick-prompt.ts`, `test/tick-prompt.test.ts`, `docs/how-it-works.md`.

### Plain terms state, part 5/5: Move landing refs to refs/tumwater/merge and write the Run trailer (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 4/5 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "State and git"; touches src/paths.ts src/git/ src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts src/operator/retire.ts src/roles/role-catalog.ts test/)

**Goal.** Two git-side renames:
- The pin for a committed but unmerged change moves from `refs/tumwater/landing/<id>` to `refs/tumwater/merge/<id>`, and startup moves existing pins with `update-ref`. `refs/tumwater/rejected/<id>` is unchanged.
- New commits carry a `Run: <id> #N · turns … · ctx …` trailer, and every prompt that greps for the trailer matches both `Run:` and `Tick:`.

**Approach.**
- src/paths.ts: `landingRefName(role)` returns `refs/tumwater/merge/<role>`. Plain terms code merge renames the function. Add `legacyLandingRefName(role)`, which returns `refs/tumwater/landing/<role>`.
- src/git/git.ts: add `refsUnder(root, prefix)`, returning `{ ref, sha }[]` from `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname)' <prefix>`. Follow the existing `gitTry`/`gitLines` pattern.
- Migration step `mergeRefs`, registered last in startup-migration-steps.ts, runs for each ref under `refs/tumwater/landing/`:
  - When the new ref is absent: `setRef(new, sha)`, then `git update-ref -d <legacy> <sha>`, guarded by the old value. The legacy ref is never deleted before its copy exists.
  - When the new ref names the same sha: delete the legacy ref.
  - When the new ref names a different sha: keep both and note it. Never overwrite a pin the new build wrote.
- src/operator/retire.ts:
  - `collectRetire` reads `landingRefName(role)` and falls back to `legacyLandingRefName(role)`.
  - `retireRole` deletes both, because a fleet stopped before its first start on this build still holds legacy pins.
  - Every other reader and writer (landing-core.ts, leftover.ts, loop-recovery.ts, loop-tick.ts, tick-timing.ts, landing-stack.ts, landing-pipeline.ts, landing-check-failures.ts) goes through `landingRefName` inside the orchestrator, after the step has run.
- Tests: test/loop-2.test.ts builds the ref's file path by hand, so update it. test/git.test.ts and test/git-ref-files.test.ts use the name only as an arbitrary ref and may stay.
- Trailer:
  - `commitTrailer` (src/git/commit-message.ts) writes `Run:`.
  - The readme role's instructions in src/roles/role-catalog.ts say new commits carry `Run: readme #N` and older ones `Tick: readme #N`, and use `git log -E --grep='^(Run|Tick): readme #' -1 --format=%H`.
  - No src code parses the `Tick:` line today: `hasFrictionTrailer` and `revisionRoundOf` read only the Friction and Revision lines. Grep to confirm; any parser found must accept both forms.
  - Tests that assert the trailer: test/loop-2.test.ts, loop-leftover-recovery, loop-merge-conflicts, loop-transient-retry, tick-stage, refusal, loop-ids and prompt-roles.
- If the vocabulary guard flags a legacy literal, end its line with `// vocabulary-ok: legacy name read from old refs or commits`.
- **Self-hosting:** safe in one part.
  - The old build pins under `landing/` until it exits.
  - The new build moves the pins before its first reader, leftover recovery, runs.
  - A crash between the two `update-ref` calls leaves the commit reachable under both names, and the next start finishes the move.
  - The trailer has no code parser, and the prompt matches both forms. History keeps `Tick:`.

**Files touched.** src/paths.ts, src/git/git.ts, src/git/commit-message.ts, src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts, src/operator/retire.ts, src/roles/role-catalog.ts; test/startup-migrations.test.ts, test/retire.test.ts, test/loop-2.test.ts, test/loop-leftover-recovery.test.ts, test/loop-merge-conflicts.test.ts, test/loop-transient-retry.test.ts, test/tick-stage.test.ts, test/refusal.test.ts, test/loop-ids.test.ts, test/prompt-roles.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Fixture: a repo with `refs/tumwater/landing/improve` at an unmerged sha. Startup leaves `refs/tumwater/merge/improve` at that sha and no legacy ref, and leftover recovery re-queues the change. A second start changes nothing. A legacy and a new ref at different shas are both kept and noted.

### `tumwater retire --role <id>` accepts a role id that is no longer configured while its branch or merge ref remains (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; done 2026-10-16; independent of the waiting series — touches src/operator/retire.ts, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/retire.test.ts, and src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts plus test/doctor-checks.test.ts only when `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` is already on main)

**Goal.** Lowering `roles.feature.instances` from 4 to 2 leaves `tumwater/feature-3` and `tumwater/feature-4` behind. The same happens to a custom role removed from `tumwater.json`. `tumwater retire --role feature-4` rejects these ids as `unknown role: feature-4`. The reason is that `cmdRetire` resolves its target through `requiredNamedRole` → `namedRole` (`src/operator/operator-commands.ts`), which accepts only `allRoleIds()` plus `knownRoleIds(loadConfig(root))`, and `knownRoleIds` adds only the configured `loopIds` instances. Retire exists to clean up the leftovers of a loop that no longer runs, so it should accept any well-formed id that still has a leftover branch or merge ref. `retireRole`'s rails need no change: `loopEnabled` is false for such an id, so the "still enabled" rail stays quiet, and the unmerged-commits, dirty, unusable-worktree, and mid-run rails apply as they do today.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/retire.ts`: add `export async function hasRetirableLeftovers(root: string, role: string): Promise<boolean>`, with a doc comment saying it is the id gate for ids no config names. It returns true only when all of these hold:
  - `CUSTOM_NAME_RE.test(role)` (`src/config/config-schema.ts`). That is the custom-role name pattern, and it also matches instance ids such as `feature-4`. It keeps `..` and `/` out of the `worktreePath`/`branchName` paths collectRetire builds.
  - `role !== DIRECTOR_ROLE` (`src/roles/roles.ts`).
  - Either `await branchExists(root, branchName(role))` is true or `await refSha(root, landingRefName(role)) !== null`. Both helpers are already imported there.
  
  This function is read-only.
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`: add `async function retireTargetRole(root: string, args: string[]): Promise<string>` and use it in `cmdRetire` in place of `requiredNamedRole(root, args, "retire")`. Leave `namedRole`, `requiredNamedRole`, and their other callers (abort, resume, wake, reset-counters) unchanged. Behavior, in this order:
  - `flagValue(args, "--role")` is `null` → fail with the same `retire requires --role <id> (e.g. \`--role feature\`)` text `requiredNamedRole` prints. Reuse `requiredNamedRole`'s message by calling it on this path, not by copying the string.
  - Empty value → `fail(ROLE_VALUE_ERROR)` (from `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`), as `parseRoleFlag` does.
  - `allRoleIds().includes(role)` → return it. This keeps today's broken-config path: collectRetire then throws "cannot read tumwater.json".
  - Else load `ids = knownRoleIds(loadConfig(root))`. On a load error, `fail(errorMessage(err))` as `namedRole` does. When `ids.includes(role)`, return it.
  - Else, when `await hasRetirableLeftovers(root, role)` is true, return it.
  - Else `fail(unknownRoleMessage(role, ids))` (`src/roles/roles.ts`). This is the same message as today, so `retire --role bogus` keeps printing `unknown role: bogus`.
  - Update the `cmdRetire` comment that says the config exists only to validate the id so it also mentions the leftover-branch gate.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: in the `tumwater retire --role <id>` stanza, replace the last line `changing nothing` with these three lines, using the same 35-column indent:
  ```
  changing nothing; an id no longer configured (`feature-4`
  after lowering `instances`, a removed custom role) is
  accepted while its branch or merge ref remains
  ```
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Control-the-roles row, change the `tumwater retire --role <id> [--dry-run]` parenthetical's clause "use after setting `enabled: false` for that role" to "use after setting `enabled: false` for that role, lowering `instances`, or removing a custom role — an id no longer in `tumwater.json` is accepted while its `tumwater/<id>` branch or merge ref remains". Leave the rest of the row alone.
- Doctor follow-through. Do this only when `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` exists in `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts` at implementation time. It is the in-flight "`tumwater doctor` names disabled roles that still keep a branch" entry, and its "unknown" part says retire rejects ids outside `knownRoleIds`, which stops being true after this change. Change its split so an id is retirable when `knownRoleIds(config).includes(id) || CUSTOM_NAME_RE.test(id)`. Every other id stays in the unknown part, with that part's wording unchanged. The check already has the branch, so it does not call `hasRetirableLeftovers`. In `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, the test "checkLeftoverRoleBranches names disabled roles' branches and unknown ones, skipping enabled roles and the director" changes in three ways:
  - Its `tumwater/ghost` case now expects `ghost` among the retirable ids.
  - Its unknown-branch assertion uses `tumwater/old.role` (the `.` fails `CUSTOM_NAME_RE`).
  - Its `tumwater/feature-2` case expects `feature-2` among the retirable ids after `writeConfig(root, {})`.
  
  When `checkLeftoverRoleBranches` is not on main, skip this step entirely. The doctor entry is then implemented against the new `retireTargetRole`, and its implementer reads this plan's Done entry.

**Files touched.** src/operator/retire.ts, src/operator/operator-commands.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/retire.test.ts, plus src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts and test/doctor-checks.test.ts when the doctor follow-through applies.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/retire.test.ts`, "retire accepts a leftover instance id above the configured instances and removes its branch". Use `initializedRepo()`. Write `roles.feature` with `instances: 2` the way the "retire refuses an enabled work instance id, not just its bare base role (part 5b/7)" test does. Create the branch with `sh(root, "git", "branch", branchName("feature-4"))`. Then `cli(root, "retire", "--role", "feature-4", "--json")` exits 0, `removed` includes `"branch"`, and `branchHead(root, branchName("feature-4"))` is `null` afterwards.
- Same file: `retire --role feature-4 --dry-run` on that fixture, before the removal, exits 0 and prints `would remove the branch (tumwater/feature-4)`.
- Same file: a leftover id whose branch holds a commit not on main is still refused with `/unmerged commit/` and keeps its branch. Make the commit with `git commit --allow-empty` on the branch via a worktree or `git commit-tree` + `git update-ref`, so main's checkout is untouched.
- The test "retire validates its arguments like the other operator commands" still passes unchanged (`unknown role: bogus` when no `tumwater/bogus` branch exists). Add one assertion there: `retire --role ../x` fails with `/unknown role/` even after `git update-ref refs/heads/tumwater/x HEAD`. That covers the `CUSTOM_NAME_RE` gate keeping a path-like id out.
- Unit test of `hasRetirableLeftovers`: false for `director` even with a `tumwater/director` branch, false for an id with no branch and no landing ref, and true for an id with only a landing ref (`setRef(root, landingRefName("gone"), mainSha(root))`).
- `tumwater help retire` output contains `accepted while its branch or merge ref remains`. Extend the "tumwater help retire shows the command's usage stanza" test with that match.

### Plain terms state, part 3/5: Add the startup migration hook and move the land queue to merge-queue (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 2/5 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "State and git"; touches src/orchestrator/ src/paths.ts src/landing/ src/loop/leftover.ts src/tick/tick-stage.ts src/status/status-data.ts src/events/ test/) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** tumwater gets one reusable registry of idempotent startup-migration steps. The orchestrator runs it before its first per-runner state read, and a CLI reader can run it safely too. Its first step moves `.tumwater/land-queue/` to `.tumwater/merge-queue/`. Queue entries carry `run` instead of `tick`, and older entries still read.

**Approach.**
- New module src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts holds the registry:
  - `interface StartupMigration { name: string; run(root: string): Promise<string[]> }`. A step returns one short note per thing it moved, and nothing when there was nothing to do. Each step must be idempotent and must tolerate a concurrent run: a source that vanished mid-step is skipped, not an error.
  - `registerStartupMigration(step)` appends to the registry; a duplicate `name` throws.
  - `runStartupMigrations(root)` runs the registered steps in registration order.
    - A step that moved something logs one `state_migrated` event (`source: TUMWATER_SOURCE`, `step`, `moved`, `detail`).
    - A step that throws logs one warning, the remaining steps still run, and the failed step retries at the next start.
    - A second call moves and logs nothing.
  - `runStartupMigrationsIfIdle(root)` is the CLI-reader form. It runs the same steps only when no orchestrator is alive for `root` (`orchestratorAlive`, src/fleet/orchestrator-info.ts), so a CLI process never moves files under a running fleet, which may still be the old build. A live fleet has already migrated at its own start.
- New module src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts is the one place that fixes step order. It imports `registerStartupMigration`, calls it once per step at top level in order, and re-exports `runStartupMigrations`/`runStartupMigrationsIfIdle`. Callers import from this file, so the steps are registered before anything can run. This also avoids an import cycle: startup-migrations.ts never imports the steps. A step's implementation may live in the module that owns the data. Later parts, and the Plain terms role ids series, add a step by appending one `registerStartupMigration(...)` call at the end of this file.
- Call `runStartupMigrations` once, from `runOrchestrator` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts), awaited before the `LoopRunner`s are constructed. Each `LoopRunner` constructor's `loadLoopState` is the first per-runner state read, and the merge pipeline's first queue read comes later. In-process callers, tests and `--once` rounds included, get the same call.
- No CLI command in this series calls the Idle form: the observers read both layouts (below). It exists so the role ids series can migrate from a CLI read path when no fleet is running.
- Add `state_migrated` to the `HarnessEvent` union, an event-format.ts case (`state migrated — <detail>`) and the label map, in its server and browser forms, with a routine tone.
- First step, `mergeQueueDir`:
  - Move every `*.json` in `legacyLandQueueDir(root)` into `landQueueDir(root)` with `fs.renameSync`, keeping the basename, because the queue order lives in the filename.
  - If the basename already exists in the new directory, leave the file in place and note it.
  - Remove the old directory once it is empty.
  - Leave the files' contents as they are.
- src/paths.ts: `landQueueDir` returns `.tumwater/merge-queue`. Plain terms code merge renames the function. Add `legacyLandQueueDir`, which returns `.tumwater/land-queue`.
- src/landing/landing-queue.ts:
  - `LandingEntry.run` replaces `tick`.
  - `isLandingEntry`/`readEntry` accept an entry that carries `tick` instead and map it to `run`.
  - `queueFiles` lists the new directory plus any files still in the legacy one, sorted by basename. `tumwater queue`, `status`, doctor and the dashboard, running in another process before the new orchestrator's first start, therefore show the full queue.
  - `dropLanding` removes by full path, so either directory works.
  - If the vocabulary guard flags a legacy path literal, end its line with `// vocabulary-ok: legacy path read from old layouts`.
- Callers (tsc): `stageTickMerge` (tick-stage.ts), `recoverLeftover` (leftover.ts), landing-vetting.ts, landing-drain.ts, landing-queue-render.ts and status-data.ts. In status-data.ts the `--json`/API key is already `run`. The in-memory `LandRequest.tick` stays; Plain terms code run renames it.
- **Self-hosting:** safe in one part.
  - The old orchestrator enqueues into `land-queue/` until it exits.
  - The new one moves those entries before its first read.
  - Observers on the new build read both directories.
  - The old build never reads `merge-queue/`.
  - A crash mid-migration leaves each file whole in one directory or the other, both are read, and the next start finishes the move.

**Files touched.** src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts (new), src/orchestrator/startup-migration-steps.ts (new), src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts, src/paths.ts, src/landing/landing-queue.ts, src/landing/landing-vetting.ts, src/landing/landing-drain.ts, src/landing/landing-queue-render.ts, src/loop/leftover.ts, src/tick/tick-stage.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts, the label-map module(s); test/startup-migrations.test.ts (new), test/landing-queue.test.ts, test/landing-slot.test.ts, test/doctor-backlog.test.ts, test/cli-queue.test.ts and the others tsc lists (~48 typed sites).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Fixture: a repo whose `.tumwater/land-queue/` holds two entries with `tick` and a torn file. `runStartupMigrations` moves all three into `merge-queue/`, removes `land-queue/` and logs one `state_migrated`. `readLandingQueue` then returns the two entries in their original order with `run` set, and counts the torn file as unreadable. A second call changes nothing and logs nothing.
- `runStartupMigrationsIfIdle` moves nothing while a live orchestrator info file names a running pid, and migrates when none does. Registering a duplicate step name throws.
- Before any migration, `readLandingQueue` on the old layout returns both entries with `run` set.
- After `runOrchestrator` starts on the old-layout fixture, the queued entries are vetted and dropped as before.
- `npm run test` passes.

### Fallback chain, part 6/7: `claudeWindowReserve` leaves part of each subscription window unused by the team (done 2026-10-16; planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 5/7 landed; design in plans/fallback-chain.md "Reserve"; touches src/config/ src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts src/gates/budget-gates.ts src/events/ docs/backends.md and their tests)

**Goal.** The team and you share one claude.ai account. A team that uses up the weekly window by Tuesday leaves your own Claude Code sessions on extra usage, or locked out, until it resets.

This part adds an optional reserve: `"claudeWindowReserve": { "seven_day": 0.8 }`. At or past that utilization, subscription Claude counts as used up for the team until the window resets. The team then moves down its chain (part 1/7), or waits if it has nowhere to go. It also lets the team leave the subscription before a run crosses into overage. The director is exempt: it runs your own prompts. Absent by default.

**Approach.**
- Config: an optional top-level `claudeWindowReserve: Record<string, number>`, mapping a window type to a fraction with 0 < f ≤ 1. Add it to the config schema, validation, the editable/known key lists and the example config.
- `claudeWindowUsedUp(account, now, reserve?)` also returns a non-reset window whose `utilization >= reserve[type]`, with that window's `resetsAt`. It returns a `reason: "rejected" | "reserve"` beside it.
- `claudeWindowObservation` (src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts) holds on a reserve crossing too, so subscription Claude jobs with no fallback wait. The observation carries `reserve: true`. Scheduling must not hold the director on it: the director hold the BUGS.md 2026-10-16 fix adds applies to a rejected window only.
- The budget gate passes the live config's reserve. Part 2/7's director view ignores it.
- A later Claude model in a chain (an `extraUsage` step, part 5/7) would spend the reserved quota before it reaches extra usage. Past the reserve it is usable only once a current reading shows `isUsingOverage`.
- A new `claude_window_reserved` event `{ windowType, utilization, reserve, resetsAt }` is logged once per window, with the same once-per-`type:resetsAt` memory as `pollClaudeWindowWarning`. src/events/event-format.ts renders it.
- docs/backends.md: the key, an example, and the note that the team learns its utilization one run late (readings come only from runs).

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/config/config-keys.ts, src/config/config-editable-keys.ts, src/config/config-example.ts, src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, src/fleet/fleet-polls.ts, src/gates/budget-gates.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts.
- Docs: docs/backends.md, tumwater.example.json.
- Tests: test/claude-account.test.ts, test/fleet-polls.test.ts, test/budget-gates.test.ts, test/config-validation*.test.ts, and test/event-format-fleet.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `seven_day` utilization 0.85 and reserve 0.8:
  - Subscription Claude role jobs move to the fallback.
  - The director stays on Claude.
  - `claude_window_reserved` is logged once.
- At 0.75 nothing moves.

### `tumwater doctor` names disabled roles that still keep a branch, pointing at `tumwater retire --role <id>` (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — touches src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** Disabling a role in `tumwater.json` (or lowering `roles.feature.instances`) stops its runs, but its `tumwater/<id>` branch stays, along with any worktree, landing ref, and paused marker. `tumwater retire --role <id>` (`retireRole` in `src/operator/retire.ts`) removes them, but nothing tells the operator which roles need it. This repo shows the gap: `git for-each-ref refs/heads` lists `tumwater/telemetry` while telemetry is opt-in. The "workspaces" row (`checkWorktreePool`) reports legacy checkout directories and stale pins only. It never looks at branches. Add a doctor row, "leftover role branches", that names each such role and the command that removes its leftovers.

**Approach.**
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`: add `export async function checkLeftoverRoleBranches(root: string, config?: TumwaterConfig | null): Promise<CheckOutcome>`, documented like `checkWorkInstances`. Behavior:
  - No config: return `okOutcome("no readable tumwater.json — nothing to verify")`, the `checkWorkInstances` wording. `checkInit` reports the config itself.
  - List branches with `listBranches(root)` from `src/git/git.ts`. Keep the ones that start with the prefix `branchName("")` (`src/paths.ts`, which is `tumwater/`) and strip the prefix to get an id. Drop an empty id, an id containing `/`, `DIRECTOR_ROLE`, and every id where `loopEnabled(config, id)` (`src/roles/loop-ids.ts`) is true. The director has its own `tumwater/director` branch and is never in `config.roles`, so it is always skipped.
  - Split what remains. An id that `knownRoleIds(config)` (`src/config/config.ts`) includes is retirable, because `cmdRetire`'s `namedRole` accepts exactly those ids. Every other id is unknown. Examples: a removed custom role, or an instance id such as `feature-4` above the configured instance count. `knownRoleIds` adds only `loopIds(config)` instances, so retire rejects those ids as an unknown role.
  - When both lists are empty, return `okOutcome("no branches left by disabled roles")`.
  - Otherwise return `warnOutcome` whose detail joins these parts with `"; "`. The retirable part (when non-empty) is `` `${ids.join(", ")} ${agree(n, "is", "are")} disabled but still ${agree(n, "has", "have")} a branch — \`tumwater retire --role <id>\` removes each (\`--dry-run\` previews)` ``. The unknown part (when non-empty) is `` `${branches.join(", ")} ${agree(n, "names", "name")} no role retire accepts — delete with \`git branch -D\` once its commits are not needed` ``, where the list shows the full branch names (`tumwater/ghost`). Both lists keep `listBranches` order, which is refname order. `agree` comes from `src/text/phrases.ts`.
  - The check is read-only, like every doctor check. It only lists refs.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: add `{ name: "leftover role branches", ...(await checkLeftoverRoleBranches(root, config)) }` to the `checks` array, directly after `"parallel instances"`.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the Audit row's `tumwater doctor` parenthetical, after the clause "waits for a workspace that call for a larger `worktreeSlots`", add ", disabled roles that still keep a `tumwater/<id>` branch (removed with `tumwater retire --role <id>`)". Do not touch any other clause.

**Files touched.** src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts, docs/cli.md, test/doctor-checks.test.ts, test/doctor.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`, "checkLeftoverRoleBranches names disabled roles' branches and unknown ones, skipping enabled roles and the director". Set it up like the `checkWorkInstances` test (`readyRepo()`, then `loadConfig(root)`). Create branches with `sh(root, "git", "branch", <name>)`.
  - With no `tumwater/` branches: `{ level: "ok", detail: "no branches left by disabled roles" }`.
  - With `tumwater/feature` (enabled by default) and `tumwater/director`: still that ok outcome.
  - Adding `tumwater/telemetry` (disabled by default): level `warn`, the detail matches `/telemetry is disabled but still has a branch — `tumwater retire --role <id>`/`, and the detail does not mention `feature` or `director`.
  - Adding `tumwater/ghost`: the detail also matches `/tumwater\/ghost names no role retire accepts/`, after the telemetry part.
  - With `writeConfig(root, { roles: { feature: { instances: 2 } } })`, a `tumwater/feature-2` branch is not named. After `writeConfig(root, {})`, it is listed with the unknown branches.
- `checkLeftoverRoleBranches(root, null)` returns the "nothing to verify" ok outcome.
- `test/doctor.test.ts`: the expected check-name list gains `"leftover role branches"` right after `"parallel instances"`.
